review_text: Wow, really love the food at Katz's  Friendly service.  I will be back more often since they've now renovated the place to add more space.  This place is a winner. The MEGA sandwich is awesome.

Had lunch there sunday. We were the only ones inside for a while (there were others outside). Food was pretty good. I had fish tacos (3) and they were good. My oldest had a salmon pasta thingy that was tasty. And my youngest had mac and cheese that was a pretty good portion for the kids menu. Our waiter did not seem like he wanted to be there though. Overall it won't be a place we go to often but its not bad.

What a cool place.  The kind of downtown food and shopping market that I can only dream of Charlotte having.  We're trying with the 7th Street Public Market but, it's not even a fair comparison. So much to choose from that it literally is mind boggling.  I feel like I would spend part of every weekend here buying seafood, meat, produce, snagging lunch at one of the huge variety of eateries contained within.  I only got to Tommy DiNic's for the roast pork, sharp provolone and broccoli rabe sandwich on this visit and it was awesome but I just wanted to try so many other places. Nice job Philadelphia!
Gluten free, delicious, and everyone that works here is great.  I count myself lucky to live within walking distance of this place

Was just here for lunch. Have to say that the reviews really live up to their hype. Their classic banh mi was deliciously fresh and well favored (I wish they had added more pate- I love pate) because pate is what makes the classic, Classic.  So it's very important that there's enough pate in my opinion. As for the iced coffee, it was good but a bit bitter probably not enough condense milk to make it sweet. Would have been perfect if it was a lil sweeter. Though their place is small, it's quite cute. Workers are nice and informative. And if you plan on coming back on your next visit(s), do not forget to grab a "punch card". You get 1 FREE banh mi of your choice for every 10 stamps. (1 stamp per every $ 6 dollars).

I'm pregnant and can get really grumpy & bitchy when I am hungry. RAWR. I saw Bun-ker on seamless and was tempted to order from them but the 55-70 min delivery wait was a turnoff. First walking in the environment is very welcoming and casual. A chilled and laid back atmosphere with mismatched chairs and tables with vinyl gingham tablecloths. It is a small space only being able to seat 22 people within the restaurant. Plus they also play old school hip hop, which sets off a cool vibe  :) The menu is very was simple and descriptive in explaining their food. We ordered the Papaya Salad & the Bánh Xèo. The papaya salad was great, green crunchy papaya with alot of acid and citrus flavors with a kick of spiciness. yummmmilicious. The Bánh Xèo is an egg crepe with shrimp bacon folded with raw bean sprouts. It was super marvelously delicious and super crispy, loved it!! For our mains I had their Saigon Special sandwich that had pork pate, sausage and bacon with picked veggies and other crunchy goodies. The bread was amazing, soft on the inside and crunchy goodness on the outside. My bf ordered the chili mackerel, I didnt taste it but he said it was "goodies goodies gum drop with a kick to it" Also the sandwiches were served with oversized crab chips.....I loved them so much I took a side order to go and munch on them in the car on our way home from the restaurant. I would definitely come back!! This place transformed my grumpy pregnant Mr. Hyde self and turned me into a very calm and satisfied Dr. Jekyll. teee-hee kekeke

This little gem has an understated elegance through and through. From the décor to the good natured employees to the simple yet carefully crafted dishes. Tsumami Tororo Soba - The Japanese yam creates a stickiness similar to okra.  You gotta try this.  It is so unique and delicious. Yakitori - Skip the Yakitori Ju and get it a la carte, it's so much better. Try the Momo with Shio. Kaisen Don - The usual suspect when you're in the mood for sashimi. Sometimes I wish they'd cut the sashmi thinner. I just like it when it melts in my mouth more than a bite sized fish steak. Desserts were surprisingly underwhelming after such a great meal.  Head over to Chikalicious on 10th/2nd to end the night right.
Their pepperoni curls up and gathers a puddle of pork fat. A puddle of pork fat. do you understand?

Fried dough w/ juicy meat filling: empanadas are flawless culinary specimens. Empanada mama's empanadas are made with whole wheat, fried to perfection (maintains a smooth crispy shell--none of that bubbly, oily nonsense--, and filled to the brim w/o flirting with the nuisance of phantom leakage. The spicy chix is no joke. It's not overwhelmingly spicy, but--as its name suggests--it's spicy. Comprende? "Spicy" is often times misattributed to "spiced" and relatively mild foods. Not here, not by E-Mama. The brazil and chocolate banana are also divine.  My sister likes the viagra and hawaiian. The arroz con pollo w/ plantains is bursting with bold  flavor, and when topped with the guac salsa verde (which is the ultimate best in the city), no harness can quell the fat girl in me. Empanadas are ~$2.50-3.00.  Entrees are ~$13-16. The mint lemonade is super refreshing but not very minty.

Wahoo! I live in Windsor Terrace and the Brooklyn Commune is a much-needed addition to the neighborhood. They have a cafe and offer specialty food products and produce. The owners are very friendly and work a lot with the community and local food artisans. I hope to try everything eventually but can recommend the BLT and prepared salads. My only issue is the parents that bring in their unruly children that run wild through the place screaming and grabbing at all of the produce and specialty food products. Parents, please control your children and have some respect for this new business - if they can't behave, don't bring them out.

YUM!!! We thoroughly enjoyed eating in this tiny yet cozy restaurant. At best I counted seating for 26, but found it very charming. The service was fantastic. Our server was knowledgeable, super nice and friendly and not too intrusive. They knew just the right time to approach you to take away plates and ask you how the food is. We started with the calamari appetizer in a very yummy ragout. The presentation was unique and the squid was very tender. We also got the oysters for an appetizer, which my husband could not stop raving about (and proceeded to order more and more of). The mignonette was a perfect balance for the saltiness of the oysters.  My husband (not being a huge fan of fish- good thing I took him to a restaurant called Little Fish) ordered the Bibb Salad (awesome dressing) and the scallop appetizer (which was perfectly glazed and prepared). For dinner I ordered the Skate with Spaetzle. The fish was perfectly prepared and my husband kept reaching across the table to try the skate (must be good if he's eating fish). My only compaint would be that the Spaetzle was a bit salty for my taste and I avoid salt like the plague (so for others it might be just perfect). For dessert we ordered this delicious key lime tart. Really fluffy with just the right flavor. All in all highly recommended!!

Wow. This place is great. I don't understand why there aren't more grilled cheese places around but it's a genius concept. The first time I ordered from Melt Shop I got the buttermilk fried chicken sandwich and shop tots with extra melt sauce. The sandwich was so good. It was moist and melty and tangy and crunchy and a little spicy. All good things. The tots were out of this world good. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. They put this great seasoning on them too. Also the melt sauce is great. I'm thinking it's sour cream mixed with sriracha. The next time, I got the one with fontina, goat cheese, pesto and mushrooms and it was even better than the first. The flavors were all just so amazing together. It was the perfect texture and consistency and the sandwich itself was very manageable and easy to eat. I ordered the tomato soup too so I could dip the sandwich which really took the thing to the next level.
Pro: distinct atmosphere, beer selection, location Neutral:food (crab salad was deece), service Con: waits and elbow rom at bar

Very crowded in the early evenings. We went super late so getting a table was easy....the Margaritas are amazing and fresh. The food is delicious and very authentic. Overall experience was great;) too bad we were filled because I really wanted to try the churro's dipped in chocolate!

Pizza is excellent. But the waiters are terrible. The guy waiting on us had to continually be flagged down. He was less than interested in us. He was so focused on doing his cleaning and other stuff. I run a business. If my people made my customers feel this unwanted, I would get rid of them. My poor rating is purely on service. Just terrible.

I strolled into Kitchen Zinc as a second option after realizing that BAR had an hour and a half wait for pizza. I am so glad that I did! New Haven may be a one trick town, but Kitchen ZINC puts a nice little twist on that very trick. It was around 8:15p on a Saturday night and every seat in KZ was packed so we took the only available seats at the bar.  We took a few minutes to peruse the menu and ordered up some drinks, 2 cosmo's and a glass of Montepuliciano.  The cosmo's were definitely some of the best in New Haven and they get points for even having that particular wine and serving it properly.  When it came to pizzas, everything looked amazing so we decided on the shrimp pie from the "white menu" and the tomato from the "red menu".   While waiting for our pies to come out, we watched others be delivered to their tables and they all looked amazing.  I will definitely be back to try others.  Ours had finally arrived, they looked and smelled amazing.  The tomato pie was a burst of fresh ingredients in each bite.  Fresh tomato, basil pesto, roasted garlic, fontina cheese and topped with an herb salad.  The shrimp pizza was decadent. Lot's of shrimp with a basil caper pesto and goat cheese.  Equally as delicious.  While they do boast artisan flair, which they pull off quite well, the pizza is in line with anything you'd expect when coming to New Haven.  Thin, crispy crust, and fabulous.  It would not disappoint even the most discriminating pizza-loving palate.   They do have a few salads, bruschetta and charcuterie for appetizers which we didn't sample, but I am eager to go back! **The pies only come in one size however, between 3 people, we shared two pies and had left overs to take home.

Love this place. My friend just moved in above it and asked me to meet her for a drink here on Friday night. It's adorable. It's all brick and has bookshelves in it and feels very vintage. The staff was super friendly and the menu is great. Definitely go here!

Came here to pick up a bag of 50 pork and leek frozen dumplings for $10. The meat was fresh but they could have used some more flavor. The skin is a bit too thick, which neutralizes the flavor of the filling, and also sticks to the pot too easily (on some occasions I had to use steel wool to scrub off the remains). Overall, more salt and less skin would have been better.

Probably one of the better bbq joints I have gone to in NYC. This place has a cool atmosphere with live music in the evening on the weekend which is great. The brisket and pulled pork were delicious.  The jerk ribs were pretty good too, but way too pricey for ribs. if you are looking for good bbq in Bklyn and don't mind a bit of a wait, I suggest you try this place out.
Excellent service, excellent wine, excellent food. Calm quaint ambiance especially outside seating. I took a group that was hard to please and they all thoroughly enjoyed. Great experience.

Ippudo, I remember when I first came here, I was dazzled by the smoke and mirrors effect of the nice environment and the friendly staff. I remember thinking the pork buns were amazing and the ramen being pretty good. After breaking the initially spell that was cast on me from before, I went back to Ippudo with a friend for lunch the other day, and I realized a couple of things. This is a place you should check out at least once, and yes you should have the pork buns, 2 for $8. Yes, that is equivalent to 8 whopper jrs or double cheeseburger at Burger King. And the while the ramen is tasty, I had to drink all the soup just to feel a little satisfied because the amount of noodles they gave were hardly enough to fill up my hungry stomach. Most of the ramens for lunch were priced at $13, just think of the burgers you could get for that price, you could feed a family. I realized, I'm usually big on quantity more than quality, not that I like eating massive amounts of cardboard but, I just don't think the price for what you get at Ippudo is better than walking down the street to other Japanese ramen places for maybe half the price for the same amount of food, but that's just me. If you want tasty pork buns, try Mei Li Wah bakery in Chinatown for 80 cents for one. So let's do some math, 10 pork buns for 80 cents is $8. Ippudo's pork buns 2 for $8 (plus tax).... 10 is greater than 2 people... Don't get me wrong, you should try this place out, and you should spend the money at least once to try it...I won't be waiting a hour to throw away my money at this place anymore...

I was in NY last October. And of course nothing is better on a nice cold day that soup! Ramen preferably! Ippudo NY was said to be one of the best if not the best ramen joint in east village/ny. I have to agree! The wait when I went was about 45 min. Was close to leaving but by the looks of the line if people whom were staggering we decided to stay. One of the best decisions of my life  the ramen was so flavorful. I can't even recall what I got, was straight fire though!  Extra pork belly, chili paste and KAEDAMA! Paired beautifully with Brooklyn breweries kaedama ale. A nice malty brown with a slight hop finish. My type if beer! Next time I'm out here, Ippudo ny is a must!

Finally, a place to get decent Szechuan without going all the way to Han Dynasty! While Spice 28's food doesn't quite measure up to Han's, that's a pretty high bar and in no way reflects poorly on the quality of its dishes. I went for lunch today and had an appetizer of spicy cucumber, which was delicious. For my meal, I got one of the very reasonably priced lunch specials of dry pepper chicken with dumpling soup. The portions were very generous (I have leftovers), and the chicken was actually very pleasingly spicy! All in all, I'm so happy Spice 28 is in the neighborhood. I'll definitely have to try their Thai menu items the next time I go. If they're anywhere near as good as their Szechuan dishes, I may have found a new go-to Thai place as well.

THE PIZZA IS AMAZING. I am a New Yorker girl. I moved to Nj when I got married. I couldn't find a good pizza place like Brooklyn New York. We're real Italian people make good pizza. Until I ordered over the phone. I never been there in person. But they deliver to the house. there pizza is off the hook. I ordered a couple of things but the pizza is the best by far.
This is the place to go for Sushi in Burlington. They have great drinks & their rolls are creative!

Took a trip to NY, my daughter suggested we go to  Harlem to eat at Amy Ruth's all I heard was wonderful things about the food.  I ordered the Ruby Dee-fried catfish, collard greens, and yams.  The catfish was wonderful, the greens were good, the yams were good.  I tasted my daughters mac and cheese and it was great!  This restaurant reminded me a little of home on a Sunday afternoon.  But did not come close to Mama's cooking.

I have been here twice, the first time I loved it, the second time not as much. I came here with my boyfriend and sat outside. The seating is really nice outside and its usually pretty busy inside and out the restaurant. We ordered the drunken noodles but the noodles were not the same this side they came out really mushy. The flavor was still good though as long as you look spicy, I believe you can ask for it not spicy anyway. The servers are honestly really nice but you can tell they are really busy unless they were just understaffed that day but we didn't end up getting too much attention. I also got the duck with eggplant and bamboo shoot, it was just alright. My boyfriend got pineapple chicken which he liked. The only thing I really liked was the chicken stock rice.

I am really a fan of the place. They have a beautiful and attentive crew, the food is always good, and the location is the best on Church street next to Leunigs..The staff manages to handle the popularity of the place very well, which is not an easy task. I've been many times and will continue to go back. The appetizer are a meal (for me) The burgers and fish & chips are huge and reasonably priced, and the rest of the menu diverse enough for almost everyone. But now its time for an update.. many of the restaurants in town (including this one) have "updated" their menus by increasing prices waaaay too much. Out of the range of acceptability for me anyway.. Sorry Sweetwaters,  but you'll end up losing more in the long run. 4 stars down to 3, and much less of me!

Everyone is always talking about going to Scarpetta's for italian food, and so I bit the bullet and went with a couple of friends last weekend.  I'm not a food snob or anything, but I do like to eat, and I really didn't find anything exceptional about the food here.  There's a bit of a scene to be had at the bar, and its also located in the Meat Packing, but relative to the difficulty it is to get a reservation here, i'm not really sure its worth it.  I felt that there are better options for this kind of food in the city, and i also felt if you're looking for a cool restaurant bar to hang out in, there are also better options.

Texas girl meets NYC pizza love at first bite!!!! My bf and I travel A LOT together, and one of the places most traveled to for us is NYC. so I've had my fair share of ny pizza. now I am NOT a New Yorker so this review may not have as much meaning as someone that lives there and eats it regularly. This is coming from a woman that had pizza 2-3X a week though....and I LOVE good pizza. THIS IS WITHOUT A DOUBT, the BEST PIZZA I've EVER EATEN ANYWHERE. Hands down. Not the most friendly service I've ever encountered but they keep your drinks filled and the pizza is out fast. Its chewy but not too chewy with a little crispness in the crust. Thin but not so thin that its soggy. It is what I imagine heaven would be like if I got hit my a mack truck. Perfect amount of gooey cheese, insanely awesome sauce and I can't describe other than its just perfection. If you havent been there, GO!!!!! i love it, he loves it and everyone should love it, its THAT good!!!!!!

Saw this restaurant the day we arrived in New York. It's very unassuming with no signs. We first thought it was a super secret restaurant seeing only people in suits and dresses go in. It actually turned out to be a cute cafe that is an oasis from the busy city surrounding it. It was nice getting away from all the noise of the city and being able to enjoy a secluded brunch surrounded by nature. Natural sunlight was able to come through the transparent ceiling and really made you feel like you were having your meal outside. Sashimi Zuke Don - One of the best things I had in New York. The poke and rice were a perfect match. They didn't skimp on the fish either. The entire dish was covered in poke, which was marinated just right and tasted fresh. Great dish to start a late day.

I just had a business dinner here tonight, and I my entire group without exception was very dissatisfied with the food.  One of the worst parts of the meal was the fish, which was suppose to come filleted but instead came with head and tail (no problem).  We asked the waiter to fillet the fish, and what came back was a pile of mush filed with bones.  Inedible.  The cheese plate was very good, but the waiter didn't remember the names of all of the cheeses.  Also, our waitress was polite, but we didn't see very much of her, and when we were finished with our entrees, we were searching for her.  Bottom line is that my group found Osteria to be below average at best -- at least on this Thursday night -- but from my perspective I would likely not return voluntarily.  As an aside, the restaurant is very, very rustic.

This will be short and sweet.  I am giving this  4 star.  The restaurant deserves a 5 star for the food, service, appearance.  The parking situation is really bad.  Would love to eat there more often but the parking struggle is not worth more frequent visits..
Perfect place to grab breakfast or lunch. I went here with a friend and everything we ordered was delicious. The staff is very friendly and welcoming, i would definitely go back.

whoa. the sangria was REALLY GOOD! I would come back just for the sangria. I got the clam pie (HAHAHAHA clam pie!!!- I am so immature) and I would come back again one day for the clam pie- but not for a long time because I am a sausage eater.

I'm sorry to say that with only one previous visit (which resulted in adverse stomach issues for two patrons), my second visit was a total disappointment - Not related to food, but service related instead. This was one of those situations where my party was unable to pass go. 2 persons of a three party arrived to be seated. We were denied seating - the entire party had to be present. When asked could we order drinks while we waited. Again we were denied service. A total disappointment.

Both food and service was decent and menu has some solid options. It's just too loud esp on Saturday mornings since it appears to be the neighborhood family hangout. Not cheap, but it is Tribeca, so know before you go.
The chef salad was very disappointing.  Service was good.

I used to live right around the corner and developed the bad habit of stopping there for take out 2-3 times a week...BUT it is all so very very good! I've had many things on the menu, Jerk Chicken, Garlic Shrimp, Macaroni and Cheese, a simple salad...like I said I tried many things and everything is the BEST! There is often a line out the door and if you eat in it's a small little loft dining space that's charming and cozy!  I moved to Washington Heights in Manhattan so I don't get there very often any more...BUT I was there on Friday for the first time in about a year and the two great ladies who own and run the place still remembered me! The food is great and the company is just as great! Now if only I can get some of their wonderful receipes! My favorite place to recommend and take my friends!
A great experience overall. Sushi was excellent and Martha Stewart was sitting nearby. That pretty much says it all.
Good place to meet up with friends and drink. Relaxed atmosphere with TVs. Mac and cheese was pretty good. Decent burger and sandwiches. Cool nautical decor. Service was decent.
Terrible service they slam food on table when it's served. Fries are done in very dirty oil they look burnt   Place needs to be updated

I used to like this place but it's gone totally downhill. We waited one hour for us to be seated for our reservation then we were charged extra for brunch without being told prior because we were a large party. No customer service at all

Let me start by saying, I can't count how many times this truck has saved me during many drunken outings.     And by saving, I mean providing me with a delicious, satisfying meal thats affordable even during the worst of times. I've had my fair share of Halal food throughout Manhattan, Queens and even some places in the Bronx, but as cliche as this might sound, nothing beats 53rd Street Halal when it comes to Halal carts or food carts in general.   First off, the service is phenomenal. Now, you may be asking yourself, "it's a food truck, how good can their service be?" Well for starters, they're fast. Seriously, they could have a line halfway down the block and you'll be served within mere minutes. Not to mention, they usually have plates already freshly made and still hot by the time you order. Seriously, I ordered a bizarre combo of falafel and chicken with rice yet even when I expected to wait off at the side for a bit, the chef handed me my plate within seconds. They're prepared for just about anything.   Now the food itself, picture your standard plate of lamb/chicken with rice from any other cart. Now, just like pizza, it's nearly impossible to have a bad plate of Halal food so let's just say that no matter where you go, it's good and you know what to expect from every spot. Now, amplify the flavor and freshness of that plate tenfold and you've got a 53rd Street Halal plate. The portions are generous and they even throw in pita bread to boot. Yeah, you don't have to ask for it, they know that too. Also, the sauces are all self-served so you don't have to worry about them drenching your food in whatever sauce you ask for, but that's just a little plus for me.   Point is, if you're in the area and aren't looking to spend over $10 on just a decent meal, seek them out. Even at awkward hours, you'll be sure to find people standing around so you can't really miss it.
Great quality delicious food. Very friendly and attentive staff, manager Alisa was very accommodating and did a great job organizing our private party. Will definitely return!
Quesadilla carnitas. Mmmmmmm. Often standing room only but it's worth the wait. Hope they get a bigger place soon.

A solid meal.  My boyfriend and I went there last Wednesday prepared to wait and have cocktails at another restaurant.  We were told the wait would approximately be an hour, we put our names on a list (specifying we wanted a table), and received a call that our table was ready 45 minutes later. The restaurant feels like a quaint shabby chic farmhouse and boasts an open kitchen. It was refreshing.  However, this is a farmhouse that is willing to accommodate as many villagers as possible, including the occasional idiots, so you will likely be in close proximity to your neighbors, who may or may not be extremely loud and ignorant. Our table was located in the middle of the main room, which was quite loud in part due to the music, and I was unable to hear my boyfriend.  If you're going on an early in the game date, you may want to sit in a place that doesn't mandate shouting.  The place was packed the evening we visited so the service was extremely slow, the syrup canister we were given was a  sticky mess, and the only bathroom appeared to be a war zone, littered with paper towels with the toilet covered in urine.  At least people are washing their hands, so that's a positive. We ordered a decent amount of food- fried chicken, deviled eggs, waffles, mac and cheese, and gooey corn spoonbread.  Everything was hot and flavorful.  As others have pointed out, the waffles are not as crisp as they can be, but the chicken was crispy and moist and the mac and cheese was perfectly cooked. The gooey corn spoonbread tasted a bit like baby food to me, but I have never had that dish so I'm not in a position to judge.   Is it the best fried chicken in the city?  I think that's clearly subjective, taking into account the fact that people genetically vary in their experience of taste.  Most people seem to like it. The bottom line is that chicken is good.  The food is good. If you don't mind the prices and are reasonable about the time you may have to wait, there's a moderate to high probability you'll enjoy it.

Fantastic meal from start to finish. My wife and I split appys. The grilled scallops were cooked perfectly and served on a bed of not over-dressed salad that had a beautiful citrus flavor. My wife got the lobster served on a bed of corn flavored with vanilla and ginger. All I can say is wow, that was really special. The local roasted chicken with black trumpet mushrooms was just the kind of comfort food you'd want on a cool fall evening. My thyme and garlic marinated grilled shrimp with the house mac and cheese was also fantastic. The shrimp were cooked perfectly..just so you get that little pop when you bite into them. The mac and cheese is a very light version, not at all heavy and served with some grilled zucchini. Bring a nice Sancerre and a Rhone red and you are on cloud 9. Service was great. Cheers.

I don't have any complains about the food here but the level and speed of service is horrendous, especially if you're in a group of 4 or more. The last time I was here at noon, my table of 4 did not get our ramen till 1.05pm and the service staff was not friendly/nice about the delay either. Today, there are other tables that got their ramen before our table of 6 did and my friend who had a similar prior experience was told that the chef deprioritizes orders from larger tables. That sucks!

1) Meh 2) Meh 3) The namesake pizza is not all that 4) Meh 5) Brewery 6) Meh 7) Hype To point One - i really think that the quality and variety of this place was diapointing - Muzzarella Pizza (just around the corner) is SO much better yelp.com/biz/muzzarella-… Two - This is NYC - there is better pizza all over, this would fly in Texas, but so do corn dogs Three - If your NAME is ARTICHOKE the pizza with it's name better be FANTASTIC and not just ok - this was gooey (not in a good way) bland and boring... Four - Waiting in line  - really? Five - Bud light and Coors on tap DO NOT make you a brewery...REALLY!!? Six - Staff/size/attitude are all annoying Seven - the line is due  to some amazing marketing or some Hilton-esque velvet-rope crap, but this IS NOT worth the hype...the owners must have paid 200 of their relatives to stand in line for the first month (brilliant marketing - silly newyorkers) \In summation - Meh
Nice old cool diner, but pricey for what you get, even for the neighborhood.

Great traditional deli food!  Everything you would want on the menu, and the prices are way cheaper than other delis in the area (or in NY or NJ) for that matter. They got our whole synagogue group of 35 people in at once on a Sunday afternoon and went out of their way for us!   The real deal.
FYI, is Ecuadorian place food form the shore

Easilly the classiest eats on South Street (which these days, ain't saying much), Foy's menu items are time tested - woderfully fried calamari, solid burger, surprisingly tasty chimichangas - with an always top-notch beer selection on tap.  Soups aren't necessarilly their forte, but I'll give them this - the dawn of fall brings with it a curried sweet potato broth with toasted coconut that's way better than it sounds. All that plus the most entertaining people watching in the city...if you're into that sort of thing.

My boyfriend and I have been trying to eat here for a while. However, when we entered the restaurant, we were greeted with an angry woman who went on about coupons before even hearing that we had one. Don't go there if you have a restaurant.com certificate. Her bad attitude made it so that the 60 seconds we spent in the restaurant will be the only minute we ever spend there. What a waste of 2 quarters in the meter and $50 spent at restaurant.com.

Had my birthday brunch here.  My 20 guests were accomodated beautifully.  Made a reservation a week in advance, they seated us downstairs.  The waitress was wonderful, she brought out these baskets of bread and sticky buns and all was delicious.  It was like a wedding so i didn't get to eat much at my own event, but i've had the fontina omelet before and I always enjoy it.  Everyone seemed pleased with the service, food and price.  Last year my brunch was held at Jane, and The Smith did a much better job.  Mostly due to the fact that their downstairs seating isn't sterile but instead brick walled with high ceilings.  Some camp reunions and drunken bachelorette parties surrounded us, but people remained tame.  Might make this place my annual spot.

Im happy to see the hipster influence in Astoria now spreading westward towards my grandparents old broadway and 46th street stomping grounds. I had a late lunch here with the girlfriend on a rainy weekday and we were overall pretty pleased with the outcome of our decision. A grilled cheese place with some style. An eclectic menu that can satisfy the easiest of cravings with some original and innovating dishes from simple cores. Didnt get much of a thrill from the soups or salads but as side pieces they were fine. The atmosphere makes for a nice changes coming off of a very busy and dirty steinway. I'll definitely hit this place up again when im on the other side of steinway.
Five stars for a chain! What a nice surprise.  I try to avoid chain restaurants, but this one is pretty good. I have been there twice and both times had a very pleasant experience, service included.

Having a get-together with good friends, Korchma Taras Bulba was picked out of line-up of places - the location was perfect, just a short walk from Broadway - and food looked very good. I got there early, and since it was too cold to stand outside, hostess walked me to our table in the corner so I could wait for rest of the company to arrive (which gave me an opportunity to look around and take some pictures, hooray!). As all themed restaurants, it is kitschy, but with all authentic elements - decorations, old pictures, white linen embroidered curtains on the faux wall window. Hosts are super-nice and welcoming, which is also one of the elements of  authentic Ukranian restaurant - they are warm and inviting people. There are several cocktails and beers on the menu - ask waitress about Ukrainian beers, they are pretty good! Now, to the food choices. We ordered a lot of appetizers, or zakuski to share - it became sort of family style to try a little bit everything, and also reminded me of holiday get-together at my mom's house. That's exactly how it was, down to homemade aspect of food that served here. This was a trip down memory lane for me... We tried blini, pirozhki, draniki, few salads, vareniki and lots of other good stuff - but draniki (latkes) with sour cream definitely stood out for me. Deliciously crisp on outside, well seasoned, with real, rich sour cream - oh, I can eat those all day every day! Pickled veggies platter was another winner - I looooove little pickled tomatoes! Do not try to get them with a fork, they will burst - just take one with your fingers and pop into your mouth! There were also whole pickled grapes on a plate that came as a surprise to me - I have not had those in a long time, they were yummmy. You get a free shot of flavored vodka with yelp checkin - which we all did. Ginger-flavored was good, ice-cold and easy to drink. Towards the end of the meal, our gracious hosts came around with array of hats and flower-adorned headbands (traditional folk) to try on and take pictures - we had a BLAST doing that! There was one more surprise waiting for us at the end of the bar, as we were leaving - traditional shot of vodka and a pickle - na pososhok! Loved the food, the service and all the fun. If you looking for something unique and different, give them a try!
If you have a date with Tiny Elvis, you should bring him here. The tacos would be the perfect size for him!

I only came here for the bar. I like the ambiance and the 60's music was great. Extra points to the server that saw me standing, thanked me for not just stealing a seat from a table and the getting me a seat. Showed me that it was a quality staff working there. I'd love to come back

The best.  Good food, comfortable atmosphere.  Owned and run by a couple who are always there - no slacking off by the staff when the owner is gone.  We, the family, used to take my father-in-law who was in a wheelchair and they were considerate about arraigning things for him to be comfortable (not always the case in other places).  At 97, his favorite was the meat lovers pizza.

How many Italian restaurants have you been to where it feels authentically Italian and not the Americanized Italian? Not many I believe. Well, if you're looking for a more traditional Italian feel as if it was from Italy, then come to this place. Before I start my critiques on this place, please make sure to make a reservation because this place gets packed!! WIth that said, I reserved a table for this place for a friend's going away party. It immediately gave me that feel of Italy just from where my table was at. They sat me in the back area which almost had that feel that you were outside and the backdrop looked like you were right outside the villas at the countryside in Italy. On to the food. I'm not a huge fan of bruschettas because when I go to Italian restaurants, either the bread is too hard or the toppings make the bread feel soggy. Not the case here. The bread stayed nice and toasty. In addition, the mushrooms with arugula and parmesan cheese was like a melts in your mouth type bruschetta. If you don't believe me, you should go to the upper east side and try it for yourself. As for the entree, I got the salmon fillet. If you think that Italian food is all about pizza and pasta, well then you don't know Italian food very well. The skin had that crispiness as if you were biting a potato chip. Moreover, the fish was cooked properly. If anyone asks you "how do you know the fish was cooked properly?" The answer is that it's not overcooked. When you're out with friends for dinner, there are 3 components of a great dinner aside from great company. A light appetizer to warm up your taste buds, an entree to indulge your savory side and a glass of wine to finish it off. If you prefer to unleash your sweet tooth, dessert is always an option. Then that would be the 4th component.
Great pancakes!!!!
This place is everything. The food is authentic and delicious. The staff is knowledgeable and charming. I love that everything is family style, it makes for a better experience in my book.

Two of us arrived at 7:30 for an 8 pm reservation for four and checked in with the host, who was very cordial but didn't have room to seat us just yet.  No problem, we'd wait outside, it was a nice night.  A few minutes later he came out and invited us in and let us sit before the rest of our party arrived.  We were welcomed and offered menus and water and told not to rush. When the rest of our group arrived, we took a good deal of time visiting and looking over the menu, were never rushed and the host / sommelier was very helpful. Be mindful that a lot of things are flexible here, portion sized can be increased or reduced to fit your party's size.  We ended up splitting a good number of the items: Kale, beets, papas bravas, mushroom tacos (great), baked brie, pork belly blackeye peas, meatballs (great), and I think one other. Most were very acceptable, with the mushroom tacos and the meatballs being something a little more special. The table service was great, not too much, drinks always filled. It's small, it's intimate, it's cozy, and I don't think I would have ever found it on my own.   Good, fun place.

Best French toast I've ever had! I am an avid bruncher and search far and wide for amazingly delicious brunch and especially French toast! My friend had organic scramble eggs, home fries, toast and salad for $4.00 and was so fresh and so good. We went on a Saturday morning and waited maybe 15 minutes for a table but it was well worth it!!! Try it!! You won't be disappointed.

This place is amazing.  I went there for the first time yesterday and we arrived 15 minutes before happy hour, and they didn't pressure us to order before HH started so that was a nice way to begin everything.   We ordered the vegan wings and a grilled artichoke and spinach salad that was a special for the evening.  The food was AMAZING!!!  I have attempted to follow a vegetarian lifestyle for the past few months, but I have this terrible weakness for buffalo wings.  So when my friend brought me here to try their vegan wings, I am happy to say they were way better than I ever expected them to be!   The protein was like the crunchy pieces from real chicken wings and mixed with brussel sprouts and it was served with an apricot horseradish sauce.  I admit the sauce sounded like an odd choice but when you try it all together...phenominal. The salad was this delicate, delicious mix of grill artichoke hearts (which slightly warmed the dressing, and it was lovely), baby spinach, capers, red onions, and a citrus vinaigrette.  I recommend this salad as great option for sharing before jumping into the other yummy food.   The happy hour times are great for people who are traveling from a distance (like myself) who want good food at reasonable prices.  They had a great selection of beer that was part of HH, and overall this was a very satisfying experience.  I will be back, and hopefully often!

In the beginning I was skeptical about the "authenticity" of this place because the menu is a mix of Japanese, Thai and probably Malaysian food too. But I was blown away. The basil beef I had was fresh and well executed. The pineapple rice my friend had was also nice. Waiters and waitresses were helpful.

Four stars because of the no reservations and no take out policy, but then again I understand that their kitchen may not be able to accommodate the volume as walk-ins suffice for their business.  The trick is to get there as soon as the door opens at 5:30 or else you may have to wait for over an hour or two depending on your party size. As for the food, it's truly tasty and a different take on Japanese food that we are used to here in America.  Our all time favorites are the sweet fatty pork, beef Short Ribs, takoyaki balls, Eel tempura with citrus salt, sauteed green beans with pork all enjoyed with the salty cod fried rice.  Pair it with their beer cocktails (Peach is my favorite), and you're good to go in enjoying it "Tapas style" with good friends and great conversations.  Definitely a MUST try!

Great find! Upon entering, we first noticed how beautifully the place is decorated. We had a lovely table for 6 by the window and we were first greeted at our table by the chef, who happens to be the owner's son. The food was delicious--we all enjoyed what we had ordered! They also can make many of the menu options gluten-free, as is indicated on the menu. While we were eating, the owner, Dominic, came over to our table; we enjoyed chatting with him hearing his stories about when he worked at the Helmsley Palace Hotel in NYC. Very warm, friendly staff and great food. We'll be back for sure!

This is another Yelp assist.   I took my husband to Fuerza Bruta for his birthday and wanted to take him out for dinner before hand.  Thanks to Yelp I was able to search the neighborhood for a really cool, nice restaurant.  I knew this was the place to go when I read the reviews on the Fried Chicken- my husbands favorite. We arrived right at 5:30, a few people were at the bar having drinks and the hostess told us the kitchen isn't ready just yet but that we could hang at the bar and she would seat us soon.  Not a problem.  It gave us a few moment to take in the cool decor  and ambiance.  My husband went to use the bathroom ( 1 unisex room ). I was beginning to worry because he was gone so long.  Just as I was about to go and find him he came out with a huge smile.  He wouldn't stop talking about the cool beer poster and the "eye exam."  Later I too became distracted when I went to the bathroom.  That beer poster is really cool.   When our table was ready (about 5 minutes later) our friendly server took our order.  We also received a roll with butter as we waited for the Bacon Peanut Brittle for $5.  The bread and butter was a great addition and helped us wait patiently for our food. The Peanut Brittle was awesome!  No more should be said about it.  We both got the Fried Chicken $19 for 2 large pieces and a salad.  As other reviewers have said this was the best fried chicken ever!  The salad was perfect, even my fried food junkie of a husband ate all of his.  The chicken WOW, perfectly crispy breading with very moist white meat chicken.  We split the "Gladys Knight It's It" peach-bourbon-praline ice cream sandwich, $4, for dessert. It was decadent and delicious! For drinks I had the "summer drink o' fun" ('nuff said)- with bourbon, strawberries, pomegranate, and benny's 5 spice. I also tried the "porch swing" (it's back!) brandy, sweet tea, lemonade, and mint.  Both were $11.  I preferred the Summer Drink hands down.  The Porch Swing was too sour for me. My husband had a tap beer and a can of PBR $3. My husband LOVED his birthday dinner here.  Service was great, food awesome, and a 12 minute walk to Fuerza Bruta on a nice full belly.
Excellent yakitori. Got the tongue, the harami, and a karubi don. All cooked perfectly. Had some tasty unfiltered house sake to top it off. Delicious. Like how the Candy Crush dude says it.

Silk City is best described as a 1950s diner meets a 1970s disco overcome by hipsters.  The Pork Belly Empanadas are delicious, a must order.  I had the Ham Hock Mac & Cheese, it was heavy on the Mac & Cheese, light on the Ham Hock (I think there was some in there).   The reason for the 3 stars is the service.  It is your privilege to be able to be served at Silk City (at least if you are sitting in the Lounge).  Do not expect anything more than your dishes to be changed and your check.  In fact, the most attention that was paid to us was when it was time for the check.  Drinks were empty (thank goodness for water), and I don't think I saw our waitress until it was time for the check.

Is it too late to put the 5th Annual Dim Sum Brunch on the calendar?  Bc I AM READY! We randomly ended up coming here after the suggestion of a bartender in the nabe. Lo and behold, it was the 4th Annual Dim Sum Brunch!  Luckily, we came in towards the end of brunch and managed to snag a table shortly after arrival.  Host was adorable and assisted us with settling in nicely prior to getting our table.  Service was great... and we ordered about 4 different small plates and 3 large plates bc we just couldn't decide! Lots of food... and yep, we ate it all!   Loved the chorizo wontons, the sweet and sour duck meatballs, short rib dumplings, and scallion and salmon pancakes.  Didn't totally love the moo shu pork... that was just ok.  However, considering the gluttony that was going on... along with bloody marys and tea... we were juuuuust fine. Music is amazing.  Definitely will be back.  Don't stop what you're doing, JL.   You're the best.

I eat only the veggie dogs, but they are the shit. I've had a few different options but I usually make my own dog jawn. The owner of the place is always courteous and helpful - he provides guidance if you look lost evaluating all your options. Anyway, haven't had a bad dog there. I suggest getting the combo since the fries are spot-on. To the people ragging on the buns, I take exception - I actually enjoy the buns. They are definitely a different bun, but I think they complement the dogs quite well.

I've heard so much about blue ribbon that when my friend suggested going here for din, I was pumped.  With regards to the space / decor, it's pretty average.  I think they're the epitome of that famous "dont judge a book by its cover" quote because albeit average, the food is relatively decent.  Not the best I've ever had by any means, but decent - highly recommend the shrimp ravioli.  Service is above par and they are GREAT at making sure your wine glass is never empty.  I'm not sure I would make it a point to come back here if not for a friend, but it was worth the try!
Hmm... Awesome indoor market - Wander around and make sure to visit Termini's and get a banana (just tell the lady at the counter)

The best boozy brunch in the city, worth a trip all the way downtown for us. The tapas are delicious and the drinks are great.  Everything is prepared perfectly with amazing attention to detail. This is one of those restaurants that you can comfortably suggest to other people and not worry about whether they will like it or not.  We use this restaurant when we have people in from out of town for business or for any occasion that calls for a brunch.

I was craving fishball noodle soup, so there is only one place in chinatown that I personally know of that makes a really good fishball noodle soup, and that's Bo Ky.  I have been coming here for at least a decade and their soup tastes the same as it did ten years ago.  The egg noodles are perfectly cooked al dente.  The soup actually tastes like real soup, unlike some other chinatown joints who give you yellow salty water as soup.  They add ground pork and some sort of salty preserved vegetable pieces in it that add a really nice flavor to the dish. The restaurant itself is basically just like all the other holes in the wall all over chinatown.  If you go there during peak lunch hour, expect to share a table with strangers while they slurp away at their noodles next to you, splashing their soup on you. The service there is basically non existent.  They give you tea in a styrofoam cup, take your order and slam your soup on your table.  Then you don't see them again for your whole meal until you have to flag them down for your check. That's what you get at Bo Ky, good food and nothing else!

Totto Ramen is the new Chicken Soup for the soul. Yay for outsourcing - Asians are just better at ...well...everything! Sit at the bar, enjoy the show - and notice the silence that envelops the restaurant as diners slurp their noodle. No one talks when they eat here, because that would disrespectful to the perfection that is a bowl of Ramen at Totto's!

Why don't you love me back??? Why will no one acknowledge there are 3 groups no one will even acknowledge to get seated for over 5 minutes. I have been so loyal, traveling to stop by whenever I can and in the area. I love the food. Read the previous review, it's very good. This last visit is a solid 3.5, I never even got my coffee.

Mighty cool vibe, bordering on the somewhat upscale - certainly in terms of price points but Agricola was totally worth a trip in on a rather cold weekday evening. Others must share the opinion - this was the only place teeming with people on a street where global cuisine options abound aplenty! The carrot soup was spectacular, as was my squash flat bread, my prosecco cocktail and the flavor from my coworkers chicken had me almost give up my anti-poultry habits! A shout out also to Mary, who not only waited our tables, but her cheerful demeanor and extensive treasure trove of local know-how was a breath of fresh air! We found our way to the hallowed grounds of campus which is just a stone's throw from the restaurant too! Farm to table fresh truly comes to life at Agricola - wonderful dining destination in a lovely ivy-league college town

Best brunch in NYC, hands down.  You have a cocktail, yummy entree, and fruit for under $20 in a place that looks like you are in the middle of Miami! I love Isabella's..it's been a staple for over 11 years...I still trek 30 minutes uptown just to visit. It is exceptional for dinner too.. not quite as reasonable at that time, but absolutely worth it.  Did I mention Alec Balwin sitting next to me the last time I was there??  (He lives in the upper west side and it is one of his staples if that gives you any idea how good it is)!

Had to finally have that burger that every yelper posts a photo of! And yes it really does look like that. PROS - Cozy, warm atmosphere, great ambiance, especially on a cold winter's night - Nice waitress - Bomb fries CONS - Pretentious host staff, you work at a restaurant people! Get over yourself - Pretentious Greenwich Village people - Kinda expensive - Not the most comfortable eating set up - my friend ate on a stool...at our table...hmmm I asked for my burger well and it was VERY pink. So pink in fact that I'm back to being a vegetarian. That said, it was delicious, I just was having an adverse reaction to eating meat. The fries were incredible. Some of the best ever. Definitely would have those again. I like, I wanted to try, worth a visit, but won't be my regular stomping ground.

I consulted many tour books on the subject and they all gave it bad reviews, so I knew it would be bad.  (Yelpers, why did you give it 4 stars?)Only reason I went here was because of friends.  My one trip to New York, and I had to experience bad pizza.  I wanted to go to Brooklyn.  Plus, the wait was long and the maitre'd took us off the list because we were outside (since it was so crowded inside).  Then he put us at the bottom of the list again.  It was only after this woman who worked there saw how pissed off we were that she put us at the top of the list again.  Sadly, Bella Pizza near my house is a lot better.  And I live in Frisco!

Came here for a NYE celebration with a small group of best friends. The vibe here is awesome, especially in the wintertime (makes me feel like I'm in a British holiday movie, ie Love Actually). I ordered a burger and it was great. The service was great. The atmosphere was fun. Would definitely come back!

Dude! Their sauces are so good. I love Wasabi so obviously my fav was Wasabi Mayo. They have the 3 sauce combo that you could get for 2.50. Where you pick and choose 3 for your big ass order of fries. Hope you enjoy it as much I did!

This is truly authentic pizza at it's best. I don't expect anything less then first class from a Vetri establishment, since I have been to all five branches of the Vetri tree. Visited Pizzaria Vetri the other night with some colleagues after work. Can't say much for their drink/beverage selection, as we BYO'd with our own flights of wine for corkage at $15 per bottle. However, the quality of their food menu is absolutely outstanding! The table of four shared Renato, Calzone, Tonno,  Salsiccia, and a shrimp scampi that was offered on special. I personally have to rated this place as having the best pizza dough around the greater Philadelphia area. Needless to say... these guys know dough! Definitely will be returning at least once a week!

Details: A Pakistani family run joint with good south Asian fare at affordable prices. Takeout would be the best option as service can be spotty when busy. Food's a bit on the oily side, but definitely one of the better Indian/Pakistani restaurants with respect to Greater Hartford standards. Ratings: Service: B Ambiance: B- Food: Beef Nihari: A Chicken Kadai: B- Butter Roti: A Goat Biryani: A-

I cannot rate 5 stars, (that would mean the food was PERFECT, EG. Free) but since it cost a few bucks out of my pocket...I will gladly give this funky little sandwich joint behind the jewelry counter 4.99 stars! I've only been there twice and ordered the #1, (pork Banh Mi) both times but I can tell you this, as far as I am concerned, this sandwich is SUPREMELY delicious. As a matter of fact, my son is in the Kitchen eating whats left of his for dinner as I type this. I am no Banh Mi afficianado...but for less than 4 bucks a pop, you could really do no better. I mean come on, a disgustingly fried burger from McDonalds cost more. I URGE everyone to go support this establishment so we have Banh Mi sandwiches for years to come. I have been to Nicky's before, which I like very much...but this place is WAY better. Plus, the little dude behind the counter is the man. You order what you want...and in less than a minute you are out the door with a bangin' brown bag lunch. Dont forget the iced coffee...best in the city, and at two bucks cost almost half of what you pay at DD's.

Decent katsu place conveniently located just off 5th Ave.  Had the berkshire pork katsu dinner which was quite nice. I like the all the little touches like being able to grind your own sesame seeds.  The one odd thing I found was that all the cooks behind the counter were all indian. However, the food was legit and I felt more comfortable when I saw several japanese business men coming in for dinner later on.  All in all, worth a trip if you are shopping it up on 5th ave or just in the area.

Very, very tasty falafels. The first time i went i got the falafel and hummus sandwich, i don't know where the hummus was(even thought the slightly bitter sauce was the hummus), but it still didn't ruin anything for me(considering my not knowing anything about this type of cuisine). Some people might think the slight bitterness repelling, but i personally find it a great icing on top of the fresh tomato and dense pea paste. best deal, the pricing makes it. 2.50 for a fulfilling falafel sandwich, what more can a poor overseas student ask for? ps. i know i know, but the guys at the counter are cute too.

Wanting to bring the in-laws to a more exotic sort of affair than they are used to, we brought them out to Monclair for Peruvian food. I love Peruvian chicken, but since I'm always going to PiyoPiyo for it, I decided to try their duck special instead. The duck was cooked to perfection! There was also duck in the rice -- lots of it! The cerviche choices were great, and tasted excellent. In-laws loved that it was BYOB and brought something interesting of their own to try. No corking fee -- thank you! Ambiance is exciting -- the wall is covered with interesting wood and the lighting is mysterious.

My friends and I went to brunch here with a group of 8.  None of us had ever been to Tartine before, but we were in the West Village and saw that it had great reviews.  At first glance, the place is TINY.  We expected to have to wait a while for them to be able to accommodate our group, but we ended up only waiting about 15 minutes.  It's BYOB and serves brunch daily, with an excellent prix fixe menu.  I had a tasty omelette cooked to perfection, and other plates on our table included french toast with bacon, eggs benedict, and a couple sandwiches from the lunch menu.  Everything was divine, and we all left very satisfied.  I would definitely recommend this place for smaller groups, as we were squeezed in pretty tight and a bit on top of the tables around us.  But all in all we were quite happy with the experience!

My review of the Ramen Bar is EXTREMELY POOR!! After waiting for the ramen to come out for about 30 minutes, i asked my waitress if the food my wife and i ordered takes longer than usual, she told me she didn't know and then walked away. 5 minutes later, seeing 6 tables that have seated after us got their food, I asked her if she had forgotten to put my order in and she told me she had "forgotten" to put my order in and that she would put it in now.... and then walked away.     So about 40 minutes on waiting for an appetizer, a bowl of Ramen and other dish, our food was NEVER ordered and apparently no one at the restaurant thought someone should have appologized for what had happened. I called the waitress and asked if there is a manager on duty and she told me "there isn't anyone here you can talk to right now" and walked away. I WAS PRETTY MAD. When I insisted on talking to someone in charge, becasue the waitress was keep telling me "there isn't anything she could do or to call", she got me this asian lady and she wasn't even wearing a uniform and she was in hurry to go somewhere. So when I was "TRYING" to tell this asian lady what had just happened, she simply told me we will get the food out soon and they would give us 20% off on the tab... AT THIS POINT I WAS FURIOUS. She treated me like i was putting on this "show" to get the food cheap or something cause instead of listening to what I had to say, she just heard what she wanted to hear and just walked away like how waitress had treated us. When my wife and I got up to walk out, that's when our appetizer comes out... they are such a great establishment. I WOULD NEVER GO BACK TO THIS ESTABLISHMENT AS LONG AS THERE ARE OTHER RESTAURANTS AROUND... ANY RESTAURANT.

Ok , but not great. I guess when you get seated between two LARGE kids b'day parties that the experience isn't going to all that great. I guess when you go to a place that caters to chocolate and munchies then you have to expect lots of kids running around and being loud. Somehow I expected a little more. The "large" Caesar salad with "spicy" dressing was lacking in taste. The greens were fresh and the chicken was ok, but the dressing at the bottom of the bowl was not that spicy. Onion rings with chocolate ranch dipping sauce were tasty, but a little of the greasy side. Here's my main complaint. We split the large caesar with chciken and the onion rings and with 1 ice tea the bill was $33.00. Lot better places for lunch around that area without kids yelling and playing on the floor. If you want breakfast or brunch and get there before Chuckie Cheese hour then it might be a really good spot. The crepes, pancakes and waffles did sound good, but then, so did the salad.

2 words - YOGURT SAUCE. Don't know the proper name but its soooo good. I always get the falafel over rice and although the falafel itself isn't the best, they give you a lot and the rice and pita and everything else is yummy. And its only $6 dollars which is a okay with me.
omg. their grilled corn was f-ing amazing!!! never had anything like it.
Love this place. No frills, great food excellent service. The chicken steak sandwiches are cheap, delicious, and huge!
Very good xiao long bao!
This place is delicious and very consistent. A little on the expensive side but worth it. Best Tiramisu around.

Very small and cozy place. Well worth the wait. Try to make a reservation if u can buy u will still probably have to wait a bit. It's a gem considering it's a byob. Mushroom figer appetizer was to die for.

I went to Perilla for dinner with my wife to celebrate  - i will say it was a wonderful evening. My wife being a vegetarian - i was apprehensive at first given she was vegetarian - but after the meal i will say it was a wonderful experience with very very good food and great service. We had an assortment of dishes with a good bottle of Lacrima D'Alba with a series of dishes. We started of with the Lacinato Kale Salad - a gorgeous mix of flavors with the orange and baby fennel adding a tremendous flavors with forbidden rice adding the starches. In addition to this we had a wonderful risotto - i will say this was wonderful and one of the best risotto's we have had in a while. Then we had the main course - which was an artful take of arctic char which had mushrooms substituted for fish - the combination of flavors work wonderfully well - with the slight bitterness and tanginess of the red lentil and mustard, the starch provided by the potatoes and the wonderful cabbage dumplings and the flavorful mushrooms on top - the combination of flavors work wonderfully well together and i would strongly recommend this to any one eating there. In addition we had the Brussel sprout leaves baked with toasted nuts (i expected pumpkin seeds etc. but was very impressed to find almonds in there instead) and a really nice and surprising sweetness coming from the chopped grapes. This works wonderfully well with the flavors in the arctic char as a great side. In all i believe this place was well worth the time and effort to get there - this is a wonderful place and i would say the chef is wonderfully inventive with an ability to bring congruent flavors together in unique and innovative ways - and provide an element of surprise / twist in the food. It was an absolute pleasure eating the food - and i also would go to say the service was wonderful and very very attentive. I would recommend this place even to vegetarians and i hope to go back there to try the meat.

View is beautiful.   Food was delicious!  Drinks were really good.  Cool bartender surprised us w berryish mojitos that were sooo good.  Table service was a bit slow, but non the less, great evening.   Will definitely go back to try brunch.
The best cheesesteak in Philly hands down! The best hoagie bread too! Perfect combination.

Hands down, one of the best bars in Philadelphia.  If you're visiting from out of town, this bar/beer hall is a must stop!  It's outdoor, but there are heat lamps if it's chilly outside.  There's long tables to sit at with games on them to make it really fun for groups and fun to get to know the group next to you. The beers are awesome - I love the wheat beer.  The food is okay, I'm not a fan of German food, so I just eat the pretzels, which are very large and delicious!

Dinner and service were fantastic. I ate at Batard the night before and noticed some similarities in the menus, both establishments had great dishes but this place had exceptional service and a better atmosphere. We tried every appetizer but the winning two were the octopus carpaccio and the heirloom tomato salad.  The duck entree was incredible! I highly recommend this place for the right kind of fine dining experience.

Food was mediocre at best. Unprofessional and mean-spirited staff was a definite shock. Needless to say, I will not be back. Owner is argumentative and unprofessional.  The owners/staff huddles at the register to trash patrons proved this to be a hostile and horrible place to dine. I wanted so much to like this place. A no go!

We LOVE Smokin' Betty's!!!!      Last night we threw a 20-person surprise dinner party for my boyfriend Dave's 30th birthday. Emily & the SB staff did everything for us from letting people bring noisemakers & rip shots to setting up a fake reservation so the surprise wasn't ruined when Dave & I got there. They were ridiculously helpful, professional & patient with my million questions. Incredible food with a wide variety of menu options for small parties & an even better staff. HIGHLY recommended for big dinners in Philly! Thanks for making his 30th so great!

Extremely disappointing.  We went on New Year's Eve to find our waitress was serving us while quite inebriated (leading to her forgetting to refill drinks and slur her words while speaking to us) and food that was sub-par at best for a final bill of $180 for two people. WORST OF ALL, the restaurant changed my tip after we left.  Because I was so displeased with the service, I tipped 10%, only to find a 20% tip had been charged to my credit card. WILL NEVER RETURN OR RECOMMEND TO ANYONE ELSE.  BEWARE!!!

I do 90% of all of my grocery shopping here.  There is something here for everyone!  From the fresh produce, numerous fish mongers, 4 or 5 butcher shops.  There are also a large number restaurants within.  Head here for the best Reuben of your life!  Wonderful new place that sells fresh mozzarella made on site.  I could go on for days about Reading Terminal Market.  Do yourself a favor and check this place out!  For foodie folks in from out of town this is  a must!

I've been for drinks a few times, but finally made it to WF for dinner. It definitely did not disappoint. Service was impeccable, vibe was perfect, music was great. As for the food? Couldn't have been better. We split the spicy garlic shrimp and crispy green beans to start--both had a nice kick to them, and were delicious classics. I then had the steak, cooked and seasoned to perfection, with classic fries and well-dressed arugula. It was definitely quite a plate of food (read: generous portion) but somehow I managed to clean my plate. The burger and arctic char (with a great corn/bacon/mushroom hash) received raves, as well. We couldn't leave without trying the cobbler, which was apple. It was hot, but one of the best cobblers I've had--the portion was huge, and the crust was almost cake-y, but in the best possible way. Drinks are great, too--highly recommend the Fig Side Car. They still seemed to be on their summer menu for food, which is a little odd at this point, but I was just perturbed because I wanted to try the brussels sprouts.
When I think of thai food, I think of Song.  The food tastes authentic and not pretentious.  You can't beat the prices either.

Short back story - we decided to go after hearing about a friend of a friend (Japanese dude) fly in from Chi town for the weekend in order to eat here.  So we asked, what kind of ramen is worth a plane ticket? The kind where you stick your nose in for the first inhale, roll your eyes back in pleasure, take a sip of the broth and toss any preconceived notions of what gourmet food is out the window.  Make no mistake, this is gourmet food.  Each ramen comes in a unique, rich, and complex broth that tastes like it's been simmering and slowly reaching perfection all day.  I had a special once, that came with a dime size dollop of green chili paste.  Awful by itself, but dip that into the broth, and the ramen is immediately elevated to a whole other level.  Genius. Their berkshire pork is also delicious - lightly smoked and full of flavor.  The pork buns are pretty pricey - at $8 for two.  But the balance of sweet, spicy, and mayonnaise exemplifies what fusion food is about...none of that grilled salmon with ginger glaze rubbish.   Yes the wait is long, but it's worth tasting something you can't find anywhere else in the city (let me know if you do tho!).  If you haven't been back for a while, this place has redone some of its on-the-menu ramens - version 2.0's.  Even better!

If you make a trip out to Grimaldi's you should def soak in the sights of that the nearby brooklyn bridge pier 1 park has to offer. Perfect place for a date: grab some ice cream, watch the sun set over the Financial District skyline, and then finish the night off with some of NY's finest pizza. Been here 3 times, each time with a different group of visitors and there has always been a line! The line usually moves pretty quickly and I've waited 30 min twice, but memorial weekend I waited 1hr45min!! For whatever reason people were loitering inside and taking their sweet time that night. Good thing to do while waiting in line is have one of your party pick up ice cream from the ice cream factory and bring it back. The pizza is very comparable to Lombardi's. For those who claim Lombardi's is better than Grimaldi's or vice-versa, they're just kidding themselves. It's like a coke/pepsi argument. For toppings I  recommend fresh garlic, extra tomatoes, and extra basil. Simply delish!

This is not the level of food we are used to get by this restaurant group! So following a 2 star review by Pete Wells of the New York times and the fact that my wife and i are long time fatty cue customers, we went for dinner 2 weeks ago.First thing , there is no point going to places which receive 2 stars by Pete Wells. If this is the standard for 2 stars, we need to seek out the 3-4 starred establishments in the New york times. The service: hipster d-bag style. our server, did not know the menu items, did not make eye contact and was generally displeased with his job , so much that when his shift was over we simply began getting service from someone else. the food: beneath mediocre. i have had better Filipino take out. This place is all attitude , without the quality to justify it! No chef on the line, cooks texting on the line and showing each other pics... My sizzling sisig had so much kafir lime in it that it tasted like soap. watermelon salad with cheap store bought cracklings, the rest of the food ( 3 other dishes all tasted the same: fish sauce and lime and that's it. Not sure if we should return to the other restaurants this group runs. We will never return to Pig and Khao though.
This was a great, place to watch any major game or fight, food would great.

What a great place....Fantastic authentic Thai food, fabulous happy service!  Papaya Salad,  Tom Kha Gai soup is sooooo good,  Goong Ob Woon Sen...is a must! Don't miss this new hot spot!  It's truly a great new addition to West Paterson.Don't forget the dessert.

A unique addition to the Astoria restaurant scene...unique in decor, as well as in the menu choices. I have dined at Sugar Freak twice and both times, I was very pleased. The food was exceptional, with a variety of different choices. The deviled eggs, mac and cheese and jambalaya are a must try! Service was exceptional as well!

Terrible service!!!! My husband and I went on a Sunday afternoon. We showed up at 1245 and mentioned to the waitress we had a flight to catch and needed To leave at 200. We sat and waited for our food for over an hour ( my husband ordered the Cuban and I was feeling I'll so I wasn't even eating) after politely asking about the status of our food and getting absolutely no response we use walked out.

The menu listed several types of balls (beef, chicken, pork, veggie and a special - lamb when we were there) and several types of sauces (pesto, spicy meat, marinara, mushroom, parmesan cream, etc.). We did the naked balls, since the boys were full from their dumplings, which was 4 balls with a sauce served with a slice of focaccia bread. You also have the option of ordering a sandwich or meatball sliders. In addition to the meatballs, this place had a great selection of sides (I'd love to come back and try the special risotto), drinks (every day is a special lemonade!) and, wait for it, homemade ice cream! You can even select your favorite type of cookie and flavor of ice cream and they'll serve up a highly dangerous looking ice cream sandwich.
not sure what i was thinking when decided to tried this place again only thing that saved the day was our server
I've had a few itens from their menu and omg...absolutely yummy! I recommend the grilled chicken melt.

Went to go claim my offer today , but the worker quickly brushed me off and said it ended yesterday may 1st. I presented him with the actual page that said visit between April 28th- May 4th to claim your reg fries and he didn't even look .  It's disappointing that they don't honor their own deals that they put up .

I had a friend in town and wanted her to experience Village Whiskey, so on Saturday we shuffled up there for lunch.  We sat at the bar and looked over the menu only briefly- I had been in plenty of times and knew what we were ordering.   Strangely, it took about ten minutes to place our drink order, despite that there were open seats at the bar, open tables inside and out, and only two people seemed to have been seated recently.  After drinks arrived, another fifteen minutes elapsed before we could get someone to take our food order, then only because we flagged down one of the three guys behind the bar to do so.  The food was absolutely delicious as always and coursed well, so no complaints there.  But even so our drinks sat emptied, and at some point my friend's glass disappeared without anyone asking if another drink was desired (oh, and it was). We are in our late thirties and both of us have strong backgrounds in the food/bev industry,  so we tend to be more understanding when something is amiss when we're out.  Stuff happens, and it has happened to all of us.   If you can't get to me because you're weeded, I totally get that and don't mind being patient.  But if you don't get to me because you're standing around chatting to the other two guys behind the bar about how your brother is a (effing) (a-hole) and what sounded like plans for a shore house, then I'm just going to get irritated.   Then irritated is going to turn into pissed off while you fire bottles from four feet away into the thrash can underneath where I'm sitting so you don't have to stop your conversation. Then we got the other charmer repeatedly slamming tins down on the bar immediately to my left every single time a shaken drink was made.  Quite frankly, If you can't get a seal on your tins without making my silverware jump, you're not great at your job.  I'm not calling for French service, here, but if I had wanted to sit a bar manned by guys with absolutely no interest in the experience of their guests AND the subtlety of a bag of hammers, I would have gone to Irish Pub.  Or maybe Roosevelts. While I was off using the restroom my friend paid our tab.  I asked what she left for tip.  She said she thought hard about stiffing them entirely, but couldn't get her conscience on board and just left around 10%.  Just in case you see this, boys- I watched that woman give 30-50% grat all weekend.  Congrats for missing out on that, and thanks for spoiling lunch.

Nice wine bar near Barclays Center. Great happy hour deals, especially with their $8 cocktails. We had 4 here while waiting for the Jay-Z/Coldplay NYE concert. Forget what they're called (Only remembered the James and the Giant Peach and some cucumber one), but hey if we had half of what they sell in terms of cocktails and liked them, the chances of you liking something there is in your favor. The only unfortunate thing is that we ordered the mac and cheese and it took too long to come out. It came out a few minutes after we had to cancel the dish as we were running behind schedule for the concert waiting for the dish. It looked yummy, but we shall try it next time once we are back in the area and have time to kill.

Great food...the food has gotten so much better over the years! They have great deals and specials...the cheddar biscuits are awesome nice fresh and warm. I always get the pick your own meal where you can get 3 items and a side. I get the coconut shrimp and it comes with it a spicy pina colada sauce, the shrimp scampi and snow crab legs for $2.50 more...it's worth it! I like getting the baked potato with sour cream and butter. Staff is always so nice and polite!

Such a darling little place. The decor is absolutely enchanting. However, the pizza option we got was disappointing. Tasted a tad too salty and not very flavorful (my friend and I spent a summer abroad in Italy so we're very picky). The bell pepper untraditional bruschetta was an interesting change of pace. Not amazingly good--just interesting. We didn't get any wine which I definitely will come next time but the atmosphere is nostalgic of days traveling throughout Europe. I imagine a great time would be fulfilled just by sipping on one of the many wine options and some good conversation.

be prepared to wait, prob an hr at prime time! this place is super tiny but so cozy and intimate. i love that you can see the kitchen. love BYOB. great wait staff. great food. although my seafood platter was a bit bland. the guy at the next table agreed - he had the same dish - and passed me some hot pepper. i mostly ate my boyfriends pumpkin pasta, it was fantastic!!! and the cheesecake dessert....was OUT OF THIS WORLD!!!

Went for a group lunch time with fellow employees. A group of 6 was seated quickly, as we were early for the lunch crowd. It was a lovely atmosphere. Plenty of bathrooms are available, I wonder why? As it was a work lunch, we were unable to consume alcohol. But, the draft list was decent. It also appears they had a selection of other fine libations. I ordered a pork sandwhich. The fries were awesome and quickly consumed. The pork came with a jus on the side. It was flavorful and fresh. The portion was large sized. I give this place 4 stars due to the quick action of the waitress. We asked for separate checks which she completed quickly for us, as we were due back to a training. She was friendly and kept up with our table, one person arrived late due to a long work call. She got him food promptly so he could eat with the rest of us.
I can't even begin to tell you how delicious the food is, how welcoming the cafe is, and how helpful and friendly the waitstaff is.  Please don't think twice- GO HERE.

What can you say when you get a combination of fresh, creative, affordable sushi with spectacular out of this world service.
