Was looking for a new sushi place to take an out of town friend and thought i'd roll the dice with this new place. We were rewarded with some of the best tuna tartar, the spiciest tuna roll, and some of the best seared salmon that i've ever had. On top of that our waiter went so far above and beyond what one would expect, that this probably gets my vote for best service in NYC EVER! I will be a frequent patron and am only torn in leaving this review by the fact that i don't want anyone else to find my secret find.

I came here on a Sunday afternoon craving budaejjigae. This is a really old-school style type of Korean restaurant - where there are limited individual dishes, and more family-sharing style entrees. Be prepared to be of one mind while ordering! Luckily, the people I went with were happy to share the budaejjigae with me - which was plenty enough for 3 people. I was surprised that it didn't come with their home-made tofu, but that disappointment was quickly dismissed when I realized there was bacon in it. Service is great - they do everything for you. Pour your water, ladle your soup, serve your rice, refill your side dishes (without you asking!) make your 'rice porridge' thing, etc. I didn't get the usual, condescending, Korean server that I get at other places. I will return, and hopefully try their home made tofu.

The good--good beer selection, good prices, good happy hour!  And the bartenders always know the beers and will help describe them and offer taste to try it out! The bad--I liked eating here a lot but since new chef they have removed my best items and replaced with bad things!  Duck fries are gone from menu. :(  I had pork sandwich that was smallest thing I have ever ordered for $10!  I have very small appetite and was still hungry after eating sandwich and fries!  I hope new chef makes bigger portions.

Went here last night with my partner and 2 other friends. They wanted to show us the new "hip" New York experience and chose this restaurant. It did not disappoint. We basically all ate a series of appetizers that were each better than the last. We had the hamachi, and it was so good we ordered another order. We had the Steamed buns. One of the most delicious things I have ever tasted. We tried two of the hams - loved it!! We also tried the brussel sprouts - another great dish. We did finally order one entree for the 4 of us to share - the pork belly. it was also great. The service was fantastic. The food just kept coming and we never were waiting for anything. Even though we chose not to have wine this time, they have an absolutely spectacular wine list - it goes ON and ON and ON. We all drank several drinks and the total bill for the four of us was about $300. It is a restaurant I will definitely come back to the next time I am in New York.
Unbelievable place for food, great portion size, great price and best of all great guys that work there. I recommend it to anyone for a quick easy healthy meal from some great people.

Just ate here with some friends.   -- Wines were $25/bottle.  The manager made a point of talking us through each selection.  Our malbec and pinor noir were good. -- We ordered a pizza with zucchini and wasabi peas on a pastry bread (was fantastico) as well as -- Server was extremely friendly and attentive. She actually followed us out the door to wave goodbye! -- Best part was dessert: hazelnut chocolate caviar cupcake with chocolate chip ice cream This place is tiny, tasty, value priced. I will be back fo mo
Sounds degusting

Went on a Saturday night and had about a 30 minute wait.....not a huge deal b/c the place is small and popular.  The hostess was really nice....she let us crack open a bottle of wine while we waited and brought us gluten free bread sticks.  We had a salad and 2 risotto dishes.....mine had pulled pork and my wife had one with their meat sauce.  Both were really yummy!  We grabbed a package of Winkies (their gluten free version of Twinkies) and headed out.....BTW...the Winkies, I think, are better then the greasy Twinkies.   My wife has Celiac's disease, so she has to eat gluten free.  However, I do not, and I though the dinner was fantastic!

Ordered the stir fried chicken hand drawn noodle. The chicken came out extremely cold and i had to have them reheat it. The dish back out but the noodles were overcooked and the meat still wasn't fully heated! However, the lady was kind in taking the dish back into the kitchen.

I was in the process of writing a review of another steak shop and its mediocrity reminded me of how fantastic this place is. You cant properly judge a cheesesteak until you've stood on the corner of Snyder and Weccacoe and gotten grease all over your eagles jersey. If your not from Philly, the area is fine you wont get robbed and yes, they are open for business. While the cheesesteak has become Phillys most famous export, the roast pork sandwich is fantastic.  There is also a Target store right there, so you can get yourself a pair of maternity pants for the ride home.

I work in an office at Broad and Chestnut, and lord knows I'm always looking for a good, inexpensive lunch spot. My usual is Saladworks (so expensive) or Grocery (there are only so many days in a week I can eat soup). And then I smelled my cube neighbor's lunch today. $7.44 got me wonton soup and what was possibly the best green curry I've ever eaten. It's labelled on the menu as a "1" on the spicy scale (3 is the highest), and I'm definitely glad that I didn't ask for it spicier. It probably would've been just as delicious, but when I'm at work, I don't want to sweat curry all afternoon. That said, the "1" had a great little kick to it. The chicken was tender, the veggies (carrots, peppers and greenbeans, maybe?) had just a little crunch in them, and the sauce was pretty close to heaven. Best part, the portions are large enough that I can easily get two lunches out of a meal. This restaurant opening actually makes me a little sad that I'm moving out of state in a week. ps. Ask the hostess to turn on the bar while you're waiting for your take out. You won't regret it.

Now I wouldn't say I love this place, but I am certainly very fond of it. It's fast and it's pretty decent and the price is good.  Only thing is that during lunch it gets ridiculously busy and there's no room to move around.   It's a great place to get really full fast, and for cheap.

I just got off the phone with a surprisingly rude delivery rep. I have Celiac disease, which means I can't eat gluten and I just found out that a couple of Mexican restaurants in the area have corn tortillas that contain gluten (which is news to me), so I called to ask if Guerro's tortillas were or were not gluten free. The first person I spoke to was male and was extremely unhelpful. I asked him if the tortillas were gluten-free and he told me he assumed so. I asked if he could make sure. He left and  came back on the lines shortly and told me they were gluten-free. I asked if he was sure. He said I had asked him to find out and he had asked someone and he didn't know what else there was that he could do. I said it is as simple as reading the package. He said oh, okay, in a sarcastic tone of voice, put me on hold, and a few minutes later a woman came on the line who told me the tortillas were gluten free. She was quite pleasant about this, until I asked her if she was sure and she also got defensive, saying that there was nothing on the ingredients list about flour so unless the ingredients list was wrong there should be no problem with the tortillas. I apologized for my overly-cautiousness but explained that it's a very serious allergy and I just wanted to make sure. I then proceeded to ask if I could place an order for delivery and in the middle of this sentence she hung up on me. I work at a restaurant that takes customer reviews and satisfaction extremely seriously, and I am really frustrated at the treatment that I just received. I understand it's Saturday night and it's busy, but representatives of restaurants need to be capable of dealing professionally with all customers, including those who have food allergies that are out of their control. I was going to place an order at the restaurant, but the last thing I want to do now is call these people back and jump through hoops to make sure the food I buy won't make me sick.

Food 3.5 stars / service 4 stars / ambience&interior 3 stars Warning: (1) Their light is a bit dark. Hardly can read menu, to be honest. We seated at 2nd floor, but 1st floor seating might be great as well. (2) There is no restaurant sign on the street or even in front of the door. Basement level. (3) They accept only either CASH or AMERICAN EXPRESS credit card. No visa card. Checked this place for Sunday dinner with one of my friends who is a great fan of tapa places. Before coming in, we were so excited to try this place's signature dishes that all the previous Yelp reviews hyped about, and here are my objective reviews. - Alta's Non-Classic Sangria. Try Red. MUST-DRINK at this place. I've tried Sangria at many different places in nyc, but I think this was one of the best. Much better than Calle Ocho, the upper-west place which is famous for weekend Sangria brunch. Alta's is not too sweet, not too dry. Just perfect. I even had two glasses for our dinner.   - Crispy Brussels Sprouts: Thumb up. Impeccable taste. Brussels sprous with Fuji apples and pistachio nuts, yammy! No more word is needed. Just go for it! - Fried goat cheese: did we expect too much? this was just okay, or slightly below our expectation. It goes well with honey that is served with this dish, but I can barely taste pure goat cheese. - Lamb meatballs: we actually liked this. The meatballs with tomato (or marinara?) sauce were very flavorful. - House-made pizza: we expected some kind of yammy flat-bread brick-oven pizza, and yes it was flat-bread, but in terms of taste and flavor, well... not as good as brick-oven pizza at other places. I liked its mushrooms and spices on top of the pizza though. - Squid Ink Paella: It was great. Paella at some place is generally a bit oily, but here the squid ink seems to balance out well. But wished there were some more seafood on this dish. Will definitely try next time again when I'm craving for red sangria.

Great place. It's so huge that it would take me several visits to get all the restaurants in. If I lived here that would be fine. But, a few hours her does satisfy! Foods amazing! Prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, olives bread and beer for starters. Incredible!
Great place. We moved to the neighborhood recently and decided to check it out and were not disappointed.

Big Wong's is authentic Chinese food. I always get their wonton with bbq pork noodle soup. Their combo (bbq pork, chicken, duck) over rice is also very good. They are also fairly fast with making it as well. I once came there and got family style entrees, it was a bad idea, their entrees were too small of a portion to be family style. None of us got full. I recommend ordering individual dishes for yourself. Not a bad place to eat and not too pricey, if you're around the area looking for a quick dine in, then this is your place!
wow.... I didn't write that review? wonderful experience.... wonderful sliced steak dinner... done to perfection.  Great wine. Fair price. This is why I live in NYC.

Great spot in the East Village! Looking for some latin american fare, I came with friends on a Sunday during brunch. It was also Cinco de Mayo, so the place was packed, but our party of 3 was seated in less than 10 minutes. I had the Quesadilla de Champignon which was absolutely delicious! It was a very tasty quesadilla with mushrooms and smoked cheese, topped with piquillo peppers and cream. My friends enjoyed the Quesadilla de camarones, a quesadilla with shrimp, roasted corn, pepper jack cheese and topped with guacamole and sour cream, as well as the Cuban Sandwich.  Each of us enjoyed our meals. The Yuca fries are also super delicious!   Unfortunately, we had a not so nice waitress. But it was Cinco de Mayo so I wouldn't have been a happy camper either if I were her.

While I haven't been there in ages, they by far have the best burger in town.  I'm a big BIG fan of the "Good Dog Burger".  I try my best to have it rarely.  But sometimes there's no accounting for my carnivorous cravings. It's also a sweet place to watch a game, go on a date, hang out with friends, or just grab a beer by yourself.  The wait staff may not be the friendliest, but they will certainly hook you up with a good beer and they are efficient.

My husband and myself went to Lo Monaco's for dinner.  We ordered an appetizer, salads and entrées.  The appetizer was fine but my salad contained a very large dead moth.  We tried to discreetly to get our server's attention. Finally she came over and looked at me as if I had put the moth in the salad.  She took the salad into the kitchen, everyone in the kitchen came to the door to stare at me one at a time.  No apology or restitution was offered.  I spread the word about the service and the moth.  We will never return.
Wish I could come downtown more often- this place is the best!

The service was impeccable. Servers catered to my every need. I was a sucker and tried the $25 spaghetti. Thought it was over-priced, but read some reviews on here and had to try it. Well alas, no sucker here! It was deee-lish! I could tell this was no store-bought spaghetti but made fresh here at the restaurant and cooked per order by the perfect al-dente texture. Sauce was so good as well. I also had the chestnut soup as an appetizer. I couldn't finish the spaghetti so brought it home and it tasted even better the next day! Worth every dollar!

I fucking love this place. Pros: margaritas that put you on your ass, fresh and flavorful food, attractive staff, incredible happy hour. Plus I can see this place from my front step. Cons: pretty small so expect to wait, especially if you're going on $1 taco night, they won't deliver margaritas to my house- rude.
Great French brasserie. You will see there the most famous people from New York, this is the place to be on the weekend for lunch if you want to be seen...

When I think New York, I think Gottino!  They have left me with one of the most memorable dining experiences I have ever had!  Upon walking through their door, you are no longer in North America; you are instantly teleported to Europe for the most fantastic brunch you have ever been presented.  Gottino, of course, is a wine bar, and their staff, completely fluent in Italian, has the talent to make great wine selections to pair with your meal.  I opted for their choice of cabernet sauvignon with my order of traditionally prepared waffles, topped with fresh fruits and berries, with thick European whipped cream - an interesting choice to pair red wine with breakfast, but SO GOOD!  The boldness of the red cab complimented the sweetness of the berry topped waffle, making the meal feel complete. The atmosphere is the second half of Gottino's equation - The interior is cozy, intimate, and outright plucked from French and Italian dining culture.  Finding a quiet corner to share with your lover, or pushing some tables together to enjoy with your friends; it's all possible.  Rest assured, you are in for authentic European dining in America when you visit Gottino!  I can't wait to go back!

Several years ago this place was just okay for me.  But this restaurant has become one of my favorites along with Segovia's in Moonachie.  The grilled octopus as an appetizer was phenomenal.  Zuppa Di Pesce was great.  The Cannelloni Nostro was to die for (OMG, I can't believe I just used that terminology!!!).  The atmosphere was superb....and the service is impeccable.  Get there by 7 p.m. on a Friday night before it gets too crowded.  Reservations a must!!!  GO!!...what are you waiting for???!!!!

Second time visiting the restaurant, still wowed.  One of my favorite restaurants. I made reservations here for my husband and his cousin from out of town. My husband typically rolls his eyes at me when I suggest tasting menus/tapas and responds with a look that says, "screw spending money on small portions that require second dinner afterwards." Well, Zahav shut him up. The man was so full after the second course (4 course total) that he had to take a deep breath to clear his confusion as to what was happening. So people, this is not a restaurant where you need to eat a "first dinner" or a "second dinner." It is THE dinner. Now, the food ranges from great to amazing, including duck heart, lamb tartar, hanger steak, eggplant, salmon, cod, sweetbread, brussel sprout, and not to mention, the bread and the hummus. Cocktail and Service, both times were amazing. I am usually quick to find fault with restaurants but Zahav is perfect! You will go home happy and full!
Absolutely delicious!  Dream of the stuffed mushrooms.  Can't wait to make my yearly pilgrimage back to NY.

Just okay.  Not somewhere I'd be dying to go back to but would have no problem meeting a group there.  The attached hotel entrance is very nice.  Didn't eat just had a beer at the bar and it was a tad pricy.

Probably my favorite NYC chow-down spot for several reasons: 1) Astonishingly inexpensive.  Regular falafel/hummus sandwich (see reason 2) or 5 for a plate.  They also have meats (lamb, chicken), among other tantalizing option, all very reasonably priced 2) Best hummus I've ever had.  I've never had the falafel, simply because I like the hummus sandwich too much. 3) THE BEST HOT SAUCE, HANDS DOWN.  And I really, really like hot sauce.  I've had all sorts of small time hot sauces from louisiana, mississippi, and the like.  Nothing beats Mamoun's signature hot sauce, available in bottles for a mere $3.50 (don't go there without getting yourself a bottle). Warning: its HOT.   4) Small time, local.  None of this corporate nonsense.  I think there's one other location in jersey.  Support the local guys! Especially the ones that do it right. 5) Cool vibe.  Situated right in the heart of East Village (st. Marks place), the small space, slightly dark lighting, and awesome middle eastern music make this an essential low manhattan chow down spot.

I've had dinner at Raymond's twice and both times it was just average.  Maybe their brunch or breakfast is the best thing around, but as far as the regular menu goes, nothing special.  It amazes me that people are willing to wait so long for tables there when there are plenty of other great restaurants all over the place in Montclair.

Do it right and well and your business will take care of you. This is the epitome of The Bosphorus' success. Nora and her son are prime examples of compassionate, dedicated business owners. From the warm "good to see you" at the door to the hug and kiss farewell. I am envious of the Essex community for having this hidden gem (literally tucked in the Nutley diner municipal parking lot). Ambiance: Beautiful moulded ceiling as you walk in and clean, elegant decor fill this Turkish abode. Food: Presentation is art on a plate! Their branzino comes in fresh from Turkey which they pick up at JFK airport. I loved their mixed cold dip appetizer. All the bowls were licked clean with our warm, crusty bread. Bosphorus salad is scrumptious! Service: Some of the best hospitality I have ever seen. Everything is done to perfection! I came for early Sat dinner (5:30pm) so I did not experience the slow service people talk of. There's a $3-5 upgrade in price compared to the Turkish restaurants in Cliffside Park but the freshness and presentation make up for it. Definitely make reservations for Fri and Sat night because Yelpers have let the secret out on this place :)

Two Fun Facts About Me(nid): 1) Since I am an Asian American, I have obviously never not been ethic. As such, I have always wondered (to this day) what non-ethnic people eat on a regular basis. I've also been puzzled as to why someone would choose to pay significant sums of money to eat "traditional American" food when they can opt for the much more colorful cuisines of Asia, Italy, Latin America, or basically any other part of the world. (Except maybe England. Talk about dullsville. Which is honestly why I have not yet given Dandelion a fair chance.) 2) Apparently I am exceedingly impressionable. Case in point: The Internet told me that today is National Waffle Day. Even though this very well might have been a false proclamation and even though I have never historically been a waffle nut, I could not get the image of waffles out of my already cluttered mind. So, being unable to function with this thought persistently nagging me, I dropped everything and dragged my lunch party over to Jones. Even taking Fact 1 into consideration, I am actually very okay that Fact 2 is true because let's face it, the chicken and waffle at Jones is awesome. Like seriously awesome. The chicken (even the white meat) is perfectly juicy, and the waffle has an expert balance of crisp and fluff, all drizzled over (or on the side!) with a creamy, flavorful gravy. My only complaint is that the chicken to waffle ratio is highly skewed toward the chicken side (the waffle is delish - give us more!). Also, I think Jones might be the only restaurant in the entire nation that dares to charge you MORE for ordering all dark meat instead of a mix. Slightly uncool, Steve. The mac and cheese is definitely in the "instant knock out" category of food. It is tasty for sure, but a bit salty and incredibly heavy. A good recommendation for insomniacs - a few mouthfuls will get your eyelids droopy in an instant. I'm not typically one who gets off at the idea of spending over five bucks on mac, and this is no exception. For this kind of price (at eight bucks a pop), I think I'd rather get it at Silk City. Overall, the food at Jones is decent, even in spite of its lack of ethnic flare, though it can be more than I would like to pay for this style of food. It looks and feels exactly like Stephen Starr would have it look and feel. It is not my favorite of his joints, but it is not my least favorite either (you can ask me which one that is, and I will tell you why). Solid 3.5 in my book. Unless my mind is changed in future visits.

Is it possible I can give this a 4.5? So in love with Public as my friend and I were, we decided to try it out for brunch this morning with sort of mixed results. We arrived at 11:30 AM, a half hour after opening, but were seated immediately by the gracious (and six feet tall) hostess at a cute table facing the bar. We were presented with teensy little scones to begin, and they were quite tasty, if not practically poppable. They contained caraway seeds and sultanas, but I couldn't tell what else. We decided to go the prixe-fixe brunch route and get cocktails and tea with our meal. My friend went the more savory route with the Public Bloody Mary, with a rim absolutely flaked with pepper and salt, with an olive, lemon, plenty of horseradish, and a lot more booze. Though I'm not huge on champagne (I am big on asti, I will say that,) I decided to go for the blackberry bellini, which ended up being raspberry. It was pretty good but the fizziness (what did I expect?) was a bit overwhelming, and I wished it were sweeter. Soon after our entrees arrived. My friend had banana-stuffed french toast with huge strips of bacon and a deluge of maple syrup. The bread was deliciously crusty and crunchy with an addictive burnt taste, and the banana was just ripe enough. I had the coconut pancake entree which contains two of the pancakes topped with ricotta, chunks of mango and a ginger lime syrup. Though this was delicious, it was verrry very sweet. I was actually extremely stuffed after eating it all, but for some reason I left wanting more. As far as service was concerned, our waitress was nice and smiled but for some reason was a let down from the other night. She was much more preoccupied and quick to get us out. But then again, that's brunch on a Sunday for you.

Sad to say that I have been back to Queens and to the branch in East Williston, and neither trip measured up to our first trip.  Dishes on both occasions were uneven and seemed to be smaller than I remembered.  Still better than most thai food, but not the destination place that I thought it was initially.

Came here this past Friday night off of a helpful Foursquare tip. Our favorite Midtown beer places, Ginger Man, suddenly was swarmed by FDNY gentlemen who spooked the bar owners from letting additional people, even though the place wasn't that full compared to other nights. Turns out that Rattle 'N Hum was a great find and a strong alternative to Ginger Man - may start coming here more often since it's so low-key. This place carries a healthy selection of global draught and bottle beer (~30-40) and, even better, a waitress who was quite knowledgeable and could offer recommendations for each person. The brews were also ~$7-8 each, which was great. We were also delighted by the fact that we came in around 11 PM and could easily find  a table. The place wasn't so loud that we couldn't hear ourselves so it was a great time for all 4 of us. The decor of the place was interesting. It felt like where an adult Harry Potter would come in for a brew - colorful flags and banners everywhere, and a couple of TVs in the back. I didn't get to check out what they were showing but I felt like it would be appropriate to watch a soccer game here. If Ginger Man is packed, Galway Hooker isn't really your thing, then walk a couple streets down to Rattle 'N Hum.
Shoped at ABC home for so many times but never been to the restaurant til now. It's amazingly delicious! And good quality of ingredient pick. Nice service too!

I love this place! I work right in the empire state building and the place is right up the block. Also being able to get plastered and make my way home is a plus. The 11am-7pm happy hour is great for getting buzzed at lunch or for after work. Look out for the $5 margaritas, cosmos, and martinis, and pretty big portions of nachos. Recently went again for a friend's birthday and the bill was around $115 bucks for like 8 of us. No complaints here!

Thank you Pat's for being vegan friendly. I still don't think you guys are the "best" though even after not eating beef anymore. There is a great place on Market Street that you would never expect to be great but thats because it's not touristy! The bread was kind of dry and I wouldn't come here when it gets dark because we had two people come up to the car begging us for money. Two girls after a concert is not very safe to come here.
I keep coming back for the stuffed meatballs.

This place was booked for us by a friend who lives nearby.  Never actually watched Top Chef, but had maybe read a capsule review in the New Yorker?  Anyway, we were told about half way through the meal, so that bit of knowledge didn't really impact our experience. It's basically a modern/italian bistro- nothing too fancy, nothing too complicated.  Simple menu, heavy on seafood.  An enjoyable experience,  Not really a revelation.  I prefered our meal at "Supper" in terms of Italian in New York.  Can I just say- I never eat Italian food in California... Let's get some good italian restaurants on the left coast!

My love affair with this place and it's sister restaurant in Center City West (sadly closed) goes back six years.  This location is pretty hole in the wall, unadorned, dimly lit--very Philly neighborhood BYOB. The must-have is the Shrimp Pil-Pil:  barely breaded but just barely crispy medium sized shrimp with a garlicky, citrusy, red chili rub. I have been known to dream about this. The grilled vegetables are also divine. It is simple but just so perfectly done. Never over charred. The red onions grilled til sweet as could be, zucchini, tomato, red and green pepper, with a few bits of feta and banana pepper thrown in is just perfect. Platters come with sautéed lettuce and Mexican-styled rice. The scallops are fabulous as are the pricey soft shelled crabs on special frequently. The grilled squid is tender but too overwhelmingly smoked for me. Love this place. Wish I could eat that Pil-Pil all the time!

Came here for brunch.  Got the fried chicken and waffles with a pointsettia cocktail.  It was delicious and I ate/drank the whole thing.  Only gave it four stars because there wasn't anything too original or different about it.  But the staff was friendly and attentive!

Came here for a birthday dinner and we had a large party.  Reservation was set at 7:30pm and the party before us didn't leave until maybe a little before 9pm?  That's a bit unacceptable since that party was there supposedly since 5pm.  And because of the (small) size of the restaurant, our party of about 30 people had to wait around the (small) bar or outside in the cold until that party left and the table was cleared and set for us. Pros: 1. Food was amazing.  I ordered the fish special and the fish was cooked perfect; moist and not dry, flavorful and a good sized portion. This was served on top of sauteed spinach and  mashed potatoes.  Cheers to the chef who made the mash with red skin potatoes and left the skin! Delicious!  Small plates worth trying and worth the price: Ceviche Mixto and Calamari Frito. 2. Sangria was made perfectly.  Usually this can be a hit or miss but you could tell they made this one with brandy and not just red wine and juice. Cons: 1. Service was ok.  There were many busers/servers around our tables (we had 3 tables) however when we were trying to get our server so we could order drinks and small plates, the guys that were at our table kept redirecting us to someone else, saying that guy was our server. 2.  Were we being rushed out?  Come on guys, we obviously are going to be dropping a good amount for this bill and if you want a good tip, don't rush us PLEASE!!! 3.  Mozzarella Pio isn't worth getting.  Save your $$ and appetite for some of the other small plates. Overall I'd come back for the food and with a smaller party.  I'll remember to eat something before coming because of the wait that we had.
MUST. GO. This is food porn....lots of it. Love the casual, open food stalls under one roof. Amazing. Casual. Affordable.

I love to order from here because I can do it online and don't have to talk to anyone. My orders always right and they have a huge selection of food! I've never had a problem with their sushi or hot foods. The only thing I can say is sometimes their delivery takes a long time but they deliver to like 10 different towns and I don't care as long as it eventually gets to me!

Heidi's House was such an unexpected find. I was walking on 78th street a few weeks ago when I discovered this little gem. I ended up giving it a try a few nights ago and all I can say the food is fabulous. The night I was there I tried one of their specials which happened to be a skirt steak. It was cooked perfectly and it was full of flavor. I am also a huge Mac and Cheese fan so I had to try the Mac and Cheese with Lobster as well. The Mac and Cheese was creamy and very good and the Lobster took this dish to another dimension. My only complain is that this space is SMALL. I am talking three tiny tables and about 8 stools at the bar small. I really enjoyed the food but it started to get way too crowded and started to feel very cramped. So if you want to try Heidi's I highly recommned going early.
over rated.... not worth the fan fare!

I was excited to try Westville after hearing it being called a healthy place for brunch. I got a Mexican breakfast dish (blanking on the name, not the burrito though) which I was very excited for, but very let down. It was basically a large pile of greasy homemade tortilla chips, drenched in a green salsa that made them soggy. On top were two over easy eggs, which were good, but got swallowed by the chips. It could've been a great dish. I guess I was just disappointed at this "healthy" brunch place that served my chips for breakfast. I'd like to come back though and try their veggie sides, which I heard are amazing.

I went to Opa for the first time the other night to try out some food from their late night specials menu (M-F 10-11pm, $3 Yuengling on draft, $4 house wines, $5 specialty cocktails, and a few food items including Greek fries). I had the slider and the meatballs, and both were satisfying for the $2/3 price tags, as was the Brooklyn Brewing Brooklyner Weiss (a beer I haven't seen yet on draft). The bartender was very attentive and friendly, as were the other patrons at the bar, who quickly included me in colorful conversation that became the highlight of my night. I will definitely be stopping by again, especially to check out their backyard beer garden which is one of the hidden gems of the neighborhood, according to other reviews.

The food is very good. The ambiance is cool, they have multiple movies playing, projected on the wall, muted. I went with my lovely girlfriend. We split a beet salad it was delicious. I had a cocktail, delicious. She had rose. The savignon blanc was $16, a bit steep. For dinner I had the uncle Tommy pie, it's shepards pie with lamb. Very good. The lady had green pasta. It lived up to the hype. I had a beer with dinner. Nice too. The table was tiny, no big deal I just remember it. I'd try it then hit up Rudys after for some cheap beers and a good laugh. Hell's Kitchen! Try out Bea I liked it.

Went back to 116 tonight after being out of town for a while, and the cocktails were as good and creative as I remembered -- the rival of any bar I've been to. I had my old favorite, the Grey Lady (plymouth gin, rothman & winter crème de violette, organic egg foam, lemon juice, simple syrup), which was perfectly mixed, and my husband tried the Kentucky Leftfoot (rye, rhubarb preserves, chervil), which was also excellent. Another old favorite is the Forth & Clyde (gin, bourbon, elderflower liqueur, honey, lime juice, chili flakes), but I don't think I've ever been truly disappointed in a drink here, and I love the way the menu is arranged by themes (aromatic & subtle, bracing & bold, etc.). We did not have any food this time, but the food we had during past visits was generally very good, although much more limited in selection than the cocktails. Other reviewers have complained about the staff, but I've always found them to be attentive and helpful. And the atmosphere is a fun break from the typical New Haven scene, with the lit-up bar, pod-like booths, and even trendy bathrooms. Really, the only downside is the price (e.g., $16 for my Grey Lady), but I just saw that 116 has a low-priced "Early & Often" menu on weekdays from 5-7pm. We'll be back soon.

Yum!   After wandering through some stores, we needed a food break and spotted this place across the street.  I had a chicken quesadilla (which is basically an understuffed burrito here) and the fiance got a beef burrito, both with guac.  Awesome... definitely what we needed.   And they have Mexican coke!   The line took a while to get through and there isn't much seating, but its a good cheap food option.

So after griping to numerous people about how disappointed I've been in Philly pizza, I was ordered to try Mama Palma's.  And so I went. The skinny:  BYO wine, they are happy to rip you off for beer (I'm pretty sure pints were $7).  Casual dining.  And I was also impressed with the speed at which our pizza came out.  A lot of the reviews kind of complain about the service (or lack thereof) - I thnk if you go in understanding this is not a fine dining restaurant, you'll be fine.  They do want to keep the tables turning over, and encourage you to leave a bit when you're done. This pizza is an original, in that I really can't compare it directly to anything else.  I was with five others and we split three pizzas - one with ricotta, tomato, and mushroom; a chicken dijon with spinach, and the margherita with truffle oil.  I thought all were pretty good, with the ricotta one taking first prize.  The crust was kind of a medium thickness, nice and chewy.  Generous application of toppings was also a plus. The downside - this pizza is not cheap.  The large ricotta one was $25 I think, which is the most I've paid for pizza in a long time.  But this was tasty all the same and for now, gets my vote for the best pizza in the neighborhood.

I was craving some breakfast food, and was happy to discover this place existed so I wouldn't have to trek all the way to the city just to get some. I do wish their brunch menu was a little bigger. Ordered the french toast which had a banana and berry topping. It was sweet but not overly sweet, and I liked how it was still toasty on the outside. Definitely satisfied my sweet tooth. Their corned beef hash, which was served in a bowl with two poached eggs, was not what I expected and a little too salty for my liking. Coffee is served in a mini coffee press for your serving of coffee. Overall, the food was pretty average to me but it's a cute place for a meal. The live jazz duo adds a nice ambiance. Staff was nice and attentive.
i was surprised by the table. it is leather covered! the food is super good. i had the bbq fries, spare ribs, Brisket, and deviled eggs. the experiences was great! will go back again!

I've eaten here twice now, as part of a large group. My company is based in Vermont, and I spend a lot of time in China. Living in Tacoma, I have many many choices of Asian food to choose from. A Single Pebble is good, even very good. The food is well prepared, service is excellent and it is reasonably priced. The last time I ate there (1/7/13) we had a selection of dishes from across the spectrum. They were all very good. What I don't get is, why call something "mock eel" or "mock beef"? this is Burlington, not Kansas, and I shiitake mushrooms are excellent, why call them "eel". Some people would get turned off by eel. So, I found this disguise stuff a bit weird. I haven't tried to order coffee here. I laughed reading the other reviews about it, so I'll make sure to try to order some on my next visit. Yes, I'd go again, but  suggest the restaurant not bother with the disguised food and just go with it. Most of us (especially the clientele for this restaurant) eat vegetarian once or more a week anyway, so embrace it.

The best sub-shop in the area, hands down. This place runs like a well oiled machine. I don't think I've ever come here and not had to stand in a line with another 8 people in front of me. Strangely enough I was always in and out in 10minutes or less. They have plenty of sandwich suggestions that are unique here. They also have the classic subs. If you're daring you can create your own. The bread is great. I do a unique combo  - Smoked turkey, honey turkey, American cheese, cheddar cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion and may. Perfection!

I am in love with this place! I've braved the heat and come here two days in a row for its hand-pulled wide noodles. The look and chewy texture of its wide noodles reminded me of Pappardelle, my favorite kind of pasta. I ordered Tomato & Egg dry noodles yesterday and Black Bean Sauce dry noodles (zha jiang mian) today. I loved them both, but I think I will order the Tomato & Egg one again next time because it is less easy to find. By the way, it turned out that these two dry noodles are offered at a discount price of $4.25 (original price $5.00) during lunch hours (11 am to 4 pm). I also tried the Pork Pancake two days in a row. The "pancake" was served piping hot and super crispy on the outside. The minced pork inside was flavorful and didn't taste greasy at all. I ordered 15 dumplings to take home today. The dumplings were just okay. I think their strength is the noodle. On my both visits, I was greeted by a young lady (probably the wife of the owner) with a big smile on her face. The space was not big, but I didn't feel too cramped or uncomfortable. Somehow, I find this Henan hand-pulled noodles (I mean noodles per se, not considering the soup or sauce) very similar to the noodles served in Xi'an Famous Food. The pancake here is also very similar to that in Xi'an Famous Food as well. Out of curiosity, I checked the map of China, and found out that the Henan province is located right next to the Shaanxi province (where Xi'an is the capital). Maybe it explains the similarity in how they make noodles out of the dough? I wish I have known more to make sense of this. Despite the similarity, I still prefer the noodles (less greasy and more non-spicy choices) here!

After getting pastrami sandwiches and sloppy joes from the Montclair area, it's great to finally go to a place that actually does pile on the meat. They don't even advertise it. They just do it. The sloppy joe could have used a smidge more dressing to pep it up a little. I guess I can't complain too much since you get a mouthful of corned beef and pastrami. They were also nice enough to give me fries even though they didn't charge me. There was a mixup somewhere in the ordering process. Overall a good solid deli, with good sized servings and exceptional service.

It's all family style seating so you may find yourself sharing a large table with another group or two.Came here to see what all the rave was about their pork soup dumplings. This wasn't the first time that I encountered soup dumplings either so I did have something to compare to their food. I gotta say, the soup dumplings are actually very very delicious!

3.5 stars. Wow, really chic and romantic interior with the white seat covers etc. I totally wasn't expecting it to be so. Bartender and staff were friendly and welcoming and it makes this place like a true neighborhood restaurant indeed. I had a tres leche to go. Not too wowed by it though...

America really has gotten soft... what with our obsession with great beer selections and "good" food. To hell with it. I'll take a PBR and some chips. What I can't live without is something that lies deeper within... deeper within than the gluttony of dribbling micro-brews over exalted taste-buds, or the exclamations of hipsters to their hipster friends (with their hipster babies) how excellent the food is. One could no sooner review Johnny Brenda's without mentioning hipsters, than one could review the American West without mentioning the buffalo. The great hipster herds move from their grazing lands in the various low-rent neighborhoods, and congregate in great numbers at Johnny Brenda's, where presumably they give evidence to superior lifestyle decisions, or at the very least swap interesting mix tapes. But mostly they exemplify yet another materialism. Resplendent in skinny jeans and offbeat hair, they concern themselves with looking and acting cool, and being well versed in beer menus and gastro-pub fare. To this extent, they plunge headfirst into the deep-end of the American delusion of the good life. If ever a proof existed of the emptiness of life-style choices as a means of averting social convention, it exists in the hipster genre, wherein the man in the grey flannel suit is reincarnated daily by the man with the tattooed family. Mom, dad, tatoo baby.... sitting across from other hipster couples, tasting each others beers and talking about food quality. The more things change, the more they stay pathetic. But putting all that absurdity aside for a moment... and what is life if not putting aside absurdity for long enough to imagine that something worthwhile exists. What lies deeply at the heart of this place is ambiance. Johnny Brenda's provides an experience of place, of people, and of a neighborhood that is un-unequaled in Philly. The ground zero of this vibe is had by sitting outside and watching the insane parade of Philly's finest and lowest walk by on a continual basis. Hot girls in tight cloths.. mothers with distended alcoholic bellies pushing strollers with sodden toddlers... utter hipster guys with hair so carefully groomed you'd swear he they just rolled out of bed with their ironic t-shirt on.... old mexican guys so gnarly you'd think you were in the back of a truck... really old guys in bermuda shorts and tube socks cruising the young girls... guys in suits going nowhere in particular, casting dubious looks your way... and so on and so on. Priceless. While you're sitting there, take special note of the empty building across the street whose empty windows and door look like the eyes and mouth of a cartoon face. Just sit there with a pitcher of Kenzinger and you'll see what I mean. And by all means, buy the Kenzinger.  Why? Is it the quality of the hops, or the care that their beer meisters put into every keg? No, because it's cheap. Just buy the cheapest beer on the menu, please... I beg you. Because cheap beer is real beer. Here is a guarantee. If you sit in front of Johnny Brenda's long enough, every type of motor vehicle will pass in front of you. Cars, vans, trucks, delivery vehicles, harleys, boats being pulled on trailers, mobile homes, huge trucks towing homes, jacked up hiphop cars blasting music, etc. I kid you not. And of course, their is always the firetruck with it's sirens blaring. A firetruck will ALWAYS pass by with sirens blaring. It's as if there is always a fire somewhere on Girard Avenue.   Johnny Brenda's provides a moment in time, and a place on the edge of a city going nowhere but deep into the heart of a gastro-pub addiction. And in this swirling mess of a backwater there is at least something to look at that is tragically real... something that can engage the imagination, and allow us to use our minds to focus on something more than a beer menu.

Lovely skylit room. Even on a rainy day, we felt like we were sitting beneath Mediterranean sun. The food was memorable and delicious, the service friendly and efficient, and the wine list affordable. Go there for lunch!
Nice place! We liked their coffee and grilled cheese.  Will come back for other food sometime.

Would've been better if I was hungry (and if I liked greasy food...and if I liked mayo). Still, met some friends here and had a few nibbles. Tried the peppercorn mayo, which was pretty tasty, and the especial sauce, which was nothing special. Can't believe how huge a regular serving is! Three of us couldn't finish one, haha.
corn = amazing

Amazing food for a great price! Stuck at a nearby hotel, as so many in Hartford are, I explored on foot.  At first, Bocca Rossa seemed stuffy and off-putting.  I was dissuaded. One lovely day, I discovered a sandwich board outside declaring a MWF happy hour and took a chance. Oh my!!!  The bruscetta was divine - I adore the ricotta with tomato and the onion and goat cheese.  All the meats are delectable - a treat for the palate. Over the past few days, beyond drinking a great deal of their delicious wines, I have explored the spinach salad (ever so lightly wilted, not over-dressed, and a true treat) as well as the spaghetti with pesto chicken (thin, perfectly sauced slices of chicken adorned tender pasta in a generous serving.) Altogether, a pleasure.  Did I mention the lovely bartendresses/waitresses?  Attentive, polite, helpful, and sweet!!! Please, give this lovely gem the attention it deserves!

Don't bother if you're getting delivery. Food arrived just under two hours after ordering, lukewarm, and with a brief apology that they were out of something (we weren't charged for the thing they didn't have, but no replacement or warning offered). Worst of all, the tom yum was watery. Jeera Thai has a surprisingly positive reputation in New Haven, and while I too have met the very sweet owner, I'm not willing to lie and say that her food is great. Or forgive this kind of lazy (how better might I describe slow and incomplete?) service. Get ready to drive out of town and dine in if you want proper Thai.

Intro: Too many good nights here. It is really one of the only nicer establishments to get a drink in West Philly. Plus Tap is a full service restaurant which is a huge plus. Basics: 1. Bar set up sucks dong. Whoever designed this place was an idiot and didn't consider humans, traffic flow, basic spacial organization, etc. It gets incredibly difficult to get around when packed. I didn't leave Smokes for this. 2. Food has been variable, but mostly a thumbs up. The pizzas are great. Thin crust, and pretty damn artisan. Go for the one with the mushrooms, truffle oil, and a sunny side up on it. Damn good son. 3. Burger was a bit dry. But well dressed. 4. Good selection of local and foreign beers. Not too craft (which I think is a good thing), but they do get pretty quirky sometimes, eg blueberry chocolate chicken tikka masala IPA from montana. Ok maybe not that quirky. Conclusion: Place where the grown ups go, or people who've learned that there are indeed other establishments besides the Stone and McD's for a meal and a beer.

Does Fogo de Chao need a 646th review? Well of course it does, so here it is. We celebrated my fiancé's birthday here. This was our second visit and we had a plan. We ate light all day to prepare and I made a 5 p.m. reservation to give our stomach's time to digest all that goodness. As usual, service was seamless since it seems that all of the staff is there to serve you. Our sides were never empty. We (read: me) went through those caramelized bananas pretty quickly. The salad bar was constantly replenished. The filet mignon was the standout and we always correctly received our medium cut requests. I didn't try all of the meat this time because part of my plan was to save room for the favorites (check out their menu ahead of time if you've never been). Overall we enjoyed a lovely evening and a happy birthday was had; however, it's nice when restaurants acknowledge the birthday person in some way, especially when it's mentioned in the reservation, and Fogo didn't. My fiancé still likes Chima better for some reason but we enjoy Fogo all the same. It's an expensive night out but worth it for special food coma-worthy occasions.
Geno, not bad at all.   But you came in second to the fella across the street.  :) Try a lil salt & peper on 'em.   Sumpin.

No longer a BYOB but we saw tables with alcohol.  I think they just posted the sign in case inspectors come, but they def. did not enforce the rule when i went .  Places like this are hard to review because most people rate the food relative to the price.  The appetizers were definitely good but it wouldn't have been nearly as good if it weren't that cheap.  The dumplings were good but I feel like its a generic Chinese restaurant dumpling.  You have to get it fried versus steamed, it does come out nice and hot.  The avocado potato salad had chickpeas and potatoes.  Great blend of favors and a unique dish from other asian cuisines.  The entrees were just alright.  The chicken curry tasted like a ketchup sauce with curry powder and the noodle soup dish was a bit bland.  Tibetan food in generally has a ton of spices that are very colorful and smells potent but just a bit lacking in taste.  These two dishes is exactly how it should be done but just were not for me.  It's a simple local joint feel.  Tightly squeezed but feels authentic.

I ate here twice in one week, it was so good. The decor is fun and has some interesting art (as the name suggests). The abundance of management keeps the restaurant ticking and they are friendly as are all the staff. The antipasto bar was phenomenal. You can choose a mixed plate of antipasto, the only problem is it's all so good that it's hard to choose. Whatever you do, don't miss the egg plant or the red peppers. Oh and the shrimp and scallops ... wow. The first night I had lobster risotto which was just fabulous. The flavors in the sauce were quite amazing. The second visit we had rabbit osso buco which so impressed my Japanese guests (and me). The wine list is fabulous and they have some very reasonably priced "Super Tuscans". I've been coming here for years but something has transformed this restaurant from very good to just excellent. I sat near the host stand and you could see that many of the clientele were regulars and no wonder. It's reasonably priced, especially for it's location, but who cares it's wonderful.

Max Brenner is the shit. I don't care how lacking in proper vocabulary that seemed, but I cannot describe it any other way. I love how if you want a delicious hot cup of hot chocolate but you cannot stay and eat; you simply walk to the back and get something to go. I am not a chocolate fan, which is weird since I love MB so much. As a kid, I have always hated everything chocolate and artificial. At Max Brenner, I feel what I am eating is not processed (yes there is such a thing) chocolate and every bite counts. Honestly though, in my 2 years of living in Philadelphia, I have never gotten a single thing on that menu that was not in the desserts section. It is not even worth it since the sweets are filling, delicious, and practical to choose as a main course. With the dark setting and the beautiful environment, I sometimes feel like I am eating in a Steven Starr restaurant.

Gotta say some of these negative reviews don't know what they are talking about. I have eaten here for years and never had a bad meal , love the brocli rabe and the gravy is fresh and good. The place is always busy so service may be a little slow but all the food is fresh and homemade. Go on a slow night for a good meal .

This place is not your average diner, which I like!  The offerings are very eclectic, with tons of organic grass fed options that you would never think of at a diner.  The idea is there, but the execution wasn't.  Had soup, which was decent, a greek salad, which they forgot the cheese and Ordered the grass fed ribeye mid rare came out well.  Definitely has a great deal of potential, I'll have to come back for breakfast.

In my opinion this is the best restaurant in Philadelphia.  The chef really does have passion about his cooking.  All the other reviews about the scallop noodles are spot on.  They are absolutely delicious.  I've been here twice.  The first time we got the 6 course tasting which was worth every penny.  We've had fluke, octopus salad, scallop noodles, beef cheek, short rib ravioli, trout, melon gazpacho, all delicious.  The cookie dough ice cream is also amazing.  Wait staff is very knowledgeable and attentive and they also make good cocktails.  Would highly recommend hitting up this little gem.

The food is absolutely delicious. I ordered the orange chicken, and it was amazing. After coming to Manhing I haven't gone to any other restaurant for chinese food. The taste is authentic and the service is great.
Pro:  Average Chinatown Chinese.

Being a fan of Beso and Blue I decided to finally try Bayou. Last night I dined with my girlfriend who saw the menu and was really looking forward to trying it. We both wanted something different which the Island doesn't really offer. We couldn't wait to try the Cajun flavor. Unfortunately we left disappointed.   I will say the restaurant and decor is great, I literally felt like I was in New Orleans. We started off with two appetizers, the Lamb Chops and the Alligator Bites. The Alligator bites we very good, The Lamb chops were cooked perfectly, but lacked seasoning. For our main entree I ordered The Steak Louie again the meat was cooked perfectly, but lacked any flavor. I never reach for the salt, but tonight I had to. My girlfriend ordered the N'awlins Chicken when it came she could not wait to dig in, very nice presentation. Again it lacked any flavor. Dessert we ordered the Crème Brule' Flambé, very cool presentation. Once again lacked serious flavor.   What really bothered me was when I received my bill. I don't like free handouts, but I think it is ridiculous for a restaurant to charge you for a refill of soda. Its not the point of the $2, its just good customer service. Unfortunately I won't be back.
avococado toast , couscous, hearts of palm salad, long island riesling (at the time i went it was byob) prob not anymore. very enjoyable place to take your squeeze.

This is my favorite bar in the area! I love the drinks and food and especially the service. Everyone is so nice and friendly. I take my kids there for lunch and then go drinking with my buddies at night. You can't beat the wide selection of $5 beers. The crowd is usually a bit younger than any other taverns around. So if you don't want to see any gray hairs, go to the Verona Inn and do some shots with the cute bartenders.
Better than Chipotle in terms of freshness and value, beef chili had great flavor.

I have had the pleasure of eating at The Kitchen on several occasions as it is within walking distance from my place of employment.   This past week, however, my husband and I ventured to The Kitchen after hours to participate in a Food and Wine Pairing class Chef Julie Carrion, Director of Catering & Education (and discovered by me on the Yelp Events Page)  My reasoning for going was two fold.  First - My husband is less of a wine person than I am, so I thought this class would be a good introductory course for him.  Second - I love wine but have a hard time when trying to decide what foods and wine complement each other.  I also get confused if the label does not have noticeable grape variety on it. The class into two sections.  In the first portion of the class we learned about wine's acidity, sweetness and tannins.  This was brilliantly illustrated by tasting Myer lemons and blood oranges (acidity), sugar (sweetness) and tea that had been steeped for various amounts of time (tannins).  I loved how she used food for illustration and broke down the language of wine into simple terms without feeling too elementary. The second portion of the class took the components that we learned in the first section and paired them with several dishes.  I was unsure of what type of food would be presented during this portion of the class, but I should have known based on the quality of the food that I have been served at lunch that the food would also be exceptional.  And that they were - from the pasta to the meats, each dish was cooked to perfection and at certain points in the evening I wished I did not have to share! Three white wines were paired with a simple orzo salad, pasta Alfredo and a shrimp scampi.  Two reds were paid with a beef and crispy chicken tender with a spicy Thai chili sauce.  I am glad that the food was served after the teaching portion of the class because I had a new found respect for how certain wines either accentuated or "did nothing" for a dish.  I also loved finding out how Mark's and my palette's differ when pairing the different dishes together with certain wines.  It was one of the first times that we were able to have an intelligent discussion about wine and it was lovely. All in all a great class.  Chef Julie is truly passionate about her love of food, cooking and Billings Forge.  She helped disarm some of the misconceptions about wine and was a great teacher to boot!  Also a special thanks to the employee that stayed past closing to help cook and plate the food.  She did a great job! I am definitely looking forward to attending another cooking class at The Kitchen in the near future.

Really, really happy about this place. In town for a convention, and I've been eating here every day. Pretty sure I could be here for a month and still eat new stuff every day. Every place I've been so far has been solid, which is impressive. Definitely worth a look!

Great Menu.  Not over priced.  Cash Only. An expected hour wait.  Worth it. The owner took our name and told us to go to the bar next door and have a drink and he would come and get us when our table was ready.  So we did that.  The bar next door was also great!  And he came and got us when the table was ready.  nice. Everything we ate was perfect.  The owner casually stops at most table and does has a quick genuine moment of shooting the shit.  Nice guy.   the only small complaint is that the server didn't bring back my change and assumed that the remaining 30% tip was hers.  And it could have been if she didn't assume so. so we left the proper 20% and that was that.  I will eat here whenever i'm in town.

[this is one of those reviews written by my sister who is toooooo busy to create her own yelp account.  sigh!] We were so excited to try Northern Spy Food and were not disappointed by the food, but we were sadly disappointed by the service.  We went at 9:30 on Friday night and waited over 30 minutes for a table for 2.  We waited another 45 minutes for our appetizers while tables seated after ours had finished their meals.  The music was so loud, that it was impossible to have a conversation while we waited for our food.  The manager was apologetic about the delay and comp'ed our two drinks at the end. As for the food, the gnocchi was terrific and delicious, as was the calamari appetizer and the duck.  The cold califlower soup was a little too sweet for our taste (between myself and my date, we didn't even finish half the bowl).  Since our dinner ended at almost midnight, we skipped dessert.  On balance, the food was great, but not worth the wait.

Attentive staff, zero attitude, warm dining environment.  Note: really small space!  Met up with my friend there at 8, was told there would be 1.5 hr wait for every seat in the house (that includes the bar)... no big deal, we went and had some wine nearby.  While the host offered to phone when the table was available (really cool), we were back around 9:15 and seated shortly thereafter.  Affordable! Quality! These two things rarely go hand in hand in the West Village.  Wine was under $10 a glass... oysters were awesome! Perfectly prepped and presented, bright, fresh.  Surprised that Jonathan E. found everything "doused" in oil.  My soft shell crab was clean in flavor, crunchy shell, moist meat, not overly oily by any means! Recommend! We had a salad as well, my friend had a white fish.  Both were stand up.  Entrees were (almost) all under $20 bucks! Can't beat that! We skipped dessert but got two yummy fresh from the oven chocolate chip cookies with our espresso...  left happy! Note- it's CASH only, at least for now...

I'm a bit shocked by the negative reviews because I consider myself a foodie. On the contrary to the past few reviews the pricing is phenomenal here. We've eaten here as a family numerous times and our bill is usually so small compared to everywhere else we go. Half prices wine Wednesdays? Gone out as a couple and once again had a few apps and TWO bottles of wine for an unreasonably low price. I've attended the Winchester for several of their music nights which were a blast. The staff seems to be very friendly. I've never had a bad meal here never been treated badly and I will continue to frequent this restaurant. The menu is perfect, enough selections but not a huge book, the kids portions are massive. My children always share one and we have leftovers. The bar is beautifully done! I can't say enough nice things about the place. I guess it's all preference maybe? Maybe more people should eat at Chilis or TGI Fridays? Anyway love the Winchester!

Best Roast PORK in the city hands down, nothing more to say besides the fact it's ion Reading Terminal so its impossible to park and run in for a sandwich, I wish he had a stand alone store out of center city. if you work in town and are in walking distance to the Reading terminal you need to go there.

This place is so much better than Caracas, the arepas aren't fried - thank you! Came here for brunch on a Sunday and was seated right away. Everything on the menu looks delicious. We got a brunch item - sweet plaintains, oxaca cheese, avocado, and scrambled eggs. For arepas - the 'Mami' and 'Arepa Pabellon'. It was all good. The green sauce is divine, put that shit on everything.
4.5 stars.  The decor and service was absolutely perfect.  The food was a 3.5-4 stars.  Very intimate and well thought out.
Get a beef and a pork sandwich both are perfect with a beer

M Wells continues to have excellent food and generous and hospitable service - my wife and I went for an early Sunday dinner -we saw an email that they got a whole tuna so we expected plenty of tuna dishes and were not disappointed.   I started with a Boulevardier and she had a nice glass of Rose.  My cocktail was great - I never see who makes them or where but they are always good.  The chef sent out a complimentary dish of Tuna Scallopini - thin pounded tuna with a bread crumb on top in a light tomato sauce - fresh and flavorful.   She started with a cheese, maple syrup and pistachio dish and I had a Mussel Soup - 180 degrees apart and both very flavorful and delicious.  Her dish had this creamy, tasty cheese in an almost 'soup' of real maple syrup along with a loaf of hot bread.  Tastes great - could even be a dessert.  My dish had plenty of whole briny mussels and  bread crumbs in a creamy soup.   For entrees she got tuna tartare, I got caviatelli with tuna confit and we split a meat pie.  The meat pie - flaky, buttery crust cooked perfectly, ground meat with rich flavor and the awesome cranberry ketchup sauce.  Her tuna tartare was delicious with egg and spices and mine was tender pasta with capers, olives and pieces of tuna confit - both fantastic.  We ordered glasses of white wine - had a sip of an alsace and it wasn't to our taste so we picked another, had a taste and it was great - they topped off her glass unasked at one point.         For dessert we got the brownie a la mode - the ice cream was great but the brownie was very dense.  We also got the fart pie to take home for the kids and on the way out chatted with the chef, he thanked us for coming again and he offered us a whoopie pie for the kids - they loved both.

This is "New American" done right. Chef/owner Kevin Addis takes classic recipes using fresh, seasonal ingredients and gives them the extra "oomph" that sets apart a true gourmet. The prices were shockingly reasonable for how richly flavored the food is; service was friendly, and the space itself was very comfortable; and being BYOB is always a big plus. Entree is a great addition to the neighborhood, and I can't wait to come back to try the rest of the menu!
This place is so delicious!!! The pork taco was very tasty and pineapple is essential. I guarantee that this place is the next Calexico.
Sake Bar Hagi maybe is the best izakaya in town, nice locatation, perfect sushi, good teppanyaki, cold Sapporo and Asahi, nice price! no snobs alowed.

Strong martinis. Yes!!! To-die-for chili fries and homemade mayo. Yea, baby! Cool music. Get out! Enough light for people watch (or be watched). Swoon! Happy Hour. Absolutely! Yep, I am a fan. More martinis, please!!!!!!...
Everything we had here was delicious and fresh. There were some really interesting flavors that were new for me, so I really enjoyed it. Good prices, and good service.
Love this place  some of the best Italian food around

I grew up in NYC and lived in Brooklyn for 14 years.  Pizza is really important to me.  It is my favorite food group. Rustica boasts its fresh ingerients and you can really tell.  There is a freshness to their pizza that I really enjoy.   Most pizza joints use the same old processed stuff - not that there's anything wrong with that - but Rustica really stands out to me. They are nice local folks and they've even shopped in my store - helping to support local businesses - also something very important to me.

As soon as I opened their door, I've noticed their beautiful flowers everywhere. Absolutely Romantic Place!  Less than 10 tables. Not a big place but they seemed busy . There were enough staff and they provided good restaurant service. I've tried their Lamb. it was  excellent! This place is one of the 'Must Try' places in NYC. I hope they make you happy as well. :)
The chicken sandwich is very good.
Arctic char, rainbow trout tempura, chocolate cinnamon mousse for dinner.  Came back the next day for lunch but forgot what I got.  It was good though!

In town for a week so wanted to meet up with friends for a quick delicious meal that was central to everyone. Found this place on yelp and decided it would be be less crowded lesser version of Kenka. It was the former but not the latter. My friends and I now have an alternative to the forever-lines St Marks joint. Standard izakaya options, but the following stood out: -astuyaki tamago - some of the best sweet omelette I have in the city. Always a key sign for any Japanese establishment -oden - hailing from LA, it's hard to be impressed by oden anywhere else. But this broth is so rich without being overly salty -kimchi cream udon - first time trying this, pretty impressed -Kara age - fried chicken that's super tender and crispy without too much batter Good but standard: -avocado tofu salad -okonomi yaki Very reasonably priced, and that's without making it for happy hour. And it feels much more spacious and comfortable than other izakaya places I've been to. Definitely coming back whenever I'm in town.

We got there early and by the time we left the place was packed! It was a Thursday night and I didn't expect this large restaurant to fill up, but it did. It was very different food and very good. I had the filet with a side of avocado, which was so simply prepared, yet so enjoyable. The filet was good and tasty, and not your father's filet. Served with lots of other goodies on the plate, it was a very filling meal. Loved the culture and the neighborhood.

Oh Tops Diner, how you have slowly declined. This place used to be my favorite diner hands down. Over the years the food quality has declined a bit. Portions are still huge, but the taste isn't there anymore. The New England Clam chowder every other friday is still great. All other diner staples are still very good. The prices keep climbing. Everytime they have a new menu, prices have gone up, but the quality stays the same or drops. C'mon Tops! You can do better.

Food was delicious, different taste from what you would find in similar category of restaurant. Staff are very friendly and make you feel comfortable. We were a party of four without reservation on a Sunday evening and when we called, we had a table available. We were probably lucky. I highly recommend this place and will be back for sure.

I'm lucky to call this place my neighborhood bar- the food and beer selection never disappoint.  When friends come to visit this is my go-to spot since there is something for everyone. LOVE the pulled pork, pretzel chicken fingers and black bean burger.  I also roll out on bed for weekend brunch just to get a bloody mary!

Once this place opened  we thought we'd give it a try.  I agree, everything was greasy.  My whole family was sick, the peanut oil (why is this healthier?) did something to us, maybe it was rejecting it.

Tiny litlle french fry place in the St. Marks area.  Don't expect to be able to sit, the seating area is very limited in the back.  I love the fact that they have so many choices in terms of condiments!  I am a total douser of all foods with condiments  of all kinds, so this is my idea of heaven.  The fries themselves are pretty good too so they are yummy with even just vinegar or the plain mayo.  Vives les frites!

Are you kidding me?   This place was OUTSTANDING!   Since it was my first time here, I went with the standard Spaghetti Bolognese (Spaghetti with Meat Sauce).  The sauce had both veal and beef in it and the spices were subtle and slightly sweet.  The pasta was cooked to perfection. Living in California, I don't get out there too often, but I can't wait to get back there. Save room for the desserts....

i stumbled upon this place by accident. my boyfriend and i loved it so much i went back with a friend and the love just kept on growing. we met the owner and i had my birthday and book release party here. they are friendly, knowledgable, & the place has a great atmosphere. they have great specials and frequently have beer reps to chat with. which is great cause i am a beer nerd. in a part of town where good bars are scarce this is one of my faves.

We ordered food for pick up and were told a half hour, when we got there, they said they needed 10-15 more minutes to make the rice and peas, fine, we took a stroll, the weather was nice, when we got back, we were told there were no more left but they were making them, did we want to 'bargain' and take jasmine rice. Well we had a hankering for the rice and peas so said no, but did he want to bargain with the price and we'd think about it, we were told NO, con-ed doesn't bargain with them for their prices, so the prie was as is, so we said oKAY, well we'll wait. We were then told by the guy taking the orders that he was doing us a favor by giving us what we ordered and that there were many orders before ours. Well I don't think it's a favor to get what I ordered and pay for, so the customer service sucked. When others came in for their orders they were told the same thing, everyone was disappointed. The woman cooking came out to tell us there is no way for them to know how much rice they need, WHAT?! We've been here before and continue to go back because we love the flavors of the food. She said the guy should have told us one hour, which would have been fine--he continued to argue with her and us about how he was not wrong and he was doing us a favor. We were really not happy with how we were treated and probably won't go back. When people don't put customers first--it's disappointing.

I recently had my birthday dinner here, and I cannot say enough good things.  We were in the private room at Apertivo, and everything was phenomenal. From the food, to the atmosphere, to the very attentive waiter Chris who made sure our wine glasses were always full! The event coordinator Jessica was amazing, and I'm a pretty picky/detail oriented person. I have a gluten allergy and Jessica arranged for the on-site baker to make me gluten free rolls (which were delicious). I was thrilled!! Thanks for making my birthday so special!

Mexican food for people who've never tasted Mexican food? We got the lucky seat in front of the photobooth - so blinded by flashes throughout the meal. A pretty restaurant and fun concept, but nothing we had tasted good.  We ordered Macho Nachos, steak tacos and shrimp tacos. All a bust - and we won't be returning. The nacho chips were cooked fresh, but very greasy. The meat on the nachos tasted like it'd been cooked in a vat of Worcestershire sauce - very salty. The main ingredient in the nachos was black beans. Nothing to write home about. The tacos came out next. I swore the waitress smirked as we ordered them, $13-15 entrees - the world's tiniest tacos on these mini platters. Cubes of beef - super salty. Shrimp was over seasoned in some sort of paste (I wiped it off and tried to cover it with lime juice - slight improvement). Everyone seemed to be enjoying drinks around us - maybe people go for the alcohol. We ordered horchata to combat some of the salt - watery and not tasty at all.

My favorite place in downtown Hartford as of right now. The 3ft beer bongs are great, the naughty nurse ale is amazing, great food, decent prices, AMAZING atmosphere, I love the back area with the pool tables and old saloon looking side. Still havent been downstairs to the comedy club

I was in Philly visiting a friend for the weekend and she brought us here on a Saturday night for dinner. The rolls all seemed to be half the normal amount (3 -4 pieces instead of the usual 6 or so). I ordered a tuna roll which was just your everyday run of the mill tuna roll. Good, but nothing spectacular. I also go a Ranger Roll. This thing was massive...massively delicious. Tuna, salmon, seaweed salad (yes, SEAWEED SALAD IN A ROLL) avocado and roe. As for the yakitori, some was good, some was just ok. I tasted the mushroom yakitori (definitely the best of the bunch), eggplant yakitori and the short rib. The short rib was too thin and didn't have enough meat to really be satisfying. Others ordered the chicken yakitori which also seemed to skimp on the meat. If i came back. I'd just stick with the mushroom yakitori, whatever they marinated those mushrooms in was pure tastiness. On to dessert...We ordered the green tea tempura ice cream. One word. BLEH! It was maybe the worst fried ice cream I've had. The tempura coating was thick and chewy. Not right at all. It should have been a nice crunchy coating thin enough to break through easily to get to the ice cream, instead I had to go searching for my ice cream through the breading only to find ice cream that was too frozen to get my spoon through. I don't want to work that hard to eat dessert. My friend goes for karaoke all the time here and says it's wonderful so I've got to take her word for it. It seems like they have some great drink specials which they only offer sunday-thursday. If i lived in Philly I would probably come back here as they offer some solid Japanese food.

We were told 45 minutes to an hour for the wait, so we chose drinks at the bar and exchanged worried, hungry glaces. We were promptly seated in about 15 minutes. The pork burger looks incredible and is really good -- I strongly dislike Root Beer and I even enjoyed the Root Beer BBQ sauce -- but I felt like I wasted half the bun because it was so much larger than the burger itself. Perhaps I would feel less guilty if the bun were smaller? (These days, If it's not the ancestral origins of the meat, it's the size of the bread accessories that will make you rethink everything you've ever done in your life and how you could help send fewer waste calories down the drain... This is a good thing, for the most part.) Nice patios out front and back, although it's definitely not warm enough yet to enjoy them.  Good beer selection, if you're into that sort of thing. The acoustics are not ideal for screaming children, so if you were thinking about bringing yours, please reconsider.
Decor was cute but crepe was just ok.  Give it a shot if you are in the neighbourhood but don't go out just for this.
One of the best cuban food places in US. Get the roast pork with yellow rice and black beans, cuban sandwich, and roast corn with spicy butter cream! p.s. i love their sangria soda!
Been a few times; the food was just okay.  Not a good value.  Very overrated.

I probably could have put a down payment on a house with all the brunches I've had in the last year. I've had some great ones all over the city, but the Memphis Taproom is by far my favorite brunch spot.  I love MT so much, I drove there from center city during that snow storm of the decade we had a few weeks ago, because a friend and I decided we could not go on without their chicken fried chicken. The food is spectacular. A lot of very simple dishes made very well. I recommend sharing an order of suicide rings, because they are one of the greatest ways to eat an onion. My favorite entrees are the fried oysters and the chicken fried chicken. If you couldn't tell, these guys are masters of frying. The oysters are deep fried in a cornmeal batter and come with some of the best slab bacon I've ever had. The chicken fried chicken is are boneless pieces of fried chicken sitting on a bed of mac and cheese that is  swimming in a pool of habanero bbq sauce.   The service is always friendly. The first time I went to MT they gave us a Trivial Pursuit board and didn't mind that we stuck around way past our meal to finish the game. Sometimes they get in the weeds, but you forgive it, because brunch isn't supposed to be a fast-paced meal. My one complaint is the coffee maker.
