They only have one coffee maker and are constantly in the process of making a new pot which gives you about a 10 minutes lag between cups. There is something sort of heartbreaking about having the best savory pumpkin french toast of your life and not being able to wash it down with a cup joe. All in all this is the kind of place you want to spend a lazy Sunday. There is nothing like self-medicating a hangover with belgian beers, while eating some of the best comfort food in the city.

Don't you hate it when you go to your neighborhood/corner coffeeshop, hungry for breakfast but they only have little danishes/muffins? Well this is your spot. I love the casual, order at the counter approach, but without losing the service and quality of a full service restaurant. The menu is pretty extensive and there are specials to make it even harder to decide. The portion sizes were very fair and the prices affordable. This is going to be our go-to spot for a quick, easy, tasty and filling breakfast in the neighborhood.

This place is like the neighborhood's secret, with great views of the city. The picnic tables and bright umbrellas line the waterfront of Long Island City, you can't help but just sit there sipping your drink and take in the view. A must if your in the mood for an outdoor beer oasis!

this place is probably one of my top brunch spots in the city IF i'm in the mood to wait a really long ass time..  brunch places are prevalent, especially in the city, and as you may know, this can change in a day or so, as spots keeping popping in and out. the wait is rather lengthy.. 30-40 minutes to be exact...you get past this... and I was deceived by its overtly adjoining room.  Holy mackerel... we walked around the block before we were able to get seated finally.  no recommended time to come in, it's busy all of the time.   $12 limited brunch special includes your choice of entree, cappuccino or tea and orange juice.  the OJ was freshly squeezed, and I couldn't have asked for a better cap, which was a segafredo brand (when I least expected it to be any good).  For my entree, I couldn't resist the salmon eggs Benedicte.  Though I can tell you I flip flopped between a few things here and there.. everything on the menu looked stellar.  The eggs were poached to perfection, the hollandaise was light and fluffly... the potatoes were crisp & seasoned amazing.... the harissa served here completely made the dish.   Every bite was worth savoring for more, until I realized I had finished it.  Even the portion was the perfect ratio. other dishes have a slight Middle Eastern flair to it, have yet to try their goat cheese omelette & pumpkin pancakes!  time to branch out.

I finally got to try the famous Fette Sau. Sure its in Philly, but i've heard the qualityis just as good. And to be honest, after eating here, its hard to imagine the original in Brooklyn being much better. The BBQ at Fette Sau is almost flawless. Their care of the meat is unreal. The meat are ridiculously tender and easy to pull apart while somehow still maintaining enough texture to allow you to get a nice healthy bite. Its like they somehow added a timer to their meat so that it holds shape until you bite it and then as soon as you chew, the meat just melts away. This is true for the brisket, the beef ribs and the chicken. Most importantly, they infuse enough smoke to make it enjoyable without overwhelming the senses. Too much smoke is a bad thing and can ruin BBQ. Fette Sau hits that delicate sweet spot of enough smoke to make you love BBQ without giving that smoke headache. The brunt end beans were equally awe-striking. Sweet, smoky but somehow not overly heavy, its a masterpiece in baked beans and most likely the best i've ever had. Now, i said almost flawless. Meaning there was a flaw and that flaw was their sauce. I found all three sauces lacking. The "spicy" tasted like plain sauce with extra pepper. The vinegar was just straight up vinegar. And the sweet tasted like something i could get from a store. All options are below the meat of Fette Sau. If you're a BBQ traditionalist (who thinks BBQ should be unadulterated meat), then you'll probably think Fette Sau is the incarnation of your BBQ dreams and I would definitely recommend eating the meat without additions. For pure meat, Fette Sau is the very best

Was recommended by a friend and am so glad I went! Must say the wait staff and food was excellent! Went on a Saturday night, in a party of two so was seated right away around 7 but there is a wait if you have larger parties and come later in the night. The decor was nothing special, and we were seated right near the walk through traffic but didn't mind because we had no wait. Ordered the Gnocchi Caprese and my friend ordered the special pumpkin ravioli. When our orders came I was given the wrong dish and ended up waiting for them to re-make my dish while my friend ate. The chef was very apologetic, gave us the mistaken meal on the house and mine. All three dishes were amazing! The flavor, sauce, and presentation were right on. The prices were very reasonable, ranging between $13-$20 for pasta dishes. After hearing the rave reviews about the cannoli, we had to give them a try. We were not disappointed! The cannolis were filled upon order, fresh and delicious!! Among the best I've ever had! When our bill came our waiter apologized again for the meal mistake and said the dessert was on the house! Customer service was an A+, will be back to try more of the extensive menu!

Unbelievable tapas.  Just love the new plates that get produced every time we are in.  The 8 hour cooked beef cheek is delectable!  The pappardelle is fav.  Foie Gras is gob smacking!  BYOB means you bring the Vino of choice and the rest can only be experienced.  Waiters know their dishes. The brown butter cake is the best way to finish of.  Just get out there as quickly as you can.

My new go to burger spot! Blows 5 guys out of the water and i have been a 5guys follower since they opened, a bit more expensive than the norm but it is not the norm! Cant wait to go back and have me some chilli cheese fries!

I love all these reviews that are like "OMG where else can you get so much dumplings for like, two dollarrrrrsssss?" Uh, how about any other dumpling place in the entire city? Jeesh, dudes. I've been here a half-dozen times and really, Prosperity Dumpling is kind of a gamble: on the days when the dumplings are good, they are phenomenal, but on they days they're not? Oof. Really not good. The same goes for the sesame pancakes with beef. Good day? Holy hell, THIS IS SO GOOD. Bad day? Greasy, burnt, and gristle-filled. Pair this with the long lines (during which I always get stuck behind a cracker tourist trying to hide their delight/dismay that "gaw-lee, maw! the signs are all in foreign here!" coupled with "um, I can use my credit card here, right?"), I'd much rather try my luck elsewhere.

Wow.. i heard about this place from numerous friends and what better time to try it out than new years eve. Really wasnt expecting much since I never really had good experiences with course menus but definately was surprised by the quality compared to the price. My wife and I tried the cod and the beef and it was cooked to perfection. Have tried gal bi jjim at all types of korean restaurants but never had I had such soft and tender meat. (Usually very chewy at most restaurants) Then there was the mixed riced pot (yuk hwe bi bim bab) which was one of the bests I had with the sauce being just right (not too spicy and not too sweet). All in all, had a wonderful dinner at such a reasonable price and def will be heading back to try their regular menu. Thanks for the memorable night barn joo! See you soon.

I've always wanted to try Boqueria and my friend Paul H. was nice enough to accompany me here. This place has been on my list to do ever since I first walked by a few years back. Unfortunately for me and Paul, every time we try to come here... we either show up at the wrong locations...  or the weather hates us. So just a note, before heading out, just make sure you know which location. Do this or you each might end up at one of the other locations like we did! There is one in SoHo and another in Chelsea... and also in Hong Kong. Boqueria is a nice, modern place to get your Spanish Tapas fix. There are pleanty of seats, high tables, room at the bar, and warm lighting to set the mood for a great meal shared with friends or over a date! I always enjoy looking at the hand written signs outside with witty one liners enticing patrons to come in. I'm just letting you know that the signs worked and that they're part of the reason why I have been interested to check out Boqueria. It's also no secret that I am a tapas fan! I honestly wanted to like Boqueria more than I did. In Boqueria's defense, Paul H. and I weren't that hungry and just chose a few small plates to split. I really enjoyed the Papas Gravas (potatoes), they had a unique texture that was very interesting in the mouth. Other than the Papas Gravas, we ordered a few other things but we both felt they were a little too salty. Although the service was very friendly, it was very hard to get our server's attention even though it was not super busy. I definitely will come and give Boqueria another chance. I really want to see what else the menu has to offer, and also to try some of the famous sangria!

delicious! great quality, fast service and affordable meal prices. after a long tiring day of walking on canal street and listening to the same phrase "you want omega, rolex, i have here" a billion times, joes shanghai is a great place to sit down and enjoy and good quality meal. I highly recommend this place for a great chinese dish and dumplings. I must say the dumplings are amazing! only downfall is, it is a new york style eatery, in sense that they want you in and out. its good for new yorkers, however me, i like to sit and take my time, not have my check on the table before I havent even finished my meal.

This is a very nice Italian restaurant in my opinion. It's not big but the ambiance is very lovely. They have a nice bar where you can drink while waiting for a table. I had a glass of white wine, pasta (don't remember the name though), and some deserts. Really enjoyed the pasta. Our table was a bit small which was not ideal but it's a small minus I'm willing to overlook.

Amazing food! Wide selection of crepes and brunch food and a great list of reasonably priced wine. We ordered the couscous with lamb stew which was not on the menu but was AMAZING! The owners are Moroccan and French, super polite and the service is great. Most of the other patrons were French too, which has to mean something.

I would not feed this food to monkeys. Instead of going to Chipotle next door my friends suggested trying this place. Reluctantly I agreed. I ended up going to Chipotle after! If there was an award for the most mystery meat these guys take the Gold. Hands down! I prefer my chicken to be cooked and want only white meat. But no there was lot of fat, dark meat and some other kibbles and bits. If there was an award for being unorganized, sending raw meat to customers. They take the Gold. They sauce the hell out of everything. But they do it so it keeps you from knowing what you are actually eating. It just makes you think this place is owned by PF Changs if they serve rubbish here imagine the subpar quality of product they serve at PF Changs the restaurant? Save your $8 and go to chipotle. You walk out with organic food not this mystery meat sauced shit.

I wanted to update my old review; my husband and I took his Greek parents here this weekend when they were in town visiting relatives. Andy's father is notoriously critical of restaurants and food (if he lived in the city we'd probably just call him a foodie). He loved it, obviously, especially the meatballs (lighter than air), and the smashed fries. But the real reason I'm updating  this review is to call out an amazing waitress, Christina C. who really made the night.  Funny, charming and well informed, Christina is a true gem. See you soon, MP!
I was lost in Staten Island stop for direction got great  lunch  and a place for sure I will return too ..(Family Feel) . across for the Staten Island ferry

Amazing breakfast. Delicious food and beautiful presentation. A bit on the pricey side, but perfect for a special occasion. I had the challah French toast with lemon sauce, Brie, and berries. Definitely try something off their brunch specials menu!

*sigh* I really really wanted to like this place because I am a Texan and I have faith in all things Texas BUT I just didn't. When I arrived I ordered an ice tea, just tea and it took over 15 mins for my tea because I guess they were washing cups? That rubbed me the wrong way but I thought no biggie. We ordered Chips and Queso as an appetizer and the Queso was soooooo bland, nothing like the Queso at home, it lacked flavor, it was thinner than what I'm used to, just a failed attempt at the dish. For my main dish I ordered a loaded baked potato stuffed with brisket because at home it's a delicious dish and I was so happy they had it. It was such a disappointment, the potato was small, just regular sized and it was undercooked, the inside was pretty firm, it lacked in the amount of butter and cheese, and the brisket was very subpar. Usually, this particular dish is served and the potato is basically falling apart because of all of the butter and cheese being melted by the hot meat in an already hot potato, it's usually pretty epic but not here. I don't want to give up on the place because I am a Texan and I believe in all things Texas. I'll probably give them another chance but I was just not impressed.... At all.

I enjoy trying new places and rarely want to visit the same place twice within a short time period...but I did here! I've only ordered from the tapas portion of the menu and have yet to try the entrees. The regular menu is solid, the specials menu is vast, the food arrives at perfect temperature, the arrangement and display of food is quite appeasing, the service didn't make us feel rushed, and the food was delicious. Much better than Ibiza or any of the other tapas places in the area.

We found this on our way through the area (thanks to Yelp) and agree wholeheartedly that it's a fine place for breakfast. The food is good (blueberry pancakes for one of us, eggs and corned beef hash for the other), friendly staff, clean environment (including bathrooms), and plenty of coffee. As a pancake bigot, I was happy to see fluffy pancakes rather than the squashed ones that many diners think are right. The corned beef hash is homemade, with different spices than the classic version. My partner liked it a lot; I am partial to the original.

A lot of restaurants during Restaurant Week end up disappointing: higher volume of customers = disorganization, pushing customers out to get higher turnover of tables, food not prepared as well as it could be. Barbuzzo showed none of these set backs during my dinner here for Restaurant Week. The restaurant offered both the pre-fixe menu and their normal offerings, but we went for the restaurant week menu. The service was great. Despite the stress of the week, the employees all seemed to be maintaining their laid back attitude and smiles on their faces. I was really  pleased with my entire meal.  The crostini starters that were offered were both delicious and really made me want more. I went for the sheep milk ricotta which was super tasty (even after just having another crusty bread with topping). The flavors were different enough to make me not regret my choice. My sister got the meatball slider, and liked it so much she refused to share even a bite (jerk). My mom got the roasted beets and could not stop raving about it. I went for the pan seared gnocchi for my third course and... yum.  I can't put into words but it was amazing. If gnocchi could be "light," this dish was, and the mushrooms were delicious. The rest of the table went for the oven roasted chicken, and the grilled bronzino and enjoyed theirs as well. (I had a taste of each, and I still think the gnocchi won). I would have been perfectly full and happy after these three dishes, but the best was yet to come. There is a reason people rave about the salted caramel budino. I'd give up my yet-to-be first born for this dessert. I will be back though, because there were so many other things on the menu that I want to try! Note: The other two restaurants owned by Marcie Turney and Valerie Safran (Lolita and Bindi) are BYOB.  Barbuzzo is not. So check out their wine selection!

A hidden gem in Staten Island! You feel like you're in New Orleans when you come to Bayou. I usually do the prix fixe menu when I go, which is pretty cheap for a 3 course meal. Some items I've tried are the beef medallion, lobster bisque, crab cakes, alligator bites and pork cutlets. I can honestly say I have never had a bad meal here. The space is a bit small, but newly renovated. The parking can be a hassle, so car pool if you can. Mondays are usually psychic night, for those interested. They do have other entertainment throughout the week, so definitely check their website for updated events.

HOT. MESS. I'm mildly claustrophobic and apparently, Batali and friends got the memo because this place is like HELL to me.   Put all of the delicious Italian products in a huge space and then PACK it with people to the point where you can barely figure out which end is up?  Oh cruel, cruel world... Had dinner with a friend.  Miraculously managed to get seated.  Really enjoyed the green lasagna dish.  But, not enough so that I'd brave the crowd again. It was weird to have people shuffling past you constantly while trying to avoid knocking your wine glass over. In fact, in order for me to return, I would have to be looking for something that I needed immediately and ONLY Eataly carried it.  On second thought, I'd probably just change my menu before I went back there again.
Personally the best soondubu house in this neighboord .
Good seafood..liked the crab fries!

Great Spanish food. Everything on the menu is amazing..I highly suggest the coconut dipped shrimp or the ceviche for the appetizers, I'm a seafood fanatic so I usually go with some kind of fish. As far as the entrees i always go for the churassco, the portion is pretty big for one person and absolutely delicious, that being said I still eat every last bite..Don't judge me lol My friends have tried the mariscadas dish which is a bunch of different seafood items including shrimp, clams, scallops, mussels etc in a garlic broth which was delicious as well. All entrees are huge so there will always be enough to take home and enjoy more later :) This place also has many locations throughout the city and one in Forest Hills. The ambiance is cute for a date night but the table settings are a little cramped if it doesn't bother you to sit 2 feet away from another party then this place is your go to spot for latin food. It's a block away from Bloomingdales so you can walk off your food with some shopping after!

I was between 2 and 3 stars. This place is pretty overrated in my opinion. I have a high standard for bagels and Bagel Box did not meet it. First of all, they didn't label their bagels and they were set back far from the counter so I couldn't tell which was which. The service was okay. We only waited about 5 minutes but the bagels were definitely a disappointment. I like my bagel to be big and fluffy. These were small and thin, and they did not seem very fresh. We ordered Taylor ham, egg and cheese on an everything and pumpernickel with veggie cream cheese. Both were just ok. I wouldn't go back.

I stopped by here with a friend on the recommendation of another friend. At Num Pang, they do cambodian sandwiches which are totally different than Vietnamese sandwiches in ingredients but great in their own regard and Num Pang knows their cambodian sandwiches. I'm a sucker for pork belly so I got the Five-Spice Pork Belly Sandwich ($8) with the Blood Orange Lemonade ($3). The pork belly was nice and tender, the sauce on the sandwich is to die for and the bread is perfectly toasted. The lemonade was not over-sweetened and refreshing. There is seating upstairs, but not a lot of room for large groups. Order to go and have a Num Pang outing in near by Union Square. I will be coming back here for more to try more of their sandwiches.

Recommended to us for good brunch, my buddy and I decided to check this spot out on a Thursday morning...our first full day during our short stay in Philadelphia. I ordered the tofu scramble (yelp.com/biz_photos/-DGs…), complete with a biscuit, potatoes and some apple cinnamon sweet dessert side, along with green tea (served in this cute tin-type cup with a slice of lemon). Pretty good. I don't know what I expected the tofu to look like. I guess I just wasn't quite expecting tofu squares...but something that more resembled scrambled eggs? Oh well. She ordered granola with soy milk. She was going to order granola with yogurt but they don't have plain, just the fruity kind. We didn't have to wait. We sat ourselves down. I've heard this spot gets pretty crowded on the weekends. If I'm back in town, I will definitely come back to order other (just-as-yummy, if not more) food items.

I decided to have dinner with a few friends of mine last night knowing that Barbuto is booked a month in advance. When I called the restaurant, I was politely greeted and the gentleman explained that we definitely have a shot to snag a cancellation on a Wednesday night. The food was absolutely spectacular! I had the risotto with cauliflower and got a chance to try my friends' dishes: steak - medium, and cod fish. All of the dishes were magnificent! My only complaint would probably be drink prices - $12 for vodka tonic (made with no name vodka). But I guess that's the price you pay for that area. Definitely a must to visit! I'm planning on coming back for brunch very soon :) Enjoy!

Was excited to try this place.  Noodle quality was pretty good, freshly made, but I thought it would have been better. Lack of flavor in our dishes (we got without broth) but the worst was the TON of bad quality (I don't even want to know what type) oil they sog their stir fried noodle dishes in.  Probably socked away 200 grams of fat with that meal.  Never again.

My FAVORITE lobster roll in nyc.  Better than Red Hook, on par with Luke's, way better than the fancy mayo-laden Pearl's.  Tons of meat, lightly mayo-ed, perfectly buttered roll and gloriously seasoned.  Fries aren't great, but that doesn't detract from the awesomeness of the roll.   It's shocking to me that folks think $17 is a lot for a roll of this size and quality.  Yes, lobster is expensive; it is also delicious.   Great beers on tap, fantastic oysters, succulent fried clams.  They also serve mixed drinks by the pitcher. uh.oh.  I miss the back garden (it's huge, with lots of picnic tables) but can hang inside (small, a bar, just a few tables, some window seats, very casual) on a winter's eve just the same.  And open late!   Thank you for opening so close to my home.  You guys make life better.
Food had lots of taste and was plentiful.  The atmosphere was great and we had no problem getting a table on a Saturday night.   I can say we enjoyed our dinner and the time we spent here.

The burgers are pretty damn good. I'm not much of a burger connoisseur but in comparison to popular Bergen Ctys burger spots - shake shack, bobby flays and five guys... Hands down this place gets top billing. In my opinion, what really brings out the burger are the accompaniments.  I got bacon and sauteed onions. I would be happy with even just that on their bun..  and the fries?  AAAAMMMMAAAZZZING.. it is already seasoned but dip it in truffle aioli - OMG... They also have a bread pudding for dessert.  I think they change the flavor every few days (??) It tastes homemade and obviously made with love.. so much better than the supersweet factory made cakes/pastries most restaurants offer.   I'm so happy we are getting modern restaurants in my neck of Bergen County.

This is where the chefs go to grab a bite to eat with wine and chill after their restaurants close. My friend who is a chef took me here at about 1am and we had a nice night feast of oysters, bone marrow ( you gotta spread it on the bread bread) and a bottle of wine. I've returned here twice afterwards but have never come here for a normal dinner but always after midnight, which I think is the whole charm about Blue Ribbon.

Grilled Codfish.  That is all I eat here, but my wife eats other menu choices and loves it all.  My Grilled Codfish: A usually massive piece of cod, grilled, a little black and crusty on the outside and deliciously moist on the inside, smothered in green peppers, onions, chunks of garlic and olive oil.  As traditionally Portuguese as it gets.  Side of boiled potatoes and nice fresh veggies, usually green beans and, carrots.  Go for it! Also, the cockles are great!!
The diner is nice, but the particular dish I ordered was not the best. Do not order the Cajun chicken grilled sandwich. However, everyone I was with enjoyed their food.

OK, so this may not be an entirely *fair* review because I've never had a full meal here, only delivery and dessert. BUT, from my numerous experiences so far, it's never blown me away. Dessert was just ok, nothing memorable. Chicken burger was a weird  chopped up patty and not tasty. The tuna nicoise salad was the worst I've ever had -- the tuna was not fresh, it was brown actually, with overpowering peppercorns on top and a way too salty mix of roasted red peppers, anchovies, and olives. Potatoes and hardboiled eggs were halved and thrown in without much thought. It really disappoints me when a nice restaurant messes up a simple dish. The entree size is $22 and I would have definitely sent it back if I was dining in. I dunno, perhaps stick to the fancier, more expensive things on the menu? Better yet, don't risk it and just skip this place altogether and go to another well-rated place in TriBeCa -- god knows there are about a million of 'em.

it's hard to find a cute little brunch place in soho on a sunday morning... not sure why.  got on yelp and looked this place up.  it's a small, cozy french cafe.  by cozy, i mean you are basically shoulder to shoulder with the peopel at the table next to you.  orderd a breakfast sandwich with egg and sausage on a french baugette.  my sister got an order of baked eggs.  both just hit the spot on a chilly morning.   high five for the host.  we put our names down on the list and then a couple comes in and just sits down at the next open table.  the host then shoos them away, telling them that table is already taken (by us).

Absolutely love this quirky spot! I ordered the grilled vegetable panini and we quickly fell into a deep consensual romance. I really enjoyed the fact that I can taste the thick cuts of vegetables and the gooey Brie in my sandwich, and it was a perfect match with my mixed green side salad. My dining partner ordered the mushroom toast, which tasted a-maz-ing. The creamed mushroom and kale is unlike anything I've ever had anywhere else. Our female server wasn't anything memorable, but we'll definitely be back again for the food.

May & Jen have become part of my morning pre-work routine.  This is a fantastic place to grab a cup of coffee and a bagel in the morning. Good sandwiches, especially thew hot paninis.  Since its near my job, I've run through all of them and have never been disappointed.  They are also diligent about keeping the hot dogs & sausages on the rollers fresh, so unlike most places, I'm not afraid for my life when I need a quick meal.  Their soups are also excellent.  Overall, a great deli if that's what you're looking for.

We went to the bakery next door, not the sit down. Which was great because we didn't have to wait to be seated. I got the red velvet/ cheesecake combo. Both were pretty dang good. Definitely a solid NY cheesecake and so many locals swore by it that I am pretty sure this is as good as it gets. My husband and I had a debate on what was better though... Juniors or the cheesecake at Peter Lugers in Brooklyn. I honestly thought that Peter Lugers was denser and higher quality, more enjoyable. DEFINITELY a good cheesecake.

Usually has great food but not recommended for groups. I set up a work dinner for my company with about 12 people.  They told us that they could not allow us to order off of the regular menu and put us at a table in the bar (even though their private room was open). The menu that they provided was reasonably priced for 3 courses ($55) but was very limited in selection.  The apple walnut salad was unbelievable - I finished every bite - and the dessert was excellent.   However, the entree was the reason for the 3-stars.  Most of the table went with the New York Strip, which for most of us was a bit overcooked.  It was an OK steak, but not up to the level of one of the best restaurants in CT.  The steak fries on the side tasted stale and dry - like they had been sitting out all night.  And there were a few pieces of spinach on the side of the plate that added nothing. Service was good but not overly memorable.  Very disappointed that we could not order off the regular menu, which I know is usually excellent.  Will be booking future work dinners somewhere else in New Haven from now on.

I am one of the fans in their Brooklyn store so I was very excited that they opened one in Manhattan! They restaurant interior decoration is definitely more upscaled than the Brooklyn one. I went couple times this month, and I realized that they improved the quality of meat and vegitable. It feels very fresh espeically all the green vegitables! We ate more than the meat. Price is very reasonable. I recomend for large group party and small gathering at this place.

"Banh mi" "hoagie" "sub". Whatever you want to call theses sandwiches they are on fresh baguettes and and packed full of fragrant herbs and greens. Watch out for the jalapeños. My sandwich had one, but not until the end so it was a pleasant surprise when my mouth caught on fire. There's also usually a long cucumber that can make the whole thing fall apart if you take bites that are too big. The Bubble tea is mighty sweet, so if sugary goodness is what you seek this is your spot. I make a habit of trying the foreign things on the counter top. The spring rolls are fresh like the sandwiches and come with flavorful peanut and fish sauce. The brown baked balls with sesame seeds are sweet, fried and soft in the center. The things wrapped in green leaves are the only thing that I have found unappetizing. Sometimes they are stuffed with a sticky substance that is similar to uncooked dough with various ingredients in the center. Other times they are filled with sticky peanut stuff. If you can get past the texture then give them a try. Service is not trying to charm you, but they are fast, and pleasant enough.
The Standard Tap sets the standard for great gastropubs.  The beet salad is awesome.

Downtown Hartford's best option for greasy American Chinese food! I do like to be a fatty every now and then though.. so I've indulged and was not blown away, but I wasn't disappointed either. If you find yourself in the mood for some American Chinese food, consider Saigon Kitchen! If nothing else but the lack of other (American style) Chinese restaurants! :)

As a whole, I liked it here and would come back.  Here's what I have to say: Sheep's milk ricotta gnudi- amazing. I would return just for this. Deviled egg- good, but I could make it at home Chicken liver toast- too heavy and greasy for me Grilled squid- good, but nothing unique Cocktails- unique and pretty good Decor- very cute Service- really great. Wonderful staff and waiters
great wings. cool neighborhood place to watch the game.

I have read reviews of this place and expected much more, maybe i am spoiled too much.... i wanted to like this place but design is cliche.....and food mediocre.. it's for B&T people.... I walked away feeling ripped off.

Not a fan. I actually had to take a few days before writing this review. First off, we were seated right away for an early Sunday dinner. The waitress came and took our drink and appetizer orders. While waiting, we finished our drinks and watched her lean against the wall looking at her nails and watching TV. Eventually she came to take our meal orders, and we asked for additional drinks. Again, they were empty as the food was delivered by the runner. We had to have him pull her off the wall to attend to us. Also, at this time we inquired about our appetizer and she looked shocked. She went to check on it and came back saying it would be out in just a few min "I am sorry, I guess It was never put in". Again we asked about another round of drinks. Half way though our meals we got our appetizer and had the runner again, pull the waitress off the wall for our drinks. As for the food, I got the Alfie's Burger. It was ALOT of meat, you could hardly get your mouth around it. It was cooked well, but just so much beef. You could hardly taste anything else on the burger. Maybe someone else would like this, but it wasn't for me. My date had the fried chicken and roast corn. It had great presentation, and it seemed to enjoy it as a whole, but the roast corn had a very strong burt taste. I understand being fire roasted, but it was more black then yellow, and tasted like burnt kettle corn. Overall, far below what we were expecting. :-(

I agree with the yelpers on this place being rated 5 i Ordered a combo with chip and drink. No fountain drinks here but some flavored bottle drinks. As other yelpers say if your looking for quantity rather  than quality not the place for you. As far quality is concerned i haven't had A chance to visit Maine so i cant really compare to Maine lobster quality, but who cares i love this place the sample portion just looks small but after eating all three sandwich, it will hit the spot but personally i like the crab rolls out of the 3rolls.  Along with root beer drink and bbq chips. This Makes me wanna come back asap just writing review. the only negativei could say about this restaurant is its location. It will take you a long time to fine a Metered parking so you will  be going in to a parking garage and spending minimum of 10. Making your 20$ combo into 30$combo. But besides that i still highly recommend this place and would come back here but park a bit further to walkof the all the food and save me 10$ to buy that yummy clam chowder.

Sorry but I just don't get the popularity of this place. I had high hopes for it based on the Yelp reviews.  I was not impressed with the food or the service.    My husband and I arrived on a Friday night around 7:45 PM. We found a place to park on the street only a block away. All the tables were full, and there were four other people waiting for a table when we arrived.  The party of four told the server they had two more coming but wanted to be seated anyway.  They were seated and we sat down in the waiting chairs along-side the wall.  After ten minutes or so, the other two people in their party arrived.  We watched while the server had a table of two who were already in the middle of their dinner get up and move over to another table that had just opened up so he could make room for the table of six.  I get that the space is limited, but that was poor planning when he sat the table for four (that were going to be six) and I thought it was rude to the people who were already eating and looked confused. I thought this was a red flag, and I should have just left at this point.  However, I really wanted to try the food, so I decided to sit it out.        A table of four opened up and a party of five had come in shortly after while we were still waiting.  The table sat there open for a long time, and the party of five asked why they couldn't just sit there and pull up an extra chair.  They sat down, and we were left sitting there waiting, even though we'd arrived first.  We were looking around confused, wondering if we were invisible.  Finally one of the guys who had just sat down at the table for four asked if we were waiting for a table and apologized to us.  That was nice of him to do so.  At the same time, my husband noticed a table for two opening up next to that table, so he thanked the guy and told him not to worry.  The table for two opened up and then were will still left sitting there.  It was very strange.  Finally a guy comes out and asks for our name (no one else's names were asked for), and I told him and he said he would make sure we were the next people seated.  There was a table open, so I don't know what that was about.  Ten minutes later a young guy finally motions us back toward that table for two.    I was irritated, but happy to be seated and hoping the food would make up for this mess. It was really hot in the area we were seated in due to the heater behind us. I ordered a few things I'd seen in the Yelp reviews.  The papaya salad, chicken appetizer (they were out of this), the stew with the pumpkin and chicken, and a seafood lemongrass stir-fry with mussels, calamari, and shrimp.     The papaya salad was the best thing we had, and while it was good, I was not impressed.  It was like a Thai papaya salad with thinly shredded pieces of papaya, lime, fish sauce, and tomato, but it was missing the delicious little dried shrimp, long beans, and peanuts. Now to be fair, maybe that's how they serve it in Cambodia; I don't know.  I guess I was just expecting more.  I can make a better one at home, and I do regularly, so although it tasted good and had some heat to it, it was a let down.   The stew was a large portion and hot in temperature, but I hated the flavor of the broth and the chicken was chewy dark meat, and there were little pieces of bone in the stew.  On a positive note, the pumpkin was good along with the greens that were in it.  As for the stir-fry, we ordered it hot, but it wasn't even mild spicy.  The mussels were tough and some of them were gritty.     A server asked if we wanted anything else, and I just asked for the bill, boxes, and some more water.  He brought us boxes and the bill, but forgot the water.  It took a while for him to come back and take the money.  I got boxes for the food because I hate to waste food, but we never ate the left-overs.   Yes the portions are large and the food isn't expensive, but I felt the food wasn't anything special, so I don't get the hype.

Tucked away on a leafy corner of 22nd St., Umai Umai sets the standard for friendly neighborhood BYOBs, Japanese or no.  The small space is nicely but minimally decorated, with an impressively sized flat-screen TV behind the sushi bar that shows a reel of their *actual* menu items with names. My friend and I were in kind of a rush (he had to catch a train) so we asked our server if it was possible to order and eat in about half an hour. She assured us it was no problem, filled up our waters and took our order immediately.  We shared a bowl of steaming-hot edamame sparkling with salt, a plain eel roll, plain salmon roll and two of their "designer roll" creations -- the Pingu and Ping Pong rolls. The fish in each maki was absolutely fresh and clean-tasting -- I especially like the purity of the generous salmon roll.  The fancy rolls were super-creative and like nothing I'd ever had before -- the Pingu was especially pleasing, all loaded with a sweet crab salad atop every piece.  Another nice touch were the size of the fancy rolls -- not only were they generous portions (averaging about $16 each), but the pieces were cut small enough that you didn't have to dislocate your jaw cobra-style to manage the piece in a single bite.   I hate it when you have to mangle maki because they are too big to fit comfortably in your mouth -- these were perfect and appetizing. Service was excellent; speedy because we asked for that, waters always refilled, polite and friendly.  The sushi chef even took time to answer our questions about the rolls were were seeing on-screen and on the counter in front of us. Fun Fact: All tobikko (flying fish roe) -- like the tiny heaps of eggs that dazzlingly adorned Umai's StopLight roll in red, yellow and green -- is dyed.  Chef said it's naturally an opaque, milky gray color that is not very appetizing, so distributors of the product dye it in bright colors.
Great food, classy people and absolutely extraordinary service. This place is a must go while visiting NYC. Madame Freda must be tried if you are not a vegan/vegetarian!

Had a good experience here. Its in a unique location, I can imagine it being much more lively in the summer. The burgers were good, you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. Its a place to try out if you are looking for something different; they have interesting combinations of burgers. The bar is a bit small and could be better but overall I do recomend this place!
Great greasy hoagies for a great price.  A must stop sandwich stop in Princeton, NJ.
The French Onion soup is just amazing. Also my husband raved about the burger. Great lunch spot. Amazing ambiance and good food.

After driving from Westport, CT to Haddonfield, NJ and getting stuck in traffic, I wasn't sure I was up for a trip into the city for a fine dining experience.  How glad I am that I rallied and joined my friends on a Monday night at Osteria. We were lucky enough to be accompanied by a new friend, Rick, who had dined at Osteria before, and he expertly steered us through the menu.  We started with four plates of appetizers: the parma pizza, the summer vegetable crudo, the wood grilled octopus, and a local vegetable antipasto, which was one of the house specials of the evening.  I've had wood grilled octopus before, and Osteria's was very good, if not the best I've tasted.  However, the parma pizza - with mozzarella, fontina, arugula, and prosciutto di parma -  was out-of-this-world amazing!  Definitely order this up for a starter on your next visit.   I enjoyed the chanterelle and bone marrow ravioli with bitto cheese as my entree, and it was the perfect size after all the appetizer courses.  The pasta was exquisite - obviously made in house and simply ethereal - it just melted in my mouth.  I will remember this dish forever.  The restaurant also brought us a treat on the house - a beet ravioli dish that was a close second to my pasta dish.  Nice touch! Everyone else enjoyed their courses - ranging from cannelloni to salmon to roasted suckling pig (a special) - but alas, we did not leave room for a taste of dessert. One final shout-out to our server, who's name escapes me (sorry!), but he was a master of pairing wines with our courses.  Kudos! If I'm ever back in the area (I'm from Atlanta), I would definitely return for more from this inventive chef.
the spaghetti was undercooked. The tomato sauce was tasteless. There were only two shrimps in the dish tho it was called 'seafood pasta'.

I live in the neighborhood and when I saw "Istanbul Lounge" open up I decided to go practically out of pity - because every time I walk by there it's empty. I later find out this is actually Leziz's new location and new name. And the food was, of course, delicious. Service was fast and courteous, the owner stopped by to check in with us after we were served. But let's be real, the food is what makes the place amazing. The way in which they use spices is both mesmerizing and addicting. These people know how to season food. Truly authentic culinary flavors, some subtle and some bold, and just really well balanced. I had the moussaka, definitely recommended. I preferred their old location, but the new place is alright too.
I was very hungry near midnight and I was grateful these guys were open. These do make a nice pizza. Best choice after midnight...
went for brunch. varied crowd, good food, great cocktails.

I love John's. They have the best sandwiches EVER!!!! Plus not to mention, I know everyone that works there, they are very close friends of the family and my aunt works there. Everyone is SO nice!!! There is no better place to get a sandwich (hoagie, chicken cutlet, pork or steak) when you are in Philly!!!!!!

Amazing place! Very busy for breakfast so I recommend calling ahead! I had blueberry pancakes and my family had a sandwich and omelet. All of the food was absolutely delicious! Fun atmosphere and fun people! We went at the very beginning of January and it was nice to get out of the stereotypical New York Times Square hustle and bustle restaurants!

Simply AMAZING. I discovered this gem flipping through the pages of ZAGAT at random and to my surprise became one of my usuals the next 2 years. 1st of all the selection is amazing with over 50 types of pasta that are all deiciously homemade and best of all very cheap! I'm not a pasta fan by all means as I believe most places are overpriced and mediocre but this place is just the opposite in both regards. Service is great as well however the only thing they are stickler about is if someone comes late they will not seat you or that person if you are already seated. House wine and desserts are dirt cheap (5$) as well as tasty (and they fill ur glass to the top!) Favorites include the avocado/lobster pasta and both seafood pastas (love the one with the black noodles!).
Perfect! I had the Slav burger and it's great! However, I ordered it well-done and it's more like medium, not too big of a worry though.
omg. these burgers were SO good.  beer was good too (and cheap)!!

The food, the service and the restaurant itself are outstanding.  Three of us ate here, all eating very different dishes all dishes were excellent.  Beer selection is wide and fit for any lover of a brew.  Wine list is extensive a tad on the expensive side but something for everyone on the list.  Highly recommend.
Everything is great We liked the kc quesdilla nY strip melts in your mouth The surf n turf salad

The Ripper!!! Deep fried hot dogs, they snap in your mouth! They are so shrivled up and yummy! I like mine with cheese and chili! I also get the cheese fries with brown gravy, and pour the rest of the chili onto them! If you take food to go, make sure they triple bag it because the oil will dissolve a paper bag before it even makes its way to your car!! Onion Rings, Hot Dog, Cold Beer, Fries! This is my type of dive! Summers they have antique car shows as well. Lots of fun! Bring Cash!

I am a big critic when it comes to bagels, but holy cow this is one of the best bagels I have ever had (and believe me, I've had A LOT).  The bagel was huge, soft and had amazing flavor. You could tell it was hand rolled. The great part is that it's right up the street from me.  I will be definitely visiting this bagel place going forward.

Living in new york, you know that you have hundreds, if not thousands of options of places to eat, be it brunch,lunch,dinner,apps, whatever. But through out the years, mine personally being 9, no matter what happened, be it the neighborhood changing, me coming and going, leaving the neighborhood, the economy, good times, bad times, one thing stays the same, Oleas food is ALWAYS good, and i always come back for more. Sure, you might have to wait a while to get a seat at 12 in the afternoon on a Sunday, and yes, your host/waiter/server may be a little flustered because theyre serving 30 people all at once for a continuos 8 hours, but in the end, with your belly full of Parmesan french toast or the simple yet delicious smoked salmon plate, you forget that wait ever happen and remember that not only was your food incredibly good, but it was just as good as the last time. When i spend my money on food, i want it to be delicious, satisfying and worth the penny. Every damn time i have eaten at Olea, and mind you, it has been MANY a times, i have been thoroughly satisfied. Whether its the Green Eggs and Lamb( oh man, that merguez!), the Sangria Marinated Hanger Steak tapa with those amazing pickled onions, those Blue point oyster( which, by the way, never even liked oysters until i ate one of those beauties), the Orecchiette, the bacon-wrapped dates, the boquerones, the patatas bravas, oh i could go through the whole menu! All in all, my point is, dont complain about the wait, because in the end, none of that will matter when you realize you have just eaten something, no matter what it is off the menu, that you will not be able to forget. I am a true, die hard fan who will always be coming back until they close those doors on me once and for all.

This is easily one of my favorite places in New York. The fried rice is AMAZING. The Roti of course a must. Besides these two, I don't really have a favorite since my friend and I make it a thing to order something different each time. I see that a lot of people get a soup/noodle dish and that is definitely on my list for the next time. But I def recommend the Roti and the Pineapple fried rice. I LOVE THIS PLACE!

This place has been getting a lot of hype and I can happily say it is much deserved! They are famous for their soft boiled eggs and challah soldiers, which looked delicious to me as people on both sides of me ordered it. But, dear readers, I of course had to try that Israeli delicacy so often botched in this city, the shakshuka. Jack's Wife Freda does a green shakshuka so saucy and subtly flavorful I had to scoop every last drop of chutney up with my spoon. The challah was deliciously fresh baked of course. In addition, the servers were wearing cute striped tops and the owners were gallivanting about, socializing with all the cool customers. I introduced myself on the way out and the owner said "See you tomorrow!" The design is simple and feels very european bistro, with lots of light and outdoor seating. I came in before the lunch rush, but did not feel hurried out by any means as the tables around me filled up. And the prices are totally reasonable and better than most you will find in the area. See you tomorrow, indeed!

I've been here twice, the first time to compare to Geno's and the second time to make sure I didn't just try them on an off day.  Turns out I'm still not a fan. The steak I had both times was super chewy, kind of dry and just not very appetizing IMO.

Um, yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. Just... just go. Things Smarmy and I had here included: scallops, which were tender and delightful and my personal fav the bacon wrapped dates with gorgonzola (whoa mama. in some circles, these are known as Devils on Horseback. who would ever run from this Devil?) pulled pork sliders, which were also super yummy, on tiny light fluffy brioches and at the rec of Mr. Smarmy, we had to get ... the bacon doughnuts. Save room for these sweet little things peppered with salty bacon. we split a bottle of tempranillo -- lots of very affordable options in the under $50 range -- and the waitress was spot on with a recommendation based on what we said we liked. the menu changes all the time, which is a sign of chevery at its best, always wanting to keep pace with new ingredients, what's fresh, what's best available. we ordered a few less than recommended by the waitress to share and it was a perfect fit.

3 star aspects, and 5 star aspects so I settled for 4 My BF and I were craving Pizza the other night and we started to head towards Zavino. Barbuzzo is right next door and we wondered if we should try something new. So we inquired at Barbuzzo. It was very busy when I walked in but I saw two tables available outside so I went to ask the Hostess if we could sit there. I waited nearly 10 minutes for the hostess to come back to her station (that was a three star moment) no servers bothered to stop and say hi or help me or tell me the hostess would be back. When she finally arrived back she was very polite and nice. I asked if we could sit outside, she said absolutely, grabbed two menus and led us out there. The Server: After we were seated outside our server (Cassandra) was right behind us. Greeted us got us water and then explained menu impeccably. She was very friendly and had this super smile (I formed a teeny girl crush on her instantly and wanted to be her friend, she just seemed like one of those awesome people you want be friends with). She took our order we got the pototo pizza, and the margarhita, and a beer (which she recommended based on the pizza we  got) Server def. 5 stars! The Food: The potato pizza was amazing!!! 5 stars! The margherita was 3 stars. The amount of mozzerella was good. Perfect large melted circles. But barely any sauce, it had dried up or evaporated when they baked it or something. So I asked the food runner for a side of sauce and I dipped my pizza. I would come back and try the pizza again and maybe just ask for more sauce.

$6 for a platter of chicken (or lamb or both) & rice, and some greens on the side. The white sauce is the key ingredient. The night crew is very fast which is good because the line can be ridiculously long. Definitely great to eat when trying to sober up, and I think it's good even sober! I've brought a few friends here who have never had it, and I have not met one person who doesn't think it's good.

Can't wait to go back!! I am not one to follow the crowd or believe the hype, but I have to say I was very impressed. The atmosphere was great for a few friends trying to have a good meal. There was something for everyone on the menu. The wine selection you could tell was very well thought out and they even had havsies. My only concern was the service. I did go on a busy Thursday night, but I must say our waitress was a little on the slow side. She also did not seem to be up to par with some of wines on the list. But, I digress, the halibut I had for dinner with an companying sweet pea sauce was delightful. The portions were more than filling. I'm glad to see that chefs are stepping up their game when come to portions, not that I'm glutton but I hate leaving hungry. I would definitely return, and perhaps bring some more friends who also enjoy really good food and wine.

Another one of Mom's favorites that she introduced to me. We would sit outside on the wooden seats and share a cone, trying to see who could stuff her face faster. I like the parmesan peppercorn (which is basically Ranch dressing, so see - I have no depth) which was my ex's favorite sauce, and he can suck it for turning me onto Ranch. Did you know Ranch dressing goes well with EVERYTHING? I could eat this place out of business. I don't get it though - fries & mayo. I've tried to replicate the sauces at home and I can't. They must sprinkle crack in theirs. Gotta get some crack...

Yes, there is fab food south of 9th St in the Slope (and on 6th ave, no less). If you're in the mood for some Italian that goes beyond the usual pasta bolognese, try the Risotto Nero (deliciously creamy squid ink sauce with just-crunchy rice). The Pecoriao salad of shaved Brussels sprouts and almonds was another pleasant discovery. The space is super tiny...only 15 tables, barely room to walk, and absolutely NO room to wait. Which is the only reason I can't give 5 stars. But the food is amazing, and worth walking around the block in the cold until your table frees up!

Came here for Sunday brunch and I experienced a fairy tale brunch experience. I actually came here a while ago and was told that we would have to wait 1.5 hours for a table of two for Saturday brunch. There were so many people outside waiting. We passed and went elsewhere. This time, I made a reservation on OpenTable. Do it! Don't wait hours outside! They called the day before to confirm the reservation. When I went in, I had to wait 5-10 minutes for the table to be ready bit I didn't mind because it's much better than the wait without a reservation. The waitress was really nice and friendly. She provided a bottle of tap water for the table and took our cocktail orders. If you don't want the taste of alcohol in the morning/afternoon, I highly recommend the passion screwdriver. It's delicious! I ordered the Benedict Johnny which is a great plate. The highlight of the plate was the potatoes. Well seasoned and so yummy. I didn't care for the corn pancakes because it was too soggy from the runny egg when I finally got to it. I also tried the Vanilla Bean French Toast which was good, but I wouldn't recommend it for one person to consumer. It is a lot of toast! Get it as a side for your whole party. When we got the bill, they gave us a survey card and a postcard (cute!). The ambience here is great and very comfortable. Hard to describe but it's perfect to catch up with friends while eating great food.

We ate here the other night for my boyfriend's birthday dinner and I was blown away by the food.  This was the perfect setting for an intimate celebratory dinner and I didn't feel like we over-paid, given how amazing our dishes were. We each had cocktails to start.  I enjoyed a wonderful lemon and basil concoction and my love went with some sort of ginger/bourbon drink; both were mixed well and complimented our food (as a side note, I found their cocktail list to be quite impressive and they even have happy hour specials, so I may need to revisit this spot in the future just for drinks).  For apps, we went with the sweet potato pakora and the crispy vegetable chili.  I highly recommend the second of the two, as the batter on the veggies had a delightful crunch and the dipping sauces that came with them packed a nice, spicy punch.     Dinner arrived in a timely manner and I enjoyed my dishes.  I went with tofu mangoli and chana saag.  My beau had the goat biyrani, which was a decent size for him (he took leftovers home).  If I had to complain about anything, I will say that our server wasn't so good at describing the portion sizes to us.  You see, I ordered half sizes of both my dishes.  I love that they even have this option just because most places don't, but it seemed like 2 halves just weren't enough.  I had to end up ordering rice halfway through my dinner.  I know this is a relatively new restaurant here in Philly, so hopefully the wait staff will be able to make better recommendations as time goes on. I thought the menu here was very easy to read for people with dietary restrictions (gluten free and vegan symbols appear next to dishes), but as somebody who is pretty inexperienced with Indian food, it would be nice if there was some kind of spice level number system of sorts so I don't burn my taste buds off.  All in all, though, IndeBlue is doing things right, so I can definitely see myself coming back - especially for their live sitar music on Tuesday nights.

An institution. Impeccable service, great food, great place. I've been going there for 8 years. It's great all the time. Late late night for a burger, a sleepy Saturday afternoon, an energetic Sunday brunch, or a quiet weekday evening.

We ordered the eggs benedict and the blueberry pancakes, of course.  The eggs benedict was one of the best that we've had in NYC.  The green onions added a nice blast of flavor to the already tasty dish.  We were prepared to be disappointed by the possibly over-hyped blueberry pancakes, but they did not fail.  These are the best blueberry pancakes that I have ever tasted.  A must try! Minus one star for the staff.  Also, ordering take-out takes just as long as waiting for a table, although it may be that the staff was too overwhelmed to remember the number of take-out orders sitting near the kitchen for a good 20-30 minutes.  We ended up waiting for our take-out order for about an hour.

My first five star review because not only is the food great ...the service is really friendly . Turned up with no reservations ...but they got us a nice table...fish tacos ..the ox tail app .to die for .and a cocktail aptly named Hemingway.

I've had nothing but awesome experiences here! Whether takeout or eat in, Vietnam Cafe is delicious, and inexpensive. Eating in, I've been there on  a date, or with a friend who has young kids, and the atmosphere was fine both ways. As for service, they were on top of everything. I also have a lot of food allergies, and they were super accommodating. If you dine here, you won't regret it!
Very good food.  Well prepared with a good menu.  Service was excellent, as well.

Its a great place that has clearly ironed out what must have been some earlier kinks along the learning curve. It was busy today but the service was efficient, and a sample was graciously offered to someone who inquired about an item. Hand assembled delicious and fresh food is naturally going to have some prep time. If you want a really fast pre-made not very good sandwich you might as well go elsewhere. If you want thoughtful and delicious food made by people that show that they care about what they are doing, then eat here.

Absolutely THE WORST...ordered a pie for delivery, not only did they send the incorrect order for a pie, but when it came it was cold burnt and not even Sicilian. They charged us almost $20 for a pie that was terrible and not what we ordered. When we called to advise them not even an apology. Absolutely ridiculous and when we called back for a second time the manager had an attitude

Very impressed with this new coffee house.  Very friendly and attentive staff, a variety of different fresh sandwiches, and the coffee is also very good.  Small inside, but cozy. Hard to find a spot like this in my area.  I will definitely be back.

I had high hopes for North End Grill as I've eaten at a bunch of Danny Meyer's restaurants which have a great combination of  stellar food, great atmosphere and top notch service. When I first arrived on a cold winter night the host did not offer to take my coat - for a high end restaurant this should have been a no brainer from the front of house. When I tried to order the lobster, my waitress told us they were sold out of it. I found that strange as we came in at 9 PM and any good restaurant shouldn't be sold out of a popular dish at that seating on a Saturday night.  I ordered the scallops with a shared side of brussel sprouts and was quite pleased and satiated. After dinner I took a quick trip to the ladies, and upon walking back to my table I saw 2 tables who were seated AFTER us and had the lobster as their main course! Shock and appalled that I was treated differently from 2 other tables, my husband and I asked the waitress what happened and why WE weren't served the lobster. She was embarrassed and apologetic about the "mix up" in the kitchen -- apparently that customer demanded that they search for a lobster for him and they "happened to have just one more".  She saw that we were upset and the manager came and comped us with dessert and drinks.  I was shocked that this happened. In short, North End Grill's food and especially the cocktails are great - the service still needs some fine tuning.  Not sure if I will go back.

Haiku: So the little owl... Small space, romantic, cozy Extensive wine list Had reservation Still waited fifteen minutes Coat rack fell on me :( But! Food was SO good Scallops would make Ramsey proud Entree worth the wait Sherry vinaigrette Absolutely amazing Made the market greens Would come back again Must try pork chops, sliders and Spicy brussel sprouts!

Awesome place to eat. They have been featured on Food Network for their fried burgers, which were awesome, but we had the best mussels we've ever had there too, along with awesome pulled-pork filled perogies. Cozy & off the beaten path, this place is a gem. It was not crowded, locals only in there. Staff was friendly, attentive and excited about the food. They grow and make their own everything, all organic ingredients. Bathroom was clean too, an added bonus!

Definitely one of the best pizzerias in New York. Their pizza is quite different from what you get at Grimaldi's or Lombardi's. Di Fara has a bit less tomato sauce, and the mozzarella cheese is not quite as good as Grimaldi's. But Dom really likes to go crazy with the olive oil and basil, which I enjoy a lot. The best way I would describe the difference is that Grimaldi's and Lombardi's are more hearty while Di Fara has a more sharp, flavorful taste. The way the flavors come together is better than any other pizza place I have ever been to. Some might balk at the prices. The price for a regular pie is $28, but remember that tax is included and no tip is expected (you pick up your pizza at a counter). So it's really more like $22 on a menu. I got a classic pie (sausage, mushrooms, onions, peppers) for $32, or $25 equivalent. Grimaldi's and Lombardi's large pizzas with four toppings would be $22 ($14 + $2 per topping) and $32.50 ($20.50 + $3 per topping), so the price isn't actually that bad. I would normally give this 4.5 stars, but I'm knocking off half a star for deficiencies in communication. In this day and age, everything is increasingly electronic, but sometimes you want a specific question answered in real time, so it is helpful for a business to have a working phone. Unfortunately, if you call them, there is a very good chance they will not pick up the phone. Their email address, info@difara.com, also does not work. I wanted to find out what day they were least busy, when was the latest I could show up and still be served, etc. In the end, at 6:30 PM on Wednesday I decided to make the 45-minute excursion from Manhattan to Brooklyn without any knowledge of whether I'd make it on time. Of course, when I got there, I got all the answers to my questions. For your benefit, I am sharing it here, because there is pretty much no other way for you to find out: 1. The lady who works there on Wednesdays always tries to pick up the phone. She also works on some Fridays. If they do pick up the phone, you can place a phone order ahead of time to save some of the wait. 2. The listed 8:30 PM closing time is the last time they will accept an order. So they might stay open until 10 PM (or whenever they finish making the pies) if necessary. However, there is a possibility they could run out of dough, so placing orders before 8 PM is recommended. 3. There is essentially no line for ordering, though this is only reflective of this particular Wednesday night at 7:15 PM; your experiences may differ. You go up to the counter, place your order, and she writes it down on a legal pad. 4. The main waiting time is for your pizza. During this time, you are free to wander around the area (and visit all the kosher shops), because your place in line is held on the pad. What I've noticed is that almost everyone is quoted a 20-minute wait time (including me), but it took about 90 minutes for my pizza to come out.

Was looking forward to trying this place for brunch, but was disappointed when they were out of the two meals I was looking forward to trying. Came with a friend who was a vegetarian and they were not amenable to making substitutions of the menu to meet their dietary needs until much persuasion. Stumptown coffee was great, but we ended up leaving to find a better-stocked kitchen. May consider trying this place again when they have a liquor license.

Sad to say that I haven't been back in a few weeks... Great pizza! Great atmosphere! Great drinks! Need I say more??? I go specifically for the Gluten Free pizza and it's great! The staff is always pleasant. There never seems to be a manager around and I often see staff sitting at the bar or hanging around. But the food, drinks and local consciousness make up for it! Worth trying!

Great little restaurant! We had a beef rib stew and it was wonderful(for those who enjoys spicy food like me...) The free appetizers are also good. If was not cheap but definately worth the price. We came in around 6 pm on Sunday without waiting but when we were done at about 7pm there were a whole bunch of people waiting for the table ...

After last night's dinner, I couldn't resist to log on and share my thoughts about this already much hyped grail of a seafood bar. It was the eve of my girlfriend's birthday, and my options were to either surprise her, or take her to City Crab (she had been there a while ago, when it was "good"). So like a good monkey I did some brief yelping and found this joint. The place looked really casual in the user submitted photos, which made me a little unsure about going there for a birthday dinner. Anyway, I decided to trust myself on this one, and I'm glad I did. We got to the place around 9, well after the happy hour crowd. We were told by the host that a table would be free in 30. I asked him about a bar we could go to for a pint before dinner and received a prompt response, which I admire. So, we hopped across the street to a local dive and after 10 minutes I got a text that our table was ready. We finished our beer and headed back over. I immediately felt wrong about having doubted the decor and ambiance. It has that feelgood, ambiguous vibe that's appropriate for couples and small groups alike, loud or quiet, black-clad or casual. We had a dozen oysters, half of which were delicious meaty blue points, followed by crab cakes and scallops on risotto. Everything was perfect. This review is getting long winded, and since everything has been raved about before, let this be an echo to all the 5 star experiences out there. The manager came over to chat for a little bit and was very eager to make sure we were having a good time. He was a really cool dude, and at the end of our meal we received a few slices of their famed whiskey cake and two flutes of prosecco. Cherry on the cake, metaphorically. PS. That whiskey cake is f*cking delicious.

Terrific Place and was treated by the staff and Manager as if they really appreciated our business. Great Food and Great Service not to mention Generous Portions and well-priced.  I will be returning again!

The day I went I tried checking in and yelp kept telling me I could not check in because I was too far as I sat inside! This was weird.  I just recently became a vegetarian and was told about this place from a girl that works at the Sweet Avenue Bake Shop in East Rutherford NJ.  We were very excited to try this place because as newbies we felt that our choices for eating out were not that many.  I have to say that everything we had was great!! We had spring rolls and the scallion pancakes deluxe for appetizers.  I had the sesame chicken with vegetable fried rice and it was so good.  The waiter noticed we were inhaling our food and actually told us to take it easy :)  I guess we were eating like there was no tomorrow. I can't wait to go back.

Sit at the bar. The bartenders are friendly and let you taste-before-you-select the handful of crafts beers on tap. Oyster selection is great, and the atmosphere is cozy. Look to have one of the homemade desserts at the end of your meal.

I walked in to ask how long the wait was, The man working there told me to get out. From the big homing I thought the service was bad. Then, I thought they were trying to do their job. We then got seated and did not receive a greeting from our waiter. He told us " are you ready to order" we had replied to let us know if he can give us a minute. He seemed so rude from the beginning. After finally choosing what we wanted to order, the waiter did not come back for another 20 mins. He did not ask if we wanted more drinks instead he just took our cups. It seemed as if all they were interested in was getting their customers out as quickly as possible. Honestly, the pizza was good after a 45-60 min wait, but the service was horrible. We came from Los angels to try this pizza and like I said, the food was good, but their service was horrible. If you're from California, please wait and go visit the el Segundo location. In conclusion, you can get some pizza from next door. They serve beer and you'll be as happy. You won't have to wait as much and you'll be off to explore the city a lot quicker and happier.

Amada is apparently very popular. At 8:30 on a Tuesday evening, there was a 40 minute wait for seats in the bar area. Luckily, there's a bar in the bar area; bars are good for drinking, and drinking is good for waiting. It is also quite charming; I took my girlfriend to here for the most romantic of dates. When we arrived, I leaned in, and whispered in her ear, "Bitch, you wait here, I've gotta take a squirt." She also needed to use the facilities, and followed me towards the back. As we worked our way past the packed bar, we found ourselves in a long hallway lit only by intermittent candles. A Labyrinth of Passion, if you will, which also happens to be one of the [laughably named] signature cocktails.* "This is a very romantic hallway," she smiled seductively, "It makes me want to..." "What? Eat? Are you hungry? Why are you looking at me like that? Are you gassy again?" I never did find out why she was looking at me like that, but our meal ended up strangely silent, and was punctuated by angry glares from her. Luckily, the food kept us occupied. We both enjoyed the crab-stuffed peppers that came highly recommended, as well as the shortrib flatbread and the cheese plate. I was less enamored with the unimpressive mushroom rice recommended by a friend we made in the bar. He was a vegetarian though; I should've known he couldn't be trusted. All in all, a slightly pricey spot with good tapas and better atmosphere. __________ *Talk to Her? Broken Hugs? All I know is that I couldn't order a Law of Desire and respect myself in the morning, so I got myself a Matador. Because nothing says "macho" like drinking in a strong, Spanish man. (On the real, I enjoyed the bourbon, elderflower and ginger concoction.)
Everything is good here!  Lasagna great, cheesesteak great, grilled chicken caesar salad great and the buffalo wings are to die for!!!

Really enjoyable. Delicious food, good service, a photobooth, and fabulous company. Came here with a party of 7. My darling BFF miscalculated how many people we had and accidentally made the reservation for 6. The hostess was really nice about it and they gave us a nice table by the window. After so many reviews mentioned it, I really wanted to try the beer-battered string beans, so we started with that and the bacon wrapped apricot. According to others (not a bacon eater), the apricot was just alright but not wow-inducing. Apparently it had garlic, which was unnecessary, since the bacon added the saltiness it needed. The string beans, however, were addictive. The ranch dressing was the perfect compliment to the fried yumminess. For the entree, I ordered the Roasted Chicken Salad, which I thought would be chicken salad on top of greens, but was a salad with roasted chicken. It was better than mayo-y chicken salad. It had walnuts, apples, brie, and caramelized onions. The chicken was moist and fresh. The onions seemed a bit out of place but they still worked. The two girls that ordered the flounder both loved it, and the burgers were good, not too greasy, and came with shoestring fries. The prices were reasonable (especially in NYC), and overall a great spot.

i wish i could describe my delight for this place with like some kind of animalistic-like sounds of joy and pleasure because plain words won't suffice. wait, you want big ass fluffy divine vegan pancakes at 10pm on a weekday?? oh, and like maybe tofu benedict too? oh wait, and maybe a scramble and some sausage and some french toast?? they got em! they got em all!! in a cute little retro diner like setting with 50s music playing! wtf, why haven't i been here until now? i don't care if i have to wait for 2 hours to get a table (the place is not huge fyi) and if they the service is minimal (which it's not, i must point it, contrary to what one review said -- at least not in my experience), they could throw the plate on the table for all i care. i don't care!! look at all this food!! this divine freaking vegan breakfast food, served all frigging day long!! [they also have veggie burgers, sammies, salads]. argh, i'm so excited!!

This place is dope. I got to eat with my hands and wear a plastic bib with a lobster on it. I went with a group of friends and we got mad nasty with the food. We ordered one of each combo and tore through em like Godzilla set loose on Tokyo. Everything had that super Cajun flavor that popped in your mouth. We also tried their Mac n cheese, BBQ shrimps, and crab cake. Those were OK. The Cajun shrimp was better than the BBQ shrimp and the crab cake was a little mushy.

Rachel is the absolute best. I'd recently switched to a vegan diet, so thought it would be a good idea to order Rachel's vegan dinner so that I'd only need to warm it once I got home as I continue to learn what I do and do not like about vegan food. My first ordered I got the BBQ Seitan with "mac and cheese" and brussel sprouts. I loved everything but I wasn't a huge fan of the mac but as I explained to Rachel, that's person based on the fact that I haven't found a mock cheese that I like to date vs it simply not being good. Rachel let me know that I can tell her about  the things I enjoy or do not enjoy so that she can customize my order. Also when I first emailed Rachel my order I happened to mention I was eating a vegan diet to focus on eating healthier and also currently seeking to lose weight. So she included an estimation of calories and WW points for me! Great personality, wonderful food, delivers to me what more could I ask for?

We stopped by here the other night for the first time and were pretty happy with the experience. The food is ok for the area (though not an authentic Asian food experience). I had the cashew chicken and it was tasty, although a bit heavy on the sauce. My boyfriend's General Tsao's chicken wasn't really very good though. There was plenty of seating and attentive waiters, so we'll be going back there, but still looking for a true Asian food experience.

We went here on opening night and had such a good time. I had a perfectly cooked sea bream fillet with rock shrimp hash. We had a dozen oysters, well fleets and bluepoints, that were expertly shucked. We had so much fun we went back last night and had another great meal. We're so glad Oyster House is back!

FYI the restaurant does NOT accept credit cards! CASH ONLY! Having checked the Yelp profile before I left and there it is stated that the restaurant does accept cards. Please someone update their profile on Yelp. BTW there is an ATM machine at the back for one's convenience i.e. for an additional fee. Salad: The signature salad was pretty interesting, great fresh ingredients, but they were a bit stingy on the vinaigrette. Main: Steak the meat was excellent in taste, asked for it rare but got bleu instead but it was still fantastic. Unfortunately this should have been served with home fries as a side not a salad. Desert: Flourless chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream, the cake was cold but tasty, ice cream was average, nothing to write home about. Service: Excellent, the servers knew the specials and gave additional information which is always a plus. All in all it was a pretty decent meal, it got there but failed to impress.
This is my favorite slider spot of all time! Love this little hole in the wall for late night snacking!! A++++ Love this place!
