While visiting my cousin who lives in Staten Island, he suggested we try John's Famous Deli because "they have the best roast beef sandwiches in New York".  I am not a big roast beef fan, but i'm always open to trying something new, so why not.   The deli is small, and not the most attractive place, but one thing that stands out when entering is the big hunk of cooked roast beef (not cold cut style) on the slicer. The options for ordering a roasting beef sandwich are in roll or hero form - I opted for the roll.  I don't believe you have much options for the sandwich but it comes with onions and fresh mozzarella and then they put the sandwich back in the oven to melt the cheese.   The final topping and probably the most important ingredient is the sauce they put on in the end. When you look at the sauce in the pan and the guy behind the counter scooping it up, it really looks like tar or a pot of italian coffee..... What to expect when eating the sandwich - the meat is tender, the taste is flavorful and the sauce is awesome....   You gotta try this place! I believe they have 3 locations and 2 of which that are in Brooklyn.
This place is DELICIOUS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  Grew up eating here, and it's one of the things I miss about not living in East Windsor anymore.

If you get to The Pig before 7:00 you will probably not wait more than 1 hour.  It's worth wait.   The Spotted Pig has one of the best combinations of world class food, great/intimate atmosphere, and a fun/sceney vibe.  Weekdays in the winter are particularly intimate as it is usually just locals.  Weekends can get pretty crazy and packed so plan accordingly. As to what to get: Devils on Horseback are not to be missed.  The Gnudi should be illegal, and the Cheese Burger is the best in NYC IMO.  I'm also a huge fan of the Chappellett Merlot.  I seldom drink Merlot but this wine is worth checking out.   Also, for you beer drinkers, the Speckled Hen Ale is the real deal.
I came over here three times about last week. Just too good to forget. I have to say it's the BEST ramen I ever had. Try it out u will figure out :)
Great food but a little pricey. Also service was a little slow to come around. Overall great place and great atmosphere.

My colleague and I went here for dinner as it is in a great location in Center City. We got there around 7:30 last Sunday. Only a few other diners in there, we got a great seat in the bar area (fun chairs!). The atmosphere is sort of modern, nice lighting (color-changing backlit bar), and intimate... would be a great place for a date. We had wontons as an app, and Green Curry and Chicken Chow Fun as our mains. All were delicious, the consistency of the curry was perfect. I love red and green curry and I feel like it is so hard to find the perfect version.  I crave this, and wish I had a place like this in my hometown. All was delicious, down to the drinks.  I forget which cocktail I had, some sort of ginger martini... 2 of those and I was a happy lady :-)  The service did not disappoint, which I saw was a common complaint on here.  Perhaps because it was not super busy? Our server was perfectly attentive and friendly, even trying to fix the slight wobble in our table without being asked. If you are looking for some great Thai, nice atmosphere in this area, I'd definitely say to give it a shot. The value was great and we were both pleased.
Love this place. The food and cozy atmosphere make it my go to spot

Best udon in town! Not sure I was too hungry when I went but the noodles were absolutely delicious! The texture had a nice bounce and the soup was tasty. Was really thirsty after the meal so there may be MSG which would be disappointing.

Been here multiple times for dinner, mostly with big groups. The food has been consistently amazing. There aren't many options on the menu, which consists of pizza (with choice of toppings, of course) and salad, but that's all you really need here. Plus some great beer. Personally, I'm a fan of the amber ale, although the blond is great, too. The dining experience is really chill - paper plates, a cup filled with silverware, a communal salad bowl, and a huge rectangular pan of pizza. I've never had anything but good service, both for dinner and at the bar. No complaints. Although I did bring a visiting friend here for dinner, and she was somewhat underwhelmed. Maybe I hyped it too much, or maybe New Haven style pizza wasn't for her.
This place was fantastic. The price were cheap, the food was excellent, and the service was nice. The green special sauce I could drink from the bottle!
Yay! Great food and drinks! I can't wait to come back. My only complaint is that my sandwich was a little dry. I wish there were more sauce. Everything else was awesome.
Really tasty and awesome service.  A great BYOB spot!!   The spring rolls were perfect!  The menu is small but the flavors of Thai food are well represented so you'll find something yummy I'm sure!

Inexpensive meal with a below average beer selection and attentive service. The ribs are not real deal BBQ. They are obviously parboiled prior to whatever cooking technique they use to finish them. While they lack that true flavor they are well seasoned and fall off the bone tender. The bar food is pretty good, especially their onion rings. It's a nice local establishment where many an off duty cop or fireman hang out, where you can get some inexpensive eats that are just about good enough.

This may be my favorite restaurant, I've been here maybe 3 dozen times since discovering it within the past year. I've had pretty much everything on the menu and lots of other things that go on and off the constantly changing daily specials... My favorite things are "large grilled mackerel" (which is insanely delicious), "squid legs in spicy guts sauce" "fried chicken gizzards" "fried sea eel" "spicy cod roe fritters" (which are now, unfortunately off the menu) "spinach and bacon salad" (which now, REALLY unfortunately, is off the menu) "pork and wasabi shumai" "lamb chops yakitori" and "beef liver sashimi." I LOVE THIS PLACE... the beer is always cold and fresh, really affordable... the shochu is priced VERY well... the service is super-friendly... this place feels really authentic, and I always have a good time here.

Delicious Pizza!!  Tried them out via Seamlessweb and not only did we get fast delivery on a Friday night, but amazingly good pizza and at a great price.  We got a large Quattro Stagioni Pizza which is topped with mozzarella, artichokes, black olives, prosciutto cotto, mushrooms and fresh basil!  I also added for $3 more, pepperoni.   Brick oven pizza goodness! The crust on this pizza is fantastic and the ingredients were extremely fresh.  This would probably be a five star pizza had they distributed the ingredients evenly.  Actually, it was pretty poorly done.  Jim had about 2 slices before he realized that the pizza had olives.  I didn't order half and half but yet only one side of the pizza had pepperoni and artichokes and one side had mushrooms and prosciutto.  They really missed the mark there.  Other than that, I would highly recommend giving their pizza a try. Their other items on the menu also look fantastic so, I am looking forward to trying things on their menu other than the pizza.  I plan to be a regular customer.
When I desire balls made of meat, I go here. 'nuff said.

Consistently voted the best pizza in NY - it lived up to the hype.  We trekked over to Brooklyn to try a pie, and I loved the thin crust, chewy-ness of their pizza - perfect balance of crust, sauce, and cheese.  Very casual environment - the tables are smushed together.  Not much in terms of ambience, but you won't care because you will be too busy stuffing your face with food.  Awesome and worth the trip there!
Came for brunch and it totally rocked. I cannot wait to come back. Food was stellar, dessert was STOOOPID good, and the service was outstanding. No need for a detailed review. Just go!

Before I moved further West I was a regular client at Desi Chaat living just 1 block away (I'd eat their food 3-5 times a week). Chaat became an obsession of mine. Nowadays I live right next to Mood Cafe and it has become a local favorite of mine (for good reason). The owner, Hassan, is a good man who aims to please and has never once lets me down. I often stop by after class not bothering to look at the menu and always asking about any new creations or concoctions as I love to explore and try new tastes and flavors. Fair warning, there is no kitchen on premises so don't expect the meals to be made in front of you from scratch and magically served within minutes. I love and recommend the samosas (with all the fixings on them) and I always ask for a nice kick of a spice. Hassan often tells new clients of his money back guarantee if your not pleased but I have yet to see anyone take him up on it. What I really love about Mood Cafe and why I happily give it 5 stars is because of the menu; it isn't stale or rigid, rather more of work of art, dynamic and ever-evolving. The other reason is because it's one of the few places that takes me serious when I say I want "back home" spicy spicy, NOT white man spicy ;-). hehehe

This was a heck of a meal. 2 friends and I sat at the bar and ordered several things to try. The portions were great for this plan. Over the course of the meal we had the oysters, crab, rabbit, cappelletti, and hangar steak. The least favorite being the crab. Everything else was agreed upon to be superb. If looking for a fancy meal in Rittenhouse you should go here.

This place hit the spot. I've been on a noodle kick recently and after the last Yelp Event, it was a pleasure to be able to walk in, get a seat and warm up. I think the broth is wonderful, but for some it may be a bit too salty. I was happy. The food is beautifully presented.  And I left full and smiling. The place is small so go early but not too early , like candice says, it takes time to get the food right.

My husband and I visited Becco for our anniversary dinner. The service was excellent and the food was very good. It is a very busy restaurant, loud and crowded. If you don't like that, don't go but other than that it was good.

Artichoke Pizza is a must if you are a pizza connoisseur. Why? These are are the reasons: 1. There are only a few options and each one is more delicious than the other. My favorite is Margarita and the Artichoke. 2. It is cash only as far as I know of. 3. It is simple, you order your slice and go. 4. There is the occasional stuffed Artichoke or rice ball. I like both. Very tasty. 5. They are very large slices. Yes, there is a plethora of $1 pizza shops around the block and they are very good as well but if you want a treat, Artichoke is your choice.

Great for a healthy grab and go in the village! Love their falafel sandwiches and plates. Great pita, three kinds of falafel, fast service. It's a very small space with a few seats at a window counter and one bench out front so definitely have a plan B of where to eat.
The wait was about 20min, it was worth the wait. Our food came in about 5min and most of the time I'm a little reluctant when my food arrives so quickly, but in this case the food was AWESOME!

Swung by here for a bite last night and was more than pleasantly surprised! The linguine with the marinara - YUM! A perfect balance of plum tomato, garlic and basil with a hint of olive oil. So simple, so tasty! My dining partner had the Veal Marsala which he enjoyed to the last bite (but says mine was better!) The tiramisu was nice as was the simple house Chianti. Atmosphere? Quiet and attentive staff without being rushed.

Print is a farm-to-table dining experience...enough said.  As Julia Child once said "You don't have to cook fancy or complicated masterpieces - just good food from fresh ingredients."   Print offers this as well as great execution, quality service and trendy decor!   ***Highly Recommend*** Six Wellfleet oysters on the half shell, champagne mignonette - BEST EVER! So good, I've thought about them at least once a day. Grilled octopus, potatoes, chorizo, olives, herb puree, lemon...YUM Print is located inside Ink48 hotel.  After dinner, go to the rooftop bar.  BEST views of NYC!!

There is a pizza joint on every corner in Hamilton so competition is tough. I've tried many of them in the 8yrs or so that I've lived here. Tonight was my first time trying Mamma Rosa's and I gave it a try based on the great reviews on YELP. Mamma Rosa's is one of the best places in town to get a pizza AND THEY DELIVER!!! We ordered a large tomato pie with extra cheese tonight for delivery. It arrived in less than 45-min. It had a lot of cheese, which I like, err, make that LOVE, and was just a really good tasting pie. The dough was mushy for my taste, not crispy as I was expecting, so I ate the edge of the crust with all the cheese piled on that. The pie was room temp when it arrived. So, it defiantely could have been hotter and the dough crisper. That said, it was still a really good pie... the secret may be in the quality of the cheese and the sauce. We also ordered BBQ buffalo wings and fried calamari. The calamari was average. As for the wings, I could not bring myself to try them. They looked under cooked to me. I admit that I am fussy about my food. The delivery guy was nice. I will definately order from Mamma Rosa again.

My friend has been bugging me to go and try this place out for months!  I finally did.  I went on a Sunday night and only waited for 15mins to get in.  Judging by all the previous reviews on Yelp, I had it easy. Simply put, the corn is absolutely the best corn I've ever had.  That said, a corn is a corn.  That said again, you HAVE TO order it if you're there.  If you're a fan of spiciness and heat, then try it with the green hot sauce they have there.  So much flavour and soooo HOT!  Guaranteed to give you a kick and wake your senses! For main, we had the grilled steak and the grilled pork chop.  Both were delicious and well made, but not really to-die-for.  For dessert we shared a coconut flan. In a word, for the price, you really can't ask for anything better than this.  I will definitely visit again on a night when there isn't a 30min+ wait.
I love this place!

Finally got to have dinner here last night. It was raining and we needed to have an early dinner to catch a movie. Rolled in a 6:15 and were seated immediately The place was pretty full for that time and the staff was VERY friendly. Very cozy place and a beautiful spot both location & ambiance. The food was very good, simple and tasty. We had: Starter - Duck Breast w/ arugula, parmesan, almonds & truffle Main - Crispy Chicken w/ asparagus home fries, lemon sherry & dijon Main - Pork Chop w/ parmesan butter beans and wild dandelion We skipped dessert. I would go back again and again. Brunch next time!

I have been coming to this Brio location with my boyfriend and our friends since about a year ago. I have enjoyed the food here up until this summer and am not sure what has happened to the kitchen and/or management, my experience here has exponentially decreased, especially during recent visits. I have also noticed a significant decrease in patrons during dinner hours lately. This review is based on my most recent meal here: My friend had her birthday dinner here on a Saturday and I had ordered the pasta pesto, I have gotten this dish here before and was really satisfied with it, having wanted something light for dinner, I opted for it again. The description of this dish on the menu reads - angel hair, grilled chicken, caramelized onions, tomatoes, roasted peppers, feta, basil, light pesto sauce. Now when one hears the word "pesto" one would assume that the sauce is made from mainly basil, pine nuts, and garlic and is green in color. However, what I got was a dish with angel hair pasta tossed in what tasted like a light garlic and butter sauce, tomatoes, grilled chicken, and some baby spinach leaves messily arranged on a plate, without the slightest hint of pesto. I am not a fan of sending back dishes but I did question the waiter, the answer I got was that there is a "very light" pesto sauce in the dish. This newly defined pasta pesto had zero flavor - the sauce was under-seasoned, the chicken was dry, and the pasta was overcooked. A friend got the same dish and was equally disappointed. My boyfriend usually gets the pasta fra diavolo with chicken and a side of asparagus. The asparagus he has gotten in the past have been grilled perfectly and sprinkled with parmesan cheese, this time the asparagus looked like it was steamed or blanched with no evidence of seasoning, when it was sent back and brought out again, they looked like they were just mindlessly charred. I don't think I have ever seen him not finish a plate of asparagus. There were 8 of us and we were surprised that gratuity was not included in our check. One of my friends found out 2 days later that he was charged $284 on his card even though his receipt read $65, when going back and forth with a manger about it he was told that the $284 was just a pending charge and the correct amount would go through the next day, smells fishy if you ask me. The spinach artichoke dip was the only thing I had that didn't disappoint, otherwise I would have given Brio 1 star. I will not be returning.

I guess this place just came under different ownership / management, as when we visited tonight they said they'd only been open 2 weeks, and I see reviews here from a while ago. First things first: This will most definitely be becoming one of our 'date night' special places. We have a couple of them - 26 Seats in Alphabet City, and Northeast Kingdom in Bushwick - but tonight's meal may have surpassed both. To start we shared the grilled haloumi appetizer which came with gorgeous fresh spring greens, the perfect thing to eat haloumi with. I had mackerel from the grill, which I was happily surprised to discover came whole, cooked perfectly with a fabulously buttery brown sugery (though not over-sweet) oil. Brought me straight back to catching and cooking my own mackerel as a girl off the coast of Ireland. Hubby had salmon steak, which came with a f*ck load of garlic on top, but somehow didn't overwhelm it. It was, like mine, melt-in-the-mouth and nyomnyomnyom. Our sides were both yummy - a mashed potato with truffle oil I will be dreaming about, and spinach gratin. We washed it all down with the sparkling Brooklynbrusco - on tap - which I didn't immediately like but which grew on me. Solid beer and wine menu. Great service, lovely folk, good music which ranged from jazzy stuff to Led Zeppelin at one point. Relaxed, unpretentious (yes! in Williamsburg!) but with enough class to feel special enough for one of our rare date night's out. Highly recommend it. We'll be back again.

Took my in-laws here for birthday and they absolutely agreed with everything I said it my first review.  They even dared to say that it was the best Italian meal they've ever had.  Service was even more impeccable then the first time around.  I don't know how they do it, but this is definitely my favorite restaurant in foody Philly!
Had the most delicious meal here.  Great ambiance, great service, delicious food.  Highly recommend the falafel (cube shape for more crunchy surface area!) & the roasted brussel sprouts.

Despite giving three-point-five stars (indicated as four), I actually love this place for its heart, concept and conveniently adventurous commute. First thing you gotta know is Enoteca only takes cash, and it's on Staten Island, a few blocks up from the Island's terminal of New York's free ferry (taking you on a harbor jaunt that serves glorious views of the Verrazano and Statue of Liberty).  What a novel concept:  seasonal, local food prepared by an Italian [Nonna] Grandma who will be rotated out of and back into the kitchen's weekly schedule. My grandmother, may She rest in peace, was from Calabria.  She put molto love and tradition into her food but, like our given Nonna at Enoteca, couldn't be bothered with the little things that trouble me as a cook or guest of cook (i.e. selecting perfect cuts, removing gristle, tenderizing intricacies, etc.).  I understand these challenges may be better addressed with other Nonnas on duty.  Outside the two most expensive meat items on our bill, all food was SUPERB. I will return with friends from out of town, so we can descend to the bottom of downtown, onto the free ferry and hike up two blocks to ENOTECA.  The service was lovely and warm.  They stay open as long as they're moving product, sometimes til 1 a.m. Categorically recommended.  Lots of drinkable, quality wine.

Been dying to go here for a while, and finally stopped by with a group of friends after work for one the "loca tuesdays" happy hour--- Half off appetizers, and drinks!! Started off with a passion fruit mojito, coconut mojito, and mango mojito-- passion fruit was my favorite. Beware these mojitos are strong, it's probably like 95% rum and 5% syrup-- but I guess you get more bang for your buck. We sampled a bunch of tapas: these were our favorites: 1) Favorite: Croquetas de cangrejo- these cakes were so nice and fresh, and they crumbled apart in your mouth- and it went really well with the mango-jalapeno salsa. These were gone in seconds. 2) Platano relleno- really big fan of savory and sweet dishes, and this dish did not disappoint. One huge slab of sweet plantain stuffed with pulled pork- 3) expresso bbq costillitas-- didn't really taste the coffee flavor, but these ribs were sweet and the meat was falling right off the bone. 4) Calamari---- the calamari was crunchy and standard, but the sauce makes this dish shine-- caper Aioli-- we practically drank the sauce, it was so good. 5) arepa con carne--- presentation was beautiful and the dish was great as well-- corn cakes with shredded beef on top 6) Mussels- huge appetizer- accompanied  with some delicious crusty bread these were not so great: 7) Shrimp skewers- the dish sounded pretty fancy, but overall it wasn't that flavorful 8) Fish croquettes- honestly it tasted like fish sticks - but the dipping sauce was good- it was passion fruit and chipotle dip. 8) The beef tacos- tacos were burnt, the beef had absolutely no flavor, just slabs of meat Overall, it was an enjoyable experience, and I want to come back here next time and sample more dishes  such as the empanadas, the fish tacos,  ceviche, and  try the sangria

The Strawberry Cheesecake was not impressive and tasted artificial. The Pineapple Cheesecake on the other hand was incredible and really good!!! I'm dumbfounded as to why the topping could make such a big difference in taste but I made sure to go back TWICE for the Pineapple Cheesecake during my recent visit.
The best seafood I've had in NYC! Annoying wait and small space but the food is not to be missed. Hits the spot when it comes to seafood cravings. I need to go back ASAP!

Note:  This review is only for desserts! Arrived at this cute little Japanese restaurant around 10 pm for dessert.  It's a hidden gem on the second story of a building with a narrow staircase leading up to it. My boyfriend ordered the green team cake roll with sake ice cream, and I ordered some kind of strawberry layered ice cream. We ended up waiting for about 15- 20 min for our dessert to arrive, ands to our surprise, our waitress brought out our desserts, along with two macaroons and a pot of tea to apologize for the delay. Such good customer service, and we didn't even complain about the wait!  The dessert presentation was extremely cute, and tasted really good without being o erwhelmingly sweet. Macaroons with soft and lightly flaky on the outside, and the tea was very flavorful. Sake ice cream was extremely unique. Will definitely come here again on my next visit to NYC!

I used to live in Princeton and was really looking forward to pancakes at PJ's when i went back there on business.  I ordered the classic pancakes and they were just ok and a little soggy. It took forever to get service and it wasn't particularly friendly. and no respectable pancake place serves corn syrup.  You have to pay an extra $2.50 for real maple syrup to already overpriced average pancakes. Too bad because they used to be my favorite.

Love freedom as love this country I am not an American but here for two years loving their food habit. This restaurants accelerated my fan of this country. Delicious and healthy food for so easy price here. Thanks.............

I was very impressed but a little overwhelmed on my first trip to the Chelsea Market. The Green Table caught my eye and turned out to be the perfect lunch spot and resting place from the chaos that is Chelsea on a Saturday! My party of five had to wait a while for a table, but it was well worth it. I'd advise to put in your name with the very pleasant and accommodating host and peruse the market for a bit. The beer, wine and cocktail menu is thoughtful and fitting. They have a wide selection of organic liquors and my friends who ordered cocktails were very pleased. The ginger-ita was especially tasty! I went for a craft brew off their list of appropriate winter beers. I really enjoyed the harvest salad which consisted of greens, walnuts, goat cheese and light dressing. My fellow diners raved about the mac and cheese, grilled cheese, and chicken pot pies. I would go back to the Green Table- even if it wasn't situated in the coolest spot in Chelsea- because of the great food, drinks and service. Everything from the decor to the liquor selection to the menus was carefully crafted and thoughtfully presented. Feel free to nibble at the health food markets, coffee bars and chocolate shops, but eat a real meal at the Green Table!

I know I'm not saying anything new, but the Blueberry Pancakes are simply amazing! We came for dinner on a week night, so we were able to get a table right away, no 3 hour wait time. The little biscuits they serve before the meal are lovely. The pancakes are filled with blueberries, and are light and airy yet still filling. The maple butter just makes them over the top fantastic. I wish I could have tried one of their desserts but was too full - next time. I don't know if I would spend hours in line to eat here, but next time I'm in the city, I'll be back for breakfast at dinner!
This place is the spot. Will be coming here from now on for happy hour. And the waitress was very pretty.

Just finished up brunch and was so pleased! We shared the breakfast omelette & brunch pizza. The pizza with sunny side up eggs was out of this world! Very nice atmosphere, friendly and attentive staff, and overall delicious food.
Deli sandwich ready to be made.

Came here on 2 different occassions. Once for lunch and once for dinner. Both times, I was not disappointed. The food is fresh and service was prompt! When I came here for lunch, my friend and I had the deviled eggs with salmon roe and I've gotta say, the salmon roe compliments the deviled eggs so well. They melt in your mouth yet you get that refreshing crisp taste of the boiled egg white. I ordered the Cookshop Mezze as my main and was so refreshing! The Cookshop Mezze is a salad divided into 5 different parts: quinoa, broccoli rabe, beets, 3 mixed beans and summer squashes. It's like a detox for the body. My friend ordered the trout & I regret not ordering it. The trout was soft and savory with every bite and to have a bit of skin that was crisped perfectly added a nice touch of texture. I had brunch with my girl friends a few weeks later. The frittata I ordered did not disappoint. The squash added to the texture and kicked it up a notch. One of my girls ordered the Cookshop Scramble and my god, it was one of the best scrambled eggs I've ever had a taste of! It was creamy because of the creme fraiche, yet it had a bit of crunchiness to it. And the trout added some smokiness to the mix. Now I know to order trout when I come back - both times, that damn fish never ceased to disappoint! Cookshop is great for groups - the restaurant has a vast open space. The polished look of the wood gives this place that clean cut country feel. Cookshop brings back that farm to table experience that reminds us of how good fresh food is!

There is some decent food here but the atmosphere is more like a zoo or an airport than a place to ingest food on purpose.  I agree that it is certainly coasting on its former glory and the fact that it is located in a terrific spot, across from one of NJ's many pharmaceutical companies and near the intersection of three major roads and a parkway.   The reason I hate this diner is that they simply don't care about the quality of the experience you have.  Time and time again I have come here to catch my breath and eat a little something during the course of a busy day, only to find myself literally assaulted by the noise.  Not normal diner noise.  Noise from the traveling salesman screaming into his cellphone at his supplier for effing something up, and/or the classless thug who thinks screaming into his speakerphone to his peeps shows us that he is some kind of power broker.  The last time I was there, both of those things happened on either side of me, and the final straw was the guy with two--TWO!!!!!--cell phones, both on speaker, who was carrying on two conversations AND yelling at his kids to sit down and eat.  Folks, this is not acceptable.  It's not. Given its location, again, I understand that many people who rely on cell phones will stop here too.  But there is a limit to acceptable behavior, even in a diner, and the Tick Tock doesn't get it.  When I complained the last time I went there, the hostess told me that they couldn't tell people what to do.  I said, yes, actually, you can.  This is YOUR restaurant...this isn't a bus station deli...YOU make the rules.   I got a blank stare.  Either they don't want to lose business or they just don't care.  Either answer is shortsighted and myopic.  I wonder how many people would come back if they actually gave a damn.

Really disappointed in this place as it has gone way downhill from a few years ago.  Not sure if they have changed hands or have been cutting back but I remember the food being much better quality.  Have given this place a few more tries but everything seems frozen or something.  Fried calamari was fishy tasting and rubbery.  It was the first time I've ever sent food back.  Duck burger was nothing to rave about.  Wait time for the food to come out was also way too long.  Can't understand how there is still a huge line to get into this place or 4 stars on Yelp.  We will not be going back.

I had a surprise bridal shower for my friend there and it was awesome! The food was amazing! Everyone loved their meal. The coconut mojito was just right and tasty. I've been craving the sea bass ever since! The best thus far! Atmosphere is nice. Plan on going back for Valentines Day;)

Fries with choice of sauces which, if you are so daring, can mix and match forming your own perfect sauce. The place is a whole in the wall joint, most appropriate for "starching-up" after binge drinking.

This place is HORRIBLE!! I would NEVER go here again and I hope this review makes people listen. The SERVERS ARE AWFUL! I have never had such bad service in my life. They are all lazy, stuck-up, selfish foreigners who can barely speak English and do their job. They weren't able to answer my questions as they simply didn't speak the language well enough. All they were interested in was rushing us out and getting their CASH. The servers were  clearly greedy snobbish. The BYOB/CASH ONLY policy was clearly a way for these girls to work under the table and collect as much money as possible. Therefore, they didn't care about the customers AT ALL. They stood behind the host stand all night on the Cell Phones!! Every time I tried to get my servers attention, she was busy texting someone on her cell phone. I saw her go over and do this every few minutes all night. She didn't care about her job at all! I came into this place to spend $$$$ on a very important dinner date, but instead all I got was a big bill and a VERY rude server. They need to hire an American server immediately. It is NOT acceptable to pay that much $ for dinner and not be able to COMMUNICATE. There were NO managers around. No owner. No nothing. It was clear that these girls were running the place and they did a BAD job. It is the owners responsibility... Mr. Pawlicki who I've heard about in reviews... to be RESPONSIBLE with this business and hire competent women and men who can speak English. This is America. All this restaurant is: a greedy transplant from France trying to bank as much cash as they can with no regard for the customer. Do not go here.

Saw this place on an episode on Man vs Food, so absolutely had to visit when I ended up coming to Philadelphia - VERY glad I did. Don't let the long line scare you away - the guys behind the counter operate like a well-oiled machine and the line moves pretty quick. Recommend the original roast pork w/ provolone and broccoli rabe (that's what Adam had on MvF) - meat was super-moist, cheese and veggies are an amazing combo. (A warning - the broccoli is super-garlicky; while delicious, bring gum / mints if you plan on having a conversation and/or making out with anyone anytime after finishing your awesome sandwich.)
Food was good. Watch out for the brownstone punch!!!!!!!

Came here for the pizza and the slim chance to be in the same room as Beyonce. Left with an immense food coma and the best pizza experience EVER (not exaggerating). Survivor's Guide to Lucali: - THE WAIT: They open at 6, but they take names down for seatings beforehand. We came around 5:10pm and got a table for two for their first seating. People who came right at 6pm were told to come back at 8pm. - BOOZE: Buy booze after you've put your name down at the store on Court Street nearby. We got $10 screw cap red wine, because we are classy and poised people. - BABIES: I don't have a baby, but apparently everybody else did. True to the neighborhood, almost every other diner came in with a toddler/infant. They didn't allow strollers into the restaurant and asked to keep the babies on their laps. There are only a couple of toppings, and most of them aren't meat. Which is fine, because you wouldn't want anything that would compromise their superb crust. We got shallots and mushrooms (the garlic and fresh basil came free). They were thinly cut and just barely cooked, which added a wonderful crunch and burst of flavor to the sauce and fresh mozzarella. The crust is light, chewy, and crunchy -- somewhere in the middle of thin crust and normal. The pizza is by no means dense -- the 2 of us split one pie. We then got the calzone, which our stomachs certainly didn't need but our taste buds did. Thank you fellow Yelpers for suggesting this. The calzone is hands down the best I've ever had -- light crust filled with fistfuls of fresh ricotta. I don't care if you're already too full from the pizza -- you must get the calzone, too.

This place has INSANE food and the guy working there is ridiculously nice.   Everything is reasonably priced and you can request exactly what ingredients you'd like in your chaat. So delicious. Stop dawdling on yelp and go!

Went to Get Fresh for brunch and was, once again, extremely pleased with my experience.  Food is consistently fresh and creatively prepared.  Best staff in Park Slope.  Attentive, pleasant, and very knowledgeable of the menu. The food, airy atmosphere, and charming staff make Get Fresh one of our favorite picks in the area.

Meh is what it says when you give a restaurant a two star rating here, and meh is exactly how I felt upon walking out after my meal.  Don't get me wrong, the food was wonderful, a real treat and a luscious throw back to the best trattorias of southern Italy. And I'm really not a complainer when it comes to restaurants, but my experience made me want to take the time and sit to write a review. The overall experience fell well short of the expectations we have of the the top restauranteurs in this city.  The service was mediocre at best.  Most of the staff left me with the feeling they were "overtrained" to be nice.  I like a more relaxed natural discourse with the staff than that especially in this type setting.  The waiter was confusing in explaining the menu, eventually admitting there were no special.  It was just that the menu had recently and completely changed.  The bus boy whisked a dish away without first asking.  I really wanted some more of that sauce on my arancina oopss...too late.  He never bothered asking if I was done before grabbing the dish.   Also Marc, and I know you and your staff read these reviews, would it kill you to put more than one amarena cherry in the tartufo?  I know they're a little pricey, but often people want to share desserts.  It would be nice for each person to get a full effect of the flavors the  chef intended.  Especially since the menu says cherries (plural). After touting the flavorgasm of amarena cherries to my significant other, upon finally finding one and digging through the rest of my tartufo  it was "Oh sorry honey, I had the only one they put in the dessert.  And jury's still out on that bread.  I'm pretty sure I can bake the same thing in my bread baker and the recipe that came with it now that I know to just add sea salt on top.  And salt does seem to be a common flavor which stands out in most of the dishes.  Particularly the pasta. The ambiance was very nice, but rather loud if you like conversation that's especially personal in nature given the next tables are five inches away from your elbow.  I did enjoy hearing about the sex life of the two energetic young ladies at the table next to ours though.  The four of us decided we're going out together next week to try a Garcas restaurant.  Thanks Marc! Seriously, it's quite a shame when the food is this good that so many other things seemingly have fallen through the cracks.

My husband wanted to treat me dinner one night after work. We had a so so meal that was way over priced. It is very rare that I can not provide a great review for a local Brooklyn spot. We left feeling like we had been mugged. The menu says one price but our bill says something else. So instead of arguing with the waiter (which is what I WOULD DO) hubby paid the bill and said "Never again." It's really unfortunate. They have a garden dining area in the back. And they seem to always have a steady crowd. But overpriced. They are many better choices a block or so away.

I wasn't sure that it was possible for one menu to contain quite so many terrible combinations of next to disgusting ingredients but then I walked into this dump. Looking over the various combinations of pizza piled with stinking clams, haphazardly strewn mexican toppings, and undercooked fish and shrimp (on a pizza...seriously?) one can't help but wonder whether this is a sick joke being played on the residents of New Haven or the brainchild of an owner with down syndrome. Props though to the smelly Mahmoud Ahmadinejad look alike behind the counter.

I loveeeeee fries. I have this issue where I eat the fries first and then afterwards I can't finish my actual meal. This place makes the love of fries and only fries totally acceptable. The types of sauces and all the price makes it awesome. not the most amazing fries in the world but pretty damn good and I see why people go. I don't know if id wait like 30 mins at night though to eat them.
Came her for lunch with my family, food was ok the portion was a bit small, the Cesar Salad was really good, the guy that took our order was a bit arrogant.

They should fire my server on the spot with an old dirty boot. Of course, its extremely busy there. I know that. The wait was about 1:30 mins for a table. I was willing to wait because the food is good. I wish I can remember the server's name so I can put him on blast, but he was the slowest/ dim-witted/ negligent server I have ever encountered. Every time he walked by, he never looked at our table when we were clearly flagging him down. We were a group of three asian girls; extremely friendly too I might add. I'm not sure if he was racist, but it seemed like he tended to the Caucasian guests more. He checked up the table behind us and and nicely asked if they needed change or what not. When I finally got his attention, he didn't wait for me to ask my question and rudely interrupted me telling me to pay at the counter! Can someone say, "how rude!" Some asian girl must have rejected him in high school or something because he had a stick up his a**.

What, you might ask, could possibly cap a day seeing Josh Beckett throw a no-hitter at Citizens Bank Park?  An amazing meal when we *thought* we were going to our second choice restaurant because the Mediterranean place down the street was full.  We even felt a tinge of regret when said first choice restaurant texted us to say some seats had opened up and we were already at Alma de Cuba. Needless to say the incredible appetizers banished those thoughts. The bone marrow and oxtail croquettes dish had layers and layers of flavor and texture. Amazing. The fried oysters were also terrific. Then shortly after our crispy pork entree arrived, the head chef burst into the restaurant holding a first place trophy over his head. He seemed like a wonderful guy and he had just won a celebrity chef pork competition.  It was that sort of night.  Smoked ribeye sliders were distributed  and the chef's friends toasted his success. This was clearly a special evening but we are eager to return for the great food, service and atmosphere on a "normal" night when we are next in Philadelphia.

If you want a happy belly go to Guayoyo. You will eat the best Arepas. So corn filled and flavorful. You can get the Arepa as an appetizer or as a meal. Guayoyo also offers a variety of other delectable options from salads to yuca and much more.  The drinks are a bit alcohol heavy but they are drinks.

A group of us (6) had a great experience dining on Christmas eve at Jane G's. Dinner started with the dumpling combination appetizer, 8 total of an assortment of 4 different varieties. These were served with several different dipping sauces. Most interesting version was the truffle edamame filled. We also tried the popcorn shrimp, which are well worth the calorie count. and a return visit, if only as a late night snack with a beer. I have to admit we went overboard with ordering entrees, 8 in all, but we were all hungry and in the mood for sampling many dishes. Cumin dry rub lamb, excellent. Shrimp with pickeled chilis, two chicken dishes, another shrimp dish, a lo mein dish, and a special prepared by the chef of pork belly. Often the case with chinese food, is that the sauces don't seem distinct or different from each other. This was not the case at Jane G's. Every dish was unique in flavor, presentation, and texture. The best thing about our dinner of course was that all the guests were willing to try new foods and sharing family style made this fun and exciting. One minor issue, the serving spoons were frustratingly small, so some of the food was a struggle to spoon onto dishes. We were all tolerant of spicey food and asked that the dishes come out as 2-3 on a scale of 5 being the hotest. I warn you that compared to most places, 2-3 is very spicey, one dish I sampled had dozens of the dry red pepper pods in it, so eater beware. I can say that having eaten Indian food in Bombay, Chinese food in various parts of asia, and sushi in Japan, this restaurant is as authentic in its flavors as you will ever find in Philly if not the rest of the US. Enjoy, I know, I did.

A good friend of mine commented on how delicious the fried calamaris were at this place and I have to say he was spot on!  That reason alone is enough to get me back through the door but there's more that keeps me coming.  In fact there's a lot more--as in a lot more pages of food goodness to choose from.  I've tried several of their menu items and they never disappoint.  It's just not "diner" food but really "restaurant" food.  There's a difference between the two and Nevada pulls it off quite well.  Plus the fact that this place is open during those late night cravings is just awesome!  They also don't skimp out on the portions.  I once ordered a dinner combo for less than $20 and I got food that lasted me for breakfast and lunch the next day! Not too bad eh.  One more thing: the diner opens their patio during the warmer weathers and I tell you it's great to sit outside enjoying your food and just watch as the cars pass by Broad St.  Great job Nevada Diner!  It's not easy to succeed as a diner here in Jersey but you seem to be pulling it off quite well.

Just got back to South Jersey from visiting a relative in NYC. We decided to eat at Casa Adela for dinner. We have been there once before. The mofongo was good but it was not what I had ordered. I ordered a plain mofongo with extra garlic and I receive a mofongo with pernil. I let that go, they made a little mistake. I'll pay the extra money for the pernil.   I asked at the beginning if they had white rice with beans, and I was told that they only had arroz con gandules. So I said "no thank you", and just went with the mofongo.  Later, as I'm eating my meal the waitress brings white rice and beans.  "Ok I'll take the rice and beans home", I said to myself, even though I no longer wanted the rice and beans. When we get the check, the waitress had charged us $12 extra. I had her add the check and she came up with the wrong number herself, but continued to say that she was right. Since we had six people in our group, we were charged 18% tip which it was fine, but she charge us 18% plus and extra $12.  The owner's son came to the register and gave me my money, but they were making me feel like I was in the wrong. I even had someone else add it up, and they were wrong.  Last time I was there, the owner, Adela was cooking in the kitchen, and the service was much better. Maybe her presence makes a big difference in the service. I will never go there again. The customer service was horrible. If you go there, make sure that your food order and your bill is correct.

One of the more underwhelming restaurant experiences I've had in a while. The boyfriend made plans to go to the restaurant after a visit to the Brooklyn Botannical gardens to see the cherry blossoms. Because our visit to the gardens ended earlier than we anticipated, we decided to walk to the restaurant. Since he usually has excellent choice in restaurant, I assumed that it would be awesome, as usual. First impressions were promising-it's pretty much what you would expect a place with the word "buttermilk" to look like...very country-esque. Hungry from a half day of walking, we decided upon the Caputo's Handmade Mozzarella with Basil and Warm Anchovy Sauce, Slow-Roasted Pork Spare Ribs, Warm Lamb and Romaine Salad, and the Buttermilk Fried Chicken (a choice that was heavily influenced by all the raving reviews). The meal also started out with a bang-the mozzarella was delicious (and I don't think it was due to our hunger!), with just enough flavors to make it interesting, but not too much as to be overwhelming. The pork was excellent as well, and perfectly roasted with a sauce that had an unexpected (but well-received) kick at the end. The second course. Sorely disappointing: The lamb salad had its moments (e.g. the cauliflower), but the lamb was not extraordinary, and the boiled egg was way too salty (so much for Bloomberg's war on salt!). Halfway through the meal, I realized that I was continuing to eat merely because I felt like it'd be a waste of $16.   We ordered the chicken despite our initial concerns that it was too ordinary. And it was little more than ordinary. According to the boyfriend, the highlight of his meal was the cole slaw (eek). The fried chicken was good, but it was just fried chicken, and the waffle was good, but it was just a waffle (with syrup that was very fluid and "pure"). His last piece of chicken was also a bit bloody. Worth $18? Probably not. Take home point: the food is fine, but probably not worth the $$$. I'm sorry to say that I would probably not go here again.

I've been here for both happy hour and for dinner. Happy hour is amazing, truffle fries were so good, and pretty good drink specials. Lots of people, making for a good scene after work. Also had a delicious dinner. Lobster bisque and wedge starters- both great. Had the scallops and short rib for entree and it was awesome! Other people at my table got the filet and thought it was cooked perfectly. Got the carrots, Mac and cheese and garlic mashed potatoes for sides and I recommend all of them- the carrots were surprisingly good! Sweetly glazed. Service was great, beautiful restaurant. Though there are a lot of high end steak house places, ocean prime is still worth a visit.
OMG big boy roll!!! If you happen to be on the are this is the place to go, I am in love with their sushi, a must try in this area.

I just ate there - August  17th - and my food was awful. I had a duck prosciutto appetizer that was so salty I could barely get it down. Then I had a chicken breast entree that smelled like it was deep fried and tasted awful. I'd never eat there again.

This place exceeded my expectations of a diner with two non-traditional menu options.  I started with a salad special made with local greens and pears and it was delicious.  My entree was the Asian Spiced Tuna Burger with great flavor.  Should you be concerned about whether SCD is just masquerading as a diner, I sampled the Meatloaf and found it up to NJ standards.  A nice perk is that you have your choice of seating inside with booths and a counter or outside in the more avant-garde outdoor garden.

Came here on a road trip home to the DC area from Stowe, VT because of how well reviewed it was on Yelp. We knew we wanted to stop by Burlington and grab some late breakfast (it was around noon on a weekday), so I looked for diners, knowing they'd hopefully have some "breakfast all day" type of deal, and this place topped the list, with good reason -- the food is great, cheap, and fast, and Earl, the young, handsome, and charming owner (I promise I'm not just saying this to make up for all the ball-busting I gave him while he was waiting on us), is a great guy who's doing a fantastic job of keeping his family business running for 60+ years. Well, Earl's "only" been doing it for 16 years, according to the story that's printed on the menu and worth reading if you at all give a crap about supporting local/family/small businesses. Which I do, if that wasn't obvious to you yet. All the locals were in there ordering lunch, since it was weekday lunchtime, and everything looked damn good, but we were insistent on ordering breakfast food. Handy's offers only three breakfast selections in its "late risers" menu section: the McHandy's (loved the jab at McD's, had to order it based on name alone -- egg, cheese, and bacon, sausage, or ham, I believe, on an English muffin, and of course I got sausage because why would you get anything else?); the Super G (some kind of egg/cheese/meat concoction on a sub roll, as Earl described it to us?), and the SST (egg/cheese/meat on FRENCH TOAST). The McHandy's is cheap at $4.50ish; the other two are about twice the price, which is still normal/cheap for breakfast/brunch prices, at least where I come from. My husband tried the SST and it was as obscenely good as egg/cheese/meat on French toast sounds like it would be. Earl thoughtfully asked if he would like to "Costanza" his sandwich since it was too hot and messy to eat by hand, and brought silverware even when my husband refused and said he could handle it. This is a man who knows the power of his establishment's food. I know I'm going to miss this place every weekend from now until the next time I'm in Vermont (next year, maybe?) when I wake up and think, "Time for diner food" and then get sorely disappointed by my local offerings. We have egg/cheese/meat combinations here in DC that compare, but no proprietor or service that compares to Earl. I don't even give a crap about baseball but I still had fun ragging on the Yankees on behalf of my sister in absentia, a Sox fan. Pros: Everything. Cons: Nothing that knocks the stars below five. They didn't have grapefruit juice, but since I asked so nicely, Earl might put it on the menu. Not that it matters since I live 10+ hours away, and who ever cared if a greasy spoon had grapefruit juice anyway? They do have orange juice, and besides, what I should have been drinking was cup after endless cup of diner coffee, but again, if it's not obvious to you yet, I could probably do with less caffeine in my life. In conclusion, EAT HERE NOW. Unless it's between 3pm and 7am, in which case you can't eat there now and you'll have to wait until later.

I can't remember the last time I was completely blown away by a brunch experience...until now. Cafe Lift is a dream come true. It really may be one of the best brunch spots I've ever been to. To start, the interior is amazing. Very casual, comfortable feel to the entire place. Exposed brick and piping all along the walls with hardware store style tables. What got me the most excited was the special board. SO. MANY. SPECIALS. Really it is a dream come true (yes I said dream come true TWICE) to walk into a place for brunch and have a plethora of creative specials to pick from...which my party of 3 wasted no time doing. What we got: (note that most were specials) Breakfast tacos: chorizo, egg, cheese, and homemade salsa which rocked my world. Baked Egg: stewed kale, white beans, roast pork in tomato sauce topped with eggs and fontina then baked. Obsessed with this. Imagine a breakfast pasta fagioli situation Cuban Sandwich Bagel w/ veggie cream cheese and salmon Banna nutella crepe with whipped cream and strawberries The ice coffee was really, really good and I am truly very picky when it comes to coffee. Service was friendly and fast. I will be back ASAP

I went to Sakura with my friend last weekend. When we first got there, it was not too crowed and just a little busy. I liked the interior of the restaurant because it had a tropical and relax atmosphere with the walls painted green and the staffs were very attentive. They serve shanghai and Japanese food. We ordered a special roll, which was the wasabi roll and it tasted not bad, but couldn't say spectacular. For the shanghai food, we ordered the marinated duck for the appetizer and lion head and the Wu xi porkchop as entrees. The marinated duck was not bad, it was tasty. The lion head was very good, when i mean its good i mean it is really good. It tasted creamy, tender and the sauce was very rich and tasty. It went so well with the rice that I had 2 bowls of them. Then the last was the Wu xi Pork chop, it was cover with red color sauce on top. The Wu xi Pork chop was very chewy, tender, very well done and the sauce was very delicious. The price were very fair around 10$ for each entree. and 5$ for each appetizers. Sakura Mandarin is very good at doing what they are. The sushi were not bad and the shanghai food was truly amazing and you'll know what i mean when you try it. By the way, the service was excellent. The servers were very friendly and attentive. 5 stars for Sakura for their delicious food, service, and price. I will be back soon Sakura!!!!

looked up this place for lunch one day. It happened to be a particularly chilly one (18 degrees w/ wind chill), and the thought of leaving my office made my eyes well up with tears, but i went anyway. It was a bit more fancy than i had thought it would be. I ordered the salmon sandwich but they were out of salmon, so i had a steak sandwich instead. May i say, yum yum yummy. It was large, perfectly cooked, had caramelized onions and it came with fries all for about $8.50. Pretty good price for a quality soho lunch. Got so full i had to be rolled home, but luckily all the meat i had gave me the sweats and kept me warm the rest of the day.

Haven't tried the pizza yet, but came in for a drink on Saturday night at the bar, and ended up having far too many expertly made cocktails. Looking forward to trying the pizza, hopefully they're as good as the cocktails.

I made reservations for a party of 6 two weeks ago on OpenTable and asked to be seated by the windows. Reservation confirmed. 5 of the 6 arrived together (1 was parking his car) and we were told we needed all 6 to be seated - there is a 15 minute grace period where afterward you lose your reservation and have to wait for an available table. Once we were all together we were seated by the windows, phenomenal view of the East Side of Manhattan, direct view of the Empire State Building. The setting has very dim lighting. We immediately got our menus - which to all of our surprise LIGHT UP! Our waitress was Priscilla (she was awesome) We ordered drinks, a pitcher of red sangria, appetizers and our entrees (all together) Everything came orderly; the drinks were YUM! Henny Mojitos and Patron Mojitos were strong and sweet, the red sangria was really good as well. We had the freshest guacamole. Chef Kelvin stopped by our table with complimentary arepitas with braised short rib - so delicious. After loud laughing, reckless NC17 conversation, reminiscing and planning vacations our entrees came... 4 out of the 6 had the Churrasco which was JUICY, slightly charred and AMAZING. The other two (including myself) had the Surf & Turf... Are you Dominican? Have you ever had Mangu? Yes? Well then you haven't had mangu like this... Sweet baby Jesus it was GOOD! The scallops were perfectly seared ... Man my mouth is watering. After another round of drinks and another pitcher of sangria we ordered the dessert sampler which included: warm lava cake, piña colada tres Leches, coconut flan, a guava and cheese fried roll and ice cream... We DEVOURED that plate. I cannot stress how great the service was. We wiped down those plates, not a crumb was spared, the food was delicious, the drinks were on point, the ambience set a great mood, the vibes were of joy. Priscilla was very attentive and sweet. Chef Kelvin came by our table twice making sure we were a happy bunch and happy does not describe the level of content in which we left BOTW. We promised to go back when the weather was a bit warmer.

Great atmosphere....nice cocktails (Happy Hour is pretty solid - you can only get them at the bar area, downstairs.). Food was excellent - try the hummus w/ jalapenos, brussels sprouts and falafel apps.
The chicken tortilla soup was delicious, the same with the ribs and fries, will definitely be back there sooner rather than later.

... a little disappointed... after reading all the great reviews I was so psyched to come here! My experience here was... OK. The Cuban Sandwich was NOT tasty. The drinks and the corn are good but not great. The wait for the food was very long too. I think I will make another appearance here just to see if it was their off day.

Jean's is by far the best cheap meal in Center City. I usually go there for breakfast/brunch type meals so I can mostly only talk about their awesome, cheap, and delicious breakfast menu (which they serve all day) but I've never had any complaints when I've ventured from my breakfasty comfort zone. There are 2 well-stocked big fridges that go above and beyond all your soft drink needs. FYI: They are closed Sundays, which is a bummer. Also, this is not the restaurant's fault at all, but  if a group of UArts kids walk in, expect the volume level to rise considerably.

Pio Pio!  Hard to forget a name like that... in fact it sounds much like when kids play and pretend to fire guns at each other... It's also hard to forget because it's my first time having chicken with a South American twist.   My honest first thoughts were "Peruvian chicken? What could be so great about it?" I could not have been more wrong.  I believe we ordered 2 Matador combos for the 8 of us.  Each combo included a chicken cut into fours, fries, avocado salad, rice and beans and tostones.  We also ordered ceviche and sangria. Let me describe in order of consumption... The sangria is really good here.  Now I say this because most sangrias have a really strong wine taste which is too much for me but this sangria was more sweet, less bitter and smooth tasting.  The ceviche was really good, not outstanding but pretty solid.  Big enough for the 8 of us to get a good tasting of it. On to the main course... Chicken!!  I was pretty skeptical going in and even as the food came out it looked pretty standard.  I picked a piece of the dark meat, dived in with my fork and knife and came out pleasantly surprised.  All I could say was, "OMG this is so good!!" Although I am a potato gal the french fries needed to be eaten with some sauce to help get them down but not too bad.  Green sauce had a nice kick to it so I used it for the french fries instead of the chicken. Avocado salad was okay.  It's literally avocado on top of some iceberg lettuce pieces.  I was the least impressed with the presentation and components of this dish but doesn't affect my overall view.  Afterall it's just salad. :) Definitely worth checking out.  Walking in it looks really small but then you get downstairs and I loved the space!!  Great atmosphere for enjoying a good meal with good friends!

They have a great lunch special for $10 (if you want wine or beer you add  $3). Friendly service, grass-fed beef. Also now they are streaming the World Cup in Brazil and have ample amount of space and plenty of TV's in all corners.

A great casual bar with interesting, but tasty food.  Anything from burgers to bbq boar to octopus.  The Standard fare stays the same, but they add specials, check the board to see what they're serving up.  It's great for happy hour or going out on the weekend.

This historic market is one of my favorite places in Philadelphia. I bring all my friends who visit me here. This place is just oozing with culture and what it really means to be a Philadelphian. It's a great place for locals to shop, eat, visit, and hang out. For visitors/tourists, you cannot visit Philadelphia and skip out on Reading Terminal Market. You will not regret your time here.

I had the Pollo Con Camarones- Boneless chicken breast and jumbo shrimp sauteed in a rioja demi glaze served over  saffron rice and tostones. I thought it was delicious and the presentation was great.  Lots of jumbo shrimp to accompany the dish.  The sauce was tasty and flavorful.  This was very filling, I couldn't even finish it all. Had to wrap the rest up in a to go container.  This is definitely enough for two meals. Service was great and the location is wonderful.  Delicious mojitos as well..
Stopped by in Philly for lunch a few weeks back.  I'm a big fan of hand pulled noodles and this place was an excellent and cheap stop for lunch.  The portions are huge and the broth was rich.

Holy crap, this place is rediculous. A friend of mine recommended this place as a must visit destination during my Philly trip. I thought he was leading me into a trap, as it was a little off the beaten path and in a sketchy area.  Despite the fact that I didn't know what the heck the person taking my order was saying (west coaster here), I am sooo glad I kept trucking, as this place was insanely good.  Makes me wish I lived in Philly-  Will definitely visit this place again when I find myself back in the City of Brotherly Love.

Really good, authentic Chinese food in northern NJ. Noodle Chu has an unbeatable lunch special. Three entrees, rice, and soup for the low price of $20.95. And they were good. We had the duck, salt and pepper squid/pork chops, and beef chow fun. The duck was good, a little soggy, but the flavor was right. Squid was a bit too salty for my taste, but the pork chops were exceptionally crispy and perfectly seasoned. These are probably the best salt and pepper pork chops I've had. Beef chow fun had good texture and flavor. Everything was prepared well. The service was typical of most Chinese restaurants.

Co-workers and I came on a Thursday for lunch. So we did come during lunch rush hour, but since we were a party of four (party max of four) it took longer than some of the smaller groups. Total wait time was about 45 minutes. When we actually got in the the experience was very good. We ordered promptly, and the food came very fast. I ordered the spicy vegetarian ramen. I really liked the default firmness of the ramen, and the broth was of excellent taste. The broth was a little peppery, but the general spiciness made up for it. Overall, the the ramen was very good, and the entire party was very happy. The cost was a few dollars cheaper than the nearby ramen restaurant ($18 including tax and tip).
Best chicken wings ever had! no wonder it's their most popular dish.

Although the food was good, the dining experience was awful. The a/c was non existent, in the front, the music was blasting and the bathroom was filthy with urine on the floor and an overflowing waste basket. You couldn't help but sweat and when I asked them to lower the music ( speaker was above our heads), I was told it was at the volume the owner wants and can not be changed. We waited over an hour to get in, on a Saturday night. On the flip side, the ax handle steak was very tender and the razor clam special was very tasty.  I hope they will address these issues.

I went to Supper with a party of 15 for a friend's birthday party since we couldn't find another place to accommodate such a large party on New Years Day. Why the two stars? It is for being disorganized and dishonest! When the bill came the waiter lied to us saying the tip was not included as he handed it to us (after adding in a 20%+ tip). The handwritten bill only had the final amount so we asked to confirm tip was not included and he lied to our faces. After totaling up the whole meal getting the subtotal amount we discovered an extra $150 added to the final amount. That was an extra 30% of the subtotal and ny restaurant tax is about 9%. When we confronted him, he mumbled there were two taxes. He tried to BS us some more to our group full of Asians thinking we are stupid or tourist from somewhere else. Eventually he got nervous and told us to pay the final amount on the bill to rush us out. Honesty the food was only average, I definitely had better meals in Italy. So do yourself a favor and make sure you check your bill if you decide to eat here.

This place is a god-send on during those late nights at Firkin. The food is exactly what you want at 2am. Unfortunately during the sober hours of the day, the food just seems average. You definitely need to pick up your food to get it warm.
Good food!

Mooncakes was the worst food I had while in NYC.  I ordered the sliced steak with cilantro/ginger sauce and the quality of the meat was barely edible...it was chewy and had no flavor which they tried to hide by drenching it in sauce. My friend  and brother ordered the miso glazed salmon and wasn't impressed although it probably was the best thing I tasted. My sister ordered the steak and pepper sandwhich and had one bite...Lets just say we will not be returning here.

This place is AMAZING! It is always the first thing on our "to do" list anytime we visit NYC! My mother has been a celiac for 25 years and swears that she has never had better gluten free food! She loves the paninis and also mixes it up with a pizza here and there. The gf bread sticks are great! I got a chicken pesto mozzarella zucchini panini that was the best sandwich I ever remember having! If you have never been you must check this place out, service is great too!!

Nice restaurant and nice atmosphere. The service is very friendly. The menu is a little pricey but worth the money on the right now. Especially when Jazz is being played in select nights by the BSOULCollective.

I am crazy for their roast chicken. The skin is crispy brown, and the meat is moist and juicy. I will come back time and again for this perfection of simplicity. It's a spacious restaurant, with an upper and lower level. Very dimly lit and the music can be a bit loud. The service has been good in my experience. The bartenders are incredibly friendly. I wish they offered a better cocktail menu than the cocktails based on Peruvian brandy, but they have a full bar so if you know what you want they will make it for you. Sangria is also quite nice. It's not particularly strong, so go for the bigger size if you're sharing. They will put the cut fruit on the side if, like me, you're allergic to the garnish fruit.

WOW!!!! This has got to be the best Mexican food in Philadelphia. My Husband and I go there ALL the time. Usually we sit at the bar and eat (except when we bring friends). The food is amazing one of my personal faves Shrimp Quesiidilia of Steak Carbon with a side of melted Manchego cheese. Love all the staff and the Chef is Superb

Not nearly as revolting a scene as its Midtown counterpart. The tapas selection is eclectic and interesting, if overpriced and small-ish.  The cheesesteak spring rolls are a favorite, and the shoestring fries are a must for any group to share. In all honesty, though, what I like most about Continental is that it attracts a certain clientele of suburbanites and "see-and-be-seens", thereby keeping same out of the Olde City establishments I actually like.
A delicious meal with excellent service!  Our favorites were the cauliflower, lamb tartare and pasta.  All cooked to perfection.  Already booked a return visit for Father's Day :)

Pretty good thai food. I still think The Sea is better. If you're out in Queens and you want good thai food, this is the place to go. I wouldn't make a specific trip to just come here though. This is more of a family style thai place, nothing I can't get in CA.

I went the night before Thanksgiving with two friends.  We arrived very early (5:15pm) and were quickly seated.  The service was so-so.  The food was very good! The reason I am giving a 3 star rating is that when we went to pay, I tried using my Opentable.com checks. The server took them along with my credit card for the additional payment and within minutes came back saying they do not accept them. I was clearly annoyed and advised him that this is not right - they are clearly a member of the Opentable.com Restaurant program. He went back and asked his manager (we could see the very quick conversation) and came back again, still saying no.  The manager did not even have enough professionalism or relationship building skills to walk over and explain, but rather stood hiding at the back of the restaurant (we could see that also).   Basically, they use the system to accept the reservation, but refuse to offer the benefits as a result of using the system. Beware of this! I will not be back!

This place had potential, but I found it to just be okay.  Was there early on a Saturday night and it was pretty empty.  Considering it's in University City - during the summer - I figured that's why.  Our waiter was very nice and pretty quick.  For an appetizer, I tried the crab and corn hushpuppies and they were definitely the highlight of my meal.  They were very tasty and melty.  The condiments that came with it were a really nice compliment to the flavors.  This restaurant also has a pretty decent beer selection if you are into that kind of thing.  For dinner, I had the pepperoni pizza and it was not great.  It was so incredibly spicy that I had a hard time even getting through the meal.  It was making my eyes water.  A pepperoni pizza should not be spicy like that and even if its supposed to be a made into a spicy pizza, there should be a warning on the menu.

First time trying a Filipino restaurant. Went for a Sunday brunch. Casual atmosphere and food were good. They have a 2 hr unlimited drink special you can get too. My friend and I sat outside in the garden but felt that the communal seating was strange as we were sharing a table with a random family. The service was great with the exception of a short haired petite girl who was very rude about not entering until exactly 11 AM even though the door was open.

we got the skirt steak,chocoloate flourless cake with homemade whip cream,  french fries and complimentary fresh warm bread. the food and the restaurant's charm took me on a journey to a land i could easily fall in love with.  oh and their wine selection hit the spot and so did the sangria!

I love me some Doma. Sometimes I'm not sure why I even go to other places for sushi. Their specialty rolls really are special. They have unique combinations of fresh fish and other ingredients. The sushi bar is very prominent in the restaurant and you can see your fish being prepared right before your eyes. On my last trip to Doma, I went straight for the sushi- ordering a bunch of signature rolls to share with a friend. Our picks for the night included the triple spicy double tuna, naked salmon, Chloe, tuna club and island. The island was probably my favorite and it included salmon, spicy aioli, tempura crunch, salmon, mango and wasabi tobiko. I'm not going to re list the menu, but whatever fish and ingredients tickle your fancy, Doma will probably have a signature roll for you. Non-sushi lovers can rejoice as well as they have a kitchen with tasty options. The restaurant itself is tiny. Make sure you call in your reservation! It's a very intimate but swanky setting. And its BYOB, which is fantastic to me. Next time I try to go elsewhere for sushi, I really need to just check myself and reread this review.
Italian factory type place. Have to eat pie there for best results. Got delivery recently and food was dominoes like. No bueno unless u want a quick slice while passing by.

Cheap, quick, and tasty. My girlfriend loves wontons, so I've been searching for wonton noodles in NYC for the whole year. I managed to go to about 7 restaurants, but none manages to satisfy me. Chef Yeung, a buddy of mine, recommended this place, kind of and off-to-the-side place in Chinatown. If you want authentic chinese/cantonese food, this is the closest next best thing to China you're going to find in NYC.

What a popular place! Even though we already made reservation, we had to wait about 20 mins to be seated, we ended up getting drinks at the bar next street.   The food was decent, the service was great.  We ordered a bottle of wine by our server's recommendation, but it didn't taste as good as we expected, guess what, he took back that opened-bottle and recommended a different one, which was much better, and we were very surprised by this great service :)
Went out with my bestie. She took me here. We had enchiladas. Delicious! I can't wait to go back and try something else. Great food. Wonderful atmosphere.

Excellent Food! Excellent Time! My buddy comes about once a week and now has the owner's phone number.  I had to see for myself, and it did not disappoint. The oysters were fantastic, the swordfish ceviche was well done, and the fettuccine with clams was out of this world.  Top it off with a craft beer and some free whiskey pound cake (despite my mother's is still the best, very impressive), and you've got yourself truly a meal to remember. Just go!!!

We went to Cuba for my boyfriend's birthday and all 8 of us loved the experience. The food was great, the drinks were strong,  and the waiters were very nice. We sat in a small cozy room w/ drapery on the ceiling and at times the room got very loud with live music from the front room, but the music didn't last all night. We started with ceviche, which was as delicious it can get. I had a paella dish and my boyfriend had skirt streak. Another friend had chicken stuffed with shrimp. That was everyone's favorite.

Perfect Dosa!! I will be here again- service for pick-up was fast and easy. The coconut curry, daal and veggies in my dosa was great. I believe I had a masala dosa which was a stuffed dosa (thin paper-like crepe) stuffed with potatoes in a perfect masala. Be sure to indicate your interest in level of spice. Mild will still be spicy enough, I think.

Overhyped, overpriced, greasy fries with mayo based dipping sauces. Heart clogging. I made the mistake of not checking the menu before I went. Small seating area, couldve been cleaner. Cant figure out the long lines or rave reviews.

Amaaaaadaaaaa. Let me tell you about Amada. Actually... wait, no, you don't need me too. Let 711 other people (the current number of reviews at this time of writing) tell you about Amada. Wait, stop. Just look at that score. Almost perfect. 4.5 stars. Just get off the computer, or smartphone, or whatever device you're reading this through, and go. To. Amada. Well, maybe it's not open yet. Then, maybe you'll want to read my thoughts. - If you're gonna get the tasting menu, come HUNGRY. Ravenous, even, 'cause it's a LOT of food. At times, we had to rearrange dishes on the table, Tetris-style, to make everything fit. Which is what makes it an amazing deal. Oh baby, I was practically rolling out of there. I can't believe it took me so long to ask for a doggie bag. - The chefs are a little heavy-handed with the oil for my personal liking. - Friendly, friendly service and amazing drinks. Please tell me you'll try a red sangria. - I really loved the skate. And the pork. - It gets crowded, so arrive early or make a reservation. Now get going down to Old City!

I like this place a lot.  It's crazily crowded (though also crazily efficient), and for good reason.  The burritos are reliably very good and not too expensive.  I like the quesadillas -- which are basically just smaller burritos w/ browned tortillas -- maybe even more.  A nice place to go on a night when you feel like just eating something quick and good and not lingering too long.  Cheap beer too.
Sandwiches are definitely meant for sharing here unless you're super hungry lol but overall great Italian sandwiches! I had the Piemonte!!

We arrived early for lunch and were greeted by some very grouchy waiters, but so what, the pizza was delicious!  We ordered the antipasto and it was fresh and yummy, then we ordered two pizzas, one meaty and the other veggie.  They brought one and we were eating it without question and then they brought 2 other pizzas and we realized that the yummy pizza we are eating was one we didn't order.  It was ok because they didn't charge us for it and we just ate the other two pizzas.  After awhile they started to all taste the same.  Don't get me wrong they tasted GREAT!  We came here because we saw it on Food Wars and wanted to check it out!

I had very high expectations for this place as I'm Cuban and was looking to host my wedding reception here. Unfortunately, the drinks and food were unpleasant: the mojitos were mostly lime juice, the croquettes tasted exactly like the frozen Goya ones, the Yucca was undercooked, and the paella was watery and had a funny smell. We had enough with the paella and refused to pay for it, we won't be going back!

You'll wonder how dumplings and pork ball soup could be so cheap but like the question "when were you last tested?" some things are better left unasked and unanswered. If you ever need to have a secret meeting that requires dumplings this is the place. They have a very soft texture that almost falls apart but aren't overly doughy and tough either.
