I've not been big on Juniors since they opened in Colchester.  I had figured it to be a pizza place trying to do too much.  But it seems Junior's Downtown has figured itself out nicely.  They make some tremendous pizzas and it's the highlight of the menu!  You can buy by  the slice or whole pies (as I'd expect of a downtown pizza joint just down the block from famous Mr. Mikes).  They do both quite well.   The space is a bit cramped but it's a Main Street establishment so large restaurant space on that building is hard to come by.  Don't expect to bring a large party in there on a weekend.  It does have several nice small group (4-5) tables and bar-style seating.  It's your typical downtown pizza joint: get in line, order at the counter, they deliver to the table.  Fountain drinks are self-serve and you can bus your table after. We tried the pesto and added bacon to it...amazing.  They have perfect crust and the toppings taste great!  The pepperoni is not at all skimpy on the meats.  Large single slices but they aren't soggy and grease covered.  Cheese and sauce seem nicely balanced and I didn't ever see or taste anything under or over cooked. Service was a bit on the slow side and the counter help felt new or at least the two girls there didn't seem to know how to coordinate work well.  But I didn't complain too much as they brought some great food.

This restaurant gets 5stars. (The diner who stole my umbrella gets zero and unless you return it you will be cursed). The welcome is invariably genuine and warm. These people know that the customer is what counts, and the customer matters. The venue is cosy but I have never been turned away without a reservation and all efforts were made to accommodate. The food always is of high quality with the spectrum from comfort to inventive covered. Good wine choice, including by the glass.

had the pleasure of dining here on Thursday.  Servers were extremely attentive and the meal was divine.   great spot for a date.  we shared the farro cauliflower cake and the fried artichokes to start, followed by filet of blackfish in parchment paper and the duck.  Make sure that you save room for desert.   decor wise-- simple and elegant.  the focus here is the food!!

My last visit to BSBH wasn't so great food-wise. The hubby and I went back for their fish fry (because it was so good in the past) and while it wasn't terrible, it was SO greasy! The fries, too, weren't as seasoned and good as I recalled. Hopefully they'll start paying attention to the food output cause the place wasn't even packed. Of course, the beer list was still up to par and the hubby was pleased.

I love this place! It's perfect to grab a bite anytime you're in the area - mid-day, lunch or even after hours. I stumbled here by accident after a party and couldn't be happier with the discovery! Been to Dos Toros Taqueria twice since then and the food is consistently fresh and delicious! My fave is the Basic (rice and beans) tacos with dollops of guac, sour cream & their yummy salsa. I also requested them to heat the soft taco shell a bit, to give it some crunch and it tasted even better. Carne Asada (grilled steak) taco is also a winner. If you're ever in the area, don't hesitate to try this place!
Despite the internet stating that they allow dogs, it isn't true! The queue was massive so we have up & left. Very disappointed!

Had dinner here earlier this evening and we were very impressed. We had the Spring rolls, pho, and vietnamese crepe. Everything was flavorful and delicious. One thing I noticed - they were very generous with the bean sprouts and herbs that came with our dishes (something I really appreciate). The decor is lovely and the staff is so nice! I don't think I've ever encountered such a pleasant staff when going to Vietnamese restaurants, so it was a very refreshing change. This place is a gem, and will be our go-to place whenever we have a craving for Viet food. :)

Great Szechuan.  They use the real Szechuan Peppercorns too!  Its hot, tingly, numbing goodness.  Im stuck on the Ox tongue and tripe, 3 days in a row now!   Just cant stop.  I really cant wait to go in and eat there with a big group so I can taste more.  So far, its been just delivery, and the food is amazing.

essentially 2 places. #1 great beer place. large beer menu, rotating specials, happy hour 7 days a week.....food is across the board an eh. uninspiring at best ok. sad really, this is so close to being a great restaurant.....ambience, the website implies that the staff is young caucasian aryan looking women wearing traditional garb. reality is 2 asian women wearing black t shirts and jeans and a grubby bearded white guy white guy behind the bar....they are not what they purport themsekves to be.........brauhaus schmitz has a great beer list excellent food staff dressed in traditional german garb oompah music. you get the real thing. .....so bottom line have your beer here but get your food somewhere else. there 2 many other excellent food places nearby to accept such poor execution on the food......schnitzel, mashed potatos, ghoulash are terrible, pretzels and potato pancakes are just ok, the knockwurst was pretty good...should be better

Caracas Arepa has become one of our regular eat-out spots. Their staff is very friendly and knowledgable of their menu. Their drinks are reasonable priced and so is their food. My favorite, Tostones Mochimeros! I can't get enough of them. And from the Arepas  is Playa Deluxe (pan seared tilapia, garlic, onion, and special mayo sauce). I  def recommend this place for a good, quick and inexpensive meal.

Heard the hype, checked it out and walked out full and pleased.  Thank you Anthony Bourdain for the suggestion! I came here with a friend and waited about 40 minutes for a table and luckily enough, we were seated at the bar in the corner right by the AC so it wasn't too bad.....actually, it was perfect! This place is PACKED and I do mean packed because they will seat you in the most random and squished places, so we got lucky. Can't go wrong with the skewers!  I waited too long to write this review so I can't remember anything now, but as usual, we ordered with our eyes and everything was pretty darn tasty.  We also got a bottle of the peach sake and it was good and all but way too sweet (as expected, duh).  Oh well. Smack in the middle of Midtown and Times Square, it's a little difficult to find, but totally worth checking out.  Remember to go downstairs - there's always a big confusion with the restaurant next door.

Amazing!!! Great taste, perfect crisp, everything perfect. But what do you expect from the founder of Grimaldi's, Patsy Grimaldi?! I can't wait to go back and try another pie. I just had a regular to try for first time. One thing I loved, even though I didn't get to, was Patsy talks to everyone. Regular down to earth conversations. I think that's great.

My wife and I always go there for our dates. We love going there for their excellent foods, atmosphere, services. After lunch, we would go to the Sculpture grounds and linger there for hours, taking pictures and enjoying the good weather! Its a very romantic getaway for your loved one!

We had reservations for 7:40 but they were pretty unnecessary, though later it did fill up. The service was fantastic, and the food was phenomenal. It's hard to categorize but they seem to use a lot of ingredients from Australia and New Zealand. The atmosphere is great too. We had the cured wild boar appetizer, then I got the New Zealand venison and my boyfriend had the snail and oxtail ravioli. We had the hokey pokey ice cream for dessert. I was delighted that it was on the menu, as well as the venison. I had looked at their menu online but it was different when we got there so I expect it changes regularly. Great place!
This place is wonderful!  Food is incredible and the staff treats you like guests in their home kitchen.

Two rolls for $8.95. Speedy and friendly service. I'm not hugely into sushi that's been in the cooler, but it was a good deal. Will definitely return to try some of the teriyaki dishes next semester when I'm scrounging around downtown for lunch.

Tiny Thai is the best deal in town for lunch, hands down. Three course for eight bucks is a steal by any standard. Their food is delicious, if a little too rich, and the wait times can be atrocious. Service is generally good.

Just came here for my bf's grandma birthday. I called in at 7pm for table of 10 and got a reservation. We arived 15' early and the guy ( don't know if he's a host) there said he doesn't have a table in the next 40 minutes. Yes, the restaurant was really packed. But well I had a reservation and we came on time. With the experience of working at busy restaurant as host I started stressing him out then we finally have the table within 10 minutes. Haha he looked so pitiful but we ended up tipping them 30%. The place was very nice and spacious in compared to other restaurants in Chinatown. The staff was very friendly even if they don't speak English very well. And they were VERY fast, food Came out literally 5 minutes after we ordered. Best service I ever gotten in Chinatown.

Yerba Buena seriously has the best french toast I've ever had in my life.  That is an understatement.  It's stuffed with Machego cheese, fried to perfection, thin, and topped with berries.  Our party of 8 ordered 4 orders of french toast on top of our individual entrees. Their version of the "eggs benedict" had ham and suckling pig on top of a small piece of baguette, served with salad and the thinnest pieces of potatoes I've ever seen. Definitely make a stop here for brunch if you are in NY and bookmark to try it!  Also, take advantage of their AYCD $12 deal for the first hour!

The amount of meat is sparse compared to the bread. The onion was bland. Know what you want before you step up to order and be specific about it. They asked my fiance if he wanted a drink to go with the meal and he said yes without thinking too much into it and feeling rushed. They didn't ask what kind and hurried him along to pick up. By the time we got to pick up, I asked what kind of drink he got and to which he answered I didn't even tell them but at this point we were just handed anything that they felt like giving us. Honestly I thought this was hilarious more than anything because I have heard about this "soup nazi" treatment from others. The one star is because the food just wasn't good. I've had way better cheesesteak from my college cafeteria.

Crunchy French toast whaaaaaat. Homemade tater tot breakfast bowl whaaaaat those are some pretty delicious taters ok those are the best damn tater tots around. Had the veggie bowl too it was good but blah compared to the French toast and tots. No frills spot just looks like an awesome old school diner. Such a chill spot. Food is on point.  I'll be back.... ...so my friend left her phone there we decided to get it the next morning so we can eat there again. I think she left it there for this very reason. Great freakin plan. We both had the Elvis waffle and chicken n waffle. Both were awesome. Can't wait to go back and try that juicy burger the table next to us ordered. This just may be my new favorite fat spot

Amazing. Took my friend to birthday dinner, we had a carafe of red wine, shared a roasted vegetable salad (highly recommend), and burgers.  They even served a birthday slice of blueberry crumb cake with a candle and tastefully no "happy birthday" song in French or otherwise! The service was great, the atmosphere is nothing like what I've experienced thus far in New York (all boroughs).  They're very thoughtful with the decor, and the service was by the far the best I've had- I overtipped generously. Our waitress was French and even the not-so-French servers delivered bread and olives with "bon appetit!".  Music was great, heard classics as well as your typical Wburg indie, but carefully selected. It's very romantic and a great place to share with friends and lovers.
I never write reviews.  But the food, service, and setting called for it.  Pancakes take you to a new place (of carb heaven).  A real jewel!

Although this is more popular as a take out place, the dine-in option is also pretty good. Pricing is reasonable and the food is delicious. Have been there 3 times in the last 2 months and will continue to dine here.

LOVE the food here. Had gnocchi, a panini with eggplant and the specials are always top notch.  Cannot go wrong here. Prices very very reasonable. Staff is courteous and decor is cute and pleasant. Very comfy. Don't forget to finish with a rainbow cookie! Best ever.  Once you come here you will return to try everything!

I think I found my new favorite sushi spot in the city.  We didn't have reservations on a Thursday night, and found that although it was pretty crowded, we were able to get seated in 5 minutes.  The ambience of FS is trendy and chic, the design clean and simple with a high tech vibe.  I love sashimi and the sashimi plate for 1 was definitely more than enough for one person- I actually shared it with my friend and it was still plenty.  The feshness of the fish and the selection was awesome.  The best sashimi- which doesn't surprise me, given the name of the establishment, was the salmon.  Melted in my mouth.  The combination of the food and the fact that it's a byob make this my new top spot in Philly.  The only thing that could use a little working on is the timing of how the food is brought out, but the waiters were super helpful, very pleasant and did not rush us into ordering.  I would go back to FS tonight and in fact, I already know where I'm going for my birthday in September!
Barcelona never disappoints!  The tapas are excellent and they have a good wine selection.

Cheese steaks, eh. ok Over abundance of patriotism, eh. ok. Having a sign that says "when ordering Speak english, this is America"...ignorant. Waiting in a long line, for what turned out to be mediocre food, in an establishment that probably makes tons of money- I wont be back

It is VERY CROWDED and a LONG wait. About 45 min - 1hr. Though you could order drinks and food at the bar if you are lucky to snag a table. We were lucky to snag a bar table while waiting but it's so crowded we felt claustrophobic with all these ppl shoved aside waiting.  An older couple asked if they can sit with us. They were from FL, but visit NY every 3 months and one is a NY native. We asked if this was "worth the wait" and he replied, that it's not the best Italian food, it's okay... you come here for the atmosphere. He said that it's full of tourists, so they don't really care if the quality is good or not because people usually don't come back. They didn't eat, just there for drinks. I totally agree. It's very crowded, alive and the decor is old school italian and classic which was nice. They won't let you bring your stroller to the table. (put in a coatroom) Bathrooms are nasty and small. Make sure to look at the menu, beforehand. The menus are on the wall and I couldn't read it since we were a little far.  Also they don't serve "white sauce" with cream. It's only Olive Oil, garlic etc. The bread was kinda dry and no butter/dipping sauce. We ordered the Shrimp White Sauce pasta and calamari appetizer.  Both were delicious and HUGE family style.  A lot of food for 2ppl and a baby. It actually tasted better the next day but it's not the best pasta i've had. I would go again  if we had a bigger group (of tourists)  and a reservation. (not with just hubbie and I since we could get better tasting food, cheaper elsewhere with less hassle)

Burgers are what we went for, and what we got! They were infact very good. The best burger I ever had? Well, not the very best, however, most likely in the top ten!  The cozy feel and service did also add to why one would try lunch here.
I still love this place....Chicken nachos are out of this world. Very consistent, and the employees are always very courteous and helpful.

I've been on a bit of a ramen kick lately and tried Nom Nom based on a friend's recommendation.  I had the miso and my companion had the Shio, both with a soft egg. The portions were huge and definitely worth the price, but the broth in both in the miso was too bland, and the shio, while heartier, was far too salty. I also wasn't impressed with the quality of noodle they used. I probably won't go back unless I happen to experience an overwhelming craving for the pork buns, which were as fantastic as everyone says they are. I've definitely had better. If you're interested in a more flavorful ramen experience, I would check out Hiro on 12th and Chestnut.

Our party of four showed up on a Sunday night to encounter a fantastic meal and great service. We really wanted to get the most out of what they had to offer.  We decided to go with two entrees and three appetizers...yes, five dishes total.  For the apps we went with the (divine) octopus salad, (the must-try) crispy sweetbreads and their (yummy) meatballs.  The octopus salad and sweetbreads were the stars of the apps.  Both dishes were really amazing and so full of deliciousness!  As for the entrees, we all shared the lamb shanks and milk dumplings.  Wow, these did not disappoint either.  Great meal and attentive service.  I'm looking forward to my next visit to Kefi!

Fantastic food, drink, and service. While the place may be so crowded at times that you'll wonder if you'll ever get served, the bartenders make each drink with their undivided attention--worth the wait. Plus, they always serve with a smile. Oh, and kudos on the burger.

we first tried this cart at the vendy awards a few weeks back.  and it blew us away.  they gave a lot of samplings and it was absolutely delicious so we just had to try the cart itself. so we went on a friday night.  i had the chicken and rice platter.  and they were nice enough to give us a falafel to munch on while we waited.  maybe the whole excitement of the vendys had made it taste even better.  or maybe it was a little off this night.  it was super tasty just not quite as tasty as i had remembered.  i want to go back because i want to believe that the vendys showed the true talent of the king.   definitely go if you are in the area.

Okay, The review is for take out tonight...It was okay...I called the order in and the guy said 30 minutes. I arrived 30 minutes later and my food was packed and ready to go...so I thought. I got back to my hotel and I was missing mint leaves and thai basil. These things go with pho...how could they forget. Other wise the pho and egg rolls I ordered were okay. Would I come back? No...the service is way to slow and the food just so so. This place might be okay for Vermonters, but not for the Los Angeles yelpers. Sorry Hong!

There are so many good things I could list about Dos Segundos, including the $4 special (Tecate and a shot of tequila), the tasty margaritas, the nachos, a certain cute server I know, etc., but I'm afraid I'd be here forever. And ever. And ever. Anyway, you're catching my drift, right? Just go to Cantina. Experience it. Drink some tequila. Eat a taco. Have a time. Call out of work the next day (you might have to). Go back for more once you sober up. Smoochies to you, Cantina! You're my BFF.

This isn't a deli, this is little Italy!  They have it all from grass fed meats, wild caught fish, cannoli/ pastry, specialty sandwiches to prepared foods.  All of it is amazing, and authentic! The guy in the back still had a thick Italian accent!  A little pricey, but you get what you pay for.

Corner Bistro - where basic betches go for basic burgers.  Really basic burgers is just about the perfect description for the burgers at Corner Bistro. I've had this place bookmarked for quite a while before finally visiting with my boyfriend and a couple of his bros.  All I've heard about CB was that they had "NY's best burgers" for pennies.  The pennies part was right - under $10 for a sit-down meal is kind of unheard of, especially in  that area.  However, I'd have to disagree with the "NY's best burgers" claim... the cheeseburger wasn't the worst burger I've ever had, but it definitely was not the best.  Not even close. The Bistro Burger here was probably the most standard cheeseburger + bacon you'll find in town - it reminded me of the kind you make in your backyard on the grill back in the suburbs... except I slightly prefer those over these.  Yes, they were cheap, but I might pay more for a more significant burger of a larger size somewhere else.  The fries were also very standard and not hot or crispy enough for me. The wait on a Saturday evening wasn't as bad as I thought.. maybe 15 minutes or so for a party of 5.  You basically show up and stand in line and wait to be seated.

I adored everything about this meal. The Walu was my favorite dish followed closely by the desserts. Chef came around to each table to see how everything was and all I could say is "It was brilliant". It's one of those meals where you leave feeling happy and content.

- It is always busy and bit caotic. Yes - It is expensive. Yes, but you can find good deals and some things are really worthed - It is smaller than it should and there are not enough seats for people who buy pizza, paninis etc and want to eat inside. Yes But This is an awesome shop, where you can find so many special products, some made by small high quality producers that until yesterday you could only find in Italy, and not in every shop. Yes, because the majority of these products you cannot find in standard supermarkets, but in gourmet shops. Then there is Barilla, Mulino Bianco, Nutella etc which you can find everywhere, and that now people around the world recognize and love. So far, all that I bought and ate was good: - fresh sea urchin from the seafood shop - jams and cookies - cold cuts - bread - hot paninis for lunch in the park .... It's not a place I could afford to shop everyday, but it's definitely a place where I would go to buy specialties. And I love specialties so I would go there often if I lived closeby! The only thing that Is not my taste is the pizza. It's good. But too thick for me. Too much.
Awesome pizza. Cool spot.
Try the spaghetti carbonara.  You won't be disappointed.
AMAZING! Dinic's! Termini! Amish Doughnut spot!!!

Given all the other reviews, I can't help but think our experience was a fluke. Ordered takeout and it was literally the worst Thai we've ever had. Drunken noodles were a stuck together glop with chicken so tough and dry we had to pick it out. Totally watery Panang curry with tofu that had no flavor, though the veggies were crisp so that was good. Tom yum soup also was like drinking water with spices dumped in, no balance or melding of flavors at all. I'll prob try once more given all other glowing reviews, but our experience was terrible.

You know it's good. You know there's a long line (get there at 12 as it opens and there's already a huge line!!). What else can I tell you? The thai short rib taco ($3) is life-changing and amazing. Why are people talking about the captain crunch burrito when the short rib taco exists? SO AMAZING

My mother came to visit me for a weekend, and she had never had falafel.  I didn't want to mess up her first experience on a gamble so I found this place on Yelp.  Best decision ever. We each had the falafel sandwich with green falafel.  It was amazing.  This is the way falafel is supposed to be- nice and fresh! The falafel balls were crunchy on the outside and delicious inside.  Lots of fresh veggies and hummus as well, and the hummus was fantastic.  My favorite part was the drink!  The mint ginger lemonade was so yummy, and I will be stopping here more often!  Mmmmmmm!!!  The biggest plus?  You cannot beat the price for the quality.   Helpful Hint:  There is only 4 or so counter seats so be prepared to go somewhere else to eat.  Washington Square Park and the Highline are within walking distance, and great places to enjoy your falafel in the warm months.

its funny how my review was taken down. This restaurant blows. everything is frozen and cross contaminated. Hendra is nice to people but in reality he talks behind the customers back. avoid at all cost zagat.com/b/philadelphia… - read below

I recommend the following plates: -philly cheese steak rolls (addictive) -french onion soup (good flavor) -fries (I'm usually not a fry fan.  These are good.) Good beer selection. Good happy hour specials. Lotsa "Slaintes" going on here!

Huge fan of their brunch. I have not tried the dinner yet, but that is a comin. My table really all hands down picked the pancakes as the favorite of the day. They were light and fluffy and had a nice zest to them. So delicious. I also had bacon with it and it was probably the best bacon that I have had at a restaurant since I arrived in New York. It wasn't too fatty and it was thick and delicious. I tried a piece of my boyfriends margarita pizza and that was equally as delicious. Just the right amount of salt and cooked perfectly. We got there at about noon on a Sunday and got a table pretty straight away. Maybe we were part lucky or maybe because we are getting old, noon is too early to be considered brunch time. Can't go wrong with a bloody mary ever, and there's was right in line with this.
Nothin' like hot, crispy, thick potatoes. Yum. A+ on their sauces by the way.

After reading so many negative reviews, i had my radar up but my good friend made reservations for my birthday and since it was for a Monday evening i figured, whats the worst that could happen. Service: pretty friendly and relaxed. We were late for our reservation but they did not give us any problem. Our biggest issue was it appeared as though they were VERY understaffed. Our waiter was very nice but did not check on us and i had to look for him. Food:  good tasting. Nothing extraordinary but definitely not bland. The appetizers were amazing. I tried the skirt steak medium well with cilantro mash. steak was great. mash was okay. It was happy hour all night btw and you'd think they would be watered down but they had some delicious and strong drinks for the specials. Overall: It was only 4 of us and it appeared its the spot to go for your birthday. A bit over hyped but We didn't feel rushed and had a great time. I just may go again and just stick to the weekdays then.

Good food coupled with fantastic customer service. Recently went in with a friend, and we had 2 taco orders, one Vegetarian, and one Chicken.  The chicken was a little dry, but seasoned very well, and not an issue for me at all.  The highlight however was the blackbeans, which were very tasty. The vegetarian tacos were with a great flavored squash, and some pickled onions for added kick. The salsa was pretty good, again not out of this world, but given the prices, far far above what you'd see in NYC. The customer service is really what put's this place over the top though.  The individuals working there are very attentive, and clearly focus on customer experience. Definitely worth a visit.

I was truly skeptical when I walked into Big Wong, it's shabby and not to clean looking. But I put that aside and was happy I tried a few dishes that were really great. My favorite was the salted fish rice. It's like fried rice with small flakes of salted fish in it and was so flavorful. Drink plenty of water after though! We also had the duck, pork, congee and a noodle dish. It's a great place for sharing and alternative to dim sum on a weekend. Plus there are a lot of bakeries in the area to get a light dessert after the salt and grease deluge.

My meal at Talula's was very good. And as stated by most, the atmosphere and service were very good. But as others have stated, I too had three issues with salt. My scallops were cooked perfectly but the bottoms were covered with salt. My chicken wing on the mushroom pate was very salty as well. We ordered radishes with anchovy butter that I had to send back. I thought maybe the anchovy butter was too much but I think it is a heavy hand with the finishing salt. They were returned quickly with much less salt. I am not a fan of their bread or desserts. So much so that we did not even have dessert due to a prior visit with dissapointment. A restaurant of this caliber needs a stellar pastry chef and consistency. And put the salt away. No better yet, put it on the table. Every one's taste for salt is different.
All it have to say is: "try the Rachael" you'll keep returning! Great food average decor not much ambiance but try the Rachael,
Much more Chinese than Chinese-American.  That's inviting for people like me, but not for my wife.  To each, his own.   Enjoy!

Good variety and flavor.  The shrimp tapas was good.  Those that should have at least been warm, were not.  Spanish wine was excellent.  Good to have variety in Hanover.  The place was full at 9 on a Tuesday.  Noisy.  And overpriced.

I enjoyed a fun Saturday night date with my husband at this charming neighborhood BYOB Italian restaurant over the weekend.  It was a delicious meal at a great price and we will definitely be back.  My craving for pasta hit around lunchtime on Saturday, and I was pleasantly surprised that I was able to get a reservation for that night - albeit at 9:30.  We drooled over the online menu, picked up a nice bottle of red and were seated promptly when we arrived for our reservation.  Service throughout the evening was very friendly.  There were a few minor delays, but the restaurant was legitimately packed. We started our meal by sharing the BLT salad, which was comprised of baby arugula, tomatoes, crispy pancetta and shaved parmesan nicely complemented by an appropriate amount of limoncello vinaigrette.  They split the salad onto two plates in the kitchen, which is always a nice touch.  For entrees the husband had a pork loin special with spinach and roasted potatoes in a white wine sauce while I had a pasta special of homemade fettuccine with sausage and wild mushrooms.  The pork loin was flavorful and properly cooked, but I think the poor guy had dinner envy because my pasta was out of this world fantastic!  The sausage, mushrooms, and sauce were all divine, but the noodles themselves would have been exquisite just with butter and parmesan.  I think taking advantage of all of the homemade pastas is the way to best enjoy Giorgio.  The portions were generous and we were sure we could not handle dessert . . . until we saw the creme brulee delivered to the table next to us.  Let's just say I am glad we made room for it. The only real downside was that the restaurant was loud.  I wouldn't usually dock a star for this, but it was skull-rattling, could-not-hear-the-waitress, could-not-have-a-conversation loud.  We had the misfortune of being seated in the upper room with two very large and very drunk bachelorette parties, so I am hoping it is usually a little better.  I am glad they were having a nice time, but when one group broke out a strobe light and started blowing their penis whistle party favors, a little polite intervention from the staff might have improved the night for other diners.  Oh well - if it is just regular "Saturday night loud" on our next trip, a star will be immediately added back.  Mangia Bene!

LOVE Louis' Lunch.  I originally went here because of a travel channel special I saw on burgers, and was definitely not disappointed.   I really like the place itself, this little vintage place.  The machines they use to cook the burgers look so neat and it's cool they've been using them for such a long time.   The burgers are amazing, and cooked in such a unique way.  I think it was the first hamburger joints in America, which is really cool.  The people working there are always pleasant and friendly.   I thought it was hilarious that no catsup was allowed!  Definitely one of the charming aspects of Louis' Lunch.

If you are looking for a good sports bar with amazing food Manhattan Proper should be at the top of your list. I visit MP regularly and keep coming back for more. I don't think I have ever had better bar food. They mushroom truffle burger is probably top 3 out of anything I have ever eaten, and I personally do not like red meat with the exception of MP's burger! It is seriously so good. And their fries are also amazing. If you don't get the burger than definitely get the truffle fries, your mouth will explode. If you want to eat healthy they also have a really good salad, the pear and gorgonzola. But get it with chicken because it adds a lot more flavor. I seriously love this place; its decently priced, they always have specials on the food and drinks and its a good crowd!
I love logans! From great food.to amazing deserts to take home food everything's awesome! Best customer servic Ever!! Thanks David! !!@

The restaurant feels a little overwhelming when you first enter, somewhat cramped with a menu the size of a lecture hall chalkboard. Despite this, on the Sunday morning we went there was a nice, relaxed atmosphere. There were a few other patrons scattered to the corners of the dining area and the servers were chatting casually behind the counter. I ordered the Irish Breakfast with toast, which consists of grilled (purple) potatoes, two eggs how you want them (over easy in my case), apple, and fresh tomato and mushrooms. All of this arrived only a couple minutes after the order was placed; however, the toast was just warm bread and I had to ask for it to be toasted further. I was initially leery of the purple potatoes, never having had them before, but they wound up being fine. In spite of the purple tone throughout they tasted like a garden-variety potato you'd pick up at the grocery store. The eggs were cooked well, with a thin, runny yolk and little firmness like I was expecting. I was slightly disappointed by the tomatoes and mushrooms. The tomato was very fresh and delicious, but the mushrooms were lukewarm and would have been improved with a little more heat. All in all I was satisfied with my meal. Sending back the toast was minor and fixed immediately, the waiter was very understanding. While not perfect, the mushrooms were delicious and the tomato was excellent. I had one major qualm: which was that the price on the big board for my meal was inaccurate. Besides that, I had a good experience, and would be happy going back.
Great place with great vibe and amazing pizza. All the dishes we tried were delicious and we will definitely come back soon.

This place is great! I've lived in Philly for 8 years and have yet to find a pizzeria that I was amazed by. Never hearing of Francoluigi's I moved to the neighborhood and now pretty much live over the place. Lucky. I have yet to try the dinning room, but the take out is friendly & the food is beyond good. Best Pizza in Philly thus far. Coming home after work the entire block is filled with the irresistible aroma of baking bread and delicious pizza.

This place is great.  Good drinks, too.  It is good every time we go.  Sitting in the bar area is not so fun for a meal, but that's a small gripe.  It's a joy to eat this food.  And to drink the tequila. The tostadas de ceviche are always worth it.  Any of the ceviche, really.  Also  good is the salmon with mole.  Although, this would be better with salmon from Alaska. This place is honest and filled with talent.

A must-go every time i'm in the city. Thick flavorful pork-bone broth, springy ramen, perfectly cooked tamago (egg) and juicy succulent pork buns. Come 15-30 min before its opening hours to escape the otherwise insane lines! Cash only.

Wedge and Fig is awesome! It is close to my office, so I try to hit it up on a pretty regular basis. It really fills a void in the 5 block radius around the Constitution Center, where restaurant options are limited to either pizza, Chinese, Starbucks, or Dunkin Donuts. I have tried multiple items on the menu, and never been disappointed. My goal is try every single sandwich (however, I don't think my thighs approve of this). My two favorites are, without a doubt, the Blue Figs and the Shackamaxon. The Blue Figs is a savory-and-sweet mix of blue cheese, prosciutto and figs on pretzel bread. The Shackamaxon features creamy brie and turkey with mango on thick, buttery challah bread. Both are absolutely divine. I've also had a made-to-order grilled cheese here which rocked my socks, and don't get me started on the amazingness that is their bacon-lattice macaroni and cheese pie - it is to DIE for. They also have a great selection of homemade cookies and cakes for desserts.
pizza is good.. but not worth the line..  nice view though
The food here is GREAT!!! I had breakfast and dinner here in 1 wk. The hostesses are very nice and the place is clean. I would recommend the fish, beef ribs and yellow rice with oxtails....
Best spicy ramen ive had other than Mono Mono...Get the extra spicy ramen...its amazing and they put the hot sesame on the side so you can add as much as you want

We ordered a couple of dishes including a Mutton Biriyani. The Mutton in the Biriyani was horrible. It was so damn rubbery that we simply didn't eat more than a bite. The furniture looks horrible. They probably got it from a dumpster.

OH my GOODness, was this good Decor was fabulous. You walk into the basement, but it's not so clear to the average eye.They play up the fact there are no windows by adding tree lined rows to the deco, plus they have oodles of space you wouldn't imagine in NY I played the "screw" menu card & just asked the waiter, What are your favorites? We got them all except for something that was fried... -cebiche limeno: I WILL be having dreams about this -empanadas: just your average empanada, but try the green stuff -Lomo Saltado: VERY japanese themed, like teriyaki flavoring. I wish I knew there would be cilantro, but still very good -corvina inca: Typical Peruvian fish, hard to tell what was fish and what was potato until you bit into it and could tell the difference not suggested, but ordered -Camarones Cuzco: oh my the yellow (orange) rice served with this was phenomenal and the sauce on top of the shrimp was pretty good We also got some Pisco's which were beautifully decorated and tastier than expected for a brandy concoction! This place is really cute & good for almost any occasion. Not too fancy where you can't just walk in, but nice with parents, dates, celebrations

I stopped here for lunch and was seated in the tiny foyer area which was great for people watching but I have NO idea what the rest of the restaurant looks like. I had the Roasted Turkey wrap and was delighted it was also served with a side salad. For someone that went through an obsession with counting calories I thought the calories looked a little low for the amount of food served (about 350) but I am far from an expert on these things and kind of stopped caring. Overall - fresh food and quick service - I love a good 'healthy food' joint so this place fared well for me and I'd go back again.

Best chicken biscuit i have ever had. Unbelievable gravy and radish combination. They put an enormous chicken finger on a homemade biscuit, which lays on a bed of radish. Also salmon biscuit is great. The guy who owns it is the man, so nice and friendly. He gave me a free french donut. Two annoying things -- the door to the restaurant is a nightmare. He should get rid of that door. It is a swinging glass door that doesn't open all the way, and is really heavy to open, especially when its crowded. Secondly, it takes a while to make the sandwiches, but that's not really a big deal.

Okay honestly I've never eaten here.  The price is too expensive.  But the drinks during happy hour....whoo hoo.  I love thier mojitos.  I've been there a couple of hours.  One 6 dollar drink will knock you off your azz.  It's my favorite standby. Due to the high ratings I will not be cheap next time and try thier food.  lol!

It's kind of expensive for the portions, but just like being back in Madrid. The Biff doesn't care much for Spain, but I'm a huge fan. They had self serve sangria, and while the bocadillos were bomb the tortilla conjured so many memories of Spain. It was perfect. On the way out we got samples of sublime jamon Serrano. What a way to round off our visit!

I know culturally Portuguese and Spanish places aren't welcoming of all cultures (aka can be pretty prejudice) but this place took the cake the other night I was there. Brought a friend from out of town there because I heard it was good but when the bar tender decided he didn't even want to look our way the ENTIRE night I knew this wasn't the place for me. I came after work....dressed business casual even. Can't understand why I was basically ignored. Oh well, moving along....

I've come here consistently in the past 5 years.  Great place for sushi!  Near the 2,3,4,5,R,A trains.  Restaurant could use an upgrade.  I typically order the sashimi platter, and just love how they put it together.  Their soups are always delicious too.  If you're in the area, and craving sushi - stop by.  You will enjoy the food for sure!

We had a gathering of 5 couples, husbands and wives, who are foodies and picky about the minutiae of fine dining in NYC. All of us were taken by this wonderful restaurant -- brilliant and thoughtful service, inventive and delicious appetizers and entrees, and relaxing and inviting ambiance. This was a memorable dining experience that we will share with others. The pricing is very reasonable, the variety of offerings on the menu are vast even though truth be told it isn't a long list and the decor transports one to another time (James Bond film from the 60's?). Go!

I went here for a University graduation reception several years back. I was invited to join my 3 colleagues (Dean's Office) for a holiday luncheon. Our new Dean, whom I report to (dotted line) treated us. His son recently had his wedding reception there. It was a very snowy day. The views overlooking Manhattan was non existent, yet the snow covered hills were a sight to behold none the less. It was empty for lunch (maybe because of the storm). It is owned by the same people who own The Manor, not to far from there. I had sirloin steak, very rare and they delivered it just perfect. Deserts were decadent. They should be ruled obscene. You need to go to judge for yourselves. The appetizer and main course, however nice is a pre-cursor to desert. I plan to take my wife and family often. Lunch with tip came to $60 per. A very generous and nice Dean I work with for sure!

I am currently eating here in the 4th of July. Yelp thinks it's closed, is wrong. Super good cocktails and also cheap beer. Awesome food, not expensive. Great wood interior, good people, great food and drinks, what else do you want? I'll be back.

I work in boring and interesting food barren Midtown West.  Because of this I was pleasantly surprised to find CAfe Hanamizuki.  It's this quaint and almost trendy cafe located around the corner of 29th and 7th on the north side of 29th Street. Um, the food was delicous! The fact that they offer spam doesn't hurt either. I went into to get the daily special for $9 which is two rolls with an appetizer, miso soup and pickles.  However once I went in I got two rolls for $2.50 each, a cup of tea and a Japanese Chiffon Roll for $5.     My co-workers and I all got the Hawaiian roll with spam and we loved it! The presentation of the food and customer service was unheard of for that price in this area. I love having this cafe in this area and can't wait to stop by after work to grab a quick snack!  I'm a fan and am so glad these guys opened nearby!

Stopped for breakfast and ordered the steak burrito. Very good. I also ordered a side of beans. Kind of pricy at about $11 plus tip. The burrito was good but didn't come with anything like some type of side dish. I believe the staff that cooked and waited on me were the owners. My waitress was very, very nice. The restaurant was very clean. I will go back to try lunch. I just know it's going to be good.

This is an unassuming hole in the wall kind of place. The sliders are awesome and are worth making a trip for. They grind their own beef. The fries are also excellent. I wouldn't call this place cheap but it's par for the east village course. I wish they had a few more beer options but that's reaching for a complaint.
wow the food here is amazing. I think i will be back soon, those black beans though take it easy on that or else you will pass some crazy gas!!! other than that great 5 stars from me

I now know how people can live off of ten dollars a week in Manhattan. 1 dollar for a set of four tasty fried dumplings, pork and chive is the way to go. The sesame pancake is like a little stuffed fluffy piece of heaven, and more filling than I expected it to be. The woman in the big hoops behind the counter calling out the orders, and the assembly of homeless people sitting at one of the tables added something a little extra to the ambience.

I have been going to Jose Tejas for 15 years. It has been awhile since I have been there. I was able to go there last weekend and the place hasn't changed one bit. The atmosphere is great but it can be little loud at times. The food is fantastic and everything is made fresh. Their prices are reasonable and their portions are big. I would recommend this place to anyone who is looking to eat a great meal and have a good time.

We had tickets at the Galapagos Art Space (Floating Kabarette) and had to pick a place for dinner....referencing TimeOut's Food & Drink Awards, my choices were: A) Traif B) Pies N Thighs C) Maisson Premiere Once I read about Traif's piggy goodness, I didn't need anymore convincing.  Maybe I took the fun out of it (or the foreplay), but I saw their menu beforehand and knew exactly what I wanted.  Here's what we ordered: - Strawberry Cinnamon Glazed Baby Back Ribs: a definite must get - Bone Marrow: it was good on toast. Gelatin fatty goodness. - Bacon Wrapped Dates: the dates were too sweet - Sweetbreads, Artichokes, Asparagus, & Maitake: I didn't love it and it was my entree (I had orderer's remorse) - Seared Foi Gras, Sunnyside Up Egg, Ham Chips, Fingerlings, Maple, & Hot Sauce: very good & versatile (you could eat this for breakfast or dinner) - Bacon Doughnuts, Dulce de Leche, & Coffee Ice Cream: another must get (eat the doughnuts with your hands, don't split them with a fork or you'll smush them) Their prices are really reasonable, we received a palette cleansing amuse bouche (strawberry gazpacho), there's a garden view area in the back, and nothing is as reassuring as an open kitchen.  Get reservations - the place was packed and we were able to pick our lonely reserved table when we walked in.

Very delicious hoagies and the people that work here are wonderful. The wait time is not very long at all and they have some of the best cheesesteaks around. Maybe even the best in the city. I've tried their cheesesteak, the buffalo chicken cheesesteak, and turkey & cheese hoagie. The only minor thing I would say is that the buffalo chicken cheesesteak had a little too much bleu cheese. However, that was nothing compared to its deliciousness. Though I wish they had sides such as fries, that doesn't take anything away.
Nota typical.chinese food. Clean, Good presentation and foods taste good. Defonitely recommended. Maybe fried chicken need to deep fried more. I like it very crispy

I had quite an enjoyable time at Southwark one very cold night when I was just looking for somewhere warm to go. The decor could be considered outdated (although I enjoy the homey feel) The bartenders obviously knew what they were doing. I particularly enjoyed the one with a dry sense of humor and a whole lot of knowledge (although some might find him to sound sarcastic) Had the farmhouse app. (meats, cheese, fruit) really nice selection and a lovely presentation and a special app. five stars for both. As others have said, this place can be addicting, and sometimes Southwark will just pop into my head and I will have to take a trip.

An excellent experience.  I had been here once before years ago so when I wandered by yesterday evening I decided to stop in.  They had an excellent Cheverny Sauvignon Blanc.  That's one of the best wines I've first tasted in ages.  The market soup was flavorful, cream based, yet very delicate.  The cod was delightful.  Fresh, well prepared.  The ingredients were all top notch.   I'd love to stop in once a week.

Perfection, as long as you go early.  My friends and I try to have lunch as soon as they open, because this place is so good it is almost always crowded after that!  This place made me truly appreciate bean curd, which is wonderful in their bibimbap.  Most of the staff is great, especially the older lady we had most recently who was more of a mom than a waitress.

I have found my Pho Nirvana. It is what every Yelper has said who loves this place. All they do is chicken and they do it right. Broth is crazy outrageous.  Even more so,  the spicy habanero-spiked sauce they give you to dip the chicken in. Cafe Su Da is totally legit.   And they give you a huge to-go cup to sip on.   Will be back soon.

For this area of town, this place is great. I really enjoyed my time here. Sadly, I don't think without googlemaps or a GPS system, I'll ever find the place. And luckily I ride a bike most places; this place is far and out of the way. But the beer is awesome. More importantly, the people there know beer. They love beer. They know what goes with what and they make great recommendations...like this one: Go to Memphis Taproom.

I still really like Istanbul cafe. However, I've found that when I want Turkish food now (which is pretty often because it's AWESOME!), I choose to go to Saray in West Haven. Not only is it cheaper, but also BYOB, which is just about my favorite thing in the entire world. Peace.

Beer list overrated The food is good. We especially enjoyed the pig tails and pig pot pie. The pig is the star. However, after all of the trumpeting of the beer list, I was expecting more. Maybe Philly is just too good a beer town and we are all spoiled, but there are lots of places with comparable beer lists, or even better beer lists.

I have no choice but to keep coming back for the food cuz its hard to get decent chinese food around here but i keep getting disappointed.........i specifically asked for more garlic/scallion for my order but as they ran out of the chicken leg i wanted they replaced it with a duck leg and left out the sauce.  the dish is just incomplete without that sauce man.....and i had to walk a distance to go pick it up.  i called them and asked them for the manager's name cuz i know he's not around at this time (1:44am) but the guy just said come another day and speak to him and hung up on me.  GREAT SERVICE RECOVERY!!   i'm going back there to get to the bottom of this.......

Through a freak accident, I ended up eating breakfast and dinner at Balthazar.  It was equally good to start and end the day. Balthazar sweeps you into its cool French atmosphere. I started my day with an egg-white omelet that was as light as a pillow. The coffee kept me flying for hours. Dinner was oysters, fish, and some cocktail mixology. Good stuff. Next time I'm going for the breakfast-lunch-dinner trifecta.

Really 'Tiny' but very very good. We were there on a hot Summers night it was probably 90 out at 9PM. But once inside & seated we ate as if it was Winter with stuffed pigs foot & wonderful food! We were fortunate enough to be with a French friend & she enlivened the meal by conversing with the owners in French. Actually there were many French speaking patrons & we felt like we were transported to Paris for a few hours..... Lovely hostess, terrific chef, husband & wife team. Can't wait to go back!
Great place! We came party of 3 , orders several appetizers... all of were great ! Service is good Nice vibe , good music My wife has already said that we will be back If she says so , we will

We were not that impressed w/ the menu. The wurst's were decent but overpriced and none of them come on a roll...I know that's the German way, but this is the U.S.A. and we like our dogs on a bun! The spaetzle was very good. The place has a cool interior design and the outdoor area was enjoyable. The german band was good, but the whole thing is a little too contrived. Also, the security guy's are way to obvious and overdone.

I love the decor. I also loved that my waiter suggested a meal for me, made tasteful jokes, filled my water glass often and brought out my food in a timely fashion. I can't for the life of me remember what I had. Not a good sign. I'm sure it was okay, though.

This popular restaurant in the East Village is always bustling popular with the young crowd strolling up and down this corridor and it helps that is right by the movie theater and NYC dorms. The cavernous dimly lit interior in dark wood pub/Brasserie feel with a fairly extensive menu and specials. The service is pretty decent, friendly and most are easy on the eyes. But what about the food? Does the crowd of eaters equate to good food? We took our friends from out of town (actually from out of the country) here during their recent visit. They wanted to see the NYC 'nightlife' of East Village and certainly there is not place better than here. We started with a couple appetizers: Artichoke Flatbread and fried calamari. Entrees the NY Strip, beef goulash special and roasted flounder. The table loved the appetizers although the Italians was curious that the calamari was served with a marinara sauce here. The beef was cooked as ordered (med well), the goulash was rich , smoky and beef tender. The roasted flounder deboned, cooked right, flakey and very good. Overall, everyone was very happy with the meal. The guest loved the vibe although it was a tad loud but manageable. So yes, the crowd justifies why The Smith is popular. Food that is good. Hopping nightlife of the East Village and people watching at its best.

Food is awesome! Bartenders are super cool. Decor is cozy...oh and the micheladas will be my drink of summer. A great place to grab a drink or eat with your friends before a show at Music Hall or walking around on the weekends. Seriously, go check it out. I spend way too much time there!

Not sure the fuss about it! My sister loves this place. It is her must go place when she comes to NY. For me... just this time maybe (too much calorie consumed in one snack). The portion is generous, the fries are good (a little salty especially with sauce), but not as special as I expected. The place is small and the seats are limited, easily to get crowded.

I really like this place a lot. Ordered their beef salad, because my friend had recommended it to me, It was really good. I also had some pizza and some grilled pork, which i had no idea what some of the stuff they added, but it was really tasty. I wanted to try their pastas but i was stuffed. Will try it next time i come back here.

Definitely overpriced and I was not pleased with the coffee. The barista actually said to me, "I steamed this milk wrong. It has too many bubbles, see?" and then did nothing to correct it. And it wasn't hot! I love the atmosphere though - even though most of the tables wobble. It's really cute and gay friendly, which is nice. Kind of on the border of a sketchy location (it is located directly across from housing projects), but the area is cleaning itself up.

Dined with a few folks and had a great overall experience. Personally, I love the west village and this place didn't disappoint! It was pretty busy for a Wednesday night. The ambiance was great and there were four of us so we didn't have to make reservations; we only waited about 15 minutes or so. Let me begin with the drinks- I started with the pomegranate martini and was not really a fan. Another ordered the "jagger" and raved about it. We ended up getting the raspberry mojito which was delicious. We all ordered different dishes and tried every one- the lamb dish was amazing, the yellow fin tuna (my dish) was great and the sauce was light and tasty. The sea bass was another great dish and the fennel potato puree was so so good. Oh, and the chicken was just okay. We ended with the warm flourless chocolate cake with malted milk ice cream- let's just say there were no leftovers, not even a crumb left! The waitress was very friendly and attentive throughout the entire night and the bartender was super nice. I'll definitely come back! I hear the brunch is pretty awesome so I'm looking forward to coming back soon.

Dim sum is pretty good. Tasty and not too oily. Selection is less than I am used to (I am from Toronto), but it will do. Have the push carts..we can on a Saturday. They have the basic dim sum. The bo lay tea is actually quite smooth compared to other tea houses. We drove 45 mins to come here, worth it and will be back.

Landmarc is my casual neighborhood go-to place that is actually quite far from my real hood but with down to earth dishes, great selection of wines and an upbeat vibe, has become a favorite of mine for years. Deliciously charred steaks with a variety of yummy sauces to choose from, daily pastas like the buttery linguine con vongole, some of the best burgers I've ever had glazed in fat, crispy flavorful fries, plump mussels cooked in a sauce so good (dijonnaise and shallots, parsley & white wine being my faves) that you'll be sopping it up with your leftover bread, succulent lamb chops and bone-fucking-marrow that will make you want to pick those bones up to suck em dry. I adore their bite sized desserts, priced at $4 and made for those (like myself) who are not big on desserts but just want a small taste. I've ordered the "one of each" sampler, for $16 that can easily satisfy a big group. Ice cream and sorbets are served in mini sized cones and yes, they offer cotton candy for the child in you if you ask nicely. The consistency of the food has been off as of late but on good days the food is still solid. One of the reasons I keep coming back is their very low mark up on fantastic wines with a selection appropriate for all budgets. Landmarc also has a selection of wines by the half bottle. As long as they offer my favorite bottle of Cloudy Bay Sauvignon Blanc for $42 to pair with my meal, I'll continue to return. They don't take reservations unless you're a party of 6+ (max 11) but I've never waited longer than 20 minutes for a table. The bar area is quite small so if you're lucky to find a seat good for you, if not I'd suggest waiting for your table outside. There are two bathrooms upstairs and one downstairs which is unfortunately right by where they grill the meats. If you haven't eaten yet you'll be tempted to steal a steak while waiting for the bathroom. The menu is nothing innovative or new but Landmarc serves well as a homely place to dine-in and hang out for those in the area or those like me who will come all the way to Tribeca in order to spend a night noshing on my medium rare rib-eye with peppercorn sauce and downing a couple bottles of vino.
Service can be a bit slow but nice.  Food is OK.  Great place to get something after being at NJPAC.

I have tried three times unsuccessfully to order a lunch delivery for 20 people to a client this coming Wednesday.  Each time the employee who has answered the phone has provided the most horrible customer service experience of my lifetime.  After 10 painful minutes on each call trying to place my order, each time the person (male) asks me to call back another time.  Regardless to say I will never in my life order from this restaurant for 1 or 30 people.  Surely this entire company will be out of business in no time due to the quality of employees answering the phones.

The good , the bad, and the Really ! The good... The wait staff We had two dinners here and both times the wait staff and food runners where great, our waiter on 9/9, Joe, in particular, extra good. Attention to detail, good attitude and they got the orders right. The food was good also. Lobster Roll, Hamburger, Cuban sandwich, scallop salad and desserts. All tasty and well presented. The DJ on Saturday night was very good. The bad. ... the hostess. We ate there two evenings 9/7 and 9/9 and both nights requested one of the upper booths. both nights the hostess said they were reserved and we could not be seated there even though I requested them on Open Table. And you guessed it, both nights the booths were not seated the entire time we where there. Empty....... The Really.! ..... the hostess....again As we were leaving on Monday 9/9 she asked if everything was ok... even though she walked pass us a dozen times crammed in at a little two top while a large booth behind us was empty the entire time.... Really...  . When I am back in town in a month, if the same hostess is there, I will turn around and walk out !

A real find! Very nicely done steaks with a variety of sauces to choose from. Excellent and unusual appetizers. Great wine list. Surprisingly affordable, too. Although it's not the best place to bring a child, if yours is well-behaved and used to restaurants, they actually have a child's menu, crayons and the like. Totally enjoyable experience.

Review doesn't include food!!! Beer selection was top notch.  Great feel to the place, including a Flemish, French and English (maybe more?) speaking bartender who ended up being the manager.   Overall just a great experience.  Exactly what I hoped for when first learning about this Belgian beer haven.

I will not come back to Grimaldi's again. This was my first and last time. Yet another case of mediocrity with hype from people who have not had good pizza. This is clearly a place you take a tourist to see pictures of how old New York used to be and to walk around in the DUMBO area. Once they're starving, anything tastes a lot (maybe a ton in some cases) better. The red and white checkered plastic table cloths gross me out. How the heck are you supposed to disinfect these things? Elbows catching on semi-sticky plastic is not an appetizing asset. Anyway, onto the pizza. The toppings were good, but our server put olives and onions on our pizza after we had only specially ordered mushroom and sausage. How hard can it be to screw up toppings and they usually taste about the same across the board unless if they're rotten (they weren't here). Soda comes in a plastic bottle (so not old-fashioned). There was no wait on a Friday night a month ago, but we left half a pizza and did not bother to take it home since it was that bad. The sauce was skimpy and the crust flavorless. I think people go here for the location since it has breathtaking views of the Brooklyn Bridge. Too bad Grimaldi's doesn't face it from inside because then there would be a positive of coming here. My quest continues for above average pizza in NYC...

It should be noted that I am a relative noob when it comes to Indian food. The first few times I tried Indian, my meat dishes were sweet (rosewater lamb and something else), and I am no fan of sweet-flavored meat. Also, I'm a slightly picky eater (onions are my enemy). So it was with just a bit of hesitation that I ordered from Ekta on Sunday. I will never hesitate again. I ordered for four people, so we got a good sampling of what Ekta offers. Within 25 minutes of placing my order, there was a knock at my door. There stood a plumpish Asian man with a huge smile, a red checkered shirt, and a big, blue necktie holding a bag of food. I only live a few blocks from Ekta, so he walked my delivery over, and the food was still thoroughly hot by the time he arrived. I know it's not an original idea, but I love the labeling of the food containers. I had the tandoori chicken, which was succulent and tasty. But my friend got the butter chicken, which was truly outstanding. I've been thinking of it ever since. We also tried the chicken tikka masala and chicken curry, both of which were praised by my friends. The only bump in the experience was the naan -- we ordered three kinds: plain, garlic, and potato. Onion naan was delivered instead of potato naan, and it wasn't awesome. Neither was the garlic version. I'd stick to just plain naan in the future.

I love southern food, and from the size of the line outside I figured I was in for a treat.  While the venue is beautiful, the food was extremely disappointing.  The gumbo was bland and boring, and the greens were flavorless, dry and cold.  But at least they got the color right.

This is one of my favorite lunch trucks and there are not many! Get a few tacos 2/$6 or 3/$8 The Chicken Satay is my favorite out of the tacos but I usually mix it up with two satay and one short rib. The Cap'n Crunch Burrito is a must have on your first visit!  Then get some bubble tea while you are at it. I have been meaning to try the Veggie Burger because I have heard nothing but good things even from my non-vegetarian friends! The truck is hard to miss among the many many trucks on Ludlow. It is at the end closest to 30th Street Station. If you go during prime lunch time you are going to have to wait, but the line and service is definitely quick!

We decided to try this place after we tried Fernandes down the road. We walked in and they told us it would be at least an hour wait.  So we decided to go the bar...we waited for a few people to get up as their table was ready.  We sat down and waited for about 20 minutes until FINALLY the the bartender came over and said "yeah" .  I couldn't even believe he said that.  We ordered a 1/2 pitcher of Sangria since we figured our table would be ready shortly since we waited so long at the bar.  The bartender didn't even ask if we wanted to look at menu and eat at the bar.  After that I was pretty much fed up, I called Fernandes and made a reservation there and we paid our bill and left.
obsessed - if you haven't been .. just go.

Time is just making this little place better!  If you haven't tried it yet - GO!  They don't accept CC's and do not have an ATM, but it's worth popping by an ATM elsewhere . . . friendly, eager staff - great little produce section - but best of all is the authentic Mexican cuisine in the back!  Wow!

This is strictly a dessert place...so don't come here for the food.  I mean...it wasn't bad...but it wasn't that great either.  It was just ok.  I had the chicken cesar salad.  The chicken was WELL DONE...like it was too tough to eat...and there was too much dressing...it just was a bad combination...a BAD SALAD.  The only thing that redeemed this place...was the oreo cookie cheesecake...OMG...it was amazing!!! So skip the food and just come here for dessert!

I should start out by saying that my mouse cursor just hovered over the five star space for a few seconds.  Honestly - the only reason I went with four stars is that I want to try a few other Ph places before I decide this place is really a five - I'm a novice to Vietnamese cooking in general. Basically I'm comparing this to Vietnam in China Town - and for the money I'd go here every time. Long story short - I am a major fan.  This place is amazingly fast, dirt cheap and very tasty.  Menu is a bit hard to get through if you don't realize what you're there to get... essentially it's all noodle soup (which is what Ph is... I found out after the fact...).  I got the gi cun - fabulous summer rolls in the upper left of the menu - and the Ph Tai... basically sliced beef in a noodle soup. With the soup bowls - get the small. I got the large and it's essentially just more broth.   Waitstaff is fast and furious - but once your order is in you need to flag one down if you need something - because they apparently won't bother you again. This place is cash only - so plan ahead!

Brussel sprouts excellent, labne was great, citrus trout was good, risotto we could have done without...didn't like it. The malbec wine was nice and the dessert called Candy Bar had an odd first taste to it but then melted into a chocolate lovers dream...super chocolate. All in all a great place to go for some really good food.

"I liked it, but I won't be back." That was my mom's final assessment of The Marshal. My boyfriend agreed with her. Tough crowd. I'd put it this way: "I liked it, but I'd only go back if I was already in the neighborhood." Since I almost never go to Hell's Kitchen (who does?), then I guess we're all saying the same thing... The meal was tasty enough. The butcher's block was a stand out dish -- three sliced meats, three cheeses, and two dips. The fresh honey comb was such a treat and the mustard literally bursted with flavor (the seeds popped with each bite!). The block came with toasted baguette, but the slightly charred daily bread also paired nicely with the spread. For our mains, the men got both mac n cheese options--solid, but not wows. The ladies stuck with the apple, sunchoke, and micro greens salad. The greens were peppery and light, but the salad was weighed down by an oversupply of sliced apple. If I sound unenthused, it's because I was. It just wasn't a very exciting meal. And, the menu didn't have that much to offer. But, like I said, a good Hell's Kitchen option if you're in the area. Then again, why are you in Hell's Kitchen??  Grab the NQR and head south!

I live literally a couple doors down from Manhattan, have ordered on a regular basis, and have always had great service and product.  However, my last order really sucked.  The pizza was cold, the crust was at least 1/3 of the entire pie, I ordered extra sauce (which wasn't added), and the pizza was burnt. I called again tonight to hopefully have them redeem themselves (I even mentioned how awful my previous order was).  The guy on the phone gave me $5 off (totally unexpected, but quite nice).  I proceeded to order my usual -- x-sauce, pepperoni, banana peppers (sometimes a mix with jalapenos).   I was really surprised, especially after having just complained and even receiving a discount -- my pizza arrived ICE cold.  WTF I live a couple doors down, and can't get a hot pizza?  Plus, I counted literally 8 slices of banana pepper and 7 pepperoni.  Really how incredibly chintzy is that ?  Without the discount that small pizza would have been $12.  Plus, it was also really well done, and was black in spots.   I don't know what to say, other than I will not be ordering from them in the future.  There are a TON of pizza places in Burlington, why should I give my hard earned money for a crappy product?

I've been eating at Su Xing for at least 6 years and was so glad to have some place to go when Harmony was sold and went down hill.  In all that time I've only ever had one dish that I didn't care for.  That was the sprial seaweed - which I don't think is even on the menu anymore. The food is excellent, plentious and the place is hospital clean.  As if that were not enough, the pricing is extremely affordable, especially the lunch specials.  They are mostly $7 before taxes and tip and include soup, side dish, entre and hot tea. I had an attack of panic a couple years back when I came by and it was closed, but was releived to see that they were just expanding into the next building. This is currently, and has been for several years straight, my favorite place to eat in Philadelphia.

Little Fish is non assuming. It is small and intimate. The menu changes frequently with fresh catches. All of our dishes were excellent. The overarching theme was that the flavor of the fish were not overpowered but shone. The accompanying veggie combos were unique and complimented the fish well. TIPS *Remember it's BYOB (with very few options if you choose not to bring booze, like iced team and one soda). *Make reservations as this place is TINY!

The first couple times I went to PYT last summer the burgers were satisfying and interesting. I had the Korean BBQ burger, which was kinda disappointing cus it's just a burger with kimchee on it, no Bbq or other flavor. The other , lobster burger was way better. The adult milkshakes are really good, but they charge me an extra 4 dollars for "extra" oreo. Which is a joke because mcdonalds puts a ton extra and doesnt even charge...my little topping rant. Don't ask for extra! Not worth it. When I returned later that year my sister was visiting from new York and we thought PYT was cool and interesting for her to visit. This time the service was spotty. The waitress overcharged for alcohol in the shake when I didn't get alcohol in it. Thank goodness I asked for the reciept she realized her mistake. But claimed she couldn't give us the original reciept. Needless to say my sister was not impressed by her average burger, for all the hype we gave. when the burgers arrived, my bf and I decided to split a classic type burger. And my sister got her own. All the burgers that day for some reason were tiny! The bun was bigger than the meat! So much for "craaaaziest "burgers. It was dried and mediocre and pathetically small. How could they ever serve someone that! At least match the bun with the burger ! Bad note: Right now it's just trendy and mostly meh. Food isn't as good, no longer worth the price and the super obnoxiously hipster staff kinda irritate me. And ending on a good note : I do stop in every now and then for an alcoholic milkshake.Who knew that alcohol could make a milkshake better!  Just kidding. Alcohol makes everything better. Ps. I have also shown up there in my pajamas and sit down just  for a milkshake, and the staff were still nice. Thanks hipsters!

Nomad's is huge and has plenty to keep you occupied. They offer laser tag, black light mini golf, mini bowling, pool, arcade games, a climbing wall, two full size basketball courts, a cafe and possibly more that I didn't notice. Certain things are kind of expensive, but what isn't these days? Laser tag is $7.75/person for 15 minutes which I think is kind of a ripoff. But I don't have anything to compare it to, so maybe that is an OK price. Overall this is definitely a place to check out at least once.

This was the easiest five star review I've ever given. I've never been so wholly blown away by a restaurant. I simply can't say enough good things about it. But I'll try... Oh I almost forgot, there was something really annoying about this place - I tried so hard for a few days to make reservations and their answering machine did not pick up. It just rang and rang and then some automated thing about calling back another time. It was frustrating because I wasn't about to give up this experience. Finally, on the third day I was able to leave a message and someone called me back in the hour and easily fit me in the next night. PHEW!!! close call. Okay, back to the rave... We arrived about thirty minutes ahead of our reservation (still trying to figure out the MTA) and expected to wait. Instead, we were seated instantly. The place is small and dim and packed and so perfectly warm. Even though it was close quarters I didn't feel uncomfortable. Rather, I felt friendly and welcome. Like I was dining in my best friend's house. The staff was a well orchestrated dance. We never once felt we needed anything. Everyone was in a lovely rhythm of filling the water glasses and clearing the plates. Everything was exceptionally timed. I was just so impressed. Drink options abounded and it was hard to make a decision but I did enjoy the run little piggy. It had a bacon salt rim that was so unique and fun. Loved it. We started with a pear salad. It was freshest of fresh pear, mixed greens, almonds, dried cranberries, parmesan tossed in a vinaigrette. My mother has already duplicated this recipe twice. A truly lovely dish. After that the broccoli rabe over texas toast with a fried egg. We saw the people at the table next to us enjoying this and knew it was for us. Dynamic dish and a brilliant use of ingredients. One can not eat enough broccoli rabe. Probably my favorite part of this meal (aside from everything else) was the salt and pepper shrimp. It was tossed in a sriracha sauce with pineapple and sweet potato chunks. Easily one of the most memorable dishes of my life. So inspired in its simplicity. The shrimp was fried but almost in a tempura way. It wasn't heavy or greasy but just a lovely crisp. Each bite with pineapple cooled the sriracha in a gorgeous way. Just do this. Still delicious but a little less memorable we had the duck confit nestled in a bed of barley and pig cheeks (my favorite pig part). At the end of the meal we loosened our waist bands and allowed ourselves one final indulgence (of the day). The bacon, dulce de leche donuts with the coffee ice cream was dessert bliss. They were very fluffy and yeasty and almost like little bits of sugar air. I just fell in love over and over with every bite. If all of that isn't enough to have you running to Brooklyn's Traif, may I also say that the music was some of the best I've heard in a restaurant. It was a great balance of hits and things you've never heard of. I seat danced the entire time. Traif is perfect. I don't know if you know or not... but seriously, perfect. Go now.

Took my family and Hubby here for an authentic Italian dinner after taking them shopping in SoHo. It was.. not what everyone was expecting. I'm guessing it was a little TOO authentic for my parents. Overall, the food wasn't bad, and the atmosphere was nice, but nobody was blown away by the food. Except maybe my sister, because she ordered this yummy roasted chicken thing.
Very nice beer selection, but the food always tends to leave me less than impressed - the wings are nothing to write home about.

Went here last night with two buddies. We had about a 1.5 hr wait which usually i am pretty against but I heard the food was worth it. Spent the time waiting in the back patio drinking Modelo and sixpoint.  Bartenders were fun and easy going, drinks were tasty and the smoking didn't bother me. Finally sat down and for the 3 of us we ordered the combo (meat/cheese) platter, the banana hammuck pizza, and the octopus. Combo platter was tasty and massive. Perfect starter. Octopus was tiny but good. pizza was perfection. I am seriously impressed with the product that they are putting out. another awsome factor is the L train is right around the corner to get you out of the slightly sketchy neighborhood. I couldn't decide between 4 or 5 stars. settled on 4 because of the long wait and the fancyness of the octopus. I expected more rustic and hearty. I will certainly return to try those sweetbreads.

Best Chinese food in the Newark area. And I am saying this as a Chinese Chinese. I have been to almost every corner of China. And the food here is not worse than some best Chinese restaurants I have been to. The fish there is great, as well as other things, such as pork and beef. The owner of this place comes from the city of Shanghai. So their taste is more Shanghainese than Sichuanese or Guangdongese, or Shandongese. Their food may not be as  diversed as those in China, but they definitely have some good cooks!

I love soba and eat it often, both at home and also out in restaurants. I looked forward to trying Soba-ya with its homemade noodles. Since the day was quite warm, I craved zaru soba (cold soba noodles with dipping sauce), and I ordered the tem zaru (zaru soba with tempura). The tempura was relatively standard, the shrimp's texture was good. The noodles themselves were more bouncy than some other places I've eaten at. One of my friends ordered the anago tempura (eel tempura), which was very delicious. The waitress gave us a pot of soba water to pour into the sauce so we could drink it as soup at the end of the meal. It wasn't really that special.
