Overall it's not a bad place, but it is also not spectacular. Note: The takoyaki hole-in-the-wall across the street is pretty good.

This place was perfect for a break from the Sunday brunch scene we were caught in one afternoon. The service is great. Drinks are fun. Food is spot on. Recommend if you're in the area and looking for some Asian fusion.

Fabulous, fabulous, fabulous, pumpkin curry! Topped off with a ginger martini.  My friends took me to this restaurant on a recent summer trip to NYC, and I was pleasantly surprised with the decor, and quaintness of this little hidden gem.   I would for sure go back, and would likely try the watermelon and feta salad.  Man oh man, that looked scrumptous.

This place is amazing and definitely worth the trip. Tried their cheese steak and will definitely return for a roast pork sandwich. I always thought that cheese steaks were soaked in grease but this wasn't the case at John's. Good flavor in the meat and a good amount of meat and cheese. So perfect it did not fall out while I was taking a bite but still had enough to get the blend of everything that was in it. It's really close to I-95 so make it a pit stop if you're an out of towner like me.
Great sushi and great atmosphere located on the waterfront. Rarely a wait to be seated and service is top notch. Love the unique dishes as well as the typical "rolls". Delicious & kid friendly.

As far as pizza places go, Pizza 1 IS IT!  Delicious food, reasonable prices, fast delivery. I'm so happy they opened this additional location because it's closer to where I live. Try it once and you're hooked.
So much to choose from....no excuse to leave hungry lol...

Jane is SO freaking good. I went here for brunch again this past weekend and my girlfriend ordered the Benedict Johnny. I hate hollandaise sauce so I didn't think I'd want to even try it. Well, the Benedict Johnny has roasted tomato hollandaise and it was so good!! Other good things to try for brunch:  Salmon Scramble and Vanilla Bean French Toast (be warned that the French Toast is HUGE).  They only problem I have with this place is that their drinks are freaking expensive and I am a huge fan of the complimentary beverage of choice for brunch which apparently you can only get on Sundays. I might just have to go next Sunday!!  It's really great to sit outstide when it's a nice day out and watch people walk by while you're enjoying your brunch.   I've never been here for dinner but I'm sure it's great.

Finally went to try this place after some late night drinking.  Line wasn't long, I got the combination on rice and pita bread for only $6.  I put on some white sauce, some BBQ sauce, and literally only a few drops of their infamous hot sauce.  I knew better cause I read and heard so much about their hot sauce, so figured I should go light for the first time. Mixed it all up together and started chowing it down.  Oh boy!  With no exaggeration, my tongue felt like it's burning, and tears started coming outta my eyes.  Yet, it was sooooooo good and I couldn't stop putting more in my mouth.  Both the chicken and gyro are really tasty; their rice is smaller and a little drier than the other halal carts.  Along with the lettuce and pita bread, all go very well together.  That's the best halal food I've tried!

I've been going to their food truck for years.  So excited they have restaurant now. Easily the best Thai food around, which includes Montclair. Pad Thai is the best I've had, anywhere. Spicy basil with chicken is a staple order for us, but everything I've had here is great and prices are more than reasonable. The owners are so friendly too.  Don't miss this place!
Location is not the most convenient but still deserves 5 stars because they have the best Cuban food in NYC! You Have to try pollo empanizado!
We stopped by to pick up some pastries. The chocolate and lemon madeleines are full of flavor and so buttery tasty. The pumpkin cheesecake was perfect. A smooth creamy texture with an amazing flavor.

5 stars because the sandwiches are 25-50 cents cheaper than their same-quality counterparts in Chinatown.  The sandwiches from Ba Xuyen have a more "ethnic" taste to them-- their pate sandwich is the only pate sandwich I've eaten that actually TASTES like liver.  If you don't like the way banh mi tastes here, you might as well give them up and order cold cut sandwiches from here on. The avocado shake is awesome.  Less so in the winter though, because the miniature ice crystals in the shake don't melt fast enough, and you end up a not-as-creamy-as-it-should-be shake.

Worst hostesses & manager experience ever! My mother, boyfriend and I went to Westville on a Sunday afternoon before she needed to catch the train. We put in our name for a table for 3 and proceeded to watch the seating disaster ensue. In stead of seating 3 people at a 4 person table who had arrived 20 minutes before a party of 4 people, the manager seated the party of 4. Additionally, instead of pushing 2 2-tops together to make room for a party of 3 or four, the manager kept the 2 tops open until a party of 2 arrived. It was the most chaotic and unorganized mess. To add to the mess, the manager was openly rude to the hostess and continually grabbed the tattered list of names out of her hand. I love the food at this restaurant but I will not be back to this location because the manager is horrible!

Stumbling across Rutt's Hut sitting above Route 21 and the Passaic River beyond is more of a region warp than a time warp, the feeling is more of being in the Midwest than 15 kilometers from Midtown Manhattan. The place is circled in blacktop and large people rumble through the doors with their eyes on the menu. As it was my first visit, I was here for the famous deep-fried hot dogs called "rippers" ($1.85, even deemed "famous" on the menu). The dog was good, but the reason to eat it might be the chance to pile on their mustard relish in any amount you see fit. My next one will most certainly skip the boring spicy mustard and be smothered in the good stuff. I'm normally a proponent of deep-frying anything, but I'm not sure it does anything to a hot dog. The dog is definitely worth the 85 cent price increase from its NYC street vendor brothers, but other than that is unremarkable. I love gravy, and therefore could not stay away from the fries with gravy ($1.90). I was in the mood for junk food, so I admittedly enjoyed them. The fries are $1.85 alone and already soggy, so the 5 cent increase is not only worth it, but hides the poor quality. Another cheapie on the menu is draught beer. I wanted to support the already patriotic stance my meal had made, so I ordered a $1.95 Coors to wash it all down. If I hadn't, the terrorists would have won. Photos here: eatinganddrinkingmywayar…
The grilled chicken was very tender and the sauce was delicious. We were given ice cream on the house. The service was great

There's no Mojito like those found in Miami; however Yuca had a close call in the mojitos they served. I loved that they incorporate sugar cane into it. What I didn't love was how small the space was. I understand that the area is conducive to big storefronts, but I was constantly being pushed by people moving back and forth.

I thought this place was alright, I'm giving it 3.5 stars. Maybe I'm just really picky but I expected to be WOWed by this place.  So after standing in line for about 30 mins or so to be seated, I expected it to be spectacular.  Our order came out pretty fast and it tasted like pizza. That's it.
Great service & atmosphere.  The staff was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu.  Food met our expectations.

The decorations are really cute, they have picnic tables and an old style lookign menu. Once you enter you are greeted by a smiling hostess then seated. I came here with my sister. She recommended that we start with the bruschetta which we did and it was delicious. We ordered sausage and mushroom pizza. It was also good. The only inconvenience was that they only accepted cash. SO before having to go into dine we had to take out cash of the ATM. I'm sure it's better for the servers. Good service and the wait for the food wasn't long.

came with groupon coupon....still end up spending waay too much.  quality of food is less than other nearby competitive chinese fondue restaurants.  This place has a YOUNG, HIP americanized atmosphere, thus the popularity among the young americanized asian patrons.  For serious diners who want  good authentic chinese fondue....SKIP IT....and go around the block instead.

There's always a long line but it moves fast. Make sure you have your money ready and know your order, otherwise you'll be dismissed! I had the chicken on rice w/plenty of white sauce (a mix b/t ranch & yogurt) Great drunken eats or late night sustenance. A $6 plate is enough to feed 2!

Rarely encountered such a degree of awesomeness. Everything, from the food to the wine to the service to the decor was picture perfect. Starting with the food: kambucha squash crostini with ricotta and caramelized onions, roasted broccoli with pistachio vinaigrette for appetizers. Both fantastic, the first one lusciously so, but well-balanced by the crispness of the second. An excellent light start, opening up to an equally fab entree combo: seared scallops with pink peppercorn and a lemony veloute, accompanied by arctic char with sweet and normal potatoes in a decadent yet delightful sauce (such ability to combine those two sensations...). Everything was coursed out without us even asking, and the service was attentive without being overbearing. Opted for a local North Fork gewurztraminer at $50 and were not disappointed in that department either - great balance between acidity and fruitiness, with layers of texture oozing on the palate. The ambiance is fantastic, too: rustic modern decor (bricks, white wood, black & white pix), lots of table space for a proper foodie party but also a very nice bar at the entrance for walk-ins and drinks. Superb.

Ramen like you want it! Had the Diablo, hotter than most in Honshu, and hit the spot. If you're a weak sauce this dish ain't for you. The apps, tako-wasabi, gyoza, were good. I'd be back in a heartbeat! No beer/sake so BYOS is encouraged. We brought Tennessee bourbon.

Good, real good, always is.  We have been many many times, and always take out of towners, as it is, a true NYC experience.  Between the 3 of their restaurants, Pastis, Pravda, and Balthazar, I like it the best, mainly because of the crowd.  The place is so big, it really doesn't matter who is in the restaurant, as I never care.  The other 2 are a be seen at the scene, and in NYC that's so boring and I hate people checking me out while I eat.  We'll definitely support all 3, but models please enjoy who you're with, or get some new friends.  My advice, go and enjoy the food and the drinks.

I am a fan, because: 1) it is cheap 2) great variety 3) lunch and dinner beffet 4) it has a noodle bar that offers quick and CHEAP noodles 5) It is cheap!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I love to come here for lunch and quick grab and go.    The place get packed during lunch/dinner hours...another thing: it is not somewhere you want to take your dates to.....Cheapest korean in k-town...gotta love it in this economy.

Do not valet park here!!!! My brand new car was severely damage in the parking lot and the manager said he did nothing wrong. The parking attendant came inside and told me that a patron hit my valet park car and was about to leave before he stopped him, he changed his story when the police came. The manager on site was not accepting responsibility for parking my car in a way that it would be easily damage. My car is 2013 Jaguar, only 3 weeks old. No care was taken to safeguard my new vehicle. Your vehicle is safer on the streets. Don't expect the manager or staff to accept responsibility for your valet park vehicle.

# of people: 6 # of times visited: 1 meal: dinner dishes ordered: charcuterie plate - yummy meaty goodness, excellent fig spread cheese plate - tasty cheeses, i dont remember what kind but i liked them pretzel - just right and best used to deliver the delicious mustard to your drooling mouth pork belly entree special - 3 slices of crispy, lardy, porky goodness. it's like thick-sliced bacon so if you like bacon then you will like this dish. it might be a bit salty for some but the greens and potatoes that come with it kinda balance it out. anyway it doesn't matter because it's so good. there were 5 other entrees but i only tried a bite of each so i won't comment on them. warm chocolate cake: it was ok. i've had better and i've had worse. the apple sauce that comes with it is really good but the sauce that i thought was dark chocolate was kinda sour so i'm not sure what it was. there was schag too which i've had at peter lugers and i always thought it was was the german version of fresh thick whipped cream but the schlag at cafe katja tasted more like creme fraiche. service: nice, patient and helpful. she spilled beef stroganoff juice on my shirt and jacket which wasn't great but they gave me my meal for free and they also gave us an apple strudel on the house. that was really nice of them. thanks cafe katja! go back: i will definitely go back to cafe katja and would recommend it others
burgers were good, not great. Was dying of thirst but bartender ignored us..... expected a lot more.
Not as great as it used to be, not as great as Totonno's, but a terrific location, open til 10:30, and great to have "real" pizza right across the bridge.

This establishment can seem a bit stuffy and intimidating on first entering, what with its dark wood paneling and clubby decor. However, the service is friendly and helpful and puts one at ease. On a recent visit the crab salad (served with a tart avocado puree) and fettucine with truffles and pancetta were highlights on the appetizer menu, while the roast chicken and salmon entrees were tender and flavorful. Chocolate crepes with chestnut filling and vanilla sauce made a delicious finish to the meal. The Union League Cafe has offered consistent quality on several visits and I plan to return again the next time I'm in town.

Fries with Old bay seasoning -- nuff said! Greasy tasty 'siesta-inducing' sandwiches. Doesn't make for a great lunch option but excellent tasting food. Need to make this a regular after-work drinks spot! 3.5 stars

Stopped by for a late dinner after a film. I knew the beer selection would be good (which it was) but I was surprised at how delicious the food was. I had a club sandwich that I thought would be pretty par for the course. However the goat cheese, creamy avocado and toasty sourdough bread really made it pop. It was worth the 15 blocks I walked and I would have gladly walked another 15 to have that sandwich again.

The closest good pho option to University City. Saigon on Walnut is too sweet and Pho Vietnam is just a tad far for an everyday walk. I came here recently on one of those chilly fall nights, ready to be warmed up before the rest of my evening, and boy did it deliver. Steaming hot, tasty soup was in front of me within minutes and I chowed down without hesitation. As usual, the beef here isn't great, nor are the portion sizes, hence the loss of star, but everything else was spot on. The flavor of the broth was just right, not requiring me to add my usual spice. The noodles were a nice firm consistency and the overall experience was probably heightened by the contrast compared to the cold I had just left. Come here for fast service pho near University City and be prepared to warm up. Might want to grab a snack after though

I am once again reminded why I never go to places  before checking Yelp first. The reason for two stars and not one is the nice ambience inside but it is way too over crowded with tables and it does get loud and hot in there. We came last night and ordered the lamb roll things, Beet salad and the other salad with the radish. The beets were over salted and served in a pool of oil, the salad had no greens in there besides cilantro, parsley and dill.... I wish there were more than two leaves of arugula in there. This salad was fresh but just not a good combination of flavors - never really thought I would find a salad I actually dislike. The lamb roll things were bland, sauce was watery and under salted for sure. Also took like an hour to come, waitress thought that was normal. Also, strange placement of bathroom... Right in front if the kitchen counter where all the food is placed before it goes to the tables. UPDATE: Had to downgrade to 1 star due to the crazy food poisoning I had the next morning after my meal :(

I had a birthday party here over the summer and it was fantastic. The homemade pasta was delicious, and I loved the wine-on-tap. In fact, I enjoyed this place so much, I brought my girlfriend here and proposed to her. They gave us champagne after she said yes. Need I say more?

A.C. Petersen was a less than pleasant experience. Where shall I start? The unbearable waitresses that cringed and rolled their eyes at each question I asked? Or the man taking our take-out order who wouldn't even dare to crack a smile? Needless to say the service was horrendous! I felt that I was a nuisance to these people. For that reason alone, I will never return. Not to mention...the food was UN-edible. Regardless of take-out or not, the food made for a paying customer should at the VERY LEAST be edible. Due to the nastiness of our service, I checked our $9 wraps before leaving the restaurant only to find that the wrap was not only in pieces, but the food seemed cold. When I sent it back, I could see the look of disgust on the chef's face as if I was some kind of idiot to send back his food. Not to mention, nothing in there was fresh. EVERYTHING was frozen. I would never recommend this place even to my arch enemy. That bad.

Maybe I'm more inclined to give a 3 rather than a 4 because I'm back in LA where I could get much better Taiwanese food, but back in Philly this place definitely hit the spot when my friends and I were craving a taste of Taiwan. The Indonesian Chinese woman who has served us every time I've been here is super sweet and very accommodating. Party of 12 in this teeny restaurant? No problem! (Don't recommend it.) I wish their Chinese menu were translated into English because this place has some really good stuff. San bei ji (three cup chicken) is a Taiwanese classic and they do it very well--sweet and rich because of the sugar and sesame oil, but not overbearing. Their scallion pancakes are too greasy, but good if you're really craving them. I've always wanted to try the o a jian (oyster pancake) because they're at the top of the list of things I miss about Taiwan, but I'm a little skeptical about seafood in Philadelphia, and I can imagine that poorly executed o a jian would make you want to throw up... and then actually do it. Because of the "secret" Taiwanese menu this restaurant always seems to have a group of non-Chinese people ordering and otherwise speaking in Mandarin. Always a hoot. Be aware that the waitress has a pretty strong accent and it can be hard to understand her Mandarin.

Since I went to Brick when I originally wanted to try Vesta, it only makes sense that I went to Vesta when I wanted to try Sugar Freak. There's some sort of restaurant transitive property going on in Astoria. The place was not what I expected at all. Their website (and some reviews) make it seem like an old school Italian place. It reminds me more of Brick - casual and slightly rustic. I had a salad to start..lots of flavor. For an entree, I had the salmon. It was a little overcooked and came with beets. I liked them more than I thought I would, but the sauce was a little overpowering..it tasted like eating salmon with strawberry sauce. Everything was still pretty good, but I couldn't give four stars because of the service. I had to ask several times for silverware, things came our at random times, etc. In general the waiter didn't act like a waiter - I think it was an owner just randomly stopping by with stuff for the table. It was a fun time and a good local restaurant but I probably won't be back.

I arrived at Soco a little early and had to wait outside until they opened for brunch at noon. They opened promptly and attended and seated everyone fairly quickly. The wait staff is very attentive and helpful. I even had the pleasure of meeting a manager who was also helpful, we had an issue with the mimosa's. I ordered the chicken and waffles based on the reviews I read about it. I thought the waffles were just ok, they didnt really have a taste of red velvet. The chicken was fried perfectly I thought and it had a nice crisp. The meat was tender but it could have used a little bit more seasoning but it was pretty decent overall.The mac and cheese was creamy but it is a huge portion, I think about three people could share it. We also ordered a basket of corn bread, which was slightly sweetened but I liked that about it. Overall I enjoyed the experience and I plan to return to try other things on the menu
I can understand some of the low reviews here, but unless you've lived in chi you probably just don't get it. Sandwiches are good, and if nothing else, get an ice cream sandwich.

I was here in March 2010 and it was very cold out but it was quite cozy inside this joint. The deco is like if a pirate owned a wooden shack; with sea and pirate mementos hung everywhere. Kids would love it here. Well, I came here for the lobster roll but they had run out of lobster, so I had to settle for a fried clam roll. It was good but when you come to a place expecting lobster, fried clams just doesn't suffice. I also had a cup of their clam chowder that had no real excitement but very tasty; it did warmed my soul though. The two guys attending the place were very cool and attentive. I wish I can recommend this place for it lobster rolls, but I can't!! But I can recommend this place for it's decent chowder, fried clams, and inviting atmosphere.

A good surprise.  Went here on a Saturday night for dinner.  Atmosphere was modern and good for a date and for groups.   Food was surprisingly good (I like the other Burke restaurants but didn't expect much from looking at this menu).  The taste nevertheless was great.  We ordered the mushroom flatbread which was flavorful and cheesy goodness.  Entrees were the lamb ribs and burger.  The lamb looked pretty good and came with a side of crispy well seasoned curried shoestrings.  The burger was the best though.  The flavors of the burger were delicious.  The bun wasn't that great, but they seasoned and cooked it well, and the cheese plus whatever else (bacon? Onions?) were great.  The side of pickles that came w the burger was okay.  The fries could improve; they weren't very crispy and I expect more from David Burke.   Overall downside is that the menu prices were expensive.  The drinks were expensive for this type of restaurant (18$+).  I would expect that for DB a Townhouse or Fishtail, but not here.  The menu prices were kind of pricey for midtown west location (food items were about $3-6 more expensive than I would expect), but I guess hotels are usually more expensive.  Flatbread was $15, lamb was mid30s$, and burger was $18.   I also know that people on yelp have raved about the candies bacon.  I saw a neighboring table order it.  It's three strips of bacon for 15$--again too pricey in my opinion.  Presentation looked cool, but not worth the price. Service was okay; nothing to rave about but they were fine and attentive and polite.  I'm terms of service, a long blond haired lady was nice but the other lady who walked us to our table came off as snobby.  Not a fan of her vibe esp since she's one of the first people guest see. I would go back.  My only hesitation would be the prices. Unfortunately it's just $3-6 too expensive but it would cause hesitation in returning.  Nevertheless, flavors were overall fantastic!

The moment you are able to sit down at a table, you are in good hands! Ippudo is an incredible place, which is why you should be prepared for a long wait as other Yelpers have mentioned. But it is worth it. Once you sit down, order pork buns and ramen and just sit back and enjoy!! Highly recommend for ramen newbies and lovers alike.

Two words.....Fish Taco. One of the best things I have ever eaten. Chef Elizabeth is the real deal.  I would put her burger up against anyone in the city as one of the best. The char flavor from a real grill is terrific and cooked to perfection because I hate ordering a bruger medium rare and never getting it done right.  Thanks for the great meal, looking forward to the next

I went here for dinner on a Saturday night, reservation for 8. Our party was not seated until 8:25 because the group before us arrived late to their reservation. This would be forgivable if they were quick to prepare the table once the group left, but it was like the staff was stuck in quick sand. Overall, the service was far below par throughout the whole night. The food was pretty good, but nothing special. The table had the pork, steak and duck. Each of us enjoyed our meals, but nothing stood out and I would say the meal was average. If it wasn't for the poor staff (a couple waiters seemed good, but it was poorly organized) then I would probably rate this restaurant as a three. Either way I would not recommend this restaurant to a friend since there are numerous other restaurants close by that are better.

The cafe is cozy, dark, intimate ... the noise level was extremely loud unless you are seated in the back.  We ordered the mac & cheese w/ prosciutto which wasn't the best I've tasted.  They mix 7-8? different cheeses but it was a bit too sharp for my taste buds.  The pizza, decent taste but a bit on the salty side.  The wine list, however, was extensive and you pretty much have a huge selection of white/red and even beer to choose from.  Yumm!! Granted we did go during happy hour, the wait time was over 15 minutes but that's probably due to the small size of the overall place.  Conveniently located, I would probably give it another try.

I have wanted to come to the Ants Pants since I first heard about it upon moving to Philadelphia. We came here for a Saturday late brunch with my in-laws after touring the Penn Museum. It's a small space, but it smells amazing and the service was really good getting everyone in and out. We loved the sweet potato fries with dipping sauces. I had the spinach, goat cheese, and caramelized onion omelette which was awesome. So. much. goat. cheese. My husband had "the Lot" which he devoured, and a vanilla milkshake, which I kept sneaking sips of. I definitely want to come back and try the french toast and the Violet Crumble milkshake.
Great food and service!

So - I'm not really sure why this place is so hyped up.  There are well over 1,300 Yelp reviews and the average wait time is 2 hours!  I was expecting the moons and stars to come with my brunch experience, but unfortunately they were not. My friend and I came here on a late Saturday afternoon and shared the following: * EGGS BENEDICT - What's unique about their Benedicts is that the poached eggs are served on top of toasted buttermilk biscuits (instead of the traditional thin English muffins).  I must admit, the biscuits are pretty darn amazing.  They are deliciously fluffy and flaky.  The sauce was good too - on the creamier side, but still above average.  The issue I had with this rendition of the Eggs Benedict was the sprinkled sliced tomatoes and green onions - both of which I do not care for.  They didn't add any additional flavors or texture, and I thought they were completely irrelevant for the dish. * BLUEBERRY PANCAKES - This is a must order - especially for those of you with a sweet tooth.  I'm not a huge sweets person myself, but I enjoyed these pancakes tremendously.  I loved that the blueberries were nicely baked into the batter - so you get a nice chunk of blueberries with every bite. * SUGAR CURED BACON - Meh.  Again, not sure why people raved so much about the bacon.  They tasted liked the store-bought microwaveable kinds with glazed sugar. All in all - I would say Clinton St. is a decent brunch spot.  However, it is NOT worth the 2-hour wait and I do strongly believe that there are much better brunch places out there in the city.  It's above average but not by much in my opinion. 3.5 stars.

SriPraPhai has a whole cult following surrounding it and for good reason. My girlfriend and her Thai friend have both said the food they've had here is equivalent to food in Thailand. The food is really excellent. Everything is on point and tastes authentic. Portion sizes are just right  and everything comes out in a timely manner. They have a nice outdoor dining area in the back which is nice to grab a bite at lunch when its not super crowded. I'm a big fan of their soups. They're very flavorful and hearty, you can tell they take time doing prep work and ensuring quality. I've had the Tom Yum Gung and the Pork Boat Noodle soup. Both really on point. Their papaya salad is also really good. You also can't go wrong with a refreshing Thai iced tea on a hot summer day. The only thing holding it back from a perfect rating in my book is the price. A lunch for two easily gets to $70, and dinner for two can be closer to $100. The atmosphere and decor inside doesn't exactly say "high quality dining", so something just doesn't add up to me. Overall definitely worth a visit and an occasional stop by for a more casual dinner/lunch if you are in the mood for something good and authentic.

I am SO happy to have a BBQ place in Fort Greene that's better than the mediocre Smoke Joint. While this place might not be the most consistent every time, when it's good (which is most of the time) it hits it out of the park. The pork ribs are excellent, the chicken is great... sides are delicious too. There a cute patio out in back as well. I hope it sticks around because the location's a bit off the beaten track of Myrtle. Please support this place!!!!

Great classic cheesesteaks. Fast service. Don't forget to say "wiz" for cheese wiz. Line was shorter than Geno's. Good weather today but we found seating easily. I think it's better with provolone cheese and onions.

Meh.  I want to love this place and I believe when they first opened, I really did.  I LOVE thai food, just love and I just find this food okay.  Its missing the punch that a lot of Thai food has.  I love a good papaya salad and while mine was the right kind of spicy, the papaya itself was ripe.  Disappointing.  My entree was a tofu, bok choy, ginger and soy mix and while it was ok, it was just okay.  I wanted to love it.   I've ordered the red curry before and again, its fine but nothing special.  The place is really quite but the service is just okay.  I love this little corner spot but I think I'll be dining elsewhere for Thai.

Really?? Are you serious?  We showed up at 6 PM on a Sunday, having pre-ordered 4 lbs of brisket.  After being let in, we stood on line for quite awhile, and eventually asked the manager what the chances were of being seated.  "Slim to none" was not what he said, but implied, in a clearly disinterested  manner.  We left.  Honestly, as long as there are people dumb enough and with enough disposable income (clearly many, as evidenced by the long line as we exited) to stand on line for a pricey piece of meat (which in no way could justify the inconvenience), "buzzy" dumps like this will thrive.  I'd rather go to Blimpie.   (We actually went to a lovely Argentinian restaurant  nearby, with great food, ambiance and service.)

I went back to Atera a couple of Fridays ago and had another amazing time.   I completely agree with previous reviewers that the friendly staff really make the experience.  There is a significant problem at NYC fine dining restaurants with staff and chef (even at some venerable counter-seating fine dining establishments where chefs are right in front of customers) rude/cold/annoyed/nasty/hostile behavior.  This shocks me.  A restaurant is not a food temple. I am coming to eat dinner, not to pay homage at the altar of anyone's ego.  Thankfully, I cannot say enough nice things about the staff and the chefs at Atera.       I estimate that more than half of what I had this time was different than the last time I visited in March (both new dishes and "old" dishes with new components).  This is impressive.  Of the new items, I especially liked the "lobster roll," the halibut with whey and chamomile, the pork with wheatberries, the frozen strawberry shortcake, the ice cream sandwich, and a cold crab and crab/shrimp/lobster? gelee dish.  I also really enjoyed the butter which was house made and flavored with Winnimere cheese.   I did not like the squid "noodles."  I imagine that if I liked squid in noodle form, this would have been great, but I don't, so it wasn't.  The broth was nice.         Just a couple of brief comments: 1. The milk punch cocktail that I had for the "snacks" portion of the meal was great.  I would love more cocktails incorporated into the beverage pairing.   2.  I opted to have the additional cheese course: the apple bread was fresh and flavorful, but I am used to a more composed cheese course.  That being said, the selection was well chosen.       Parting thought - lots of things were even "better" than my first visit.  The foie gras "peanut" was soft and spreadable, not rock hard, etc.  I can tell this is a team that cares about getting a little bit better every day. I appreciate that ethos.

I'm a huge chicken pot pie fan and am always looking for new ones to try.  The Dutch Eating Place's chicken pot pie isn't close to being a traditional pot pie with the flaky crust and all.  Instead it looks more like a chicken dumpling stew, and it's so delicious that I don't even miss the crust.  The "pot pie" is full of hearty chunks of chicken and tender dumplings.  The soup is really flavorful.  You can get it in 3 sizes ( a small cup, a medium size that comes with coleslaw and bread, and a large container).  The only reason  I got a small was because I wanted to save room for dessert.  In addition to the good food, the people who work there are friendly and  informative.  I wish I wasn't allergic to apples because their apple dumplings look mouthwateringly delicious.

We loved it... We went on a Saturday night  had the nite to ourselves without the kids.  I say this because the wait for our table was long, so we hung out by the bar and talked and then finally we were seated.  The waitress was knoweledgable , attentive and friendly.  Individual pizzas were delish!!!!! would go back again.
Didn't eat here, but did get the Fresh lemonade.  It was so good and fresh.

Holy S***, this is good food. I don't believe in over-hyped reviews, but Comme Ci Comme Ca is more than deserving. It's addictive. My co-worker got my office hooked, I got my boyfriend hooked, and he got his office hooked. This is my second trip back. I've had both the bismati and cous cous. The lemon chicken is my favorite, but I also enjoy the beef and kofta. The merguez doesn't ring my bell, but some of my co-workers favor it. The Royales, in my opinion, are an overload of flavors. It's just too much. I ask for just beef and chicken - over bismati they charge *I think* $9. I don't have much experience with Moroccan food, but the flavors are incredible. The Andalusian and Casablanca sauces are a must. I've yet to try to the olive sauce, but I'm excited to have it next time. Portions are huge, 1 plate is lunch for two days. It's never heavy, I don't feel weighed down. I encourage everyone to try it.
This place has great middle eastern food!!  They have seating the back with some awesome cute decor too!   The falafels and salads are awesome!

This is family-style Italian American food at its best.  Take the warning of the waiters seriously - their portions are giant, enough to feed an entire village in Italy.  It goes without saying that this place is most apt for group dining.   Bread service was basic but good.  The calamari was of classic Italian American style - heavily breaded and fried in high temperature.  It came with a rustic and delicious tomato sauce.  Spaghetti and meatball was great.  The meatballs were of the perfect density and flavor.  The sauce was, again, rustic.  No fancy 2-hour red wine reduction bolognese, just bright and flavorful marinara with small chunks of tomatoes.  The lasagna was textbook.  Nothing unique - just comforting and nostalgic.  The seafood linguine special had good flavors, with generous amount of shrimp, clam, and mussels.   Service was casual and pleasant.  The interior of the restaurant was spacious with high ceiling.  Decor was nondescript.   You might wonder why I gave this place a 5 star but Del Posto a 4.  Well, it certainly doesn't mean that the cooking here is better than that of Del Posto.   Carmine's is simply perfect for its category.  It's home-style cooking meant to be shared by large groups.  Now I wouldn't take your FOB Italian friends here to showcase New York's Italian repertoire.  For example, the pasta in general is less al-dente than how they do it in Italy.  No doubt, this is Italian food Americanized - influenced by the abundance of US produce and the need for efficiency in a giant, fast-paced restaurant.  But if you are looking for something reliable and comforting, while eating with a group of people, Carmine's would be an ideal choice.

Noodles are good. The broth is clean, not overly salty, and light even though it looks like it would be heavy and dense. $4.75 for the mixed beef bowl. Tax included. Yep, bowls arrive in plastic but that's because if you can't finish it, they'll give you a lid and bag to take home with you. Bathroom is in the back, through the kitchen.

wow! What a deal! $4.50 for a GIANT sandwich filled with delicious meat, pickled veggies, cilantro and spicy mayo (whatever that sauce was, sooo good!) I asked for spicy and found actual pieces of jalapeno in my sandwich. The guy at the counter was happy and nice. I was super excited to spend so little on lunch when I had just SPLURGED on a new pair of clogs from No. 6 store around the corner! But yeah, the sandwich was as good as the $9 ones that you can order elsewhere. Yay love this place.

How I could make a visit to NYC and not give the renowned Ippudo a try?!? It would be foodie sacrilege! That being said, I was told the wait was an excruciating 2 hours but as luck would have it, I waited a mere 1.5 hours to be seated. No biggie, right?  In this case, the wait was well worth it. Now after waiting an ungodly 1.5 hours, my stomach was literally running on fumes and I was about ready to chew on my menu, luckily the efficient staff had me seated and served in record time! Impressive...now onto the food and libations, shall we? I started with some Nigori and Sapporo and the evening was already off to a great start... The first dish was the pork buns. How can you go wrong with beautifully fatty pork belly perfectly seasoned with a tangy spicy sauce, sandwiched inside a warm and fluffy bao bun...Momofuku eat your heart out! It was so darn guuuuud and highly recommended! Tuna tartare A refreshing start to the meal. The tuna was well seasoned with a nice lip smacking kick to it. Served with crunchy endive spears, the texture combination with the soft succulent tuna was perfect. Chicken wings These enticing little morsels were fried to a deep golden brown and the sweet glazed crispy skin was simply amazing! It locked in the juices, leaving tender juicy meat underneath Ramen It goes without saying that the ramen was heavenly. It also goes without saying that I devoured my bowl like a beast! But most importantly, it was easily the best bowl of ramen I've had on this earth! No, I won't go into the details like the irresistibly chewy and slippery noodles or the insanely flavorful broth...you'll just have to try it for yourself. Some things simply must be experienced first hand. And this is definitely one of those things! Happy Eats!

If you need finding some filipino also American you can take a trip here with the best part of your choice.This is an especial place in this city as they have stuff from different countries.Inviting others to take trip here because they take order even through phone.Like to agree with others review obviously it location convenient amazing service friendly.

Quite possibly the best Mexican food around, better than the often praised Rosa Mexicano. The very casual atmosphere and the easy going wait staff remove you nicely from Manhattan's pretense. I hope this gem will stay around for a long time without losing its quality.

Known as the place where lots of Yale grad students and professors will go for pizza, I've had pizza delivered from here a few times. Unfortunately, it failed to impress. The pizza had a bit of a cardboard consistency to it and the tomato sauce was too bland. You can do a lot better in New Haven.

3 of us walked in on a Friday evening and was told there would be an hour wait. For some reason we were able to be seated in 5 minutes, but no complaints there. While the food tasted home-cooked, it didn't really wow me like it did for everyone else who came here apparently. - Grilled octopus appetizer -- ordered per Yelp's suggestions. It tasted good, but the texture threw me off. Maybe it's just how fresh octopus should taste (I'm too used to Chinese-styled octopus), but it tasted really rubbery and...slippery on my tongue. - Greek-styled shrimp -- pretty good, but not exceptional. Tastes like shrimp. - Mediterranean sea bass -- well-cooked but nearly tasteless, which is disappointing given that it's the most expensive dish we ordered. We had to dip the fish meat into shrimp sauce to give it some taste. At least they took out the bones for us. - sides: lemon potatoes and horta -- while horta is just a bland veggie (a healthy option), lemon potatoes are THE BOMB. They are unlike any potatoes you've eaten before. DO IT. - complementary dessert -- not sure what dessert it was, but it was orgasmic. End of story. So really, the only memorable items were a side dish (lemon potatoes) and a free dessert. The heart of the meal was lacking, in my opinion. Like I said, the food tastes home-cooked and healthier (not coated with condiments), but if I wanted that then I'd eat at home rather than spending $40 outside. What I will give Taverna Kyclades is that the service is good--a bit rushed, but the waiter was very friendly, funny and attentive.

I can't get over how fabulous Beau Monde is... Just had a sweet crepe with Cherry Compote, Creme Anglaise, and Vanilla Ice Cream yesterday afternoon, while my friend enjoyed a savory crepe with the Shrimp and Seafood Sauce special. As always, the crepes were mind-blowing.

Place is run like a boot camp,what's on the wall is all they have,that's it.service is good but the food is kinda bland,People that I usually speak to say the food I'd delightful.I have had better food in a pizza shop.prices are ok but I think your better of trying it and making your own decision,I'm not busting down the door for there food any day soon!

I have been looking for a good Mexican restaurant in the city and didn't find any luck until I came across Xochitl.  The menu is full of delicious entrees, but my favorite part of the menu was the build-your-own guacamole; it is by far the best guacamole I have ever tasted!  The service was very kind also, they always made sure there was a drink on our table and that we were satisfied with the meal.  Xochitl is now one of my favorite restaurants in Philly.  The tequila bar is fantastic; there are so many great cocktails on the drink menu my friends and I love to try.  My girlfriends and I are definitely taking advantage of Xochitl during restaurant week this week and next!  If you are looking for a good tequila cocktail or a delicious Mexican meal, I highly suggest you come to Xochitl -- for the great service, drinks, and food!

Took an hour to get breakfast. Very long wait and no apology but food was good. Had tofu scram dish which isn't a lot of food  for $9.50 so I added a side of black beans to fill me up. Love the atmosphere and creative dishes

Overall, this is a pretty good pizza joint in NYC.  I've had some good ones in NYC but this is up there at the top.  We went with my family of 15 people and they did a real good job at serving us and suggesting the right amount of food.  There are a few things that I didn't like: 1) They didn't like when I asked for ranch.  I don't know when pizza became all snobby but I've noticed lately that when I ask for ranch at pizza places, it's looked down upon.  I don't care if you like A1 sauce with your steak or ranch with your pizza, you're the customer!  If I want some ranch, give it to me.  If you don't have it, just say you don't have it and leave the attitude in the kitchen.  Hehe - I just like ranch with everything. 2) Bottle of soda is literally a mini bottle...with no free refills...for $15,000...I guess it's a NYC thing but I'm used to having a large diet coke with my meals. 3) They charge $25 for us to bring our own cake and eat it there.  Now I would understand if it were small party and they were trying to be cheap with not ordering dessert at the restaurant BUT we were a party of 15!  Either 1) we didn't want to pay for 15 desserts because we already paid for a bunch of pizza/salads/drinks/etc or 2) we just like the cake at the dessert shop or 3) they don't have cakes so we ordered one.  Don't charge us $25 to cut it up - if you have to, try to consider waiving to larger parties as a favor for bringing in a large party. =D

We had the best night. Live music, the owners brought over a basket of toys for the kids, the food was great. Perfect atmosphere. They also won the mac&cheese competition. We have 7 kids. It can be hard to find a table sometimes but they cleared a place for us right away.

So the HB and I decided to try out Lea..it was close by and they didn't require reservation if you have a party less than 4. We were greeted and seated very quickly on a Friday night. It's cozy...We were seated by the door near the kitchen, which had a slight draft, but overall we were cool. We took some time to look over the menu and drink menu and opted to go w/ Smelts for apps and margherita for entree. for our drink - we went w/ the one that had sorrel in it. I don't remember the name of it. The apps was pretty good. The fish was slightly bland, but it came out hot(temperature), which I always appreciate and the chic peas were flavorful so it balanced it out. Our drinks were ok, but I wouldn't order it again...It had a bitter taste to it, not what I expected. We then sat there for a WHILE waiting on our pizza. Patrons came, got seated and received their pizza before us :-/. I wasn't particularly happy abt that, but whatever i guess at this point. Our pizza finally arrived and it was pretty good. I try to stay away from cheese although I love it so much, but hey it was a Friday night! Our waitress was nice and informative but after the pizza arrived, we didn't really see her anymore. We finished the pizza, got the bill and left. We were in a hurry to go to a show, so we were unable to see the dessert menu. Maybe I'll return, IDK...the menu wasn't that appealing to me. I did like the decor and the atmosphere though...maybe I'll be back for a drink at the bar.

I'll probably get death threats cause I'm not huggin Jose Garces nuts this time like all of Philadelphia; and yes I'm breaking my rule of yelping after only dining once, but I have decided I should be saving more $ these days if I plan on making some plan trips in the near future, plus the recession is still rockinandrolling. About a month ago I took my pops, the legendary Chiman to dinner. He mentioned he was trying to eat lighter so instead of our usual steak dinners I brought him to Amada. First thing first we were raised w/ only a few simple rules at the dinner table by the Chiman: only pussies didn't finish your plate and get seconds. So why may u ask I bring my dad to tapas restaurant like Amada's... cuz I had a gift card and he said he wasn't that hungry. Crab stuff peppers= bangin, so were the wild mushrooms. I thought the stuff lamb was tasty, but my dad claimed the cheese overpowered the very little lamb. We got another dish that wasn't memorable enough for me to remember. Review is going pretty good so why the 3 stars? The chicken paella was pretty bad. First off ,no la soccarat, come on Jose for 40 bucks a pop u can't skip out on the best part. Secondly, it was way over salted, I felt like I was eaten rice shaped salt. Thirdly (if that's a word), my pops kept on say "in ironbound in Newark u can get thees mus cheaaper." Fourthly ( still not sure if a word) I had to eat the whole platter since if u remember Chiman's #1 dinner rule: only pussies didn't finish their plates. Fifthly, I think chicken paella in Jose Garcia's language means ex lax cause I had one way ticket on the porcelain train for a bit and my pops was ok. In all fairness chicken was cooked very well....

I found this restaurant through a groupon deal and based on the food alone, I was glad to have found it. Upon entering the owner greeted us very warmly and advised us that we could have any table (the place was empty except for one large family in the back). We ordered a mixed salad and were delighted at the freshness and flavor - we were also delighted with the size of the side of feta. We both got the Branzino and it was absolutely fantastic - not too heavily seasoned which allowed for the flavor of the fish to come through. The restaurant has a large selection of fish, all of it looks great and are about $20 each. The fish comes with a little mixed veggies so if you are very hungry then I recommend a side (we were fine with the fish and salad). We didn't plan on getting dessert but we loved the display of Turkish desserts a we opted for the rice pudding. It was soooo creamy and satisfying. So why three stars, because the place is a bit rundown, the toilet wouldn't flush, there were flies buzzing around our table the whole time and we received a dirty glass. This looks like a small family owned business and I loved it, but they need to work on cleanliness a bit more.

I'm seeing some negativity in a lot of the recent reviews, but I had a very good experience here. I like that they have a good selection of really interesting beers that are brewed on site.  I had an IPA, a Russian imperial stout, and their Forbidden Fruit.  All were of very high quality and reasonably priced.  The Forbidden Fruit, though,  was not really my cup of tea, being more like a cider. I was pleasantly surprised with the fish and chips I ordered.  They serve up a really big piece of cod, and it's not overly breaded.   The ambience is good, and it's pleasant to sit at the front bar with the big windows looking out on the street scene.

We came here for Brunch and it was a blast. The drinks were a bit too sugary but if they are offering unlimited for an hour that explains it. The definitely believe in a 'Hair of the Dog' policy as well in regards to strength-but that is NOT a complaint. The french toast was delicious. I have a sweet tooth and thats the way to start off a meal..it was our app. The best was the fish tacos. Full of flavor, tangy, creamy, crunchy. The juevos were just alright but I don't think good Juevos exists in this town, just like great Tacos are hard to come by despite the proliferation of taco joints in in this town. Either way a great brunch spot.

i came here a few weeks ago on a warm and sunny saturday for brunch. the restaurant has very spring feel to it, with long wide windows that allow in ample sunlight and on a day when there's a light wind outside, the atmosphere inside the restaurant is one of picnicing in the gardens. the service here is amazing as well. i ordered the ham crepe and my friend ordered the andouille sausage. both were very good, but they kind of skimped a bit on the toppings used. there was a lot more cheese than meat, and for what it costs, it would've been nice if there was at least a bit more meat. it was the first time i'd ever had a square crepe, so extra points for presentation and creativity. i really wish i had enough room for dessert because i have such a soft spot for strawberry and nutella crepes. but the crepes are pretty big and i was too full after brunch. i'll have to come back again sometime to try the sweet crepes. if the sweet crepes are as good as the savory ones, then i can't wait!

This was a really bizarre experience. We walked in and there was a prayer group type thing that was going on in the restaurant, which consisted of about 15 guys talking loudly, and yelling at times, in some other language. I'm actually glad it was another language, since it made it kind of humorous, but it was still weird. I ordered lamb karahi, and I am 95% sure I got goat. I've eaten goat probably a dozen times before, and it tasted like goat. I've gotten lamb from Indian restaurants countless times, and what I got here did not taste like lamb. It was also very tough. Unless they gave me poorly cooked lamb that had a really off taste, it wasn't lamb. Also, I ordered kabuli naan, which is what is usually called peshawari naan or some variant of that at most Indian places I've gone. It's the one that  has dried fruits and nuts inside, and is typically delicious. The thing is, this did not have fruits or nuts inside. It tasted strange, so I opened it up, and there were a bunch of globs of white, sugary dough. I am not kidding. I tried some of the white stuff on its own to make sure. Sugary dough, and absolutely not dried fruit as the menu claims. The waiter was nice, but that's pretty much the only good thing I can think of to say about this place. It pretty much seemed like a scam to me. The food was a lie, end of story.

Super friendly staff and really fast service time coupled with great food and a setting right in the middle of Reading Terminal. Unlike some of the vendors, they have their own seating. The place was plenty busy even during the post-lunch hour. So keep in mind that seating may be hard to come by at peak times.

It's a typical campus-indian-restaurant, the food was decent, and I enjoyed that the flavors were  little spicier than in other places. On the other side, we went there for the buffet and arrived 15 min before closing. I understand it is a little late, but the guy who seems to be in charge of the place was really mad at us, looking anxiously desperate for us to leave the restaurant.

My friends and I had a wonderful dinner at La Sirene last night, from start to finish: excellent service, delicious food, and cozy space. Being allergic to all things from the sea, I was a little nervous about going to a French seafood bistro.  Happily, La Sirene has an expansive menu, with many tasty meat and vegetarian options. We didn't have a chance to pick up wine on our way (it is BYOB), but our server provided us with a "dial a bottle" number to call - within 10 minutes (and for a very reasonable price), we had wine on the table.  How great is that? As for the food - simple and delicious.  I had the roasted beet salad, followed by the pork tenderloin with morels (which was cooked to perfection).  For dessert, we shared the profiteroles (fantastic!) and the meringue (not my favourite dish of the night, but not terrible). All and all, a great dinner - I'll definitely be back.

Learned about Totto Ramen through LivingSocials email distribution.  Walked over one day during my lunch break.  I wanted to get take out, but they don't offer it.  However, the host made sure that I got in and out easily because he was understanding of my time crunch.  I ordered the Niku-Ramen which has a lot of meat and comes in a bowl twice the size of the other dishes.  It was delicious!!! The atmosphere was pleasant! The cooks and host and wait staff are all in good spirits, singing to the music that plays and just there to make it an enjoyable experience for you.  I suggest when you go you sit at the bar and where you get to watch the cooks!!  Very pleased and will make it a regular lunch spot.

2.5 stars.The empanada's are actually worth 4-5 stars besides the non-meat ones since there is really no point in eating an empanada sans meat. 2 stars (if that) for the inconvenience and attitudes of the guy I spoke with on the phone. Granted, I've been told recently by friends that since I've moved to NYC my attitude has been slightly more demanding, so I may be partially at blame. But I called to place an order for a handful of people and had to wait for a 3rd phone call back from the appropriate person to speak with me. When I finally had the right person on the phone to take my order I told him I wanted to place my order right then and there and not have to wait for a 4th call back since I was getting annoyed with all the back and forth for a lousy 6 person order. He cut me off, was rude for the entire duration of our phone call, and eventually pushed me to cancel my order and hang up on him. And I could barely hear him since it was so loud. If I'm spending $150 on food, at least try to be pleasant dude. Not worth the BS.

I don't know if their supplier has changed, their recipe has changed, or if I've tried macarons at so many places that I can compare their quality and taste better than I used to, but I'm not really a fan of their macarons anymore. They're super sweet. Take for example their lilac flavored one that was so sweet it was on the verge of tasting like candy. Their pistachio macaron was so sweet I couldn't even finish it. I took one bite and had to throw it out (which is naturally upsetting as a box of 5 will cost you $13.75). I really used to love their jasmine-green tea macaron because of its delicate flavor, but I can no longer say that about this macaron. So unfortunate.

Last weekend, I decided to stop mourning the loss of Fathom Seafood and go to EGG for brunch. I wanted to hate this place out of sheer bitterness but I have to admit, my brunch was awesome. I cant' speak for dinner for yet, but everything we ordered for brunch was great. I had the crab hash with a sunny egg which was fantastic. I couldn't stop eating it. Everything went really well together and even better with a bit of ketchup. Next time I go back, I will definitely order the sunny eggs over grit cakes. My friend ordered it and it looked awesome. That aside, the atmosphere was easy going our waiter was amazing at refilling our waters which was absolutely necessary after the Saturday night we all had. I appreciated it more than he probably knew. All and all, I really loved my brunch and will absolutely go back in the future. I still miss Fathom, but EGG has given me hope that I may just get over that void in my life.

Probably the best halal for portion to price. Little do people know, there are actually four carts. Cart 1 is the most popular, you will know because there is a long ass line. Cart 2 prepares the meat and brings it to Cart 1,3 & 4. Cart 3 is next to the drinks cart. Cart 4 is across the street (which has almost no wait) As K C. mentioned, the guys here have dealt with so many tourists so they aren't the friendliest but you can't complain cause they serve so many people daily. I prefer getting the combination of chicken and lamb. Avoid getting chicken alone because it is dry. This will make you buy a drink which are overpriced. Hot sauce: I don't know how my friends can smother this all over. This sauce is FIRE. The white sauce is great but I try to limit even though I'm already eating unhealthy as it is.

Went here on a Friday night on a whim (and we had some discount coupon) but I am glad we did. The food was outstanding. We had an appetizer of grilled baby squid as good as I've ever had and an eggplant app that was also very tasty. The real highlight was the saccetti (sp?) pasta , little sacks which were stuffed with fontina cheese and prosciutto and served in a delicious light sauce with shrimp. I can't wait to go back. Very reasonable pricing for this quality and a BYO to boot. Thoe chef and owner Maria is literally a liitle old italian lady (well not so old maybe) who can really cook.
I absolutely love this place. Amazing food, good service, amenable prices. Easier to get I of you're dining alone. I love their noodles, some of the best I have found in the city thus far.

It was not perfect. Alaskan king crab was beautifully luscious but underseasoned. A diver scallop was a hair overcooked. An absurdly unctuous piece of foie gras was too generous (yes, I said it) without the balance of any starch. But what I experienced at the Chef's Table at Bklyn Fare was something better than perfect. Chances were taken. Elements should not have fit together. Caviar bedded in fried potato bits? Black truffle shavings snowstormed over a Japanese risotto? Hot Parmesan-Reggiano foam over cold split-pea soup? Sardine and basil woven into a *potato chip*? Pulling it all off takes fearsome technique, a great respect for the ability of ingredients to shine, and a heck of a vision. A *sustained* vision when you're talking about 30-odd courses. Without the assistance of (outlawed) note-taking. I thought I could maybe remember 10 in detail before petering out. I even asked a lovely lady seated next to me to help. But I maxed out at 3. Because every single course shot for the moon, and after a few minutes, I just wanted to float in waves of incredulity. A bounty of canapes to start: sashimiesque fish with an underlying brushstroke of sauce and a floral garnish. After the fact, can I tell you which of the [hirame, saba, shima-aji, kinmedai, shake, toro, etc.] was paired with a subtle [ginger, shiso, cilantro, saffron, yuzu, trout roe]-based sauce and a [radish, orange, arugula, leek] blossom? No. Can I tell you that any of these fish could have held their own in the first-class Manhattan sushi temples, that the sauces kicked them to a different level, that each flower (anywhere else a mere pretentious flourish) contributed a wonderful bit of textural contrast as well as a flavor grace note... that these courses delivered on the promise that Sushi of Gari proposes but never quite fulfills, i.e., the translation of Japanese raw-fish elements into an exciting nouveau medium? Um, YES. What can I tell you about a Shikoku oyster nestled in a cup, a screamingly fresh slice of cucumber and a burst of creme fraiche hidden beneath, a translucent gelee layer vacuum-packed on top as if to preserve its beauty for future generations? How about that it was the most perfect oyster dish this side of the Grand Central Oyster Bar's pan-roast? Or a round of toast topped with Hokkaido sea urchin and a slice of black truffle? That it deserved to join Marea's uni/lardo starter and Kyo Ya's uni/yuba delicacy in the pantheon? It may be obnoxious to refer to other places, but touchstone, even legendary, dishes from those others are what came to mind: head-to-head comparisons with the very best that all of NYC has to offer. And BFare acquitted itself shockingly well, time after time after time. Wagyu tenderloin I've had at Del Posto, at Daniel, at Per Se... All trumped by BFare's coarse, perfect salting and a wisp of plum sauce. A piece of langoustine, lightly battered then fried, defied the physical laws of heat transfer -- how could the crust be so exquisitely crisped, yet the crustacean within be so evanescently cooked? I can't even think of a comparison for that one. A step back, to lesser plates: an octopus with marshmallow tenderness, but anodyne in flavor. A "chawanmushi" with mushrooms, a gloppy dashi base, and streamers of eggs more reminiscent of egg drop soup than the namesake dish. I told you, not perfect. I guess in some make-believe world, 30 straight high-wire plates could inspire you to hold up the "Perfect 10!" sign every time. But I like a Tim Krabbe quote about chess: "The initial position... is a draw, and any move after which it is still a draw must be seen as perfect. And such moves are very easy to find...: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 c6 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.e3 e6 5.Bd3 Bd6 6.Bxd6 Qxd6... and so on: the kind of game you sometimes see between weak club players. The Perfect Game is not worth looking at." BFare is clearly not shooting for perfection like that. Instead, the tastes and the aesthetic are manifestly those of Chef Ramirez; his idiosyncratic imagination is for anyone to see. Yes, the standard ambitions are on the sleeves of everyone there: the head chef, the cooks, the servers... Even the customers! If they were like me, they spent 45 minutes hitting "redial" ad nauseum to get through to the restaurant at a precise time on a Monday morning six weeks prior (a forbidding task that had me PTSDing to the early Momofuku Ko days). But his singular drive is the best argument in favor of a place that I was initially skeptical about. "If it's so Japanese-inspired, why not just go to my omakases instead?" I'd wondered. 3 years of kvetching before I went, but I am here to tell you now: if you can't understand the appeal of allowing such a sweeping yet intimate culinary vision to take residence in your head for a few hours, then I have nothing left to say to you. Probability of return within 1 year: 1%

When the bill came, I was shocked to see that a plain Iced Tea cost a whopping $4.00!!!  And since there are no refills, I had ordered two for a total of $8!!! Since the food was just mediocre, and that they charge an crazy amount for plain Iced Tea, I WILL NOT be going back there.
I like the crunchy bread, fresh veggies, good flavor sandwich. I wish they would give me more meat in the sandwich...! I like their great service :)

Went here for lunch today. I had a salad and my friend had a burger. The salad was very good, but a little over priced in my opinion. My friends burger looked incredible! The seating outdoors was great.
I seriously can not wait to go back here.  So many different varieties of food, and so many unique food items to buy that I woudn't know where to find anywhere else!
Beware of Greeks bearing gifts.....but not these Greeks. Loyal customer for years now. Two thumbs up for simple, Greek cuisine. Do it!

$16 for a burger and fries...I just don't get it. Very over priced...this is Burlington people!!! And the wine list drove me to drink beer...paying so much for a glass of mediocre wine makes me insane. Burger was ok, but a bit undercooked even for medium rare.
Beef risotto (starter) was extremely good. So was warm chocolate cake (dessert). Very good service too! Expensive but worth it!
Oh! Quite nice.
Very good food.  Something for everyone.  I generally dont like salsa, and even THAT was good.  Just a little pricey for the small portions.

Went in on a Sunday for dinner. Not a lot of folks around but great service from Cait our waitress. Had the spinach and artichoke fritters - tasty. I had the lamb gyro - very good with the toasted pita. Good chimays and the burger was yummy too!!

I have been living in New Haven for almost three years now. Alpha Delta is hands down one of the top restaurants in this city. They have the best pizza in the city, be sure to try the Alpha Delta special pie, the Buffalo chicken pie with some blue cheese sauce or ranch drizzled on top is delicious, best Buffalo chicken pizza I've had. It is not like the traditional New Haven shit pizza which is tasteless sauce and a little bit of cheese on a burnt cracker crust, if that's what you are looking for stay away from this place. The pizza is amazing but it is not even the number one reason I eat at this place on a weekly basis. I can say this with all honesty and after trying practically every wing in this city, Alpha Delta has the best buffalo wing in town. I lived in Buffalo for a couple years and it does not approach the quality of a good chicken wing (as it is called up there), but it is a legit wing, very saucy, perfect amount of heat, extra crispy outside and well rendered fat. Try these wings. Last but certainly not least, Alpha Delta is home to a sandwich that in Buffalo would simply be called a chicken finger sub. Fried chicken fingers, doused in buffalo wing sauce on a sub roll with lettuce tomato and mayo. At Alpha Delta it is called a Wenzel Sub, I will seriously miss this sandwich when I move. It is amazingly delicious, perfectly balanced, it's a must try item. The steak sub was in heavy rotation before discovering the Wenzel and it is a pretty damn good sandwich, especially with BBQ sauce.

I love this place, my friend introduced me to Joya recently. It is my favorite restaurant. I love their vegetable spring rolls, mango joya salad and the pad see yu (not sure if I got the name right but its the flat noodles ha sorry). Thai tea is also awesome! I was once putting my name on the waiting list on a busy friday night when I saw a fight break out right in front of me. Somebody got sliced in the chin with some glass. But this has nothing to do with the workers or Joya, it was just the uncivilized hungry hungry hippos that couldn't wait to be seated.

Best dumplings I've ever had. I order my takeout by looking at the price to make sure I get my fill, and this place was a struggle to get to $10. Ended up with far more than I could ask for, and the most delicious dumplings and sesame pancakes ever. No idea how they can turn a profit selling to people like me.

Great dining experience.  I had pasta filled with bone marrow and it was one of the best dishes we've ever had.  Service was lovely, the sommelier was ace.  Very nice atmosphere and absolutely worth the price.

Street vendor cuisine at it's finest. Mixed meat and rice. Free bags while waiting in line, ayce sauce, good amount of grub for only $6. Looks like I'll be staying across the street at the Hilton next time I'm in NYC.

Everything I've ever eaten here is delicious.  Even my father, who is the pickiest eater I know, loves it here.  I've had the chicharon de pollo, Carlitto's way chicken, suckling pig, paella... it's all amazing.  The ambiance is great too.
The food was so good we can actually share a meal between two people.
very good drinks, just overpriced. paying for the fun atmosphere. neat design, good music, fun young people, waiters and waitresses. overall, i'd recommend it.

Thursday evening, went to dinner with my girlfriend to celebrate our birthdays.  We heard the food was really good, and we wanted something simple, delicious, and laid back. If we were going for the bar, it might have been fun, but not for dining.  For starters, the music was really loud... No problem though, it's a bar, I get it.  My biggest issue with atmosphere was that it's so small, bar patrons that are standing behind the bar stools basically have their asses in your face.  We were unlucky enough to have a group of 6 or 7 college hipster girls next to us who were so loud we couldn't hear each other at all.  The music was bearable and we could speak over it, but with the group of girls on top of it, we just stopped talking to each other so we didn't waste our breath or lose our voices yelling. The staff was pretentious and douchebaggy.  Our waiter had a condescending attitude, seemed overly rushed (but never really seemed to be doing anything besides walking from one side of the bar to the other) and paid no attention to us after we had gotten our food.  After our food was taken, we waited over 20 minutes for him to even acknowledge us to offer the check, and he'd walked past us in that time a half a dozen times. The only saving graces were the hostess who seemed genuinely nice and friendly, and the fries. Sadly, even though I really wanted to like this place, I won't be returning any time remotely soon unless it's the only burger joint left in Philly.
Failing to see what the fuss is about.  Yes Jay-Z, Bono and Batali are investors but I fail to see the point.  Brunch was good but not out of the ordinary - basically just plain average.

Delicious puttanesca pizza without it being overbearing with the anchovies.  The artichoke and prosciutto white pizza is outstanding.  Lots of simplicity but filled with flavor.  The herb salad is to die for!  Definitely worth checking this joint out.  Get there early for Friday night seating and you'll be grateful.
i love the sandwiches from this place. my family believes the sauce is magee soy sauce but it still tastes awesome. meat is delicious but sometimes hard. still good.

Pretentious is the only word other than expensive I would use to describe this place.   A group of us went to lunch there.  It was not crowded when we arrived and didn't get severely busy until about 40 minutes after we ordered.  Once the food FINALLY arrived, it was ok, yet nothing to write home about.   I had the brat sandwich and it was $16.95!!!!  1 brat with sauerkraut on a long crusty bun with homemade aioli.  Not worth the price.   The service was lackluster; I've received better at McDonald's.   I will never eat there again.   Save your money and go elsewhere.

It was a nice place. The dessert creations were beauitful. The atmosphere was relaxing. But the taste was forgetable, and a little disappointing. It taste like desserts we could've order at any other Japanese restaurant. It was good, just not spectacular. The tea we order was lovely. We were expecting to have tea leaves in the pot, that could be refill later on. Turn out just a pot of tea and no more.

Boyfriend and I stopped here last night for my belated birthday dinner. I was a bit iffy based on the reviews, and I'm still feeling that way. We were started off with an amuse bouche of mushrooms marinated in herbed olive oil. Boyfriend and I aren't huge on mushrooms, but we really enjoyed these ones. We then ordered drinks. I got the Satan's Whiskers cocktail and Boyfriend ordered the Victory Village beer. My drink came out wrong the first time -- it was supposed to be gin, vermouth, orange juice, Grand Marnier and bitters. They forgot the orange juice and it tasted like what I presume Satan's actual whiskers taste like. The hostess quickly switched the drink out for me and though it was insanely strong (not good bar strong, more like drinking straight from the bottle strong), I suppose it was accurately described. Boyfriend's beer was spot on with the description and very smooth. Our app's were the highly recommended Szechuan Duck Spring Rolls, and they were really awesome. (Thanks, Yelp!) I've never had duck before, but I'd be more likely to try it after this. Then dinner came, and the weirdness began. First of all, entrees come by themselves with no sides, so it gets a little expensive if you want an actual meal. Boyfriend got the hanger steak and I got the salmon. For sides (which had no descriptions whatsoever on the menu, just the name and the price) we ordered the truffle parm frites and Jasmine fried rice and broccoli rabe. The salmon and steak were definitely good, although the steak was cooked unevenly (was ordered mid-rare and came out mid-rare to mid-well depending on the spot in the meat) and the salmon skin was so insanely hard I couldn't cut through it with my butter knife (they don't supply real knives on the tables here, so the kiddies are safe). The truffle parm frites were very yummy, although I didn't detect any truffle oil. The real disappointment was the rice and broccoli rabe. "Jasmine fried rice" here consists of an entire red onion in huge, long strips, a little bit of rice that I wouldn't really consider "fried" and some scrambled egg. I hate onions, and this was mostly onion, so that was the end of that for me. The broccoli rabe was cooked in too much oil and had entire flakes of crushed red pepper all over it. It was edible, but I prefer my vegetables in their more natural form, and someone who doesn't like spice could not handle these at all. Service was OK. The hostess was very involved in the meal and a pleasure to deal with. The waiter seemed like he was just there for his paycheck. I would go back here again, but probably skip the drinks and ask a TON of questions before I ordered anything from the description-less menu.

I love this place. I have been here about 10 times after I discover this great place.  All of the food I ordered tasted very good. Service was also very good . I  recommend this restaurant. Love them.

The rotisserie chicken was absolutely delicious - moist and flavorful!  The owner, Joe Brancaccio, was so determined to ensure I was satisfied that he was kind enough to throw in a couple of extra yummies! I would definitely recommend this place to anyone (it was worth the trek from Bed Stuy) for the food and the great customer service.

The fabled Employees Only - a must stop for cocktail aficionados and a great place to take out-of-towners to impress. Although I would've preferred a seat at the bar, we were relegated to a table off to the side. No harm though as the table service is on point and everyone who swung by took great care of us. Instead of grabbing a cocktail off the menu, I decided to order a bourbon old fashioned. You'd think this would be somewhat boring, but I like to use the classics as a measuring stick for a bar's talent. Employees Only certainly didn't disappoint in that regard, but I'm definitely coming back to try the house specialties next time. A spot worthy of the hype, but beware that around 10pm on a weekend the noise level gets a little insane, so conversation can be a little strained.

no neckties necessary to enter the Double Windsor, just an appreciation for good craft beers in a relaxed environment! I've been hearing tales of this joint for a while now from my Yelp peeps, and since it was just a few blocks away from Rhythm and Booze, this was our next stop on Saturday night. the impressive beer list immediately caught my eye. it leans towards American craft brews, lightly peppered with a few European imports. I enjoyed a nice ol' glass of 21st Amendment IPA. the beers are in the $6-8 range, which is decent. bartenders were fast and friendly. the food menu looks good. it's a little more limited in quantity but has items like bacon mac and cheese, catfish sandwiches, falafel burgers, mussels, and more. color me intrigued, especially by that falafel burger. very nice vibe here. shift it a few blocks over to Park Slope proper and it would be packed to the gills. instead, it was busy but not insanely so on Saturday night. we were able to get a set at a small table with some other random people, then shift to another table when that cleared a few minutes later. and there was a big TV in one corner of the ceiling playing "Ben Hur" for some reason! this is the kind of bar that Windsor Terrace has long needed. keep up the good work!

I don't like frozen yogurt generally, but I like Red Mango -- no, I love Red Mango!  The fruit flavors are so delicious, especially peach and mango.  This stuff is amazingly flavorful and refreshing, not cloyingly sweet.  The store is always clean and the staff is polite and helpful. What's not to love?

I had the French Onion soup and the Salmon w/ Couscous.  The soup was very good and the salmon and couscous were separately the best I have ever had of each!   The salmon had a great crispy crust but not over done.  the couscous was so fresh and buttery.  I basically licked my plate clean.  Really looking forward to coming back and trying something else.  Really, well done chef.  The service was very good as well.
