Matt & Marie's is a great new lunch option in Center City.  The sandwiches are great, the staff is friendly and the store is clean and bright.  I would agree with a prior reviewer that the explanation of each ingredient as the sandwich is being made is a little over the top. However the thoughtful combinations, fresh ingredients and yummy bread are worth whatever explanation they want to give. I tried the Uncle Guy's Turkey (highly recommend) and my husband had the Italian Stallion. We were both very happy with our choices.  The sandwiches are deceivingly filling and absolutely worth the $8.50 price tag.   Can't wait to make it back to try some of the other offerings.

I called and was sold a deal of ribs, boneless wings, wings etc for $75 I asked for extra celery in substitution for no soda as we were in a bar I was told no substitutions so I said I would pay for the extra celery They said no problem but delivered chicken with no ribs I called and they said they would bring One hour later I called and they said I would have to pay for them as because I ordered extra celery I negated the $75 deal so everything was a la carte. Be real careful what you order Did not even need the ribs but they were not even trying to make right what they clearly misrepresented Although many choices in burlington we were in town visiting our son with a group and we waited for wings to open but were embarrassed by their lack of professionalism Really too bad
Myer's has ruined me for all other bagels shops.  They are simply the best I have ever had.  Do not miss the Montreal Spice!

Honestly, this place should get 4.5 stars because the pros really out way the cons by a land slide. First of all the location couldn't get better as it is only a couple of feet off of Times Square. If anyone has eaten in this area you know that due to huge influx of tourist most restaurants charge an automatic 18% gratuity to your meal regardless of your party size. This high class establishment does not, impressive!      As you walk in you notice the decor, rustic modern but very much warm and welcoming. I must say though the hostess and waitresses aren't easy on the eyes! My wife and I was seated fairly quickly for a busy Saturday night, it seemed like they had endless sitting for them to be able to accommodate the revolving door of people walking in. Even though the portions are family style the seating was not which is always a plus when you want to have romantic night out alone.      The food was decadent and flavorful, you could actually taste the freshness in the seasoning. As I stated before the portions was plentyful so we ended up sharing a plate of chicken parm over penne (Three people could of eaten from this plate). If you order the meat over pasta it is only a $10 extra charge as opposed to paying $25 more for a side plate of pasta. The meal came out to under $50 with soft drinks, bread and tip. For a couple to eat for that amount of money in Times Square and have the quality and portions be what they were is the reason this place has now gained a loyal customer for years to come.

When the liquor petition first appeared in my apartment building a year ago for this place, then going under the thankfully temporary moniker "Art Burger," it promises to plant an innovative and inviting restaurant in an underserved part of East Williamsburg and Bushwick. Now well into the project, I can say the owners here have succeed at their somewhat pretentious sounding mission. The all glass windows stretch around the corner, showing passers by that gentrification is in full swing on the Avenue of Puerto Rico. The smart interiors, with reclaimed schoolhouse benches and a long bar facing the kitchen, of a theme with many other nearby places but with enough personality to not be seen as simple copies. The menu and beer selection isn't large, but both are well edited. The Shipyard is a particular favorite pint and there's a nice selection of seasonal cocktails. The burger is best nearby, impressively juicy and served a mountain of fresh-made and well seasoned fries. The entire sized portion of the mac and cheese is a filling amount of food for $10. If you live in the neighborhood, it's worth liking the restaurant on Facebook for the continually shifting offering of specials. The chef here stretches to Middle eastern, Turkish and even Continental cuisine, with fresh fish and seasonal creations that vary from very good to excellent. A great and no longer particularly new addition to the area, it's a testament to its success that it's hard to imagine the area now without it.

Had dinner here last night.  "A-OK" sums it up nicely. The atmosphere is pretty mundane.  Nothing special, but no immediate turn-offs.  Then, my father in-law commented he hadn't been there in 10 years, and nothing had changed.  OK, well...  It's just dark... I'll get over it.  Then I noticed that I had two different forks.  No, no... not a salad fork & a dinner fork.  Two different styles or forks.  .... OK, that's enough elitism. The service was good.  Very friendly, from the host welcoming us through the wait staff clearing our table.  The food was also quite good.  I went pretty basic w/a strip steak and potatoes.  My wife tried the chicken stir fry & really enjoyed it.  This does however lead me to the only real problem I had.   The menu is very, very... very confusing.  Appetizers... Korean dumplings, fresh mozzarella, hummus.  Entrees... Enchiladas, lasagna, stir fry, fresh fish (many options), steak... What? I don't for one moment blame the waitress for her confusion over what was & was not available on the gluten free menu, or what sauces were served with what dishes.   The chef needs to take a good look at the menu & clean it up.  One last point that did really frustrate me....  They have a gluten free menu (which actually uses the word Celiac on the cover).  And on the first page it actually says that you have to specify things like "no wheat berries" in the rice.  OK, if you are "catering" to gluten allergies, OWN it.  Don't make me decipher your menu.  If I say "I'm allergic to gluten," you should know enough to take out the wheat berries.  (The server did, to her credit)
When i first came to the yak, i love the deco and the atmosphere. I order the butter chicken w/ side dish of garlic naan. My life was so complete!!! Their food is delicous!!

I'd like to share as to why the small juicy steamed dumplings here are truly amazing.  If you understand this type of dumpling, then you know it is hard to make.   1) The texture of the dumpling dough has to be right.  Right enough so that the dumpling itself doesn't rip, and the juice of the dumpling does not seep out. 2) Each of the dumplings will naturally create its own juice within the dumplings because the core of most dumpling meat is cabbage.  Cabbage will naturally produce water once it is cooked. 3) Flavor--these dumplings are top-notch in term of flavor and size. So, you really do get a enjoyable and worthy dumpling experience here.  They are one of the best here in the U.S.  However, if you've ever been to the restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan called Ding-Tai-Fong, you will agree with me that, that restaurant is really the best!  This is their specialty and all the locals and tourists pile there on a daily basis.
Solid Italian food and excellent pizza.  Service can be spotty. I've had great waiters and some who forgot we existed.

We came here for a birthday dinner. It was very casual - about 9pm on a Tuesday, just 2 of us. Aside from our waiter acting awkwardly and an interesting vibe in the restaurant. We were treated very nicely as a couple and seated quietly in a back booth, despite the rest of the room being fairly empty. The food was awesome - we split beets, I had the market salad & he had brisket. A beer or two and the sweetest Hummingbird cocktail. For dessert, the crazy fudge sundae. There was a table of rowdier men near us who weren't too bothersome, but complained loudly about the price of drinks. One thing that bugged me a lot was the TV screen over the bar - it was so distracting throughout dinner and made the restaurant's atmosphere more confusing. I was excited to come here having heard great things. Our server was very attentive and helpful, if a bit creepy, and the food was great. I left a little disappointed with our overall experience.

To begin...I'd like to say that I absolutely love their food!!....IF I can actually GET the food served to me at a decent timeframe from when I actually place my order (rolls eyes). I'm a native NYer, but my mom lives around the corner from this place. When it first opened up, every time I visited Philly, I wanted to go to Rose Petals. I loved the initial purpose behind the creation of the place. After the first visit, I spared mercy on them for taking more than 30 minutes to bring out my order. On the second visit, I wasn't so light. But I admit..I am addicted to their rose petals delight french toast! So I knew they'd take forever but would give me what my hunger craved. This past weekend, I visited Philly and reminding myself of their ridiculous wait-time, my sister and I (we both frequent this place quite often), decided the BEST route, would be to do their takeout (rolls eyes once again). Well boy were we wrong. Now my sister mentioned to me that she ordered take out once and they gave her the wrong order (she ordered french toast--they gave her, what I assume was pancakes, which to me were a stack of dry, round, flat, and cold, chalk thingys---i'm not a fan of them.) But nevertheless, here we were...willing to give their services another try. On 3/8/14, I call around late 9am, ordered our simple order and the girl (btw, she was very pleasant) told me 20 minutes. Now, dealing with their "20 minutes" before, we decided it best to give them 30 minutes before leaving to pick up our food. We get there and lo and behold, the cashier tells us our order isn't ready yet at 35 mins later. I go back outside and wait another 12-15 minutes on our food. I walk in and the cashier once again says, "i'm sorry, its not ready yet. We're just having a busy day". I hold my tongue because this isn't a new york restaurant and it's still in its "start-up" phase. So...back out to my car I go to wait another 10 minutes. Alright, i think an hour later is SUFFICIENT  enough time to have a simple order complete. Plus, i realllyyy had my heart set out on those delight french toast! So I trudge back in there and the cashier says "your order is coming out from the kitchen now". So I stand there...and wait...and wait...for said order to come out the kitchen "now". After ten minutes of now waiting at the counter, the co-owner, a nice hispanic (i'm assuming), woman comes to me and says, "i'm sorry, do you want a refund?" No explanation to what happened to my order that was "coming out of the kitchen now". I was so pissed off, I turned my back and left as quietly as I came. I wanted to ask her if she could "refund me MY TIME WASTED" All in all, Dear Owners of Rose Petals, you make good food. Your husband is a really great cook along with his staff. And the girls in the front although slow most of the time, are genuinely pleasant. I also support the restaurant because it is in honor of your deceased sister Rose and also in honor of breaking domestic violence within relationships. BUT, I REFUSE to order from you all because by the time you bring out people's food, ten years might as well have gone by waiting. Please work on your service more!! Oh and REFUND ME my time wasted that morning for more than an hour and a half!

Amazing experience at Xixa- from the atmosphere to the wait staff to the food- just amazing. As this was our first time, the waitress (I think her name was Jenna), gave great suggestions on the food. She was informative and attentive to us without being too intrusive on our romantic evening. The duck lettuce wraps, the grilled carrots elote, and the tuna ceviche were some of our favorites. The churros were a perfect end to our meal- crispy on the outside and light on the inside- not chewy at all. All the food was served at the ideal temperature, texture, and with amazing flavor combinations- overall a perfect meal. We'll definitely be returning for another on point meal!

Went there again with 2 friends on Tuesday evening. I wonder why it took me one year to go to the Boil again! It was still as delicious as I remembered! It was the first time for my friends, and they absolutely loved everything! Definitely the best seafood restaurant!
Excellent local joynt. Great food. Fast service. Great beer selection. Open late.
Love this place it's a foodies dream! It can get a bit overwhelming because of all the choices of food and the weekend crowd. This is always a must whenever I come to Philadelphia

WOW.  This is how Italian food should be all the time.  I came here on a Wednesday afternoon and it wasn't crowded at all.  I'm usually not a fan of Italian food because I find it to be too heavy but since I live close by, I decided to drop in here to see what the fuss was all about, and boy, am I glad I did.  I have to say at first I was confused with the menu because all the items seemed pretty cheap so I asked the lady behind the counter if the portions are very small (I was thinking that maybe this was a tapas-style sort of place).  By her accent, I'm guessing she is not from America, and when she answered that the dishes are big enough for a "normal" person implying that Americans eat way too much (lol and yes, I agree), I'm pretty certain she's not from the US.  I think my question caught her off guard, but after a few seconds, she kindly explained to me that everything on the menu is a main dish, i.e., not appetizer size.  Everything on the menu looked really good but I finally decided on the spinach ricotta gnocchi with tomato sauce.  I was sorta scared that the gnocchi was going to lean heavily on the doughy side like most gnocchi you find at most restaurants but when my dish came out, i was really pleasantly surprised.  It was not carb heavy at all;  it was more like spinach and ricotta balls with a light dusting of flour on them.  They were AWESOME.  The dish also came with a side of focaccia bread which I used to scoop up the tomato sauce.  Everything tasted really, really fresh.   The dish was a perfect size; I left feeling full but not overly stuffed.  For $7, I got a relatively nutritious meal.  I'm not sure why people would eat at fast food chains when places such as this exist.  The price is the same, and this is waaaaaaay tastier and healthier.  A huge fan and will definitely be coming back to try everything else on their menu.

How have I never reviewed Jose Tejas? Shame on me. I've been eating here for more years than I can count, yet there's very little I can add that hasn't been said already. But let me at least add my voice to the chorus. I really don't know how Jose Tejas pulls it off. This place is packed from lights on to lights off. Sure, you may be lucky enough to get a table pretty quickly during the brief lull between lunch and happy hour, but the place will always be crowded. And I really don't care what anyone else says, the food at Jose Tejas is always consistently good. It may not be the most authentic Tex-Mex you will find, but everything they serve here is super fresh, packed with flavor, and just a real treat to eat. For me and for many of the reviewers you have heard from here, Jose Tejas pretty much sets the bar for all Tex-Mex food in the area. Other places don't even come close. My personal favorite are the blackened chicken fajitas. Definitely request grilled peppers to go with the grilled onions if you order them. And always get the jambalaya on the side. Again, it is not nearly as authentic as real jambalaya normally would be, but it is no less delicious. It's also amazing how inexpensive it is to eat here, especially given the quality of the food. Even alcoholic beverages are very reasonably priced . I can only assume it is because of the sheer volume they move through the space. The parking experience can definitely suck during peak hours, which seem to be just about any hour of the day. On my most recent trip here I had to park in the office complex that's on the corner of Route 1 North by the traffic light, and the walk all the way back to the restaurant. Pretty insane when you think about it. The good news is that people are starving when they come here. And luckily, the food comes quickly, and is consumed even faster, which means tables turn over constantly. So while the wait times and the crowds can sometimes feel discouraging, it goes much faster than you'd think. Just find a nook near the bar, order a margarita or three, and nibble away on the free, bottomless baskets of hot, greasy tortilla chips. It is sooooo worth it.

This review is based not on the food, which was delicious, but some of the most disorganized and chaotic service ever.  Four of us arrived at 7 pm for a birthday dinner and soon after ordered drinks.  45 minutes later I had mine but my friends had not.  One had ordered a virgin bloody mary and the two others vodka on the rocks.  Not complicated.  About 7.55 our appetizers arrived.  Still no more drinks.  We were told after repeated requests that the bar, which was in front of us, was backed up and the waiter himself could not make the drinks.  There was one bartender.  Then waiters seemed to gather to try to sort the mess, the bartender left, and finally the manager stepped in, very late in the game.  We all got drinks about the time the entree arrived.  Why the manager did not see what was going on and step in we could not understand.  It was a train wreck.  And by the way our waiter, who was doing the best he could, delivered the vodka on the rocks with a lemon twist with a lime wedge instead.  Under the circumstances we felt lucky to have drinks at all.  Quite a shockingly bad experience for a good restaurant and not at all appropriate to the quality of the food which was great.
One word review: Yum. Multi-word review: The food is fabulous, and the service is even better.  Eat here.
BEST PIZZA IN NY. It's not a joke. Lombardi's wins, hands down. Their pepperoni, sausage, and fresh garlic pizza is the way to go.
Deliciously HUGE pizza!!!
Believe all the hype. If you can get a reservation.

The market sides are perfect for this CA transplant when I'm feeling fresh produce deficient. I always have trouble deciding since they are all excellent. The burgers are solid, there is beer or wine and the service is pretty great considering how busy they always are. Plus the neighborhood is cute.
Pretty typical. Sometimes stop here when it is convenient.  But better Pizza locally at the Montville Inn and DeLizia's (Boonton)

4.5 stars. The food and decor are 5s. The service a 3.5. It gets really busy so I guess that's the reason service is sometimes lacking but I can overlook it due to the quality of the food. Try the guacamole, jalapeño cornbread, and the steak tacos. And the margaritas are to die for!!!!

Went for lunch on the weekend. Nice Cuban atomosphere. The virgin sangria was really good, so bring in your favorite wine and they will add it in. The food was good, it was lunch so I just had appys and a pork sandwich. I think it was a bit on the pricey side for what it was.

Try the amazing arugula and proscuitto pizza, the best thin crust pizza ever!  We asked for it even though it wasn't on the day's menu, and they agreed to serve one up, luckily for us.  I would make a special trip down to eat at Adrienne's.

I've had Ethiopian food once, but then I heard a presentation from an Ethiopian chef about the health benefits, so I've been more eager to have more of it since then. Seeing this place open in my neighborhood was very exciting! WV has amazing food, but every now and then, you want some spice! This is going to be my new go-to place when I want spice. The portions are generous and well-seasoned. I had the Bordeaux wine and really enjoyed it. I asked if the injera was 100% teff, which it is not b/c of the water here. However, they mentioned they are trying to import 100% teff injera. I'm super excited for that! I loved the atmosphere - the music was tastefully ethnic (meaning, not jarring or too aggressive), nor was it too loud. My date and I could enjoy our conversation but still enjoy the atmosphere. It is well decorated and the space benefits from their use of candles. I can't wait to get my vegetable on here! Collards, cabbage, beets, oh my! I am very very happy this place opened up. From a previous review, I'm now interested in their brunch!

The service was incredible. The food was amazing. My favorites were the fillet mignon and the lamb (although my girlfriend found the lamb too salty). The salad bar was terrific. They had a great selection of veggies, meats and really great cheese. If you're looking for a great meal and really in the mood for steak, this place is great! I went during Restaurant Week, but I would totally go back and pay the full price for the experience again. However, not a place I would recommend taking a first date. The servers keep coming by and offering you different cuts of meat which is great, but your conversation is interrupted throughout the whole meal. Even though I enjoyed the salad bar, I would not recommend this place to vegetarians.

It's all in the name! And it's all about the food! - great ingredients, high culinary art, perfect balance, amazing combinations, innovative pairings - all to please your taste senses. And the atmosphere there is perfect - exclusive and cozy, but not too pretentious. You should expect to spend around $100 per person (depending on your drinking habits).

Dear lord this place is amazing. My boyfriend and I were planning a trip to Vermont and I had bookmarked this place because it fell under the coffee category and was right around the corner from the hotel we were staying at, so I figured it'd be good for a breakfast stop, however a coffee shop this is not. (They do serve coffee though and it's good) Once we got up to White River Junction though it was pissing rain and we kind of wanted to just hang around by the hotel. I was sick of driving and there wasn't a whole lot around so we settled on eating here. They don't really take reservations per se (or names) and it was a zoo on Saturday night. When we showed up at 6:30, the hostess advised us to come back around 8 as it should be a little emptier then. We did just that and were seated immediately. We got the stuffed grape leaves (my first time having them, ever) and I ordered the doner kebab. My boyfriend got one of the guvec things - I think it was the lamb. For dessert we got the apple maple baklava (we were on a "Hey we're in Vermont, let's get lotsa maple stuff" kick. Everything was super delicious. The service was good, there was a minor snafu where I had ordered an iced chai and they brought it to me hot, but they happily rectified it. The decor was pretty adorable too.
The pork buns may have been the best thing I've ever tasted. Also Dilla was playing while u ate it which didn't hurt.

Just around the corner from Curry Row is this cozy & chill little neighborhood place with grand ambitions. The staff is pleasant and professional. The menu is solid. They sure know their oysters here. And so can you if you take advantage of their $12 for 6 oysters and a beer (or soda) happy hour special. They select about 6 different oysters to be included in the offer. You get to choose any combination of those highlighted on the list. They even include some west coasts varieties! Did I mention the slice of delicious whiskey cake that you might be offered if you are a nice person? I'm looking forward to having a proper dinner here some evening. These photos that people have uploaded are making me hungry!

This place was ok. Their food was tasty, but a bit over priced in my opinion. My boyfriend got the rice bowl and I got some sushi. Quality was on par with Yakitori Boy so I was a little annoyed that prices were $14 for a dragon roll where you can find that for $8 - $12 at other spots in the city. Service was fantastic however. Our waiter was really nice and the wait staff was also great. Not sure if I'd return though.

The food here is better than most buffets. I don't eat sushi so can''t comment on that. I like the spinach rolls. The Chinese dishes are slightly above par.  The boneless pork is very good. The Crab Rangoon is almost always right out of the fryer. The steak from the steak station is usually very tough.  The dessert station is sub par. My ice tea never went empty so I don't understand why anyone is saying the service is bad.

First brunch experience here in Philly (actually in my entire life), and oh man, I can see why now brunch is such a thing. My friends and I initially planned on Green Eggs Café, but because we would have had to wait 45 minutes for a table, we came here instead. Not only did the waitress seat us quickly, but the place also provided a very toasty ambience. (No pun intended.) I ordered a plate of their special egg toast: two poached eggs served atop a homemade split English muffin, with smoked salmon and asaparagus on the side. (I opted out of the Hollandaise sauce.) O-M-G. While I didn't get that runny yolk porn experience, each bite was a delicious sensation of salty and savory. Also, that English muffin was on point - so chewy and carb-y. I definitely recommend this place for a nice brunch minus the the terribly long line.
Touted by many as THE best in NY, I'd have to say no.  I just couldn't get into their various options.  But as a NYC institute it shant receive any less than 3 stars.

Man....This place has some TASTY fries~~~  The special sauces are cool, but I can only tolerate so much of it.  After awhile, I usually end up eating them natural or with some good ol ketchup. The best time to check this place out is in the afternoon when it's slow.  To wait on the long line on a weekend evening is crazy and diminishes the value of what you're craving.  That's how i feel at least...
Oldest brewery in Philly. What else is there to say. Place can get crowded but beer was great! Have not tried the food which I heard is pretty good. Need to go back for more!
awesome veggie food prices are a little steep but taste makes up for it!! try the chicken nuggets and salt and pepper chicken strips
We enjoyed one lunch and two dinners with friends. Lovely atmosphere, great food and salads, good service.. We will all return often. Thanks Copperhouse!

I was disappointed during my last visit here. There was definitely something wrong with the fish. The server did offer to have another dish prepared, but I don't like to send food back to the kitchen. But I was surprised that it did not get removed from our bill, even though I clearly didn't eat it. We, instead, got my husband's espresso on the house (which was ordered with sambuca but that was on the bill). It was insulting. I feel like the server should have tried harder to make us enjoy our experience. I guess every restaurant is entitled to an off day. Regardless, the level I used to hold this restaurant at has dropped significantly and I'm not sure I would return. I won't pay good money for bad food.

The burgers in this place do not warrant "Best of NYC" classification. They are basic burgers, /could/ be solid stuff ... but the meat quality is low-end grocery store chain 70/30 type stuff. A real shame when you consider Ottomanelli's butcher shop is just south not too far away, as well as other great butchers in the city. The lettuce was limp and soft, tomato slice not ripe, the bun just average. Fries are tasteless and the skinny, generic kind that come out of a mass produced factory type place. There are other places with good solid burgers in the city and a better beer selection to boot. After-effect. Feeling like I needed to wash my greasy mouth out and crampy, gawd get this out of my body type feelings.

Went here only because I got a half price gift certificate from groupon.  groupon.com/r/uu17256828 The pizza was very good. We got the margarita. My only complaint would be the service. It seemed like they were well understaffed on the front end--one waitress for the enter dining room. So she was not very attentive. Also, the food seemed to be kind of expensive. There was 3 of us in my party so I didn't think we would use up the whole $40 gift certificate, but we went over!

I've been here so many times and I never had a chance to write a review. If I could, I would give Num Pang 10 stars!! This is a great little sandwich spot that holds a place in my heart! haha Their meatball sandwich is delicious!!!!!!!!! The carrots, cilantro, the sauce, Delicious! The lines are usually long, put its not a long wait.  They'll take your order right away. There's not a lot of seating upstairs. The seating was never an issue because I took it to go.

My daughter and I were visiting New York for a few days and researched celiac-friendly options. Bistango popped up several times so we decided to give it a try. We were very happy with the choice. The first question the waitress asked was whether anyone had food allergies so we were instantly at ease. Service, ambiance, and food were great. We would highly recommend!
Cute place, great decore, amazing food!  Also, all of the servers are pretty sexy. :)

Totally chaotic and extremely expensive is the best way to describe eataly. It is certainly not Italy. There are many issues here, the first one to catch my eye was the produce section which offered limited items that were blemished, wilted and not very well presented. Second, there is no line management. The cheese and cured meats are serviced by the same counter, so after waiting over 15 minutes while the customers on line in front of me, tasted almost every cheese in the showcase, the counterman then  arbitrarily looked up to serve a later arriving customer ignoring the group of people that been waiting. The patron behind me was furious and the fact that they had no provolone enraged him even more. How can a market that touts abundant Italian products does not have provolone? The fresh food counters were not impressive. Nothing here that you cannot get at your upscale Italian market or at whole foods. The offerings are limited. We couldn't find whole wheat pasta  - either fresh or dried.  The bakery, chocolate counter, fresh pasta offered very few choices. There were lines and long waits at every restaurant, each looking & feeling more like a cafeteria. We were able to get a table at the meat restaurant. The food was enjoyable but, if you're spending upwards of $30.00 for an entrée, a little atmosphere is expected, without having shoppers milling about, looking over your shoulder into your plate.  In my opinion the concept is lacking - restaurants should be more secluded, away from the masses. There are too many dead ends and ropes arranged into mazes. Tourist and non-native New Yorkers may be impressed, but there is nothing special here. It is a one time experience and I will not return. Expensive and unimpressive.  There is an abundance of excellent Italian markets & restaurants in all five boroughs.  You do not have to go far for the real thing and you do not have to go here.

Small Mediterranean food joint near union square with counter service a small seating area for maybe 15. The food was awesome pulled pork platter a++,brisket a ++, vegetarian platter a++++, Service with a smile

Both spots are great I believe there's one in Park Slope and one in Bay ridge. Both places make great brick oven pizza. Def got my stamp of approval 5 star! all day every day. Margherita pizza is really good at Peppinos you will savor every bite. They even deliver pretty far. So if your in the Ft Greene area and your in the mood for some pizza give these guys a call.

Boyfriend took me here on our monthly date night. I'm actually not a big fan of southern food but Pies-n-Thighs, you've converted me into a Southern belle. At first glance, it seemed like there weren't enough tables but the hostess led us to a back area with a lot more so don't panic about wait time.   What we ordered: the fried chicken box, the superbowl and the bourbon pecan pie. The fried chicken is PERFECTLY cooked- crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. The biscuits were nice and soft and the sides were well seasoned. The service here is also superb. The staff was friendly and more than helpful.
try hldias meatloaf. Best meeatloaf ive ever tasted. better then moms. waitstaff is always helpful and very friendly. great date night spot or just a guys night great for both
ALWAYS AMAZING BEER ON TAP! AWESOME FOOD! Looooove the fried pickles.
This is one of my favorite places in the city. It's authentic and fun whether you sit in the tiny restaurant or take out next door. The corn is a must try, as well as the plantains.

Reasonably priced and quite delicious. Very impressed with the menu, presentation, and flavor, and really don't have much to add in that respect that other reviewers haven't mentioned. So, why the three stars, SB? Well, the service was quite terrible. Our guy didn't mess anything up but it was impossible to get his attention. When we did, he was indifferent and impersonal. He was a real downer to an otherwise excellent meal.

I first came here after an article in outdoor magazine, Year (1994) I made a trip with my brother out of boredom 202 miles form DC. It was worth the drive! 2 Amys in DC should learn a thing or two from this place. you leave wanting more !!!!! now they expanded and are all fancy but the food is still good. 5 stars

Everything from start to finish was perfect. The decor is stunning--while it was too cold to dine al fresco this evening, I couldn't help but take a picture of the spectacular garden. I am not one to order a cheese plate--thinking it a waste as there is nothing to cook on a cheese plate--but do not go here without ordering one!!! The buffalo cheese was phenomenal, as well as the Italian cheese that was a mix of goat's and cow's milk cheese. Any restaurant with a cheese monger is after my heart. My family and I then split the veal papardelle and a pea ravioli in a goat's milk sauce. While you may think the cheese course is enough of an appetizer, don't pass up on the actual starters. The portions aren't that large, they are light, and they are plane perfect. Don't pass up on the wonderfully seasonal vegetable dishes either! We opted to share the beets and ricotta and the mushrooms. I have never tasted such flavorful mushrooms, nor have I have ever before wanted to bath in a deep bath of ricotta. For my entree, I opted for the scallops prepared in a ginger sauce, served with a mint pea puree, carrots, and some other root vegetable. They were silky, there was decadent, they were light, they were everything scallops are supposed to be. Others at dinner ordered the salmon--breathtakingly fresh--the duck with rhubarb--no words--and the halibut in a bacon sherry, all as good as my own dish. To finish things off, because at a restaurant like this it would be sinful to skip dessert, we order homemade raspberry sorbet, warm chocolate pudding tart, and the petit chocolate cookies. The petit chocolate cookies were actually my favorite. If you're not that hungry, these are perfect, because they are small and very sharable. They came with a carrot cake woopie pie, a pignolli cookie (heavenly), a salted caramel cookie, and a dark chocolate cookie. Needless to say, I WILL be back to Talula's. I'm about ready to make the splurge on Talula's table too. And I must go to Talula's for brunch now, too. Needless to say, I recommend Talula's Garden fervently. The waitstaff as well was incredibly knowledgable, helpful, and just pleasant. GO GO GO

The first time I ever came here I had quite the mediocre experience.   The decor was very nice. Really enjoyed the ambiance of the place.   The food was just alright though, and a bit on the expensive side for the quality as well as portions you get with it.  I've had slightly better noodles and marinated egg, but their broth was delicious.   However my biggest complaint would be the service received.  Primarily by one of the waitresses.  A short Asian waitress was just simply rude to our party.  First, another server mistakenly brought the wrong item out.  Our friend had ordered the spicy miso however a regular miso was brought out and the server had indicated it was a spicy.  This can be a simple mistake and can be easily forgiven and overlooked, however, what happened next was atrocious and exemplary of horrible customer service.  The Asian server/(possibly supervisor?) came back and  gave us attitude about what was ordered and whether if what was received was the spicy or the regular.  If we were a first timer, how are we possibly supposed to know?  And the server told her to taste it, all with the nastiest attitude.  It of course was the wrong miso.  We were all in disbelief with how the server treated a customer.   It seemed like she was blaming us for the restaurants poor expedition of food coming out of the kitchen.  I will note the original server who made the mistake and all the other servers were completely pleasant and very nice.  It seems like the one shorter Asian server was a bit of a poison and dark blot to an otherwise good experience.

Consistently good stuff. I prefer the crab roll to the lobster roll while my lady prefers the salmon sandwich, but everything I've had here has been good. Dollar oyster happy hour is great and the best around. Always fresh and delicious. Laid back ambiance, nice staff and open late. It's a little pricey, but you're getting fresh seafood and being able to walk in half-cocked at 1:30 am and get a crab roll is amazing.

I been here twice for company-related events and loved both experiences.  It is an upscale, trendy place with simply decor. Waiters were friendly and responsive. Between both visits, we partially tried the whole menu as well as great wine list. During holiday season, large company events book up fast so plan ahead and book at least 2 months in advance if you want a party of 10+.  I worked with Robin and she made great food selections.  They have various prix-fixe menus, which is more than enough for family-style sharing portions. Suggestion: Brussel Sprouts, Duck Shawarma, Bone Marrow, Phoenician Fries, Falafel, citrus trout, various Hummus, various kebabs

My father lives in Taiwan so I grew up eating Taiwanese/Chinese food.  I find the quality and deliciousness of Formosa's food unsurpassed by any other Chinese restaurant in CT.  I often order takeout for easy dinner parties and all of my friends rave about it and make me feel like champion for very little effort.
Horrible! They don't use gloves and that's gross. The service is rude and the bread was barely fresh. Better cheese steaks in NY!

One of the best pizza places I've been. It's byob which is even better, but the glasses they give you are jelly jars, which is very uncomfortable to drink from. I noticed several customers brought their own wine glass, which is a great idea.
pretty good Mexican food if I say so myself.

Since August, my boyfriend and I have been frequent visitors to Jose Pistola's.  The steak nachos are the best either of us have ever tasted.  I was so convinced of this that I brought my sister and neighbor there on this past Thursday night for the nachos and wings.  During our meal, I commented to our server and manager that the nachos didn't taste as I remembered.  I pushed this thought aside until I woke up at 4am with severe abdominal pains.  After visiting the restroom 4 times in one hour, I texted my sis and neighbor to tell them about my dilemma.  They too responded they were in the bathroom.  On Friday evening, it was confirmed we indeed had food poisoning.  After sleeping most of the evening on the bathroom floor, I gathered my strength together to call the restaurant.  When I finally got through to the owner, "KC," he informed me that his A squad was on duty on Thursday and he knew the food was right because he hadn't received complaints from anyone else.  I didn't eat a thing on Thursday till I got to his restaurant.  What's the probability that all 3 of us would suffer from the same ailments at exactly the same time if it wasn't because of their food? My sickness was so bad, I even vomited the water I drank!!   I know people joke about places being a hole-in-the-way but still visit anyway, but take my advice, cross this location of your "to do" list.

Recently I had dinner with some friends at Pulcinella's in Burlington.  I have heard  a few good things about the restaurant and have smelt what seemed to be great food coming from Pulcinella's while shopping at other places in their plaza.  My experience did not reflect what I had heard about the restaurant or the wonderful smells coming from it.  First impression was that the booths are very small.  One of my friends is pregnant (only 5 months) and had trouble fitting into or getting comfortable in the booth; this in turn makes me feel awkward.  I cannot imagine that any larger people would be able to eat at Pulcinella's for this reason. Beside how small the booths are, the seating is made of hard wood (no padding) so it's uncomfortable to want to be there for longer than necessary.  Usually when I am out with friends we like to eat, have some drinks, and enjoy our time for a little while after dinner.  In this case we just wanted to call it a night. Everything mentioned above resulted in a poor first impression to me but I figured it's just a poor, thoughtless design.  While I understand that can be great for an intimate setting between a couple it may not be for a family or friends gathering.   The first impression did foreshadow the way the rest of our visit would go. My group ordered the cheese bread of the kid's menu because it sounded yummy and we wanted a variety of appetizer.  The cheese bread was not just drizzled with olive oil but drenched.  I am not a huge fan of soggy bread so I tried a bite and decided it's not for me.  Next our main dishes came; my chicken didn't seem to be cooked all of the way and my friend's meal tasted like "dirty socks and diapers" - his words not mine.  After dinner I decided to use the restroom and when I was in there I noticed the Orkin rodent control box in the rest room - there were a few actually - out in the open.  While I appreciate the attempt to keep rodents from surfaces where food is stored/prepared, I feel that it may be a better idea to hide these items so the general public isn't turned off to eat there. I wasn't too enthusiastic about my experience at Pulcinella's - it was what I would expect from a box store like Applebee's or Chile's...though my recent experiences there with friends were actually better.  My stomach was very enthusiastic a few hours later though as I spent most of the night in my bathroom and couldn't go to work the next day.  Then I read the reviews - I'm not the only one who has experienced this.  I did not have seafood or anything out of the ordinary and I am glad I wasn't daring enough to order anything "different" this time.  How can you get sick from chicken?  If it's not cooked thoroughly, if there's droppings or germs left from rodents on the preparation surface, silverware, or plates, ETC.  Moral of my story: To the people at Pulcinella's - you should read reviews and look into this before someone decides to sue you.  To other readers - buyer beware.  At least the customer service was okay - that's about it.

Sorry guys, this place is all hype... as much as i wanted to love this place (bringing together a group of friends raving about how good it sounded)  after about an hour weight, and being crammed in a communal table, and then being asked to shift seats around so the blond table of 18 yearolds can sit.   You better hope the balls are good But the balls are sad to say no good.  Dry and inconsistent says the nytimes and i couldn't agree better.  Portions are very small, but prices arent to much. but nothing was special about this place beside the icecream sandwiches that were comped since we had to move around to accommodate other guess.

I had high expectations for this place as I have been to many rodizios around the iron bound area. I have never been so disappointed in such a whil going out to eat. I ordered mixed meat platter which consisted of all the rodizio meats on one plate. I told the guy medium. The meats came to my table as well done and extremely dry. I only had a few pieces and stopped eating and Lost my appetite. I come from a family that brought me up to always finish my plate. This time o just told the guy to throw it out. I am so mad and dissapointed and I complained but the guy said nothing but sorry.

Maybe I came on a bad night but the ramen noodles were so-so.  The broth was tasty.  I ordered the Tori Ramen and it comes in a chicken and pork mixture broth with some bamboo shoots, spinach, pork belly and half of an egg.  I like the broth like I said but the noodles did not taste fresh, but it wasn't awful.  Not a huge selection of red wines here.  They only had one choice while they had three choices of the white wine.  But they do offer mixed cocktails too.  The decor is pretty nice.  Very dark and the tables are close together.  The place is not tiny but its not grand either.  Get there early because lines do form outside the door.

Do yourself a favor and visit DiNic's when you are in Philly.  Forget the cheesesteak (unless you go to Jim's 4th & South) DiNic's sandwiches are the best!  The pork with spinach is great and the Italian sausage with peppers and onions is a must try.  If you like provolone, they have the sharpest I've ever had. Nice people, nice place!

I was a little surprised that this place was good, because I have this skewed opinion that restaurants in Times Square are mediocre. We had Tony's arugula salad and penne with vodka sauce and mushrooms. The salad was just salad, nothing special, but the pasta was delicious. The sauce was well seasoned and tasty. We also ordered the Tiramisu for dessert, which was my favorite part of the night. I don't know what to say about it, except that it was just a good Tiramisu. They got it down.

This is actually a great place for very very small groups (4 people MAX). Their burritos are decent (though mostly overrated), their fried pickle chips are admittedly amazing, and their margarita pitchers are the real reason I ever used to go there. Try to get there for happy hour or after 10pm because the pitchers are half off.  It's also very vegan/vegetarian friendly. They're a lot more accommodating when they have their outdoor seating open, otherwise you could be stuck there for hours just waiting to be seated. I used to love this place... until this weekend, when some friends and I came here. There were 10 of us (which is understandably a lot), and they looked at us like we were from another planet when we asked for a table. It was a beautiful night, and all of their outdoor benches were lined up outside, but for whatever reason they refused to seat us.  I get that it's popular and gets packed, but they could lose the attitude.   We walked across the street to Gunner's Run, got seated immediately, had an amazing dinner, and dropped about $400 that El Camino lost out on. I work at a cafe in old city, so I get that places have their 'off' days, but places like El Camino in the nolibs area... need to seriously calm down.

The food was delicious! The service was fast, attentive, and they had great suggestions. The appetizers were phenomenal. We got the tasting plate which was a little small for six but perfect for four. my friend also ordered the chicken soup which was filled with chicken, rice, and vegetables. It was very flavorful!!! I had the entire fish of the day and it was cooked a little to wet for ,my liking but i like my fish on the dry side. my boyfriend and friend wanted a chicken dish that ended up being sold out, so the suggestion they received was delicious!!! We had tres leche and flan with our cafe con leche and i was not disappointed!!!! We were the last table seated for the night and they had run out of a few items, but were able to make suggestions of something that was similar that we would like and it was right on the money. As I stated above we were the last table seated, but they never rushed us or made us feel uncomfortable about being there so late (though we still felt bad).  They were quick to answer questions and very helpful! Would love to go back!!!!!

I've been coming to this place for more than 10 years, and it has consistently been one of the best places I've ever been to in the city. Today was no exception rolling in here for brunch on a crisp fall morning, with very nice specials, and friendly service. Walk in the door, BAM, greeted and seated, at the same time, "Want coffee?"     No, but we do know what we will be drinking. Pass off to our exceptionally cheerful waitress, who delivers our drinks and then our scrumptious croissant and muffin basket arrives. Drop the order, of crab meat omelette with onions and peppers, and we're set.   (the main course did take a little while to arrive, but it was worth the wait)   (see pictures) The potatoes were a little bland, and I wasn't feeling healthy for the side of fruit today, but the omelette was full of tasty crab meat, and cooked to perfection.  The entire package, including service from beginning to end was really great. Hands down,  one of the best and coziest places I know in the city.  I only take people I really like to this place.

I've been here six time so far in the past year. I've never been disappointed. The bagels are the equal of any in of the better bagels in Burlington--I'd say they're best. I've taken my staff here for lunches and ordered pick up for lunch meetings at work. No complaints. They've got something for everyone. I love the Turkey Club on an "everything' bagel. There are breakfast sandwiches made fresh to order available all day. Fresh is the key--you can taste it in each sandwich. They don't try and do too much here, which can cause a place to do nothing well. I can't say enough about the staff.  Never a scowl, never  attitude. They're friendly, helpful, and can recommend a sandwich if you're having some trouble deciding. I grew up in New Jersey so the Taylor Ham (pork roll) egg and cheese sandwich brings back such great memories. My only suggestion would be to stay open later one or two week nights. I'd love to stop on the way home and pick up sandwiches for dinner.

I was truly hoping that this restaurant would get better with time.  It has not.  A lifetime Cedar Grove-ian was looking forward to an upscale restaurant in town.  Not to be.   The hostesses and staff look past you when you walk in - but eventually get to you - I am sorry, are we bothering you? Gave them many chances to improve.  Brunch is poor at best -  fried pancakes?, overcooked eggs, hashbrowns in the style of McDonalds?  Tea selections are poor.  Lipton and Tetley is not a tea for this type of restaurant.  Would you serve Folgers coffee? Dinner: meals have been consistently poor - overcooked pasta and shrimp and rolls, twice.  Rolls brought out burnt and well into meal.   Beverages from bar are amateurish - who can't make a cosmo?  Gave bartender another chance to make it right - -same result - watered down, clear, and without taste.  Long Island Iced Tea fine one night - a coke the next, what's up? Pass this restaurant up and go to Calandra's in Caldwell or Porcini's in Totowa. For a great meal, consistently in Cedar Grove - go to Espisito's. This restaurant is to pricey to make these errors.  Shame on you.  Who is in charge?

I stumbled in here on St. Patrick's Day, looking quite the drunk little leprechaun (plastic green hat and all!).  Not only did the hostess and my server treat my like a sober human being--they actually treated me very kindly! The burger was nothing amazing, but holy crap that bacon peanut brittle!  I would go back and just order a tub of that for dinner.  The most amazing bar snack ever!  It looks like just a bowl of glazed peanuts, until you bite into the tasty little morsels...and then a mouth addiction is born! My pal had the fried chicken, and she said it was amazing (it looked it too!).  So maybe I'll order that next time, as well as a take home container of the brittle...which of course, won't even get me through the walk home! The space is super tiny, though, and you'll pretty much feel like you're at a communal table with your fellow diners.  I'm sure the 2 dates I was next too looooved my drunken ramblings...at least I made the 2 girls look that much better to their dates ;)

i came here for chicken and waffles... i missed the breakfast menu by 15 minutes, so i settled for the grilled cheese sandwich and tomato soup and it was AMAZEBALLS.  our server was really friendly and had really great hair.  i was impressed with the food and her perfect curls.  i will definitely be back to try the chicken and waffles no later that 11 am.

I've been coming here for years, and it has made me a total fan of East African food-ways. The flavors are robust and hearty and the atmosphere is warm and homie. Best place this side of the Hudson river. It's like a great family meal every time (at an Ethiopian household, anyway). The owners are great people too, so nice. I'll recommend this place to anyone. This is some serious home-cooking. Warning: First-timers, get ready to use your hands.
Friendly staff, cozy place but not quiet. Had the spare ribs and the glaze was fantastic. Great selection of beers. Definitely will he back.

A history buff's wet dream of gastro-experiences!!! I've been to Fraunces a few times now and love it every single time. Just the feeling one gets when walking in the halls of a gorgeous Colonial Era building with the added significance of it being George Washington's haunt is enough to make this place worth it. Add on very respectable selection of beers and whiskeys as well as a very interesting and well done menu, and you have a recipe for a great pub experience. The menu is a very well done and interesting mix of traditional pub / Americana, some modern inspiration, and traditional dishes. The oysters are fresh and tasty (as well they should be, we are in oyster central over here). The roasted beet salad has some great flavors going on. The potato and leek soups is a great dish from an era that no longer exists but here. But the Whiskey Cured Salmon is the draw of the starters and is amazing as it reads!!! Mains I've had the smoked pork loin and shepherd's pie... the loin was tender and juicy with a nice herb sauce to top and the pie was meaty and firm like it damn well should be. It's all about tradition at Fraunces. Great Anglo-American traditional dishes done right, a few new additions for the more experimental eater, good libation selections, and the sweet taste of history with every bite. So, stick a feather where you can, call it modern macaroni, and get down to Fraunces on the double quick!

The best restaurant in the "Curry Hill" area. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu, except the Veggie Burger salad that is. They always add a little something to make the dish exceptional. For example, French Toast has creamy nutella in the middle, the BBLT has a Balsamic mayo kick, and the Grilled Cheese has a zesty pesto sauce. This restaurant is quality. The best delivery in Murray Hill, I'm a big fan.
Everything is great on the menu.......  Even the salads are addictive.  I love eating here often.

I came here in a group of four. It was pretty crowded so we had a wait of at least ten minutes. But the food was good and filling! I had the Crab Cake bahn mi. I didn't expect a sandwich to be that filling but I probably could have saved half for later. My friends who has soups had very large portions and we were all pretty satisfied. 4 stars because there's just not much space... but that's almost all of the spots on W3rd street.
Fresh, well executed.  Small place with nice staff, fantastic tacos.   Will return.

Certainly visit Eataly you will not be disappointed.  Some items are priced high, but it is the city.  Had the grilled octopus...best ever.  Chill place, always movement so you can find a spot.  Let the spot you find guide your palate for the day.

As I walked through the Chelsea Market, I was drawn to this place because of the farm-to-table, sustainable food. It also serves local beer. I ate lunch on a Friday. When I sat to eat when they opened, the place was empty but when I left, it was completely full. The grilled cheese was AMAZING and the servers were great. I had a bottle of Malbec and it was equally amazing. The "market greens" that were served with it were overly oily and did not seem as fresh as I anticipated, but that was a minor detail in an overall great experience.
Perfect place to go after drinking to absorb all that alcohol. Fries were cooked well and you must try the peanut satay and, of course, traditional Belgian aioli/mayo sauce were the BEST!

This review is from 4/26/12 I just was lazy and didn't finish it until now. Had my first bloody mary here.... ewe. It was SO peppery I couldn't breathe. Our waitress is was not great...  she was super awkward and kinda dumb. Lol and didn't check on us at ALL. The food was decent but way over priced... not going back there.

This place serves damn good pizza. Pizza is found on every block in NYC, and New York is generally considered to be the best place for pizza. Nearby, you will find many places that offer $0.99 slices, but keep walking unit you find this joint. I've been going here for the past year and it never disappoints. Here's what slices I recommend. The Tomato and Basil slice is the best pizza I have eaten. It's a great mix of flavors, and it creates a truly good slice of pizza. What I like most about the slices here is that the crust is thin, but the cheese and toppings are piled high. Unlike other pizzerias, I'm actually full after eating 2 slices. The next best slice is the Lasagna pizza. It is, as you would expect, topped with the typical lasagna ingredients. Just like the tomato and basil slice, this pizza has a thin crust, with a generous amount of meat, cottage cheese, cheese, and tomato sauce toppings. The Grandmother's pizza is the square (Sicilian) slice, and for some reason it is the most popular. Personally, I am not a fan because there is just lots of bread (crust) and less cheese on this slice. It's good, but I wouldn't recommend it. A lot of people think it's a sin to get chicken on pizza, but so be it. The Breaded Chicken Tender slice is another favorite of mine. It's topped with lots of breaded chicken (obviously), and it just tastes damn good. Do yourself a favor, and pay the extra dollar or two for these delicious slices. Patzeria is my favorite pizza in NYC.

Great place to shop for food that is fresh, delicious and quick service. Desserts of all kinds from baklava to home made chocolates, wonderful, wonderful, wonderful. Parking is a problem. Wish they were open till 9 pm.

Good stuff! Very clean place. Before I say anything about the food, you have to know that this place has the nicest restroom I have ever seen in any restaurant. Great atmosphere! Love the little bench, plant, and wall colors. It doesn't even feel like you are in a place of business despite having a hand dryer (BTW a strong one, they didn't chintz out just because they are a small business). The toilet seat was so clean, I didn't even flinch when my 4 YO daughter jumped up to sit on it, and I didn't even mind sitting on it without placing TP all over it. A true rarity, and delight! My daughter also loved the sink because she found it easy for her to work all by herself. They even leave a can of Glade air-freshener in there, just in case. That all said . . . The food was all prepared well & the other five reviews I see here are on the money. This may sound silly, but I loved the fact that the water they serve there actually tastes GREAT. I am accustomed to getting tap water in restaurants, non filtered & possibly poorly covered up by a wedge of lemon. This ice water is so good they could sell it. Their iced coffee is smooth & tasty. The special green Pandan drink with coconut & jello in it is tasty too, my wife (a 100% Filipina) loved it. We opened with Lumpiang Shanghai as an appetizer.  Mmmmm good. This was my daughter's favorite of the meal. I liked the sauce that came with it. Worth getting again for sure. I had the Som Tom salad. New experience for me, and it seemed like it was great, but the spices seemed a bit strong to me. Don't get me wrong, I do like spicy things. But, I kept thinking that I was tasting a strong dose of ginger, which I don't mind in small amounts. The thing is, I know there was no ginger in there, so I believe this was actually the lime juice somehow working with the other spices. I ate it all, and I am glad I did, but I'll try another salad in the future, and maybe come back to this when I'm expecting it. I also had a chicken meal that I forget the name of. I believe it was pandanus chicken. It was tied together with a pandan leaf & served with pandanus sauce. Very tasty. The sauce really makes it. I even got a little side of even MORE Som Tom salad (chuckle). This one could easily become my regular meal if I were to be a regular. Grilled pork belly was what my wife had. She says that it tastes like it should, really good, with lots of fat. Deserts were Sans Rival (GET THIS!) & Halo-Halo (as good as you will find on American soil).

I think this place must be better for drinks/in the evening because I was not impressed by brunch, but am surprised by all the positive reviews. The space is cute and rustic - very small. I can see it being a nice intimate date spot. The brunch service is slow and sometimes inattentive, albeit friendly. The food leaves much to be desired. I had the quiche lorraine which was bizarrely both undercooked and overcooked. The crust was extremely dense and difficult to cut but the egg mixture was runny and slightly undercooked. i somehow needed all my utensils - a knife to saw the crust, a spoon to scoop up the eggy part, and a fork to get it all together. The bacon is like jerky, extremely tough and somehow lacking in flavor. I'm of the school of thought that certain things are pretty hard to mess up: pizza, bacon, etc. and will be good even if they are bad. This bacon proved me wrong - I couldn't even eat one piece! All in all, a wasted brunch experience. There are too many other wonderful places in New York to try to waste a meal here.

This place is legendary in Brooklyn. There's usually a line just to get in the parking lot or to order your pizza. Get the traditional square pie; you won't be sorry. The spumoni, ice cream, desserts are wonderful too. The restaurant side of it seems little less organized and it wasn't as enjoyable as sitting outside with the pizza. (Which is why I gave 4 stars instead of 5)
Nothing special. Not sure how this place is getting 4 stars.

This is my first Portuguese restaurant... Hubbie has been coming here for a couple years...and ALWAYS come for a meal here when he is in town for work.   This past Christmas, I tagged along with Hubbie for his company Christmas party.  We were able to visit Valenca and The Big Apple in the same visit.  What a treat! We started with some olives, bread, and Sangria.   Croquetes de Carne - meat croquettes.  Good.  Nothing different from all the others I have had.. Bolinhos de Bacalhau - Codfish pastries - I prefer this over the meat croquetes.  I love cod.  And this was well made and prepared.  Chunks of cod in every bite. House salad - Perfect salad with green lettuce, tomatoes, carrots, cucumbers, red cabbage, Main Course: Filet Mignon on Hot Stone - 2 nice-sized filet mignon for 25 bucks.  What a deal.  It comes out raw on the hot stone.  You cook it to your liking.  I personally like my medium rare and that is how I ate mine.  It comes with Spanish rice and home-made potato chip and garlic butter. Finished the nite with a Cappucino cake.  It was good.  Should have ordered a cup o' joe to accompany, but it was getting late...so I took a pass.   Salud!

Manager Carlos is amazing!! It was our first time here and the food was amazing. We had their burger, lobster mac and cheese and their chrrasco steak. Sangria is amazing. He even had our servers sing HAPPY BIRTHDAY!!

As a Frenchy, I am usually super critical about anything French in the US. After all, I'm French, so complaining is part of my culture! I booked a table at Amelie shortly after Valentine's Day, as I was out of town on that day and couldn't take my better half out for dinner. Overall, we had a great time  food was delicious, portions were more than decent, and service was super courteous. My favorite part: when our waiter figured that my girlfriend didn't speak French, he instantly offered to switch to English. Kudos! That doesn't happen much, and my girlfriend felt even better at that place. The good: we were at a table in the corner, which gave us some intimacy in a very crowded restaurant. Also, the waiter would just jump over the bar to serve us, which meant that he wouldn't have to struggle through the whole crowd to bring us our plates. The bad: it was pretty cold outside, and when some *cough idiots cough* careless customers would enter or leave while leaving both doors open! it could get pretty cold at our table too. The ugly: I'm not sure I would have enjoyed our dinner as much had we sat at a table behind the bar. Looked like some people's heads got knocked over a few times. But hey, it's New York!
nice environment. This place is located at a corner with window/outdoor seating! Great food! The drinks are slightly overpriced.

Good izakaya w/ good food.  There are so many dishes but are all reasonably priced.  Casual vibe is reminiscent of izakayas in japan.   We were four, so we tried as many dishes as possible, and they even have wine!  Yummy chicken wings that are actually so easy to eat.  We ended our meal w/ salmon and ikura gohan.  Definitely coming back when I want good and unpretentious food in a casual, friendly place.

came here for brunch. the decor is mediocre. the food is bomb! super yummy. and im not crazy about mexican food, so i guess that says alot. coconut mojito was delicious. however i then ordered that spicy margarita everyone talked about... neither me or my friend could finish it. SO SPICY. not a good spicy either. just tastes like u swallowed jalapeno with rubbing alcohol. lol other than that, the food is great

This place has got it going on.  Other neighborhood establishments should take service training courses from Chavela's.  Obviously, the food is ridiculous or they wouldn't have been able to expand to a larger space.   What I love about this place is that they take care of you swift and courteously even though it is pretty much always packed.  No attitude, all smiles.   I have only lived in the Crown Heights vicinity for nine months but I have tried many other places and there is a definitely lack of service driven environments.  I hope the success of places like Chavela's causes others to step up their game.

People who adore Philly, please don't hate me for what I'm about to say.  If ever I had a reason to return, it wouldn't be for the Art Museum or Boathouse Row, lit by lights on the waterfront at night.  It wouldn't be for the noisy public transportation system or the honking drivers that seem to be everywhere, day or night.  It would be for PARC, which is like a little spot of French heaven in Rittenhouse Square.  Now, for non-Philadelphians, it's important to know that Rittenhouse has an urbane ambiance.  The best places to shop and dine exist in this little city square.   Parc is in the heart of that, with wicker furniture littering the sidewalk during the warm weather.  I've visited Parc both in the summer and winter, but in the summertime, it is just like a Parisian cafe, complete with cosy tables and interesting sights.  I can understand how some people might not like how closely the tables are put together.  It is very European, and Americans aren't used to sitting so close to one another as they eat.  Another couple had to squeeze in next to us, and it almost felt like they were a part of our dinner party. On to the good stuff: drinks!  Parc offers a wide range of hand-crafted cocktails, most of them with unique twists on a familiar theme, like a cucumber cooler.  They even offer sodas like Orangina for that continental flair.   Their wine list is extensive, and on my numerous visits, I've found the staff to be very helpful in making recommendations.   The menu is written in an old-fashioned font and is simple.  Rather than florid descriptions, Parc gives you the title of the dish and relies on your trust to sway you in ordering.  The first time I went, I had the Steak Frites in the bar area.  The bar-tenders were gracious and quick.  My drink stayed full and strong for the duration of my visit.  The restaurant was full, but the low-lit atmosphere was nice.  I found myself wishing I'd come with a date because of the romance the lighting inspired. On my second visit, I sat outside and the server was equally attentive.  That time I started with Shrimp Cocktail.  The Shrimp were exceptionally fresh and sweet, letting me know that Parc cares about absolute freshness when selecting its ingredients.  My friend had half a dozen Littleneck Clams, which were arrayed on chipped ice with seaweed.  I sampled some, and they were equally fresh and quite light on the palate.  I followed the Shrimp Cocktail with the Beet Salad, which featured the hearty taste of the beet balanced out with a light vinegar dressing.   Every time I've walked by Parc on a warm weekend morning, it's been filled with brunchers.  I'm dying to try it, to really get a handle on the whole experience.  Although I no longer live in Philadelphia, I'd love to return, if only to see if my fantasies about the Parc brunch live up to my expectations.

"It was the best experience I've ever had." - Really hot Bengali/Nepalese girl I honestly thought it was okay. Dim lights and a window seat for 2, the atmosphere was pushing my buttons, but in terms of pancakes, it didn't quite meet my expectations. I mean, I'm no pancakologist but after reading all of the reviews claiming these were the best pancakes they've ever tasted, it was sort of a let down. Don't get me wrong, I'd do more things for those pancakes than I would for a klondike bar but I don't think I'd put in the 1-2 hour wait for it. Also, make sure the bathroom's locked; the door must've been loose and I might've just ruined some guy's appetite. ...I'm still haunted by the things I've done for a Klondike bar.
Great fries and burgers.
Great halal food!
So Good! Sit at the bar if 1 or 2. Ask for recommendations.  They have fish you have never heard of.  They are all good! Love the Green Tea Iced Tea! Just LOVE!

This place is pretty good! I came here with a few friends a month ago and we had a great time. The service is very attentive and the atmosphere is relaxing and casual. My friends got the sushi buffet and they loved it (lots of yummy sounds). I got the teriyaki chicken and it was really tasty and nicely prepared. It's a BYOB place so plan accordingly and you'll have a good time here!

I took my friend here for the early bird dinner special ($18.00, from 5:30 pm to 7 pm) on Wednesday (5/15). My friend arrived at 5:30 pm sharp, but the waitress didn't seat her until I arrived. This was understandable because the early bird special could get very competitive sometimes. I've been going to Soba-ya for over 10 years, and it is always a safe place to go with friends. It is never too loud for conversations, and we can sit comfortably. I've noticed that the quality of lunch special tends to be somewhat inconsistent, but the dinner special never disappoints. I used to order the hot soba, but sometimes I found the broth a bit too salty. So I ordered the cold soba the other day, and I did like it better. Maybe I will start ordering cold soba from now on!

Grilled Corn Mexican Style served with mayonnaise, cotija cheese (hard cow's milk cheese that originated from Mexico. It is named after the town of Cotija, Michoacán), chili (sic)powder and lime by two thanks. That is all you need to know about this place.

Seriously amazing grilled cheese! I got the Brielle which has Brie, Cranberry chitney, caramelized onions, and toasted pine nuts. It also came with home made potato chips which were so addicting! Definitely worth checking this place out

Great margaritas, especially the blood orange.  The food is very good, but I still prefer distrito, especially if you are going out with a big group.  Lots of guac options, we ordered 3 different kinds and they were all great.  Fish tacos were another highlight.

Went here for dinner w/ the fam earlier this month.  tuesday night dinner at 8:30p - found awesome street parking (meter, yuck) - but it was right outside the restaurant.  got seated right away, awesome. our service was great. now the food review: appetizer: mac & cheese - must do it!  there were 3 of us, and it was the perfect amount to share.  not too much where u fill up.  it was really delicious, bread crumb topping too.  perfect crunch. mom had the fried chicken & was very happy with it.  sister had the pot roast meal - also really delicious.  i had to get the grilled cheese & tomato soup almost out of default.  i always wanna get that to compare w/ other restaurants to see who has the best.  definitely didnt care for their grilled cheese.  the tomato soup was pretty good though.  gave my leftovers to my little brother.  made me realize i should not go to comfort foods restaurants anymore and get back to eating healthy!

Delicious BBQ Pork banh mi.  I'm definitely going to have to come back and try some of the other menu items.  Fast, friendly service too. It's not the most authentic of places, but the food is great and the price is right!

Really enjoyed the food and low key ambiance at this Batali outpost. Unlike Babbo, there is a more casual atmosphere that doesn't make you feel uptight about how you're holding your silverware. The food is also more approachable, and dare I say, more palatable. When I visited Babbo, while everything was "good," I consistently criticized the saltiness of all the dishes I sampled. While at Lupa, I mustered very minor complaints. We decided on starting with the rabe and stracciatella, lingua, and calamari farro. As someone already noted, the lingua is a bit sour as it's pickled with onions. But paired with the rabe, it was perfect. The calamari farro was nice as well, a good balance of textures. We followed these dishes with the evening's special of pork shoulder and the garganelli with tripe ragu. Again, the two dishes were good independently, but superb when combined. Everything was stellar, however the fresh garganelli pasta was especially noteworthy. Surprisingly, we had ample food leftover. Which, by the way, the leftovers tasted even better the following day. I learned haphazardly that finding the right combinations and pairings of dishes is what makes for a good experience at Lupa. Every dish chosen worked well with one another, each dish complementing the others. We all agreed that though Babbo is good, it wasn't memorable enough to return. And considering the difference in dish prices, I'd say Lupa is more worth a visit, as it's also a more youthful and less contrived Babbo without compromising quality in any way. PS. The music play list is basically the same at both restaurants, which includes a lot of 80s rock and pop. + 1 for playing my favorite Psychedelic Furs songs ever. - 10 to the table next to us who couldn't correctly identify any song and then proceeded to shamelessly sing them off key anyway.

very interesting. i've tried their food many times and do continue to go back when I'm around but the honest truth is that their really isn't anything special about this. It's definitely just the hype.

This place was very good, have enjoyed the steak, BLT, and hamburger and all were delicious.  This is a sister to Jin Ramen, another delicious restaurant.  This is another great addition to the neighborhood in a location that has been difficult to fill with a  good restaurant.  I also recommend the stout beer, it was great.
Amazing crispy pizza!!!

It took us three tries to get into this place, first two times we went the wait was well over an hour so we passed and went to the other Mexican joint around the corner. They don't take reservations, go early and during the week to avoid a wait. Best margarita ever!! We got the habanero grapefruit margarita and it was awesome!! Enchilada Mole and Enchilada Verde were the best we ever had!! Third time's a charm!

Have come here twice now.  The team from Little Neck on the same block has done it again.  The food is completely different than over at little neck.  The decor is clearly less nautical and is basically basement chic.  But don't let that grungy appearance deter you from enjoying some creative cuisine.   The menu both times was very similar so it allowed me to try lots of different things. The first go around I had the foie gras dish with brioche, the carrot dish and the waygu steak that I split with a friend.  Don't let them tell you that you need 4-5 dishes.  Even for this hefty fellow and big eater, three were fine.   The second go around, I shared with the wife, the cabbage (house cured boar belly), the duck special and the sweet breads.  Plenty full and no room for dessert.   The staff was super friendly as well.   Looking forward to a return trip.

I had such an incredible lunch here yesterday! It's funny, I came here once in August and wasn't blown away. But yesterday, I was in love with every aspect of my meal. The wait to be seated took some time, but I'm willing to let it slide because the restaurant's high ranking ensures that it is always packed. My friends and I waited in nearby Herald Square Park, but the weather was beautiful so we didn't mind. However, the service inside was better than I had expected for such a busy restaurant. Also, I accidentally flagged down the wrong waitress to make a change to my order and miraculously, my food arrived the way I had wanted. The banchan and tea were great! We ordered Seafood Pancakes to start, which were baked to perfection. For my main meal, I ordered the Kimchi Cham Dubu - it was absolutely delicious. I've never been happier with a Kimchi stew at a Korean restaurant considering I'm more of a Bibimbap person. My friends also enjoyed the Bulgogi Stew and Kimchi Jigae. The prices were more or less on par with K-Town for lunch. I came here for dinner over the summer, and found it a little overpriced. However, the lunch prices are more affordable. If you're new to Korean food or a longtime fan, this is the place for you. The wait is a little long, but you'll undoubtedly be satisfied with your meal.

Not good for a quick coffee to go. I'd always seen people with the five leaves cup and wondered if it was good. So I stopped by the to-go window today to try it out. Big mistake. There was only one guy ahead of me and it took like 10 mins to get his latte. The barista was a free spirit bro and really took his time I guess. After another 5 mins I got my small Americano.
