I handed him a five dollar bill. He disappeared into the restaurant. After a minute of waiting for my change I called it quits. Does the Americano cost five dollars? I don't know. There was no menu in sight to cross reference and I didn't have time to wait any longer. The coffee was good. 5 dollars good? No. Like 2.50 good. But no coffee is worth that wait. Especially in a hurry in the morning.

The only reason this restaurant is not worthy of 5 stars is because you are from out of town and have a much better knowledge of superior brisket joints. I am not you and Delaney's gets 5 stars cause it rocks my socks. For NYC brisket, it really does not get much better (fette sau dont kill me, I have been and continue to be a loyal/regular customer). It is also very simple. Not 100 menu items - I like straight forward. "Brisket: more or less fat?" "Oh you want kick ass potato sald and red slaw? Here have a heaping serving of both." "Now go get a beer at the always uncrowded bar and smother you food in pickles and onions." - Well done guys.

very accommodating staff and large portions. Haven't had a bad meal yet.  a delicious treat.  The beef ribs are amazing and i always get the mac n cheese on the side it is very good. I dont usually order mac n cheese out. Im a total MNC snob.  If you like wawa's MNC then you just dont understand.  I tried on several occasions to get the curry shrimp but they never seemed to have it.  when i finally landed it i was kind of let down but it was still very tasty.
Incredible selection of meats and they all just melt in your mouth. If you don't like this place, we could never truly be friends.

I had a nice Basque Scramble (egg frittata) with chorizo and salsa verde, I think they forgot the pepernata and the polenta? The flavors were good, I was starving so I could have had anything at that moment. I think that if it came with some kind of starch it would have been much better. I also had  Bloody Mary that was standard. I think for the price it was OK not great, but four starts for the nice environment and company.

I can't really speak to the xenophobia accusations, I had a perfectly good interaction in terms of service personally. On the sandwich side of things, I guess I rate this place a 3.5.  It has a pretty different style steak than Pat's, but overall I prefer Pat's better and if I'm gonna make the trek out here I probably would return to Geno's because of this.  I'm glad that I can say I've tried both of these famous joints though. The meat is in thicker, fuller slices unlike Pat's style, which is thiner, smaller chopped up meat.  This unfortunately leads to the meat being dryer.  I prefer Pat's because it's juicier and tender.  Bread and onions were good though.  I tried American when I was here, but I have since become a whiz convert so maybe I'll come again to try a whiz with.

I was really excited to go to Ants Pants and I'll be back.  I was definitely not as impressed as I wanted to be.  I loved the clean aesthetic.  I loved the coffee and the sweet potato fries with chile sauce rock.   I was saddened to see the manager snap at the new dishwasher.  I know that happens and people get stressed, but I just had a sense that entire staff was really busy and morale seemed low. The breakfast burrito I ordered lacked major flavor. I will go back because I think it might have been an off day.

This place is areal deal NY Slice.  Ive visited so many places that claim to be the best but Prince St really it.  Get the white Slice with Prosciutto and thank me latter.  The regular slices are everything you could dream for and the Square slices are killer.  They are no L & B but hey they also much more acceptable. The only downside is the pizza can be a bit pricey but it is totally worth it.

Ok, look: I haven't eaten meat in a couple years, and I still recommend this place.  I grew up in Philly and my parents have been going to Nick's forever.  I have since moved away, but every once in a while I still get overwhelming cravings for a roast beef sandwich from Nick's, and as a vegetarian, that speaks volumes about how great this place is.
Had the beef stew. Excellent. I will be back.

I was a bit skeptical about the high Yelp rating but I finally got out here and I was really impressed! I had the masala dosa, spicy, which he serves with sambar soup and coconut chutney, for only $5. He has to slice up the dosa to get it to fit in the takeaway container so you don't get to see the impressive gigantic rolled up dosa like at some restaurants, however, he lets you look at it while it's cooking. The dosa skin, sambar, and chutney were just as good as any dosa I've had in a sit-down restaurant. The masala filling itself was maybe not as spicy or flavorful as it could be, but still good, especially considering it comes from a street cart. Can't wait to get back out here and try some of his other dosa offerings.

the food is a bit salty in my opinion.. but other than that everything was great.. the two of us ordered three dishes: enough with the free bread, and we had a very good time there. definitely going back again.
Excellent food, super authentic. I would have given it 5 stars if it wasn't because we were expecting to sit at the table in front of the chefs

Fun little place.  I liked the poutine and my chicken po boy sandwich was tasty.  It's not the best poutine in NYC, but I think it's respectable. Service was very friendly.   This is a great location and worth a try.

Who do I sell my soul to for this Wild Mushroom Truffle Risotto? I could eat an endless bowl of this, forever Forever ever? Forever ever. My friends and I still have dreams of this risotto to this very day. The Niokolokoba sirloin steak with pepercorn sauce is smashing. Really great food.
Wow cuban food so good cool atmosphere and good service

Over all, the food was very good and the restaurant is beautiful. There were some flaws: - A small stone in the lentils - The cannelloni was too salty. - Although it was nice that the manager spoke to us personally to explain that they had run out of an entree, it was still fairly early in the evening to have run out and it was the only vegetarian option on the menu. The service: - We had to wait a long time to order - The tables was not cleared between courses creating great clutter - The wait person did not offer us second drinks, nor did he ask us if we wanted coffee after the meal - Also, to promote their opening, the restaurant had coupons on their website for a free dessert with every entree. We printed out the coupons but left them at home. At first, the wait person pretended that the there were no such coupons. When we described them, he simply refused to extend to us the courtesy of the complimentary dessert, something that would have inspired customer loyalty.

I just moved into the neighborhood so I'm systematically trying the restaurants around me. After seeing slightly better than average reviews for this place, I figured I'd give it a try.  It was also the only sushi place (there are 3 within a block) that had a crowd on a Wednesday night so I went for it.  I got the 3 Flavor Fish Sushi Dinner which is 2 pieces of ahi, salmon, and yellowtail sashimi with a "special roll" that I couldn't figure out what it was.  It was enough food for 16 bucks and the sashimi was good enough, the roll was a bit below average, but the real object of my scorn is the wasabi.  It smelled like some sort of distasteful synthetic variety, tasted the same and wasn't really as "hot" as I like it.  Kinda put a pall over the whole meal.   I may go back to try some their other dishes, but not until I try ALL the other sushi joints nearby.

It has been crowded the past couple of tuesdays that I have been there because of the special, 5 buck plain pies plus price for additional toppings. That deal is  valid on Tuesdays from january to february and the lines are long. It is worth it though.

The Sunrise Luncheonette was a nice, clean, simple luncheonette. There was a lunch counter and also some tables and chairs. Service was swift and friendly. My chicken Salad Wrap (you can get the chicken salad on any bread) was light and tasty and came with fresh, crisp lettuce and tomato. The platter came with pickle and cole slaw. My friend and I shared an order of french fries which were nice and crisp on the outside while soft and potatoey on the inside. The home brewed tea was a bit strong. Other beverages come in bottles. A customer who left as we entered said he enjoys the homemade soups there several times a week.  The prices were very reasonable.
The food there was fairly good

We stopped in Mulberry & Vine to take a peek at the new healthy food stop in the neighborhood.  It's bright, open, spacious, clean (at least for starters), and cozy. We only wanted a quick look, but the male server by the coffee & cookie area was so friendly we ended up staying.  He offered us a try of the snickerdoodle cookies - very tasty.  Then he told us we could try anything we'd like.   We went to the other end of the counter by the salads and noticed the asian garlic pepper beef with pickled onions in the hot area.  The girl by the salads said we could not sample the hot items.  It's too bad, because we ordered this item.  I would have to say it did not leave the best impression.  The sauce was good, but the beef was not tender and it wasn't what I would consider a hot item - I wish it had been warmer to enjoy.   We, also, tried a sample and ordered the african curried tomato soup with bits of peanut.  It was delicious, warming, and satisfying.  I would recommend this item. I would say this place is nice, but I wish they would extend their sampling as they are a new business - to build loyal visitors,  people need to find their favorites.  Their choices of sustainable packaging and local ingredients are an added bonus - these are the types of responsible businesses we should support. It's already, unfortunately, seems to have turned into, yet another TriBeCa mommy hub for the women with nothing to do, but lunch and leave their children's messes everywhere - SNORE!  For the kind parents that are responsible, give their children appropriate boundaries, and are wise enough to impart manners - we salute you and thank you for bringing up proper citizens of the world!   I sincerely hope this restaurant adopts firm policies about the expected cleanliness of their guests - as in, please leave your tables clean upon departure.  It would be great if guest's children were not running wild through the place and strollers we're not blocking all entrances as well - adults need places to relax, too. We'll be back!

So this is the second time I've been to Bobby's Burger Palace, and I want to say that I am still impressed at what you can get here. I give props to one of our nation's Iron Chef to be able to create a burger chain that is pretty successful in portraying his ideas/beliefs in the food he creates (if you watch The Food Network, you probably somewhat know what I am talking about). The restaurant has an outdoor seating area, but no upper level. They sell alcohol, too! Food I was there with a friend, and we traded half of our food with each other so we were able to try the different burgers. I tried half of the L.A. Burger, half the Dallas burger, and half of the sweet potato fries. Everything was amazing! I liked the L.A. burger over the Dallas, though, because the combination worked really well together (the avocado was amazing). What made the food even better were the condiments provided right at the table! It consisted of: ketchup, mustard, jalapeño hot sauce, chipotle ketchup, and a burger sauce. The jalapeño sauce was AMAZING with the burgers; the burger sauce was decent, too, but it tasted like steak sauce. The chipotle ketchup goes really, really well with the sweet potato fries. Finally, my friend and I both also ordered milkshakes. They were really good, but I think they are too small for $5. Service Service was great, too! Bobby's Burger Palace is a store in which you order at a counter, take a number, sit down somewhere showing the number, and wait for a staff member to bring the food. Food come out soon after we ordered, so it's pretty fast. The server overheard us a few times and answered questions like "What's the Burger Sauce," and gladly gave me the answer.  When we sat down, the staff came by very quickly and gave us utensils. When they brought us our food, they also asked us if we want an explanation of the sauces, which I thought was very nice of them. Pros: Food is very good and came out fast, the sauces!! Cons:  Limited Seating, Parking around area is hard to find. Recommendations: Put some jalapeño sauce on burgers, eat fries with the chipotle ketchup and/or the spicy honey mustard given on the sides.

We found the Hartness House Inn in May and decided to have our wedding there in September. It was perfect every aspect of our stay, our familys visit and our Honeymoon there was amazing. Alla was very pleasant easy to work with and extremely thorough with all the planning. If you are looking for peace and quiet along with a romantic setting look no further. The staff, rooms, food, experience definitely top notch in my opinion. Love this place. The photographs of the wedding were spectacular, and the package deals are very reasonably priced along with the room rates. Their spa is the icing on the cake it truly puts you into a dreamland. I would recommend this Inn to anyone looking to just get away from it all, or a romantic trip for two or bring the whole family this place is good for any occassion.Thank you Alla, Alex and the Hartness staff for making our Big Day the perfect day. Much Love the Lears.

When I'm looking to impress people from out of town, this is where I go.  You cannot go wrong!  I have to admit, I was hesitant on the change from Twenty Manning to Twenty Manning Grill (complete with meat choices on the "Beef, Duck, Pork, Fowl" banner outside), but I'm in love with the place all over again!   The cocktails still make me feel like a classy lady and the menu options are delightful (butternut squash ravioli, scallops, crabcakes, half-baked Tollhouse cookie and ice cream) and the comfort food-esque daily specials make the choices expansive.  The only complaint: portion size is too small, but I guess that's what you get when you're trying to impress!

I have eaten at DeLorenzo's since I was a kid before the cops patrolled at the Hudson Street location.  Very happy they opened this beautiful store.  So worth the wait.  For a family of 4 we eat two pizzas there and take two home everytime.  We just can't get enough.  Sam is always friendly, and busy.  We like to eat there as the pizza is so much better fresh out of the oven.  Love the old time pics that are hanging in the new store.  This is not your average pizza place, this place is exceptional!  Be prepared to wait - it's worth it!

Recommended for:  lunch/dinner/snacks with friends, good tea. Food 5, Service 5, Ambiance 4. Cha-An didn't let me down.  Walking up a steep staircase, you enter a japanese oasis.  We were seated toward the back, and the restaurant was quite.  The menus come in a big book.  The majority of the book is dedicated to all the types of tea that they have.  After a little while, we finally decide.  I really like places that are truly authentic, and authentic in look, food and service.  The waitstaff spoke japanese, the bathroom had the bidet from japan (push button robo toilet - sorry guys, we don't have it), and the food and tea - AWESOME! Ordered the matcha green tea float (tastes like cool melted greentea icecream - very yummy), a chocolate soufle with rasberry pure (rich and delicious), black sesame creme brule w/black sesame icecream (HOLY MOLY THIS WAS AMAZING!) and I got green tea from Kyoto. This hit the sweet spot.  My waitress checked up on me every 10 or 15 minutes to ask if I wanted more tea.  They served the tea in a little pot that has enough water for one cup; but that is one cup of truly delicious tea. I thought we had the best black sesame creme brule and ice-cream at Sakagura, but Cha-An, you have taken that title!  For amazing tea, desserts, service and more, check out Cha-An.  I'll be back to try the regular food, which I can only imagine, is just as good as everything else. Sean Approved:  Zettaini ita houga ii yo!!!

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this restaurant before.  This is by far my favorite Cuban restaurant in NYC.  Everything I've had has been consistently good. -Croquetas de jamon: flavorful, creamy -Pollo guajira: great combination of sweet plantain with savory chicken -Ropa vieja: crispy plantain basket with shredded beef, sooooo good! -Bistec de palomilla: My favorite, the steak is juicy! -Tres leche: doesn't taste like coconut, tastes more like pineapple but still good. Overall a great place to go to.  They have several dining areas, upstairs front is near the live music; upstairs rear is a little quieter and the downstairs lounge is great for happy hour specials.

Tried Miriam before a show at the Barclay's Center ( a couple of blocks down the street). We arrived with no reservations in the midst of a snowstorm and were shown to an empty table. The place packed up fairly quickly thereafter. My girlfriend feels like there were not many choices on the menu. We ordered the kadaif wrapped shrimp with the harissa aioli. They were good, but only 3 on an order. I feel that the waitress could have done a little bit better in explaining the meze options. They are very small plates and there is a discount for ordering four. Our entrees were good but not memorable. I had the Dorado with fennel purée (did not taste the fennel) and vegetable ragu (seems like it was only lentils). It tasted good, but I expected more from it. My girlfriend had the chicken shawarma. The chicken was well cooked. The green tahini was nothing special and the mango chutney had an odd taste.   Dessert was the best part. We shared a baked middle eastern cheese with kadaif. It came with crushed pistachios and pistachio ice cream. Do not be discouraged when the waiter brings out a tray with the desserts. They look terrible on the tray but you will pleasantly surprised with dharma they actually bring to the table.

We used to love this place until this past week. My company comes here multiple times a week for group lunches because it's close to our office and we usually have a great experience but after last week we will not be returning. We made a reservation through open-table as we always do, and we even got a call the day before to confirm the reservation. When we showed up to the tavern they had no record of our reservation and made us stand there as they seated multiple parties coming in after us. They finally seated us (after I had to complain to the manager with all of my employees standing there feeling embarrassed). They sat us in the back of the restaurant at a table that looked like it was sized for children, with tiny little mini bar stools with no backs. Since we were hungry and running late at this point we dealt with it. It took 15 minutes to have a drink order placed and then took an hour and 10 minutes for our food to come out. Now what blows my mind about this is that we all ordered the steak special which is uncooked and comes out raw on a hot stone. So how did it take over an hour to prepare uncooked steak? The others at the table had cold sandwiches so nothing even required cooking except our french fries! Sorry to say it's probably the last time we will go there for our weekly group lunches. Time to find a new favorite spot.
it is not good place

I feel sad to give one of my favorite restaurants a bad mark.  I used to  love this restaurant.  We went to breakfast there this morning and I did not feel the love.  Service is so important to me.  I love feeling welcomed and special.  (isn't that why we pay a little extra?)  My water was not refilled -- nor my coffee.  I had to ask.  I had to track down the waiter to get them to take my credit card.  This should not happen at the Fountain.   There are too many other good restaurants with great service for me to go to.

This is the second time I've dined here since they opened, and I'm really glad we decided to stop in.  Their escargot, paired with their simple salad to round off my meal, was delicious, and my boyfriend was very happy with the burger.  Although I wish it came with more fries for me to mooch.  For dessert, we enjoyed their profiteroles.   We sat at the bar and the bartenders were incredibly friendly, if not spread a little too thinly due to how packed the restaurant was.  It's great to see Chez Moi doing so well, and I look forward to coming back again and again.

What a splendid dining experience I had at Westville Chelsea. Every step of the meal was superb - I very very rarely speak so highly about a dinner out. I hate paying high prices and getting small portions and almost always leave disappointed. But not at Westville. First of all, they were packed, with a 20 minute wait for a table. But we luckily snagged 2 bar stools and they serve full menu at the bar. Sweet. My boyfriend ordered the fish & chips. I ordered the hot dogs with chili & cheese. He still can't stop talking about how good the fish was, even weeks after we ate there. And my hot dogs were out of this world. Top-notch meat, awesome chunky chili and drippy melted cheddar. So. Good. Our bartender/waitress was extremely attentive, even bringing my boyfriend a sample of a mixed drink he was debating about getting. He didn't end up ordering one, but it was really thoughtful of her to let him try it. Anyway, what else can I say? Westville gets a gold star in my book and I GREATLY look forward to visiting again.

I've always been a fan of Jones, and I'm clearly not alone since this restaurant has been around for quite a while. I swung by after tonight's Yelp Elite Event for a bite and was not disappointed. The menu offers something for everyone. Since our threesome was all in agreement that the "cheese hold the meat burger" sounded great, we decided to share it as an app. This pseudo-burger consisted of a soft and buttery roll with a giant slab of haloumi cheese, lemon aioli, lettuce and tomato. We hacked it into threes and I was instantly wishing there was more to go around. Our server told us it's a new addition to the menu, and to that I say: "Well played, Jones. Well played." I also had the ahi tuna tacos, which were good, but not as good as the non-burger burger. Everything in the tacos is served cold; essentially ahi tuna in taco shells, with lettuce, cilantro and a spicy aioli. I'll be back for that haloumi burger.

My boyfriend and I were really excited for Jacob's Pickles to open.  I loved the whole industrial look of the place, I loved the beer list, and I was excited for chicken and biscuits!  But everything was kind of blah.  The service was nice, but slow.  (Slow on a slow night.) My Mac & Cheese was way too salty and tasted like Penne Alfredo. The beer was way too expensive. The music was bizarre.  Overall fun concept, but a disappointment in execution.

The Fine Grind: A Coffee Bar. This is an amazing coffee house. It's small but all the staff is so nice and the drinks are so delicious. They have free WiFi, live music on Wednesdays, gourmet gift baskets, mugs, tea, fresh coffee beans, and TFG t-shirts. They make fresh brewed coffees, the finest espressos, cappuccino and flavored lattes, gourmet teas and chai, "blendesso" frozen drinks, frozen hot chocolate (froho), fresh brewed iced teas, bagel sticks, yogurt muffins, hot panini, salads, hand crafted biscottis and delicious specialty desserts that change with season. They also have an assortment of absolutely delicious, melt-in-your-mouth organic brownies, blondies, and other desserts. A very popular dish is their fondue pot for four, but it can feed well over four. The atmosphere is colorful, chipper and comfortable. They have wacky, curvy, puzzle-piece type tables and warm colors to compliment the local artists artworks decorating the walls. Everything is decorated down to the cups and dish ware with curvy designs and warm colors. They even have small board games and question games to help you have fun with some friends while you are there. This is definitely a nice hang out, when it's not too busy.
stop #23 on our FOODSTRAVAGANZA still ranks as #1 for pizza in my book. better than anything i had in italy (see previous review).

Stopped in here because the weather had gotten warm (time for a shake) and because I had heard their bahn mi was one of the better ones in the city. The staff were all very nice, and my sandwich was ready fairly quickly.  I knew I couldn't finish both my avocado shake and my whole bahn mi and not feel like my stomach would explode, so I opted to enjoy my shake in the sun while walking to the D train, and put my sandwich to the "does it hold up for a 45 minute ride home" test. The shake was interesting.  Also it was huge.  I was very full when I decided to just toss the last bit out.  I LOVE avocado, but I've never thought to add sugar and milk and turn it into an icy shake.   I had ordered the roasted pork bahn mi, so it took a little longer to make than a #1 would have.  I had asked for medium spicy, however, I'm not used to jalapeños on my bahn mi, so that took me by surprise (and I therefore took it off the other half of the sandwich).  Other than the jalapeño, though, it wasn't that spicy at all.  One thing I didn't like about this sandwich was the bread.  I wish I had read in advance that they toast it, and I would've asked for it as is.  That's why I gave this place only 4 stars rather than bumping it up to 5.   I like that they offer quite a few variations of the sandwich, and the decent list of hot and cold drinks is nice as well.  If it was more convenient to get to, I would definitely be in here often enough to try more of the sandwich and shake options, however, it'll have to be just a nice treat when I'm in Sunset / Borough Park. I've tried quite a few of the options for bahn mi in NY and while I haven't tried all of them, this is definitely near the top (other than the bread), especially considering the price and the options.  If you're planning on having a picnic in Sunset Park, or wandering around Greenwood, this would be a great place to stop for lunch.

I just went here for the first time last night because we heard about their half price wine night. Woo! What a good deal, we got a 37 dollar (originally 74!) bottle of Brunello, you just can't find that in any other restaurant in the city. It was delicious and accented our leg of lamb entree perfectly. Everything is so wonderfully seasoned and cooked perfect with such wonderful flavors. We couldn't avoid ordering the mezes because they are perfect little "tastes" of a bunch of things. I highly recommend and we will definitely be back.

The West Village is a relative Sahara for diners and drinkers, especially those on a budget or expecting a quick bite.  Plenty of larger, higher-end restaurants abound (their product may or may not justify the time and money spent), but small, quick meals are hard to find, excepting the ubiquitous pizzerias that are, coincidentally, quite awful in this neighborhood as well. I began to wonder if the Sarah Jessica Parkers and investment bankers who populate this tony zip code were not pressuring local chefs to serve up enough $10 lunches. Could the glitterati survive off of the Waverly Inn alone? The dearth of a quick lunch, a snack even, weighed upon my mind when I was rescued, simultaneously, from financial constipation and hunger by the delivery of assorted pita sandwiches brought by a good friend.  Small, harissa flavored falafel balls, eggplant and hard-boiled egg sandwiches and smoothies from A Thousand and One Nights were undressed from their paper bag gowns and wax paper robes to reveal the sexiest, most delicious treats I had yet to enjoy anywhere near Greenwich and 7th Avenue. The kitchen that produced this bountiful dish was just around the corner.  Taïm, tucked into a cubbyhole space on Waverly Place, boasts 3 or 4 tall stools in the window and another facing the wall for super-serious, penitent or recalcitrant diners.   There is a bench outside, but most of the business is takeout.  The storefront crowds awkwardly but patrons are patient with the gymnastics required to swing the door open and order all at once. Each time I have visited since, I have ordered at the counter from a frumpy blonde girl of indeterminate origin (her accent suggests Australian or South African) who likely is as lacking in work permits as she is in acumen and efficiency; nevertheless, she manages to convey my wishes to the cooks who plate surprisingly satisfying salads of marinated beets or carrots and the other Israeli treats upon which chef/owners Einat Admony and Stefan Hafziger (the two are married, as well) have borrowed and improvised. No surprise, Admony is a trained chef and Hafziger is a veteran of Bouley's best kitchens.  The two have kept it simple but flavorful.  Fries are served with a saffron aioli whose hay-like fragrance is just enough to ballast this dish. Falafel comes in three flavors: cilantro-parsley-mint; roasted red pepper; and harissa--the last of which I am inclined to order.  Smaller than usual--about the size of a melon ball--these chickpea delicacies radiate with flavor and are vibrant greens and reds.  They can be ordered as a plate or served in sandwich and served with Israeli salad (hummus and baba ghanoush as platters).  Of course, this all sounds so familiar to anyone who has entered a falafel stand (my favorite is Falafel Drive-In, in San Jose, CA). The Sabich is what separates Taïm from its competitors.  A staple of Tel Aviv street food, the sabich was brought by Iraqi Jews for whom this eggplant, egg and salad pita was a Saturday morning meal ('sabah' means morning in Arabic).  Released from city of Ramat Gan, sabich has become a hit for young Israelis on the go and it is easy to understand why.  A balance of tasty veggies and protein seasoned with amba (a mango pickle) and wrapped in a portable pita, this is the reason to frequent Taïm.   I ate these sandwiches with Moroccan carrot salad (garlic and cumin swirl in olive oil) every Sunday this summer between 4 and 5pm, and I never needed to eat again until Monday morning. To slurp on one of the $5 smoothies is something of a luxury, and a budget breaker if you want to stay under $10.  However, the date-lime-banana combination is the perfect compliment to a meal.  Smoothies are also flavored with the likes of pear, Thai basil, coconut milk cantaloupe or ginger.  For $3, brown sugar lemonade will slate your thirst and leave you wondering what refined, white sugar is for besides baking. Taïm might be the best place to eat in all of the West Village, budgets be damned.

It's not a usual review but a statement about Wings At the Brainard Airports good taste in evening party music!  Back by popular demand, Saturday May 18, 2013 after 10pm GRUPO PODEROSO Carlos E. Perez. sings at  Wings At the Brainard Airport . 20 Lindbergh Drive . Hartford. 860-241-1114 and no cover for this great dance band!

Here on  a work trip, saw how packed it was and thought, it must be good. Place was PACKED on a Tuesday night. Gauc was amazing and I had the Mahi Mahi tacos...so good, and the lime corn for a side. WOW. Everything was cooked to perfection, flavors were spot on, and not greasy .

Absolutely the best vendor chicken I've ever tasted! It was crisp on the outside and soft on the inside, yet it was very well-done, just how I like my chicken.  The pita was soft and fresh.  The service was very friendly, and  I was offered a falafel appetizer as I waited.   Best vendor experience ever!

My rating is only based on the service and the wine I drank. The service I received was excellent as the bartender greeted me and made sure I didn't wait to long. I asked for some suggestion since they specialize in wine. I told him what I was looking for and his suggestion of wine was right on the money! I however was a bit disappointed to pay $16.50 for a glass of wine in an airport. I did like the fact that they have some much outlets underneath the bar to charge your phone/laptop. The place is nice with a nice decor.

I was a little worried about this place being off the beaten path and being able to catch a taxi back to our hotel from here in the evening. Web pics only showed dark/lonely 21st St.   But, it is actually right on the corner of 1st Avenue and taxi was no problem. We three made a reservation for 7:30PM Halloween night but got there an hour early with no problem getting seated.  Ordered Crispy Pata, Sizzling Sisig, Pork Adobo, Bangus Sinigang & Kare-Kare.  I can't speak for the latter two I (Americano) only ate the Crispy Pata, Sisig & Adobo which were all very good.  Actually its only the 2nd time I've had Sisig actually Sizzling, could hear it coming from the kitchen (and on an Iron Skilet on wooden serving board!)   The waiter was great and the food came in short time. If Filipino food is on your short list of things to do in NYC, I highly recommend Grill-21.
Awesome little spot. Nice Decor & Ambiance. Friendly waitstaff. Food = AMAZING. my new Thursday spot.

I kind of love that they just do their thing here and don't take reservations. Chill place with chill staff just looking to cook and serve some quality seafood. I like to start with some oysters (they were out of some types last time I was there - not sure if this is typical) and a glass of wine and a simple fish entree (seasoned and cooked to perfection). Your meal can be quick or you can choose to sit a little more casually while sipping your drink. Most importantly, it's very casual and reliable. Some person below complained about staff screaming orders and eating in front of patrons. That person needs to loosen up and go elsewhere for their seafood fix.

This is some good stuff. You can't get food like this everywhere. I love the authenticity of this joint. Every time I go I get something different and I haven't been let down yet. Get their carne asada tacos! You can't go wrong! Worth every penny!

My girlfriend and I are new to the area, so when we find a great spot, we seem to keep coming back. We have been to El Almacen many times already. We usually go during late in the week since it is too busy on the weekends and always get the same waitress - Kelley, who both my girlfriend and I LOVE.  Yes, the restaurant seems to hire only very attractive waitresses - but we never have anything but great service. And since when is having an attractive nice waitress a bad thing?  She always lets us know the specials for the night and gives us recommendations AND she stays on top of our drinks - the MOST important thing! ha! Its nice to feel like we are regulars already! Now to the food. The food is outstanding. The avocado fries are delicious. As well as the fish tacos. The skirt steak is perfection. But they also have other options if you are not a meat eater (like my gf).  Our meals come out relatively quickly. The chocolate cake is pretty basic, but the other deserts - the crepe and the churros are unique and delicious. I recommend this restaurant 100%.

Last night for one of many birthday celebrations, my brother took me to Vernick.  It was by far one of the best meals I've had in Philly .  Being related to a chef brings about some worthy connections in the culinary world.  When we first sat down at the chef's counter, we were greeted by former coworkers and a friendly server.  The wine and cocktail list had a great variety.  I drank a bougelais throughout the meal and my brother had the cl smooth, appropriately named and fresh! The chef sent over the the crispy potatoes and grilled shishito peppers with lemon zest.  A great way to get started.  We then ordered one of the special toasts with chicken liver pate and red onion chutney - just outstanding!  I have to explicitly state that you could eat just the toasts at Vernick and be totally satisfied.  We watched the Sous grill dozens of sourdough slices to perfection each and every time.  We also ordered the hamachi and were sent the arctic char - both delicious and fresh.  The char served with the crispy skin was mouth-wateringly good, drizzled with what I think was a chili/truffle oil.   The house-made mozzarella was a must and the mussels were a different take on the traditional bowl with broth and bread.  These were deconstructed, shell-less and served with soaked croutons, cabbage mixed into the dijon broth - just divine! We ordered the potato ravioli which was a great size for sharing and really savory.  I love that the lamb pieces were on the outside and not minced into the ravioli mixture.  Great sauce with haricot vertes and a herb crustini sprinkling on top. The chicken liver pate toast wasn't enough for us so we order two more toasts to finish off the meal: the fromage blanc and komquat and the beef tartar.  The fromage was a great combination, a bit sweet and took me right back to Paris.  The beef tartar had fresh horseradish and what I think was small bites of Pecorino cheese.  I loved them both! Overall, I think this might be my new favorite spot in Philly, and luckily it's right around the corner.  The service was friendly and paced well.  I loved sitting at the counter and watching the magic unfold.   Oh and the pecan pie with a candle for dessert was just the best finale!

Sangria by the Liter!!! What a great way to spend a summer evening by yourself, with your intimate partner or with a group of friends. You can by Sangria by the pitcher for $40. And they have a nice selection of bar food and other specialties like calamari which I suggest.

The food is five stars, but our experience was marred by the service and the tight quarters. 1. The food, I really enjoyed the food. The ricotta pancakes were superstar. The pancake was good on its own, without the the taste being hidden by a bunch of toppings. The mrs. had the moroccan scramble. She  didn't enjoy it is much as the she should've liked. She regrets not ordering the BLAT, which is a great name by the way. 2. The tables are extremely small when compared to the amount of food provided. We had to do a lot of maneuvering to fit everything on the table, and unfortunately a casualty occurred. The coffee spilled, and the waitress made no attempt to clean it up, apologize, or refill (they charged us for the refill later) 3. The atmosphere was cool. It is very hipster and eclectic. Its very good to people watch and to observe all the different styles and personalities walking in and around the neighborhood. The experience would have been top notch, but the whole coffee incident sort of soured us. For 50 bucks, it would have been worth it.

This place is great, not the best ramen i've ever had (albeit ranks top 3), but it certainly lives up to the hype. There are only two ramen dishes I get whenever I'm here: the Shiromaru Hakata or Akamaru Modern. I don't have any desire to try the rest because these two just hit the spot. I also like their chicken wings and pork buns (obviously). Plum wine adds a delicious touch. The place itself is nice, clean, etc. Standard. Nice ambiance, friendly staff. My first time coming here I waited for 2.5 hours before we were seated. I was hangry by the time I actually got to eat, so make sure you plan your timing appropriately. Otherwise you will be waiting. I'm sure if you came here during the middle of the day, it wouldn't be an issue.
Love the salads. The sandwiches are good, especially the windy city. They could use a little more oomph in flavoring though. Overall, a wonderful addition to the neighborhood and great service.

A late edition to the jean-george line of restaurants, stands an over pretentious and butt end location (literally opening into the west side highway) restaurant. Quick synopsis: My sister took me and my mother here for brunch as a mini celebration for her swearing in ceremony. Prix fixe menu is not the way to go. My mom even commented that their chilled cucumber foam (complimentary of the chef) tasted like cold "pickle water."  It was probably meant to "cleanse" the palate, but in my thoughts....cleanse what?? We had barely consumed anything but their wine. I don't get this place nor are the dishes very memorable. All I have to say is thank god for the bottle of prosecco to dumb my taste buds. I will add one star more because of one positive aspect which is the the decor. Very chic with modern flare. A lovely feel of openess and great natural lighting due to the floor to ceiling window treatment. Unfortunately as with everything looks can be deceiving. Again...a place my sister chose, hence a very "Jessica place" as we like to call it.

There were indo chinese options, but we didn't order any of those. We ordered the chicken tikka masala, samosas, a lamb dish, and an eggplant dish. All of the meat was cooked beautifully. I really enjoyed eating here more than I thought I would. I don't know what I was actually expecting, but I was pleasantly surprised. We finished everything. EVERYTHING. We would have licked the plates if we weren't in the restaurant. Samosas were meh. The desserts weren't anything to write about. You could probably get the same thing during buffet time. Speaking of buffet time, they have it for lunch and now I really want to go here for lunch buffet if things are cooked as well as they were for our dinner.

Tops is great. I've never been disappointed coming here. How many diners do you know sell alcohol I don't know too many. My girlfriend and I are addicted to there breakfast cocktails. The bellini is Everyhing! They have ever cake known to man on display here and it's delicious. I love tops. I've been to a few diners in NJ and this is def the best Diner in NJ hands down.

Went there for brunch yesterday morning with my wife and three others.  We are definately Philly foodies and love the food at the owner's other location (N. Third). I ordered the pork belly omlette and it was awful!  Small omlett, eggs were over cooked and the pork belly was almost unedible!  My wife and cousin both had the classic eggs benedict and once again the eggs were overcooked.  Yolks were hard boiled, poached eggs are supposed to be runny!  They were also chinsy on the side potatoes.  (potatoes were good!)  Also, it had to be 80-85 degrees in there, a/c was horrble and we were all unconfortable.  Service was decent but even if the food was good (not), if you are uncomfortable your experience is already ruined!  I was really disapointed and will never go back.  Go to N. Third instead.

Quick Fixx has been a consistently awesome go-to place for eats in my neighborhood for me even before I moved into the neighborhood. The day I rented my first place in Philly, I stopped in Quick Fixx because I needed just that: quick food, and healthy-ish, if at all possible. With their expansive salad menu prominently displayed on the wall, I quickly made the decision to slowly inhale something before the apartment open house. I ordered the goat cheese salad, which was delicious and delivered to me in around 10 minutes. Win! [And then I successfully rented my current apartment. Win again!] I remember especially loving the strawberries within the salad, currently replaced by (probably) more season-friendly apple slices, which are also quite nice. This salad has a nice balance of fruit, veggies and a little carbs with tortellini thrown in for good measure. This is the kinda combo that I know makes me feel full for a long time without the sluggishness of consuming a heavy meal, so it's kinda become my perfect option for lunch. Having just lovingly described my usual order, yesterday, I stopped into Quick Fixx and tried something outside of my usual, which was the arugula salad and the pierogis: yum! This is a more simple salad consisting of arugula, parm cheese, and dressing, but the dressing used for the arugula is kinda special: it's savory and lemon-y and just lovely. As an unofficial pierogi expert (qualifications: Central PA native, kinda Polish), these were great! They were fried in a way that felt lighter than I've tried elsewhere and had a nice amount of filling. The filling itself was pretty standard, but good. I'd be interested in trying the jalapeño pierogis someday. I am thankful to have this wonderful little spot on the edge of Rittenhouse that offers year-round freshness!

I was lucky enough to get a table on an early saturday dinner at Char No.4. Everytime i walk by, it's packed. So i'm curious to see what this place is all about. The food is yummy, to read more about it, see beeneatingaround.blogspo…

We had a great dinner here the other night. We kept to the vegetarian options, Sichuan spicy cucumber, salt & pepper tofu and Buddha's sesame beef, and were blown away. We'll return the next time we're in Burlington. I only wish they had a second location in Boston.

I am truly a fan!!! Got the chicken over rice (fried rice + ginger white sauce + kimchi + salsa).  The chicken is so flavorful and the ginger white sauce is so creamy but not heavy (i.e. with the kimchi on side).

We are serb natives and went to this place while visiting nyc for a taste of home.  We ordered the cevapi, pljeskavica and karadjordjeva.  They were delicious and had authentoc flavor. The bread and ajvar (red pepper spread) were a little bland and you could tell the ajvar was not homemade.  Other than that all of the prepared food was delicious

Went on a sunday for Brunch, filled with young "hipsters" got there a little late around 2:30ish, waited about an hour :(, Unfortunately I did not get the full food experience because they ran out of quite a few items on the menu. I love that its BYOB... we brought champagne and made mimosas. FYI they do not take reservations. We had disco tots-- super yummy- not enough gravy, fried green tomatoes- a must if you come here. For my entree I had the chicken and waffles, it was really good but lacking some flavor, I tried the pulled pork sandwich it was good but the pulled pork I make is better (to others it may be great but they never ate at my house), I really liked the corn flake chicken sandwich it was very tasty. For desert we had red velvet bread pudding, it was not cooked all the way- raw in the middle.tThe staff was really nice.  I think its hard for this place to keep up with the volume of people it attracts. Not sure if I will go back again but its a cool place to check out.
Good for traditional Japanese but staff is rude.   They talk down to you if you are not familiar with the menu.

I don't often give a place 5 stars, but Highlands just really rocks. It has great cocktails, wine selection, unique drafts, and of course an enormous selection of whiskey and scotch. It's also a really sexy, but relaxed, atmosphere. I've been there dozens + times for cocktails and about a handful of time for food. While Scotts aren't generally known for their culinary savant, the chef here really does excellent things for Scottish cuisine's reputation in NYC. Everyhting that I've eaten there has been delicious, I really cannot recall disliking anything. On a recent visit I was particularly wow'ed by the scallops appetizer. Service is fantastic! But come on an off night. Fri/Sat can get unbearably busy!
Still don't see what all the fuss is about. Food is mediocre and service spotty.   Lorenzos is close and better.

Amazing. The combo platter from this place is the tastiest, manliest meal you can have for $6 in NYC. No frou-frou sh*t here. Just well-seasoned meat on a fluffy bed of rice drowned in a delicious white sauce. It's as if David Beckham (the manliest guy in the world) shot magic all up in my mouth. Yes, that good. Also, yeshetero. Random tips: 1) I love spicy food as much as anyone I know (to the extreme, I'll drink bottles of 500K+ Scoville unit 'designer' hot sauces for fun), but don't overdo it on the red sauce. You want to fully taste how good these plates are. 2) Even if you don't like lamb, go for the combo platter. I usually think lamb tastes like a weird mix of flowers, gamey-ness, and meat, but it's well done here and the chicken alone does seem like it'd be a touch bland. 3) Lastly, some cabbie told me that you can jump the primary line by telling these dudes you're in the 'cab line.' Normally, I would dismiss this, but this cab driver's name was also Leo, so he must be awesome/telling the truth.

I returned to Sawatdee for dinner on Monday night. It was night two of my Thai cravings and I had to satisfy the beast. The hype of Sawatdee's opening has definitely waned and we were able to score a table with no problem. Service was notably better than my previous two experiences at lunch and dinner. Water glasses were kept filled and everything was cooked just the way we asked. For a starter, we shared the grilled chicken skewers with peanut sauce and cucumber relish. A nice little bite before the meal and not too heavy, either. I ordered chicken pad Thai sans tofu for my main, and I opted for a two star level of spiciness out of three. At first, the dish didn't seem spicy, but it was a deceptively slow burn. By the time I was three quarters of the way through, I was chugging water and had to tap out. Next time, I'll go with one star of heat. Truth be told, I'm kind of a heat pansy. But my meal was damn good nonetheless. I don't know what they do at Sawatdee that is different from other Thai places, but the noodles are just so much better. They easily swirl around a fork and are never stuck together. And the flavors of all the ingredients really pop. That was especially true for my dining partner's dish, the pad kee mao gai. Wow, was that good. I'm not positive that my cravings for Thai have truly been satisfied at this point. It probably won't be long before I'm back for another fix.

I had the PAPILLOTTE: Tilapia with carrots, potatoes, onions, and herbs in a white wine sauce steamed in parchment paper with a side of haricot verts and mashed potatoes. My friend had the RISOTTO AU POULET with chicken, string beans, potatoes, fresh basil, garlic and onion. Both dishes were excellent! The place is cozy and laid back and the staff is friendly. I will definitely be returning back soon. Two Thumbs up!
It was delicious.
This place is awful.  Super unprofessional.  Completly unorganized.  Food is mediocre.  Do not waste your time, or your money.
This was our first outing @ Red Basil we are very impressed,  The Vegetarian spicy eggplant was so good. We will be coming back soon

Last weekend I ate here for the second time. The flavors are great and so is the service. Only things holding me back from giving 5 stars are: 1) I feel like there is SO much left on the menu to try that I can't truly judge the food yet and 2) The interior of the restaurant isn't amazing and while the wide open feel is great for big groups it wouldn't be a good atmosphere for a romantic date night. Definitely excited to visit again and try something new!

5 stars for service & fun! My friend who newly relocated to Philly and I found out that this place was serving homemade s'mores for Philly Beer Week so we stopped by... specifically for that. haha Despite being very indecisive over their very extensive menu/list of beers, our bartender (darn me for forgetting his name) was super nice in giving recommendations and time we needed to finally choose. He was also tons of fun as we hung around for at least a couple hours and always checked up on us, even if if it was cuz I drink ice water like camel.

I love this place! They have the best breakfast sandwiches with the freshest ingredients and delicious bread. Even their ketchup tastes better than usual. Their homemade fruit iced teas are the perfect beverage for summer days. Plus there's a bunch of other snacks/drinks you can buy, you can pick and choose from different beers and make your own six-pack for only $10. It really doesn't get any better than this. Favorite coffee shop in Greenpoint for sure.

I almost wish my friend hadn't taken me here... he's effectively ruined Israeli/Mediterranean fod for me.  DC simply has nothing like this, and as much as I love Lebanese Taverna, Amsterdam Falafel, etc. this is simply in a different league. My friend ordered the mixed Falafel Platter and I had the Sabich Platter, which came with fried Eggplant, Moroccan carrots, Israeli salad, an egg, hummus, wheat pita, and three dipping sauces.  WOW.  This was so fresh, so well prepared, and so flavorful.   The guy behind the counter was very friendly and he was the one that actually recommended the Sabich Platter, as I was trying to decide between the Falafel platter and that.  My friend and I shared our dishes, and his falafels were some of the best, if not THE best, I've ever had; small, perfectly fried, great spice, each flavor more unique than the previous.  Also, I'm not usually a big fan of tabouleh, but their version of it is really quite delicious.  I also had the date, lime and banana shake... so good. This place is three blocks from my friend's spot in Greenwich Village... guess where I'm going next time I'm in the city.  Taim and Murray's Bagels are officially on the "must eat while visiting my friend Austin" list.
La Calaca Feliz serves up a banging margarita. On top of its superb beverage options La Calaca Feliz has an overall great menu. I recommend the plantains, the corn, the carnitas taco, and nachos.

I really liked this place.  Great vibe, a bit noisy but it was fun.  Staff very friendly.  Food was excellent.  Tuna carpaccio, smoke trout appetizers and lamb shank entree with polenta, cheese plate were all above expectations.  Would go back in a heart beat.

I love this restaurant. The front is casual bar +food, and the back is a surprisingly light and airy restaurant. Totally feels like the South, or as close as you can get in Brooklyn. I had a sweet tea sour which was very sweet, but all the drinks and beer looked good. We shared a salad and jalapeno cornbread to start, both which were basic but delicious. I had the meatloaf sandwich which was AMAZING - thick pullman bread, perfectly cooked and seasoned meatloaf, tangy slaw, and homemade potato chips. mmmm so good, can't wait to go back! My date had the trout which he liked, but was overshadowed by the smoky crispy onion rings on the side. I wanted to try the bread pudding but was too full... Great vibe, great food, and get the meatloaf sandwich!

Not worth the wait or the money.  Soul food may not be the most common cuisine in this city, but there are definitely better places.   I wasn't a big fan of the ribs... the sauce is loaded with sugar, but there's not much else to it.  less sugar, more spice!  don't get me wrong, sweetness is good, but southern food is about flavor too.  when I order cheese grits, I don't want just grits with cheese sprinkled on top.  there's more to it than that. it's not a bad place, but if this is your first soul food experience, don't let it be your last.

Good food and awesome drinks (beer and cocktail selection are great). The service is great as well. I've been here for dinner and brunch now and both times I left full and content. I have no complaints about anything the restaurant has control over.
Our server was very friendly and personable. The food was DELICIOUS! Will definitely go back again.

I'm sure the food would have been fine if I'd been able to eat any of it ... especially since my friend so highly recommended it and said how popular it was. But unfortunately it is one of those Thai restaurants where all their sauces have been pre-made and contain either or both soy sauce and fish sauce. The other dishes that did not already contain these were the entrees but none of the entrees were vegetarian/vegan. This meant a vegan gluten-free person like myself literally could not eat anything on the menu. So we had to leave. I understand that this makes it easy for the kitchen to quickly put together dishes when they are ordered but is not good for serving anyone with food allergies or sensitivities. At least our server was understanding and made the effort to go clarify with the cooking staff. And she understood why we had to leave. And the decor inside seemed pretty nice.

Delicious!! I've been to a few places for chicken and waffle and this one, so far, is the best! My hubs got the steak and eggs and he finished it in 2seconds. The Mac n Cheese not only looks good, but it is so crunchy, yet tender. Will be coming back

This place is fine if slightly hipster is what you're looking for in a diner. I went for breakfast and was in the mood for some conventional diner egg plate, but they were a bit short in this area. It seems more like a lunch/dinner place. One of my pet peeves with any restaurant is not having decaf coffee. Long gone are the days of tasteless decaf, so why not have some on hand?

Disappointed: This place used to have great pies....I haven't ordered in a while...so I was craving it .  I ordered one of the "Gourmet" pizzas called the Genovese....it sounded incredible.... Pesto, garlic, sausage, mushrooms, mozzarella $17.95 for a small (6 pieces).  Should be great for that price I was drooling in anticipation When I got it....  The garlic was overpowering to the extent that I don't even know if there was pesto on it (IMO: the pesto and sausage are the focal points of this pie).  The mushrooms were fresh, but the crumbled sausage was less than scarcely sprinkled on the pie.  The sausage was not fresh, it is probably processed and ordered in bags. Almost $20.00 for six tiny pieces of THAT?...   No way!!!! I don't mind paying that much.... But if you're going to charge that much...and call it "Gourmet"........I expect to have my mind blown My advise.....GO TO JOEY GARLIC'S

Wowza! I've been craving a "Boiling Crab" (from CA) type of food ever since I moved out of the Bay Area.. I was visiting some friends in NY and we decided to stop by this place. I've actually tried this place during my last visit in Jan 2014 but somehow this experience was much more different-- in a good way! First of all, our server, Asa (sp? - cool dude w tattoos) was superb. He was very attentive and addressed our needs instantly. Actually, we didn't even have to ask for much. He was just on top of everything. He and the busboy were pretty efficient. And by that I mean refilling our waters, constantly (but not overbearing) checking in on how everything was.. etc. etc.  I remember customer service being on point the last time I was here so, glad that didn't change! Next? the food! Amazeballs. The sauce for the shrimp was pretty darn tasty! Compared to the Boiling Crab sauce (come on, this comparison is inevitable), it was creamier and a lot less oily! BC sauce is delicious but oily. The Boil's sauce is just beyond my tastebud's expectations. Whooot for happy tastebuds! TIPS: CASH ONLY! They have an ATM inside in case you forget your moolah. The last time I was here, my friends and I came pretty late... I believe around 8 and we had to wait. SO there will probably be a wait. This time around, my friends and I went when they opened at 5 and were seated promptly. So go a little early if you don't want to wait. Guess it depends how busy the night is, though! Anyway, yes I recommend this place and definitely will be back (if I visit NY again.) The cajun fries are pretty awesome too!

I visited in August but I'm bored at work thinking about biscuits so writing about really good biscuits gives me some sort of strange satisfaction. I came in a group of 6 for brunch on a Saturday and the wait to be seated was not bad at all even though this place was very busy.  Our waitress was nice, our service in general was fast and we were in a bit of a hurry so that was appreciated.  All of the food we got was done just perfect; it was delicious and the presentation was delightful (mmmmhhhhhhmmm). They do southern food better than most places I've been to down here in VA, although maybe since I'm in Northern VA it's not southern enough. On second thought, writing this review may have just made me a little dismayed that I'm not eating here right now.

I've gone here twice now and both experiences have been good. The first time, I went with some buddies and chilled at the bar first.  Had straight tequila on the rocks. The bartenders are hot and cold and moody. The 2nd time, went on NYE with a group of 10. Both times, we had good waitresses, one was a nice Brazilian lady and the other was an Eastern European lady with a deep accent.  Both were attentive and nice. Food(as I remember): Guacamole: good for a latin, non-Mexican restaurant. Crab Croquettes-Meh, too heavy and not enough crab. Basically a crab cake. Shrimp Quesadillas(both times)-Great taste, good balance. Fondue-Very good, love the mushrooms and the spices. Arepa Con Carne-Good not great. Plantano Relleno-Amazing, one of the best tapa i've had there. Steak Tacos-Solid. Cerviches-All 3 were fresh and pallete(sp?) cleansing. This place is a little small but the food is good and it's perfect for a pre-going out dinner.  The only downfall is the the bartenders are a little surly, the bar area is small and compact, and the staff(manager) could be pushy. Overall, i'll return.

Suh-wheet Baby Jesus. This place is delicious. I ride my bike and motorcycle by it all the time and have never stopped. I should have years ago. The turkey BLT was awesome. Pile of bacon and lots of turkey and avocado. But it wasn't a big fat deli sandwich. Well made, right proportion of one ingredient to another, held together as I ate it. Man.

I went there on New Year's Eve and waited around for 3 minutes without anyone greeting us. I finally had to pull the waiter aside and tell him we had a reservation. There was one waiter working. On New Year's Eve. One waiter. Wtf?! Great food, bad, bad service.

This place is truly a hidden gem! It's on the second floor. The Food was amazing, service was great, went in during the week around 8pm. Definitely make reservations, byob!! I'm definitely going back.
I had baklava and the lahmbajeen flatbread, and I've had the tawook in the past. A great deal especially with the Yelp thing. Good for a working lunch for two and close to the university.

This place is so underrated and amazing. Every item I've tried on the menu over the years is incredible-- the cheesy bread, chocolate milkshake, coffee bubble tea, healthy rice, vegan tree wrap, vegan tree sandwich, the golden nuggets -- all so filling and tasty consistently. Friendly service, adorable positive atmosphere, and cute decor. Fast service as well :) all around great. Can you tell I'm a fan? Young 20-something's and children would love this place. Give them your money!

Ok, so this place had me at biscuits and gravy. Let me add that the smothered eggs biscuits and gravy is very good. The cajun bloody mary is a nice spicy twist on this classic brunch cocktail. We will be back for brunch again.

She lost a star.  The original chef is gone taking the gnocchi with him.  And the pizza isn't quite as "on" the last few times I've been.  Still happy it's in my hood, but it's no longer a 4-star joint.
I've only been here for brunch. Wonderful atmosphere, great brunch, good service. This place has been added to the list reasons I have fallen in love with Williamsburg.

I love the menu here - really unusual choices and combos that you can't get elsewhere in the Greater Burlington area. I've never been disappointed with my order and I feel the prices are appropriate. The staff are friendly and really seem to love working there; they make recommendations for food and beverages. I especially recommend their fries & garlic aioli - yum! The only downside is the size of the place. It is a little small for their popularity, so there's often a wait for tables at lunchtime, which is when I go. I have brought 2 friends there for their first visit and they both loved it!
Super comfortable. Good lighting.  Super staff.  Good beer.  A step above good bar food.  And.... Right in my neighborhood.  The one bad thing is... Well, I haven't found it in 6 visits.

We were waiting in line as walk-in guests before it opened. There were only 4 walking seats available and a couple were waiting ahead of us. As there was no check in system, two girls behind us walked in and just sat down the rest seats without checking other people before them. We questioned the waiter but she just replied: what do you want me to do? Like ask them to give the seats to you? Would you please just provide a checking system to avoid such issues again? and to girls who just sat and might be having dinner right now, I feel bad for you guys as you were quite when we were arguing with the waiter. You took advantage from others and you knew you were wrong.
went back last night, and they have perfected the rice and added a hot and extra hot variety of salsa. Everything else was on par. I'm adding one more star. I'll be back within a few days.

Brunch here is always worth the wait.  The appetizer of fresh pastries and breads is enough to fill you for brunch, but of course then you;d be missing out on the fresh fruit, brioche french toast or sour cream hazelnut waffles, dependent on your tasting preference-- all of which are to die for!  The scene can be chaotic but is usually fun and once you settle into your seat you can easily people watch - I love the table in the "center-back" corner, its the best to for a little intimacy but to still be part of the scene. Pros: Fantastic food,  decent service and usually one or two people that you actually want to run in to! Cons: Can be over-crowded and have a bit of a wait- but where in NY doesn't if it's good?

When I travel, I make a point of seeking out the oldest bar in a city. I like history and I like booze so if I have a chance to combine the two, I'm gonna do it. After wolfing down a cheesesteak, checking out the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall, we hoofed it aways, turned down an alley and found McGillins. It was established in 1860. The inside was toasty warm. Their brews were good. The service was great.  It looked like Christmas threw up all over the inside because their holiday decorations were crazy. The place was LOUD. The menu offering was unremarkable and reasonably priced.  I wasn't there to eat. I was there to experience history! and BEER!. The beer that I had, of their own creation was great. If you want a loud, friendly bar with cheap eats and great beer that just happens to be historical, then I think this is the place for you!

Stumbled upon this place while walking in Williamsburg. Um well it was cute, but the chicken from the chicken and waffles tasted "clean" sort of like soap lol? I feel like maybe I had a bad batch. I have faith in this place. If any of you go check it out let me know if your chicken tastes like soap too lol. Darn.
Food is good. Location and styling are excellent. Front of house is hit or miss. Wait staff is rude. Overrated.

My husband and I just moved to NJ from NYC recently and have been on the hunt for good pizza in the area. We went to Star Tavern based on a recommendation and on all of the great Yelp reviews.  The place is super casual and noisy.  A great place to bring kids.  And there were a lot of kids in there. We got there around 7.00PM on a Friday and the line for a table was super long. We waited about 30 minutes but grabbed some beers at the bar which made the wait a little better.   We just got the regular pie which was pretty decent. Like other reviewers said, it was overly greasy for my taste, but it still tasted good.  I definitely liked it, but I have to think that there is better pizza in the area.  So we will continue our search.

This place needed no introduction the first time I went for brunch. No one shuts up about Vesta. Had the Hangover Pizza and ate the whole thing myself. I was thinking about it for days... Still am. It hit just about every spot you could hit.   The girlfriend got the Warm Bankie. Rich and savory. I want fried eggs on all my pizza from now on ;)

Have been a regular for the last 3 years.  The corn cake alone makes it worth the trip. Try the Camarones (Shrimp) al  Diablo if you like spicy or stay with the basic enchiladas verdes.  The Mexican rice is very good as is the limonada ore limeade.  You are treated to homestyle service as  if you're part of the family.  All together the experience is very good Mexican food at a reasonable price.
This is the best and Roy, Deborah and Sayid are the greatest. There is a reason it has lasted so long.

I have to write a review because this is one of the few places that I will go out to eat. I can't have gluten and they are always able to accomodate me. I have been to this location about 3 times and all the staff members were well trained and knew what I was talking about. You could have knocked me over with a feather when a 17 yr. old boy jumped right in to make my bowl and knew what I could and could not eat. I think the staff is great. They were all very helpful. As a courteousy to the rest of humanity, I won't go in there when it is busy because I can only have one person touch my food and that upsets the dynamic of how Chipotle serves their food.
The food here is of top quality and gets crowded and noisy.  BYOB is recommended to numb out the loud acoustics.
Always great service, delightfully chill vibe and delicious fresh sushi at a great value.  Also, coffee cake is mostly all the delicious crumb parts so they know what's up.

I love Fitzgerald's and although I just realized that it REALLY hasn't been around since 1928, it doesn't take away from the fact that it's a fun place to have a good burger, a drink and some laughs. I grew up in the area and have since returned, asking some other locals where I could grab a good burger and Fitzgerald's came up.  Let me say, my husband, friends and I are were not disappointed.  We since have gone back and they have always been consistently tasty.  Be prepared for a wait on a Friday night for a table...but if you go on the later end, the wait gets better, PLUS you can be there for their Friday night live band (nothing too heavy, but usually quite entertaining). Prices are moderate (burger is a little more than it would be at a chain, but 10x better) and service is good.  Ambiance is relaxed and lively.

I love this place! I hope they never leave. I've been there about 12 times already. Staff is awesome & the food, the coffee & the deserts,  are delicious. My  personal FAVORITE, the Chorizo MAC N Cheese!!! You have to find out when they have it on the menu first. I haven't heard 1 person say they didn't like it. The fish & chips? YUM! Oh & the sauce that comes with the fries. Can't even tell you whats in it but everyone should try it at least once!  The pork, the roast beef! Yum Yum! I've tried alot of their foods and I have yet to be disappointed. They have WI-FI, & it's a relaxing atmosphere with a fireplace (electric one) & good music . Oh 1 more important thing. They Cater! Had my Superbowl party catered and a friend of mine had a huge party catered too. I can tell you people at both parties were very pleased!!!!

As an indian..its hard to get great indian food in the city but this is it..and in my opinion the only great one...they do some unique mixes like spicy tandori shrimp which is insanely good...also the service and the area is nice..

I've been here many times - different seasons, different people, always good memories though. Mostly for Sunday brunch. I'm surprised I haven't reviewed it before.. O_o So here we go.. In short: Great lunch special. Great food. Great service. Great owner is probably the reason :) Very personable and warm atmosphere. Every time I come here I feel at home. There's just a special energy in this place, I guess.. Dumplings with peanut butter sauce are the best! And that table by the window is mine!!!))))

Came on a Saturday around noon and the place was already half full. We tried the crab and pork soup dumplings & braised noodles. The skin was not too thick and the soup was flavorful without being overly salty. Put some of their hot sauce and vinegar - it was an explosion of flavors. So good. The braised noodles came with lots of veggies and the broth was very light. It reminded me of home and it is definitely a comfort dish. Get it if you want something on the lighter side. I will be back to satisfy my xiao long bao cravings.

Kefi transports you out of the city for a brief interlude while you dine on delicious Greek food. The cuisine is an affordable option for Greek-food lovers who want something fancier than Uncle Nick's, without going too upscale. Kefi is energetic and boisterous, in part because the friendly staff does such a fantastic job handling group reservations. The vibe is often celebratory on weeknights and weekends, with groups of friends toasting their fine Greek wines around their round table. Sheep's milk dumplings, tzatziki w/homemade chips, swordfish, mezze...all very satisfying and perfectly fresh.
Best kind of bar. Unpretentious, cheap, friendly. Come with a group and make friends with Jeff, and you will leave happy. Better than the bro-magnet bars that make up most of South Street Seaport.

Definitely a good choice in an area that is lacking them unfortunately.  The portions are a pretty good size, and the food is not just your mainstream Italian fare that you'll find at any American Italian restaurant. The squid ink linguine was pretty good, though a little salty for my tastes.  The appetizer that has all of the fried seafood and and peppers is excellent.  The menu says that it's for two people, I'd say it's enough for three people probably.  The desserts looked yummy, but unfortunately we were stuffed. The restaurant is pretty busy around 7, so I definitely recommend reservations, but by 9 or so it's pretty much all cleared out.

The reason why I am giving 2-stars is not the food quality but simply what my fiancé observed that made her not touch her meal. The lady cooking her food came in and didn't wash her hands. She reached her hands into a container of raw meat, cooked the  food, and then cut a bulky roll and put the food on it. She didn't wash her hands after touching raw meat and then proceeded to touch everything else in the kitchen. Just plain nasty.

Fun atmosphere upstairs near bar with a great cocktail list. Service was excellent, although maybe trying a little too hard. Lots of interesting options for appetizers and sides a little light on choice for main dishes. I enjoyed the oysters, scallops, cheese plate and spinach salad. For the main course I had the pork belly which was a risk. There was way too much fat on it for my liking, where there was actual meat it was delicious. The house made bread and spread were great, as was a very rich chocolate soufle. Apres dinner enjoyed some belgium beers at the bar as a topper.

Will you please stop yelling!?! I don't even know what you're saying!! Ahhh ramen - Every proper Asian loves their noodle and this little person is no different. I guess I came on a good day since there was no wait. I loved the atmosphere and seeing a bunch of Caucasian New Yorkers yelling in Japanese was very amusing...for the first 5 minutes. Then with every order there was more yelling. The restaurant was full, so the yelling never stopped. I wasn't sure whether to laugh or cry - midway through my conversations I'd forget what I was saying because I'd look up to see who was yelling, lol. It added to the atmosphere though. One can't be upset for that. I had ordered the Tori noodles, which were amazing. The broth was light but had the most flavor I had ever had in a broth. For $2 you can add more noodles, but as the menu warns you, you need to make sure you saved enough broth for it. Steller deal. For desert, we had a tofu custard topped with a choice of sorbet. I was hesitant over ordering the tofu custard, but am glad I did. It had a very strong and rich custard flavor, but without the heaviness in the texture. It was amazing and I would highly recommend it to anyone. Asian stamp of approval.

I love this place and go there anytime I'm in the mood for Japanese food other than sushi. The service is great and the food even greater. Everything here comes in small portions so you can try several dishes at once. I usually go there with friends and we all share what we're ordered. I would especially recommend the pork belly but everything I tried was delicious. They also have a great variety of sake for you to try. If you can, ask to be seated in one of the booth in the front room as the back room is a lot less impressive.
Totally a hidden/underrated gem, and the best cheesesteaks I've had thus far in Philadelphia. Really nice, conversational people, too, who represent the character of Philadelphia well.

We were visiting NYC with our cousins and wanted some yummy japanese, didn't know where to go so the 4 of us started to yelp, and finally after a long hour of going back and forth and being indecisive my boyfriend says "we going to Sakagura"! We were so happy that someone decided. YAY, Japanese!!! We came to this restaurant, as we were directed to walk down the basement, it felt sketchy but when we stepped into the restaurant everything changed, the decor reminded us of Japan, the smell just brought happiness to our faces and the sound of people eating and chatting just made us feel safe and that we had made a good choice!  we didn't make an appointment, so we waited for 20 mins and when we sat down and the food came, then the sake. Wow, every dish we got just blew us away, the duck, the pork, the sashimi but I especially loved the uni soup with the poached egg. AND then there was desert, I love black sesame  and their blk sesame creme brulee topped with more black sesame ice cream was ridiculously good.!. Well done boyfriend! I can't wait to come back this fall! :)
Great food and service, but very expensive. Double check menu for price and portion size before ordering.

Went for lunch off the highway based on Yelp reviews.  Got there and everything looked so good in the pizza case - had such a hard time deciding what to eat. Went with the veal and shrimp parm platter. It was so good. I would go back often if I lived in the neighborhood.

I went to Reading Terminal Market just to get sheep milk for my puppies. I'm not a big fan of overcrowded - pricey market. I don't know whats special about this place.. maybe I need to spend more time there...

On dismal, dreary winter nights, nothing beats an evening of good beer, good company, and good food. For Pete's Sake delivers all three, quickly melting away the January blues. The space is comfortable, full of friendly people, and even when packed it's not so loud that you can't carry on a conversation. The beer selection is decent and the burger was perfectly cooked and served with plenty of soft, delicious fries. All that aside, the selling point for me is the bartender. I spent my recent visit here watching in awe. Charm, grace, speed, good looks, the boy had it all. His hands were in perpetual motion, rinsing glasses during the few moments he wasn't pouring drinks. He seemed to know most of the customers by name, and cheerfully chatted with my friend and I as we picked his brain about sports trivia and beer selections. As more and more people came in, he juggled it all, effortlessly able to judge who needed another round and who was ready for the bill.
