It's not just cute, it's what this place is about! Good fun eating! We had a choice between Prixe-Fixe and a la carte. The Prixe-Fixe was $50 a person, but a la carte had better options, for me at least. All their food looks fresh in the deli-style fridge. You have many options from delicate yet hearty chowder to salads to all-in-one meals. My seafood chowder was unreal, the bechemel not too savoury or dense, all the seafood was soft and perfectly cooked. Seasonal vegetables like squash that give in with every bite. I could eat it every day for a year. i swear. It puts all other chowders to SHAME. It was topped with blanched heirloom tomato. Our entree was the seared tilapia with a sprinkling of capers, sauteed seasonal veggies and mashed potatoes. All done to perfection. The tilapia however could have been thicker and a little rarer. Other than that, the white wine sauce was the cherry on top. About the restaurant itself, it's cozy with mismatched furniture. Features a seating area by the front door and another larger area for groups in the back. A kitchen, to reflect the neighborhood itself: small, open and inviting. Remember to bring your own bottle of wine, there's a place to buy some next door and don't be shy with the chef. He's snappy but so much fun! I can't help but reiterate what others have said: this is gem and the best kept secret of the neighborhood. I'm not going to blog and post and blow up this place, but I'll bring a friend and hope they do the same. Cheers.

raw bar platter, cannot go wrong: 6 oysters (coast to coast from the redwood forest to the gulf stream waters), 2 clams, 3 shrimp. must don the pre-requisite bibs while enjoying a dozen maryland blue crabs steamed with lemon & old bay. a  touch too much old bay for moi, otherwise quite tasty and not as much of a pain as you'd think self crabbing would be.

Any place with a consistent 2+ hr wait and lines almost everynight deserves a try right? I wouldn't wait 2.5 hours for this ramen but it is DEF a must go-to spot. Ambiance is really cool and staff is friendly.  Good vibes and great NY feel to it.  Being a Cali girl, I have pretty high standards for Asian food in NY and I'm used to Asian food that is better or equal in taste for 1/4 the price. So I'd have to say, this ramen is one of the good ones.  It's a good portion for NY and Ramen always leave you full anyways.

With all the excellent places in Philly, ok isn't good enough.  I didn't find a single appetizer interesting, and the desserts were equally uninspiring ( creme brulee?  Still?) entrees were decent.  Service was...also uninspired.  Any place where the server says " are you still working on that" automatically loses a star, in my book.  All in all, ok.  Wouldn't go back.

I love this place! Always fresh and so fast and easy.  I will walk several blocks out of my way to go here even if to just bring home some pizza for later. It's the only pizza in NYC I crave.  Such different topping, too.

This was the first meal that I had in New York & omg  the combo plate with the white sauce is ridiculously gooood! l just wished it wasn't so cold in New York so I could have enjoyed this a bit more. Definitely looking forward to coming back here the next time I'm in New York!

Amazing! Amazing! The place is a dive, but the food is tasteful. The omelette is baked the corned beef hash is homemade and the orange juice is fresh squeezed. Best place for breakfast! Worth the trip if you are coming from a distance. Enjoy!

Oh....my....gawwwwdddd + drinks at the bar come with these delicate waffle cut chips that are deep fried amidst fresh herbs that just RESONATE on your tongue. Scarpetta should really look into packaging these babies and selling them!!! We ordered many things that night but here are my top rated (I recommend that you DO NOT deviate from what is listed below) + SEARED SEA SCALLOPS roasted mushrooms & summer vegetable 'agro dolce' the best way to describe this is Monica from Friends describing the roadmap to a woman....7....7...7...7...7..7!!! +SPAGHETTI tomato & basil simple, may seem as plain, but this baby is loaded with unexplainable richness that is indescribable for words. Combine this with the dish described above and you're in the money. Ambiance is great - intimate and modern. I recommend limiting your party to a group of four and eating family style so that you can sample a wide range of dishes without overindulging. Great for: * a double date * a first date * a place to meet her parents

New Town Deli and Restaurant is a little gem located in the no- man's land between Callowhill and Spring Garden Streets.  Clean and reasonably priced, New Town is a favorite breakfast and lunch place for the cops, cabbies, firefighters and government workers who work on Spring Garden Street.  Service is friendly, and the owners, who are Greek, have a firm grip on American Comfort food.  I have been to New Town several times for lunch, and always get the specials, which are delicious.  Today was the first time I ordered breakfast at the New Town, and it did not disappoint.  Breakfast for two, friendly service, and bottomless cups of coffee were less than $12.00.       There is no parking lot, and, at lunch time, parking on 9th street can be a challenge. No parking issues during our 7AM arrival for breakfast.       New Town also delivers, will fax the menu of daily specials to your location, and has a comprehensive sandwich selection.  All menu items are available for take out.       The hours are Monday thru Friday 6 AM until 3 PM, Saturday 6AM till 1PM.  Closed Sunday.       So- reasonable prices; great food; clean bathrooms and friendly service make  the New Town a "go."

Not only is this fabulous Restaurant but it has to be the BEST Gluten free restaurant in the city. It is a MUST dine at for a celiac's. Be sure to have dessert they are always amazing. The home bread is to die for and the pasta is alway perfect! What is so fab is you can eat with your friends and family and not suffer because of your gluten issues. Try the Belgian Beer from Greens is it gluten free and divine!

I liked the food here, though not enough to give it 4 stars. I had the Churrasco, and unfortunately it tasted burnt, and the meat was not very tender. My friends seemed to enjoy the food, though they only had appetizers. I also tried the arepa. My feeling is that they try to do too much to the food that should be simple, and in Lat. Am. simple is tasty. I might go back, and try something else next time. Perhaps I will have better luck with the food.

easily the best mexican restaurant i have been to in a while! i sampled a bunch of little things and everything was so good! to drink i ordered one of the specials but they were out of some part of it so the waiter (who was the nicest, funniest man, ever, and forced us a to use our horrible spanish speaking skills) suggested a pomegranate margarita, yum! we got guacamole with some type red sauce and cheese in it which was delish and the avocados were so fresh creamy in my mouth! the chips were fresh and warm. the queso fundido was perfectly warm and "cut-able" without a million tiny strings going on forever with fluffy warm tortillas on the side. i split my entree and had the guacamole stuffed mango fish (i forget the proper name), it was crispy fish with the cool, creamy guac with a mango sauce on top served with rice and sweet potato puree...at this point i couldn't eat much though as i ate several of the pickled carrots and jalapenos they provided but the last one defeated me, it was spicier than most habanero's i've had in the past and therefore killed my palate and ability to breathe for the next 20 or so mins. and still it was a great meal, i can't wait to go back!

best mojitos ever! i've only had the appetizers but it was really good... the bar area gets a little dirty in after-hours. empty plates, used napkins, etc. sitting around. didn't know about half priced tapas, will have to come back for that!

Light, fluffy and perfectly fried falafel.  Had the platter with all three varieties and they were all delicious.  Sauces were interesting and fries were outstanding too. Having tried Taim's falafel I am inspired to recreate these at home.  No more dense falafel out of the box.

I really felt like the evening was a complete waste of money. I went to Degustation for my 33rd birthday celebration with my husband and 3 foodie friends.  We planned on doing the $80 tasting menu; which is advertised as 7 courses.  I chose Degustation for their innovative looking menu and the chance to sit around an intimate open kitchen.  The restaurant itself is lovely and the wait staff was incredibly attentive.  The food was interesting and tasty; however when our 7 courses were over we all went out for pizza because we were still quite hungry.  I have done many tasting menus before and have always felt I had eaten a meal when it was over.  Last night was incredibly disappointing as I felt each course was literally a bite or two and we left feeling as we had just eaten an appetizer.  There was no energy in the open kitchen that made it worth having an open kitchen, some of the chefs looked angry and unhappy to be cooking which made watching them uncomfortable and not interesting.

Great spot with a solid laid back atmosphere.  There is a General Store in the front selling dairy and pastries.  I had the country pate with egg and bacon, it was great!  Can't beat it.  There is a good selection of craft beers and a good cocktail list.  Worth a trek in from Manhattan.  You will not regret evening here.  The service was also friendly and professional.

In Philly for the weekend.  While at Reading Terminal, I discovered the Wursthaus booth, which is affiliated or owned by Brauhaus Schmitz.  Currywurst for lunch put me in the mood for a German dinner and atmosphere. The German beer selection is extensive, and they claim the most German-specific beers on tap anywhere.  I was unfamiliar with most, but my waiter sensed my uncertainty and brought a sampler to try. For dinner I had two sausages: Bauernwurst and Speckwurst with the spatzle and another side I can't remember.  All were authentic and delicious. Atomsphere was also great.  Tables are close, and the place has an energetic vibe.  One table was taking jager shots while our close by neighbors were drinking beer from das boot.  We struck up a conversation with them, much as you would in a German brauhouse.   I wish we had a place like this locally.  Would suggest to anyone interested in visiting Germany for dinner, while in Philly.

Dos Toros is hands down the best burrito place I've been to in NYC.  I've lived here for 5+ years and as a native Californian all I crave when I walk into a Mexican spot is a little bit of home.  Dos Toros delivered.  The food is fresh and delicious.  The Carne Asada is supreme.  I love love love it.  Not to mention how all the food tastes like food, and not like mass produced product.   I think what really sets this place apart and makes it the best, is the staff.  They really listen and give you what you want.  I'm a picky eater and I got  it my way. The design elements are also really strong.  It is very much "California in NY" kind of look.  I have to admit the best part is the reclaimed tin ceiling.  Really nice touch.  The music is perfect for the restaurant, it fits the vibe.  The energy in the place flows really nicely and everyone seems to be enjoying themselves while they're inside. I say for sure check it out.  Its the best.
Food is great.... Too bad the place is kinda small and wait time for table can get long.. Like I said, food is great!!!!!

I came to try out this place on a Saturday afternoon. The wait was a lot shorter than Grimaldi's and we (5 people) got seated in 20 minutes or so. I definitely had a high expectation after reading about the odd and complicated history behind this place and Grimaldi's. But unfortunately, I was very underwhelmed with their margherita pizza. The crust was so soggy and flimsy, the sauce was very plain and the cheese was nothing special either. We got a large pie with pepperoni and mushroom toppings as well, but we didn't have much luck with that one either. In sum. Juliana's pizza doesn't come anywhere close to that of Grimaldi's, or even Patsy's, which I consider a step below Grimaldi's. Just don't bother to visit here, and go wait in line for Grimaldi's right next door.

Moto is an example of a place that just got it right. The date cake and salami with bulgarian feta are my favorites. Also fantastic is the meatloaf when they have it as a special. Pretty much my favorite place in the world. If it was big enough to host my wedding, I totally would have had it there. They just opened another bar called St.Maize in south w.burg which will eventually have food too, I can't wait.
Ok place.

Tops, Tops, Tops.  This is all I heard from my Jersey folk since I moved here.  They have a huge affection towards diners here.  Me, I find diners to be nauseating.  I just don't see a high enough turnover rate.  Ever since watching Kitchen Nightmares, I feel that all diners' walk in freezers have stale food. My turnover rate hesitation usually runs true in most of Jersey diners, but not diners like Tops.  There is always a line out the door, so I definitely control my OCD ways here.  We ordered the big breakfast thingy, then short rib grilled cheese sandwich, and chicken and waffles.  All good.  All greasy.  All fattening.  If you like diners, go here.  The food will always be fresh.

Because of all the praise this place has garnered - here, in the press, and through word of mouth - I feel like I should be giving it 3 stars.  And, being a resident of the BK now, I am eager to support all of the great restaurants in the livest borough.  But truly nothing about our meal was the least bit memorable. As others have noted, the service is quite bad for any restaurant, especially a "nice" restaurant, and especially one getting so much attention.  Our waitress was completely detached, not once did she proactively recognize we needed anything, let alone check-in and ASK if we needed anything.  There was a good 30 minutes between courses and she didn't stop by this entire time...despite my empty wine glass desiring that more vino fill it up. And the food was so underwhelming.  The mussels we actually sent back - something I literally never do as I dislike the embarrassment - because at least two were clearly not fresh.  The pappardelle was bland and under-seasoned. Same for that night's special greens, despite the presence of grilled nectarine and peaches!  And even the Vietnamese spare ribs, which we all thought would be a sure hit...they were fine, but no one at the table was excited about them.  Not next to so many sub-par dishes. The only enjoyment was due to the dumplings which deserve their praise, and the goat cheese panna cotta with rhubarb.  One great appetizer and one good dessert does not warrant a trip to Red Hook...and we all live within two miles! P.S.:  Be prepared for mosquitoes if you sit out back...they actually have bug spray for people to use.

Great spot for a celebratory drink in Midtown Manhattan. That in itself isn't saying much, except for the fact that the cocktails here are light years ahead of most places anywhere. Also, the wood carvings adorning the bar are unlike anything I've ever seen. Huge lions heads or something. A dramatic touch to an already-impressive space. It feels like you're drinking cocktails in Jeffrey Lebowski's private library. I love it. Like myself, though, if you're not rich, this bar can be intimidating. You'll walk in and your brain will immediately begin to fire the 'I can't afford this place' neurons, which can be both healthy and exhilarating once you've started having fun here. And there is fun to be had; you just have to be careful spending the money to find it.

Best bar in all of Astoria that I've been to! Also, the only bar I've been to! Whoo... ok, yah, so obviously I'm not qualified to make such a comment since I've never been to other bars in Astoria, but even in my experiences going to bars in Manhattan and Brooklyn, I must say that I was pretty impressed by this place! My two roommates and I arrived at around 2AM on a Saturday night after visiting a Hookah Lounge. We walked in and it was very crowded. As we squeezed past people, a server approached one of my friends to take drink orders, but when she found out we weren't going to take a bar table, she dismissed us and walked away without really explaining anything. It wasn't particularly rude or anything, but she was a bit confusing and could have explained why she scurried off. Luckily though, right after we got our drinks, a booth in the back opened up and we were able to slide in. Just a note to all the folks: credit card tab minimums are $20, so make sure you split a tab if you're not planning on getting more than 2 drinks. I ordered a Whisky Sour (always my go to) that cost $8 and tasted alright. They didn't butcher it with too much sour mix like they do at a lot of places, but it wasn't very strong either. I then ordered a well-liquor whisky on the rocks and suddenly remembered, as I drank, why I never order well liquor on the rocks. Ah well, whatever. The booth area was nice and it felt like I was in a rustic cottage in the middle of a field. The brownish-yellow aura of the ambiance creates a mellow feel, perfect for conversation. Mind you though, my roommate who had been here before said that usually the entire place is packed, including the booth area in the back, so perhaps we got lucky with having a "quiet" space for conversation. A waitress approached us when we got seated and told us that there was a different service system for the tables and asked for our bar tab so that she could take care of us. She wasn't the most attentive waitress. Didn't have any other complaints though. I like the Southern, homey feel to Sweet Afton and I'd like to be back, especially if it isn't too badly crowded like it was this time around.

We were there Tuesday and liked it very much. The coffee was good and strong, and the portions more than sufficient. We arrived just before 12 pm and did not have to wait but there were many people there. I had a special  Brunch of The Irish and my husband had the lox & onion omelette  which we both enjoyed.  The quarters are tight but the wait staff is very nice. We thought the food and service were very good. We would certainly return.

Ye Gods!  Great spot, nice ambience, good service, and I get what they were thinking but jeezus what crappy delivery. The food here is nothing short of suckey. Great ideas, but this place needs to either fire the cook, change the menu or both. If what they said in another review is true, that they came up with the menu by getting drunk and smoking a lot of pot, all I can say is the cook must have been getting drunk and smoking a lot of pot when he cooked our food. A downright abysmal dinner. The worst we've had in years. Ah you oh so cool but know nothing about food out-of-towners would you please stop posting your ridiculous reviews so that people who really like food won't waste time and money eating in places that if really rated correctly would go out of business....fast. Your revews are as pretentious as the food in this so not French food establishment! I feel like I was ripped off.

What a perfect place to plan a birthday celebration! Mario, of course, was fantastic JUST like the yelp reviews said. He was very accommodating and helpful in planning the menu and timing of the SURPRISE party for my boyfriend. The food was amazing, but mostly the homemade spaghetti was a HUGE HIT! Everyone was raving about this hidden gem. I'm so glad for planning my boyfriends 29th birthday party here. 27 people came out (we pretty much had the whole place to ourselves) and it was the most fun and intimate dinner party ever!!!!

After seeing a show on Broadway, we trekked to Cho Dang Gol. We arrived at 9:50 PM and though the closing time is posted as 10:30 PM, we were brusquely told that the kitchen closes at 9:50, the exact moment that we arrived.  If the kitchen closes earlier than the time advertised and posted, then the business should post that information somewhere so that potential guests are aware of that information in advance; however, such service and consideration seems to be too much to expect from this business.  Fortunately there were other Korean restaurants in close vicinity that were able to garner our business and appetites.

I have been here probably 7-8 times and gotten great food every time.  There's a lot of it, it's yummy, and it's cheap (and fast).  I've gone here with Chinese people who also lov it, which I think means it's pretty good Chinese food. They have a more extensive menu now since they moved to the new larger location and I tried the lamb skewers/kabobs, which were delicious.
Their award-winning panini with speck, Brie, and pate was very good. Cappuccino was excellent.

I love this place! the sushi is simple and  tasty simply divine sushi :) Our service is always so pleasant, the staff here is excellent . I recommend the the white tiger  specialty roll and any of their Sushi Ala Cart  and the Sashimi  if you wan something sweet try  the tempura bananas with green tea ice cream.

Very disappointed very disappointed in manager asked her name she doesn't give out name of the phone so I was she the manager she replied yes I complain about my seafood platter said it was very little of nothing it was more so a french fry platter food very moist not fried hard she says my problem I should have checked my food before I left understandably been there before never shrimp clams and scallops then one piece of fish understandable but everything else a complete complete mess top it off she said I should have called last night but your sign says you close at 930 a time I got home 10 o'clock so why would I call if sign say close 9:30 I called first thing this morning and there's nothing too offer customer I know better next time that 2 charter pot

Peruvian cuisine? I think not. Upon browsing the menu, I was excited to see many traditional dishes, yet the plates did not live up to the hype. We were served aji, but no canchita, which is a Peruvian custom. Appetizers. Ordered choros and a medley of appetizers that resembled Taco Bell rather than Peruvian cuisine. The choros were lacking heat and the aderezo was poor in itself. I under the aji de gallina, which tasted more like some sort of Italian cheese pasta than actual aji de gallina. Any way the food was rather lackluster and no where close to authentic and the service was poor and un attentive. The atmosphere however was the best part of the experience . You want real Peruvian cuisine cross the bridge into jersey and go to any corner store in Kearny.
gourmet hot dogs with a variety of creative toppings and an awesome selection of dipping sauces. craft sodas. fresh hand cut fries
I loved this place, the food is hands down awesome and fresh, not greasy but so much flavor. Pricing is reasonable and fare wait time. Award winning dessert fresh fresh fresh

Finally a real chef on the UWS. Sat at the bar last night with my hubby--Stefanya the beautiful and talented bartender made me the most wonderful apricot margarita that went perfectly with the snapper ceviche.  The service, atmosphere (yes not kid friendly amen) but mostly the fabulous food will guarantee the success of this great new spot!! Already made my next reservation!

Best pizza in Harrison. You can't go wrong here. From their extra large slices to their Sicilian pie (THE BEST EVER) to their meatball or chicken parm sandwiches, everything is great. The meatball topping is actual meatballs sliced. Awesome! They even have a chicken salad with fresh mozz, sun dried tomatoes, and balsamic vinegar that is great. The one thing I must say is that sometimes their delivery times and service leave something to be desired, but they do get busy.

Staff are complete d-bags what happened to service with a smile? they were rude, obnoxious and pretentious. you work at a RESTAURANT, who do you think you are?! i have never been to a place where the wait staff thinks they are better than their customers. this was appalling. not worth going to unless you feel like being degraded

This is more like 2.5 stars.  I came here with lower expectations than usual - I've never been to a hibachi place that is based on flashy performances (by choice).  The first thing they ask you when you arrive is if you want to sit on the hibachi side or sushi side.  I didn't expect this, so make sure you know what you want when you arrive.  We were there for hibachi, so we were seated immediately.  I thought the prices were a little higher than I expected, but in the end my husband and I decided the amount of food you get makes it worth it.  The service was not the best, but we eventually got what we asked for (like chopsticks or more water).  The food is OK - nothing I'd ever crave, but it wasn't bad.  I got the beef and shrimp and my husband got the beef and scallops.  Each order is an entire beef strip and you get several pieces of shrimp or scallops.  Each order comes with soup, vegetables and either fried rice or noodles.  The soup is tasteless.  The thing that makes the price worth it is the sake that comes with the dinner.  Like all flashy hibachi places, the chef cuts the meat in front of you, sprays fire up, throws vegetables into people's mouths and squirts them with water.  He also squirts sake into your mouth until a little bit after you motion "stop".  In addition to the Asahi I had, I was pretty buzzed by the end of the meal.  Not the best food or service, which is usually the primary things I judge about a place, but we all had fun and it only got better with more sake.

A lot of the reviews mention the crowds, but we went on a quiet Sunday night and had a great time.  The bartender was helpful with beer choices (huge selection)  and I am beyond excited to have cappucinos and alcohol all under one roof.  Their wine selection includes a group called "Orange."  Introducing me to new things--I like it.   I haven't tried the capps yet, but that is next.  Such a welcome addition to the nabe.

SO GOOD. I was at Hotel Chantelle last night for an event and randomly ended up at Zest for dinner. It's a cute little place on the LES with unexpectedly great music. It's also BYOB with no corkage fee -- note to self for when I return. Service is ok but the waiters and waitresses are all so nice and accommodating. Had shrimp shumai to start -- didn't love it...it was a tad fishy. But the sushi is super fresh and yum. I usually go simple -- with a salmon avocado roll and sweet potato roll. The salmon tasted really fresh, which is not always the case. You can't really go wrong with sweet potato rolls - it's fried (my little indulgence) so it has a nice crunch to it. My friend who had never tried it before loved it. She got the Dark Angel, which is a specialty roll with spicy white tuna and shrimp, lettuce, avocado and seaweed on the outside. Omg. SO good. Definitely getting that next time. Just saw someone else's post -- a Yelp check-in gets you free edamame. Will def do next time.
Great selection of craft beers and nice Tex Mexish food. Between the new Flagship Brewing and this place, Staten Island for the afternoon was really nice.

Very hard to imagine the good reviews here even after discounting the one-off bad visit thing which can happen. However for mussles to be served very noticeably far from fresh (in two separate dishes including the boullabasise which I was afraid to eat) and shrimp and white fish gray and frayed - those things are not imaginable in a place with even a line cook who should know better.  The bread is an abomination - cure looking mini baguettes served hot - but wreaking of dough conditioner as they appear to be industrial versions of Pillsbury dinner rolls. Again - in a French place - foney cheap bread.   Got to say the waiter was not hostile (but far from friendly) and took mussles off the tab. The avocado and shrimp salad had nice fruit but the shrimp were drenched in some god awful sauce. Maybe for good reason. Cute place and I can understand how SoHo shoppers from NJ would like it - but Geeze. I'm not often harsh in reviews but Geeze this place was bad.

Pretty good turkey, cranberry, gravy, and stuffing.  I got a wrap and am regretting it.  I am sure it would have been a lot better on rye or another bread but I thought it would be too messy having all of those ingredients inside.  The pickle was very good, nice and sour!  I would give it more stars if there were more turkey on the wrap and if I had gotten a different bread.  It is also a little pricey for lunch, mine was $8

I consider myself something of a sandwich expert, a connoisseur if you will, having compiled a literally countless number of steaks/hoagies/etc. during the course of seven year career in the professional sandwich-slinging industry. (Not to mention my own recreational efforts at various Dagwoods and other delicious examples of the sandwich arts.) Jake's Sandwich Board meets and exceeds my high expectations for stuff crammed inside a roll. My first foray into their offerings was the Farmer's Market, a rather toothsome vegetarian option.  Jake's may waft the alluring fragrance of roast pork out onto 12th Street, but this belies the fact that you can get your kicks without meat here.   A second visit yielded their November/Thanksgiving special, the Turducken (citypaper.net/blogs/meal…).  I'll let you glimpse that photograph and read the ingredients yourself and let you come to your own conclusions.   Most recently, I opted for the Schmeer.  The turkey and veggies were phenomenal, though if forced to point out a shortcoming, the roasted garlic spread could be more assertive.   I have yet to sample their pork, brisket or rib-eye sandwiches.  Based on what I have had so far, though, I maintain some pretty high expectations.

If u havent eaten here... You are officially a freakin Zombie! Real food, real fast, real people.. Giving you the best they got everyday.. Breakfast is great and lunch is phenominal.. They even carry Clinton Iced Tea in the carton. Need I say more.. Did u hear me people!! They got "boxes"! Stop your bullshittin and get there. Tell Ray that Mikey sent ya.
Love there. I can pick up my lunch before work!

I have been to a lot of pizza places through the years from California to NY and this is the best pizza around, I have friends from NYC that said, "I do not eat jersey pizza" well I forced them to come here and they will no longer say that, especially when they no longer eat pizza until they are in the area, best ever!

I have lived in the neighborhood for 9 years and watched this great bar grow. They have simple tasty bar food that's fresh. The drinks are proper and the staff and owners get it. Great space all around.

Can't go wrong with this place. It is the perfect cheap meal. I have tried most things on their menu and all have been very tasty. The burritos are a great deal, filling and will convince you to never go to chipotle again. My personal favorite is the 3 tacos deal. For 10 bucks you get 3 tacos and rice and beans on the side. Load up with some hot sauce they have in the store and you have yourself a very satisfying meal. Tortillas have a lot of flavor, meat juicy and tender and fresh veggie ingredients. This one is a win.

OK, I realize that going to Pepe's in New Haven is like a religious pilgrimage for many, so this review goes against the majority, because I feel no place has ever been hyped up as much as the "Original Frank Pepe's in New Haven".  I work in New Haven everyday, but my job is too fast paced to stop in to Pepe's for lunch (or do a takeout, for that matter).  But today I was off from work and had an afternoon court date, so I thought it would be great opportunity to have lunch at Pepe's. Arrived at 11:30am, still some booths open.  Good timing on my part, soon after there was a line outside the front door.  This was Monday morning, can't imagine what the wait would be like on the weekends, or a weeknight for that matter. Ordered "America's #1 Pizza"  (as the little sign on my table proclaimed) -- the white clam pizza, with bacon.  Server asked me if I wanted anything to drink with that.  I ordered a diet coke.  She came back soon after with a tiny glass of diet coke.  I'm almost glad it was in a tiny glass, the beverage tasted "flat" to me. Well, I wasn't here for a diet coke, so I waited for "America's #1 Pizza"...and I waited....and I waited....and I waited some more.  Boy, after all that waiting, you expect it to be really damn good, huh ?  After more than 30 minutes of waiting, the pizza finally arrived on my table. "America's #1 Pizza" ?  Nope.  Hardly.  Not even close.  Tasted like charcoal flavored bread with clam juice on it.  To make the claim that it is "America's #1 Pizza" is pretty far fetched.  If you really think that is great pizza, you have a few screws loose. Ate about half of my white clam pizza with bacon, that was the best I could do (and I normally have a heathy appetite).  Had to use the bathroom before leaving -- needed to wash off all the grease and charcoal on my fingers.  Very disappointing, why anyone would wait in line for this is beyond me.  I still reek of all the garlic that was on that "pie".  Least I shouldn't be attacked by a mob of Vampires any time soon.

They have a lot of pizzas with arugula as a dominating topping, but the crust, the freshness, the richness is all there. The atmosphere is dim and relaxing, though a bit too dark sometimes to read the menu. Great wine/beer selection to pair with your pizza. Much of the pizza selection is relatively healthy/light, but is contrasted by the richness of the toppings and your drink (whether it be a nice lager or a Riesling). I highly recommend the Greenpointer if you're in the mood for something light yet filling.  I'm not gonna write a huge review on this because the pizza itself is too good for words. You gotta come here and experience it on your own!

I have loved this place since first visit. The food is amazing. I love the unique pairings, they amplify the flavor of each dish. I first  tried the popular lobster roll, and I loved it! Since then I've been bouncing around the menu trying different things. There hasn't been anything I haven't liked- actually, I love it all. I definitely recommend coming here and trying something new. Great quality delicious food!!

Mezetto came out of nowhere to deliver a surprisingly solid fusion Mediterranean light dinner. Great for sharing: the cheese plate, the dips (spicy feta my fav). Then the octopus and the shrimp were really good - the grilled octopus in particular. Throw in a huge Greek salad and some nice Chardonnay and you're good to go.

These are the kind of places you need to go visit! Granted it is in a very congested area. But, it's well worth the trip. Practically, everything we have ordered was amazing! The Cuban Sandwich was great. Toasted bread, meats galore, the flavors in your mouth and the textures is unimaginable. If they tossed in an egg and avocado.. I would have been in heaven. The smoke Chops. Was something different. It looks like chops, but It taste just like ham! Oh how tricky they can be! My favorite dish was the Chicharron Pollo. Was probably the best. I can eat that with rice. All day! and of course the best for last. The Seafood and Meats Paella was amazing. Make sure if your want to order that. Order it first. It takes about 45 mins to an 1 hr. It says it feeds 2? but easily 4-5 ppl. I only took a star down. Due to parking as always!

I never write any comments on yelp or any other type of social media. This all happened on the night John D (1/19) was there. His review is not accurate. But I for one would  like to commend the new owners and the service. The night I visited the Taylor's   there was a patron that was  getting out of hand with a bartender making some comments that's was uncalled for.  I for one was glad when he was removed from the restaurant so my family and I could enjoy our food. I found the eggplant tower and pizza awesome.  I would recommend Taylor's Tap & Grill to my friends and bring my business clients there.

Ok. Just get a beer at the bar. Beautiful view. Not expensive. However I made the mistake to eat here. 1 1/2 hour wait. Sit down and are told that about a third of the entrees are not available. Food mediocre and really expensive for what it is.

Food is good here. But lose a star because of service. 45 minutes after ordering I finally had to ask the waitress for some bread and what was taking so long for the food and she said they were short in the kitchen so it was taking longer than usual. She should have come over, brought some bread, explained they were short and apologize in advance. Not let me sit there with nothing to eat for 45 minutes and no idea what's going on. Wife ordered double vegetables and they forget it. Asked the server to bring an extra side of vegetables and he never did. Just careless. Have had other good experiences here so just need to clean this up a bit.
Huge Grand Slam combo contained chicken, pork, shrimp, sausage, egg, and rice, all topped with a yummy curry gravy.  Come hungry, and leave sleepy.

Love this place.. Food is good drinks are great.. Everything in the menu is delicious. Great customer services. We ordered the empanadas to start which I recommend to everyone who is there. They were so delicious and had a mouthwatering taste. For the platos Fuertes, we ordered the Paella Valenciana, which was AMAZING. Being Spanish myself, I am always the first to judge everyone Else's so called paella but Yuca definitely know how to make a good one! My friend had ordered the Puerquito Cubano which was just as good. The meat was so tender it was falling apart and full of flavor! Overall it was a good place to get some decent Mexican and some strong drinks!

This place is great and although I wouldn't call it "hidden," it seems pretty down-to-earth and a good laid back place.  I came as part of a large group last weekend, and they were really accommodating to us.  They had a lot of great NY state and otherwise unique craft offerings a bit off the beaten path of other well-stocked craft beer bars.  We also split a poutine (fries with cheese curds, gravy and an egg) and these were excellent.  Everyone seemed to have a great time.   The only complaint I have is that they don't seem to open for lunch.

Currently my favorite restaurant in New York. Everything from the food to the service to the atmosphere (specifically the music and lighting) is perfect. Highlights: braised rabbit gnocchi, pork chop, coq au vin, macaroni au gratin, and try some absinthe while you're there.

El Vez has a lot going for it:  great atmosphere, unique cocktails, and an array of guacamoles to choose from.  Go for the crab.  It's awesome. Things aren't cheap here but they're not outrageously expensive either. Go make funny faces in the photo booth.  Especially after a few blood orange margaritas.

Moooore like 3.5 stars.  The service was great - our waitress and the bartender were super friendly and attentive.  However, the food just wasn't as good as it sounded on the menu.  Their mac and cheese was pretty good, but my lobster roll didn't taste so great.  The lemony mayonnaise overpowered the lobster entirely.  Meh.

I have been to Giorgio on Pine twice now with a large group and it was such a fun atmosphere. The service is great and Giorgio himself is so accommodating. The food is very good and if you have a gluten allergy there are options for you to substitute for gluten free pasta. I recommend Giorgio on Pine for groups 8-10 as well as a great date spot. Fun and Service 5 stars!!

Went here last night with my husband and our two close friends. It's been since 2011 since we had come here so I was a little hesitant because my first time here i wasn't impressed.. Last nights meal changed my mind but the service was a little less than be desired! Their salad dressing is crazy good. And I love myself some fried ravioli.. this time around I got the Crunchy Chicken Thai Wrap and I loved the flavor, the lightness of it, and the aroma! They didn't over power it with the peanut sauce which was nice! As for the service, they are always spot on with their drinks. As my friends boyfriend put it, "they are like the butler from mr deeds"! If you have seen the movie you will understand!  But that is where it dies, after waiting and waiting and waiting with no update, we finally had to ask our main waiter what was going on with our food.. Then we began to see that our glasses weren't being refilled even when she can back 3 times to tell us our food was on the way... The final time we had to ask for refills!! Only good thing about that she comped us our drinks for the evening!! Other than that, the place is nice, contemporary, and chic for a diner.. I actually enjoyed my food this time!

came here with a friend after a relaxing afternoon at the spa, so was already feeling good and then this place happened.... prob one of the best meals I've had all year. Had to wait a little bit for a table but enjoyed wine at the bar and the wait was worth it. MUST TRY the sheep milk ricotta- i know everyone else recommends it too but it is literally that delicious. my friend got the pasta with duck and i had the pumpkin tortelli and it was phenomenal. the chocolate sourdough dessert also was amazing-never had anything like it. not a thing touched my lips tonight that i did not LOVE. cannot wait to go back again. so good!!!!

Arrgh!  Matey!  Arrgh! Every time I go to this place, I want to talk like a pirate.  And much to the annoyance of my friends, I do.   The food is not as good as City Fish, but I do love their lobster bisque, and I love the fact that you can actually purchase fresh seafood.  Also, you gotta love the JAWS poster.  I mean, a pirate-themed seafood restaurant?  How could you go wrong?

The atmosphere of the place is very dynamic: cozy seating area, bar, and a shopping area to buy their homemade hot sauce among other items. You get a lot with what you order (at least with omelette I got). The fries are amazing, because they don't skimp on the seasoning. Tip: Eat your fries with a concoction of mayo, ketchup, and their homemade hot sauce . If it wasn't for their amazing service and friendly staff I would have given 4 stars instead of 5. But the people who work there are super friendly, laid back, and easy to talk to, so if you demand more of that damn delicious hot sauce they will bring it with smile on their faces.
This place kinda sucks.

This place makes their own pasta and its sooooo delicious. If not the best pasta I have ever had. There is a long wait at Osteria Morini in Soho because the place is always crowded. I have had the Gnocchi, Sformato and calamari to share, I wanted to lick the plates  off after I was done. The portions are small and overly priced. I have been here twice and both times I have sat at the bar and we got this bartender with the pony tail.  I don't know his name but I feel like he needs a chill pill before he starts to deal with customers. Both times this guy seemed like he didn't want to be there. It's okay though because Tirado makes up for the hospitality of Ostoria Morini. Tirado makes sure you are seated and keeps you company with great conversation while you wait to be seated. We love the food and Tirados company so I won't be surprised if I become a regular here.

I visited here recently fondly remembering a time I tried a friend's takeout from here years ago. However, I was disappointed. The price isn't really a 1 $ sign, I paid $13 for enchiladas with overcooked chicken inside. I'm not a fan of leaving bad reviews- especially when the staff was nothing but friendly and efficient, but with an abundance of Mexican food in Philly, i'd say skip this one.

This a cozy place on the lower east side that houses some of the tastiest treats in NYC. Highlights? The pretzels and the fried chicken are outstanding. Good beer selection (drafts and bottles) and a wide array of whiskeys. All the food was spot-on in terms of flavor and presentation. It is worth a trip from the boroughs or the 'burbs to try The Redhead.
Quite simply, we've lived in NYC for 4 years. We've gone to many of the "top" restaurants in Manhattan. Grindhaus beats the pants off them. Order the full menu and share and be blown away.

Excellent restaurant in an unexpected location, an uninspired section of Hamden near Home Depot. Came here in a group at the last minute on a snowy night and were treated very well - with lots of attention and explanations. The tapas choices were all interesting - we most enjoyed the short ribs and the meatballs, also the ceviche. And the desserts were very interesting as well.
Great Irish restaurant !

Lunch on the run at Junior's is not the rush rush eat it and beat it experience. Sit at the bar, service is fast and efficient, complimentary tangy cole slaw and pickles, get a delicious burger in about 5 minutes. The burgers are better than Macy's Cellar, and better than Peter Luger's (both places have outstanding burgers so Junior's is truly exceptional). Big portions, prices are reasonable considering the quantity and quality of the food. Junior's is famous for cheesecake and deservedly so. I can go to Junior's for lunch, sit at the bar, have slaw pickles and a great burger, a big coffee and two refills and be out in 40 minutes without rushing. Looking forward to my next visit. I'm a repeat customer. Very highly recommended.

Very sub-par at best.  I would rate it 1 star for the food, but bumped it up to 2 because our waitress was awesome and really helpful. The decor is very cute.  The best thing you get is the free salsa verde!  The black beans tasted like straight vinegar and the "drunken beans" are very similar to the taste of baked beans.

I'm typically a sucker for burgers from nearby Village Whiskey, but if I'm trying to save a few bucks (or a lot of bucks if we're talking about VW), I gotta say I was pretty impressed with their standard burger. It's 1/2 the price of the VW burger too. Bang.

Like no other!!!!!!!!!!!! The best dining experience in NYC in 2 years. Excellent food the perfect service and the prices, cheap!! I recommend this restaurant if you want to have an excellent dining experience.
Nice light lunch.  Caffe Linda salad with chicken was good.  It was busy, but for a cafe it wasn't too noisy.  We'll come back!

We ordered a "house special" Sicilian pizza from Marco's yesterday afternoon. While the pizza arrived in a somewhat timely manner (just over 45 minutes), the crust was burned on the bottom. After calling them to let them know they agreed to replace the pizza. An hour later the second pie arrived and was UNDERCOOKED and doughy, not to mention that there was less of everything on the pizza, less cheese, less meat, less vegetables, but more sauce! I couldn't help but think that we were suffering for their mistake. They would limit their loss by skimping on the ingredients for the second pie. It also didn't help that they were skeptical about the pie being burned in the first place. For a $20 pizza I expected better. We will not be ordering from Marco's in the future.

Nice little place. They have a modern wait list that will utilize SMS on your cell phone. I think they slightly (and by slightly, I mean half an hour extra) overrate how long the wait will be just because of how big the horde can be; many people leave after hearing it (1+ hrs). But of course, if everyone assumes the wait's overrated, then it will become de facto... Anyway, we got the pumpkin waffles with appled butter, dried cranberries, toasted cinnamon-cardamom pecans, and warm baked apples and the salmon wrapped poached eggs on toasted black bread with green "goddess dressing", whatever that is. Now, I almost always get some kind of egg dish for brunch/breakfast because I usually skip breakfast during the weekdays. So I could be biased. I do love waffles and pancakes, but....I love eggs more. I like pumpkin-spiced foods as well, but personally I thought the waffles got a little boring after awhile. I wish you could order a half size. The cranberries and pecans kind of help, but it quickly becomes one dimensional. On the plus side, the dish overall isn't too sweet, so if you're worried you'll end up with the equivalent of chocolate frosted sugar bombs, rest assured, you will be safe. The salmon wrapped poached eggs on the other hand....delicious! Perfectly cooked eggs. Not the biggest fan of pumpernickel flavors, but it wasn't overpowering at all - perfectly accented the rest of the dish.

Wonderful hand pulled noodles! I do have to say I was surprised how un-spicy the spicy lamb dry noodles were, but I easily could have ordered wrong. Super relaxed crowd during lunchtime. Next time, I would probably get the super chicken thing like everyone else says to get. Ah, and Large there means SUPER LARGE!

Some girlfriends and I decided to take advantage of Restaurant Week and try someplace new.  We voted on LaScala's because of the ample RW choices. Prompt seating and they validated our parking pass.  Nice!  My appetizer of Sweet & Spicy Chicken Wings was REALLY good but one of my friends was not as impressed with her Baked Meatballs.  I thought my entree of Sausage Papparadelle was excellent but 2 others in our party were not as pleased---I think they both ordered the Parmesan encrusted Tilapia.   My sangria was just so-so but the Italian Creme Cake that I had for dessert was delicious.  All in all I was quite pleased with my dinner and I would definitely return.
Man, they have some good ramen.  It was worth the wait.  I have never like pork buns until now - these were so good.
Order a burrito al pastor and it was delicious. The service was excellent. Really nice staff.

Came here for my friend's birthday but I was NOT impressed.  First I sat at the bar at the front waiting for my buddies - I tried ordering for 3 minutes before the female bartender decided I was worth her time and took my simple order (sauvignon blanc!)... the waitress was engrossed in a conversation with a "regular" about her date the night before.  Shallow!  Is this how people do their jobs?  it took another 2 tries to ask her how much it was to settle and go to the table... ( and yes, she was engrossed in the SAME conversation.  lame!) Once at the table for the 9:30 reservation, the appetizers were good (we had the spinach/artichoke dip and anchovies/squid special) and I ordered the filet mignon.  What a surprise when I got it and it was entirely cooked through!  (I ordered medium!)  I was shocked b/c my friend raved about the food here.  I NEVER EVER send my food back (i used to work in the food industry so i know what happens when someone does) but this time I did  becuase it was blatantly freaking cooked through to well done... and the waitress returned with my meat chopped in 4 places and said, "the chef disagrees with you.  If you look at the middle, it's medium"  DUDE, it was barely light coral pink.  OMG, like - it was WHITE on the sides and barely blush pink in the middle.   Granted it was already 11PM when we got our entrees so I didn't want to make a stink - and I just TOOK it back like a total wuss.  Ew.  If it were earlier and NOT a wednesday (i was tired from work!) I would have fought that to the end.  So BOOOOO Freemans.  Booo to your chef that cooks the steak well done and refuses to re-do it to medium.  This place has non-existent customer service.  It was the WORST steak I ever ate in my entire life.  OFFICIALLY.  Well done steak acceptable for starving dogs and death row inmates - not paying customers who ordered their steak MEDIUM. I doubt I'll come back here since obviously the customer is NOT always right and their service straight up sucks.

Quite a few options for the vegetarian... The eggplant Parm is fantastic, as well as the cheese omelet. And there is your standard tuna and egg. They have rice pudding and tiramisu which I cant wait to try.

Went last night with my rents.  They think Brooklyn is the red-headed stepchild (like me!) of Manhattan - so it was a pleasure to take them somewhere with such flavors and high quality. We had delicious tapas, salads and wine. The waitress had a little bit of a tude.. but the food made up for anything that could have happened. Oh, and news flash:  If taking a date, there is a cute, little private table in the back - reserve it.  It comes equipped with sexy lighting, privacy and romance.

Located on the Upper East Side, you can get 1 gyro for $3.75 or 2 for $7. Come on! That is simply awesome. Granted, this is a new establishment and the price is likely to go up in the near future. Go try it out before it happens. So here are the goods.. - Place is clean. Friendly staff. Most importantly, the food is fresh and healthy oriented. Try the whole wheat pita. It is surprisingly delicious. I get the souvlaki's every time. Fries inside the gyro. Best idea since the invention of microwave and PS3. Greece style all the way! The fries are not overly greasy and the spicy mayo in the gyro compliments the fries well. - If you are a Lenox Hill employee, show your ID for a free soda with your order. Not sure how long that is gonna last but take advantage of it. - Get a reward card, you receive a stamp for each gyro you order. 10 gyros = 1 free gyro. the bads... - Only a handful or bar chairs. Not a place to sit down and eat.

So after always hearing about Kochs, reading reviews and walking by peeking in, I finally turned the door, but it did not open but luckily someone let me in. All the pictures on the wall were overwhelming and the barely see thru meat case told me Kochs was a fixture in my working district of Univ City. I was greeted with delight by the cook? My coworker had called in order so I just had to make sure we  were on the same page. The cook was hella funny as he helped the lady before me. He wouldnt let me retreat to my phone to text he engaged me in conversation while stuffing my face with delightful deli selections I really love the horseraddish cheese...because that was the first thing i ate I think it threw my tastebuds off to the rest of the meats, pickles and cheeses I sampled while I watied for my order. In between chuckles I found out that they have so many convienent ways to get an order in, texting, online, and they use my fav Level Up (if you have not joined do so). I had to say no eventually or I would not be able to enjoy my Cornbeef Special with horse raddish cheese. All in all it was a delightful experience. If you are in a hurry call it in or text it so you can get in and get out. I had some time to kill and I enjoyed the cook? candid sense of humor. My penny is on the shelf now. I will def be back and I will take advantage of the specials like the U of Sciences or Resturant School Special. I didnt notice a VA special, but the Cook? said if I came up with one he would list it. So check it out maybe one day my VA special will make the cut. The sandwhich was full of goodies piled bigger than my mouth, cole slaw, russian dressing and gobs of meat. I only managed to eat half....at least I have dinner now...
Food...meh.  Over sauced and unrefined.  got sick off of the food that tasted bad to begin with.
You have to try the Grandmas pizza. Amazing! Also love the chicken, shells, and broccoli. The lunch portion size is huge. It's like a dinner alone.
Japanese food and curry. What isn't there to like here? Was the review too short?

Finally! On a Sunday afternoon, a party of 6, and 4pmish, we only had to wait 45 minutes to be seated @ Ippudo! I was super excited because my brother (@Droolius.com) really hyped this spot up! We ordered the pork buns, which was exquisite with the fatty pork pieces and airy buns!  If I could have had my way, I would have just ordered the yummy white buns by themselves! So I ordered the Shirimaru Hakata Classic with Extra Egg ramen and my boyfriend ordered the Akamaru Modern Ramen (one of Ippudo's specialties).   My Shirimaru hakata classic really reminded me of SSG's ramen (YELP list: yelp.com/list/my-left-co…), where I fell in love with pickled ginger & soft-boiled eggs in my ramen!  The main reason I ordered this ramen is because it was one of the few listing the pickled ginger!  I loved it!  However, I noticed that the ramen here did have MSG (unlike SSG), because I definitely started getting sleepy after inhaling my ramen! :( Now that Akamaru Modern Ramen was pretty different & spectacular!  I really enjoyed the infused garlic oil.  The broth was pretty awesome! And, there was a wasabi ramen available that day.  My boyfriend tasted his friend's ramen and said the broth tasted just like wasabi! LoL.  I bet that cleared any clogged nostrils! This place really lives up to its hype.  IF you are a ramen aficionado, you should definitely come here!
Best Lychee Martinis! Happy hour until 10pm. Keith is a great bartender, ask for his famous Jalapeno Shot! Best Shrimp Lo Mein ever and decent Sangria. LOVE !

I've been to Num Pang a few times now and each time has been nothing short of excellent. The sandwiches may be a bit on the smaller side, but they sure don't hold anything back when it comes to taste. In fact, it's the perfect amount for a solid meal -- and if you're feeling extra hungry, you can compliment it with some of the best corn on the cob in the city (right up there with Cafe Habana's). So far I've only tried the pulled pork and grilled skirt steak sandwiches (both recommended) but reading some other people's reviews makes me want to go back and try some of the more exotic sandwiches (peppercorn catfish or coconut tiger shrimp? Yes, please.).

This place is the best! The staff was full of genuine good conversation! The one thing I appreciated is the fact that they keep the pork free from the rest of the meat. ....and the food is GREAT! My husband and I enjoyed EVERYTHING!!!!! You are welcomed to park in the back.

Vietnam Cafe serves semi-upscale Vietnamese food that is absolutely delicious and quite affordable.  The interior is impeccably clean and bright.  The service is on point.  The portions are rather large, and everything I tried was profoundly tasty.   My lady and I started off with the Banh Xeo, the crispy crepe ($9).  This was a wonderful app, but I would've appreciated a little more pork and shrimp, or at least a little less bean spouts.  They went crazy with the bean sprouts on this one! Tasty nonetheless, and I could've drank the dipping sauce. For entrees, we split the Bun Tai Hue (beef lemongrass soup - $7), and the Ga Nuong Toi Que (basil chicken dish - $14.50).  Both entrees were generous!  Considering the soup was the cheapest thing we ordered and by far the favorite, I'd say that gets my sincerest recommendation.  Both entrees featured bold and complex flavors, perfectly cooked ingredients, and provided us with leftovers!   This meal certainly did not break the bank.  It was a super-solid experience, that I'd put right up there will all my favorite Vietnamese spots in New York.  Great value, highly recommended.

Absolutely delicious!  We were very impressed with our dinner tonight.  In fact, I think I stated that I was in heaven while eating the freshest salad with homemade stuffed raisin bread, homemade pickled veggies, and of course, the pizza.   Can't wait to go back to this cozy joint.

Everything was good here but short of great. I dunno, to me it just lacks soul. Great space - really nice and clean looking. Service was too fast. Food came out of the kitchen at record speed. I started with the ricotta that everyone raves about. It was good and there was plenty of it. Nothing great about it though.  Next up was the lamb sliders - good but they were tiny and a joke for $11 an order. Main was the roasted garlic chicken. That was the highlight and very good. The portion size was huge. Overall, food was good but nothing great. Everything tastes fine but it lacks that little extra something that things on the next level have.

We (5 adults) went for a special occasion dinner last month on a Thursday night.  We got a reservation (8:30ish) pretty easily just a day or two beforehand.  The table was ready for us upon arrival.   The signature cocktails were all quite yummy, though when a friend ordered a Manhattan (not a signature drink) with bourbon, he was unimpressed by all three bourbon choices, which is weird, given this is such a classy restaurant. Hungry, we ordered a cheese appetizer as well as a charcuterie tray, and both were delicious.  The server took the effort to explain to us what each meat and cheese was, and even where some of the cheese was from.   I was impressed by our waiter, who was very familiar with each menu item and when I asked, "Would you get X or Y?" he instantly gave me his feedback, which I LOVE in a waiter.  I hate when servers say, "Oh, well, it really depends what you like."  I wouldn't have asked your opinion if I wanted to go with what I like.   Anyway, I got a local fish dish (can't remember what kind now) and my friends got short ribs.  Everyone was pleased with their dinners, and unlike some of the other reviewers, I thought the portions were quite sizable and appropriate.  My meal was a little on the salty side, but I'm super sensitive to salt, so I probably should have told the waiter ahead of time.   We didn't get any dessert, but I can say the restaurant was awesome in terms of food quality, selection, and service.  I would definitely go back.

Nice design, good selection, but with Berry Park just a block or two away, why wouldn't I just hit the roof deck? Tack on a star if it's raining? I guess...maybe? Edit: Did I mention I got some shitty dude telling me that I don't know anything about beer after I reviewed this...wtf?

I come on to update my review because as you can see the arrogance of this place is unreal by the response to my review from Joe M from Sushi Lounge.  I have been to this place many times so you would think the way a person who works for the restaurant would be less arrogant in a response to someone who has been at their establishment a handful of times, maybe even almost 10.   Not because I wanted to but because I just ended up there, the first times were ok but the high prices got ridiculous after a few visits.  You know that place were you always say, "Why did we go here?", this is that place.   Because of Joe M's response this is one of the many reasons I will never come back here.  If this is how this place treats its paying customers then I do not want to go to a restaurant which does not make things right, better yet who responds in such a arrogant way.   Not to mention a few of my friends have had a BAD experience at this place as well.  Meaning the manager and host gave them a problem and attitude for sliding over to a next table when they had no one in the restaurant and they sat them right next to the only table in the place.   Between the high prices, the small sizes of the rolls, and the arrogance, I will never come back.  I don't care if on Wednesdays you offer half price martini's, your martinis are still expensive because they are already close to $15! I don't care if on "many nights" you have 1/2 pricing, because you really don't if you did I wouldn't write a review like this.  Get over yourselves Sushi Lounge.  Do yourself a favor and go have a nice expensive sushi dinner in NYC.
I ordered the red sangria for the first time at Cheesecake and it was super sweet an lacked fruit. Other than that our waitress was super friendly and the food was perfect.

It seems the 'specials' never change.  I don't know why they aren't just added to the menu.  The food is well prepared and the service is excellent.  THere isn't much to chose from if you don't like steak, but that's why we went to a steak house.  I had the filet mignon and it was made pefectly.  My husban had the aged steak - it was good, but not worth the money.  Overall it's a very nice evening out.  Good for a romantic dinner if you choose a booth.
By far, the best pizza in the country!!! Made the old style way, with Real Mozzarella!! in a REAL Brick oven!! Well worth the wait!  A Real Pizza is just in the Sauce and the Cheese!!
amazing!

the food was excellent and so was the desert but the problem i had was that of the several times ive been there all the waiters are men and their arent any woman. i just found it odd because usually when i am at a restaurant there are both waitresses and waiters but here it is just waiters
Pretty good and a good price.

On a rainy day, my friend and I decided we were sick of the usual Big Wong fare, and that we wanted to try something new in Chinatown. Just whichever restaurant called to us we would eat at. (No Yelping allowed). We made our way from the tourist traps of Canal St to Grand St, and over to Eldridge St. I'm ashamed to say that I'd never heard of Super Taste. But on that rainy night, after rejecting countless restaurants (even the similar hand pulled noodle across the street), fate brought me to the somewhat shabby doorstep of Super Taste. The "decor" of Super Taste looks kind of like...a cafeteria in a village school. Plain wooden tables and chairs along the walls. And a big sign on the wall with their offerings. The place is not particularly busy. Mostly just a single person at each table. Curiously a small boy eating by himself at one of them...he is slurping away at his noodles..with a fried egg on the side. I'm sold. We walk in, not knowing what to expect...or where we were supposed to order... Yes, there is table service. Or at least..sort of....: "#1 and #2 please", we told the girl who waved us to an empty table. "YI HAO ER HAO!!!!!!", she screams to the back, in what is obviously a much practiced bellow. So what did I think? $5.50/bowl: The spicy beef noodle broth tops Tasty Hand Pulled Noodle. Hands down winner. The KNIFE CUT NOODLES are thinner than most places, and just springy enough, unlike some places where I feel the need to let my noodles soak a bit before they are ready to eat. AND THEY ARE SO SLIPPERY, which makes them difficult to eat, but the texture is SO DIVINE.\ TIPS: ASK FOR CILANTRO! They will give you a container of chopped cilantro to add to your noodles! I also recommend doing as the little boy did, and ordering a fried egg on the side! $3/bowl: The Special Fujianese Wonton Soup is also really delicious. They are almost like shumai in a deliciously rich broth. They list this as an appetizer, but I think this would be enough for a meal for me. $3/ 8 dumplings: The dumplings are also very good. They have a lot of stuffing inside, and are pork and vegetable. I think that they are not as good, or as good of a value as Prosperity Dumpling, although these are steamed and quite large dumplings. So conclusion: I was lucky enough to be drawn to Super Taste without the help of Yelp, but if you are reading this review, I'd like to hope that I've convinced you to trek off the beaten Chinatown path, and hit up Super Taste! Oh by the way..did I mention I ate here two nights in a row? Yes it is that good. And yes I wasn't sure if you are supposed to tip here although I did anyways...someone let me know?

Food was great, service was as well.  It was evident that everything was as fresh as it gets, and the ambiance was a perfect fit, it felt very "at home" .  Get the Farmhouse Flatbread, but as our server told us, "eat it slowly".  Thats a challenge indeed!

This week was our 2nd "restaurant week" visit to this fine Italian restaurant. Our first was earlier in the year. Do no miss going to this fine dining establishment! The menu is small, but thoughtful. There was the restaurant week menu, consisting of about 3 starters, 3 entrees, and 3 desserts. The regular menu was a price fixed 2-course menu. The cold zucchini soup was tasty and satisfying. The pate was hearty and delicious. For the main dish, we both ordered the skate wing, which was prepared perfectly, on a bed of white bean puree. Desserts were the perfect finish- the chocolate "creameaux" was incredibly rich, but not overly sweet. The olive oil cake had a wonderful citrus flavor. Reasonably priced wines are available by the glass. Service is impeccable. Go to this restaurant now!!!
great original NY cheesecake! I like the one topped with strawberries....not too sweet, creamy & light with a yummy crust.

wow, i must've been just as lucky as ken k. when i came here we literally waited 15 minutes.  my girlfriend dragged me to 53rd and 6th for a food experience that she said would haunt me once i returned to cali. i watched warily as the man scooped chicken, lamb, rice, and pita into the little aluminum pan.  i winced as i saw him douse the entire combo in white sauce (refer back to my phobia of white condiments) and watched as he dribbled a little bit of red sauce over it.  i leaned in and whispered "more red sauce". he raised one eyebrow and asked me to reconsider. i growled "more". so he gave the overall dish another good squirt of the red stuff.  we walked a little ways and opened up our cartons to eat. i wish i had just taken the entire bottle of the red sauce cause that was MONEY.  the combination was beyond anything i had eaten before. 5 stars all the way

I've always been curious of vegan food, but I guess I'm just too scared to try it so I thought to just try it out with this place first. a few coffee and some sandwiches. I am a fan now, this place made me wanna try new things. plus the friendly baristas helped me a lot too.

Really? This is a pizzeria to be found in Pennsylvania, not in NJ. Oh wait, it's next to the Pennsylvania Dutch Farmers Market so what a coincidence! Starting with the pizza, it's doughy and they use low-cut ingredients. Hot and cold subs are sub-par, you don't get a lot and you pay more than you would at other places. If you're looking for pizza and hot subs, drive 15 miles north to Milltown and points north. For cold subs, go to Hoagie Haven in Princeton. Truly a travesty this place exists and patrons are okay with it. Truly a difference once you cross into South Brunswick from North Brunswick it seems...

We were walking around and needed something to eat and drink and accidentally found Ivy. The atmosphere was great, food was good and the staff was very friendly. Went back several more times during the week and had the best time. When you're in Midtown check out Ivy!!!

The food here is DELICIOUS and reasonably priced! The only thing that is keeping it from 5 stars is the service. Was here on a Saturday night with reservations at 8pm for a party of 4. It was pretty busy but there were only 2 servers. It was a blonde woman and a shorter man. The man was as friendly as he could be I guess with how busy it was and the small wait staff but the woman was very unpleasant. She just looked like it was a burden to serve us. We were never approached by the waitress buy we had to wave her down each time we needed her (to order drinks, to order apps, to order entrees, to get water). Each time she begrudgingly brought us what we needed without so much as a word or a smile but with a look of annoyance. The Yucca fries were delicious, as well as the tequenos. Loved my chicken/avocado arepa. I would definitely come back and give it another try (when it's not as busy) but if I have a similar experience with service then that would probably be it for me.

Five Stars for the Tiramisu! Now La Lanterna di Vittorio makes a Tiramisu the way it should be made. It melts in your mouth (you really don't need teeth for this dessert). It's sweet but not too sweet, and the alcohol taste is just right, not overpowering like other places. The very thin bottom layer of the cake is soaked in alcohol. The light cream in the cake and the espresso powder (and some cocoa powder) at the top of the cake complements so well with it. Now many bakeries or cafes make their Tiramisu very cakey, in a way that there are a couple of sponge layers across the cake unlike La Lanterna. But I truly do like the way  La Lanterna makes their Tiramisu because they know how to balance their elements out so that it's not too cakey, or mostly you taste is just cream. A slice of this deliciousness is $5.99.  A great bonus is that you can buy the whole cake! In addition the fruit tart is pretty good too. The crust is semi-hard like the way it should be. It totally does not have that frozen flavor when you bite into something hard. There's a bit of a custard in the shell, where the fruit is sitting on. I'm really glad that the various fruits were fresh and sweet. I terribly hate eating sour fruits when it's meant to be sweet especially if I'm paying money for it. Now for the setting.  On the outside, it looks almost like it is a regular tenants building. From the inside, you see the winter garden in the back though. The winter garden is nicely warmed, so you won't get chilly or have any mist floating around the room. There are clear glass windows, so you see the sky above, and the green plants and vines outside. I'm very happy that I do not see the streets and people walking around, because I want to feel like I escaped from whatever is going on outside of NYC (in general) to have a comfortable and casual meal here. This is exactly how I felt when I came in. There is also a floor downstairs to dine in. I recommend couples to go downstairs for dinner because it's such a great ambiance down there. The only thing providing any sort of light are the candles on the tables. It is a great place to have a nice intimate conversation with you and your partner. The service was very good. If you were to order entrees, drinks, and desserts per person, your bill will come out to be at least in the $20s. Please check out the website for the place provided. Unfortunately, I haven't had enough regular entrees there to really rate the food.

5 stars for spaghetti - I have inappropriate dreams about this dish.  So simple yet so amazing.  Must have crack in it. 3.5 stars for creamy polenta. Been there, done that. 4.5 stars for the bread with the meat and cheese baked into it.  A meal in itself! 0 stars for the hostesses looking my mom and I up and down (my mom is not in the best of health) and trying to seat us at the drafty small table in the front of the bar room even though we had a reservation.   3.25 average rating, which is a shame because the food is worth it, the staff is not.

Delicious, affordable, great atmosphere, BYOB!  It doesn't cost a lot and is really good and simple and somewhat healthy.  Last night I had cous cous but before I had the chicken kebab platter and let me tell you the kebab is the kebomb!  My stupid boyfriend had the vegetable kebab.  But back to DAR 525 go have a party with your friends there or get some take out!

Pretty pricey for semi decent food. I had the burger and it was the most mediocre bland burger I've ever had. Medium rare, came out almost well done and was dry and crumbly. The bread was significantly bigger than the burger, to a point where I ended up eating just the burger and ditching the meat. The burger itself didn't even taste that good. The fries were good, but that's about it. Decent service, but the only thing saving this place is the vibe. Great atmosphere. Not sure what the happy hour is, or if they even have one, but this would be a cool place for that. Probably not coming back, definitely isn't worth it.

The Spotted Pig offers some amazingly fresh plates. I came here for brunch with my girlfriend the other day and was very pleased. The food was very good and the atmosphere was super trendy. Although the prices of the brunch drinks were a bit expensive, the food and the atmosphere makes up for it. Please check out my video review on my YouTube Channel! youtube.com/mealsandreels
Great for canoodling and yummy desserts!  Plus a fun hole in the wall type spot.

We needed to seat a table of eight for a meal that was accessible and delicious -- interesting enough for the foodies amongst us, but familiar and comfortable enough for the parents who are a little less adventurous. With Rye serving American comfort food at its best, we made the booking. The restaurant is, as one expects, Brooklyn-chic, which is to say that one can expect dark-wood panelling and a candle-lit dinner, though it's still a completely comfortable and welcoming space and, when we arrived, it was devoid of loud music which almost always detracts from conversation. Between us, we ordered the following: -The Brussels sprouts, which were delicious but, then again, they were deep-fried and served with pecorino and bacon and so they couldn't possibly be bad. -The crab croquette was good but, at $10 for a croquette the size of a squash ball, it may have been a little dear. -Several people ordered the meat loaf sandwich, served with onion rings. It was indeed delicious, having stolen some off my girlfriend's plate. In fact, it was so delicious that it begged the question why it needed to be served in sandwich form in the first place. -The mac and cheese was also very tasty (yes, I have a tendency to steal from the plates of others) - with a richness and creaminess that represented the height of decadence. -I had the pan roasted Scottish salmon, which was very well-prepared and certainly hit the spot. -For dessert, doughnuts were shared by all diners at the table and two of us shared the banana split. The banana split may have pushed me over the edge for the combination of ice cream, bananas, caramel and nuts was exceedingly rich. That said, it was worth it. Conclusion: We were looking for a fairly low-key dinner option for people with varying degrees of palate sophistication. In Rye we found a completely unpretentious little spot, which serves good drinks and great food in a comfortable environment. In a neighborhood in which "scene-y", "noisy" and "pretentious" are adjectives thrown around, this is a great little spot that is worthy of your patronage for those casual group get-togethers or romantic dinners for two.

Finally hit Cafe Cluny up for a late brunch on Saturday. We lucked out and were seated right away and decided what we wanted in minutes. I ordered my standard Eggs Benedict (especially because it comes with fries here - delicious!) and my buds got the salmon plate and the special of the day, a turkey brie croissant sandwich (clearly we are not on diets). Of course, no brunch is complete without a drink. I got a mimosa and the rest of the table got bloody mary's which was one of the best I've had in a long time. Our waiter explained they steep the vodka with a variety of pepper for a week and then strain it into fresh squeezed tomato juice with lime and horseradish right before serving. Superb! The coffee is also freshly roasted and while I'm not a Latte or Cappuccino girl, my friends raved about their cups. I also love the decor and setting. Feels like you could be in a bustling, bright French cafe instead of Manhattan (without the 'tude though!) All in all a great brunch place to enjoy with friends and people watch while munching on really tasty food. I can't wait to go back for the BLT or burger.

This review is ONLY for the Clams & Garlic RED pie. Excellent. Succulent fresh local clams- shucked, chopped & placed on the pizza when ordered. Nine relatives are "co-owners" of the CHAIN- 7 locations w 1 in Yonkers NY.
