I strongly feel & history attests, that in the food world (see my Colony review) that when a good thing is expanded upon it looses it's authenticity, quality, uniqueness, originality and & maybe even..... it's flavor. The original does serve a good pizza. BUT like all kinds of food, particularly pizza, it is subject to criticism, critiquing, & reviews. I am not a Pepe's disciple. But you can just read the other 300 plus reviews & go compare for yourself or you can go to "My Pizza List".
I ordered their "famous" hot wings and when they came out I took a bite, then quickly realized they were cold in the middle! Gross, NEVER AGAIN.

Great brunch spot in Chelsea! The backyard patio is the perfect place for a casual, Saturday brunch. My friend and I ordered the burger and chicken & waffles to share. The Burger w/ cheese and spinach was bursting with flavor and amazingly delicious. The fries were perfectly cooked and the aioli that accompanied it was tasty. We also really enjoyed the chicken and waffles. The waffle is more of a french toast, but just as delicious.To drink, we had the grapefruit mimosa which was just as yummy as the food- not too sweet or sour. I thought the food and service were great overall. Definitely go with the burger. If you're not too hungry, share it with someone along with something lighter. The food is delicious but can be a bit heavy, so come with an appetite!

A friend and I went to Sofia around 10pm on a Saturday night per a mutual friend's recommendation. We were seated quickly, but waited a few minutes for menus and water. Ok, no big deal. Several minutes later, our orders were taken. By this point it was busy, so we weren't too concerned about the lag. Our wine came, and while being pretty overpriced ($12/glass minimum), it was very good. The real problem came after our wine. We finished our glasses... and waited. And waited. Our waiter walked by our table to attend to other patrons not once, not twice, but FOUR times... and never said a word to us, or even discernibly looked in our direction. (By this point, the restaurant was nearly empty, and the staff was in no way busy.) Our glasses were removed from our table. Our waiter walked by AGAIN. Still nothing. Tried to wave him down, and he never looked in our direction. At this point we waited another minute or so out of politeness. We then left exact change on the table, and left. Needless to say, I will not be back.

We got there at 5pm on a cold Saturday night, it opens at 5:30pm. There's a small space that allows 6-7 people to stand in out of the cold while waiting. By the time 5:30pm rolled around, there's a long line of people half way down the block waiting to go in. The food. Keep in mind this place is supposed to be authentic in terms of Thai street food. Emphasis on the street food part. We got the wings, pork neck, beef salad (with sticky rice), condensed milk ice cream affogato and Chinese doughnuts (油条) for dessert. The wings can be ordered regular or spicy. The spicy version is spicy as in black pepper spicy, not jalapeño spicy. They are really strong tasting, heavy on the fish sauce and garlic. So were the other two dishes, ie everything was really salty (makes sense for bar / street food I guess). Overall I wouldn't go back there again. I can get better wings elsewhere and since I'm not a big drinker the hyper strong tasting food is not for me. O, the sticky rice is actually glutinous rice / sweet rice (糯米). By the way, it was 35 degrees outside not factoring in wind chill. By the time we left the restaurant at 6:45pm, there were no lines outside at all in case you would like to try it.

Yummy yummy yummy. totally worth the long wait for the food. i cant get a handle on what kind of place this it, its a bit country goodness, a bit mexican, a bit southern, a bit diner..not quite sure, but i really dont care because the food it good. very clever creations on the daily specials and there was even a celeb sighting involved, which is always fun. the one con--did not keep re-filling coffee, which might have earned that last star....

PLEASE NOTE: this review is solely based upon my cupcake experience here. I gave it two stars because it has a promising menu which I intend to try out at some point. That being said, if you are looking for a cupcake in Astoria, this place is to be avoided. I will be the first to admit that I have a cupcake problem - unfortunately, I have yet find somewhere in Astoria that can quell my childish cupcake cravings. After three separate visits to II Bambino for cupcakes, I felt compelled to write a review. The cupcakes are dry, flavorless and dense. They taste as though they've been frozen & thawed. To add insult to injury, they cost $3 each. Honestly, you could find a better cupcake at Trade Fair.
Last year, I asked: " But why don't you have lunch available during the week??!" THANK YOU FOR OFFERING IT NOW!!!!!
"SECRET WHITE SAUCE" IS THE SHH! -- youtu.be/78q8MdzkeDs "No line-up when we went. Haha, suckers! The halal cart guys package my Chicken over Rice ($6) dish to-go." -- youtu.be/WMzf5TUzmPg
Cash only. Open Late. Great place to hit after the bars. I got the Artichoke Pizza by the slice. I think my taste buds were in heaven for a bit.

The food is great but a little overpriced.  Their cluttered charm is also one of their pitfalls, as there's a bit of sensory overload between the display cases and the massive menu board when you walk in.  It's hard to pick out what you want when there are options everywhere.  That said, their bakery items and their savory items are both great, and I love their smoothies.  The BLT is my favorite sandwich, and if you've never had a kale and mango smoothie, just ask them, they'll make it and you'll love it.  This is one of my "treat" spots when I want to splurge a little on myself, but I do wish they had some more affordable items so that I could come here more often.  Also, I wish they delivered.

Overall Rating: 3.5 Stars. Sometimes the tumult of the East Village needs to be abandoned in favor of the more placid side-streets of Alphabet City. Having emerged on the other side of Tompkins Square Park unscathed (using my tiny friend as a human shield), we were in need of a warm and cozy setting in which to grab a glass of something or other. With Grape and Grain having been on my radar for quite some time, I thought that this would be the perfect opportunity to explore their brand of food and drink. On a Wednesday evening, the place was bustling, though not to the point where it was impossible to find a couple of seats. With the requisite candles, exposed-brick walls and wooden furniture, Grape and Grain embodies the vintage-chic that one has come to know and love in this part of the world. With good music pumping through the stereo at a reasonable volume (read: conversations can actually take place without appealing to screaming matches), this is a great setting for a low-key get-together with friends. As far as the drinks menu goes, there is a moderate selection from which to choose (don't expect to be blown away) and - having opted for the Cabernet Sauvignon and Temprañillo respectively - we thought that both options were good but certainly far from memorable. That said, the bartender was incredibly friendly and helpful and we were seated before the resident chef at the bar who was throwing all sorts of cheese-laden carb-based delights (read: pizza) in a toaster oven throughout the course of the evening. The food did not exactly look like haute cuisine, but I'm sure that it would serve as an excellent option if one needed to temper one's inebriation levels. Conclusion: There comes a point in life when blaring music and over-crowded bars no longer make for an enjoyable evening. Grape and Grain is an excellent intermediary that is neither the pretentious wine bar, nor is it the anarchic dive bar; instead, this establishment is filled with people simply looking to enjoy a relaxed evening in good company, in a welcoming environment - if you have a similar plan of action, this is certainly one place to keep on your radar, should you find yourself in Alphabet City.

i've got to bump this place up to five stars. I've gone so many times now, and the food is always so freaking good. The mee siam is just divine. Really, really, mouthwatering; insanely scrumptious. And the Malaysian Popiah appetizer? Who the hell knew that turnips stuffed in a rice crepe could taste so exquisite? And, seriously, these dishes are $6 and under. I think Taste Good must be getting a lot of business lately, because they've spruced the place up a bit. They've put some framed photographs of food on the wall, and they've upgraded the menus. I'm glad they are doing well. I also just wanted to add that the waitresses here always provide a great service, and even though the restaurant is always full, we've never had to wait for a table. Whenever I get grumpy about living in a neighborhood that has no parks, no movie theater, and no bookstore, I think about Taste Good and I feel good....get it? Ok, cheap delicious food is no substitute for green spaces and culture, but it comes pretty close.

This is an awesome go-to spot for creative, unique, delicious but not pretentious burgers. I recommend the PYT burger. The meat was pretty good quality for the price, the bun was soft and sweet, the bacon was abundant, and the sauce was rich and flavorful. The PYT burger reminds me of the shack burger from shake shack (my ultimate burger). Also, free glass of beer with check-in's. Beer battered onion rings and fries were nice and crispy. You can't go wrong here.
Food is good, though drinks could use some work.  Summers on the roof are a West Hartford tradition.  Crowd varies from college students to middle-aged.

I'm not really into Jamaican food but I tried the Beef Patty with Coco Bread and fell in love. The mild patty had a light kick while the soft, thick Coco bread calmed it all down. The combination plus the coconut soda I had made a full on experience I wouldn't mind having again. Maybe I'll find something on the menu that will slowly get me into more Jamaican food.

I have been here a few times for dancing, just for food and for larger events. The food is good and prices are on par for the neighborhood, I like the white bean veggie burger. The beer list is greatly improved from the early days, the free beer with check in to yelp is a nice touch. The staff really makes this place what it is, every time I have been here the place has been mobbed the staff remains attentive, friendly, and on point despite the loud volume and drunken hoards of people. I was here during equality forum and everyone managed to get served quickly, they even had someone expediting the bathroom line(though that person may not have been an employee).

This place was super tasty. I went for lunch on a weekday and the place was totally packed. We got seated pretty quickly though. We started with the haloumi which was incredible. It's a cheese appetizer with garlic and grapes, so it had a lot of flavors. I still think about it! I got the steak sandwich and it was cooked perfectly and was pretty filling. The portions here aren't huge, but where in NY are they? Rhetorical question. I'd definitely come back here and try their brunch. Since it was so busy in the middle of the week I bet it's insane on the weekends though.

I'm not too familiar with Brazilian cuisine -- but I must admit I'm getting better, learning more and eating more of it! A large part of this is thanks to one of my college friends. He studied abroad in Brazil for quite some time, so he's my go-to guy. We originally planned to hit up a restaurant a block or so away, but it was very crowded with a 45 min wait. Luckily, BarBossa was right around the corner! And I'm so glad we ate here instead. The inside is tiny, tiny, tiny. But they use their space pretty efficiently. Small, yet intimate. We sat at a corner table which to be honest, was a bit small for my liking (barely could fit 2 plates/2 people)... but we made do. For the main course, I ordered the Feijoada as per my friend's suggestion. If you don't know what that is... it's traditional in Brazilian culture -- black bean pork stew with collard greens, farofa (or as we like to call it, the "dust") and rice. It's comfort food for sure. I was happily surprised at how much I enjoyed it! There were definitive layers of flavor in every bite. The pork was tender and delicious as well. Overall, a solid dish. I had a bite of my friend's sandwich, the Calabreza (pork sausage, caramelized onions, Gruyere cheese and pico de gallo) which was tasty too. The dessert however, was interesting. We ordered the Romeo, Juliet and the Lover. What a name for a dish! I was immediately intrigued. It's what I would describe as a sampling of sorts. They had 3 Quenelles of Guava paste, Dulce de Leche and Fresh Ricotta. Not my usual, but definitely worth the try! Suggestion: try tasting them alone and then together! Let your pallet work its magic.

I usually don't leave reviews but this place was too good NOT to leave one! I ordered the carne asada tacos with everything and the especial, a deep fried quesadilla with meat and toppings added in! Both were AMAZING! I thought we had really good Mexican food here in Cali but I honestly want to make the trip back to New York sooner just so I can eat here! It was that good!
awesome atmosphere and delicious food!!

Finding this cash- only hole in the wall is good fun. But once you're here, the slightly short menu gives you a great joy. The food here is sublime, I had the Okinawa Taco Rice which was just tasty. Coffee was mixed, but still beats many Manhattan joints. Service was timely, and the tree inside was a pleasant sight. All in all, a great Bedford choice if you just walk 2 blocks from the the L.

Came here with a couple girlfriends and though the service was friendly and very fast (almost frighteningly fast...I mean was this food pre-prepared???), the experience was just okay. The ambiance is a bit too bright and cafeteria like and the food was plentiful but a bit bland. The fried calamari were okay but nothing too memorable. My shrimp pad thai was quite bland overall even though it was a huge portion. I think I will stick to Spice for my neighborhood Thai fixes.

2 years since biting into my first pommes frite yet it still always feels like the first time whenever come... Ok, maybe a little inaprope for this conversation about french fries, but in all seriousness Pommes has to be my favorite guilty pleasure snack in all of NYC. I love the staff here and I love their sauce concoctions. My new/current favorites are Vietnamese Pineapple (perfect blend of sweet & salty) & Eggplant Mayo (tastes like bacon, so how can you go wrong?) Tastes just as good in the daytime as it would past 1am...ok I will stop there.

Affordable good food. Their prices are very reasonable & if you're looking for a quick bite this is your place.  Just careful not to drip any sauce on your coat.  I was really enjoying my chicken sandwich that I noticed all the sauce has dripped down all over my coat.  I didn't like the falafel it was dry so I tossed it, maybe because I'm spoiled with good falafel & kabobs in LA.

Drinks are a bit more then am used to. But it is a bar so ya kind of expect it. Good thing is the bartender doesn't make weak drinks. And the bar-tending staff was pretty chill, which is a plus.  I did not get a chance to try any of the food, as i had previously eaten elsewhere.

I was looking for a delicious, inexpensive meal in Hell's Kitchen, and Pure Thai delivered. It quickly won me over with its unique menu and bustling vibe. We started with the curry chicken puffs, and they were perfect; the pastry was light and flaky, and the curry wasn't overwhelming. I ordered the wok basil chicken with rice as my entree, and the serving was more than I could handle - not that I'm complaining! It had a nice little kick to it, so the jasmine rice was a fantastic complement. I had a Coney Island Mermaid Pilsner to drink, and it was perfect with the spice. It's a small and crowded space (although not uncomfortable), and we lucked out by getting there before the dinner rush. Within a few minutes, the place was packed. Despite the crowd, our server was attentive and efficient; my water glass was never empty (a FANTASTIC thing when you're eating spicy food). My girlfriend and I both enjoyed the appetizer (she loved hers, too), our two entrees and two beers for under $30. The entire dining experience was tasty and a lot of fun. That means I'll be back next time I'm in NYC.
Music is great, good crowd. Fun times.  Food isn't all that, but I can look past that for the atmosphere.

Black N Brew is a cozy breakfast/brunch cafe that has everything from bagels to BLTs to pancakes.  They also have an equally impressive coffee/latte/smoothie selection that is made to order.  The inside wall space has local artwork for sale and the outside features a huge mural made by the one and only Isaiah Zagar.  The atmosphere reminded me of a laid back California eatery.  I opted for the vegan tofu scramble with a side of potatoes.  It came out quickly and was really tasty.  My only complaint would be that they gave me buttered toast to go with my vegan dish, but they remedied their mistake as soon as it was brought to their attention.  It seems like there's something for everyone here and it's definitely worth the trip.  If you can't find street parking, the Acme is right up the street.

I tried to eat here. I can't say I actually did. We were a party of six. I ordered Shepherd's Pie. When the food came it became apparent that my food was not in the mix. The waiter told me that another server had snagged my order when it came out and that a new one would be up in three minutes. Ok, stuff happens. Three minutes passed. Then 6 minutes. At the 10 minute mark the manager came to our table and asked how everything was. Our server had forgotten entirely about my meal. At this point everyone else at  our table was nearly done with their meal. I told them to just cancel my food. Their compensation for not serving my lunch? You would think they would work to make it right? A free appetizer card delivered with the check. Sitting at the table while everyone ate was uncomfortable not only for me but for our whole group. More was required. I spoke to the manager on the way out. She reiterated her apology. Disappointing. I won't be going back. Ever.
I brunch- because of this place!! Their Eggs Norwegian is an all time favorite i cant seem to stop craving!!!

Overall a great experience, but i found brindle room quite expensive for the food. The salmon was good, but I was less impressed with the sides. Pumpkin gratin (meh), braised kale (cooked well! but generally flavorless), mushroom bread pudding (the best), and the couscous with kale (meh). The potato donut bites were delightful and wish I had the option to order more. Happy hour drink deals were fantastic, I really enjoyed the house wine and it was only $5 after 10pm. Best parts were the drinks and donuts. The food was quite good, but very expensive and I've had better elsewhere.
This is the go to chicken spot in Rahway. Everything that I've tried was really good and the prices are great too!

I have one major complaint about Angelos Family Restaurant and Pizza, which means I cannot recommend eating there. The complaint is based on the fact 'the customer is always right', and they should make the pricing on the menu clear. The extra money we paid is irrelevant.   Although the food was good, I felt cheated when I got the bill. My wife and I each had a salad and we shared a Margherita Pizza. The waitress took our order and we told her we wanted a pizza that was on the dinner menu. The only price we saw on the dinner menu for a Margherita Pizza was $12.95. When she brought the pizza it was good but it was not worth $19.00, which we found out was the price when we got the bill. The owners wife explained to me we had gotten the large pizza that they sell for $17 for take out orders only & she promplty showed me a take out pizza price for $17. The waitress never let us know we were going to pay much more for the margherita pizza she recommended on the menu.   I asked Mrs. owner why $19 nto $17 - she replied we ate the pizza with the rest of our meal in the dining room. I should have known the pizza pricing I was payng was not on the menu. I told her why should I pay the extra $6 dollars. She promptly said have a nice evening.

Went here for lunch, and would generally never go out of my way to write a bad review, but the food was just awful.  The bar seats were so close together, people were practically sitting on top of each other.  The food took a really long time to come out, and when it did my food was inedible.  I ordered a catfish sandwich - the fish was off and extremely salty and the potato salad was drowning in vinegar.
Cool place to hang out and grab a drink. The food is different and delicious! Def a nice change from typical greasy bar food. Laid back but classy all the same ;) loved it.

I went here with my boyfriend and it was such a great date night. It's very small and intimate, and a bonus for us was being able to walk to it from home. We each got 4 rolls and soup, which seemed like a lot to the owner but hey, I can eat! We said we were fine with waiting a while since he said it would take time to make all of them. I think the whole dinner took 2 hours, and that's without dessert. I thought it was perfect though, because it allowed us to have a nice evening together without feeling rushed. The sushi rolls we chose all tasted very fresh, and I particularly liked the rice in the rolls. It was fluffy and sweet, and there was a lot of it. It didn't take away from the fish, however. I don't remember which rolls I got, but I remember thinking I probably would've been happy with any of them. The only reason I didn't give u1 5 stars is because I still like Jo-Sho in somerset better.

The best cafe in ditmas pk, alway looking for a new gem in bkny, the food, is exotic drinks are great! Tbe allure & vibe of the place is awesome, only - Is the space, wish it was a bit bigger, and only cash cafe, I usally pay with cc.
Better than average pizza. Not really sure what else to say lol.
Thank you yelp for finding us this gem!  Excellent food!!!!! Good service, love the fries!!!!  Now we stop every year as we head north skiing!

I come here if I'm in the area. You don't have to wait for food and it's relatively cheap. Glass noodles are my favorite. I also love the kimchi rice. My only complaint is about seating. You have to keep your eye out for empty ones. If there's no room and the weather is good, I recommend eating in the park by 6th ave. Note: beware of the animals, they are not afraid of you!

Better than the sum of its parts.   When I think of August, there really isn't anything that's incredibly special.  The food is impeccably prepared, but there's nothing on the menu that's really special.  The atmosphere and decor is really pleasant, but it's not spectacular.  The service is always solid, but there's no fawning over you.  The pricing is reasonable for the quality of the food, but it's not cheap, nor is this a spot where the food is impressive due to it's poundage.  But when it all comes together what you get is an amazingly pleasant and satisfying dining experience.  Isn't that what you want when you go out to eat? I've eaten there about a dozen times since it opened.  Once on a busy night we, like some other reviewers, had to wait about 20 minutes for our reserved table.  But it's a small, intimate, restaurant, and that can happen with second seating's.  The portions aren't huge, then again, this isn't an Applebees.  Take the scallops: typically 3 large scallops over a bed of flavorful greens for $8, if I remember correctly, but they are done to absolute perfection, soft with just a hint of browning on the surface.  Dinner for two will run you over $100 with tip if you do a couple of appetizers, your entrees, desert (they're all good), sparkling water, and cappuccino.  That does put August in some serious competition in Philly, but it more than holds its own.  I'm booked for dinner there again, tonight.

Gave this place a try on Mother's Day and was impressed. It was a fixed menu since it was a holiday but the food was delicious. We started with the calamari which was nicely breaded and not too chewy (wasn't a fan of the sauce though) and the shrimp wrapped in bacon. I went with the baby back ribs which were a good size portion with a good amount of meat on the bone that just fell right off once in your mouth. The fries were covered in garlic but all in all my meal was excellent. My mother had the pork chop which she also enjoyed and my brother went with the New York Strip which looked like a good sized steak that he also said was delicious. We were all too full to dry out the dessert which is a sign of a good meal. The restaurant has a very nice layout, large open space, there is a giant bar that helps separate the seating that is the first thing you notice when you walk in. The bar has a large selection of high end liquor, beer and wine. I look forward to going back soon and getting to see their full menu but i'd recommend this place for someone look for an enjoyable meal at quality restaurant.

My wife and I celebrated our anniversary here and after really enjoying Distrito's, we were very excited to try Amada. I had the opportunity to try his AC location a few weeks earlier and left not overly impressed, so I was a bit worried about coming back. I'm happy to say that I enjoyed the Philly location much more than his AC location. I even ordered some of the same items, and it looked different and tasted better at the Philly location. We got to the place a bit early for our reservation, so we went to the bar and had a few drinks. Someone had told us they had the best Sangria's and so my wife went through the three that they had, and agreed that they were the best Sangria's she's ever had. Once it was time for our reservation, the hostess came over to the bar and found us and let us know that our table was ready. We started off with the Mixito cheeses and unlike the AC location, they let us pick the three that we wanted. We went with the Aged Manchego, Fresh Queso de Cabra, and the Ermesenda. All of it was delicious, but the Ermesenda with the chocolate hazelnut puree was my favorite. Next up was the Chipirones Fritas (fried baby squid) and the Gambas Al Ajillo (garlic shrimp). We both preferred the garlic shrimp and although the squid wasn't bad, we probably wouldn't order that one again. Flatbread was next, and we went with the Costillas de Ternera. This was presented and tasted much better than the one I had at his AC location. Our last tapa was the Madre E Hijo, which is a chicken breast topped with a fried egg. I wish there was more fried egg on it, but it was yummy. We couldn't leave without dessert, I went with the Moca, which is a chocolate torte with vanilla mousse, coffee, and butterscotch. My wife ordered the Tarta de Manzana, an apple tart with sheep's cheese and roasted apple sherbet. Since our waitress learned it was our anniversary, they both came out with a candle, which was a really nice touch. Both desserts were good, but the Moca was clearly our favorite! Overall, service was excellent and it took us a little over two hours to get through our seven tapas. It was a very enjoyable meal and we would certainly come back to celebrate a special occasion.
Fries were basic. Tasted like Five Guys. Tomato basil soup was watery. Beef sliders were decent. Cashier stayed on the phone rather than serving customers.

Everything about this restaurant is amazing!!! First off, the place is beautiful with a classy and sophisticated decor, a wonderful bar (try some of the drinks created by one of the bartenders... forgot her name), and a unique and interesting open kitchen... you'll even find the bathroom to be an interesting experience. It's obvious that they spared no expense when they designed and built this place. As for the staff and service, they are among the best I've experienced at any restaurant I've ever been to. They are courteous, friendly, attentive, extremely knowledgable and very accommodating. On my most recent visit I was served by Jason Ferrer who did an outstanding job, and when there was a minor issue, it was quickly addressed and rectified by the very helpful manager Brian. Finally, the food... delicious, delicious, delicious! I've been there at least a dozen times and every meal has been excellent! I'm particularly a big fan of the "chef's tasting". I initially tried the restaurant, and the chef's tasting, utilizing a voucher that I purchased on Groupon. Since then, I have taken advantage of these exceptional offers for the chef's tasting from both Groupon and Living Social a number of times, even giving several as gifts. They have even extended the same deal when I've been there with additional diners. But I must say that the chef's tasting is well worth it, and a must try, even at the regular price. It's comprised of five courses, with each of the first four courses made up of different dishes to be shared based on the number of diners... by the way, they will accommodate special requests, allergies, etc. and will even let you try the peshwari naan if you ask. As a result, I've had the opportunity to try numerous different dishes and a symphony of flavors. Every dish I've tried has been consistent, absolutely delicious and never disappointing. If you haven't been there, I highly recommend you try it. If you have been there, I strongly encourage you to experience the chef's tasting. Unforgettable!!!

Oh my earth. So happy I are lunch here today. The chilled leak and potato soup was amazing! French fries yes I will have those. But not just your ordinary fries. A little spicy and cooked perfect. I have to say everything here is above and beyond what one would expect. Will be back and often!

I love love love this place! The risotto is fantastic and the breadsticks are to die for. They usually have pretty good deals on bottles of wine as well! The only thing I want is a larger space! The seating is very snug. I bet if they got a bigger location the prices would go up too so I'll take the cost effective tight quarters. Highly recommended!
Sigh. I miss Manny's. Are you guys ever coming back?

If you want some spicy hot crispy chicken this is the place to go. I came here for brunch and could not wait to eat southern fried chicken. The place itself is fairly small but they do have a full bar and a working television. The price for the hot chicken (and you can have it mild, spicy, or really spicy) is ONLY $13 for three big pieces of chicken and a side. It kind of took a while until I got my food even though there weren't that many people at 10am but it was totally worth it. You get a thigh, piece of breast, and a drumstick. I got the extra spicy and to my tasting it wasn't scorching hot but enough to get my taste buds going and getting sweat head for a bit. The skin is probably my favorite part of the dish. It was super crispy and juicy at the same time. SO much taste and I had to eat the whole thing. I got the grits as a side and it was buttery but did not like the chives on top. Still pretty good. Then I got 2 eggs on the side, red potatoes, and toast on he side because I usually need to eat some eggs for breakfast/brunch/lunch/or dinner. They say it is two eggs but definitely looked more than two eggs were used. I think they blended in the eggs future daughter and son in laws in there as well. The toast was more on the crunchy side because they do not add butter or margin right after as there are some on the table. I probably would come here again as they have other southern comfort foods that sound delicious like fried baloney sandwich or their fried chicken on a burger.

I grew up three blocks from this place, spent a good 18 years in the neighborhood, and saw Geno's go through quite a few changes during that time.  Recently, since about 1999 if that is recent, the place has suffered a barrage of bad publicity, bad stocking choices, and bad management changes that has spiraled not only the image that Geno's spent so long building, but the quality of product and service. Look - here's the deal - you are in South Philly.  Regardless of how gentrified or diversified you think the area has gotten, you are still in South Philly.  Many generations have grown-up and still live in the same neighborhood, street, and even house as the ones before (both brother and father still on same street and even brother now living in father's birth house).  The South Philly Italian culture is very different than most people from more worldly and exposed regions may be accustom to and it tends to grate them the wrong way or espouse an emetic feeling from their deep suppressed nethermost region. Geno's, not unlike most things and people from Philadelphia, are over criticized and not appreciated for what it is.  Note much in Philly has some ulterior motive or purpose, or tries to cater towards a specific demographic.  It is, truly, just what it is.  Geno's grew up around the Italian market which was a place immigrants went during the 30s and 40s to obtain cheap, poor quality, food during the post-depression era.  Once the yuppies (of which I admit I have grown into) moved into the area, they tried to make it a high-end outdoor Dean and DeLuca ... it isn't that, and you shouldn't be surprised if the locals get a little ticked off when they see their neighborhood grocery store or for that matter steak place start to change.  I remember going here as a kid and getting a steak sandwhich being surrounded by all people I knew from the neighborhood.  We used to go after school sometimes and it would be all Catholic school kids from around the area.  It wasn't until Oprah got a hold of this place, and the roaring 90's took foot, that the almighty dollar drew in more tourists and outsiders.  Most tourists would just settle on grabbing a steak from Oliveri's or on South Street rather than venture down to "Pass-shunk" (not Pas-e-yunk even if that is how you pronounce it). Bottom line - it's South Philly ... if you are coming here for sightseeing and a steak, don't you want the full experience?  If you have ever been to Italy, in particular the "real" northern industrial towns of Italy (Torino, Milano, Verona, Bologna) then you know, as I do, that South Philly is about as Italian as you can get, and Geno's is a close second.  The attitude is part of our culture, accept it or grab a steak from a tourist trap on Independence Mall. That said --- whew, nice rant huh, the steaks are OK and nothing special ... I prefer actually Jim's on South.

I loved jacobs pickles but the other night the service wasn't there. They were rude at the hostess table and rushed us out. I went to some other spots around there and decided I wanted fried Oreos. When I went to pick them up I was short changed by 10 dollars and the hostess argued with me so I just left. I'm sad this happened at one of my go tos.

The decor of this place is AMAZING when you consider that this is not a high-class restaurant. I pretty much never care about the interior of a restaurant, since I am there for the food, but the design of this place will blow you away. I will be honest and say that at other places I have had Thai food for a little cheaper and sometimes a little better. But that being said, this is still the best place to go in at least a 1 or 2 hour radius, if not more. The price is much better than at other similar restaurants in the area and the quality is also better. I have tried the Pad Thai, Pad Kee Moaw (Crazy Noodle), Pad See Ew, and the Shrimp Fried Rice. All were very much worth it. The service was also great but mostly because this place is new and is not crowded as of yet. They will probably need more servers if it ever becomes full. Even if you aren't a big fan of Thai food, just come here to see the interior. This restaurant is beautiful.

I love the feel and look of this place and I have no idea why I went here. It is odd for me to go anywhere that would have the word Tavern in it, but I am happy I did. From the person seating us to the wait staff just grand. Not often eating Lamb as it tends to tear my stomach up I took a risk since I love it and had the Lamb Pappardelle, yummy. There are so many places to try in NY when visiting, I am just glad this turned out so well and would go back.
This place is pretty cool! I love the pizza and their lemon ices! My boyfriend is obsessed with their Spumoni ices!  I go at least once a week. :)
Meh. Just very average. For gluten free you can't get much more than eggs and bacon. If you can eat gluten it might be a nice and cheap option.

Beautiful, historic italian place. We sat on the covered outdoor patio, which felt more like a greenhouse, and it was perfect for a rainy day. My husband and I both got pizzas. The crust was crisp yet chewy and bubbly. Just perfect! If this isn't authentic new York pizza.... Well, I don't care to find out what is! Service was very kind and courteous. Could have been a little quicker with bringing the check after we were done. Bathrooms were cramped but manageable. Definitely a romantic spot and I would go back in a heartbeat!
Not a traditional Spanish Tapas but food was pretty good!!! Have good selection of wine too!

Best freaking waffles ever!!! I'm a breakfast lover and I'm so glad i found this spot. The breakfast burrito with Taylor ham was great too. Can't wait to try one of their beautifully displayed desserts soon.

8/11/12 - Joint Wedding Shower Had a wedding shower here and it was wonderful  Service was over the top great and the food was phenomenal.  We have been going to Nauna's for years, so this was a great choice for our special occasion.  They gave us the run of the back dining room all afternoon and we were able to clear out in time for dinner service. The staff was very nice and helpful during the event, making it a wonderful experience. The buffet selection received rave reviews from our guests and we look forward to having our next event at Nauna's!
The unlimited mimosas were worth it.  Our waitress kept filling up our glasses :)

I must have walked by this neighborhood place a hundred times, but the outward look of the place didn't really get my attention, until I saw the windows open one day, letting in the warm afternoon sun.  I walked up to customer eating there, and simply asked him how the food was, and he replied, "Excellent!" with a big smile on his face.  "Try the turkey club."  I thanked him walked in, and did what he suggested.  WOW.  The club sandwich was really, really good.  With a superb, little mesclun and arugula salad on the side (instead of boring fries), I knew that this would be my new "favorite place" on Ninth Avenue.  The next time, I ordered the cheeseburger, and again was pleasantly surprised with the overall quality and taste of the burger!  The waiter was so thoughtful that he actually made a Coke float especially for me, since it wasn't listed on the menu.  This kind of service deserves kudos, and along with the great selection of surprisingly good bistro food and fabulous brews, makes this little joint a definite destination when in Hells Kitchen.  You won't be disappointed.
great for a tasty meal after walking around town.  friendly service, great food and a casual atmosphere.

Great menu and inventive cocktails (although some are a bit too sweet). Reservations are recommended since the place is small and gets packed on weekends. They do have a room downstairs for large parties though. Try booking through Savored for weeknight reservations and you get 20% off. We tried their tuna ceviche, guacamole, empanadas and fish tacos for apps. All were great (especially loved the fish tacos, best I've had probably ever). Entrees were the cod, salmon and a beef special. For dessert, we split the churros. Will be back soon!
Excellent & clean diners with really good price. Old US decoration and great burger. Perfect place to stop by after a walk at liberty park!

The Host was awesome and told us there was a 30 minute wait. My husband and I got a cup of coffee and waited patiently and not 20 minutes later our table was ready.  The reason for only 3 Stars is my French Toast was burned on one side, the bread with my husbands poached eggs in tomato sauce was burnt and the potatoes in his dish were uncooked.  Great location, Great Vibe but some attention needs to be on the food coming out of the kitchen

D - is for Delicious, as I found the food they served. I - is for Ironic, as the hipsters I there observed. N - is for Nourishing, as their organic ingredients must be. E - is for Eggs, found in the feta herb omelet served to me. R - is for Return, which I won't be able to do today. but not for lack of want/ quite simply because/ i live 2500 miles away! :(

Their brunch is fantastic , order from them almost very weekend. Really good menu, food is tasty delivery is quick and service is friendly. Their eggs Benedict are very very good!! They have real fresh squeezed orange juice too which is nice.

I'm not too familiar with this area, but when my friend was in town and said he was around Penn Station, I chose this one from the Yelp reviews (which didn't disappoint!). This place wasn't too crowded after work Friday, had a good beer and drink selection, and had ample TVs if you wanted to watch sports. Our waiter was incredibly nice and attentive, and the fries we ordered were pretty good. Would definitely go back if I'm ever in the area.

I am SO happy Laduree came to the U.S. These were my favorite macarons in Paris and I'm so happy I don't have to cross the pond for them any longer. You cannot get better macarons in NYC than Laduree, that's for sure. They are around $3 each but worth every penny. I particularly love the salted caramel, pistachio, and chocolate. Try to come on an off time like during work hours because on the weekends the lines get pretty long.

I found this restaurant to be totally uninspiring. I came for dinner with a friend last week and was quite disappointed, as I have heard only good things. To start, the service was slow and felt sluggish. For food, we shared the blue fish to start which was tasty and came with a heaped pile of toast and pickled onions. For main dishes, my friend had the winter squash vegetarian dish and I ordered the roasted chicken. Again, everything tasted good but both the food and atmosphere lacked excitement and creativity. Something just felt off. Looking at the other reviews, maybe this is because I came for dinner and not brunch. I will give it another try at a different time of day.

My boyfriend and I went there for dinner recently and had a great meal.  The place is small and tables were a bit too close together, but since the place was so cute and romantic, I would have to describe it as "cozy".  Unfortunately, we did not know it was BYOB so we had nothing to drink, so be sure to bring your own bottle.  We had the special that night, the lobster taco and it was EXCELLENT!  We loved it so much we wanted it again instead of desert.  I had the ox tail and it was very good.  My boyfriend had the roasted pork and that was even better.  If we lived in Williamsburg we would be there all the time.
Not the worst location to grab a drink. Somewhat touristy. I prefer the upstairs bar. They have a 'roof top' but thats a complete joke.

Came here for a quick grub before raging in NYC.  I ordered the artichoke pizza and it was absolutely amazing!  What a perfect way to prepare my stomach for a crazy night of drinking! The pizzas are pan style pizza and they are HUGE.  I was only able to eat 1/3 of the slice. I will definitely come back here for more when I visit NYC again!

A few months ago we moved from East Rock to Westville.  Curious to see what the other side of town had to offer for dinner, we decided to try House of Chao.  After reading Yelp reviews we decided on the General Tso's Chicken. Chao is unlike most Americanized Chinese food.  The chicken is huge chunks of real white meat, LIGHTLY battered, and actually a little spicy.  It's a breath of fresh air from the heavily battered mystery meat you usually get where the menu can only claim spiciness. We've since eaten many other dishes, everything being very tasty.  Ingredients are fresh, veggies are cooked nicely, and nothing has been too oily.   The eggrolls leave a bit to be desired. Overall I highly recommend this place.  We haven't actually eaten in the restaurant, so I can't comment on it other than it looks clean. Most menu items are around $10, but there are a few around $12.50 (seafood). Things you should know: - The average time they tell you when calling in your take out order is 45 min, so don't wait til you're starving! - No delivery! addendum I subtracted a star from the original 4 due to slow staff/service.  The take out time has gone from 45 minutes to an hour and half for ONE order of General Tso's Chicken!!!  What?  Walking into the restaurant I waited almost five minutes before I was acknowledged, which is sad.  Its a small joint.  Still the food is good, but the staff is underwhelming to say the least.

California native here &, although this may not be the most traditional banh mi shop around, this has OFFICIALLY become my favorite. There are a few different options, but I always go with "The Hog" or the "Lam'bretta" extra, extra spicy with a side of sriracha to-go. There are obviously more traditional options, but I've come to think of this place's banh mi's in a whole different category of banh mi  -- in the same way I think of "Mexican" food out here. It's not what you had originally craved, but the particular spot has such good food that you begin to crave that location's items as their own separate genre. The basil limeade fizz has been perfect the only two times I've ordered it, but I honestly prefer Vietnamese iced coffee at other locations more. They DO have a frequent buyer card though, so make sure to get on that!
People here swear we owe them our buisiness. They need to lighten up and appreciate good customers! Food is good though!

Chose this restaurant to have dinner last night with my family because of the great reviews and because it was around the corner from our hotel. Let me tell you, they brought their A game!  The food was amazing!  Everyone enjoyed their meal!  The decor had us feeling we were in Havana....so beautifully done!!  I strongly recommend the Rainbow ceviche, the oysters and most definitely, the chocolate cigar.  Next time in Philly, we will definitely be back!!

What an experience! If you are a "foodie" willing to leave traditional comfort zones, this place is a must try. The chef is creative. The staff is engaged. This is not a romantic hide-away. This is seriously great food at reasonable (for NY City) prices. Wine list is small, but well chosen. Trust your server for recommendations. I was about to mention the highlights - but that would be each dish that we tried. Two of us shared 8 different plates. All wonderful.

I like small menus. I actually prefer them to larger because it gives the chefs a chance to perfect the recipes so I was pleased with the options here. To be honest I was a little annoyed that they didn't have a choice to pick more than one meat without paying an arm and a leg for both (e.g. chicken and ribs or brisket and pulled pork) if you're a single person. Most BBQ places I've been to have that option although most BBQ places I go to are in the south. If you have a group they do offer a good deal to try a lot of items on the menu. The meats and sides are sold separately (no meals). In my mind there's no such thing as gourmet or upscale BBQ so the prices are a little high. I only ordered cornbread and BBQ Fries. I think I'll stick with Southern BBQ places because I was disappointed with everything except the cornbread which was absolutely delicious and most like what I make at home. I should also add that my father owns a BBQ restaurant in Mississippi so I have pretty high standards and expectations. The server could tell I was annoyed so the manager gave me a complimentary mac and cheese. The mac and cheese had too much nutmeg (which usually enhances the cheese flavor but you shouldn't be able to pick out the distinct seasoning). The BBQ fries were topped with brisket and cheese sauce. The brisket was salty and the sauce was tasteless. I cannot complain about the atmosphere or service both were great, but I'm a foodie and smoker's (meats not cigarettes) daughter so being unimpressed with the food gets 2 stars. Fans of this place more power to ya!
Great food and great service.  Our waitress Natasha's super friendly and knowledgeable that I want to eat everything she recommend. The drunken spicy shrimp boil was amazing!!

I used to live around here.. and so I semi- grew up eating this. Best chicken ever! It's as good or even better than PioPio for a fraction of their cost.  This is a take out joint so duh you would expect it to be cheaper. No tip required means funds for the next time you come here. The green sauce is amazing.. It's a little watery-er and chunkier than the green sauce at Pio Pio, but it's nonetheless like crack.   If I were you, I would get as much of the green sauce for free as possible and buy more if it's not enough to drench your chicken and rice in. They have inca cola which is a plus. I recommend having it since it's not your average soda :) It's like a pineappley-sugar-yellow coke made by the Coca Cola Company. The place itself is kinda dirty... well that's an understatement, it's pretty gross and greasy all around.  However, it doesn't reek and I still would dine in at their tables so it's not that bad REALLY lol. They offer PFR and beans as sides too. PFR is rather greasy. Reagrdless I always get chicken+pfr+beans+inca cola.  There's a park 2 blocks away towards the west (doughboy park.. or whatever they want to call it now), which might be a nice place to take your meal to and eat on the stone benches/tables on a nice spring/summer/fall day by the grass under big shady trees. PS I still travel from practically Long Island to come eat this time to time.. if that says something. :) PPS. God their door is hard to open.

I've been to the AC location a few times and have loved it, so I was pretty excited to come to the original spot, and wow, was just blown away. The food is incredible, and they have a regular and gluten free menu which makes things easy if memebers of your party have dietary restrictions. The problem I have, is that I want to try so many other things on the menu that I haven't in the past, but it's just too difficult for me to not order the things which I have eaten in the past and crave again! The decor was fun, slightly loud as can be expected, but not too rambuntious.  Service was attentive and friendly.  Drinks strong, and prices expensive, but reasonable for a great experience. Amada ranks up there with my favorite restaurants, and I would certainly come back and recommend it to anyone.

Little pricey. Great food. Small portion though. It's more "explore new taste" than "get a post-meal coma". Very popular place and service is excellent. I do love the fried cauliflower! And some lamb and chicken. Very mid-estern taste and modern classy decor.

This is our go to pizza place.  My entire family loves it.  i usually pick up but tonight decided to call and have it delivered.  I called 411 tonight-Jan. 2, 2014 for two Margarita pies and much to our dismay 411 operator gave me the number to Anthony Francos pizza.  We did not know until the pizza was delivered so cannot tell you how disappointed my family was with the mistake.  Not only was the pizza expensive but it tasted Awful.  Next time I will make sure to ask what is the name of the pizza place before I order.    MAKES ME APPRECIATE FRANK ANTHONY"S EVEN MORE NOW!

to quote Yelp "Yay! I'm a fan." I am always looking for places to remind me of back home, and this place fits the bill. The owner is very friendly and courteous. They have a full selection of Bit Shot soda and Zapp's chips. If you haven't had Zapp's chips then I don't know how to help you. But I will try to help you. Go to Cheeky and try the Jalapeno or the Crawtators. They sandwiches are a bit small but they're more filing than they look. They place is small but also kinda quaint in it's size. And having worked in a winn dixie in highschool, seeing the old winn dixie advertisement was a nice touch.

On a normal basis, I would not come to this tourist spot but I watched a show just across the street and decided to stop by. We sat at the bar during our stay and didn't have to wait for a table. We only came here for steak cut fries and strawberry cheesecake. The fries are nothing special. This is my first time having Junior's strawberry cheesecake. It's good but not notable. I like my cheesecake a bit fluffy with a graham cracker crust. Junior's is really dense and uses a shortbread crust. Cheesecake Factory has a place in my heart for sure. Sorry, Junior's! My bf ordered a White Godiva drink and it was pretty good. I ordered a cup of hot water and I got to say that that mug is huge!

Delicious. Walking distance from my apartment, and I like to walk here for lunch some days. I always order a large sandwich and save half for the next day. Makes my lunch around 4.25 per day. Plus they are LOADED with meat and cheese, so you really get your money's worth. Great little local place.

As a personal trainer in the city it is always nice to have a great spot to go to between clients that serves some healthy and delicious menu choices. Several of my clients are locals of Bakehouse and the restaurant gives off a very noticeable family vibe. Great staff, great food, great service. Try the Tuna Nicoise Salad, Scallops,  or grab one of their fresh juices to go on a Saturday or Sunday morning to start the day. Three Thumbs Up and great addition to the West Village and NYC!

This place is quite the find.  I stumbled upon this today and was taken by surprise at the $8 lunch menu.  I ordered the taro fritters and Pad Thai with shrimp.  Both were really delicious.  The Pad Thai had a little something different than other versions I've had; I liked it a lot.  The restaurant has a great modern, trendy atmosphere.  I can't speak for dinner pricing, but for lunch $8 is a steal for the Village.

I was pleasantly surprised by the ambiance here. I was expecting something more diner-esque. This feels like a real restaurant with some home-y touches of family photos and kids toys laying around. Oo man, seeing that Godzilla brought back some serious memories. Nostalgia at its finest. For dinner the music was indie hipster funk. I realized later that the tempo kind of made us ansy/fidgety though. Coincidence or does someone working here know something about human behavior and tricks to get customers in and out faster?? The music definitely made me feel a bit rushed, thats for sure.   Many of the popular brunch items are also available at dinner (not including pancakes or french toast). I was un-pleasantly surprised that the portion sizes were relatively small. When I think comfort food and fried goodies, I imagine plates being piled high. The food was decent, but lacked the home-made quality that is seems like the atmosphere is going for. Fried Green Tomatos: Pretty good, not the best I've had, but passable. Fried Mac n Cheese: This dish always *sounds* delicious but usually frying mac n cheese tends to dry it out so its usually a flop. Their version was better than most and I enjoyed the kick of the sriracha! *I saw a few tables that actually ordered the regular mac n cheese dish. The portion was much larger and it looked creamier. I think I'll order that next time and ask for them to bring me a side of sriracha.* Veggie Burger: Got this based on a glowing recommendation made by our server.  The patty was decent, not notable, though I did enjoy their special sauce. Fries were average as well. Friend who got the Chicken & Waffles said the waffles are better than the one they serve at most places (which tend to be subpar) and the chicken was pretty good. Everyone else ate most of their food, so I assume it was relatively good, but not enough so for anyone to compliment. What really disappointed me was my most anticipated part of the meal: dessert. The desserts were TINY and unimpressive which really bummed me out because their description was really why I wanted to come here in the first place. I mean Caramel Apple Pie and Red Velvet Bread pudding SOUND amazing right?! Not so amazing in reality, more like something your little sister whipped up in her easy bake oven! Verdict: I'm not raving about it, but I'd give it another shot and would like try out their brunch (though most of the menu items are the same).

Blah. The girl and I shared the Crab Mac: "Lump crabmeat, tomatoes, spinach, crab cheese sauce, and a crab cluster claw." I make no assumption, but it wouldn't surprise me if their method of composing their mac dishes is to take their stock mac and cheese mix (already finished), cut additions into it, bake in crock OR microwave, transfer to crock, broil, then serve. Just a guess... There was no flavor melding in this dish. In one word, it was modular. Each piece of spinach, tomato, and crab hung isolated in a sea of mac. Spin-Art Dip, Crab Mac, one draught beer, one non-alcoholic apple cider, plus tip: $50. $8 for the Dip, okay, that's somewhat reasonable. $20 for the Mac, no way, that's steep. I won't be back. There are far better and well-priced options on the Winooski strip.

Breakfast this morning... Fast, attentive, excellent service and the food was good! Fair price, fun place, worth a stop in. And for those who added a review and were 'disappointed' - go back to your own little town and see if your best place comes close - clue: it doesn't. Thanks Juniors.

I just hopped in for the beer. Large selection and the guy was really helpful. I wanted some Mad Elf and he pointed me to a bottle that was really similar in taste and content. I hate though when bottles don't have prices by them. I don't like being surprised at the counter. The place is pretty empty most of the time, honestly. So I've always been unsure about actually staying there to eat since it never seems that popular. Gotta try it out tho next time.

Such a pretty space, and the service is excellent, but everything I've had there just falls a bit short of the mark..great ingredients, the menu sounds fabulous, but it just never works as well as it should. The whole [dish] is always less awesome than the sum of its parts [ingredients].

I really enjoyed Smorgasburg Mighty Quinn but I just couldn't love their store. The employees are super friendly! It might be that at Smorgasburg it's more fresh and delicious straight out of the oven whereas in the restaurant they seem to have heated up.

Hands down the most amazing sliders I've ever had. I plan on returning whenever I happen to be in the area. It was quick and friendly service and at the time that I went there wasn't too many people so it made for a comfortable meal. The fries were okay and I've yet to try the milk shake. But I look forward to trying it whenever I get a chance to go back.

I was a little disappointed on my return to Barrio Chino last weekend.  It wasn't as good as I remembered.  The vibe is still wonderful and I love the concept but the food was a little lackluster.  The most disappointing change though was the quality of the caipirinhas.  The caipirinha remains my favorite drink on earth so I get very excited whenever a bar offers them.  My caipirinha barely tasted like lime at all - it was incredibly strong (which is normally a good thing for me.)  This was just overpowered by the taste of the cachaca.  Oh well.  It was good while is lasted.

I really enjoyed the experience at fogo . I took a friend there for the first time for her birthday and she was very pleased.  I have dined at similar restaurants such add Chima's on many occasions and the service there started to get unpleasant.  Thank you fogo:)
Very friendly owners.  Decor is dated but the food is so delicious.  Do not let the decor distract you because it is so tasty and cooked fresh.

Took the kids here to celebrate their fantastic school year. Straight A's all around and for honors and Advanced Placement classes to boot. My dish which were the pork chops were edible in fact nothing was left on the plate but disappointing. Appears they just dusted some old per-cooked  chops with plenty of adobo and some lemon or lime juice. My only recommendation is find yourself another restaurant if you are looking for good hispanic food. By the way, the service was good , the setting is comfortable and were seated in a sun room like seating area. Those parts were good. Shame the food was not up to the same level as the service and atmosphere.

1.5 years.  The approximate amount of time Zachary Taylor was in office, or the amount of time I went without Kefi due to its closure/being busy and no longer living in MoHi. The answer is both, but alas, absence did not make the heart grow fonder once we were reunited. To be fair, the food itself was decent, albeit not as good as I remembered.  The sheep's dumplings were merely okay but the sauce was very flavorful, just begging to be scooped up by an extra order of bread.  The lamb burger was also average at best, nothing special and honestly, there are many better burgers in the neighborhood. So far, the restaurant is probably earning a solid 3 stars, but then what merited the drop? The service, oh god, the service.  The food took something like 45 minutes to come, while dessert, which was nothing special and shouldn't have taken that long, took 20.  Any request required attempting to flag down a waiter, already incredibly difficult, and actually ensuring the waiter remembered your request by re-flagging him down and reminding him.  The ambiance was also lacking, especially in the basement.  There was an old moldy smell, though it was very faint, and the place just seemed unappealing.  Perhaps it was the lighting, or the setup of the basement, but this place has definitely lost its charm.

Decent place. I'm a fan of the kale salad and have had some yummy oysters here too. I usually get whatever salmon they have and it is always fresh and good. I wasn't as in love with the fried chicken as many of the other reviewers, but I may just not be a fried chicken person. The wine list is not the best. They are always super nice here, so I give them an extra star for that.
Black sesame creme brulee     matcha green tea   go get them!!

I really wanted to love this place, but I just have to say it was OK. The service was excellent and the decor is adorable, but the food is mediocre, and certainly not worth the price. I went here with a bunch of my girl friends for dinner and we didn't even have to wait to get a table. We started with the pretzles and dip, which was a cute idea, and the dip was good, but eh.... not sure I looovved it. I had the lamb, which people have raved over in other reviews, but, again, not sure I would say the same. I have absolutely had far better. Another friend had the burger, and she said it was "just good". Two other friends had salads and sides. All in all, not going to go back. There are so many other places that are so much more delicious.
It's so darn good! Try the short rib slider and let it melt. One of my favorite restaurants in Brooklyn.
I'm from New Orleans and love this place. The seafood is fresh, the staff is friendly, and it's a fun atmosphere. All in all, this place is off the chain!!!

Great tasting pizza! I had gotten two large slices.  One broccoli and the other cheese.  I enjoyed the broccoli more than the cheese as the bottom crust was crispy and the cheese was gooey just like how I like it.  The cheese slice was great but didn't have a crispy bottom crust.  They have a variety of pizza in display.  The grandma looked good but I wasn't in the mood for sausage.  It'd be nice if there were places to sit.  Only options are standing or sitting at the theater steps across the street.

Good service.  I'll give them that.  On a Friday night, they got all the food out for our party of 12 at the same time so they get an extra star.  But the food was two stars.  I had the crispy buffalo chicken sandwich, which was neither crispy nor sufficiently buffalo, but was a chicken patty.  I was expecting something like fried chicken on a bun.  Not so.  The flavor wasn't all there either.  My wife's salad was meh. But there's one guy working there who looks like Charlie from It's Always Sunny In Philadelphia, so it has that going for it.

This place looks like someone's kitchen.  It's cute and the guy who either owns it/is always there is really nice.  My vegan friend and I just go and order a bunch of different things to share.  What I like about it is that the portion sizes are pretty small and cheap so you can order lots of different things.  Their menu is very extensive from "chicken nuggets" to sushi, and they have some interesting things on there.  Everything I've ordered from here has been really good.  We did have an issue one time we went where the broccoli (just a side order) was so salty I literally couldn't eat it.  I never send things back but this just wasn't edible.  I'm sure it was some mistake and the waiter apologized and took it right off the bill.  Usually when I go, there's not anyone else in there which is a shame because it really is a good spot!

Given this place multiple chances but it just sucks. The staff is slow and rude. Last night I went and the waiter reached over my plate, rolled his eyes when I asked a question, and then scoffed at his tip. Unreal.

I am in love. Cute, Cozy, awesome fresh salads and pasta, In love with their soft Mozzarella cheese! I cant wait to go back. Lunch was $12 with tax and tip, ni drink included. Come, get two dishes and share ;-) The desserts also looks incredible, so did the Sangria!

I gave an additional star because the General Manager of the restaurant exhibited an impressive amount of concern and attention to the issues I mentioned in my post. His professionalism and customer service warrant an extra star.

Best Gyro Ive had in years! Garlic bread with Mozz cheese pretty good too. Hubby got a greek pizza and as much as he loves spinach, it had too much. Next time he will add some addl veggies or perhaps some chicken. Or he should just try a different one. :o)  They do say that they will 'make a thin crust' upon request.....I think they mean they will make it more Italian style...but we did not try this...Im not a fan of greek pizza but i do like their food. They also have Greek entrees on the menu, like Souvlaki, Pastitsio and Moussaka.  After having such a delish Gyro, i would definitely like  to try the other greek items! We also tried a meatball, it is HUGE and chubby, very soft. Not crazy about the red sauce, but overall, this place is good, just keep in mind, do not expect Neapolitan pizza, this is definitely the breadier Greek Pizza style.  But i HIGHLY recommend the Gyro! It was in a tender warm pita, and was very good. Next time i will try the Chicken one! ps I cannot comment on the Tzatziki sauce, as i do not like cucumbers or yogurt :o)

I thought it was a coffee shop from the window, but it turned out to be Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine! My boyfriend and I connected and are having a great, unique meal! The people are 10/10 friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend that you come here for a nice, unique meal!

I am a lover of Cheesecake and this is, by far, the best cheesecake I have ever had. It is no wonder that they have been in business for 60 years!! They have a wide variety of flavors. Some of my favorites are Salted Caramel, Makers Mark Chocolate Bourbon, Strawberry, Banana, Caramel Pecan, and Dulce De Lache. The Chocolate Moose is to die for, you should try that one too. The prices are very reasonable for such great quality ingredients.

This place lives up to the hype. The food is great and the place runs like a well-oiled machine. I live really close by, so I've tried just about everything on the menu at this point. Burgers, hotdogs, fries, corndogs, shakes and concretes are all amazing. Worth checking out if you're in the mood for some fast food!

Great new bar that has a good, laidback atmosphere and a ton of space so you don't feel crowded by all of the hipsters in their flannel shirts and skinny jeans. Might be hard to find a beer to drink if you're like me and you're partial to the Bud Light or the Heineken, but I understand that's not their scene, so I can deal. Played really good music and I like the colored Christmas lights.  They made it feel very warm and homey for some reason--or maybe that's because it was 4am and I was shitfaced.  Either or.

Have eaten here on several occasions and all of the food is top-notch,. The wait can get long and the bill can get steep. It is Midtown after all though. Highly recommend the wasabi shumai and the hamachi collar.

Ok, I'm from Chicago, so I have certain pre-conceptions about pizza.  However, I came into Lombardi's determined to try their specialty, the margherita.  While I'm not too big on the crust (a bit too chewy and much for me), the pizza itself was very good.  They also have a good number of local brews on tap, essential for a good pizza.  I can't say I'm sold on NY style pizza but I still enjoyed my experience (and meal!) here.

Came here for lunch a few weeks ago with my boyfriend and we were not impressed. The steak sandwich and the frita cubana were just ok. I haven't tried any of the actual meals nor will I. There's definitely other better Cuban spots out there!

I've gotten food from here probably 50 times. Simply the best felafel sandwiches I've ever had. Get the hot sauce in it and the carrots as a side dish. Call in your order or be prepared to snuggle up to everyone else on line inside the place. Also consider where you will eat because it's virtually always too crowded to eat in!

WOW! Colombian food to die for! Delicious food for cheap. For about $8 you get a meat of your choice (pernil, roasted chicken, ropa vieja, beef stew, etc) and 2 sides (rice, beans, plantains, avocado, etc). It is A LOT of food. It gets really crowded as it is a small place but the line moves pretty fast. Don't plan on staying there because it is small and crowded and usually very hot. Closes early around 5pm.

l was going to My Bagel Heaven for years. It looks like they are under new management now. The new management is much to be desired. You walk in there and they are constantly playing a channel from their own country that no one else watches or wants to watch, but them. There's always a language problem w/these people. They don't want to learn English any better than the little they know now. They think they can run a business w/the little English they know and just get by with whatever problems that occurs because of it. I've always gone in there for a taylor ham, egg, & cheese on a seeded rye bagel. There's this one taller man who can never learn what "seeded rye" is. Month after month, he just can't learn. There's a woman who works on the register that always has to pick out the right bagel for him. When you watch him, he just gives this head shrug (duh) and then either asks someone else for what they want or stands around, instead of learning his trade. You'd figure he would have learned after a few months. No! You'd also figure that management would want to know what's going on. No way! He doesn't care. Nobody is minding the store. Last week, I went in and asked for a taylor ham, egg, & cheese on a seeded rye but make it a double. Again, this guy doesn't know what it is. After all the trouble of someone showing him what it is, they they made a single. It was $8.00. It was a single. I asked - "This is a double?" They had to make it over again. Today, I went in there for my usual single taylor ham, egg, & cheese on a seeded rye. This same guy again didn't know what again and held up a 1/2 loaf of toast (looking like an idiot) LOL!. I shook my head - "No, that's not a seeded rye bagel. I need a seeded rye, seeded rye". Well, they messed up and made a double. The price was $7.10. When I asked the girl why this 'double' (which I didn't order) is $7.10 and last weeks double which I ordered was $8.00, then all of a sudden, the cook (who I never spoke to before) came over and called me a F'ing A hole. That's the last thing you do instead of asking the customer what the problem is. I was going to tell the cook what he told me but I kept my cool and asked him why am I being charged a different price for a double, which I didn't order, and last weeks double was $8.00. He didn't know what to say. He gave me $3.00 back. There were no apologies. Another words, to make a mistake is human, to forgive is not my policy! What farm did they pick these clowns off of? What a bunch of low lives! I'll be spreading the word about this place. Hopefully, they will go out of business. You don't treat your customers like crap especially when it's your fault to begin with! Learn English! Watch what goes on in your own business instead of being A hole's yourselves!

Very cool new hangout on Orchard. I Yelped my way to its very lofty review and figured it was worth a visit for a low-key and affordable early supper before hitting up The Slipper Room. It was another snowy Sunday in New York and the place was blissfully quiet at 6 pm, with several tables for 4 available. A single bartender was managing the bar area and the wooden tables. The ambiance is Brooklynish--rustic, low-key, everything screaming LOCAL. Although there were credit card decals on the storefront glass, they were not accepting them that day for some unstated reason--but they did let me start a tab without collateral. No worries, I made an HSBC run while waiting for others to arrive. Here I have to give brownie points to Black Tree for being cool with one person sitting in for a party of 4 when they're not all there, even as the place was starting to fill up. Few others are this open-minded these days. The drink menu is great--they have excellent drafts from some of my favorite beer makers, like Southern Tier. I had a butternut squash beer that toasted me nicely with a single pint's worth. They tend to use relatively local purveyors of food and drink, and this was reflected on the menu as well. The "animal of the week" was duck, which made me very happy indeed. They seemed to be out of several things that we wanted (that's "farm-to-you" in action), so we got a tasty cheese plate before proceeding to sandwiches.The duck banh mi was phenomenal. My gf's veggie sandwich was great, and my friend's lamb burger was also superb. I would leave five stars, but they did screw up a couple of things. My buddy's lamb board was supposed to include both a burger and another lamb dish, but they only brought out the burger, without ever telling him that they were out of the other thing. When the bill came, they charged him full price for it, and when he questioned it, only $2 or $3 were removed. That's a bit stingy, and more than a little odd, considering that they never adjusted his expectations. My happy hour beer was also priced at the regular rate and I had to go up to get the bill adjusted as well. My guess is they had the poor girl behind the bar working too hard once the house was full. Come on, guys, a little help! Hopefully they work out the kinks, or I will just have to get used to the farm-to-table quirks. Otherwise, this is an absolutely adorable place to hang with your friends to grab great suds and delectable sandwiches.
We love Sheri's food. We have been going to her for years and will probably continue to do so for a long long time. The service is excellent and the food has always been to our liking.

Good pizza!  Nice selection of different beverages.  We came for lunch, so there was no wait, which was nice.  We got a 1/2 and 1/2 pizza - sausage on one side and gorgonzola on the other.  Also a birch beer and a creme soda.  Yum.  Service is spotty.  The waitress didn't seem to care - I guess if you are that popular, you are not concerned with the service.  She also gave us incorrect information on pizza sizes - FYI, small is WAY big enough for 2 to share.  Oh well.  It was yummy and fun, despite the service.

i'm in love. i've been to a lot of vietnamese restaurants in this city which most are the same pho, summer rolls, broken rice but this place has a wide variety of stuff and it's very affordable, plus free parking when you can find it!. It's hard to tell the difference between places but I think if you want to try new stuff and have authentic vietnamese food this is the place to go! I'm definitely going back and trying their other vietnamese items. The service is pretty decent for asian places (we're not known for our politeness).

An additional 5 stars to PIZZA Barrio! They have the best pizza in town! I made the wise choice of going here for Restaurant Week, which offered an app, flatbread, and dessert for $15. What a great deal! I had the bacon marmalade with focaccia as my app -- a delicious concoction made with caramelized onions and an assertive (but not overwhelming) bacon flavor that coated your tongue without destroying your palate. The focaccia was lovely and baked fresh (we asked for more and they kindly obliged). I got the pesto pizza -- a generous amount of homemade pesto atop their extraordinary dough (light, yet doughy with great elasticity and crumble...and no burnt bits!) with ripe red tomato slices and perfectly proportioned spots of melted mozzarella. Perfectly seasoned. And the flatbread size was very generous for one person (I had to take half home with me so that I had room for dessert). I'm pretty familiar with Barrio's sweet fare because of the morning bakery, but the raspberry tart I had for dessert was new for me -- zippy raspberries in a lovely custard with a light crust. Yes yes yes. I need Pizza Barrio to be open every day! Please? :)
Big, chaotic and fun.  Had the bluefish at the Pesci restaurant and really enjoyed it

I must have done something to seriously offend the Brunch Gods, because I cannot find a great place in the state of CT for Sunday morning brunch if my life depended on it. I have had Spicy Green Bean bookmarked for awhile now and I honestly couldn't wait to try it out. When we walked in this morning, i kept my hopes high despite the general grunginess of the place. (Seriously though, this place needs a deep cleaning.) The menu looked amazing. I legitimately couldn't decide what to order and I was already planning out my next several weekend visits to get to try everything. I went with the "California Eggs Benedict" which was supposed to be served with tomato, avocado and bacon with hollandaise sauce and a side of their "homies." To start with the good: the home fries were very good, and clearly had been freshly made. I especially liked their use of different potato varieties and addition of green onion. Yes to all these things. My eggs benedict were immediately a disappointment when I cut into them and realized the eggs were hard. When I order eggs benedict, it's because I love the oozy gooey-ness of a runny egg mixed with hollandaise sauce.
