I honestly would have persevered through, but I realized that they were missing the avocado and bacon. 2/3 of the ingredients were missing? After trying to flag down our waitress many times, I was finally able to get her attention and she assured me she would have the kitchen make me a new plate with the proper ingredients. Perfect. I thought, this meal is still salvageable. Well, I certainly did get a plate back a few moments later, but it was the same eggs (still overcooked) with a sh*t ton of hollandaise poured over it to cover up the fact that it was the same plate. I had a few pieces of salty cold bacon and  avocado thrown on top of this hot mess. My husband had the special (Pecan Pleeeeaassee) Which was a pecan waffle served with scrambled eggs, home fries and came with a complimentary milk shake. He said the waffle was very dry and did not feature enough of the titular ingredient: pecans. The scrambled eggs were scrambled eggs. Absolutely nothing special. Now, I will admit that we didn't realize that the milkshake was of the boozy variety, and perhaps we should have read the description more carefully, but I feel like the waitress should have verified that he did, in fact, want kahluha in his milkshake. Needless to say, when he took a hefty sip he was surprised by the ingredient. Along those same lines, I was shocked to see the table of young adults next to us order their meals and be served mimosas. I understand that the omelets come with this complimentary libation, but maybe they should be served a regular OJ.... now i am no teetotaler by any stretch of the imagination, but to me that's just not good business practice. The waitress never carded them, and I mean I don't know 100% that they weren't 21 but I did over hear them talking about SAT scores. Also funny how some tables got served complimentary chocolate chip cookies while others were not. I think it's a very cute idea, but comes off as insincere if you don't have a standard practice for every table. I guess we weren't deemed worthy of these cookies. All in all I am seriously disappointed by our meal this morning. For all the Yelp love I have seen here, I had some high hopes that were dashed. Maybe (MAYBE) we will try this place again because I hate to judge it based on one experience, but I won't go running back any time soon. Sad Face.

We went here a while ago for Brooklyn Restaurant Week and it was fantastic.  We actually live right down the street, and would definitely go back more often if we could afford it.  As some others have noted, it's almost always completely empty, and I'm not even sure how they've stayed open this long.  Even though the food is delicious, the atmosphere is kind of a bummer because you're usually the only one there.  Maybe it's just too expensive for this part of the neighborhood.  But yeah, the food's great.
Great. Loved it.

Dos Segundos was a very good eating experience. I had decided earlier in the day that I needed a margarita and looked on line for a suggestion. When we walked in and I looked around I realized that the place was packed and it was 4:40pm on Friday afternoon. After finding a table close to the bar, our waitress got our drink order, a pitcher of Lime Margarita, which we were told were on the happy hour menu for $15 a pitcher. I can still feel the smile on my face when she said that. The bowl of chips with two types of salsas was a nice touch as they took our drink order. I got the tilapia tacos and my wife got the chicken quesadilla and they were both very good. As we enjoyed our dinner and I ordered a blood orange pitcher of margaritas I knew that this was my type of place. I would suggest getting an early table if you don't want to stand and wait because the place looks like it runs a very good weekend dinner business. We liked it alot.
Delicious authentic Korean food. The service is a bit spotty but my expectation for most low key Asian restaurants in term of service is not very high. Will be back.

I have been a fan of SONG for quite sometime now; I regret not writing a review sooner.  I guess I just never thought they needed my review- that is how great I think this place is.  The decor is simple and functional yet chic and tasteful.  The food is delicious, cheap, and fast.  My wife and I go at least twice a month and the manager/owner(?) always greets us with a smile and a hug.  What more can you ask for?  When we go, we look forward to trying whatever new combination they have on the specials menu.  Oh...  And if you go on the right night- the guy with the rings is the best bartender; definitely opt for a drink while you wait for your table.

3.5 stars. Very nice place with an affable group of individuals running the place. My rating is completely predicated on the Pho! I have yet to try other things on the Menu, but in looking at others Pho was not their most popular dish. Regards to the Pho. Portion size is below average compared to what I usual see and get. Flavor is good and not too salty! The pho was engulfed with fresh meat, cliantro and spices; thus making me a happy consumer. The steak and tripe was done perfectly, meaning not overcooked or undercooked! just perfect medium texture. The sprouts and peppers on the side were very good/Fresh. Therefore, the overall dish was tasty and zestful. The only reason I am taking 1.5 stars away is the portion size to price ratio.Their large size compared to most places is equivalent to the small and priced for the large!!!! I was not full from the meal like usual; hence, a little dissapointed in that factor. Nonetheless, good and fresh pho with a fun environment.

A great view from the terrace over the waterfront and the Statue of Liberty and atmosphere that belongs at a carribbean bar, but the grouchy service is what stood out. For such a huge bar, they only have 5 beers on tap, and half were kicked when I visited. The staff was also super rude with a "what do you want?" at the bar. The hostess also directed us to the wrong area for the party we were attending. They do however, have mini golf in the back and a remain a fantastic place for having a beer outside. We didn't try the food but the seafood looked pretty good.
They have pick up service, BYOB cozy seating.  Wide selection at reasonable prices. Definitely worth second return

My husband and I come here pretty often for our Pai Thai. The decor is cute, and the servers are friendly. A nice local BYOB gem. One tip: ask for their homemade hot sauce, its really good and unique!

Another cozy restaurant on a great street.  Market Table was a small, intimate restaurant with wooden tables and large windows.  People watching, even on rainy days is still fun at this restaurant.  I started out with a nice glass of Sauvignon blanc while I waited for my date and I also had time to peep on to other peoples tables and see what everyone else was ordering. I was told by the manager that these were the best items on the menu: appetizers: - beef carpaccio -  homemade cavatelli   - warm octopus salad We ordered the beef carpaccio and it was absolutely delicious.  It was paired with a lovely green salad and french fries- yum!  The dressing on top was also incredible.  What a lovely dish. Entrees: - crispy pork cutlet - sautéed skate wing - whole grilled bronzino  (whole fish- bone in) I ordered the special which was a Grouper with yummy mushroom risotto.  Wow the grouper was awesome.  Very tender, white fish, and grilled to perfection.  It had a smokey taste to it as well that added to the flavor of the dish.  My boyfriend had the salmon and it looked great as well. Both fish that we ordered were incredible.  The next I am back and I going to have the cavatelli and the branzino- bone in yaya!

I ordered the breakfast pizza with truffles ( not truffle oil, actual truffles ) and I didn't notice that it had prosciutto on it so I asked our waiter " Jimmy " if it was ham and he saw that I wasn't happy. My friend explained to him that I don't eat pork, and he kindly offered to replace it, even though it was not an error from his side. Great customer service! And now that I'm happy I truly enjoyed my delicious and crispy pizza.

Nice ambience, though the place can get a little loud. Sit upstairs if don't want to yell. We took the prix fixe menu. Three different pasta dishes on the same plate. A Bolognese, Ravioli with beets and mushrooms (strange), a white cheese and basil sauce (I think).  All very good. Big portions (too much). Nice wine list. They have two. The economy wine list where all of the wines are $24 and the higher end wine list. Waitstaff was fantastic! Fun spot!

One of the best Japanese curry I have. Simple menu and the portion is big. It is a borderline hole in the wall place hidden at the corner. But their rice is great and chicken cutlets are just crispy and tender. Great midtown lunch spot.

We met our daughters at Heirloom on Sunday morning to celebrate one's birthday with a delicious breakfast. What a great decision! The breakfast choices included something for everyone.....and everyone was impressed! From the chunky stack of blueberry buttermilk pancakes, to the eggs cooked exactly as we ordered, to the healthy choice "Study at Kale" Frittata, the food was exceptional. The wait staff was friendly, attentive and good at their job. We would highly recommend Heirloom for a delicious, home-grown breakfast!!

I love this place, great place to go on a date or even for dinner w/ some girl friends. Nice pasta selection, I got a whole wheat pasta dish which was great. Obviously the wine selection is great as well. Really cool atmosphere, I could see my self spending hours at the bar. Waitress was nice too. I went for a family party, they gave us a room downstairs with a long thanksgiving style table very nice and quiet. Will definitely be back

Every last Friday of the month, Live Band! You have to be here to enjo.y it   Only been for the band once.  Nice mature crowd, great artists, and as always the most gracious host, Junior!  Gotta get back soon, Besos!

Massive sandwiches. A very unique West Philly deli with a lot of character.  Just ordering your food is an experience in itself. I've gotten full off of the free samples before getting my sandwich. Overall very satisfied with this place. One down side is the prices can be a bit steep for sandwiches (around $10), but you definitely get what you pay for in terms of portions.

Went here late Saturday night for some post Bubble Lounge food. Phenomenal fried chicken that was extra crispy, succulent and loaded with flavor. Really impressive - especially for a serving at 2am. The Mac and cheese was also top notch (although one of our companions said Virgil's had better which I need to investigate). The burger was also really good albeit crusted with salt which made it impossible to put down but - damn salty. The fries were ok - kind of cold and a mess but nothing special. I wanted to try the waffle and pie but didn't get a chance so will have to come back for it. The restaurant is southern comfortable - serving drinks and water in mason jars. It took awhile to get our food but I assume that's because it's made fresh - it could be because they are slow but that chicken was so damn good I'll give them the benefit of the doubt. The bathrooms downstairs are a hike but on the way there's Pacman and a photo booth - I used neither but I liked that they were there. I'll be back for pie someday...
First time here and it was pack about 45 min wait time wasn't bad oyster slider wad good n filling atmosphere was fun fresh seafood definitely going back

Walking around, my friends and I randomly stumbled upon this seemingly quaint restaurant.  The country decor is charming, but that's all that's charming.  The food is pretty good, not great.  The bad review is based on one waiter.  That's right, one waiter ruined this place because it set the tone for how gross this place must be to allow their staff to behave so crudely.  The waiter to which I refer was average looking at best.  He must have thought himself divine.  He was wearing shorts above the knee and a shirt that was only buttoned once with his entire and very hairy chest hanging out.  My non discrete friend did a 180 to take a look when I first noticed as she saw my aghast face.  I learned later that he asked her in a snippy tone, Do you need something?  I don't care how obvious she was, he deserved to be laughed at overtly.  I think that he was actually expecting to be celebrated.  When he leaned in to place a candle on our table, his hairy chest was an inch away from my lips.  I like my  lips.  I don't want his hairy chest next to them.  He kept fondling his own chest in between serving tables.  It was appalling. Upon leaving, I said something to another staff member who responded by politely nodding.  However it was obvious that he thought I was a prude.  I'm not.  I just don't appreciate waiters in shorts and a restaurant allowing a waiter to expose his chest.  There was a table next to us, clearly out of town and the male was just staring dumbfounded.  Disgraceful. Perhaps there is a clientele to which this is acceptable, but I don't want to know anyone in that camp.

Their cheesesteak is the real deal!  Part of me doesn't want to review this place out of fear that even more people will discover it.  The hours are a drawback as they aren't open very long.  I've also seen them run out of rolls a couple of times.  I actually watched a guy run over to the Superfresh, buy a roll, and ask them to make him a cheesesteak with his roll.  You know it's good when someone is willing to do that!

Good times can be found at Empanada Mama. It's a cute little place that serves up some interesting cocktails with a huge variety of empanadas. Being from Chile and growing up on these little pockets of heaven, I wouldn't say the Mama serves up authentic empanadas BUT they are pretty good and the price it right. The fried ones weren't greasy nor where they heavy which is usually the case. Open 24 hours, this is a great place to grab a snack, light meal, or soak up all the alcohol you drank after hours. I love these little hole in the walls. Every city should have an Empanada Mama. Life would be a better place.

I have been going to Chickie & Pete's for years.  This is definitely a Go-To Place to watch sporting events if you can't watch the Game in person.  How can you not enjoy the atmosphere where the TV's are everywhere and everyone in the place is ready to have a good time.   Chickie & Pete's is the kind of place you have to take "out of towners" who are sports nuts so they can see how Phildadelphians Love Our Home Teams - it's nothing like seeing the looks you get because of the intensity that is shared by Philly Sports Fans!! Now, the food - of course - you have to have the Crab Fries with melted cheese.  The other selections of seafood, wings and yes the Lobster Cheesesteak are items that keep you coming back to sample other things on the menu.   Without a doubt - on Game Day - it's a FUN Time, and other nights - its a good place with good tasting food.
Great food and service. The place is a little tight but no big deal. Definitely recommend it!

Sat outside under near the heaters on a crisp fall night with some friends.  The concept of Caseus seems pretentious, but it really is just about good, hearty, and delicious food.  After much contemplation I decided on the burger with a duck egg... and bacon (of course!) it was glorious.  The beer selection was adequate, and we all left with our bellies smiling.  I can't wait for another meal at Caseus!  Next time I promise to get the grilled cheese.
Quinoa and raw mexican kale salads are great.  I get the raw mexi with no corn because corn is disgusting. Today there was two corn kernels in my salad which sucked real bad :(((((

Taking a break from our usual haunts, the wife and I journeyed down to the LES in search of cheap eats and found this gem through Yelp. We were seated promptly, and our busy but attentive server got our drinks - a Corona Light for me and a margarita for her. The margarita was freshly made and I immediately regretted not getting one. We then ordered guacamole to start, and I got a steak and fish tacos. She got the taquito platter with a ground beef taco on the side. The guac was amazing - flavorful and thick. The chips, likewise, are quite thick to handle the dip. The wife prefers thinner chips but I like the bite of these slabs. My tacos were nothing short of perfect. The rice and, in particular, the refried beans that accompanied my wife's platter were awesome. She wasn't a big fan of the taquitos - I didn't try them, but they were pretty pale (not deep fried maybe?) and the filling seemed unimpressive - but she did like her taco. The worst thing about this place is that it is SO loud you just want to eat and leave. We would have stayed for another round but we could barely hear each other!

3.5 stars Let me start by saying the DJ and the Food at Fat Buddha are nothing but awesome! My girls and I came here trying to get our drink and food on and were pleasantly surprised by how amazing the food was. Me and my friend ordered the Korean BBQ and my other friend ordered fires and the Dragon wings which were also really good. The Korean BBQ is good enough for me to make a trip back to this place. It is so so so good. The special sauce they put over the rice and marinated beef compliments the dish so well and you can even ask for a little extra free of charge. The DJ was spinning amazing music. A lot of old school hip hop with great beats and a great flow to all of the tracks he played. My pet peeve with this place and the reason why I couldn't give it four or five stars is because as amazing as the food was, you can only get the happy hour deal they have when you sit and eat at the bar. When I got there at 7, the bar was already full and people didn't look like they were moving so there's no way my friends and I (3) were all getting seats next to each other. We had no choice but to sit at a table. We decided not to order any drinks because the fact that we were paying $4 or $5 more for a drink because we were sitting at a table, while people at the bar literally a step away from us were paying less, realllly turned us off. Happy hour should apply to the whole establishment, not those lucky enough to get a seat at the bar :( So we had our meals and enjoyed the good music. The service was also pretty good as our waitress was kind and attentive. I would love to come back here for the food because it really is amazing!

Was there for lunch today.  The Jamaican chicken was good but sauce was unexpected and a little heavy. ( no description of it on menu) Ropa vieja was good and large portion.   Mojitos was good.  Service was ok considering the place was half empty. Will be back to sample more of the menu

Fried clams is the number one thing I order when I dine at a seafood restaurant and the fried clams are not bad . They are crispy and juicy ! Shrimp cocktail : typical shrimp cocktail you would order at any other place . The shrimps were large and fresh . Cocktail sauce was a plus . Clam bake for two :  This dish includes steamed clams, mussels, lobster, kielbasa, corn, potato . This was very mediocre , we expected more from a highly reviewed place like this. Oyster shooter : It was strange and the flavors did not complement well with each other .

"I thought it would be crispier." That's what she said! (It made the hubs laugh.) It's a sort of mixed up pizza. Certainly not thin & crispy, but not spongy, like most American pizza. But also not Neapolitan, as is the style of the day. Whatever it was, however, worked for me. And their red sauce is really spot on. And get that roltolo with the pesto. Buuut. .. ugh, the set up. So awkward. There is no where to wait where you won't feel in the way. You just stand there with your rapidly warming wine or beer. And don't get me started on bottled cocktails. I get the space issue (plus not paying a bartender, which I get but don't condone.) but the selection is never all that good. Combine that with such limited wine selections - stick with beer? I guess, if that's your thing. And I hate communal seating. Especially when there are so many children. I guess I forget that when chefs and their restaurants are spoken of in these exalted tones, that it's still just pizza. Kids like pizza. I think Vetri could have just found a larger space.

I can't believe the hype this place gets,I tried the artichoke slice last night and think it's just awful!! A tasteless mess of glop with a few pieces of artichoke on an almost french bread/Chicago crust slice,just thinking about how disappointing this was it really shocks me that people actually like this. I prefer pizza like Joe's Pizza,if you want thick crust try the sicilian,that's pizza. You couldn't convince me to try Artichoke again even if the slice was free,lol. Don't believe the hype.

Every now and then, I have a little food fantasy about Pomme Frites. Just saying "pomme frites" makes me feel more classy. I tried the War Sauce, Roasted Garlic Mayo, and Mango Chutney Mayo. All were delicious. It's a small little place, but a gentleman kindly made room for me at one of the tables, so I was able to enjoy my paper cone comfortably.

I was stoked to eat here after reading the New York Times review. Super friendly hostess greeted us and promised a 20-25 minute wait that turned out to be 8 minutes. The highlight here is the food. I sampled the moist brisket but ordered pulled pork. Not an overly large portion, but it was enough. Coleslaw was totally unremarkable. Pickled cucumbers did not have the right balance of sweet & sour in the marinade. Side of beans was very good but I had better at the former Rub (RIP). While the food was good, the room is horrible. Given the choice between here and Port Authority Bus Terminal, it would be a tough choice. The place is so loud, if you don't know sign language you will never communicate. The dilemma here is the price - it is cheap!! Maybe a carryout destination. What's nice is having some BBQ destinations. Hill Country - still my fave, but Mighty Quinn is worth a try. Sound deadening earphones are worth considering.

Great food is voyage worthy. Right before I graduated early I guilt tripped my ladies to meet up for pizza (If you have to order a whole delicious pie I need friends as back up so I have an excuse not to eat the whole thing myself...I know I have food issues, it's ok I run!) It was a two and a half hour journey just to get there but it was amazing. No place to eat, no worries we will stoop it outside. Long wait, no worries we have a large mass of friends to take turns. The same guy makes pizzas all day. Tried two different kinds and both were amazing. The quality of the ingredients really shines through to make this pizza special.

My friend took me here for the first time on my birthday. We were disappointed because the restaurant had mistakenly tweeted that it was dollar tacos day, and we hadn't seen the correction posted later. Personally, I think the restaurant should have assumed responsibility for their own mistake and given us the discount, or at least apologized in some way, but the waitress was pretty unapologetic. Oh well. Luckily, the nachos we ordered instead made up for it--loaded with pork, cheese, guacamole, jalapeno peppers, sour cream, these nachos were truly unforgettable. HUGE serving size and bursting with flavor, and could probably be enough for an entree for two people to split. I also ordered the shrimp taco and the al pastor taco. These were delicious but very small and expensive--definitely would be worth it given the dollar taco deal that happens once a week (as notified on Twitter and Facebook). I also got the Fairlane, which was pretty good but a little strong for my taste (read: it didn't taste like Ocean Spray). Fun environment, solid Mexican food, will definitely be back.
music.  food.  service.  price.  atmosphere. make 5 stars.

My date and I both have specific dietary restrictions and we chose this place because "gluten free" pasta was on the menu. Yet, when we asked for dairy, nuts (I'm allergic) on the side the server became clearly annoyed. Instead of coming back and explaining to us politely we were then served with a visit from the manager and personally reprimanded for our requests among them "Bread crumbs on the side- That's not happening!" and this on a gluten free pasta plate! Just rude, inconsiderate, and pushy. The food is good. But after having olives, a salad and pasta I was still starving and went home to heat up leftovers. Rest assured we will not be coming back to this place. I'd rather make great pasta at home and save myself the headache and embarrassment.

I'm a Fatty McFatty and even I can't finish a plate of their awesomeness in one sitting.  Food out your ears.  Everything tastes fresh - you can see the meats cooked / prepared right there - and there is a wealth of sides to choose from to dress up your plate, bowl, pita, or flatbread.  Hummus is smooth and delicious - and in addition to your sides, you get a bunch of freebies you can toss on top / in whatever it is you're gearing to chow down on.  Good luck with that, btw!  You'll need 2 stomachs.  Everything sits great in the tum, and the service is expedient a-la-Chipotle assembly line.  Nom nom nom nom nom.
Delicious food and chill atmosphere. Po' boys were delicious! Will definitely be back when I find myself in Philadelphia again.

after 3 previous attempt to dine at this restaurant we finally got a reservation at a decent time and boy was it delicious! we ordered the tasting which included ginger pork salad, fried chicken, yellow tail carpaccio, baked pork knuckles, and the famous hakata ton ton hot pot. service, price, quality, and ambiance was perfect.  looking forward to return to try more of the menu!!!

I went with a girlfriend during restaurant week . I loved the decor but the venue is very small.  I'm not sure if it was because I ordered off  the prefixed menu but I would say the plates seem tapas style from the portion size. I ordered as an appetizer the braised beef short ribs Chihuahua  and the Crepas de Manzana for dessert. Both were delicious. My entree that was another story, I ordered the Sea Bass with yucca puree topped with pickled slaw. The cut of bass was extremely small, the yucca puree was taste-less and the pickled slaw didn't work well with the sea bass creation at all. I was kind of disappointed that I was still hungry after a "3 course meal" and a cocktail but the staff was very attentive and friendly and I talked to the manager who was wonderful, about maybe frying the yucca or something other than the puree option. I would go back but  I'd order something off the regular menu, maybe the portion sizes would be a little bigger for the price.

I came here last night with great expectations, but left feeling "eh" about the whole experience.  Customer service was seriously lacking, and the main dish had no flavor besides excessive peppercorn.   I tagged along with friends who were loyal customers of the other Han Dynasty locations, including the previous Philly spot before they had moved.   The service was slow, it took around 10 minutes for the waiter to come over and greet us.  When ordering, he explained that there was an upcharge for brown rice, which is normal, but he lost his credibility when he said that this was due to a brown rice shortage in the facility..... really?? After he took our orders he went to a table where his friends were just seated and chatted with them for a while before putting our orders into the kitchen =/  The Dan Dan noodles were great, but that was the height of the whole experience.   I shared the hot pot, which I've had from the NJ location and fell in love with.  This hot pot was much different.  To start, it came out with two handfuls of dried chilis and peppercorns thrown on top.  I scooped these out as I couldn't see how they would add any meaningful flavor to the dish.  From the first bite I couldn't taste any discernable flavor except for dry-flaky peppercorn.  Each spoonful had so many peppercorns in it, it was terrible to bite into them as they ruined the texture and flavor of the dish.  It was spicy, which is fine ...(10) spice is okay by me, I shared another (10) dish with a friend and it was much better in flavor.  The hot pot was just so unlike the same dish from the other location that I was very disappointed.  I explained this to the waiter and asked if I could switch it out for something...anything else.  He took the bowl back to the kitchen and returned some time later saying he wasn't able to do this.  "Each restaurant has it's own chef, who makes things his own way" blah blah blah. Basically, your taste buds are screwed up and how dare you question my taste as a chef.  This was a terrible attempt by a lazy kitchen/waitstaff to help the customer.  I was upset as the dish was not worth the time or money.   Overall, I don't think I will visit this location again.  They seem to be wanting to be more than they are, what with the grandiosity of the interior, but with such slow and unpersonable service, they aren't close to matching it.  Waiting for 10 minutes to be greeted is irksome, at least throw in a free drink/spring roll, or trust the customer when they say that their dish tastes awful.

Perfect date night location! I came here last night with the boyfriend for Philly's Restaurant Week. Let's just say that when I first heard that Rest Week was coming up (maybe some 4 weeks ago) we instantly knew that Fogo would be on our go-to list. Arrived at 7pm and were immediately seated. Love the salad bar and we learned our lesson from the first visit last year to just nimble on some of their refreshing selections. It's always nice to have a plate on the side just to cleanse the palate in between the meat buffet. Impeccable service and kind, attentive servers. Loved the energy, loved the food, loved the service! What else can I say?

I actually like Cuban and love the Cuban sandwich.  Sandwiches are a great excuse to eat pickles and mustard for me.  This has it all!  I know that sounds so queer.  Eh, we all have our things.  But the place is good and reasonably priced for this damn city.

This place was hard to find but made the experience more intriguing.  Even their restrooms were fun.  The food is spectacular, perfect harmony of skill, art, and taste.  I enjoyed the list of sake to choose from.  When I went, the place was packed.  The staff there worked as a team and made the busy night seem calm.  It is a must try and must return when you are in New York.

Really yummy Belgium fries. Now I am boring and just use regular ketchup or the frites sauce--but friends of mine have gone mad with some of their other sauces. Maybe I'll venture out and try some others ...well unless garlic or onion is listed as one of the ingredients--yuck !(some Italian I am)
A cheap delightful meal with an ambiance travelling you into an old Japanese comic book. Meals are under 10 dollars and will you up like your grandmother at a Thanksgiving dinner
Food was good, not great, overpriced for what you get in my opinion.  Fast service and friendly, portions were a really good size.
Really amazing Mediterranean food. I loved the Chicken Shish Kabob. Ask for the green sauce on the side if you like spicy and you won't be sorry.

My company Mti Inc will have our first annual Christmas Party here on the 17th of Dec 2013. I haven't had any time really to check out this new place. But I heard from so much people that it is a great place to have your lunch or dinner here at Church Publick. So as soon as I tasted the food I will make my review but for now it is a great place from the outside and I am really looking forward for my companies Christmas Party here next week. Have a great day.

Why has this place got a few bad reviews is beyond me. I guess the menu isn't everyone's cup of tea but anywhere that serves pig head , pate , terrine and  bone marrow  is going to win my heart . The pigs head is a must ..complete with pitta bread and dressing ...this beauty will feed 2 -4 of you depending how hungry you are . Its rich and decadent , a real treat for pork lovers. The bone marrow was perfect , very juicy and amazing flavor . They have an extensive beer list ..,.its not cheap but then you aren't ordering a bud light so pay the money . All in all this place is a winner ...im definitely going back. 2nd review.  The whole pig and lamb feast. Ok its Nov 25th and we are back, this time with a party or 25 in the rear garden patio compete with heaters and covers... What didnt come out in this pig and lamb feast. Started gently with a nice 3 course charcuterie followed by spicy sausage , blood sausage , pork sausage...oh man this is sausage heaven. Now on to some veggie sides , kale salad and a beet salad accompanied with double fried thick cut fries with dipping sauces....seriously I dont think pommes frites couldn't do better. Just when you think how can there be more they bring out the whole roasted pig and lamb. The pig is cut up into sections for you to choose what ever part your heart desires served with pitta bread and tzatiki sauce. Its too die for. I didnt even make it to the lamb . I probably wont eat again for a week truth be known. Amazing food . Fantastic service banquet style. Perfect for a birthday party celebration.
Fish and Chips are delicious and fresh.

Just awful. They need to update their website and their menu. Website claims free valet parking on Friday and Saturdays and not only is it not free, there's no valet parking at all. We ordered the Scallion Pancake/Braised Beef Short Rib | Marscarpone | Shoestring Sweet Potatoes | Cherry Pepper, for $13 and they brought a plain, rubbery scallion pancake. When we asked where was the short rib and the marscarpone cheese, the waiter said "oh we don't have that any more but it's only $6!" like we should just be happy and not be upset that they didn't update their menu or tell us when we ordered it that it was just a plain scallion pancake. The Peking duck spring rolls had only a few tiny flecks of duck and no promised " shoestring sweet potatoes." We sent both appetizers back, shared one very mediocre "Special" chef's sushi roll, asked for our check and left. Might be OK for just sushi and cocktails but you can get better, more reasonably priced sushi elsewhere. And don't go for dinner! Overpriced, horrible food.

i got it here - probably the best elderflower margarita i've ever had.  yum!!  but don't come here for the service, the lady in charge is seating seriously has issues with communication but the bartenders are super friendly...
I love their espresso drinks, but for $4 for a capaccino, I would like some place to be able to sit down and enjoy it.

I order from here at least once a week. This place is the best place in the neighborhood hands down. Calling and ordering is very quick and easy, unlike many other places who barely understand or hear you when you call them. Delivery is quick and the food is GREAT. My only complaint is that their pricing is a little high for the quantity of food given, but I guess they make up for the pricing with the quality of their food.

Recently enjoyed a later dinner here with a friend.  Server was very attentive.  Food was served quickly and was hot.  Excellent homemade pasta.  I had the spaghetti and my friend had an eggplant pasta special and both were delicious.  Olive oil and balsamic served with the bread were very good.  Bring cash.

Have been meaning to get here for a long time and finally did the other night. Was immediately greeted by a nice, warm atmosphere and the bartender, Lincoln, who did a great job making us comfortable and walking us through the menu. My wife and I both started with beers (yes, at a wine bar, I know) but I couldn't resist trying one of the many, many wines when mine was empty. The service was outstanding the entire time and my only regret was that I wasn't more of a wine connoisseur so I could get even more out of the experience.

We tried Tilt this weekend and first - the fries are amazing.  The service was very friendly, but slow considering it wasn't crowded.  Kids and adults had fun with games and the beer selection is awesome. I'm mostly writing this review to try to convince the owners to change the painting on the women's bathroom - there is an image from mortal combat of an almost dead female character and the words "end her" painted above.  Really poor, poor taste for a women's bathroom.  Stop and think a minute about who your patrons are - women and girls - and how this might look to someone who doesn't play mortal combat or even so, thinks violence against women isn't something cute to paint on a bathroom door.  Please change.  Please.  I'd even accept Ms. Pac Man, as cliche as that is!!

Best Italian food in  FiDi so far. Being new to the area it was just what I was looking for. Love the old-fashioned pizza and the traditional fare as well. Great prices for the area. Can't say enough how much I love this place.
Excellent food and very crowded bar scene.

If this review was for margaritas only, it would be 5 stars. I've been here for both lunch and dinner, only complaint about taste is the hanger steak quesadilla. Very tough steak, minimal flavor. Tuna tacos are wonderful, the spicy burger is great! I can't understand why they only offer the giant table side guac though, and for $15 (WHAT?). Does not make sense to not offer a smaller portion, especially if you have not brought an army who happens to love guacamole. Also I wish you could order different tacos in the trio instead of just 3 of one flavor, but that's just me being nitpicky. Overall this is my favorite spot for afternoon margaritas and I am overall pleased with the food, however I would rather come for lunch than dinner as it gets incredibly noisy.

This place is right next to MilkBoy, and honestly - I had never noticed it before. I came here last Friday night about 8pm with 3 others, and we were able to get a table with just a few minutes wait.  A 4th joined us a bit later, and they were accommodate us easily by moving us to another table. They sell cans of beer (Sapporro, Sly Fox) for $3 which is awesome. We got some edamame for a snack to start, and we each ordered a bowl of ramen (one ordered Gates of Hell - holy spicy!). The one I ordered had a lot of spice in it. The bowl was big and pretty full with a lot of tasty ingredients - pork, egg, corn, sprouts, scallions, etc. Lots of noodles. Clocked in around $11, and I was definitely full. The beers were also nice and cold. I think this place is a winner. I'll come back.

This place is my mecca. Seriously. Any product that makes you wait as long as they do, better be fucking good. The wait is worth it, the product is worth the price, the ambiance sucks, because they aren't selling ambiance. They are selling pizza, and they are fucking good at it. Having lived off pizza for age, eaten it on 3 continents and dozens of countries, including Italy, Di Fara is so far my best and most favorite.
Delicious mac and cheese!!!!

After having been out of the country for nearly a month, you come to miss the basics. Plenty of amazing meals throughout Spain and Greece but when I got back I wanted, satisfying, straight forward and familiar. I wanted a fucking burger. Not just any burger however, it had to be representative of the desire but also take it to heightened levels, especially after the ridiculous levels of eating that we had experienced/put ourselves through, since the beginning of the trip. We were going to Minetta Tavern. Now I'd been to a couple of Keith McNally's other ventures; Pravda (love) and Balthazar (overrated imo) and needed to see what his golden restauranteur's touch was going to yield. Could a Londoner with Chefs from a high end French Joints deliver on the American classics? The resumes were certainly stellar, so we had to check out the hype. Still being on Madrid time, the lunch we had was more like going to dinner except it was at 11.30am. However this gave us the advantage of getting in what I was told and read, were hard seatings to come by. We were immediately sat in a booth by the bar area. Great diner/tavern feel from years past and we were greeted by very friendly host and service staff. After perusing the menu we went with: - 2 Black label burgers - selection of prime dry-aged beef cuts with caramelized onions and pommes frites - Thick cut Bacon - Duck Hash Now you would think that those items are nothing really to rave about but the quality/care put into the products and ultimately the execution, is what makes this place great. I've been to plenty of places that take comfort food and gussie it up but Minetta, definitely does it right. Phenomenally cooked burger. Perhaps one of the best I've had all time. The thickness, the rareness, the beefiness of the essentially roughly chopped prime aged steak. Well textured fries with a great ratio of crisp to starch. Salty, robust duck confit hashed with potatoes and then really thick cut slabs of bacon, not on the burger, but on their own. Holy fuck was it good. To top it off, the service at Minetta was excellent. You don't think of much of the place when you see it at first, but they take care of you very well. Service is affable, comfortable and appropriately timely. You couldn't really ask for much more unless you were going to dole out another two Michelin stars. Minetta is definitely a unique intersection of comfort and haute. I guess that formula has served them well. But unlike Balthazar (sorry Mr McNally), this place delivers on the hype.

Nice little brunch place with a variety of breakfast-type foods, "dessert" foods, and lunch food such as sandwiches and salads.  I ordered Jen's Crespelle and a sweet crepe for dessert...both delicious. the Crespelle was a burrito/crepe shell with eggs and bacon, with a suggested topping of syrup. Not too sweet and made me very satisfied. The Nutty Monkey Crespelle for dessert...well, that was a hit and won't be forgotten - think crepe, bananas, and nutella. Wait staff was consistently on the ball with coffee refills, even with every table filled. There is a small waiting area with about 7-8 seats as you wait for your table or your group to arrive. Only negatives were that it can get a little loud for us quiet-talkers and it is CASH only.  They do provide an ATM, but with the accessibility and use of cards, cash only restaurants can no longer be seen as quaint... Overall, no question I will be back.
I always get the cambodian style noodles. Just one word in this review and that's YUM!!! I never get anything else when I eat in.

I stopped in here on the way up to my sisters lake house. I opted to go with "The Chopper" because it reminded me of something I had in the past and really liked. Although I thought that the steak was pretty tasty it was not very well cooked or tender. If you go to a steakhouse you have to judge them based on their steak and mine was okay. Although I was a little skeptical of the steak fries at first (they are essentially four wedges/quarters of a potato), they turned out to be pretty good and very crispy, which I like. The salad bar was pretty solid as well

A Michelin recommended and award winning restaurant down in the lower east side. Known for their fluffy Maine blueberry pancakes, served morning and night. This place is usually packed with loyal customers, willing to wait an hour plus for these pancakes. Luckily, my date decided that it was smarter to go when they reopened for dinner around six. We didn't need to wait and sat immediately. Unfortunately, the first pancake I ate had a long hair in it. I pulled it out of my mouth and was immediately turned off. Appetite was gone at this point. Disappointment because it was suppose to be an award winning pancake. Boo. Foursquare recommended sugar cured bacon. A fantastic choice! Salty and sweet, bacon at it's best. Eggs Benedict is my go to order for a breakfast meal. It was simply, at most average in taste. Bland because I had to add salt and pepper. I've had better elsewhere. I did like the use of their homemade biscuits. Hot apple cider and homemade biscuits. Cider was a disappointment. They didn't even fill my cup all the way. The foam made it to the brim so I thought there was alot more in there, in actuality, not even half way. Hot was an understatement. It was warm with a huge dash of cinnamon. It tasted like it was poured right out of a store bought jug. The biscuits were good tho. Not too greasy or salty. But definitely soft, flaky, and fluffy. I ate two! Love the intimate size and atmosphere of the place. But it could be a little overrated now that I've been here. I will try the pancakes again, maybe if I'm in the area. Server didn't asked me or the other tables if we needed anything else or how our food was. The water was refilled at proper times throughout the night.

I got the roast pork with wonton dish with hand drawn noodles. It was delicious and only $6.99. The only thing was that some of the roast pork pieces were dry. Also, their dumplings and broccoli are good too. I went on a Monday night around 7:30 and I got my food quickly. Good service.

This place is awesome. Came here for Sunday brunch and only waited about 20 mins. Didn't know a lot about it, but saw on Yelp that they had a pre fix menu and a friend picked it because it was close by. I was pleasantly surprised to see that for $14 you can get coffee, 2 mimosas, and a delicious plate of blueberry cinnamon-pecan french toast (or any other combo)! Seriously? One mimosa alone is usually $8! Everything was great and I will definitely be back. Its right off the subway so even coming from Manhattan would be worth it.

Arrived on a Saturday night to an expected long line running out the door. Long enough that people stop and ask, "what's going on here tonight?" Nothing, we're just trying to order some BBQ. Total wait for me was a little under 30 min. It's counter service, which simplifies the process. Brisket: Excellent. The right amount of tenderness and fat, sliced from a piece that was trimmed sensibly. It's served sauceless, so it really benefits from the sauce they have on the side. The sauce is decently balanced, but *sweet* is dominant. The best thing at Mighty Quinn's, though I wouldn't say "the best". Pulled pork: Very good. The balance of moisture, smoke, and flavor was pretty similar to the brisket, but I would've liked the cut a little fattier. It comes with sauce on top, but it's the right amount. Burnt ends: Mediocre. Had high hopes, but it ended up being dry, stringy, and oversauced. Kind of reminded me of a cheap 'pulled-beef'. Doesn't hold a candle to what I'd consider the gold standard of burnt ends, at The RUB (edit: those were made with rib tips rather than brisket, so maybe it's a poor comparison) . Sweet Potato Casserole with maple & pecans: Mediocre. This sounded GREAT on paper, but it seems like they used quality ingredients that just didn't play well together in practice. The pecan flavor was a little too bold, and it was missing either a bit of fat or sugar (despite the advertised maple syrup). This was nothing compared to the Boston Market sweet potatoes, which despite its humble pedigree, is freakin awesome. But that might be the sweet tooth talking. 3.5 stars. The burnt ends might've been having a bad day. If you didn't like the brisket.. try coming back on another day - there's always some variation. edit: Gonna revise this up to 5 stars. Learned my lesson last time and decided only to order the brisket on my next visit. I can't stop thinking about it. Get it.

Absolutley fab!! best bbq food i have ever had and I will def go back, superb value for money also the food lasted days. Nice seating area and what more could you want in free coffee as well while you wait!!! Great place to eat!
Spaghetti with crab meat is sooooo good. Mussel is also great. The same lady who works there is always super friendly. Great spot in south Philly to sit and just hang out.

Cheap. Wide variety of Korean food. Fast. And in terms of the authenticity of Korean food (which is probably never gonna happen in NYC, purely because the main ingredients are different from those in Korea), I personally think it's way better than those other Korea town restaurants. And because these food are cooked right before placed on the stove (?), I get less concerned about all those food doubts and all.

I walked in here with my friend yesterday for lunch.  I was really overwhelmed when I walked in by all of the lunch crowd in such a tiny space.  We both ordered the cuban sandwich and finally sat down...it was the best cuban sandwhich I have ever had.  I was worried it would be greasy/heavy as some reviewers have said...but I think it was perfect.  I want to go back and try everything on the menu! Definitely a lunch must if you work mid town. And don't even get me started on the cafe con leche.
Best pizza in the area by far. The crust is unique!

Luluc makes me happiest on a quiet weeknight when the candle light is soft and so is the decibel. Please someone stop me if I suggest Sunday brunch here again. Ever. It is so loud. Chances are if I'm sipping a Bloody, I don't want to be screaming to make myself heard across the table. Granted the Bloody was good and didn't have too much schtuff in it-- I hate when I feel like I'm drinking a garden. Chickpea salad is a fulfilling light brunch. Eggs benedict and home fries look like a drool-worthy caloric festival of delight. Waiters are on the hustle and seriously on top of things. Pretty inexpensive brunch but they should offer a Bloody or mimosa brunch special like others in the area. Finally, I know it's the thing in this 'hood, but can you please accept credit/debit cards, please? Don't you know we'll spend more money if you let us? It's pretty funny to watch the one deserter at the end of the meal go on the ATM run though.

I've been here once about two summers ago, and to be completely honest, I was more than disappointed. Why come here for a Philly Cheesesteak when food carts all over Philadelphia offer equally authentic cheesesteak sandwiches? The magic cheese whiz was a little unappetizing, but people don't come here for the food, but more for the "been-there, done-that experience." To my disappointment, the cashier shouted at me for seemingly to have taken my time to order, and corrected me for incorrectly calling the fries "French Fries" instead of "American Fries." Sorry but not sorry, I didn't have the time to finish reading the menu before I was yelled at. I think being Asian-American here made the situation worse (based on the way I was treated by the cashier), and the Italian Market up the street past 6pm made me feel out of place and uncomfortable. To be fair, that was one of my first experiences anywhere outside of UCity. I heart Pat's across the street is nicer, but I haven't been there personally. Aside from the bad treatment, I'm just glad I've made a trip down there, and whenever asked the "Pat's or Geno's" question, I always gladly pick Pat's even though I haven't been. At least I don't think I'll be yelled at my the cashier there.

Quick, cheap lunch done right! Tina's is delicious, with tons of options. I ordered the beef stew, which had huge, flavorful chunks of beef and potatoes, served on a large bed of rice. Be aware, some of the meats are not really seasoned, Cuban leans toward the bland side compared to Mexican. My only real gripe is the tostones, they were a little off on texture. Go for the sweet plantains instead.

This review is for the Lavazza cafe. Please get it together Eataly!  You are surrounded by office buildings and while tourists can afford to be patient, working adults are trying to get to work! Please consider revamping the ordering process at this cafe in order to provide efficient and quick service to your patrons.  It should not take 20+ minutes to get a coffee, especially in Manhattan.  The espresso drinks are very good--hence the second star.
My family just stopped here on our way up to Boston. The pizza, salads, and pasta dishes were unbelievable. Not only that, but the staff was incredibly friendly. Eat here!!

I recently traveled to Philly to explore the historic sites and had the opportunity to sample cheese steak sandwiches at a couple of establishments. At Sonny's, I ordered a cheese steak with cheese whiz and onions.  Full flavored, doughy rolls, and clean, crisp onions.  Not at all greasy, and the meat tasted like beef.  Yummy beef.  It was the clear winner in my taste-test.  I will be returning with my folks and we will continue the exploration. Why not four stars?  The two vegetarians in our group were disappointed that there were no all-veggie options.

After a long day of sightseeing and braving the cold and frigid Winter of 2014, there's nothing like a nice bowl of pho to warm up the soul. This place was closer to a 3.5 stars. The pho was fairly priced and quality was good enough that I would come back. What made me lean towards a 4 were the fresh sides of lime, sprouts and ample herbs, including sawtooth herb in the middle of winter.

Had a wonderful dinner at Vesta last night!  The food was amazing, the atmosphere was perfect and the service was top notch   Our server, Evan, made the whole night worth it.  He was so attentive.  He suggested the mushroom bianca pizza and he was right - it was amazing with a little flirt of truffle oil drizzled all over the top.  The calamari was good - not mind blowing but definitely fine. We will definitely be back and are happy to find a nice little cozy Italian place in Rutherford.  The price was a tad higher than we wanted, but we ordered wine, app, entree and dessert so it is hard to come away cheap!!
One of the best in New Jersey. Great Food ,We go there a few times a year for special occations Love the Chef's Specials and Fresh Vegetables

The food was nicely prepared but the service was HORRIBLE.. A red headed waitress that served us was named Mari. Mari was a terrible server that hardly ever came by to service the table. Her fake personality was transparent. I must add that she was very clever and started to finally pour us some water when the bill arrived.. Obviously trying to prove she was worthy of her tip that she.. added to the bill herself without permission. (Afraid that we wouldn't tip her because of her low caliber of service) I'm so disappointed to see a lack of professionalism. Whoever hired this waitress should give a second thought because one negative experience was enough for me not to ever go back. Tackling a hefty 20 percent tip was very unprofessional. And we only had 3 people. Simply Unbelievable. This was a review dated back from September 2010 that was never posted.

What a sensory treat to my tastebuds this was! Stuck in New York because of the Uk weather, a friend invited me over to Williamsburg for breakfast. The five leaves was perfect. The lovely Ozzy manager, squeezing us into a packed cafe after only 5 mins of waiting.... a lovely large cup of really great tasting coffee and a plate of 'big breakie' that was as tantilising and titilating as can be! The 'big breakie' consists of two perfectly cooked hash browns, wonderful thick bacon .. not overcooked like most places in the US, deliciously runny poached eggs, the biggest doorstep brown toast I have ever seen and yummy mushrooms. Really a delight and I will definitely be coming again when im next in town

Well if there is 0 or negative stars then this place deserves it badly:-) The wait staff has absolutely no smile on their face. The food is 1 or 2 stars but the big issue is cleanliness. If  North Brunswick food inspector is doing his/her job properly this place would be closed down yesterday! Let me tell you However, the hostess was the grumpiest I have ever seen. She had no smile and never spoke a word with any one. She took a piece of b'day cake and eating it hiding it . { I don't mind she taking the cake but not sure why she was hiding the cake as she ate it}. Time to eat food ..each EVERY plate was so unclean,  had so much left over food layers from previous 10 different parties that I decide to pass the dinner. So next I said let me eat some milk sweets..The sweets served tasted made with slimy sweet milk. Clear sign that sweets  has been sitting in the fridge for 10 or more days. My family member who ate the food had major stomach ache. More over I also saw the manger was looking at his watch since the time party started...he was trying to shut the party down as soon as he could. So don't go there if you really want to enjoy your party. N. Brunswick food inspector or some police officer if you are reading : Pls shut down this place and save some lives please, before some one gets seriously food poisoned again!!!

i actually love dmitri's but could not give it 5 stars because the service is not that great. however, the food is to die for. we always get the greek salad, mussels, and for entree my favorite is the soft shell crab. the waitresses are nice but because it can get so hectic, it sometimes takes awhile for them to come to your table and they can be forgetful or slow at times. this place does not take reservations so either come early (before 6pm!) or be prepared to wait at the bar across the street for at least 20 minutes. p.s. the table by the bathroom sucks so avoid that table if you can!

Julie So I've been here a couple of times for dinner and it's always packed and the food is decent with lots of variety.  Drinks are pretty steep on prices but ur paying for atmosphere.   I came here to avoid the lines at all the little quaint brunch spots around town that serves awesome french toast but makes you wait on line over an hour like Sam's Morning Glory.....   And just as i thought, the Continental was empty for Brunch.  And it was a great experience.     I went with the Tofu skillet.  It's soft tofu in a light curry sauce mixed with zucchini and some other veggies.  Small slices of pita surrounds the bowl and the portions are big enough for a large dude.  I thought it was just delicious and exactly what i was looking for.  Ordered some Turkey sausage on the side but will pass on those in the future.  The sausage skin became chewy in my mouth and the taste was awkward and dry. My mate had the Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon.  Very good and no fishy taste to the salmon.  Sides of potatoes were a good compliment.   The service was great and the coffee cups were always topped.  It was such a pleasant surprise and I would definitely consider coming back to try other offerings on the menu.

My boyfriend and I went here last week to celebrate a late Valentine's Day/our 2 year anniversary and we were not disappointed!! We had an 8pm reservation and were seated with drinks by 8:07...not to mention that our food arrived by 8:15--despite that the place was packed!! Even though the food arrived quickly, it was still delicious! It is loud (though I was forewarned from other reviews!) so this is not a place for quiet, romantic dinners. Great food, nice wine list!

The stars are for the lovely space, drinks and music.  Food needs to be improved if they expect return dining customers in our foodie neighborhood.  Seafood seems to be an especially weak point for them.

Undoubtably the yummiest Thai food in New Jersey! I caught wind of this place when talking to a friend about restaurants etc. and when we got on the topic of best Thai food around he mentioned topaz in Belleville, I was rather skeptical, it seems everyone has there favorite when it comes to Thai. But in the end a few months later I gave it a go when in the area and HOLY SHIT! I was blown away... First time around I ordered the massaman chicken curry and spilt there "local favorite" Thai tacos for an app... Oh my sweet baby Jesus I could prolly eat 20 of them little tasty bastards!!! Just recently I tried there other local fav, crispy volcano chicken. I about creamed my  jeans! highly highly recommend! Very laid back atmosphere, attentive staff and incredible flavors at unbeatable prices! You can't go wrong and I'm geeked to try the entire menu :)
Sit in the garden if you can manage to wait for a beautiful outside seat.  We shared a bottle of wine while we waiting for a table to become available. you will not be dissapointed!

Cute and busy little joint!  I thought it would be really stuffy in there because of the size and how many people were crammed in there, but it was not at all.  The AC was fully going and we didn't smell like the food when we left.  Looked like mostly locals and no tourists.  The prices were incredibly good (around $5 per soup)!  We got beef brisket soup and tendon soup and a starter.  I was a little disappointed by the skinny hand drawn noodles...I prefer mine ticker so I can have that chewy feeling.  These were almost more like spaghetti.  Also, the beef was not tender and kind of fatty.  On the positive- the broth was super flavorful...I wonder how they do that.  I would come back again!   Also...cash only

We randomly stumbled into Porteno while heading elsewhere, needing dinner on the way. What a happy accident! We peered inside and saw a busy little restaurant, with candle lit tables and a busy bar. Despite walking in, they were able to accommodate us; so long as we were finished by the time a booking they had arrived, which was plenty of time for us. Our waitress was friendly and attentive, without being overbearing. It was pretty tough to decide what to choose from the menu, everything sounded great, and on arrival, it was. I asked one of the girls I was dining with how her meal was, she just looked at me and said, "I'm not talking, am I?" I went with the chicken dish, and it was probably some of the best chicken I've eaten. The mains weren't huge (don't get me wrong, they weren't small either, just not large enough to feed an entire family), which meant for the first time we had room for dessert. So very good. I had the chocolate mousse cake, which is essentially chocolate mousse in a hard chocolate shell, and my friend had the creme brûlée. Both was delicious. If I make it back to NYC, i'll be heading back here.

I loved the Elotes the most. The other entrees were delicious too. This is not a place to go to for ambiance or a romantic dinner. And its way too cramped. Ambiance means a lot to me, if I just want good food, then there are plenty of hole in the wall places. But all in all, I did enjoy the dinner overall, not a bad experience.

LOVED Skappo. during my visit in Connecticut last week, my friend and I were looking for somewhere to go out for dinner. Originally, we planned to go for seafood but when we couldn't decide where to go, I hopped on my trusty YELP! (; and began the search for a restaurant with great reviews. While searching, I came across Skappo and remembered that during my Yelping at home before my trip, Skappo was one of the few restaurants I had in mind that I wanted to try. So, Skappo it was. I was surprised to see the restaurant rather empty, but then again it was pretty late in the evening and it seemed like the entire area of New Haven was empty itself. We were seated at a small two person table, and there was one other table with customers in the restaurant. First off, the family that owns the restaurant is great - Yvette was our server, and her mother Anna, who cooked our food from what we understood, was amazing. She came out of the kitchen to greet us and speak to us. She was absolutely so sweet, complimented us, and welcomed us into her restaurant. As for the food, I loved every dish we tried. Being completely unfamiliar with this type of Italian food, I felt very annoying asking Yvette to literally explain each dish that I was interested in to us. The dishes I were debating between were all very different, and I really appreciate that she spent the time explaining the components, tastes, and textures of each dish. It really allowed for me to choose exactly what I wanted. Another thing I liked was that they use very homey, mismatching plates for all the dishes. The plates were all very cute, and since they all didn't uniformly match, it felt like you were dining in someone's home eating a home cooked meal. We ordered the: - Salsa Tartufata con Mozzarella Fresca: sigh... i LOVED this crostini dish. I was a little hesitant to try since I love mushrooms, yet hate certain textures of mushrooms at the same time (portabello). Yvette assured me that this dish came with more of a pasty texture and small mushrooms. I absolutely loved this dish. The mozzarella was fresh and delicious, the black truffle and mushroom spread was so tasty. - Pasta del Giorno: the pasta of the day when we ate at Skappo consisted of an irregular shaped pasta, red sauce with peppers and eggplant. I'm usually not a big fan of red sauce, but this red sauce was good. What made me absolutely love this dish was the texture of the pasta. The pasta was so soft, but not soggy... Melt in your mouth texture. Not sure what it was about it, but the texture was just perfect. I don't think I've ever had pasta quite like it. - Tilapia del Giorno: the tilapia was also very tasty. very fresh, soft, and tender. - Polpette di Manzo con Spinaci e Salsa di Peperoni Rossi: As for this dish, I didn't try it since I don't eat beef, but my friend enjoyed it a lot. Oh yes, and I had a glass of the Syrah/Sangiovese wine that went perfectly with my meal. I had a great experience and Skappo and would recommend it to anyone who likes Italian. For me, this was definitely a newer and different experience - the menu is very different from the Italian restaurants we get out here on the West Coast. Too bad the Skappo Merkato was closed after our meal. I wanted to buy items to bring home and hopefully semi re-create my Skappo experience. Next time!

A great pizza is the sum of its parts, its ingredients. The thing that stands out for me is that as well as this, the integrity and taste of each component of a Lucali pizza is fabulous. Quite simply: I have not eaten a better pizza. I also love the BYO aspect and ambience. I even like that on a freezing, snowy Wednesday night we arrived at 6pm opening time and there were already folks waiting (and shivering) at the door. Ahhh ...Lucali sets the bar so high!

His: Almost missed walking by the place. Service was standard. Good was pretty good. Drinks as well. While waiting for my lady, i did enjoy the more than normal interactions of the patrons. Hers: Though I was late, enjoyed myself. Wish the locations of some of the tables weren't in odd places. Food was ok and drinks were rather good. Would come back. Overall: Decor was decent. Food and service were above average. Nothing was overwhelming, but worth coming back to.

I came here with a friend for her birthday and its a tiny yet intimate place. The serving bartender/host was very patient with my friend as she tried different wines. The Lobster Macaroni is amazinggggggggggg I advised you to order that first!. Our meal of classic mussels was served on the extremely soft side, my friend and I didn't like it too much as all but when the new host/bartender/cashier arrived his gorgeous self made the trip perfect. :)

Fri Sat Sunday nicely offers a quintessential Philadelphia restaurant experience but also deviates from what you'd normally expect in a cozy Rittenhouse spot.  With classic dishes and meticulously prepared food, they cater to a fairly diverse audience and simultaneously maintain a neighborhood vibe.   It's intimate, but not in the Audrey Claire/trendy Rittenhouse way.  It's not BYOB, which is somewhat unique for a small place, and the crowd here is slightly older (a la local yuppies).  There are definitely more adults dining here as opposed to 20-somethings. Prices reflect the more mature audience as well (while not overly expensive, it's definitely pricey).   I have had three really solid meals here in the past year.  I got the eggplant entree twice (really really good, very cheesy and flavorful) and the crabcakes also impressed me.  Wine list is quite thorough and the cocktails are delicious!   If you're looking for a nice diversion and want to have a comfortable and reliable meal, this is certainly the place to go.  Just make sure you make a reservation beforehand!

I had just come back from Kansas City and Arthur Bryant's, so when my friend suggested we go for some BBQ, I was worried I'd slam the place with a low rating.  Thankfully, Uncle Willie's is EXCELLENT.   The place is small, homey, and clean.  The menus of various BBQ joints around the U.S. was a nice added touch, and it was especially cool to see an old menu of Arthur Bryant's, considering I had just been there.  The menu was clearly several years old as the prices were considerably lower than what I saw.  Damn you inflation.   We ordered hot wings with celery sticks, sweet potato fries, burnt ends dinner with mac 'n cheese and cole slaw, and KC style ribs with collard greens.  The wings were crispy, meaty, and flavored just right.  The celery sticks...WOW.  I know this is a BBQ place and people probably don't want to hear me rave about celery sticks, but sometimes it's the little things a restaurant does that make you go, now that's a 5 star restaurant.  The sticks were exceedingly tender... I never knew celery could be so crisp.  Sweet potato fries were excellent as well, and not too oily, which I liked. The burnt ends were extremely flavorful and tender, though one negative note is that it seemed the restaurant had maybe sauteed the burnt ends in some oil after the BBQ process (it was a little greasier than I remember burnt ends to be).  Meat on the ribs was falling off the bone.  The cole slaw as Lizzie T. mentions, is fabulous.  I never knew what cole slaw was supposed to taste like until I tried it without the mayonnaise.  I don't know how I go back to the crappy mayo version now.  I thought, unlike other reviewers, that the mac 'n cheese was a miss.  I thought it was too heavy, and it dropped like a brick in my stomach. Ultimately, Arthur Bryant's being the original BBQ restaurant that it is, was a notch better...but this is West Haven folks!  Uncle Willie's is downright AWESOME.  Once I buy some of Arthur Bryant's sauce from the internet, Uncle Willie's just saved me a plane ticket to Kansas City.

I love the set up, the conveyer-belt with the color/price-coded plates of food, the way all the orders etc go through apple technology (iphones or ipods to put orders into the kitchen) and the airline-esque buttons at the table to help you get the attention you need in such a crowded place. I think they have the BEST make your own roll going (as a vegan you can order a HUGE (2.5 diameter by almost a foot long) roll for under 10 bucks - you're not paying for add ons like fish or crab or cream cheese) and it tastes like awesome. the sushi bar is more than willing not only to tell you what something is but give you a small sample so you can decide if you want it in your roll. We watched the opening ceremonies on the big screens. For the low number of tables i've never waited more than 10 minutes even with a party of 6. only thing missing? I liked the old menu better. But I'll agree that the new one is more sophisticated. Do ask how large the dish is before you order - some are cereal bowl sized and others are serving dish sized and around the same price.

I am from VT, but currently live in San Diego.  This is my new favorite place in Burlington!  We had drinks with a group of people near the fireplace.  The atmosphere was amazing and the DJ was great to listen to.  I am missing VT and Juniper already!

I frequent Moto but I figured it was time to write a review! And a little update for yelp, Moto finally takes credit cards! This place is my go to neighborhood spot. They consistently have amazing food, a wonderful ambience, and great service. Sometimes the live music gets a little too loud and intense, but I suppose that's all part of it. The other great thing about Moto is that it is quality food for the right price. Servings are medium-sized and the food looks and tastes great. Their wine and beer selections are also reasonably priced, and they offer a wide variety. This place is great morning, afternoon, or late night. A little hard to seat a lot of people at once, but they do the best they can. I like it most when I'm just with one other person or a small group. enjoy!

The food wasn't horrible, but, as other reviewers have pointed out, the service is quite bad. The waitress seemed downright angry with us for not being prepared to order immediately upon arriving, and was not pleased when we asked for separate bills. If it wasn't for the horrible service, this would be a decent Thai restaurant. But, as it is, I won't be coming here again.

Good prices. Veggie burger with chipotle sauce is amazing! The seitan special was really salty- which was unpleasant so ask for no salt! The sweet potato fries are amazing- I didn't really like the table service tonight- I miss the old fashioned way order at the register and then they bring you food- but I guess that way you didn't have to tip so they now make more money

All all around a great place to be.  Great ambiance, stellar quiche, and pleasant staff.  Cheese platter was perfect and the prices pretty.  Good for a date, girls night out if you're in the area or just want some wine. Oh yeah, scallops? do it.

Bring home the bacon!!!!!!! No really, you'll want to. This is by far the number one reason why I am giving these guys an extra star. This was THE BEST bacon I have ever tasted in all of my years of dining out in NY. You should not come here without ordering a side if you are a bacon lover. The title doesn't lie you may want to order an extra side so you can bring home the bacon. I had the pleasure of having the kale with eggs. A bit on the pricey side if you consider I didn't have cheese and the cost of two eggs and kale. I felt like they could have put more kale on the plate. It just didn't seem that substantial... but it was delicious!! My friend had the grits with some kind of muffin with gravy and their scrambled slow cooked eggs. All of which I tried and all of which were delicious. Had I not ordered the bacon (which was a sizable portion) I would have been starving after only ordering the kale with eggs. Date Rating: 8 Pick up Scale: 3 Strong Suggestion: Leave your name at the front and walk around the neighborhood while you wait.

Four-star food, five-star service.  For example: I ordered a Manhattan neat.  The bartender brought one on the rocks, and our waiter rushed over, grabbed the drink, apologized, and made them make me a fresh one rather than simply straining out the ice.  VERY attentive.

Another Rez Week pitstop. And it was yumtastic. Seriously, go here. Even when it's not Restaurant Week. It's definitely affordable during the other 10 months of the year. Now, be prepared. If it's an eventful night with lots of folks, it's kinda loud in there. The acoustics of the place are more suited for a recording studio than a romantic dinner but it's ok. I came here with one of my besties and we had a table for two which allowed us to work it out and also be entertained by the conversation happening next to us (one girl hated her gf's new boyfriend....they just don't get him, it's a cultural thing. HA). The food was amaaaaaaaazing. The waiter was cute (but probs gay, wah) and the drinks....well I got a funky one because I thought I was being adventurous  (it was the strawberry, pepper thingy.....don't do it.) But because it's Mediterranean, it's all about eating things together, not having defined courses, which was nice. The bread was too good; the MEAT....stop (both the chicken kabob and the lamb, die.). The dessert was aiiiiii but it didn't matter. I will be coming back here again. Eat well, kids.
Only place around here to get delicious authentic Cuban food. Must try the empanadas and ropa vieja!

Crowded but always a good time. I don't think I've ever not gotten a table outdoors when the weather permits. I like that you can share tables with folks without it being weird. Obviously their beer is good - my favorite is the Heiferweissen. But their food is amazing too. One of the best veggie burgers! I wish they had normal ketchup instead of just curry ketchup though. You can also make smores by the fire pit for $1.

I've been a visitor to Philly a few times, and look forward to stopping by Oyster House when I can...consistent knowledgeable and friendly service.  The special cocktails are tasty...love the steamers and lobster roll.  Big chunks of lobster, lightly seasoned, not too much mayo

Start with the fried calamari-to die for and perfect with a squish of fresh lemon juice. Next, any pizza, that's right any of their pies are just wonderful. Good crust-not too thick or thin, nice and crisp, perhaps a couple of charred spots for nice contrasting effect. My boys loved the buffalo chicken pizza with hot sauce and bleu cheese sauce drizzled on top. My daughter adored the vodka chicken pasta. The salads are good, the sandwiches solid, I doubt you can go wrong with any choice. This is the sort of terrific neighborhood spot that any town would be lucky to have. You can stop in and grab a slice or a sub, or sit down and have a nice but casual meal, with waiter service. The pizza kicks the asses of Bunnys and Reservoir down the street.

Istanbul Cafe offers some great Turkish specialties. The imam bayildi, baba ganoush, iskender kebab, and patlican musakka are excellent places to start if you're not as familiar with Turkish cuisine. My primary issues with Istanbul are that the service can be slow when it's crowded and that their lighting is incredibly dim. It almost feels like you're eating in a cave. That said, I'd still recommend the food highly. Even if you don't feel like dining in the restaurant, they're very prompt with takeout orders and the quality/quantity of what they give you is just as good.

Started with a drink at the bar. Female bartender that made our drinks was not friendly and was spaced out. I got the farm martini which was supposed to be garnished with pickled vegetables. It had one small onion with it. That onion was tasty, but don't make out like you're serving some special drink by putting a little "brine" in a standard martini. Who I presume was the head bartender was very friendly, chatted, and tried a liquor with us (Skinos....unusual and pretty tasty). I will note the bar has an excellent selection of liquors and was a very nice place to have a drink.   We had checked in with the hostess prior to going to the bar because it was before our reservation time. As our res time passed, she never came to get us so we had to go ask to be seated.  Despite the restaurant being almost completely empty, we were seated right next to the only other table in the room.  Odd.   Our server was average at best.  When she asked if we had been to the restaurant and pronounced the name differently than we had or anyone we'd heard say the name, my wife commented.  The waitress's response was "It's Latin. There's only one way to pronounce it." with so much attitude it was absurd.
