But I guess it being Princeton you're going to run into a lot of that.   For the food, I got the "Farmhouse Dinner" for $45, which included a salad, short rib, and dessert.  My wife had the nettle pasta and the burrata.  The salad and especially the burrata, which was served on toast with sweet pea puree and asparagus, were both great.  My wife's pasta was very good.  The short rib was delicious, however the portion of the meat and the potato puree was very small for the price.  The dessert, which we split, was the rhubarb-berry slab pie.  It was tiny...this was no slab.  It was mostly pastry and had hardly any insides, though the cream it was served with was tasty. Overall, I would say lots of potential here, but service needs a huge boost...if I'm spending over $200 for dinner and drinks, the service better be good.  And don't serve small, overprice servings of produce that you grow on your own farm.  If anything, that should lower the price because you're not paying others to grow and distribute it.

I wish I had the chance to give this place a glowing review as I have heard the ambience and food are impeccable. However, after making a reservation 3 hrs in advance - we were still not seated nor even acknowledged. Understandably, small spots get busy, so knowing this we called in advance to see if stopping by for dinner was even an option. The lady on the phone said it was busy and that she could definitely seat us at 9pm. That was at 6pm. Ok with waiting and glad we at least had a reservation somewhere, we didnt bother with any other places. Decided to drop by 20 minutes early to chance earlier seating, but it was still packed, which was to be expected. The lady came out when she saw us and said "i thought i told you 9." No problem, understand, we'll come back. After strolling around in the cold- we came back as she instructed. This time, no acknowledgement, and no table. After standing there for 15 minutes- we realized she was taking someone's order. Looks like she gave our table away. Thanks for the heads up. Not like she didnt have my number and she should have at least called if she was afraid she wasn't filling her tables. Food and "ambience" will carry you quite a long way here, but the hallmark to a great business is the whole package, which was definitely lacking. Luckily, this debacle led us to Tanoreen- where though we waited another hour for a table, they called and actually had it ready as promised. Certainly saved the night!

Eats were decent, and reasonable. Wings are not fried, but they are falling off the bone good. We were accused by someone as "decending on the plate like vultures", guilty as charged! Guinness was fresh, great temp, drank it for hours. For the beer geeks, they even had Lagunitas IPA. Staff was efficient and friendly. Music, while not Irish, was a good blend of inoffensive Alt Rock. Think I may have heard Soundgarden while we were there. One pool table, one dart board & a killer Golden Tee golf machine where you get to say hello to everyone while they wait to use the can. Cheers!

I was looking for a French restaurant near my apartment and I found this one. I have to say I wasn't expecting it to be great, but it was better than great, it was amazing. Growing up with a French father, I've grown to love French cuisine and I crave it every now and again. This place not only feels like it's stuck in the middle of Paris (due to the chalk board wine list and old French posters), but the owner is extremely nice too. Not to mention the food was absolutely delicious. I had the chilled tomato soup special to start. It wasn't gazpacho, but it had similar flavors and was delicious. Then I had the grilled salmon with lentil salad and bacon - delicious, I would get it again. My boyfriend had the escargot, which were cooked perfectly (not too chewy, not too crispy) and the steak frites which had a delicious peppercorn sauce. I plan to go again soon to try their brunch.....

Not worth the hype. Meat is moist but flavorless, broccoli rabe just tastes weird on the sandwich, and the provo and bread were nothing special. I know we're a minority but I agree with the few folks here who wondered why this was named the Best Sandwich in the Country.

Been here mostly for brunch. There's something for everyone here. Their French toast is amazing though. Benedict is not bad as well. Lots of space, but there's always a wait. Make sure to use open table!

Pretty darn good.  I couldn't eat more than 2 bites of the artichoke pizza cause of the amount of cheese involved.  It was a tasty, salty, and creamy mess of deliciousness.  But no way could i finish a slice by myself. I preferred the Sicilian.  The tomato sauce was awesome and the fresh basil really rounded out the slice.  I enjoyed the crunchiness.

This place is a historical landmark, one of the few original buildings in NYC.  Fraunces Tavern is an Irish bar serving up Irish bar food in an old building that has been around for hundreds of years.  I definitely enjoyed the historical location and seeing how much of the original structure still remained and think about the people who have been through here.  I had the pot pie here and I must say it was a very good meal.  The service from the kitchen was pretty fast and they have a great selection of beers.  I would definitely mark this place down as a place to try brunch.

I've come here once before, and must say it is a gem hidden near Willowbrook Mall by 46E. Watch out for the driveway, it comes faster than you expect, and one side is a ONE-WAY only. In short, the garlic knots are big and awesome, try the cracker pie, which is the thinnest crust pizza you will ever have, not short on taste. We also had the stuffed mushrooms, which were tasty too. Warm and friendly inside. I love their tagline: You're only a stranger once.

Yesterday, Valentines Day 2013, i took my wife to have lunch at Max Downtown. We had a similar lunch last year and it was a nice experience but yesterday was a nightmare...no one greeted us at the door, out server , Maureen, took forever to greet our table and then took her sweet time doing anything we asked her for. Need a wine list?  Wait 10 minutes... Need to order wine?  We had to wait 15 minutes for her to bring 2 glasses of wine to our table...Want your empty plates cleared?  Wait 15 minutes then flag down a server assistant to do it for her...no special Valentines menu was offered, unless you consider a pot pie a Valentines Day specialty  Overall it was a horrendous experience and one we won't be experiencing next year or any other time for that matter!  oh yes...one last thing...they also overcharged me (albeit $1.00) for my entree but that's a conversation for me and the corporate office...You've been warned!!!

Despite some pretty constant changes in management and wine list, this place never disappoints.  The food has remained consistent across three or four managers in the last year, and even as the wine list and availability is changing, there is always something new and interesting to taste.  Ian the bartender is one of the best things about the Upper West Side, and it is a great treat to be able to occasionally watch some major sports event without having to stand in a crowded bar drinking beer. (love my beer and college football, but sometimes it's just not what you're in the mood for, ya know?)  My husband and I particularly love the "salad pizza" or Vegetarian flatbread if you want to get technical, and the option to add perfectly cooked flank steak to most options is great!
Definitely a good option for solid Vietnamese. Standard Vietnamese fare. A lot of the usual. Good service, good atmosphere. Awesome smoothies, too! We will return. Ask for Phil. Phil is the man.

Love the chocolate here. It seems if you love this place, you dislike Verde, and vice versa. I like creamy milk chocolate items and max has that it all shapes and sizes. Been here 10 times and have no complaints. It is pricey, but well worth it. Even the non chocolate drinks are awesome, Mint lemonade concoction is just awesome.  Love this place.

The service here was the worst I have ever experienced than any other place I have ever been.  The hostess had such a rude attitude towards us and did not accommodate  when asked to be seated from the bar to the table.  She was so discourteous and talked back to me without any reason.  Because of her behavior, I had asked for a manager, she lied claiming it was herself and gave us more attitude. I would never go back there again nor recommend any of my NYC friends to.
Overall, the food is fairly decent.  Try the hot yogurt soup - its really good. The lamb and chicken dishes are fairly good too. I loved their hummus, yogurt and bread combo.

Stayed at the Refinery Hotel (upstairs from the restaurant) for about a week.  I travel a lot and don't usually like to go too far from the hotel for dinner and drinks as I usually have to be at the client office early each morning.  In most cases, the "restaurant downstairs" sucks, which makes my trips worse.   This one could not be further from what I've come to expect.  I love Parker and Quinn, it is cool as hell.  The decor and everything is done really well and not over the top.  It's not too small, not too big, just right.  The food is great, staying there all week I tried pretty much everything and it was all really good.  Invited one of my friends (local TV producer) to breakfast one morning and he also commented on it.  Invited my clients there for a celebratory dinner, said it was one of the best steaks they've had. I've been having a hard time writing this review because I was trying to come up with a way to convey how cool the staff are, and I guess that's the best way to sum it up.  For those of you that are as cynical as I am about customer service, take my word for it.  These are some of the best people you will ever meet.  Jimmy, Zach, Tessa, and everyone else at PandQ, you guys are awesome, can't wait to come back.

Came here once and can't wait to go back to try more :). Me and my friends came here and tried the [1] avocado salad, [2] chicken momo(pan-fried dumpling), and [3] Phingsha (a noodle dish). This place was quite small, could seat probably around 15-20 people. It isn't very well lit but they get some natural lighting from outside. The avocado salad is mixed with spicy seasoned potatoes which gave it a nice little kick. I usually don't like avocado dishes but this one passed and i would order it again, especially since it was only $4.50 and was quite filling. The Chicken momo was super good, one of the better pan-fried dumplings i've had. it's plump and flavorful from the moist chicken mixed with the herbs. This dish also came with a slaw on the side, which was great when eaten with the dumpling which gave it another crunchy element to the dumplings. crunch with the slaw and crunch from the pan-fried dumpling skin = win. The Phingsha, a noodle dish sauteed with beef/chicken (we choose beef) and veges, came with a nice warm piece of bread, similar to na'an. This dish wasn't my favorite, it reminded me of eating Jap Chae at a Korean restaurant but the flavors were all there and my friends enjoyed it. I can't wait to go back and order from their "recommended item" menu. Which i didn't see until after we ordered our food. It is right above the cashier, on the wall, so look up if your are having a hard time deciding what you want to eat.
The service was not friendly, and my pizzas were average. This place is fine if you're just looking for a bite, but don't choose it for a special night out.
Best Reuben in town hands down!  Pastrami is fantastic as well.  This is not just a tourist spot this is the real deal!  I eat there way too often to be honest!

I don't think this place needs any more reviews. Let's just keep it a secret... My visit to NYC a few weeks ago meant a much needed trip to ippudo. Luckily, this location just opened up not too long ago and we didn't have trouble getting a table during lunch time...although there were some complications in the kitchen that day, leading us to what seemed like a 2 hour lunch. Anyhow, I couldn't imagine how this place could have such good ramen. If you've had ramen in Japan and crave a hearty, well cooked ramen with perfect noodles...this is it. Both the spicy broth and bold miso broth were great. I could eat this every week, maybe even every day? Appetizers were good as well. The simple cucumber with sesame oil and furikake seasoning and shishito with yuzu salt, yum! Restaurant is very clean, new, and authentic looking Japanese entrance. I really wish they had one in San Francisco. Will definitely come back for their delicious ramen!

I've been to Memphis Taproom 3 times, so far. I think the food is great, the service is great (knowledgable staff), and the atmosphere rocks! I love visiting bars and restaurants where everyone seems to be in a great mood. Though it's loud, we'll say boisterous, it's welcoming and lively! The food is consistently great. I try something new each time. I remember the first time, I had the pork sandwich, expecting pork bbq, and it wasn't with bbq, but it was still delicious, and hot! I had the chicken fingers dinner with mac and cheese the second time - equally scrumptious. Then, yesterday, I was there for the no-repeat week (beers on tap). I had the Mams's Little Yellow Pill, I think. Very smooth, yet tasty, light-hearted beer. Started with the cheddar soup with a cider touch, and I haven't had soup that great this entire winter season! I fell in love with the battered dill pickles dipped in Horseradish sauce. Loved. Them. My brisket burger was not too big, as some gastropubs seem to do to me (I am small!!), but not too small, either. Just right. I almost cleaned my plate. Go here.

The thousand layer bread (I only saw one layer!) with curry dipping sauce was tasty.  The Asian tea leaf salad was unique and very good.  The Jungle sauce (we got tofu) was disappointing to me.  Not enough spice or flavor to the curry.  I tried my friend's mango chicken which I thought was more flavorful but is sort of like a sweet & sour sauce as another Yelper here pointed out.  It's not too expensive, but not too cheap.  No complimentary tea, etc.  (You can gets cups of "Burmese" green or Jasmine tea for $1.00.)  Beers are something like $4.50 with the standard, not-so-great Asian imports...  A bit expensive I think?  Service was excellent, fast and friendly.  But I would not necessarily go out of my way to come back.

My girlfriend and I literally sprinted over here on a hot Thursday evening in July, after we finished dinner at Fishtail by David Burke. Worried the entire time that we weren't going to make it, the fact that my gf was half a block behind didn't phase me. We finally made it, just under the 7pm wire. As you approach the store on the street, its elegance immediately stands jumps out at you. Walking in, we were immediately greeted with, "Bonjour!" -- good thing I took all those years of French in high school in college, as I was able to engage in a small "what's up" kind of dialogue with the employee who greeted us. Being that it was basically closing time, the line was short. I then heard two discussions take place. The first was "It's 7pm, why did you greet him with 'bonjour' and not 'bonsoir'?" The second was, "It's 7pm, I thought the door had been locked already?" Anyways, there was no snotty French service here. Despite it being closing time the staff was friendly, attentive and polite. They answered any questions about their different flavors of macaroons and we ended up choosing six, tho I can't remember what they all were - Green Apple, Pistachio, Salted Caramel... that's all that I can remember for now, but at $2.70 per macaroon, all the flavors were outstanding, as they should be, since they're flown in from Paris each day. These were like no other macaroons I've ever had before. A picture of Laudrée's macaroons should be next to the word "delicate" in the dictionary. Bottom line is that I don't know much about macaroons, but these were easily better than what's being served downtown at La Maison Du Macaron. Laudrée's macaroons were also so much better than what was served during dessert at Jean-Georges. Jean-Georges should actually be ashamed of what they're serving and redesign their macaroons after doing some taste testing here at Laudrée. Yelp's 5-star rating speaks the truth - as good as it gets.
Always have a great experience at UVA. One of the best italian restaurants in the UES by far and with a young vibe.
3 entrees, 3appetizers, salad and a carry out appetizer all for $65? Yup. Good was off the hook excellent! Good service too!

Luckily I saw in the news a week earlier that Jimmy Fallon stopped by here for cheesesteaks for some reason, or I probably wouldn't have ventured over here to get one of the best cheesesteaks I've ever had. This is more like John's than it is like Pat's/Geno's/Jim's - it's a tiny little shop that is frequented by way more locals than tourists. There are a few cramped seats at a counter inside, with a few more tables outside. There is gruff, yet somehow friendly service, that moves quickly to handle the crowds. Most importantly, the cheesesteak was really incredible. I got it the way the lady recommended, with American cheese and fried onions, which is also my favorite way (I'm not as into that neon whiz). The sandwich was huge, with a ton of delicious chopped up steak. It wasn't heavily seasoned, but it still tasted great. Whenever I go to a place like this or John's, which are crowded and still have small wait times, I'm baffled at why people wait in lines down the block at Jim's. Sure, the cheesesteaks at those places are good, but they're either as good as or not as good as these tiny local places. Do yourself a favor and skip the insane lines at the obvious places - come here instead for one of the best cheesesteaks in Philly (and therefore, the world).
This place is amazing. The sliced meet is good quality, and a much better value than many of the more famous delis throughout the city. Highly recommended.

So my friend that we were visiting, had this on our "must do's" while we were in town, and who was I to disobey?  This place has a line, and luckily for us, it wasn't too extremely bad this day, and it has a great view right next door, which helps to pass the time. Anyways, it was definitely worth the wait, the food was great!! I was told that this is one of the older pizzerias in town, nice little family owned spot. I am glad we had a chance to visit here, put it on your list when you visit NYC

Oh, Ashbox. I love you. I have been working right around the corner for over a year now and this is my go-to spot for lunch. I love this cafe so much that when I think about moving away, Ashbox comes to mind, and I realize how much I would miss it. I normally get the Tofu salad- it's a mix of greens, homemade tofu (which is super soft!), grape tomatoes, cucumber, kelp, sunflower seeds, and this amazing homemade lemon miso vinaigrette. delicious. Pair this with a Spicy Salmon Mayo Onigiri (rice ball) which is my fave of them all and I've got my perfect lunch. The miso soup with fried tofu is also great. My mom's japanese, I've lived in Japan and know what good miso tastes like and this is pretty comparable. It's perfect for those cold winter days. This place is always nice and toasty as well (a nice escape from my cold office). When I'm feeling like I need something a little heartier, I go for the Turkey or Egg Salad sandwich on ciabatta bread. You can't go wrong. The staff are always very friendly and polite. I've gotten some free drinks and cookies here with my to-go orders before (I think because 1. I'm a regular 2. I tip them every time 3. They love me). It can get a little crowded after noon, but there are usually plenty of seats. If you come after 3 on a weekday you'll dodge the lunch crowd.

I went there twice. The first time I was very impressed with the tapas, the sangria and the music (some Manu Chao, Jarabe de Palo, Julieta Venegas). Very tasty and quick service. The 2nd time, I went with the same enthusiasm but, despite it being a weeknight again, the staff seemed too busy/overwhelmed to even talk to us. The 1st person asked us what we want, we said we want a table, he told us to wait. 5 minutes later we hadn't heard from anyone. I asked another person, she said she'll check to see if there's something and came back 1-2 minutes later saying there's only place at the bar. Not sure why this was, there seemed to be some empty tables (maybe they had an event to prepare for, not sure) but we were hungry and left. I'll definitely go again, but did have a bit of mixed reaction.

I'm not really a "see and be seen" kind of girl. That said, give me a sunny 75-degree afternoon, an outdoor table across from Rittenhouse Square, and a delightful little cheese plate, and I'm game for pretty much anything.  While not personally my aesthetic, Parc is without question attractive: its decor, its food, its people; and while we invested only in a few cocktails and a cheese plate, both were up to snuff.  Our waiter was cheerful and balanced attentiveness with allowing us to linger quite deftly.  However, I'm not sure a cheese plate can truly carry the weight of more than 3 stars, and the cloud of pretension that hangs over the place is 2 stars worth of 'no thank you.'

I really don't like being told that the chef changed how something is made months ago and that I have been eating buttermilk for who knows how long.  That is not cool.  All of the seitan dishes were either removed from the menu or they were changed to include animal junk.  Basically this place has gone from being awesome to just another burrito shop for the vegan community.  Boo!
Outstanding! Had to kill an hour before picking my cousin up at the airport & I couldn't have been more happy. Great beer & the cheese plate was very good.

The BEST pizza downtown.  No doubt about it. Two types of pizza here. Old Fashioned pizza- thicker crust.  VERY delicious.   Regular 10" pie (is reading 10" as fun as it is typing it??)- thinner crispy crust.  Also VERY delicious. If you are a skinny bitch and/or pretending to be, you can order the arugula salad.  It is delicious and so is the dressing.

Second visit. Totally dissatisfied and kinda frustrated. Not pleased with my food...a little expensive for what it was, both times. The onion, veggie dish- $15!!!! Seems crazy...especially cuz it was just bad. I explained my disappointment to our waitress and she said "sorry". Hoping it gets better, but it will be a long time before I return. Sad, because I live 3 blocks away.

I went back to Artichoke.  I think it has really gone downhill.  The margharita slice sucked....small and not very tasty.  All sauce, no cheese.  There used to be at least some cheese....I don't think I will be returning for my once a year stop.   I heard all the hype about this place and it drove me crazy that I never tried it.  I actually went last Wed night, arriving at 9:03.  The line was not too bad---I was at the front within 15 min.  However, I had to wait an extra 10 or so to get a slice of the Sicilian.  I exited at 9:28.  Not too shabby. I wanted to try one of each--the regular, the sicilian and the spinach/artichoke.  I actually took them all to go and put them in my oven at home, since I live in midtown.  Contrary to what people say, these slices reheat perfectly well.  As to my review, I found them all to be good slices.  The spinach artichoke was the most interesting, as it reminded me more of a fancy wedding appetizer than a slice of pizza (perhaps b/c I sliced it into rectangles wherever possible, much like foccaccia appetizers).  I enjoyed the unique flavor, but can't see myself craving it like others on this board.  The regular slice was good, but not the best I've ever had.  The Sicilian also was good, but since that is usually not my thing, I can' t rave too much about it.  Also, I am not the biggest fan of basil, so the strong basil flavor didn't make it better to me. Ultimately, this place is definitely worth trying once, b/c you won't experience flavors like this anywhere else, especially that spinach artichoke taste.  That being said, it is not the be all end all of pizza, which I am beginning to feel does not exist at all.....The line isn't too bad, considering you wait at least 30 min when getting a delivery, and you get to watch them make the pizzas and indulge in the unique ambiance that is this little pizza shop. The price is also a STRONG selling point as it is dirt cheap.  Well worth a trip if you are not from the neighberhood but wouldn't make it a weekly or monthly event...

I love tapas, and I'm glad to add another tapas restaurant in the city to my list of go-to spots! This place has everything but space (minus 1 star for that)...great food, great wine, and great service.

I love the blueberry shake!!! I always just go in here for the shakes and just the shakes. I think the burgers are okay but the fries are delicious. I haven't tried the potato burger yet but it looks delicious.

This was my FAVORITE pizza in NY....and I ate a lot of pizza that week. The line was superrrrr long - all the way to the next door pizza shop which we seriously contemplated going to, considering it was drizzling on and off. However, I'm really glad we didn't - the line ended up taking around 30 min. The pizza was perfectly soft and crispy and flavorful and the service was excellent. The prices are comparable to all the touristy NY pizza spots - about $30/pie. Being from LA, that is kind of a ridiculous amount to pay for a large pizza, but it was totally worth it. AND they have a location here in LA, yay!

I must be missing something. I finally got to the dapper dog during the trenton ave arts fest.  I ended up going with a dog with cabbage slaw.  Their sign didn't list many exotic choices so I went with the thing on the top of the list.  Maybe it was a limited selection due to them being inside the festival? Anyway, the dog itself was good, but I know that I've had better.  The slaw was crunchy and flavorful and I ended up adding mustard to it.  Putting the dog and slaw on a Sarcone's roll was what really made it for me. I know I need to go back and try one of their more exotic choices.  When I get back there, I'll make sure to post a review update.

My wife and I went there specifically because it's a pet friendly restaurant and we were able to bring our french bulldog, Molly, along with us. We ate outside, cafe style, and whole experience was really great! We were greeted nicely, our waiter was fantastic, enthusiastic and friendly. The owner/manager came out and visited with us for quite awhile, shared videos of his own dog and shared a cup of grilled chicken with Molly, which made him her best friend for life. Susan and I both thought our meals (both daily specials) were very good, and that we're looking forward to going back again. Because we were outside, Molly was on the job as the french bulldog ambassador and lots of people stopped by to say hello, admire her and ask us about her. I recommend The Elbow Room highly.
Everything here is amazing, particularly El Pastor

So far this place has the best cheese steaks I've ever stuffed my face with. I don't know what exactly it is that makes their steak and cheese subs so damn good but it's perfection. check this place out, it worth it.

i've eaten here twice the last two times i've been in new york, and i would honestly have to say that this is the best food i've ever had IN MY LIFE. EVER. the first meal was in may 2008 - my fella's birthday dinner. we still talk about the arctic char tartare to this day. the smoked trout was superb and the special that night was ragut that i still dream about and crave completely. i don't remember what wine we had, but i know it was excellent. the staff treated us like royalty - and brought us a cookie plate for my fella's birthday. everything was just perfect! we were just in nyc in august and this time instead of dinner, we had lunch at grammercy tavern. again - SUPERB. PHENOMENAL. AMAZING. PERFECT. i started out with a summer green bean salad that i am also still talking about. how do you make green bean salad worth talking about!?! i don't know, but i think it was the orange vinagrette. it was so good i actually considered ordering another one and just skipping the entree. i didn't. but i wanted to... for my entree i had a fish dish that was also very summery. to be honest, i can't remember what type of fish it was... i think drum, but i'm not sure. it had a delightful dill sauce on it, however that was perfect for a light summer lunch. we keep saying the next  time we go to new york we'' try something new, but i mean, honestly... if ain't broke don't fix it. did i mention this is the THE BEST FOOD I'VE EVER EATEN....

My favorite sushi I've ever had (even BEFORE I was vegan). Great flavor combinations, beautiful presentations! Prepare to amaze your sushi-loving omnivore friends! I don't think anyone would be disappointed with this stuff. The Mighty Mushroom is really the best! But try them all, you won't find a bad flavor. Quick note: it's really counter service only. They have about 10 seats. Don't expect to eat here, just grab n go!

I love Kafana. I am part Serbian so it is nice to have a place in the city where I can eat food from home when I miss it - and Kafana always delivers. I've been here a couple of times and the food is always outstanding and very authentic. Their Mesano Meso (Mixed Meat) platter is great, and can feed two, or even three people comfortably. The Zeljanica and Lepinja sa Kajmakom appetizers are also delicious. I especially recommend getting the Lepinja - the kajmak was the highlight of one of my meals at Kafana and if you are particularly looking to try something very unique and Serbian, kajmak is it. I've also had the Karadjordjeva which is delicious, and very very filling. The only thing I didn't care for is their wine list - none of the wines I had at Kafana stood out. Service is decent, the wait staff is friendly, but not too overwhelming. Sometimes it's hard to flag them down to get the check, but I am willing to overlook that. My dinner companions, who are American, loved Kafana and can't wait to go back. It's a great place for any meat lover or anyone wanting to try something different.
sallys vs pepes...  they are both excellent !!

the gluten free bread was very good and tasty, but it was a little crumbly in my vegan delight sandwich. maybe it was just all the weight of the fillings that made it that way, though. even though i'm not a vegan i was a big fan of the vegetable combinations they used (avacado, hummus, eggplant, tofu, to name a few).

OK, Ok. Let's get this out of the way. It's not very "Astoria", that's for sure, but that doesn't mean it's not something that Astoria needed. I love the Sweet Afton. Friendly and fast service (even if the asking-names-thing felt a bit forced from my server) and delicious cocktails and food. The spicy cherry margarita is not f'ing around. It will burn the crap out of your mouth and make you want more in the same sweet sip. The pickle martini is salty heaven in a glass, with a spicy kick at the end that will make you it's slave. The red lemonade was so good I had 3 when I really only meant to have 1. Get the fried pickles. Don't even think about not getting them. The burger was amazing (got the Irish Cheddar and Bacon) but I felt the bacon was slightly too smoky for my tastes.. then again, it WAS a Sunday and I'd already had a LOT of bacon that day. The macaroni and cheese my boyfriend ordered, however, I couldn't stop eating. Plus the place looks good. The only complaint I had was that it was way too bright where I was sitting in the back.. they must have read my mind on that, though, 'cause the lights were appropriately dimmed. All in all, Sweet Afton is an awesome bar worth your time. So quit whining about the Brooklynization of Astoria and just go get a drink already.

A (pricey) taste of Japan's famed karaoke bars. I first booked a karaoke room at Yakitori boy for a double birthday party for myself and a friend. The staff were friendly and accommodating, particularly when scheduling issues for the room came up. Be sure to call AT LEAST 3-4 days in advance when booking a private karaoke room. The food was absolutely delicious. If you like sushi or tempura, be sure to order some because it's great here. I particularly loved the sweet potato tempura. My only complaints: -the karaoke system in the private room had an outdated song list and was very complicated to operate. -for an average night out, this place can be very pricey. Make all your friends participating aware of the cost of the room. -Keep your eye on the clock; if you go over your time, you're paying for it.

This place is so overrated. There are three Halal Guys carts on the corner. The line was not really long but the workers at the cart on the corner on the same side of the street with the Hilton hotel, were rude. (the cart that does not sell drinks) We got the lamb and rice and chicken and rice. The lamb and rice was better than the chicken and rice, but that is't saying much. Both were dry, overcooked, and flavorless. I do not know if the 5 star reviews are from people who have not had really good halal food but this was mediocre at best. I have had halal food from food trucks in DC that tastes better. One upside was the white sauce which was delish! The red sauce is extremely hot.

I'm obsessed with Mexican food. I've moved on from my burrito phase to empanadas. Two can make a meal and when paired with sangria, it is perfect. My regular order is the Viagara (seafood) but everything else I've tried here is great. it does get busy during peak times but it's open 24-hours so you can stop by whenever you want to get your fix. It's great drunk food and I always see people stumbling in after a night out in HK. Service isn't the best and the place is cramped but the food and price more than make up for it. And whatever that green sauce is, it's da bomb.

I honestly have to hand it to the Epicurean Management, because they seize to amaze me in the number of great restaurants they put out.  My favorites are l'artusi and dell'anima (in no particular order, of course). L'Artusi is named after is named for Pellegrino Artusi, who published a cookbook called The Science of Cookery and the Art of Eating Well; apropos, this place definitely allows you to eat well.  If you want to truly impress your future ex-girlfriend/ex-boyfri end, bring her[him] here.  Sit him[her] at the bar kitchen; enjoy the ambiance, and point out the "cute" stickers and postcards posted around the kitchen top..... and order the following.....fluke ceviche, chicories (the anchovy dressing is actually quite delicious, just bring gum or a breath mint for later), spaghetti, roasted quail, and hanger steak.  I'm actually getting nostalgic writing this. Unfortunately, I did not leave any room for dessert....a great excuse to go back. Enjoy! P.S.  I really hope they put the grilled octopus back on the menu!

I was more than a little disappointed this weekend when I was seated outside and I asked my server if there were any brunch specials. Rather than tell me what they were, she said they are on the chalkboard inside, go in and look. That rubbed me the wrong way. But I'm glad I got up and looked because the fried egg tacos they had on special were great.
For Trivia on Tuesday night, get there at 830 pm and get a table - they fill up fast. Also you can get a 1 Liter beer in October.  Great brunch and $4 bloody mary's - yum!

I don't like Chavela's. At all. Maybe it's because I moved from Texas where I was spoiled by decent Mexican food, but every time I go to Chavela's I leave feeling ripped off. I don't get the positive reviews for this place. Could we please raise our collective standards for what constitutes good Mexican food in NY? Maybe then we'd be graced with something better than Chavela's bland, poorly executed take on the cuisine. I would give specifics, but it was so unmemorable that I'm having trouble recalling. I've tried every taco? They were all unapologetically meh. Chewy tortillas, flavorless filling, you get the idea. One star for the nice staff and one star for the comfy interior. If you're meeting friends here, have a drink, avoid the food.
Pretty good thin crust pizza.  Had the arugula pizza and it was like a giant salad on a pizza.  Pretty good although I thought the sauce was a little sweet.  Good drinks and a good atmosphere though.

This place is splendid, my friend and I was walking around the area looking for somewhere to eat when we notice this lovely little place. We had just come from another bar/restaurant that was over packed due to a party event but for a good cause. Even so, we really just wanted a simple place to hang. The night we were here at "Grape and Grain," a jazzy band played cool relaxing music which went well with the mellow theme. I loved the home like feel to everything about the place, down to the un-matching plates each person received their food in. We went during the winter season, so coming out of the cold weather into a cozy little find like "Grape and Grain" was just what we needed. The food was nice but the wine bottle choice that my friend picked out was too bitter for my taste. It was a great find in a spot that we didn't think would be there! This just shows how grand it can be to explore certain areas of the city. You might find an unexpected treasure such as this location!

Day by Day is usually where I go to lunch/brunch with people when I meet them in the city or go to rittenhouse. This is definitely the best place for brunch in philly! The food is amazing, and i'd say that the french toast is the best i've ever had. it's called day by day because the menu changes somewhat frequently, I love trying the new sauces when they change for the french toast. But i've also tried the huevos, the forentine which has everthing i love: spinach, mushrooms, poached eggs and awesome roasted potatoes. I'm a real dessert guy too, and these guys have good dessert. There's not a dessert menu, you just walk in a see a case of what they've got this week. They've always got cake (I like they're carrot), or a cheesecake. And there's always a gorgeous pie. The waiters are really nice and relaxed, they always know if a soup is vegetarian or not, and tell me what's in something on the specials menu. I'm glad they've got a good rating here because for their prices and casual atmosphere, the food cannot be beat. And lastly, the decor. It's not the best here, i like a nice restaurant design, but it's not essential as long as the food is great and the place isn't dirty. I get really upset when restaurants sink a lot of money into their looks and the food doesn't match up. i don't want to give my rittenhouse secret, but it's always fun to bring one of my friends who hasn't been there before, they become as much of a fan as I am.

A sweet Southern beauty with so much taste and class. The biscuits are divine. The style is so reminiscent of the South. It's quaint and charming. Go. You'll love it and chime to your friends about how cute it is.

The tasting menu was absolutely delectable.  A friend and I split the menu so we were able to have a taste of everything.  One of my favorite dishes was the zucchini flower (dishes are arranged according to what is in season we went a few weeks ago) and duck breast served over noodles.  For dessert we had the molten center chocolate cake and warm banana pecan crisp tart which tasted yummy.  Service was very attentive and friendly but there was a little waiting for each course to make its way to the table.  Went on a Saturday night without a reservation around 8 and was told they were booked for the night.  Luckily my company already had a table.  It is wise to call ahead to make a reservation.  I will be returning!  Be aware the prices are on the high end but it is definitely worth it.

this place is solid. in a neighborhood bereft of decent grab-and-go options, ba'al is a welcome respite. i do think the prices are a little..."soho"-ish.  $5.50 for a sandwich on the small side, but the quality is right on. the falafel is a delight and the pita is fresh and fluffy and full of carby-goodness. if you get a platter option, be wary of some of the sides. they are not all created equal, so choose wisely. (i wish i could remember which ones rocked more than others, but you should be able to tell just by looking at them.) the service is super fast, and they don't bog you down with an unnecessary plastic bag. just a box with a rubber band around it and you're good to go. (just make sure to grab yourself a napkin!)
Boss. Great food, coffee, service, and ambiance. Wish they were open late night though.
This restaurant has a truly romantic atmosphere. Took my girlfriend on a date here and had the time of our lives

I went for brunch and waited more than an hour to get in. The crowd was very non NYC - post college, ex frat types. The food was very unmemorable and I do not know why this place is known for their brunch. I would not go back or recommend.

Went here with my boyfriend for his birthday, the pork belly buns were great and the Ramen was good, a little salty, but nothing to compare to Ippudo. A great spot for after work Ramen, without the long line!!!

Came here for their brunch and we were able to get three small tapas options along with unlimited bloody marys and mimosas for $17.95. Funny thing though is that I passed by here the day after and the price had gone up to $20. My friend and I chose six items to share. The tomato cocotte and breakfast taco were my least favorite. The tomato could have used more seasoning and the taco was super crumbly and dry in texture. The potato pancake was tasty, but it was accompanied by a sweetened creme fraiche, whereas we would have preferred it unsweetened. The duck hash with the poached egg was very tasty though as was the coconut french toast. The favorite of the meal though was the monte cristo. Cheesy, savory and with a hint of sweetness from the bread. I could go for a whole sandwich of this. Yum. The bloody marys and the mimosas were also very good and the brunch was a good deal for everything. Even at $20 it is a good option, but I am glad I got it before the price went up!

At first glance, based on cursory menu-surfing, Cafecito may seem unremarkable.  However, this charming little Cuban eatery is well-worth a visit.  What it lacks in menu novelty is more than made up for in execution.   While you may find a decent Churrasco (complete with chimichurri sauce) at seemingly every Cuban restaurant in New York City, Cafecito's version ($20) is exceptional.  Juicy, flavor-packed, perfectly medium rare and impossibly buttery with an accompaniment of lime cured onions, yellow rice, black beans and tostones.  If, like me, you prefer the sweeter maduros, fret not.  Your professional and accommodating wait staff will be happy to sub the plantains at no extra charge or fuss. Camarones Al Ajillo ($18) were similarly a delicious treat.  Large succulent shrimps with garlic, citrus and butter, served over yellow rice with a side of sweet plantains.  The kind of plate you usually eat on vacation in the Caribbean complete with the happy feeling, minus the pricey airfare! You can't go wrong starting with the tasty mini empanadas ($8, you get three so try one of each!) and mojitos, and finishing with the unique Cuban Bread Pudding with espresso caramel ($5). PARTING THOUGHT: Talk about a great reason to visit Alphabet City!  Extremely delicious food, affordable prices?  I'm in!!!

the wall of apples seemed impressive.  a nice, unusual treat.  the decor is nice. romantic. not overly rich. service was perfect. BUT the food,..eh, i've had better.  maybe it was an off night, but when most go to a place like this, there shouldn't be any off nights.
My favorite dumpling in the city.  And the cheapest.  $2 for 8 steamed veggie dumplings.  What's not to love?

Loved everything about it! Been twice and looking to go back... The pizza gets the buzz (and well worth it) but the apps and entrees are why I've gone back - the pasta is hand crafted, lamb meatballs superb. Cocktails are innovative and D-lish, service is friendly and professional. The feel is casual and comfortable -
Good food, ambiance and a great price.  I haven't had their mac & cheese but after all the rave reviews I just might have to go back and have some.

I really like this place. It is in a trendy area & is very nicely decorated inside. Fairly large space with a fairly small menu, but everything is very good. Portions are a bit small, so order that extra side ;-) There is a great option here to be kind of a wine of the month club member. You are assigned a "mail box" & every month a featured wine will be waiting for you to enjoy with dinner. It is only $50 if I live in the area I would deff join. Great restaurant for large groups or intimate dates.

Went here for a little mid-afternoon breakfast hungover brunch which seems to be a staple in the brooklyn community :P I immediately knew I need some sort of alcoholic drink to set my levels straight and went with the mimosa of the day which was lavender.  It was DELISH and did the trick.   They suggested that we get one of the share dishes from the menu as we did and well I wasn't that happy about it.  Peaches and cheese don't go together no offense. I then ordered the blueberry pancake ----- YUMMM antioxidants and fluffy buttery goodness - need I say more. My friend got the stuff french toast and said it wasn't bad and my other friend ordered the BEC sliders which he also liked.  The food is okay and hit the spot but I wouldn't go off the back end to get here to eat. I think it's also a little pricey for the quality.

I was very impressed with how nice it looks. Great atmosphere, first-rate design. Sat at the bar and had delicious glass of Torrontes for $8, and the salmon sandwich for only $9, and it was off the charts. I think they haven't been open too long, so I'm happy with how good the food and service were for a new place. A great addition to the north slope, and I'm definitely going back!

I used to work here and the fact that I would still eat here says something. I don't like mayonnaise or mustard, so my sauce options are pretty limited, but seriously, try the poutine, you won't regret it.

Came here close to closing time on Friday, & I went in with very low expectations, just in hopes of being surprised. The decor was nothing special to comment on, so onto the food. I ordered a miso ramen, & so did my boyfriend, while my sister ordered the karai (spicy) ramen. I know that this is a self service establishment, so why were some customers getting their names called to grab their food, while others had their noodles delivered to them? If it's a self service establishment, then keep it that way, as to not confuse customers or it will seem as some customers are receiving preferential treatment. The staff at Nom Nom were very accommodating & friendly, & the noodles came out fairly quickly after we had ordered. The broth of the miso ramen was milky, with a good pork flavor mixed with a tinge of miso. The pork was a little chewy, but only had a thin strip of fat, which is what I like. The noodles were a bit chewier than al-dente but went well with the soup. The only gripe I had was that the egg was whole, and not soft & ooey-gooey on the inside, but hey at least you get a whole egg instead of half of one, right? My sister seemed to enjoy her karai ramen, but stated that it was nowhere near spicy. Nom Nom seems to be adjusting well & I hope that the quality of their ramen only increases as time passes.

I came here about 2 years ago while visiting my uncle in New York, and I loved it! We went for lunch and I wasn't really sure what to expect, but I was very satisfied. I ordered a veggie patty salad with fresh apple slices. It was delicious! I love places that cater to vegetarians, so I was very happy with the menu. The atmosphere is casual, the decor is super cute, and the servers were very nice. My one complaint is the wait, it was a bit long, but totally worth it! If you're in the New York area, definitely try this place out!
I love Ippudo ramen. It is my favorite ramen in NYC!

I love Fat Salmon, partially because I live near by but mostly because it is excellent, creative, delicious sushi at a good price.  If you do it right (one drink each, avocado salad to share, a special roll and two regular rolls to share), you can have a Saturday night dinner date out for ~$50 total.  I always leave full and satisfied.  Take out is delicious, too.

This place has my name written all over. It a paradise for me with exclusions though. The drinks are strong! And damn well better be for the price. So i will definitely be back for a drink. Food on the other hand... Let's say the old fashion feel melds into the cuisine in regards to taste. I enjoyed me interesting take on a shepherds pie but I also had a clam chowder (manhattan clam chowder) and just eh was what my tummy has to say. The clams were good though. My date did not enjoy her food one but with reason.(oh and our soups were barley luke warm) She had a fish soup and said the mussels taste very off :/ that's no bueno then her main dish was soaked in beer, we'd say for a bit to long. Aside from food being a downer this place is amazingly cozy and worth a trip (for the drinks). Music isn't too loud and it's appropriate for the setting. As always my complaint with restaurants-gets to dark when they dim the lights down (can we put an end to this trend already? I don't want to sleep in my food:)

Found this cart in front of the Laguardia Community College in LIC after reading about it on Yelp. Paid about 4 bucks for one of the more interesting meals of my life.  I really like that sweet ginger cream sauce and the cheesy spicy goodness in the tacos.  Chicken and beef meat were good too.  Also they are friendly.

My girlfriend and I took a trip to New York this past December, and I am just getting around to reviewing all of the places we ate at. Being in the largest city on earth with a million decisions for food coupled with our desire and need for quality, comforting food, restaurant decisions were much debated, but in the end a total shot in the dark with only Yelp and Zagat for references (which we all know can be extremely misleading at times). We had planned on coming here, for we were in the mood for Thai and it was close to the Theater District, before Jersey Boys. We miscalculated on time, and after sitting down and being served water, realized the time and had to leave and stop to get an apple and some pizza on the way to the theater. However, we liked the menu and decided to come back after the show. A worthwhile choice I must say. The decor, as is custom with all Thai places, was polished, sleek, and in fact fairly modern compared to most Thai places I have eaten at. I loved the atmosphere it created. We opted only for entrees since we had pizza before and candy during the show. I ordered the Pad Thai, and if I am not mistaken, my girlfriend ordered the Pad Kee Mao, one of her favorite Thai dishes. I had never tried Pad Thai before and this dish was the propulsive factor that illuminated my hidden love for Thai food. I have ordered Pad Thai at many places since, all of worthy quality, and none has yet compared to this one. Everything seemed so fresh and light for a noodle dish. It was not too oily as can happen, the egg was scrambled well, it was not too fishy from the fish sauce (I make Pad Thai myself a lot now), the tamarind balanced it out well, and the tofu was not too soft and mushy as can happen easily when not prepared properly. I know my girlfriend's dish was great as well, though I cannot recall many specifics about it. The best element of Thai food is undoubtedly the price. We were scared about higher prices in New York, but surprisingly they were about what I have found elsewhere, from San Diego to Los Angeles and Santa Barbara. I know that there are many Thai places in New York, and even a good deal in the immediate area surrounding this one. Sadly, I only tried one other one, though  we were tempted to come back here since we were so pleased. However, I would recommend this place. Not necessarily over any of the other places, but separated from comparison and judged not on relative terms, I think it is warrants more than the rating it has been given here on Yelp.

Although I've never been to a country club, I imagine that Rouge must be something like it.  Pricey, exclusive, and filled with ladies who lunch or accompanied by their blazer wearing husbands.  I should have known we were in for something else when a Tuesday lunch was greeted by the hostesses with "Do you have a reservation?"  Um, lunch, Tuesday, hamburger...reservation??  In any case, we had heard that the burgers were some of the best in Philadelphia, so we had to find out for ourselves.  However, Rouge's burgers were nothing but average. First, the meat was under-seasoned.  You would think that with gruyere and caramelized onions, the burger would be anything but bland, but neither added or complemented the burger as a whole.  Second, the meat was a bit dry and fell apart.  I ordered the burger at medium, but the juices ran out making the bun soggy, leaving the meat dry and in pieces.  Third, $20 including tax and tip for burger and fries is outrageous when the meat is anything less than top quality.  Give me Village Whiskey's or Bobby's Burger Palace over Rouge's burger any day.  It's a beautiful restaurant with friendly staff, but as a lady who tastes, I can do without Rouge.

It's a delight when a great staff serves an equally great meal, and this was the case at my first visit to Kiwiana.  I was fortunate enough to sample many of the dishes and found each to be unique and complex in their deliciousness.   Starting with pickled mussels was a terrific choice.  The fried chicken entree served with truffle honey left me ripping every edible bite off the bone in a near-primal manner. And last but certainly not least, tasting the passion fruit flan reminded me of that scene in Pleasantville when everything turns from black-and-white to color.  Truly amazing flavor.

Food is really quite good and I have sampled most of the menu.  I am impressed by how consistently they are able to produce excellent plates.  Service is efficient and friendly.  Only complaint - it seemed half of NYC was there.  While this did not impact the quality of our meal (hats off to them), it took us nearly 15 minutes to squeeze out after navigating a long, backed-up coat check line at the jam-packed bar area.  Fire code violation?  I think so.  But I would definitely recommend this place and wish them continued success.
Thanks for a wonderful bridal shower for my daughter! The food, atmosphere and service was great!

I've been in here a few times now and while I think the place is pretty good, I don't see what all the fuss is about. It's funky and unusual and all that, but aside from the novelty of it being in a more or less "undiscovered" part of Chinatown and/or having the guy there churning out the hand pulled noodles manually, it's quite good, yet still pretty ordinary and nothing really to get your "noodle" excited over. It is a bit of a dive and each time I've been I believe I was VERY fortunate to find a place to sit in this sparsely tabled eatery. First time I was here, I had the dry noodles with meat sauce and a LARGE (there's only one size) order of fried meat dumplings. Even though they were supposedly fresh, I was disappointed with the texture of the noodles. They were softer  and limper than I was expecting or would have liked and nothing really special. The meat sauce was like nothing I'd ever had in a Chinese joint before and was unique and tasty. This dish reminded me of that "Skyline Chili" they serve in Cincinnati on the spaghetti - especially after I doused it with a small bit of hot oil. Mmmmn! Chili Mac! Unfortunately as I said, the noodle texture was a bit of a let down though :-( Dumplings were good, but I like the Tasty Dumpling ones: yelp.com/biz/tasty-dumpl… much better because being just as good or better, they sell for only 5/$1.25 at that place and they come out as promptly as you could ever wish for. Promptly. Which leads to another issue here. They're pretty disorganized. You never know to whom to place the order with here. Most times the waitress is MIA and the noodleman comes over to ask what you want. Then the order gets mixed up. Last time, we had two similar orders: two No. 2s and one fried dumpling order. After two other tables who'd come in after us got their stuff immediately, noodleman finally came over and then retook our order. We eventually got our food. Every time I've been here, this mode of service has been typical. The noodles in the Brisket & Noodle Soup I've last had were better than the ones I'd had on my first visit. They possessed a little bit more body and didn't feel so limp and overcooked. The broth was another story though. It basically had none of the  rich flavor associated with Chinese soups and as much as I never leave food behind, I only sampled a few spoonfuls of the soup itself before abandoning it for good. Funny, just about every Chinese patron I've seen eating here has always done the same thing with their soup too. I guess they "know". If I hadn't dressed the soup with a hefty amount of the minced pickled greens they supplied on the table, this broth might not have had any flavor whatsoever. As for the brisket, while tastily spiced it was EXTREMELY gristly (even for MY tastes) and was not very pleasant to chew through. Anyhow, the place is still pretty good and I'll certainly eat here again and bring out of town guests and the uninitiated to expose them to a slice of the more seedy side of Chinatown. However, I think I'll be checking out other Chinatown noodle houses like Eastern Noodles: yelp.com/biz/eastern-aut… before I revisit Lan Zhou again (but I WILL revisit them, make no mistake about that!).

i used to have gerbils.  as part of their diet we would buy them a salt lick, which is a solid round circle of salt.  they would eat it throughout the week.  i'm not a gerbil...i don't really like gerbils anymore, but the food at The Cambridge might as well be a salt lick.  HOLY PARCHED BODY! i have dined here many times and God Damn everything is salty...it has gotten worse because the first time i ate here the food was pretty good...now salt cereal.  they are geniuses on some level considering the more salt licks people eat...the more beer they drink.  i will say that the nachos are delicious and honestly it is a great beer bar!!   the Cambridge probably has about 25 beers on tap at all times and are constantly rolling them over...both domestic and international.  this is a great place to come for a drink and the atmosphere is super nice...great dark woods with a vintage like feel. i can't finish this review without mentioning the unmentionable.  i was here about a month ago having dinner with a friend and all of a sudden i saw a mouse run across the dining room floor.  i gasped b/c i didn't want to scream and cause a commotion, but it was definitely running around...i kept my eye on it.  Cambridge...here is a tip: get some mouse traps or else the Philly health department might have a few things to say...although they won't shut you down.  Here in philly we love the grit...just check out the hoards of food trucks without running water in west philly. cheers!

i love Nizi Sushi gooood food always packed but its all good. Unfortunately that is in the past now, new owner does not served the same quality of food like what they used to have.  Sorry Guys...wish you the best thou

Does what it says on the tin: pounds and pounds of hot, messy, juicy seafood to order with your choice of seasoning. We came in with a group of 9 at 7:30 PM Saturday night, and were seated shortly before 9 PM. The host will text you when your table is ready, so we wandered to the sports bar upstairs for some beer while we waited. We got it seasoned with everything, and it was delicious. Heavy on the garlic, so be ready to ward off vampires afterward. Crawfish, shrimp, and crab legs all delicious. Our waitress was kind enough to show us how to properly peel a crawfish - the staff were all really nice! The best part? Taking off your gloves and realising your fingers don't smell like food. Score.

Char No. 4  Rocks!   One of the most exciting menus in all five boroughs.   If you're not a  local, its worth the trip to Cobble Hill to check out the  hopping bar and restaurant scene.    Great vibe as you enter the restaurant and are greeted by an endless wall of the best Whiskey and Bourbon.   As you sit at the bar, you see an eclectic, cool, and hip crowd under a ceiling of whiskey barrel shaped lighting fixtures emitting a caramel glow to the room. Creative and smoking hot appetizers include the melt in your mouth devilled eggs, out of this world Lamb Pastrami, simply the best thick cut bacon accented with spiced cabbage and cashews.   One plate was better than the next.   We chose the hangar steak with rosemary garlic potatoes and the grilled  shrimp with grits and andouille sausage.    Spectacular!   The flavor jumps off your fork and reminds me of New Orleans best and most innovative menus.   Both  entrees were perfect portion sizes, and delicately arranged on the plate.   The desserts were out of this world.   Hands down the best homemade butter pecan ice cream anywhere.   Don't go home without trying this. Great service by an attentive and courteous staff. Very excited to return a few more times  and try the other items on the menu.

Holla for the pig, the cerdo, the porc, the porco at this succlent jizoint near the 14th Street.  Charcuterie plates of the hizam with warm artesanal bread rizes to the top.  Succotash is the stash hidden under some fine, crispy, sea bass that's one of the only dishes that won't add to yo' ass.  Since I be an asian, rollin in at 5'1", the strawberry shortcake calls my name, but baby I'd go back for them ribs tomorrow.  Fat Bastard needs to roll up so that he can stop pumpin the Chiles and start with the Ssizam!!
Service is ok, but the food is definitely good, just the portion for the stingy ray is too small for the price. Other dishes are fine.
Heard a bunch of hype for this place. but tried it and this place is bomb. its pricey. a bowl of ramen for 15 bucks. def worth every penny..

This is a bit of a late review, but this was easily my best meal of 2011.  We reserved  the chef's table in the back after thinking this was actually another restaurant.  What a wonderful mistake! The chefs are a few feet away doing their thing, the waitress was very nice and helpful.  All we had to do was sit back and choose the wine.  Each course that was brought to us was better than the last.  We left very happy.  And I'm not gonna lie, when I think about moving to Brooklyn, I google map the distance of my potential address to Battersby.

The food is really good. I have nothing bad to say about it. But I think it is ridiculous that they don't take reservations. It really bothers me. Why go somewhere and wait when you can reserve a table somewhere else? Fan of the flood but not the restaurant.

Totally still a fan!  Pulled up to the bar with two friends and we just kinda hung around for a while and then eventually got some food. They did drop brunch service on the weekends which I am sad I never got to try, but they did add a price fix Sunday dinner to make up for it.   Started out with a few Michelada's (Beer, Lime Juice and Spicy Tomato concoction) and a salted rim.  I got mine with PBR...classy, I say! I got the one eyed Caesar again.  Can't go wrong with that salad ever!  The lettuce has the perfect amount of dressing, plus the toad in the hole runny egg crouton thing and capers just makes it heavenly.  Then I got the shrimp and grits.  This sausage, shrimp and grits dish is as much of a necessary try as is the fried chicken.  Amazing combination of spicy flavor from the andouille sausage and smooth creamy grits (Get your minds out of the gutter....)  That is down home southern cooking at it's finest.  My friends got the Lobster salad, which had dill, not a huge fan of dill, but the salad was light and refreshing.  They also tossed over a piece of the flatbread with no mushrooms but the sausage was added.  The flatbread was perfectly crunchy and topped with the marscapone and onions and sausage.  Delightful.   Service was super friendly at the bar.  They even tossed us a cookie to go for dessert.  A ranger cookie with coconut.  Apparently, it was an old skool girl scout cookie recipe.

Went there for dinner on a Tuesday with a good friend of mine Things I enjoyed: - The service! Everyone was super friendly, my glass was constantly full, all questions were answered, etc. Someone had mentioned in another review about walking in and being asked if we had a reservation, and their reply of "no problem" . That happened, but it was more of a check I think , for us at least - The food! Their bread is delicious! :) I had the mac & cheese (Tuesday special) and it was fantastic! It was so filling and so absolutely wonderful. Tasty and comfort-foody in all the right ways!  The bread crumbs were toasty and crunchy and the peas added a little bit of a sweet pop.   My friend had the veggie burger and loved it. PS the shoestring fries were very nicely done. - Outdoor seating... I loved where we sat, plenty of space and it was nice outside! I was worried service would slow or we'd be forgotten, but no such deal... - Draft selection. I love beer. I love Dock Street Rye IPA. :) Their other choices were good too! I just love IPAs the best. Things I did not like as much: - The chocolate cake. It just wasn't anything special. :/ A little too dry, a little too sweet. I would definitely go back and try some other sides/foods. It was a great experience and I want to go on a Monday and get the hotdog (A friend told me it was delicious!) or a Saturday for the Lobster potpie.

Outstanding sushi. Loved the white tuna sushi, sunflower roll and the Mountain Roll. Attentive wait staff. They even gave us 4 pieces of a chef special roll to try - on the house. All of the fish was extremely fresh.

Loved Pio Pio. Perfect for your Peruvian cravings!  Seasoning is always great, as well as service, selection and atmosphere. The sangria is PERFECT to go along with any dinner you have here and their portions are plentiful, so you get your bang for your buck. I can't wait to bring visiting friends here.

Heard a lot of great things for this place so we decided to check out the place. Went for lunch on a Monday so it wasn't too busy or loud. I ordered one of their specials, the hot pastrami on ciabatta bread. It was...very salty. I was starving so I just proceeded to eat the rest of it while dipping it in ketchup and putting fries into it to lessen the saltiness. Quite disappointed. But!! They do have a good selection of beers which might be a reason why I would come back here, not the food though.

This is one of my favorite spots for a late-night drink and snacks. It's very French but not in a snooty or prissy way, just down-to-earth, charmingly cramped, bustling, straightforward. Everything I've tried on the menu has been great: small plates prepared with care and attention to flavor details (served to you by French Jake Gyllenhaal--seriously). The beets with tangy creme anglaise really benefitted from the crunch of the nuts (as my friend put it, "wow, beets don't have to suck.") The coq au vin is rich and flavorful without being overwhelming. I've also had various things from the winter menu that are delicious, warming, and not excessively heavy. The wine list is, again, charming (both in presentation and content). Mostly tends toward traditional expressions of grape varietals and regions from good producers. I usually go late and have rarely had to wait, but I wouldn't recommend arriving at dinner time with more than one person as it's a tight space and clearly a neighborhood favorite.

I read these negative reviews and I have to agree (although I never got to taste the food).  I placed an order, similar to a previous post, and at 1 hour 20 mins, I called to find out what happened to my order.  They said that my address didn't exist.  Even after I had given them detailed directions, they still insisted it didn't.  They then lied and said they called my phone, but they didn't.  I will never order from them again and I hope you don't either.

Well, it's Nyonya. So it's 90% Chinese food and 10% Malaysian, all good though. I've always shied away from here though since Penang is so, so close and they have better prices, friendlier employees and more open seats than Nyonya. Cute carry-out bags, though.

Brought to you by the talent of Cooking Channel! This place doesn't take reservations so be prepared to wait. The decor is organic, trendy and fun and the bar is lively. We definitely waited for close to 45 minutes to get a table but the food was delicious. The brussel sprouts (clearly I'm on a kick here) were really good because they are mixed with pears which adds kind of a sweet/savory taste. The mac n' cheese is also delicious. I had the lamb threeways for dinner and it was some of the juiciest, tastiest lamb I have ever had. I HIGHLY recommend this place but not on a night when you are already starving.

I went with a friend during the Phillies playoffs. We are both loyal fans of the Phils, and could not see the game due to the Cablevision nonsense. At the time, the joint was nearly vacant, except for a few drunken old-timers. The multiple televisions served their purpose, and the food and drinks were great. But then one of the old-timers got fresh and started harassing us. Since it was a very public incident, you would think the staff would intervene, but they did not. This old inebriated man continued to harass us for the better part of the night. Two girls, trying to a watch a Phillies game, do not appreciate old drunken Mets/Yankees fans. Capisce?

Spectacular!!! You can not go wrong by dining at Lithos. The owner Chris and Mike are warm and wonderful and always welcoming to their guests. The food is beyond fresh. Fish shipped in daily! I hate feta cheese however this is the ONlY place that I LIVE for the feta! I eat it alone it is so melt in Your mouth good. I recommend the grilled eggplant with feta it is delicious. Actually everything I've eaten here has been terrific!

I go here whenever I start to fade away from the dull monotony called "chores" and "to-do list." I get espresso here because it's actually pretty decent! I also love their cappuccino. I've sat in the back patio and had their wine and cheese. It is such a cute, quaint place, and always clean. I was surprised at how big it actually is; the front coffee area looks a bit cramped, but the back opens up, and outdoors is more spacious. Sadly, I can't eat any of the panini due to my gluten allergy, but it smells yummy! Every once in a while, they have a gluten free dessert (panna cotta). I hope someday they will have gelato! Then it will really remind me of Italia...
Simply put their classic 'red onion sandwich' is my favorite food to get in Burlington.  Great sandwiches, bread, soup and treats.  I love this place.

Of five cheesesteak places that I sampled in Philadelphia, Dalessandro's and Campo's were the only ones worth eating. Tony Jr's, in Rittenhouse Square, Geno's, and Jim's on South St. sucked. The sandwich here is huge, the bread is perfect. The meat, although rather finely minced, was gristle-free and flavorful. My sandwich on balance, could have used more Wiz. Next time, I'd go with provolone for sharper cheese flavor. Everything I saw being served to the happy, hungry customers at the counter looked appealing. The pickled pepper jars are a nice touch. The ladies taking the orders and serving could not have been friendlier or more efficient. In terms of cleanliness, attitude, and food quality and quantity, this place is the polar opposite of Jim's, which was the worst, and most overrated, of the places I tried.

A great place for small groups, dates or friends just meeting up after work... and possibly the best happy hour in the Center (still).  The HH food is a bargain.  The Wine and cocktail menu is perfectly varied.  The bartenders are a great asset to this place, especially Chris B.

Affordable, delicious food in a fun setting.  The menu ranges from steamed mussels to burgers and fries.  One of the best deals in town:  Sunday cheeseburger and fries with a beer for $13.   Be prepared for a bit of a wait during weekends. A great spot for a quick drink and cheap eats!

Dead babies are not my cup of tea. But I'm getting ahead of myself. A coworker recommended Fort Defiance to me some time ago, citing their excellent drinks. (Indeed, the cocktail list takes up two-thirds of the restaurant's menu.) What he neglected to mention was that I should have seriously considered bringing some semblance of a weapon while traveling to the remote location: FD is a 20-minute walk from the nearest subway station. And not the Sunday-in-the-Park-with-George kind of walk. The Eff-we're-gunna-get-mugged/raped/shot-or-some-­combination-of-the-three kind of walk. Once safely inside, my companion (Laura W. - a trooper) and I were met with a small, charming, inviting space. The servers were equally pleasant, not to mention adept at helping to navigate the menu. Ours (I'm told his name is Drew) first suggested a cocktail crafted from Breuckelen gin: "It tastes like lime-aid." Spot on, except it was ten times more amazing. Best of all, it was obvious that behind the drywall of delicious sweet/sour flavor was a s*** ton of alcohol. (Swoon.) To close the evening (and prep myself for braving the cold during the much-anticipated walk back), I selected the Hot Apple Toddy. Our server was right again - it tasted like liquid apple pie. To bad I wasn't as enamored with my dish - the Grilled Baby Octopus. I was expecting legs, but the young came whole! I stared in horror at the tiny browned corpses. (I usually successfully disregard that I eat food that was once living.) I tried the legs first - funky (in a bad way), but teeth-clenchingly tolerable. But then I got to the heads. Chewed once. Winced. (Breathe, Kira, breathe.) Chewed twice... OH MY GOD, DEAD BABY HEAD! I quickly swallowed it, downed my Breuckelen cocktail and pushed the plate away, shaking.

Thanks Yelp, we drove from Forest Hills to the City for something different.  Someone mentioned Williamsburg and found Rye because of the volume of reviews.   The food was terrific, but almost overshowed by the cocktails  The Old Fashions are dead on, with 1 1/2 inch cube of ice (one cube).  Crab cake with the jalepeno/ avacado salsa was perfect.  My shrimp/ scallop kabab had a nice kick, but probably not for the guy looking to fill up.  The St. Louis Ribs, wet, were finger licking good.  My party of 4 will be back!! The only downer was the service.  The staff was knowledgable and friendly, but seemed to be forget about us.

Great restaurant, the service is excellent. My favorite dish was the brussel sprouts.  Each dish had a unique taste that differed from the others, they also have a great wine selection and a variety of interesting desserts.  The decor is very minimal and the restaurant is split up to cater to groups and a section for more intimate tables.  The price is reasonable for a quality restaurant like this.

Though the food is a bit overpriced, I think it's a great place to go if you want a step-up from the typical greasy burger joint. The staff recommends ordering the burgers medium-well, with a little pink inside, and I'd suggest doing just that. The meat is tasty, well-seasoned, and perfectly juicy. The buns, a typical roll topped with sesame seeds, is okay, but the sauces and toppings are divine. I'd recommend trying the chipotle sauce and the Napa Valley burger. Goat cheese and watercress are a great twist on the typical burger! You MUST try the pistachio milkshake- thick, flavorful, and perfectly mixed, I definitely crave it at times! The fries are pretty unimpressive- don't waste your time. I wouldn't recommend the cactus pear margarita. Though it sounds good in theory, it's crammed with salt and not well-mixed. The staff is attentive and service is fast. The dining room is clean, hip, and cafeteria style. A great place to grab a quick bite when you're craving some fancy junk food!

Basing this on delivery service through GrubHub... Moved to the area from Queens about a year ago and miss the 150+ restaurants that used to deliver to my apartment. Found Nolita on GrubHub and decided to give it a try while not really expecting much because other delivery/take-out hasn't impressed so far. I was PLEASANTLY surprised. Food (Nonna's spaghetti and meatballs and the italian wrap) was really, really good. Fries were very flavorful as well although not super crispy because of the delivery time but I can't really fault the restaurant for that. Delivery itself was relatively speedy so no issues there. Overall would definitely recommend and I look forward to checking out the actual restaurant in the near future!

So I've been here twice and I really like it the chicken was really good and the green sauce had a nice kick to it. The salad avocado tomato and some lettuce I was in heaven with a vinegar dressing and the fries were good not to oily, how can I forget the sangria!! I drank 3 glasses it was nice and sweet not bitter how some other sangrias tend to be. I'll go again. Really weird they only take american express and cash boo!!

Came here on a Wednesday night  around 7:30pm with a few former coworkers for dinner (group of 4) and cranked open a few wine bottles we brought with us.  The space is a modern yet rustic look and doesnt feel like a pizzeria.. if anything it looks and feels more like a restaurant. Right away we were greeted by a pleasant and lovely girl who seated us right away. We started with appetizers and ordered the eggplant rolatini and the antipasti salad for 4 with extra meat and cheese. In addition to this a complimentary basket of toasted warm bread was served with a balsamic and olive oil dipping sauce.  All was very good and plentiful - the servings were extremely generous. For entrees we all ordered the chicken parm and it was all thanks to the owners walking over and greeting us and giving us their recommendation.  The chicken parm was served with our choice of pasta in various sauces.  We all went with the penne pasta in a home made vodka sauce .. it was delicious and very very filling. The chicken was very tender with a crispy outside in with lots of cheeses and just the right amount of tomato sauce.   For dessert we shared the last slice of cheesecake the restaurant had along with our coffees.  It was delicious and I'm not a cheesecake fan but this was the perfect balance of sweet and salty.  We also received complimentary shots of sambuca with our coffee which was very nice of the owners to do. The best part among the great service and delicious food? The prices.. they are well priced for the area and wont break the bank, especially with the BYOB concept. I will def come back here again and recommend this place to my friends and family.  We got a winner!! :-D
