Ok. I really wanted to know what went wrong because of all the 5 star reviews for this place. My friends and I decided to go there for coffee before school to try something different since we've always passed by the place and never really went it. My God, I regret everything. The owners were extremely rude and inappropriate. One actually had the nerve to tell us this "was not Starbucks, ladies." when we simply asked a question about the coffee. While we continued to order, their snarky and sarcastic attitudes pretty much ruined my morning. I will never go back to this place. Which is too bad, because the cappuccino was pretty good. These people seriously need an attitude check!

My sister claims this is her favorite restaurant in NY so I was excited to try! We had late reservations that I made via Open Table the night before. I guarantee if I wasn't coming here on a weekday, it would have been difficult. We started out with drinks, I had the Moscow Mule, it was good, but I've had better. My sister and I shared the steak (medium), brussel sprouts, and french fries. The brussel sprouts were the highlight of the dinner - super delish. The steak was chewy, i believe it was a steak w/ potential and it wasn't made to the best of it's ability. The french fries were bleh - kind of too crispy. What bothered me the most was that the table next to us had a different waiter. I overheard him read off the specials...I was curious as to why our waitress didn't even mention that they had any. If all the staff isn't properly trained to do everything the same...what is the point? I felt bad that I didn't have the same feelings towards this place like my sister did. She loves it, and i didn't :( Read her review! Brenda B.

I become a bigger fan of Cedar Point with each visit. This place is 4 stars and rising. Drinkwise - you can't go wrong here. I'm a big fan of their varied beer list, from drafts to cans to 12 oz. bottles to the bigger bottles. The selection is always top notch, and the prices are affordable.   They also have a great happy hour and daily drink specials. Foodwise - the Fried Chicken & Waffle is incredible.

It was a pretty cool place in a really cool neighbourhood. Speckled Hen ! Burger was pretty decent but the fries were definitely over- salted, even for my taste. Salad was pretty decent. Plan to come back for more sampling. Yes... pigs everywhere....
One I the better falafel spots.   Better than many around and solid flavor.  Get the Harissa flavor sandwich.

Whiskey lovers, you'll be impressed when you enter Maysville and you see the expansive wall of Bourbon, Scotch, and other Whiskey options.  Coming to Maysville for this alone is enough, but having the food is an additional treat.  First thing you'll get at your table is a plate of scrumptious little corn muffins that aren't too greasy.  The squid ink spaghetti and the poached chicken were delicious.  I was just surprised that this place was so empty on a Friday night at 7pm.
Best Pho and Shrimp Pad Thai in Chinatown. My wife and I try to eat here about once a week and we are constantly recommending it to friends.

Tinto to me is like the cool kid's table at lunch I always wanted to sit with in middle school. Then I sat there and realized yeah everyone is pretty and stuff ...and nice enough...yet I was a bit underwhelmed. So instead I went back to sitting at the lunch table where we farted in snapple bottles and passed them to unsuspecting people. After dining at Tinto 4 or 5 times over the years I agree the food/drinks are decent, as is the decor & service as it should be at this price point. Yet I'm hard pressed to remember anything truly memorable. Then again Spanish tapas aren't really my thing. I just realized this review isn't really a review....thus pointless...thus I wasted your time....my apologies...enjoy the weekend.

I have eaten here several times, however my recent venture 10 days ago was a disaster.  The food was not as excellent as usual.  In fact, the chicken satay I order was not good at all.  My son usually eats several helpings but barely got through one this time.  The roti kanai, which I love also left a lot to be desired.  And the service just plain sucked.  I might give it one more chance due to past experience, but I was highly disappointed on this visit.

Fantastic produce where I found some shishito peppers which were lovely.  Great gelatos. They have one of my favorite chocolate Gianduiotti and amazing olive oil selection.  I am also a great anchovies fan so their anchovies selection is pretty awesome.  I love the restaurants in Eataly, always enjoy the curdos, whole fish etc. etc.  I really do enjoy this place as much as I enjoy Chelsea market and wish it was less crowded on the weekend so I can actually see everything! :) Winter truffle menu, must try!
This is great pizza! Quintessential New York pizza, in fact! If you're visiting NYC, this is an absolute must.  This is America's first pizza, after all.

Overwhelming! It's no wonder so many people are here with the great location this place has. There are several options for eating, a bar, take out, grocery, etc. The bar is first come first serve, but we got lucky and found a seat within 15 minutes. Both of our pasta entrées were about $20, they came with olive oil and bread. lots of hustle and bustle, very New York, tasty food!

Song has a very sleek and sexy building, but the food does not match. The food is very cheap and very Thai, but it is not very impressive. On top of that, there are way too few waiters and service can be a little slow. One last sore spot for me was that my water glass had a giant lipstick mark on it and some of the other dishes seemed a touch on the questionable side as well. Cheap Thai in a nice building with cheap service and cleanliness. Side note: cash only!

Ok, so Wafa's just relocated to 100-05 Metropolitan Ave. so she could have more room for just a 4-burner stove and a couple of tables.  Can't wait to have more falafel and lamb yumminess living in perfect harmony on my tastebuds.

Panevino has delicious food and great atmosphere.  On the down side, it is overpriced and quite loud in the main dining room.  You will usually have a wait if you go during weekend lunch or the main dinner hours, but if you go a little bit early or late you're good to go.   Their orange iced tea is fantastic!  I love it.  Their bread is also delicious.  I have to tell myself every time not to fill up on the bread! I am a creature of habit, so I usually just get the same thing -- your typical salad with greens, pinenuts, and tomatoes and the lettuce is always fresh and the dressing is light and my salad isn't soaking in it.  For my main dish I usually get the penne pasta in a red sauce -- which is served nice and hot, and the pasta is never over-cooked (just the way I like it -- al dente).  The only downfall is that the meal is quite expensive - I think for 2 salads, 2 pastas, and 2 iced teas - with tip it came out to around $75 or so. If it were cheaper, and less loud in this place, and less of a wait, I would give it 5 stars.  Luckily usually when I go to this place I'm not the one who is paying, so I have a great time!  Ha. I have found that the food is good though, and if you can score a seat outside or in the porch area that's inside right before you get to the patio, you're better off because it's not as loud.  Just don't expect to always walk in and get a seat right away!

The food here is pretty solid but the prices can be steep, especially if you're ordering a bunch of margaritas. If you're looking for affordable and divey, check out all the Mexican joints near 9th and Washington. But they do offer some inventive dishes: - Ceviche is pretty good - Custom guacamole (try with black truffles) - Tamales - Fish or Brisket tacos

Beyond the great people, service and sustainable & local specialty dishes, Brooklyn Commune is heavily involved in the community, hosting events for children and families, supporting local artists and food producers, and serving as a CSA pickup for the neighborhood. I don't know the owners personally, although it's apparent that they're passionate about creating a great place for everyone to enjoy - not just another hipster hangout. The prices are a bit more than what you might expect for most Windsor Terrace establishments, but I personally feel that they're more than reasonable considering the great offerings that Brooklyn Commune brings to this neighborhood. A few other things to note: -No wifi -Outdoor seating is available on nice days -Spacious inside, including the bathroom -Music varies from day to day and plays at a moderate volume level -Bring-your-own beer/wine
Came here for my 32nd birthday. $20 all you can eat pasta + $20 bottles of wine + BFFs = good times.

Definitely more of a takeout place - the place is way smaller than I imagined it to be. Prosperity was on my list of must trys and I finally got to order from here recently. Does it live up to the hype? yea it's pretty good and for the price - it's almost laughable. Wish there was more seating options though otherwise it's awesome. $1 for 4 fried chive dumplings and depending on if you get chive or cabbage $2.50 for 8 chive boiled and $2.50 for 10 cabbage boiled. I got the cabbage one and it was pretty good - probably would get chive next time as it has a stronger flavor. 10 for me was more than enough to leave me stuffed - if you're a dude with a big appetite 15-20 will do the trick You can also buy frozen dumplings 50 for $9 - awesome deal for homemade dumplings.

I adore this place. It is like a HUGE farmer's market. I like the fact that I can get fresh organic produce while sipping Old City Coffee (my addiction). In addition, the food stands have something for EVERYONE.  I don't recommend going on the weekend unless you go about two huors before closing.

Amazing! I've ordered from Jordan's twice and each time was great. Food is delivered fast, hot and with a smile. The Georgia Hot is classic and yummy. The Mac Supreme is indulgent, spicy and filling. I also love the deli pickles.

Visiting Philadelphia  last April, my friends and I knew that we had to eat cheesesteaks at least twice.  We decided to hit Pat's and Geno's since we had seen these "Cheesesteak Corner" competitors featured on some TV shows.  (I have since been informed by a native that this was a poor choice and subsequently obtained better recommendations which I will try on my visit next month.)   We ate steaks from both stands back-to-back and much preferred Pat's.  They had a more extensive menu, enabling me to add mushrooms and peppers.  It seemed more authentic too, without the slick orange signage of Geno's.  Ultimately though, the sandwiches at Pat's just plain tasted better.  Our whole group of seven agreed that Pat's was better.   So even if I go on to have better cheesesteaks in Philadelphia, I will always have a special place in my heart for Pat's.

I stopped in here for a drink before a concert. Um, jackpot. Had one of the most delicious Dark-and-Stormy's of my life, people. They know what they are doing here. (Sidenote: The bar is made of a layer of laquered cigar boxes. So badass.) From the looks of the food and the happy, smiling faces chowing down, I will most certainly need to head back.

Unqualified yes. I enjoyed a delicious meal here last night with three good friends. We had two pastas, a pizza, a bottle of wine, an appetizer, and dessert and it was only $30 a person. The aspect of Rubirosa that sealed the deal for me was the soundtrack: they played all of my favorite, favorite songs from the 50s and 60s.

I've been going to Ippudo for years.  Let me just say I've been to many ramen places in the NYC area, and the Ippudo franchise I feel has THE BEST ramen to offer.  I can't even count how many times I have been to the other Ippudo at East Village.  That establish has a OVER 5000 reviews.. so I'll review this one! This location at the Westside in Midtown is a nice alternative to your Ippudo craving.   It opened earlier in 2013 and the interior has a different feel than it's East Village counterpart but (so far) I notice that the waits are shorter.  Only thing that may give you a long wait is if you have a large party (of around 6 people) because they only have 1 large table to accommodate a party that size.   As for the food, if you have to wait for a table, do yourself a favor and try the pork Hirata buns.  The bread they use for the buns is so soft and the pork is delicious with the sauce they use. For the main course, if you are new at Ippudo, the best bowl of ramen to try first is the  Akamaru Modern, a pork-based ramen with some garlic flavoring.  This is my favorite bowl of ramen to have when I have already tried their special ramen.  There are different times of the year where the special ramen they have on order changes.  Specials are a wide-variety and I suggest reading what is contained in the ramen before getting it.  These special ramens are very unique and are interesting to the taste-buds to say the least.  Let me just say though, if they offer a Wasabi special ramen (not the non-meat Wasabi ramen on the normal menu), do yourself a favor and try it if you can take the Wasabi flavor.  This special bowl of ramen (that had MEAT!) made me instantly fall in love with this place.   The other bowls of ramen I like on the menu are the Shiromaru Hakata Classic and Karata men ramen.  As for ramen toppings, I personally like spiciness, so I always get the Bakudan (Ippudo's spicy sauce).  You get an amount of it that is shareable with others, so not everyone has to get the sauce if they want to try it. Also, you cannot go wrong with a poached egg (Onsen Tamago) in your bowl of ramen.  Finally, you meat fans can get extra chashu pork in your bowl of ramen along with..... very very good braised pork belly (Kakuni).  The Kakuni here tastes awesome and you will not regret getting it. Now here is the main reason why I enjoy Ippudo very much are the noodles.  The noodles here taste sooo fresh and they are made al dente.  It's hard to describe it, but you can taste the freshness of the eggs in these noodles somehow.  Because I enjoy these noodles so much, I always get a "kae-dama", which is an extra order of fresh noodles that are made which they give you after a few minutes to add to your bowl of ramen.  As a suggestion, if you do plan to get a kae-dama, do not finish your entire bowl of ramen soup (don't go slurping all of it yet!) so you have enough soup base to submerge the new order of noodles and essentially have another bowl of ramen! Finally, I have to say that the service here was top-notch.  I personally drink a lot of water during my meals and the server was very attentive and I did not have a time where I was lacking a refill on my drink.  Also, the server was very friendly and would take the time to chat with us, which is always great.   If you want to try a good bowl of ramen and have not been here, PLEASE do  yourself a favor and come here.  Yes the prices are higher than many other ramen restaurants in New York, but in my opinion, it is worth it!

This place is great.  Good coffee and smoothies, and today I discovered that the food is also excellent.  I tried a pre-made grilled chicken sandwich and was really impressed.  They toasted it for me and served it hot, fantastic. My only complaint is that they were out of hot cider today.  Next time...

We had to wait for so long to get a table.i went to this restaurant with some friends to try the famous bistec,but we did not find what we expected. The music was bad. I really enjoy the maduros and the black beans.

Honestly thought the place a pretty cool. Unfortunately I felt disrespected by the waitress when what seemed to me like she was blatantly racially profiling myself, my friends and family. I am originally from the area so I know that 6 well dressed black people stick out like a sore thumb at an upscale bar in Glastonbury.  I have worked the industry nearly 10 years now and half of it bartending and I know that her behavior was unacceptable. Not too sure If I would return here. Too bad the place was fun.

I'm actually sad when I show up and their shifting over from brunch/lunch to dinner...everything I've had here - I mean EVERYTHING has been spectacular!  Their brioche....brings me from 0 to happy in nanoseconds....it should be illegal to have something THAT good.  The cherry on top - the treats for my dog that I get from there...and even my dog things they're heavenly divine!

Checked in at La Viola on Sunday night on a reccomendation. Living in the Bronx for 4 years, I grew quite fond of the casual Italian restaurants in the neighborhood. La Viola had that feel. This place proves that you don;t need fancy dishes and cutlery to get the point across. What's the point? Serve homestyle Italian comfort food. This place was a little pricey, but in my eyes worth it. Another CASH ONLY BYOB, i'm willing to pay a few extra bucks to stuff my face if i dont have to pay for the vino. We started with the antipasta and the mushrooms. The mushrooms were delicious, several different types cooked in a savory brown butter sauce. For my primera i had the Ravioli alla Viola, which was a Lobster Ravioli in a pink sauce. It was great, not too heavy, not too fishy, but could still taste the lobster in the sauce. My date had the Orriechete, which came in a brown butter and mushroom sauce with sausage, and that was very savory and filling. For the secundi we split the special, which was a rack of lamb covered in fontina cheese over polenta and zucchini. This was SO GOOD. Smothered in cheese, drizzled with a red wine demi-glace, It was perfect. For dessert we split a tiramisu, and i could barely walk out to the cab. Definitely pulled a Tony Soprano after this meal and unbuttoned the top button of my pants when i sat down to watch tv.
Got brunch here, place seems it would be much better than it is, all food was average at best

we had very high expectations of this restaurant but were skeptical as we have been to other highly rated Asian "fusion" restaurants including Momofuku Noodle bar that were good but not great. This was outstanding.  This was not just Asian food made with good ingredients, this was inventive Asian fusion food made with great technique. We got there early before 6pm and the wait staff was both attentive and helpful, even though we brought along 2 rowdy young kids. Grapefruit Cream Pie - candied grapefruit, Ritz cracker crust.  It was like a really, fresh and tasty, Key Lime pie.  The crust was slightly salty which was a nice counter-taste to the tart/slightly bitter grapefruit.  REALLY REALLY good - we got 2! Thai Iced Tea Parfait - This was like a jello-y like cold terrine with a lemon-y mascarpone and almond/chocolate crunch.  It too was REALLY good and fresh Steamed Buns - This was really outstanding.  Having had Peking duck and others in the past, I was blown away by the tenderness and flavor of the pork.  Very very good BBQ Rib Sandwich - this was the disappointment of the meal.  It was good, the bread was crispy and slightly sweet.  The meat was tender like a pulled pork sweet/sour sauce.  But it wasn't a WOW.  Good but no spectacular. Edwards Wigwam Country Ham - This came with toasted baguettes and coffee-flavored mustard. The ham is good and tasty.  The coffee-flavored mustard was interesting but a little too strong and I couldn't fully get around the combination. Apple Kimchi - very good again.  Fresh, new inventive taste on a common dish.  This was topped with a great bacon.  The apples were crispy and still retained their flavor despite taking on the kimchi red seasoning. This is definitely worth a visit - it's a very inventive, fresh, take on Asian food.  Having eaten at Slanted Door in SF, I think this is far, far, far better. The wait staff comprises cool, 20-ish hipsters.  They appear a bit distant cuz they are "cool" but are really nice and very helpful.  Maybe because it was 6pm, but we were very satisfied.

This place was THE go-to spot for pho, as it's closer to the Princeton area than other places.  Overall, the food is good.  Some of the fried items are a little bit on the greasy side, and the portion:price ratio is a bit lower than you'd expect.  Service is pretty good, and the staff is pleasant.  Credit card only is a bit of a deal breaker, so make sure you get cash from your banking institution of choice before going. All told, as some newer places are opening in the general area, and I find myself in Philly and NYC more, I've been getting my pho fix that way.
This is quite a phenomenal restaurant. Excellent service, reasonably priced, hipster ambiance, and every bite we had was heaven. Would definitely come back and bring all my friends.
Fantastic food, try the drunken noodles. BYOB and reasonable prices. I've tried many other thai restaurants and this is my favorite.

I found this place because of the ridiculously long line at Totto. We only had to wait a bit at prime dinnertime hours on a Saturday so I was already happy. They have pretty good Thai food at okay prices. I didn't try it, but they don't kid around when they say something is spicy. My friend was sweating. I thought the food was good, but I ordered the pork and crab noodles and I got NO CRAB. We asked the waitress about it and she said the crab was in there... so I thought, okay maybe it's just hidden/mixed really well. But I finished and there was no crab. My other friend ordered the same thing as I did and she also had no crab in her noodles. I was disappointed, but it's a bit hard to prove and not be an asshole when you've already gobbled the whole thing down (which admittedly, was good... but if I order pork & crab, I want pork AND crab!!). For $12 I felt a bit ripped off, but they were also able to feed me immediately so.. I can't really complain too much. Their thai iced tea was yummy too, though you don't get much of it. I'd come back but next time I'll double check my food before I scarf it down.

I had brunch here last Sunday (1/31).  While the food was actually quite good, I had many complaints about the restaurant, which made my experience pretty awful.  I will likely not be going back. 1) It was freezing in the restaurant.  Everyone was wearing their winter coats, some people even had winter hats and scarves on.  When I asked the waitress about it, she said it was because it was in an old building, which seemed like a strange excuse. 2) We ordered the bottomless mimosas, which was a special they advertised but it was impossible to get anyones attention to actually fill them up when we were finished.  We would ask another server, when our waitress had failed to come to our table for a very long period of time and still never had it filled up until we finally made a big deal about it. 3) I tried to order a burger, which was one of two non-breakfast foods on the menu at 1 pm and they had "run out already".  Strange they would not have more burgers that they would run out so early, or the waitress could have at least mentioned it to us when she handed us our menus. 4) The service in general was just awful.  I realize this can happen from time to time but combined with all of the other issues, it made it even worse.   So in conclusion, while the food was great, the service and cold weather made the dining experience pretty bad.

I was super excited for these macaroons from Paris, and nervous about the long lines!  Luckily, on a cold day on MLK, there weren't many people out.  I tried the rose and another red one (I forget already-strawberry?).  I will say that these fillings are the best I've had.  However, the outer parts are the same as La Maison du Macaron. The macaroons aren't very decorated, either.  You'll have the standard, brightly colored ones, but without any specks of gold/silver, etc.  All in all, the macaroons are pretty solid and worth trying here!

I met up with a friend for lunch and the place was pretty quiet, which was nice. The waiter treated me like a weirdo for wanting a sandwich without bread. He acquiesced, proof that you can make gluten-free happen here. However, eating paleo/dairy-free/low-carb is nearly impossible. Verdict: The food tasted good and I might come back, but would probably end up preferring to try someplace new.

I've been living away from Park Slope for a couple years and just now returned and reconnecting with all of my delivery spots in park slope. this used to be my go to favorite for thai.  before song it was lemongrass, but i tired of them quickly and stayed with song for a few years. Something has changed dramatically in the past couple years. I've ordered there 3 times now and everything has been just ordinary.  Not what I remembered at all.  Just recently I order the ribs which came completely plain and dried out, no flavor, except for a dipping sauce.  Summer rolls were tasteless.  Couple other things I ordered were tasteless too.  Menu format has changed so I wonder if they're under new ownership. I don't know what happened here cause this was always my go to place for thai.  So many other places in north slope just mediocre. Regrettably.  Song too.

if you're looking for great seafood this is the place to be. I am never disappointed when it comes to Kyclades. The stuffed shrimp and lemon potatoes are melt in your mouth delicious. I can truly say that anything i have every ordered from here has always met my expectations. Whenever i have friends in town i always chose to take them to Taverna Kyclades. Everything is so fresh and clean and that is important when it comes to seafood.

After my friends and I hit the MET museum-McQueen's Exhibit, we decided to come to Minca for dinner. All three of us ordered the Tokyo Tsuke Men, the dipping ramen? I have tried it in Tokyo..and i loved it so much...so i was hoping to see if Minca offered the same quality.. Unfortuantely it did not live up to my expectations, the sauce was quite diluted and it was a bit salty. The noodle was good and the pork was alright! My gal pal and I were still hungry after we finished our noodles, so we decided to order another bowl of noodles to share. We had the pork ramen with soy sauce. It was ok as well, again, it was a bit on the salty side... Other than the ok food, the service was excellent, our waitress was so sweet and kind....but i just dunno if i would come back again...

Soon after finding a booth we received chips, salsa, and a fresh juice mixer to healthy up our tequila. While we waited for our food, we were able to appreciate the deliberate diner-esque feel. It is a different ambiance from Cafe L'aube, slightly more welcoming, though L'Aube seemed better suited to be inside NexFab design studios. Fish tacos,  2 for $10, were nice plump tilapia strips with a perfect complementary spicy, sweet pineapple salsa and  hit of smoothness from the crema, avocado, and cheese. Cafe Ynez also boats a rotisserie for chicken. Whole chickens are available to eat in or take out. A thin and very herbaceous skin contained a  smallish  but meaty chicken. The spicy tomatillo sauce is nice, but not even necessary because of all that potent skin flavor. A whole chicken and 3 sides is $15.  Guacamole was good, as it usually is (except when its bad and then the cook should be slapped). The corn was fine, but the truffle butter that came with it was brilliant. And the slaw/escabeche provided that acid we are all addicted to now. A pretty well rounded meal package

Too pricey, food is ok Smith is one of the most common surnames in the US so it's no wonder The Smith is anything but special.  Once I sit down it usually takes me 10-15 minutes to figure out what I want because nothing really pops off the menu. I ate here the night before running the marathon and as soon as you walk in the waiter brings you glass bottles of sparkling and still water which they leave on the table along with a bag of bread.  I was  looking for a pasta dish but settled on the BTLE ($12) since french fries were the closest thing to a complex carb and nothing else really stood out.  It was ok.  Someone in my party got the Mac and Cheese which I ended up finishing, again was pretty mediocre (I think they felt sorry for me). I went back a second time recently for brunch.  Expectations were high since dinner last time was so blah.   I tried the Chicken Sausage Poached Eggs ($13) which was actually very, very good.  My girlfriend ordered plain eggs and bacon which she also thought was good but they didn't have hot sauce for her??? Actually, they brought her this bottle of red water that supposedly was hot, but it made her eggs soggy.  Overall, my brunch experience was much better than my dinner experience but I think my final bill was over $50 for breakfast.  For my money, I think there are several better places nearby to try. I do like the decor at The Smith.  The floor is black/white tile WWII style.  The tables are spacious and was perfect for my pre-marathon group.  The north wall has a series of naked photos of the female anatomy from the 1950s that are great conversation starters if nothing else. My Take: Go to The Smith if your parents from Ohio are in town
Fantastic, innovative food. Awesome cocktails and drink list. Top notch staff. A must visit.

This place is amazing!!!! Hands down some of the best mexican food in nyc :-) this place is like a hidden gem as there is no clear sign of the restaurant so you definitely don't want to miss it. Definitely order the mole enchiladas - my husband who dislikes enchiladas loves eating them as well. I definitely will come back to try the tacos and desserts as well as some margaritas.
Nice place for a date :) funny that is italian made by mexicans hahaha but is really good

this place is one my absolute favorites. the decor is awesome too! favorite dishes are the vegetarian arepa, Assad negro and the vegetarian pablon - SO delicious. the French fries are served built in a jenga tower. the fried plantains are amazing and the dessert truffles are made from raw ingredients on site and are unreal. byob!

We went as a group (my cousins who get middle eastern food consistently - my brother and I (of middle eastern descent but never really learned to make it) and my boyfriend who grew up with blander food). Since we were the only ones in there and were a little disorganized in ordering - the service wasn't spectacular. My boyfriend ordered a pizza first and the others all ordered Shawarma (they raved about it) I got the veg combo - very good. but the pizza came out after we were all basically done and was burnt on one side pretty badly. Not the best. (all the meals came out separated by 3-8 minutes). Also most dangerous car crashes was on very loud. That appealed to my relatives, however. Anyway, we will come back for another taste.

Just a hop skip and a jump away from the Morgan Ave stop on the L Train, Roberta's looks like a dive bar surrounded by warehouses. We walked out of the brisk,snowy evening and through two heavy red curtains only to be greeted by a rush of warm air and punk music. We were quickly hurried to a room off of the main dining room, (a large great hall type space with a plethora of long, communal dining tables) and sat adjacent to a wood stove that kept the area toasty. The atmosphere (waiter, aura, menu, etc...) was a bit pretentiously hipster, but the prices (for the pizza at least) were reasonable, and my friend and I were not disappointed in the least with the pizza. We ordered the Millenium Falco, a pie with a perfectly light layer of mozzarella, tomatoes, some sort of delicious sausage, and a smattering of aromatic basil. The crust, additionally, was delicious, with the perfect blend of an outer crisp, and a bit doughier of a center. The beer on tap was a bit pricey, but gave representation to microbrews from across the country (along with the necessary option of a tall boy of Modelo Especial), and although we were unable to partake, the selection of after drinks looked to be quite adequate. I would recommend the pizza at Roberta's (only because I have not tried the slightly more expensive entrees) with enthusiasm, the only qualification being that, to enjoy yourself, you must be able to withstand a fairly inconsequential, but constant, din of pretension and punk rock. I, for one, was sent back to Manhattan sated.

Everything on the menu is awesome. I have never had a bad pizza or bad service. The owners are very helpful and everything is super fresh! Also, not a bad place to just sit down and enjoy your pie right there in the store.

Warning, do not be deceived by the pictures on yelp.  Chicken and waffles are only served on weekends here. I went there on a Monday and even though it was a Federal holiday they were not serving the weekend menu and wouldn't accommodate my request for it.  I would definitely recommend that they change that.  I hate it when a place has different menus on different days. Overall the food was good but I wasn't blown away. Had the pancakes and chicken sausage which were tasty but the sausage had an overwhelming taste of sage and lavender.  A pretty expensive meal for breakfast, about $45 for me and my husband.  The atmosphere was nice, clean but cramped (definitely felt like I was all up on the next table).  Service ok but we waited a while for the food. Would not recommend if you have a large party because chances are you will be waiting for seats.  But for two it's fine.  I may try it again if I'm in NYC on a weekend just for the chicken and waffles.  But otherwise I could take it or leave it.

Yum!  I had never heard of Japanese curry, be prepared, it is not like Indian or Thai curry really at all.  But it's pretty yummy.  Quick and friendly service, lot's of Japanese people were eating there when I went, which is usually a good sign.  I feel like $7.50 isn't that great a price for such low brow fare/atmosphere, especially in this neighborhood where there are a lot of great really cheap options.  But this is good stuff, I'll definitely be back. I got the chicken curry, it's rice with some curry sauce on top, topped with a large piece of breaded fried chicken.  They also have hot sauce at the table that is a nice addition.  Next time I will try one of the "toppings".   Warning, there are no vegetarian options here because the curry sauce has pork in it.

Love, love love Veggie Heaven! I have been coming here for a very long time and every time is a great experience. Even when they are packed, they always seat you as fast as possible and the waiters and waitresses are always calm, friendly, and attentive. I always end up getting the spring rolls (best I ever had) and/or the scallion pancakes delux as an appetizer. Both amazing. The scallion pancakes delux is a meal in itself! For my main dish I usually go with General Tso's Chicken. It's not really chicken, of course. I actually don't know what it is - but it's great! I always get it as balls, not flat. A little brown rice on the side - yum!! Also, if you love watermelon the watermelon juice is a must! Doesn't taste like fake candy-like watermelon. It tastes like they took the freshest, sweetest, watermelon of the bunch and puréed it. Great on a hot summer day. Never really tried any deserts. Just the green tea ice cream and it was pretty good. I'm usually too stuffed for desert. The only reason I'm not giving 5 stars is because I haven't really explored the menu enough. I always mean to, but end up sticking to my old favorites. The dishes I have tried have always been amazing. We like to take our meat-loving friends here. The ones who complain the most on the way there are the ones who are always asking us to go back! A great place for vegans, vegetarians, and meat lovers who love their vegetarian buddies!!!
Came on a Saturday night, the place was packed.  But lucky for us, we got seats in the lounge area.  We didn't order food, but ordered lychee martini's all night.  They were nice and strong.

Let me start by saying the pizza is decent.  However it's not the best I've ever had.   I'm a big stickler on service.  There's something about great customer experience that keeps me coming back.  Appears that this has been forgotten by the employees recently.   A recent trip to the restaurant I noticed the staff at the door treating customers like cattle and rude.  As if they took for granted that customers made the business.  Especially repeat customers. After being seated, it took too long for service prior to ordering and the wait staff hardly came back to check on several consumers.  Poor experience and I am more than happy to try other pizza places like Lacili's.  Thanks to Grimaldi's poor service, I stumbled on a better place with service that makes you feel appreciated. Customer experience is top pririority.
I ordered the three roll special, it took over 20 minutes for them to prepare my food, disappointed. overall, their rolls were pretty blend nothing special about them.

I finally got to go to the much celebrated Buddakan! This was to celebrate with a large group so it limited our menu to the family style choices. It didn't matter though. The food was outstanding! The only problem is I didn't always know what I was eating. I remember one dish was a tuna pizza which was really good. The dessert was a mixed tray and was great! The service was exemplary. I can't wait to go for a regular dinner!!!

The hot dogs were more deep fried than at Hiram's and I liked that a lot. A slightly crunchy chewy exterior that burst open to reveal the delicious goodness that is ground up meat parts. The relish that many Yelpers mentioned was really great. Onion rings were excellent as was the birch beer.

I have lived in Greece for an extended period, and this was like going to a friend's for a homemade meal. The atmosphere is warm, Ellaini is very friendly and helpful, and the food is fantastic.The pastitsio was delicious, and in a very generous portion. I recommend getting the meal--adding the salad (the real thing--tomatoes, feta, onions, cucumber, kalamata olives, and dressing, and importantly, no lettuce!) and baklava really makes it a full experience. The baklava is mind-blowingly good! We will definitely be back. Like, a lot.

One of the best grungy, hole in the wall places for cheap eats in New York City. I've been going here for lunch, when working in the area, since 2009. I always get the large roast chicken, roast pork and roast duck combo on the bed of white rice and cabbage. Always fantastically good. Arrive before or at 11:00am for shorter or no lines.

A fantastic place to visit whether you're a local or a tourist. Fresh foods from the farmer's market stands, eclectic gourmet baked goods from local vendors, and some of the best regional food you can find in the city. If you like roast pork sandwiches, or cheesesteaks, or Amish food, this is a great one-stop shop

on the wrong night of the week, the waits here can be ridiculous! on a summer evening though, if you can score a spot on the patio, it's mighty nice.once you're seated, however, it's always fast and delicious.  this is hands down my favourite thai in the city! LOVE the pad thai, the spicy noodles, the curry and omg i could eat those tiger shrimp rolls all day!! mmm... tiger shrimp rolls. the calamari is good too.

Been craving for dim sum like crazy so we tried this place today...service is terrible, they don't understand what we ordered and the food came out not what we want..and forced us to order everything...The food not even good at all...terrible terrible terrible..never come back here again

Uncle Moustache is an excellent Lebanese restaurant with French cooking influences. The owners were very friendly and were passionate and proud of the food they were serving. I had the appetizer sampler as well as the Ouzi, which is truly amazing. The decor is very unique and displays the French influence on their cooking. All in all, I would highly recommend this place.

As much as I would love to really like this place just because it shares the same name as mine, I wasn't particularly  to fond of this place. Came in here for valentines day dinner and the place was so small and compact it just felt uncomfortable. The tables were placed so closely to each other that the whole entire time there, the couple to our right was so obnoxious and we could just hear every single conversation their having. Definitely no privacy and lack of your own personal space. The food is ah-ok very average Italian food I've experienced better even in olive garden ! Def not coming back. Oh and this place is very dark also hard to read menu !
Crazy cheap. Tasty. Filling. On my way to work. Or on my way home. I make myself a regular when I am on my last few dollars.

This place is literally a hole in the wall. I was right next to it and didn't even notice!!! There's no big sign or anything that has its name. I just saw the small menu where the line was and was like "oh, this is it" I got the pork belly sandwich, correct me if I'm wrong but isn't banh mi Vietnamese ? Well I'm Vietnamese so I'm pretty certain. I've never heard of a Cambodian banh mi. Anyway... Back to the sandwich.... It is freaken EXPENSIVE for the damn banh mi. This place should have 3 $$$ for the price for what it is. I paid $9.25 for a freaken banh mi!!! Where I'm from... It's like $2!!! Well after ordering, I waited for it and went upstairs for seating. I bit into the sandwich and it was flavorful, and has all the other components a regular banh mi has .. I liked the sauce that they put. I tried my friend's meatball sandwich but it was whatever. Stick with the almost $10 pork belly. I also had some of my friend's blood orange lemonade and it was too sour. It just tasted like bitter lemonade. I wouldn't go out of my way to eat at this place again. Not for $10!

3 and a half stars: Well thought-out dishes that didn't always get executed properly, Professional service from a well-oiled wait staff and a quaint colonial atmosphere with a touch of romance. Read on.... Oh Yelp how I love thee, let me yelp the ways..... 1. Awesome way to find out about restaurants to check out and which restaurants to avoid 2. Compete with someone to see who gets the most compliments! LOL 3. Find a constructive way to get your anger out if the place really stunk as opposed to burning it down in the middle of the night! LMAO But yelp there is something about you that I REALLY DON'T LOVE AND REALLY DESPISE! You need to allow for half star ratings! It's driving me crazy. This place is a textbook example of 3 and a half stars. It's better than "A-ok" but it doesn't quite reach the status of "Yay I'm a fan". I am in a state of curmudgeonly critic limbo! What do I do? Well... My heart tells me to go with 4 stars but my mind says 3 stars. For this review, the mind wins. It's fall short in some areas that my mind cannot forgive. Here's the breakdown Food: 3 and a half stars: For our appetizer, my girlfriend had the baked brie while I had the polenta with sausage Bolognese The polenta was a solid textbook dish. The polenta was deep fried producing a nice textural contrast between the soft polenta on the inside and the crispiness on the outside. It was a good solid dish but not a homerun. It could have used a bit more seasoning and lacked the internal creaminess one looks for in polenta The sausage Bolognese was the star of this dish. It was very tasty served in a simple marinara sauce that worked well with the polenta. It accomplished what a sauce is supposed to do. Compliment the dish without overpowering it. I tried my girlfriend's baked brie in a raspberry sauce. It was tasty but she makes a dish similar to this that is better. The baked brie had a croissant like consistency but I didn't really feel that the brie was the highlight of the dish. It tasted like a store bought croissant with a little cheese in it. Nothing in the dish really jumped out except the raspberry sauce. It was really sweet but really good. For our entrees I had the Potato crusted sea bass in a dijonaise sauce while my girlfriend had the filet mignon. The Sea bass for me was good but the dish didn't really come as advertised. I was expecting a potato crust much like one thinks of panko breading . Instead, the "potato crust" was just a bunch of French fried onions on top of the sea bass. Not cool and definite false advertising. Very disappointing. However the dish redeemed itself once I tasted the sea bass. The fish was prepared perfectly, fall apart flaky and just enough seasoning without overpowering it. Plus it was a good portion size. (Size does matter LOL) The mashed potatoes that came with it were quite good. Nice creamy texture with just enough butter to make your heart stop but not so much where your heart stops permanently. Excellent accompaniment The haricot verts (Green beans) that came with it were also really good. Had a good snap and crunch that worked well with the other components on the dish. Very pleased with it. I sampled my girlfriend's filet mignon with shitake mashed potatoes. It was good but again not a home run. You could definitely taste the Madeira gravy which I felt overpowered the dish a bit too much. The shitake mashed potatoes were good but I don't think the combination of the two made sense. They should have been served separately. It felt like a prize fight where each element wants to be the star of the dish but cancelled each other out. **** Something that stood out for me was the supreme attention to detail in plate presentation. Every dish was beautifully served. I am convinced that the chef or someone in that kitchen has a food stylist background. Every dish's presentation was well-thought out, whimsical and inviting. When a fleur-de-lis pattern is in the raspberry sauce in both the appetizer and dessert that says something about attention to detail. If only the food had that kind of detail, we would be talking about a 5 star restaurant. **** Service: 4 and a half stars. Our waitress was professional, personable and efficient while at the same time projecting the aura of a strict Catholic school teacher that I had in high school. She consistently took care of refills and made sure that we were happy with everything. Excellent waitress. Atmosphere: 3 and a half stars: The colonial inn motif is definitely warm and inviting. It reminds me of a Norman Rockwell painting. Very Americana, very traditional. The inside of the restaurant is charming with a hint of romance. It is a classic bistro in every sense of the word. As I mentioned in my intro, this restaurant is a classic case of the 3 and a half star review. The food is good albeit executed inconsistently, and the service and atmosphere are great but it doesn't add up to 4 stars

My delivery order came as a wet sloppy mess all over the bag.  The lemon used in my salad tasted like a chemical, clearly from a bottle.  At least my soup had some crunchy fresh veggies and the mushroom dumplings within were pretty tasty.

I've been to Cafe Orlin twice now, both for Saturday brunch. This review is specifically about my first visit. The good: - The freshly squeeze orange juice was delicious. Like a burst of sunshine in your mouth. - The Eggs Blackstone and my friend's Eggs Norwegian were perfectly cooked, well-seasoned, and ideal NYC affordable brunch food. - Plenty of seating inside and on the patio. Wonderful view out onto the street from our table by the window. The bad: - When I asked to put my name down, the hostess got frustrated with me and told me to go away while she walked around the patio aimlessly. Turns out there were roughly 7 other people who hadn't even put their names down! When she finally got to asking for names, she asked if we remembered who came first. No we didn't since that's what the list is for!! - Service was slow, and my water was never re-filled despite asking for it twice.
Delicious food. I got a Crêpe Bregère and it was incredible. The atmosphere is incredible. The decoration is odd and romantic. The service is great and the flavors are amazing.

I love this place. It's a nice spot for getting food and drinks late night. The owner is soo sweet, and the workers here are extremely nice. Last time I came here, I got the ramen, and it was delicious. My boyfriend always gets hot sake here. It's a cute little spot to catch up with friends!! Definitely recommend checking this place out if you're craving Japanese food.

Been here a couple of times now. The owners of the store are extremely nice, and they sure know how to make a great hoagie! I've had the Allan Special and Karen Special thus far both are were huge, definitely big enough to share. Each sandwich is packed with multiple meats and you can add any topping you like. I would recommend this place to anyone who is looking for a great sandwich in Point Breeze.
Superb dining ala Italiano   Arrived early and soon after the throng came in ,for good reason the food is delicious. Tasty , light authentic Italian fare at reasonable prices. I will return.

I've passed this place many times.  I was curious, but the name and decor didn't speak to me, so I didn't bother to do much more than look at the menu and keep walking each time.  Then a friend came to town and said she would love ceviche.  As we headed toward Coco Roco, we passed Surfish and noticed the garden, which stopped us in our tracks. Feeling the Peruvian vibe, we went for it, and were surprised at the offerings. Holy ceviche...delicious, tender, and unexpected, though a bit too sour for my taste (and I'm told I sucked on lemons as a girl), but really memorable.  Then the paella, but not before the sangria.  Both were winners also.  I won't bother going into detail except to say that the dishes were very pleasant, subtle but lovely tasting, and beautifully presented.  The paella was "wet" and not overly cooked, and had a heavier balance of saffron, which I prefer.  The fish serving was generous for a single entree. Overall, the restaurant is a very nice spot for Park Slope (a great date or friends night out venue), and their chef is going to be on Chopped (Bravo) in the middle of July.  So if all that together is not an indication of goodness and potential, well then, who really knows.

Love this place. Very large selection of Beligian brews with a wide range of alcohol content, all served properly in their corresponding glasses (my favorite part, actually). Food that compliments the brew very nicely. Cosy and warm. Knowledgable and friendly waitstaff. I always stop here on my way to book signings at the Union Square Barnes and Noble. One night I and an out-of-town guest from El Paso, who truly loves his beer, stopped before a book signing by Amy Sedaris. At his request, we then stopped there again after!  Highly recommended for any brew lover, not just those who love Belgian beer. You'll feel right at home.

Despite the shroud of mystery and exclusivity surrounding this place, I must say that it's a mediocre discovery at best. A friend and I went to Bohemian on a Monday night.  When I called to make the reservation no tables were available and we could only sit at the bar.  We didn't mind being sandwiched into a tight space between two other parties, but the chairs were exceptionally uncomfortable and strangely angular. For our meal we had the revolting fisherman's salad.  I can say with confidence that this is one of the least enjoyable things I've eaten in my life.  The textures were mismatched and there was an overwhelming flavor of shiso (or something within that family of spice) that was very disjointed from the seaweed and many types of seafood in the dish. I was most excited for the very bland uni and caviar rice bowl.  The uni was fresh and the caviar was perfectly fine, but the rice wasn't seasoned and this dish is primarily rice.  Therefore it was primarily tasteless. The last dish we shared was the mediocre foie gras soba. Not good, not bad.  Definitely more flavorful than the uni and caviar rice bowl, but not by much. The first two things we ate were really were exceptional and packed with flavor.  I wish the cucumber pickle in tosa-zu jelly and short rib sashimi had been the beginning of a delicious experience, but they were truly the stars of this meal.  Incredible small plates packed with flavor slightly compensated for the lack of "yum" to be found in our other dishes. I will say that the intimacy of this space is a lovely treat.  The service was wonderful and the two dishes we did enjoy were spectacular.  If it wasn't for their attentive staff, cucumbers and short rib I would definitely give this place 2 stars at most.

I went there with my ex boyfriend... the food was pretty good, but I realized that everytime I go to this restaurant...my food comes out lukewarm. The restaurant decor is nice...alot of space. The waitress we had was not good.... and she was SICK!!!...Shouldnt see be home....who knows, she probably was coughing and sneezing in our food... Gross...!!! The chances of me going back there are slim to none...Not a horrible experience, but there are many better places...so why go there?

After a couple text  invite messages from my cousin upon discovering this place while driving in the neighborhood, I finally gave in, what the heck! So, with the whole gang fully attired for this small, very simple, and an empty stomach, we tried it out. We ordered a couple appetizers like : Summer Rolls, Crab CHIPS and the traditional Banxho. I'll just say that the Crab Chips is my fave, we ended up ordering a few more =), then for the main course, I ordered the Lemongrass shortribs, while the rest of us ordered the Cari-ga or Chicken Curry. I am happy with what I ordered. Its basically like BBQ pork, and the portions are not small neither too much. Also, the chicken curry was nice, but doesnt come with Rice which I think would have been better because the curry sauce is too strong and needs something to balance it. Service, cant really complain. The food came one by one, just as we wanted it. The servers are fast and friendly enough. Its a small place, and dont expect much. It could be pack. Food is good though, I just didnt see any Vietnamese person around, I don't know if thats a good sign. Prices are a bit pricey, for the ambiance and food, yeah, pricey. I agree with the other yelpers. Will I come back? Absolutely!!!!!!!!!

Dinner review. Little Owl was on a friend's "to-eat" list for ages and, after the taxing endeavor that is trying to secure a reservation, three of us ventured over to this West Village hotspot for a late dinner. As a huge proponent of whimsically-named establishments that are highly regarded, I was more than a little excited. I think we all were. It is fitting, as we shall see, that upon returning to the Little Owl website to review what we ate, I was confronted with Frankie Valli's "Who Loves You Pretty Baby?" \Begin{Rant} Why do restaurants feel the need to adorn their websites with music? Please be more discerning in your choices if you must blast music through my ears for god's sake. \End{Rant} The place itself is as cute as everyone claims it is - candlelit, cozy and intimate, though I was the third wheel on this particular excursion and so all intimacy between the couple that constituted my friends was eradicated on account of my presence. Suffice it to say, the sight of my person in the candlelight does little to get one in the mood. But I digress. While we had a booking, we had to wait for around thirty minutes, which we were all too happy to do for the management was both friendly and accommodating, offering us a glass of some sparkling alcoholic beverage to ease us into the dining experience that would follow. The menu has something for everyone and we decided to share a few appetizers, which included the bibb & beets, basil lobster and gravy meatball sliders. The bibb & beets were definitely the highlight of the show, though the other items failed to sparkle. For all the hype surrounding the sliders at this place, we were all more than a little disappointed - if you're expecting anything beyond a meatball on a bun (a la The Meatball Shop), you're going to be dreadfully disappointed. With regards to the main dishes, we all went with fish of some form and, though we all feigned enthusiasm, the dishes certainly didn't live up to the hype. Therein lies the problem: If I happened upon this place without an ungodly waiting list on a Saturday night, I would be pleasantly surprised, but this place is lauded as superb both near and far and I think that it has, perhaps, reached it's trend-by date: the quality of the fare does not live up to the magnitude of the hype. Like Frankie Valli, it's time in the spotlight has undoubtedly come and gone, despite the fact that we are still accosted by "Jersey Boys" on Broadway. This is not to say that The Little Owl is not good, but people really need to temper their expectations quite a lot. Naturally, we all had dessert and while I opted for a selection of gelato, my friends ordered cookies of some variety, which apparently left plenty to be desired. Afterwards, meandering around the neighborhood, we exchanged views on the place. Trying not to hurt the feelings of the propagator of the whole Little Owl hype machine, we all gave nods of approval but even she wasn't fooled. We were all a little disappointed. Conclusion: This is a lovely little place if you merely happen upon it for brunch/lunch/dinner (though walking in for dinner does not seem realistic at all). However, I fear that people consider this to be a West Village institution and, as such, it doesn't live up to that grand title. The setting is utterly charming, the service is friendly and it is a good place at which to kick back with a glass of wine and a couple of old friends but don't be taken in by the hype for you will be disappointed.

I have a freaking picture of this pizza up in my profile and my dumbass forgot to review this spot ;-).  Definitely in the top 10 pizzas I have ever had!  We went there last year on a quick stop in Brooklyn.  We had to wait outside for awhile because we got there right when they were about to restoke the oven with new coals.  We got inside and ordered 2 pizzas.  One cheese and one pepperoni.  I grubbed down like a mofo!  Good cheese, good pepperoni and a little basil on top.  Excellent pizza.  The best I ever had....nah...that goes to Totonnos....but still good and its a must stop if you are in Brooklyn.  As far as the pizza nazi outside......  He was extremely nice to us and kept us updated on how long it would be etc.  Dont F with him and wont F with you basically.  He even shook our hand and said thank you for coming on the way out so he cant be that bad right????

Had to book reservation about 2 months in advance, but it was worth it. I had the gnocchi, which was very very good. It wasn't the doughy kind I'm used to but much more of a fluffy cheese/dough combo.  I also sampled the duck liver with cocoa powder- again like nothing I have ever tasted before in a very, very good way. It's awesome that it's BYOB and I think Nick (Top Chef winner 2013) makes it a point to come out to each table at least once during the meal. He brought our table our dessert!
Best burgers I've had to date... Tied with the Stand burger, but cheaper

I was dining at this establishment with friends I was visiting and if I was not with friends I would have walked right out.  We ate at Ten Stone on May 31st and I had the worst service and food I have possibly ever had and I have been to every major city in the states. We were told by our waitress Meghan that the kitchen was switching over and no food could be served for 45 mins.  This was pretty crazy.  They would not even bring us bread and then 20 mins later a table sits next to us and gets nachos brought out to them.  They had a different waitress.  Not only was the waitress poor at giving decent service the manager was behind the bar talking to one of the cooks.  She was no help at all and when I asked that the manager comg over the waitress suggested that she not.  The soda was flat and the managers answer to me was to throw them in the sink and tell me that if mine was flat they all would be flat and made no offer of any other drink suggestions. Lost money right there.  While we were waiting for our food 10 other tables had food delivered.  This made NO SENSE if the kitchen was switching over and they coud not make anything.  Run don't walk from this place no matter how tempting it looks.

Went there with some friends for dinner, much better experience than last lunch Still loving their iced tea~~ but their tom yum soup, crispy sesame jalapeno mushroom and the rocked shrimps are very good :D Love the portions of the dinner entrees, will go again

Had the chicken gyro and souvlaki both with the tzatski sauce...Both were really tasty and was glad they had hot sauce to add which made them even better.  Came out hot and fresh and the fries inside were actually crispy.  Will definitely return..

The negative reviews seem way off. While $5 is high for a mango lassi it was large and good, and the food prices are on the low side. I liked the $13 Saravana special dinner (menu says availability is limited.) Intriguing variety of items, including a surprisingly thing with beets and spices. I haven't been into beets but this was a great combo. While I'm usually into meatier restaurants, this place spotlights how vegetarian joints can get really creative. The cheese masala dosa was so appealing that my dining companion had to politely warn me that I was taking too much of it.
I love layovers in Philadelphia!
Best ramen I've ever had. Waiting times can be a bit long though, but it's well worth it.

After eating a steak at Pats, my buddy wanted to try out Genos.  He placed an order for a provolone with.  Not sure how much it costs because I grabbed a table while he was ordering.  I think it was $8.00 or so.  He gave me half the sandwich and it was tasty but not as good as the neighbor across the street.  Genos steaks were thinner and more dry.  The bread was softer though which I appreciated.  The provolone on cheesesteaks really doesn't do it for me for whatever reason.  This sandwich did have a lot of onions on it and they were good.  Overall though I don't know if I would specifically crave a Genos steak in my life. It was a good/respectable sandwich but far from great.
Yeah, everyone knows this is a good place but the owner is a pain in the neck, just ignore her... She's in the back most of the time anyway.

We came here TWICE, once back in September  2011 and again this past November. The food itself is decent with good portions. Unfortunately, the service here is not so great so beware.  Both times we were served by the same waitress, who I couldn't believe was still employed. She was dense, lazy, and apathetic, far from what you would expect from a fast-paced, family-style restaurant like Pietro's. The noise level gets a little ridiculous during the evening so if you want to give Pietro's a try, I would recommend going for lunch. Nothing about this place is particularly attractive. Had there been a specific dish I really enjoyed, I certainly would return; but that was not the case. I doubt I'll be returning anytime soon.

Meh. The actual hot dogs are comparable to other deep fried hot dog establishments in Clifton. Pros: You can get a beer and a hot dog Easy to park Cheap beer Cons: No chili dogs No place to sit I don't like relish Contrary to popular belief not the best hog dog joint in NJ. It's good, but not great. I just don't see what people love about this place.  Maybe it's the fact you can get a beer.

I've been here several times and am never disappointed. The place is authentic and family-owned, not like a lot of tex-mex places out there. The staff is super friendly and always willing to recommend dishes if you are having trouble selecting (which can happen if you love Mexican food like me). My favorite dish here is definitely the burrito platter, but you can never go wrong with the tacos del pastor, which is usually my 2nd choice. As soon as you sit down the waiter/waitress brings you chips with salsa which is great to munch on while you're waiting for your food. Guacamole is also on point! Not a lot of places around here have good guac but I can attest to this one! Will be coming back again and again.

4.5 Stars I lived in California for too long so I just couldn't give a perfect score to a NY taco spot. Where to start...ok so first it's located inside Chelsea Market and it doesn't really have a store...you have to go inside another shop to locate it....it's going to be on your left if entering from the 9th ave entrance. The steak taco was insanely good...that beef was different from any other beef I have tasted from a taco...juicy, fresh, flavorful...it's like little pieces of hanger steak cooked to perfection....3 different types of salsa at the counter with different spice levels (the spicy one was really spicy) gives the taco the whole package... At $3.50 a taco, the quality definitely justifies the price.

BUYER BEWARE!!! I was heard about and was recommended to eat this pizza place from radisson hotel in hartford when i stayed there recently for an event in the city. front desk girl swore it was great pizza and new york style. Pizza is gross! I was hungry and they insist this was the place. Pizza is the worst I ever had. Ever been to new york? This is nothing like new york pizza. Just because it's thin, doesn't mean it's new york style. Pizza was dry, hot while the box is closed it seems but when i got it delivered and opened it, 2 minutes later the pizza got cold. half hour later looking at a few slices left over, i wanted to vomit my brains out. Never Never again should anyone eat this place! If you stay at a hotel in hartford and they tell you about this place, stay away stay away. they do serve other food too but no way would i go near this place if they paid me. there were other menus i was given so there are other  places in hartford to eat.

What a beautiful place to bring your date to and devour a 10 course meal.   The set up for this place is an open kitchen and it allows you to interact with the chefs.  You'll will be amazed by their technique's on producing such high quality food.   The 2+ hours are spent here was worth every penny as the service is impecable.   Reservations are a must and it is only good for couples.   Try it once and you'll be itching to try it again.... Cinco Stars!

Great brunch!! We stopped in after shopping in SOHO/Chinatown. Located across from NYU, this restaurant has a great vibe and atmosphere. We came during the weekend Pre-Fixe time of $20 for my food, a cocktail and coffee!! I ordered the smoked fish platter that was the best thing I are in New York!! By far!! I'm so glad I saw Chef Duffy on Bar Rescue to know about this place!

This place has never disappointed us since the week it first opened. The oysters are fresh, the house cured salmon is awesome and the squid salad is a real treat. Come in early enough and take advantage of the happy hour special (6 oysters and a beer for $12). You can easily do two rounds of the special in a heartbeat before you move on to the other items on the menu. Just as great is closing the night with the whiskey cake. As they say, you cannot purchase the whiskey cake, you have to earn it!

This one is just a pleasant place to grab comfort food and drinks.  The interior is cool and comfortable, the lighting is chill and the food is better than average.   Quality ingredients are used and the waitstaff is young and friendly.  Their cocktails are money. I'm giving it 4 stars for pretty good food, and value.  I'm not an expert but their Motzoh Ball soup was hearty and damn good.

This became our regular choice for Indian food in New Haven. As in, I wrote this review in 2007 and I'm still eating there today. Well, not today, but you know what I mean. The buffet *is* available 7 days a week. And the variety on the buffet is as nice as everyone says it is - you can always find a mix of hot and mild, veggie and meaty, fried and fresh on offer. The hours are convenient and so is the location. The price is right, the nan is refreshed frequently. The staff is friendly too. And I had my first ever carrot halwa here, which is now one of my favorite ways to eat carrots. But I think the lassis are too sweet and the dinner entrees are overpriced.

It's french-thai not really authentic thai taste. So come with less expectations. I ordered red curry veggies, thai papaya salad, and chicken curry puffs. Overall the food is less flavor and more sweet!

I'm really bummed to write this because I was really excited about this place- they really do have a great ambiance, a great (but very slow) bar, and some awesome stuff on their menu. However, their entree of pork belly was not good, and made me really sick for the rest of the night. If you go there, stay away from that!

The hubby and I got away from the teens for an hour to enjoy a really great cheese plate and a nice glass of prosecco.  I really like the atmosphere and the bartender was friendly and quick with our water refills.

Popped in as a party of 4 for an early dinner on a Saturday night.  They were able to seat us (it was about 6:30) without a reservation.  I did not read the yelp reviews ahead of time on this place, which is very unsual for me, so I had no idea about the half bottle of wine only situtation that they have going on.  I really like wine so I was ok with this.  Half bottle of gruner please! We sat downstairs and had the calamari and meatballs to start.  The calamari was lightly battered, but I didn't particularly like it.  The meatballs were very tasty.  Another dining companion had the french onion soup.  She finished the entire bowl so I am assuming it was good. I had a burger for my entree with cheddar.  I asked for medium and it was more like medium rare.  No big deal, just beware they tend to undercook.  The burger was great and came with some nicely dressed greens and a big portion of fries.  My fiancee had the pasta special of the day.  Tasted A-OK to me.  We shared a nutella eclair for dessert.  I must have been a bit too excited for it, as it wasn't that good.  The ice cream was very good.  However, be aware that if you order more than one scoop (as my 5 year old cousin famously said "never order just one scoop"), you will receive more than one cone.  It was unexpected.

Whoa- if you're considering just go RIGHT now-- this is THE best brisket EVER. Thick, charred, spiced crust around fall apart/melt away meat. We went last night and had the brisket, pulled pork, cornbread, collard greens. I was so delightfully surprised with the collard greens too-- they tasted like they'd been tossed in a spicy vinegar; it was so unexpected and sooo welcomed. The environment was dim and hip. Go there!! Service was theatrical and attentive!

The absolute best french toast I have ever had in my life! ... And that is what I've been telling everyone since I came back from my trip to the Big Apple. I had a lot of memorable food on my quick trip there, but the french toast at ABC Kitchen totally blew me away. I'm not sure why I felt compelled to order french toast and when it arrived in front of me it looked like two large brown bricks. But when I sunk my fork in to cut a corner off I realized that these are giant fluffy Texas toast-style sweet bread slices! And OHMYGOSH was it delicious. I forced my eating partners to try it and they agreed that it was the best on Earth. I know it's hard to make really bad french toast, but the stuff at ABC Kitchen was just so surprisingly perfect! We started our brunch with the pretzel-crusted calamari, which tasted really fresh. It comes with the traditional red sauce plus an interesting deli mustard sauce -- maybe that's supposed to be a good pairing with the pretzel crust? I didn't love it, but I don't really like deli mustard anyway. It was hard to identify the pretzel-y part of the calamari but I will say that the coating was very crunchy and tasty. It should also be noted that everyone in my party enjoyed the ambiance in this place. For a restaurant in NYC, it is so spacious and open. The decor was clean and a bit country, and we liked it. Also, as a scientist, I very much appreciated that the milk for my coffee arrived in a beaker. I never knew I take so many CCs of milk in my morning beverage!

It was so bland, and on top of that, we found pieces of RUBBER GLOVES inside our sandwich along with the cheese. It was one horrid experience after standing in the line for nearly 40min. Never thought nearly 200 reviews would be so disappointing.  I don't understand what is the big hype about this place. I just DO NOT UNDERSTAND why people are loving this place!

Nothing about this place made me upset. Even the cleanliness and decorative bathroom put a smile on my face. The place itself is adorned nicely and the staff help create such a welcoming feeling that you know as soon as you walk in that you will be visiting this place again. We came here to try out their 4pm-7pm hh which includes 3 different wines for $10. The flight pairings (as they call it) are specified in their menu but it does not mean that you are limited to those options. With the help of our waiter my friend was able to create her own wine pairings and absolutely loved it. I, on the other hand decided to just stick to their Jacques option and I was extremely content with it. We also had the warm pistachio crusted goat cheese ball with honey, which is part of their flight hh plate as well. It was only $6 and totally addicting and appetizing. A glass itself is $6 so if you decided to switching from the hh special to a glass it would still be affordable. I think this is an awesome way for beginner wine tasters, as my self, to experiment with diff wine options at such a low price. However, if you are clueless about wine, as I am, then I do suggest you visit this place with someone who has at least a little background to help guide you btwn the wine options. The waiter is also extremely helpful, but keep in mind this isn't a wine tasting event therefore you can not completely rely on them. Overall, it was a great experience and will be returning as soon as possible! FYI, cutest thing: they bring your check in an actual book rather than a check book!

Came here with 2 friends after watching "Phantom of the Opera" on a Tuesday evening. On our menu: stuffed mushrooms, zuppa de mussels (in white sauce), and angel hair pasta w/ meatballs. The mussels and pasta entree were a hit. Those were some serious meatballs!  The stuffed mushrooms tasted a bit like pizza (stuffed with sausage) so we weren't as excited.  Due to our hearty appetites, we chowed down anyways. Service was excellent. Our waitress was friendly and recommended a few drinks for us.  If you're looking for large portioned, family-style entrees and convenience to Time Square, Carmine's is your stop.
And I thought Vanessa's dumplings were good....whOaMG!  These are lighter, tastier and the Sriracha isn't watered down!  No where to sit, but so yummy, who cares.

This place was last minute decision. It wasn't bad at all and we had a group of 9. We got seated in less than an half an hour. The staff is nice and the good isn't bad at all. I had the 18 piece sashimi and very good. I also the ton katsu ramen and it wasn't bad. It wasn't the best but still pretty good. For dessert I has the mochi tempura and again it wasn't bad. I would definitely be coming here again. Make sure to check in on the yelp app if you want to get a free asahi beer.

This review is based solely on the falafel sandwich platter. The sandwich as a whole is good, but I'm not a fan of the falafel itself. Mine was heavy, pasty, and possibly undercooked. The texture was entirely unappealing, almost wet inside. The flavor was not much better. It was super salty, and the parsley is way too dominant. At first, I thought it was just a cooking mistake, but then I remembered that I had this sandwich once before, and the falafel was a problem then too. The condiments (pickles, tomatoes, lettuce, sauce), wrap, and fries are excellent.  I will definitely give this truck another try, but will get a shwarma sandwich next time. The service is pretty friendly.

I haven't had the pleasure of eating at Sabrina's for almost 2 years because the wait is always so terribly long but I won't hate on those who actually wait because the food is well worth it! I finally went on a Friday morning when there was no wait at all and in the end I left pleasantly plump. I ordered the Barking Chihuahua without the marinara sauce and woah was it good! My mother ordered the Challah French Toast with a side of fruit and bacon. We were both overwhelmed by large portions but it was all well worth it! The food was amazing and I don't think that I was able to eat a full meal for the rest of the day! I will definitely be returning!
The food is good, service is reliable, open 24 hrs, and they serve booze. What else do you need in a NJ diner? Enough said.

This is a hole in the wall to go spot.  I recommend the cha sui fan (boneless spare ribs over white rice) and cherng fun yue don (rice noodles with fishballs).  The only down fall is that the wait to order is long.  Get there when it opens or you'll be waiting close to 20 mins

A typical family style Italian joint. Good food, huge portions & great service.  There will be a wait for seats & the place will get loud. The owner was very nice & I loved the fish I ordered. I noticed all the pasta dishes around me were amazing. You will definitely get what you pay for.

Donuts are OK... Every time I've ordered from here my order was screwed up. They will however replace the order free of charge but unfortunately they screw that up also. Not worth the trouble or the hype. You might have a shot at getting close to what you order if you call while  business  is slow.
THE SANDWICHES HERE ARE SO GOOD AND CHEAP I ALWAYS EAT LIKE 2 BECAUSE ITS THAT GOOD AND CHEAP! Get the spicy pork Bahn Mi!!! AMAZING

Bear with me while I delineate an analogy: if the clusterfuck of Vietnamese places on Washington is like a pack of wolves, Nam Son is the lone wolf. It hangs out by itself apart from all the other wolves (being up by 16th and all). This particular lone wolf is not the alpha dog of the pack, but not the runt either. It's a very average, run-of-the mill, middle-of-the pack kind of wolf. If the pack were starving, it wouldn't be the first one that all the other wolves cannibalize, nor would it be the last wolf standing. The menu here is pretty massive. The broken rice and pork combo with fried egg was pretty good. A little too much fat and gristle for my liking in the charbroiled pork, though. The shredded pork was fine, and the quiche was okay. No complaints about the fried egg. The summer rolls were fairly tasty and quite large. Hue style noodles were different from pho, with thicker, chewier noodles, though not particularly spicy as the menu claims. Their bahn mi is decent as far as bahn mi goes. Not the best ever, but certainly not the worst. The bread was too flakily toasted for my liking, probably to hide the slight staleness. This place is worth a visit if you're craving Vietnamese food and you're in the area. But perhaps there are better wolves to eat further down Washington. (I'm not entirely sure how that fits in with the analogy, but I'm too lazy to figure it out.)
