5 stars: fast service, delicious food and great price. Every time I visit nyc I always have to swing by this spot.. Sometimes even twice. The workers are always super nice and the food is yummy! I always get the combo. definitely a spot you want to visit if your in NYC. Or even for the locals.

The ambiance is modern and chic. Came here for brunch with my friends, the host and waiters were very nice. They have a good selection of food choices, you can order brunch items or non-brunch items. So it made everyone happy. I ordered the spinach salad with poach egg, sauteed mushroom and pancetta. It was a good portion and was actually quite tasty. Price is typical compared to other locations in the city. Overall, I recommend this place and would come back again!

Coming from the Bronx it's hard to find good Spanish food that's not from a bodega.very nice for dining in friendly staff take out speedy the food was sooo good!!!definately recommend and will be back

Every town has a restaurant that has been cruising on its past reputation rather than its quality.  For New Haven, Claires is at the head of the parade.   The food has a certain uninspired attention to flavor and seasoning.  Through the years I can't think of a single time I've left thinking "that was a great meal" If you are going to Claires with another person, make sure that you both order the same item.  The wait staff is too undertrained, and unmotivated to be able to get different items to the table at the same time.  This is especially true for ordering a hot and cold dish at the same time. If you are the person who orders the cold meal, you will be faced with the uncomfortable position of having to pick at your meal politely while you wait up to a half hour to warm up the cafeteria entrees in the window.

It passes my friend's three rules for a diner: open 24 hours; endless cups of coffee; waitresses who call you "sugar." Omega Diner is all that and more.  I'm a big fan of diners--cheap, easily accessible comfort food with a side order of nostalgia.  The laminated menus filled with more meals than one restaurant could possibly prepare, but they do. And breakfast any hour of the day you like. I come here often when I desperately need pancakes for dinner, or don't feel like cooking, or have picky eaters as out of town company.  Their daily dinner specials come with salad AND soup (which I order the matzo ball, which comes as one huge ball and it IS delicious) AND a dessert for less than one entree down the road at TGI Fridays.  It's just a feel-good comfort food kind of diner, which will always hit the spot with me.

a great restaurant to hit when your parents are in town visiting (read: their treat).  i'm not ashamed! hell, i don't even remember what i had ("meeting beforehand before drinks" wound up being like 5 drinks).  food was mighty good though.

If there is a Laduree within a ten mile radius, you better believe I'm going. Yes they are pricey, but these are among the BEST macarons on the planet. We got a half dozen box on our last day (because I like to be fancy and eat macarons at the airport. Laduree macarons stay fresh longer than most and don't get gross and flakey.

Not only did I love the food (avocado tacos!) and drinks (best margaritas you can get!) here, but the staff was amazingly friendly and welcoming. I don't know what happened to these other random reviewers, but not only did I get my order accurately and quickly, but it was also with wonderful customer service.  Unlike the other odd people I've read on here, I took the time to ASK the names of the people helping, so I know it was Rob and Eileen that made helped make my day great. Sorry, but I don't think Rob's efforts to help customers pay for their meals is in the least bit sketchy.  I plan to spend a lot more time here and will definitely recommend Gueros to all my friends.
I came here for brunch on a Sunday and it was packed! I got Audrey's egg sandwich and an oj. Both were delicious. Service was simple but friendly. It was a really cute spot in a nice area.

Max Downtown is one of the few places in downtown Hartford that doesn't completely suck. When you come to Hartford to visit or for business, you can be sure of two things; 1. Hartford Sucks and 2. Max Downtown is a solid choice for lunch or dinner. Prices are a bit on the upper end of things and honestly, while the food is solid, it's not really close to CT's best. Their menu isn't overly robust and doesn't change too often but they do have a special soup as well as one or two special entrees for lunch and dinner which adds some variety. If you happen to drop by after work, their happy hour menu is solid and affordable($2-$8 food specials with decent portions). I work in the area so I drop by from time to time for lunch and always have a solid meal. I'm never blown away by what I have but I'm never disappointed either, that kind of consistency is pretty nice to see. For the cost, it'd be nice to see a bit more flair in the dishes especially since this place gets heralded as one of the best in CT by some people. The dishes are pretty good and the consistency keeps me coming back but for the price you're paying, you expect a bit more. At the end of the day, it's good food that's a bit overpriced but the fact that Hartford is solely lacking in many other choices is the reason I find myself back here more often that not. Honestly, the food here isn't 4 stars, maybe 3.5 at best but the dearth of other options means they get a zip code adjustment up. This is not a place I'd drive out of the way for but if you're in the area, you could do a lot worse especially if someone else is paying.
Yeah they got some nice food here im learning to try and cook this style of food so I can enjoy it at home ;)))
Nasty toppings- including frozen spinach. I just don't get the fuss. Harry's in West Hartford is a million times better!

Pretty good food but nothing to aww over. We split a bunch of things on the menu. The flatbread, burrata, and a pasta dish. Nothing memorable, definately not bad either. A litttle on the pricey side, but you tend to expect that near meatpacking.
best huervos rancheros I've ever had..and stuffed French toast was delicious but a bit much..usually very busy so be ready to wait..

So good!!! I had french toast and bacon- it was perfect!  The staff is great, service is fast, and the prices you can't beat.  I paid less than $7 for all my food.  Don't come with more than 1 other person because this place is small, but it is definitely worth the trip!!!

Had the complete joy of tasting a sample of their food during Bloktoberfest! I adore Thai food, and was so excited to keep coming back for more. The chicken pad thai and spring rolls were delicious!!! Will have to check out their full menu. I'm huge fan, and you'll see me coming back!

NOT a fan! I think I got spoiled by Fette Sau that this place seemed barely mediocre. I don't get why everyone likes Mighty Quinn's fried beans, it's SOOO heavy. I couldn't eat that stuff alone... I needed like rice or something! :P Their sides were not very impressive either compared to Fette Sau. They don't have that much of a variety; their veggies were over-cooked. I think I just felt constipated and overwhelmed by the extreme savoriness. It felt as if I dumped BBQ sauce in my mouth and swallowed it. Tip: DO NOT eat the small green peppers. Unless you're in a competition to out-man your friends. They're SUPER spicy/hot/tongue-on-fire WOW. (Possibly speaking from experience...)
Everything about ABC Kitchen is perfect. The atmosphere is relaxing and cozy. The quality of the food is excellent, imaginative and completely yummy!! My new favorite place in NYC!

This place is pretty satisfying when you crave halal. But the first time I ever had it, I was hooked instantly. I went back there three nights in a roll to satisfy my cravings for Chicken and Rice. The bad part resulted from my manic addiction was that I suffered from heavy diarrhea deuce for a whole week. I could not stop squirting. Nonetheless, the food keeps me coming back from time to time. Hot sauce = WINNNINNGGGGGG.

Love this place to bits, but hate waiting in the long line. If you want to try Ippudo very badly but don't want to wait on line, go on a weekday during their lunch hours or right when it opens up for dinner. Ippudo (originated from Japan) provides authentic Japanese ramen to its customers. The ramens and the hirata buns are to die for!! The ramens are so savory & fresh, and the pork soup is out of this world! Out of all the ramen places I have tried in NY, Ippudo is the best!

Sooo good! I got the price fix for $16.95 before 6pm which was supremely worth it. The Greek meatballs were nice, sauce wasn't too acidic (big plus) and the green olives added a lovely touch. The sheep milk ravioli in butter sage sauce were really delicious! The rice pudding was much different from what I am used to and the rice tasted slightly undercooked, but the sauce was lovely and the entire dish as a package was very good. Definitely going to keep them on the radar!

The food in this Chinese Restaurant is to die for!  We've eaten here many times over the years and have never had anything but a wonderful meal.  It's not cheap but it's well worth the money.  The food is the best Chinese food I've had anywhere.  Their meats are tender and delicious as are their vegetables. My husband took business associates from Hong Kong here and they said that it was the best Chinese food they'd had anywhere in our country. I highly recommend a trip to this restaurant!!!
Get anything here, it's the healthiest it can get. Food, service - both awesome. Can I give 10 stars?

This might be my favourite restaurant ever, anywhere. Granted, I've only been here a few times as I'm an out-of-towner but every meal I've had here was so damn good; beyond my expectations. The first time was a few years ago when my boyfriend and I were wandering Bedford looking for a place to eat. We passed by this place and didn't think too much of it but ducked in for a little lunch. We were surprised by the spacious back patio and had the best lunch. A black bean burger for him and a beet salad for me. Both were perfection, and for under $30 for the both of us. The last few times were in the fall when I was visiting for about a week. I made the walk over from my place and sat down in the back by the window for a solo lunch on a weekday. The cute server seated me and offered me coffee and a glass of water right away. I ordered the leek salad and a side of flank steak. I have dreams about that steak. It was flavourful, juicy, delicious... Absolutely perfect. I left completely satisfied. The next day, repeat the whole thing except with the brûlée beet salad. The slices of goat cheese have a crispy brûlée sugar coat and balanced with the blueberries and the beets... Ugh, simply so good. Of course, I got the steak again and it was just as drool-worthy. I can't wait to come back and visit your wonderful city and to have another meal at this little gem of a restaurant.

Overcrowded, waited over half hour with a reservation!  The waiter had a narcissistic attitude worth an aging Broadway diva.  Lebanese salads (warm eggplants and the bean paste) were OK, bone marrow was repulsive (not my first bone marrow but the worst one).  Kebabs not worth the wait and DEFINITELY not worth the price.  All-in-all - this is a try once and never come back again pretentious for nothing place

Good pizza. They have a special, two slices and drink for $3.99 or $599 for two specialty slices and drink. My one complaint... No napkins on the tables. You have to get one at the register. They instructed me to pay after I finished my pizza.

quaint little place for brunch on an otherwise unattractive stretch of 21st in astoria.   i had the buttermilk pancakes with honey ricotta, toasted walnuts & whipped cream.  the pancake wasn't amazing but the honey ricotta and walnuts made up for it. the GF and others in our group had "A Warm Bankie": fried eggs with polenta, asparagus, mushrooms & truffle oil.  it was pretty great. the service was attentive, especially for our group of 7 and the vibe was nice and mellow. they didn't have places like this when i lived over here. nice addition to the neighborhood.

I haven't had hand pulled noodles since my visit to Penang a few years ago and this place does not disappoint in comparison. I had the hot and spicy beef soup and the black soy bean dish. The hot beef soup was decent, but I'm not sure what part of the cow the beef came from. Nonetheless it was still tender. The black soy bean noodle dish came with some broth, I really got to enjoy the hand cut noodles in that dish, filled me up real good and hit the spot. It's fast, cheap food, and I'll be coming back again. I was lucky enough to encounter the screaming lady, she seems to operate at one volume, which is 11. It's a tiny spot but she screams as if she's trying to talk to you across Grand Central terminal. It was fun, the girl who served laughed along. Supertaste indeed.

Ah...Sweet Jane.  You will forever own a piece of my heart you sexy minx, you. This is the restaurant where I met 5 of my closest girlfriends for dinner to reveal that I, Ms. Commitmenphobe, was engaged.  The collective gasp followed by squeals is something I will never forget.   Our waiter brought out a complimentary goat cheese flatbread pizza since he couldn't help but overhear the good news (we're not particularly a quiet group).  I thought that was really sweet and definitely something he didn't HAVE to do.  The flatbread was pretty darn tasty! I had a little of everything and everything was fresh and delicious.  I can't wait to be back! Thank's Jane!

This place is awesome. The food is very good, served in clean, simple porcelain dishes and glasses, very good silverware but at the same time, casual. The service is what it should be, no rushing, you feel like you can stay all night if you want. Good prices.
Had their kurobuta katsu-don. Very good. I saw someone having a katsu curry that looked really good. Must return before I leave NY. in a few days.

I am not a fan of takeout chinese at all, I always find it too greasy. But after having Yoan's garden tofu and vegetables in garlic sauce I fell in love with chinese takeout all over again!! flavorful, non greasy, and fresh!! five stars for sure. added bonus is the great price!
Nice small little shop.  I always come here for Vietnamese hoagies.  Best tasting.  Worth my 30 miles drive.

We've been going to Conte's for well over 30 years...its the best pizza around.  Yea the decor hasn't been updated in 40 years...and yea the menu is limited but how many places continue to have a line out the door after 40+ years on a Friday night?  Their specialty is pizza and thin crusted pizza at that.. don't expect much more.  Now that I got me thinking....we'll be headed over tonight for our regular infusion of the most delectable pie this side of the Hudson and the Deleware

Came here for a large group dinner for 22 people.  Lots of fun but the venue was off for a couple of reasons: - food in general was good. We had a set menu with 3 appetizers (salad, mozzarella sticks, meatballs), 3 pizzas (sausage&pepperoni, cheese, and kale), and 2 pastas (rigatoni and tagliatelle). The kale pizza (not even sure if it's kale) remained pretty much uneaten. way too bitter. - Our table was more or less in a hallway between the front room and back room.  There was very little room to move around and we were right next to the kitchen so there were a ton of people moving back and forth the whole night. - At one point, the staff told us to "keep it down".  The entire restaurant was really loud plus we were in a separate area next to a bustling kitchen. Not sure if it was necessary for them to scold us Good place for a date, wouldn't recommend for a large party.

this place is awesome and well worth the long wait for the food.  the westside location definitely has a shorter wait time.  i've only had the pork buns and ramen so i can't comment on the other items on the menu but I would eat here all the time if i could.

I think they did a great job with the space, but the service and food is mediocre at best. The coffee was good, but it seems like all of the food is frozen, not fresh - my toaster croissant was cold in the middle. The servers were a bunch of young kids who are new to waiting on people, but they are very nice. I would just make sure to keep your laptop safely away from where they are placing you cup, unless you want to risk disaster. It's not really the fault of the servers, though - the mugs have square bottoms and they have them on mismatching round saucers.

My running partner, mother and my son had reservations for our "carbo load dinner" the night before the Rock n Roll Half Marathon. My first time in Philly and Varalli was just breath taking. I am an italian food lover and had an amazing lobster ravioli by far. For my next visit to Philly I shall go back to Varalli and try other of their speacialty dishes! Thanks to Marianne's Assitant for the amazinf restaurant recomendation!! YAY!!

Really enjoyed the ambiance, which somehow made me feel like I wasn't in New York.  The food was decent, but not great.  The rolls were amazing - warm, doughy goodness!  The rest of the food was a let down and didn't seem to be made from great quality ingredients.  I enjoyed the corn soup with fritters and salmon with corn grits, but I hated the bronzino...it was very thin and burnt on the bottom, so there was very little fish to eat and the fish I did eat just didn't taste good.  The chocolate cake was good, but not worth the calories.  I'd go back for drinks, rolls, and ambiance, bit probably not for the rest of the food.

This is my second time to this restaurant.  I love their pancakes! They have different types of butter, that is so cool.   This time when I went I notice their service is so cool and attentive to their customers.  They provided various tastes of their fries and other food.  The wait staff is fast and attentive to your every need.

This place is just plain great. I ate one of the best pasta dishes I've had in a long time. It was penne with chicken, sundried tomatoes, and mushrooms in a cream sauce. It blew me away. Plus, as I am always critical of the value, this place gives you plenty of food bang for your buck. My friend ate goat cheese salad which he raved about all night. His organic chicken was impeccable as well. This is definitely going to impress anybody with a critical palate, and would be a great place to bring a date for a late meal. The only downside was that although friendly, the waiters/waitresses took a while to notice us when we needed something.

Fantastic food! I had not had such a good caldo verde since I left Rhode Island!  There were many other wonderful Portuguese items on the menu and I would've liked to have tried them all, especially the mussels & clams. But realizing that my eyes were bigger than my stomach, my sister and I opted to share a perfectly cooked T-bone, baked potato & salad.   The service was wonderful, very attentive.  The prices were very reasonable & the manager, Paulo, is a darling -- Will be sure to come back to this place when we are in the area again!
Gandhi's has delicious food and very nice owners. They always make me feel very welcome to visit.
Loved this place. My pizza was so amazing. A NYC must visit. Bring cash though no debit or credit
solid dishes with inventiveness and good price

Caveat emptor on this review.  Went to Distilled on what must have been an off night for the establishment.  This can happen to a restaurant for many reasons.  Someone didn't show up or forgot to turn on the oven and it sets everything into a downward spiral for the evening. It's a small food, sharing food menu which is how we like to order so, naturally it suits our style.  The food is excellent and we shared a pork belly starter, watermelon salad, cold broccoli and steak.  Mrs G comments on the onion ring garnish that accompanied the meat. The room is large, open, high ceiling with acoustics considered so, it has the buzz of a lively place without the need to shout.  The decor is modern and plain.  The music is trendy.  Outdoor seating is plentiful. Back to the beginning, the manager did not charge us for the steak after the waiter had already told us we would not be charged for the salad.  It's a sign of professional management when they know they effed it up and make a conciliatory gesture.

great thai food and a cool atmosphere...the pad thai is a must have...i found this place when i started construction on my restaurant (right across the street) and have been back several times since.....i say give it a try!!!
We had the bass it was wonderful, melted in your mouth. The pasta sauce was authentic and the almond cake was baked to perfection and this is coming from a baker.
The food is fine for a central Jersey pizza joint, but they can't seem to get my order correct.  The food matters little if it is not what I ordered

I've been to just about every great pizzeria in new England and Pepe's was unbelievable!!! It's not brainwashing as some novice indicated. It's the quintessential pizza. The oil is a sign of quality chess. That's whole milk cheese baby!!! No provolone in there! The dough is fresh and light and the texture is crazy unbelievable. I've tried sally's and is equally good! Nothing fancy for me... Plain old pie is the only way to go. Don't bother with any of the fishes on pizza yuck... Sacrilegious if you ask me! Try the regular pizza and take it nowhere!!! Eat it hot and fresh
Great fast burritos! The salsas and guacamole are delicious, a great alternative to Chipotle! Only wish they hadn't removed the fountain sodas!

I am always a fan of this cart. I've been here late at night, for lunch, and for dinner. Food is always fresh and in gargantuan proportions. Chicken over rice is the staple. Get the lamb and chicken combo when you're in the mood for more salty. And if you're in the mood for spicy, get the sauce on the side... because it will just numb your mouth for the next few hours you're awake.
quaint space, good food, cute server.
Food was awesome at this place and price was great. Just needed a better waitress to make it perfect. Took a girl there for a date and loved it.

Really, really random decor that somehow manages to work... and I think it helps make the restaurant open to any type of customer.  I went for my birthday in jeans and a shirt, other guests were in business casual.  Their bread is amazingly good -- sweet and salty and buttery and delicious -- and my only regret is that they served it so soon to when the meal came out.  I got the ahi tuna -- DELICIOUS -- and my companion got the Duck Duck Goose, which came with a few too many exclamation points on the menu but was still really good.  I don't know if it beat Firebox on the duck, but it was still great.  It's good to have a handful of special occasion restaurants in town, for the times when I need a really good meal, and I'm comfortable putting Dish up on the list with Firebox.  Yum.
Buns great. Cocktails... Well they use canned mango purée. A big no-no. And their Korean inspired dishes are mostly flops. Head to the Noodle Bar over this place Every time.

The Service: The Bouley waitstaff must be trained in all manners of hospitality and are also able to read your mind. Out of nowhere people came to give us bread, fill our water, bring our food at the precise moment after I was finished thinking "oh I can't wait for the next course right about...wait...oh here it is." The head mind reader also knew when I was going to use the facilities because he escorted me to the top of the stairs when I got up. The service and the care with which the waitstaff treats their customers is superlative in every way from the moment you enter and from the time you finally leave. The only thing that was missing was my wheelbarrow to cart me out of the place, because of.. The Food: Mr. David Bouley has mastered the fine art of preserving the light of King Arthur's sword to cut through the richness of unicorn tears mixed with the buckle of a leprechaun's belt. Each dish from the tasting menu - we enjoyed ourselves at Bouley on a late September's night, for seasonal reference - tasted fresh and ingeniously prepared. My husband found himself giggling at the beginning of each bite, which can only be attributed to the the dish being made with a shaving of the One Ring in its sauce. I was lost in food heaven as the plate was set before me, and then lost in food ecstasy when the dish was explained to me by a house elf, and then finally lost in food ermmygerd as my subconscious surfaced to remind me to slow the hell down so that it could process every complex cluster of paradise that I was allowed to consume. BLUF: The food and service were outstanding. Couldn't think of a better place to celebrate our wedding anniversary. Other notes: Dining room upstairs is gorgeous - the softly glowing vaulted ceilings are luxe, but not overt and makes you feel like you're dining in an eggshell. Decor is French countryside cool, with velvet frames encasing relaxing bucolic scenes of lavender fields and poplar trees. The bread man and the sommelier were absolutely personable and charming. Can't wait to return here again. Bravo, Bouley!

I have  been coming here for several weeks.  Brick Lane has awesome food!  Raghu, the manager, is always friendly and helpful when helping me chose what to order and describes to me the level of spiciness that is used in the preparation of the food.  All the wait staff is friendly and pleasant and it is a joy to come here for a sit down dinner or take out. Brick Lane has become of my favorite Montclair restaurants!

Parking is difficult.  But what's even more difficult is seating- I bet this place isn't more than 700 sq ft total.  Very tiny so be prepared to wait on the weekends.  This summer they've been putting a few tables outside when the weather is nice so that helps.  The wine list is short and the menu is short, but what they have is good.  A different risotto every night and other specials as well.  Prices are what you would expect at an upscale wine bar.  Their truffle fondue is to die for!!  I crave it so much I'll go there just for that.   P.S. the restaurant name doesn't really come from their Bin 228, but it is a good wine choice.

I got a plain grilled cheese because you have to get that right. It was ok pretty greasy and cheesy. The staff was very friendly but the place is pretty grungey. Prices are kind of on the high side for bread and cheese. Why I gave 2 stars: 1) I can make a better sandwich with better ingredients.                                2) The sandwich made me SICK, and I never or rarely get food poisoning. (Not surprising considering how dirty everything was) with that being said I don't think I will be returning.

Food is great and the place looks fantastic. Service is very good (a little overbearing, you don't need to explain to me that "this is the potato"...). I am not a fan of oysters so I skip the whole seafood tower thing (I heard it's supposed to be great, though). The seabass was amazing. I will definitely be going back!!
I don't see anything special after going here. Food was OK for the price but that was it.
This place has great authentic Portuguese cuisine!

AMERICA'S FIRST PIZZERIA!!! (4 stars) Everytime I come to NY as a damn tourist, I have "eat thin crust pizza" on my list of things to do. Locals are probably reading this and saying "what a loser". Well, I can cross that off my list. DONE. 4 stars because of the history and the simplicity of the pizza. I've actually had better pizza in SF (thin crust) but if pizza was this good back in the late 1800's... DAMN. I'm a fan of thin crust pizza (NY style) over deep dish (Chicago style), something about the biting into a thin crust to get that crunch tickles my fancy. That's how a pizza is done. Shopping around the area and eating at the other neighboring eateries we passed this place and made an attempt to come here the following day. Came here around mid-afternoon, the place had a small wait of 10 minutes (usually it's a much long wait but got her after the lunch rowed and before the dinner crowd. There was a party of 5 and we were escorted out of the building and down two doors into another building which happens to be an extension of the restaurant. STRANGE! Ordered simple pizza and sangria and was served fairly quickly. HEFFER-STYLE STATUS. Margarita Pizza ($16) - The pie had 6 slices. Not everyone was eating only a few of us so this was perfect. Slices were decent portions but it is thin crust so one will not just fill you. Kept the pizza simple so we can taste the crust and the sauce. Both very good, i enjoyed the crust and the sauce was kind of saucy for the thin crust s if it wasn't all melted together and was layed on. It wasn't so heavy either, felt feeling great after eating 2 proportionate slices. Will I be back? Yes.. I can't believe I ate at America's FIRST Pizzeria. Until the next review...

Umami Burger was a perfect meal after hours of walking in Soho. It's not long of a walk less than 1 mile away. I do highly recommend getting the truffle burger! I also tried the hatch and it's good but not as good as the truffle burger. And definitely get it medium. Juicy. Also try to get seated upstairs on a Sunday night. You get to watch the game! Amaaaaaazing
Drive from East Hanover, NJ just for the pizzas and it was worth every mile. Friendly service. Went to Sally's down the street to compare and they were so rude we walked out.

Decent enough, I'd say.  Especially if you're used to eating Subway's meatball sandwich (which I am VERY guilty of).  I don't think it's really worth waiting in line.  Especially when you're drunk.  Meatball Shop is definitely quite scene-y then.  If you know where to get a good meatball sandwich or dish, well, you won't really think anything special of this place.  I do know where to get a good meatball -- hint - any Italian deli in Brooklyn.  And Ferdinando's in the Columbia Street Waterfront District.  Overall, I don't really have that many complaints with this spot.  I just know there are better places and for less.

I have been here a number of times and each time I want to come back for more! It is completely different than the old Schuyler Diner. They did a fabulous job remodeling, very clean and the decor takes you away from the typical diner feel. They have great burgers, wraps, paninis and breakfast items. It isn't too expensive and it has something for everyone's taste buds! And who couldn't love that extra 20% off your bill once you check into Yelp! ; ) My favorites are the buffalo chicken wrap and guacamole burger with sweet potato fries!

I really enjoyed the meal. It was enough food to feed four persons on three entrees. Service was good.There was free soup before the meal and fresh made potato chips with the meal. I would definitely go back!

I love this place! Villa Di Roma is by far my favorite Italian restaurant in Philly. Every time I come back to Philly my first stop is always Villa Di Roma (I hope to land around dinner time so I can head right over there). This place is so laid back, you see people here in sport jackets and you see people here in track suits or shorts, anything goes. Every table has their own feel and is autonomous from each other, so dress how you like. What can I say, Villa Di Roma has some of the best Italian food around. The entire menu is just awesome, from the chicken cacciatore to the lobster and shrimp over linguine to the mussels in red. The musts when coming here: start with mussels in red, either for yourself or to share. Get some garlic bread so you can dip it in the gravy. You also need to get the villa salad, you'll thank me later! For dinner, anything goes. Anything from the menu is pure win. The meatballs here are so good, even if you get seafood or a meat dish, I recommend getting a side of them just for the opportunity to eat some of the best meatballs around. For dessert, the obvious choice is a cannoli. If you want to try something else that is delicious, order the tartufo (vanilla and chocolate ice cream around cherry puree, formed in to a ball, dipped in chocolate and frozen)... I'm dreaming about it right now. Just a reminder, they only accept cash! I make the trek all the way from the Main Line, and on my flights home from Arizona I dream about stopping there for dinner. If that isn't enough motivation to come and try it, I don't know what else is.
Great food, service and atmosphere. Wonderful selection beers. Some selections are a bit small, but oh so delicious. Top 3 in town.
Can't say enough good things. Food was delicious, prices were reasonable, place was clean, friendly staff, nice music. I love it!

Exactly what I wanted!  Perfect Tom Yum soup to get rid of my cold, great laab and red curry chicken.  Nothing revolutionary, but *exactly* what you want when you order those dishes.  Love it, and looking forward to going back and trying some of the specials.

I was recommended to try Lyn's several years ago by my friends, who all said it was one of the best food trucks by my school. Since then, Lyn's has become one of my favorite food trucks in the University City area. If you're ever in a rush to work, have only a couple quarters in your pocket, or just want a good hearty meal for 1/3 of the cost of other restaurants in an area, Lyn's is definitely the place to go. I primarily go for their breakfast food, and ask for a sausage egg and cheese on a long roll, which usually comes out in under 5 minutes. This extraordinarily cheap sandwich can usually last me through breakfast and half of lunch (depending on how hungry I am at the time). To add, the woman who usually takes the orders is very nice, and has a darn good memory of customers. If you want a decent sandwich and want to spend next to nothing, I would definitely recommend this food truck.

Not my favorite ramen restaurant in Japan, but definitely hits the spot and satisfies my ramen-craving in the US. Delicious, well-crafted Ippudo Ramen. Tastes just like the Ippudo I've had in both Osaka and Tokyo. Authentic. Worth the lines. Gochisōsama-deshita!!

Modern is my choice for best New Haven-style thin crust pizza. Always comes out crispy with some nice char marks from the brick oven. Taste-wise, it easily matches Pepe's or Sally's, but you'll rarely need to wait as long for a table to open up and the staff at Modern is much friendlier. The calzones are also stupendous.

I am a fan of this sushi place. Rolls taste pretty good and they deliver. Nice place to have in your neighborhood. Specialty rolls aren't cheap here (if you wan't a good deal on those, try Mr. Sushi in Wayne, 22.95 all you can eat, any time, and they offer awesome rolls). But the regular rolls are very cheap here so that's what I would recommend it for.
been here a few more times since my first review. so good every time. EVERY TIME. BURRRGGERRRRRRRRR!
La va is our local coffee spot with great food, caffeination and free wifi. The place to go to meet your friends, cheery staff, outdoor seating for you and your pooch too.

The place is (currently) BYOB but they do charge a "corkage fee" of about $3. Boyfriend and I split   1/2 rack of 7 fairly meaty ribs with coleslaw, half a pickle and a side order of potato salad. It was alright, nothing to write home about. I've had better coleslaw, better potato salad (actually, just next door, at Sugar Freak) and much better ribs. We also got a couple small slices of apple pie on the house. It was barely edible, really dry and bland. I didn't know it's possible to mess up something as simple as an apple pie... The best thing about our dinner was the fact that we waited for food for like 2 minutes. I might come back and try one of their sandwiches.
Incredibly good authentic Pueblan/Mexican food in a tiny hole in the wall in East Harlem. Inexpensive and delicious. Recommendation: carnitas torta and a Mexican coke.

Cuban and Italian don't go together. Upstairs is wannabe classy food. Downstairs note that Hartford doesn't need more cheesy/sleezy clubs! They once didn't let me in b/c I was wearing flip flops. Come on! This place is a sleezeball magnet, and the food is shabby and WAY overpriced.

This review is dining in June 2014. It's too bad that the location is a bit far off and I don't get to go as often. I returned after 2 years and the food has gotten even better and I was very happy with the dinner. In the beginning, we were struggling for a bit to find the entrance with all the construction in the front, but once we did, it was a different scene. The restaurant is crisp and elegant and maitre'd very friendly and attentive. Some menu items that still linger in my mind because they were so delicious: - butternut squash soup (the waiter will pour it on your plate in front of you so that you get to have it at its warmest temperature and all the crispy bites in the soup maintain their crispiness in your first bite) - rice cracker crusted tuna - chocolate pudding (I don't know what the flintstone chocolate looking purple things were but they were goooood!) - deconstructed lemon pie It's funny the best part of the meal was the appetizer and dessert (and excellent service!). I can't recall the main dishes so well...they were good but nothing original.
Their featured wines are delicious. Had the quail last time.

This place is really big, good for groups. I had the truffle fries ($5) which were really good but that was the only thing I enjoyed out of the meal. I also ordered Rosemary wings($9), it was burnt and pretty dry. Definitely not the best wings I've had. I didn't even finish half of what's on the plate. I also tried their pizza, Emilia ($13.5) which also isn't good. I won't be back any time soon.

Right after zumba class the other day, I was looking for a lovely hearty meal. I found it here! I tried a flatbread, and my friend tried the gnocchi veg lasagna.  The flat bread I had was SO good! It was the fun guy - with mushroom, and fontina and rosemary.  Overall, really tasty. I did think it was all a tad expensive, but overall, a great place. It's tiny, it has nice clean and well light up seating, so I thought that was nice. I'd go back if I was in the g-ho hood.

Love this place. Great environment, great margaritas, and fairly priced food. We like the chicken macho nachos, crab guac, combo fajitas, taco sampler & corn on the cob the most, but most dishes are good, although the soups aren't great. We've brought lots of friends here and theyve all loved it.

Moved to Woodbridge about a year ago and missed eating at Thailand Restaurant in Clark which me and my wife both love. However, I can safely say I thinm we found our replacement. Although the place looks a little odd, and has no windows in the dining area, the food was fantastic. Everyone was also very attentive and polite. We tried the curry puffs and I had the Pad Prik King Chicken. All was delicious and hit the spot. We also used a GroupOn for a discount to boot. Will def be coming back.

Oldest bar in Philly! I went on a business trip in Philly and was looking for a sports bar  just to relax and hang with the locals.  It was a little hard to find, in an alley on a small street, but once i got there it was pretty pub-like inside.  They have a bunch of micro-brew beers on tap from the local area and since I wasn't from the area I was all over it.  They also have really inexpensive happy hour and daily specials.  Beer was pretty in expensive overall, average price about 5 dollars for 24 ounces.  Didn't try the food, but there were tables for you to actually have a sit down dinner.  Great place to just hang out, embarrass yourself with Karaoke night, and catch up on some sports.

Perilla somehow manages to fly under the radar considering how good the food is. If I hadn't lived nearby, I probably wouldn't have have known that it even existed. But trust me, it's one of the most enjoyable, well-rounded dining experiences you'll have. Food is outstanding - I spent a solid 10 minutes taking tiny bites of the Spicy Duck Meatball to make it last as long as possible. It goes perfectly with the egg that it's served with and makes for a great starter. For the main I had the Arctic Char - balanced perfectly with mustard broth and potatoes. You know you're at a great place when the sides are just as good as the main itself. Service and atmosphere are just as good as the food. There is nothing pretentious or snobby about this place, and the waiter we had was extremely helpful in picking out a wine and narrowing down the menu options.

This place lives up to the hype. Blueberry pancakes are absolutely heavenly. Golden, fluffy, melt-in-your-mouth deliciousness, topped with that super-fresh blueberry compote. Plus, I just wanna drink that maple butter. Is it worth the 90 minute to 2 1/2 hour wait? Well, that depends on how hungry and how patient you are.  The waits are a huge detraction from going to this place. I don't go unless I'm prepared to wait that long. I love the Southern Breakfast. The times I've gone I've usually talked my dining companion into splitting that and an order of pancakes with me. The end result is the perfect breakfast that I dream about for days afterwards. Not the place to go to for ambiance. It's crowded, the tables are tightly packed together, and the staff tends to find creative ways to pack three people into a two-top, five people into a four-top, and so on. I will say that the servers are usually very nice though. If not for the ridiculously long wait, I'd go all the time. Maybe that's a blessing in disguise. P.S. - Clinton St. - your website SUCKS. Please change it.  I get there's a long wait to eat at your restaurant, there should not be an equally long wait to load the menus from your website.

"watch out for falling caterpillars" this is my new favorite weekend spot! i went for brunch on a warm september weekend and was absolutely charmed by their lovely back garden, the quiet atmosphere, and the excellent refreshments. i was sitting under a tree that is apparently home to a family of caterpillars, but that didn't bother me. i'll be back soon!

Going on a Weds is the smartest decision you can make this week!  That is tomorrow!  It is $5 for the 5 sandwich combos!! I had the Meat lovers combo and the fries with cheese split with my hubby and we both left totally satisfied. They have savory, sweet, vegetarian and all types of delicious mini sandwiches! This is going to be the best spot for the summer to watch games, grab beer and most of all chow down and eat some yumminess

I've been to Roberta's in New York, but I was also lucky enough to sample their pizzas at Bonnaroo this year.   I decided to have a late dinner at Roberta's pizza. Roberta's is located inside the Christmas Barn, which has air conditioning, is decked-out in twinkle lights and has a DJ. We tried the margarita pizza- one with pepperoni (which was actually salami), and one without. I don't know how Roberta's can make something so good so far away from their restaurant, but they totally do! This was an absolutely perfect pizza. We kept raving about their tomato sauce, which tasted fresh, plain and simple. What would I have to do to convince Roberta's to open up a location down in Nashville!? I LOVE Roberta's. Even at a festival!

This was a great restaurant. We really enjoyed the food and wine, it was all delicious. I had the cod dinner and it was the best tasking cod i ever had. The presentation was beautiful and the service was excellent! The tables are a little small and the seating a bit tight which made us decide to go elsewhere for dessert. I would recommend making a reservation especially if you have more than 2 people in your party.

In the heart of UWS where you find the largest population of single women in the city, this place surprisingly has more men than women eating. The reason is - the portion is huge. Brunch pancake ends up looking like the Naan at middle eastern kebab place... no kidding. Fried pickle is fantastic, beets taste great. However, the western omelette tastes just so so. The one I had was very cheesy, oily, and too ordinary. It was lack of the flavor that made me want to order it again.
Pizza is ordered by the pie. There's usually a long line and it's very touristy. Cash only.

Came here for dinner twice and both times were really good. The food here is pretty good but it really depends on what you order. The two times I was here, I ordered 2lbs of the shrimp, cajun style and lemon and pepper. They tasted the same to me. DELICIOUS.

At this point there are enough detailed reviews of Jamonera that I don't need to describe every moment of our evening there. It was an enjoyable dining experience, certainly not a miss, but neither was it a hit. Every aspect of the evening was a bit off; every upscale gesture didn't quite work as the owners planned -- and not just the food or the service, but the space itself, from the strange restroom area to the humorous "phone booth" entrance to the restaurant. I'll point out one area of our dinner that sums up my feelings: the dessert. We ordered miel y mató, four shortbread wafers with a honey-sheep's milk cheese spread. Aside from the fact that it was as much savory as sweet -- better presented as an appetizer than as a selection for the end of the meal -- its execution was flawed. The wafers were delicate, the cheese heavy and thick. No matter how carefully I held the wafers, they shattered into pieces when I tried to get the cheese onto them (which caused my dining partner a few giggles -- as well as extra pieces to nibble on). Don't misunderstand: Jamonera is very good, but its sibling Barbuzzo has set amazingly high standards for this block.
My god this place rocks my world. Shime Saba Kinokojil Kake Udon Bukkake Udon Cum 2 me.

I enjoyed this place. The issues the other reviews discussed was not a problem for me. I have the potato cakes and they were great!  I'm going to be dreaming about those for a while. Service was great. I enjoyed it!

If you are anywhere remotely near this food cart come here. If you are in New York City come here. Seriously. Go out of your way to pay these guys a visit because they are amazing. The line will be a little long but it will be worth your time. Their meat is flavorful and the rice fluffy and perfectly cooked. The sauces are like no other. Their red sauce will burn your mouth in the best way possible and the white sauce helps cool everything down. For how much they charge, it's great value. You will be full when you leave, for sure. Come here when you're drunk. And sober too.
One of my favs!!! Yummy cheese platters, fresh food, and eclectic ambiance. Refreshing in the summertime and super cozy in the wintertime!! The patio is beautiful.

So i was visiting NYC with some friends from Europe.our hotel recommended Pylos, as high end place.the place is very elegant, food was great ,(though u feel like you are rushed through the meal, which makes it feel commercial)the experience was very  pleasant !!!!!

Pros: the food is actually pretty tasty. small, but nice, outdoor patio! Cons: everything else. they advertised a cinco de mayo margarita special. when we asked about it: "no, it's regular price." worse yet, the margarita was disgusting. literally just tasted like sour mix on top of ice. there were probably four parties total in the restaurant at the time (including my party) and we didn't get our lunch orders out until 35 minutes after we ordered them. it took so long i had to ask for mine to go, and when i did, they gave me the wrong order! despite the food being pretty good (though definitely NOT great) and them having corn tortillas, the negatives outweigh the good by a lot. probably will not be coming back.

Great ambiance.  The food was above average and reasonable priced.  We enjoyed the zucchini pancakes (although a bit rich) and the hummus was superb.  The burrata was a bit of a disappointment in that it was more solid and like mozzarella than burrata and felt similar to what you'd get at the grocery store.  The favorite dish was the chicken farci, which had spinach inside and was moist and well done.

Excellent food.  Did not know it was BYOB, wish we had brought a bottle to enjoy our meal.  The dining room is cozy and pleasant.  Great for a date night.  The prices were decent, and the offer of extra rice was appreciated.

My girlfriend and I were wandering around Queens looking for the nearby Eddie's Sweet Shop but we needed a bite to eat.  We just happened upon Wafa's, without any knowledge of its popularity.  We learned soon enough as we sat down and saw the assorted articles posted on the wall (which included a Michelin recommendation. The restaurant is pleasant, but not particularly outstanding.  It's basically a wide open restaurant that I imagine could easily seat 40 people if not 50.  Wooden chairs, wooden tables, some tasteful decoration on the walls and rest rooms towards the back.   The restaurant was fairly empty but we were there at an odd hour (around 2:30PM if I recall correctly).  Service was nice and quick (ex: my water was almost never empty). The few folks that were there seemed to be friendly with the owners as they were involved in a robust conversation.  It's always a good sign when a place has folks who come back again and again. We weren't there for a full blown meal, so we ordered a bit of a variety.  This included: FALAFEL (Appetizer) I've eaten a lot of falafel in my time, from street meat carts to Crisp and Maoz and places in between.  This falafel was good and I would put it at the higher end of the spectrum, but it wasn't the best ever.  It had a nice crisp and a nice flavor which had more of a garlic hint than I expected.  That may have been the tahini sauce however.  Worth getting for sure. HUMMUS (Appetizer) This hummus is one of the better restaurant hummus dishes I've had (I'm comparing it to favorites of mine such as Hummus Place and Crisp).  I will say the garlic hit was *strong* and I loved that.  Again not the best I've ever had, but definitely on the higher end of the "favorite hummus" spectrum. CHICKEN SHAWERMA (Entree) This dish was tasty and we actually didn't finish it (saving room for ice cream after all) but had we done so we would've been totally stuffed.  The chicken had a nice, light flavor - not overwhelmingly seasoned like some places (especially street meat carts) do.  It had just the right amount of flavor to be good without going overboard. I enjoyed my experience at Wafa's and would gladly go back.

I liked the eclectic menu including pig head and brined trout.  The thinly sliced pig cheeks were delicious and served simply.  The assorted vegetable plate was our favorite.  It included a wide variety of braised veggies including turnips and parsnips.   Service was spot on as I expected from a Starr restaurant.   I like the open format, especially the neat counter surrounding the kitchen to watch the chefs do their magic.  I hope to sit at the counter next time I go.

Wait on a Friday around 12:45pm was estimated to be 25 minutes. Actual wait was closer to 15 minutes. I had the fish tacos with rice and beans. Tacos were flavorless even with the salsa. Fish was dry. Rice and beans were okay but seemed overly buttery/oily to me. Had to try the corn based on yelp reviews. $5.95 for 2 corn on the cob with mayo, grated cheese, and chilli powder. Nothing special and overpriced.

I've been coming to the Pure Health Lounge for a couple weeks now. They have really fresh food and really tasty smoothies. I honestly have gotten the same thing every time, which is an Asian salad and a Caribbean breeze smoothie, because it is so good. The service is really good, and the owner is present a lot of the time taking orders and handing out samples, which is really nice to see. I really wish that they had a combo deal where you could get a smoothie for a couple bucks with the purchase of a sandwich or salad. Overall great place, and it's definitely going to become a usual stop for me in New Haven.

Incredible food.  The food is made with love and it's the best Mexican food I've had east of California.  Tremendously fresh and delicious tamales and their carnitas tacos  make me happy just thinking about them.

Fantastic ambiance, amazingly cute staff, literally transports you back to Paris. Croque Monsieur - this is a complete yes. As someone who doesn't even like ham, this one works. It's very unoffensive, thinly shaved, good quality. The bread is super crusty on the outside, soft on the inside. Cheese is melted on top in a non-oily soppy greasy way. Bechamel sauce keeps it moist. It's expensive, but you actually get a really good portion (2 sandwiches) and it's a pretty substantial sandwich, so you don't need more. Servers are attentive and refill waters all the time.

Although brunch starts at 11am, Public is a fantastic space to spend a hungover Sunday morning. The New Zealand influenced seafood mixed with breakfast favorites help you through the pain. Perfect first date dinner place as well.
Hot and delicious. I've never been disappointed. This is very authentic.
The freshest and most delicious vegetable "pitza" bar bone. I have it at least once every week.

Woorijip has been on my TO DO LIST since moving to NY. I can recall the last time I ate Korea, Saturday May 22, 2010 with my brother at 2pm at Brother's Korean BBQ House in SF. That's how much I miss good Korean Food. So I finally made time because the yearning has been killing me! I've been feening for all of my favorite ban chan for two weeks straight! I was super excited as I walked down the alley of W 32nd.  I was elated at all of the Korean Restaurants and eager to see the sign for Woorijip! I walked in and ignored the cute AA dude at the window and went straight for my tray.  I was supposed to get the food to go but I ended up grabbing a seat right after paying and devoured my food!  Yes, I did not remember to take a pre-consumption photo! that's how excited I was lol! I loved it so much, I returned the following day. I spent about $9.50 each day and the cashiers were ooober sweet and friendly! As crowded as it was, I also did not have a problem with seating. Food I tried and loved: Spicy noodles Bulgogi Mook/Acorn Jelly (MY FAV BANCHAN OF ALL TIME!) Kimchee fried rice Tips: I take the red sauce from the tempura looking thing or the beef roll  and drizzle it on my spicy noodles for an added boost in flavor Don't buy either rice option and just stuff ur plate with food.. since they sell the kimchee fried rice warm in a togo container with egg for $3 at a bigger portion or plain rice for $0.50 or $1.00 ...

I live in the neighborhood and recently was delighted to see this new restaurant in town.  A group of five of us sat outside in their quaint patio and had a delicious meal.  The chef cooks fresh, beautiful, and tasty food.  I had a yummy chilled roasted pepper soup and half of the chevre/beet sandwich.  My husband had what he described as the best egg salad sandwich that he has ever had.   They also serve brunch on the weekends.  This place truly is a highlight in Olde City and I would encourage everyone to patronize this place!

My friend's mom was in town this last weekend and when I heard Cuban food for dinner I hoped right on the family train to Coppelia.  It's a straight up diner but with a little Latin flava.  We had to wait about 20 minutes for a six person table on a Friday night at 8pm which was not bad at all!!!  They were also very attentive at the bar and even later at the table as well.   We hung out at the bar where I ordered the El Nino Michelada.  Strangely enough I don't think I've ever had a michelada so I can't make a perfect comparison but this one was slightly different as it was made with tequila and had a hibiscus rim that was salty and fiery.  The combination of the beer, lime and salt on the rim may the drink almost foamy and bubbly.  It was DELICIOUS.  This picture is terrible.  It looks way better in real life. For dinner we shared, again because no one could pick just one thing.  The highlight for me was definitely the guacamole which comes with dried plaintains and other "chips" besides just regular chips which was cool and the arroz con pollo with chicken breast, yellow rice, red peppers and egg which was more like a chicken fried rice.  It was fairly spicy with large chunks of grilled chicken and vegetables.  I'm also not sure what rice they used but I'm still thinking about it. The ropa vieja with slow cooked shredded beef in tomato salsa with peppers and chiles and rice and  beans and the salmon with boniatio puree, otomatillo salad and orange-habenero sauce were also very good but again not to the level of the con pollo. The Havana salad with kale, quesco fresco, pepitas, tomato and lemon-mustard vinagrette left much to be desired unfortunately as it came to the table very undressed and the proportion of kale to toppings was grossly in the "green." The best part of the whole experience? The price.  This place is diner pricing for phenomenal food and I didn't even get to try half the items on the menu that some amazing like the "oxtail empanadas."  I will definitely be back for lunch since it's right down the street from work.

This is a wonderful little italian restaurant. Really enjoyed the atmosphere, the place is intimate and on this visit we got a great table. The ambiance was great and the service was just as good. Our waiter was attentive without being annoying and made great suggestions from the menu. I chicken dish I ordered was expertly prepared and cooked perfectly.  I must say though that the stand out of our meal was the Risotto and Butter Lobster, it was pretty spectacular. While its not the most inexpensive option out there it is well worth the price, definitely check it out.

The food is amazing as is the beer selections! I've come here for lunch many times and am always blown away by the food.  The brisket is AMAZING!! The only thing I didn't like was that it was a bit too dark ~ but that's me being nit picky.  Bring some friends and have some drinks, you're going to enjoy yourself!

A cool spot with great drinks. The food was good, but pricey. French onion soup was delish. Service was quick and friendly. Definitely will go back for drinks and apps.  Looking forward to summer on the rooftop.

Had drinks at the bar and had a great time. Decent beer selection and the bartender was great. There is an upstairs and downstairs bars so I imagine it can cater to large crowds which is always a plus when you aren't in the mood to wait for a drink. All the food whizzing by me looked good too. No complaints here!

I tried to snag a table on a Weds. night without a reservation and of course the place was jammed, so for New Years Eve we made reservations about three weeks in advance. The place was full again but we got seated right at our reservation time and it was perfect from there. The ricotta crostini was light and delicious, the pumpkin angolotti a little sweet but yummy, and the scallops were absolute heaven. And then there was dessert (do not pass it up--the dessert chef is fabulous!). The whole time the servers were attentive but not invasive, and there was complimentary champagne at midnight. It was the best way to ring in the New Year...much better than freezing our butts off in Times Square!

Gotta love sweet afton. One of the few bars in astoria that's not a greek cafe or a old man dive irish bar, not that I don't like old man irish dive bars. Walked in the first time and thought to myself "oooh, so here's where all the out of towners go to get trashed". Decent selection of beer. Food is fantastic, go for the mac and cheese and bacon. Go for the fried pickles. Avoid the pigs in blanket, they're a rip off. Good crowd, ok prices, great fuckin food. Gets one star off because the bartender didn't know what i meant when i asked for a well whiskey. Lots of twinks in this place.

Wonderful food and it was fun to sit at the counter and watch the prep.  A little pricey, but I saw a sign the following day for 1/2 price pasta after 9pm so I would check to see if they have specials on certain days.  Would definitely return when in the neighborhood.

I had a very good time at Brahaus on a Sunday night. The service was excellent with refills provided frequently. The decor is very authentic  and warm. The food was very good. I had the House Special Brat Platter. It comes with two sides. The Potato Pancakes were crispy and tasty. The Brat came with two jars of mustard. One jar was sweet and the other was spicy. This restaurant is very popular. I would recommend trying it on a weekday or a Sunday. They have a nice pew near the bar to wait

You definitely can't go wrong with ordering the Wiz Cheesesteak sandwich! It was great!! The down side is that its cash only but there are some ATM's nearby. In my opinion, the place is a bit touristy but it's been open for many decades so that wasn't a shocker. This is definitely a place to try if you're visiting!

I have been here a few times now and enjoyed each time. Great service, nice atmophere.  Good food  But its th Yummy Oysters!   Keeps me coming back - Always fresh - nice oyster man - sat at the bar and he comped us some treats! Friendly bartenders - and they  accomodate my cuke martini  request - some places don't ( and they have Chopin vodka)
I agree with all the positive reviews.

Boyfriend and I both had the tasting menu with wine pairings. WOW, what an experience. This place was on my "go to" list for some time and after a arduous reservation experience, we finally got a good reservation time. The space is beautiful. We both started out with a cocktail at the bar before heading to our table in the dining room. They've nailed the modern/country/homey feeling without being at all kitschy. Our waiter, Alvaro, was absolutely top-notch, slowing down our courses as he noticed we were really enjoying our wine pairings. He took a lot of time talking to us about each wine pairing. He was phenomenal -- exceptionally knowledgeable, warm and thoughtful. Highlights of my meal were the squab, soft shell crab and the cheese plate for dessert (i'm a savory dessert person...) What a meal...

My family and I have been going to this restaurant for a few years and I've ordered takeout many times as a resident of Nutley. Pasquale the owner has always been a friendly face when you sit down to dine and he always made us feel welcome in his place. This time, he never even said hello but consistently visited the table behind us because he knew the family sitting there. This past Saturday, we went there to have a new year family meal and was very disappointed. We had a party of 8. Staff sucked. Waiter hovering over our table and grabbed plates at every chance rushing us and making us feel like we didn't matter. Perhaps you shouldn't overbook every god damn night and allow customers to stand there staring at you while you try and wolf down a meal. Restaurant is too packed and you can barely back your seat up without sitting in your neighbors lap. Based on other reviews , I can see I didn't imagine the treatment we received. Food has always been good but we ordered rice balls that came out raw in the center, highly disappointing. Again, rushing. The high note was getting our coffee for free. Sadly , it's time to try a new place. Pasquale, please read these comments as constructive criticism ,  you may be packed all the time and don't care about people not coming back, but you should care.

Not too much space (and even less when everyone's coats and other winter gear is piled up on the seats) - but the atmosphere and the food definitely made up for it. Fried pickles - why would you want to fry a pickle? (Why do we fry anything, for that matter?! Because it'll taste damn good.) Slightly spicy, but not too much to handle. Sweet Afton's burger - actually tasted like a steak burger, yum. I'm jealous that Astoria gets this fun little spot all to itself.

For my BDay dinner the first & last time we were there yesterday (we WILL NEVER RETURN BACK!!!) we had the seafood jambalaya, which was UNEDIABLE.  It had several types of seafood (Crawfish, shrimp, scallops, etc) as well as a spicy Cajun sausage and was served over watery seasoned rice - NO ONE from 3 of us didn't eat more than 2 spoons of this terrible dish. Tuna fish we ordered was just over grilled dry piece of fish. Chicken fingers and French fries - so plain - absolutely no taste. Shame on their chef. We were so stupid to pay for it. $200 for 5 of us with no dessert. Their sangria drink we asked to replace for a beer. And their "low romantic lighting" can't hide a very dusty chandelier light fixture. EVEN WITH MY VERY STRONG STOMACK I GOT TO RUSH TO THE BATHROOM AFTER THEIR FOOD. STAY AWAY!!!

This is casual basic good food. I had breakfast today and it came out piping hot. The bacon was crispy but not greasy. The eggs were cooked through and the home fries had just the right amount of crisp.  The coffee was good and they kept the refills coming. I definitely want to come back to try the soup for lunch.

I have been to jose tejas on numerous occasions and have tried a number of different entrees, appetizers, and drinks. The food and service is always great. Try anything on the menu and you will not be disappointed. Also, their pina colada is the best I have ever had! Lastly, I am reluctant to mention this but I hope this will get the attention of the owners and/or the management. About a week ago I was circling for parking (parking is a pain in the butt on wknds) and I saw two ENORMOUS rats running from the direction of the kitchen towards the dumpsters. These were not the cute little mousey rats like the ones in the movie Ratatouille, they were...oh God just thinking about them makes me sick. Needless to say we turned our asses around and went elsewhere. Did that deter me from returning a week later to enjoy their delicious food? No...no it did not.

On a street where many restaurants have staff outside showing menus to passerbys to get business is Bistro Les Amis, I went here for brunch one saturday. I knew it had to be good by the fact they didnt need someone outside and that the tables inside were full. It was a little too chilly to sit outside, so we just got a table inside.  The tables itself are a little small, but the restaurant is very quaint.  I felt like I was in a cafe in france.  I had the bacon and bleu omelette which was pretty good.  Never saw bleu cheese offered in an omelette before, but it was quite good.  They originally brought me out the wrong order, but quickly came with the correct one, so that was fine.  The service was very attentive and they brought us more bread when we asked(which by the way was delicious).  I'd imagine this place is great for a date, but I'll have to come back for dinner to decide that.  Overall its a good restaurant in a good area of soho, away from all the traffic.  Would def recommend if in the area.

I have been meaning to try this place for awhile.  Well, I am glad I finally did! The burger was excellent!  I have gone to many places that tout their great burgers or have a great reputation, Two 8 Two has them all beat!  I have already gone back a second time to make sure the first time wasn't a fluke, it wasn't.  When I want to go out for a burger now, Two 8 Two will be my first choice.  Brought a California friend who always raves about In and Out Burger and her response after the first bite was 'Oh My God, it's delicious'. The service was also prompt and friendly and the prices were definitely fair for the quality being served up. The fries were also excellent, both the regular fries and the sweet potato fries...I haven't tried the Chili Cheese Fries yet, but I am sure I will in the near future.

The first thing I notice is the atmosphere, but it's the last thing I care about. Efficient wait system, put you name on the list hanging at the door. Open cooking area that gives you a good look at the big vat of fresh chicken broth being made and roast pork being seared in front of you. Nice. The kitchen is small but they turn out the bowls fast. I ordered the Chicken Paitan Ramen For a chicken broth, this was excellent. Just the right fatty content for a chicken broth. There was some rice floating around, which was just weird and distracting. The pork was good, but could have been a little more moist. Searing shouldn't dry it out, such is the point of searing. There was a good fat content though, so that saved it a bit. The noodles were very good. Cooked just right, they start out a little hard, but that what you want. Quickly they start soaking up the broth and get perfect. If the start out soft, they are a soggy mess by the end. The seasoned egg was excellent, but should be served as two halves. Also, you need to order it as an extra, it doesn't come standard. At $10 a bowl, it should be included. Boo. Service was attentive. Rating: Will definitely be back. Hopefully they'll have a pork broth for the fall. nycramenaddict.blogspot.…

This place is great! Awesome food & cheap but strong drinks. (8$) I love that you pick up the food from a food truck in the backyard, how cool is that!? The back yard is filled with tons of seating& solar powered lights. Awesome spot!

As someone who is very particular about how my eggs are done I was very happy to discover this place. The eggs are cooked through but not tough like at many breakfast places. The bacon is very good and well prepared, not too crispy, not too soft. Both Baker's blend coffee and Cafe Europa coffees are great. Even the potatoes are good, with nice spice and the middle melts in your mouth like butter. The French toast is little too sweet for my taste but also well prepared. It's been a while since I had such a pleasant breakfast experience. I will definitely be coming back frequently.

Completely not worth the price! I am not sure how the bill for three people was almost $100 for lunch! Extremely overpriced and overrated. The service was poor and the salad with strawberries consisted of a handful of arugula with two strawberries. Do not plan on ever going back. We left hungrier than before we arrived

When I visit my brother in Nutley, one of the places that I always hope to eat is this place.  I love their food there.  It's simple but captures the essence of Vietnamese food. I love the rice crepes.  The Vietnamese pork sausage with fish sauce is great!  I always get something with seafood (squid or shrimp), and the food is tasty (I concur about mustard greens being really good!).  The portions are great but it is a little pricey for the portions you get.

After being a Temple student for 2 years, I finally made it over to the Crepe truck. Man they are delicious. I had the tuna crepe, which included a ton of vegetables and mozzarella cheese. It was only $4.50, $5.25 with my drink, and it was HUGE. Better than any sandwich I could've gotten. My only complaint is that the sauces made it a little soggy toward the end, but the only way to fix that would be to eliminate the sauce. Both of my friends were satisfied, they had steak and pork I believe, and there is a nice array of beverage options. I can't wait to go back and try the dessert crepes!

Been here twice gotten the same this fries and the shroom burger.  Very disappointed with this place! I'm a vegetarian and I've tried a lot of veggies burgers in the past.  This one is 6.25 ish for a rather tiny fried ball of grease on a soggy potato bun. When I bit into the grease ball my mouth was scaled with liquid gross cheese. The fries look like they came from sysco frozen and refried.  I only got half through my meal before I was grossed out and left.  For a dollar more I could of gone to hip city and gotten a burger that tastes good and is adult portioned.

I love Employees Only! Went there for the first time with a friend and was skeptical because from the outside it doesn't look very nice. However, we you walk inside is cozy (a bit dark) and elegant. The drinks were amazing and the service was superb! The mixologist gave me a drinks menu, which I looked at but was still confused about what to order. He saw my face and asked me what kind of flavors I liked. He then proceeded to make a drink that tasted like heaven! I didn't taste the food but it smelled delicious.

Had the corn empanadas, plato paisa, and my wife had arroz con pollo. All gluten-free all pretty good. First the empanadas... very addictive. I could have just kept on eating more and more of them and would not stop. They were the equivalent of an Indian samosa with latin flavors. Very, very good. The aji sauce it came with (vinegar based) paired really well with the fried empanadas. Then the cocktails... the guava mimosa was waaay better than the orange one so give the tropical flavors a try. Wanted to try the mango one too but I'll wait til next time. AND trust me, there will be a next time. The plato paisa... soooooooooo good. The steak was marinated and cooked perfectly for such a think cut. The rice was excellent. Bacon was to die for and I ordered the chorizo and it was AWESOME. The slaw was a great companion to the food as well. All in all a very good but indulgent plate of food. The arroz con pollo however, could use some help... just sayin... Now for the best part...the service. Super friendly and helpful for my celiac, gluten free wife. They made sure that what was labeled GF on the menu is truly GF and that's a great relief. They have done their homework. We will be back for sure.
Akamaru Modern is seriously the best ramen I ate in NY. Their pork buns are a bit small and pricey. But their ramen took the cake! So good! It is definitely a 'must try.'

I really just cant get over how good everything is here. I have been about 5 times now and each one blows me away. I recently brought a group of 6 girlfriends with me, each sampling different grilled cheese selections, they each were amazed at how tasty they were.

This is my new favorite place!!! Last night it was my 4th or 5th time there and it keeps getting better.  A very diverse small, sexy and cozy hideout right in the village... The drinks are amazing and A+ for creativity. The food is fresh, tasty and delicious. The ambiance is FUN with different music from 80's, 90's and nice current artist. You can write your own confession on the walls of this place or read someone else's, anyway you are bound to stomp on few funny one that make the place warm and fun. The most important part though, is the People that work there. They make sure to Welcome you and assist you as soon as possible. Erika, the owner is a delight of a person and makes this place a unique one with her vision. My friends and I were impressed by how low key they are and how they ensure you are having a great time, even if is closing time, Oops! (just once!)   This place is perfect to go for drinks, or dinner, alone, as a couple, or in a group. I can't wait to try the winter menu, they told me they have some nice surprises. Can't wait to go there again and continue trying their sexy and funny drinks. My favorite so far is the Love affair and Devil's Advocate ;)
Amazing food. If your new to this place I highly recommend the tasting platter. Its the way to go. Great service. Nice place for a date night.

The food was good, the service was fine and yes the beer selection is huge, BUT wish they would serve some of the dishes they are known for instead of brunch only on Satuday. You can't get any of the really good mussel dishes they offer, nor can you get the shortribs. Burger was very good as its a blend of 3 cuts of meat put thru a grinder. Eggs benedict with crab instead of Canadian bacon came with a great Bernaise sauce. There is only one egg, but it is still a good dish. WIsh in the future they offer some of their other lunch items.

Went there a few months ago and the food was excellent.  This time, just OK.  Soup dumplings were delicious.  Pork with garlic sauce was very good.  Chicken with garlic sauce was just good.  Son's beef Lo Mein was bland.  Daughter's Sesame Chicken was huge globs of fried breading surrounding a speck of chicken.  Bill for 4 was $70, a little pricey for Chinese.  Also...no liquor license so BYOB.  Went on a cold night and people are CONSTANTLY opening the door since there are no reservations and it's always packed.  May seem minor but really unpleasant if you are sitting at the front part of the restaurant.

I can't stop coming back to Good Dog, it's like an addiction. The atmosphere, fun (seriously, how can you not smile when hundreds of photos of dogs are staring you in the face). Bartenders, fun. Food, AMAZING. Our group of friends has started using Good Dog as a meeting place so we can have lunch before doing whatever our Saturday afternoon plans are. Most of us have a menu staple - the Salmon ruben is by far my favorite thing on the menu. Some of my friends have a borderline physical addiction to the good dog burger. Of course if you're looking for something a little more leafy, even their salads are amazing.

I went to  The Good Fork this past weekend  -Never been to Red Hook before- Just found this place walking around-  I was by myself - Had a great time-!!!!! The food is really farm fresh - melts in your mouth - Had tasty butternut squash appetizer dish and a great pasta dish- The pasta was one of the best I ever had !!!- The food is delicious -food presentation was beautiful  Great service - Friendly bartender (I ate at the bar -the  owner was also very hospitable-  Go and check it out for yourself !!!!!!!= Marilyn from Manhattan

Best burger I've ever had... great service also. Came for the first time this week.. am already back. Great fries. Must try the prime chop house burger. Or the Cajun melt. Amazing... tons of veer options. Cool atmosphere..

Cafeteria is wonderful! The food is amazing.  Mac & Cheese spring rolls are ridiculous!  The cheese with the texture of the outer crust is delicious.  And don't forget the smoked gouda sauce.  I also had the burrata salad which was a wonderful combination of sweet (the grapes) and savory (the tomatoes) with the balsamic dressing bringing it all together.  And last but not least, the deep fried oreos with shake shots.  Its a lot to handle alone, but its perfect to share. My one complaint is that the service is slow.  They seem to have plenty of people working, but it took about 8-10 minutes for someone to greet us once we sat down.  That is a little too long.  And once we placed our entire order (apps and entrees) we did not see our server until the very end when we were asking for the check.  The bus boys were very good at keeping our water glasses full. Overall, I would highly recommend dining here.

Very disappointed that their happy hour prices are only for those sitting at the bar, not if you are at a table which may be three feet from the bar.  This is just plain silly, and as a result I will never go back again.  Its not the money its the principle.
There we go. Gave them another shot. Looks like they just had a really off day, or an off-batch. The miso soup is successful this time! The 3 roll combo was fresh and delicious :)

There is a lot of background story when it comes to this place, which I actually wrote out, but thanks to my stupid browser skills, I lost it.
