My friends have been telling me about this place now, since it opened.  They talked about the ingredients, the real fresh mozzarella.  How, it's the only place they'll get the pepperoni, because it's THAT good.  They talked about the owner/chef, who measured each and every pizza to his standard, and no one else's. I cannot describe the anguish these conversations would exact on my body and soul.  I have to thank Curt  and Slice of New York for helping assuage the torment, but still... No matter how much they talked it up though, I went last night and the goods matched the praise. I should give it one star and dissuade others to go there and help my friends who are locals, so they won't have to deal with crowds.  But nah...

I recently moved to Woodside. After arriving here and walking by Peking BBQ, two things came to mind. A. This place looks like a piece of shit. B. There are always people waiting inside. Normally that can only mean one thing.... it's awesome. I've now been in Woodside for about 6 months and I've eaten at PBBQ about 8 times. It's a prefect meal and super cheap. The chicken is succulent and they serve up some of the best fried rice out there. Can't beat this place.... go ahead and order a #1... you're welcome.
Ok service , and good food but bit pricey .

I went in ready to give this place a 4 based on the ambiance and prices, I couldn't avoid it-- a 5 had to be given. "Why?", you may ask... the food was excellent! Here are my humble opinions on everything we ordered: 1) Pork dumplings in chili oil- This was my favorite appetizer. The sauce was great. 2) Steamed duck buns? (I forget the exact name)- The flavor was good. I'm not a big fan of steamed buns in general. These were good, just not my personal cup of tea. 3) Drunken Noodles with Beef- Oh wow. I'm still dreaming about this dish. The flavor was phenomenal and the beef was nice n tender. 4) Green Curry with Tofu- Yum Yum Yum. 5) Spicy Fish entrée the Waiter recommended- I'm not really sure which one this was, but it was great! 6) Ahi tuna dumplings- These little guys were crispy and delicious. The ambiance was a little more upscale than I was imagining. There was colorful lighting with some louder club-ish music playing- I felt like we were in a swanky little lounge. Each entrée was very filling and about $15, which was really reasonable! I hope to come back to Philly just so I can chow down on some more drunken noodles!

I love this place! Great happy hour where you can their nachos for half off, and they are to die for! Regular margaritas are on special too, but they are inconsistent depending on bartender. I love the seitan spinach tacos, chorizo and potato tacos, pez(fish) tacos, and cochinita pibil tacos. My sister went and said the pork tacos are dry and I've heard the chicken ones are nothing special.

Came here with two friends last week after a volunteer event in LIC. We asked the coordinator to recommend a place, and she picked this one. Ehhhh. I had two arepas, the carne mechada (shredded beef) and the mami (roast pork and avocado). Overall, the flatbread was hard and dry and didn't seem fresh at all. The carne mechada meat was really dry even after slathering it in green sauce. The mami was good, but I was a bit wary of the grease pool leftover on the plate. And the much-hyped brown sugar lemonade was really sour. I did like the hot sauce though. Maybe I picked the wrong items or they had an off night, but I wasn't impressed. Oh and portion-wise, I would recommend 1 arepa + sides rather than 2 arepas + no sides.

My girlfriend lives for the roast pork mei and fried wontons, she orders it atleast 4 times a week. We tried a few different Indonesian restaurants and this is the best HANDS DOWN! Only downside is that this is a cash only establishment, but they do deliver!

After my multiple failed attempts of coming here I FINALLY CAME HERE!!! I was super excited since I was crazy katsu that day and for the price, you definitely get bang for your buck! I ordered, the pork katsu with that f... thing...and then some extra curry. Great! the rice could have been a little bit better it kind of tasted.. mushy.. but the katsu was fried perfectly and great flavor! This place would be a good place for a grub dinner and those metal trays that the katsu is served in reminds me of medival times castle that my middle school took me on for a field trip.. not so much feeling that part.
Whether you are a tourist, or just happen to be in the area, the pizza at this tiny joint is worth having at least once on your life.
Positive: Good food, decent lunch special price Negative: uncomfortable seats, small parking lot

Came here for a quick bite while my friends and I were waiting for a table to open up at Ippudo. I didn't have breakfast, so I was really craving some food. We originally tried to go to Central Perks, but it turns out that it was closed or it moved or something because there was no sign of a Central Perks nearby. We ended up yelping a cafe because none of us knew the area well. Up popped Ceci-Cela. Onwards we go! We were almost headed inside when we saw people with these delicious looking crepes right outside the door. The guy could totally tell we were staring at his crepe and he told us to give Eight Turn Crepe a try. That's how we ended up at this place. Automatic downside, it's a small place. Barely any sitting room. It's more of a grab and go place. Plus, the lights were flickering on and off the entire time we were there, which doesn't really add to the ambiance. Anyway, since we were headed to lunch soon, we didn't want to fill up on crepes, so my friend and I split one. We ordered the Strawberry Banana crepe. It was ready within a couple of minutes, but we had to step outside to eat it. The place was getting really crowded. The crepe was delicious and fresh. There was cream or yogurt, but it wasn't too overwhelming. Usually when I have cream in my crepes, I feel heavy afterwards. But this cream was very light and I didn't get that feeling afterwards. I was okay with the packaging. It reminded me of hot pockets. You had to rip off the paper as you were eating. Overall, had a great experience and I'll definitely be back soon!

I was born in Italy and lived there for 18 years before coming to the states. So naturally I have something BAD to say about this place. Really nothing special about this place, the highly reviewed pasta special is really bland and doesn't really taste like anything. I was embarrassed that I brought my parents here following some good reviews. There are many other great places in the area. Go there!

Went here for a birthday dinner with the hubs.  Overall, very good, cute BYOB on a cute block of Passyunk.   Since it was a birthday dinner, we opted for the 7 course tasting menu, which, while decadent, was not an insane amount of food.  Everything was delicious, especially the fish (I forget what kind) crudo, pate, and scallop with gnocchi.  The salmon and pork were yummy, but I felt like I could make something similar at home.   My only serious complaint is that many of the dishes were over salted.  I appreciate that restaurants use more salt than the home cook to make the food taste good, but it almost ruined a few dishes, in particular the spring pea soup amuse bouche, where the sweetness of the peas was completely overpowered by salt. Service was great: attentive and friendly.  It looked like it would be nice to sit at one of the outside tables.  I'd definitely like to go back!

I don't usually do Latin brunches, but I tried it at Yerba Buena -- I would never have guessed that Yerba Buena would be so packed at that time of day.  Well, it was and we stood waiting for about 40 minutes before a table opened up.  Note that this place takes reservations, and while ours didn't show up on screen, we were lucky to have worked something out with our (ahem) charms and "smooth talking". I came here with some friends, and I ordered the ensalada de pollo (chicken salad) which was light, savory, and quite tasty.  The portion was on the smaller side, but I was pleased with the quality so I didn't mind.  Instead, I satiated myself on $12 all you can drink - 2 mimosas and 2 peach bellinis.  By the time we were finished, we all left a bit light headed! Overall, service was pleasant and attentive. No complaints except the wait and occasional smell of chlorine, and the exponentially increasing delay to serve as we moved along on our drinks.  For me, I think Yerba Buena will be a remarkable one-timer.  For some restaurants, it's just destined to be that way.  4 stars for memory keepsake.

Came here for dinner after the wedding ceremony. The bride and groom had reserved the private room for the wedding party. Talk about fancy and well thought out, nice china, unlimited appetizers and of course the wine was flowing. I ordered the tuna tartare, Boston salad and the beer tenderloin with horseradish reduction all were absolutely delicious. You expect a certain kind of service and food standard from a 4 seasons restaurant and this one definitely delivers!!

The weather is finally cold enough for me to fully enjoy soup dumplings again! Came here early on a Sunday night (5:30pm) and had to wait 10 mins to be seated. I was a bit surprised that they were so crowded so early, alas there were throngs of people waiting by the time we left! As always, their soup dumplings (the regular pork kind) were the best! The scallion pancakes were fried to crispy perfection. If you're not sure what to order, pointing to the magnified pictures on the wall for assistance. We had the shanghai style noodles with shrimp and beef. They do a great job with these noodles, as their not too salty of in a pool of oil. Will be coming back here soon!

This place is awesome. Super tiiny but that just adds to its charm and coziness and didn't bother me at all. There was only one guy (Prob the owner) who was the host and waiter for all the tables. All the food came in a good amount of time. The mushroom cigars were amazing, we weren't sure what to expect but we were pleasantly surprised! The lamb was cooked perfectly with a ton of flavor and the chive mashed potatoes were also delicious. I also recommend the peanut butter pie - light and smooth and perfect. Also this place is BYOB with no corkage fee. My only complaint is that we were told that they needed the table back - we made a reservation at 6:30 and we left around 8:30. At a small place like that I can understand that they didn't want two people hanging around for a long time after they eat. I would definitely come back here, either for dinner or maybe for Brunch!
Great food and service.  I'm picky about my Cajun food.  Closest food to Nola I have found since I moved.

We sat here at the bar on Wednesday night and liked it so much we came after an art party at the Rubin on Friday night. Nice pours of wine ;) ... also try the smooth criminal. Oh my yumminess. I also had the grilled mahi-mahi fish taco appetizer which was very good. The drinks are a bit pricey but typical for the style and location of the restaurant. I'll go back for cockails but probably wouldn't do dinner there.

In all seriousness, I have no clue how this place stays in business. I'm not talking about quality - I'm talking about sheer weight of meat in their hoagies. I worked in a deli during high school - I have a general idea of what meat costs. I don't know how they do it. The hoagies are spot on despite their size (it's like a diner sized portion with the quality of a high end restaurant!). I have not found a better hoagie in all of my travels. They get busy during lunch but if you have an hour lunch break, it's worth giving up a chunk of time to wait for this quality!

Attentive service, very pricey. We arrived at 830pm with a reservation and were promptly seated. Took a bit for our expensive martinis to arrive. Good, but nothing worth the 12$ each. Calamari was good but came perched on a huge piece of wilted cabbage that took up most of the dish. Flatbread was good; tangy sauce and super thin. I had the sausage and Rabe pasta, and my wonderful girlfriend got the duck. Duck was excellent but again came paired with a wilted vegetable garnish that was both garish and unappetizing. My pasta was average, but cost 23$! For pasta shells with very little sausage and some Rabe, I was robbed. We finished with a desert of hazelnut mousse cake topped with espresso cream, which was outstanding. Light and fluffy and had a pleasant understated flavor; simply awesome. The food was above average overall and the service was good, if a bit slow at the beginning. But the pricing is high for what you get, especially for pasta dishes. My recommendation is to definitely try the restaurant out, like we did. Just avoid the overpriced martinis and pasta and you might end up having a great dining experience. Oh and avoid the weird radicchio wilted mess that comes with most of these dishes, it tastes like grandmas socks. P.S.Our server, Lynn was very good.

Pulled pork better, I mean way better than the roast pork.   Don't be fooled, get the PULLED PORK.   Went here again and grabbed the brisket, pulled pork with provolone and sweet peppers and a roast pork with broccoli rabe and provolone.  My mother and Aunt split the brisket sandwich and they seemed way more than pleased.  I got the pulled pork and was so glad.  It was like an upgrade from the roast pork.  But my wife did get the roast pork with the cheese and broccoli rabe and was really happy, so no denying that their product is good.

So it's cramped; whatever - in my experience, best eggs in Hell's kitchen. I had the scrambled pancakes with a side of scrambled eggs (the side of eggs wasn't on the menu but the waiter was really nice). My friends had the goat cheese scramble with spinach, and the vegetarian sandwich. Nothing but raves on the food. The coffee was fresh and refills were swift. Couldn't ask for more.

Been coming to Blue Ribbon Brasserie for about 8 years or so and it is always consistently good food and service. Hands down they alway get it right.  My favorites to order are oysters, ribs, bone marrow and oxtail marmalade, steak tartare, fried chicken and complete it with cream brulee. Excellent wine and cocktails too!! Do it!!

Great neighborhood gem found! I hope they're here to stay! Been eyeing this place since they've opened and was a little skeptical to try but decided to given their great reviews. The zucchini pancakes were awesome, lightly crunchy on the outside and a healthy mushy center. The hummus was really good too, full of spices. It's not the usual hummus where it sits in a bed of olive oil. The octopus was just perfect and tender to the bite. Ribeye was great, steak was great. The chocolate raspberry cake was delicious with its rich chocolate frosting. The portions are good here too. I have no complaints! We saw the table next to us order the stuffed peppers...it looked delicious, will definitely order that next time. Service is also very good. Will definitely be coming back!

If you are willing to wait for 30 mins outside just to get inside then another 15 minutes to be seated, then you are in for a great treat.  We didn't have much expectation except that it is conveniently located across the Metropolitan Museum of Arts. But their menu while limited and maybe a bit pricy, it's all worth it. I have the sausage with sauerkraut and Dijon. I must say it was delicious. Their spicy egg with paprika is also excellent. But their desserts are the real surprise.  The Vienna Dark chocolate cake and apple strudel were out of this world.

This place is excellent. Very happy that I live a block away. It was recommended to me by a co-worker, so I figured that I would try it. I had never tried milk fish before. It was excellent. They also educate you on the food and the sauces. The cocktails are also amazing. Seriously good.

While I've heard a lot about this place from family, I never got a chance to try the food! I arrived around 7:40pm on a Thursday evening, we were told the wait would be 30 min. We said we'd wait. 50 min later, we were told we were next. When I asked the hostess where we were in line, she gave me a snippy, "you're coming up soon" and ran off. 5 groups AFTER that we were finally seated. Once seated, someone came by with menus and sliver-ware and that was it. For 10-15 minutes, we sat as the waitresses passed us by. No greeting, no asking for drinks, NOTHING! At that point we got up and left. It's a shame that I never got to try their famed grilled corn, but I will certainly not spend one penny at a restaurant that does not treat their guests properly... no matter how busy the establishment may be! If you go to this restaurant, plan on waiting MUCH MUCH longer than they tell you, and don't expect any fast service after that either!

Surprised by all the Big Fish haters. This has been my business travel standby for many years. Big Fish will serve you fresh fish, unlike most other nearby places. I've occasionally had a piece that whiffed, but more frequently the day's catch is of very high quality. The bar service, happy hour menu, and bread basket are also pluses. Alas, complaints about service and unjustifiable prices are reasonable. The prices, though high, are about in line with the Princeton area. +1 star for Danielle, an excellent bartendress!

Dive bar with lots of places to sit and great selection of beers on tap. Very good prices as well. The bartenders were great, very patient and knowledgeable. Bathrooms are big, but there is only one of each. They would do themselves a favor to add a few stalls, instead of the one toilet in each.

The restaurant is tucked in a nice quaint town in NJ.  It's a small restaurant, where the food is packed with great flavor and taste.  The only flaw I had with the restaurant was the prices, it was a bit high for what we are used to. The decor had a nice modern ambiance, which was comfy.  The service was immaculate for a small quaint restaurant.  The Malai Kofta, chicken tikka and mutter paneer are very tasty and delicious. I will come back to this restaurant as long as I am within the area.

I have heard sooo many good things about this spot! Unfortunately I give it a 2 star because of the service. Let me give you a run down right quick PROS: Lovely area! Makes you want to buy a bike with a basket and put a little yorkipoo in it! Food was okay. I ordered pancakes with sausage (nasty) and hashbrowns...which the hashbrowns were BOMB! Pancakes really tasted homemade and light...sadly I love ihops pancakes way better. YIKES! CONS: The hostest was really nice but thats not what made the experience bad...She was OVERLY nice...so nice we waited an hour and some change to be seated and the place wasnt super packed as expected! There was a group of women who finished there meal about 10 min ago and was just sitting there talking about how lonely and single they are (im sure). The hostest asurres me that their tap is being rung up and we should be seated in 10 min. Kool...but then 20 min pass by...and I ask politely if there getting up soon. She said o yes they are.....OKAY 45 min go by and my friend walks in there and tempts to ask the group of ladies nicely when will they be done?...but before she could finish...the hostest said "They'll be done when there ready" WTF!? How rude of her to let paying customers who have been so patient wait for overly talkative women just sit there like their the only freaking people in the world!..I think the hostest should have politely told the group another party is waiting to be seated. She was waaaay to nice in letting them just sit there. She had no balls to tell them to get their butts up!.....but since she told my friend "they'll be done when their ready" was an invitation for the group to chill longer..which they did!!! No way! With that said....I dont care much to go back....food wasn't all that. ihop NEXT STOP!

I first went here in 2003 when I lived in Queen Village for a year!  My husband, at the time, was Moroccan and he found this place very authentic and we are their a lot!  I just moved back to Society Hill this spring and I started going here again!  I love this place - grape leaves, kabobs, hummus and olives and feta is my favorite!  Also the babaganosh (sp?) is excellent!  Eat in or take out no difference!  I think they've been there 35+ years!

No Philly trip is complete.....yadda yadda yadda.... Come for the experience, I suppose, but the sandwich  - wit wiz - is average.  Eat here late and drunk like I did.  Please, oh please, do not make this your dinner if you are visiting.  There are far better places for lunch and dinner than this (e.g. National Mechanics for lunch, Matyson for dinner) if you are in the city.   And for Pete's Sake (or Geno's or Pat's) if you people want a REAL sandwich, go to Jimmy's on Belmont Avenue in good ol' Youngstown, Ohio.
Toroniku Ramen.....my mouth waters just thinking about it.....
Great prices for good size yummy portions. Whats not to like?

Took a friend for his 50th birthday. We walked the grounds- had such a good time. I am sure the bottle of champagne I had before then helped. we had some 'fun' in the grounds and took a bunch of photos. We then had a nice dinner in the less formal area- he was in that mood. After we took over the floor seating by the fireplace with a few after dinner drinks. What a good time and service was great- bartender was great.  I just reminded myself to go back!!!!

The food is a mixed bag. Some dishes are unbelievably great however specials were anything but. The service is mediocre at best with menu shoved in front of you with no explanation. The wine service provided was excellent however when a main was cited as lacking no solution was offered. Why ask if you're not going to do something? Overall, bad return of value for money and service was atrocious. Look for somewhere better. They exist.
Perfect falafel and chicken platter. Fast and friendly service!
Their almond milk (housemade almond milk) latte is AMAZING. I've never had anything like it. I also loved the quiches and treats we got there. I wish they had one in San Diego!

Hubby and I dined here midweek, celebrating his birthday, and we were surprised to see the dining room so full, given the economy. Most of the other diners seemed to be on their company's tab. I had the prix fixe dinner with seafood gumbo, broiled salmon, sauteed mushrooms, and mini mousse cups with berries. The gumbo was N'awlins quality -- thick and spicy -- and I consider myself a gumbo connoisseur. The salmon was a large, deliciously seasoned filet, but I had asked for it very rare and it came medium-well. The server did offer to take it back but I can't justify wasting food like that. (If it had been well done or overdone, as Big Fish usually makes it, I would have, though. So good thing I asked for very rare, or it probably would have been overcooked.) The mushrooms were okay -- not worth ordering a la carte, but fine for a prix fixe offering. Mousse cups were yummy. Hubby had Ruth's chop salad, a very rare T-bone, sweet potato casserole, and creme brulee. All were excellent and he was very pleased with his meal. The staff was very friendly when talking to you but service was slow and not particularly attentive.  In fact, we had to request more water when both our glasses sat empty for over 5 minutes. Other reviewers here seem to think the service was good, so maybe all those large business gatherings distracted them? The wine list was pricey, as expected, but the offerings were good. We rate the food at 5 stars and the service at 3 so overall it gets 4 stars.

Awesome Burgers but a little messy. If you can get past that you are in for a delicious burger!  Good price and big portions, I will def be going back. Also a lot to choose from then just burgers, they have chicken sandwiches and hot dogs too

I have been coming here since it opened, and am never disappointed.  I recently took a friend here that was visiting from abroad. He travels a lot and has been to many restaurants.  I always try to pick a "local" place that he will enjoy.  I'd not taken him here before as they didn't take reservations for a while.  Thankfully they do now and it makes the world of difference. As soon as we walked in my friend was impressed by the ambiance of the place.  It is very warm and welcoming, in winter as well as summer.  The food was delish, and fresh.  He had a pasta special with duck ragu that he was impressed by.  I had the gnocchi with pesto sauce (it comes with a different sauce but they are quite flexible with whatever you would like to order) which was light and tasty. The wine selection was good and affordable.  I have always like that they do change the wine list on occasion and you will come across some wines that you won't find in most other restaurants.  I don't think I've ever had a bad wine here tbh. The patio out back is lovely for sitting outside, or there are seats in front. Highly recommend and will keep going back.

Another hole in the wall sushi joint, in the middle of NJ that is an absolute gem! Place is tiny, but those who eat there are definitely regulars. Waitress was on top of her game and gave us fresh recommendations. I suggest the ... Spicy crispy crunch Elizabeth roll Saba (pickled themselves!) Flying fish roe Probably the best miso soup I've ever had. Definitely a place I would revisit.

It was 11PM and I was running time square in heels dodging every sewage/drain hole to get to this place in time before it closed. No lie, this place was in the cuts hiding in the darkest streets ever. I made it just in time to pick up the red velvet slice... I did this shit all backwards. But, it's all worth it in the end.

it was Yuca Bar to the rescue last night when we were told at our original destination (Bourgeois Pig) that there was an hour long wait for a table.  "there's a tapas place near here that my friend really likes," i said, and just as i was pulling out my phone to call her and ask where it was, i realized that it was right across the street.  that made that easy. we were seated immediately, somehow, even though the place was bustling, and i'm not sure why other reviewers have complained about the service because i thought it was great.  our waiter appeared at exactly the right time to take our drink order, our food order, and our second-round-of-drinks order, and he was very friendly.  so we were happy already, and then our drinks came and they were delicious, and then our food came and that was delicious, too.  plus, everything was so reasonably priced -- $5 for the mojitos, margaritas, and caipirinhias till 8pm and half-priced tapas on tuesday nights -- so we each spent about $20 for 2 drinks, 4 tapas split among the 3 of us, and tax + tip.  that's pretty damn good. don't get me wrong, i still adore BP, but Yuca Bar is more than just a back-up plan: it's dilemma-inducing latin deliciousness. **update 4/18: i've been back many times for consistently excellent dinners, but today was the first time i'd been for brunch.  and it, too, was delicious!  i got to try the crab cake benedictos and the arepas benedictos, and they were both great.  yuca bar comes through for me every time.
Woohoo

Their baby back ribs, pulled pork and burnt ends (with the original sweet sauce) blow away any other ribs in Connecticut ... or anywhere else outside of Tennessee in my experience. Fall off the bone, sauce that makes you lick your fingers. And their coleslaw! Perfect. Sliced (not chopped) fresh cabbage, some carrots, black pepper, vinegar, and no gross mayonnaise. So don't miss their North Carolina "everything" hot dog--with chili, coleslaw, the works. Their jalapeno mashed potatoes have WAY too many jalapenos -- and this is from someone who likes jalapenos. But I'm not gonna take off a star just for that. Even if they served nothing but those baby backs, they would deserve 5 stars.

Suspenseful process to get a reservation and witty email request resulted in a tailored response (+1).  Courteous and helpful servers (+1).  Delicious cocktails; the jaguar was well-blended (japanese whiskey based drink, highly recommend) (+1).  Tasteful food with reasonable prices given quality (+2).  Oh, we had the uni croquette, beef sashimi, mac/cheese, pickles, burgers and soba, read the other reviews for more detailed explanations.  Portions were not as tiny as expected.

Half off appetizers from 4-7pm. I'm a happy camper. Suggestions: Honey wings - AMAZING Grilled Chicken Quesadilla - Equally AmazinG! Plantains for a little fun - crispy and oh yeah Amazing. Great and attentive Bartender/Waitstaff as well. Great location close to train station. I would give more stars, but as someone else mentioned, some of the main courses could be a bit tricky. For example, the fried rice comes with a lot of dishes and it is a little dry. Some of the dishes could use a little less salt as well.

The standard tap is more than a bar to me. The Standard Tap is like an old friend. Consistent and loyal, always welcoming, no matter how long I stay away. The food is great, and their are plenty of options. they have a nice beer list, and I always find something I want. The music never disappoints, and I can almost hear it whisper" I know you love this song, Steve" They are known for their burger, but in the countless times I have been there, I have never had one. Too many other choices. some of my favorites are bratwurst and sauerkraut, chicken pot pie, Muscles and chorizo and the lamb sandwich. Like an old friend, I probably take the Tap for granted. I might forget to mention it when discussing "must try spots" I know it doesn't need me to sing it's praises, but its always nice to hear, so... I love you buddy, thanks for being you.

Had my first wiz wit from Pat's way back in the day. Tasted Geno's and thought it was less fatty so went there for a while.  But Pat's is back on the map with the best wiz wit around. Forget the mushrooms folk's, save that for your pizza.
I love their food and desserts. However the last brownie I had tasted like fridge..yuk!

I have had delivery from Volcano about 7 times. Food is usually good. A few times I was not happy with the quality. They used to deliver and separate the cold items from the hot items. They no longer do this. So your hot soup will be sitting next to the cold sushi. Decent stuff, not exceptional.

Astonishing that so many Yelpers are gaga over Balthazar.  My  wonderful husband and I arrived at 6 pm, the only time we could get a reservation, and the door was chock-a-block with tourists.  The pretty young woman behind the reservation dias was on the phone and completely distracted and everyone waited around for a while.  When we were finally ushered to our table, the meal was a blur. Once our polite waitress took our order, our appetizers were out immediately.  Several wait staff hovered while we ate.  The moment we were finished, our entrees, which had been on a buffet near our table, were presented.  We were interupted numerous times during romatic conversation with an obligatory "is everything okay?"  The food was decent but I've never felt so pushed through a meal in all of my dining experiences in New York.  Balthazar is clearly about "turning the tables."  And as to the "scene," well, great, but you can see a lot of these tourist prowling around 5th Avenue and SoHo.  It's all about the money, baby!
This place is practically the only thing at South Street Seaport that is back in fighting shape after Hurricane Sandy (as of June, 2013!) As good as new. Drunken fish soup is still the best.

Awesome food!  I've ordered a different sandwich every time I've been there and they're all amazing!  I highly recommend the mackerel/leek sandwich or the portabella sandwich, two personal favorites of mine.  The place itself is a hole, but that's usually where the best food is found.  I only mention that because I passed right by it the first time I went there, no awning or sign and it was a rare occasion where there weren't customers spilling out the door.  All in all I love this place and will continue to support them as long as they're cooking up those sandwiches.

Loved the wrap shack when it had a shop in Old City. The Rittenhouse location has a bar which is nice....got a couple of beers and the buffalo chicken wrap. Perfect combination.  Very low key spot. Had a lovely time.
Nice ambiance, good food.

Everyone talks about how great this place. I personally think it's just alright. My only knock is that it's a little pricey for the portions. It can also be a bitch to get good seating at the bar but I suppose that's because I've only gone at peek hours.

I dediced to have my birthday party here for the big 2-9.  I gave a buzz and they were thrilled from the get-go to have us.  We ended up as a group of 15.  They gave up a private room on the 3rd floor that we all fit into perfectly.  The decor of this place is absolutely amazing. The waiters were attentive the food was delicious, and the BYO component was INCREDIBLE.  They did a great job of accomodating vegetarians, non-lamb-eaters etc.  The total came to $33 a head with tax and tip included, and we'd ate a ton, drank even more, danced with the belly dancer, and laughed for hours.  I love this place, I always have, and the way they handled my birthday really only elevated Marrakesh in my mind.  It's not the kind of place you can go to all of the time.  It's a longer meal, and a lot of foods, but I'll certainly be back here as soon as the mood strikes, and I will recommend it to everyone and anyone looking for a change of pace.  These guys have class.
Every time I eat at this place I run to the bathroom. I will not return to this place now that chipotle is open!!!!

I have been twice before for wine and a snack, but this was my first dinner experience and it was disappointing. They really try to upsell you (which I'm sure is part of their remit, but it's awkward nonetheless).  They explain that the food is best shared so you should order a lot of plates. That you really should order a plate of meats and cheeses to start, before all the plates of food you want to order.  After we ordered, they pretty much asked if we were sure we didn't want to order more plates. More than once.   I felt like I should apologize for only ordering a soup and a pizza, but that is what I wanted.  Ditto for one of my friends who got 3 cheeses and one of the plates from the meat section as her meal.   As they tell you, the plates are small.  A pasta small plate is not entree size, but with an app I think it's enough for a girl.   It is a little pricey for the portion sizes so my expectations were high. Onto the food.  This is more subjective, but I didn't love my meal.  The pizza I ordered was described as chorizo and clams, with a white bean béchamel.   It was very heavy on the beans, had a few bits of meat, and I didnt see or taste clam.  My friend liked the mushroom/truffle one. My soup was the potato with scallop and bacon, and that was tasty. I tasted my date's pasta dish and thought it was underwhelming.  It had a bunch of ingredients, but it mostly tasted like runny egg yolk.  He also wasn't a fan. Another odd policy is that they are byob, but charge a $10 corkage fee after the first bottle. You are still better off bc the wine list is $10+ per glass.  But why do this when most places in Philly don't ? I wanted to like it. I feel like saying this implies that I'm not a cultured, adventurous eater or something, but I just wasn't that into it.

The New Wave Cafe is one of those places I will stop by while in the neighborhood, but like the neighborhood itself (sorry, QV-ers), it's generally unremarkable. A great selection of beers, for sure, and a friendly staff to back it up.  Once a friend and I played a game of Scrabble at the bar, and got some tips from the staff and patrons alike.  It was the most participatory game of Scrabble I've ever played. The decor is so-so - along with the jukebox, which was one of those expensive computer kinds.  The New Wave isn't terrible by any means - it just doesn't do much for me.

ya-hoo! what a find.... meggy & i kinda ended up here on accident, kinda. and when GPS got us there, we ended up in a strip mall across from a dennys next to a liquor store... it didn't look like much from outside. Then we took one step in the door, and everything changed! Great atmosphere, mood lighting, pretty blue lights and hold on here it comes.....happy hour! sushi & beer! The whole staff was super friendly but not annoying, the sushi, edamame and beer were fantastic and the price was right. Clean bathrooms, the absolutely only thing I would change is the music... kinda elevator-y. But then a guy came out and played live music so yeah, this place is great.

Best meal in New Haven right now. First of all the interior is stunning. But the food is just spot on. Everything is simple, clean, and delicious, without trying to be French or Italian or whatever the concept is. It has influences from alot of places, but is most of all what was fresh and delicious around New Haven. The atmosphere allows a great long casual dinner, and on top of it all, the price is extremely reasonable. Two people with multiple drinks, apps, entrees, and desert and exactly 100 buck. I would pay alot more to eat that meal again.
Good burgers with unlimited fries and drinks!

I went here for happy hour a few weeks ago, and as I was disappointed that there was no "happy hour" I was not disappointed in  my experience in village whiskey. The drinks were fantastic- great exotic combinations. The veggie burger was probably the best I have ever consumed. I have been here several times when I cannot even get in for a seat, so be prepared. The drinks are small and expensive but delicious, but hte food is reasonably priced. I will definitely be back!
Got the grilled chicken platter. Tasty but why was everything cold? My friend swears by them, so I'll give them another shot.

Yummmm. Especially the porchetta. And that's coming from someone who does not eat pig meat (although she tries it from time to time to she if her taste has changed). We held a bridal shower here. Jacque was awesome and worked out all out needs. I would certainly recommend to anyone, even if it's just for a pork sandwich.

As many other reviews for the Rib House mention, this establishment seems a bit dated & run down both inside and out. I stopped in for lunch with a coworker one afternoon. My coworker ordered the baby back ribs, I ordered the St. Louis style ribs. Both were tough & still stuck to the bones. What they are calling barbecue sauce would do better as a sweet & sour sauce on a Chinese buffet, I'm glad I had it put on the side. I was told the ribs have a nice rub on them but could find no evidence of a rub or marinade. I felt the baked beans & coleslaw  came out of cans or paper cartons. They both tasted alright but definitely didn't taste like they were made in house. If this was voted the best ribs by the New Haven Advocate I have a hard time believing the reviewers know anything about barbecue.
Great cocktails, fantastic affordable wine list, best burger in NYC, love everything they do.

Best Italian food in the state. Everything on the menu is delicious and the service is outstanding. Can honestly say I've ever had a negative experience at Gabriele. The bread alone is worth the visit!!
The fries are ok, the dippings are very good. Mango and garlic are my favorites.

Very good pizza.  I especially enjoy their specialty pizzas like the buffalo chicken pie.  One slice is like a meal. Hero sandwiches are good and are sold for a very reasonable price.  The pizzeria's location is right across from the large public high school so expect large crowds between 2:30-3:30.

I love the pizza here. My friends and I have been going for about four years now and we all love it. Their personal pies is enough to fill a person and have a couple slices left over. Never really tried anything else there but the pizza is definitely worth it.

I've walked by this cart a few times, and tended to think it couldn't be any different. But I always see a huge line. So we decided to try it. We waited about 30 minutes, and we finally got our combo platter. We only got one because we wanted to save room to try to other places. When we got our platter, it was amazingly good. Everything is well-seasoned, the sauce adds a kick with the spice, and the meats are tender. We devoured it and regretted that we didn't get two. Next time...

Short and sweet on this one. I've eaten @ almost every place on this street over the corse of a lifetime. Some are better than others, others are the cookie cutter variety, still others serve dishes that set them apart or offer a nicer atmospher. Either way I feel it's more or less a nice exsperience. This was a pleasant reprieve from the rainy hot Saterday nite stroll. We ducked in for a cocktail & small plates. Rocky was our server. He was warm, gracious & professional. The type of better end service  one anticipates in LT. Nice glass of Pellegrino w lemon, Proseco- on the drier side. Ceasar salad w grilled calamari (pan fried not grilled but nicely done), stuffed artichoke which was cooked properly but I didn't care for the anchovies, capers. A little too much bread crumb & not enuff broth for dipping. But overall, it was fine. Pleasant interior but on the very low lighting side. Great service. Clean. Average prices.

I've always been a firm yelper...taking the word of my fellows seriously. To say I was looking forward to this would be an understatement!! Couldn't wait to try it. Headed down for a late brunch, around 4:30, we had a half hour wait, but, the weather was so beautiful, I barely noticed the time pass. Got a seat at the table right next to the kitchen window...for me thats a good thing, I like to see how things are done. We ordered a coffee, hot chocolate, the southern breakfast, clinton st. omelette and a stack of pancakes to share. Not a long wait on the food at all, maybe 15 minutes. As the plates arrived, my first impression was wow, not what I thought it would look like. First glance, the grits were an odd cheddar color. The hubby's omelette had an oddly smooth texture on the top of it, the potatoes looked plain. Now, like I said, this was at first glance. I didn't want to make assumptions, so I dug in with delusions of grandeur dancing in my mind. Without being long winded, my breakfast was awfully mediocre. The eggs tasted as if they used pre mixed eggs in the cartons, commercial, mass cafeteria kinda feel! The grits were bland, thick, luke warm and saltless. The "sugar-cured" bacon...lmao. I don't know about the cured part, but, limply cooked with some sugar tossed on is probably a bit more accurate. The fried green tomatoes were just that...I preferred the movie. My hubbys omelette was pretty bad, unfortunately. He was anticipating freshly cut and grilled peppers in a sea of buttery, fluffy eggs. Instead he received soggy peppers, most likely canned/jarred in a not so tasty "egg like" concoction. The brioche bread was dry. The "hash browns" were a ball of unseasoned, potatoes fried hard on the outside and barely cooked inside. At this point, I was hoping that the pancakes would be the saving grace of the meal...I wanted to love Clinton St. Baking Co. The pancakes were fluffy and tasty, can't complain about that at all. They were perfectly golden and the addition of the maple butter syrup saturating the soft layers of goodness further cemented the fact that this is their staple product. Though I loved them, it couldn't erase the whole experience that was overshadowed by the bad meals. The $13 pancakes were barely a band-aid to remedy this debacle. If the prices were that of Ihop, I would lower my standards and not expect so much, but, their prices are a far cry from such and I expected way better than I got. All in all, for $51. 27 plus tip, I'll take a pass on Clinton St. in the future. That's a hell of a bill for a sub par breakfast/brunch. I usually rationalize paying that much for food that's great.  I don't know what it used to be like here, but, it's far from that now. Maybe its a change of cooks, ingredients, whatever! I've been throughly disappointed in our general Yelp consensus of Clinton St. Baking Co.!!!

Reading Terminal Market has a ton of different choices from breakfast to desserts, so if you're unsure of what's in the area or if you want something quick, try any of the little shops here. Have a good look around before deciding on anything. Most places take credit cards. Definitely stop at the donut shop in the morning. Warm just-made donuts!!!!! WHAT! There's a great spice shop that carries every spice under the sun - amazing to peruse.

"Never again", I said to myself because the wait was insane. Since then, I ended up going back twice already. Sadistic? Nope, I've just figured out when to go to minimize the wait. Forget the weekends. Go on occasions when you have a free weekday. And even so, do not go before noon. Best of luck! Love: - buttermilk biscuits - sugar cured bacon - hot apple cider

*Cash only* Hoagie Haven is an institution in Princeton. The sandwiches are HUGE so be forewarned - a half size is plenty for most. My two favorite items are their buffalo fries (french fries coated in hot sauce and the most delicious mild blue cheese sauce) and their cheesesteak. Pro-tip: order double meat on the cheesesteak. Just do it.

family style is the way to go here, and stick with the pastas. Warm room, nice buzzy feel, not as expensive as we expected. Good for a birthday or special occasion for sure. Fun to meet at bar in hotel before or after too.

**TOO CHEESY FOR ME** With all the rave reviews on Yelp, I expected it to be a WOW experience, but alas, it did not WOW me like the others. Granted, Scott was very passionate about pizzas, but a bit too nerdy for  me. There were three pizza parlor stops: Lombardi's, Joe's, and John's. We spoke to some neighborhood Italians on the way and they told us that these were not the best pizza places; just historical pizza landmarks. So if you expect the best pizza pie experience, you may be disappointed. We were not interested in visiting a pizza supply store, so we stopped by Ray's on Prince instead and ordered the Sicilian which was very good. Again, this was my personal take on the tour, it just wasn't for me.
Soondodu is just OK. Can't compare with another Korean restaurant I've been to. But the kal Bi is so great. You must try it.

Let me preface this with I've been to a lot of the brunch spots in Philly -  honey sit n eat,  green eggs,  Sabrinas cafe,  cafe lift,  and breakfast boutique. They all offer something a little different and its hard to impress me because I tend to be a picky eater.  However,  Cafe La Maude takes the cake in terms of freshness of food and quality of service. When you enter, its got a definite cozy European cafe feel to it.  Parking is sparse but by chance we ran into the owner who was so sweet and offered us a spot nearby.  He even dropped by later at our table inquired where we were from and how we heard about his place.  My friends and I all respectively enjoyed our meals and the serving size was pretty large.  Come with a hungry appetite :) I only wish this was closer to Elkins park because this is my favorite brunch location in Philly!
Can't complaint, but not recommended.

BIIIIG portions. Be ready to share or take home lots of leftovers. Food was good. I understand its a Portuguese restaurant but if it is clear the customers do not speak Portuguese lets go to English instead of continually speaking Portuguese and confusing everyone. Liked the parking lot across the street for customers.

The service is terrible!!! The guy in charge skipped some people when they stand in the line waiting to be served. I think the staff there think they are the GOD. Customer has to worship them. Soup is very very salty. Bad bad experience. We will never come again.

Wow, what an incredible meal. My girlfriend and I shared two appetizers that were to die for: the grilled octopus and ricotta gnocchi. (I absolutely recommend the latter dish, it was maybe the tastiest gnocchi I've ever had). We then shared the Chicken Tagine, served on a bed of couscous and raisins. The meat fell right off the bone. The serving sizes were just right. The service was also phenomenal, making a tasty meal into an overall delightful evening. Our server, Taylor, was wonderful. She made excellent recommendations and was always by our side to refill our glasses, even despite the busy Saturday night dinner crowd. Thank you, Taylor! Will absolutely be visiting again!
Dario's is amazing. I always get the tortilla bowl,  and the flavors always deliver.  They are well worth the price. If you're arround the area,  I would recommend coming here at least once.

I ordered a large cheesesteak pizza, buffalo wings & fries on Saturday night @ 10:00 pm, anxiously waiting 20 minutes to sink my teeth into a juicy oozing cheese pizza slice. Lo & behold when me & my boyfriend received our pizza, we opened our box & to our dismay, saw a plain cheese pizza with a side of soggy limp fries. We ate a slice of pizza each & were pretty grossed out by the stale yeasty taste. The only good thing about our experience were the mild buffalo wings which even though they were mild, had good flavor & had plenty of meat on each wing. Frustrated, I called Trios again & told them about our situation, & was told that the guy who took my order incorrectly had already left. So the woman who heard what I had to say gave me a credit for a new pizza & entered my information into their computer system. Based on the experience that I've had with Trios, despite the good reviews, I'm pretty sure I won't be redeeming that free large pizza anytime soon.
Nothing great. Bland food. My guest got food poisoning after. Unreasonably small portions. Good decor and vibe.
Came here for lunch while in town. Usually a quick lunch is one that I dont put in high regard but these guys did it right. Delicious chicken chow mein and dumplings.

I had the Seared Uni Bowl twice in three days, each with a 30 minute, then 20 minute, wait.  If that doesn't say something about how much I like it, I don't know what does.  The sweet freshness that is uni charred by the blow torch then topped over seaweed-sprinkled, shoyu-drizzled rice with a dab of grated wasabi root - so. good.   The spicy ramen and the cha siu pork bun are good too, but my favorite is the uni bowl.  The spicy bamboo is not worth getting. Expect a wait, even at 10:30pm on a Saturday night, and cash only.

So I FINALLY made it out to SoCo after hearing about this place since the summer... and I can report that I was not disappointed!  This spot is def for the young, black, & fabulous.  Beautiful people, fantastic dj spinning neo-soul and r&b classics, and good food.  If you're about ambience, this is the place to be. Came on a Sunday for brunch after church.  Had the Chicken & red velvet waffle since it sounded unique & this is supposedly their specialty.  Chicken was good & tasty, but I did not like the taste of the red velvet waffle.  Was very doughy & not sweet enough.  Didn't taste anything like what you would expect from red velvet.  Very overrated.   BUT, my creamy cheese grits were off the chain!  Rich & creamy, and since I'm from the south I consider myself a grits connisseur.  I did not have the mac & cheese (trying to stick to new years resolution & not blow out the calories), but would def come back to try them.   Overall, good brunch meal & fun dining experience.  Will def return.

Wow. Just wow. I think I'm in love with this place. The skirt steak sandwich makes vegetarianism sound like death. It's so tender, juicy, and perfectly spiced. To top it off, delectable chili mayo takes the sandwich to even greater heights. The pickles are also a must-try. If I were an incredibly rich bottom-less pit, I may make myself sick here trying every sandwich. The hardest part of your meal will be choosing what to order.

This was the 2nd time that this restaurant tried to pass quarter hainese chicken for half a chicken!!! I told the the server that it didn't look like half a chicken there and she told me that it's not really half a chicken (and her fingers signaling quotations).  So, I asked her then why am I being charged for half a chicken when I'm not getting "half a chicken?"  She called over the manager.  He came over, dug around the plate of chicken with a fork and told me it is half a chicken.  I told him that there was no breast meat on the plate; so how that that be half chicken.  He took it back and 10 mins later, appeared half a chicken.  The manager disappeared somewhere in the kitchen and we heard not one word of apology from anyone. Terrible service.  Just one word of advice:  CHECK YOUR FOOD TO MAKE SURE THAT'S WHAT YOU'RE PAYING FOR!!!
Cool grinding of seasame for the Tonkatzu. Oden with Daikon was nice. Spicy tonkatzu ramen was not impressive.

The food here was beyond outstanding. Every first bite we tried was filled with big eyed expressions, a leaning back from the table and an "Oh my God!" statement. Seriously... the beef Ren dang (sp?) was to die for! I don't know if ever in my life, I've had beef melt in my mouth ... literally. And the flavor..! But the appetizer of indian pancakes dipped in that sauce... WOW! The other dish we had was mango chicken. Ummm yum!  Nyonya is definitely one of the best out there and their pricing is really good. I highly recommend the satay and the roti canai. The taste is very authentic, and I am sure to be back soon.

Its a small place run by a family so the atmosphere is very laid back.  The food is damn good, I just wish the place was a little bigger. Thinking I should give them one star so it doesn't get any more crowded.
I stopped at Carmine's for lunch. I ordered chicken Marsala and rice. The sauce was fantastic, the chicken was soft and the rice was tasty. I will definitely be returning.
Not your average Halal cart. Hugeee servings and great sauces. Be around the area by 7/8pm to skip the crazy lines

i dont venture out to brooklyn for food often enough, so after scoutmob instructed me to dine in brooklyn for the $25 3-course dine in brooklyn special, I dutifully complied. Tabare had a lot going for it: a good crowd and vibe, convenient location by the Bedford stop of the L train, tasty food, and pretty reasonable prices (especially with the dine in brooklyn deal). So why only 3 stars? About 90 minutes between our appetizers and entrees. Unacceptable.
Just came into Centro with my girlfriends for the apps and drinks! We ordered the calamari!! It hit the spot with the sweet and sour sauce! Delish!

okay, i'm a reasonable person and i know how to admit when i've been wrong, and i have to say: roberta's gets a pardon for it's previous discretions. i was very dubious of the suggestion of giving them another chance, but since i recently moved to the neighborhood and good places to eat are rather sparse, i figured it was ultimately in my best interest to try. this time my experience was the complete opposite than my first visit. the staff was timely, attentive and they had all the ingredients available to make salads! hooray! my bf and i have also ordered roberta's for delivery (as we are now out of range of our previous delivery pizza- motorino) and it arrived surprisingly fast and in exceptional condition. in a former adversary i've discovered a new ally. thank's for getting your shit together, dudes! hearts.

i really wanted to like this place after hearing about it from so many friends and family. I checked it out, the owner is a great funny guy, but the food is sub par. the chicken is bland and its just bad. the falafel was good, but it justify the meat and rice. I enjoyed sammys a lot more.

Hell yeah, it's worth the hype. Got to Grimaldi's right when it opened on a Tuesday morning and there was no wait. Crust is divine, the fresh mozz is even better. Roasted peppers are homemade and sweet. It's all about the quality, baby. Cannot wait to return.

AMAZING!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I have been coming to Kennedy Food Garden since around 04'-05'.... I always got their amazing hoagies on the French bread and the Romaine lettuce. Its so fresh and they never served me anything short of excellent. I have tried their salads as well their chicken salads are the best... And unless you eating for 2 or more (jk) dont think you can eat their huge salad in one sitting!!!! I love this place!

I was very impressed with this restaurant! Sometimes finding authentic and delicious Mexican food can be a challenge. At Xochitl everything is fresh and exciting, from the food to the atmosphere. The staff was very friendly, and the layout and design of the restaurant stayed true to Mexican style. The menu is loaded with tasty options. Dishes range from the authentic guacamole, to tortilla soup, and the eclectic entrée choices. I decided to go with the camarones con caldo, which is a MUST! Seared shrimp, sweet plantain cake, chile broth topped with an avocado salad. Also the drink menu is a must! Nothing pairs better with a meal than a good margarita or martini. And lets not forget the most important part, dessert. The donuts come out with fruit dipping sauces to try from which is the perfect way to end the meal. I definitely will be back soon!

Probably one of my top two or three go to spots in the city.  I have been many times but always seem to find something new to go with the old standbys.   The quality of the ingredients always seems to be extremely fresh. Definitely the best Tsukune I've had in the US.  GIve the Tontoro (pork neck) a try.....

I absolutely love this place. There's a lot of options for sushi in this area, many of which are quite good, but there's just something magical about Yamada. As cliche as it sounds, I do believe these folks put love into their food-- it's very difficult to maintain such excellent consistency otherwise. My girlfriend and I have been coming here several times a month since discovering it last year, and the food is always perfect. Definitely try their signature "Yamada Roll" and don't forget to BYOB!

This is a mixed review. I have had many good meals at Keepers and in my lifetime I can only think of one other time I bothered complaining about a meal. Last night I took my mother out for her 70th birthday. She had the Salmon and I had the Kielbasa. Hers was excellent and mine was not. It simply was not good. I had about 1/3 of it and decided I could not continue. Our waitress saw that I did not eat very much and asked if I was happy with it. I explained that it was just off and it was simply "not good". She came back a few minutes later and said she was "sorry for the Kielbasa and they would be taking my beer off the bill".  Take my beer off the bill? That was the best part of the meal! Besides, its illegal to comp alcohol in Vermont. How about taking the awful Kielbasa off the bill? Even without my main coarse the bill was well over $100 for 2 so I am still scratching my head about the decision in the kitchen to offer the drink as compensation for a terrible dish. I wanted to just forget about the experience but I drove by a burning tire on my way home from work today and it reminded me of the meal so here I am on Yelp. The dish should have been comped. It left a very strange message to comp the drink instead. The Keepers I have known for the last 6 years would never think of doing this.

I live down the street from Five Leaves, so I've eaten here a few times, and the food is pretty good. The burger is excellent, and I've never had to wait that long, as I've usually been during the week, or at less busy times. It's a fairly solid choice. This review is more specifically about the service, or lack of. In fact, service would imply a problem with waiting, or orders being mixed up, or something of that nature. This is about simply obnoxious people. I've stopped at that coffee window a few times, and each time, the service has been almost comically rude and dismissve. This morning (7/28) was the worst though....I got off my bike and walked up to the window to get an ice coffee.  I wait a little while (no big deal, I can wait) and the guy from behind the bar came over, scowling.... Him - *silence* Me - "hey, hows it going?" Him - "whats up?" Me - " could I have an ice coffee please?" Him - *silence*. Pours an ice coffee, places it on the counter...simply says "$3.50". Me - "great, thank you very much" and hand over $4. Him - *silence*...turns around and carries on talking to a collleague. Me -  (admitedlly sarcastically) "great! thanks very much! Always a pleasure!" he still doesnt turn around, or even look at me, but one of his colleagues almost appologetically acknowledges me. Yep, readers paying attention to the story would note that not only could be not muster basic common courtesy, he then made the decision for me, that I didnt need my change. For what it's worth, I'd never tip in coins, so I usually take the change and then leave a dollar bill, but I've never had anyone literally not bother to give me change as they deem it to be too small. Anyway, it was the guy with the dark beard, and I think was wearing a blue hat. He really needs to find a new job. In fact, his line of work is irrelevant, basic common courtesy isnt that much to ask, is it?

Gaia Italian Cafe was fantastic. I visited this place last month and I'm looking forward to visit this place again. Because they have good quality of food and service. I can say this place is highly recommended.

Being from Miami, and visiting NY I can say that these are one of the worst empanadas I've had. Not authentic what so ever, and the service was terrible. Not worth waiting in line to try this place out

Would eat here every day if I could, gladly weaving my way through the lunch and dinner crowds to get my hands on an absurdly cheap okonomiyaki slice or a delish bento. There's probably better made Korean food in K-town, but I would bet my life you won't find it as cutely packaged, cheap, and varied as at Woorijip. On one side of the restaurant, there's a long buffet of Korean yumminess for a paltry $7/per pound. There's a "warm" boxed food section closer to the back of the restaurant on the same side of the buffet with pancake samplers, different bentos with different meats, and soups/stews. THe other side (the side with the register) has a the "cold" boxed food section. I think the best deals are here, and the most veggie friendly stuff: bibimbop, kimchi, nori bentos, a whole host of deliciousness that people tend to (but shouldn't) overlook whilst bee-lining for the buffet. I'm heading back for one more trip before I leave NYC today and couldn't be more excited! Don't miss out!

Finally made it here the other night after dying to go forever and left very happy!!  Loved the decor, so cute, and all of the staff were super sweet!  The watermelon salad was light and refreshing and so good.  The calamari was perfectly done.  The roasted bell pepper was good but not great.  I had a great experience though and I cannot wait to go back!

Really, really good falafel.  I mean really.  It's also cheap and good for those in a hurry if there isn't a line, which there frequently is.   Friendly staff except for one old, cantankerous man who is just funny. One problem is that the menu is not easily spottable. In fact, it's a paper menu pasted onto the food area.  This leads to people not knowing what they want until they get to the front of the line.  Then it's a lot of hemming and hawing and the line slows way down.  I'd suggest going to the front of the line to read the menu, decide, and hop back into line but the place is so small and crowded that this isn't an option.   Why not just make a big sign?

We recently went to the Inn at Weathersfield for my sister's 30th birthday. Thanks to the kind hospitality of the staff, we felt right at home from the start. Everything from our quaint rooms to the exquisite dinner were right on spot. Would definitely recommend for family get-togethers. Also a dog boarding service just down the road called Willow Farm that was really convenient for us.
One of my favorite spots. Great for dates, celebrations, or even just a night out with family or friends.

Come on now... Wildflowers has been a staple in this area for decades!!!  What amazes me about this place is the "cohabitation" of locals and the infusion of corporate America which has infiltrated the area over the past decade. Here's the Deal...Don't come here looking for cloth napkins. It is what it is...the place works as a good "watering hole"   Both the restaurant and bar side are consistently busy...The food will surprise you. Their pizza  & burgers are very good and they usually have a list of specials which offer some interesting options.

Woorijip brims with a myriad of freshy, inexpensive, tasty Korean dishes; available hot and fast. I figured this place would be really good and authentic since almost every person in the restaurant was Korean. Huge selection of finger food to eat with a good amount of different kinds of soju, sake, and beer as well as yummy korean drinks. Food I tried and loved: Spicy noodles Bulgogi Mook/Acorn Jelly (MY FAV BANCHAN OF ALL TIME!) Kimchee fried rice. The atmosphere isn't anything to brag about, but this place is for the cheap good food, not the decor. Definitely come here if you need a quick bite of good food to grab.

Perfection. Delicious food, beautiful fresh flowers throughout, impeccable service..my new favorite restaurant. Everything we ordered was incredibly tasty, from the calamari and carrot salad appetizer, the chilled corn soup, the prok belly sandwich on foccacia with basil aioli, or the red snapper, I was very, very happy. Then, the fresh strawberry pie with amaretti ice cream, just yes! I can't wait to go back. Go!

had (many) tequila drinks here.  AMAZING CONCOCTIONS.  all the bartenders are awesome, but Vinnie is my favorite.  he is truly The Tequila Whisperer-- tell him what ingredients you typically like & he will make the perfect (off menu) drink for you.  the guac was super delish, but also I was extremely tipsy so perhaps not the best judge.  the ambiance is really nice.  zero vegan options for dinner, but worth a stop for drinks.

went last night, seated very quickly, service was great, waitress had good recommendations. i had the $25 pre-fixe menu, which was a good value, crab cake was good & vodka penne was good. My husband had the Special jumbo diver scallops with mango sauce, which was amazing and cooked perfectly. Had the house wine Pinot Grigio at $7 a glass, great deal. Also, we purchased the $30 yelp gift certificate which made the prices more reasonable, as they are slightly on the higher end. However, i'd prefer this over the Olive Garden across the street from it. All in all, i recommend it!

I don't LOVE it...I've been here a couple times.  I've had better pizza.  It's good, don't get me wrong.  The prices are decent, and the other dishes look really good but for some reason we've only gotten the pizza each time.  The decor is really nice, but they pack everyone in like sardines, and they have to move out the table you're about to sit at so you can get to the booth on the inside...that part really bothers me! Especially when you're on a date and don't really want to be bothered by commotion next to you, or other people's conversations (and you don't want them listening in on yours!). It's in a cute area, cobblestone street with a beer hall and a couple nice restaurants.  This one little area is definitely a highlight of the Financial District.  And when it's nice out they put tables outside for all the restaurants, pretty nice.

This review is only for drinks. In Riva is adorable and in a prime location to attract all the people on Kelly Drive.  It worked.  They are bike and dog friendly aka tons of bike parking and a huge outdoor patio seating area that overlooks the river.  The only bummer? Happy hour prices are only inside.  But, I can live with that. We got a specialty cocktail- something with vodka, wine and orange soda.  It was delicious and refreshing.  They also had a cheap beer special.  The total bill for 3 people at 2 drinks each was under $20!!! The service here was great.  Everyone was extremely friendly, welcoming and attentive.   Rumor on the street is they're going to start doing zumba and salsa classes on the deck in the summer.  Stay tuned. Excited to revisit In Riva and try out their brunch this summer.

Guys. I can't say enough. I've never written a review before but I had to in this case. Nice bunch of guys. Great food. Love the pizza and the strombolis. PLUS - delivery is FAST. When you're looking for a pizza place in Bella Vista/Society Hill/Queens Village that can make other items just as well. This is your spot.

4/5 stars for me here. I came here on a weekday for brunch. I've always walked by this place in all seasons and called ahead to see if they could accommodate 2 and I was in luck. We walked in and were seated right away. I knew the food was good and the atmosphere cool but I did not know they had such a great brunch deal. There is a pre-fixe option for bottomless brunch or half liter of your choice of drink. They also have multiple options depending on how many people are in the group. For example for 2-3 people you can order 1 pizza+ 2 small plates+1 side. That is what we did. It was just enough for two people and we each had a half liter of a brunch cocktail. We had the margherita pizza, the french toast, the cacio e pepe and of course, applewood smoked bacon. Where to start? I thought the french toast was a little too soggy for my liking. The taste was great, don't get me wrong but it was soaked in brown butter. I know I know, how can anything soaked in brown butter be bad? It was just too much. I did love the  twist with rosemary focaccia and the berry compote. The cacio e pepe was super simple but was delicious....soft scrambled eggs, cacio cheese and cracked black pepper. I am really being picky here but the bacon was very undercooked. I like my bacon crispy but I'll eat bacon pretty much anyway it's brought to me but this was too much. Now, onto the pizza. The pizza was really good. A nice crust, not too soggy in the middle. The size of the pizza is meant to be split and have as a shared dish with some other smaller plates.  Overall I liked this place and am curious to get back and try other menus. Until next time...

So I said I would update my review based on more than a bite of my sister's sandwich so here it goes: I brought my mom here and the first words to come out of her mouth were "OMG Grandpa would have really enjoyed this!" This makes Appetizzios an instant 5 stars in my book. We were here for a late lunch so there wasn't enough Italian bread for the 3 sandwiches we were getting, but this led me to the great discovery of the Whole Wheat Italian Bread. Woohoo! Really good, I'll probably request it every time. I love it here and the staff is really awesome - big charmers. Best Italian place I've been to since I've moved to Lyndhurst and I will def. be back for more. You feel like family in there. The sandwiches are HUGE, so I can never finish them, and I've never been so excited to eat a leftover soggy balsamicy sundried tomato, mozzarella, & basil sandwich in my life!! It was delicioussss! My mom let me have her leftover half yesterday, which I enjoyed last night with a glass of red wine. I am pretty sure I had Appetizzios for 5 different meals this week. haha Seriously, that good.

This place is A-OK. I recently had the hangar steak special. Service is friendly and efficient. They have outdoor seating as well. The menu has at least one thing to satisfy everyone in your dining party. Good bread!

I ate here Tuesday night, the food was tasty, the service and portions good. When I woke up wed morning I was sick to my stomach and in the afternoon I was puking. Very unpleasent. I cannot be 100% sure this was the restaurants fault but I checked the NYC health inspection report and there were 28 violations:  167.153.150.32/RI/web/de… including violations for potentially contaminated food.

I give this place 3 stars, and an extra half because of the effort of local sourcing if quality ingredients. The restaurant is in the lobby of the cira center, i.e. a large office building, so it is a little awkward. I would recommend sitting toward the back inside for a more restaurant like atmosphere. You have a "nice view" of the Philly skyline up front but it's one cacophonous cavernous echo.  The menu has a few interesting parts and is a little confusing. Snacks, like nuts and popcorn, would make sense for the bar, but the waiter actually suggested that we order them with dinner. The food was good but a little pricey with most entrees being around $30, appetizers around $15 and snacks like heirloom popcorn for $9. Our server kept checking in with us to ask if every dish was ok...which seemed kind of annoying because it felt like an interruption rather than good service.  The roasted chicken was a sizeable portion - if you're hungry order that... Also, the petit fours (a blood orange pates de fruit and chocolate covered marshmallow) was a nice touch. Good, but not sure I would want to come back often given that it's out of the way and not that mind blowing.

5 dumplings for $1... you can't beat it! The pork fried dumplings are the best! This place seems like just a little hole in the wall, but they have an A rating and the service is always fast. The food is so delicious. This is my favorite place to eat in Chinatown (NYC).

amazing authentic food!!! I'm not a fan of Indian food but the truth is I haven't had much experience with it.  The Tandoori platter had such great flavor!!  I got the pad thai for dinner because I wanted to play it safe.  I was  a little worried when I opened it and there were lots of veggies in it that you wouldn't see in traditional pad thai.  It was AMAZING though.  A bit different than some really traditional pad thai but fantastic flavor and I love how the veggies added great crunch.   I wasn't expecting much from this tiny restaurant but it is a must try in West Caldwell

I stumbled upon this place on a sleepy Sunday afternoon. It was strangely empty around noon, but the brunch menu looked appetizing so I went in. I was a party of one, but didn't receive any strange looks from the staff when I asked to be seated. I climbed into the comfy sofa seat at one of the high tables. Something about the decor of this restaurant makes it feel very inviting and homey. For lunch, I got the Italian rosti and a latte. The latte was incredible and I thought "are you serious?! this is so good" as I took the first sip. Stix prides themselves on their coffee making abilities which you can read more about when you get your check. The Italian rosti was very delicious too and was pretty sizable (I couldn't finish it). The only qualm I have is that it left me feeling thirsty for the rest of the day. I'd happily try their other brunch dishes too. The service was attentive and friendly here to boot.

I was there in August for my mom's  Birthday, service was Fantastic and the food was delicious. I got a cake for my mom which got destroyed in the cab ride, thankfully the hostess and one of the chefs (I forgot his name) fixed it up for me at no charge. Can't wait to go back... By the way the paella is Perfect!

Go to Salinas on pay day because you can easily spend a ton of cash. Worth it? Yes, on a special night. The ambiance is fantastic, warm soft lights and trendy up beat music makes it great for an intimate dinner. I wouldn't suggest this restaurant for groups larger than 4. We arrived earlier than our set reservations but we were seated immediately in the garden which was covered on account of the rainy weather forecast. . The tables are set close together so do not be surprised. Our waitress came shortly after and got our drink orders started. Cocktails are $15 and Sangria is offered in small and large pitchers - large pitchers serve about 8 glasses worth. They also had a small selection of beer and a wide selection of wine. Out of the 6 cocktails offered, I ordered a vodka, mint and peach oolong tea mix and was not disappointed. It was mildly sweet, smooth and strong. It tasted very much like a mojito but was a lot smoother. Well worth the $15. My brother in law drank a bourbon, honey and lavender mix and was also very happy and slightly buzzed after the first drink. I took a sip of the sangria and it was one of the best I have ever had which came of no surprise considering that Spain is known for their awesome sangria. For starters, we ordered the GRILLED OCTOPUS that other yelpers have raved about and yes it is all it is said to be. The grilled octopus has a smoky and savory flavor. I was in heaven the minute it touched my lips. However for $19 I would have expected more than three 2 inch pieces of grilled octopus served with a teaspoon sized piece of boiled potato. I am just saying. We also ordered the PA AMB OLI which is grilled country bread, garlic, tomatoes, olive oil and sea salt. It was basically a spanish style brushetta but the tomato mixture was thicker and not as chopped as italian brushetta. We also ordered the GAMBAS AL AJO FRESCO and meh. Shrimp with lots of garlic in a mushroom stock/gravy. I wish we would have had more bread to soak up all the juices left over after eating the 9 pieces of medium sized shrimp. Who shares 9 pieces of shrimp? Not 4 people. Maybe 2. Ok so the tapas taste good but definitely not worth all the fuss.  I think the cheese platter for $19 and the trio of spanish meats would have been better for a group of 4. Next time? For dinner, we followed all the great yelpers and had the ROSSEJAT RAPIDA $25 and an order of the PAELLA MIXTA $54. As soon as the entrees were brought over, our senses were overtaken with the aromas and silence took over the table after the very first bite. Yeah it was that good. The ROSSEJAT RAPIDA was described as being a mixture of different textures highlighted by a saffron cream sauce. It looked yummy. Me and hubby shared the paella which was one of the best I have had. The rice was soft but not soupy and you could taste the saffron, cilantro, garlic and tomatoes that are so characteristic of this spanish dish. It had mussels, octopus, chicken, chorizo, beef and shrimp. Now being that I don't eat meat I was able to pull out the chunks of meat but not the chorizo. Honestly speaking I am happy that the chorizo got through because it was incredible. This paella can also be ordered vegetarian style which we failed to do but next time?? We skipped dessert and decided to have great coffee for less than $10 somewhere else. I did see that they had a cheese and guava dessert for $19 which the table next to us ordered and it looked really good, especially for all the cheese lovers out there. I have to also point out that they have one of the best restrooms I have ever seen. It smelled like I had just walked into a temple and was oh so clean. Afterwards we walked around town for a bit. So many different types of people and something to see at every turn. There are nearby clubs and bars so the night does not have to end early but it just might have to after paying that bill.

This review is of the cafe. which should have been vegan-yummy. The online menu says tofu, lentil burgers, hummus.
