Of those, they had only hummus, and they were so low they would give me only a tiny schmear.  The salads were boring and too small for the money. Both stars in this review go to the delicious greens & split pea soup, vegan and delicious. Even the low level of salt was perfect.

Was in the area on a Tuesday when there was a blizzard & decided to come because there was no line. Yay! I had the classic burger which was really good. The burgers are a little more rare than I'm use to in my burgers. My friend was so hungry his burger was gone in a few minutes. Unconsciously I followed & ate my burger pretty fast too.. then blamed him for making me eat so fast. I'm glad I did because the last few bites I had after my fried pickles did not taste as good. The bread soaked up the juices and got mushy. The fried pickles were a bit too salty for my taste but a refreshing contrast to my savory burger. The service was meh. Like literally that was how their attitude felt. Maybe because there was a blizzard? They got the job done quick and minimal. Overall, good burgers but I wouldn't go out of my way to come here. P.S Eat your burger fast! before it gets soggy :)

Don't ever go here if you're vegetarian. Almost NOTHING on the menu that looks vegetarian, and even if it looks vegetarian, it was probably cooked with meat (the "traditional" way, in CB-speak). I got lumps of meat on the plate of vegetable sides I ordered. My worst dining experience of the last 5 years.
Nice bar, nice location. Not too loud and good prices.

The food is good, but they left two ingredients off my sandwich. One being bacon, the other being the dressing... you know, just the items with flavor. I would probably go back, but I would check my order before leaving the restaurant.

Mmm..mmm..We just happened upon this place while taking a walk after shopping for electronics downtown. We loved it!! My crepe (Chicken and Asparagus and goat cheese) was awesome and I ordered the pear cider. Needless to say, I was looking on my phone to see where I could order the pear cider near my home. The two dessert crepes (one berry, and one banana nutella) were delicicious! Look out though, this place is tiny! But thMat made it even more special that we were able to score a table.

This is the place to go!! The food is the best around. It's been my go-to car for years and its never disappointed. It's another cart in the same family of Halal Guys made famous on 53rd & 6th so the food is exactly the same, only without a line. It's everything you have dreamed your Halal experience should be like. Quick, cheap and good.... It's worth going the extra block over for truly the best experience you can have in NYC eating.

I have been here only twice. The first time I wasn't sober, but this time I was completely aware of what I was eating. The first time I do remember having a BLT and it was simply delicious. This time I had the grilled chicken salad. I wasn't extremely hungry but it was good. This place is clearly a hot and noted restaurant. We waited for 30 minutes (which isn't to long), but that was during the lunch rush. The first time I went was after a party and the line was crazy (thank God I didn't have to wait in it lol) I would say go there try it out and if you are like me and you don't really like loud places....ask to sit downstairs. The upper level has louder music, a lot of crowd chatter, and the tables are closer. The lower level is more of the lounge vibe, softer music, and less people. So it's basically two worlds in one.

I have to say, this place has improved markedly from its opening. The prices are better and the offerings are broader. In general, they've really stepped up their game. We went for the dinner for the first time since last summer and were pleasantly surprised by the revamped menu. There were much more reasonable offerings as well as better prices on the mains. The quality was good (didn't knock our socks off but it was definitely tasty) and our server was prompt and attentive. Glad to see this place has worked out its kinks. We'll be going back more often now.

Yummy higher end sandwich shop in a great location. Place was very clean and staff super friendly. Not the cheapest sandwich place around but it will kick the A$$ of any local deli, I know Ive been to most all of them in the area. Mushroom soup was awesome as was the BBQ chicken and Beef sandwich were over the top delicious. We each got one and split them which was more than enough food.

We ate here twice on our vacation, it was that good! Friendly service, free hot tea (and it was really good tea too) and delicious noodle soups! My wife had the chicken soup both times, i had the beef soup the first time and the stir fried beef noodles the second. Loved everything! Did I mention "cheap" too? Many noodle soups are only $6...amazing, since I would've happily paid double that price for meals that good. Both times the staff happily accommodated for our small kids, providing us with extra bowls and scissors to cut the noodles into kid-friendly bites.

TERRIBLE experience with wait staff on NYE no less!!! I took my whole family to Riposo 72 on NYE since it has a decent wine selection and was close to the park, so that we could catch the fireworks. When we got there, the restaurant was half empty (probably a first for me, its usually busy). Since we wanted to stay out of the draft from the doorway, we choose a table in the window and proceeded to settle in. I had a long day walking about so I asked the server if I could switch my stool for a high back chair. SHE SAID NO (although there were about 10 free high back chairs along the bar). Now, having been here a few times, I thought that she was being difficult, but thought that she might be fine if I told her that I would change it back if the bar started to fill up. CLEARLY I UNDERESTIMATED HER DETERMINATION TO KEEP THE CHAIRS, NOT THE CUSTOMERS HAPPY. She promptly came back over and ask my party to LEAVE, since I had not adhered to her chair rule. SUCH RUDE behavior and on a night when most ppl are just looking to have a few drinks and kick back. Needless to say, MOLLY RICHARDS, the server, should not be in the customer service business, or really have any kind of job where she has the power to be rude to people for very little reason. Though I have always enjoyed Riposo 72 for its ambiance, the food and wine are ok, and not good enough to tempt me back given the bad treatment.

La Lanterna is one of those NYC finds that you'd rave to your friends about. It has a cute and charming outdoor patio that is enclosed by glass ceiling, and the tables are surrounded by small trees, plants and flowers. A friend had suggested it, and I decided to take my boyfriend to meet my parents for the first time. We were all very impressed with the outdoor space, and the food was to die for. We started with the over-sized bruschetta with goat cheese and grilled red pepper. It was so delicious, that I've attempted to make it for my friends twice since being there. My boyfriend had one of their pizzas and he loved it! My parents and I had their lasagna, and we absolutely loved it!!. They make about 4 different individual-size lasagnas. Everything was individually and freshly cooked/baked. The staff was very friendly and attentive. Only thing I didn't like is that there was construction going on inside, but this was back in October, so it's possible that it's over by now.  Since I went in early October, it was a tad chilly. I'm not sure if they have heat laps in the winter, and if they dont then they really should because it would make it so cozy. Overall a great experience, and highly recommend for a cute date!

Absolutely lowkey...absolutely tasty!  Started w longneck clams, the Canadian flight of oysters, then we had a dorade & branzino (both w herbs & oil).  We missed out on the $1 oysters, but will definitely be back...

This is my favorite spot in Greenpoint. Staff is friendly, food is delicious, coffee is good. Prices are right. Best Sandwiches in Greenpoint. Great place to grab a bite, chat with friends or study. Only downside is that their wifi isn't exactly the most reliable and they don't have AC.
Very tasty.  Warm, personal service. My son loves all of the shark dishes.  I definitely recommend.

Eat it and believe. Totto Ramen is a crowded, busy restaurant spitting out tasty bowls of chicken-broth ramen to the clamouring crowds.  I like the creaminess that a little miso adds.  My dining parner got the "extra spicy" bowl (which was fairly spicy but no one would be injured by eating it). Good quality ingredients and the add-ons look to be less expensive than the competition. One of my favorites.

You know a place is great when you cant name the best thing you ate because they were all just.so.good.   We debated ordering the tasting menu, but ended up going a la carte.  We had: bacon tater tots scallop crudo oysters burrata ribeye panna cotta I can honestly say everything was excellent.  Even the bathroom was clean and maintained nicely.  Will definitely be back soon.

I always have fantastic food (I've been here many times for their lunch buffet) or drinks (a great place to stop in before a night at Brasil's) when I go to Karma. Not to mention the staff and the owner are always very friendly and accomodating which makes me feel like I've been coming to Karma forever!

Hmm... Juventino...walking past this place at dusk, it was usually empty while other restaurants were bustling but during the mornings, it can get PRETTY crowded. I decided to take a closer look. Interesting setting. You feel like you are sitting at your grandma's kitchen. The accents of the book and newspaper covered tables is delightful along with the colorful flowers situated smack in the middle. The waitress is really nice, shes a southern sounding girl. Very knowledgeable about whats on the menu. I ordered an oatmeal with fruits and a glass of fresh squeezed orange juice. Before i received my breakfast, i was given a complimentary  tart with strawberries on top. Another blonde waitress was VERY knowledgable about where the fruits came from and told me a little about where all the fruits came from and they do come from New Jersey and are locally grown. Very nice woman. MMMMMM.. Very delicious along with the sweet and cold orange juice. The oatmeal is VERY organic tasting. Im not going to lie, im used to Quakers oatmeal right out the box.  But this unrolled oatmeal is simply delicious and not complicated. It is dressed with fruits and berries on top. Sugar(stevia?) and milk were set at the side. Very thick grains, i felt very pleased eating this and i know i will be back. This is great for family and friends alike. Very spacious restaurant with excellent service and smiling staff. Great...just great. The people who are giving this place bad reviews are most likely people who entered with a bad mood or just dont like anything in general! I love this place and i know you will too!
Somewhat expensive, stay away from steak. All other dishes good bit on the salty side...wait staff not so good. Two people with from each and no desert coil run you $80 easy without tip.
If you dont want to make a trip to chinatown great option for viet sand. I just wish the chicken was like the city. Other than that its great and still enjoy the chicken sand.
First time eating Philippine food and was not disappointed. A bunch of pork and most if it was fried.  Tasty.  I even are the blood pork which was surprisingly delicious
over priced bad food
I went here once and the food was barely edible. Yuck. Never again.
Love it everything was on point ! very satisfied! I am Italian, made me feel like home! truly my best pick! Love it truly! And honestly couldnt have been better!
Probably the best huevos rancheros I've had in the city.  Also tried the sourdough pancakes - amazing.

This is one of few pizza places you go to and think about going back forever.  Pizza is one of those foods that is easy to make good but to be of this quality takes something unique.  Go early this place gets crazy

I've been wanting to try this place for a while so my friend & I came during her lunch break today to try this place out & use a gift  certificate that I had. First thing I noticed was there was only 1 person working. Even though it may not be as busy during the day, I definitely felt like there should have been at least 2 people. The poor guy was running around trying to help everyone. There were 4 tables in the back, including us, & a big group in the front. There were also people getting take out. That is definitely a 2 person job. Especially since this is during people's lunch break. I do give him props though. My friend had the Tuna Pizza $14 from the appetizer menu & the Alaska roll $15. Tuna Pizza: "Crisp Tortilla Fresh Minced Tuna, Cilantro, Seaweed Salad, Tomato and Spicy Sauce" I am not a huge fan of seaweed salad so I can't judge this dish too much. I do wish they had more tomatoes though. Alaska Roll: "Spicy California Roll, Fresh Salmon On Top With Sweet Miso Glaze, Yuzu Miso Creame Friache" The miso glaze is pretty sweet, different from the usual rolls I've had. I had the Tuna Zento Sushi Square $14 "Square Sushi with Eel, Avocado, and Plum Paste. Topped with Tuna or Salmon glazed with Sweet & Spicy Sauce" you could also get salmon instead of tuna. I wanted to try this because of a lot reviews mentioned it. It was cool that it was square but in the end, it just tasted like I was eating rice. And rice also fell apart easily. I also had the Tsunami Roll which is not on their website but I do remember torched tuna on top & tempura eel inside. I did like this roll though I am not usually a fan of tempura, especially shrimp. I liked the torched part. As busy as the guy was he refilled our water often & was quick to come over. Being so dark outside, you can't really look in & tell big it is or how far back it goes but this place is pretty small. It's not necessarily a bad thing, I would just want to keep that in mind during busier times. What we ordered: ' Tuna Pizza ' Alaska Roll: try if you like something a little different & kind of sweet ' Tuna Zento Square Roll: mostly tasted like just rice + Tsunami Roll: torched tuna & tempura shrimp

Meh. Your average pricey New York restaurant -- acceptable, but not exceptional. A safe choice if you are in the neighborhood, but not worth traveling for. Points of distinction: kid-friendly; personable hostess (particularly in a city where hostesses are often outright rude).

Went to galli based on the good reviews in yelp. I doubt all this reviews are real and if they are I don't understand 4 starts in yelp. Food is good  but not great. Pasta with cream sauce like an Alfredo. Lemos chicken with butter. I am sure people order those dishes a lot. Contort food from 20 years ago.  I thought service was all over the place. Bread not good @ all. Arancini (risotto rice balls) did anybody had those well done in a good italian restaurant. Probably not. I know this is not an italian place but more like an American italian restaurant. I get it, but it could be so much better. To much butter everywhere I mean everywhere, the clams tons of butter. Not need to put so much butter for the food to taste better. I am sure they do very well. But not a 4 start in yelp. Few more good people on the floor, a little more attention in the food and the presentation and it could be better already. Cheers

Beenn going here since it opened 7 or 8 years ago. These guys make the best chicken and rice i've ever had. Big plus is the gigantic portion, and incredibly marinated chicken which they marinate in these black plastic bags. They've been friendly ever since they came and the big guy is a really charismatic person who turns the customers into friends. You'll even getva free falafel waiting for the food if he knows you or you're a mildly attractive woman haha we all have our vices. Great place and I was so excited to see it's awesome reviews! UPDATE-He won the Vendy AWARD for 2010!!!

we are on the fence about this place.  my opinions about this place are all over and my initial feeling definitely towards the one star rating. a friend called ahead to make sure they would be able to accommodate our party of six if we were to arrive at a certain time.  even though they don't take reservations, she didn't mention that this would be a problem.  when we arrived we were immediately met with resistance.  the hostess didn't want to seat us, saying that she probably wouldn't have room for us.  my friend told her about how we called ahead to ask about seating being an issue and so the hostess reluctantly wrote us down on a list and told us it would be over an hour for a table.  an hour and half later our table was ready and unfortunately the wine store portion had closed.  this when i learned a very important detail about philly: wine stores legally have to close by 10pm. one would say probably that might have been pertinent information someone should have told us when writing our name down for a table, knowing that our table wouldn't likely be ready before the wine store closed.  our party comprised of people who are from philly and didn't know this bit of information either, which was the biggest disappointment and buzz kill i have ever experienced. but since garces is a byob, we paired our cheese and pate with... beer.  it was difficult to get myself to a point of acceptance that our evening was ending this way.  i covet the rare friday nights out without our son, this was not how i wanted to end it, but seeing how i was very hungry at this point and i had no other choice, i very slowly calmed back down.  i have to say our waiter was a true professional about my mood and a trooper considering it must have been a long night for him as well. there is a wide variety of imported and domestic cheeses.  the charcuteries and cheeses are an excellent value and i can only imagine (and certainly not by my choice) how well they would go with the wine.  i was most impressed with the truffle lavender honey- a type of honey i was told at the la jolla farmer's market is a rare, rare find.  honey was delicious and perfect with the hard sharp cheeses.  i was skeptical of the garlic duce de leche sauce, but it was also excellent with the hard cheeses we selected. the upside of dining with vegetarians, i could order pate and it's all mine... well not all mine, i did share some with my husband.  the chicken liver mousse pate was excellent as well.  just wished i had some champagne to wash it down.  the guys acquired some unfiltered heffeweizen, and the pairing wasn't half bad. as an entree, my husband and i shared the duck confit salad.  the quail egg was delicious with the duck and salad greens, but the mustard was too much of a contrast and i wish there was a little more duck in it. to make up for the miscommunication, they brought out 4 desserts for our table to share.  they were exquisite.  the dulce de leche chantilly cream puff dessert was definitely the table favorite.  the pistachio macaroons were also delicious and more rich than i expected.  the dark chocolate tart was the least sweet of the 4, but rich.  dessert is definitely something to save room for here.   i am also not a fan of automatic gratuity and here they charged 20% for the six of us.  while i am sure we received 20% worth of service, i prefer tips being at my discretion.  while they made up for it as best the possible could, i am not sure that i would wait over an hour to eat here again, or even longer than 20 minutes for that matter.  i would just buy the wine and food to go and enjoy it elsewhere.
yes. get the white clam. it is actually that good. Red pie. SO GOOD. wow writing this review makes me want to go back now haha
very good! Great service! good prices
One of the best restaurants in NYC! Very cozy, and the staff are nice. The owner gave us tips on how to cook their salmon, which was INCREDIBLE!

Yelp came through on this one. I needed a good breakfast joint near Penn Station and Johny's fit the bill. There were 3 of us total, but lucky for us the table in the back was available. I got the egg white and spinach sandwich from the healthy breakfast options (yes there are several) while my kid got his chocolate chip pancakes, so everyone got what they wanted. Full bellies all around...a perfect start to a beautiful day.
Excellent service and excellent food. The waiter rattled off about 50 specials (not exaggerating) and we ended up ordering from those. Absolutely no complaints, everything was perfect.

Wow, I need to come downtown more often!!!! Came here the other night after volunteering at the Hartford Public Library and was worried that I would be walking into the sketch part of Hartford; but when I turned the corner, I saw this cute little area that had plenty of parking and restaurants/bars. This restaurant is literally across the street from the convention center and probably a hot spot for any of those traveling in the area. Cool area - I want to come back already! When you walk in, the vibe screams a little uppity but it isn't at all....well, it might be since I saw a bartender get yelled at by an angry customer who wanted their credit card back instead of having the bar keep it to keep his tab open (high-five to the bartender who handled the situation - she did it with pose and was friendly the entire time to the customer - awesome customer service). There are zero tv's in the bar or at least I couldn't find them so if you are looking for a sports bar, might not be your spot. I ended up sitting at the bar which was PACKED at 7pm on a Thursday...I guess that's a good sign. There was only one bartender which I was a little worried about slow service but the service was surprisingly great. I ordered a draft beer and split two apps with my friend. We had the bison nachos and the bison sliders which came out in lightning speed....honestly, I think I had a sip of beer and the food magically appeared. Again, I was skeptical on why was it so quick but OMG, when I bit into the slider, it was ahhhhhhhmmmmaaaazzzing! So delicious!! I'm kind of wanting to go back right now as I write this review. The nachos were also tasty but could have had a little more cheese on the nachos and probably some more bison meat but, it was only $8 so it was kind of understandable. A friend that was with had the green and hot burger (I think that is what it was called) and she said it was very flavorful and the meat was melting in her mouth. The only reason I didn't give this place 5 stars was because I want to go back and experience an actual dinner there. I'll be in very soon and will be updating this review!!!

Love love love this spot! The food is great the ambiance and decor super cute and it's super affordable. I came here with 3 friends we all had apps, entrees and ordered a bottle of wine for 60 bucks! This place is one of the many reasons I miss NY!

Came here for a buddies' birthday dinner and was not disappointed.  Place was crowded, Sat. night, but didn't feel overly crowded...it was a good mix of people.  Food was very good.....string bean appetizer and flounder entree were both very tasty.  The green beans are like crack so be wary that you won't be able to stop eating them until they are gone. Server was very attentive and kept the wine flowing....it probably flowed a little too much, but who am I to complain.  Dinner for 4 with a ton of wine came to like $250.   I'd definitely come back for dinner and to try their brunch.

My friend and I arrived in NY and after checking into the hotel walked down the street and stumbled across this charming bistro.  We both had the recession proof lunch - appetizer and sandwich for $12! We enjoyed a lobster BLT, iced tea and wonderful atmosphere. After the lunch, when we were paying our bill, the owner/chef started a pleasant conversation with us. I HIGHLY recommend this bistro for anyone in the Gramercy area!

GOOD LORD!!!!  this  place is GOOD!!!!!  OK calm down!!!!  Deep breaths!!!  alright first of all upon entering this place it is once again a fire hazzard :(  but cozy.  The fries are freshly made and you have the choice of about 20 different sauces to try from. My girlfriend and I ordered the irish curry, wasabi mayo and one thats called the war sauce.  It contains a mixture of onions, peanut satay and frite sauce.   The irish curry was your typical curry.  It was ok but it wasnt a WOW with the fries.  The wasabi mayo on the other hand was great and with a kick it would knock you off your feet.  The war sauce was also great with a peanut oil base and onions it brought the flavor out of the fries.   My favorite was the wasabi mayo but i still didnt try all of them so i dont know which is the best.  The fries are great and are made by pinoy pride and are of high quality.  Crispy and flavorfull.   The prices are good and of course i just wish the sauces were free. Overall very good place. HELL one of the best places to go in NY. GO NOW!!!!!

This is a must try in NY and one of those restaurants I go back to over and over in NY. Def worth the wait. Their pork buns are one of the best I've had which are way better than Totto Ramen's pork buns. The ramen is pretty good although Totto Ramen is better in that department.

this used to be my favorite dive bar in new haven. cheap food, nice beer selection, AWESOME belgian frites, and even cooler atmosphere. UNFORTUNATELY, rudy's closed and move to another location. now it feels like a TGI Fridays, the food is pricy for what it is, and it totally lost all of its charm. i suggest you go to Elm Bar instead. this is the bar that opened in Rudy's old location, and it's essentially the OLD RUDY'S but with a new name.

So, Luke's Lobster is a chain. Also, yes, the rolls are small, and I saw them take them out of a plastic bag on the counter (so they are not fresh).  And yes, the sandwiches are expensive.  But FOCUS, PEOPLE! None of this matters! Go here! Order the lobster roll (and the crab roll--a close second)!  You will not be disappointed. The sandwiches may be small, but they are ALL succulent lobster (or crab) meat, very minimally dressed.  (The shrimp roll was sort of unremarkable, however.) My boyfriend and I spent like a week's worth of grocery money here for lunch on the Saturday before Memorial Day. We ordered the Noah's Ark (two half-rolls of each of lobster, crab and shrimp, two pickles, two drinks and two bags of chips: $38), plus TWO extra lobster rolls. And boy, was it good. Remember that aforementioned, apparently store-bought roll? Well, when slathered in butter and grilled, it turns into a slightly-crispy-on-the- outside, gummy-on-the-inside, perfectly scrumptious vehicle to lift that little pile of delicious lobster meat to your lips! Seriously. So. Good. Other points: The décor was charming, the staff friendly and I loved the bluegrass music playing through lunch.  My only complaint about this place is that the sandwiches are so delicious, you want to sit and enjoy them, but it's a fast food place.  As you eat, there is a line going by your table. There are people waiting to sit down standing next to your table staring at you, waiting for the slightest hint that you will soon abandon your seat. This is a little uncomfortable, esp. if (like we did) you brought a six-pack of beer having heard it was a BYOB and are trying to enjoy a leisurely lunch. I would probably just try to find an off-peak time, since we got there right before the lunch rush. It was just a small blight on an otherwise enjoyable experience.

We ate at the Grill for the first time last evening. My husband had the chicken gyro platter, I had the chicken curry, and we shared an order of chicken samoa. He had a can of diet pepsi, and I ordered an Afghan Lassi. The samoas were crispy and stuffed full. My husband said his chicken was seasoned very well, and was very moist. My chicken curry was very flavorful, and the naan bread was great for sopping up the sauce. We both loved the fragrant, delicious rice. The service was very good and the prices were more than reasonable. What a gem! We'll be back!

Food Rating:  3.75 This place was recommended by a friend.  The place is hidden and located downstairs.  Lines are pretty long on a Saturday night... and they don't take reservations.  Boo. Food was pretty good overall but on a foodie rating scale, it's 3.75 rating overall.  The friend that recommended this was in her early to mid 20s... and this is her go to place if there are friends out of town or as a date place, which I wholeheartedly agree.   Here is a rundown of what was ordered between 4 of us: 1) spaghetti (made with ketchup) - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… 2) fried maitake mushrooms - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… - yum! 3) raw octopus - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… - yum! 4) tuna cheek - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… - yum! 5) okonomiyaki - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… - eh.  This one here was very dense.  Bf and I didn't personally care for it. 6) tempura sweet potato - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… 7) shishamo - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… 8) agedashi tofu - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… 9) tongue - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… - the meat was overcooked.  a bit tough.... not what I had expected tongue to be 10) asparagus & bacon - yelp.com/biz_photos/p_2z… - yum.  anything with bacon and grilled is delish.

The service is arrogant and it starts with the head guy -owner- manager- whatever you wish to call him The tables are DIRTY most of the time and if you ask, the manager will smirk at you.   IN all honesty, the food is not bad - but why go for overpriced indian food when there's other nice indian food in the area - without the bad attitude?

If I were a bagel, I would want to find my untimely end here. I would sacrifice my bready body to become their painkiller sandwich. The hole inside me would be filled with the love and warmth that is scrambled eggs with sharp cheddar cheese (and spicy ketchup, if you're feeling a bit spicy!) Make sure to grab an iced coffee - it's not cold brew, but it is strong and delicious, not unlike me. The ladies of gleaners are planning on making a calendar this upcoming season. I'm helping to secure the dragons they're going to need to pose with. There will be a companion soundtrack with music by Dio and friends.

Had lunch there today with an old parisienne friend of mine who's unbelievably allergic to garlic and onions. Tall order for a Turkish place but still, we had a great lunch and the waiter took extra special care to make sure she didn't kill over. He was also cute and I think he had a slight crush on here but I digress. Anyways, I happily enjoyed the grape leaves solo. Recommended!

This is a cute little place. Typical home town diner style place to eat. We like to eat at the counter and watch the guys cook--entertaining and friendly.  It's a nice place to go when you just don't want to make your own breakfast on a Sunday morning.  Eat with the locals and enjoy some great pancakes with fruit!
i ordered pizza over 6 weeks for guys working on my house, the quality was consistent and staff always friendly. they answered the phone promptly and were courteous.

Even though it's about a half hour drive for me to get here, the food is TOTALLY worth it! My boyfriend and I make a pilgrimage to La Costenita almost every weekend for Mexican "brunch."  It's a little Mexican grocery store with a little "deli" in the back where they cook up some ridiculously good and *authentic* Mexican food.  The lady who owns the place is awesome (very friendly, loves sharing her culture and cuisine, and wonderful service). It's not a fancy restaurant, but the food is much, much better than ANYTHING you could ever get from a Mexican restaurant.  I don't know why she hasn't opened a real restaurant! We've ordered different things every time we've gone here, and everything on the menu is delicious!  The lady marinates and prepares all of the meat and salsas herself, and everything is made to order (so lots of room for customization). Even though it's just a little breakfast-bar type set-up with stools, I highly recommend you try this place out.  I have been extremely disappointed with all the Mexican restaurants I've visited so far in New Jersey after relocating from California.  This is the only place I look forward to going to. They do have carry-out, so if you don't want to sit and eat at the store, you can take your food home.  Another thing I like about this place is you can see the entire area where all the cooking is done, and it's pretty clean - small but clean. Eating at La Contenita feels like you're having a meal at your friend's house or something because everything is down to earth and good, with generous portions!

I don't normally write reviews but I've been to this place twice in the last two days. Hell's Kitchen's 9th Ave has its share of faux-asian fare, but Pure Thai Shophouse isn't one of those places.  Actually, I've never been to Thailand so I don't know if this is real Thai food, but I can say it is fresh and it tastes good. Over the past two days I've tried: Lunch- Green Mango Salad, Rambatchuri Crab and Pork Dry Noodles, and the Taro (as well as Mango) Sticky Rice Desert. Dinner - Green papaya salad with Salted Blue crab, Calamari, Shrimp Pad Thai, and Nue Yang Special (skirt steak on a bed of cauliflower, broccoli and green beans) The Salads were comparable, quite spicy and tangy. The dressings burst with flavor. Everything was fresh. The Rambatchuri dry noodle was amazing. Perfectly cooked Egg noodles. Blue crab was a little scarce but the sweet pork was abundant. The portion was healthy. I actually requested a little soup broth on the side and was really happy I did. The deserts on both occassions were absolutely gorgeous. Sweet cocunut sticky rice with mango or taro (thai bread pudding) on top. Not too sweet. The Calamari was not heavy and cooked just right. Accompanied by a sweet chilli sauce, surprisingly mild, it was a perfect app to share. Finally, the Nue Yang I saved for last because it was the star dish. The beef was cooked perfectly and sat on top of  lightly- steamed greens. The dipping sauce was had tang, heat and sweetness. I don't know how they did, but they pulled it off. In the end, I washed all each meal with a Changs and came out well under $20. Needless to say, I will return to this neighborhood gem, even if I have to wrassle a mix of youths and families for a tiny stool in the corner.
Very rare to find such an authentic Malaysian food on the go. My gf and I have been here twice and certainly will return for more delicious food.

Vesta was a great experience.  We met the owner and he let us sample a few of the local beers they carry.  The servers were great, the interior was cozy and had a very warm feeling to it.   You've gotta try the Potato and Pancetta Pizza.  It has potato, pancetta, caramelized onion, arugula, apple, and goat cheese.  Tastes nothing like a traditional pizza but amazing none the less. The Baked Orecchiette was great! The Brussels Sprouts were a little too charred for my taste but had good flavor behind it.  The mussels were decent but the broth had more flavor than the mussels themselves.   Overall a great experience and a great time!  The pizza is definitely something I'm going back for.  I hear their brunch is awesome!
i was only there one time

Just had an unexpected fabulous dinner here. Very authentic Italian food and the staff is wonderful and pleasant.  Please try the grilled ceaser's salad. It is delightful. Seafood lovers will love the variety on the menu. Bring a bottle of wine with you when u go. It's a byob. Love it and I would absolutely go again and again...
Wow!

Ambiance: *Street vendor with a long but fast moving line. *Located on many corners, but I went to the one across from Moma. Food: *Delicious and cheap! Got the mixed plate $6! *Awesome service, definitely a must try!

Pizza is fantastic! Ambiance is awesome and trendy, location is perfect with an indoor and outdoor seating option. the only reason it doesn't have a 5 star is because theres always a 2+ hour wait. But if you just want the food without the service, theres a take out option right next door! Sick spot!

Besides the not so spectacular beer menu - the food is horrible. I went here with a friend of mine after hearing some hype about this place. Service for drinks and food was slow and served with attitude - PLUS when I did get my beer, the glass my beer was served in has lipstick all over it! YIKES! Hello?? is anyone at the bar paying attention? Needless to say, that was my first and last trip back there. And if you are looking for Belgian beers, there are MUCH better places in that neighborhood and around the city!

YUMMY!  YUMMY!  YUMMY! If you like chocolate, this is a great place to eat.  Their dessert menu is huge, so take your time and choose wisely.  They have a small, but delicious lunch/dinner menu also.  I've tried each of their pizzas and they're very tasty.  The french fries are worth a try.  Their dishes are really large, but can be shared to leave enough room for dessert. Their crepes and cakes are good.  Fondue was ok.  The hot chocolate is thick and comes in a really fun "hug mug".  There are still a ton of desserts I can't wait to try!

Came here with a few girlfriends two nights ago and had a pretty good experience. Our drinks were brought to us pretty promptly and bread followed a little later. There was olive oil on the table, but I was a little disappointed that the waiter didn't bring over the pepper grinder at this point since we all were opting for oil over butter. I ordered the focaccia rigatoni, which was pretty good. The creamy tomato sauce was very tasty and the chicken was not dried out; some of the sundries tomato pieces were a little large for my taste, but it was still very enjoyable. Our table of four split two desserts- ricotta cheesecake and chocolate mousse cake. The chocolate mousse cake was good but nothing memorable. The cheesecake was definitely the better dessert of the two, but definitely could have been more flavorful. I was happy about the fresh whipped cream and berries that accompanies both cakes on the plate (the blueberries definitely helped make up for the lack of flavor in the cheesecake.) Overall, pretty good meal but somewhat forgettable. If I'm seeing a show in the area, I might come back again.

This interestingly named bar is a gem in a neighborhood that you do not expect it to be in! They open at 5pm and the kitchen opens at 6pm. Parking can be hard to find, unless you are willing to pay a meter.   With that being said, I had a great experience with my sister on her birthday last night at this place! We came in for a drink before our reservation at 6pm at Traif restaurant which is around the corner. The waitress was so warm and inviting, offering recommendations on their very extensive menu of alcoholic beverages. They have whiskey galour and so much more!!!! The waitress helped us make sense of it all and was so attentive. Our candle light went out due to a draft and she came over within 30 seconds with a lighter to light it back up :-) The decor was warm, hip, and intimate, great to sit and have good conversation over a drink. The music was great as well, from rhythm and blues to rap to rock. I ended up having a delicious Beer Cocktail made with lemon, champagne, beer, and bourbon that all came together beautifully, with explosions of different flavors with each sip. My sister had the Bourbon Hot chocolate which was delicious and very flavorful. The hot chocolate was creamy and rich, followed by a kick of bourbon! The complexity of each of the drinks were apparent, yet the ingredients all came together like a beautiful symphony in your mouth. The bartenders definitely know what they are doing. The cocktails are $10 each (well worth it). I will be back to try the different drinks on the menu and the food, which I hear is very good.

This place is one of the best-kept secrets in the city!  The big tray chicken is amazing!  The pork pancake is so good and the bok choy is also great.  The BYOB policy makes it a great deal!  I highly recommend!

I've been here twice for brunch. My sister loves this place (it's probably because she lives within a few blocks). I go for the burger Sunday when you get a juicy delicious burger and brunch drink all for $15 (a bargain in NYC). Both times I've been I have noticed it is mainly NYU students and a younger crowd, but they have a decent beer selection and solid menu at that price point. Next time I go, I want to try the Slow Roasted Pork Sandwich with kimchee aoli. Delish. The overall vibe is lively and usually pretty busy, but then again, it's hard to find brunch spots in NYC that aren't packed...I'd go back for beers and casual dinner with friends. Overall, it's a decent place. The same owners of The Jane (where I've also had brunch), but I preferred The Smith's food over Jane.

I'm not a big whiskey drinker, but I think VW might change that... all in due time. One cocktail I had was bourbon with lemon, honey and maybe a little ginger and it was so refreshing. Also, one of the best things about this place (besides the liquor and the burgers) is the bartenders...they've got more skills than most of the "mixologists" in the city with none of the attitude. I'd definitely suggest snacking on some of the pickled items (beets or truffled cauliflower) while waiting for your heavenly red meat patty to arrive. Also, you must order the duck fat fries - do it!

This place is clean organized and cozy.  But don't let the size fool you they have one of the best empanadas you will ever taste. The guy that takes your order is very friendly.  They are made fresh in 10 minutes or less, and are inexpensive.  The spinach & ricotta  and chicken are some of my favorites. They also sell home made tropical ice cream that is delicious.
I went to Ten Stone and got the best service from Kate . Thank You Kate. The Fresh Tuna steak salad was great . I get the best service from Kate

Oh Mo's, so badly I wanted to love you.  Halfway between my apartment and school, it's conveniently located and prices are totally reasonable.  Homefries?  To die for.  But the toast was over-buttered, the service subpar and the pancakes like bricks.  Wanting a place to be good, it appears, does not in fact make that place good.  The brunch quest continues.

Excellent service and good food. This would be four stars most cities but NYC has so many great places. The Brussels sprouts were great. Everything was good to excellent. New York expects great for this price.

With a great combination of dank beer selection and good food, Devil's Alley now has a spot reserved as one of my permanent lunch options. I ordered the beef brisket sandwich, which I had been eagerly anticipating based upon my pre-lunch menu research (yes, I do that).  I even deflected the very tempting three-course Beer Week menu in order to try the brisket.  While I certainly enjoyed it, its not nearly the best brisket I've had--good brisket should be tender and almost-but-not-quite ready to fall apart but this was a mess.  I could also have done without all the cheese and horseradish sauce, which was not necessary with all the flavor in the meat.  It kind of reminded me of a similar sandwich I ordered on special from Continental or Jones about a year ago.  So, basically, it was good but I was expecting much more. The gaufrettes were nice.  Who can complain about perfectly crispy waffle chips?  The baked beans were also very good, though not what I look for in baked beans.  I apprecaited the chorizo and pieces of brisket (or pork) in there, and they were incredibly tender, but the flavor was kind of subdued. The half-dozen drafts offered me some choices that I had difficulty deciding amongst.  The PBC Coffee Porter was exceptional.  The Lion Winter Ale was above-average.  Next time, I'll have to order the sampler. The service could have been slighlty more attentive.  It was almost fifteen minutes before the server took my order.  After that, while still a bit slow, not really anything to complain about. Overall, great place that could use a few minor improvements.

I have only had the buffet-style take-out. Three items + rice or lo mein for $6.25. The food was typical Chinese food. If anything, it was pretty mediocre. I had the lo mein (nothing special), mapo tofu (pretty good), spicy chicken (good flavor but weird fatty chicken pieces), and fried tofu (inedible greasy rubbery tofu). The options they have at the buffet line are hit or miss. The workers are also extremely unfriendly and stand there without a smile and look completely impatient. Decent for a Chinese food fix but I'd look elsewhere.
Excellent restaurant.  Highly recommended.  We enjoyed our meal from appetizers to dessert.  We will return. :) Update : Forgot to mention, excellent bloody mary.  The real deal with horseradish.

Haha, are you even going to read this review? Probably not. You're just going to go to Geno's and get a steak. You're not going to care about the legacy or racism this business prides itself upon. You're not going to be bothered by their deplorable practices, or the shitty way in which they treat home owners in the neighborhood. So I will just say: if there was one business I could wipe off the face of the earth forever, it would be Geno's. I'm tired of tourists taking strained bowel movements on my front steps at 4AM because Geno's won't let them use their bathroom.

Great experience & fast service. This restaurant is dimly lit very sexy and the food was delicious. I had Sunday brunch, chocolate chip French toast ,cheese eggs & a melon mimosa yum. The staff was friendly and attentive. They also brought out this delicious cornbread with a strawberry sauce before my food was up. I would so come back again maybe for dinner next time. Oh they also have a small outdoor space, always a plus in the city on a nice day.
Best middle eastern food in PA, by far. Just moved to NY and wish they would open a location here..

Very disappointing! First of all, this place is suppose to open 11am but all the food was not ready until 1130-1145a. The food that came out early was not even hot. As far as the taste of the food...could be better. Nothing to rave about. Also, the seafood was in a separate room. Not sure how customers are suppose to know this. Good thing the lunch buffet was only $6.99 (not including the drink).

Where to start...? 50 cent tacos on wednesday, and they are actually good! Daily specials that are both affordable and delicious. Craft beer rotation as well as those "other" beers. History. Great service. My only complaint is that it gets packed very fast. So show up early.

I have to say that despite Bistango's gluten-free menu, I was not blown away. Again, I more than appreciate the effort, but I should still hope for good service and food, right? I ordered a rice pasta/vegetable dish, and while it was overall tasty, it was drenched in olive oil and was quite bland before I added some pepper.  My friend ordered one of the specialty pizzas, and after initially being served the wrong one, found the correct order to be too cheesy - like anything could have too much cheese! I didn't get to take in much of the decor since we were seated outside, but since it was early dinner/late lunchtime, it was hardly crowded. Our waiter was friendly and made no mistakes besides the pizza mix-up.   If I lived in the area, I don't know if I'd become a regular, but the appeal of pasta makes me want to give Bistango another chance. Next time, though, I'll order something with more of a kick.

Walked in stayed a few minutes, but had to leave, as the AC was not working.  Incredibly loud from happy hour crowd.  Small menu, could not really find anything we wanted to eat.  They have drinks on the menu that are not available, as they are "Winter drinks".  If that is the case, then change the menu.  It is late May.

Found this place as I walked around Philly looking for a good bar for a beer on St. Patty's and found a beer Mecca. I was so blown away by this place. As a matter of fact it may be Philly's only redeming quality... oh and of course the whole Declaration of Independence thing... If I ever happen to find myself in Philly again I will get my hotel as close to this place as possible. With Chimay and the Duvel in my gullet along with some amazing frittes... I would prefer to be in crawling distance. Cheers!

Service What surprised me the most was even with the long lines and being outside. This street vendor actually seems surprisingly jolly. They are very animated and even makes jokes as they collect you cash. Food The white sauce is delicious and the gyro is favorite part then the chicken. I definitely recommend getting the combo because you can get chicken and lamb. Value Excellent $6 dollar get you a pretty big plate of food. Thought personally if the line is to long at the original I would go to the neighboring cart which I think is actually owned by the same company.

After scouring my surrounding area in the brutal heat and humidity, we stumbled upon this "French Mediterranean" place. Buuut it's mostly French (unfortunately); none of the standards like hummus or kebabs are here. However, the food that IS here is quite good. There is a $15 lunch special that we, being the cheap Jews we are, ordered (it comes with an appetizer and an entree). For appetizers, I tried the Truffle Macaroni and Cheese. Shit, they couldn't make that sound stupider? Pairing expensive and elegant truffle with something as kiddy as "mac and cheese"? They may as well have spelled it "cheez." Now that that's out of the way, I must say that the mac and cheese was delicious. It was a decent portion of macaroni with some white cheese and I'm assuming truffle oil, and topped with shavings of great quality parmesan. I also tried my Jewfriend's butternut squash soup (this time there was a fancy French term for it on the menu), and it was creamy and had a good kick. As for entree, I had a Salmon Burger. It was good, with a nice level of moistness, and was served on a brioche bun with lettuce and tomato, with a side of salad or french fries. Naturally, I got the salad because I'm not a fat shit anymore. My vegetarian douche friend got a veggie sandwich, and I heard no complaints from him. Service was good (just one waitress), decor is blegh in my opinion, and prices are reasonable. JUST GET SOME DAMN SHAWARMA ON THE MENU!

Oh my goodness! Huge portions of meat filing! Big 5 pcs of dumplings for 1 buck?! Oh heck yeah!! Amazingly delicious fried or boiled! The sesame pancakes are also very delicious! tastes like pizza hut pan crust with the vietnamese sandwich filing. It's a no brainer, get your butt over here and have some dumplings! For my fellow Koreans, buy the frozen 50pc dumplings for 9 bucks and make duk mandoo gook out of it. Prepare yourself for some serious wow!
Fantastic burgers! The Breakfast Burger was perfectly prepared and incredibly tasty. The service was great, the atmosphere was comfortable and the beer was fresh. What a meal!

This is an excellent restaurant. Ingredients are the highest quality, preparation is creative and more than competent, and service is impeccable. I write only to note two issues for your benefit. First, it's noisy. In my opinion, in a good way. But for those I dined with (working dinner w/ professional colleagues), it was too much. Second, it's slow. We had the prix fixe. I have been to other high end establishments at this pace, but be warned that it is leisurely. That's all. Highly recommended.

I'm going to keep this short and sweet - the exact opposite of Terroir's 50 page menu! Overall a solid 3.5 stars. I rounded up because of the great service. The wine selection was great. Lebanese wine on the menu is always a plus in my book. The food was good (get the meatballs!), but the portions were small. We had to go through 3 rounds of ordering (and several bottles of wine) before we quit. Anyway, besides the menu, this place is chill. A nice solid place if you're in the area but not worth a trip across town...

Great spot to hang, listen to live music, and bring bae. We ordered the Manchego cheese, Roast Chicken, and Mac N'cheese, all of which was DELICIOUS! The music was great but finished by the time we got there. great energy here at this cafe.
My husband and I love ordering here. It's huge portions, so fresh and so cheap! We love the chicken schwarma platter and baklava! The owners are so nice, too!

I went here last year for restaurant week during lunch with a friend. I just wanted to write a quick review (mainly so I can have this restaurant saved on my yelp account). Delicious! From the soup, the homemade pasta, to dessert, delicious! I usually look for good deals and base restaurants on how good the food is compared to how much it costs and let's just say a few weeks ago, I made reservations to come here to pay full price for a meal.

Great little place on the edge of town! The fish tacos were fresh and delicious, we shared them as an app. The lobster Mac and cheese was rich, creamy, and loaded with lobster, definitely recommend it! They do have Hopewell valley wine by the bottle, but we brought our own wine. The menu was eclectic and offered something for everyone, from tacos to mushroom mac and cheese to bacon wrapped scallops. The wait staff was very friendly and attentive. And the free, private parking lot was a definite plus-tough to find downtown. This is a perfect place for a casual date night or a dinner with friends!

My gf and I ordered takeaway over the telephone and she could tell that the person taking the order was having difficulty hearing her because of background noise. I assured her that all would be well, given my excitement about the menu. Unfortunately, she ordered a turkey burger and received a bland veggie burger instead. She was so deflated by the taste and texture that she ended up sharing the decent fries that came with my tasty wings order. She was reluctant to write a review, but since I'd like to try something else from there, I figured I ought to post a review. The wings were piping hot and the sauce was fine. I'd try something else since I'm a northerner with southern roots and I always get excited about southern or southern-ized food.

$$$ ambiance and food quality with $$ price. Modern European interior design - very chic, New American cuisine - tasty and healthy. For brunch fare, I highly recommend the steak and egg, note that they serve wagyu beef.  For lunch, I'd recommend duck salad. Seat outside in their garden on a sunny, and slowly enjoy their thoughtfully prepared dishes. Bon Apetit!

Only tried the pizza and calzone. Pizza (pepperoni) was great but not earth-shatteringly amazing. Tried pepperoni and mushroom calzones. Mushroom calzone was absolutely delicious: thin slices of portobello + homemade ricotta. Highly recommend. Will be returning. Looking forward to trying more things here.

I've heard some mixed reviews on Geno's and I figured I would give it a try. I wasn't all that impressed.  I waited in line for about 15 minutes.  I ordered a cheesesteak with the whiz and onions.  I finally received my cheesesteak opened it and took a bite.  The cheese whiz and onions were amazing.  As for the steak itself, it was very dry and cold.  I think I will try Pat's next time.

My seemingly nutella-less and fluff-less Nutella Fluff shake emerged after 12 minutes, and in a coffee cup*, yet I didn't hate my experience at this tiny storefront down some stairs**. The staff at this tenant of the Atrium Shops were friendly as elsewhere but seemed a bit overwhelmed based on wait time and the loud discussions about how in the weeds they were. Nutella-Fluff $5.51 -$5.00 $1.00 *The fact that it was immediately sippable through the tiny hole indicates they overblended it a bit. **the address is correct but not helpful unless you see the sign and know to descend. This has more reviews so I guess it's the OG, but too lazy to check via FTR and/or Google.

I thought I would just saunter in here on a Sunday night and plop down at the bar and have dinner.  I would probably have half the bar to myself, right?   Wrong-o. The place was jammed.  I was able to get the last seat at the bar and good thing as after that, there was a waiting list, just to sit at the bar.  I bet the restaurant was fully committed.   I bet this is for good reason, because this place is fantastic.  The decor is sort of TriBeCa rustic, and the space is a good size - not some cramped West Village joint.  I ordered a cocktail and the pappardelle.  Ohhhhhh, the pappardelle.  It was tossed in a lamb bolognese that was infused with mint.  Clever fellas.  My grandma used to love cooking a rack of lamb and serving it with mint jelly.  The mint really made the lamb bolognese.  The pasta was cooked perfectly and had a dollop of burrata on top.  The portion was big enough for dinner - not some tiny small-plate BS or massive "family-style" BS either - just perfect. I can't wait to go back as they have a roast chicken for two that I have heard is off the charts.
A wonderful japanese/korean experience. The scallion pancakes are AMAZING!

Consistently good and reasonably priced, Petite Abeille  offers no frills, quality food. I've been for brunch, lunch and dinner, on numerous occasions. With now four locations (my favorites are Union Square & East Village), Petite Abeille is serving up authentic Belgian cuisine, from waffles to mussels... to great beer. For brunch, their authentic Belgian waffles are awesome. Served plain with powdered sugar, or with strawberry sauce or berries, or even with a scoop of vanilla ice cream, their waffles are a close tie to Wafels and Dinges (my favorite food truck--post coming soon). For lunch, Petite Abeille makes the best Croque Madame I've had since I was in France -- a grilled sandwich with ham and gruyere cheese with a sunny side up egg. Their burgers are also good, and their tuna is surprisingly memorable. For dinner, my favorite starters are the fried calamari and french onion soup; both are made just right, and keep me coming back for dinner. Petite Abeille is also known for their PEI mussels. My favorites are the classic tomato broth with tarragon and the creamy white wine and shallot sauce. The creamy beer and bacon broth is flavorful, but a tad too heavy for a massive cauldron filled with mussels. Monday is half price beer. Tuesday is half price wine. Wednesday is all you can eat mussels. And Thursday is Lobster night. Delicious brunch served everyday.

I used to love going to Jimmies a few years back. They seemed like they used to be on top of their game. Nowadays, not so much. I am nostalgic towards the Savin Rock memories they have plastered all over their walls, but my experience there is something I never want to remember. First off, you'd think a place specializing in seafood would have decent lobster bisque. That assumption was my first mistake. When it came out, and I see another Yelper noticed, it had grown an awkward thick skin on the top of it. I literally had my wife take the first few spoonfuls off the top, because I was refused to eat some thick slop they mislabeled as lobster bisque. It was mediocre tasting when I finally did try some. Too salty for me. Next, the waitress was nothing but completely rude. She not only reeked of cigarettes (and Jimmies has a strong seafood scent, so being able to smell like anything else is impressive) but everything she did was rude and snappy. I couldn't help but get distracted by the bright green piece of gum she was chomping on as she served us. The icing on the cake was when we sat there for over 45 minutes waiting for nothing other than a toasted tuna sandwich for my son that she originally forgot to add onto the ticket. Ridiculous. Only receiving two stars because I remember how it used to be when I was younger.

Just came back from lunch here and am already itching to go back. It's in the old Bonte space, which I actually think is a better fit for Luke's. Has a very New England feel as soon as you walk in with the wood panel walls and fishing nets. When you open the door, the smell of drawn butter hits you, and you will instantly melt. Spring out the extra few bucks for the combo. The Maine Root Sodas add another bit of uniqueness. I tried the Root Beer and Ginger sodas, but will definitely go for the Blueberry next time to be immersed in all Maine deliciousness. I was a little disappointed at first to not see fries on the menu, but after my first bite into the roll, I understood. The chips add the perfect amount of saltiness to the meal, and are not overly heavy like a fry. As for the roll- pure bliss. Perfectly toasted buttered bun with a generous filling of fresh lobster meat. No fillers here. Just lightly seasoned so you can still savor the true lobster flavor. Yes it is a bit pricey for a quick lunch, but the quality is on the same level, if not higher than other seafood restaurants in the area. It's worth every penny.

Oh baby baby, gimme some more of THAT! Popped into Peaches HotHouse with a mean growling stomach, looking for a late brunch. I could have blindly pointed at anything on the menu and been happy-- it all sounded that good. I went with the corn cakes, andouille, and fried egg; yes, yes, and yes. The corn cakes had a sort of crunch on the outside, and then a nice pancake feel on the inside. Sweet corn was scattered throughout, and gave it that creamy sweetness I was looking for. The andouille was too good for words. Too. Good. For. Words. And the egg was cooked perfectly. This review really is a simple one. It come's down to this: Peaches, I love you. See you again soon.

I wasn't thrilled with this place. Maybe I didn't order the right thing? The jalapeno poppers were good enough--you could tell they used fresh jalapeno, and were filled with cream cheese which is SO much better than cheddar. Main entree? Not so good. On the menu it says the shrimp and grits comes with cilantro, which I personally prefer in smaller quantities (bc it is usually so liberally applied by restaurants nowadays). So I was asking our server how much cilantro was on there, to which she replied with something along the lines of "the normal amount". Thanks for that. So I asked for my dish light on the cilantro. When it comes out, turns out it's a cilantro sauce. Which the dish badly needed to balance out the richness. Would have been nice of her to try and describe the dish to me somewhat! The shrimp were pretty overcooked, and the grits had a funny flavor and were sweet. Maybe they picked up some flavor from the cast iron serving dish? I ate about a third of my entree. Of course the waitress didn't comment on that. I think she didn't like me bc I wasn't drinking. I had a bite of my friend's pulled pork sandwich which was pretty good. And the host was really nice and helpful!

Second time here. Food, wine and prices are 3 stars, but the staff is really friendly and the bread is pretty good. I've tried the octopus salad, flatbread, cheese and meats, French fries and goat cheese salad app. The goat cheese app and fries were the best things there.

The best Thai place in NYC. It's crowded for dinner, and pretty tiny but the sevice is great and you feel comfortable - hey you are in a city where space is expensive! We have been dining here since the beginning of our moving in NYC. Although most likely there is the line - but it is efficient - you can go arond and they call you when your place is ready. We coudn't renounce to this Thai after we had a baby, and kept going with the stroller. The baby loves the food too

Having read the positive and negative reviews, we did not know what to expect. Traif was busy so our table was in the noisy area just opposite the bar and it was hard to hear. Our waitress was so friendly and positive that she made up for the noise level. We went with her recommendations and were generally delighted. We had 8 items for a party of three and were happy with all of them except the last. The peach salad was terrific, the brussel sprouts outstanding, scallops, shrimp, foie gras, and tuna were all delicious (the tuna portion was very small but I loved it served on the eggplant tempura). Wish we had tried the missions figs. We ordered the short rib sliders instead of the glazed baby back ribs and that was our only misstep. The sliders were fine - just not nearly as interesting as the rest of the items. Also we had cocktails earlier at another place so were not able to try anything from the intriguing cocktail menu. Won't make the mistake next time!
Great selection of sake but the service felt rushed, my okonomiyaki was burnt, I was over charged on my card, and the soybeans were not that great. Awesome music though

Unfortunately, I have to retract my aforementioned comment on their bubble teas. I usually never order any of their fruity flavored bubble teas, but I did a few weekends ago. Huge mistake because it was powder based. Sorry, powdered fruit is unacceptable and I won't be repeating that mistake again.

Had a great time. The boyfriend and I were looking for a place to watch the hockey game and this was the closest place we could find. First off the service is wonderful. Eamon was a great bartender and a very attentive server. We never had an empty drink, food was prompt, and we had wet naps before we could think to ask for them. We got wings, loaded fries and the bruschetta. They were all great. The bruschetta had a unique bbq taste to it, the wings were plentiful, and you can never really go wrong with fries. The atmosphere isn't for everyone but I enjoyed it. It has a divey feel and plays music for an older crowd. I like that kind of music and I don't mind dives so I had a good time. I'll be back if I'm in the area. Don't forget to check in for a bogo drink!

I walked in after the theatre and was very surprised to see the place packed! Got the last table available and enjoyed our meal and service thoroughly. Wife had large Chicken salad and I had very good sauteed liver. Ambience was great.  It has a NYC vibe. Would definitely go back--but next time I'll make reservations.

We came in for a quick snack before a show.  There was one open table in this tiny restaurant, and we were promptly seated.  The server was extremely friendly and easy-going, but very busy (we had to remind him about our water and about our extra bread).  They had a great bottle wine deal, which we were obediently suckered into.  The gluten-free bread was good (not great by my gluttonous standards, but good).  We shared the small cheese plate - which was a healthy serving of four cheeses - and the meatballs.  Our food was quickly serviced and we were on our way not much later. In conclusion: if I were a gluten-free eater, I would definitely go out of my way to get here.  If I were in the neighborhood, I'd return for a quick meal. I wouldn't go out of my way to dine, but we enjoyed our snack!

Love the ambience, the beer on tap, and the service. I've never been there on a busy night, but the food is good, bartenders are really friendly, and it's on a quiet corner. What more can you ask for?  :D
This soup is my addiction.  Seriously.  Best place for lunch in China Town.

Food here is very good. I liked the fritto misto and the lamb three ways. The rigatoni bolognese was also tasty. The problem here lies in the attitudes of the waitstaff and hosts who seem to be ambivalent about fulfilling their roles in the restaurant. For example, when I check my coat give me a coat check ticket. When I ask for bread or water don't ignore my requests. Simple stuff. otherwise pretty good food.

Pizza Brain is a high quality pizza shop behind a vintage veil.  The setting is simple and mellow.  Bar stools and memorabilia face the oven and a few tables are set up on the Little Baby's side.  The service is free spirited and seem like they enjoy making pizza.  No use spoiling the experience, it's worth it for the pizza. The pizza is good.  One of the best plain pies I've had in the area, affectionately named "Jane" by the creators.  The specialty and white pies are high quality and worth the buy, but I constantly find my self coming back for a slice of the plain Jane.  It's a combination of its parts: the crust is crunchy with black pepper polishing the bottom, the sauce is sweet and slightly spicy and the cheese brings it all together.  The addition of fresh basil on top is both aesthetic and tasty.  Cowabunga dude.  *****

The Little Owl is a charming little place on what is basically a movie set of the West Vilage. It's so charming and pleasant, in fact, that I've been there a number of times even though I've never had food that was anything other than B- or even C food. This last visit i ordered the arctic char, which, when it came was a piece of fish s little bigger than a deck of cards that was rare and oily on the inside and dried out from the grill on the outside. The only other thing on the plate was an indifferent green salad that looked like it was just a grabbed handful from the "mixed greens" bin at Fairway. This, for $19. I've been underwhelmed by the fish before as well--maybe it's not that the food is so-so, it's that the fish is! the lunch menu isn't large, though, and faced with the prospect of a hamburger, omelette, of filet mignonette, I guess I keep going for the me thing. I'd say that this is a wonderful place for a date or lazy afternoon, but not a place to travel to for the food.
Great food, good prices and friendly service.   In from California not knowing where to go after a tour and found this on yelp. Highly recommend!

Definitely one of my top 5 brunch spots in the city. Food's creative and extremely tasty, great ambiance that matches the neighborhood's character, prices are reasonable, and they serve La Colombe. What more could you ask for? Been coming here for years now, and they never disappoint.

Went here for brunch with some friends. Super laid-back place, cool vibe, and funky food. I loved the innovative combinations they made, combining Filipino and traditional American breakfast food. Service was great, they were patient and explained a lot of the menu items for us. I decided to try the prawn dish with poached eggs. I didn't really enjoy it, I thought the flavors didn't combine well. The flavored spinach or kale- I'm not sure what the vegetable was- definitely didn't sit well with the rest of the dish, and it was smothered onto the eggs and english muffins. But the prawns were delicious! And after trying all my friends' choices (the mango french toast- superb!), I was pretty disappointed in my dish. My friend got the eggplant dish- it was something like a fluffy omelette and he wasn't terribly impressed either. I definitely appreciate the innovative fusion, but I thought the taste of the food fell short. I'd say presentation, service, and atmosphere is definitely great, but for the sake of taste, the food wasn't spectacular.

Brooklyn Ice House is as good as it gets. Awesome backyard outdoor area with tons of benches to hang out with friends. I honestly can't think of a better place to go on a Saturday afternoon with friends. Since you're in Red Hook, things are definitely going to be much cheaper than in other parts of the city. But the one thing that will keep me coming back is their Frito Pie, which is basically nachos made with fritos - topped with chili cheese and jalepenos. Seriously, my friends and I must have devoured 5 order of these. Their pulled pork sandwich, bacon wrapped hot dog, and burgers aren't half bad either. I can't wait to come back again the next time I'm in the hood.

First let me say their mozzarella is good and fresh, a bit salty but its a good product. Now lets get to my reason for one star. The owner, or at least I think he's the owner (big guy) is RUDE AS HELL! On a number of occasions he's made comments that I was interfering with his life by shopping at his store and giving him my money. The nerve of me to come in when he's busy. But the icing on the cake was Easter morning. I called the shop on Saturday and asked if they would be open on Easter and if they would have fresh mozzarella. Gentleman on phone very politely stated yes they would be open. My BF went there in the morning for me and when he asked for the mozzarella the owner said " I hate these F-en guys coming out on Christmas and Easter". REALLY? Don't worry, won't happen again. I'll take my business elsewhere. You're not the only place around and frankly you're overpriced.

Service is good, atmosphere is great. Cute little place with doors open to the street. I agree with another yelper-remember the food being better 2 years ago. This time I had the ravioli, which didn't taste homemade at all. Sauce didn't have much flavor either.  I don't think I'll come back again.

i went for brunch with a small group and thought it was very nice.  service was friendly and we were never lacking anything. i got the crab eggs benedict - which was mighty tasty and i enjoyed the potatoes and field greens on the side (the greens were really well dressed). another got the challah french toast and devoured the entire thing. and our other friend got the create your own omelet which she said was also really well done. i'm not sure about other meals but i will highly recommend going for a weekend brunch...remember BYO mimosas!

O.M.D. Oh my deliciousness! I've only tried the pork belly sandwich, but that's what they're known for! I had the corn on the side as well, which was interesting as well. This is really about the sandwich though. Yes it's already been compared to a Banh mi, vietnamese sandwich, and that is what I compare it to. It is just like that and more! It is so fresh, hot and flavorful. I am not the most experienced in eating pork belly sandwiches but from what I hear, they can come as being too fatty and flavorless at some places. Not here. At Num Pang, the meat is charred...but not too charred! If I must say anything about the corn, I think it was unusual. However, I ate it, and my boyfriend who hates anything unusual, is actually addicted to it! About the building, it is another one of those NYC spots that you can't find unless you look really hard. So small and dark, you won't notice it, but you can smell it at least! One more thing -It is really a take out place, but there is supposed to be seating upstairs, which looks pretty cool. Oh and BTW, they were in Maxim for a best sandwiches review - it was a weird one they made, like pig head or something.

Things you need to know -CASH ONLY! -Cheap. You can eat a meal for about $10. -You might have to wait in line because it gets crowded. There are only 2 chairs to sit on while waiting. If those chairs are occupied, you will have to stand. While we were waiting, the waiter came over and took our orders. I like the efficiency. I had the lemongrass chicken with bun (noodles). The amount of chicken they gave me was generous! It was pretty good to be honest. Toilet are average, could be nicer.

This is amateur show. Period. I am clueless as why people would go there -- the only conclusion I can draw is THEY KNOW NOTHING ABOUT GOOD SUSHI!!!!! The rice is grainy and hard. The seaweed (nori) is soggy. The Sushi is simply not cohesive. The Shumei tasted like came straight out from microwave. Ok, the miso is good. But that's the only thing. Don't waste your time. Sushi here is amateur hours.

Service was fast. I was expecting more n the flavor of the good. Not much of a step up from TGIF's. The ambience is clever but the quality of the food is lacking. I would not recommend this as a destination. If you happen to be in the area and want a step up from Chili's you'll love this.

I am confused why people dislike this place so much. I noticed the little touches that made me appreciate this place that my sister pointed out. For example, listing local farms where they get their food from (very SF). I also like that it wasn't crowded. I can understand why some may dislike the food here mainly because the menu is 'earthy', but everyone I was with including myself enjoyed it... Try the Ploughman's plate.

Ate dinner there tonight with 4 adults and 7 (yes 7) kids and it was great! Had the pasta with eggplant and ricotta salata, spaghetti with clams, pappardelle with veal and mushrooms which was awesome, and some pizzas, and meatballs. Everyone loved the food, our serve was great, and they managed to accommodate us without a reservation! The best part was the Nutella pizza! Great lil place!
zomg yes

I went here with the boyfriend after he enjoyed a nice after work visit with another friend.  We usually don't sit outdoors, but that's mainly a distaste for sidewalk seating, so the sideyard patio is a huge plus.  They do need some kind of insect-control.   I recommend ordering the sangria here very soon before they realize that their glass is way too big for the price, and could serve it in a glass half the size without a problem. I ordered the tofu burger off of the special menu, which was interesting.  I ordered it without cheese or mayo, which wasn't needed anyway because the burger is very moist.  The only downfall is that the burger isn't the same consistency throughout, so once you take a bite, the tofu can slide out of the fried shell that surrounds it (don't know how to describe it...) if you're not careful.  BUT, all the flavors were good.  It would have made an excellent tofu scramble, just maybe not the best burger substitute. Also, we forgot to order eggplant fries at the beginning, and the waiter brought out an order on the house for us to try!  They are awesome huge steak fries sized slices of eggplant.  So juicy and yummy. They will get better, as the service was a bit awkward, but genuine.

Let me first say that I'm not a fan of French cuisine.  I'm a bit clueless as to what to order, which explains why I ordered the pasta instead of something more frenchy. The restaurant ambiance is very cozy with a tables along both walls in an open layout.  Not a bad place for a date night, although I did come here earlier in the evening so the place wasn't packed at that time.  Service was very cordial and friendly.  The gentleman who greeted me offered me any open table. So as mentioned, I ordered the pappardelle pasta.  Probably not the best choice at a French restaurant.  It was a bit average - the pasta itself was good, but the sauce was a bit bland.  Portion size was reasonable, but being more of a meat and potatoes person, I was missing the meat.  My dining partner ordered the duck con fit and said it was very good.  I don't eat duck so I can't really comment as to how good it was. Overall, it was a good place for a good meal.  I'm not a fan of French cuisine so I can't say I'll return.  If I was a fan, this may be my regular place because of the kindness of the staff, the non-pretentiousness of the restaurant, and the reasonable prices of the menu items.  If you're a fan, give this place a try.
