Two stars might be bit of a generous rating.  Are the people who gave 5 stars smoking some of that philadelphia crack I hear about?  Now I've only dined there once, and definitely will not be going back, but the food was a complete turn off.  I ordered the black cod, usually a fairly easier fish to prepare but not your typical italian dish I admit, and it was completely over cooked and prepared in a sauce rich in oil and not complimenting the fish at all.  I barely ate half.  Our waiter was another bad spot.  Completely unprofessional and emotional.  Keep your shit at home broooooooooooooooooo!  Salad was good but not too adventurous.
Misconduct Burger is no Gooddog Burger, but still good (get it with the spicy mayo).
Best french fries I've ever had. Please support this place and go there often so I will always be able to eat these fries. Thank you. My BF says the burgers are amazing.

I have passed this location so many times and it always has a long line outside...this time no line so figured, let's give it a try! If you have more than 2 people? Get ready for a wait...they say 10 mns but we waited a lot longer as at least 6 other parties of 2 were seated...5 of which came in after us...so as we sat there starving and waiting, everyone kept coming in, waiting a few mns and getting seated.  That was frustrating...Mind you we had 3 people, yes awkward number, but when we were finally seated, there were 2 other 4 tops available!!  Plus be sure to go in the waiting area where the hostess is, this is separate from the dining areas. (to the left) Ok now on to the food... we went during brunch and the specials looked good.. I got the barbie and ken's his and hers sliders -- one topped with mixed greens/prosciutto/creole mustard/brie was good, but the one with mixed greens/cranberry-strawberry-red onion compote/brie was not.  The meat is not seasoned well and they're quite thick/large for sliders...2 were pretty filling.  This came w. a side of sweet potato fries (YUM!) and slaw that had green apple slices. Bf got the brunch drunk love special -- breakfast shrimp and potato cakes w. tarragon (no shrimp in sight, no taste of shrimp either), topped w. arugula, grilled asparagus, grilled balsamic filet (eh), poached eggs (creamy) and a roasted tomato-shallot -dill hollandaise sauce (somehow cheesy...quite dark for hollandaise).  His came with a side of home fries which he didnt understand since he had the potato cakes...that's a LOT of potato on one plate....He also got a side of bacon which was good. Mom got the 2 eggs any style bfast.  Cant really go wrong w. this...2 eggs, home fries and toast w. orange marmalade.  She got a side of sausage which was tasty. I think the overall winner was the coffee.  Soooo good i dont even know how many refills i got...Next time i'll get a cup while waiting (oh yes, hot coffee in the wtg room). So all in all this location did not win me over...I like the other one better.  All servers and the hostess were friendly tho, so please don't think service was bad.  Guess we were expecting more w. the food since this place is always packed.

I brought my team here for lunch today and everybody loved it! I got the turkey sandwich that was SO great.  The perfect ratio of meat to bread (I like meat!).  My team members are raving about the Italian Stallion and the Prosciutto sandwich.  Everybody was impressed by the home made, high quality meats and toppings.

Inspired by the balmy mid-March weather, we stopped in for a mid-morning treat. Though the clouds overhead deterred us from sitting outdoors, the indoors was pleasant enough. I had a bagel with cream cheese and lox- no frills, fresh, and more reasonably priced (@7.25) than some other local places. However, the no frills part may deter some from this version of the treat, which could certainly be embellished with olives, capers, tomatoes, and the usual fixins.' The coffee and espresso was eye opening and bottomless. The staff was friendly and reminisced about their twenty years in the hood. The best part of our sit down: we discovered a battered "Where's Waldo?" book in the corner and realized we had both sub-consciously committed to memory his page by page locations. I will definitely come back to sip coffee and read in the morning hours (on weekdays) and look forward to trying the promising lunch menu.

I've found it incredibly difficult to find a good, authentic Chinese restaurant in Connecticut, and the only reason I came here was because my Chinese friend told me that "all the Chinese people talk about it...I don't know how good the food is, though."  Well, I thought, I'd give it a try. I ate here with my brother, hoping for a nice meal and a good dining atmosphere, especially given the positive reviews Butterfly received on Yelp.  The first thing I noticed after our food arrived, however, was how quickly the food got cold -- much more so than I have experienced at almost any other Chinese restaurant I've visited.  Perhaps the food had already been cooling before it reached the table? The real nightmare started, however, when my brother noticed that the steamed fish we ordered still had scales on it, conspicuously sticking up in the air.  It really didn't bother me that much, but my brother thought it was a huge deal.  He complained to the manager, who took it upon herself to tell us that this was the first time she heard the complaint and thus, would only tell the cook to be more careful "next time".  Not happy with her response, my brother asked for a discount, to which the manager responded by only giving us 10% off our entire order.  My brother asked instead for 50% off the steamed fish dish, to which the manager -- clearly pissed off -- begrudgingly agreed to...though, not before telling us that we shouldn't be asking for such a steep discount given that we ate nearly the entire dish (uh, so are we just supposed to NOT eat the dish if you refuse to give us a replacement?). Needless to say, I left the restaurant in a sour mood.  I guess the food was okay, but the service was so rude that I would need to be forced to go back again.

You know you've picked a good restaurant for dinner when, 3 minutes before the end of happy hour, your waiter lets you order two rounds of drinks each to stock up at happy hour prices. And drinking that much wine certainly doesn't take away from the food. As a group of 5, we got: the cheese plate, flagship salad, meatballs, veggie flatbread and two mac and cheeses (the original and the pork belly). Suffice to say, it was clean plates all around and I'm sure I'll be back.

I'm in New York wanting to try something new, something ethnic. So when Japanese gets thrown into the mix, I feel a little - eh, I've tried that before, maybe something else? But boy was I glad to have gotten the chance to try Sakagura. I am a big fan of Japanese food - whether it is sushi, ramen, izakaya .. you name it. I went to Sakagura for lunch (they have a special lunch set that is definitely worth trying!) and their service was really great. They have imported sake from Japan and a really nice interior that brought me back to Japan. (Their bathroom is so amazing! A must see! haha) Having soba with sobayu automatically racked up points for authenticity! & their sesame ice cream with sweet soy sauce. Yes, soy sauce was really great to try.

I visited some of my best college friends in NYC this weekend, and UVA was the final dinner before my flight Monday morning. And wow, what a way to end a really fantastic weekend! Eight of us spent almost three hours enjoying food, wine, and great conversation around a dark wood table next to a fireplace, the atmosphere was perfectly cozy and intimate. I'm a huge Riesling fan, and thoroughly enjoyed the Mercer Estates Riesling that we shared -  notes of apricot and lime, delicious. Those were the elements that really won me over, but the food was good too - though not the best I've ever had. I ordered the homemade ravioli stuffed with artichoke and ham, served in a goat cheese tomato sauce. I thought the pasta itself was a little too thick for the delicate sauce and filling. Overall, it was a wonderful experience, and I'd definitely recommend it...actually I've already told everyone else I know that lives in NYC to check it out :)

I really liked the atmosphere here! The pizza was excellent (it's not traditional napoletano pizza, but it's the square thin-crust kind) and the drink list is EXTENSIVE.  I was impressed that a pizza place had such an extensive martini and scotch list!  Service was great too.
Had A great culinary experience at Mezetto ... the food the service the wonderful atmosphere ....I will be going back soon to have this special Falafel in a bun!!!!
went there for a saturday lunch with some friends and we were well treated! very cozy and finely decorated place with deliciously food and tea.

Came here last night on a whim as my girl had a job nearby .. really YUMMY!! I had a spinach, cheese and ham omelette - now I ordered turkey bacon so they effed up (not a big ham fan) but once I took a bite I was like, man, this ham is AIGHT! Oh, and tons of spinach in the omelette .. My girl had a BEAST of a chicken club that came with fries .. YUMMY .. we had our waitress, Blanca (who was A-MAZING, I mean really, when I'm balling the the BOSS I am I will leave her a hundo as a tip) Anyhow - so my girl has Blanca fix her coffee to go (She's very particular) and Blanca wrecked shop with it .. Cafe con leche style . Yup, I want to go back right now.
This is by far my favorite restaurant in Manhattan.  It beats 11 Madison Park hands down. The food was so unique, so tasty and brilliant. I cannot wait to go back!

Considering I only eat dumplings when I go to Chinese restaurant and the pork and crab dumplings are what this place is known for, I liked it. The waiters are fast and pretty much tell you what to order so word to the wise don't take too much time because they want to turn the tables over fast. You're also going to be seated with random strangers so that might be something to note too especially if you plan on putting away some tsing tao's.
I have always liked this place. But I went again today and the service was atrocious. I generally do not write reviews, but i was appalled. I've had better service at IHOP.
Shrimp tacos, crab guac, and blood orange margaritas a must!

I absolutely loved the chicken thigh and the pork skewers.  Gizzards and chicken thigh "oysters" weren't as tasty as I thought they'd be, but provided a nice contrast to everything else.  I also enjoyed the donburi and chicken karaage.  The place is rather small, but we were seated quickly.

This review is for the champagne brunch on Sundays.   I splurged with 6 other friends and came to Moshulu on an empty stomach hoping to eat a bunch and get nice and toasty.  The decor is a little uptight, like country club or hotel, but it's interesting to be dining on a floating vessel.   We were quickly seated and informed about the buffet-style brunch and unlimited champagne, mimosas and kir royales, yum!  The food was your standard selection of 2 carving stations, pastries, desserts, soups, salads, and some carby dishes.  Nothing was spectacular, though we all kept on going for the pork belly mac and cheese.  Even though the food was nothing to shout about, I was impressed by the great service.  They really keep the beverages flowing and keep your table clear so you can continue gorging yourself, haha.  We'll definitely be back for another brunch splurge!

totally a fan - would've given 5 but my expectations of the classic I got was a little different than I thought.  Still delicious.  My girlfriends was way better though.  So If I got hers, it would've been 5 stars. Pork buns - drool.

I live in Iselin and knows all the restaurants around this place.  I use to drive by Urban spice number of times but never had been there.  On account of my job, I travel a lot both in US and International and a restaurant geek.  Today, after watching a movie I thought I will check Urban Spice and let me tell you it is a sub-standard hyped up restaurant.  I walked in at 9 pm and had to wait for 10 min.  There was no usher and I went inside and asked someone to give me a table. I was seated after 15 mins.  I ordered two glasses of house wine,  Murg Dum biriyani, Vegetable Kadai and a Chicken entree. Inspite of my wait,  I would have given good rating if the food was reasonably good ins but let me tell you,  the food was abysmally of  poor quality.  I paid around 77 $ and left very disappointed.   I would never go there again.
I've never had to wait to get a table here. The staff are always super friendly and really accommodating. The pizza is absolutely delicious and I can't fault it.

Came here for fried chicken after being turned away from root and bone. chicken and waffle came w 3 pc of chicken, it's tender, moist, lightly battered, but it's lacking the flavor, kind of bland! it certainly didn't wow me; waffle was soft but not crispy. it's not on brunch meun but we ordered it anyways, friend had shrimp and grits, it was presented in a very pretty way, love the sausage, shrimp was abit on overcooked side, I also love that it came w little bit of snow pea greens. The restaurant is in the center of LES, on a corner street, w all doors wide open, it's huge, w different seatings indoor and outdoor.  Our waitress was friendly and cute but slightly inexperienced. I'd go back to try other things but probably not fried chicken.

I've been coming here since I was a little girl so this place is home to me.  My parents were married here.  My bridal shower was here.  My daughter's Sweet 16 party is going to be here in August 2013.  Great food and ambiance.  The best part is that you can have a party or wedding here for a very reasonable price around $40 a plate depending upon the options you choose.

DO NOT TAKE CHILDREN, or anyone else for that matter. The food here is fine. Nothing to write home about but also nothing too great. Solid 5/10. However, what really stuns me about this place is that it has only 1 bathroom (one of those 1 toilet rooms for both genders). Given that there is only 1 bathroom, both men, women, and children will be using this. So why the owner would decide to line the walls with pornography is not understandable to me. Not just one or two pictures- literally all four walls covered with it. I cannot imagine if I brought my kid there for lunch and they ended up walking into a bathroom like that. Totally inappropriate and seeing as they didn't check id at the door, potentially illegal (distributing obscene images to a minor anyone?). I would avoid this place until it gets some class.

I come here about once a month with friends for a small drinking session. This is my to go place for drinks and small dishes (izakaya). The prices are really good and the food is delicious! I love their green tea udon and their nabeyaki to name a few. They also have specials, which include sashimi at times. Pretty fresh. Of course we have to get drinks here, but since I'm not a sake person, thry have many other options such as plum wine and mixed drinks. Very good. I always get this drink with the jellies in it. Totally my style haha. From service to food/drink selection and prices, this place deserves a five star. Also the area is in time sqaure, which usually = subpar food imo, so this is a well appreciated place for their location.

Heck yeah!! These dumplings are awesome! A little bit of a pain to wait in line for but worth the weight. Most of the time I'm not sure what I'm getting but it is always good!!! If you are in the downtown area and need something yummy this is it!!

Always walked by but never came in until a friend recommended this place.  First off, this place is huge...  Never would have known from the outside.  Sat on the second floor which was very cozy.  The waitress greeted us and after chatting found out that they have karaoke and that they serve til 2!!!  We shared a sushi platter and a couple of special rolls which were delicious.  Not an expert sushi eater but what we had tasted very good and very fresh.  Finished with a couple of sake bombs.  Overall, friendly staff and very tasty food.  Will definitely be back!!!
Went here last evening and had their veal chop. It was excellent. My wife had the polenta with mushrooms and it was delicious. I finished the veal with her polenta. Would recommend it.

I really enjoyed my dinner here. Went here on a saturday night with a reservation and there was no wait (5 stars just for that!) The interior is very cute and french--everything works well together and the place felt very intimate. I got the salmon tartare appetizer, which was amazing! It was SO good, and it came with a very well-dressed side salad with veggies and even some fruit (i think mango?). For my entree,I got the salmon, which was cooked to perfection with a very crispy layer of skin on top. The restaurant is on the high end of mid-range, and perhaps even a bit pricey, but I thought the food and service warranted the higher price. Definitely would recommend this place and would love to come back.

Best Greek food in NYC!! Love this place, I go here all the time cuz I work on the block and I never get tired of it!! The red snapper and the sea bass with lemon potatoes always hits the spot!! Def recommend!!

The ramen taste alright but the meat portion isn't quite that much. I most likely would choose terakawa ramen because u can choose any size, plus it cost less than here. But I do like hiro's takoyaki because they have more octopus in it and it's slightly bigger than terakawa.

First time to the city!  Went to carmines for our first NYC meal...almost spoiled us for the rest of our stay!! It was a holiday so the whole city was abuzz.  Carmines was a madhouse (totally a good sign!)!  We lucked out and snagged seats at the bar where, despite being swamped with orders, the multitasking genius of a bartender hooked us up with a Very decent chianti.  I decided toindulge in one of my old passions and ordered  linguine and clams.  The bread they bought was nearly to die for and the conversations with friendly new yorkers was an added treat.  The food came and it looked fresh and smelled heavenly.  The smell was NOT deceiving!!! Every bite was off the chart! Not overly creamy Like most linguine and clam dishes I have had in the past at "wanna be" Italian places.  The pasta tasted homemade as well.  We all ate every bite on our plates.  My mom ordered eggplant parmesan...and it was off the charts as well.  It took all my self control (which was running thin due to the chianti) not to lick the platter!  We  indulged in some tiramasu for dessert and it was insanely good. All fresh ingredients, and it makes  all the difference.  Thank heaven it is located in the middle of a big city where you HAVE to walk it off.  If you plan right, you can cruise a few rounds, shop and go back for round two!! A definite NYC Do !!!!

This is in my top 3 places to take people when they come to the city from out of town. I hate to be repetitive but... SOUP.  DUMPLINGS. There is simply no comparison.  I was skeptical at first but after my first bite I was in love.  I am not a big guy but I can finish an entire helping by myself (if you've been there you know that's terribly gluttonous).   I LOVE that the servers scowl at you if you don't start with the soup dumplings.  So awesome. Everything I have ever had here is good.  The noodles are good.  The standards (Kung Pow, Tso's) are good.  The crazy stuff is good.  Just a fantastic all-around Chinese restaurant. I do hate that they don't take reservations and sometimes the wait is a bit... well... just whets my appetite more to be honest with you. I gotta say, though, why won't these darn places start taking credit cards?  Hit an ATM before you go because they are cash only!

good food, but very slow service.  BUT the live bands were awesome and made the wait tolerable! It was very relaxing to listen to the music and eat some good food.  The   southern fried chicken served with mac & cheese and okra,  was really good!  A bit pricey but i enjoyed it!

Every single time I've been here, I've always had a reservation. And every single time, I've ALWAYS had to wait at least 20 minutes to be seated. They clearly take way too many reservations. Two Saturdays ago, my family had a reservation for 4 for my father's birthday. It was for 7:30PM. Granted, this was a Saturday night, but we still had to wait 20 minutes. What's the point of a reservation then?  When I asked the manager Tom at 7:45 why it was taking so long he said "We're waiting for tables to get up". Not only was that the same lame excuse we heard when we checked in, but honestly it doesn't matter. They clearly don't understand the concept of a reservation. On the positive side of things, I told our server Jeff that I was vegetarian and he did a good job of notifying me of the hidden animal products in different dishes. But the bar was overwhelmed and drinks took a while to come out, another sign that they weren't equipped to handle as many people as they took on. Tom later came by to "make sure everything was okay" but honestly we would have rather been sat on time than have some random schmo come aimlessly small talk with us. They gave us a big piece of cake for my dad, which was polite, I guess. Overall: at PF Chang's in Princeton, your reservation means nothing. The lettuce wraps are always good though.

I really wanted to be blown away by ABC Kitchen however after our experiences, I was not. Overrated? I think so. I did enjoy the ambiance. It's casual, inviting, has large opened space, upbeat and has a bit of "shabby chic"-ness to it. The patrons range from a young couple in their early 20s on a date, a group of girls dolled up for the evening to a couple in their 50s enjoying a casual dinner out. Unfortunately, I was less than enthused about the food. It was just not memorable enough which was surprising for me since I've heard so much praise. I'm not saying food was bad; just not something I'd expect from a Jean Georges establishment. Service was great. Upon arrival we were immediately shown to our table and the entire time the staff was courteous, polished with our water glasses constantly refilled. I even forgive them for messing up on my order. Perhaps I'll return. I hope for a better food experience on the next visit.

Yesterday I went to make a reservation on OpenTable for The Smith and it said 1:30pm was available, as I clicked 1:30 - the system said the time was no longer available. I was very annoyed. I called the restaurant and the hostess very nicely offered to put us on the wait list at that moment, so when we went there we wouldn't have to wait as long. We arrived before 1:30 and were told 15-20 minutes. After about 15 minutes we got antsy and considered going elsewhere. The hostess wasn't being very helpful and just kept saying the same amount of time and we ended up not sitting until 2:30. I was quite irritated. Luckily we had the nicest waiter ever, and even though it wasn't his fault that we waited so long, he brought us complimentary chips, french toast and drinks on the house. He was fun and nice and appreciated our sense of humor. And as always, the food was delicious. A bit upset the mozz & tomato sammich was removed from the menu - what's that about?

We have been coming here off and on for a few years. Tonight I called ahead to watch the steelers game, and bartender STEVE answered the phone. Steve was accommodating and made sure we had what we needed while watching the game. We had decent cheese steak spring rolls. My fiancée had the chile (7 out of 10), I had the Muscels (too much garlic but good otherwise). This place will help you with what you need based on my experience. ASK FOR STEVE.

This is the real deal, or at least as close as you can get in the Upper Valley. Leaves Dirt Cowboy, Rosey Jekes, and all other pretenders in the dust.  Very good coffee/espresso (the barista today made an orchid out of the foam today). Best scones by far--if you like the drier/crispier kind vs. the cakey/doughey kind. My husband swears by their coffee cake (especially when warmed). Have also had BLT's, chicken salad, and other luncheon items there.  Charming place with comfy sitting and communal table for reading the provided newspapers.  Also, very nice staff. White River Junction is really a great up and coming town--a little piece of Seattle in the Upper Valley.

I've discovered that I am definitely not a fan of tapas. I came hungry, I left hungry and broke. The flavor was okay, considering everything was small plates and they do mean very small plates. Gave it a try and it's not my kind of place. I guess if you're a foodie and like to brag about the latest overpriced restaurants you've been to, than this is the place to be! Our waiter was frustrated because we didn't know what we wanted, yet didn't lend any help or suggestion, we had to ask which was followed by a deep sigh. Too snooty for my taste. Don't get me wrong, presentation was nice, clean and beautiful just def not for me

Food is great here. Talk about a hole in the wall, this place is tiny. We were lucky enough to walk in on a Friday night and not need reservations. So many great dishes it's recommended you go with a group of 4 and try as many as possible.

When here for their Sunday Pasta Tasting dinner and it was such a treat. I am not a big pasta fan by any means, but once in a while a tasting of homemade pastas reminds me of Babbo. The space is very rustic and quite big, Had 8pm reservations and were seated promptly. Very nice and relaxing inside, very comfortable. Service was very attentive and we ordered some wine and the side of asparagus to accompany the pasta tasting. There were 4 pastas. The first was a ramp Spaghettini, which I loved since I am a fan of ramps, second up was the cavatelli with morels and asparagus- love the morels, lumaconi with sausage- this was ok, I am not a sausage fan, then we ended with the garganelli with rabbit and olives- I did like this one. Desert was roman pine nut tart, which was interesting, I prefered the lemon tart without the pine nuts and my friend go the olive caked instead, which I have to say- is DELICIOUS. All in all, a great evening. Will be back to try the regular menu for sure.

This is a great neighborhood spot wish it was in MY neighborhood, it's a little but of a treck from Astoria. But it was so good I wanted to sample all the dips so I got a plate with an assortment the babaganoush, humus, were fantastic, along with the tabbouleh , and the lentils and rice everything Tasted so fresh and light. I also had the chicken tawook which was yummy as well! Ill be back soon!
mediocre quality food with top quality prices. This is clearly an "on-trend" spot for see and be seen, but if you're looking for quality food, your money is better spent elsewhere

A lovely french bistro. when I'm here, it makes me feel like NYC in the late 90s - a throwback place that is genuinely cool and a neighborhood spot. the food is classic and delicious, the fish entrees are wonderful. the servers were a bit unattentive.
My favourite is the artichoke but the crab deserves a mention also.  This ranks up amongst the best pizza I've had in NYC - have yet to have a bad experience =)
You have to stand in line to order at the counter and then wait for your food. The food is just average. It is often times hard to find a table if you are in a group. Worse Danny DeVito eats there.

About 20 minute wait on Saturday afternoon to get seats on a high table. Booth tables take longer so I settled with the one by the cashier. Food was above average. Salmon benedict was on a heavier, saltier side. Nonetheless, it tasted good with the potato side. Mashed potato that comes with it is really buttery and flavorful! Belgian waffles is light and topped with fresh strawberries. Strawberry sauce made it really fruity and sweet. Such deliciousness if you want a not-too-sweet dessert brunch! Cafe au lait was good as well. They give you cube sugar!

Got the caccio e pepe pasta at la pasta (which was delish but really rich) and spent the rest of the evening drooling as we wandered around the store. It is gorgeous! I have no idea how they are able to keep it stocked with products that look so gorgeous and stunning (well okay I saw someone checking on the meats so that's probably how...). After a month of dreary winter veggies in the store, seeing their wall of lettuces made me ridiculously happy...not to mention the wall of cheese and prosciutto. We went on a weeknight (and early) so it wasn't crowded, but it was filling up fast. Still, it is fun to check out.

The place was packed, but despite that the service was great. All the steamed buns they have were awesome, and the spicy miso ramen was also delicious! I'd recommend anyone go here for a quick lunch or a dinner with friends. It's not a large place, so definitely make a reservation. Also, if you have food allergies be ESPECIALLY clear about them, I warned them of mine, but they still served me food with the allergens in it cause they didn't know.

I had been thinking of coming here for a while, but Scoutmob officially brought my boyfriend and me to Hope Garage for dinner. The dining room was nice and spacious (which is a blessing in Williamsburg), but still maintained a the comforting atmosphere of a cozy restaurant.   The waiters were very friendly and kept checking to make sure it was ok that my roast chicken was taking a bit longer because it was cooked to order (I kept telling them I would never argue with freshly cooked food). Said chicken was very juicy and spiced nicely. The spinach, corn, and potato sides were nothing to write home about. My boyfriend had a tasty pork belly BLT, but his potato leek soup was the highlight of the meal. It was creamy, had the right amount of saltiness, and came with flavorful chunks of bacon. Hope Garage has a great "mix your own cocktail" featured on the drink menu. My pomegranate vodka soda hit the spot with its clean flavors. There were only a few people in the restaurant when we arrived at about 7:30, but business definitely started picking up about halfway through our meal. It's good to see more people discovering the pleasant vibes and delightfully unpretentious food in this joint.
They make the best marshmallows. The peanut butter smores is beyond delicious and the rice krispy treats are out of this world.
Eh, for whatever reason, I like the Teaneck location much better-also the food and it's quality varies greatly from T- different cooks I guess-but I really like consistency.
Burger was ok.  Guess if you had a beer, you'd find the burger more tasty.  Fries were good.   I don't see what all the excitement is about
Cutie Patroller is always on the prowl in downtown NYC for cute places and great food Cheapest Dumpling in my hood!!!!!!!!!!!!! Stop by for snack or lunch!!

This was a wonderful find on our visit to NY!  It almost looked closed when we arrived since it was kind of dark . . . thank goodness it was open!  They had an Italian whitefish special with potatoes and spinach which was outstanding . . . probably the best fish I've ever had.  The seafood pasta (with thick homemade noodles) was delicious.  The prices were amazingly reasonable. The place looks like a converted house and was packed and quite noisy when we arrived. The service was very good. The food was fabulous!  Worth the trip!

Well, I must say, I went into The Industry with very low expectations (that's just my personality) and I was pleasantly surprised. Came on a week-day evening to get some food with a friend and we sat outside so I didn't get to see much of the interior except when being seated. No one else was sitting outside when we got there (fools!), but when a party did come they sat them directly next to us despite there being about 6 open tables. Leave some buffer room next time! Waitress was friendly, knew the menu, no problems whatsoever. I ordered the seafood BLT which rotates what seafood they use and this night it was beer battered fried shrimp. Sandwich was sooooo good, but the bread they use was like a cinder block. My jaw physically ached after eating the first half, so for the second I just used a fork and knife and discarded the bread completely. Place is 3 blocks from my house, I'm sure I'll be back to try more.
Love love love this place! Bagels aren't that good. But their sandwiches are to die for and their bread is fantastic!! Everything's home -made!!

Visiting Philly for the first time. I would go back? We got the chef's menu, 2 orders of the least expensive of the two chef's menu. The wait staff was excellent, social, informed, and friendly. The food was good, interesting especially the cheeses and their pairing, e.g. cheese with chocolate or honey, interestingly delicious. Smoked pork chop tasty but not tender. Since we ordered two of the chef's menu, it would have been nice to have two different items instead of two of the same, like dessert for example. I would go back when/if in Philly again.

Meal was great!  Good ambiance, delicious food, and wonderful service.  Got the shrimp cocktail and artichoke and spinach dip to start.  Artichoke dip was to die for.  For main course I got the shrimp risotto and my fiancé got the filet.  Risotto was great with nice fresh tasting shrimp and the right amount of truffle butter.  Fiancé enjoyed his steak.  We were too stuffed for dessert but they had a nice selection.  Will go back for the flourless chocolate cake.  The owner was very gracious and came around several times to check in and chat with us.  Plenty of parking.  Will definitely go back soon!
My friend will kill me, but I'm sorry to say - the sauce killed it. Good crust. Good mozzarella. Bad sauce. Definitely not worth the wait and way overrated. Sorry, friend.

This place is great.  Their guac is good & the salsa is different and awesome!  I've had 2 different enchiladas and they were ok - a little bland.  BUT my bf and sister have gotten the burritos and they are amazing! I've learned my lesson ... burritos it is!
NOOO! Taboonette discontinued the Halloumi salad, and replaced it with some other version with beets and a vinaigrette. That was by far the best thing on the menu. really hope they bring it back :(

Food was great, all flavors really well developed.  Had the Tuna-Guac-Tar which was superb, the paper thin fried wonton skins were like air and the tuna was delicious.   Lamb meatballs were perfectly cooked although the tzatziki was a bit bitter and could have used more dill.  Pork dumplings were great and super spicy which kicked things off well.   I had the pear salad which was quite good and my friend had the beet salad which she liked.   Pear & ice cream dessert was excellent as well.  Only complaint is that the service started off great and then disappeared, left us with dirty plates and empty water and wine glass. I would have ordered another but no one ever came by until we flagged them down to order dessert. I watched the waitress come into the room, hand a bill to one table and then not even look at any other tables before she went back out to hang with the hosts. Even when we were paying the bill, it was as if they were done with us.  I loved the place but the fall off in service seriously dampened the mood

Came here for dinner at the suggestion of a friend.  It's a cute little cafe, very fun atmosphere and crowd.  I ordered the cold ginger-tomato soup, the seafood stew, and the chocolate Guiness cake.  The food and drinks were all pretty good and I left feeling satisfied. One plus, the service was very good and our waiter was fun and helpful.  Overall, the food was good but not amazing.  I'm not in New York very often, so I probably wouldn't return unless I were staying for a longer period of time.

Pasta is good, never tried the pizza, but the pasta is good. Be careful with delivery though - it takes FOREVER and is rarely what you ordered. Otherwise for pickup, it's good. The staff could be a bit friendlier..
Always a wonderful place for a drink and a meal. Wonderful food, unique cocktails and staff who define wonderful, gracious and friendly.

This place is my favorite! I've been here a few times so I'll just list my favorite dishes: Brussels sprouts- best I've ever had. They come in a yogurt cream sauce and they're just so so good Cheese steak egg rolls- awesome. The egg roll itself is almost sweet and with the siracha ketchup the flavors are just on point. Lobster Mac and cheese- note:it's really orzo. My boyfriend was sad, I didn't mind at all. I've never ordered anything I didn't like here! It gets really crowded on the weekends but you can always pop a squat on the rooftop and enjoy the food. Beer selection is good, the drinks are super fun. The Capri cooler is an adult Capri sun and I loved it. Some might say it's kitschy but I think it's great. I didn't like sitting in the swinging chairs though, makes it difficult to stay still while eating haha

Ok, everyone raved about this place but it was so crowded when I went that I felt like I had to stake out for a table. The burgers were delicious, flavorful but boy were they greasy. I looked like I ate a bucket fried chicken with all the napkins I had to use. Now, I didn't have the shake but my friends did and they loved it. I probably will never order a shake only because I'm not really a shake person but I trust my friends taste buds so I think you should definitely give their shakes a try. If you are craving a really greasy, hearty burger then order one too.

Be certain to call first, because they are very unreliable. We tried it twice over a period of eight days and it wasn't open either time. Our first attempted visit  was about 5:45 PM on a Thursday. We drove around a bit, but found no other place to get a meal in downtown White River Junction, so we just hit the road and ate at home over an hour later. The next time we tried this place was about 7:45 AM on a Friday, and again, they weren't open. The odd thing is that they were open on Christmas when I called to inquire if they'd be open the following day. It all makes no sense to me. When ARE they open? Only on holidays? They need to have consistent hours that make sense to customers, and they need to keep to those hours without closing early, for whatever reason.

$14 brunch comes with a non-alcoholic drink, is more than enough food. More creative brunch than most in the slope. My duck confit sandwich was good, not great, very rich. The smoked fluke fish hash was fantastic, and they've clearly got poaching eggs down. The polenta with salsa verde was good, but not as bright as I had hoped. The side of bacon was good, but $1/strip good. Expect strollers. Get the watermelon ginger agua fresca, it's mild but definitely a great drink in the summer. Especially to cut the fat from your brunch.
Good cheap eat -  Mango Chutney Mayo and Parmesan Peppercorn both very good! very limited seating

We've had pizza a few times from Goodfellas, both delivery and dine in.  Very good. We decided to try something else off the menu - bad idea.  Eggplant Parm dinner was inedible - seriously had to just throw it away.  Eggplant was tough and barely cooked, breading on it was soggy and an odd color.  Ceasar salad was also awful.  The dressing tasted like someone added a little water to an almost empty bottle of dressing and poured it on, and the romaine was not crisp.  Sausage and broccoli rabe was edible, but lukewarm and not much flavor.  And the garlic bread - stale.   Delivery took well over an hour. Overall a HUGE disappointment.

Went there again the other day and was less wowed than the first time we went a few months ago. Not sure why, it was a weekend night and it was packed. I was getting the feeling that it was just not special the second time. I had the basic burger and it was good, but for some reason I was expecting a better experience. The server was good, the beer selection was good, the other food on the table was good but it wasn't an "ah-ha" dinner.  I'll go again to see if its really a destination burger place.
i have grown up with Michelangelo's and i love their food. i recommend them to everyone. wish their menu was online.

A tree grows in Brooklyn and so does a Cafe Luluc.   I have been coming here for dinner since the first week it opened, years ago.   It used to be one of my main spots to grab a late night bite to eat in a neighborhood that was filled with early closings.  Since then, the options have grown quite a bit and Cafe Luluc's kitchen isn't the latest one left open anymore (not even close!) A great place to have a casual french bistro meal.  I even had dinner here one New Year's Eve.  It's the kind of place people in the neighborhood will go to during the week when they don't feel like cooking.  The food is quite tasty, especially the grilled shrimp salad.   Jean-Luc is the manager--talk to him about Argentina or anywhere else in the world he's visited, he loves to travel.

The food is ok but mainly because they use very rich ingredients and let the foods speak for itself.  The service is great and the atmosphere is good for a nice dinner date or a low-pressure lunch date.

We tried this place because of YOU, fellow Yelpers, so thanks as always for posting your reviews! Two adults and two kids all enjoyed this place immensely! We love Wafa who was a perfect host!  She made us feel that we were visiting her at her home. She shared the secret of why her kafta is so moist...she grinds the meat freshly herself! We ordered a vegetarian plate and a pick 3 meats plate.  Wafa suggested we have the former as an appetizer which was a good idea.  All of us raved about the hummus which was creamy and flavorful. We had a bulgar wheat and lentil mixture...forgot the name...which was hearty and tasty. Falafel was good and moist. For the 3 meats we picked kafta...ground hamburger and lamb; shish tarwook...grilled chicken breast chunks; and lamb shwarma. We had taboleh and fries as sides. I didn't like the consistency of the chicken, which was squeaky like undercooked chicken.  It was white throughout, though, and everyone else loved it.  I guess it was just me. The kafta was the best I've ever had! The shwarma was juicy bite sized goodness. The tahini sauce on the side was perfect for dipping, especially the pita. The hot sauce was really HOT! Only my son liked it. My daughter ordered split pea soup.  No one liked it...too bland. I think it should have simmered longer to blend in the flavors. No worries...every thing else more than made up for it! We had a ton of food left over!  Enough for lunch the next day.  Save room for baklava! It is served warm and is not messy like the Greek version. We will go back very soon!

By far the worst experience I've ever had When an owner thinks his cheesesteak sandwich is the shit, and treats his customers like shit It results in an epic diarrhea That's what it was Poor customer service Poor manners And a very very shitty meal Keep up the attitude boys!

Went here on a rain Sunday for dinner. And like everyone said, it's quite a wait on weekends. We got here around 7:30ish had a 50 minute wait for our table. In between so, the host also said there was a 20 minute wait for buzzers. So I had to come back in 20 mins to pick up a buzzer?!? To kill time we bought drinks at the bar. And if we wanted to, we could have ate there too but decided to wait for an actual table. Maybe it was just our time around but overall, our food was a little on the SALTLY side. I had ordered the GAUCHO CHICKEN (with verde sauce) and shoe fries. My bf had the TACO & ENCHILADA combo. One with cheese and the other with chicken. We also had a side of YUCATAN PLANTAINS. Everything was tasty, cooked right and came out warm, but seriously, i could have used less salt on my fries, and didn't really need salt on my plantains either. My boyfriend said that his chicken taco was salty too - and for him to say that says a lot since he likes adding salt to everything. This place really deserves a 3.5 rather than 3 only because the food is cheap and their classic Margaritas are only $5. Other than that I wouldn't find myself visiting again unless it was for someone's birthday. The night we went we had a rowdy young Indian group celebrating something a few yards away from our table. And oh yeah, I would not advise bringing infants here either. A couple maybe 15 feet from us had brought their 3 month old and by the time we left, the father was outside with the baby while the mother was still eating. It's really not suitable since this place is known for celebrating birthdays and such.

I think I liked the waitstaff more than I did my food. We had such a nice, funny server, which makes the difference with a meal. The people here really seem like they love their job. Place is really intimate and homely, and the prices are awesome. Would recommend getting here at 6p as there wasn't much of a wait, but near 8p there was a crowd outside. Some dishes I would recommend getting: Tagliolini with seafood Gnocchi Salmon Crocette Chocolate Mousse Cake Bonus: if you a bring a friend here for a birthday, the waiter will enthusiastically sing with you.
Really good pizza and fresh ingredients and pairings but waaaaayyy took over priced for the size which is an 11" inch pie ( we measured it).

So don't get me wrong with these 2 stars - we will definitely go back. Eventually. -1/2 star for the owner guy to seat us then 3 minutes later ask us to move because he had a party of 3 to seat at our table. He was very nice about it, but still. -1/2 star because it took AT LEAST 30 minutes for our dinner to come AFTER our appetizer plates were cleared. -1/2 star because I ordered my steak medium rare and received it medium. And there were, like, 2 leaves of swiss chard on my plate - be a little more generous. It's a veggie! -1/2 star because I had a total of 5 slices of steak, and the equivalent of 1 whole slice of fat/gristle/bone. So really, it was only 4 slices for $25. And, again, only like 2 leaves of swiss chard. -1/2 star because DH ordered his steak medium rare and it came rare. And his egg was overcooked (not runny at all, which would have been ideal). And the greens on his plate were WAY over-salted. -1/2 star because the sauces on our respective steaks were over-salted. I like salty foods, and it was almost too much for me to take. -1/2 star because I am still hungry (came home and ate 6 of my own potstickers). (so really, i guess this is 1 1/2 stars, but I rounded up.) Our server was very nice. The bread (from Balthazar) was chewy and the butter soft. And the wine was very reasonably priced. The tuna tartare and dumpling appetizers were delish. We will be going back - it's a nice local place. But it may only be once or twice a year now, since Red Hook is way out in BFE and the food/service wasn't exceptional. And if you don't live in Brooklyn, nearby, I wouldn't bother schlepping.
What can ya say, it's just bomb ramen. (And awesome waitors/ waitresses/ vibes)

I came here mainly because of the suckling pig, but after eating here, the fried chicken is the real star! I ordered crab toast, calamari, and chicken/pork sausage as starters. Crab toast stood out while the rest were still delicious but not memorable. Suckling pig was good....but not something I would return for. The chicken on the other hand. MMMMMMMMM. Amazing.

Really enjoyed lunch here today. They had a menu a little different from the run of the mill restaurants around this area. I decided to try the Shepard's Pie and was not disappointed. Great beef flavor. Carrots and peas were cooked perfectly. I don't like them undercooked. Mashers were flavorful and creamy. Gotta give props to the wait staff. They were all were friendly and attentive but not overly attentive. I will be enjoying a meal again here soon. I think the chicken pot pie is calling my name.

This place is a little gem! The ambience is cozy and intimate, the basement was candle / fireplace lit with a classy jazz feel. The indoor garden space is simply adorable. On a Friday night, we were seated immediately in the basement near the fireplace, absolutely perfect for the cold winter night. It was crowded but not overwhelmingly so. I disliked that the jazz room was so seperate from the rest of the restaurant (and a $12 dollar + 1 drink minimum to be seated in there), but luckily the music could be easily hear throughout the basement. The wine prices were surprisingly great and the desserts were delicious.
I had a sour dough chicken sandwich and it was pretty good. But its a little expensive.

5 stars for value and tastiness. For 2 of us, we got: -- The seemingly mandatory Roti Canai. Yummy, tender, chewy bread. Fragrant, flavorful gravy. A+ -- The Crab with House Sauce. The sauce is a sweet chili sauce. You really have to work for your food here. They give you a set of those nutcracker things, and you have to get down and dirty with your crab if you want any meat in your mouth. But it's worth it. -- The Beef Rendang. The beef melts in your mouth, it's so tender. The Sauce is great, and goes well with the... -- 2 orders of White Rice. Nothing to say here. Recommended all the way!!

Food was ok, service was friendly but slow, atmosphere a little strange but good.  On a Tuesday night My wife and i had the drunken noodles and Laotian stew (more or less a saucy stir fry served in a pot) .  I thought the drunken noodles were pretty good: it was moderately spicy, had a good flavor, maybe a little small in portion and light on vegetables.  The stew was just ok - it tasted a little bland compared to our other dish.  So the restaurant still has the feel of an old diner but had curtain to give a good sense of privacy between booths.  I would be ok with coming back but I think it's about the same as all the other Thai places in the greater Hartford area.

Tried this pizza for the first time after a long night out with friends, and the size of one slice was so overwhelming I couldn't have more than a few bites (it was 3 am), but I remember my tastebuds reeling from shock at the ridiculously rich and unique flavors of the artichoke slice. The kicker, however, is... the next day, my friends and I consumed the leftover pizza from the fridge cold, and we KILLED it. The pizza cold was freaking phenomenal. This pizza is so worth the $4 a slice. Don't make yourself sick and finish it in one sitting. Refrigerate it and consume it as a snack the next day. It'll still be mindblowingly good.

We went last nigh (may 17).  Got there just at 7. Waited 15 minutes to order and then waited an hour and 15 to actually get our food.    Food was ok but the owner was not - just plain surly when we tried to find out where our food was (we were warned it might take up to an hour) but at an hour and 15 it was still a wait.   OK food, bad service (they got us the wrong chicken dish and apparently that was also my fault as well - can't win) NOT GOING IN AGAIN till they either figure out the kitchen or the music crowd goes away - too bad we used to enjoy going there.

What a fabulous way to splurge! The Kobe Style Course was amazing: the most tender beef cuts! Served with fantastic miso soup (great base), a perfect mushroom packet (tender and really flavorful), sukiyaki bibimbap (a runner-up comfort food to mac'n'cheese!), and who doesn't love s'mores (when was the last time you had s'mores!)? Sauce-wise, I preferred the vinegar-based Ponzu sauce (spicy and house sauces were good, too). A nice addition to the "new" restaurant strip on Callowhill!
It was completely fine, once again. Actually, more than fine, as they had a specialty drink that was really delicious.......For inexpensive bar food, it was great!

Had this diner on my list to try after seeing it listed in a food article as one of the Best Diner's in South Jersey. Drove about an hour to get here and it was worth the trip. Huge place...diner and Lounge. We were seated in the Lounge and had the same Diner menu as the main dining room Definitely not your typical diner. Lamb Koftas sharing plate were delicious and I could have made a meal of them if this was an entree on the menu. Interesting menu of non-traditional diner fare, but we opted for sandwiches, Turkey Club and Turkey Special, both freshly carved turkey breast, very tasty.  I would have liked a denser "deli" style rye bread, but it was still good The bread was served in a brown bag, just like a french bakery, and we actually packed up the uneaten loaf and took it home for later. Not sure I'll be back any time soon, but I'd definitely visit here again when I get a Diner urge Would love for them to offer more Greek dishes, since this is their background.

With many Japanese restaurants in the area, Izakaya got it right.  I tried several dishes and have not found many other restaurants in the area using quality ingredients and a commitment to satisfying customers.  Will definitely make it my go to place.
The food was good, but not amazing. The service was excellent, though, and the Byob policy makes it an easy, chill dinner. Try it if you like ethnic!
I bought a sausage sandwich at Home Depot and ate it in the parking lot and it was delicious.

I love meat lots of it! I am one hell of a carnivore. If you love all you can eat quantity with great quality, Fogo is the place for you. I eat here several times a month and this place never disappoints. Staff professional, knowledgeable, friendly, and always very  tentative. Here are a few tips: Go hungry or go home. Don't fill up on Carbs ( this will allow you to consume as much meat as possible) Try and save room for your sweet tooth, deserts are spectacular. This place has a great ambience and décor. It is one of my favorite spots in Center City. Bring a date,  family, or just have a night out with your friends.

Ohhh mama - give me some fried chicken!!! I'm not sure if it was because it was a rainy Saturday afternoon or because the freaks come out in Brooklyn, there was the strangest crowd of people I've ever seen at this restaurant. Several vanilla ice hair cuts and the most bizarre outfits.    Aside from the freaks the restaurant itself reminded me of some spots in rural Alabama -no frills just focused on the food.   The wait service was odd, I think they do team waiting, b/c we had almost every person in the restaurant at our table at one point or the other?? would have been nice if they told us that in the beginning. Now for the food: There was 6 of us, so almost everything on the menu got ordered. Starters: Fried Green Tomatoes --Yum! these were awesome, but the weird Ranch like sauce that came with them should have come on the side. Main: Chicken box w/Cheese Grits  -this was by far the best thing on the menu, came w/3 pieces of chicken and the Grits were incredible!!!  The roll was hard?? maybe a bad batch, but that should have been softer. Pulled Pork w/potatoes: this sounded good, but was Blah! Dear restaurant add some type of BBQ sauce to this!! and more meat! Beef Brisket w/Mac'n'cheese: Brisket was BOMB.COM, but the mac and cheese?? I think I can make better out of a box, where the creativity here? just standard --it would be nice if they crushed goldfish and baked it or added anything to make it unique--bacon?? Great beer on tap, and best of all the 'boxes' were $11-13bucks --hello Brooklyn!! incredible

They serve  good, big, consistent burgers cooked how you like them in a variety of possible styles.  Good selection of beer and prices are ok, if just a tad high.  I've been here a handful of times, mostly with Groupons and never left disappointed.  Also, if you come in the summer you can sit outside in the nice courtyard area and have a good view of the skyline. I would probably stick to burgers and beers since it's just a bar style place.  The appetizers are good too though.  I don't really like how they have started adding automatic gratuity for Groupon customers, but it is a reasonable amount so I wasn't upset.

3000+ Reviews on Yelp for a food cart?? New York Madness. So I had to try it. We had just finished our Broadway show of Jersey Boys and I was starving. Walked down a few streets... the location is pretty self explanatory. 53rd and 6th. We passed several other food carts on the way... wasn't sure if it was it. We thought if we saw it we would know. And surely enough... The only cart we've seen with a long line. The line wasn't too bad. But you can tell by the looks of it. This cart was the one. There were about four others adjacent to it on the same block, but only this one had a line. Their sign read "Halal Guys." So the first things I saw on Yelp were "Chicken over rice" and "lots of white sauce." That's what I got. And yup it was as good as the 3000 reviews says it was. Lots of shredded meat over orange looking rice with some lettuce/cabbage on the side. The white sauce was great. So was the bbq. Didn't try the hot sauce but my friend says it was very very HOT. Also tried some of my friends gyro (lamb). It was a bit more saltier and flavorful, but I think I preferred the chicken more. The bowl was easy to eat and go. They also have caps that you can put over the foil/aluminum bowl and take home. I was impressed. Stellar New York Street Food from a Cart. CHECK. Bring CASH.

This place has an assortment of breakfast & lunch items at a price that you would expect from a roach coach and not a brick & mortar restaurant. My only complaint is that they never answer the phone when I try to call ahead to make an order, but it's not that bad considering that no matter what you order there, it's done within 10 minutes. Their turkey bacon, egg, and cheese sandwiches haunt me in my dreams with how delcious they are,

It's so much fun to go here with friends. I love the everything but the kitchen sink salad. I recommend the classic beef meatballs and tomato sauce. My friends usually order the other ones and they're also great! Would get 5 stars if there wasn't such a long wait EVERY time!
Food was good and reasonably priced. Entire staff was on their cell phones the entire time I was there. Not very professional, but nice spot overall.

oh ohhhh ohhh ... ohhh i experienced gastronomic orgasm here. my mouth started to water as i was writing this. their dumplings are so cheap. $1 for 5 dumplings. ohhhh... whoa and it's sooooo goood. when i went there, it was around 4pm or something, so the place was filled with schoolers who were yelling to order food. this really reminded me of my childhood when i went with my mom to get some after school cheap snacks. there are some seating available for 5 people max. but i guess you can move to the park in front of the school. but i went in the winter. hmmm i wondered where chinese people there did tai chi in the winter... ok enough of that. i need to contain myself when i talk about this dumpling place. oh and if you can't find it, it's right behind the school!

I went here on a lazy holiday Monday for brunch and it was such a great choice! It was very busy so we put our names in and had drinks at the bar, which were good. Pretty standard. We were seated before we had even finished our drinks. We sat down and immediately honed in on the brunch offerings, which were limited to one small page but the choices were great. My friend and I both ended up ordering the mushroom benedict which was sooooooo good! I am vegetarian so usually I have to ask to substitute something for the meat in eggs benedict so it was really nice to just have it on the menu. The sides of fruit and breakfast potatoes were fresh and delicious. I will definitely be coming back here next time I'm in the city!

I love love love Pylos. Without a doubt I can say that it is truly a crown jewel in East Village and Alphabet City dining scene. This is my go to restaurant for out of town friends and family. Let me start by saying I have some high expectations for Greek cuisine. My sister lived in Athens, I have visited the islands multiple times and my mother loves to cook Greek cuisine. One of my closest friends was born in Greece and married there last summer - so I am a SNOB about authenticity. Pylos measures up! The restaurant is chic and cute. Not too bright but not so dark that you can't see the menu. I love sitting at the long tables and the clay pots on the ceiling are a nice touch; I find the wine display to also be very chic. The restaurant is small but does not feel crowded. The outside is unassuming - don't let that fool you. My last meal there was lamb shank - which is flavorful but not greasy - and the moussaka which always tastes fresh (no pre-made tomato sauce or bitter eggplant slices) is perfectly seasoned and is very hearty.  The saganaki is also great and I love their selection of fish dishes - have had both salmon and the sea bass. I am more of a cocktail person but the waitstaff is friendly and will recommend a great wine to go with dinner. I have never had them talk down to me while recommending wine (a pet peeve of mine) or try and force a bottle of wine in a price range above me either.   I have recommended this restaurant to many out of town friends and they always enjoy it and have taken my parents here many times. Depending on what you order and how much wine you have, the meal can get pricey but not bank breaking. If you are on a budget, so for their brunch which is still a great menu but more affordable.
Chicken and rice is cheap, filling, and some of the flavors are there. The rice had flavor, but the chicken seemed bland.. I still don't understand what's so special about the white sauce.

for me this is the best type of place. You can feel the love that the owners have for their gem. I love Korean food and the this bibimbap made me very happy. Service was spot on. Fried chicken and waffels were fantastic! Will be going back.

I have to say that when I read the reviews I wasn't too excited to try the place, but we decided to roll the dice anyway.  So glad we did! We showed up around 11:45a on a Sunday without reservations; we were seated immediately.  Service was friendly and prompt.   He got the lemon curd blueberry pancakes and a side of biscuits & gravy; I got the cremini mushroom skillet special (I added kale) and a side of bacon.  Both dishes came with duck fat fried potatoes.   Everything was good!  Just three tiny complaints:  I ordered the bacon extra crispy and it wasn't crispy at all; they initially forgot to even bring it out.  The duck fat fries were something I was really looking forward to, but they tasted like regular home fries to me.  I LOVE duck fat fried things but these weren't anything special.  Lastly, as a place that boasts farm to table, it would have been great if there was any representation of the origin of the ingredients in the dishes.  If they hadn't been so busy I would have asked, but it would be nice to see it listed someplace.     They were really very busy right before we arrived and again right after and we still got our food at a reasonable time and my coffee was refilled as soon as it was empty.  Took a little while to get the check, but like I said, they got slammed.  I'd go back again for sure and next time I'll take some booze for the BYO, we just forgot today.

Food, wine and service were amazing. comfortable, unpretentious, and reasonably priced. Try the Paparedelle oxtail ragu and the meatballs appetizer for a hearty, classic dish. As for dessert, the homemade Nutella tiramisu and Ricotta Cheesecake were the best I'be had and the coffee was rich and delicious. I would come back here everyday if I could!

I went there today for lunch and it was GOOD! They have a 9.99 two course lunch deal. The cayote salad was pretty good. It tasted like a Medditeranean salad with a sweet corn kick to it! The chicken enchiladas used the green sauce rather then the red sauce. I usually get the red sauce, but either way it was good! My coworker had the tortilla soup and she enjoyed it. I would def come here again for lunch! Thanks again B!
Excellent! Fresh fruit, veggies and delicious baked goods.

Great eats!  I got the amazing steak w/ yummy fries!  Burgers are recommended here too!  Can't ever go wrong w/ bone marrow and foie gras!  The best part is the pistachio tequila cocktail - my fave in the whole world & A MUST!!!!!!!

A group of us ate at Amada recently and after all the plates had come and gone, my impression of the restaurant was the same as before I knew it exist.  The upside to Amada was the service.  The wait staff was very polite and gave great descriptions of each dish.  The vibe was pretty chill, a good spot for conversation with a big group.  Having said all that, the food was just average.  Everything we ate seemed to rely heavily on some variety of sause or seasoning, a flavor other than what it was we were actually eating.  It all tasted very rich and I had trouble eating more than two bites of any one thing.  I guess we made the mistake of ordering from the 'large group' menu and didn't actually pick what dishes came out.  My favorite plate was the mashed potato ball (I'm sure they have a nicer name for it).  And the lavender honey that came out with the cheese plate was great.

I went on a Sunday at noon with a group of 5. There was a line but it moved relatively quickly and they let you know your place in line via mobile. The sweet potato fries and truffle fries were yummy. Crisp and not too oily. The sauces they come with are fun to try but the fries are good on their own. The burgers were juicy and flavorful. You should get them medium rare as they suggest. We tried the original burger and truffle burger. We all really liked our meals! We got a cinnamon chocolate chip ice cream donut to finish off the savory meal. Ice cream donut sandwich? Genius idea but mediocre execution. It was cut into 4 pieces and seemed like it had been made and frozen. Not a "must-get" but a sweet ending to a sweet meal.

Went here a while ago, but still remember how much I loved this place. It's tiny, so the wait can be long, but sooo worth it. I ordered the Cioppino, which I don't think is on the menu any more, but I was really impressed by the portion size and the price! I could barely finish my meal, though since I really wanted to I did. Service was very friendly and welcoming, though there's no waiting area at all in the front so you either have to wait outside or at the bar next door. Come early, and not with a big party. If I were to guess, the place fits 20-30 people tops.

I happened to see a picture of their pistachio and goat cheese encrusted New Zealand rack of lamb on Instagram and just had to try it. The food was excellent! From the bread to the entrees everything was delicious. My boyfriend had the lamb and I had the filet mignon. For dessert we shared Nutella filled zepoles, sherbert with a white chocolate shell, and their french vanilla creme brûlée. The staff was very friendly and provided great service. Overall I'd recommend trying them out and we will definitely be back again!

Pricey, Small portions, and Cramped. I must commend the wait staff as they have a good atitude for the most part  a dying breed amongst  NY restaurants/diners. I would give this place a better review if it had better food ,for the price it just flat out lacks. Also the breakfast portions are too small, though I do hear lunch/dinner foods are bigger. The last few times I've went for breakfast my sunnyside up eggs have been lukewarm and came equipped with a child sized serving of french fries on the side. The booths are a bit small in this place and some rock back and forth which can be irritating. I would excuse some of the shortcomings of this eatery if it was more affordable unfortunately at its price point coupled with the current economy Jackson Hole just isn't for me :) Im sure others must disagree as the place is packed for breakfast most of the time.

Want the best brunch of your life? Come here and order the eggs over their arepas. Seriously life-changing. Their food is SO good. Particularly brunch, but I've had dinner and drinks here too (good sangria... from what I can remember hehe. Might have drank too much....) They have unlimited brunch drinking as an option... so if you want some fun, this is the place.

Great tasting pizza! I clearly got too much food but I wanted to try many different things. I got a couple garlic knots, a slice of lasagna pizza, grandmas, broccoli and cheese, and a Margherita. It was way more than I could handle but I'm glad I tried them because everything was amazing! My favorite would have to be the lasagna followed by grandmas. The place itself is tiny and very hot. Servers were friendly and helpful,
The serving sizes are huge and the prices are quite good. Asiana offers a good selection of sushi and noodles and I haven't been disappointed by them yet.

I'm a bit indifferent about this place.  The menu is very small, they have little to offer variety wise, and the customer service was lacking.  The food and wine are good here, just be sure to make it very clear how you would like it cooked.   Ambiance is romantic with dimmed lights, very intimate, but the place is tiny inside and tucked away in an inconvenient location.

Awesome! Now that denying the arrival of winter is no longer feasible it's time to explore the avenues in which one can reasonably keep warm despite snowstorms and below freezing temperatures. Sure, staying indoors wrapped in a cozy blanket with a hot cocoa in hand is always a good option. But for those who prefer not to turn into a temporary hermit ramen houses are an ideal venue for getting together with friends. In most of Japan ramen is a quick meal. You'll find ramen shops near train stations where commuters will have a bowl on their way home after a long day at work. Often these places won't even have seating. All you see is a line of 'salary men' in their business suits behind a low curtain hungrily slurping down steaming bowls of noodles. And then there are cities like Hakata, where ramen making is an art form and ramen houses are destinations. Tonkotsu ramen is one of Hakata's claims to fame and it is this flavorful pork bone based broth that has become widely popular even in New York. There are talks of Ippudo opening a Midtown location but until then Totto Ramen on the west and Hide-chan Ramen on the east serve the best ramen north of Ippudo. And in some ways, Totto Ramen, more so than Ippudo, evokes the typical ramen experience from Japan. Unlike the flashy interior of Ippudo, Totto is cramped and rustic, so much so that the steam from the kitchen practically serves as the restaurant's main source of heating. Here the star is chicken instead of pork and the resulting broth is lighter, smoother, but equally flavorful and satisfying. The wait on any given evening will be more than an hour and the best strategy would be to sign up for a table and hang out at a nearby bar while you wait. Despite this, a bowl of Totto's spicy ramen is undeniably worth waiting for. Aside from these three ramen houses in New York, there are many more that have popped up in the last few years. Some can trace their roots from Japan and some rely on its celebrity chef for its popularity. But only these three deserve to be mentioned among the best. So take advantage of the cold weather and check out each mentioned in this list. Only then do you have the right to name which ramen spot you judge to be best. For more info, check out my blog listed on my profile!

Best pulled pork I have EVER had in my life.  (I've had some damn good pork too).  'Decent', 'lesser cousin', 'good on rainy days'? Wtf is wrong with you people?? this place is AMAZING. Roast pork over yellow rice, with a side of sweet onions and plantains.  Try it, and tell me it's bad.  I dare you. Tina's is my #2 favorite lunch spot overall in midtown.  No idea why it doesn't have higher ratings.  It's also just under $10.  And if you're a girl, it'll probably serve you two meals. You really can't lose with Tina's.  Seriously, this place ALWAYS hits the spot, unless you're allergic to amazing food.

I was first introduced to this place and to pho altogether by a co-worker and I haven't even bothered to try anywhere else because I don't want to be disappointed, this place is that good.  Never seen food served quicker, pho broth is delicious with a very generous amount of noodles and meat (I don't think you need anything more than the small portion) and the BBQ pork summer rolls are amazing (I've even just popped in once to take a couple orders of them home).  Ventured away from pho for luch once and again was not disappointed, pork and rice platter comes with a very generous helping of very tasty pork and enough rice to go with it.  Servers are always very friendly, seat you mediately, and there are always so many of them working each day that it never takes long to get your order taken and brought out to you.  Love it here
Great Vegan food! The service is great. They have an awesome menu. I love the Mozzarella Sticks! I also love the fries with all the different toppings, YUMMY IN MY TUMMY!

The dining area was very disorganized and suffers from a lack of service.  Saw many customers walkout / or be kicked out from the dining area due to confusion and extended wait times.  Maybe I just went at the wrong time.  Food quality was decent, but I expected much more after waiting an hour to be seated, and another 30 mins before the waitress even noticed us.  Supermarket is over priced, but did have a lot of variety and specialties.

It's hard to stand out in a crowded pizza market but Mancinnis does this easily. Stopped for lunch and the staff was very friendly yet genuine. Pizza is served quickly and they have great service to boot. It's a small establishment so a tight fit but worth a wait to enjoy the casual vibe

Ugh...  Years ago this place was top notch, but recently visited this place for lunch with the family and what happened???  Service was terrible, waiter could give a rats-@ss about anything.. casually strolled around, watching tv, went into the kitchen and didn't come back until 15 minutes later.   Had a simple burger with fries and even that was a mess... charbroiled alright.. more like grill grizzled and the fries seemed like they were over cooked and hard.   Scratching this place off the list as there are other diners in the vicinity that are much more friendlier and better food.   Keep away!

My wife and I just happened across this place one day, looked cute inside, so we decided to have some dinner.  It was absolutely lovely - and the ambiance was great.  Two musicians in the corner just made the night that much more quaint.
I could eat an entire meal of just the yellow rice and red beans. Rotisserie chicken and steak with onions are both excellent

Wow that was an awesome meal!  I got to sample many dishes as I was with a large group and it was all fantastic.  If I went back alone I'd be at a loss as to what I would get because there are so many good dishes. My favorite has aspargus on top with a light cream sauce.  Yum.  Service was great and the special things we requested happened.  I was very worried about eating in Little Italy because all the sources say you can't find a good restuarant.  Not sure where they've eaten, but it's not here!

Portions are decent like everyone else said but can be on the greasy side( I ordered the chicken teriyaki) sushi is ok. Service is pretty quick but the delivery woman was extremely rude and even caught an attitude with me. Almost makes me not want to order from them again.

I called, said I wanted to pickup food for takeout.  Whoever picked up said sure, placed me on hold and then transferred me to another restaurant without telling me.  The guy at the restaurant I was transferred to took my order and then when I told him I was on Grand Street and would be there soon, he got angry, said wrong number, and hung up on me.   When I got to the Grand St. restaurant, I placed my order in person.  It only took 10 minutes.  I got the Hainan Chicken and the Malaysian Buddhist for a vegetarian friend.  The chicken was good.  The Malaysian Buddhist had a prawn whisker in it...but the food is still decent enough that I would return.

I LOVE this joint! I think it's a great sandwich spot and LOVE that it's owner operated, not a chain.  The owners are cheery, and have very busy hands.  We ate lunch here yesterday and a steady stream of people came in while we were there.  It's clearly popular, and it's popular because everything is fresh, the people behind the counter are fabulous and it's a great deal!   As an aside, I especially like that they actually close for a short period of time to go on vacation each year.  Just further underscores that the owners are committed to their business, but also know the value of taking a break to refresh and rejuvenate.

I don't even know where to begin.  This place left me literally speechless.  I could probably write a 5 page review, but I'll spare you and give you the highlights. *Parking is a pain, almost $30.00 for two hours... unless you get it validated!   GET IT VALIDATED! *Tommy DiNic's... best sandwich ever! *Termini Bro's Bakery... yummy cannoli, do yourself a favor and get one! *The Head Nut... teas and spices, and snacks galore!! *The Famous 4th Street Cookie Co... I recommend the White Chocolate Chip Macadamia Nut. *Four Seasons Juice Bar... Good Lord I wish we had one of these near me!   Those are all the places we hit in my short 2 hours here.  I feel like I could take another trip to Philly and spend at least a week in Reading Terminal Market and just eat my way through.  The people who work and live near here are so lucky! I've reviewed each of the above places individually too... check em' out!
My wife is Greek-American and we have dined at Taverna Ouzo 4 or 5 times. It is authentic Greek cuisine with nice ambiance and an okay wine list.  Definitely worth checking out
I went Saturday night and the food was fantastic. Sevice was good. The place was definitely loud but the food was so good that you didn't even mind. Great salad. Great fish.
I really like this place. I really appreciate the fact that the staff is very courteous and thoughtful. It's a little loud but who cares! Wine is flowing and the steak is delicious!
good Italian restaurant, medium size place

wow i'm surprised this place doesn't have more good reviews! I am a first time visitor to Philly, and it was actually my first time I've ever had an authentic Philly cheesesteak and I thought it was DELICIOUS! I really thought this was a go-to place for locals, because it was very busy and the atmosphere just seemed like the place to go to! The price is very expensive in my opinion though but then again, i don't really have anything to compare it to. I liked all the difference choices you can get, and i thought fries were really good. They are very huge though, so I would recommend you half it with someone like i did :) Across the street is Geno's, which I was way too full to try after coming from Pat's, but my friends and I ventured over there so that the big boys of our group could try one and compare the two places back-to-back. All of them said that Geno's was good, but Pat's was definitely better.

The spinach dip, Hawaiian ribeye, and salmon were all superb. We had no room for dessert because we ate every bite of our meal. The staff were prompt and courteous! The meal, staff, and ambiance was worth every penny!!!!

My boyfriend and I decided to check this place out after we heard they were now doing Monday night trivia.
