The trivia facebook page informed us that trivia started at 8pm and included $2 sliders and $3 CT craft beers. Sounded perfect. We walked through the door 5 minutes to trivia time, happy we weren't late, only to discover that trivia was actually starting at 8:30. Upon arrival, the place was pretty dead, including the music which consisted mostly of songs by Muse played at practically a whisper. We cozied up to a two-top table near the bar with plush velvet seating and waited for the server...and waited...and waited. She must have walked by our table about 10 times without so much as a look in our direction. Both of us, having worked in the service industry, are sympathetic to waitstaff especially when it's busy - however this girl had two, yes TWO tables in addition to ours and couldn't be bothered to even smile or say hello. Unacceptable. So after 15 minutes of waiting, we ordered our beers at the bar from the friendly and knowledgeable bartender, perhaps the only pro of the night. I had a CT craft wheat beer and my boyfriend had a pilsner, both delicious (okay, second pro of the night). After sipping on our beers for another 10 minutes, our waitress finally decided to make an appearance, apologizing for the long wait and explaining it was her first night on the job. (I fear the staff they have on busier nights). We were famished at this point and decided to order a couple sliders (regular burger and philly cheesesteak), the falafel balls (off their "International Tapas Menu"), and a Mouth Water burger which had cheddar cheese, fried onion, and avocado on top with a jalapeno sauce served with fries. I am appalled by the lack of quality in their food. Granted, yes it's bar food - but wow. It was really bad. The falafel balls were dry and flavorless and about the size of cherry tomatoes. There were about 6 or 7 of them arranged around a dish of what was supposed to be tahini sauce. The sliders were mostly bread and also completely lacked flavor. The avocado on our burger was light yellow and looked like it was scooped out of a plastic unlabeled container. The fries were soggy and soaked in grease and oil. Terribly disappointing. As for the trivia, it was OKAY. I understand it's a new thing but it was a real turnoff how unorganized everything was. I probably wouldn't have minded as much had everything else been better. All of this being said, the decor of the building is pretty awesome and it's massive inside; it truly has a lot of potential. Too bad I will not be spending my money here again in the future. :(

Great sub sandwiches here. They don't skimp and ration their meat portions like other sandwich shops. The prices aren't too bad, either for the quality. The guys behind the counter were very friendly and seemed to legitimately enjoy working here.

The artichoke pizza is delicious!! We ate inside the dining room which was unbearably hot because there is no air conditioning and the drinks were warm because they don't have ice. I really feel bad for the staff there because they work in such a cramped place that gets really hot in the summer.

I had the pleasure of dining here for lunch on a Monday of a holiday weekend. With reservations at noon, it was not busy at all so I basically had the choice of any seat in the restaurant. I opted for the open kitchen counter since you're able to see the food being prepared, cooked, and assembled. Obviously it's not quite the same experience of sitting at a sushi counter, but the experience was still great as you feel like you're part of the kitchen and can strike up conversations with the chefs at any time (i.e. the grill master in my case). As mentioned in many of the previous reviews, the service was phenomenal. My waiter was very knowledgeable regarding the menu, guiding me through the standouts and taking my preferences into consideration. I saw the head chef Floyd Cardoz numerous times throughout my meal walking around the kitchen inspecting the food being prepared, giving me the assurance that the food I was eating was how it was supposed to be. Chatting with the grill master, I was able to find out the more popular dishes and his recommendations about the newly added entrees on the menu as well. The manager even stopped by at one point to say hello and make sure I was enjoying my meal. I re-iterate, service was top notch. Moving onto the most important part of the review now...simply put, the food was delicious. Each bite of the cod throats appetizer (as recommended by my waiter) was extremely tender and juicy. This was my first time eating cod throats, but it will definitely not be my last. The sauce underneath was tasty and did not overpower the dish. But the only complaint I have was that the lightly fried coating was on the salty side. For my entree, the grilled sea bream was bursting with flavor in every mouthful, paired nicely with a crisp Greek white wine by my waiter. The salsa, cabbage, and bacon each added a new dimension to the perfectly cooked fish. Even with the abundance of flavor, the spotlight of the dish was still on the fish. Finally, for dessert, the butterscotch pot de creme did not disappoint. Personally, I could eat the single "maltmallows" that topped the dessert all day. Subtle hints of aged whiskey in medium fluffy marshmallows are to die for. I'm not normally a fan of desserts because they are too sweet, but the chocolate streusel mixed with the butterscotch creme was decadent. And for those with a sweet tooth, if you dig a little deeper, you'll find a sunken treasure pocket of caramel to sweeten the deal. Overall, North End Grill is not perfect, but is on a very good track. Service is exceptional. Food is delectable, with just a bit to iron out. I will definitely be back to try the rest of the tempting menu. One unfortunate note to add, but will not be held against them in this review, is that I did notice a few dishes ready to go out, sitting idle and cooling for 5 minutes or so. With more new employees coming in and given this establishment is still relatively new, I have no doubt these small kinks will be addressed.

Great spot but their location is just hurting them soooo bad, not many people know about the place as its between Queensboro Plaza North and Astoria. Been here for dinner twice and enjoyed it both times. However, hard to see this place last long as they have Manhattan prices for their food. The food is exceptional though, but you cannot charge so much for LIC. I know people could afford it but thats not the point, you want people to come back again and again due to your location. The Burger might just be the cheapest and best thing on that menu for the price. If you  want to impress your girlfriend or parents then this is also the spot. The food is really good, I have tried a bunch of dishes as went in a group of 6 and did a lit mix and match.

My family's go-to spot for special occasions. Josh and Josh have been making great food and great dining experiences for years, long before any of the johnny-come-latelys in the neighborhood arrived. I had my first marrow bones here and haven't turned back down the path to decadence.

We were lucky enough last night to get bar seats at Casa Mono at the last minute. It was to my sister in law and I's surprise that the cooks behind the bar are as cute as the food is complex and tasty! Who knew Mario Batali only hires cooks who look like they should be sponsored by skate and snowboard companies? It was a really funny paradox- and luckily they were also all very talented chefs. We loved that the tapas proportions are large enough to share b/w 3-4 people, but small enough they you can order a variety of plates- everything is so good there it's impossible to narrow down menu selections. The pumpkin encrusted goat cheese, foie gras,and artichokes with salsa verde were my favorites, but out of the 7 plates we ordered, there's nothing that I wouldn't have again. Our service was just average- pretty inconsistent with checking on our party, refilling water, etc. and he took too long to get us the bill.  The wine our waiter recommended was also sub par- it was pretty much the polar opposite from what we requested- however the selection there is so diverse I'm sure there we got stuck with one of the only bad bottles in the house. The food and overall ambience there compensate for a few missteps - I definitely will eat here again.

4 stars for something different...Only Italian wine and food.  Huge bar, and a ton of seating.  This place will definitely do better than the Italian joint that was previously there... I love the tapas option...I can leave this place without feeling like I gained 10 pounds in one meal, and I get to try a little bit of everything. The meatballs are a good choice, the pizza is OK, and the meat and cheeses are solid.

In the last two years, I've probably been to Verlaine's about 20-30 times.  Its one of those places where you just can't go wrong.  For starters, happy hour  is until 10pm every  night! The happy hour drink menu, although not super extensive, is pretty good and you can't go wrong with their signature Lychee martinis.  Not the strongest drinks in the world but if you have enough they can take you to your "happy place".  They also serve a nice assortment of asian fusion tapas.  Personally I've tried the shrimp, chicken dumplings, chicken satay, and ginger wings and all were seasoned well and flavorful.  Not to mention the food comes out fairly quickly and is always hot.   For a LES bar it isn't as divey as you would expect (although I would hate to see it in natural light) and while itts definitely not a fancy bar its a step above some of the other grungier bars in the area.   Be warned - it gets VERY crowded as people filter in for drinks after happy hour at other bars has ended.  There is pretty much one hostess who also waits tables but somehow she manages to turn tables and make sure you get seated.  Service isn't stellar but they get the  job done.  There is a DJ who plays decent music and although it can be a little loud at times, its not unbearable. All in all, if you're looking for a happy hour bar where you can eat, drink and be  merry, Verlaine is definitely a good option!
Excellent food and service.

Love the food and the cocktails were delish!  We had a pretty large party and Duino Duende went beyond our expectation. My Fish Tacos were amazing!  Live music from the room next door at Radio Bean was a perfect addition. I will return -  again and again!

I have been here on numerous occasions, and I have even schlepped to Harlem before this one opened.  Each time, but the last I was not sober, and now I can write an objective review and also pinpoint that when inebriated I make wise decisions.   This is the best BBQ in the city, hands down.  Keep things simple if you're a first timer and opt for three meat platter and choose the holy trinity of pulled pork, St Louis ribs, and the brisket.  You will find God.  No controlled substance required, other than the food before you.

Stopped in this whole on the wall last night. Was lucky enough to stumble upon it on yelp. People need to be open minded when walking in, the friend I was with asked me if I was crazy for ordering food I kindly said no and ordered the beef sandwich. The place has an A rating and most of us know to find an a rating around china is a sight for sore eyes. The guy that prepared my food and rang me up was nice, I barely had to wait. Now when I got the sandwich I was kinda skeptical cause it wasn't a large portion, when I was done with it I didn't feel fat, over stuffed, I felt perfectly full and the beef sandwich itself was great. I also got the bread pudding which was amazing. I would rate this a 5 but I'll hold off until I get to try more of their stuff, and I'll definitely be coming back.

I went today for the first time and I ended up with a waitress who obviously had an attitude problem  and a hearing problem. She messed up on two of our meals and then had an attitude when asked about it by another waiter. It was a turn off. The reason why my family and I stayed is because of the French waiter who was very  professional and welcoming. As a French woman, I must say that the food was fine after it was corrected. I am not sure what was her problem...perhaps she did not like my unique family...not to sure. I was not going to argue with her because I had my kids and I was not going to waste my energy on rudeness. It was my first and last time in that cafe. Thanks to that waitress. Merci au serveur Francais:)
Mango Chutney...period.

What a delicious brunch on Labor Day! We were starving and scouring Yelp to find an acceptable establishment. This place fit the bill. It is tiny and only seats about 19 people but the food is quality. It's delicious comfort food. We ordered their eggs florentine which comes with a savory mashed potato side. Not bad. Their French toast is to die for with a cinnamon crust, powdered sugar, and a tart but yummy strawberry sauce. We were full beyond belief after sharing both items. Hope to return again. Prepare yourself for possible sarcasm though. I called before making the trek there to ask if they were serving brunch and the guy, who ended up being our server, answered with a snicker and said, "What do you think? Do you hear the background?"  I said "ok just checking since it was a holiday". He laughed again and said "See ya when ya get here". It kind of irked me but I figured what the heck. Turned out he was really nice, though sarcastic, and we had an enjoyable time.

I am giving it three stars because I have had too much expectation of this place. Hakata Ton  Ton is famous for their considerate preparation of pork feet that make them more edible. Unfortunately, I did not like such "edible" pork feet. Rather than claiming myself as a barbarian, I am trying to point out that their speciality, Grilled Tonsoku, was over-pounded and mushy that I felt like I was eating a pile of slime under a layer of crispy skin. Such preparation maybe a backlash of this place since I have definitely had some "real" pork feet with more texture in both NYC and Japan. However, they do have great hotpot and gyoza

There's a lot to like about Kennett, but I only went for the lamb burger.  I have to admit, I wasn't disappointed. It's so flavorful that even though the lamb is only served on a bun topped with some creamy radish coleslaw-type sauce, it's still impressive.  The meat doesn't need anything else.  I ordered medium rare and it came out pefectly. Kennett has a beautiful atmosphere, a solid drink list, and good service.  It puts off a slighly snobbish vibe, but that's my only real gripe.  If I'm paying $15 for a burger I'd rather do so at Village Whiskey.  And I don't need you to tell me that "Everything is locally sourced and organic; anything that is vetegarian can be made vegan..."  That's fine, just print it on your menu like the rest of the info. The dessert menu has some real treat on it.  Save room. Bottom Line: Good food, chill place, and good drinks.  Highish prices will make repeat visits rare.
Great food, service, and staff. We had a very enjoyable breakfast!  We will definitely be back.

since it's one of the few "brooklyn" y places on 4th ave, i wanted to like this place, i really did. have you ever had moules frites and thought you could eat just mussels and fries forever? that's how good these were. +5 stars for quality of food and decor. -1 star for being douchey about our table not wanting to drink anything but water and coffee at 4pm on a sunday afternoon. i'm sorry for violating your french sensibility of drinking nothing but espresso after noon but i'm a coffee hound and need my punch in the face dark brew of coffee. -1 star for sighing loudly and acting put off when an out of town visitor needed an explanation of what aligot potatoes were. maybe you were going for verite in service with the holier than thou attitude and i shouldn't dock stars but i didn't enjoy it. I'm going to come back because the food is good and I want to support these types of places in the neighborhood but once some place else opens up with nice servers, i'm outta here.
This is hands down the best sushi I have ever eaten. I always get the chef's selection and I am NEVER disappointed. If you love sushi you must dine here.

This place came highly recommended, and I see all these five star reviews. Granted, it's just a first impression, but I can't say this is Parsippany's absolute best. I'll give it a tie, but with two others right next door to me, I'm not going across town for this. The crust was perfectly thin and crispy, the cheese and sauce were just right. The mushroom half was great, the anchovy half was unfortunately light on toppings. That, and maybe my pizza standard is just overwhelmingly high, but I don't see enough here to give it a star over my local favorites, or to tie it with the best place or two around Jersey that I've had. I do leave the possibility open on a later visit. Maybe I'll go for the grandma pizza (or the drunken grandma) and it will swing my vote.

One of the marks of a good restaurant is how its chefs handle vegetarian dishes. I went to Bogota with a guy to whom meat-eating is practically a religious experience, and who raved about their non-veg entrees. Suffice it to say, I wasn't sure there would be veg-friendly options, let alone any decent ones. I was so, so pleasantly surprised. We shared a fishcake appetizer (yeah, I'm a flexible vegetarian), which was much more moist than most seafood-cakes. Then I had AMAZING marinated portabello mushrooms with some cilantro mashed potatoes and kale. The chefs knew what they were doing - the mushrooms were amazing, the sauces accompanying the food was amazing, and the veggies and potatoes were flavored in the most wonderful ways. There was nothing plan or perfunctory about the veggies dishes - they were handled with as much thought and skill as the meat ones. Bogota has a great wine list - the Agentinian Pinot Noir was fantastic. Our waitress was so friendly, really knew the menu and was not shy about helping me pick my entree from the list of ones I was considering. All in all, it was a great night out. I'd encourage anyone - vegetarian or meat eater - to go there. It's rare that a meat-eating guy and a vegetarian girl can go to the same restaurant and leave equally impressed.
Great restaurant, really good food and low prices. We love the place, and I love their red curry in particular. The only negative is that there can be a pretty long wait at times to get seated.

Hosted one of my birthday dinners here for me and 15 of my closest friends and it was a big hit. Food is exceptional here... local, clean and unpretentious.  We had a $60 pre fixe menu which included apps, main and dessert.  It was the right amount of food too! It's a bit hidden from the main road but I kind of like that.  They sat my party in one of the semi private areas of the restuarant so noise wasn't an issue for us at all. Our server was very funny and attentive as well.

A Classic. Diner style excellence performed to a near perfection. Awesome for families. The only thing holding this place back from a full 5/5 review is their lack of cleanliness around the place, as well as the occasional smokers around the premises. 4.5/5 for Creemees!!!

The quality of food makes up for the lack of choices. The service was average, table layout decent we happened to get a good table but only after a 20 minute. It's obvious to me that they were a 3 star restaurant trying so desperately to be a 5, but I guess that Williamsburg for you. Oh, too many gays for me to rush back...

Tough call, as I really wanted to dig the experience. Decor was egregious, as were some of the staff (others not at all!). Everything we ordered radiated a clear taste of sea and brine, which is not to everyone's liking, but I think you take your lumps when you order good seafood in a great place, and so this is more to personal taste. We didn't have the time for the menu tasting, although it sounds like it's a required kind of experience here. I have a feeling that could add a star or two by itself.

Great brunch! I love the hummus and falafel, all very tasty and fresh.  Great cappuccino too! The only con is it gets really crowded and doesn't have that relaxing atmosphere it used to have in the beginning.

Pellegrino ranked Momofuku as the 37th best restaurant in the world. The WORLD. Really now? Someone must have spiked the sparkling water at Pellegrino headquarters. Suffice it to say, Momofuku is not the 37th best restaurant in the world. It's not even the 37th best restaurant in the country, the state of New York, or New York City itself. That being said, it's still pretty good, it's just grossly overpriced. For similar quality at half the price, you can check out Myers & Chang in Boston, MA.
ok..atmosphere fun...sat outisde as it was nice day........had a few drinks...appetizers.....ok for what it is..

This is my 2nd time going. First time would rate 5 stars. I would say that the Cuban Sandwich trumps the hamburger two patti thing that they have(in all fairness i'm a true carnivore and usually order things medium rare or rare-this came well done and crispy). The banana lychee sangria is amazing as are the pastries and strawberry butter. Reservations are advisable unless you want to get seated at 330.  I also do not care for the chipotle ketchup. I know its random but its so off for a place that has most everything spot on.  Oh the coffee is great too.

Oh Natureworks, sweet Natureworks... how i love thee!  For those who enjoy mildly-bland, super healthy food (thats not meant to be a jab... im serious! it almost FEELS healthier when the food is a bit on the bland side) this is a great spot!  If you happen to remember the old-school pump (before it became burrito-style, make your own plate... tear.), this is pretty much the same deal. Even the turkey burger pizza style has been resurrected!! But that's beside the point... because i love it.  And you will too. If not, throw a little soy cheese on your meal and keep on' truckin.

This is a fun spot! The decor recreates a 1970's American living room and the food is all traditional American. My friends and I found this to be the perfect place to take a Japanese visitor. Our Japanese friend ordered the Thanksgiving Dinner and got a taste of American life. But under different circumstances Jones probably wouldn't be my first choice. It's a little pricey, the food was only okay and I definitely felt that my friends and I were rushed along by the waitstaff.
Had great lunch here. Nice salad and pizza. Great value and great location. Will definitely return.

I have been here a couple of times and the pancakes are indeed delicious. However, I used to walk by after capoeira and also hang out at the desert truck next door, and notice that there were always Korean or Japanese tourists outside. They seemed to wait longer than the others. Based on my own experience as well, the person taking names at the front (forgot what that is called) gave a vastly different wait time to the people before AND AFTER me. I hung around to listen because there was something about the way she looked at me, she seemed to think for a second. I also observed that people who came after us were seated before (two parties), and that the Asians who came at the same time as us were still waiting outside by the time we left.

I stand corrected about the best sushi in Fairmount. My roommate kept telling me how amazing this place is but we put off going because she also told me how expensive it was. The quality is definitely worth the price, although that doesn't mean I can afford it weekly like I wish they could. Super tiny spot, so I'd recommend making a reservation. Their menu is pretty big with a wide variety of appetizers and decent selection of special rolls. The special rolls are quite pricey ($16-19) but they are huge and the fish they use is really fresh. They are probably most known for these since they include non sushi like ingridients like pine nuts and fruit - but it all works! I kind of wish they incorporated more raw fish in them though, a lot of them were mostly tempura and other cooked or non fish ingredients. My favorite part was actually the regular rolls. I got the spicy salmon, and instead of a mushy mixture, they use bug chunks of fresh salmon lightly coated in spicy mayo. These were pricey too at around $8 but also large and I might even prefer them over the specialty rolls. Service was pretty fast and friendly. The best part - They're BYO!
Great coffee shop to work in. Lots of space, adn lots of beverages to consume. I just wish their chairs were more comfy.

Dear The Tacos El Bronco Food Truck, I love that you were perched right outside our N-train stop every night that we were in NYC.  Truly, within stumbling distance.   I love that you were open that one time at 4:00 am when tacos are the perfect food. I love that you have that magical salsa verde that I didn't learn about until day 2 and made up for it then. I like that things arrived (mostly) quickly both with and without a massive line. Always in my heart. Suzanne

Eh. Not impressed. I think this place would have gone out of business years ago without the supposed "competition" with Gino's across the street. I'd give these guys a 2/5, Gino's a 2/5. If you want something good, try Jim's on 4th and South 5/5. There are several other 4-5 star places around other than Jim's, but don't waste your time with these "authentic" places. The bread is all chewy and the meat is like something you get from 7-11.

I love this place but I really hate the fact that Mariah Carey is played EVERY single time I go for lunch, without fail. Some light Japanese classical would help the ambiance. Other than that, solid food, and terrific lunch deals! The service is very kind. It's not on the menu, but order a lemon roll. Delicious. eco tip: water always comes with a straw, so ask for your water without one!
Solid food, cute restaurant

I lived in Woodside for 10 years. Peking, in my opinion, is a landmark in this small town. I usually order the #3 which is chicken, pork fired rice and a salad. The rice lacks a lot of flavor but the rotisserie chicken simply melts off the bones and the green chili sauce is what really completes the meal. The amount of flavor it provides to the whole meal is simply amazing and the salad is the perfect way to end your meal. For $5 you get a meal that does well to the stomach.  Over the years this place has started to change; everything from the place being renovated to the flavors of the food. My last experience with Peking was the worst, the food is over seasoned and it didn't taste the way it used to. I hope this isn't a continuous trend and an one time occurrence. If you ever pass by the Woodside, you have to try Peking. It's a must! Become a fan on facebook! facebook.com/pages/Pekin…

Don't let the seemingly simple menu at Cookshop fool you - this place is fantastic.  After making reservations a few weeks in advance, I met up with some girlfriends for brunch here on a Saturday.  To say the place was packed would be an understatement.  Per usual, when I checked in they let us know that we wouldn't be seated until our entire party had arrived.  One of my friends got a late start and was nearly 30 minutes late.  We were concerned about losing our table, however the host could not have been nicer - as soon as she arrived, we were seated immediately. I was more in a lunch than breakfast mood, so I decided to give the burger, which came highly recommended, a shot.  I am a self-proclaimed cheeseburger aficionado and I was not disappointed by my decision.  The burger was juicy, the bacon was perfectly cooked (I really hate overcooked bacon), and the white cheddar was a perfect compliment.  The fries and Bloody Mary were delicious as well. Cookshop definitely gets a thumbs up from this girl - I can't wait to try it for dinner!
Food was great. Boyfriend had been craving chili cheese fries so I found this place and he loved it. The sliders were delicious and the black and white milkshake  was amazing!

I have a penchant for picking restaurants at random, and this was one the best choices I've made in a while.   The service was impecable, and my seafood platter (salmon, mussels, crab, shrimp, and scallops) in a panang curry sauce was enjoyable to eat, and pleasing to the eye before I dug in.  If you're in Chinatown and want good Thai, Erawan has my vote.

Came in here while waiting for the taping of the Daily Show. The staff are very friendly, the place is clean, the prices cheap and the food is good. We had the Retro Burger and the grilled chicken. Both came quickly and were good for the price. Happy hour specials are on before the show $1 off draft beer, wine and well drinks. Great place to kill a couple hours.

Went there for Sunday brunch.  I grew up two blocks from the restaurant and it was the first time back in thirty years.  Glad to see the neighborhood coming back. The food was very good with some creative, if not slightly weird offerings, as were the drinks.  I would definitely go back.
best bagels!!!!! best place for lunch !!!!!

Unfortunately, most of what we had didn't taste like much of anything. Fried chicken was bland. KFC is more enjoyable, and at a fraction of the price. The fried gnocchi & cheese and pork tacos were also disappointing.  Korean BBQ wraps and bacon fat popcorn was tasty, but one decent dish out of four and yummy complimentary popcorn is not a good batting average. Maybe the restaurant just needs time. On the plus side, the service was good. I'm just disappointed that a restaurant named after my favorite flavors in junk food wasn't a slam dunk the first time around.

We stumbled upon this place while looking for nice Italian restaurants in the area.  The interior is inviting and more spacious than a lot of the cramped restaurants you'll find in the area, so we decided to give it a try.  To our surprise there was a cozy, pleasant garden area in the back, which was heated and warm despite it being the middle of winter, so that is where we sat.  It was a romantic atmosphere that really added to the "European" aspect of the experience, and one person commented that she felt like we were on the set of a movie. The food was very good, though the portions were a bit on the small side.  Just enough to fill us up without feeling stuffed.  A couple of us had the black bass special and one person had a ravioli special.  The bass came with cous cous and was topped with a shrimp bisque that was incredible along with a hint of lemon.  For dessert, I had the Affogado, which was a little smaller than I would have liked, but good nonetheless (how can you go wrong with gelato and espresso?).  The service was attentive and pleasant.  Decent wine list.  We would definitely go back the next time we're in the area.

I chose this location for a quick, late-night dinner after moving into my apartment. Moving can make you very hungry, so we were starving when we dined at Mamoun's. We ended up spending ~$60 to feed 3 very hungry people, at which point we were satiated but definitely not stuffed. Additionally, I was unimpressed by the flavour of their food and quality of service. I would rank my experience as mediocre, at best. Verdict: This cost/value ratio wasn't worth dining here again.

We swung by Brauhaus on a whim after watching the Flyers kick some Buffalo butt on Thursday. Little did we know, we'd be joining in on the Karneval celebration. Bags of hot, sugary fastnachts made their way around the table and paired surprisingly well with my Erdinger. A shared plate of chicken jägerschnitzel with sides of potatoes and potato pancakes (again, we were several beers deep at this point - double potatoes were necessary) plus an order of delicious sauerkraut balls and I was in heaven. German heaven. I've decided that Brauhaus is well deserving of the full five stars. They're the place for great German beer and food in this city. And I am pretty stoked for their upcoming expansion as well.

Been here twice. The first time was a better experience. I ordered the chicken and waffles (white meat/ fried). It was really good. The second time ordered the same thing dark meat this time and it wasn't as good. Both times had the cheery kool-aid, super sweet, still good tho. Might go back and try something else.

The walk over the bridge to Brooklyn, the line I waited on for 30 minutes to get inside, the close (but cozy) table settings.... ALL WORTH IT! The pizza is incredible!!! I can't even describe.... simply the best! Definitely have to make it at least once (then twice, three times.....). Once you're in, the service is great and the the pizza comes pretty quick. Hot fresh unbelieveable pizza... There's an ATM inside just in case you forget that it is cash only. So far, my favorite pizza place in the city... even if I have to run over the bridge to eat it! (at least I burn the calories on the way back)

My husband and I went to Umi this past Saturday afternoon with high expectations. I've been looking forward to the opening of Umi since I first heard that it was in the making. On this Saturday afternoon, at around 4ish, the restaurant was by no means packed but there were several  booths of people. To make a long story short, the belt was almost completely empty (save for the weird mayo covered rolls and cold chicken teriyaki that no one touched) the entire time we were there. What we did get to try, was just about what you'd expect from food sitting around for an hour or two. We also only got one round of drinks (we each had an Umi Mojito that, save for the fact that mine had a dead fruit fly in it, were delicious) as our waitress disappeared (which seemed like the norm for all the wait staff and the chef in the center of the belt). For the money that we spent, I would have rather gone to any of the other wonderful sushi places in the area. At least we would have left full and satisfied and not reeling from the utter disappointment.

I like it, I like it ALOT... It's cute, and cozy and perfect for a date or a meetup with your friends. They serve wine and beer ; no hard liquor b/c they are located tooo close to a church..  #cray ... but.. the service was impecaable and they kept the restaurant open b/c I had a craving for an apple dessert which I got. This nice fluffy pastry was hot and delicious... I'm going back b/c I can't wait to try the rest of their menu. #LOVE THEM. .. The only problem I have with them is they don't market themselves very well. They barely have any lighting so it's very hard to find them and the sign is sooooo small .. I didn't even know what the name of the place was called until I asked the waiter. Hope they can get their name out b/c it would be a discredit to the neighborhood if they were to shut down.

Sips and Bites, I love you! So, so much. But please for the love of goodness bring back the Capsule Sandwich! I was told it would be back once brussel sprouts are back in season. I have no idea when that is, but please know I will be forever grateful if that bad boy returns. Regardless, a loyal customer always.

Have been meaning to try this place for a while & only ended up here on Sat night because the place we intended to go to (La Ziza in Clifton...previously reviewed) seems to be inept at taking reservations & advising customers of what to expect upon arrival.  We had a reservation & they specifically asked me if we'd like inside or outside seating...I told them inside, yet upon arrival I was advised there was only outdoor seating available, as there was a function & some kind of buffet going on inside (both upstairs & downstairs).  It was pretty humid out that night, so we passed.   OK, so we decided ot head to King of Shish Kabab.  It's a fairly small place & was full when we arrived at about 7:30.  When I saw only one waitress I was a bit concerned about how service might be, but she really did a great job.  (However, I still think that on a Saturday night they probably could use more help).  We ordered a ton of food (baba ganoush, falafel, spinach pies, tabouleh salad, kibbe, and split a kabab platter that included various skewers, rice, a salad & hummus).  Everything was very, very good & the prices are really fantastic.  Our bill came to about $35.  Definitely would recommend, but if you're looking for ambiance, this isn't the place for you!
The best , yes BEST ,brunch in the city !!!! Blueberry pancakes , enough said.

I effing love this place! Dinner:  pretty good entrees, nice atmosphere... but those bread rolls.  omg those are by far THE BEST bread rolls EVER.  i loved them so much the waiter sent me home with extra which is also a plus.   Sunday brunch:  UNLIMITED SANGRIA and different kinds of it.  the food again was really good and not at all expensive.  just make sure you can nap afterwards because all that sangria definitely put me to sleep.  Oh and their chocolate banana macademia pancakes in dulce de leche sauce was amazing.  *drools*

Used the Groupon deal on a Friday night in January. It was dead inside. We had a reservation, but definitely not needed. I imagine it might be busier in warmer weather when you can sit outside on the water. The inside is dark, in a good on an old ship way. You could say it is outdated, but overall a neat place to have a meal. We had a table with a great view of the bridge. First, I will say the service was excellent. Our waitress was friendly and knowledgeable. She quickly brought out warm rolls and took our order. We started with the salt and pepper shrimp which were actually really delicious and was a great size for sharing between 2 people. Unfortunately, this is where the food stopped being great. I ordered the scallops with the gnocchi and port sauce. This meal was so disappointing, especially at $32. The scallops were grey, rubbery, and lacked any real flavor. The gnocchi tastes like french toast and the vegetables were basically a mix of brussel sprouts and undercooked carrots. Very strange combination that I really regret picking off the menu. My fiancee got the ribeye with crabmeat. While the meat was cooked okay, the crab was mushy and quite unedible. For $50 this is not acceptable. We chose to skip dessert based on our entrees. I really think this place has potential to be a cool dining destination, but their entrees need a lot of work and their prices are just too expensive. Even with the Groupon deal, I felt we overpaid for what we ate. There are much better places to go in Philly for less money. I will not return to the Moshulu anytime soon.

Decided to order delivery. One of my co-workers wanted sushi, so I chose to order with her. We never tried this place, so we gave it a shot since it got some decent reviews from our other co-workers. First of all, our food arrived a half hour later than when it was supposed to get here. When I got the call from the delivery driver that she was here, I went to get it and the woman was apologetic and nice. Totally different than talking to her on the phone where she sounded kind of cold-hearted and mean. A star for that. The food: We ordered the maki combos where you get 2 rolls and it comes with a miso soup. My co-worker ordered Boston rolls and I ordered a Spicy Tuna and a Shrimp Tempura roll. Now, the Boston roll was okay, but the shrimp inside it tasted not very fresh. It was very sour as if it had been dipped in lemon juice for days. The spicy tuna from the very moment you looked at it...was very unappealing. The tuna was dark red, purplish, and black. Doesn't sound fresh, does it? It wasn't. I had trouble eating that one, but I paid for it so I ate it anyway. I'm expecting a stomachache later. I'll probably be barfing and everything disgusting in the bathroom later. The second star was for the Eggplant miso and miso soup. Now, those were good. I'll have to try out their Chinese food, Egg Roll Express, next time. No sushi for me from here ever again, though. Go to a real sushi place if you want better sushi.
It was ok not great but alright, are server was real good and the food have experienced better.

Based on the Yelp reviews my friends and I were hyped to come here but sadly this place did not live up to its hype. Our waiter was rude. We were served chips and guacamole upon arrival, we hadn't even ordered drinks yet. We assumed this was their complementary "bread basket". When the check came though we were charged for this item and when we questioned the waiter we were told in an off-putting tone that, "Yes, we made an error but you should not have eaten it. You should have returned it." Excuse me?! Why are we in the wrong? That and the "Pending Grade" due to sanitary conditions will earn this place a spot on my "never ever return" list.
corned beef hash ube waffles and fried chicken sisig with vinegar sauce

Munches hit the nail on the head with their,"FAT SANDWICHES"..they are the best around at a low price..if your up early,check out their breakfast too.I pass by every morning and stop in at least twice a week for breakfast.My favorite is the Jokers wild fat sandwich..I'd definitely check out Munchys if you're in the area.they have 2 locations now..Wayne & Little Falls

We almost missed the bucket of spuds when ordering.  That would have been a real shame.  Adding two fried eggs on top of the home fries with delicious cheese and salsa made this a meal in and of itself.  The sourdough french toast and the gingerbread pancakes had us all leaving stuffed. Is it expensive...yes Is it worth it...no doubt Can't wait to come back!
The lunch special is awesome. Decor is awesome. Staff is awesome. This place is awesome! So go try it yourself and be awesome! Sesame Tofu. Calamari. Awesome!

This will be my first review in three months, and with good reason. Traif, or "unkosher" in Yiddish, served some of the best dishes that I have had in months, in a trendy yet casual setting. Backtrack three months to Morgane, one of the worst French (or otherwise) restaurants to which I have been, and my ensuing hiatus from Yelp. Although I had a few decent meals between then and now, none inspired me to get back on until Traif. Its 4.5 rating truly reflects its quality. With a menu that can change from day to day, Traif offers a fresh selection of seasonal products in unique and and flavorful combinations. The plates are intended to share- similar to tapas- so it is ideal to order a few-- or more!-- depending on the size of your party. That said, reservations are recommended, especially if your party is large. In addition to their spectacular selection of dishes, Traif also offers a full bar- and delicious drinks as well!
I had no expectation going in. Now I love the place.
One of the best pizzas in NYC :) its not cheap though but worth it

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Chinatown. The menu is pretty large and varied, so there is something for everyone. The portions are huge and around $7 or $8 for a dinner. I wish I could make it here more often! It's delicious and you won't be disappointed.  Make sure you have cash on you, though, as they don't accept credit cards!

Our experience at Pok Pok was exceptional on all levels.   FOOD IS AMAZING... not just one dish... every dish.  I spent a month in Northern Thailand, and it's tru Pok Pok is the closest I've ever come to authentic Northern Thai (or any real Thai for that matter), in NYC. Granted it was a Monday night, so we didn't have the 90-minute weekend wait (though we still had a 30-minute wait, we were sent to the Whiskey Soda Lounge and thoughtfully watched over with drinks until our table was ready). Service was incredibly quick and attentive.  Our server made great recommendations on the number of dishes and types of dishes to order, to provide us with a variety of tastylisciousness without overplumping our bellies. The Catfish is a MUST.  The Chang Mai sausage is a MUST.  Both these dishes capture the fresh & fragrant, lemony-minty-chili-ness of real Thai food.  We also had the pork shoulder-pork belly and it was fantastic... deep, rich sauce filled with complex layers of spices that unfold in your mouth.  Even the broccoli and mushrooms, while simple, were the perfect off-set to the spicier dishes, with a subtle but exciting flavor. I immediately wanted to return the next day, for another meal. TIPS for a great meal at Pok Pok : 1.  Go early in the week, after they've spent Sunday recovering from the weekend rush.  They're re-stocked, and re-energized, and the wait is a fraction of the time. 2.  Ask your server what is particularly good THAT NIGHT.  This changes, it seems, from night to night, so just like ordering street food in Thailand, throw any cravings off your foodie boat, and go with the flow. 3.  Don't order similar dishes.  Make sure you get dishes with different flavor profiles, so you can taste how they compliment each other.  And don't shy away from subtle flavors... they enhance how the spicy ones hit your palette. 4.  Don't overindulge on whiskey before your meal!!  This will kill your tastebuds and anything spicy will seem to fall flat in your mouth, as you'll miss all the flavor layers.   5.  Skip the dessert and opt for the Mango Coconut drink instead... heaven in a stainless martini glass.  The perfect finish.

Southwark is one of Baby's and my favorite restaurants and go-to spots when we want a wonderful dinner back in my old 'hood of Queen Village. We never fail to have a great meal there. And when the weather's nice, we make sure to get a table on the lovely back patio. The staff is professional and knowledgeable (but  without  any hint of pretension or condescension) offering friendly and attentive (but not annoyingly so) service. There's a reasonably priced (at least as reasonably priced as possible under the prehistoric PLCB policies) wine list with a nice selection of wines by the glass. And, of course, there are the cocktails - Kip (who I first encountered at the New Wave) and George have done a wonderful job at reviving the fading art of cocktail-crafting. The menu changes regularly and focuses on local and seasonal foods (Many a time I would see Sherry and Kip shopping at the South and Passyunk farmers' market on Tuesdays.) Having discovered it at VaLa Vineyards, we frequently start out with the baked Shellbark Farm's goat cheese. We've savored the full gamut of entrees - duck, pork, steak, chicken, fish - and never been disappointed. (Baby and I just wish their home-baked bread was served warm - last time we were there it was actually a little cool from the kitchen which definitely detracts.) Desserts are delicious and never heavy or overcloying.

A cute spot, filled with romantic couples (and blasting rock music). All we had was the Pig Out for two: very satisfying. I know, the $49 charge looks steep, but it's worth every penny. The noodles weren't as warm as I had expected, but they were still tasty. The pork belly was rich and succulent. I wasn't impressed with the other options on their menu, but this dish is very good.

I went there about a year ago and loved it! I returned on Saturday and mas very surprised by how the quality of the food changed. It seemed under seasoned compared to what it used to be. Sangrias were amazing, and the little bread they give you with the black bean or strawberry spread is to die for! The mojitos are some of the best I've had as well!

not even happy with this place. here from out of town.  came to see our team play. stupid white girl hostess gave. my table to another party because since we were all black she thought they were with me. REALLY!! so after three loud complaints and LOTS of B.S our game 30 minutes later is on . not happy at all. i will not be back nor will i EVER reccommend:-(

Wonderful place for quick tacos. The fried avocado taco is excellent. So is the fish. I probably come here once a week. The only thing is that every time I go there it is packed. They should open a second location deeper in crown heights.
Best Chinese food I've had in CT. Is fresh not greasy and portions are great the staff is friendly and welcoming. Great location you can also get a drink next door at wine harvest.
Great cheap italian food.  I've never eaten in the actual restaurant but I'm never disappointed by what I order.
came here for brunch. $20 pancakes haha. The drinks and food were good, but the whole experience was a bit pretentious. Yuppy central
Very cute coffee shop.  I love the back section which looks like a greenhouse with all of the natural light.

Banh Mi is still a relatively new food to mainstream Americans, but one establishment looks to change that. Does JoJu make a compelling case to provide resounding support, or should we all just move and find a different establishment? If you're the type to walk quickly past a neighborhood and not really take notice of all the business around you, you may easily have passed by this JoJu many times without knowing it. The small banh mi place is located on Broadway as part of the tons of shops that are inside one building before the underpass that lets you cross over to the Elmhurst Ave subway station side. If that doesn't clear it up for you, just Google Map it - believe me, you'll want to.   The size of the location is pretty small but there's a decent amount of seating for an establishment of this size - about 12 people can be seated. The tables are clean, the furniture is of some quality and feels like there was some sincerity put into the thought of the design of the place - rather than "just put something where people can eat". What the real star of the show is the menu of items. Just about everything on that menu is simply delicious. The appetizers whether they may be simple summer rolls or some satay are executed perfectly. I've visited this place a number of times, and a number of my friends who I have recommended this place to agree. Best of all from their selection - besides their iced tea which is a MUST - are the banh mi. Each one that I have ordered has had an on-the-mark toasting of the foot long baguette has a nice crisp taste to it. No matter which sandwich you order, the ingredient are fresh and have the "just finished being prepared" taste. If there's any gripe this reviewer has about the sandwiches, it's only that there simply isn't enough stomach room to order every single item off the menu. This review may sound too overjoyed about this establishment, but I'm not the only one. I rarely agree with food critics but it seems like this is something both I and the NY Times can agree on. To find out more about this place - just go there! SUMMARY - PRICE: For a little over the price of a meal at Subway, there's no question you'll be thinking this is the better place to find a sandwich - and a Vietnamese one at that. - DÉCOR: While its menu is certainly affordable, the design doesn't feel like a cheap after-thought - FOOD: After visiting a place like this, Banh Mi is certain to enter your vocabulary   - even if you might have tried other places before. NOTEABLE MENTION: Fast, friendly service and free WiFi also help make this place great. Also, in case you were wondering, you can actually peer into the kitchen as you order, and see that the cleanliness is impeccable. This is great for a place to take some to go or sit down with a friend.

I've been to other Garces restaurants and I think this was probably my least favorite. I met someone for a 10:30pm reservation.  The place was packed.  I'm not really a fan of how the seats are set up so close to each other. Don't get me wrong, I love being able to hear three conversations at once, but I was having sensory overload upon sitting down.   The water that was poured for me had something that resembled a tooth or a kernel of corn in it.  The person I was with, disgusted by the site of this water, put it on the table next to us that was temporarily vacant.  It was bussed away without any notice of the staff.  We didn't make a big deal about it; this was a special dinner and we had bigger fish to fry.   The meats and cheese that came out were very good.  Exactly how they should.  Don't know if the dipping sauces with the cheese were necessary.  Just seemed like bells and whistles.   The courses that came were pretty tasty.  The pork ribs with fennel and orange - not quite it's season yet, were good.  The wagyu beef was phenomenal - that red wine sauce was the single best thing I tasted that evening.  The octopus was terrible - I wanted to love this dish, but it the texture of the octopus was dry and mushy.  I was missing that subtle meaty chew I usually like out of the octopus.  The flavor was also off - like the spices had been overtoasted.  The server comped us since we only ate one or two of those mini hockey pucks.  The bacon wrapped dates weren't very good either.  Dry, unloved.  This trendy food item has finally jumped the shark. The scallops and the lamb chops were expertly prepared.  I liked how they are very simply seasoned to let the ingredients speak for themselves.   Didn't stay for dessert.  The server we had was very nice and personable despite whatever hospitality blunders had occurred.  I would go to any of his other restaurants over this one.
Great flavorful food, awesome prices, BYOB! Recommend the duck appetizer!

$10.50 for a hoagie? Really? Nothing special here peeps, move on. Very bland hoagie and as good as the rolls are, there are soooo many other places in the city and its surrounding areas to get a good/great hoagie. Very disappointed. Service was fine, shop was empty so I didn't have to wait long like some others have stated in their reviews. Pricey Couldn't believe the blandness of the hoagie, nothing really popped out at me. I got the medium, was substantially smaller than the medium Primo Hoagie and the ones from Pastificio. Tried, not going back. That's my story and I am sticking to it.
why do people in brooklyn still sprinkle parsley on everything

This review is purely for its employee attitude. I came here last night for dinner, and thought I may have left a scarf there. Today, when I called, a man answered, told me after 2 seconds that he doesn't see a scarf, and when I asked to talk to someone who was working there last night, he told me to "come find it myself" and hung up on me. As a result, I called back, and asked to again, please talk to someone who worked there last night, as this man kept on saying he wasn't working at the time. I hear him put me on hold and curse at me to another employee in Chinese. Since he wasn't aware at the time that I did understand Chinese, I told him, in Chinese, to please stop insulting me. He replied that with my "garbled Chinese and English," he had no idea what he was listening to. This continued for a while, until he finally asked me to leave a number that he will call once they find the scarf. Overall, while the restaurant's food is alright, definitely not stellar but decently tasty, there's no reason why people should spend as much money as they do just to receive such rude customer service. As a patron of this restaurant ever since its opening, I am disappointed at how the employees treat their supposedly valued customers.

Any time I want a burger, I think of going to Rouge. The meat is nicely cooked every time I eat there, the caramelized onions and gruyere cheese are just two great additions to the already perfect burger. If you want a great burger go to Rouge!

Came here recently for a friend's bday dinner with a party of 10+.  Let me start by saying that this place is not very big.  The front of the restaurant is where they seat the larger parties, then the middle is the full bar and the back is where they sit the rest.  Half of us were sitting up against the wall on a wooden bench.  It was supported by a makeshift cushion that constantly slid when someone moved in and out.  To say the least it was not very comfortable.   Now on to the food, we started out with a few appetizers:  Sisig, it came in a small pan with a garlicky aroma but unfortunately the flavor and taste did not match the smell.  The pork pieces did not taste fresh.  Lumpia Shanghai was next, instead of the traditional egg roll shape it came in a straw-like form with only 4 pieces.  It tasted ok but nothing special.  Pork BBQ, there were 2-3 skewers and like sisig it smelled better than it tasted.  The glazing tasted ok but the actual meat was not very desirable. For entree, I decided to go with the Bistec, which was in a very decent quantity.  The marination could have been tangier and again the quality of the meat was not great.  The beef was very tough and required excessive chewing.  A few people had the Kare kare which was served in a peanut butter sauce.  The peanut butter was so overwhelming that it was very hard to consume the entire thing. To go against our better judgement, we decided to order dessert.  We shared the flan and the coconut sponge cake.  Both desserts had the right amount of sweetness but lacked the flavor and texture.  The flan was too firm and did not have the creamy consistency.  The sponge cake was not very spongy and tasted a little stale. The one bright point was the service.  The waitress/hostess were very nice and attentive.  I know it is not easy getting out orders for a large group, but I felt that did an above average job.
Fried chicken is great. Nice waitstaff.

The Anchor was very busy on a Saturday night around 10:00pm, but we secured a great spot to carry on an analysis started at Ordinary. I can't say much, because my experience was pretty straight-forward: a fun and lively bar on a Saturday night, full of 20-something and 30-something-year-olds. Good service and an energizing environment; an all-around good experience. Verdict: Yes, I'd come back!

Talking about FRESH... This place understands what fresh does for taste and the presentation of their food! AND this was delivered!!   My first and only experience was just a couple of days ago and I can still remember the feeling of GREATNESS after eating their pizza.  I ordered half meatball /mushroom and half anchovies/onions pizza with a mixed field green salad with tomatoes and olives.  Everything was wonderfully fresh and delicious!! So, if you want a fresh and deliciously hot pie deliver to your house, THIS IS IT!!

Just ate here on Friday and was pleasantly surprised. Great Belgian beers, nice mussels, amazing salads and desserts. Super friendly service and kids got to eat free (that night at least). Will go back!
Horrific and so not worth it!! I am appalled. Lamb chops and lamb kebab was not worth the 25 bucks. I would never come back.

Maybe it was because it was a friday night and they were packed out (had to wait for about an hour for a table for 6, but we didn't mind because we were at the bar) but everything tasted subpar. The grilled steak was swimming in a broth that wasn't too good. The mussels had a fishy aftertaste, and overall, it was not an impressive experience. Nothing made any of us say "Wow this tastes good." The only marginally good tasting things were the pineapple fried rice and the pad see yue. This place fell off, used to be much better. But the atmosphere overall was not that great either. Super loud, like a cafeteria lol.

Il Corallo is always a favourite, especially when I am craving pasta! Last night I went for a simpler choice and got the Taglierini Aromatici and it was, phenomenal, as usual. The noodles were so delicious and chewy, i could eat them for days. For starters, we got an order of crostini with vinegar glazed chicken liver (it was one of the specials). The crostini was delicious until I unknowingly bit into a giant piece of pepper in the mix. But all in all, still one of my favourite Italian places in city :)

Plan B recently opened in Milford, CT.  I am very impressed with the look of the bar and restaurant, Clean, the atmosphere it's great & the food it's delicious.  I am not much of a burger eater, but the meat it's fresh and cooked just right or the way you ask for. To sum up, the burgers are delicious and the ambiance of the restaurant lives up to Max standards. Great Job.... to the Chef Manager and Waiters.

pasta!  cheap wine! great pick before a show. When we were there they needed to switch our table towards the end of our meal for a big party that was coming in. To apologize for making us move they brought us a tray of every dessert being served in the restaurant that night! chocolate mousse, canolis, fresh fruit, cookies, chocolates, it was to die for. I would have been satisfied with even one of the desserts, but being able to try them all made it an awesome memorable experience! great place!

I came over to this restaurant because I had to crash at a friends place neaby (those brooklyn raves are all nighters all right) We had a super late lunch at around 3pm and still had to wait in line. I ordered the biscuits and sausage gravy and it was the tastiest thing I have had ever! The biscuits were oh so good and the gravy was well made too! I would definitely make my way over to brooklyn just to eat at this place!

I lived in Lawrenceville for 4 years and though I ate at many places in the area, I had never tried Penang. What a shame that I missed out! Boyfriend and I were in the area and were hungry and indecisive, as usual. We weren't so hungry for a buffet or a diner but we are picky enough not to settle for fast food or whatnot. So, we decided to try Penang, despite a few unfavorable reviews on Yelp. The inside is large and has nice ambiance. The waiters were nice but not totally attentive. The menu has many options but isn't overwhelming. Some items seem really expensive while others very inexpensive. I chose Captain's Noodles with a side of coconut rice, which I mixed into my dish. The meal was great, portion huge and it was  hot, fresh, and very very yummy. The coconut rice blew my mind and I'm suddenly addicted to it. Boyf got pad thai with chicken and he said it was pretty tasty. We were too full to try anything else. I knocked a star for not having the most attentive wait staff and also for $3 unsweetened iced tea and $2 for a can of diet coke. For the two entrees, two sides of rice and the two drinks, our bill was $28. Not bad and we both have leftovers.

What do I love about Bo Ky?  Hmm... EVERYTHING!  I had been going to Bo Ky since the late 90's.  No. 9 and 18 are my favorites, with soup on the side!  The taste is out of this world, the chili sauce is to die for, and the owner brothers are very friendly.  Yes, I moved to SF from NYC, and I miss their dishes, there is no such place in SF, and I tried bunch of places!  I went back to NYC in Sept 2012, went to Bo Ky, satisfied my cravings, and I was really happy that they opened up a bigger place called Grand Bo Ky!  I think the food is better than I remember, and the price, OMG, it hasn't changed!  God bless Angle and his family!!

My boyfriend is obsessed with this place on  so many levels I had to write a review. We have eaten lunch and dinner here as well as dessert many, many times.  The food is interesting and unique but expensive for what you get.  For instance, a bagel with peanut butter and chocolate is 6$ and there is like no peanut butter on it and the bagel is chewy.  But seriously, who could pass up the experience of eating a chocolate peanut butter bagel? As for desserts, Max Brenner has my all time favorite dessert: The Euphoria Chocolate Peanut Butter Fudge Sundae.  O.  M.  G.  Best thing I have ever eaten.  Ever.  If I could each this every day I would.  It has everything you could want: chocolate, peanut butter, peanuts, chocolate sauce, peanut butter sauce, chocolate ice cream, peanut butter ice cream... my mouth is watering. All in all: expensive but a trendy and cute experience.  GREAT for dates and DELICIOUS desserts.

I'm not a big fan of BAR as a dance club (needlessly expensive covers and bad DJs), but as a restaurant it's excellent. Great selection of house-brewed beers and some of the better New Haven-style apizza that you'll find anywhere. Everyone I've taken here has been a fan of the mashed potato pizza with bacon and garlic, and for good reason. It's completely delicious and not something you'll find everywhere. I happen to love their eggplant pizza with red sauce as well--it really complements the crispiness of that perfect thin, New Haven crust. Grab the house salad with bleu cheese, pears, and caramelized pecans and a pitcher of beer (the Toasted Blonde and Damn Good Stout are ideal) and I guarantee you won't leave unhappy. Just a quick note: it can get crowded. Really crowded. Like, sometimes packed on a random weekday afternoon. So don't go with a large group of people and expect to be seated immediately.

Yes, I'm empanada crazy. This is my empanada quest story. The place is nice and clean. It looks like they have an outdoor seating but only for the summer. The order taking and serving is organized. The menu is well-thought out. Except that the Hawiaan empanada I tasted did not have sweetness and great amount of pineaple fillings. I compared this to Mamas Empanadas near Queens Mall. They put more pineapple fillings so their empanada is juicer and tastier. The Mamas price tag is 0.25 cents more though. My only complain is the sign of no pets. I understand that most restaurants and eatery do not allow pets but for goodness sake, I'm only giving you my order and payment. The high counter service is 2 steps away from the door w/c basically counts like an counter that could be outdoor. I know and read the sign and the rules. I'm only there to pick up a little piece of empanada and we are gone. What's the problem with a small dog to a service dog? In fact, service dog is dirtier than a small dog. Don't look at us, like we carry diseases! I like that when I walk with my dog that we walk with purposes. Eatery like this, do disservice to any dog owners. It's not fine dining; it's fast food. You have outdoor seating why don't you use that for dog owners to enjoy your establishment but instead you frown upon us - like - we are second rate citizens. We are all here to do business. Do not discriminate. Cater to dog owners too.

Cheap, amazing, buffet style. Place is F'n incredible yo! Cool dudes too! **PRO TIP: Do NOT load up on the buffet!!!! Go straight to the dude who's handling the stuff on the skewers. Ribs, Bacon Wrapped Chicken, Steak. Boom you're outta there after tossing some fries and rice on your plate. Sidenote: Be careful when you're ordering from the skewer dudes....they all tend to just start adding way more than you asked for haha...whatever tho stick it in yo fridge for tomorrow!

My boyfriend and I were looking for a place to get brunch near times square and we found this place. It is quite small and the ambient could be better, not really romantic. But the food was great! $13 for the best eggs benedict I have ever had, unlimited coffee and mimosa! Definitely recommend!

Best brunch in the Princeton area. There bagels are excellent, will compete with the best NYC bagels. The staff is friendly and helpful, and very courteous. We are moving out of the area and the thing we will miss the most is this place- it's one of a kind!

This is a cute spot, good vibe and GREAT food. I tried the Taleggio, sun dried tomato and chive oil crostini as my app & It was so fresh and tasty. For my entree, I had the Artichoke with goat cheese, sweet onion and rosemary oil panini..I can't say enough about it...my mouth was doing backflips..amazing and again, very fresh. I can't to go back and try everything else on the menu.

Read all the reviews online and decided to try it for myself.  Great pizza and worth the wait.  Constantly a line outside for people to get theirs and that is amazing considering they were from all around the world.

I am no burger connoisseur, but I thought it was a pretty good burger.  I got the 500 degree and it was juicy and flavorful.  And the bakery bun, makes it that much better.  However, I am a french fry expert and did not think the fries were that good.  Every bite I felt my arteries becoming more clogged, but I think it is worth a try.

On my way to MoMA, I saw this cart and there way a long line waiting to buy food, so I figured if the line was long, then it must be good.  After I left MoMA, I was starving, so I walked back to this cart and got in line. I ordered the Gyro & Rice, and they asked if I wanted hot sauce on it. I said yeah and they put some on. Then the guy asked me if I had ever had the hot sauce and I said no. He took my plate and scooped the portion with the hot sauce off and served me a fresh portion, and told me "oh, you'll kill yourself if you eat that! It's even too hot for Mexicans!" and then he gave me some hot sauce on the side. I was laughing so hard.  It was the most delicious gyro & rice bowl I had ever eaten!!!!! I HIGHLY recommend this cart!!! And yes, the hot sauce was really hot, but it was good!

I was very much looking forward to dinner at Market Table.  I've walked by the restaurant so often and I admired the decor and menu every time. The decor is stunning and the ambiance is inviting. The wine menu was sophisticated and I was impressed. However the food was mediocre.  I had the chicken entree and it was very salty. My friend had one of the specials and the food was cold. When we asked if the chef could fix the food or if we could reorder, our waitress said it was against restaurant policy. They only charged us for one entree which was more than fair but it's a shame we left with a negative opinion on the food because it's unlikely I will go back. The staff was also not friendly and somewhat aloof.

A very good Italian restaurant!  We went on a Thursday night and it was crowded.  Reservations are highly advisable!   The owner is very amicable and makes for a pleasant dining experience.  The pizza here is delicious!

The Counter, is mediocre and overpriced.  the avg price for a meal for two here feeds four at chipotle or panera which are literally two steps down in either direction. Ordered a 1/2 lb burger with fresh mozzarella, spicy pickles & sundried tomato aioli on a Hawaiian roll. The burger and roll were good, the aioli was nearly flavorless, the fresh mozz equally lame and it's a "premium" cheese so it cost extra, opted for the accompanying side of fries which I probably had about 5, more like potato sticks and I could taste the onion from the grease in which it was fried, wasnt really feeling them. Spicy pickles, I received ONE. My adult shake was pretty good, sadly it took about a half hour to hit the table along with the food. This place needs help, ASAP.

This is the best little noodle niche I've found in NYC. The Spicy Totto Ramen bowl is incredible. The portions are huge for their low prices and you can't beat the cozy hole-in-the-wall atmosphere. I've heard the wait is usually pretty awful but I went for a Valentine's meal and had about a 15 min wait, which is rare. It is cash only which is something to note before going, but we found an ATM just a block away so you'll be fine even if you forget to bring cash. Overall, the most delicious noodles and I highly recommend!

Just found about this place from a friend, I was impressed by the service of the stuff they are very attentive and polite, service as it should be. To the main part the culinary experience is truly outstanding, I ordered a unique dish that I did not see anywhere else, The Lamb Shank in one word Wow a burst of juices and the most tender meat I had in a long time. The deep flavor of the lamb is there the spices are just right a real gem. After such a great main course I ventured to try the dark chocolate mouse needless to A M A Z I N G !   My new favorite place

Service was pretty good. Food not so much. Came here for dinner on a Friday night. No wait. I had the Indian pancake and my friend had a mixed rice type of thing. It was just parathas but they were ok. I'm not sure if it's the same Spice they have in New York (was lunch for few years) but wasn't a fan. Dessert was good-some gelato with chocolate syrup and the waitress was nice enough to give me extra syrup and whip cream cause I told her I wanted a lot of chocolate. Probably come back for their dessert. And for that reason I'm going to give a more stars.

This restaurant is amazing! I've loved it since before it opened (I have to admit that I know of the the peeps behind the scenes, but I am not biased) and finally got the chance to experience the restaurant on their first night of evening hours. Now, again, if I go to a restaurant that I've never tried before and it has a burger on the menu, I will automatically order the burger, even if I throw out the idea of trying something else. Nope. Burger. Why? Because if you can make a good burger chances are I'll like almost everything else. On the other hand, if you screw up the burger, we won't be able to hang.  With that said, I ordered the burger and I'm so glad I did. I asked for medium and it came back more medium rare than medium, but I'm actually pleased with how it came out. It had a ton of flavor and was moist and juicy.   Everything on the burger was perfect too, the bun, the cheese, the lettuce. It was all perfectly put together. The burger came with a oyster potato hash which is divine. No. I'm not lying. It's freaking divine. I highly recommend that if you don't get something that comes with the hash that you order it on the side because it's worth every bite. My friend ordered the octopus and I had a bit and it was delicious--perfectly seasoned and grilled and soft. So good! For dessert we shared the apple crisp. Now, it is good, but was a bit off. I'm not sure why or what exactly made me not love it, but it was just alright. Part of me just wants to say that there was too much salt, but there was something else that threw me off and I can't recall what the flavor was. The red wine that we had was delicious (can't remember the name, but it was the first one on the list) and the coffee I had after dessert, to balance the fact that I may have drunk a little too much wine was really good. I can't wait to return to try brunch and maybe even lunch. Oh and before I forget--ambiance and music--total wins each! The music playing totally reminded me of my ipod, which is clearly why I'm a fan, but it fit the ambiance of the restaurant perfectly.  The back is small, so don't expect too much space, but once you're inside, it's cozy and warm and perfect for cold nights like last night.  Also the staff is very friendly and welcoming/helpful. They really made the experience all the more fun.

Pretty standard Thai food, as the menu here is more or less identical to menus in most generic Thai spots in NYC. I got the calamari and the dumplings in peanut sauce. The calamari was good, but nothing special. The dumplings, however, were really delicious, especially the peanut sauce. You should definitely get this!!! As for the entrees, I got the drunken noodles with duck. The noodles itself were good, but the duck was kind of overcooked/charred so I didn't enjoy that part as much. My boyfriend got the beef spicy basil fried rice, which was actually really good! Other than the charred duck, this is a good spot to check out if you're craving Thai!

I dropped in for carryout around 12:30 pm and ate my lunch in a park between Thomas and Worth Sts, just west of Church. I thoroughly enjoyed my whole wheat pita stuffed with vegetarian delites of some sort. The food was served up quick and with a smile. The seating was mostly taken with small groups and couples or I might have eaten there. Nice day, though. This is my second visit and I can say it is consistently good.

Went to the bar last night for dinner - 99% of the booths are completed now to address the other reviewer.  I had the Maui wrap and hubby had the turkey wrap.  We tried regular and sweet potato fries and both were good.  The stand out to me was the pickles -I would put them on par if not better than Eli cannon's.  looking forward to going back because there are other items i'm curious about.  Little feedback -less news on the TVs and more sports....don't enjoy watching mad jim Kramer investment guru.

BOOOOOOOOOOOM !!!!  WA  Wa Weee Wahhhhhhhh! That is one damn good restaurant. The burrata is fricken unbelievable. Next up was the short rib sando smothered in arugula and dressing. Also my server was absolutely amazing. I wanted to see if they would serve her on one of those amazing rolls, but alas they wouldn't . As for the atmosphere...yabadabadoo is all I have to say.

I'm not sure why so many of the people that have commented on this place are not considered by the app, but please scroll down and see the ones that are not considered in the overall rating. Those are the ones that seem to be most accurate? I love Yelp but it's weird that they have seemed to exclude all the negative reviews of this establishment. That being said, there is an amazing draft beer selection here. Possibly best in town. Service is in line with the negative reviews, though.

This is a nice little bar with a good beer selection in both draft and bottle. The place is a long narrow space with a bar that runs almost the entire length. So there are a lot of spaces to sit available. They also have some small tables and a large booth on the back wall for large parties. My only issue with the place is the kind of cheesy/lame nautical theme. I feel like I'm in a place that bought up the old fixtures from a Red Lobster or some other terrible restaurant. The service was a little slow, but only because it seems like they never have enough waitresses on duty if your at the tables. Service at the bar is much quicker. All the staff are knowledgeable about the beer selections and are very friendly.
Better then pats. Problem is they mass produce cheesesteaks so they are no longer fresh.

If it wasn't for a good friend of mine who recommended this place on a random night, I don't think I'll ever discover MEW Izakaya? This place is so easy to miss because the door to the basement of the restaurant is very small! But once you are inside, it's like a whole new world (sings Aladdin), even tho it's a basement but he place is clean and decorated beautifully, sort of like you are sitting among fireflies. Try to come here early because this place WILL get pack! We came here during their happy hour (6pm-7pm) and we ordered the sushi special as well as the $3 Sapporo draft.  Along with the specials, we also ordered the Geso Kara-Age, Chicken Kara-Age(fried chicken), Age Tofu, Omu Soba, Potato Croquette, Garlic Fried Rice, Buta Kimchi. Some of my favorites are: Garlic Fried Rice- Who knew Garlic Fried Rice could be so good? Such strong garlic flavor and on top of the rice, there's a perfect poached egg, just break the yolk and let it melt into the rice and you have perfection!  This was so good that we had to order 2 of them to satisfy our cravings! MUST GET!!!! Omu Soba- Soba wrapped in egg omelet, who wouldn't want that? The egg brought such awesome texture to the soba and the soba had great flavor! Definitely good and picture worthy! MUST GET!!!! Chicken Kara-Age- Boneless fried chicken, I don't know what batter they use to deep fry these things but they are so juicy and flavorful! Just make sure you don't pop them in your mouth right away because you'll get burn and end up with a blister on your tongue like me! MUST GET!!!! Geso Kara-Age- No meal is complete without a little deep fried calamari legs, crunchy outside, soft and chewy on the inside... just can't get enough of these things!
