Not overly greasy and batter had excellent flavor! MUST GET!!!! Price- Pricing is very reasonable, dishes runs around $5 -$10. MEW is definitely best experience with a group of people, that way you can try a wide variety of food! Try to get here during their happy hour; $3 Sapporo draft is excellent! Just keep an open mind on the food options here and you'll have a great time!!
I live in NYC and every time I visit Philadelphia I need to eat in this place many times The food, the staff and the energy of the place it's just AMAZING! I wish I will have this place in NYC.
Still a favorite when I come to Vermont. It's definitely not cheap, but the soup is so good... As are all the other dishes I've tried.

Big fan of Vinted, actually surprised I've never reviewed it before!  I've been here many times, most recently about 2 weeks ago, and I've always really enjoyed my experience. The place is small, dimly lit, and intimate.  It's modern and comfortable, certainly sylish.  The cockails are quite good - they've recently revamped their cocktail menu and their version of the Old Fashioned is wonderful!  It comes with candied ginger...yum. The food is served tapas style and while it's pricey, it's very good.  You HAVE to start with the risotto balls.  I'm always skeptical of a "known for" menu item, but the truffle risotto balls really are good.  (I will note that they seem to have grown smaller throughout the past few months...)  Some of my favorite menu items have disappeared from the menu (the duck buns! the short ribs deviled eggs! the tuna tartare!) but, after several days of internalization and thought, I realize that restaurants with chefs who care about what they do often mix up their menus to keep things interesting and seasonal.  Fine. The most recent trek we ordered the truffle risotto balls (obviously), served piping hot, as well as the burrata/prosciutto, the scallops, the hummus with scallion pancake (a refreshing take rather than the typical pita chips!), and the lamb meatballs with feta, whipped eggplant, and mint.  Everything was wonderful!  The scallops were a bit salty, I'll admit, but they were cooked perfectly. The waitress was clearly trained well - when we were ordering, we said we'd like to have a longer meal and have the plates spaced - she interrupted (not in a rude way) to say she would time the plates to make sure we enjoyed our meal to its fullest.  We did! Oh!  And I can't forget Vinted's claim to fame - their wine list!  Vinted inherited the super-cool wine temperature-izing system (it's a thing, don't question) from Uncorked that offers perfectly chilled or just temperature-ed wines in perfect pours for a myriad of different types of vino.  Back to the waitress, I asked her about various reds, as I was in the mood, explaining my palate, and she recommended a perfect wine for my taste, as she did for my friends.  Very impressed. I highly recommend Vinted for a good, winey, small plates-y evening.  It's not cheap, but it's a nice hidden gem in BlueBack Square.

My brother and I really enjoyed this place for lunch on our first trip to Philly's Chinatown. Try their Malaysian Iced Tea- it's delicious! Good service too. It gets busy since it's right in the heart of Chinatown, but we didn't have to wait to be seated and were not rushed to leave either. Definitely would recommend this place to others.

This could be the best restaurant i ever been to. The meatballs are amazing and they way you on order them is so different that it is a event itself. I read on multiple reviews on Yelp about the long wait to get seated to the restaurant but during my 2 visits in early december 2011 i got seated at the bar as soon as i I walked in both times. My favorite was the lamb meatballs served with pasta. On top of all it's affordable. A meal costed me around 25-30$ including tip.

This claims to be a "kid friendly" establishment. It definitely is not! My family and I stopped in on a Saturday night, were happy to be seated right away and our order was taken promptly. We then had to wait 30 plus minutes for our food to arrive (simple meals: hamburger, chicken fingers and chicken kabob, nothing special) during which time we were trying to keep a 6 year old and a 1 1/2 year old entertained. Our toddler was happy so he screamed twice and it echoed very loudly through the diner (which has nice decor but large amounts of empty space for sound reverberate). A waiter, not our waiter, promptly came over to mumble in broken English that "he can no do that in here". I asked what he would like me to do and he just shrugged his shoulders and walked away. More irritating than that was the fact that we were seated in a booth, divided from another booth by nothing more than a small ledge and some fancy iron scrolls. The couple on the other side felt the need to tell me that I should take him outside and continued to express their opinion throughout our meal. These pompous jerks felt that because they were from Princeton, had no children and came to a diner dressed in button down shirts, dress pants and skirts that they were somehow better than my "middle class" family in jeans and Tshirts. Sadly, the attitude of the staff seemed to be the same. I have never felt so unwelcome. A small note to all diners and restaurants: If you are going to claim to be kid friendly and provide high chairs, you should expect the children who sit those chairs to make a little noise. Especially if you make them wait 30 minutes for their food.

As in the photos here, the onion the lady at the shop used on our sandwich was stinky, old, limp and so bitter, it ruined everything and we even scooped all the onion pieces off the sandwich because we just could not eat it. Talk about quality control. If I were her, I would at least pretend to care and reach for the sandwich bar to check the onion because I saw a few sandwiches on their menu come with onion. I would not want other customers to have this bitter experience. Disgusting practice that could and should have easily been prevented and should certainly have been corrected when we pointed out to her specifically that she 'should taste it because it's really nasty,' Would certainly NOT go back.

I never knew ramen could have so much flavor!  This place was great. We arrived around 9:45pm on a Friday night and was told the wait was 1.5hrs.  That long of a wait for soup?! I thought it was a little crazy, but decided to give it a try. I'm SO glad I did!  The staff is friendly, quick, and extremely efficient.  They definitely added a nice touch to the overall atmosphere of the restaurant. We ordered the chicken wings (super crispy with the right amount of sauce) and I had the Akamaru Modern. It was a great meal all around. My only complaint is that they ran out of their pork buns before we got to order : (.  The bartender told me not to worry though because I'll be back again. He was right. I'll be returning Ippudo, hopefully next time to try those legendary buns!

So far, I've been only giving out 4 stars for Viet Sandwich shops because I find that something is always missing in the mix. All of these shops have their pros and cons and that's what differentiate them from the rest. -Nam Pang is more Americanized but their menu has a very interesting mix of varieties. I found their Pork Belly to be a bit bland but their bread is the best I've tasted so far. -JoJu is an excellent option when you're in the Queens area and their meats are on the sweeter side. But the bread is a little bit on the crispy side. -Banh Mi Saigon (In Chinatown) is still by far my favorite, but their bread doesn't do the sandwich any justice. As for Xe May, they bring on another twist into the mix. This is a small shop with about 5 stools and 3 guys running the show. Once you place your order, they immediately assemble the sandwich together. You also have an option on how spicy you would like your sandwich to be. I opted for the Super Club Classic sandwich with medium spice which entails a spicy mayo sauce made with Sriracha (similar to the ones you get in Japanese restaurants). Xe May is definitely more authentic compared to Nam Pang and the slices of BBQ pork and headcheese are very flavorful. However, I'm always having trouble with the bread. If any Viet Sandwich place can make their meats as flavorful as Xe May, Joju, and Banh Mi Saigon with Nam Pang's  bread, I'd automatically give them a 5 star rating. I didn't get to try their Ice Lemonade with Basil or their Ice Lychee Green Tea, but they look delicious!
Can't. Stop. Coming. Here.

I celebrated my graduation at Gato along my family who traveled from Mexico... we all LOVED IT! there was no dish we didnt like, and my family's experience in NYC reached a new standard. All is excellent: the grilled octopus, the scrambled egg, the paella.... Just go! You can see Bobby Flay working the kitchen! flawless! Service was EXCELLENT!

Really amazing spot. A little off the beaten path, but that heightens the "aha!" feeling that you've uncovered a little gem. Great food and a brunch to die for. Great coffee. High quality food with upbeat, attentive and friendly service. I highly recommend.

Was pretty pleased when I came here with a friend for dinner. I'm not sure if we missed the 2 for 1 happy hour-do they tell you about it? Goat cheese salad: the goat cheese is the best part. there was so much lettuce-you could definitely split this. Babaganoush: very creamy and smoky, but I missed the eggplant flavor zuchinni cake: pretty good, I mean when are crunchy cakes bad? Kadaif wrapped shrimp: this was totally yummy-the sauce was really good. burekas: these were yummy, but I find burekas always are. Overall, everything was really solid and the atmosphere is quite pleasant.

This place is too small and the food is overpriced. But I always find Brazilian food in NY too expensive, probably because I'm a Brazilian. I had the feijoada with calabresa and it was good. The music was good though, good Brazilian music.

The cassava cake is my all time favorite and their coffee taste great! I stop here whenever I am in the neighborhood. The employees are super friendly and it's always a pleasure to stop by their for a quick coffee and cake/muffin on the go.

Went here for dinner and was not impressed at all. Doesn't have a fine-dining feel at all, more of a let's see what we can buy at Ikea and throw together in the middle of a meat/cheese market. Asparagus anti-pasta was a disappointment, too many flavors and the raw asparagus and porcini mushroom combo just didn't do it for me. Black and white cake was a letdown as well, the vanilla/chocolate mousse was enjoyable, but it was on top of a ginger/nut/cake concoction that tasted like a crappy, incredibly dry trail bar. Highlights were the cheese plate, funghi pizza & bronzino. I'd recommend heading here on a nice day with a bottle of wine, sitting outside and getting a cheese plate and a few other small dishes. But definitely the worst dinner I've had in Philly for the money spent ($120 w tip). Corkage fee on a 2nd bottle of wine is a bit ridiculous as well, especially after you bought it there.

This whole mess of a place is a great concept that falls short on many levels. The service is unorganized and chaotic. It took me 20 minutes to get my cookies, pastries and leave. For the quality of the product (dry, substandard, bleh) the prices are exorbitant. I don't mind paying a lot, but it better taste food. Maybe the tourists came in and bought all the good stuff? I hate to admit that I've had better muffins at Starbucks. Pretty disappointed. Which doesn't surprise me because the only Batali establishments I like are Lupa and the other one in the West Village. I think we'll stick to Sullivan Street/ Grand Daisy for our baked goods.

WAY MORE THAN JUST A "dive bar"!! This is one of my all time favorite places to come to in Philly. So much to do..pool tables, bumper cars, wall to wall graffiti, amazing specialty drinks, beer specials all the time, amazing happy hour deals, and super delicious  food. Free arts and crafts Sundays! Bar bingo once a month! I can go on and on! Such a great place to just come and hang out all day. Greatest place in the world!!!!!!

This has got to be the most heavily reviewed restaurant I've been to. I give Batali's Lupa 4 stars because of this: It was after a long week. I was meeting a friend there. I got out of work early so I took a long walk. My friend was late, so I had a long wait (it really wasn't that long). We get into the restaurant with out a reservation. We get sat immediately. I order a drink that had limoncello in it. We order the piccolo plate of different cured meats. (I can't quite remember what it's called, this was a few weeks ago). Hazy from the drink and the mild exhaustion, I slip a thinly sliced piece of cured protein (it was the salumi) into my mouth and feel like the nurse had upped the morphine drip. It was that good.
I love their food most meals I've had were so good I usually order for delivery, and the portions are just right.
good food. good atmosphere. good people. GORGEOUS CHEF. winner!! :-D

Where can you get any better cakes and desserts than in a "Wiener Kaffeehaus" (Viennese Coffeeshop). Sabarsky's pastry come as close as it can get to the legendary places Demel, Central or Sacher in Vienna. If you are not coming for the sweets, their austrian dishes are excellent, fresh and very authentic. The wine selection maybe pricy, but you certainly get very good ones. Overall, a sure hit, never been a miss so far. And by the way, if you want to read Austria's trashiest daily newspaper, they have the "Kronenzeitung" and the "Standard". Na bitte, a Melange..

Heard they had amazing burgers and stopped in for a late lunch on a friday afternoon. Be aware from 3-5 they only serve a few items off of the menu. I assume to prep for dinner service.... Its decorated with pigs, surprise. We were seated upstairs.There are mini stools for seats at the tables. Super uncomfortable.   Staff seems a bit rude. The entire time we were there the kitchen staff was running up and down the steps, loudly. Stomping I should say. In a huge hurry, frantic. Ordered some burgers, a med and two wells. The food took forever. The waitress said it was because we ordered well done burgers. Well duh... But a well done burger doesn't take 35 minutes to cook. The med burger was raw and had to be sent back. In which case they just half ass reheated and returned my same burger to me. The fries were okay, although the sliced fried garlic chips in them were delicious. Im not a huge fan of rosemary and was a little disappointed to see the pile of fries covered in it. $55 for three burgers. I'm not sure if the calm before the storm of dinner service had everyone there in a shit mood, but the staff all seemed miserable. Also the beer list is not very interesting. It has your typical "beginner"  beers for wanna be good beer drinkers. To be hip, ya know.

Sorry friends; my experience at Mark was alright. I was starving when I wanted a burger. It was a party of 10, and I was impressed that everything was made just as we ordered it. It's a very laid back place with friendly staff. Our waitress forgot an order and gave us a free slider. The sliders were good. I was a big fan of the fries! Especially with the jalepeno ketchup. mmgood! Def will be going back for fries!

I'm going to have to come back to this review one day when I have a little more time but Rat's is an overall fantastic restaurant! The food is top notch and the decor is so fun and classy. The service was very, very leisurely which some people won't like, but if you aren't in a rush and truly want to enjoy a nice, relaxing meal this is the place to go.

Arguably the best pizza I have ever slayed. Lombardi's is one of those establishments that if you are walking by, you just have to pop your head in to see what all the fuss is about. There is a sign outside that reads "Best Pizza on the Planet", and if you think for a second that it's tacky or any establishment could write this, they then have an actual plaque stating that the location has been declared a national historic and legendary pizzeria by PMQ magazine and the New York Pizza show...ANDD been indicted into the Pizza Hall of Fame....ANDDDD recognized as New York's first pizzeria!! How could you not enter this pizzeria for a pie? Considering my mates and I just ate brunch we all just wanted to sample a slice, so, we ordered a large 'zah' with Rosa Grande Pepperoni and I opted for a side of anchovies. From the first bite it was hard to assess if this really was the best Pizza in NYC and possibly the best I'd ever had. As the pie cooled down, it soon became clear that this was indeed an exceptional pizza. It was seasoned perfectly, blistered crusts, scattered toppings and thin as ever. Truly a remarkable pizza...Best I'd ever had? I'd have to eat there a few more times to determine that, but definitely way up there. This is a must if you go to NYC, it's affordable, filling and in the beautiful district of Soho. A must.

I enjoy coming here when I cant decide what I want to eat in the area. The crabmeat soup dumplings are really good. I also love the scallion pancakes because they are super crispy and i love the sweet dipping sauce. My sister and I always love to order the chicken pan fried noodles because its pretty big. That dish is best eaten there because the noodles get soft pretty quick. I personally really enjoy the braised noodles with scallions and pork chop. Its very flavorful compared the other braised noodles. My friend order the braised noodles with beef and it was very plain while the pork chop one was very tasty. I have also had the Noodles with meat sauce. It was surprisingly small and pretty salty. My friend had the Shanghai lo mein which they recommended and it was surprisingly good, but maybe a tad greasy. Overall, I did enjoy eating here and I definitely would come back for mainly the crabmeat soup dumplings, scallion pancakes, pan fried noodles and the porkchop braised noodles.

As others have said, go for the Korean food. The stone pot bibimbap is freaking addictive, I'm dreaming about it as I type this. Don't be afraid of the raw egg on top, by the time you toss it around in the hot stone bowl it's fully cooked. The assortment of condiment dishes that come with the Korean items are a joy unto themselves (kimchi!). I don't usually order the same thing every time when I go to a restaurant, but this place is one of those few exceptions.

AWESOME THAI FOOD! Probably the best I have ever had. Anytime I am in the Paramus, NJ area for work we go here. The decorations are really neat, its a great atmopshere. They work with you if you have food allergies as well.
You can find just about any type of cuisine. The food is great.

This was my first experience at Devil's Alley.  It was neither bad nor good, but provided a nice relaxing environment for us to enjoy our food.  The ambiance here is probably what this restaurant has going for it.  Low lighting, fireplace upstairs, and a loud bustle makes this a good place to hang out with friends for drinks or dinner. The food is okay, I'd say your average bar/pub type fare. The service the night i was there was sub par.  The server was inattentive and we had to be on the lookout for her to flag her down so that we could get more water and ketchup for the table.  Anyway, could just be one bad server or one bad night for the server, so overall i wouldn't say that changes my impression of the place.  Just fyi for those scanning the reviews and seeing lots of the same comments!

Greek Lady has the ultimate trifecta Cheap, Tasty and Fresh. I'll add one more on there, they deliver in like 15-30 minutes almost ALL the time. I've been here to sit down with friends and ordered to my house and the quality is always consistently great comes out hot and fresh. Good lettuce on your gyro, hot off the spit that you can see through their glass kitchen. The gyros are what we all come here for. I only buy the lamb. The tzatziki Sauce is wonderful. I've also gotten salads as well as spanikopeta, and I have even ordered breakast from them. The meals are always filling and I never regret ordering from the Greek lady. If the desserts aren't sold out GET ONE. Every dessert I've had from these guys is amazing though if you order after dark they'll tell you they're all sold out since they must be making them in house. Whenever friends of mine visit from out of town and want something light and yummy, I take them here.
Great place.  Wonderful, friendly service.  Fun system in place for ordering and seating.  We never felt rushed or like a nuisance.  Overall, a fun, cool place.

I randomly stumbled in here while looking for a place to rest my shopping weary feet and just have a drink w/o having to order a full blown dinner.  I LOVE LOVE LOVED this place!  It's the closest thing so far that I've found to reliving the glory days of Oktoberfest in Munich.  They have Hofbrau on tap, yummy warm pretzels with sweet mustard.   Forgot that weisswurst was that whitish breakfast sausage that I didn't like when I was in germany and I didn't like it here either.  But everything else was so phenomenal and the owner Andrew and his wife are both so friendly and hospitable. I wish there was a place like this in LA, I'd be there like every other night:  small, cozy, a place to have a drink and talk about life with friends, and have a bite or two if inspiration strikes.  There were a lot of interesting sounding things on the menu that I didn't get to try, but hopefully I will next time I'm in nyc :)
Great, I love this pizza!!!!  Just pricey.

WOW. Small place in the middle of nowhere on 10th Ave. I cozied up to the bar, ordered a beer and looked over the lunch menu. The lomito sandwich. Never even heard of it before (which shouldn't have surprised me considering my lack of familiarity with South American food). Steak, Ham, Fried Egg, Cheese. Yes, yes, yes, and yes. Had a spinach empanada to start which was solid and then came that sandwich. El lomito completo fue increíble. Can't wait to go back for dinner.

This review is for breakfast during the week + - toasted baguette sandwich with bacon, fontina, arugula, thyme, was pretty big and satiating - Although I do like the fact that their OJ is fresh squeezed, it was kind of acidic tasting - - Temperature; this place is freezing. The wife had to eat in a coat- - Poached egg and salmon was kind of small; the wife seemed to enjoy it - Poached egg and salmon on toast was pretty burnt; idk if that was intentional - Price; $35 (incl tip) for two breakfast sandwiches and two OJs seems kind of pricey OVERALL - I wouldn't recommend this place for breakfast unless you're coming around to linger

Upon entering, you can feel the pretentious young entrepreneur vibe from the ladies with the very short dresses to the men with the tailored suits.  So, you'd think the place was like beyond amazing, right?  Why would all of those people flock over there? I have no idea! I'm Dominican, and the main courses were as on point as a broken pencil! Soooo bland! Bland on the Water! The arepa appetizer and the chocolate cake dessert are what caused me to give this place 2 stars.  Perhaps, in trying to cater to different tastes, they failed to give their food some taste.  Such an expensive disappointment!

I went to Five Leaves for the first time this past weekend. I'm on a mission to try Williamsburg brunch places since I live in the hood and haven't really! I got there around noon, but was not seated until about 12:45. A 45 minute wait is pretty long, but then again, this is brunch time so no surprises for long waits. There is a to-go coffee bar, which is great when you're waiting out in the cold. I ordered a flat white, my recent Aussie obsession, and was delighted when they were able to make it especially since it was an off menu item. I've had a few flat whites in the city now, and I would say this one is on the stronger side. It was $4. The interior of the restaurant was a bit rustic, otherwise known as my favorite type of décor. I ordered the duck pot pie and truffle fries and my friends ordered the mushroom toast. The waiting time for the food was a bit long for the pot pie, but that is understandable since those take time to bake in the oven. I thought the pot pie was alright, I expected it to be a bit creamier, but it was a bit more on the solid side. I can't really think of the word to describe it, this is probably not going to be the most appetizing imagery, but think of the texture kind of like canned tuna. On top of the pot pie, it was probably more of a biscuit than a puff pastry. I probably would not order it again, since it did not meet my expectations. The fries were quite good. Not too oily, and it was very hot. You can tell they did just make it. I tried a piece of the mushroom toast, and it tasted quite lovely. I would definitely come back here again for the ambiance and try some of the other items on the menu.

Like Hannah K below, I revisited Miya's after a long absence and was so very, very disappointed. They've replaced a lot of their ingredients with more sustainable substitutes, which would be awesome, except that it has seriously diminished the quality of their food. I ordered the new versions of all my old favourites, and they were all terrible. Some tasted so bad I couldn't even eat them. I was so looking forward to coming back, and was SO sad afterwards.

Very Japanese style ramen. The price is alright and the taste is also good. If you're in the area and in the mood for ramen it's a good place, but not extraordinary at all. If you go for dinner there is usually wait time, but personally I'd just go for lunch and get in and out.
Very delish! We walked all the way there thru soho just to get to this pizza place! And let me tell you.....THE BEST PIZZA EVER!!! You MUST go!!
Best Mexican food in Bayonne - The guac and chips are awesome. Only downside would be the rice and beans that come as sides for a lot meals

Second time here.  Very friendly staff and food is good.  They need to expand the menu for more choices but solid local place to go . Pizza and wings are very tasty . This time I had veal parm hero . Very good and good prices I will be back
Do not come here. They have a grade pending due to live roaches and vermin.

Fantastic Tapas Bar.  It is a small restaurant which does not have the capacity for big groups.  It is an intimate dining setting, with close tables and a very friendly staff.  We went on a Friday night and had to wait, but they were very nice about the wait and right on point with the time estimate.   Their menu consists of a variety of dishes with great flavor and a fantastic variety.  The Sangria was fantastic with a pitcher at only $23! (Which is a deal in New York).  It was a romantic dinner, the food was great, the service was on point and the atmosphere was fun.  A definite must for Tapas and Sangria!

Okay, the white sauce is good, it's worth the wait. I get it. But there are two other carts owned by the same people serving the SAME food with NO LINE within easy walking distance. Just look for the signature 53rd and 6th Yellow t-shirts on the other street corners if you're skeptical, but the stuff is trucked in from the same place to all three locations. But hey, if waiting in line is half the fun for you, or you're so drunk the words on the Yellow t-shirts are swimming before your eyes, then don't let me stand in your way. In fact, please stay in line and sober up while I go get me a plate of delicious food from around the corner. ;)

The two stars doesn't mean this is a bad place.  It means that I just didn't really like it.  I wanted to- I was really down for the idea of a year round rooftop bar, so when the Groupon came around, I figured that was the perfect opportunity to check it out. As other reviewers have mentioned, this is an upscale-ish place in the center of Glastonbury.  I can enjoy classy as much as my beloved dive bar, so I knew what I was in for.  But there was a vibe I couldn't quite put my finger on, but was not into.  Also, the prices are very high considering what you get.  I know, when you're in a nice place, you pay a little more for the ambience and service, and I'm sure Rooftop 120 feels justified in charging a more because of the rooftop location.  But.... what are we really getting a view of from up there?  The parking lot?  Rooftops are cool, but sitting up on theirs just didn't really feel that exciting. As for positives, our hostess and waitress were both very nice and efficient.  I liked the wrap around booths, and the throw pillows were a nice touch.  My $12.95 martini was quite good, and although the beer list wasn't that interesting, the prices weren't that bad.  I can definitely see why people get into this place.  But honestly, I've had better in West Hartford center- places just as nice, with better value for food and drink.  I'm thinking of one place in Blueblack who does a nice cheese plate for $10, while the one I ordered at Rooftop was tiny and $5 more. Bottom line- I think there are better places to spend your money if you feel like doing it up, but I guess I can understand the appeal here, especially if you go during happy hour.

I only tried the wonton soup, too. But wow. Compared to the ones made in Chicago, this one tops them all! The wonton are HUGE, FILLED with shrimp. The wonton noodles were good, too. SO worth it for $3!

Expectations were set high with a three-hour wait. Our party of four was seated at a six top booth with two inches space between the tables and bar stools added to make it seat eight. When the next four top was seated we joked with them about our proximity. Started with Devils on Horseback and bruetta.  Both were good. Was a little surprised at the tiny cheese serving for the price, but impressed with the flavor with the beans. By the time our entrees arrived we were all sweating in our crowded booth.  We realized we were luckier than the poor table with their back close to the bar getting hit by everyone walking by and closer to the loud annoying guys sitting at the bar. The two guys in our party separately went to the unisex bathroom and were hard-pressed to decide if it was better than a Texas porta potty in August.  They said it was cleaner, but melt-your-face hot and amazingly small. Entrees were fine. Service was fine.  We had planned on dessert, but were ready to leave the uncomfortable hot table and sprinted to the door when the check was paid. I think I might have loved this place if the wait was 45 min and the dining experience was reasonably comfortable. As it is, I say skip it.

Well I must say I was expecting much better food than what I got reading some of the previous reviews. I had the shrimp creole gumbo(appetizer) and the skirt steak(entree).  All I can say is the appetizer was alot better than the entree and I haven't had gumbo in a long time!  The green sauce they put on the steak I didn't care for(strike #1) so I asked for A1 sauce and was told they don't have any steak sauce only ketchup & hot sauce (strike #2) and I asked if I could substitute the potatoes that the dish comes with for fries. I know it's all the same to most people but I like fries better, so anyway I was told I couldn't substitute although they don't have that disclaimer printed on they're menu(strike #3). And the only reason I'm giving them 2 stars is because the service was good and so was the gumbo. BTW dont order the mardi gras drink unless you like your drinks extra sweet and no buzz at all!!

North Third has great drinks and great food. It is a semi-regular spot for my wife and I and our friends. My wife loves the brunch and swears it's the best place to get a bowl of tomato soup. Their margherita pizza was an unexpected delight. And we usually don't pass up the edamame. As someone that doesn't prefer parking downtown or taking the train, I like the location too. And I would be amiss if I did not compliment their service. Give it a shot!

I really want to give this place more stars for service, but my overall experience here was terrible, and I won't be returning. I came on a Saturday morning and wanted to enjoy a nice breakfast by myself. The line to be seated was long, but it kept moving. However, I didn't know it would take twenty minutes for a table for ONE. Several people of two were seated before me and I didn't appreciate that at all. The host kept making sure that I would be seated in two minutes, but he literally said that every five minutes. The only good thing about this place is the owner, who seems to have a lot of passion for his restaurant. He was very welcoming and made sure that I was ok. When I was served, it seemed like I was being rushed to get out and let another group get seated. I ordered pancakes which was OK, pork sausage which was harder than a rock, and eggs over easy which was a little over done for my taste. Finally, they don't take cards, but they don't even have a sign that says cash only!!! I should've just walked out without paying instead of walking all over Washington ave to find an ATM.

Really freakin' HOT indoors, and outdoors, on a sunny day you'll have to deal with the beaming sun. But in the evening it's a nice and chill spot. The drinks are okay and the food is just as good as their SoHo location. DELICIOUS GRILLED CORN. It's a real friendly low-key cool peeps type place, definitely a good look. Wish it was in my hood. Points for being an eco-friendly, solar powered establishment.

I've been itching to come here ever since I moved into the hood. Crepes.. and alcohol?! Y'know, just maybe a few of my favorite things.. I was slightly concerned at first due to the very mixed reviews on Yelp, but I personally found it to be pretty good. I shared a dessert crepe (~$8 for three topping choices; $1 for each add'l topping), and ordered two beers for a grand total of less than $20. Prices are definitely reasonable, especially since the crepe was rather massive. Service was nice and fast, as well. However, the interior is probably not ideal for a first date. I guess there's something cute about having to share a candle in order to read the menu five inches from my face, but I'm willing to bet that not everyone would be into that. Overall a very dimly lit space, and also pretty loud. Would come back again, because really, what other bar around here serves crepes? :)

I have been to Marrakesh a couple of time now and it is definitely one of my favorite spot in Philly. I know that anytime I have out of town people coming to visit me, I will try to bring them there. Let me start me the ambiance. The place is located in a small alley near South Street and you have to knock on the door to get in (kind of freaky when it is your first time. I would recommend making a reservation as they can get a lot of people and the restaurant is not that big. I have never been in Egypt so I cannot tell if it could be an Egyptian restaurant but it sure looks very different and original. The service is great and I like that they bring some entertainment to your meal during the week end. Now to the food. Oh MY GOD! It is so much delicious food that even if you are full and you feel you are not going to be able to stand anymore, you still keep on eating! My favorite is the bastilla. It is just amazing but I also love the platter with eggplants, carrots and cucumber/tomatoes salad and the honey almond stewed lamb. Again everything is delicious but if I had to choose three, these would be my choice. You can read on other reviews about the menu so I will spare you the details but I can't emphasize enough on the quality and quantity of food provided. The place is BYO and the meal is $25 per person 9not including tips and taxes) which I find very cheap given the amount and quantity of food you get.

I never ever write reviews but I'm going to have to for this one. First of all, I'm not going to be biased about the food at all because of my experience with the people here - it's good. Food alone I would probably give a 3.5 to 4: Safe bet for picky eaters, very straightforward, well-cooked but not "unique" per say. BUT my meal here was ruined completely by the waiters here, and with that being said, I have to downgrade my raiting to a 1. There are tonnes of restaurants that have good food AND good service, don't settle for just one of the two; they are not trade offs. I have never experienced such snarky comments from waiters in my entire life. This old guy (beware of the angry Santa if you do come here) literally barged into our conversation, so that he can offend me personally on a topic that is irrelevant to him. And then when the bill came and we wanted to split it amongst cards and cash, he complained to us about it. I mean, are you seriously complaining about getting paid? You're a waiter, and we pay you in tip; don't be a smart ass as if you own the place. One day the god awful service here is going to get this restaurant a bad reputation (and from reading this reviews it already has), or worse, end what could be a successful business. To whoever the owner is, I think it's time to get some new faces and clean out these cocky guys who do not grasp the point of the service industry. Fire these waiters who will one day close down this restaurant. I'm not the only person who feels this way - other reviewers on here would also agree.
Fantastic Sunday night bar. Ambiance is great. Live acoustic music and great food.

Food (5/5)   Decor (1/5)   Service (1/5) That doesn't actually average to 4 stars, but it's a bit hard to overlook the fact that the dumplings here are REALLY good.  This isn't a place you go on a date.  It's not a place you take your parents (as they might be appalled by the sanitation).  And it might not even be a place you would take your friends from out of town (unless they're super cheap and love dumplings).  It's a place you go to take out (yes, take out as eating in the cramped 10ft x 10ft space filled with hungry people waiting for their dumplings is not a very enjoyable experience) delicious, mouth watering dumplings to eat elsewhere--maybe on the street a couple blocks over where it doesn't smell quite as bad.  So forget the fact that the guy at the counter isn't exactly patient (though speaking Chinese helps) and that the restaurant looks like a hole in the wall transplanted directly from Mother China.  The dumplings are really good and come at the dirt cheap price of 4 for $1.  These are not your mother's dumplings either.  These are jumbo dumplings and 8 is a pretty large meal for me.  Or better yet, buy their frozen dumplings at the even cheaper price of 50 for $9.  Take them home and cook/eat them at your leisure in the comfort of your own apartment.

I've eaten the Eggs Florentine and the Vanilla Infused French Toast. The Florentine was bland and flavorless (although the potatoes it comes with were not bad). The French Toast was soggy, not particularly tasteful, and there was no "vanilla infusion" to be tasted. The syrup was mediocre. I think this restaurant has been overrated; I am sorry that I went there on Yelp!'s recommendation. I would not go again or recommend it to a friend.

My husband and I went here when they opened last year.   The food was delicious.   We finally got back there last night for Caldwell Restaurant Week and had selections from their pre fix menu:  3 tapas and dessert menu for $24.95 I had an egg & potato omelette, chicken empanadas & mussels with wine sauce. All were expertly prepared and the portions were quite large for tapas.  The only thing I would have to say is that the empanadas were a bit salty.   For dessert I had the coconut rice pudding which was slightly warm and melted in my mouth. This is a restaurant not to be missed in Caldwell.   Highly recommended.

Okay, I've seen this place on TV several times and finally was in the area with just enough time to pop in for an early first lunch. They couldn't open right on time as there was a TV crew there filming another special on Hamburgers, but about 11:15 the door swung wide and in we from the forming line poured.  I bellied right up to the bar (and having done my research) and ordered like a regular.......... Check their website to get a few hints. It's just a burger OK?  Well, it's a pretty darn good burger, not over cooked, nice and juicy.  The meat is flavorful so you don't need ketchup, which is strictly verboten.  Part of the 4 stars is the experience and seeing vertical broilers and a system for making burgers that probably has not changed in who knows how long.  The potato salad is served first appetizer style, it's kind of warm (you can tell it was just made) in a paper cup and plastic spoon.......... It's pretty good, highly recommended. Bottom line, I would definitely  go back.

Just your run in the mill pizza place.  Great to grab a quick lunch during your lunch break.  Really good buffalo chicken pizza.   Big slices!  Delivery good be a little better sometimes you have to call several times to get through then delivery could run over an hour.  But all in all, good, decent, cheap!
Hipster doofus vibe.  Had a salami and hot peppers sandwhich nothing else..was good..picnic bench seating..strange.
One of the best burgers out there !!!  Only downside is the wait at times but as long as I expect this, no complaints.  Great atmospheres and location (West Village).
A true gem of a place.    Wonderful staff fantastic food.   It doesn't get any better

Almost turned around as we walked in, when the hostess treated us very rude.  She just did not want to be there and you could feel that.  Maybe she was having a bad day, but come on that's your job, to be friendly and greet folks as they come in.  Glad we stayed, the beer selection was good, impressed with all the organic/natural menu choices.  The spring onion soup was perfect on a cold drizzly afternoon.  We were sitting close to the back of the front room by the kitchen and was able to chat with the chefs a bit, they were super nice and funny.  It looked like they enjoyed what they were doing which in my opinion is important when preparing food.  We were limited to the bar menu so I would be interested to try this place for dinner, just hope its a different hostess or her attitude has changed.
Everything is served family style.  The food is excellent and the price is reasonable.  A OK.....

NO. way too crowded all the time, food is ok, things are pricey, but i don't really care. I can avoid it or just not buy anything, however, when i chose to spend the money, service turned out to be horrible. What we experienced couldn't even be categorized as "service". It was an angry woman at the panini / sandwich station yelling at me and my friend and continuing bitching about it with the rest of the panini-making staff and yelling into the air while swinging her arms and rolling her eyes like a manic. We both ordered their at-least-4-italian-word-long sandwiches. Given the chaotic line and crowd constantly pushing forward, we didn't quite have enough time to decide and remember the sandwich names, so we just picked whatever looked good in the display box. At the serving point, this woman turned around with a bagged sandwich and said Prochetta or something. We asked if it was the 2nd one from the end of their display box? While confirming on the menu to see if it is indeed what we ordered, due to a chaotic mess at the paying point and many people waiting for different stuff. Instead of doing her job, she just started screaming back to her staff while facing us, as IF we didn't understand English.  "What the hell? they don't even know what they ordered... who ordered this?" (kitchen staff pointed at us, then she continued) Yah and they're just fucking standing around. (threw the sandwich on the counter and continued cursing) My friend and I were so traumatized by the whole nerve-wrecking line process we couldn't even react to that extreme rudeness! like many reviews said, a totally over-rated place. Of course they wouldn't care, they've got all those one-time tourists traffic to rip off from. Service is a key that I value heavily. This place is full of people who don't know the meaning of it. That's it for me. never spending any money there again.
Great original food , very nice veriaty and delicate flavors. Recommend the oodon soup which is huge and great especially on a cold day

Excellent place! I was hangin' in Philly (near Old Town) on a Sunday night and was looking for a casual place to drain a few beers and eat some good food (not typical bar slop).  I found NM on Yelp and thought I'd give it a try - good call! I sat at the bar and instantly struck up a conversation with Evan the bartender - super friendly!  As it turns out, his buddies from California showed up and we spent the next few hours tippin' pints, bullshitting and having a good time. Since I did not want to wake up with a hangover, dinner had to happen... Veggie burger - whoa!  This was NOT your typical frozen Garden Burger (I like those, BTW), but a killer veggie burger (must be a kick-ass house recipe!) In all, I had a GREAT time.  I loved the vibe, service, food and drink.  No doubt here... 5 stars!

As the new kid on the block, Monument Lane does a good job of landing itself in the consideration set, but what that set actually is (comfort food?  gastropub?  new American?) or how Monument plans to distinguish itself from the competition remains to be seen. My friend and I stopped in for an early dinner a week after the restaurant opened its doors.  Upon first glance, Monument definitely has the typical West Village, cozy, farm-to-table decor down (accompanied by the requisite servers in plaid shirts), and the service was pretty good.  Monument also seems to welcome feedback as they present your bill in a little notebook where guests can leave comments/doodles; hopefully the staff actually focuses on the comments and not the doodles. We started our meal with the whole wheat pretzels with gouda dip (an appetizer I don't see very often; liked the dip).  We then moved on to fresh ricotta fennel with lemon and grilled half artichoke (I was a fan of both) and ended with the spice-crusted lamb sirlion with rosemary barley and English peas (very satisfying, loved the barley). So while the food itself was a rare 4 for 4 for me, my memory of Monument Lane is unfortunately dominated by two incidents: our server telling us that their tap water is thrice-distilled and that they couldn't offer the dessert we wanted because the chef wasn't satisfied with the day's batch of it.  Yes, there is such a thing as TMI. I have Monument Lane on my list of restaurants to revisit once they've figured out what direction they want to push in and what's actually worth focusing on.

Go here and eat. I've uploaded a photo of the BBQ oyster. I will be attempting to recreate the duck and Boursin fritter for the rest of my life. The patio is small but charming, and if there's one place where NYC is more pleasant than in the summer, it's Nawlins. And hah, the L train is actually more pleasant than air travel these days. So yeah, for the time that Tchoup Shop is open, go here and eat.

Dinner for 2, friday Age dashi tofu Udonsuki Tempura a roll of some sort All delicious. Udonsuki is meant to be shared, full as I was, I didn't suffer finishing it.  Piping hot, will steam your clothes, and dominate the table if you're at a 2top. Age dashi tofu had an initial crunch that's so elusive, not a chewy blanket face down in the sauce. Tempura, bright and crisp, great flavor, clean oil. Service Gracious and unhurrying. Between the undonsuki tableside and the timing of delicate, fried dishes arriving at their peak, you can feel the level of attention. Spare and well divided space that balances openness and privacy and intimacy.  This does not read as well from the front/entry as it does from being seated at the tables.

After all the opinions about Minetta it was a must go on this trip. The place has a classic old school feel. We made reservations and recommend you do the same. The place was packed but it was friday. The service was great. Very nice and helpful. Really added to the whole experience. We split everything starting with a pork belly app. Thats was just enough for 3 of us. Really rich and buttery, which was just the beginning of this theme. Then the black label burger which was one of the best ever. Great char. But the winner was the steak for 2. This could have easily fed 4. It was rich and every bite was tasty. Also came with two huge racks of bone marrow. This was unreal. Most and best steak I have ever had and damn near passed out afterwards. Definately a last meal on earth type of feast.
Nice spot for a drink, but very disappointing kitchen. The strip steak, mussels, Caesar salad, and flat bread were all disappointing.

I must say it is the best brunch on the Upper West Side.... and not only because its all you can drink sangria! hehe I have been there for brunch 3 times and dinner once. Twice at brunch we sat in the bar area.. (get there before 12 if you don't make a reservation) But we have met some of the best people sitting in this area! I prefer it over the regular seating! But be patient. They get super busy so drinks and food can run a little slow. The food and staff are always wonderful!

I came here for lunch with my friend and we were sitting around for 20 minutes wondering what was taking so long. It turns out the waitress forgot to place the order with the kitchen! I wasn't thrilled given that I had to be back in the office soon. Eventually the food came out and they gave us each a free glass of watermelon juice because of what happened. My friend also found a piece of hair in her food. I'm not sure if I'll be coming back but the restaurant decor is beautiful.
They seriously give you more fries than you can eat: order 1 regular as you go.  You can always order more! The Poutin was well recieved by another person in the group.

Love this place! Sushi/ sashimi is always fresh and creative. They have the classics as well as delicious innovative culinary delights! The place is neighborhood and local and great prices. I recently moved to the area from nyc (and am a foodie) and can say that this is one of my favorite sushi places. Owner is helpful and friendly. I love the mango mingo roll and the naruto special roll. Mmmm! I come here nearly once a week and its always been a great experience.

This review is for the sushi, NOT the hibachi, which I suspect is better. Though the restaurant is classy looking, our experience was not so good.  Ordered the tamago (egg omelette sushi), as this is often a good indicator of their quality and food storage (you don't want to eat at a place where the tamago tastes of fish).  The waitress asked us what that was, even though it was on the menu... We were surprised but explained it to her.  Surprisingly or not, when she reappeared, she brought tobiko instead, and not very fresh at that.  I ate a bite of mine, but advised the fella not to eat his because it ha that weird buttery taste of slightly rancid food.  Seriously?  We explained again, and actually did get the tamago on the second try, but it tasted if fish and was not very good.  We also got the sushi for two, which was ok, but I would have preferred one or two fewer pieces and a bowl of miso soup included.  To top it off, we were charged for both the tobiko and the tamago.  Bummer!  For sushi, go to Ichiban in West Caldwell or for rolls go to Sushi Cafe instead.

Took the fam there with an amazon local deal. We were really happy with the food. You can tell the dude has a lot of passion for his food and making it taste great. We got the southwest, smoked chicken, kids burger and blt with chili fries. We ended up absolutely stuffed and happy. Excellent cheesy goodness.

Mother's ruin is great. It's a "default" place for my friends. An AWESOME default. I've only recently ordered food from here and all my friends and I have got to say is: French Onion Grilled Cheese Sandwich. Sodium up my life please. And then let me give you my money for some mezcal dranks. P.S. An order of waffle fries feeds like 27.5 people.

I usually do not rave about any restaurants but I had to write a review for Sanfords. 1.  Customer Service.  We were seated promptly and greeted warmly by the hosts.  We went for dinner at 9pm and the restaurant was busy but not crowded.  Our drinks were served promptly and water was consistently refilled. 2.  Decor/Atmosphere.  Sanford's has developed a perfect blend for the chic and nightlife atmosphere.  Warm colors of the furniture provide the base with the glow of soft lighting to give the nighttime feel.  The front end of the restaurant is open air but the street noise did not affect our dinner.  House music played in the background but at a level that did not have me shouting at my date or straining to hear only 2 ft away. 3.  Menu.  A quick skim of the menu at Sanford's shows a unique take on classic diner favorites and includes a section of its signature dishes. 4.  Food.  I ordered the Crispy Chicken Wrap.  My date had the butternut squash ravioli.  Her ravioli melted in your mouth and had that sensational buttery flavor.  I could've done without the almonds in the cream sauce or maybe had them chopped vs. sliced almonds but nonetheless the flavor complimented the ravioli.  Now the wrap is the reason why I decided to write this review.  The chicken is a panko crusted fried chicken which was made perfectly.  Crispy on the outside while maintaining the juiciness of the chicken breast on the inside.  Usually places pile on the red onions causing the flavor to overpower the rest of the sandwich leaving you wondering if it was an onion sandwich you ordered.  This is not the case with Sanford's.  To top it all off is the house made ranch dressing.  This was the cream on top.  It was so good in fact that I requested extra dressing to bring home with my other half of the sandwich.  This brings me to my final point on the portions which will definitely fill you.  The ravioli is listed as an appetizer but came out as a main course size.

Biggest plus: a scallop crudo which was truly outstanding.  And the wine list which (as many have mentioned) is great. Biggest minus: a pork chop that managed to be both over and under cooked at the same time.  Outside was dry, but it was completely raw near the bone.  And one of the only reasons I order pork chops is to gnaw on the bone!  (I guess since I was there on a first date, maybe it was better that I didn't.)  My date was polite but also didn't like her dish.  I didn't taste it so I won't comment further. This is not a neighborhood lacking in good pork chops, so they should either improve it or take it off the menu.  It was disappointing enough to more than eliminate the pluses I mention above, although I guess you can do alright here if you don't order mains.

It was so worth the hour long wait outside. My friends and I really enjoyed it. They let you pick toppings you want on your pizza. It's $2 for half a pizza and $3 for it on a full pizza...you might as well get it on your entire pizza. It was extremely greasy but that's what made it so good. The cheese is the best part, I think. The staff was pretty cool. Make sure to bring cash. It's CASH ONLY.

Visited with the family (4 children) on a Friday night.  It was very quiet in the restaurant.  We were the first group to sit and only two others say the entire time we were there.  There was a healthy take-out business though.   The restaurant is very clean and nicely decorated. We sat at a large coffee table with a nice sofa and some interesting chairs.   Ordering is at the register. The choices are many.  My wife and I really enjoyed the clam chowder and house salad (mesclun with blue cheese and bacon!).  We each had a panini (Cubano and the Steak).  Both were very good.  The kids had a grilled ham and cheese, pizza and chicken nuggets. The kids food was excellent and $4 each (including drink and side).  What a deal!  Restaurant is BYO and has wine glasses, cork screws, frosted mugs and buckets of ice!   The staff was very nice. Food was brought to the table and tables were bussed.   We find it to be a great place to get a high quality meal at a reasonable price in a comfortable setting.  Will definitely be back!
totto Ramen is good however kinda annoying you can only pay with cash can't really have it more than once a month. but the pork bun is ADDICTING literally could have like 10 of them
I really like the food , but i would appreciate it  if you could  put a Fan , that way doesn't Small ...a Humid inside

Cast Iron Soul is New Haven's best kept secret, in my mind. Most people aren't even aware that New Haven has soul, let alone soul food. Well, as a southern girl hailing from South Carolina, I have strong opinions about my fried chicken, fried okra, cornbread, and BBQ. I have to say that Cast Iron does a remarkable job of bringing the a South to the Northeast. The helpings are plentiful and reasonably priced. For the entree plates and 2 sides, you get the option of fried chicken, pork chops (blackened, fried, or smothered in gravy), fried catfish, whiting, pork ribs, pulled pork BBQ and a selection of true Southern sides (fried okra and Mac n cheese are my favorite). You can choose between small and large plates, but even the 'small' plate is gargantuan and can last at least two meals. The fried chicken is super juicy and crispy the way it should be. I also had the blackened pork chops, which are two thickly sliced cuts perfectly seasoned and drizzled with a chipotle aioli. Next time I'm going to have to try the smothered. The ribs are also super tender and are served in a tomato based sauced. The sweet tea is also delicious and teeth-achingly reminiscent of how they make it back home, served ice cold in a mason glass. If your sides are already not hurting after you finish your main, try the desserts - they're all good, especially the peach cobbler and banana pudding (which they often don't have - so ask when your order everything else). You can also get dessert to go. The first time I ate here was at their old location and they had chicken n waffles, which are my weakness. I wish they would bring them to their new locale on Dixwell in Hamden! The staff are also some of the friendliest people I have ever met. You can tell they cook with love and soul - both of which you can taste in every bite.

Went to the Farm for brunch today. Food was good, but for the portion size, the prices were high. The shock really came ,when we got the bill, at the end of the meal. $3.50, for coffee, REALLY??? Most places include coffee with brunch, but aside from that, I have never paid that price for coffee in Brooklyn. If you want bread with a brunch entree, that doesn't include it (like an omelet, who doesn't give you bread, with eggs) it's an extra $2.00. When we spoke to the manager about the price of coffee (which by the way, is not listed on the menu), he was condescending, which was not necessary at all. When we paid the bill, after asking if we needed change, he didn't even bring back the right amount! Won't be back!!!

Can we say yes? My favorites: - the Southern Comfort is a cornbread waffle topped with catfish and gravy.  Holy smokes is it good - the omlettes are great The people are super sweet and service is great.  They accommodated my large group in their small space with no problem. The only item I would not recommend is the safe sausage, but I don't know if I like sage so it could be personal preference. Enjoy!

This is literally the first yelp review I've ever written - I've never been impressed enough  to bother before now.   Amazing food, gorgeously rustic space with a welcoming atmosphere and attentive and friendly service. The food was beautiful. Quality seasonal ingredients star in a healthy and innovative menu that  follows through in execution. Everything we tasted (most of the menu, because the prices allow or it!) was expertly prepared to showcase the ingredients with thoughtful additions and garnishes that added delightful bursts of flavor and texture to create a truly nuanced dish.

Every time I go to Balthazar I love it. The food, service, ambiance, decoration are perfect. I would especially recommend to go for a nice French breakfast. Yet it is as good as it is for breakfast for other meals of the day. Definitely a must go in NYC.

inexpensive but  very good.  everything I ate here was good.  I loved dumpling!  My friend from Milwaukee read an article about this place in newspaper.  so we came here when he visited.  the place is not big and does not have a lot of tables to eat in, so anticipate some waiting time.

Continuing on my quest for a go-to sushi restaurant, I did a Yelp search for sushi places along my route of errands.  With most places closing for "lunch break" from 3 - 5 p.m., my search brought me closer to home and I ended up at Sake. When I walked in, I was warmly welcome by both the girl and the chef.  They handed me and menu, and asked if it was for here or to go.  I ordered the Fire Cracker Roll, Belleville Roll, Vegetable Roll and the Kanypo Roll.  Yes, when I try out a new sushi place, I like to go all out and try at least three different varieties. I was told to have a seat and she brought every thing to me.  The Belleville was absolutely amazing. I couldn't believe how amazing it was. The perfect combination of all my favorite items - eel, avocado, crab & cucumber. I fell in love and ate three pieces before even trying any of the others. The vegetable roll was ok. But then you couldn't really expect a roll filled with rabbit food to be that interesting, now could you?   The Fire Cracker Roll was my second favorite.  Spicy salmon.  Need I say more?  It was just the perfect amount of spice to not burn the taste buds off my tongue. It will definitely be making it to my 'order again' list, along side the Belleville. The Kanypo was ok. Not a big fan of Japanese squash. I had to try it though.  Now I can never say that I passed on it and wonder what it was like. Finishing my two favorites and almost the other two, I forced myself to move and pay the bill.  While closing out my bill, we made small talk.  I let them know how much I loved the food and would definitely be returning.  The one downfall for some would be that they do not deliver.  However, if you want "FRESH" sushi, you really should get off your bum and eat it if not right then & there at the restaurant, but at least pick it up.  Freshness makes the sushi so much better. I definitely loved the friendly welcome & service I received here and will definitely return.  They made me feel like I was a lifelong customer on my first visit.  A way to my heart besides having amazing choices (which they do) and even more amazing food is fantastic customer service.  They definitely met all my expectations and then some.  I can't believe it has taken me this long to find this little gem, especially since it is right in my very own town.

I was hyped to try this place, but I have to say I prefer Ippudo. This ramen was certainly above average, and worth the 30 min wait we had for lunch. I had the totto chicken paiten ramen while my partner got the miso ramen. The chicken paiten ramen was our favorite. Definitely delish and had a lot of layers of flavor. The veggies, noodles and garnish were all on point. However, we just weren't fans of the miso ramen.... Maybe our palates just weren't wired right or maybe we got a bad batch.... everyone seems to rave about it on yelp, but to be frank- we just thought it tasted slightly weird!! Not off like spoiled or anything, just slightly- not quite right... Anyway, that's why this restaurant gets 4 stars instead of 5. I would still highly suggest checking this place out with their chicken paiten ramen!

Pretty darn good ramen. I wouldn't wax poetic about it; I think there are better ramen spots.. but you really can't go wrong with Ippudo. Both the Tokyo (Roppongi) location and the NYC location are on point. I always leave satisfied. However, along with the popularity comes the crowded nature and wait times. I prefer the ramen at Totto when I'm in need of a fix. Something about the broth there makes me happy.

This changed my standard for comparing all dining experiences. At this quality of food, attentive service (which is salaried! No tipping - Japanese custom), and prices - I cannot fathom how people bother with so many of the overrated places in the city. Every single time I eat here (and it has been well over 10 times), I'm so excited and happy! This is one of the best in NYC. Eat here. Boom!

This is a unique cozy restaurant situated in the middle of Montville that you want to love upon walking in. They do some things very well in providing a relaxing environment, excellent coffee, and offer home baked pies which are 5 stars all around. I was a little disappointed in the food, my hash browns were cold and dry and the burrito was well constructed but it tasted to cheesy and mushy on the inside. The coffee alone is a reason I'll return and I'll give the food a second shot.

Like many of the gems opened in the Essex Street Market, this diminutive booth is well worth a stop.  Boubouki offers a bit of Greek home-cooking, courtesy of Rona Economou's grandmother's recipes. The small menu varies, a mix of savory and sweet baked goods, and salads.  The must-have item is the spanakopita, or spinach pie.  The acclaim for it is deserved.  That triangular slice of pie is blissful, thin layers of flaky, crisp phyllo topping a melded filling of fresh spinach and cheese, savory and perfect.  I've had the privilege of eating Greek homemade spanakopita; this is every bit as good, albeit a different style.  A flatbread topped with feta, tomato, olive oil, and herbs was also well-made, but less impressive.  Quite tempted to try a pear cake; another reason to return. Prices are a bit expensive, but I consider this slice of Greek home-cooking a business worth patronizing, and the prices worth paying.

Service was good. We had the delicious baked clams, calamari and steamed mussels to start. Main dishes we decided on the black linguine with squid, fish, shrimp & mussels, crusted flounder on a bed of spinach and veal chops. All were very tasty and worth going back for. Lastly, I must recommend the Sangria, It was awesome.
You have to try the pizza here. They make it in-house.

Went with a huge group of 20 people and it was great! They kept the wine carafes and amazing food coming. Our favorite was the cumin chicken, as well as the veggie appetixers that you scoop up with pita bread. At the end of the night we were all really stuffed, and couldn't even eat the fruit dessert. The bellydancers were a little sketch too- its such a beautiful dance tradition but do they really need to grind on the guys to get dollars shoved in their skirt? Definitely a detractor, so I'll go back on a weeknight.

whoa whoa whoa! i went back and had their sabich platter. what a great alternative to falafel. a huge layout of hummus, israeli salad, moroccan carrots, fried eggplant, hard-boiled egg and their incredibly fluffy pita. im not crazy about their israeli salad (needs more lemon and salt or something) but the carrots are not to be missed and i layered slices of the egg over eggplant and drizzled some pickled mango chutney on it (part of the trio of sauces that comes with your dish) and it was amazing! again, tight squeeze which can get pretty frustrating, but if you're lucky enough to get a seat it'll pretty much make your day.

The pizza was great, I shared the margharita pizza with my sister but I wish I had gotten my own to eat all by myself. The overall atmosphere was pleasant, and Saraghina is definitely a place both where the family can get together and have a fun meal and two people can have an intimate date by themselves. My only complaint is that while the staff was friendly, they definitely did not cater to their customers' needs during my visit. It took forever for our waiter to even notice we had finished our meal, and only then did he tell us that the place only took cash payments. We did not see any signs or indications that this was the case, and my sister had to leave and get cash from a nearby store. The waiters and waitresses seemed to rush between tables and overall Saraghina seemed very understaffed.

So being from California I am a stickler for some good Mexican food.  I grew up eating authentic Mexican dishes, at home, at least 3 nights a week.  That being said I usually don't love the big Mexican restaurants that mass produce my favorite food, but I do enjoy this place.  The Cantina is a place I like to frequent.  I really enjoy their burritos, they are huge...just like they should be.  The service is always good, no complaints.  I tend to go there when I just can't handle being at the pope.  The decor inside is super cute and if you want a Margarita, try the strawberry its on point!

I wouldn't say this is very authentic Mexican, but it is definitely very good. We ate on the deck which had a very cool atmosphere, high top tables, hanging lights, plants everywhere. My favorite part by far were the drinks.. MASSIVE mojitos made with fresh ingredients. Jose Pistolas is unique and great for a change of pace

1/2 burger and veggie burgers on Monday and Thursday! Taco Tuesday! Pierogie Wednesday! $1 PBR pounders on Friday and Saturday nights! Crafts day and other theme events on Sundays! Tattooed Mom is indeed a bar that gives you an abnormal excuse to be happy everyday of the week! Grant it Sugar Moms does too, But I feel that Tattooed mom does it with less smoke and pretentiousness. It also doesn't do it in a basement and brings out a better crowd. I should have bought that up in the last review. But hanging out with 20 plus of the Yelp crew, eating Unicorn cake, basking in all the incredible figurines and artwork, and encountering an incredible server named Bobby has helped me up my love for Tattooed Mom.

Great food, though a bit pricey. Usually good service. I have ordered for delivery and gone in to eat, and each time the service is relatively quick and reliable. Tonight, we ordered about $75.00 worth of food, and over an hour and half later had seen no sign of its arrival. I called twice, both times someone said they would call the driver and get back to me. No one did. When the driver DID finally show up, there was no excuse as to why he was late and the food was bad. We ended up ordering from another place.

My worst experience ever at Macaroni Grill. I am done with this franchise. Bad service. Cold meal. I don't care attitude. I don't know how they survive!  Such a disappointment only anniversary no less. Manager threw coupons at us for "next time". As if..

The wait doesn't matter. As with all the other reviews, the staff is super friendly, the food is great, and it has a great vibe. There are chairs to sit on while you wait, and we got free coffee, cookies, water, orange slices, strawberries, and lemon pork. Try to get on the patio, its nice out there!

A perfect place to meet up with friends to catch up or to pre game. They have a wide selections of Korean fast food and good selections of beer.  Seating's are plenty but it's first come first serve.  No waiter service.   Sort of like a cafeteria, but with better food(with beers) in a chill environment. And if you don't like that, you have a problem.

Good, not great burritos but you get a lot for your money. Like, a real fucking lot...I got a chicken w/peppers, guac, veggies, etc and it lasted a lunch and a half. It was a little wet and the chicken was pretty meh... overall, this place gets 3 stars for quantity over quality.

Not worth any of the hype or the money.  I ordered the Philadelphia burger, I think I've eaten better burgers at backyard BBQs.  A delicious strawberry milkshake, average sweet potato fries and excellent service.
The standard in upscale.  Great Asian fusion and the presentation is wonderful.  Very busy place.  5 stars.
Crepes, coffee and croissants - the best way to start a Sunday is at this lovely cafe + the staff are fantastic especially with kids!
I have been four times and it has been great....fresh, great display and very reasonably priced.  Great addition to the neighborhood.
Many Options -Great for any tourists to visit or non-tourists -Varieties of Food -Great Atmosphere

This place is solid. The food is badass and the drinks are mesmerizing. True beer flows from the taps. If you land on a live music night, you won't be disappointed (unless you hate live music, in which case, you're lost). Very few homeless-looking kids, and even fewer douchebags. I find Cubana to be, in the words of Trent Reznor, a warm place. I only wish it were closer to where I live. Seems to be quite mellow during the week and quite lively on weekends...Schedule to taste.   PS - Don't listen to the fat guy, a Cuban sandwich and some yucca frites will do your stomach right. If not, you haven't finished your Cuba Libre.

One of my top brunch spots if I'm taking a friend around town. The restaurant is packed with hipsters on the weekends, so get there early or head for one of the two bars to get seating--- first come, first serve.  My fave brunch dish is the egg skillet dish. mmm mmm!

If I'm going to be paying ~$50 for tiny portions, it better be delicious. Such is not the case with Casa Mono. I really don't believe this restaurant is worth all of the hype. Ordered 6 tapas for 3 people. We were given complimentary bread with olive oil. The bread wasn't very soft and definitely was not warm. For the tapas, we first had the razor clams, mackerel, and duck egg. The razor clams were decent, I mostly just tasted oil though. The clams themselves were a bit overcooked too. Nevertheless, a unique dish. The mackerel was tiny and nothing special. The vegetables literally tasted like I was drinking vinegar though. The duck egg was ok. It was just one egg with three pieces of mojama (salted tuna that was REALLY salty). Next came the skirt steak, bone marrow, and quail. These were a much better showing. The skirt steak came with 8 pieces, cooked terrifically and full of flavor. The Romesco sauce was sweet and the onions were a necessary touch. The bone marrow was really sweet, but I enjoyed it. The pickled watermelon served with it tasted like pure vinegar, common theme here. Really a very unique dish, but a TINY portion. The quail was super tasty, but only three tiny pieces here. I doubt I'd come back because of the $15+/tiny tapa. I found myself licking the dishes to get my money's worth even though I was mostly tasting vinegar. But if you find yourself here, I'd recommend just getting 2-3 skirt steaks.

What a fun place to dine... Most were hipsters but there were a fair amount on non-hipsters... Like me.  Liked the feel of the dining area and the eclectic music made it better.  AC/DC, Al Green, the stones all were represented.  The food was outstanding! Had the pot appetizers (which are seasonally rotating) and they were a mousse (portabello mushroom was one) roasted marrow and razor clam "egg salad" all of which were outstanding.  I had the pork chop with goat cheese polenta and maple glazed Apple...to cook a thick chop takes work and they did it very well! Had the cheese cake with mango ice cream...odd mix but it worked! I would have like to see more wine selections but what they had was quality.

Really chill atmosphere, but I wasn't a big fan of the barbecue... maybe I ordered the wrong thing (I had the pulled pork)? I was really excited to check out the food here but it didn't live up to the hype. Great service though!

Every time I go to NY, this is one of the places I need to go.  I was skeptical about their chicken and rice at first.  After waiting 20 minutes in line, I found my crack.  Best $6 I ever spent.  White sauce and the hot sauce = goodness.  I wouldn't go nuts on the hot sauce though.  It burns...   I wonder how much the owner of this cart makes.  Only 5 workers and a cart.  No need to pay rent for a building.  The workers are also very respectable.  Once I was drunk and forgot to get my change, one of the workers went over to me and gave me my change.  A++ customer service.

Pretty good fish and chips place. One might think its a bit  overpriced but the portion of the fish is good and its fried in an awesome "secret" batter.  The portions of the sides cold be  bigger though.   Overall good place to fix you fish n chips craving.

I honestly cannot think of a bad thing to say about Moshulu. It deserves the AAA Four Diamond Rating. Service was professional and knowledgeable about the menu and wine list. The dishes I tried, had a perfect flavor balance. The Fois Gras PBJ with port wine fois gras jus just melted in my mouth and the duck breast with sun dried cherries and almonds was damn near flawless.

Okay, so food was alright, but the service? Horrible! I walked in here to have no one greet me, no one to check on how the food was after it was served, and then had to wait nearly 20 minutes after finishing my food for the bill to come!! Is this normal for this place? Went here twice, each time with terrible experiences

The best dishes here merit four stars, but the food is uneven. The roast chicken entree I had was terrible. Even the dark meat was dry. The breast was so dry that it took two glasses of water to get it down. I know it's only one dish, but plain chicken is really a good test of a kitchen's quality. It's easy to make a bad one because you don't have anything to hide behind -- and this kitchen failed on it. The prices are indeed low by the standards of quality restaurants in NYC, but they achieve those prices by skimping on expensive ingredients like meat and substituting large quantities of rice, potatoes and other starches to fill you up. If you like starches more than meat -- like most of the women I eat with -- that will be fine with you and you'll happily pocket the savings. If you're a meat lover, it's false economy.
Review is only for drinks.  Went to the bar for whiskies and it didn't dissappoint.  Huge selection, helpful bar staff.

This place is fantastic in just about every way!! What a lovely and unexpected find. What I ate: Guacamole - ok it's $12 but WORTH IT. A guy comes out from the back with his guacamole-making cart and prepares it right next to your table. Like actually cuts the avocado open, grinds it in a mortar, mixes ingredients etc. Who does that?! And though it doesn't taste like Gorgonzola, which is what it said on the menu was an ingredient, it was super good! Feeds 4 people, orrrrrr can be shared with 2 really hungry people who haven't eaten all day and are hungover and its already 3pm. Also had "The JC" which is a poblano pepper topped with potatoes topped with 2 sunny side up eggs topped with chorizo topped with sausage topped with bacon topped with a tamale. So much stuff? All so good! Also had the hot chocolate mixed with horchata but that was nothing special. I want to come here everyday. The staff is really inviting and casual, the decor is comfy and the food is so unique. Yay for an exciting, new and fresh kind of food!
Fun ambiance and delicious burgers perfectly cooked! Pie looked delicious but left me a little dissapointed.

My experience here was quite lovely.  My beautiful date and I arrived 30 minutes early, anticitpating a long wait.  To our surprise, we were the 2nd couple there and were promptly seated just after opening.
