Our waitress was attentive, and opened our bottle immediately.  Our pizza was brought to our table surprisingly fast.  It was delicious. Due to there being three in our party, the bill was surprisingly cheap.  Somehow, we weren't charged the corkage fee which was very nice.  Only $4 off but still welcomed. Thank you, Lucali.  I consider myself a fan.

So obviously this week i went to big restaurants only. Got there with 5 friends and order food like crazy, the dishes are huge, classic Italian and so good. Garlic bread i love you. The place is in Times Square, full of tourists and loud people but hey at the end of the day we all love to eat and that was great. Too bad the plates are so big i can't imagine going there alone, maybe for my birthday!!
I love Mexican food but was disappointed with our dinner. Steak tacos were poor to fair at best. Chips and salsa good. What a downer!

This place always has a 30+ minute wait for brunch and I know why - it's the best brunch in Park Slope.  Soooooo yummy.  They have the basics down!  All of the ingredients are fresh, local, organic, and of the best quality.  Even a couple of eggs and bacon will be nicer here than anywhere else in the neighborhood, it's like they put magic in as one of the ingredients. Things I've had and would have again:  the bread basket (seriously, so nice), the 3-eggs and bacon, hibiscus tea, coffee, mimosas (they have fun little twists with different juices and whatnot), pork chop, and pork hash. Very much worth the wait!  And worth checking back a little bit early, sometimes people bail out of their wait list and you can get in sooner.

The Empanadas here are delicious and just right ! I love restaurants that cook their meals in the same taste and caring way, even after years, the flavor does not change. Empanadas are made with corn flour, whole grain or white flour texture. My all time favorite is the platanos maduro con queso/sweet plantains with cheese and the Hawaiian. The cod fish one is also delicious.
very cozy. cute. romantic. take a date
The seafood pasta is unbelievably good! The atmosphere is right on point, is perfect for a date. But the group of customers are much older than I expect.

We stopped here last night for some chocolates. We went here once when it was Chocopologie with the lamest selection of chocolates/desserts (i.e. they were out of everything). Since opening as Chocolat Maya, the place looks nicer, less of a mish mash, and nice seating (though cramped, but that's just a fault of the layout and size of the space). They had an attractive selection of interesting chocolates which were all labeled and included the norms (caramel, truffles, mint) but other ingredients like balsamic and chipotle. We each had 3 and they were quite tasty (total bill for 6 chocolates was $9 which seemed typical). The server was busy, but friendly. The place also serves drinks which is pretty cool, though we didn't order any. The front case that had some cakes and macarons was dim and didn't look as appealing as the selection of chocolates which were up in front of glass and easily visible. I'd go again for another selection of chocolates.

In the Rittenhouse area, Dolce Carini is definitely one of the better pizzerias if you're looking for delivery or pizza by the slice, though from previous experience, the Sicilian pies aren't that great. Mega Fries [$6.90] Bacon, cheddar, mozzarella If you're going full-on heart-clog, try their mega fries. Creamy whiz, tons of mozzarella, and crispy bits of bacon was interspersed throughout the well-seasoned fries. Be sure to have your Lipitor prescription on standby. Eggplant Parmigiana Sandwich [$7.50] Fresh, crusty bread was filled with oven-roasted eggplant that wasn't overly breaded. Mozzarella covered it all, with a tart marinara dressing on top. Not bad. Tomato White Pizza [$17.15] Dolce Carini being a pizzeria, I had to order some. Looking for creamy garlic and cheese flavors, I went with a white pie. This thin-crust pizza was fragrant with garlic and was studded with ripe tomatoes, which lent some acidity to each bite. So if you're in the Rittenhouse area, pop on into Dolce Carini for a few slices and don't hesitate to try their garlic knots or sides.

Ichibantei...I put this on my "to-do" list a year ago but only now did I "happen by" it and went in. So as you can tell by any of the other reviews, this is Japanese "comfort food," meaning lots of savory dishes. My bf and I came here after having a few drinks at Keybar down the street, and "comfort food" always satisfies drunken munchies! I was surprised that it wasn't very busy on this warm Saturday night. It was mostly young couples on dates? We were the only white people being served, which also surprised me.  I enjoyed the chill vibe they had going on... reggae music playing and reggae memorabilia decorating the space. On to the food...the chicken karaage is definitely the highlight! Fried, but still tender and juicy on the inside. The tonkatsu was really good, too. All entrees over $12 come with miso soup, rice, and vegetables, so you get a quite a lot of food! It's not a bad deal at all! Be warned: It's CASH ONLY. Hit that ATM before coming!
Clean and easy to use...

I had my last meal in 2014 there, the service was impeccable. My waitress recommended infused vodka shots and I was even offered a vodka shot with pickle bites when I left. Authentic Ukrainian food and the decor was Russian/ Ukrainian country style. Had ginger, pepper and pickle flavored vodka shots, which were very strong.
Good food great staff just don't be late for your reservation because you will wait :)

I was here more than a year ago, but I don't think I'll ever go back. I was so excited to try this place because I always walked by and it was constantly busy and smelled delicious. But I was so unimpressed. First off, our waitress was so rude that we actually asked for a new one. And we got one, but she wasn't very nice herself. And instead of trying to make our experience a little better, ended up just ignoring us for the most part. To start out we got the El Vez guacamole with some beans and sour cream and tomatoes and all that jazz, and none of us thought it was anything to die for. It was decent, but for the price I expected more. We split the black bean enchiladas and the grilled beef tacos, and I kid you not, both were burned. There's no doubt in my mind that they could have been delicious if they weren't...But we were so fed up that we just got the check [after flagging our waitress down for about 15 minutes] and left. I've talked to a lot of other friends that have gone here and no one else has had this kind of experience...but like I said; for me, once was more than enough. If I were you I'd save your money and go elsewhere.
Officially my new favorite Italian restaurant The food and service is amazing. We tried the tasting menu and it was perfect. Can't wait to go back next week!!

really good brunch-had the chicken BLT-delicious fried chicken, biscuit, perfect bacon, served with cheese grits.  and Husband had really yummy sausage and gravy on biscuit.  Our food took a long time, but the waitress handled it well, apologized and got us a free round of drinks-beer and bloody mary.  the sign of a good operation is how you handle an issue, and they did well.

I came here for an early dinner and drinks with colleagues on a business trip. Service is pretty fast. The place was pretty lively and busy.  Interesting decorations; we were seated next to a bunch of miniature wall figures. I had the chipotle chicken tacos. The portion size was pretty small so try something else or get another order with it if you want a bigger meal. Still, they were very tasty and had a nice mild flavor to them. I'd recommend this place as a casual, lively place to come get a drink and enjoy a relaxed time out.
We tried the Cuban sandwich. It is the best sandwich I've ever had in My life So far. Only 4 stars is given because of the small place.

-1 one star for the person hacking and spitting in the kitchen area in the back. Chinatown is notorious for being dirty but this was too obvious for me to ignore. Otherwise, the fried dumplings are amazing ($3 for 11), especially with the hot chili sauce (more sauce than the chills) and the garlic soy vinegar sauce combo (the non sriracha sauce in the sriracha bottle).  Another thing that I just wanted to note: it was served on a dented metal plate, which made me feel like it was dog food.  Nonetheless...really good. The only dried noodle dish there was the noodle with minced beef ($5.50) that came with a pretty generous serving of bok choy.  From the menu, it's hard to tell what it could be, but for those of you who know Chinese food, it's ja jiang mien.  It's not the best I've ever had, but if you add the garlic soy vinegar sauce and hot chili sauce, it turns out to be pretty amazing! Service is not unfriendly.  CASH ONLY!  I liked the food, but again, the snorting and hacking made me cringe as I was eating.

Always a great goto for lunchtime delivery spot!! With so many options of great empanadas to choose from, u can literally eat there everyday and not have eaten the same thing twice!! I would put the sofrito sauce on my cereal if u let me. Yummyyy! (Gave it 4 stars cause delivery takes a while. 5 on every other aspect tho.)

Come here for drinks with a friend or friends...you can act silly and get drunk and no one cares because most likely they are far more intoxicated or white trash and don't care...its always a fun time random bands and drink specials.. the bartenders are a little slow when its busy but it gets really busy on band nights. The one bartender looks like celine dion lol. Cheap drinks served in old fashion glasses..can't go wrong..pretty good wings too def worth a drop by.

This was our first time going to the Max Brenner in Philly. We've been to the NYC one a couple of times. You can call ahead and put your name down. We originally had one server and another came by and said she's our server instead. Really confused and we weren't sure who to order from. Waitress wasn't very attentive, forgot our water and silverware. Overheard table next to us wasn't satisfied with her service either. Food was on par with the other Max Brenner.

Yes...yes, and yes again. Everytime I come to Smorgasburg the very FIRST thing I do is search for these guys. The triple pork saltena and raspberry soda is to DIE for...literally. I'll just die. That's how good it is. It's slowly baked -- not fried -- and it's like a pork stew inside this fluffy cake. Add some mild hot sauce and cheese and you're done for the day. And let's not get started on the freshest sodas I've EVER had. They make their own, and they are so fragrant and healthy. A top notch thirst quencher. I went there with my dog today and boyfriend and these guys are just so nice. Gave my dog water, had a conversation at their little bar, and even gave me a free soda. Such a great business, great food, and awesome people. I'm coming back guys!

On a summer evening the Continental's rooftop deck has some charm. You can smoke out there, that's for one. The baby trees smattered around the patio give the space a less concrete-boxed in feel (it is, in actuality, pretty boxed-in). I can't speak to the food, since none of it looked all that original or impressive. We each ordered a martini. I asked for mine with three olives and the waiter gave me the option of whether I wanted the lemon rind stuffed olives or the traditional. I asked for two lemon and one regular and he didn't blink twice. The lemon stuffed olives ended up being quite a nice mash up of flavors and textures. All three of us were rather disappointed by the plastic glasses in which our martinis were served. While it wasn't the most expensive drink I've ever bought, at $10 we expected the satisfying clink of glass on glass when we cheersed. Drink was decent, nice and dirty. This is not as 'special' a place as it sells itself, but isn't completely without its charms.

It really is good.  I'm not always a super-thin crust fan.  I don't like charred pizza, and I like a little bit of a pillowy texture.  Lombardi's pizza was neither charred not cracker crisp.  It had just enough pillowy bite to be satisfying.  On top of that, literally, the tomato sauce and mozzarella were really high quality.  You could taste a little bit of Italy in each bite.
really enjoyed our dinner at this fantastic spot; perfect service and ambiance to fulfill any special occasion.  apps, main and dessert were great. the type of place where you can sit all night.

Came here for a girl's night dinner for 4 to kick of the NYE and regroup after the holidays.  The atmosphere was perfect, great music playing, attentive service and a fair amount of space between tables.  We split a delicious bottle of Pinot Noir (although I felt their selection of good wines under $50 was pretty limited) and caught up on life.  The food was good, but not great compared to other NYC fare. We shared: Mushroom ceviche: good but the sauce was slightly vinegary (even for a ceviche), which I don't mind but my companions weren't big fans. Scallops: a popular one with my crew, well-cooked. Sunchoke soup: wish i had a whole bowl to myself, this was great! Chatham cod: well-cooked fish and nice broth and little potato/onion pancake. Ricotta cavatelli: OK but not a standout pasta (I am spoiled by eating at Babbo just last week) I will say that the bread was awesome (rosemary foccacia, sourdough, and a saffron raisin roll).   We had a great time overall and would definitely consider returning, but with all the great restaurants in manhattan, who's got the time?

I went there a couple months ago but I absolutely loved this place! Definitely not your average asian restaurant! The deco is nice and fashion, and the service was good. The food is absolutely delicious, especially the korean BBQ beef. We reordered twice in that dinner! lol My only complain is that this portion for each dish is kinda too small, which could be expensive for people who eat a lot. But it's in the city and a nice place, I would say it's worth the money! :)
The best pizza ever!!! My husband always surprises me with the best thing ever... mushroom and red onions... SOOOOOO GOOD!!!!

Food: Had some appetizers only. Liked the mozzarella and garlic bread alot. Bread was toasted well, nice and crispy. Mozzarella was melted just right, so that it was confined between the bread and not leaking out or anything. Drink: Full bar and low end selections of wine. Macro brews for beer and few craft beers on tap (always a plus). Cocktails aren't weak by any stretch of the imagination but not stiff either. Just in between, which is serviceable for most chicks. Service: Average. Crowd/Ambiance: Crowd and decor has a fell of where old friends come to catch up. Front end of the establishment opens up so you can see the bustling street of 3rd Ave. Spacious place and comfortable enough seating.

Food is decent, but not a big fan of tapas style like here. But I do enjoy watermelon cocktail and swinging (birdnest look alike) chair. A good place to have few interesting cocktails and appetizer. But I wouldn't recommend dinner. Waitstaff was VERY particular about not seating us until everyone was there. My party was missing only one person. (I think it's awful to have people hang out in non-existent lobby when there are LOT of empty tables.

very limited selection of soba. TIGHT seating. cash only. had the hot chicken soba that everyone raved about. i wasnt convinced. and also the cold soba i think with mushrooms. not gonna lie, pretty good. but somehow i was expecting to be blown away by their soba. soba-ya is just as good. maybe i just like traditional soba. that's oretty much all i can say about this restaurant. maybe the lack of personal space is enough for me to not want to go back. i mean if you are a soba fan, you should check it out just to check it out. as for me, i am over hyped restaurants and bars.

I have been a frequent customer for lunch and dinner and have never been disappointed! From the greeting by Rich Tullo to expert courteous waiters, Lou s food is delicious! All around the best New Jersey has to offer in high end Italian food!

Went here on an early Sunday evening. We were promptly seated.  Service was slow, it took them about 15 mins to take our order.  We ordered 2 apps and 2 entrees which the entrees came out almost immediately after the entrees.  No time to breathe at all. We ordered the Spinach dumplings and Golden Triangle?(Ground shrimp and chicken inside a fried wonton).  Both were decent and i've had better.  Note, there were 2 of us and ONE appetizer is more than enough. For entrees, we ordered the basic.  Myself, the Shrimp Pad Thai, and my wife ordered the Pad See Ew.  The Pad Thai was OK, I was excited about what Yelpers said but I found it slightly disappointing.  It was too tangy, too acidic and not sweet enough.  The noodles were cooked well though. My wife thought that the Pad See Ew was good, very light sauce and tasty.  I also ordered the Thai Iced Tea which was delicious and refreshing. We liked the atmosphere and will return for a pre-going out meal.  It seems more like a trendy lounge with Thai food than a Thai restaurant.

Uh oh, I'm hooked! I wrote my original review after one visit but I've been back about five times since! Now that it's warmer there are a few small tables out front which is a big plus. The food is always great and the owner/waiter/cashier is such a nice guy! The other day I had a bangin' iced coffe and on a prior visit got an ice cream cone. Tip:  Although I mentioned previously that the food isn't very spicey, you CAN get some spice on the side which really gives it some punch.

I'm not that impressed.  I've ordered from here once and I've eaten in once with a party of 6.  The food is just ok.  The service was slow and lackluster.  I know we had a table of 6 but it took them 50 minutes to make our food and the waiter hardly came around.  If this is normal then this is not a good place for you to dip out to during a one hour lunch break. Food wise I've had an eggplant and polenta parm and I've tried the shrimp curry.  Both ok but nothing I am dying to go back for.

My boyfriend is a craft beer enthusiast, and I love to eat, so gastropubs are our favorite places to go. We walked in and were seated immediately in the back for which I'm glad because the front of the house was really loud and crowded, but the back is quite secluded and quiet. Service was fast and friendly, but this is about food. Truffle fries were oh so mediocre. I LOVE FRIES. I LOVE TRUFFLES. This did not satisfy either of my cravings. It's more like parmesan fries with a scent of truffle oil. Mussels were off. They smelled off. I didn't even want to dip the bread in the sauce. It was just disappointing. However, my boyfriend enjoyed his alcohol and I enjoyed the ambiance and company.

I love this place but not for dinner. I love the brunch offered here. It has become apart of our family events and for good reason. Each brunch item is made to perfection. The goat cheese omelet is delicious. I gave Buttermilk four stars instead of five because their drink menu is non-existent. They offer this Bloody-Mary thing with an oyster on top WHAT!? YUCK! If that sounds yummy to you then go for it. As for me i would love hot chocolate, orange juice, or a Bellini that doesn't come in a tiny glass. Other than poor drink choices this place is a high recommend.

This is a solid place for your Japanese crepes. The place is small with maybe only a couple of stools near the window to sit. The place gets really crowded so I would just take it to go and not try to stand around for a seat. I tried the Azuki Berries and it reminded me of my favorite crepe in Tokyo. I personally love the red bean and green tea taste together. The green tea custard was also a nice compliment (not too sweet) to the green tea ice cream. The presentation of the crepes is pretty and the window display in the store is nice (just like Japan!).

It's sort of odd that I haven't gotten around to reviewing Silk City until now. Maybe because I quit going there for a while? Anyway, in the interest of more fully yelping my life, here goes. The diner side makes me very happy, especially the maple bacon cakes. Yum! And the hangover helper? It does exactly what its name implies. Gotta love a diner with a full bar too. The club side gets too crowded and sweaty for my taste and the music can be hit or miss, but despite all that I always end up having a good time there.

Inexpensive, delicious, fast. Great for a last minute meal pick-up if you spend your commute wondering "what will I make for dinner tonight?" then remember that you can't, in fact, whip up nachos and a burrito quite like theirs.
Great burgers!

Everything from the atmosphere, the service, the food, and the beer was incredible. The only negative thing I can say is that seating was somewhat cramped and our table of 3 was probably designed for a table of 2. The main highlight of this place was the cask beer. It was sincerely the best beer I've ever had in my life, and why this isn't a normal thing in America is beyond me -- it's an absolute must if you dine here.

3.75. Is it worth and an hour and 20 minute wait during the height of dinner? No. Although this place serves a serious earthy, al dente noodle, flavorful bowl of ramen, I don't necessarily think it's the best around. Is it better than Momofuku? I think it's equal in rating but very different in structure. Is it better than Ippudo? No. Beware: CASH ONLY. There's an ATM at the corner of 52th and 9th if you forget.

5 stars because i can't think of anything they could do better. fries are double-fried well, and they have 20+ sauces. i wouldn't wait in a long line, but when you can slip in and out quickly it makes for a great snack (twss).

First time I was here right after they opened (3 years or so ago). It was a short visit to new york, but i remember going downstairs to this cute little place every morning to get breakfast. Friendly staff, good coffee and food. Really like the interior. Good job, guys!!!

3.5 stars, actually. First of all: best corn ever! I'm a huge fan of corn on the cob with queso blanco, but Cafe Habana clearly puts more effort (and spices) into their ears than any other downtown restaurant. Mine was super spicy this time around, but the afterburn was pleasant. Also, the Tres Marias was a great dish--a corn "bowl" filled with sun-dried tomatoes and goat cheese, with a side of rice and beans. Delicious! My friend got the fish of the day special, which was striped sea bass in a caper sauce with white rice, and it was pretty bland. Just a whole lot of lemon and butter. Some cons? The service was pretty bad. Forget about refills of water or getting your change within 15 minutes after you ask for it. I can tell they're swamped, but wouldn't you want to rush people out the door if that's the case? All in all, I know I'll come back, but only when I'm really craving that sweet, cheesy, and spicy corn on the cob...

This past weekend my husband I celebrated valentines day together at this fine restaurant. The seafood salad is to die for. If you have the chance check it out. Don't valet, we paid $30 for 1 hour parking.

I found Sopranos with my Garmin. I really want  some New York pizza. This didn't remind me of New York. I walked in, and the slices of several pizza varieties were sitting out. I fact, I noticed the slices which I ordered, looked like they'd been sitting out, except what I ordered. There was a pizza with French fries of it...kind of disgusting looking. If I had turned on the next main road, I would've found Tonys pizza. They warmed up my slice of sausage and my broccoli Alfredo. The Alfredo was decent. But the sausage, meh, not so much. I found it difficult to order, cause I don't think they understood me, or maybe the other way around. Anyway, it wasn't like I thought pizza from New Jersey (40 minutes west of N Y C) would be. The eating area, was a typical hole in the wall, and there were people waiting for their order. I won't be back. The pizza slices looked old....so I am still trying to figure out who, this side of N Y C has good pizza. This didn't quite do it for me.

I went there with two friends and thoroughly enjoyed the evening. The place was packed despite it being a rainy Monday, but we were seated promptly for our 8pm reservation. Each of us ordered one appetizer and one entree, and their sweetbread appetizer & escargot appetizers must have been one of the best I've had in the city. Their seafood ceviche, however, was a disappointment both on the plate and on our palates... It's not their specialty, after all. The entrees were very good, but not as memorable as the appetizers, I wished I had ordered two appetizers instead... We were also excited to read great reviews about their desserts, but the two we shared were a bit too sweet and kind of boring. All 3 of us loved their espresso and coffee, as well as the festive atmosphere and great service. Although I prefer to go somewhere more quiet for a date, it's a great place to dine with a group of friends. With a bottle of very tasty and very reasonable red wine (around $40), we spent about $80 per person after tip. Not cheap, but certainly well worth it for their solid performance on food, wine, and service.

This place was AMAZING!  The food was delicious and very affordable - less than $20 for 2 people.  The people are super nice and the pancakes super fluffy.  A must stop for breakfast food when you are in NYC.

Awesome little wine bar that's as authentic as it gets. Most of the food was good but I asked for my steak medium-rare and received it well done. The Pistachio-crusted goat cheese ball is a must, truly one of the best appetizer I've ever had.

Shanghai food is incredible. Had the pork/crab soup dumplings, Shanghai noodles and sesame chicken. The nice cold Tsingtao was the icing on the cake! 5 stars and would give 6 if possible. Coming back soon!

3.5 stars, but be aware that I'm not the biggest burger / meat eater since I tend to like lighter food. Sunday night reservation for 4 at 7:30pm. The inside is not pretentious, very warm feeling (I guess it really is a tavern). The waiter told us to stop looking at yelp. I thought that was funny. Appetizers: Below Average: Veal agnolotti (special): not impressed. The pasta felt undercooked. Veal inside was fine. Average: Bone marrow: was good, but very fatty. Comes with caramelized onions and bread. Good: Oxtail and foie gras terrine: this was great. I like oxtail in general. I had both the black label and the regular burger. The black label burger is much better quality meat. I had both burgers medium rare but the black label was a bit juicier and easier to eat / didn't taste as "fatty." The regular burger was still good, but a bit drier (in comparison). It is also more heavily seasoned; the cheese made it saltier. Overall, if I came back again, I would for sure get the black label burger just because I know I'm not a regular to the restaurant. However, the regular Minetta Burger is still great and on par with a regular high end restaurant burger. It only doesn't sound as great due to comparison with the black label. Dessert: Chocolate mousse: Divine. I wanted to get a souffle but my party was too full. The mousse was great though...slightly "cakey" outside and a slightly thicker (but not too thick) mousse inside.

I spied 3-4 spots in which to stand & enjoy your pizza, but My Pie is really a to-go type of joint. Mozzarella slice ($3.27) was tasty through and though...just enough sauce, stringy cheese, thin, chewy crust. Textures were on point. Perfect with a dusting of garlic powder. My super nice pizza guy cut my slice in thirds, making it more lady-like to walk down the street while stuffing my face with pizza! Not what I'd call a typical NY pizza, but delicious & definitely worth another stop next time I'm in town! Great find!

Lamb, fish, cactus, and steak tacos were consumed. Lamb - delish. Fish - excellent. Cactus - interesting. Worth trying. Steak - spicy as hell. Watch out. They warn you, but take heed! Chips and salsa were ok. It's completely liquid salsa, so if you prefer the chunky style you may not be satisfied. Great prices, but it's pretty loud inside. Nice servers. I'd go back.

Joe's Shanghai Restaurant has won many awards, and currently has three locations (Chinatown, Midtown Manhattan, and Flushing, Queens).  When we ventured to their Chinatown location, we realized just how popular they are. A huge crowd waited outside the packed restaurant. It's rare to see this kind of line outside of weekend brunch time, Shake Shack, Ippudo NY for ramen, or Grimaldi's under the Brooklyn Bridge. New Yorkers don't usually like to wait for their food. It's gotta be really good to be worth the wait. At Joe's Shanghai, they wait. When you're first seated at one of their communal tables, the first thing they ask is if you want the soup dumplings. I guess it takes a bit longer to prepare, so they want to get that order out of the way :) We tried their crab and pork ones (technically called "steamed buns" on the menu). They were so delicious and definitely a fun experience to eat. The pork was juicy and the crab flavor was prevalent throughout the broth. I would have happily placed an additional order for more of these. Definitely next time! We also ordered their scallion pancakes, which were crisp, chewy, flavorful, and just slightly greasy. Definitely a good choice as a starter. As our main dish, we tried their sesame chicken. It was the crispiest sesame chicken I've ever had (which is worth noting as the sauce usually makes it soggy), but it was a bit overcooked and dry on the inside. Fortunately, the sauce was tasty, and steamed white rice and broccoli came free with our meal. Overall, this is a fun spot to enjoy Chinese food in Chinatown (a balance of "real" Chinese food and "American" Chinese food), the prices aren't bad although the wait can be. Definitely worth stopping by to try their fabulous soup dumplings!

This place ROCKS!!!!! The food is so good and the service is great! On our last night in Brooklyn, the rain gods were running amuck but we decided to brave the sheets of rain and wind to get one last good meal. I am so glad we found this place! The ambiance is actually really cozy and romantic. The back room is a great place for a date! We sat in the front to watch the crazy weather. For a starter I order the mango martini- strong, apparently like all drinks served in Brooklyn. Mommy likes! I order the sampler and he ordered the cous cous with chicken. The sampler is for people like me who refuse to settle on 1 craving- a little bit of this, a little bit of that and a LOT of yummy. The tahini and hummus were on point, could have done without the arabic salad but it was so good I made my BF have food envy. His, however, was equally as good. The chicken was SO tender and tasty. We both enjoyed our meals so much we thought about returning the next day for breakfast... A MUST-VISIT!!!!
To be honest don't recall too much about this place. Was satisfied when I went but food wasn't necessarily memorable or what I would seek out in Chinatown.

This review is DECADES overdue! There are two groups of people that I hope read this. Tourists who are visiting our city and the directors for Fox Sports. Every time I watch an Eagles game I want to scream from the rafters REAL PHILADELPHIANS DON'T EAT HERE!!!! For reasons that completely escape me, people are led to believe that Philly people frequent this place. It's even mentioned in a few tourist pamphlets that the city puts out. The guy who used to own the place was a blatant racist.  The radio spots he'd run were nothing short of hate propaganda and the infamous "English Only" sign just screams spend your tourist dollars here.  On top of that the food is mediocre  at best. So for the love of god dp not patronize this place. Instead send your tourist money to Jim's steaks on South St or just follow the real philly people to Tony Luke's

Cute little place not far from Columbus Sq.  Nice atmosphere, great service, varied menu.  I had Senegalese sea bass and it was very nice.  Flavorful, not really spicy.  The owner came out and he's a very smart man and you can tell why the restaurant is doing so well. I hear they are opening  a larger place in harlem.

Food was pretty good.  I was IN LOVE with the ceviche we had; it was the best I ever tasted.  The rest of the tacos were tasty but, all in all, good but not great.  I was surprised over the Michelin stars since I was expecting spectacular but boy did that ceviche make me happy.  It was really good.
We had a RW lunch for 3. This is 2nd time to try their RW lunch. Everything from side breads to dessert was good. Hand made pasta was tasty. Staff was friendly and attentive.
Pros: Super cute!!! Farm-to-table High quality food Cons: Long wait, but what restaurant in NYC doesn't have a wait? Small portions

my favorite restaurant in montclair!! my boyfriend and i use every special occasion as an excuse to go to mesob. the doro tibs (chicken) dish is truly amazing! ingudai tibs (portobello) is also really delicious. every meal comes with 2 veggie sides, and i'm pretty positive i've tried every single one - the best is probably tikil gomen (cabage and potatoes). the ambiance is nice, the staff friendly (but at times a little bit slow or a little bit inattentive, but it definitely doesn't bother me enough to have an unenjoyable experience there). it's somewhat small, so i would make a reservation for a friday or saturday evening during dinner rush, as i probably would for any montclair restaurant on the weekends. the wait can be 1 hour long. byob, so grab a bottle of wine at the liquor store 2 blocks down the street. really cute/different place for a date. also, every friend i've recommended mesob to that has never even had ethiopian food before loved it. all in all... love it love it love it. check out mesob.

This place is awesome for brunch. If you're in the neighborhood and looking for brunch, I definitely think it's much better than Sabrina's down the street. They have great pancakes and crespelles (kind of like paninis), but I always end up getting the huevos rancheros. The pico de gallo and sour cream combination is so tasty, and the chorizo is a perfect amount of spicy and salty, the crispy fried tortillas add a bit of crunch, and the beans add a bit of creaminess to the dish. It's a good, non-pretentious place to head for just a quality brunch.
Both the cheese steak and the freedom fries were not that tasty. I was a bit disappointed.

Had dinner for our one year anniversary here. Overall the place looks a bit dated, but was not inconsistent with my expectations (seemed like a classic-elegance as opposed to super trendy type place). Pros: It's on a boat Lobster bisque (4 stars) California shrimp crunch (4 stars) Cons: Service. I am usually not fussy about service, but for the price that I'm paying at this place (which totaled $160 for two people pre-tip), I expect the following: To not have to ask for plates to be cleared To not have to remind waiter that we already placed our drink orders To not have to ask for a second drink To not have to ask for a knife with my main course (which was then never provided) Waiter to know the menu (was told I was getting 3 scallops but got 4 -- in reality a pleasant surprise, but demonstrated lack of knowledge of dishes) Waiter to scrape away bread crumbs on the table (again, don't normally care about this, but expected it based on price of the restaurant) Besides the two dishes in the Pros section, the rest of the food was mediocre. We got the asparagus side dish (which was basically just steamed asparagus, nothing special but cost $11), the salmon main, and scallops main. The salmon was a bit odd, combining pan seared salmon, smoked salmon, and salmon roe. Nothing outstandingly bad, but just not that great. Scallops were pretty tasty if not a bit oily. The best tasting part about the scallops dish was the gnocchi, of which there were about four (small ones) included in the entire dish. The bathroom was a bit dirty (nothing atrocious, but for $160 per meal I expect a fancy-ass bathroom). Toilet paper not on the roll, paper towels left on the sink, that kind of thing. The service was extremely fast. We arrived at 6:45 (15 minutes early for our reservation) and were finished by 7:30. I would gladly have sacrificed service speed for more attention to details as noted above. Finally, we had the hostess order a cab for us after the meal, after which she promptly left the hostess station, never to return. We heard the phone ringing, twice, luckily assumed this was our cab, and ran out to catch it. The cab was about to leave after having called the restaurant twice to let them know he was there. There are plenty of better places to spend your money in the city, so I would not recommend that you do so here.

Very unimpressive. I came here this weekend for brunch with an old pal, and had heard good things about Henri.  My experience however was so disappointing I'm shocked they even have patrons there. For the record, most of my concerns had to do with the service, although the food, while adequate, was fairly average and hardly worth raving about. Ok so I can understand not swapping out items on a plate, like french fries for home fries, but the waitress practically insisted I order a side of fries in addition to the home fries. Do I have two heads on?   Then, when I wanted a side of toast, she again insisted my only option was to get a baguette with jam. wtf? Can't I just get a side of toast, even after I sad I would happily pay for it.... why be so restrictive with bread? does any of  this makes any sense to anyone? It's not like Henri is a renowned establishment in the city with a celebrity chef. For chrissake, it's a diner in long island city!  And IMO should really be more accommodating to its patrons. No worries, though, I'll never be coming back. An  honest 2 star rating.

I have been here twice and always a perfect meal. This is an BYOB restaurant. There is a wine cellar right next door with reasonably priced wine.  The rest. Is newly renovated in August with a brighter and more trendy feel.  The price for food is also very reasonable given the quality of food and location.
Nice ambience, but the food is a total disaster. My grilled cheese looked terrible and tasted worse. The soup was most likely poured from a Campbell coup can. Don't eat at this craphole dump.
I've always had a fun time here, great beers, bartenders and servers always nice... everything fun until i have to pee and walk up 3 flights.

one of my favorite summer brunch places. amazing back yard, love the dishes, always done well, and on sunday they have banana nutella pancakes! pretty awesome all around. not without hiccups, but the courteous staff and the good vibes compensate for little snafus. happily frequent this cute joint.

If you come hungry, try the pretzel sandwich here. And compliment that with a pint of Southern Tier. Their happy hour isn't slammed with people from here to heaven, so you can get some sweet drink deals if you come before 7!
Homemade guacamole is delicious!

Yes you can find great cheesesteaks in Northern NJ. Parkside is a rather nondescript looking place on Belleville Avenue. But don't let that fool you, the cheesesteaks are very good. The meat is a high quality sirloin, moist and tender. The bread is fantastic, and holds the sandwich together well. Apparently it's sourced from a local bakery. The only slight downside is the bread might be a bit much for the amount of meat that is in the cheesesteak. Still a very good sandwich though. Had some fries on the side and they were basically just fries. Apparently I saw someone order a chicken cheesesteak as well, which I didn't see on the menu, so I guess they serve that too. Def worth checking out.

S+P was a hit for brunch. The burger was tender and juicy, and the egg and bacon gave it the right amount of sinful greasiness. The poached eggs came on a massive, crispy, golden bread slice instead of a puny muffin and were also laden with bacon and hollandaise. The fries come with a blue cheese mayo which is to die for. And I haven't even mentioned they have a DIY Bloody Mary bar. Nuff said on food. Decor and ambiance was also really charming, with the bar up front, tables round the corner, and a big room for dinners/ private event downstairs - place is brand new, so no wear & tear yet. And service was attentive and always on point. we left happy.

My first time there was Saturday the food was delicious. Fried fish and shrimp was so crispy and not over fried and the batter they is wonderful and they have a special hot sauce that they make that is spicy and wonderful.

The first 45 minutes I spent at Jane (before being seated--WITH a reservation) would not warrant a 4 star rating, but the food made up for it. We arrived for our 2 pm brunch reservation at 1:55, and per usual on a Sunday at brunchtime, the crowds were spilling onto the street. Our res was for 4 but only 3 of us ended up making it. After basically elbowing my way to the hostess stand to check in, they asked if our whole party was here (yes), and we were informed that they were running behind, because "people weren't getting up from their tables," and it would be at least 15 minutes before we would be seated. Allright, no big deal. We headed outside and huddled under the awning as it was drizzling. 15 minutes later (now 10 minutes after our reservation time), I went inside to check on the status of our table. The hostess asked if my entire party was here (yes...still), which indicated that she didn't remember/take note of our arrival at all. She said "I would like to say it'll be 10 or 15 more minutes, but it'll probably be longer." Great. Headed back outside, and managed to snag a seat on one of the benches. Overheard 2 different groups talking about how they had been waiting well past their reservation times to be seated as well. After 10 more minutes of waiting, and seeing a group with a 2 pm res get seated before us, we were getting pretty antsy (and hungry!). Then, as if by divine intervention, one of the managers popped his head out of the door and handed us a bowl of fresh glazed doughnuts, saying, "I stole these for you." Seems like he knew we were anxious/annoyed and that was the consolation. Well, there's nothing a little fried dough (and a cute guy, hayyy) can't remedy. We were seated about 10 minutes after that (so...around 40 minutes after our reservation time) and things went smoothly from there, barring our waitress's less-than-enthused (read: OVER IT) attitude. The food: Started with Bloody Marys, which (along with mimosas and a few other drinks) are complementary with a brunch entree order. With entrees at $19 or less, this is a fantastic deal. Especially because the Bloodies are BANGIN. If you like em spicy, don't pass these up. My friend didn't like the taste of her olive, but I hate cocktail olives anyway so I couldn't weigh in. The nutty fruit bread that came in half of the bread basket was fantastic. The white bread on the other half was pretty run-of-the-mill. But the strawberry butter? I'd eat that off a stale piece of wonder bread. Delightful. I got the Salmon Scramble, which sounds like an awesome dance move. It was huge--couldn't have been less than 5 eggs. The smoked salmon, chives, and the bit of mascarpone on top are as good a go-with for eggs as you could want. I went for the rosemary french fries instead of home fries. Crisp and herbaceous. HUGE portions of both. Easily splittable...didn't even look like I touched the food when I was full. I tasted the home fries off my sister-in-law's plate, and they were some of the best I've had. Home fries at brunch can sometimes be a throwaway/plate filler, but these were seasoned well, crisp, not oily, and had thinly sliced caramelized onions throughout. So it's a toss up between these and the fries--can't go wrong with either. All in all, right up there with the best brunch food I've had in the city. And I've been to a LOT of brunches. Make a reservation...and if you have to wait, at least you'll get some doughnuts out of it!
Came back and tried their artichoke pizza. It tastes like cream of spinach soup smeared onto a crispy pita.

Outstandingly fantastic grilled octopus salad! Perfectly done whole fish (lavraki), and some kick-ass cocktails to boost.   Will come here any chance I get. Btw, the place is absolutely spotless. Not even a single water spot on the plates or glasses. I like!

The bagel shop has been making their bagels smaller and smaller . They are very expensive for the size and quality of the bagel . They are very clean but I remember coming here as a kid and getting that bagel you were craving .
The only downside to this restaurant is the one hour wait. But it is well with it. Egg custard to die for. And you know it is legit because have the guests are Japanese.
Nothing special will not go back. Service was painfully slow. Everytime we wanted another drink we had to get up and find the waiter!! Don't sit outside they forget about you then expect a tip.

Totally downgraded to "meh." I've been here about ten times since they've opened 6 months ago, so I speak from continued experience. The food is fine - not great, but fine. It's not the worst in the neighborhood, but I'm always left a little disappointed. They seem not to take care of the little things - like they don't cut sandwich in half if you get takeout. If you eat in, they don't time your meals to come out together (think: hot sandwiches on table at 6:30 and calzones at 6:45.) Clean restaurant, generally not busy, good burgers, decent pizza (better than Plaza) but not good cheesesteak, sadly. BF says, "I CANNOT believe that 'cheesesteak' is in their name - shameful." This happened to me here for the fist time ever - my called-in pizza order not even prepared or in the oven until I arrived to pick it up (I was 5 - 10 minutes late, store was not busy, plenty of staff.) The mistake was not acknowledged - I just had to sit and watch as my pizza was created and cooked while being told, "it's almost done - it's almost ready - just another minute." I would have been totally fine with a simple "oops! we forgot!" - I could have run next door to CVS for milk or something to pass the time - but I was so burned that they made me sit there for 15 minutes that I vowed never to return. Well, two months passed, my irritation cooled, we got a text ad for $5 pizzas and we decided to give it another go for a cheap takeout dinner. Guess what? SAME THING HAPPENED. When I figured it out, I just sat there, so angry that I couldn't say a word. It was an empty restaurant - was totally awkward to just stare at them - and I couldn't wait to get out of there. I just decided to complain by not giving them more of my money - and by downgrading my yelp review. Take that! It's a little sad, because we live and work literally around the corner, eat out 5 - 6 days a week, are patient customers and are regulars at other local restaurants. One particular owner has been there for most of my visits and he seems decent, and the staff is pleasant. But there's just so many other choices, and careless service just drives me crazy.

Me & my wife's go to cart for good tacos. Their tacos are fresh and the meat is well seasoned, their al pastor is excellent & they don't skimp on the pina. The process are great and the guys are friendly.

Carmine's serve very big family style portions, and orders can serve minimum four people. I always get the fried calamari, and I've recently tried the baked clams which is also pretty good! My friends and I also ordered rigatoni with meatballs, and I didn't know their default style of cooking any pasta is al dente. So if you liked your fully cook, let the staff know before they put your order in. Overall a great place to go out to eat with a big group!

All the food is very tasty. We've been here with friends a number of times. Downside is the beer list; 3 good beers is just too little these days. Service is a little hyper for my taste. Spring rolls, dumplings, fried brussels, sliders were all very good. Will bring friends here again.
I'm sure you've read the same thing over and over again in all the other reviews, but the grilled corn is reason enough to go down to Cafe Habana.   Go there, and find out for yourself!
A good day out with a special friend. Perfect place for casual date.

Went to this one twice during our three days' stay in NYC from San Francisco Bay Area. The first time was based on Yelp review. The second time just wanted more great foods, and I ate 10 SLB and other foods. Why SLB is so good? I found that the key is the skin. In other places, the skin broke for a 80% chance, then no soup and no taste. Here, 90% chance it wouldn't break and it can hold the soup and have the good taste.

The cheesesteak and cheese fries are awesome but they're a bit overpriced.  Plus it's difficult to go here without being surrounded by drunks or wackos (at basically any time of day), but that's okay, I'm usually drunk upon arrival as well. It's a little nervewracking to have to specifically order "wit wiz" or however they want you to do it, and they look at you like you have three heads if you fail to recall that drinks are sold at the "next" window. So if you're okay being a drunk idiot who'll pay top dollar for a pretty good cheesesteak, check it out.

Great place! I have now been here twice, and both times I have left happy. The atmosphere is pleasant, the service is great, and most importantly, the food is beyond words! I would recommend the burnt ends, guacamole, macaroni and cheese, and sweet potato wedges. The apple cake (which is free after your meal!) is also really good! I can't wait to go back, especially since they are expanding and recently got their license to serve beer.

balls..eat my balls..i had the 'everything except the kitchen sink salad' with ckn meatballs and mushroom gravy..yes gravy..not a sauce..the salad had some bomb ass cauliflower, beats, arugala, cucumber, and apples. the pork and pesto was good as well..pesto was very tasty..i prefer it over the mushroom..also the vanilla root beer float..was ass kicking..i normally hate root beer but the one they selected is awesome.. it's a MUST eat..its cheap..n it's gooodd

4.5 stars! I got the reuben and it was delicious. The meat was tender and cooked to perfection. The meat was piled on a perfectly toasted bread and the sandwich came with a slice of pickle. There were two sides to the store. There was a side you could order for take out and another side where you could sit down and eat. We went to the side we could sit and eat and I was glad I did because the girl serving us was a delight to talk to. She was so friendly and welcoming. She was so helpful and chatted about things we could do on our day trip to Philly. Sitting there and eating was a great experience in the crowded market as people came and went. Strangers were so friendly as they joked around with us as we ate our food. Great food and great company!

I've been a loyal customer of Posto for years - the pizza (and salads!) is outstanding, the atmosphere is fun and the music is great. However, what keeps me coming back? The staff. They greet you the minute you walk through the door and make you feel welcome. Even on Friday nights (the night on which I most often frequent Posto after a long work week) when the restaurant is packed, they acknowledge you with a big smile and 'hello' the minute you arrive. They offer you something while you wait for a table and they keep you apprised of where you are on the wait list. When they seat you, they are attentive, helpful, friendly and fun. Then they bring you the best pizza, thin crust or otherwise, in town. From the first time I visited Posto, I was won over. I moved out of the neighborhood 4 years ago but still go out of my way to visit this location of the Grupo/Posto/Vezzo family weekly for dinner because it's the best, most inviting, and has the nicest people working there. The owers did a great job putting this place together and I hope the winning combo of food and staff never changes! I love this place.

This place has decent service, but mediocre food. I'd have to highly urge against eating here for anyone who values cleanliness, as there are cockroaches in the kitchen and many few health or sanitation regulations are followed. Also, a friend who ordered food for delivery had to send half of it back because he found a small white worm of some sort in two of the salads. . Most of the negative reviews listed below are very accurate, particularly the portrayal of the management staff. I mean, any place that lets their kitchen end up in that state, is obviously a little off and highly unprofessional. Super overpriced for the quality of food as well. You're better off going to any of the other lovely restaurants in the Montclair area. They may tend to also be on the pricey side, but at least you won't have to fear pests or disgusting germs being part of your meal. Ultimately, I'd have to recommend passing this restaurant up. Otherwise you'll probably regret it.

Valley Shepard Creamery has wonderful fresh mozzarella and roasted tomato sandwiches. I swear there was a pound of cheese on my sammy. This place is just wonderful. We went on a Sunday, and although some places were indeed closed, there was still more than enough going on to slightly overwhelm me.  The high star rating this place has is well deserved.

The "Tentazione" panini at Via Quadronno was the hands-down, absolute best panini I've ever had any where: prosciutto, mozzarella, rucola and shrimp.  The cold breakfast paninis are fantastic as well.   What's more - they make an excellent cafe au lait.  A great choice if you are in the area and looking for a good lunch or a light, european style breakfast.

The Habana Outpost is run by the same people who own Cafe Habana in Soho. The restaurant is super simple and verges on divey. You walk in, order and pay for your drinks and/or food from the counter, get your drinks right away and wait to have your name called from the modified kitchen/trailer out back making the food. The seating is primarily in the large backyard concrete courtyard with lots of tables and umbrellas, but there are also a few booths and a counter inside. As they really don't have air conditioning beyond a fan or two so sitting inside while it's super hot outside isn't any better than just dealing with the heat under an umbrella outside. They've got a few great sounding frozen drinks ($8), but I opted for one of their $2.75 draft beers (in 12oz plastic cups), a great deal considering they were good beer choices. I also got their famed Cuban Sandwich ($7.25). They make theirs with pulled pork, ham, swiss cheese, chipotle mayo, pickles, on a slightly toasted roll. I thought the sandwich was great, the meat was seasoned and cooked perfectly and the slight toasting/pressing of the bread added just the slightest extra warmth and crunch to each bite. The sandwich is the same in the city but they charge $9.75 and give you fries with it. I wouldn't have minded more meat but at the same time I didn't think they skimped. I think the place is really good in most aspects but it's got a few little glitches I wouldn't mind see changing (no napkins by the tables, no easy to find trash cans outside, cash only, cook that didn't know one word of English, pricey frozen drinks, and no AC inside). I'll definitely be back when it's nice out.

Let's get this straight....classic Bánh Mì  is a product of the influence from the French colonialism...therefore firstly it is in a french baguette...not a hogie, not a sub, not on a roll. The bread should be crunchy on the exterior but hollow on the interior. With pork pate and butter as a spread. The meat  consist of various cold cut  from pork with pickled carrots, radish, cucumber, cilantro and for heat hot pepper. So now let's address Banh Mi Saigon...bread...no...its like 13" long!?! Pate...check..pork..uhmm...there are two types of pork but here's there's only one. Pickled carrots and radishes...check. Cucumber & cilantro check. A Vietnamese person anywhere to be found...nope. This is a good sandwich shop which calls it self Banh Mi Saigon but it should be called Banh Mi Hunan. It is close but yet so off on the real deal. As a good cheap lunch sandwich sure but I've had better else where. For those who don't know it would pass as that but for the purest it hardly comes close. While there are some amazing Banh Mi places in Brooklyn(Sunset Park) my search continues for one in the city. So far the closes would be Paris bakery where I actually can order in Vietnamese and Vietnamese people actually do come here and eat.
I finally tried Adrienne's again and still I'm left with a 'mehhh' feeling.  It's good pizza, but I don't really get what people rave about.  It's just thin crust pizza people, relax.

Loved the atmosphere, its upscale but still laid back. Wait staff a little slow Cheese board and the Toast were both excellent Salad and Salmon were both prepared perfectly but nothing special I would go back

This is just a really really cool place. It's basically a pizza museum, and the Chili Garlic Chicken Honey (Federal) Donut pizza slices I had were some of the best of I've ever had. Don't knock it 'til you try it. Extra props for all the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles/Pizza memorabilia.

Food okay, Service Awful.  Okay, so the steak was okay.  Not the best Ive ever had, so to pay $50.00 for a steak with horrible service, I would not want to spend that kind of money.  Afterall, the service is part of your overall experience, and I was not happy.

In New York City, everything comes with a price EXCEPT sparkling water at The Smith.  Yesssss! Recommend: - sitting by the open garage-style windows when it's warm (you get the benefits of still feeling the a/c with a bit of warm air and good people-watching) - pancakes with caramelized bananas - all-you-can-drink sparkling water for FREE

Often quite crowded, and to be honest some places are not that good, and everything is a bit pricey.   General tip do not bother getting any Asian food here, go to Chinatown which is on Arch and Race Streets between 12 and 9th.  Some of the same places but will be cheaper  The jewish deli is good as with a cajun place.  Stay away from the English pub, the food there is not good and overpriced.

Three stars because the people there are very nice otherwise I would have rated them a two. I ordered a simple sandwich, a sausage parm.  I've had them at many places and this is the only place I've had that it's a hybrid sausage parm/sausage peppers & onions. It seems to me they cook one batch for either sandwich, a bit lazy I think.

Went to South Street with some of my friends to look for a new place to grab a bite. As we parked our car, a couple walks by talking about this great place they just went to. I asked them which one were they referring to and said La Fourno. The place is cozy. The service is great!!!! Every item we ordered -- delicious!!!! Truly an Italian restaurant in the heart of South Street. We are definitely coming back to La Fourno with more friends and families.
best turkey rueben ever!!!! love this place

This place is excellent!  At work, we often order our lunch from near-by restaurants and have it delivered.  Being in the heart of busy Rittenhouse, the food is usually overpriced and takes forever to arrive.  A coworker stumbled upon The Quick Fixx lunch specials menu one day online.  I have ordered from here 3 times (always the same exact meal) and every time have been extremely satisfied by the food, the quick deliver, the kindness of the employees and the unbeatable price tag.  Today we ordered and the gentleman delivering returned all the way back to us with the plasticware he had forgotten to throw in the bag.  I always get the Arugula Salad and the Sunchoke flatbread.  I think together with a soda it totals $10.  It usually take me two sitting to eat the whole meal- but the point is it is delicious and fresh and comes highly recommended by me.  I should branch out and try more here.  I think I will and soon!

In the words of the delightful Kelly Clarkson.... What doesn't kill you makes stronger,   Footsteps even lighter Doesn't mean i'm over cause you're gone So in my quest for progress trying to move beyond the wreckage of my failed relationshop, I'm making baby steps.  Therefore, I went to a bar/restaurant in the neighborhood of my old b/f that I always wanted to try.  Naturally I sat with my back to the window so I couldn't see the street, but just being in that neighborhood was a small victory for me. And how lucky was I that they had super sweet waitresses, excellent beer and great food?  I'd say very lucky. Started with a nice flight with some dark and light beers, followed by an Ommegang Abbey Ale.   For food had the western burger, which was delicious (see picture) with bacon, cheese and onion rings.  Plus fries on the side.   This is a sports bar type place but they are very open and have plenty of variety in terms of beer, food and crowd.   I feel stronger for having been here and I'm willing to go back!

Mamma mia! The moment I laid eyes on this corner restaurant, I knew it was a gem - it looks like Tony Soprano is inside, eating, right now. I was not surprised to read about a mob shooting that took place here a few decades back. If that doesn't add to the authenticity, I don't know what does. And it just got better. The room was mostly full, a small dining room with pictures on the mantle and good old tunes playing quietly beneath the pleasantly noisy conversations around us. And our meal was gorgeous, not to mention delicious - great mussels, great eggplant rollatini (I usually don't like eggplant), amazing manicotti and the most beautiful plate of seafood cioppino I've ever seen. We chose from an abundant wine list, and saved room for some of the best tiramisu I've tasted in a long time. But the service - I might go as far as to say that this was the best, most perfectly timed service I've ever had. Our waiter, a middle-aged, mustachioed fellow, never offered his name, but he did time our plates perfectly, left us alone long enough to digest, and even combed our crumbs away. The busboys and water servers were all spot on, too. They really earn their money at this place. This place was just stellar. I look forward to knowing them well enough to ask for the non-shooting section.
This could be a really great place if the waitress had not completely ruined my experience.  She was rude and horrible to deal with.  What a shame, because they have a really nice bar and good food.

twas quite all right... the eel bowl was very good. the ramen was good. got the thick noodles. was happy about that. it wasn't as creamy/oily/salty as the other japanese places i've been. although, i kinda felt weird about paying so much for ramen when i could just be satisfied with an ichiban at home.... (-2 stars for the prices) seemed a little too nice and clean.. and "posh" in there... i like my food dirty and made at places with holes in the wall.... enjoyed it.. but i wouldn't go home raving about this place like mad...

In theory, Pomme Frites should be an awesome place to grab a quick bite, they specialize in only one food, have gigantic portions and offer way more than the standard ketchup as a means of enjoying your fries. However, when you strip away the massive assortment of Mayonnaise Dipping Sauces and the Belgian style interior design, what your left with is only exceptionally oily steak fries that are a multitude more expensive than what you can get at your average fast food joint. Here I ordered a large thing of fries alongside some of the signature Pomegranate Teriyaki and Mango Chutney sauces. The order only took about five minutes and they were quick to hand over the fries. The problem with this is that the fries are served in a wonky shaped cone and about a tenth of my order fell off in the process of it simply being handed over to me. While I know it's authentic to serve it this way but the entire process just felt very heavy handed to me, maybe the paper could be larger or less flimsy. To its credit though, the large fries were pretty much the only thing I ate all day and by the end of it I could hardly even move but I felt this was more of grease and fat overload (from the Mayonnaise) than it was from the food actually being fulfilling or well made. While I was able to finish it (barely), most of the other people around me quit about halfway through. It was probably a better idea, I felt completely trashed after eating it. A small would be more than sufficient. While all the reviews on Yelp seem to love the Mango Chutney, I wasn't really a big fan. I don't really feel like the sweet taste of Mango really complements mayonnaise much at all let alone when paired with French Fries. Likewise, the Teriyaki Pomegranate sauce came off as a bit strong in the Horse Raddish sense of the word, not necessarily spicy but a bit offensive nonetheless. My friend defended this place saying that it's the most delicious thing in the world if it is near 1 am and you are drunk after hitting up a few bars but honestly, if you have to be drunk to fully enjoy the food at a place, is that really that high of a standard at all?

OMG! I love this place!!! Even with the 1.5 hour wait lol that's how amazing it is! It's not much of a wait anyway since you can just go happy hour anywhere in st marks. I got addicted after my first bite of pork bun. The pork belly and the sauce is just AMAZING! I went back my second time and it was even more amazing than I remembered! My friend and I were having foodgasms left and right and just moaning while we eat lol and in between each bite we would look at each other and say 'omg this is so worth the wait!' I've only tried one of the special spicy ramen and the akamaru modern but they are to die for! So suck it up and just wait those 1.5 to 2 hours because it'll be well worth the wait! Good things come to those who wait and you won't regret it or you can find me and beat me up xP

Came here and tried four empanadas. The spicy chicken and the viagra (some sort of seafood mix, with juicy chunks of crab and shrimp) were delicious. The tuna jalapeno was OK (the jalapenos were good, the tuna was meh, and the flavors didn't join together all that well). Sadly, the corn flour -- chicken empanada was pretty bad. All in all, I'd say that it's a notch below nearby Shachi's Arepas, but it's quite a good deal for the price.

went to this place 2 days ago. I know that most people see this joint as a bar and i'm not reporting the bar experience as i went there for dinner. On monday and tuesday they have a $20 three course meal, which is a fantastic deal. I had mussels marinara to start, followed by a 20 ounce t-bone steak, nicely grilled with mashed potatoes and an almost tart for dessert. Everything was great and fresh. The place is nice inside, but nothing to rave about. It does have a bar, but i cannot report on that as the only drinks i had was wine. This was my second time there, both times were great and a great value. Wait staff was quick and attentive, although it was so empty that you could not expect anything else.

How come no one has ever told me about Barbuto before? Apparently it's nothing new and yet I've never explored this corner of Washington and w. 12th. They close their reservations one day in advance, so be prepared for a wait if you walk-in like we did. We checked in with them twice, because they didn't seem so busy to warrant a 1hr+ wait, and by the second time the table was ready, a bit earlier than they had estimated. The venue is very sexy. Everything is open and revealed. The kitchen is open to the tables, the tables extend out onto the sidewalk through a seemingly wall-less structure. I think that sexiness struck some of the patrons, at a nearby table a girl couldn't stop sitting in her date's lap. We started with the salad caprese for the table. The special pasta was a paparadelle with pancetta, mushrooms, and onion - the winner of the night. We also had steak and gnocchi, but the caprese and paparadelle were the standouts. Finished the meal with gelati (mint and espresso) and the semifreddo. The gelati was not very gelati-like, lacked cream and shape, and it got all melty.   I would give them a 4.5 if Yelp gave the half star and Barbuto would get a 5 if the wait  was shorter and the service a tad more prompt (albeit enthusiastically friendly, our waiter was nowhere to be found at the end of the night).

Best Spanish restaurant in NYC. Ambiance, Food, Hospitality, Food & Prices its all there. Make sure to go on flamenco nights, performance is amazing their selection of Spanish beers and food is right on the spot. I could go on writing about how good the place it is but you should go and experience it yourself!

Absolutely LOVE this place. I've eaten here numerous times and even celebrated a birthday here last year. I've tried several things on the menu and enjoyed them all. Drinks are great, service is attentative. It can sometimes be chaotic at the front door so I would definitely recommend a reservation so you're not forced to squeeze into the tiny area while you wait..But otherwise, awesome!!

Food is ok.  Nothing to write home about.  I ordered the smoked salmon benedict.  A bit underwhelming but it was a nice day out and enjoyed the ambience of al fresco dining.  It's a cute and classy little place.  I just wish the food was amazing so I'd definitely want to come back.  I think I might try somewhere else next time.  Returning here would be by default unfortuately.

Terrific mix of sweet and savory brunch. Pancakes are terrific and so is the service.  Highly recommend the brunch cocktails.  Besides that, space is gorgeous and a little tough to find but worth the visit.

This IS your father's diner, and that's exactly why you should search it out. The Windsor is not some wannabe box with a laminated photo-laden menu and "servers" in place of waiters/waitresses...it's the real thing. I love it--inside and out (see my photos)--and if you're into diners, you will too. Frankly, I can't remember what we were served but I remember leaving the place feeling good about the visit. See those donuts on the counter? The owner told us his wife makes them one day a week. I've forgotten that too, but my photo is dated on a Wednesday in August 2011, so be on the lookout for those yummies if you're there midweek. This place is on my permanent mental map of diners worth a big detour just to visit again...places coast-to-coast whose memories are of nice people and ok food--special spots that preserve on our byways the "civilization" enjoyed by, yes, our fathers. A legacy worth passing on to our kids. =================== July, 2012: 2nd visit...during noontime rush-hour. I won't "demote" my review to 2 stars, though I wish there were a 2 1/2. Clam chowder: not sure there was a clam in it, but what WAS in it seemed suspiciously like chunks of BREAD!  I've never had worse. I've forgotten what else we had (the chowder shoved everything else out of memory), but we'll give the place one more chance because we like IT, if not as much its food. Sorry.

Typical collegetown 24 hour diner,....well UHA atleast.. and maybe some trinity folks too. perfect diner after pulling an all nighter or drinking...always bumped into random groups of people that I knew.. even had some foods fights.. The food was all too greasy.. however  I LOVED the American Cheese Omellette.. alas, ever since I graduated from college, no one ever wants to go back there with me. :(
Careful, check the hours. The point of closing at five? I just don't get it.

Food was fantastic!  Waitress was so pleasant and gave excellent recommendations.  Love the BYOB!  Portions were perfect, especially since French food is so rich.  Walked out feeling very full with 1 appetizer shared, dinner and 1 dessert shared.  All of the pate's were phenominal.  What I loved the most was how the side dishes and main course paired so well together.  The flavors melted in your mouth.  The only downfall is that this is listed as a romantic restaurant but it was loud and you sat so close to your neighbor that you could hear all of their conversation.  Not a deal killer - still had to give it 5 stars simply for the food and service.

What a find near Battery Park. If you can find it, that is. Classy wood-paneled interior, sweet and hospitable service, and the pizza . . . ! We were grabbing an early bite before Henry V, and a small pie was perfect for the two of us. The Barese is a combo of sausage, red onion, fennel seed, and peppers (which I never found, but didn't miss). Beautiful dough (thin but not crispy), fine mozzarella, and a perfect mix of toppings. Moretti is the only beer on tap, as I assume most people order wine by the glass from the ample list of choices. The tiny pillowy rolls that come out beforehand taste like the same dough, but accompanied by a zucchini/white bean puree. So good, I almost had no room for pizza. Almost. Minor downsides: * lots of groups with kids on the early side can be loud because of the acoustics (good for you if you have loud kids, bad if you are particularly sensitive. We are neutral, and it was not a big deal); * Tables outsides are in direct line of some overhead vents that blow warm (!) air; * It's tough to find. This may help: It's on the far west side of West Street, west of the bike path between 1st Place and 2nd Place. Don't confuse it with the cafe slightly to the north. Definitely going to find excuses to return. Skyscraper Museum is around here somewhere, right?

Cheap food, and fast, this place hits the spot.  Their veggie samosas were spicier than I expected them to be, but I'm weaksauce when it comes to spice.  The kabab sandwich is a bargain for how much you get, and the platter lasts you for more than one meal. If you're the high-maintenance type, you'll hate how this place has no seating, and how it doesn't look sparkling clean. Good cheap food, yes, but if you plan on paying with plastic, you need to spend over $30.

since this was just down the street from Pho Pasteur, I figured I would give this place a try as well. Overall, I was little impressed, mainly because they lacked decor and the food tasted so so. The soup  tasted normal and as a previous post said "canned" broth. It tasted like there wasn't a freshness factor to it. The pork chop was I think cut too thin so when cooked it was too tough and did not have juice in it afterwards. Prices are normal compared to the other places but I don't mind paying a little more as long as the place makes me feel comfortable.  Pho Dang just doesn't have that comfort feeling to it because of the lack of decor, I go out to eat to have the full experience and I like to enjoy my meal and a way to do that is for the environment to be well decorated.

I love The Boil more than Boiling Crab in San Jose, CA!!! I never tried Boiling Crab in So Cal, yet so I can't compare. I like the sauce and flavor at this place. The Cajun spice is very good and full of garlic. Boiling Crab so dull and bland, with very little sauce and no garlic chops. So disappointed. The Boil is pretty good overall. My fav is actually garlic butter with no spicy or medium spicy The Boil sauce.

Nobody does it like Mark Iacono and his team.  This is my favorite pizza in all of NYC.  The menu is minimal and that's because you only need three things in life: 1.  Their pizza 2.  Their calzone 3.  Their nutella pizza for desert. AND, its BYOB.  It gets no better.

I've heard my friends talk about Pio Pio so much but this was my first time here. I like the multilevel space but it does get packed and the noise level rises accordingly. So I wouldn't recommend it for a first date or anything but I do recommend it for groups of friends looking for good food and drinks at reasonable prices. I love their maracuja pisco cocktail! For food, my friends and I shared the chicken and seafood platters, ceviche, and empanadas. Everything was delicious. The staff are all friendly and attentive. I'd definitely keep this in mind for similar outings.

Its really hard to find a good place to eat around the midtown/murray hill, so this to me is a great find. Its a cute, humble lil' bistro, so groups of more than 4 will find it difficult to find seating, however they do take reservations.  I had the french onion soup, and grilled chicken sandwich, while my friend had the croque monsieur (pretty big portion). The grilled sandwich was ok, but i was very pleased with the soup, came out very hot, and it turned out to be very hearty- highly recommended. The only negative thing i have to say is that the staffing is basically one waitress who is also the hostess.  They could use some help.  I'll be back though!

My second visit to Cafe Lift was even better than the first. I went with my boyfriend, who lives only a few blocks from Sabrina's. I told him that like Sabrina's, the food would be awesome and creative... and that unlike Sabrina's, there would be no hour-long waits outside, no hosts picking and choosing the next diners based on god-only-knows what criteria, and no elbow pads necessary as there would be ample room between tables. We walked in and sat down immediately. Once my coffee was placed on the table, I searched the vicinity like a junkie for Sweet'N Low, but there were no pink packets in sight. Our server saved the day by procuring some from behind a counter. A few minutes later, she dropped off some complimentary chocolate chip bread pudding. I forgot all about that from last time so it was a nice surprise and really good. My fritatta special with breakfast sausage, jack cheese and spinach was great. The bf had a panini with prosciutto, sharp provolone and some other items, which he loved. Part of me wants to be greedy and not share Cafe Lift with others, but I also want this place to be around for a long, long time so I am obligated to spread the word. Get thyself to brunch!
i was here for 3rd anniversary. we had a great service, great food being here was  excellent for our memory you should visit here at least once.
SO BOMB!
Great foods and great drinks, they have even pairing wines with pizza!! It was a great customer services. Overall, stylish, tasty, great restaurant :)

We just returned from a two week vacation to NYC. During that two weeks we went to the Pig FOUR times. Four times. And it wasn't nearly enough. On our first visit to the Pig, on our first night in NYC, as luck would have it, we landed a seat at the upstairs bar when a 90 minute wait for a table turned a bit too long. Ryan the bartender became our NYC BFF. He makes the most amazing drinks, is incredibly knowledgeable about the food, and he recommended bars, restaurants and local flavor that basically turned our trip into Ryan's Tour of NY. On that first night we spent about 3 hours chatting it up with Ryan and the other customers. It felt like home right there at the bar and we happily returned for more. Then entire staff is warm, friendly and FUN. The food is comforting, delicious and Oh, the drinks! The drinks are inventive and creative without pretension.
