Just had lunch here few days ago, and it was truly fabulous. Had a big delicious seafood salad, and my dad had a great crab cake sandwich, all followed by amazing capuccinos. Very reasonably priced too. Go there!

This place is like a mill or a factory, you are in and out quickly. Its loud, very very loud. Its always packed. There is not enough space for all the tables and you end up sitting and brushing against someone else's shoulder. Not comfortable at all. But food is definitely worth it. Very delicious, fresh, and tasteful. The customer service gets bad at times, especially when it's packed, all of a sudden the owner gets an attitude!!!

I had a good time and lunch today. I opted Soba noodle soup and Ebi tempura as a set from the lunch menu. It was a happily-filling lunch. The memorable dish was soba noodle soup, the broth... Least favorite was the tempura, light but soggy. The ending gesture, a small dessert, was nice. The corner counter was a comfortable spot to sit in the restaurant if you are alone. It has more room. My server, Julie, was efficiently polite. Although it was busy, we chatted and shared our New York stories. I am coming back for lunch soon.

Panino Rustico is a welcome addition to Bensonhurst. There is great coffee, paninis, crepes and free wifi at the cafe. It's a good place to study, grab a bite to eat, and catch up with friends. I recommend any of the classic paninis with prosciutto di Parma, and a banana and nutella crepe that's drizzled with Hershey's chocolate syrup on top. As a few of the other reviewers have mentioned, service is a little slow because there's usually only 1-2 guys in the back assembling the paninis and toasting them. Well worth the wait, though. You won't be dissapointed if you come here, so check it out!

Such mixed feelings about this place. Miya's prides itself on creative takes on sushi, so eating here is something of a fun adventure. But if you're looking for solid, simple, straightforward fish this is not the sushi place for you. In terms of taste, the star was a pumpkin soup they gave us at the beginning. That said, the service is great and the atmosphere is fun. Just kind of depends on what you're looking for.
This is my second time to eat here! The place is always pretty! I ordered the red and white sangria for me and my girl! I love their sangria!

4 stars for atmosphere. The outside looks like a museum, but the inside is a dingy Philly bar with great happy hour prices. My wife and I got a pitcher of Pimms, which we really enjoyed. We ordered guacamole and they were just okay. Both the guac, salsa, and chips all looked and tasted like they were from 7/11 down the road. However, 4 starts for atmosphere, attentive staff, and a great pitcher of Pimms. Cheers!

WORST SERVICE ever! And I'm not speaking from one bad experience. We live in the neighborhood & have tried inatesso at least 6X. With the exception of one good experience sitting at the bar (I think bts name was Karen?), inatesso has let us down every time. Unknowledgable bartenders, aloof servers who seem bothered to be waiting on you. Last time was the deal breaker- we were there with another couple. We ordered a salad to share and a pasta to share, friends ordered large pizza. They brought our salad, a little while later our friends pizza, 15 minutes go by... "Um is our pasta coming?" The waitress looks around and says she's going to check and walks off. Then walks back to her computer (clearly entering our order, which she forgot) come over and says it coming soon. Another 12 min go by, our friends are totally done with their meal and still no sign of ours. At that point we fold and tell the waitress to cancel the order. After a few "it's coming, it's coming"s, she says okay. Not once was there an apology, no acknowledgement of things going wrong. NO offer to rectify the issue, or even an offer to still being the pasta or wrap it to go! I'm a hospitality manager- this is TERRIBLE service. Plus the place was dead!! Don't waste your time or money- Adrienne's pizza bar is well worth the few block walk and it's the same owners... practically same food... And 10X better experience!

A Monk's by any other name would taste as sweet? I'd have to squint to tell the difference in the menu and beer lists, but I think what makes Belgian Cafe interesting is that it's a neighborhood bar rather than a center city institution, and perhaps this makes more sense. I went last night and got a beer and the steak frites salad (I didn't feel like getting mussels). The meat portion was small but commiserate with the price and I didn't feel like weighing myself down anyway. It was better prepared than I actually expected. The fries were standard Monk's fries with their delicious fry sauce. I've become awfully tired of fries lately, but I just can't stop eating that sauce. Also, there was plenty of outside seating on a pretty nice day at 5:30. Note: I observed that the mussels were not served in a pot and I found this to be weird. If you must eat mussels out of a pot, be advised that you could be in for trouble.

Me and my friends heard about this place and the hype about it so we went to try it out. I thought the line meant hours waiting in line, but when i got there like at 9 pm, the line was only 45 minutes. So, there is this old man at the door that calls you in. Me and my friends were a group of three and so he called us in to be seated, skipping the 15 people ahead of us.  Me and my friends thought it was too good to be true, after waiting in the line, so we lingered, not being able to tell if he wanted us to come in or not.  He ended up clapping his hands at us to hurry up!!! So I thought that was kind of weird/rude.  He also never smiled. The tables are super close to each other and the tablecloths were dirty, but maybe it is what is to be expected at a busy place like this.  If you order a soda, the soda comes in the bottle and they give you a glass of ice.  I just got water (which they don't refill for you automatically; you have to ask for it!).   We ordered the large pizza, half cheese, and half pepperoni and olives. Some of our crust was black and burnt, but I really liked the basil. Maybe it was because I like basil, i don't know. But I didn't like the pepperoni or the olives at all.  The pepperoni was wayyyyyy tooooooo salty!  My friend liked it.  I thought the olives were super strong, but my friend like that also.  My other friend enjoyed her cheese only half, saying that it was reallllyy good. The personalities you see here at the family-owned restaurant are big.  While inside the old man ended up joking around and smiling with his staff.  Our waiter was nice, but did not have a big personality as the other waiter who came to our table to talk with us.  There is also a little boy that is working.  He was so adorable! So all in all, I was underwhelmed, but the pizza did not leave me feeling disgusting, which was good! I enjoyed the ice cream I got across the street at the Brooklyn Ice Cream Factory (I recommend the coffee flavor).

I'm not a huge fan of pisco sours but the bartenders know how to make an awesome one.  The staff here is great - they are so sweet & attentive.  I've been here for drinks & boozy brunch.  Both times we never noticed when our glasses were empty.  The food was great.   I'm definitely going back

While the decor is dark and the music choices are a bit odd (Indian dubstep?) I can't complain too much about the food. For ten bucks you get a hefty meal, and this is a great place for a quick lunch. It's somewhere between a real restaurant and a take out place, so just be warned its not overly fancy or a good place for a formal date. I got the Mysore masala dosa and it was decent and very large, though I feel it could've used a bit more heat to it. The cilantro chutney was fabulous and my only gripe is that there wasn't a larger portion of it. However I did not care for their sambar, it was a bit too thick for my taste and also lacked the heat I was looking for. As far as I can tell, you don't get to pick your level of spiciness either. (I'm not sure if this is something you can even choose for a dosa, so pardon my ignorance if it's really only found with one certain taste.) The old school type of dosa was decent, but  I get the feeling the true stars are the build your own kind. Hopefully I'll get to try that soon. Not the best South Indian food I've ever had, but not bad.

I went to Calle Ocho on a warm Saturday night for dinner - the place is lively, loud and with nice enough mood lighting. After being led through the bar - the restaurant part of the place hidden in the back - you reach a huge dining area. Our seats (two people) were in the corner by a huge dinner party, and while it was a little cramped, it added to the atmosphere (for the most part). I had the paella and a mojito - stunning. The mojito came with a huge stick of cane sugar, and was about as perfectly made as any I've ever tasted. The Paella was piled high with...well...everything. Including a large hunk of lobster, still in the shell. It was an absolutely delicious meal. The only slightly low point (if you can call it that) were the Bombas - maybe it's my ignorance, but there was so much sugar over them that it was nigh-on impossible to eat them without crunching down on it. The filling and the ice cream were delicious, though. All in all, I will be back. Especially considering that mojtios are $5 on Mondays. Something horrible is going to happen to me as a result, I'm sure.

Love, love, love! The food was delicious and the atmosphere was great. Ask to sit in the garden, it was very cute. As far as food, we started with tomato mozzarella, cauliflower and meatballs all which were great. I do not even eat cauliflower and I think it was my favorite appetizer. For my main I got the gnocchi which was also amazing. Will definitely be going back!

The food, oh the food, delicious soups made from scratch, salads so fresh you feel your face being slapped, sides, cole slaw being a family heirloom, red skinned potato salad and I can go on. Top quality beverages, sandwiches which leave quiet and savoring the wonderful taste and freshness, and don't forget the desserts, trust me, if you didn't save room take some home or to the office.

Cheap, fast, and cash only.... I'll let you ponder that one for a bit and see what images come to mind... no, no! I'm talking burgers here! Some have said Corner Bistro is their favorite burger in the city, while I wouldn't go that far I'd agree that it's a very good burger. They have a very limited menu, but that's the beauty of the place. Another huge perk - the burger is $7 and the cold beer you get to go with it is $4. Where else can you find that in the West Village? Service is a bit lacking, but they are efficient and that's what really matters. Great low key tavern atmosphere. FYI Cash only... but that is $15 well spent my friends... 3.5 stars.

Came here for Brunch because of Triple D so I feel like Guy Fiery owes me money now... Let's start we the positives - the outdoor entertainment, the host guy is awesome you almost forget the time listening to him... Oh and if you waiting longer than 15 minutes you get one of his famous jokes, pick a spicy one. - the Waffle batter is great. - the chicken that comes with the waffle is Bland Bland Bland, have the salt prices went up? maybe they ran out if salt, pepper, paprika, onion & garlic power... What else does one add to fried chicken, I never made fried chicken but I bet you money if I do it'll taste better than the chicken @ Queens Comfort today. - Balls of Fire, I like spicy food I love heat however when all you can taste is heat all the other flavors are kaput, dead gone with the wind... No bueno - the music Loud Loud Loud & the place is so small and the table (yeah the table one long communal table) I was seating between a big girl and some drunk frat dudes, not good I was feeling a bit claustrophobic & my head started to hurt a bit. - I was really looking forward to dessert the Piña Colada Bread Pudding sound it amazing however I ran out of there as soon as I ate my waffle... Well it took about 5 minutes of looking around & signaling to finally get the check, so don't expect good service either. Maybe if ones comes during the week the food & service is better but I don't know if I'll ever find out.

Green Eggs is another great place to have so close to Broad, for those of us suffering from a dearth of breakfast spots in Point Breeze. I recently visited on a weekday morning for breakfast, joining the friendly neighborhood crowd - without the weekend brunch wait.  The service was great, although the food took a bit longer to arrive than I expected. This time around, my dining partner and I stuck to menu staples rather than binging on their yummy (but usually over-the-top) specials. The quinoa porridge was a unique dish, flavorful and filling. Green Eggs does a decent rosemary breakfast potato: delicious but would have been better served a bit warmer. The pancakes - ordered with fresh fruit on top - were standard but well-received. Also: nice tea selections and the fresh-squeezed OJ is expensive but solid. Overall, Green Eggs is a good staple. It can stand up to Sabrina's and Morning Glory, even if you opt for their dishes that don't induce a post-brunch food coma. A quick note: Green Eggs no longer takes credit cards. A small sign on the table explained the switch to cash-only as a way to cut costs without raising menu prices. Fine with me - there is an ATM in the bar section, with a surcharge of only $0.99!
Always good. One of my favorite. The old lady is a staple. The staff is always nice food is Great

A very cool bar with a neat theme--the devil!  The place has two floors, decent priced beer with a good selection, and awesome bar-food.  Seriously, they have some great food!  The staff is generally nice and the prices aren't bad.  It's not the cheapest bar, but also not too expensive, and it's very well priced for the area.
Boar pasta is insane

One of my FAVORITE hole-in-the-wall places.  I LOVE their jerk chicken!  Their stew chicken is also yummy for those rare days that I want to eat something more mild.  Fall off the bone meat, perfectly spiced and seasoned, plus all kinds of great sides to accompany: cabbage, choice of rice (jasmine or rice and peas), salad with their tasty homemade dressing, and plantains (Salad and plantains are only served if you eat there.)...what's not to fall in love with! (Hold on...I need to grab a napkin to wipe up my drool.) I always bring my visitors to this place and they too fall in love with whatever dish they decide to order.  One of my friends is a huge oxtail fan, so that's what she ordered and loved it.  I never tried it until that day.  Also delicious, but a bit too fatty for my preference.  I'm also not a fan of the calypso shrimp, but don't let that stop you from trying it.  Their bread pudding is also good, you can definitely taste the rum. I really need to get around to trying other dishes, especially their specials, but everytime I have a craving for The Islands, I cannot help, but order my usual. FYI -It's BYOB and cash only.   -There are about five tables upstairs and a few outside when the weather is nice.  There is a $2 service charge for dining in though.
Tasty and cheap!

I absolutely adored the Marketfaire location, and got seriously depressed when I realized they had closed. When I found this location, I was ecstatic. While it's not an exact match to the mall location, it's close enough as makes no nevermind. If you're in the mood for udon or a quick roll, it is totally the place to go. For the price, theirs has no equal.

My friends and I went to Zento for dinner. I have heard so many good things about the place and they do have awesome sushi! The new location is only a few doors down from the old place. It's definitely much bigger. Our server is very friendly and she recommended some drinks they were having on special. We tried out a couple of sake cocktail but they tasted more like flavored water. So I changed to Apple sake which is very tasty and easy to drink (Dangerous!!!) I got the duck hand roll and love roll. They are both delicious. Writing about this is making me hungry! =) I cannot wait to go back there next time. Definitely get reservation beforehand. Although the new place is much bigger, I still don't see how you can have a large party (more than 6 people) sitting at the same table.

Tiny hole-in-the wall place, but I think that adds to its charm. It's not the kind of overpriced Manhattan restaurant where you're paying for fancy decor, trendy location, or the waiters' tuxedos... here you pay for excellent food, plain and simple. I lived in Lyon (the self-proclaimed gastronomic capital of France) for a bit and this is up to par with any of the restaurants I went to there, or anywhere in France. BYOB is a plus. Would definitely recommend, especially for a romantic date with that special someone... ;]

The cheese steak with american cheese was great! However, dining with a 3 inch COCKROACH on the wall was horrible.  The american man behind the register walked buy and bused a table and made a comment to other customers that were eating saying "yes, she's looking at you" refering to the COCKROACH.  The man then came back with a large paper bag, and used the bag to then kill the COCKROACH on the wall.  His response was that it's summer and the weather is hot there for that's why the COCKROACH was on the wall.  There is a large tip jar at the register, they should use the money from the jar to buy some RAID!!!!!!!!! I won't be going back there!!!

Where did this place come from? I'm trying to decide where to eat last Sunday and all of a sudden I discover that Cafe Lift  has the reputation as the brunch place du jour. How did this happen? Nobody consulted me. I needed to get to the bottom of this. My initial report on Cafe Lift confirms the following - The concepts are there, but the execution needs some follow-through. Example: The ultra sleek, modern furnishings are aesthetically catching, but aren't necessarily comfortable to sit in. The lemon-ricotta pancakes w/ fresh peaches? It's what I dream about at night, but in my dreams the peaches are ripe. (In fairness, the Jens Crespelle my GF got tasted splendid, and I immediately became jealous) I know however that I'll need to ride the Lift again before I make a final verdict. There was simply too much on the menu that sounded delicious to base my whole opinion on some unripened peaches. I'll be coming back to this steel-and-pipe laden establishment for round 2. P.S. I don't know if it's this place or the Loft district in general, but somewhere there's a magnet that attracts girls that look like Feist. So if you've ever watched the Mushaboom video and thought "This is everything I look for in a mate", I'd start looking at Cafe Lift.

Something about NJ restaurants. Its never consistent. The first visit is great and every visit there after is so so. Stamna seems to buck that trend for me. Whether it is the gyro platter for lunch or grilled whole fish for dinner. It keeps me coming back. The taste and aroma remind me of my honeymoon in Santorini. The best lamb, zucchini pies, and greek cuisine in Essex County.
Great Pizza, Margaretha was my favorite service was a bit slow but worth it.

This is one of my favorite New Haven restaurants. The food is always spectacular. The menu rotation is good for change ups, but they always seem to take off the meal I liked from my previous visit. My first time there I had a roast pork loin (I miss you) that was amazing - haven't seen it in 2 years since. I think the nay-sayers here are a little hard on the entrees because they are fairly simple. There isn't  10 different oils and 3 kinds of foam on your plate. If you are the kind of person that likes all of the bells and whistles when you eat out, then maybe you won't like Zinc. I like to taste the food I order and not be overwhelmed by added flavors, but rather have them compliment and enhance the taste of the meat, fish etc. and Zinc provides just that. EVERYONE SHOULD DO THE CHEF'S TABLE NIGHTS! They host 4 or 5 a year and have themes (Beer and Cheese, Greek, Cinco de Mayo)  and you learn something too! All inclusive for $35 (or $25 each if you book them all) is not a bad way to spend an evening. We went to all 4 last year - started out as my wife and I, then us and 2 friends, then us and 6 more people and the last one we had a total of 14. I'll throw in 1 con/piece of advice. If you have a choice between the booth side and chair side always take booth. The chairs are REALLY uncomfortable.

Recently they changed their prices and with it, seemed to decrease portion size. Still relatively good dosa (it is the only place in town that makes them) but I felt a little slighted last time I was there.

Returned to Joe Allen last night after a long unintentional absence and found it lived up to expectations from past visits.  Star studded!  Jerry Stiller, Ann Meara, Victor Garber and Ron Rifkin were all there, along with another guy, whom I have yet to positively ID (it was Zach Grenier from 24 and The Good Wife). We stopped here after a show and enjoyed the burgers, chicken sandwiches and lamb shank. Salads were good and the toll house cookies with vanilla ice cream were a fitting conclusion. The $29 Cotes du Rhone was a little warm, but nice.
Roti Canai, Som Tum (Papaya Salad) and Panang Curry made an absolutely delicious and wonderful takeout lunch. I highly recommend this restaurant. I know that I'll be back!

Been here at least 5 times, always satisfied; refined cooking, great selection of sakes ( literally the "sake cellar", Ichinokura Himezen and Kakurei, yay! ) Food (5/5) daily special soba set for a quick lunch and tasting menu for a slow lunch ~ dinner time star dishes (izakaya-like small dishes): a. kamo roast - tenderly roasted duck b. jidori shioyaki - tenderly (again) grilled chicken, dip it in the aromatic yuzu sauce c. gyutan - tender (yes, tender) beef tongue stew d. chawanmushi - tender (...) egg custard steamed in a cute cup filled with bite-sized goodies including a ginkgo nut e. others: grilled squid, firefly squid, inaniwa udon ( silky smooth for a change ), ochazuke, assorted sashimi, black sesame crème brûlée and sake manju or soba bun with matcha ice cream to finish, and certainly sake sake Ambience (4.5/5) intimate, carefully decorated with a relaxed courtyard feeling, very cute bathrooms Service (4.5/5) nice staff, always make reservations though sometimes you may obtain only 1hr window at the bar during peak hrs

It's an unassuming little place that is difficult to miss, even when you're looking for it. Once inside, though, it was a nice space to sit and enjoy a meal. I had the gouda sandwich and split the mac and cheese with my friend, who had the fontina sandwich with mushrooms. Both were extremely tasty, and I would definitely come back to try out the other food here. All in all, a nice place to come and enjoy a nice meal with friends.

only one word can describe the food here... YUM! Well known for their tart and spicy corn this place is what some might call a hole-in-the-wall restaurant. But it is more than that. It is a restaurant that strives to sell delicious foods that are hefty in portions.

I just had the Dine In Brooklyn Week Prix Fixe dinner for $25. Appetizer: Lamb meatballs (2pcs) were just regular meatballs you could get anywhere...definitely nothing special. Entree: Chicken breast  (well they gave me a leg) with polenta...average chicken, no special flavor of any sort but not bad. Desert: Chocolate Torte with vanilla ice-cream. The best part of the entire meal. Very light, melt-in-your-mouth deliciousness. Customer service was decent, nice ambiance, give it a try.

I come here quite often for lunch during the week.  It's usually three of us and we pretty much order the same dishes every time we go.  Beef Chow Fun, Beef Pan Fried Noodles and one of the two....Sweet and Sour Pork Chop or Orange Beef.  That's plenty of food for three of us and one of the guys that comes with us is a BIG eater.  The dishes come with complimentary house soup or we sometimes go for the hot and sour soup. We're regulars so we go there for the food and not really the service.  But honestly, we've noticed the service has gone down a little bit.  We've seen some new waiters at the place and they are pretty poor at their job.  Spilling food, dropping food off plates, not following up if the dishes are good.  It's fine for us but for other customers, that's not acceptable. The prices are very reasonable.  For the 3 dishes we usually pay $24-$27 (including tip/tax)...that's only $7-8/pp which is reasonable for the amount of food we get.  They definitely have lost customers since Qin Dynasty opened up across Rt. 46.  That will be another review....

I am slowly working myself through the entire menu. The sandwiches are heaping piles of flavor. You cannot go wrong with any of their sandwich offerings. The pork is unbelievably tender, and the brisket is flavorful. Both benefit from a hearty Sarcones roll. Do not forget to order a portion of the potatoes, then plan a nap for the remainder of your afternoon.
Im relatively sure there is a decent bar somewhere under the thick layers of old city douchiness that cover this place, but its definitely not worth digging for at midnight on a saturday.

Came in for brunch with a group and loved the food..especially because you get two options and everything is delicious. The only downside is the service since you have to chase the waiters around to get another mimosa/bellini/drink.

This restaurant is one big room.  It is not a warm room, temperamentally; a lot of black and white, glass and chrome, softened by the old wooden bar.  I was here on a Thursday night for Happy Hour.  We sat at the narrow counter facing three oyster shuckers.  Seating is tight along this counter.  It was a pleasing note that not everyone was a 20something and we were able to chat a little with people on both sides of us.  The Londoner oyster shooters were good, with a dill-flavored gin, and they were only $3 on happy hour.  The happy-hour oysters were James River oysters, small and not too flavorful.  If you eat your oysters with cocktail sauce, that doesn't matter; but, if not, I would not call these a bargain.  A smaller number of larger, better oysters would have been a better approach for me to have taken; live and learn.  Fwiw, I noticed the Naked Cowboys were big, don't know what they may taste like.  All in all, I was underwhelmed and this is a 3-star-minus review.  My wife asked me if I thought the shuckers were enjoying their jobs.  It was, unfortunately, a rhetorical question.  At the counter, you are facing them and watching them the whole time.  All that ice, frequently refreshed, and the black-and-white of the oyster shells make a neat sight, though.  Service overall was excellent in every way.  I wasn't unhappy about being there, I got my oyster jones tended to adequately, but I doubt I will go back anytime soon.  Just didn't click for me.

Good atmosphere.  Menu read great and the food looked fabulous.  Then the food was presented and the flavor was a bit of a disappointment. Everything tasted good, but nothing stood out.  The pumpkin pancakes kind of tasted like pumpkin.  My goat cheese and spinach omelet was heavy on eggs and little on filling.  The toast was reminiscent of IHOP. Go to hangout and have brunch, but leave your expectations for breath taking food at the door.

Pretty decent food here. Most of the items on the menu are Americanized Chinese meals sadly, but there are some authentic Chinese food here and there if you know where to look. This place is unlike any other restaurants. The place is kept unusually clean unlike other restaurants. The atmosphere of this place is very nice. The waiter are very nice and are very helpful in making choices for you. Overall, I'd come back again.
pretty good for brunch good bloodies, good portions

Not a bad place to stop off for a pint after or before a good flight, but not much different from the other bars within the airport. I was hoping for more I guess, not really sure why since you don't see many Irish in sunny places lol.

Oh boy, the rare one star review! Came here for a Saturday breakfast before my wife had to get to work. It's a cool space with tile floors and leather seats as well as dark wood everywhere. The service was poor at best, we saw our server once and he was very sullen the entire time, never a smile or a greeting. Had to essentially flag someone else (manager?) down to order and had to actually go to the server station to get a check. My food ($14 bacon and eggs) came out cold and had to be sent back. My wife's "malted waffle" came straight off a hotel style waffle iron with a pad of butter on top ($13 for a waffle, no sides). Would not return again. If they can't manage a reasonably straight forward breakfast service then I can't imagine what their dinner service is like.

Oh god Nick's. I just have to say the name and my mouth starts to water. This is one of my favorite places to take non-Philly friends, especially if we are looking for something cheap. The best meal in the house: Lager, gravy fries and a Roast Beef, overboard. I've tried the roast turkey, it seemed a little dry. So I'm going to stick with what I know and love.
delicious. favorite dish: mezze. some of the dishes are overpriced though.

Food is very good.....BUT servers are another story....there isn't an host so when you enter --you stand at door at least 5 mins  before someone acknowledges your presence.....girl at counter just does her work and doesn't look up....after being seated a menu is placed on table..no explanation or suggestion....2nd cup of coffee is hard to come by.  Kafe lacks ambiance and courtesy.....
The food was fantastic !!! :) Is a good spot to picnic as well :)

El Vez has a fun, cool vibe - perfect for dinner with friends. Of course, the prices are more inflated than no frills Mexican food, but you're paying for the ambiance as well. The guacamole was tasty as advertised. I liked that it wasn't heavy on fillers (mayo or sour cream) like most restaurant guacs are. My husband had the taco sampler and I had the enchilada sampler. Our faves from the bunch were the crispy fish tacos and classic chicken enchiladas. Overall, the food was good and I would not hesitate to return. Added incentive - I can't wait to hop in their old timey photo booth next time!

Really good, reasonably priced Mediterranean food.  I usually get the Kruveet or the Zuchinni cakes and recently tried the cookies (all of which are are delicious).  I stop by a couple of times a week and do schoolwork here and the staff is very warm and polite.  Great place!

I love Sanfords, and for one reason: the meat. And I'm not talking about no dish you order off the menu. I'm talking about ARMANDO, baby. Oh my god, what a hottie he is. I probably shouldn't tell you all this, but one night me and my friends Dave and Shawn came in after a night of clubbing, and Armando was there looking absolutely divine. We all had some drinks, and he came back to our place and had a serious f-in party. I have never been manhandled like that. Shawn almost threw out his back. Armando was just so strong. He's a soccer player, boys. A goalie, and boy what hands. So yeah. If you fellas are out in Astora late night and you want something hot for the afterhours, go to Sanfords and ask for our favorite manager, Armando. Que paso, Armando, you naughty naughty nino. Pablo from Astora

The food wasn't bad, and even though we had to make reservations the place was half empty. We had burgers, fish and fries. The guinness beer was not very fresh. The service was very slow even thought there was only 3 tables with customers. Food wasn't bad but very overpriced for the quantity served. We have had better. We will not go back.

As old-timers will remember, First Avenue around 14th Street used to be home to a small Filipino community. There were several Filipino restaurants as well as grocery stores. My first encounter with Filipino food was at one of these restaurants, and it did not encourage me to try again for many years. But then I heard good things about Maharlika and decided to give it a try. The food is actually pretty tasty. My group of four tried the lumpiang barquillos, kare kare, pancit bihon, and lamb adobo, with sides of pea shoots and baby bok choy. None of the dishes were standouts, and frankly I don't think that Filipino food is as interesting as, say, Thai or Vietnamese cooking, but it makes for a nice change of pace. If I were grading this place on food alone, it would get 3 stars. But then, the food is not what defines this place, because they are in possession of a much rarer, indeed unique attribute: The Most Annoying Waiter in the World. I know, you're skeptical. Perhaps you think you have encountered The Most Annoying Waiter in the World elsewhere. You have not.  Note: I do not say the WORST waiter in the world. There are far, far worse. But for pure teeth-gritting, soul-killing irritation, this guy takes the cake. It's not just that he describes each dish, and each sauce or condiment that accompanies each dish, at tiresome length and in excruciating detail. It's not just that he intimates in an ongoing and  positively bullying fashion that you are in for the culinary experience of your life (which you are not). It's rather the dripping condescension that suffuses his enthusiasm. He speaks to you as if you were a second grader about to try adult food for the first time, or as if this were your first meal at a restaurant other than Appleby's, and you had to be led tenderly by the hand lest, left to your own devices, you should make some fatal culinary error. Admittedly, the annoyance is leavened by a kind of dinner-theater amusement at times, but on the whole he manages to suck any possible enjoyment out of your experience of the food.

Alright for a gastro-filipino food but  this place was a miss for me... definitely a toned down version of any filipinos nanay's cooking... this is obviously for the American pallet but it definitely will fill those cravings of the homeland... so if your a foodie I'd say it's a place to stop by and frequenting will be up to you! bring cash cause they don't take cards which is a FAIL on any place I go to! What we had: Spam fries- definitely was a surprising pleaser for my Hawaiian friend who was present at the dinner! this would have horrified my nanay and tatay but hey you gotta try everything once and this was a good call Lumpiang Barquillos- Interesting and weird the flavor was a miss and the plating was not impressive really unappealing actually I wanted to swing that away... Pampangan Style Sizzling Sisig- this was okay I can see how it is a crowd pleaser but I must say Pig & Khao is much better as it is what they are known for Kare-kare- ;( I love my kare kare so this just was like a sad coaster ride that didn't give me any thrill... the taste was subtle and lacking... when you eat this kind of food you want the first taste to be the best and it sadly wasn't ugh... Sinigang Na Isda* - The seafood in this was overcooked but the overall taste was actually great I usually like my sinigang really tangy but this was actually impressive with the balance in this one Filipino Fried Chicken And Ube Waffle- I was told I had to try this and it was so disappointing the chicken was dry the waffle though was good and the syrup interesting taste ube was obviously pretty but something felt missing to this whole thing Overrall it was okay and I am always happy to stop by a filipino establishment but sadly not a place I would frequent

Stopped in here Saturday night while trying to kill some time before going out to to dinner.  Good selection of beer and yummy spinach and artichoke dip (yup that's right -- I eat before I eat).  After sitting at the bar for about 45 minutes watching the bartender concoct some crazy bloody marys, I decided to order one myself.  Take a look at the ingredients picture I uploaded.  Best. bloody. mary. in a long time!!  Take advantage of the Scoutmob special and check it out for yourself!
sofias wine bar is a sweet little gem! we had the meatballs along with the prosciutto pizza, and it was amazing! I highly recommend this place!

While waiting for our table at Lombardi's, we contemplated making a quick run to Cafe Habana for the infamous corn. After very little debate, we made a mad dash and picked up a few ears and started munching only to find out our table was ready. We snuck the corn in and snuck bites under the table. Hot corn juice dribbling down our chins and cheesy, spicy, stolen bites of the most awesome corn EVER - totally worth the scolding we got for bringing 'outside food.' Just a few days after, we went back for more corny goodness and a shared platter of roasted pork, beans and rice. YUM YUM YUM YUM -- the only thing that could've made it better are the added dramatics of breaking the rules and eating it in another food joint. NYC and Cafe Habana-- I'm coming back soon...and I'm definitely coming back for your CORN!!!

Very cute coffee shop. Quick and nice service. A group of us were about to head out for some afternoon fun. Since Mother Nature is angry and is giving us heat waves, we ordered iced drinks. All were tasty and did the caffeine trick.
Great salad, always good food. Nice service. LONG line and very small space for big group.

I booked a party here recently.  I have to say the food is very good, and they have a nice menu to choose from.  The wait staff is also very attentive and accommodating.  As for the manager of the establishment, the day of my party, not sure what happened.  He was very rude telling me as soon as we got there that we were late and had to leave by a certain time.  I reminded him, that when I booked the party reservation 2-3 months prior that we were going to be late, therefore he had extended the party room for an additional half an hour.  He said he would have to check his book.  He later came back and apologized because he had checked his reservation book and saw the note he had written when first reserved.  As a paying customer and spending quite a bit of money on a group of people, I do not feel this is the way to address or treat your customers.  Check your book before addressing your paying guests in a non-customer friendly way.   He later, also addressed another one of my guests with attitude, where she came to me and said that she did not like how she was treated.  After this, he did not show his face anymore and the bill was given by one of the waiters, which was very nice and appreciative of our business.  Too bad, it didn't come from the manager or owner. I frequent restaurants all the time, and have planned a number of gatherings like this one.  This is the 1st time I have ever been treated in such an unprofessional way, in this type of setting.

Now most don't know, but Cincinnati (my former city before moving to Philly) was a hot bed of amazing northern Indian food. I know, it's hard to believe that anything in Ohio is spicy or brag-worthy, but it really was "the shiz". So after searching for something comparable in Philly and coming up empty handed, I had pretty much given up -- that is until I met EKTA. Now the mere fact that they will deliver all the way to my office in Rittenhouse, without charge and in a timely manner is unbelievable! Add that to the free dessert and the delicious food and you've got a winner. We've ordered a few times from there now and done it up family style and I've never been disappointed with anything. I usually stick to the veggie dishes like masaladar chola and saag paneer, but the lamb vindaloo and butter chicken totally knocked my socks off.

I still thank for the friend who let me know into this little secret place five years ago back when it's still at the original location on Broome street off East Broadway.  Take it from me, and believe in the words other reviewers written, the sandwich is that GOOD.  I gave myself every possible excuse to buy their delish sandwich whenever i have a chance to pass by Chinatown, or even when I'm 20 blocks away it's still worth the trip to swing by. Yip, they are YUM YUM YUMMMMMMILY GOOD...

My friends from Boston introduced me to this place on my last trip to NYC. They said Joe's Shanghai has the best Xiao Long Bao in New York. I was addicted ever since. Came back after a year and they are still as good. Xiao Long Bao are these little juicy dumplings with soup and minced pork filling. Eating it requires some chopsticks skills. You have to carefully pick it up without breaking the skin. Slowly dip it into the dark vinegar sauce, bite into that ball of love and let the milky broth take over your savory sensation. It is a common dish that a lot of restaurant serve but very little truly excel. While I haven't really tried that many XLB in East Coast, I do believe Joes's crab meat XLB is among the best in the States. I have yet to find a restaurant in San Francisco Bay Area that is comparable. The only rival maybe Dan Tai Fung in LA. Knowing how busy they could get during lunch hour, I made sure we get there before they open at 11. We were first to arrive but some people gathered there shortly after. We were seated immediately and our dumplings were served promptly. Just as good as I remembered. Skin with perfect texture and thickness that is chewy yet delicate. Flavorful and generous amount of broth. Not too fatty nor too salty. I do find the fillings for the normal one a bit plain but the crab version is flawless. Totally worth a trip to Chinatown. If you wanted something else other than the dumplings, the Shanghai Fried Bean Curd and Shredded Turnip Shortcake aren't too bad.

I'm a big fan of Tex-Mex food so I had to give this place a try. Don't go to Nor Libs too often but have been here twice. The first time we ended up ordering wayyy too much food, but it was good. Love the mexican corn here. Not a huge fan of the nachos, by I'm probably biased because I went to college next to the best nacho restaurant in the country (in my opinion)! However, the totorilla chips tasted fresh and homemade. Could have used more cheese, one can never have too much. Also ordered the mac & cheese. The waiter pushed us to order chili with it, which ended up being completely unnecessary. The chili consists of huge chucks of beef, which was good but more like a side dish than combo. Maz & cheese was very good too. My second visit was during Yelp cocktails week. $2.50 margaritas are hard to beat! They were very tasty, but more sryupy than I prefer. Our waitress was alright. We were a table of 7 and she kept forgetting one or two things. Wasn't a huge deal though. For my meal I had a steak burrito, which I thought was very tasty. My friend ordered the gringo burrito, and she said it was plain and tasteless. This place has it's ups and downs, but I would go back if I were in the area.
I'd probably put mamouns over Oasis but their cabbage is real solid and it's still only 3 bucks. They're also absurdly fast which is definitely a plus. I wanna check out the shawarma plates.

I have never eaten poboys and am glad that Beck's was the place I had them. I had the shrimp poboy and cajun fries and the shrimp was crisp . It was great. Husband had the Jambalaya and could not stop raving about it.  Next time, I am back in Philadelphia, will definitely make sure to stop at Beck's. Please open a location in NJ please :) Definite try : Jambalaya, Poboys

Much fanfare had been given on the Internet about the burgers at Good Dog, a bar located on 15th street between Walnut and Locust, especially in regards to their Good Dog burger which comes stuffed with Roquefort cheese. I opted for their traditional burger, prepared medium - which is how I ask for all my burgers. Medium gives you just the right amount of pink for it to be juicy, but not still mooing. I came during the lunch hour on a Friday, so it was full but not packed and I sat at the bar. And waited. And waited. When I was at the point of gnawing my arm off I was so hungry, my burger finally arrived on - SURPRISE! - a brioche bun! (But that was on the menu so I guess I already expected that. Plus, I could tell by everyone else getting served their food before me.) Their fries came with a side of their housemade aioli for dipping. It was kind of like a watery version of the onion ring sauce at Burger King. I prepared to dive into this delicious burger, my palate poised to receive the succulent, juicy meat. But, lo and behold after first bite, I realized not only was my burger not even the slightest bit of pink in the middle (it was hard to tell at first in the dim lighting of the bar), but it was dry, overcooked and charred - lettuce, tomato and ketchup used as an attempt to cover up the grill marks. I was starving so there was no way I was sending it back at this point and so, I trudged on and chewed through the meat like a dog chewing on rawhide. I was extremely disappointed. No flavor, just the taste of burnt beef in my mouth. And let's not even get into the brioche bun being used yet again in a completely unoriginal attempt to fancy-ify this overpriced bar burger. ($11?? Seriously??) Regardless of how busy your kitchen is, the least you can do is try to prepare food to your customer's request. I can only imagine what would have happened if I ordered a steak there (if they even serve steak; I have no clue.) Or if I had some kind of food allergy. (I actually think I did have some allergic reaction to whatever was in their aioli after I left. I've never known myself to have food allergies before, but my throat felt like it was closing up and made it hard to swallow.) I guess they just figured it was better to overcook my burger then undercook it, and that does not a good burger make. Bad dog, very bad dog.

LOVED this place. Not just for vegetarians. Came here with two carnivores and they enjoyed it. Get the meatballs with kale pasta. SO GOOD a little spicy but awesome. And for drinks- I def recommend the bramble! And the service was phenomenal. Most fun bartenders!
very Italian place, one best pizza in neighborhood and spumoni soo good!

If you are looking for a perfect brunch spot - you should look no longer. On a sunny Sunday, the wait is typically 15-20 minutes, which is not a problem when there is so much to do around. The ambiance is wonderful - tables outside, inside, and in a cute little green garden room in the back. The decor is really cute and really makes you feel at home. The food was amazing - one of the best egg benedict dishes I have had. The orange juice is great (mind you - I don't really like orange juice) and the bloody mary was made well. Definitely going back and suggest you all go and enjoy!!

They have a great deal on oysters and clams and I was very impressed with the service the bartender gave us! The only reason why this doesn't get 5stars is that their wine selection doesn't have anything worth drinking and the place is really small, trying to go there on a weekend night is ridiculous.

Noodles are eatable, but not good enough to get more stars. I ordered beef Pho and beef was overcooked, soup base not favor enough, its cheap and serve with big bowl, just not that impressed of their food a lot. Restaurant have two floors, very old style atmosphere, I've experienced a better one in Chicago.

The food here was good as well as the service. I really enjoyed eating here and look forward to coming here with some other friends. The waiter was also very attentive and friendly which i appreciate.

Service, food and atmosphere was all amazing. Obviously on the pricier side of NYC fare. Had 4 apps for 4 people and entrees each. The short rib app was amazing as was the Raw tuna. I think the best entree was the Lamb Osso Bucco, must try. Did not enjoy the artic char, tastes like a smoked salmon but maybe that's what your in to.

Best veg Gen Tso's.  Mostly soy chicken- not a dough ball with a marble-sized piece of TVP at the center... and the sauce is always perfect.  I eat here more often than anywhere when I want to hide away and decompress from a stressful morning.  I aldo dig how they add some protein to Mei & Chow Fun (veggie ham or chicken).

Great pick by a friend (both of us from the South). Nice selection of beers (check out their seasonal offerings) and pickled starters (cukes, tomatoes, beets, jalapeños, green beans, etc.). Biscuits are dense -- not fluffy but perfect for dredging the pork belly beer mussels broth (broth itself was ok; not as flavorful -- the restaurant can do better... maybe it needs more butter... or citrus... hmm...). Buttermilk fried chicken (caesar) is excellent. Juicy and tender. Perfect pairing! Service was a distraction -- made a couple mistakes with our pickled starters and didn't offer a dessert menu after entrees. Table not bussed completely before check was dropped. Felt rushed. A bit disappointing after a satisfying meal.

My sister had recommended this place a while ago, and we happened to remember it during our visit. Of course the day after dining there, my sister shrieked that they dropped to a C rating - oops. I guess ignorance is bliss, so long as you don't have food poisoning. I really wanted to like this place more. The decor and vibe is sleek and swanky both inside and out, with lots of gold mirrors, chandeliers and dim lights, yet something was a little off. Maybe it was the metal mesh chairs, the awkwardly cramped inset booth across from us, or the lights were just oddly placed. Anyhow, we ordered the tofu pad Thai and the spicy basil chicken. The pad Thai was the better dish, and the tofu was sweet like inari. The basil chicken was lacking some spice, but still flavorful and steaming hot. My main issue was with our server. He started off fairly friendly, and later offered to refill my bf's soda. When he returned with the refill, he notified us it would be an extra charge. We told him to forget the refill not because we are cheap, but out of the principal that he didn't tell us about the up-charge before he offered it. He seemed pretty pissed and took his sweet time bringing our check by, so we had to ask someone else. Overall the food was good and the prices are reasonable, but I'm sure there's better Thai places around.
Very traditional Korean cuisine, awesome food! No wonder the place is also busy pack with people. There is always a wait, but it is worth!
This is the absolute worst malaysian food ever. On two different days, was served food that was inedible. Never could find anything I liked.

Poached egg with greek yogurt and chili oil. Best. Breakfast. Dish. Ever!! Public also has great bloody mary's and the rustic bread they serve as gratis is delicious! We avoid going anytime after 2pm, as it gets a bit too loud and a bit too sceney for our taste.

Just had brunch with my girlfriend, and I would say that the food is a 3.5 the Chill-a-Killers were really tasty, the poached eggs in the benedict were overcooked, the standout was the homemade chicken breakfast sausage that was a 5.  The staff was nice, personable and attentive, the mimosas were ok (the cucumber one wasn't for me but my girlfriend loved it), the coffee was good, overall I would give it another chance.
Every time i get delivery from here i am always disappointed. Items are always missing or incorrect and they refuse to offer a refund. Letdown...

Go here hungry, seriously! I went here with my husband while we were on vacation in Vermont and ordered the argentinian steak.  While I think the idea of cooking it yourself on a hot stone is interesting, I can say for sure I do not want to do this over and over again.  It is definitely an experience, so check it out if you are in town.  It's a very busy spot. The food was decent, the servers were kind.  The salad bar is great.   I wouldn't know this from personal experience, but trusted folks told us to skip the seafood and to not allow them to cook the steak for you.  Check it out on an empty belly :)
One tray of your meatiest meats, please.

The blueberry pancakes were above average- the rest was nothing special.  I don't think that there was anything baked on site.  The service was awful- slow, rude and unhelpful.  I found a hair in my food and asked for a replacement- they told me that it was probably mine and I should just eat it.  Imagine!  Skip this place- it's for posers.

Very, very close to being a 5-star review.  Rex REALLY impressed me when I went there a couple weeks back.  I wasn't sure what to expect going in, but the food, interior, everything was way above expectations. It's very welcoming, comfortable, quiet enough to talk in here even on a Friday night.  Obvious New Orleans feel.  Seemed like a cool crowd ranging from tattooed hipsters to button-down folks in their 50's.  Everyone seemed happy. My girlfriend and I wanted to try as many things as possible so skipped entrees, had the moules frites, chicory salad, mac and cheese, and crawfish pot pie.   The frites weren't anything spectacular (small, bit soggy) but the moules  portion of the dish, the bath in which they lay was freakin fantastic.  Big plump fellas swimming around in a pool of bacon-y pleasure.   Despite the heavy promotion on here the mac & cheese still exceeded expectations.  Crawfish and chicory were similarly way above average.  Had us talking after tasting each one of these how impressed we were at the whole experience.  Didn't leave a food baby in the stomach afterward, which is very important with rich foods like these. Service was OK.  Waited awhile to have anyone come up to us but certainly not to the level others have mentioned on here.  I definitely want to try this place again, maybe for brunch and you should too.

What an amazing experience. Thank you everyone at Gramercy Tavern for giving me and my boyfriend an unforgettable memory. Everything that we were looking for and expected was above and beyond. Customer service was the best I've ever received dining out in the city. My boyfriend, who gets easily upset by poor service was raving about Gramercy Tavern all night. As for the food we both got the prixe fixed menu. He got the beef carpaccio, lamb, and assorted cheeses while I got the spinach farfalle, sea bass, and strawberry dessert. It's was delicious, unique, and artfully plated. We received complimentary prosecco and coconut cake which were delicious. I loved that Gramercy provides top notch food and service and makes you feel comfortable without all that boujie vibe.
Absolutely awesome! Taste so so so so good!

This could have been a good experience... IF -had they not totally forgotten about us and made us get up THREE times to get service. -It was literally, here sit, here are some drinks, then waiter disappeared the whole meal. -After looking for the waiter a few times he finally sent a girl back to take our order. Food was served, and again, nobody to be seen. Got up again to get service. -The check came and we tipped based on the horrible service, a very standard tip, not even deserved at all. The waitress came back and DEMANDED a higher tip. I politely said "tipping is based on service and since you pretty much left us alone the entire time, that is what we are leaving." Never ever going back.   APALLED!
Great for drinks.  Terrible for food.

Oh. Dear. Gods. The escargot at the Blue Hill is amazing. Little tiny snails (I know, I know, and I just don't care) absolutely swimming in their individual little pots of butter and garlic. You can charge me whatever you want for a fancy French name for a gardener's hated nemesis, and I will pay it, because they are tasty. I know all you who are squeamish will think I'm crazy, but that is all right. I will eat your escargot as well. And dip my bread in the little cavern of buttery deliciousness left behind. And then I will let out my belt three notches, and vow that I will rock-climb on the morrow as punishment for my indulgence. But I won't. And that will be my secret. Also, our waitress never wavered when my friend and I told her a) we'd be ordering a bunch of appetizers instead of an appetizer and entree and b) that she was not drinking wine (a teetotaller, that girl. Madness, I tell you). I know I always got a little skeptical about my tip when those things happened, and kudos to the waitress for not letting her fear show in her service. She was a doll. Tip your waitresses well. Spread the word.

After giving it another go I would re-emphasize that it's good, but not THAT good.  It's only pizza... the Mais is delicious but really not worth $16 for such a small pizza.  I don't see what all the fuss is about.  If you like super pricey small pretentious "PIZZE" than this is the place for you.
The Avocado toast was good. Grainy, healthy and hearthy. I added an egg to it to make sure I'd get full.

The food was good, but the cockroaches were another issue.   I was with a friend, dining on the rooftop and had just finished eating when we saw a cockroach running down the tree next to our table.  Since we had another round of drinks coming, we just scooted our table away from the tree and told our waiter.  No discount, barely an apology, nothing. Then we saw another one on the ceiling, so we paid our check and took our drink inside. No sooner had we sat on the couch inside when we saw ANOTHER one running across the back of the couch behind us.  We ran out of there as fast as we could, and I have not, and will not go back.

I will always love going to this tapas restaurant. I'm a big fan of their sangria and intimate atmosphere. I highly recommend their guacamole, ajillo queso frito and paella of course! You can never go wrong with this Staten Island eatery!

1 dollar for 5 fried dumplings!!! Are you kidding me?? That's so cheap... Another hole in a wall.. If I never yelp it.. I will not enter here and eat because it's way too small where you can't find a sit and you have to get it to go.. Hands down for the best fried dumpling.. The scallion and meat combination is soooo perfect which I don't even need the chili sauce to go with it.. My friend love it as well.. One thing.. It's way too oily.. when I bite it.. the oil just drip from the meat till my hand.. which I felt a little disgusting.. but well.. I still ate them all.. BECAUSE IT'S WAY TOO GOOD!!!!

We came here for brunch and it was a fantastic meal. I tried the breakfast stromboli, which I've never had before. It was phenomenal. You could taste a hint of sourness in the dough from the yeast which complemented the egg, sausage, and spinach perfectly. We also had the lemon ricotta blueberry pancakes which were amazing, though they were served without maple syrup (but it was provided when we asked). The servers were pretty aloof as others have mentioned, but once they put the bread down in front of me, I stopped caring. Can't wait to go back.
Small family place with yummy comfort food. BYOB and enjoy!

The lunch specials are awesome, 3 rolls plus soup and salad for $10.95. They put avocado in the philly roll which is so good, the spicy tuna is on point and the shrimp tempura roll is pretty good as well. So nice to have a delivery sushi joint in Bayonne with good food. Thanks so much guys for the prompt delivery and great food!

One of the best dim sum and chinese restaurants in the city of Philadelphia.  The food is amazing and fresh, I always look forward to coming here, my go-to chinese restaurant. The soup dumplings by far are my favorite.  Juicy, tasty, and fresh.  We have tried several different dishes (scallion pancakes, shrimp dumplings,drunken noodle, spicy hot pots,mao po tofu, flounder in fish sauce, and the list goes on..) Every time I come here with my boyfriend or friends I'm never disappointed.  Being BYOB makes it even better.  Would highly recommended with friends/fun date night out!

I love how there is pretty much a vegetarian option of every dish on the menu :) (for you carnivores there's pretty much any form of meat you would want available for each dish as well). The Cantonese style Lo Mein is not the traditional american chinese style of lo mein that one would find at the typical chinese restaurant or take out spot. Instead, the Cantonese style lo mein consists of thinner egg noodles. It's still good, especially with the sauce, but be forewarned that it may be different that what you are expecting if you don't have much experience with Cantonese fare. The vegetarian dumplings are very large, and a little awkward to eat.. but some of the best I've had. The dumplings are filled with an assortment of minced asian veggies and mushrooms (not faux meat or tofu like some other places). Complementary tea is always in good taste. Not the rock bottom cheapest spot in Chinatown, but still inexpensive. I would happily frequent this spot. :)

The best ramen I have ever had. I've only tried Ren's Ramen in Maryland and by far, the miso ramen at Totto was delicious! Add corn and bamboo shoots and it's golden. My friends and I waited for 1.5 hrs... well worth the wait. I'll come back to this place when I am in NY.

We've been to this bakery several times for their deli. We used to rate the food quality as excellent but more recently it is just average. The service on the other hand has moved from above average to severally below average. Let me set the stage. There are a total of 7 workers behind the counters (it's a big and long bakery), not including those "in the back" who prep, bake, etc. 3-4 out of those 7 employees are near or at the deli area. However, only one person will actually make sandwiches, provide cold cuts, or salads. And this one individual is VERY MEAN. He doesn't acknowledge you or have any eye contact. There is a good chance this might be why other employee's won't get near or assist. He is also very slow so the line just backs up. Even though people were lined up before the 5pm cut off for the deli, he yelled at them to go away and just left. It's just unbelievable; we've seen this happen the last two times we went. We will never return or recommend this place again.
Great place to explore new beers. They have a varied selection of beers, for all tastes.  Unpretentious and pleasent. Music is good, aiming towards the mainstream but not quite there.

We ventured to the Ironbound section of Newark for rodizio, but what we left with was an experience. First the GPS led us from Jersey City through some back roads and streets that you wouldn't want to be caught by yourself after sundown. Secondly, we spotted what looked like Fernandes, but was actually the cafe/deli version of the restaurant where you could get burgers and sandwiches. This happened to be a block or two from the actual Fernandes, which was inconvenient because we had to walk a few seemingly treacherous blocks in Newark to the world famous Fernandes. I recommend parking in the fenced in parking area that they offer. Once you enter the Fernandes castle from the back, you pass through 3 massive doors that lead you through an outdoor living room into a very nice dining room budding with activity. It was just a Monday night and they were very busy, although we didn't have to wait for a table. I didn't have to think about what I was going to order, because I knew I wanted rodizio. I just looked around and at one table skewers of sausage and chicken legs were being served and at another - bacon wrapped filet mignon. My girlfriend was inexperienced in this realm, so I just ordered for her. Don't take the wait personally, because the way it works is that you are seated by the host, your order taken by your waiter, and then actually served all evening by different people that have their own roles. Meat skewers will pass you by until the servers prepare fresh rice, beans, french fries, and fried bananas. You also have access to a nice sized salad bar. Tip: don't fill up on the salad bar, you'll thank me later. Each cut of meat, whether it be the sausage, chicken, or various types of beef, were all seasoned and cooked to perfection. We had a really great time and will recommend to friends and family.

Went there for brunch: 3 in my group got the frittatas, one the cheeseburger (maybe hamburger? I forgot what he really got), and I got the waffles. Not one complaint from anyone- Frittatas were light and not too dense; cheese/hamburger was a nice hunk of meat and cooked nicely; waffles were light with perfect whipped cream to fruit ratio. Also got the pickles- I am a sucker for homemade pickles and these did not disappoint AT ALL. Service was pretty good- refills made quickly and waitress was perfect mix of attentive but not overbearing. Definitely recommend!

I feel like I just wasted $15 on lunch. I ordered the lunch red chicken curry, and it came with wonton soup. The wonton soup was great- the broth was flavorful despite being a touch salty, and the wontons were delicious. The red curry chicken- well that's a whole other story. The curry sauce was a really weird consistency- almost gelatinous, and while it was spicy, didn't have a great flavor. The chicken in it was also weird- it had a funky texture, and zero taste. There was also some green peppers, potatoes (very gummy), and eggplant. I wouldn't order Thai here again. Definitely don't get the impression it's authentic. Based on the wonton soup, if I ever gave this place a second try I might stick to the Chinese.

Outstanding visit.  Our waitress Daniel  set the bar for great service and was friendly and attentive.  Pizza was great came in for a beer devoured an entire pizza.  Came in for the Conehead IPA which is one of the best IPAs I have had in a while and was going to go home with a growler of it until I tried the Burliner Weisse with raspberries.  For me a near perfect beer and based the the flavor profile was amazed it only came in at 2.9% ABV.  If you love craft beer you need to come.  Love pizza ever more reason.
Mango Chutney sauce

The best Italian Hot Dog in the world. Been eating them since I could walk. The potaoes and the roll is the key to this dog, many have come close with the dog portion and the onions and peppers but noone has the bread and potatoes! Awesome!

AMAZING! Went here for restaurant week. The asian pork was melt in your mouth . Wasabi mashed potatoes and edamame ravioli are def a must! The Flavors hit every spot imaginable. Plate Presentation was beautiful n to top it off  Service Was impeccable!

African falafel sandwich is good, but wish it were packed a little more. French fries are OK, kind too crispy for my preference and pricey for $3.25. I like this place but I won't go out of my way for it. Maoz's salad bar is still one of my favorites.

Bad. Just bad, in every way possible. I understand this is the first day, and things take time to settle in. But they didn't even stumble out of the gate, they face-planted in the starting block. The food? A joke. I ordered a create-your-own stir fry dish with: egg noodles, bamboo shoots, bok choy, tofu, and spicy garlic sauce. The noodles had the distinct consistency of Ramen noodles, which isn't necessarily awful, except when you consider that my order cost me $11. The bok choy? In about 3/4 of a lb of noodles, I had 6 small pieces. The tofu? Maybe, mayyybbeee, a quarter cup of it, if I'm being generous. The bamboo shoots? Couldn't tell you, they forgot them. The sauce was actually fairly spicy, but wasn't anything special. The wait? 40 minutes. This is a 'good food fast' concept, except they forgot the fast. The layout for the workers makes about as much sense as nipples that double as bright pink highlighters. Everyone is tripping over each other, and no one knows what they are doing. The touch screen ordering system is brand-spankin-new, and is already having issues. I know this, because in the time i stood around waiting, I got to observe them plenty. Sanitary? Nope. Some of the staff didn't have gloves on, and were grabbing the salad items with their bare hands. There isn't much raw meat or anything going around, and the place is clean because it is brand new, but I saw people picking up trash/refuse, and then diving into a salad. Oh, and I forgot to mention, it wasn't stir-fry. It is called stir-fry, but the only correlation with stir-fry is that some of the ingredients were cooked in a wok. The noodles were boiled and placed directly into the dish. The ingredients (the ones they remembered) were cooked in a wok, mixed with sauce, and placed on top. By the time I got back to the office, the noodles had fused into a solid mass. Two of my co-workers went with me, and both of their lunches were just as bad. One got an on-the-menu noodle dish (of which he had the same complaint about the noodles, and his beef was very fatty and chewy) and the other got a salad (it came with the wrong greens, and without 3 of the 6 toppings...and it cost $12). The upshot: They went 0 - 3 with our meals, and first-hand I saw three people give up and leave and 4 return their meals. Everything is overpriced, and the service time is awful. The processing time will most likely improve as the staff learns how to do their job properly, but the food is still not going to be worth it.

I dined here a few years.  Recently I went back there for a friend's birthday dinner.  I was excited to have the Black Label Burger again, but to my surprise- -  Price of the burger went up (now $28). -  The burger was much smaller than what I remembered.  I couldn't finish it the first time I had it. This experience was quite a disappointment in paying so much for something that I can easily get half the cost elsewhere and much tastier.   This place is now overrated and you are better off going unless you want to try their souffle.

Given that I rarely venture out in the lower east side or the east village, I was pleasantly surprised to dine at this place. Small restaurant but cozy. Amazing drinks, and very good food. Will be back for sure, and would recommend it to my friends. Also, service was very good. Our waiter was very attentive and willing to surprise us and our guests with awesome drinks choices.
OMG THEY"VE OPENED FOR DINNER, Couple of nights a week!!!  YAY!!!
Great gumbo and catfish po boy. Good service and good tunes. Highly recommend this New Orleans spot! I'm definitely going back.

A wonderful brunch place that has beautiful decor. I've visited twice in the past month.  First visit on the morning of a weekday and the second time at noon on a Sunday.  Were able to get a table on Sunday pretty quickly considering the time we arrived. The eggs Benny and French toast were very tasty. The pancakes and fresh fruit are average - nothing amazing about them.  The coffee was delicious. Our waiter was very attentive each time. This is a great cozy place for a tasty brunch at a GREAT price!!

First off, so glad that places like this exist.  For those who only want to put real food into their bodies, this is a great spot to have around. I am, however, a little surprised that they used ice in my $7 juice.  Really?  The juice is small enough and they're watering it down with ice?  I'm okay with paying a premium for high quality food items.... but I'm not okay paying a premium for watered-down high quality food.   In my experience, it's not "the norm" to put ice in juice.  I'd prefer my juice to be room temperature (like normal), anyway, and got a headache from drinking it cold.  Wish they would have asked.

After a horrible experience at a little byo (cuban petes-DONT DO IT)...in montclair, we came here, as a "sure thing." Cheesecake Factory, always is that "sure thing" ... the food was great, service was good, and the night was enjoyable! Your chicken dishes rock and the steak Diane ....YUM! Always recommend!
4 stars for food 1 star for the service but nothing says 'sorry' like 4 free desserts! if you come here, you must get the octopus salad

Not much to say about pie-n-thighs that hasn't already been said. Chicken box is off the chain, and my discovery of chicken and waffles here has certainly increased my cholesterol 10 fold. Cheese grits were on point, and the biscuit was not only gigantic, but delicious as well. The sour cherry pie was a nice finish on an outstanding meal. I would subtract half a star if I could because they do not take reservations, which I so desperately want for Mother's Day. Will return soon.
Food was awesome. Service was great. Pricey but worth it! Deff would come again.
second time here still same consistency !! service food ambience!!! caroline the mg was so helpfull and atentive !!  segio is the bes mixologist ever!!! i really wanna try brunch!!
sheep's milk ricotta & Uovo pizza & garlic pork loin & salted caramel budino for two!!! Can't be more satisfied and full!!!
They deliver, serve great chicken, and are very friendly.  In Newark can you ask for more?

Mouse in the house!  My wife and I went there for dinner this evening.  We sat in the back corner next to the corner table against the wall.  A couple sat next to us...it looked like their first date.  All of the sudden the guy just got up on the back lounge chair and stood on top of the lounge chair.  His dated looked at him like he had two heads.  He didn't say a word....he just looked all around the floor like aliens was going to attack him.  Everyone was staring but he didn't say a word.  He finally came back down to earth and softly said....I saw a mouse run over my shoe.   Yikes!  All the patrons around him freaked out....I must admit I was laughing at his dates reaction.  She rolled her eyes and said I thought your shoes were on fire or something.  Needless to say I don't think he made a good impression with her....lol. Not cool when your date stands on top of the chair looking like a fraidy cat.  lol..... Now....back to the rodent.  I'm actually calm knowing that this is a problem with many NYC restaurant kitchens.  What was NOT cool was when the Matre'D came over and said well.....sometimes mice comes in, we can't help it.  Basically there was no urgency in his voice, it was biz as usual.  Also none of the waiters seemed fazed.  The couple relocated to another table but that lack of urgency is solving the problem leads me to suspect that there are lots of mice.....and they see it often. In terms of the food, I've been to this restaurant more than several times.  The food is great but they simply use too much salt.  Each time we ask for low salt, it seems like they put even more salt. I'll think we'll take a pass for a little while until they clear up the rodent problem.  I hope Management will take the problem seriously.

I read the reviews, trying to prepare myself for what to expect at Momo Sushi. I was still so off. So, let me preface this review by saying, it did not live up to my expectations. I really did not like the dim red lighting... at all. Maybe I have sensitive eyes, but it just started to hurt my eyes after awhile. Also, it didn't make the food look any more appetizing to me. I don't know about most people, but when I'm paying for a dining experience, I like to inspect my food and observe the overall aesthetic, color, presentation, and design of what I'm about to eat... but maybe that's just me. Now, onto the sushi: it was good, but I've definitely had better. And the complaints from other reviewers about the dry/stale rice? So spot on. We ordered the lamb curry as well, and the rice was crunchy to say the least. I don't get it-- why??? I also don't like the idea of sitting at a picnic table next to people I don't know. Sitting in tight small quarters with strangers is something I am not accustomed to... and I tend to get claustrophobic quite easily, so again, maybe that's just me. The server was nice, but I had to hail him down a few times to refill our waters... and that's not easy to do when it's dark, unless you have a glowstick or something to wave at him. Overall, I'd grade them between a 'meh' and an A-OK. I think people who like Momo Sushi are more into the concept of what they offer (in terms of "hipster" ambiance and a twist on the traditional sushi roll). It's not for everybody... it certainly wasn't for me.

Very anti-climatic after reading all the hype. Good for a one time gimmick, but not much more than that. The fries are OK; not bad, but not great either. The "double" frying thing really produced no noticible difference in the quality of the fries other than making quite a few of them overcooked. The sauces were very ordinary too. Halfway through the meal, we both said that the fries at a place like McDonalds would have been better. We also got a small poutine (a Canadian dish), which was very unique. Basically it's fries, gravy and fermented cheese. Very flavorful, but a tad on the heavy side. I wouldn't run back for it either now that I think about it. In the end, Pommes Frites is about average I guess. I suppose not every place is a life changing experience.

it was interesting to eat food inspired by australia and south-east asia. lots of drinks and menu items you probably won't see anywhere else in the city. having had a large selection of their dishes, i found it to be very hit or miss. my main gripe was just a general lack of refinement, which perhaps could be expected, as the head chef was not there that night. it was the type of thing where there seemed to be a good amount of consideration in conceptually balancing the various elements of a dish, but when you eat it, you find there to be too much acid or not enough salt, etc. my favorites were the kobe beef tongue and the shiso wrapped fried oyster. helpful staff

Well I'll be damned, not since Purple Yam in Brooklyn did a Filipino restaurant get 5 stars from me! My standards are understandably high when it comes to Filipino restaurants. After all, I'm Filipino, I'm a foodie, and I can cook a lot of Filipino dishes. So for me to dine at a Filipino restaurant it would have to be either because I'm with someone I'm trying to introduce the cuisine to, or if I'm craving something that I can't easily make myself. So over the years I've tried different Filipino spots and I either leave disappointed, unimpressed, or thinking 'yes that was good but not quite 5 star worthy'. So I've heard of Maharlika since it first started making waves in the village and my brother even had dinner here while he was visiting some time ago. But it wasn't until my bf decided to take advantage of a howaboutwe deal for brunch that I found myself at Maharlika's tiny East Village digs. First I have to say something in response to my brother's review.. The setting isn't swanky. This is your average village casual look. I do, however, like how they named each item on the menu using famous Filipino folks. Speaking of the food, my bf and I ordered the sisig, which everyone raves about and my bf really wanted to try after remembering the sisig at Pig and Khao, and the Eggs Imelda. Both are extremely good! And the sisig is quite authentic. But I was more than impressed with the Eggs Imelda. It's their take on Eggs Benedict.. So pan de sal instead of English muffins topped with laing (OMG!) topped with poached eggs. It comes along with some green salad, sweet potatoes, and head on prawns! So awesome in so many ways! First of all, I would never in million years think to combine laing with eggs Benedict! Laing is a regional dish from Bicol that is taro leaves cooked in coconut milk and peppers.
