And I haven't had it in years! Well Maharlika not only put it together in this crazy combination but they made it work! For this alone they get 5 stars! And did I mention the sisig was excellent? We washed these down with their champagne cocktails. We tried the guava, kalamansi, and mango versions. My bf loved the mango and I loved the kalamansi. So yes brunch was amazing! I'm definitely gonna put this on top of my brunch list when I go out for brunch with friends. Oh, make sure you make reservations though since the line can be pretty long. Lastly, the staff were very nice and friendly event though they were super busy. Can't wait to come back again!
The Smith was recommended to me by a co-worker.  I met friends there for breakfast and we al loved it.  The food was amazing and the service was great.  I would go back again.

I soooooo love this place!....everything smells so good and there is something for everyone. Sometimes, I just want to walk through just to smell the food without purchasing anything lol. If your bringing people in from town to Philly, this would be a great spot to hit because there is something for everyone there.
really nice wine bar all i can said amazing they was so friendly i was really impressed  im going back there for sure my roommate she tell me abut this place  i really love it wow

I have been to this place several times and have always enjoyed the experience. We keep going back and dragging our skeptical friends because the food is so awesome! The menu is divided into Indian, Nepalese and Tibetan vegetarian and non-veg. So there are plenty of options for your more hesitant friends. I personally love and always order from the Nepalese section - the food reminds me of a cross between Indian and Chinese cuisine (though that doesn't do proper justice to the interesting layers comprised in Nepalese food). It's quite spicy but that makes me even more of a fan! If you go, do give the samayabajee (non veg or veg) a try - it's always a hit with our friends - a great intro to the cuisine considering you try crushed rice with several sides (comprising dried sauteed and spiced soy beans and other curried items). One more thing - the Nepalese band that covers Beatles songs and old Indian/Nepalese songs on Fridays and Saturdays is pretty awesome! They take requests and add a fun twist to your evening. Please do give this spot a try - you won't regret it!

I've heard a lot of good things about Vanessa's Dumpling House but I wish most of them were true. I've tried most of the dumpling in or around Chinatown and their dumplings are good at best but normally adequate. When I go to a dumpling house, I'm going to judge them on their dumplings despite having a menu of over 20 items. The skin is too thick, the filling is too dry and there is very little crisp to the skin. Their other hot item, the sesame pancake with your choice of meat, is meh. For better food go to Prosperity Dumpling 2 blocks away though Vanessa has better decor and a large sitting area, that is if you can find an empty seat, if that's important to you.

I worked very close to El Fuego and probably one of the only Mexican places in downtown Philly. Food - 4 I could somewhat compare it to Chipotle. Its pretty good. They give you a choice of Chicken, Spicy Beef or Steak. I have tried all 3 and are very good. Only thing to keep in mind is that the spicy beef is very juicy so it may make your burrito soggy. Atmosphere/Customer Service - 2-3 Beware! If you coming during lunch time, it gets very busy where there is no room to stand. I would usually have take my meal 'to-go' because of there are never any seats open. I like how the line moves fast but the down side is that the noise level is loud and its very difficult to hear the people who make your food. I have had occasions where the person is very rude because they can't hear you and vice versa. They should take the time to understand what the customer is saying and turn the music down so they don't mistakes in your order.

I went there after work with my coworker, I was craving for some Sushi. My friend had a Ramen Noodle which she said was good. I had the Shrimp Tempura...oooo myyy myyy, never had it before & it was DELICIOUS! The place is cute.

Wow! Food was absolutely amazing. I started with the hamachi tartare, which was good, but not outstanding. Probably wouldn't order again. Then had the tagliatelle bolognese which was most excellent. The pasta was so fresh and was definitely homemade. I ordered the cod as my entree and WOW, i was blown away. The cod was perfectly made, not too rare and not too cooked. The fish was served on top of manhattan clam chowder and was the perfect compliment. I ordered a "glass" of pinot grigio and regretted it since it was $14 and was less than half a glass. Overall, I can't wait to go back, but maybe next time I will go with drinkers and order a bottle of wine instead!
Update to my review: we've since been back and they've switched to some more traditional music, which gives the place an authentic, relaxed feel. Food?  Still hitting it out of the park!

Props to this place for introducing me to avocado toast. Thick avocado spread with some chili pepper, and lime (albeit, a little too much lime) over a slice of toast? Genius and simple. Definitely doing this more often. Couscous with side of sausage. Large portioned and very unique flavoring. Still enjoyed this place. Quick Tips: Cash only Super small place, so get in early or expect to wait!

On a Friday afternoon before going on a helicopter tour of Manhattan, we headed down to the West Village to try out Fish.  We were so excited after seeing their menu on their website. Food: 4.0 stars The oysters were so fresh and the RED WHITE AND BLUE special makes them a bargain (for a big city seafood restaurant).  We got the Lobster Roll too which was delicious but overpriced for what we got.  The Lobster Roll is more of Lobster Salad Sandwich than other more conventional Lobster Rolls.  Still, the seafood here is so fresh and delicious. Service: 3.0 stars Service was standard.  Nothing to Yelp home about. Location: 3.5 stars Located in the heart of the West Village. Ambiance: 3.5 stars The restaurant was not what we expected from the website.  It is more of a local seafood eatery than a restaurant.  Still the charm of the restaurant and its humble attitude make it a great place to have a delicious meal. Price: 3.5 stars The oysters and RED WHITE AND BLUE special is a great deal.  The sandwiches are definitely over priced though.  Expect to pay $10-20 per person. Overall: 3.5 stars Definitely a great spot to go get lunch if you are in the mood for some delicious oysters and seafood.  While we really enjoyed our lunch, we couldn't help but be a little let down in comparison to how excited we were coming into the village for lunch.  Still, definitely a great place to try.

Good quality food.  It completely hits the spot when I'm craving something that my abuela used to make.  The veggie burrito is huge and worth the money.  The food takes a while, so if you're in a rush, I would call ahead.  But it's worth the wait.  They are closed on Mondays.

A great place to go if you want to get ripped off.  Have ordered deli sandwiches, like ham or salami, on hard roll a couple times now.  Hardly put on any meat or cheese.  Like, seriously pathetic amounts.  Scant tomato, and one tiny slice of onion. Can you spare it!? Have had other things here, that were good (like chicken parm or buffalo chicken sandwiches).   But I hate the feeling of being ripped off.  Especially since it has happened to me more than once.  For six  and change, expect more than a salami and cheese slider.

Oh, yes, this place lived up to the hype.  The macarons here are good.  The service is excellent.  I went during lunchtime on a weekday and there was absolutely no line.  There is a framed display in the front with pictures of the macarons and their flavors.  I just wished there were little tags next to each macaron selection behind the glass with the names of the flavors instead of having to refer back to the single main picture.  They also offer limited time special flavors not found on this menu that need to be explained by the salesperson.  It can get annoying trying to decide what you want if there is a huge line.  The salesperson helping me was very attentive and patient with explaining the different flavors.  I also bought a financier and a madeleine cookie.  I wasn't so sure about the financier at first because it had such a hard exterior.  My mind was changed after one bite.  The interior was soft and flavorful.  Definitely better than those I've had at Financier Patisserie but it does come at double the price.  The madeleine was good and on par with those from other stores.  I'd still say that La Maison du Macaron is my favorite place for macarons.  They seem to have more of the plain fruitful flavors that I like (e.g. mango, strawberry, blood orange, passion fruit) whereas Laduree has more unique flavors (e.g. rose petal, strawberry & mint, black currant & violet).  Maison is also a more convenient location for me and a quick walk from the F train.

GET THE TRUFFLE BURGER. Went on a Friday night with a friend around 6:15ish after work; totally expected a wait but was so happy when I heard "5 minutes". Yes. I guess we made it right before the dinner rush because when we were seated, a swamp of people came in. I got the truffle burger ($12.50) and my friend got the cali burger ($12... she said it was amazing). People always ask me whether Shake Shack had the best burger and I always thought it was overrated (shake shack is awesome but definitely not the best burgers ever). This truffle burger is the best burger I've ever eaten. The meat was so juicy, tender, and the sauce.. savory and heavenly. Makes my mouth water thinking about it. And the buns. The Portuguese-styled buns. Toasty, soft, and a little bit sweet. AMAZING. The sweet potato fries ($4) wasn't the best I ever had but that's not to say it wasn't great accompanying my burger. The sauces that it comes with are good compliments to the fries. Service is not bad. The guy was pretty nice but kind of looked "whatever" about his job. But the burger doe. That's what earned the 5 stars. We also wanted the donut ice cream sandwich for dessert but they said they never got the shipment so they didn't have it. A must try for next time.

I've been here a few times. The staff is friendly. The chocolate chip cookies are the best coffee shop snacks around. The coffee is very good though today's tasted a bit burnt so they don't get that 5th star that might have been theirs.

Yes the food is consistent and the beer selection is great but can you over look staff with attitude and waiting forever for your check only to find out they lost your credit card?? We called ahead and were told the wait was 15 to 20 minutes and put our name on the list.  Once we got there we were told it would be 35 minutes.  Our pager went off around that time but when we got to the desk was told there was a miscommunication but would be given the next table. OK, no problem. So we stood right in front of them and watched them proceed to give the next table to another group. When we questioned them we were told "I am not going to explain our system to you". Well, obviously your system doesn't work but moreover, don't lie to me. I said I would be speaking to the manager and she said she was one.  Of course we knew better so we spoke to the main manager while we were endlessly waiting for the check.  Let me say at this point we were pretty happy; the food and drinks were good and the server was very attentive.  After coming back and after waiting yet another 5 minutes for the check to come back, the hostess came up and was saying how dare you say something about me and my people - I'm not charging you for the meal. I wasn't looking for a free meal and wasn't insulting her staff, just her for lying to our faces,  really I just wanted to know where my credit card was. Well,  they had no idea. I had to cancel the card before I left and also left behind my loyalty card.  We used to be really big fans but won't be going back again.

I ran into these guys at a pop-up by Madison Square Park and had their fried chicken sittin' pretty in a generously buttered up, fresh out of the oven buttermilk biscuit. It was insanity, so I got a second one, which says something because they baked the biscuits as they went so each one takes anywhere from 5-15 minutes to make, depending on their inventory. It might not be the same sitch at the brick and mortar.

I was walking on Hudson this morning and was attracted by this lovely lovely cow outside of Bubby's and decided to go inside for a sit-down breakfast to embrace a sunny Friday morning, and oh boy was I in for a surprise. This place is SERIOUSLY over-priced. The cheapest breakfast item (excluding the sides and drinks) on the menu was $7 and that's just California Grits, and the Oatmeal here is even $9. I thought to myself, oh well, if the food is good, it's worth it. So, I ordered the Jalapeno Chedder Scrambles with multi-grain toast and home fries and a cup of coffee.  It took about 15 minutes for them to prepare my plate and when it was finally brought to me, everything just looked very average. Took a bite, and I was angry at that cow. This place sucks, not only it's pricey but the food also sucks; those scrambles did not go well with the white chedder, the toast was way too over-toasted for me, and I could totally do without the home fries....so bland so bland...I almost had to dump half bottle of ketchup and black pepper to down my breakfast; ok, that's a bit of an exaggeration, but WTH?! Anyway, the scramble eggs were $16 and the coffee was $4 and everything was bland, to say the least. Seriously I could spend $25-ish on dinner in a lot of places and have a way more amazing meal than this BREAKFAST. ::Shake Heads::  Don't think I'll be back. PS: Service was actually okay, but apparently this place can get really crowded; many TriBeca parents take their kids here for breakfast and I had to sit through several screaming sessions towards the end of my meal. :::sigh:::

This place was too hyped up by yelp reviews.  I had the Akamara Modern and the broth was good but way less than the amount of noodles. The service was a little pushy, with 4 different staff members asking every 5 minutes if I'm still working on my ramen. That was annoying--do not say, "take your time" when you're gonna ask every few minutes if I'm done eating. Also the server did not know the difference between having separate bills and splitting the bill, I mean how could you work in food service and not know that? To be honest, this place doesn't even compare to Totto Ramen which has about the same length of wait time to get a table, better quality and flavor ramen, plus more appropriate portions and pricing.

Didn't realize they had a C rating until my friend and I walked out of the restaurant.. Oops. Aside from that (I can't worry too much about it, what's done is done and I didn't get sick): Pro: affordable, good vegetarian options, cool decor, seated fast on a Saturday night. Con: were rushed by (occasionally rude) wait staff, only 2 bathrooms for a huge restaurant, pretty sure they use MSG. I had the Tom Kha soup with vegetables and Basil Fried Rice with mock duck. The soup was very good, a lot of fresh vegetables in non greasy broth. The main dish was good, but very intensely flavored/salty in an unnatural way. Not only that, I also had a massive headache for the rest of the night. So I'm pretty sure they use artificial flavor enhancers and I'm really not a fan of those. I would probably not come back here. Because of the C rating, because they were really rushing us and when we asked for a dessert menu instead they brought us the check (needless to say, they missed out on us buying a dessert) and because if you know how to cook food properly there is really no need for MSG.
good

Cute and cozy I recommend this little place to anyone and everyone. My buddy Harvey did the ordering which is always a grand slam. We started with Thai dumplings, curry puffs and a very unique appetizer "Thai Tacos." To my knowledge they don't exist anywhere else. Their culinary creativity is on a whole new level. We then had the Pad Thai, noodles are always a hit but, these noodles were out of the ballpark. If you're as advantageous as I am, check out Topaz in Belleville, NJ.

Came here for dinner and was a big fan. The place is small and cosy with sidewalk seating. It was quality Brazilian food that was well prepared. I have yet to try the brunch but I can see how this place can get packed. The food is well prepared and I had zero issues with the service. Then again I also ate late @ 10pm when busienss was slower. Both plates we had (filet minon and moqueca) were simple yet very good.
The 2nd was better than the 1st. No pork extravaganza yet. Instead the prixe fix lunch with all fish. Excellent albeit the vegetables on the trout would have worked better less charred.

I wasn't really impressed. I ordered the crispy fish salad, which had too much citrus for my liking, and I thought the corn nuts did not go well in the salad.  I tried my special lady friend's avacado salad with wahoo fish, hers was a bit better, more thought out.   The server seemed like she was new, and didn't really know what she was doing.  She seemed to get confused by our orders, didn't know which beer was which and just set them all down on the table, and the appitizer came out with the entrees.  I dislike when restaurants use food runners to bring out food and then you never see the server again.  I don't like asking the food runner for drinks or utensils but there was no one else around.

Once in a while, nothing will satisfy, save for gross quantities of meat.  In these cases, avoid Braza and visit Brazil Grill.  I would take very little from the prepared foods, and very much from the meat skewers.  The bonus is that you can get all the meat you want at once.  And while it's priced by the pound, you'll pay about 1/3 what you will at Braza...unless you can put away four pounds of meat. The meat is well and simply prepared.  Good meat needs but salt.  This is good meat. And the guy who runs the place is ultra friendly.  Unlike the management of Braza, who seem to have undergone some sort of frontal lobotomy pact.  Have a grape soda or have a beer.  Here's to the good life!
The best fries in the New Haven area. Very creative menu and great drink options as well. Go check it out.

The restaurant has a very cool atmosphere.. goes well with the name. There was nothing really special about the food. An okay selection of beer. The place wasn't a bad experience, but missing that wow factor. It's worth another chance, but not my first place I'd go to for dinner.

Definitely one of my go to places to eat when it comes to pizza!  Rich in flavor, you can tell the ingredients used are top quality.  As soon as you walk in, you want to try one of everything! Go for the Buffalo mozzarella, it is DELICIOUS.  Not your ordinary pizza place, if you want to try something different and guaranteed good, this is your spot!

We lucked out and got outside of this spot 10 minutes before they opened for dinner service. Before we knew it there was a line down the block...so make sure you come early! We were seated right away. The inside is modern with a communal type seating. We ordered the soft shell crab special appetizer they had. It actually tasted like it was over seasoned...the flavors were just a bit much. I tend to prefer soft shell crab fried and this one was not. I got the spicy ramen and I absolutely loved it....not to mention it was a cold and rainy NYC night. It was a huge bowl and piping hot. The broth was so flavorful and not overpowering with the spice at all!

I ordered here from seamless, which states a 45-60 minute wait.  After waiting 80 minutes, I finally called and was put on hold for 5 minutes so that they could "check the kitchen for my order".  During that time, two different people picked up and put me on hold again.  When the person finally came back to discuss my order, he stated it was heading out the door now (as if to imply freshness).  I received my order 15-20 minutes later and it was COLD (ok, not cold, but lukewarm, which is really pretty cold).  I tried reheating in the oven and while my quesadillas were tasty, everything else was terrible.  I will never order from here, again.  By the way, a $2.00 side of guacamole is literally 2 tablespoons in a very little dixie cup.  NEVER again!

I thought I wrote a review for this, but I guess not. One of my fav thai spots. Inexpensive, yummy and consistant. Came a couple of time for lunch and dinner. The lines are really long for friday/saturday dinner. So when I want to go on a weekend I usually go for lunch. The menu items generally looks the same with the choice of chicken/beef/ seafood and vegetables. What I usually get here is the calamari, pad thai, and the curry dishes. I haven't tried a dish that was bad. They have a back yard patio for the summer time but I must warn you to not sit back there because there are misquotes lurking everywhere.. Ended up with 3 bites after dinner on a nice summer day last yr. So I don't sit there anymore. I will visit it again.

The food is solid for late night cart, don't get me wrong, but it is identical to multiple other Halal carts in the area. If there isn't a line, step right up... But if there is a line go down the block

I go to this Nyonya in Chinatown as well as the one in 8th Avenue in Brooklyn. Both are wonderful and serve delicious food! I LOVE THE ROTI CANAI! If you go to Nyonya, order one! It's so good. I could eat a whole bunch myself but I'm a lady... sort of. ^_~ My friends and I (5 of us!) ordered 3 Roti Canai to share and trust me, the moment our waitress set them down, there was no talking... just us devouring them like the hungry fiends we were. Just so that it doesn't seem like I only go there for the Roti Canai, I actually do eat their other food. I love the Indian Mee Goreng, the Fried Pearl Noodles and the Mee Siam is good too! As for meals that you can share family-style, you can't go wrong with some Hainanese chicken and Chinese watercress with preserved bean curd. The Spicy Thai chicken was oily and not spicy. I enjoyed the cucumbers on that dish more then the chicken. Also, the Sizzling Seafood Combination Delight was a disappointment. It came in this not-so-tasty semi-clear gunky sauce, the plate was not sizzling (and I know sizzling) and the seafood was mediocre.

Great place to go for a quick lunch or happy hour. I have been here three times and love the laid back atmosphere and the friendly wait staff (especially Henry). The grill breads and wings are great for sharing and paired with the fun cocktails makes for an awesome happy hour.  The burgers are also fabulous. Look forward to trying more menu items.

Read all about it...This Nook (no words); is a great little spot in Hell's Kitchen! Food is delish...Great friendly Service! Strongly recommend making a reservation & taking advantage of the BYOB, (A huge+)...also Bring cash, they don't take credit cards.. I've been twice now & they were extremely time conscious & got us out in time for the curtain! We Sat in the Window...people watching was priceless!

It felt very much like a large brasserie you would find in Paris.  Some of the negatives mentioned in earlier Yelp posts seem to have been ironed out over time.   Pros: Interior is very well done, they took special care with the details. The food is very good! I especially enjoyed the onion soup, steak-frites, salmon and trout amandine (whose haricots verts [greenbeans] were to die for!) Cons:  Loud, though I found this actually lent to the restaurant's atmosphere. The wine carafes are not that great, choose something else from the wine list.  Pricey (not bad by fine dining standards, but another place I can't really afford).

Just plain, uncomplicated happiness is what comes to mind when I think of Great Jones Cafe. I've met two friends of mine here for dinners on occasional Sundays over the last several years (they are fanatics about the chili and always order it). The honey-drenched corn bread is very good. Last night I had a huge mess of pulled pork sandwich that was very, very tasty. Love the hamburger. Wouldn't turn down an offer to have an oyster po' boy here, ever. It's a small place. Sometimes way too small for the overflow crowd that shows up, but it wouldn't be the same if they ever expanded (hope they don't). They have a small, little bar that I've enjoyed sitting at, too, although I almost never come here just for the bar. One time, though, I remember having a pint of something (Stella, maybe) and watching the cook whip up some of their fine meals through a window behind the bar. A sentimental favorite and more.

I love falafel and Mamoun's is a great spot to get my fix. Their falafel sandwiches are great and a major steal at $2.50. I've also had the shawarma, hummus, and baba ganouj - all of which are delicious! I only recently discovered that they are open super late. That is probably my favorite thing about this place. Give me fresh hot falafels after a long night of drinking and I'm in heaven.

Amazing food, service, and atmosphere.  Bottom line: pretty good. My beau and I walked in (without reservations) on a Sunday night, 8pm, and they were eager to accommodate - a few minutes at the bar and a few wine tastings* later, we had a table. The menu selection is small, but varied (didn't see any vegetarian option, not that I was looking), and I recognized an Asian-influence immediately: baby bok choy, oyster sauce, pork belly.  Fortunately, I wouldn't consider it Asian-fusion.  Here's how our meal broke down: Appetizers: - Spicy duck meatballs were delicious; note: they're itty bitty meatballs. - Peekytoe crab cake was subtle and refined.  A must have! Mains: - Hanger steak (with the infamous sunchoke creamed spinach) was amazing.  Cooked medium, it was perfection; tender, juicy, flavorful.  The side of spinach and mushrooms were complimentary. - Summer ravioli was good, though our least favorite of the night. - Side of baby bok choy and chinese broccoli was flavorful and a perfect reminder of the Asian-influence mentioned earlier. Dessert: - Raspberry-Apricot Melba was delectable. - Lemon Fennel Donuts were to DIE for! Sweet, warm, and with a gooey center. This is a great 'date' restaurant, cozy atmosphere, however, the seating doesn't allow for much privacy. Overall, the service was awesome - very attentive, knowledgeable, and not overbearing. *The bartender (Erin?) was plain awesome.  She let us try wines without any hesitation and quite knowledgeable as well.  We only tried the 'by the glass' wines (which could have been a bit more affordable though). Spicy duck meatballs: 4 stars Service: 6 stars! Having Harold actually cook for us, in the kitchen: priceless!  But I'll get a photo-op with you one of these days! Caught Wylie Dufresne (WD~50) having dinner here on our way out!  Cool!

Went here on a late Sunday morning. If we had gone to sabrina's around the same time there would have been at least an hour long wait, this place had plenty of room. The food was great, great option for beverage as well, although the beverage option may be slightly overpriced. Great service. Has a decent dinner menu as well.

I had the ranchero benedicts, they were ok, not as good as I expected, after reading the reviews. I am not a big eater but I have to say it wasn't a big portion, and it was expensive. I wouldn't go back. Food was good but not great, and too expensive for a lunch.
Just like back home in Hilo! love the Kalua pork and the Teri burger, just needs Poi to be perfect.  Ka maika'i nua, Ono grinds!

Wonderful place!  What a special and unusual meal. Small bistro atmosphere and great personal service. Our waitress took great care of our large group and the owner even brought out an extra plate of eggplant to share. The food was all excellent - I tried a bit of at least 7 or 8 dishes. My favorites were the Thai cocoanut shrimp and the steak topped with melted Gorgonzola and dried shiitake mushrooms. Other reviewers need to understand that tapas are small plates, so for a full meal you should order 2 or 3 plates. This is great place to spend a special evening!

LIC Market is a restaurant that is so charming, clever and delicious that you can't help but adore it and hope for its success!  For the caliber of food and service, it absolutely deserves to be much busier than it currently is!  Go now before everyone else finds out!!! Everything I've sampled so far has been reasonably priced and delicious: 1. "Liver & Eggs" ($15) - I'm not sure you can get much more decadent than a plate of creamy scrambled eggs in extra virgin olive oil with cubes of foie gras generously sprinkled all over it.  It takes full and absolute focus to make eggs this way, stirring constantly, ensuring a smooth creaminess and textural consistency.  It's not the largest plate ever, but then I'm not sure I could have survived a larger portion.  This was just right for pure indulgence 2. Braised Slab Bacon ($10) - To complete my breakfast, I ordered the slab bacon.  I was also swayed when our waitress mentioned that the chef LOVES this dish.  It was delicious.  Not the standard type of bacon, this is slow cooked and incredibly juicy.  A lot of the fat melts away to become a decadent sauce/gravy/juice that you can dip your bread in.  It's a HUGE piece of bacon, so I'd suggest sharing this with others if you find it on the menu.  I could be happy just eating this and a baguette 3. Market Burger ($12) - I had a few bites of my friend's perfectly cooked (medium rare), juicy, high quality meat with melted cheddar and a dollop of aioli on a carmelized onion bun.  My conclusion: this was one helluva tasty burger and the truffled oyster mushroom hash was in constant danger of being mooched (by ME!!!) 4. Risotto ($13) - I understand that the ingredients change depending on the availability of seasonal ingredients, but I enjoyed the version with apples, onions and blue cheese and found it innovative and unexpectedly delicious! 5. Seared Mushrooms ($5) - a solid size portion with ample garlic and a sprinkle of fresh thyme and toasted almonds 6. Oyster Mushroom Hash ($7) - if you aren't already getting this with a burger, you'll absolutely want to order a side of this delicious truffle-y treat! 7. Brussels Sprouts ($5) - expertly carmelized and tossed with bacon and figs!  Sweet and salty and smoky and slightly bitter all at once! 8. & 9. Upon recommendation from our waitresses, we got a sweet finish in the form of the Crème Caramel and Apple Crisp.  Both were comforting and rich and I was really tempted to commandeer both for my personal consumption!  As you can imagine, there was nothing left to take home! Parting Thought: I desperately wish I could go to LIC Market for lunch!  LIC office workers - I hope you realize how lucky you are to have LIC Market in the hood!!!  No matter what, I'm definitely hitting LIC Market up for brunch!

Honest to God, the BEST Italian food in New Jersey! The chefs passion for food comes alive on the plate. My personal favorite is the selection of homemade pastas. No matter which one you try, you will not be disappointed. And I absolutely love how everyone who works there has a hand in the food prep. Truly an enjoyable experience, well worth the drive (I drive forty minutes)! One piece of advice, make a reservation or you may have a very long wait.

Yes it sure is cheap.  Under 5 bucks for a very good sized sandwich. The flavor didn't at all blow me away.  It was mostly bread - very crusty, crispy type not too flavorful bread.  I got half spicy.  Probably should have made it all spicy to give it more flavor. The problem was there was so little pork and veggie filling inside that this makes it a sandwich I would never return for. Looong wait.  Nice older man working there though.

Went to Tinto tonight for restaurant week. Great rosat sparkling wine. As for the apps., the two cheeses we tried were excellent. The chorizo was tasty but accompanying egg salad was bland and added nothing to the dish. The salad with serrano ham, figs and goat cheese with a citrus dressing was fantastic. For the second course, the hangar steak brochettes were very tasty and tender. The sea bass tasted fishy and the cockles were so -so. The chicken with whipped potatoes was pretty damn good but according to the menu was supposed to be served with brussels sprouts. I'm not sure exactly what the green veg served with it was, but it was pretty good although definitely not brussels sprouts. The "duck confit" was not confit but rather more like a duck breast. Whatever it was served with on the bread was rather pungent. Definitely not the best duck I've ever had. I love Chifa and Amada so this was rather disappointing. Now for my biggest complaint ...the Stepford service-they all seemed to be devoid of personality and preturnatural. There was no attention to detail and was certainly not worthy of the beautiful interior, great beverages and better than average food.

Cheap and delicious. Summer rolls ($5.50): awesome, with sizable shrimp within and a big serving of the peanut sauce. Beef pho ($7.50): big portion of beef and noodles, with an impeccable broth. We asked nicely and the cashier was able to split the bill between two credit cards.

3.5 stars Came here on weekend for one of the lunch sets - plenty of seating, but the place started filling up around 1-1:30PM. Seating is also pretty cramped, so you literally are easedropping on your neighbor's convo. Lunch sets available with the large trays with entree plus small side dishes. FOOD: -Chicken Katsu Don lunch set with the hot soba - fried chicken with omelet over rice. I liked the chicken katsu, but wasn't feeling the soba. It was too soft in texture, and my BF felt the same. -Sake oyako don lunch set with cold soba- with salmon and salmon roe over rice. The small side dishes tasted OK - not that great, compared to OOTOYA closeby. Also the side dishes are tiny. In sum, pricey for what you pay.

After a concert at the Academy of Music we wanted a late night snack. At 11 PM this place was crowded and we had to wait 10 minutes for a table. The duck pot pie was not tasty and did not have enough ingredients in it. It was more like a runny soup. They forgot to include the caramelized onions on the burger I ordered and they only put a very small amount of American cheese that I had added. But the burger was done medium rare as I ordered and was very tasty. The roll was big enough not to fall apart and was not stale. My big problem was that in the early morning I awoke with chills and incredibly severe abdominal cramps that made me almost go to the ER. This was followed by the nausea, vomiting, and diaahrea. I presume this was food poisoning probably resulting in tainted meat or mishandled meat. They were extremely busy that night and in that situation things can happen. I will not be going to Good Dog ever again.

First, I have to say I have walked by cask Republic several times. For some reason, I've always decided to go to another restaurant. Well today was the day that I went here. How foolish was I, to not have gone here sooner? My server Hannah, was amazing. I ordered the heirloom tomato gazpacho and the kale salad. For a drink, I ordered the clown foot Clementine beer which I highly recommend. Let me start with the gazpacho. It was absolutely delicious. I have never had such a fresh and tasty gazpacho soup. The kale salad was fresh tasty and the dressing was beyond delicious. I also ordered at Hannah's recommendation the grilled chicken on the side. It was amazing. Everything I had was fresh and tasty. The gazpacho was so good I had to take a large order home with me. Although the restaurant was very busy, the manager made his way to my table with a complimentary glass of Cedar Creek beer, which is kind of like a dessert beer. All the staff were very friendly. I have to say, this is probably one of the best restaurant I have ever been to in Connecticut. I honestly cannot wait to go back. I would encourage everyone in the area to give this restaurant a try.

* outdoor seating so I can bring my puppy.  +1 * waiter who brings water to my puppy.  +1 * good selection of food - from sweet to savory.  +1 My sister ordered the buttermilk waffles, and I think this was the best dish for brunch.  My mac n cheese was good, but, really huge.  And I'm more of a sweet breakfast person, so I'm not sure why I ordered mac n cheese, but it was tasty.  But i'd go w/ the buttermilk waffles next time.   I'd go back!

I can't believe that I have only been to the North Star twice but what a cool venue. Went last Saturday night to see Fishbone (one of the greatest live acts ever!) and had a blast. The venue is small and intimate but the sound can be crappy if you are up front (we were). Both times I have been here (the first for Ruder Than You, The Pietasters and the Toasters last Halloween) the place is so small that you can talk to the artists as they always seem to be hanging around out front or in the bar area. Ticket prices are reasonable and they always host the up and coming or the niche bands that might not draw in a larger venue. Great selection of beers on tap at reasonable prices for a concert hall. Haven't had any food here but might try it in the future. Looking forward to my next show here.

Went their for my birthday....what a huge mistake...the chicken cutlet over day old linguine was soaked in the water from the pasta, (my dog wouldn't even eat it when I took it home), which covered the whole dish.  YUCK.  The oil used to fry my husband's shrimp and fries was rancid as we could smell it and tasted even worse.  Service was also disgusting.  OH WELL, live and learn.  Stowes, here we come if we want fresh fish!!  Anywhere but Jimmy's.. Can't rate it, it was that bad.

A friend of mine wanted to try some Mexican food. We were around Union Square and spotted the long lines in this place so we had to check it out. We came on a weekday around lunchtime in the afternoon. The wait time for this place was around 15 minutes. Most of the people here seem to be students. It's hard to believe a tiny place like this can fit this many people. My friend and I ended up getting the bean burrito because he was being health conscious. ^_^ There are a lot of beans in this burrito along with some rice and sauce. The soft taco was pretty good and the whole thing was a bit overwhelming. However, it did have more flavor than I thought. The staff was nice and the tables were a bit close together but not too uncomfortable. This place is always crowded so you are lucky to find a seat which I did. ^_^ If you're looking for a quiet meal, this would not be the best place either. It's usually pretty loud because it's pretty croweded. Unfortunately I am not a big fan of Mexican food. Once in a while, I can eat burritos and tacos but from seeing the huge lines all the time, this place is not a bad option if you are around the neighborhood looking for Mexican food.

Very nice meal! We went for lunch on a gorgeous Sunday afternoon not bearing in mind that it also happened to be Father's Day.  Neither the Spring special lunch menu nor the regular lunch menu was available that day, so we decided to choose from the a la carte menu. As you walk in , you almost feel like you're heading to someone's French garden for lunch.  You forget immediately that you are in New York City.  The fresh floral arrangements, garden furniture and and floral paintings really set the ambiance and you pretty much instantly get the feeling that you are in for a nice experience. As we browsed their menu, we were given wonderfully delicious baked breads.  So fresh and warm and quite tasty.  I really enjoyed their apple raisin bread the most.  I had to stop myself from eating more so I'd have room for my appetizer.  Anyway, as we sat there a couple and their what looked to be a child of about one year old.  First thought that entered my mind was, 'NOOOOOOOO!'    *Goes on her soapbox** That child won't last 10 minutes without balling or acting up, much less 2 to 3 hours. Dining in an establishment like this takes about that long with all the courses.    Why in the world would you bring a small child to a fine-dining restaurant?  Makes no sense to me.  In fact, it seems sort of retarded. If you can afford to eat at such a place, you can certainly afford a sitter for a few hours while you and the Mister go some place nice.  This is not TGIF.  I began to get leery.  Then before our amuse bouche came out., sure enough, the child not only began to cry wildly, but was screaming as all the guests in the dining room sort of tried not to give these young parents the look of disgust. Please tell me this was not going to be my lunch experience.  Just when I began to get annoyed, the parents quickly high-tailed it out of there before they could order and left the restaurant!  Wow! I thought they were just going to take a little walk to calm the baby down, but they actually left the restaurant.  Did they not know this might occur?  Ughh, all I know was I was happy.   So on to the food! The amuse bouche was a very light melon soup with chunks of smoked trout. Perfect for the season was the cold melon soup, however, didn't really mix well with the saltiness of the trout. It was a strange combo, so I didn't really finish it.  Next up was the appetizer.  I had the Chilled Kumamoto Oysters, Oscetra Caviar with Homemade Radish Pickle, Thinly Sliced Live Sea Scallops with Parsley Juice.  Very fresh and very delicious!  I love caviar and I love Kumamoto Oysters even more!  I was very pleased as the flavors really suited each other. I could have easily have settled on more of these as just my main dish. I decided to go with the Fresh Washington State Black Cod Organic Buckwheat, Sunchoke Cloud with Black Onion Powder. By this time, I was getting a little full but I still enjoyed the cod. It was well prepared and quite fresh as well.  I was pleased with the dish, however, I was still craving those oysters!  I skipped ordering dessert, however I was still presented with  the Hot Caramelized Anjou Pear Valrhona Chocolate , Biscuit Breton, Hot Toffee Sauce Réglisse Sorbet and Tahitian Vanilla Ice Cream.  Nothing like warm pears!  I could barely touch it as I was pretty full, but the Reglisse Sorbet was pretty divine!  Wow, so delicious!  We also had petite fours along with a mix of various chocolates and cookies, I just could not!  The coffee was also quite delicious and bold.  A great accompaniment for the dessert. All in all, with great service, minus baby and gorgeous ambiance, I would go back here for lunch however, I cannot imagine going for the $95 lunch tasting menu they were offering for Father's Day.  I was happy with the portions and selections I got, but despite that, I see this as a one-time dining spot for me.

I absolutely love this place. Within 5 minutes of my first visit I felt like I was in an extension of my living-room. I sat down at the end of the bar and the barista/bartender/new-bestfriend brought me my drink right away (contrary to some other reviews.) Midway through my drink I  was approached, and sadly the little chat we had was not flirting but a tactful request for my food order. Since my usual diet consists of UTZ spicy potato chips and Burritos I didn't recognize any of the ingredients and was weary of what seemed to be another fancy-named-food co-op-vegan-yoga dish that should end up on instagram rather then my stomach. BEHOLD, I WAS WRONG. IT WAS DELICIOUS! The chef artfully crafted a delicious bowl of goodness and I've been a regular ever since.

Was there 8/2/14. Real good beer selection. Service was good. Decor was blah, but not a major factor in my rating. Pizza was very mediocre. Had half pepperoni, half sausage. Pepperoni was OK, but sausage was totally bland. Overall, not well seasoned. Go to Flatbread or better yet Verita in Burlington instead.

Love this place. One of my favorite spots in the area. The seating is VERY cramped. You can literally breathe on the next table's plates while butting in their conversation. I've always ordered the grilled skirt steak sandwich and friend plantains. Fantastic.
Awesome pizza with cool toppings and a soft chewy crust.

I wish I could give a half star. Restaurants are not only meant for food but for experience. I came in as a party of nine, clearly able to see 20-30 tables open and empty. The host was confused & replied 'I don't know' to how long it would take for a table, we were coming up with scenarios we even agreed to sitting at multiple tables. As for working in the service industry I understand that a party of nine may take a few minutes to accommodate, but a party of nine bringing in business should not be told I don't know, and refused a table because there are multiple reservations, the resturant was empty & there was no manager on site. It is a shame when your restaurant is gorgeous, the food looked wonderful, but the people employed are up on their high horses acting as if they own the joint. Mid conversation with the host with half a brain, a woman came up in tears so angry and upset about her experience and said "everything was awful, I will never come back" the host stared blankly rather than getting a manager, she did not care one bit. I would have been fired if that was me in my place if work. Absolutely terrible service. If a managers reading you need to re evaluate your servers and hosts, this is a sculpture ground filled with wonderful art, maybe you would be better off jiggering some sculptures to run the restaurant, people would take a better liking to them. :)

I love, love, LOVE this place!  Their menu changes daily (the only constant is the grass-fed hamburger which is a must).  I try and order something different every time I go here.  One night I ordered the porkchop - which was as big as my head, I finished the whole thing it was so good.  Another night I had the seafood stew and another I ordered a pasta dish.  I've never, ever been disappointed.   Because their location is a pretty tight space, the place gets packed pretty quickly so I always try and get there as early as possible for dinner.   This place is a must for anyone who has an appreciation for really, really good food!
Loved this place!   It's small and noisy, but that's the italian way.  Definitely the best italian food i've had since I lived in tuscany.
totto spicy ramen is one of the best things i ever ate!

The meat is pretty good, but the sauces are very very meh.  The hot sauce is way too hot, which they use to cover up the flavor of the chicken and the lamb.  Couldn't taste the white sauce with all the heat from the hot sauce.  Doesn't compare to, say, Sammy's on 21st and Park.

Wow it's been two years since I last visited this restaurant. So from June 18-24th, it's Malaysian restaurant week and my boyfriend and I were prepared to see what was being offered. Since the Chinatown Nyonya was taking part in the Malaysian restaurant week, my boyfriend and I decided to try it out. The restaurant was super crowded that they had to give a ticket number to people. My boyfriend and I were lucky enough to score a window seat! I was so excited since there was still light outside, I knew my pictures would come out nice! We took a look at the restaurant week menu and it didn't appeal to us one bit, so we ended up ordering our "usuals" Roti Canai, the taste and textures were pretty consistent with the ones I've had in Brooklyn Nyonya's. Haianese Chicken is my boyfriend's favorite menu item in Nyonya. My boyfriend really likes white meat, but the server told us we can't pick and choose and the boyfriend mentioned that typically we can pick and choose, but we made do with what we had. It was quite interesting how there was a lot of sauce on the bottom. However, the discouraging part of this entree was that there was little meat on the chicken. Sarang Burong is one of my personal favorites. It was actually slightly bigger than when I usually order it in the Brooklyn Nyonya's and definitely more veggies, but not enough chicken. Chicken Rice, same and consistent. Malaysian Iced Tea, not worth it. It was $3.50 and you know what? It tasted just the same as Chinese milk tea and Chinese milk tea costs two dollars less than the Malaysian Iced Tea. Nyonya is a good restaurant for any type of group dinner or date. The servers are friendly and the service is on point and the restaurant is quite spacious. It wasn't an entirely bad experience at Nyonya except I wish their food quality would be a little bit better.

Octopus salad was outstanding. I never knew octopus could so tender. Not much greens, so it's not a healthy option, but it's just plain delicious. Pappardelle with sweet sausage was also deeee lish. And the homemade focaccia bread was warm and oh so good. Prosciutto was also tasty, but when is it not. Plus I had pata negra the other day so I'm spoiled. Delivery was super fast and everything arrived fresh and warm.

Overrated. Sicilian slices were good but not great. Garlic bread was greasy. Sub was ok, nothing outstanding. Service was non-existent. Not worth seeking this place out after seeing flattering Yelp ratings.

This is not a restaurant, it is an experience! They have a seven course dinner, like a group sitting. It is easily missed, it is a regular door in an alley like area., you knock to get in. It is a cozy environment, and decor is very well done. It is slightly cramped. When you get there, they put towels, yes towels, over you, so anything you spill, can just go on that. Then you wash you hands, and then the food starts. The food was in enormous portions, given we were just three of us, but we enjoyed all the courses! The chicken in the phyllo dough was unexpectedly delicious! the mix of sweet with the chicken flavors was great! The next course of chicken was so tender, it just came off the bone. The lamb was the next course and wow, loved it! Ofcourse dessert was fruit and baklava...and the baklava gave me my full rush on sugar, and rightly so. And we all liked the mint tea, we actually asked for seconds!

The place was alright. The food was definitely good, but it wasn't amazing to me. I think it is mostly because of the crust. I like how they cook their pizza, but I wasn't digging their crust. However, it did fill me up and I did enjoy the place. Line is crazy long though so be precautious when you get in.
Pretty decent food. We ordered the Buratta, Cavateli and Carne. Good food. Ambiance is a bit blah

Everything on the menu is delicious. My goto meal is the Bronte althought I will occassionally switch it up with their pasta, my goto is the spicy sausage rigatonni. Small place, but worth squeezing into for their food. Friendly service.

A solid meh - as someone who cooks Italian on a regular basis, knows about buying fresh pasta and making great dishes, this place falls short.  The food looks good and the place is nice, especially when it's summertime with a lot of legitimate outdoor seating (mostly 2-tops).  Random neighborhood too, not great people watching from the seats. If you are looking for a romantic place that looks the part, especially in warmer months, this is the spot - for top-quality Italian food, try somewhere else.

My girlfriends and I were visiting NYC and woke up really late on a Sunday. We had been planning to go to some famous brunch places.. but we woke up really late and really weren't in the mood to be waiting in long lines. So we went to this little crepe place around noon. The place was pretty empty, and there was no wait. We all ordered a savory crepe. I ordered a 'Special'-- Pesto Chicken, Asparagus, Goat Cheese & Chipotle Mayo. I added scrambled eggs for $2 extra. I've gotta say, my crepe was MONEY!!!! Best crepe I ever had. If the review was on my crepe alone, I would give 5 stars. My two girlfriends both tried my crepe, and said it was definitely the best one. I also tried my friend's crepe-- Crepe Vegetarienne. I may be biased, because I'm definitely a meat kind of girl.. but I thought it was bland, and made for rabbits. My friend had to ask for ketchup to kick up the flavor. For dessert, we all shared the 'Nutella and Banana' crepe. The Nutella was hot, gooey, and delicious! The textures of the Nutella with chunks of Banana were a party in the mouth. I have a big appetite, but I was pretty stuffed after the meal. The atmosphere was little and quaint.. perfect Sunday brunch atmosphere. If I'm being nitpicky though... I don't like the high chairs. Overall.. will visit again next time I am in NYC!

I went here for the first time just the other day. I only had the egg drop soup and meatless fried rice, but it was pretty good. There was a lot of egg in the soup, and it was delicious. The fried rice was ok, but I didn't realize ordering the meatless fried rice meant it was mostly plain--just rice and onions. That was my mistake though, so next time I'll order the vegetable fried rice. They have hot tea available for anyone at a table in the dining area, which I thought was great, but the tea tasted kind of strange to me. Overall pretty decent. I'd go back to try more of their food--which they had a pretty good selection of.
hang town fry is amazing!! brunch!!

Arrived for lunch promptly at noon on a Wednesday and found an open table.  Service was efficient and friendly; drink order taken immediately.  We both ordered the Fried Zucchini BLT and it was delicious.  The zucchini was breaded and fried, not greasy at all.  The sandwich came with one slice of tomato, a little shredded lettuce, mayo and two small pieces of bacon  (I did not eat the whole wheat toast -- just my own diet preference).  The combo was tasty, if a little light on quantities for $10.95.  The sandwich did come with a choice of two sides.  The only non-carb side was coleslaw, so I doubled up.  The coleslaw was good, but standard; not sure it was homemade.  Slightly disappointed that the sides come in those little plastic cups with lids. Over all a good choice for lunch, but nothing spectacular.

I had heard good things about sushi yasuda from a few friends and despite not being a huge fan of sushi, I was curious. The food was great. I don't really understand or know how to describe what to look for in seafood (freshness? taste? texture?) so I was surprised when I enjoyed the sashimi so much. We got the blue fin tuna, king salmon, sea bass, and arctic char, amongst various others. We ordered off the a la carte menu and in hindsight, it would have been much better to order off the prix fixe and pick a few a la carte ones that weren't available on the prix fixe. Overall, I can say that I've discovered a craving for sushi/sashimi that I didn't know I had in me. Would definitely go again to try their omakase. I would give five stars but the menu was confusing and our first waiter was in a hurry / didn't want to explain how to order efficiently. The rest of the service was solid and no tip necessary.
BYOB is dangerous because my friends and I always get too drunk, which leads to us getting shushed at and ruining date nights. It also makes the food 10Xs better.

Save the drive to New York, Central Jersey destination lounge has arrived. It's truly first class place with no details missed. If you're looking to impress a client or date, this is the place. It's a great jumping off point to set the mood for a the night or on the flip side for some after dinner/show spirits. The selection is amazing, my friends and I have come to call this place "Graduate School for Scotch lovers"... and I LOVE going to class. Being right next door to Wine Chateau to pickup some "homework" on the way out is the icing on the cake. Stay classy New Jersey!

Best greasy dumplings I've ever had.  Not the 'best' or most refined, but this place is fucking heaven if you've been drinking. This place is shockingly cheap as well - 4 huge friend pork & chive dumplings for $1, sesame pancake with duck for $2 ($1 if plain), 8 veggie dumplings for $2.50. The place is the definition of hole-in-the-wall and is of questionable cleanliness, but staff is quite awesome and efficient. This is type of finds I love: cheap, fast, tasty and no bullshit.

Following other Yelpers' reviews, I realized that the old Tweed spot has converted into an American seafood restaurant. And what's made me excited was the offering of $1 oysters. Well, Summer is coming and there's nothing say Summer more than seafood. The place itself is lofty, decorated in an old world hotel bar room scheme but happy hour here still attracts a large crowd. Once upon entering you'll be greeted by a very friendly hostess, since we're having dinner, we were led upstairs. The menu itself is quite exciting. It's more adventurous than your regular traditional American fare. Raw bar, crudo, carpaccio, intriguing ingredients here and there, flourishes; it's full of things that I really want to eat. First off, raw oysters. When I first asked the waiter whether we can participate in the Happy Hour festivities, he said no, but that doesn't mean we can't order the $1 oysters. They are sold by 5, so we had 10. It comes in a bed of ice with lemons, cocktail/horseradish sauce, mignonette and 2 miniature bottles of Tabasco. They are not exceptionally huge but they are still a good size, fresh, clean and tasty. I know a couple friends that would go gaga for these and I'll bring them next time and each get at least 10. The crudo sampler is cute, This day we had kampachi, fluke and salmon, The fluke being our favorite. The curry oil and sea bean went surprisingly well with raw fluke. The portion is a bit small but it's fun to try something different. I've long had pig ears, it's popular as street foods in Asia and the ones here are crispy fried and came with hot sauce. It's almost like a meatier bacon, surprisingly not too greasy and the portion is good. The idea of having roasted bone marrow is awesome but the problem is that there wasn't a lot of it in the bone, definitely not enough to spread over the four buttered toasts it comes with. I wish there's a lot more of it because at the end I don't even know if I knew how it tasted. They also offer a bourbon and use the bone as a luge, but it doesn't hold a lot of appeal for me. Keeping on with the unusual we ordered the pork jowl, it comes highly recommended by the waiter. He explains that the jowl is usually very tough but the jowl was cooked for 9 hours and comes out tender and juicy. He's not very far off. The dish comes with a slightly spicy cheesy grits that is very delicious, a few whole spring onions, slightly bitter and cute and crunchy breakfast radishes. Thinking that it's not quite enough, we also had a roasted baby beet salad, multi colored roasted baby beets with a creamy goat cheese with a side of arugula. It's one of the best things of the night. I'm coming back next week with new friends to try new things.

Went the other night and we enjoyed the service and the food. My mussels were delicious with a touch of african  spice and my friend loved her fish.  Service was attentive and i always had my water glass filled!  The chef/owner was even nice enough to say hi and make sure we were happy.  Thanks for the great time.

On my recent trip to New York, I visited this place and was floored by the delicious nature of my dish despite being simple. After sitting down, I spotted a Chicken Pot Pie being delectably consumed by someone at the table next to me. Jealous, I asked the waiter what that was and it was a Chicken Pot Pie. He said it's not on the menu (I couldn't spot it if it was), but he said he'd be happy to hook us up with it. Win! The waiter also gets points for keeping up with my insatiable need for Diet Coke. Good service, busy/loud environment, and great food. It's pricey, but you don't go to Times Square for a cheap meal.

We were excited when this place opened in our neighborhood - a new brunch spot is always welcome. We were also excited about the green and sustainable concept. Unfortnuately, the first red flag was that the menu boasts seasonal fruit. I can tell you that kiwis are not seasonal year round and somehow they're always included. I'm concerned that the owners just use the seasonal label to justify charging more instead of actually using seasonal or local produce. Second, the service here is consistently bad. We keep going back expecting our experiences to be vindicated and we just continue to be disappointed. Third, for such a modern atmosphere, it's lame that they now have a $30 credit card minimum. What? You don't even serve alcohol. How would you like me to get my bill up to $30 if I don't have cash? The one redeeming quality is that the food is pretty solid. The quinoa porridge is excellent and their specials are always great choices. We just make a point of getting our food to go now. One last thing - this place is not in Newbold!! It's on the east side of Broad. The Newbold Neighbors are promote the boundaries pretty hard so I have no idea how this place got classified as in Newbold.

I'm Asian, and I love to karaoke!  Karaoke is in my blood.  When I'm not karaoking, I'm at home playing Rock Band 2 (singer, of course).  When I'm not karoking or playing Rock Band 2, I'm singing in the shower or in my car.  This place is the place to go for karaoke. I know this place is a little trashy and a little college-ish, but I've NEVER had a bad time there.  Drinks are cheap and plentiful.  As I drink, I feel younger and younger.  On Wednesdays, you can't beat 2-tacos-for-$1.  Sandwiches are cheap.   The upper stairs bar is clean and respectable when the downstairs gets a little crowded. Supposedly, this is the oldest bar in Philly.  You can also get a feel of history while you're here.

Wonderful place to get a cheesesteak if you're on the way home from Center City.  Also the lines are shorter (than the joints in South philly) and the steak is just as good.  I feel my arteries clogging now. For someone who rarely finishes anything, I always eat the entire steak. No leftovers.
18" pies. Personal favorite is the BLT Ranch pizza. Family run and very friendly.

It's time for an updated review of Song.  I think like most Slopers who first come here, they love the place.  Great prices, food, service.  But lets face it - they is WAY too much sauce in your stir fry it could be sodium soup.  Guys gotta chill out.

What's not to love about Habana Outpost?  The sexy outdoor vibe, the yummy cheap food or the frozen mojitos?  seriously.  it's even solar-powered.  this place is a must visit and one of my all-time favorite hang-outs.

I was so impressed with the food, I opened up a Yelp account solely to rate this restaurant.  My wife and I came here last weekend looking for authentic Italian food and that's exactly what we got.  Gaia is a sweetheart and was more than willing to guide us into choosing a nice variety of dishes that suited our tastes.  We ordered the spinach gnocchi, meat lasagna, two paninis, an appetizer of walnuts, honey, and cheese, two desserts, and two Italian sodas, all coming in at just under $40.  This food is authentic Italian, so don't expect to order meatballs or chicken parmigiana here, just homemade Italian food prepared with love.  I would put Gaia's paninis up against anything the city has to offer, even more so when you consider the value--$5 for a sandwich stuffed with the highest-quality, fresh ingredients.  If you have one restaurant to visit on a weekend to New York, this would be it!

Very expensive Sangria!  For $38 ($50 after tax & tip) I have to say I expected more than a small ice filled pitcher of Sangria.  The glasses used were ice filled too  - perhaps to disguise how little was being served?   The rest of the meal was quite good but the price of the Sangria was aggravating and tainted an otherwise good meal.

Wow. A friend and I went here on a busy Saturday night. Although the waitstaff was pretty slow, the food was excellent. My date and I ordered four rolls of different varieties of taste and texture. It was outstanding. I can say this visit presented the best sushi I had ever eaten. I will be returning. I do wish they had a more diverse dessert menu, though.

I will always have a soft spot for Penelope's.  I used to come here all the time with my friends who lived around the block and my ex bf.  I still come here on occasion when I want a cutesy comfort food spot. When I went with my ex we always ordered the spinach and artichoke dip, mac & cheese and grilled cheese which we loved.  They usually have a least one decent wine as well.  I still order one of these things till this day.  This place gets way too crowded for brunch and is better suited to go to during the week for lunch or dinner.

This place is very sophisticated for Williamsburg..  I do not feel like this was New Brooklyn Cuisine, it was a straight forward New American Restaurant.. But with it's oyster bar, it's steaks and cocktails, this is as traditional as Williamsburg is going to get..Loving that everyone's fall menus are in.. Some hearty and delicious food is starting to show up.. We started dinner with the fried green bean dish.. Instead of using a commonly over used tempura battered, they went regular flour, egg, bread crumb.. Served with a honey mustard. The beans were perfectly cooked inside, with the crunch on the outside, a very nice starter. We then moved onto a wedge salad.. This might have been the best wedge I have ever had.. A classic dish done skillfully.. The wedge was cut into manageable pieces.. There was wonderful chunks of blue cheese with dots of blue cheese sauce through out the plate.. The bacon was not overbearing and they were perfectly paper thin little batons.  It almost looked like they cooked them pressed down on a silpat and then just sort of shattered them into pieces.. It was a nice touch..  A great salad. For entree I ordered the trout while my lovely lady ordered the pork chop... I thought my trout with capers in a brown butter sauce was excellent.. They deboned the whole thing for me in the kitchen, brought it out head on and whole.. The brown butter was delicious. A perfect plate of fish.. Miss A's porkchop I will be a little more critical about.. I felt the chop was missing a brine.. It was slightly over cooked to my liking.. By restaurant standards, I would say it was perfect.. They had this Calvados Jus that she really loved.. Mashed potatoes and apple sauce were really delicious as well.. I think we only had a couple of beers when we went, on Wednesday.. Our waiter was really nice, the room was really lovely..

It's often tough to find an Italian eatery that isn't either cheap/easy (pizza/heroes) or higher end/fancy (entrees at $20+). Giovanni's manages to slide right in that middle gap and provides some pretty solid food and ambiance.  I don't think there's anything costing more that $12/14 (other than wine) and this includes some seafood dishes and veal.  Bravo for them. Are you going to discover a new, esoteric dish that was eaten by Roman soldiers 400 years ago?  Nope.  Are you gonna get bread, a nice chunk of lasagne or a couple of veal pieces in a decent sauce that'll fill your tummy?  Yes. It's a nice space with brick, tall windows and modern meets retro vibe. The staff are friendly and there's a full bar.  Cocktails and beer were around $6.  Wine, however, seemed a bit more complicated and higher priced (which is normal). I'm happy to try this again when in the mood for neighborly Italian. - Jon

Overall, great addition to the handful of wine bars in Center City and yummy pizza and wine. Good: Once you walk into the small but well decorated establishment, someone greets you promptly and seats you at a table.  The staff is knowledgeable about the menu and give great recommendations on food and drinks.  I also love that you can sample the wine prior to committing to an entire glass. Food is fresh and reasonably priced.  I've had several of their pizzas, and the sausage was my favorite.  The yummy smattering of delicate sausage with scattered globs of mozzarella and peppers makes me hungry just thinking about it.  (I don't think my description makes the dish sound that tasty, but that's how I see it in my head, and believe me, it's good.) I really liked their asparagus and chopped boiled egg combo as well.  It's pretty simple and not overpowering, but a nice prelude to a pizza. The wine selection, although kind of small, changes from time to time.  And the wines themselves are reasonably priced and good.  They have several beers that are available, but you're not really going there to drink beer anyway. And they offer sparkling water for free! Bad:   The space is a little cramped, and some of the tables are a little lopsided.  I remember we sat down at a tall table near the door (avoid this one if you can- it seats two), and it was wobbling like there was no tomorrow.   The place also would benefit from the use of air conditioning.  They do have fans and open all the windows/doors.  Currently, the place has the unfortunate combination of summer weather, lukewarm water (no ice), and lots of people in a little space emitting a ton of heat. I think the progression goes: The good, the bad, and the ugly.  But it's not really ugly.  The decor is very clean and the menu written in chalk on blackboards adds a nice little touch. I like this place.  If you get a chance, sit down with a couple of your friends, kick back, and eat some delicious pizza and wine.

PANCAKES. That is all you need to know or order. We came for Saturday brunch this morning and even after walking in the rain, the PANCAKES made the experience worth while. Crispy on the outside, fluffy, soft and perfect on the inside. Incredible goodness with every bite. I actually ordered an omlet - which was good... but not as good as the pancakes I tried off of my friend's plate. Sharing is caring!
I had the Ishka steak (provolone, spinach, roasted peppers) - delicious.  Had some juice to it.  Nice roll, good mix of meat and topping.  Need a few more peppers to get a 5 star.

Ok - gave them another try.... and another. Didn't mess with the sandwiches but instead went with the traditional entrees - roasted chicken on rice with beans, mondongo soup. Good entrees, good price. Not sure what happened with that first sandwich but solid 3.5-4 stars afterward.

We heard good things about this place so we celebrated husband's and friend's birthdays here. We liked it here! Louis was our server, and he was really cute, sweet and thoughtful- someone you'd want as a friend. Food was excellent. Grilled octopus was tender, flavorful and delicious (portion is small though just to warn you). The mussels were also lovely- white sauce with lots of garlic. We probably ate 7 baskets of bread because of the delectable broth. Pappardelle Tartufate... had to order it because so many yelpers raved about it. They did not disappoint. Absolutely amazing. I will dream about it tonight. Ginger creme brûlée and tiramisu were both really good and was a great way to end the lovely meal. Will definitely come back for special date nights!

I thought the sushi burrito was a pretty cool concept so I had to check this place out. And I was very happy that I did! We got the Crunch and the Mexicana. The burritos were pretty heavy but very flavorful. I was worried that there would be an overwhelming amount of rice, but no! It was a good balance between the filling and the rice. The Crunch was light and delicious. The Mexicana was more saucy but still very flavorful. The pork belly in the Mexicana is a must-have. It was extremely tender but it was sometimes difficult/messy to chew through. We also got the corn tempura which I really enjoyed! It's something that I could munch on all the time. There is seasoning that you can add more of, depending on how much of a kick you want. Definitely try this place out! But be prepared to eat it outside since there isn't much of a sitting area there.

I can only rate this place based on the one time I've been here. But holy moly... 5 stars for the Reuben Pastrami sandwich. A nice size helping of pastrami. Flavorful. Good bang for your buck. $7.95. Will definitely come back again.

You cannot get better than this place! Where do I even begin. Well, this is my favorite restaurant in all of NYC. The prices are incredibly affordable making this the perfect destination if you're on a budget. (cash only though) The food is INCREDIBLE. So fresh and tasty, and is always served very fast. The servers may not be the best, and it sometimes can take a while with your check but once you get the food, you can ignore all of that . The ONE and ONLY time I had a bad experience here, the owner came out and comped my entire meal. I didn't even have to say anything to him, he just knew we didn't receive good service. The neighborhood around this place is also beautiful, it's the perfect spot for a date. Decor, food, ambiance, everything about this place is top notch. Highly recommended.

This is some damn good bbq.  The only brisket that can compare comes from Delaneys.  Order at the counter and find a spot to sit when you get your food.  Reasonably priced and very good quality.   Best BBQ in Manhattan.

We have been here several times since they opened and each time found it completely underwhelming...They took the great burger selection they once had off the dinner menu in what seems like an effort to upsell...so we tried the steak frites and it was so tough it was basically inedible.  Also had the $13 Mac & Cheese and figured it would be amazing but it was just bland and cold.  It's just really not worth it although some people do seem to like to pay a lot and get a little... Update 10/11; we just went here again recently with a larger party, figured we'd give it another try and again it was terribly disappointing for all of us...I won't go into a long spiel, but who likes to spend hundreds of dollars on mediocre food?!

The falafel was extremely refreshing. As much as I love falafel, I never did think of it as refreshing. You can really taste some very strong fresh herbs and spices in there. The pita is seasoned in a way that I've never had before and I really really really like it! Brown sugar lemonade was recommended to me by the cashier. It was not overly sweet which is a good thing. It also was unique and refreshing. Baba ghanouj was out of this world. Incredibly creamy, vibrant, and smokey. I would definitely go back here the next time I'm in New York.

I tried coming to this place a few times and got shot down by the wait time. The first time I tried to go, the wait was about 2.5 hrs, the second time I tried, they werent taking any more walk-ins. I guess third time is the charm because I came here on a monday afternoon and the wait was about 30-40 minutes so I decided to stay. The hostess will send you a text when your table is about to be ready so you can go wander around. Between two people we had the.. Chocolate Chip pancakes Southern breakfast Egg benedict Eggs on both dishes was cooked to perfection. Pancakes were moist w/semi melted chocolate chips and oh wow, warm maple syrup is heaven.

a neighborhood gem...Delicious grilled calimari, fresh salads,  perfectly prepared risotto, flavorful and balanced pastas, thoughtful and carefully selected wine list at modest prices, and richly chocolate dolci. Everything we ate was fully flavored and freshly prepared. A wonderful meal for any day of the week.

Made a reservation on a Saturday night at the last minute for a party of 5 at 8pm.  It was one of the only places I could find one, which isn't great for them, but it was for us!  We ordered a bunch of the small plates for the table to start.  Some favorites included the watercress salad, beets n feta, and the brussels and bacon oh and the bundles.  So unusual and delish, don't be scared by the black pudding!  Least favorite was the lentil dish due to the fact the lentils were pretty undercooked (more than crunchy, hard to chew).  This was easily overlooked though due to the high quality service.  Other than that though the starters were incredible. The server was very accommodating and made me feel as though my  dietary restrictions (which I typically try to down play and work around the menu on my own without bringing attention to myself) were not an issue at all.  We ordered the salmon, which while it was a tad overly salty was perfectly cooked and simply prepared which was refreshing.  The lamb burger was excellent as always.  The pizza with locally foraged ramps, nettles, and fiddleheads was a big hit.   Most of all I was impressed by the excitement of the staff about the ingredients on the menu and their ability to make us feel as though our experience was important to them without being overly cheesy or phony.  It is rare to find this these days.  I find more often than not that service in many restaurants in Philadelphia seems overly contrived as of late and/or inattentive & irritable.  Overall I was VERY pleased with the experience and proud to present such a stellar neighborhood joint to our friends who don't typically dine in the QV area (silly city folk turned suburbanites).  They were more than impressed. Great job Kennett!  I am excited to return and make this one of my neighborhood go to's!   I recommend to all, date nights, boozers, foodies, families and out of towners.

Ate here for restaurant week and loved every course! From the fresh guacamole and the empanadas, to the steak and the pineapple upside down cake for dessert. I was skeptical about the steak having to be cooked medium rare because I'm not a big steak eater and when I do get it, I like it medium well, but it came out great! Service was typical restaurant week service, but not as terrible as some people experience. Nice ambiance inside too. Would've ordered some empanadas to go at the takeout diner on the first floor since they were only 2 for $6 but they were fresh out by the time we were done dinner a little before 9. I'll definitely be back here, especially since Chifa closed, but if you liked that place, you'll enjoy Rosa Blanca too.

A pregnant friend dragged me to Midwood to get this "world class pizza that will blow your mind".  Having studied abroad in Italy, I declared that to be impossible but I would go with her nonetheless.  I didn't want it to be good because I don't like to be wrong but the truth is the truth..holy pizza dough, this pizza is amazing.  It's worth the $5/slice...
Pretty good.  I'll be back

Mmm whenever I get a craving for a Vietnamese sandwich, I rush over to Banh Mi Saigon!  I always get the spicy roast pork option, but perhaps I'll change it up next time.  Never a disappointing moment!  They have a pretty efficient system, even though it gets really crowded during lunchtime.  Their new and bigger space definitely helps.

I came here yesterday for my birthday lunch.  I was worried that the wait was going to be insane, since after all this is Ippudo, but we arrived around 11:45 and were seated immediately.  There were a bunch of empty tables left, and the restaurant didn't seem to fill up until about 12:30pm. I ordered the Akamaru Modern, which was delicious as usual.  My boyfriend got the Karaka-men, which is one of the spicier ramen dishes.
