While it was also very tasty, I thought it was a touch too spicy for my taste.  I have more of a mild palette and the heat hits you in the back of your throat, so I don't know if I could have eaten an entire bowl of it.  He's a real trooper though, and ordered an extra serving of noodles to go with his bowl of ramen. We also got the Yamitsuki Goma Kyuri, which is a cucumber appetizer.  Really good!  It is very light and refreshing, and a very simple dish that doesn't lack flavor or sophistication. For drinks, I ordered the shochu drink with fresh grapefruit juice.  Didn't realize it was one of those drinks that require you to squeeze your own juice from the fruit and mix it in yourself, but I will admit that after doing so, the drink really hit the spot.   I saw a bunch of people ordering the pork buns, and I kind of wish I had given it a try because they looked really good.  Maybe this will be an excuse to go back? As if I needed one to begin with! :)

This place is a hidden gem! Have been frequenting Roberto's for two years now and have had a great experience every time (for both take-out and dining). Authentic Italian cuisine (so incredibly delicious and better than many other more popular Italian restaurants in the city), fast and friendly service, as well as a great atmosphere. Portions here aren't overwhelming like many Italian restaurants, which some people might complain about, but that's because their focus is more on the taste... and believe me, everything I have tried here so far has been tasty. Only downside is that they don't deliver, but then I would probably be ordering from them every other day. Also, their valentine's day fixed menu is especially yummy!

On our way back from Atlantic city and because I am traveling with my father, (who insists on Peruvian food) we found ourselves at oh! Calamares. Now, when I say we, I mean myself and my mother, father, and sister. My parents are native Peruvians and as a result, I know what to look for in good Peruvian cuisine. Walking into the restaurant we were greeted warmly by staff. The restaurant has nice decor and is different from other restaurants that I went to. The staff was also very attentive. In terms of the food, I ordered the eschebeche de pescado and it was nice, I enjoyed it. We also ordered the Peruvian drink Chica Morrada and wow, YUCK! Doesn't have lemon or apples or anything in it so it has a very corn-like flavor and being Peruvian-American, growing up with Peruvian food I know this is NOT what it is suppose to taste like. Also they didn't aji or chanca at all which is weird.  My mother is vegetarian and not there were really not a lot of options for her at all. The beans she ordered were basically boiled, no spices added or anything so that was disaspointing. My sister had aji de gallina which was good but not great. Overall, for a place full of fellow Peruvians the food did not live up to the expectations. However our wait for a table was only 1 min for a table on a Sunday right after the new Jersey Peruvian festival (waitress asked us if we just came from there).

This place is like crack. If you can't handle that, don't go. But if you can stand the subsequent insatiable cravings, definitely go and definitely order a side of the broiled char siu pork because whatever they give you in the ramen bowl is not enough. It will never be enough. It's that amazing. I've never been to a place that puts such care into every aspect of the ramen bowl. The noodles are cooked inside a whole chicken. The broth is rich and flavorful but not greasy. The char siu pork... perfect. If only there was something remotely comparable in Boston. I would eat Totto Ramen at least once a week because, yes, the lines can be a deterrent for the impatient and hungry--but seriously, well worth the wait.

The interior and ambiance are great, however, once packed, the noise and acoustics get a bit overwhelming.  Still, the food was wonderful, and they had a Gluten Free and Dairy Free menu for me to work off of, which made it easy to make safe selections. Crispy Brussel Sprouts which were perfectly grilled and seasoned, some of the best I've ever had and the Grilled Shrimp & Chorizo Skewer - delicioius! Waitstaff was very friendly and helpful.
Nice, cool location, food tastes good, large guac bowl is awesome, but the inside of the place is starting to feel dated.

At the Philadephia Food Expo a few weeks ago on Jefferson campus, I won a $25 gift card to go. As I was debating when to use it, they also informed me I won a free happy hour. My boyfriend and I decided to go for dinner and happy hour. Now, my free "happy hour" was not explained well in the slightest. (Since then, I had won another one, and the details were more well explained). Due to the confusion, the manager was more than accommodating for my 9 happy hour friends (even allowing my alcohol-free friend to get half-priced apps even though she didn't pay for a package). Drink selection was decent and we made our money worth it for the alcohol! Boyfriend and I also had dinner before hand. The servers were attentive and had excellent mannerisms. Our bread and oil came out quickly - it was a foccacia-herb type loaf with excellent flavoring. I ordered the Cavatelli Tartufo while he ordered the Rigatoni Pizzaioli. The flavoring was rich without being overpowering or too heavy. The portion sizes were generous for the price. I would definitely return again.

Coming from Los Angeles, Mexican food in NY left much to be desired. Luckily, Tacos El Bronco entered my life and I can say that it's as good as my faves in LA! I must say though that I'm speaking specifically about the tacos--especially the al pastor and lengua. Mmm! It's also served with everything it's supposed to--double tortilla, LIMES, radishes, cebollas, and 3 options of salsas. The burritos are okay (there's rice and beans in it), and the horchata could be better (always tastes a little watered down). All in all, a meal here always makes me happy! Only wish I lived closer!

I tried Hummus & Pita Co. again and have to give it a higher rating.  And no, I didn't go the free lunch offered by Dave (owner/manager?). I had mentioned in my initial review the food itself is good, but my main complaint was the layout.  They changed the layout since the first time I went, and it's definitely better than when they first opened.  The fill-its and toppings are separated, and it's not nearly as confusing as it used to be.  The staff was also really patient and walked customers through the ordering process. As for the food: - Falafel was good, still fried but moist.  Preferred it to the shwarma. - Get the Spanish eggplant, a really tasty Fill It - Grape leaves were pretty good, but a little sour

I came here for dinner after working out at the LA fitness. I was the only customer dining in. I saw a few people came for pick up and to-go orders. The TV was showing the kicks being destroyed. An older guy came to dine in as well after my tamale came out. The tamale for smaller and less flavorful than the Peruvian tamale I'm used to. But it was good with the tomtillo salsa I got with it. I got the beef enchiladas with salsa verde without cheese and sour cream. I have to watch the empty calories. It's a nice family owned place. This place used to be a just ok pizza place. I'm glad something more ethnic and flavorful took over. I want to come back and try the tacos. My friend said it cheaper than the other place on route 46.

i adore this place. the fried chicken is crispy, greaseless, and DELICIOUS.  mushroom flatbread was a bit salty last time, but still tasty.  not a big fan of the dip with the chips, but all my friends are big fans.  cocktails are amazing--the revival and aviation are great.  service is always good, from the waitstaff to the bartenders, and you can actually hear your dinner/drinkmates talk.  a great place for dinner or late night drinks/snacks.

One of my favorite brunch spots in the city. Their breakfast options are great, but I normally go for the cheese burger. Their edamame is also bangin'- it comes with this awesome sweet/spicy Asian dipping sauce. I always ask what's in it, but forget the minute I walk out the door. Oh well. The wings are also tasty. Lastly, they generally have a pretty good draft list and their mimosas are on point. I'm not much of a dancer, but I have always had a good time at their events. DJ Deejay spins there frequently, and his events are a lot of fun. MMP, anyone? Just be prepared for how crowded it gets. It's worth noting, though, that even when it is jam-packed on the club side, the bartenders are awesome and you don't wind up waiting around.

Great brunch, we were seated right away.  The vanilla bean toast is all that, and the biscuits and gravy were spot on as well.  We each had two cocktails, they were that good.  Excellent service.  Would definintely come back.
Awesome food... excellent customer service... my new go to spot for desi food....nice decorations

Ordered the Iskender Kebap (thin sliced lamb with tomato and yogurt sauce), cucumber yogurt dip, and falafel for delivery last night and only have good things to report.  The lamb was flavorful, lean, and tender, the falafel was moist, and the dip tasted fresh.  Added bonus was that the food came quickly and the delivery guy made it right to my door instead of ignoring the instructions I put in and getting lost like most other places.  The lamb was not cheap but the portion was huge and the quality was great.  Looking forward to trying the Adana Kebab next time.
I am so excited to have found this place! It's adorable, the baristas are super friendly, and the food is delicious. I wish I could spend every morning here!

I go here at least once a week, as I am so addicted. My favorites are the Prosciutto Crudo and the Margarita, wash down with a San Pelligrino Pomelo. Having lived in Rome, I can honestly say this is how they it in Roma.. All fresh ingredients, friendly staff and the owner is really nice too. This is a special Pizzeria and if you want fresh pizza. like they make in Italy then come here..Nobody is making better Pizza than this place. Would give it 10 Stars if I could.

This place is incredibly difficult to find at first.  When you first try to find it you feel like you are following a path to a werewolf den.  Kind of a weird place to find but it is worth it. I was going to list all the dishes we had but then I remembered I have no clue what we ordered.  We did some sushi but really focused on the tapas like sharing of the small plates.  We had about 5 to 6 dishes between the two of us and were very happy.  Some of the dishes were aggressive in terms of taste profiles but it felt very authentic.  I would definitely go back but you need to take someone there that has an open pallet and is a bit adventurous.

I've been here twice already and it's just fantastic.   I came for brunch and had the eggs Imelda.  It's definitely the best brunch I've ever had.  The flavors in all of the dishes are just so unique and amazing.   I came for dinner once and we started with some fried chicken skin.  I love chicken skin, and when you fry and make it into a potato chip like thing, it's even more amazing.  Also had the spam fries, which kind of tasted like mcdonald's chicken nuggets........which makes me question if they actually are chicken.   For my entree I got the oxtail which was amazing.  Very tender, went well with the peanut sauce. All together, great, unique, and creative meal.  I'm definitely coming back again.

It's almost spring or as i refer to it "stand on a street corner in NOLITA season"  I love Cafe Havana and sadly, so do about 60 gajillion other hip souls...there is always a wait, and it's worth it!! You must get the Corn (also note - this can now be had to go around the corner at the take-away spot) Once the weather is hot you MUST have a corona and lime - this is no ordinary C&L, they HALF FILL the glass with fresh lime juice which makes for a drink so refreshing and tasty i would put it in a sports bottle and take it jogging
I vote PATS!  Whiz wit.  The best.

This was the first restaurant that I ate at upon my arrival in Philly with my cousin.  He met me as I got off the Chinatown bus from NY and we went straight into this restaurant for lunch.  My friend who had lived in Philly recommended this spot to me, and it was as she said, "the bomb!" The Roti Canai and the Coconut Shrimp are incredible appetizers.  I ordered the Mee Siam for my entree (I don't remember what my cousin ordered) but I do remember that we were both pleased with what we got.  The service was great and as my first introduction to having Malaysian food, it was very memorable.  I wish that we had something similar to this place in Los Angeles.  The closest thing that I have tried to this spot is Burma Superstar in the Bay Area.   It's a guarantee that when I return to Philly, this will definitely be one of my "to go to" spots!

Not so satisfied with the service I got at this place. The waiter looked like her was up all night from looking closely at his reflection. If you aren't going to give a s***, should I actually tip you? This is your job like it or not do it right.

Randomly stopped by here on a Friday night with a friend. Hard to find, but well worth it. Super cheap and very tasty, fresh made (worth the wait) panini's. Friendly staff, small place, super chilled. I saw cheap cheap breakfast items so definitely gonna come back here for more.
NYT Review "Very Good" nytimes.com/2013/06/30/n…

We came here on a Thursday evening and I was so pleased with the find!  The atmosphere is super inviting and warm. The service was excellent all evening.  We loved our wine, eggplant dish, falafel and burekas.  The leak patties could have used some more seasoning, but were still nice. I will definitely come back.

I wish that there was a possible 10 stars! This place is so head and shoulders above any similar type food that's quick. Had it for the first time last week and keep coming back for more, food is so delicious and the staff is so awesome and friendly. Such a different customer experience than going to any Chipolte where you are headed through the line like cattle, and shortchanged on every single ingredient that is put into your meal, and then charged over $10 for about $5 quantity of food. It would be one thing is chipolte ' s ingredients were as high quality as they used to be, but honestly it is just garbage. Tres Carnes actually tastes like a real restaurant, not mass produced crap. Chipotle it's over, officially I'm breaking up with you...
Very cool ambiance. Can be small if you're with a group, but that is more than made up for by the house cocktails and amazing food. One of the best Thai places in the city.

Had this for lunch today. It was bad. Inside is out dated. The cheese steak was a step for steak ums. The waitress was rude. When I asked where the rest room was I was told they do not have one. Some one needs to call the board of health. I will not be going back.

Extremely satisfied with my Sanford's brunch experience. Arrived around 1pm on a Saturday and was immediately seated. The service was a little slow in the beginning, but I did need some time to figure out my order since I wanted everything on the menu. After ordering, the service was much more attentive. They refilled my tea and water a couple times without me having to ask. The brunch deal is choice of Mimosa, Bellini, Bloody Mary, etc. and choice of Coffee or Tea. $14. There's a wide selection of egg dishes as well as chicken salads or sandwiches plus their famous (apparently) pulled pork sandwich. Peanut Butter Banana pancakes sounded incredible. I opted for the Zucchini, Ricotta, Tomato, Pesto Frittata. Well done, large portion with a side of home fries and your choice of toast. Very delicious dish and they didn't slack on any of the ingredients. My BF got the Waffle Medley with berries, whip cream, syrup. He had a craving for waffles and it hit the spot. The thing was huge. He also had a side of Bacon which was an extra $4. Our Bellinis were really good. The check came to about $34 for the two of us. I kind of liked the dim lighting. It's good if you're hungover and looking like a mess.

Seriously, walk away....quickly. If I could give negative stars I would. The only thing that semi saves this place is the cute 50's decor. Came here hungover, looking for some good fried food. Ordered a cheesesteak and onion rings. How can anyone mess up onion rings?? Well they certainly did. First off $6 for 5 onion rings is ridiculous, even johnny rockets gives you more than that. Second they were disgusting. Like freezer burned and then fried disgusting. I could not. I should've known to cancel my $8 cheesesteak from that experience alone. I ordered a cheesesteak with onion, mushroom and peppers...the only thing edible on it was the bread. Nice fresh bread with chopped up horse meat inside and nasty old mustrooms and dried up peppers. I was STARVING, hungover and because of this though I could keep 2 bites down. It was disgusting. Thank god for the milkshake, which was not anything notable, since all it is is milk and vanilla ice cream to wash out the nasty meat taste from my mouth. I don't how a place like this is still in business with such disgusting quality meat. To top it off prices are not cheap. Save yourselves.

I crave their tomato soup almost constantly. It comes topped with adorable grilled cheese croutons and has power to instantly silence me (save for the occasional moan). The music can sometimes be a bit loud, but the food makes up for it. The burgers are wonderful too and though it's known as a trendy spot, the food really does live up to the hype.

Came here the other day with a girlfriend and wasn't steered wrong.  The food is AMAZING.  Make a reservation if you don't want to wait.  We didn't make one, and waited about 40 mins before we got seated.  Our fault for NOT making one. I had the newly fashion cocktail to start.  I'm a new bourbon drinker, and if you're new like me - this is the drink for you.  It's tasty and fragrant.  Yum. For apps, we got deviled eggs.  So flavorful and yummy.  so so good. For Entree, I had the pork chop.  It was an awesome big HUNK of meat that was as tender as it can get.  If you're a porkchop fan, you need to partake in this. Will be back here again.

Oh, Bayou, Bayou... Over the years you evolved, changed, grown up. What once was a simple place with funky decor now is a step to upscale dining. Still, elements of old Bayou I loved remain: New Orleans decor, butcher paper on the tables, friendly service. While it never "wow" me with food, it still a solid menu if you're craving a taste of creole in Staten Island. Fair warning - their mixed drinks are strong. Blue Bayou martini was excellent. Shrimp and herb risotto appetizer special really made my evening, it was done just right. Seared tuna was cooked like I asked, medium rare, I wish it had a little more seasoning. Breaded calamari that accompanied it was perfect - I would definitely trade tuna for more calamari! All and all, it was OK, other than annoying lady on next table that kept pushing me adjusting her shawl, I enjoyed it.

Have been going back here for over 10 years - still produces fantastic, simple food.  BYOB is a nice touch - got the grilled octopus (our favorite), a greek salad, and shrimp scampi - everything was perfect.  Went to the restaurant at 915pm - perfect as we did not have to wait.  Recommendation for your first time - patience (wait staff can move at a slower pace than you may be used to).   Simply the best Greek food we have found.
Really great service and food. The prices aren't bad. Nice place to go for lunch with friends. Been going there for years and never had any complains. Very nice people and speedy service.

I have to be  honest - it is tough for me give the small guy a bad review in this world of corporate nonsense; however, i have to express my disappointment in the cafe. The staff is extremely nice and helpful; however, I filled one of their bulk bags with something from the bulk aisle - you know where the dry flours, rice, and other grains are. To my astonishment the next day upon opening the package I sealed and dumping my grains into hot water to cook, there were brown living bugs all throughout it. That was one of the most disgusting food instances that has ever happened to me.  I would imagine bulk bins of grains would have to be severely neglected for a long period of time to get infested with bugs. I hope they read this review and clean up their bulk aisle to avoid this happenening to others as they were very nice people.

My husband and I had huge expectations for this place.  We even saved it for our "last hoorah" on our last night in New York (we moved to San Francisco June 2013).  Wow, this place was highly, highly overrated.   The food was decent, but certainly not great.  And definitley, waaaaaay overpriced.  It kind of felt like a restaurant that was trying to be a five star restaurant and charge five star prices, while delivering food that in my opinion was "meh." Also, as others have pointed out, the service is super slow.  Don't get me wrong, we like long, drawn out meals...but this was just obnoxious.  They had parties of two or three being added every half hour or so...but we could tell that they were trying to get everyone "caught up" (for those who were doing the tasting menu) so they could mass-produce the various tastings.  What this meant was that those of us who had gotten there half hour before those who joined later ended up having to wait around for them to try out the tastings we had already had.   I think this place is a great idea; however, the quality of food is just not where it should be.  This restaurant lacks coordination - I think they need to master the timing of their dishes, figure out a way to service their customers without having them sit around for half an hour between tastings, and lower their prices.  You're not a five star restaurant, so stop charging such high prices!

Great staff and service, cozy and inviting interior and interesting food and drinks selection.   Loved: * Crispy pig ears (glad I was talked into ordering it) - truly crispy and nicely balanced with picked cabbage * Ribs - great peppery rub! * Dee's nuts - cashews, cocoa rice krispies, bing cherries and bacon...think best trail mix cluster kind of thing you will ever taste * Beignets - only dessert on the menu, fried to order and served with dark chocolate espresso * Hitachino wheat beer on tap! Didn't love: * Oysters - too much going on, hard to taste the actual oysters * Blowfish ceviche - interesting concept with the smoke but adds an odd taste to the dish Outdoor patio seating a bonus for warmer weathers.

I knew I had to come to this place when I looked at the menu and saw an abundance of pork product... my favorite being bacon... on the menu. I came for brunch with a friend who lives in the neighborhood and recommended that we go here. The brunch menu looked delicious and I had some trouble deciding. My friend said she always wants to try new things, but her favorite was the Char No 4 benedict and she had a hard time straying from that. We both got the same thing, go figure. It's their version of a Eggs benedict sandwich, minus that nasty hollandaise sauce. Instead, it hets replaced with a bacon gravy... which really, I mean how can you go wrong? A vast improvement over any hollandaise, I don't care how good you tell me it is. The coffee was delicious as well. I will have to come back and see if I will be able to get anything else off the menu.
I have been eating here for the last 30 years and in spite of that I still go there for a wonderful breakfast. Great omelets, eggs and of course, those pancakes.
Yummy brunch, classy.  Decor on the walls was beautiful butterflies!  The service was great too.

I am charmed.  I want more. We started with a beef noodle soup for the whole family to enjoy.  Our son is really into soup noodles these days, and Sugar Freak did not disappoint on that score. The shrimp & grits were nice, but not entirely what I had expected.  The shrimp were small and the grits were thin & runny, but the creole sauce was fantastic.  My husband's chicken sandwich--with mac-&-cheese piled on top--was tasty:  crispy and creamy in all the right ways.  The stylishly rustic bathroom might be my favorite in Queens.   Given that I haven't yet tried their cocktails (other than the mimosa that came with my brunch entree), I'd say that I have a handful of reasons to try Sugar Freak again, and soon.

I remember this place as a little one. My grandfather never liked it and preferred another sandwich shop that is no longer open. Our friends and family swore by Cooper's reubens but my grandfather was steadfast in his disdain.  This weekend, while my family was here from down south we decided to grab a couple sandwiches.  What can I tell you, grandpa was right.  The meat is just way too fatty and bland.   The other ingredients were fine, no complaint about the bread, dressing, etc. the meat is just "blah"  It's really sub-par and can't touch any Jewish deli I've ever been to.

Good lord, this place is delicious. I got a Montreal spice bagel with jalapeño cream cheese. I coincidently came in on Free Bagel Day which made this experience even better. The Montreal spice bagel was so good I bought a dozen to go. Service was speedy and extremely friendly. Highly recommend!
Food was very authentic- unique noodle bowls are a nice touch and something different that couldn't get at other Thai places in area - service was a+ Definitely  recommend

Still Awesome!!!  They may have moved, but still making great pies.  The outside seating is a nice addition.  We did have a short wait, but it was the first night open, and it was certainly worth the wait.

I make a point to come here every time I'm in New York at least once. The quality of the noodles alone is enough to make a trip out to Doyers street to get here, but that is merely one facet of why I am so incredibly enamored with Tasty Hand Pulled Noodles. The prices are super cheap, and the quantity of food you get (whether it be dumplings or soup) is always rather large. Not only that, but the service is incredibly quick, you get unlimited amounts of hot Jasmine tea, and the atmosphere is cramped but incredibly homey. I always leave feeling full and happy with my experience, which is all I can ever ask for honestly. This restaurant is everything to me... I can't express my love for it properly.

I love this place!  The dutch pickle place in the far corner makes the best spicy pickles.  The Dutch Eating Place is a great for breakfast, and the Turkey sandwich stand makes a turkey, cranberry, and stuffing sandwich (Thanksgiving on a roll, to Jersey-ites) that is amazing.  There are crafts, and lots of knick-knacks to browse.  If you're a "cheese-head", like I am, stop at Downtown Cheese.

It is ridiculous how much business this place gets.  It's also a ridiculous wait that I cannot understand sometimes even in bad weather.  But it sure is good.  Real good.  Damn good.  Delicious good.  Crazy good.  The kind of food I crave in a strange way.  I think I could eat this breakfast, lunch, and dinner.  More specifically, I can eat that Mexican Corn, Roasted Pork, and any of their Pollo dishes on any given day.  I think I will come here tomorrow.

it was 2:30am on a Saturday night we all had the munchies after spending the night at a lounge and we thought where to go?  "THE MEATBALL SHOP!!" we waited half an hour to be seated had the special naked meatball with the spicy meat sauce ** FYI - the spicy meat sauce was not spicy and this is coming from someone who can't really eat spicy foods overall, the meatball was delicious will have to come back again

One of my favorite life-shortening gastropubs - so good that I generally go at least once every time I hit Philly.   Pros: anything your doctor wouldn't want you to go anywhere near - short rib cheddar fries, BBQ Pork Sammy, Wedge Salad, Kentucky Hot Brown, pickled Truffled Cauliflower.   Musts: the Whiskey King burger with seared foie is maybe my favorite burger in the country.  Bourbon glazed cipollinis, applewood bacon, blue cheese, and an absolutely ridiculous slab of seared foie on every perfectly cooked burger.  Order it with something from the extensive bourbon and rye list and you'll be joining me there on every Philly trip yourself. Cons: gotta go with at most 1 other person, because there are almost no three- and four-tops.  Place is tiny, but worth the wait in my estimation.  You'll be tempted to head to the Shake Shack down the street when you hear the wait - but don't do it.

The burgers at Village Whiskey are amazing. I've tried the (lentil-based) veggie burger and a plain hamburger. The Kentucky Hot Brown is also a delicious turkey option. I would give 5 stars, except they have a no reservation policy. You need to be at the restaurant to put your name down for a table, and the dinner time wait can be upwards of two hours. The food will not disappoint you though!

This place is such a welcome change from the usual hot dogs, burgers, and pizzas in the area.  I've had the tuna burger, sweet potato fries and tuna salad (the ginger dressing rocks).  Everything has been delicious.  Extra points for the condiments bar (teriyaki ketchup, spicy mayo, and wasabi mayo to name a few).  My only gripe is that I often see homeless people soliciting for money while I eat there..   I don't know what can be done to avoid it but it makes me feel a bit uneasy so I no longer dine in.
Great Asian cuisine Recommend the hot n sour soup No msg homemade Leek dumplings and shrimp soup bun too Clean homemade and really good

Their food is amazing i will admit, but there is always a long line for the halal cart that is famous. I'll be honest, it's not really worth the wait, it all taste the same, and the people that work in that cart often switch to other carts to work like they are taking a tiny break because there are not as many customers going to those other carts surrounding it. If you got the time to check it out, I suggest you do. Don't eat it too often though!

Food and service were good, waitress was extremely knowledgable and patient. We were a party of 5 and got seated right away on a Saturday around 11am. I wish they had outdoor seating! I hear they just started delivering 7 days a week which is a plus!

Our second visit to Acacia was with a larger group (5 couples) last night (1/26/08).  Reservations were for 6pm.  We decided on Acacia based on an excellent previous experience about two years ago. Several appetizers were served less than hot, others completely cold.  One basket of bread was served for the entire table, no butter.  Only found the small vessel of olive oil on the table by accident.  Would have been nice if the server attempted to clear some glasses and tell us about the oil. Waited longer than an appropriate amount of time for the entrees.  Food was generally very good, however, one order was completely incorrect and needed to be taken back. Dessert was good all around.  Only problem was the server didn't seem interested in offering coffee to the entire table and refills had to be requested. Here's the shocker.  After what I would consider a generally nice night out with friends, within minutes of paying the bill, we were asked to leave!  Not because we were being unruly or rude.  Because they wanted to flip the table!  It was after 9pm at this point. Apparently, they felt it was our fault that others were waiting for an hour or so for that table.  I'm pretty sure that responsibility falls squarely on management.  How long has this place been in business and they don't know how to manage reservations? Needless to say, all 10 of us are extremely disappointed and appalled at the lack of professionalism exhibited by this restaurant and their staff.  Never again for us after that. Maybe they should just stick with smaller groups (2-4 people).  That way, they can focus on their short term profits and let the larger clients go where they will be appreciated.

I came her based on a recommendation from an acquaintance and was completely happy in every way. My brother and law stopped here before a show at the Trocadero and were able to get our order in time to see the opening band. The food is delicous -the rolls are soft yet not too soft with meat cooked perfectly and slight crunch of onions not overdone like some others. The cheese was melted into the steak and mushrooms were delicous -just exceeded my expectations and they even have a nice small cooler full of local and national craft beer which is a plus.

You know what's great for a hangover? Sitting right next to a baby whose keening wails pierce your brain over and over again until you are forced to palm his head like a basketball and casually toss him over the wall of Cafe Luluc's picturesque garden, much to the horror of his mother. Thankfully, I didn't have to destroy any families last Saturday, because this little guy was the quietest baby of all time. Why? Because his mother kept feeding him little pieces of Luluc's FANTASTIC pancakes. No one could possibly have any problems as long as they get a few bites of these crispy, yet fluffy wonders. They rival the best I've ever had (Clinton St. Baking Company), but they are half the price, and don't require a two hour wait. And even though they are accompanied by real maple syrup, they don't require anything except perhaps the fresh strawberries and bananas provided. Luluc's expertise extends to savory options as well; my bacon, cheddar and tomato omelette sprinkled with chives was aesthetically perfect, and as tasty as any egg dish in recent memory. And although the fries were merely passable, the accompanying fresh greens (dressed in what I believe was some sort of basil vinaigrette) more than compensated for their counterpart. Combine charmingly simple, yet perfectly delicious food with affordable prices (the aforementioned two dishes came in at $18 plus tip), efficient service and a pleasant garden, and you've got my new favorite brunch spot.

The Good: - Excellent draft beer selection - Walls of teevees for your sporting pleasure - Friendly staff - A stripclub-esque DJ booth The Bad - Tiny wings, cheese fries were fries with kraft singles on top - The Aerosmith and Nickleback paraphernalia
The outdoor patio is prime real estate for happy hour, take it from me the St Gin cocktail & all their martinis are to die for!

Had the angry Dragon, Philadelphia, Boston, and tuna avocado roll. The Philadelphia and angry Dragon roll was so amazing. Really great decor,  friendly staff. Will come back. Although driving route was slightly sketchy, the experience was well worth it once I stepped inside.

Despite the copious number of items in the tome of "All that is Wrong with New Jersey," there are 2 things the Garden State does better than anyone else: bowling and diners.  Combine the two, and you get a small thermonuclear explosion of pure, unadulterated awesome.  Anyone who has never been to a NJ diner has never been to a real diner.  So, after a night of bowling with my friends at Van Houten Lanes, we decided that the only way to end the night was to go to a diner for deserts.  I had never been to the State Street Grill, but as soon as I entered it, I knew it was going to be an enjoyable experience.  The place is clean and well decorated, with neutral wooden paneling as opposed to the usual high gloss of many other diners.  The result is a very warm and inviting place that looks very large without seeming cavernous.   My friend and I each ordered a slice of carrot cake, but were disappointed to discover they only had one left, which I gave to my friend.  Then I learned they had a NY style carrot cheesecake which I ordered instead.  One look at that slice of heavenly custard and I had a hunch that the tradition of exceptional diners had not just been met, it had been exceeded.   Then I tried it.  All remaining doubt went the way of the dodo as my taste buds transcended this mortal world and my mind was brought into a state of bliss... also just like the dodo.  My friends assure me the rest of the food is just as good, and I will definitely return to check the validity of their statements.  I am confident I won't be disappointed. PS. Bonus points were awarded for having a bucket that read "Extra Heavy Mayonnaise," sparking a heated discussion among my friends as to what that could possibly be.  My bet is they use extra love.
Delicious topping (I got the clam pie) but quite expensive and when getting to the last pieces of pizza the base got super chewi and hard to bite off. But still, a beautiful taste.
4.5 stars.. downgraded because of the wait/cramped barstool seating which can make enjoying these delightful items a little more awkward. I love breakfast food! yum.. The apple dumpling is AMAZING!!

I believe this is probably one of the best pizzas I've had in NY.   The crust is very thin the outer crust is charred as others mentioned which is something I usually do not like but it was still flavorful and tender. The sauce is light, the mozzarella fresh, buffalo style "globs" for lack of a better description...pictures ppl have posted here are accurate. Service was very efficient - almost a little too quick but not in a bad, pushy way... Had the diavolo which wasn't spicy as described but the right combo of salami and cheese.  Also had the goat cheese salad with pine nuts in lemon juice - that was very fresh, light & delicious. Liked that they had an Italian MTV-type program playing in the background, I don't know why, that's just me. The space is completely wood covered - cute.  I think it could be a lot of fun if you came with a group of friends.  I thought the people who worked there were polite.  The tables are a little jammed together...so I'm sure if you went on the weekend you'll be practically sitting in your neighbor's lap - which might not be a bad thing...

I really don't know why I waited so long to try this place.  I really love Thai food and I normally go to Pattaya (which is also very tasty.)  My friends recently went there during University City Dining days and had a great experience so I was looking forward to trying it, too.  My opportunity came when my friend wanted to "go out" to celebrate her completion of the bar exam that day.  At first I thought she meant "go out" like to a crowded bar somewhere downtown but when her husband explained that we were going to Vientiane Cafe I was more than happy to tag along.  I think one of the reasons I had never gone there was that it doesn't look like anything special from the outside, so I was surprised to see just how large it was inside when we got there.  The ambiance was nice.  I felt like we could be ourselves, talking about the "bag lady" at the bar, and be boisterous without being awkward.  But it was still quiet enough to enjoy a more relaxing meal.   We had a group of 7 of us and they easily and quickly accommodated us.  Between the seven of us I think we all ordered either the Panang Curry or the Pad Thai.  Both were delicious but the panang curry was truly something special.  I really don't know how they made it so good but it was SO good.  It makes me mouth water just thinking about it now.  One thing I will say, though, is that the spice levels really don't matter at all.  The have a scale of 1 to 5 with 5 being the spiciest.  I got a 4 and most of the others got 2, however they all tasted the same, which was not so spicy.  Normally I would have been really upset that it wasn't very spicy but the flavor was so good I didn't even care. On the downside, prices were pretty high and the service was only so-so.  Also, they are cash only which I find really weird and inconvenient.  With that said, the deliciousness will definitely draw me back again!

I'm new to yelp. I'm a yelp baby, if you will. I want to write a positive review, but Caseus, I have to tell you, I've got some beef with you - and it isn't grass fed. My boyfriend and I were here as they were boasting a southern special - fried chicken and "southern style" braised bacon.....Please, Chef at Caseus - Don't insult southerners like this! I lived there for 15 years, this didn't come close. Just because you slap southern in the title, it doesn't mean it is! Take a trip there at least!.. Two stars for attentive service. Other than that, you're lack of respect for the southern cuisine was a little upsetting. It just goes to show, Northerners don't know what fried chicken is all about.

This place was fantastic!   I went with three of my girlfriends the other night and I was blown away by how good the food was here.  First of all, the menu is pretty diverse; there are a ton of things on there, so it's easy to find something that everyone will like.  Secondly, all of the dishes are pretty inexpensive - I don't think there was an item on the menu over $20 (most of the selections were around $10-$12).  Thirdly and most importantly, the food was delicious...did I already say that? There were a lot of reviews for the Asian Tea Leaf salad and the Thousand Layer Bread - so we ordered both of those.  The Tea Leaf salad was definitely not my favorite and seemed really over-seasoned and over-worked.  On the other hand, the Thousand Layer Bread (which is not 1,000 layers) was delicious.  We had it with the curry chicken dip and it was really good.  We also had the crab rangoon, which were. . . pretty basic. This place is BYOB but be warned that there is a $12 corking fee for each bottle of wine you bring.  I thought I could outsmart them by bringing a giant bottle, but the waitress was too quick for me and told us that since it was a large bottle, it would cost $24.  That's probably the only bad thing I have to say about this place. I definitely recommend it!

My second trip to Becco didn't disappoint. This time I went with the three Pasta special. It was amazing. I am still trying to figure out how to make the cocoa ravioli with pumpkin stuffing.  The fried mozzarella was heavenly. For dessert the dessert sampler was a win, with me having a hard time which dessert I liked better. This is going to become a must visit for every trip to NYC.

chicken burro for the winnnn. excellent beans and rice. i will dock 1 star for not having sweet plantains that i so strongly desire. if you are a fan of lightly salted yellow plantains, try the side dish, because the lime dipping sauce is very good. midori margarita - oh hellllll yes. the price is right. a great place to go with the girls to catch up and get loud because its damn loud in there anyhow!
AMAZING BAKED CLAMS! Veal don pep, string bean salad, fresh moz, EVERYTHING is great!

first off, the Burnt Ends and this place are AMAZING! If theres any reason to come to this place is for that delicious "meat candy" as the our waitress seegan(i hope im spelling it right) called them. Not only is ALL the food amazing, the service is just as amazing. As soon as you walk in, you get a warm welcome and a nice smile from all the staff.  Our waitress was very helpful and very attentive with our drink refills.( the root beer here is the bomb as well) I give the place 5 stars because the atmosphere was great, our waitress attentive to our needs, and the food was Great!

I have add much better Ethiopian food elsewhere. To start of the review, they don't have honey wine. The vegetarian combination is 25 bucks which serves for two but there is none for people dining alone. The food was okay, the lentil entrees were not up to par. The lentil sambosa was undercooked. No complaint with the service though.

this review is for wedding and similar events. we have been there several times and found the food to be poor quality and not much variety.  the preparations are cheap, poor taste and not creative at all.

These dudes will scare you. They know that they scare you, and they love it. It's their thing, don't take it personal. Know your order way ahead of time. Literally, practice it. Have your money (cash only) out. Close your eyes, step up and say your order (should be no more than 4 words)...and say nothing else. The sandwich is well worth it.

We were looking for a place to eat around the Hells Kitchen and stumbeled upon The Hourglass Tavern.  Both of us are picky eater with appreciation of good food. The food at The Hourglass was not just good, it was near perfect. The homemade bread, the salad, the main dishes were delicious and  the service was outstanding. We highly recommend this place.
To me, there is no better falafel, than that at Mamoun's. Anytime I'm in New Haven it's such a treat to go there!

Went here only because we couldn't deal with the line next door at Grimaldi's, and realized this place had some affiliation. Upon a quick Yelp, saw that the reviews were good, so went for it. Hubby and I were able to be seated right away, though it was a pretty crowded Sunday evening. Ordered two glasses of red (liked his better than mine) and the Margherita (always gotta go with the basic when trying a pizza place for the first time). Pie came out surprisingly quickly. Have to say, we were both sadly underwhelmed. While the ingredients tasted fresh, there seemed to be a major lack of flavor. We kept hoping it would get better, but it just... didn't. In the end, we didn't finish the pie and didn't really care to take the rest home either. Pretty cool though that Patsy Grimaldi (who I obviously thought by the name was a woman until I saw the name on his jacket) was walking around greeting customers and bringing things out to the tables. He even approached us as we were leaving and asked how the meal was. Of course, I smiled and said "great!". Mediocre pizza or not, it definitely wasn't enough to make me insult a cute old man!

Minca, the savior of my late night craving for ramen in the alphabet city. I dont really remember the day i was there, i only knew it was cold, dark, and the how i craved ramen. I was satisfied. We were there 15 mins before closing, and i was prepared to be hush out of the spot but we were greeted by the kindest waitress with the most beautiful smile i have ever seen, "welcome" she said, and i was in heaven. Must be the crave factor, and i was also extremely hungry. After came back down to earth, i realized Minca is actually pretty compact, however that does not mean they only have 3 items on the menu. PIcked my soup base,  noodle, and some extra desired morsel, and this time, heaven came in a bowl. It was Good. So good that i ate half of my friend's experimental ramen after chow down mine where he had to order another one. Pro: Not crowded (must be the alphabet city magic. who would WANT to go pass Ave A?) Thick soup base with tons of flavor (some might find it too powering) Friendly staff and fast service. con: pricey but understandable. A bit salty at times. PS: Hard to find parking (good luck) and easy to miss the spot if not paying attention. (its in the middle of the block)
What a great place for weekend brunch!  It's located in a great neighborhood.  Even though I over-ate, I walked it off with a stroll around the neighborhood which has great architecture.

I've walked past Bridget Foy's for decades and did not come in until this past week. We were warmly received by the hostess and seated immediately.  Our waiter, however, seemed to be having some trouble. He came eventually and took our drink order.  When the drinks arrived, we were ready to order.  He said he'd BRB!!!  Awhile later he finally came around again. Food order went in, food came out. Food was a mixed bag.  Some things were tasty, some were meh.  The calamari was pretty good, the mac and cheese was unfortunately pretty bland.  The parmesan grilled cheese with tomato soup was good, but it's a big sandwich. This may or may not be unrelated to my lunch at Bridget Foy's, but after eating there, I had no appetite for almost two days and an upset stomach. Boo. Glad I finally went in, doubtful I'll go back.  Nothing that was truly special.  Sorry to say.  :(

Half price wine or champagne? Send it!  Got the salmon and the seafood fettuccine. Don't bother tryin to finagle a stack of their world famous pancakes at dinner time. Turns out its a strictly breakfast item. Hmm. UPDATE: went for brunch- the pancakes are outrageous!! So rich, and I loved the crispy edges. The syrup was light and not too sweet; a perfect compliment to the hot cakes.  The eggs florentine were wonderful too. A balance of rich flavors and decent portions.

Service was great. Loved the salad - mixed greens, goat cheese, dried tomatoes with chianti dressing! Excellent. We ordered the Wednesday special even though it was thursday (the waitress was really nice about it). Prosciutto, truffle oil, arugula. It was good, but for some reason some of the grains tasted undercooked :( was disappointed by that. But I love risotto, so I'll definitely go back for more. So glad we got a salad and 1 risotto, it was perfect combination.

I thought the food was really good. We ordered take out. Based on the reviews of other yelpers, we ordered the asparagus & gluten, and as-you-wish. Both were good, but we thought the homestyle tofu was the most delicious dish we ordered. We also got the scallion pancakes. I've had plenty of tsong-yo-bing in Taiwan. These were a little dry - and not very doughy/flaky - but ok. This totaled $40. I think they increased prices a little since updating their website menu, but otherwise good (relatively healthy) food option. And of course they deliver!

Kinoko Soup. Seriously - possibly the best soup I ever had, bar none. Everything is fresh and tasty. Did I tell you about their Kinoko Soup? Only complaint: vodka came out a bit watered down and drinks are pricey.

First time eating here, I read some of the review here in Yelp, but still had some doubts if it was a good place to eat. Boy was I wrong. From our waitress explaining the menu and food to the quick service and Amazing food, I recommend this place 100%. I had the 5 course tasting menu that give me 4 savory dishes and 1 dessert.  off all the dishes I had the two the stood out is the Rib eye with the potato Leek hash brown with creamed spinach. the meat is cooked medium rare with this jus that pulls everything together. it almost melts in your mouth. And then I had the Caramelized Torija. Its this bread pudding, flan tasting awesome looking thing of  a dessert served with a grape fruit section. Will definitely go back and try the 10 course tasting menu.

Got here at 11:00 on a Friday morning.  Was told we'd have to order from the brunch menu by the time we got seated.  We were disappointed at first, but a lot of the breakfast items are also on the brunch menu.  Waited outside for a little over 1/2 an hour.  The pancake samples were a nice preview of what was in store. 3 French models were seated at the table next to us.  We wondered why they received their food first, until we saw what they ordered.  2 mini pancakes with butter and blueberries on the side.  They all ordered the same thing and not one of them finished.  What a tragic waste.  They kept staring at our food in amazement when it arrived: -  Blueberry pancakes (3 regular size) -  Brioche French toast -  grilled chorizo -  sweet potato fries.   All normal size.  Nothing on the side.  The way it's meant to be eaten.  The models must have thought we were pigs devouring this feast!  We didn't care - we weren't there for fashion week and food's not for looking at where we come from! The pancakes were definitely our favorite.  Fluffy perfection.  French toast was also delectable.  Carbs at their best!
College students make better pasta than this in their dorm rooms.
The food is a bit better than your average diner, but this is not a 'diner' per se. They do not sell milkshakes (?!).  Service was awful besides.

Classy. Upscale. Comfortable. Whiskey. Beer. Yep....that sums it up. Great bar that had a ton of beer selections that would satisfy any beer connoisseur. This place has a boy's club type feel that I envision power lunches taking place in, but is equally romantic and relaxed that I felt comfortable just hanging out with friends having a few drinks after dinner in the city. Only letdown was the service--our waitress was missing for most of our time at the table and we had to flag a manager for our check. Seems like they could use an extra hand or two, especially for the busy Saturday night crowds.

always fresh la colombe, the nicest staff ever, the most interesting and esoteric cast of regulars, new art every month and ample outdoor seating! i love this place, seriously, i'm there almost 2 times every day. and i mean EVERY day. and though i have yet to do it, if you order the "holy diver" in the voice of ronnie james dio you get ten percent off!

We were lucky enough to get a reservation on a last minute trip to NYC for a birthday celebration. Everything was fantastic. Fresh oysters, tuna tartare, scallop special, lobster mac & cheese (WOW) and molten chocolate lava cake. All were or nearly the best we've ever had. The servers were great and almost seemed to appear just when you needed them.

A real gem.  Unlike Faneuil Hall in Boston and Harbor Place in Baltimore, locals actually can shop here for fresh foods to cook at home.  Food is a bit more affordable than those venues- had a great order of dumplings for under $5.   I'm not into this cuisine, but for those that like Pennsylvania Dutch cooking and baked goods make sure you don't go Sunday as those stands (20% of the stands probably) are closed for the Sabbath.

Pros- Song is a beautiful restaurant with a backyard space. My glasses were always filled with water, thanks to a busy working staff. Cons- CASH ONLY! no reservations! 1)Underseasoned fried calamari; you must drench your seafood in sauce to get some flavor. 2) Beef pad see ew was too sweet and the over cooked beef was hard to chew. 3) Fried rice was too salty (no wonder my water glass was always filled) Maybe the chef was having a bad day, but it is no excuse to serve poor food to paying customers.

What a difference it makes between coming to a restaurant on Saturday compared to when I was previously here on a Monday night. We arrived at 8:15 to a crowded restaurant and one table for 4 was available. Hostess told the owner there were no other reservations. So you figured they would give us the table right? Nope! They made us wait 15 minutes for this tiny table for two. Food was a hit or miss. Lasagna was very good (although the sauce was ordinary). Chicken was blah. Antipasto had low quality cheeses (whoever heard of blue cheese as part of an Italian antipasto?). By 9:00, place was pretty much empty. Service was ok. Owner works hard, but there are a few kinks and consistency issues that need to be worked out. After dinner drinks on the house were a nice treat, which swayed my review from 2 to 3 stars.

I am very disappointed in this place. It used to have the best pizza around. Last week I went and Had a glass of wine at the bar and put in an order for a pizza to go. 45 minutes later I had to grab a waiter to check on my order and he brought my luke warm pizza to me. Also it did not taste the same. I was there about a month ago and tried to get a table and there were people milling around waiting and finally one of the "customers" told us we had to sign a sheet a paper to be on the waiting list for a table. We walked right out. There is no organization there.

Tucked away behind a parking garage is 500 degrees. It is a quaint burger spot on Sansom. To start off the place has phenomenal hours, it is hard find a solid burger at 3am in Philly. The menu gives the customer a variety of burger options, something for everyone. I ordered the 500 burger. A classic burger, their way. I ordered it medium well- it was more medium not complaining. The toppings complimented the burger nicely, however I couldn't figure out what the house sauce was made of, it didn't have much taste. My experience overall was positive, a good alternative burger when you need one. If you go try the 500, buffalo blue or the turbo. Enjoy.

I couldn't possibly think more highly of a restaurant. Visiting NY this past weekend, I found myself wandering around and between meal times. I thought, "If I could stop in anywhere for a bite to eat, where would that be?" -- So stop into Gramercy Tavern I did. No reservations, no time to go back to the hotel to change into something more appropriate, just "this is the ideal situation for me right now" mentality. I was by myself, so I sat at the bar. Everyone who helped me was wonderful, especially Jeremy (?) the bartender with the vintage Singer tattoo who listened to what I was in the mood for and recommended the Baby Carrots, Farro and Swiss Chard appetizer. It was perfect. Very fresh and delicious, but not too filling (I had plans for dinner a bit later in the evening). I started with a glass of Syrah, and was then coerced into another glass and a half (not that it took too much arm-twisting... it was more like an offer, really).  And by the time I got home, I realized that I had been treated to a glass and a half of wine. I'm thinking that I should start dining alone more often... this was truly one of the best experiences I've ever had. Thank you Jeremy, thank you Gramercy Tavern.

Best Pizza in Hartford, if you like fold-able huge slices with a cornmeal dusting on the crust!  Location of store sucks, but free delivery makes that a non-issue for me.  I lived in NYC for ten years and this place is most reminiscent of NYC style pizza!

Instead of simply repeating what everyone else is saying/typing, just do yourself a favor and GO! I'm super picky when it comes to Japanese and Korean Cuisine, especially the "simpler" dishes like SOBA.... If I had one meal left one earth, I would really have to debate on Ippudo, it is simply that good. Actually, not good, GREAT. I no longer live in NYC, however will go back in a few weeks and this is my first pit stop. Yes, the line is long. Yes, the place is trendy. Service? 5/5 Food? 5/5 Location? 5/5 PERFECT
Recommend this place! Incredible meals, outstanding service and amazing atmosphere.

This place is amazing. First off, I always love to patronize an establishment that promotes and pairs with other local businesses. I was here for one of the food and wine tastings with The Wine Thief which was very well done and more than worth the amount paid. The host/hostess is always elegant, professional and welcoming, the service is always on the top of their game, energetic, thoughtful, and willing to please and the drinks are one of a kind a true triumph of masters of mixology. The food is very good but expect NY prices I have come in and spent well over 250 from time to time just covering two. The atmosphere speaks for itself and most certainly makes you forget about your being in New Haven. Always ask for recommendations if the drink menu seems intimidating, the staff is very knowledgeable and always have great suggestions. When in doubt, start off with the Four Thieves, The Grand Prix, or my ever favorite Church Key (Cheers John). If you're not sure where to start with the food, start off with the fries with truffle oil; they are amazing and have a most delicate and ticklish mouth feel. Or dabble into the cured meat and cheese plates; always a favorite of mine. Mussels have always been an all time favorite of mine and 116 Crown does not disappoint if you're a die-hard seafood fan. Finish off with a "Float" for dessert just make sure you have the number for a taxi at hand, you can tend to be so absorbed in all of the details and fragrant drinks that you might forget how to walk on the way out. If you're looking for a quiet place, go early especially on the weekends. And do try to dress up a little and add to the atmosphere. Enjoy! I look forward to continuing my patronage and introducing more to the experience of 116.

The food is good However the service sucks!!!!! Not only do you have to wait on a line like at a school cafeteria but you have to deal with the mean lunch ladies aka their waitress. I never had such snobby wait staff, they really think they are to good to help you. I really liked the food but totally not worth their attitude.
My choice for Whiz wit.  Still solid post drinking food, but since I don't drink like that anymore, I have more alert taste buds, and they still a pretty good.

Delicioussss chicken and rice!! No joke. You have to try the halaL guys if you happen to be in New York. Try to walk by their food cart and you will die a little inside. The red sauce is soo spicy. Don't attempt to add generously. Both the gyro with rice and chicken with rice were yumyumyum! Ask for sauce on the side.

Great for drinks, great for dinner, only mediocre for brunch. I am constantly impressed with the beer selection. I've been a loyal patron for a year or more and still manage to go in and find a new beer I haven't tried yet. The dinner is also awesome - the pizza, chicken press, gnocchi, and burger are all great choices. The brunch, unfortunately, is so-so, and since Sabrina's just opened up in University City I would recommend that for brunch over Tap (which pains me to say because I love it in every other way). Also, the bartenders are insanely friendly and awesome!
Best pancakes EVERRRRRR!!
Their tzatziki and house red are dope

Tip: No longer byob. They serve wine and beer. I tried this place after reading "Little Princes", which is set in Nepal and I recommend reading if you like traveling.  I read about momos and then ate them at Cafe Himalaya. They are so good! I thought I had tried all the dumplings there were-- Japanese dumplings, Korean dumplings, Chinese dumplings, Sichuan dumplings... and now Tibetan dumplings!  I've gotten both the veggie and chicken and they're both fresh.  Of course fried is greater than steamed. This place gets 4 stars because the food is really good for its price.  You can definitely get a meal under $10. My boyfriend loved the Chili Dofu-- it sounds simples but the flavors blend really well together to make a dish so delightful!

Blue Ribbon, been to both locations multiple times and I would say they are on par with each other.  Now onto the food... Escargot - Ever since I was a child, I always found snails to be uhhh lets say non pleasing to the eyes or the thought of eating it was blah.  Buuuuut I grew old and wiser and tried  the escargot at blue ribbon.  To my amazement, it crushed all my childhood perceptions on snails.  Thank you Blue Ribbon :) Beef Marrow & Oxtail Marmalade - JUST ORDER IT Fried Chicken - There's nothing like it, moist, sweet and salty chicken that will make you slouch in your seat as you chew away.  (Ordered multiple times) Rack of Lamb - I'm a sucker for Lamb and the rack did not disappoint.  Perfectly cooked, moist and flavorful. I just love this place...till next time

Finally. Good mexican food in the five boroughs. Not just good, but really really good. Cactus tacos, amazing. Corn w/ spicy sauce & Cotija -- even better. Prices, atmosphere were great too. We'll be back.

The best thing about this restaurant is that they are very affordable.  I did also really enjoy my pasta dish (Ravioli with asparagus and mushroom).  On the downside...it is extremely loud and crowded in here, the service is very abrupt and unfriendly, the pizza was terrible, they only have one wine by the glass option which was bad and did i mentioned that the pizza was terrible.

I think about having the butcher's steak all the time. It's so tender and tasty and all at a very reasonable price of $15. Loovveee the sides which are all great from the ones I've tried: pan-fried truffle mash, long beans, and spinach gratin. I've also tried the veal flank steak with chimichurri oil which was okay but not spectacular. Dessert!!! Vanilla ice cream with pork cracklins and chocolate sauce. Okay, it was a bit too rich eating it alone but it's good for sharing. If you do decide to come, be prepared to wait. No reservations are taken and full party needs to be present to be seated.

They have my favorite cocktail in the world as a happy hour special - The Dark and Stormy. I make it at home all of the time, but I love it even more when it is handed to me for $5 or less! I have heard great things about the food, so I will have to make another trip soon!

Very disappointed in this restaurant, I heard a lot of good things before I went. I took my girlfriend out for dinner and drinks; first the service was awful it took 10 minutes just for a waiter to come to our table.  Then after we ordered our food and drinks it took 15 minutes for our drinks to come and another 20 minutes for our food. The food was lack luster at best; I will not be coming back.
My first ramen experience was great at Minca. The place was packed but the staff was really great. It was nice to sit right at the bar and watch the cooks on the other side - impressive.

The food here is soo delicious! There was a wait to get in for dinner but it went by quickly, as there are a lot of nearby places on the street to wander around in for killing time. I had kimchi soondubu which was really flavorful and good! There was a pleasant selection of banchan that accompanied the meal. The food came out quickly and everyone I was with seemed to be very satisfied with what they had ordered. The restaurant had an upbeat atmosphere with nice decor that contributed to making the experience a positive one. Our server was attentive and good about making sure we were taken care of. I will definitely come back in the future!

An excellent and interesting menu! The food was excellent.  There is an exceptional balance of both the 'usuals' and different options from which to choose! You should definitely make this a stop on your way through Burlington!

The best price for a quality lunch around. The establishment is also extremely clean, which is something that many midtown delis lack. The employees are so friendly, I can't help but walk around with a permanent smile while I'm there. AND The selection of gourmet foods, which include a deli full of  sandwiches, a hot bar, fresh made to order salads, and Asian Options (Soba, Udon, Ramen, and Bibimbap) is second to none with extremely reasonable prices when comparing to the area. I shouldn't even want to add this positive publicity because I don't want to see my favorite lunchtime eatery get too crowded and highly demanded, which economics 101 suggests will increase the prices as well. Regardless, I can't help but spread the word because this place is that good.

AMBIANCE:  Cute, brick exposed place.  Went on a nice summer night and all the walls were down facing the street and there were several tables outdoors.  Nice breeze.  The menus are handwritten just to add to the appeal.  To note, this place is like the one crowded restaurant on the street--for good reason!!  Of the patrons, I noticed quite a lot of male on male meals.  They know where the good stuff is. SERVICE:  Great.  Constant water checks, prompt service.  They let you sit and relax and do not rush you out the door like many NY places.  We had an 830 reservation for 5 which was immediately honored upon our arrival even though it was quite crowded inside. FOOD: In order of favorites --FREE DELICIOUS FOCCACIA BREAD W OLIVE OIL AND VINEGAR...save some to dip in the sauces of the pastas! --Calamari ($9): grilled calamari over a bed of arugula.  Note that this is grilled calamari and not breaded/fried.  It was quite a hit with my family..especially since the flavors spread onto the arugula as well. 1.  Spinach gnocchi ($14): HOMEMADE w gorgonzola sauce;  EVERYONE knows to order this and it did not disappoint!  We had 2 orders!  Super creamy,  the size of the dish was quite large, especially considering that is is too rich to finish alone (but sharing is caring!).  The gnocchis were sooo soft and DO melt in your mouth.  If compared to Uva..Uva's gnocchi had a distinct truffle taste...comparable softness of gnocchi but completely different flavor...this was more like what I would describe as a thick alfredoish sauce (Butter, half n half, thick cream, you get the idea).  Both delicious.   2.  Tarliatelle al ragu ($13): HOMEMADE w tomato sauce and ground beef;  MMMMMM this was MEATY and RICH!  I ordered this for my dad and he ate it all..if you like meat then get this!! 3.  Spaghetti alla chitarra ($13): HOMEMADE with fresh chopped tomato, basil, tomato; rich in flavor, also had chunks of mozzarella.  Quite tasty. 4.   Special of the day: pasta with tomatoes, asparagus, and shrimp;  oh man...I ordered this for my mom and lucky me I got to eat all her PRAWNS (huge huge huge) because she has high cholesterol.  I would say this dish had the least amount of flavor but made up for it in PRAWNS.   PRICES: Cash onlyl!  What you pay is totally worth it..and the prices are not bad at all.  The pasta's were all from $11-14.  Lambchops were the highest price of $27.  Second highest is the Sirloin steak $25.  The fish of the day is market price.   ***For 5 pastas, 1 appetizer and 3 Peronis, the bill was LESS THAN $100.   I chose this place for my Dad's 51st birthday dinner and it was a success.  My family enjoyed their meal and everyone was happy and full and I did not go broke when handed the bill.  5 stars.

What a hidden gem! It's located right next to the famous Grimaldi's but what most people don't know is that this place is owned by Patsy Grimaldi. Thus, you can skip the long lines at Grimaldi's and come here. I went on a Sunday at 6 pm and there was no wait, unlike Grimaldi's which had about 30 people lined up on the sidewalk. Our server was extremely friendly and attentive. We ordered the margherita pizza and it was DELICIOUS. Although they should technically be the same, I enjoyed it a lot better than when I ate at Grimaldi's, which is still good also.

As me being a native brooklyn girl. This square pizza is the best. i was there last friday and i loved it. The spumoni was good, and the square pizzas are excellent. That and a nice ride to coney island after that is the best, you can't beat it.

Los Gallos is definitely off the beaten path, but it is a must. I asked a few Mexican friends where they go and Los Gallos was a consistent answer. Since Los Gallos is BYOB, my girlfriend and I now go on weekends. It is a great substitue for Cantina. It is cheaper, better, and you never have to wait. The only thing Cantina has over Los Gallos is outdoor seating. Contradictory to Yelp information, they do accept credits cards!

Was first in line, 8am on a Saturday, by 8:20, the line was to Houston St.  The wait was worth it.  Tried the popular blueberry pancakes...absolutely incredible.  Love the hipster vibe this place has.
Wonderful restaurant! Good price!!! Each dish serves 3 people easily! My favorite is the spaghetti with meatballs!

Going out to eat is about living in the moment, and for brunch moments this Has to be my favorite spot. Try to come hungry though as the portion sizes seem to be more American than French. Interior looks like the love-child of Japan and France but pulls it off masterfully. Servers have always been attentive, given great recommendations, and not been pestering or overbearing in any way. Management presence is almost nonexistent; always a good sign. It's a well put together menu with some great salads, wines, beers (including French dry ciders woooo), and appetizers (their escargot is fantastic). Never had room to sample the desserts--some day. Even their outside seating area, though sparse, is nice. Overall the focus of this place is its terrific mix of sweet and savory crepes. Everything else just accentuates this strength. My only suggestion would be to overhaul the cheese program (little expensive and nothing is listed) and to disassociate yourselves from l'etage (shudder).

EAT HERE!!!!!!! I absolutely LOVE Momofuku Ssam and Noodle Bar.. I've eaten here a ton!! I haven't been to Ko yet but definitely intend to try it. Be sure to order the Pork Buns!!!!! If at the Noodle Bar definitely get the Kim Chee Stew and when at the Ssam Bar order as much as you can!! Amazing food!! Great vibe! Cool staff! Great music!! Try the Milk bar next door for desert!

Giuseppina's is one of those places where I kick myself and say, "Why haven't I come here before?!" A mere 10 minute walk from my apartment, this place serves awesome pies in the most unassuming location. 3 friends and I came by around 8:30 on a Sunday and there was no wait. The interior is intimate and candlelit. It's a very similar setup to Lucali, where it's an open kitchen and you choose your own toppings for your pies. They also put tons of fresh basil leaves on top- my favorite! Our server was attentive and I loved his Brooklyn accent! He pointed us in the right direction for wine as well, so props to him for that. (Oh yes- one difference between this place and Lucali's is that they do have a wine list, whereas Lucali's is BYOB.) I'm sad that I didn't discover this place sooner. Dare I say it- I like it better than Lucali because it's less hyped and easier for me to get to. Hope I can return before I leave New York next month.

I had an appetizer, four pastas, a main, and a dessert with 2 cocktails, plus the freebies they throw in. Let's just say that 1) the crudo: raw yellowtail had too much salty condiments which drowned out the fish 2) the pasta was too heavy, especially the red sauces, 3) my suckling pork was just at that point where there was too much fat to meat, though the skin was an amazing crunchiness, and 4) my pear sorbet had too much grit in it...

The milkshakes here are sooooo yummy! I loved the salted caramel one and the black and white was pretty perfect too. The service is quick and when you're having a fat kid Friday, they have all deliciously bad things you could want. I had the cheeseburger and cheese fries and P had the cheeseburger and hot dog. All were good, but I think I'd rather skip the food and just come back for the milkshakes, which are exceptional.
Love this place.  Delicious, fun, and friendly.

Our first visit lead to a second visit. we had awesome crapes, panini and French onion soup and wow what a fantastic waitstaff .. if ever in Burlington, VT a must stop!! gr8 food, drinks and atmosphere  Don't be discouraged if there is a line they move quick and it'll be well with any amount of wait time.
Great food at a decent price. They put their own spin on a variety of classic Cuban dishes.

Very fresh oysters. Great deal with their oyster riot special. My friend is a bug oyster lover and he really enjoyed everything. We also got the oyster po boy sandwich,delicious!! Service was all right, a little slow, not no major complains.

After wandering down Chestnut street from my hotel looking for a place to eat I came across Han Dynasty.  From the outside it was very unassuming but once you enter it's a beautiful old building with interesting architectural details.  I'm guessing it was  maybe an old bank. There is a large bar area and they have a great selection of beers and spirits.  The bar staff was very attentive. I'm rating this 4 out of 5 instead of 5 star due to the following reasons: I was not greeted by the hostess as she was busy chatting with an employee and the food was ok, not phenomenal but not bad either.  They also bring out the food in random order depending on what is cooked first.  They did tell me about this when I was given the menu.  My appetizer made it out 10 minutes after my entree. I would eat here again.

Great place!! I've now been here 3 times and each time has been wonderful. We usually go out for someones birthday and something i appreicate in a restaurant is when we are not rushed. The staff takes their time and lets you enjoy dinner together. Food is just fantasic. I've got the crab cake the last 2 times and it's the best crab cake i've had. Calamari is awesome. Drinks are great! Can't complain.

Food was great but the server was not attentive to hos customers. Did not come back to see receive feedback on the food or to refill our drinks. He was too busy sitting at the bar on his cellphone. Three stars for the service.

I was in the mood for a banh mi and I heard this spot just opened, so I figured I woudn't be disappointed.  I ordered Da Mo, and the chicken (no lie) tasted like Bourbon Chicken that you get in the mall at the Chinese buffet counter.  I'm  not saying it like its bad, cause I used to love me some Bourbon Chicken.   The vegetables were nicely pickled, the bread was toasted and buttery and the chicken was moist.  As a previous reviewer stated they weren't offered a stamp card, I wasn't offered one either. I just asked about it and my card was stamped just like that, BOOM! There is only window bar style seating offered, so don't expect to eat in if you're more than a party of 2.

I think we were pretty fortunate cuz we got there around 6pm on Saturday night & there were 8 of us. We got a table in less than 20 min, the food was like any other thai place (the calamari was chummy!) It was just a nice, dimmed place to eat & chill...not a place to talk deep or linger...wish it was in Manhattan but then its in nice nabe around Brooklyn Heights so I don't mind going out there (I think my roots are bit too deep in Manhattan, kakaka) My entr was similar to a chinese fried broad rice noodle, ahhaa, but its all good!
Fantastic! Absolutely a favorite with large portions and fresh ingredients! Cozy atmosphere.

As if this place needs anymore reviews.. yes this is the top tier gold standard for ramen. It's basically a must visit and the only reason I can't go 5 stars is because it so often has a 1-2 hour wait. Worth it? Probably, but there are other ramen places almost as good, especially one that comes to mind in Brooklyn. Yea, it's likely the best ramen you've ever had.
The food is very good, unless you have been to Louisana.  I spent more than ten years as a judge for a Cajun Cook-off, and I can definitely say the food, though good, is not award winning.

I've been here two times: once for lunch, another for dinner.  Lunch was great.  I had their Cobb Salad, and it was delicious.   Dinner was not so great.  I ordered the Prickly Pear Margarita, and was excited when it came out in a huge glass, but quickly realized it was because it was mostly ice, and watered down.  I also had very high hopes for the freshly made guacamole, only to be really let down.  It was all avocado, which I love, but there was no heat, no garlic, and no cilantro.  I did have the chicken, and beef tacos, and they were quite good.   I will probably give it another try, but not in the near future.
Been here for brunch a few times, definitely worth the price for some of the dishes like the waffles. Nice farmhouse style dining, a bit cramped, but will do!
The pork and lamb tacos are amazing.

Was in the mood for something fresh & tasty so decided on Hibachi & Sushi.  Been here a handful of times and happy to report we've always had excellent service & great food! The place is huge with tons of seating & parking - (living in JC, parking is much appreciated!) Great place for big groups & families. I usually do the hibachi (cs my daughter loves it), but the couple times I've ordered sushi it's been great! I'll Definitely be back to try more of the specialty rolls!

This place does not deserve a four star food rating. Best part of the meal: a tasty octopus appetizer. But the lamb shank (for which we had specifically come) was awful.
