The meat was not falling off the bone; it was nowhere near the bone. What we got was just bone--plain bone--and bits of tough meat in a glutenous tomato sauce. Pork medallions were overcooked and came in a glutenous sour sauce. I can only think that the cheap prices are influencing the food reviews. A 17 dollar lamb shank--wow! But not if you can't eat it. For a good lamb shank go to Nice Matin a few blocks away.

The Spotted Pig is a restaurant that immediately springs to mind whenever one mentions NYC. Not only is it headed by one of the biggest female chefs of our time, but it's also got big shot rapper Mr. Jay-Z as one of the investors. Add the Michelin star and numerous accolades it's received over the years, you'd be hard pressed to find anyone who hasn't heard of this place. Not surprisingly then, The Spotted Pig is perpetually packed at any hour of the day with a line wrapped around the front door. The bar area both downstairs and upstairs were packed even after midnight when the bf and I dropped in for a very late supper after some shenanigans nearby. We were pretty fortunate, being a party of two, as we were seated at a two top upstairs immediately after checking in at the receptionist's desk. Even though this place is dubbed as a gastropub with fairly high-priced fare, the ambiance is straight up casual and laid-back. From the borderline tacky lights on the outside to the cramped dining room and bar filled with a million piggy tinctures and various other things, I was actually pretty surprised by how much it resembled a neighborhood pub. But of course, the food here is steps above what you'd find at a regular pub. The renowned chargrilled burger with roquefort is incredibly juicy and rich, generously basted in butter on the grill with just enough pungency and flavor provided by the roquefort cheese. The accompanying shoe string fries are some of the thinnest and crispiest potato sticks I've ever tasted, yet elevated by the addition of garlic and rosemary fried with the fries. While I personally would never be able to finish that decadent burger, just about everyone else in the dining room had no problem at all putting it away. Attempting to find a lighter option on the dinner menu, I ordered the prosciutto and ricotta tart with marjoram. The smear of creamy ricotta and thinly sliced prosciutto layered on the impossibly flaky and warm puff pasty tart had enough salt to satisfy a late night craving but still managed to be balanced. I also liked the marjoram on top, similar to baby arugula, as it provided some much needed herbaceousness. The chicken liver toast is no joke here either - creamy, livery and rich - made more interesting by the slightly sweet balsamic that the little livers are cooked in. I think it goes without saying that The Spotted Pig serves the perfect late-night grub. The drink menu here is well curated, everything from the popular cocktails, to craft beers and a smart list of wines. I was glad to see a number of wines from California, including a Sauvignon Blanc from Heitz that I found hard to turn down, as well as some California Cabs. I was happy with the 21st Amendment IPA from SF I ended up ordering, especially as it was priced surprisingly well. I'd be happy to come back. I'm not sure if I'd be able to tolerate a 2 hour wait on any given night, but weekend brunch and late-night supper seem like good bets.
Mr. Sushi is my favorite sushi place of all time. Consistent quality, good price, and friendly owners. I highly recommend the oyster sashimi.

Delicious!!!! I never had a lobster roll before so don't have much to compare to.  However it was delicious... Fresh lobster with light mayo, lemon, pepper on a toasty warm bun.  What a nice way to start the summer.  It makes me really want to travel to Maine to see what the big fuss is about. Def worth it.  The crab roll was so tasty also with no filler but pure crab meat.
I had high hopes; good reviews and I received a glowing recommendation from a friend.  However, I found the pizza to be mediocre.  Plus, Lombardi's delivers to my door, which is in another league.

Wound up here at two in the morning after one drink too many with my boyfriend. We ordered oysters and steak tartare, a decadent meal of raw flesh to celebrate life. It all tasted pretty good (as I said, we had had a few drinks). Well, the next day I got really sick. And I don't mean hangover, I mean the kind of sickness that sends you to the bathroom with pain in your stomach. Yes, as in food poisoning. Something's definitely wrong in that kitchen.

Gotta give him the props for making some very delicious Dosas in a cart. I didn't get to try the Masala dosa or the Simosas but I will definitely try them next time. Then I might up the rating to 5 stars.
Totto Miso Ramen, please!!! I waited twenty minutes for a seat, pretty reasonable. It only took me half of that to indulge in my bowl of miso ramen. Delicious. Enough said.

Diner, Dive, somewhat clean ...Can't complain. This place always satisfies my hunger no matter what mood and no matter what time.  Tonight for dinner, I had waffles with bacon and my dinner pal wolfed down a big swiss bacon mushroom burger deluxe.  YUM-O!

We had a very nice experience at the Heath.  The wait staff was friendly and attentive, the live jazz was just the right volume to add to the great atmosphere.  The food was really good.  we started w burrata, pork pies and a cheese platter. All were delicious.  I had the scallops which were tender and delicious, and french fries that were perfect.   The prices seem a little high, if you look at the menu, but you are paying for live music and the atmosphere.  They also do not rush you, so you can have a pleasant dinner. I would return and/or recommend to friends.

The dumplings in here are great. I had a good time in there, it was quite hilarious. They threw the plates at us as if we were dogs. I have read and heard bad reviews about the service, it didn't bother me. I just thought it was funny. Fried dumplings were delicious. You can easily walk away without paying because nobody seems to care if you pay or not. We did pay, but they forgot what we order so we had to remind them. If you get easily offended, definitely not your place, but if you love dumplings that should not be a problem.

Beneath the blue awning is this neighborhood gem. If you're looking for an intimate setting with friendly and fun vibes, join the pack. The dim setting, long wooden tables, the ropes around the bar area made me feel so hip. The tables allowed for us to have interactions with our neighbors on either side -really infectious good feelings. I'll admit that I had no idea what Austrian food tastes like, but after this experience, I can tell you that it's damn good. We coupled our skate, schnitzel, and shell steak with the most delicious rose` and stayed for a good three hours. I loved the crusty breading on my schnitzel and the steak was cooked perfectly. The whole meal definitely satisfied my ravenous appetite. And we just had to leave room for some cappuccino and dessert. If you really want to indulge your guilty sweet tooth, get the lime parfait. Don't even know how they made something so refreshing, but I couldn't stop licking my lips. Growl... I'll be back again.
Juniors never disappoints. Got the Mac & cheese, combo reuben (pastrami and corned beef) and a vanilla ice cream soda.  Obviously couldn't finish anything. Food was incredible!
Why fly to Italy when you can walk to Eataly...

I am no hipster, nor do I typically enjoy what I would term hipster locals, but Standard Tap manages to just be a really cool, chill place with good food. A bunch of my girlfriend and I came here for brunch on a rainy, chilly Saturday and we ended up staying and drinking for about 4 hours - the food was great, and the waitstaff was really nice and flexible and accommodating (especially as I realize that after 4 hours of drinking, 6 girls might not be as charming as they think they are!). They have a great selection of local craft brews and a good menu. I'd definitely go back!

Awesome!!!! Love the decor, love the concept, and the food is beyond everything to what we think about the Alsace-Lorraine dining experience! The gratinee flambé one is the ONE! Please, don't go by without a try!

Perfect place to bring the in laws -- had an establishment feel about it, great service, delicious fish. Between us all we had the sole, halibut, ahi tuna, crab cakes, scallops, lobster mac n cheese, creamed spinach. Everyone loved their fish, tasted fresh and well seasoned. The lobster mac wasn't great -- both my mother in law and I make this at home and both are way better-- this one tastes like a ton of butter, lobster bisque and cheese on top, OK but not great. Dessert was FAB- creme brûlée and chocolate mousse cake- YUUUUM. It's definitely on the expensive side but great quality and everyone seemed super nice!

Ate here after seeing their catering at mayfest.  Really nice people running it.  Great  huevos  rancheros! You also have to love the fact that everything you see inside is on sale from the books on the tables to the chairs.
Delicious. Not too expensive. The cheese fries are spot on. Go if you're craving fries!!!! Ours were actually a bit too salty but it didn't make that big of a difference.

Dinner with close friends tonight. All the apps were amazing, full of flavors. We had soup and some of the salads, they all exceed my expectation. Our favs are the eggplant and the beet salad. What's also great is the free olives and toasted warm bread basket. For entree my spicy chicken had the perfect spice and spicy enough without going over broad. The lamb with honey and prunes was good but you really have to like it sweet to enjoy that one. No dessert in the menu but they have the teas. I also guess they want you to have full Moroccan experience because on the TV was a show with belly dancers. All in all will visit again. BTW the chief was the waiter too.

Having an awesome dinner on our last night in Jersey. Thought we were stranded at the hotel and doomed to delivery but on the recommendation of the hotel and other Yelpsters, we called and they came & picked us up. Had the red sangria which was very well balanced.   They greeted us warmly and everyone was very gracious.   Soup on the house to begin and the bread....what can I say fantastic. Clams casino & shrimp in garlic sauce was the best I've has in years.   Split the Pallea Valencia.  Enough for 3.   Then excellent musical entertainment table side.  Will definitely come back next time  back in Jersey. BYW dessert was great. And u must have the Spanish coffee.
This place is great. You should eat there.

Come here for the food (which is pretty good). It's pricey, though, especially for college students. The servers are pretty rude, and the delivery guy never seems to be there. They also seem to take a break every day from 2pm - 4:30pm, so service can be erratic. Variable delivery times, ranging from 40 minutes to 2 hours (yes 2).

Cafe Matisse is definitely a place for nice place to unwind, and have a structured, evening meal in downtown Rutherford. Now before you go in, you should set aside at LEAST 2-3 hours for eating here -- it's all tastings, and you can choose either 3 or 4-course meals. Each come with a dessert, and all the choices are GREAT. I had NO complaints with the food, the way it was prepared, or how it was served -- all was FANTASTIC, hense my 4/5 rating. My only knack was the amount of time -- I had never been here before, so we arrived at 7:00 p.m. and didn't leave until a few minutes after ten. We all did the 4-course meals. It was just too long -- I LOVE a nice dinner to relax and unwind, but 3+ hours is a bit overboard for me. THAT is the only reason I'm giving Matisse a 4/5!

I'll preface this by admitting, I am not from New York. I decided to visit my little sister on the Upper West Side and was told to get the 'chicken and rice combo with white sauce' at this local landmark. Cost me $6, add another $1 for a bottled water. Surely, I was not disappointed. I can't say much more about it that hasn't already been said in the nearly-400-some reviews on Yelp. The food is delicious. The meat is seasoned and cooked well. The white sauce is good... IN MODERATION. It disgusts me to see some people just glaze their entire platter with liquid fat. Their hot sauce is FIERY. You might sweat a little, and it might be painful. It's one of those burning pains that reminds you that you're alive. Don't be a pansy, just try it. I now understand why this place is so popular. I ate here twice during my trip and while the line may seem daunting at times, it moves at a steady rate. The service is forgettable, but who cares? At the end of the day, you're getting a delicious hot meal for 6 bucks -- a rarity in Manhattan, apparently -- and given today's economy, you'd be a fool to complain about that. (I originally thought about giving this place 4, not 5, stars because (in my mind) cart/truck vendor food in the Bay Area (Oakland, specifically) offer better food, in higher quantities, at lower prices. But for NY, it's very deserving of 5 stars.)

Such nice personal and personable service! Nothing too much trouble. High quality ingredients, masterfully put together. Menu much larger than I expected. Love the Tarte w the goat cheese and honey. Awesome Mimosas. Nice if it was a bit larger but then it would likely lose its charm.

I have been back to Eataly a few times, mostly to grab gelato or some specialty food.  I still think it's massively overpriced, but the selection is pretty awesome if you are looking for something specific and uncommon.  Still not a great spot, but good enough to move from a 2-star to 3-star review.

Not worth the prices. I don't think it was bad but I can think of way better food for $10 per person. $8 for 1 arepa is almost and insult. It is like $7 for a taco. Lower your prices and watch the money pile up. No one gets it anymore.

First time trying Viet food and it was great! I got lemongrass chicken and spring roll bun. Only con is that it did take awhile and food is a bit expensive for the amount you get compared to a Chinese lunch combo.

Must have: Coconut drink desert , wrapped chicken wings. The food is very reasonably priced and waiters are friendly and nice. Place is usually packed but not impossible to get into. Never had a bad experience there. Best Malaysian in the city. I always go back and then go back again.

This was our first foray into Philly French restaurants (pardon the alliteration).  We stopped in on a Saturday afternoon after walking, shopping and sight-seeing.  Needless to say we were very hungry.  We picked Beau Monde due to the location, South St, and the Yelp reviews.  I'm going to say up front, it was a solid four stars.   The day was a little cool, but we sat outside anyways.  There were plenty of tables inside, but arranged so patrons had to sit very close to other patrons.  Several of the tables hadn't been bussed yet, so we opted for a patio table.  The hostess was friendly and our service was pretty decent.  We ordered a French onion soup to start.  The soup was rich and hot.  It didn't have that overly sharp after taste that many canned French onion soups tend to have.  The emmanteler cheese was a perfect compliment and tamed the bite of the onions. My girl ordered a buckwheat crepe with tomatoes, mushrooms, and swiss cheese, while I got the Coq au Vin on buckwheat crepe.  Both dishes were quite delicious and a welcome respite from the all to frequent flavors of dining out.  The Coq tasted like a French stew and I immediately had visions of us sitting in a cafe in the Loire river valley on an autumn trip to France.  Her crepe was rich and dripping with flavors and was too big for her to finish.  We topped off with coffee and conversation. The only real negative to the whole experience was the price.  One bowl of soup, two crepes (albeit stuffed with warm goodness), and one coffee was over $40 dollars.  Beau Monde isn't Parc in Rittenhouse (where you also pay for the views of the park) or Maxime's (where you pay for being in Paris).  They obviously didn't cook the Coq au Vin just for my crepe alone, so I have a difficult time seeing why a couple of crepes, a soup and a coffee should be $40 in Queen Village with views of row houses and two other restaurants. I hate to sound cheap (and I'm not considering my generous tip), but price should be reflective of the entire restaurant from location, to quality, to service, to availability.  It's not the only French restaurant in town, or even on that street corner.   Will we go again?  Absolutely, when we're in the neighborhood.  The food and service were more than decent, though not worth a special trip across town for.
i dont know why i wait but i do.  i like this place and try to go on off times.  waiting for good philly breakfast spots i guess is the new trend.

Great experience and great food! Our server was great and he offered us a delicious free cookie for dessert! He was very attentive to our food needs as well-- it took a little while for the food to come but it was well worth it! My sister got the turkey wrap and loved it. I got the veggie burger on a pretzel roll. It was amazing! It's worth the wait!  I've been here two other times since, and breakfast is amazing as well!

Being born-and-raised in Greece, it actually hurts a little to give this place a poor review. I was there for a quick mid-day lunch and got a Mythos, the lentil salad, and the zucchini croquets. The lentil salad was DRENCHED in salt. You couldn't taste the lentils, because all you could taste was SALT. When the server asked me how everything was and I complained about the salad being drenched in salt she responded "yeah, they do that sometimes" and walked away!!! That, along with the dude at the entrance screaming at a bunch of Greek women "your mother is a whore" (in Greek, but still...) really turned me off about this place.

I'm normally not a sandwich for dinner person, but I loved the vegetarian sandwich with black beans, plaintains, and avocado. Even my fiance loved his vegetarian sandwich and he considers dinner without meat as not dinner.  It has the right salty and sweet flavors ad the toasted Cuban bread is perfect with it.  I also liked the kale and avocado salad.  Lots of avocado too. There was no skimping here. My fiance is a huge deviled eggs fan.  I'm not really, but Cubana Social's eggs could convert me.  They were actually spicy.  Even my deviled eggs at the James Beard House the next day did not top these.  Next time I will have to come hungrier. Service was a little slow, but friendly enough. And the live band that played added to the atmosphere.  But Cubana Social, if you are going to bother with a live band can you turn off the cheesy movies on the screen projector?

Pio pio continues to be one of my favorite restaurants in NYC!   The ambiance in this restaurant is really nice - you could come here on a date or bring a bunch of friends.  It's so surprising to me how big this place is too... how the hell do you have that HUGE room in the back in a restaurant in Hell's Kitchen?  Make sure you make reservations, as it is especially booked on the weekend.   For food and drinks, definitely go for the Sangria.  Excellent ratio of fruit to alcohol.  As for the food, make sure you try the ceviche!  That's why you're going to a Peruvian restaurant, right??  Try something unique!  You can get the Piqueo Pacifico, which is a combination of different ceviches, or just skip to my favorite one - the Nikkei (sooooo yummy).  As for the chicken, I've had the Matador Combo and the Aji de Gallina.  I prefer the aji de gallina because it's unique: shredded chicken with white rice and an incredible yellow sauce.  The matador combo dish just has typical South American plates like beans, fries, rotisserie chicken, but eating everything with the magical green sauce makes it so much better.   I've yet to try many more things on the menu, but I am excited to come back and explore the other dishes.

I've always seen the line and walked past. But this time after that smell... mmmmm that smell. I knew it was time. Honestly, the line moved extremely fast! They're really efficient 'cause they know their stuff. Unfortunately very little interacting involved (they even prepare 2 white sauces and 1 spicy sauce in your bag for you instead of asking), but I'd rather be in and out with this kind of line. The chicken had awesome flavor without being sickeningly greasy! -- I think that may be since it wasn't the most flavorful chicken over rice I've ever had though. Luckily portions are huge, and they even give you a few slices of pita bread for only $5. Same low prices even with all the popularity! Great stuff. With such a fast-moving line, don't hesitate to try this New York staple!

We swung in here on a Saturday afternoon to grab a late lunch.  I have been here before but never to eat.  We sat at the bar because the booths were all filled.  The beer list here is always solid with a good number of interesting beers on tap.   We ordered up right away; my wife going with the cheesesteak empanadas (of course) and french fries and I rocked the octopus salad.  The empanadas were tasty (My verdict on the beer sauce is still out because I haven't decided whether I like it or not yet.) and so were the fries and the aioli that came with the fries. My salad was pretty good and I really enjoyed the chorizo vinaigrette but the octopus was pretty tough. The fried chick peas added a much needed crunch to the salad as well.   I can't say too much more that hasn't been said already. I would definitely come back to try some other food options but overall this place is pretty laid back and has a great vibe to match is solid food.

I was really surprised it took us so long to try Mercato. We went there on a week night and it was still quite busy. Not overcrowded, but you can tell it's a popular place. We started with a charcuterie appetizer which was so much delicious food. and we were basically already half full off of the bread and the delicious butter spread they gave us. We both decided to go with pasta dishes as our appetizers. They were delicious hand made pastas which we enjoyed thoroughly. All in all, we had a good experience at Mercato. It's a bit on the pricey side and a cab ride away for us so not sure how often we will be back, but we enjoyed it nonetheless.
We really enjoyed the restaurant, waiters were attentive and helpful and the food delicious and interresting and atmosphere was fabulous will go again when we in NYC

It is my experience that this is a place that you must have reservations to get in on the weekend.  I went with my husband and sister and we all loved everything.  Of course we shared everything too!  If you want fresh sushi you have to try Doma.  The restaurant is small but very hip.  Besides great sushi we had excellent service.  Our waiter was Alex, who only works the weekends.  DOMA IS A MUST!

A friend in the area kept raving about this place, so it was nice to be able to stroll in for lunch and see what the fuss was about. And what fuss, there was almost every type of food and drink imaginable in this once-terminal station. Great open air market atmosphere with all types of food to eat. Lots of different local snacks, desserts, food, beverage, cheese, sweets, gifts... the list goes on and on. Definitely check this out for a big variety of cool market and foodstuff.

I absolutely love the concept and enjoy the atmosphere being a big fan of Italy and everything about it. Looking at the food, cold cuts, desserts, gelato and everything else makes me really happy. Unfortunately, everything here is overpriced. I saw the same pack of breakfast cookies my Italian friend bought from their local grocery store for $1 euro and was sold here for $6. Talking about markup here. I do admire the ambition of the store and it sure is an eye-popping experience just walking around.
Pizza is worth it, not gonna bother to get into it..just ditto on all the other reviews

Who Would Have Thunk:  Tapas Served in the Heart of Caldwell Enjoyed our dinner at Xunta España. We tried a tasty Chorizo a Prancha (Grilled Chorizo with Caramelized Onions), hearty Caldo Galego (Broccoli Rabe, White Beans, Potatoes, Chorizo and Ham Soup), Champinos Bevedos (Mushrooms and Onion in Brandy--would not re-order), and perfectly cooked medium rare Faldra a Prancha con Espinaca (Skirt Steak with a Chimichurri Sauce and side of Sautéed Spinach). See pics Pluses: + Most dishes offered in Tapas portion and regular portion size intended for sharing (ración) + Fresh ingredients. + Complimentary olive bread + Friendly staff. Owner stopped by our table. Said they opened June 2013. + BYOB. Wine was opened and served in quality wine glasses without corkage fee + Some dishes marked Gluten Free Gripes: - Only one:  For a small restaurant, it was noisy on a Saturday evening. Open daily for lunch and dinner with exception of no lunch on Sunday. Will return. I will also attempt to make at home the Caldo Galego soup...many recipes online. Tip:  Avoid hassle of finding street parking. Park in rear. Public parking lot.
was a fan of this restaurant until the night i ordered the salmon and immediately got sick after. I 100% received food poisoning after this meal. So gross.
I stop here a few times a week for pizza.  It is right down the block from my job. Good pizza, not greasy, good crust, not too thick

I was so happy to find this gem! The restaurant is small but has a great personality. I went twice in one week during a visit to NYC and I was very happy both times! The service was great, the GF pizza was delicious but I could not get enough of the GF rice balls! Oh and the salad was fresh and crisp! Absolutely love it here! I recommend this place to anyone that wants to experience all the delicious food you may have to put aside because not many restaurants offer GF options. Will definitely come back!

For afterwork cocktails -- this place is a fire hazard! I hear such great things that maybe I should return late night or on a weekend :( I was looking forward to the infamous bespoke experience, but this place was awfully crowded. My boyfriend and I arrived fairly early (around 6-7PM), and there were no seats at the bar. I was really disappointed because I thought the whole bespoke experience was about watching the bartender make your drink. The host assured that she could handle the order..so she provided a checklist for us to advise what ingredients we wanted (rums, sours, sweets were the categories I believe + more). I asked for a few suggestions, but felt rushed & it didn't feel as authentic as I anticipated. The drinks are very strong.. so I guess that was the plus. About 30 minutes into our night.. we were asked to move to another table to make room for a bigger party. I was a little annoyed because 1). we were comfortable with our seats and 2). who does that! There was a little confusion in terms of our new seats - the host had to tell the other party it was reserved for us. So much confusion,etc. After our next drinks - we decided to leave. It isn't the ideal place for a quiet date.. It felt like a loud bar for the professional, 30+ afterwork crowd. I'd have to go back to truly have an interactive mixology experience - afterwork isn't the right time.
bad, bad, bad, bad. old chef was much better.  burgers need to be crispy on the outside.

I stumbled apon this place last week in NYC with some friends and it instantly felt like home.  The bartender was an old man with white hair and a beard of about 60,  We were there for about 2 and half hours and they played Neil Young the entire time while the bartender sang along. Loudly.  The door man was friendly and the place was just fun.  $2.50 drafts, also didn't hurt.  We got some chicken sandwiches and fries and they were ok but, if you're going there for food than that your mistake to begin with.  Next time I'm in NYC it's going to be the first place I go.

Like everyone said it's bigger than you would expect. The outside of it is small but once you go downstairs it opens up. The first floor is a bar and intimate for two people. It's very dark and the music makes it hard to hear everyone at the table. I went with 5 other people and we tried the chicken that was recommended. They were very big pieces and was very juicy. we tried the appetizer sampler and they are very tiny and not worth it in my opinion. The biggest hit was the risotto with a sunny side egg and filet Mignon strips. It was perfectly cooked. This place is definitely for large parties and for sharing family style. The dessert was lovely; also party sampler. We looked more like animals going after everything. Come hungry and it came out to about thirty per person which wasn't bad at all.

I went veggie for a night with some veggie fans. result: Yummy seasonal local. A little pricey for the plate of artichokes, but I left very happy and with a bottle of wine, it wasn't unreasonable at all for a good meal. The husband and wife team chatted with us about the challenges of being a small business and sourcing your stuff, delivery, etc. *Decor-wise: I do wish they had something else on their walls. Even something unoriginal like old-timey diagrams of plants and veggies or antique mirrors that are a bit crackled or tinted would be cool. Def check out the freshness over here.

Came here for a glass of wine and an early dinner in the downstairs cellar. Their happy hour specials are great and my $5 glass of the featured white- a sauvignon blanc- was actually really delicious. The main attraction is the mac and cheese and it did not disappoint. It was rich and bubbling, with oblong, rolled noodles instead of the usual elbow macaroni. The happy hour portion is the perfect serving size- not too much, not too little. The only thing I didn't like about this place was the lighting above the tables. While the tables themselves are beautiful- broad, dark wooden beauties- the harsh, direct spotlights above made me feel like I was being interrogated. There were also some lounge-y chairs in the middle of the room that I might opt for next time.

El Diablito has become my 'go to spot' for Mexican food in the East Village. Their place is small, colorful, and clean. The fish tacos are excellent: inexpensive, the fish has a soft texture that tastes beer battered, and the sauce is delicious. Two tacos and sides of rice and beans can make a very filling meal. Customer service is prompt and the food seems to be prepared fresh.

This place is amazing. A beautiful, contemporary restaurant with authentic, sushi masters that create beautiful and delicious pieces of some of the best Nigiri & sushi in Manhattan! If you don't want to break your piggy bank, go for lunch and get their lunch specials. You won't get top selection like Uni or Aji, but it will still give you a sense of what wonderful sushi they offer. Their lunch specials (mixed Nigiri/Rolls or Sashimi) range from $23-$30 - a deal for such delicious Sushi. Will definitely return for Omakase next time for dinner. It sounds nothing short of extraordinary. Reservations are highly suggested.
Must try the Viagra empanada.. The shredded chicken is ok sometimes it can be dry! Oh and don't forget the green sauce.

Customer service is good.  Tables are nice.  Meat is superb! Good portions for your money. I had ribs, hubby had brisket.  The char on the meat rocks. Definitely taste the hot BBQ sauce on the meat.  I prefer to eat my ribs dry but I used some of the hot sauce and became addicted.  Meat is very tender.  I can just eat the meat, hot sauce and a beverage.  I don't need any sides.  The sides are OK.  They put corn in the cornbread, not my thing.  I wish they had red velvet so I could try it.  I will go back.

Not bad. The complimentary bread was ok today. Middle part was cold. Special : watermelon grilled salad was so tiny but the watermelon tasted good almost taste like cured meat bc it had the charred grill taste. Lists of wine to choose from, 3oz, 6 oz, bottle. I had lobster roll with fries and my friend had half lobster and clams . She didn't like her meal. But my roll was good.
This makes me want to move to the neighborhood! Adorable and café con leche was flawless. Love!

Popular and busy with tourists on Saturday night, surprisingly the food was very good (Northern Italian cooking mostly). the prices were on the high side - but that is Manhattan... Parking is very tight around the narrow local streets (so narrow that our car's side mirror was clipped off by a passing car...) good reviews (Zagat "best Italian restaurant in little Italy"); Service was friendly and attentive, place was fairly modern-tacky and clean. Coming from the suburbs, I had better Italian food at lower prices, - but, again, that is Manhattan.
Cheese is grated to order by hand. The owner makes each pie him self. Service is very slow so don't come here unless you have plenty of time. He cooks pizzas at a time, so people queue up and watch.

This place has great Ethiopian food. We tried three different dishes and loved them all. The owner was really nice too. He gave us information on how to make our own Ethiopian food! It was a great experience both times we went. The cafe atmosphere was nice too.

The thing that struck me about this place was that the sleaze factor was ultra-low.  I don't know if it was because it felt a bit like an after-work/neighborhood crowd early on a Thursday night or because they let in a lady with a baby, but the place seemed relaxed and casual.  The vibe was intimate and the decor classy, but without overdoing it. The bartender was super nice, making me my non-alcoholic cocktail (I know, why am I allowed to review these places when I don't drink) and checked to make sure it was okay and gave us water separately on his own initiative.  That was just hospitable. The other thing that struck me about this place is that they played really good music.  You don't expect that from a place where a baby is also present.  They played this great combination of Hip hop and EDM and I was appreciative.  We went to a charity event at Marquee afterwards and the music wasn't nearly as good there. In any case, I liked the intimate casual feel, nice decor, great service, good music, and  all the people there who looked like they were there looking to just chill more than anything else. *Update*:  Came here again on a date and I have to say the hospitality here is unparalleled.  You feel like you are visiting a hometown bar with everyone greeting you hello and bye like they know you.  I asked for a table (the one straight in front of me) and they gave us a better corner sofa table with more privacy and space.  And the waitress was so kind and sweet.  Order the duck nachos.  Really good and where else are you going to have duck nachos.  This time they were playing bluegrass/folk type music so think it varies by night.
Delicious brunch spot. I had some sort of brisket thingie. Don't remember the exact name of it. Some other good options I would like to try. Everyone's plates looked delicious. Especially the burger.

Went around 6:30pm on Saturday night with a friend. There was no wait and it wasn't too crowded. We were seated in the back at one of the tables.  Very cool/cozy decor and atmosphere. We shared a gumbo with rice which was okay but could have had more meat in it and some of the rice seemed uncooked or maybe it had just sat and dried out a bit.   I got blackened catfish platter with sweet potato fries. A thin nicely seasoned piece of fish and a small bunch of sweet/savory/salty fries which I would have enjoyed more of. My friend got one of the pulled pork po boys (which I tried and it was tasty). Both came with a well dressed side salad on the plate. Next time I'll probably try one of the drinks, a po boy sandwich, jumbalaya or mac and cheese.  Lots I'd like to go back and try, but I wasn't blown away by the service or the food. Maybe next time.
Best thai food in LI. Great selection specially for vegetarians. Papaya salad is awesome.
I have been here multiple times and I have not had a bad meal yet. I'm usual a sushi person but I've tried the udon a few times and I've enjoyed that too.

I am currently craving this awhile I'm typing up this review and I'm excited excited to be back in January to eat this again. I love Halal Guys! Probably the best $6 I've ever spent in my entire life. Basically how it works is you start with rice, salad and pita bread then you pick your meat. I choose the chicken and lamb and it was such a delicious meal. It's actually alot of food, it can serve up to 2 people. I think I added too much red sauce though but it was still good overrall. This is a must if you're in New York. I had it at least 4 times during my 2 week stay in New York! The line tends to get super long and it's a free for all for your seatings.

Honest Tom's is one of my favorite places to eat in West Philly. They only have tacos and burritos on the menu as well as a couple sides but that is all they need. Since you get two tacos with an order my favorite thing to get is one sweet potato and one chicken, both of which are very tasty. I don't really like the burritos except for the breakfast burrito. I wish they had more seating available because sometimes you just can't sit down. During the warmer months they have seating outside though, which helps things to clear out a bit faster. The ingredients are fresh and you can watch them cook while you wait. Tacos are only $6 for 2 and burritos are $8 which I think is very reasonable. The chips and guac are also very good if you feel like chipping in the extra bucks. It's a great place to go with just one or two friends so you have enough space to sit and (from University City at least) you have some company for the walk!

Awesome Sunday brunch -- The Smith gets 4 stars because it takes reservations and actually honors them! I made a reservation for 4 on OpenTable... changed it to 5 the night before... changed it back to 4 upon arrival. As soon as my whole party was there, we were seated within minutes. Despite there being a mob out the door and overheard walk-in wait time quotes of 1 hour. So my friends and I were seated and served promptly. The Smith is excellent for very reasonably priced food that tastes more expensive than it actually is. I'd been here before for dinner and had some amazing mussels. Not exactly brunch food, so I settled for the Ranchero Scrambled. The brunch menu comes with a free cocktail. Naturally, I ordered a Bloody Mary... which would have been the very most perfect Bloody Mary I've ever had... if there were even a hint of alcohol inside. But it tasted amazing... considering it was free. I think they were like $13 at the bar, so I consider it a bargain. Anyway... my Ranchero Scrambled was divine. I would say that out of all my friends, mine was the smallest portion there... and I still ended up being full through the rest of the day and night. Service was very efficient and this place definitely has the Sunday brunch routine down. I would highly recommend it to people... just make sure you make a reservation!

I watched a segment about Zahav on Fox and was impressed by the Passover menu, which appeared to be an interesting variation on the traditional Seder meal. Since it was the first night of Passover, my wife and I decided to give it a try. My wife was not interested in the contents of the Passover menu and decided to try some of the a la cart items.  She ordered first, and then I told the waitress that I wanted the Passover meal.  She told me that we both had to order the meal. We explained ( I don't know why we had to explain) that my wife was not interested in it.  She told us that it could only be had if we both ordered it.  Since the Passover meal was the only reason we were there, we should have paid for our drinks and left.  But the weather was terrible, so we stayed and were literally forced to order something else, none of which lived up to the hype of other reviews. Besides the bizarre menu requirements, the food was just fair, and the prices were high for what we got.  I doubt we would have gone back in any case, but forcing us to adhere to their ordering requirements is a no-starter.  By the way, we were given no explanation for this absurd requirement.   Next time we want a Passover meal, we'll make it ourselves or go to the local deli and get better food for about 1/3 the price.  Two stars for this place is generous.

I didn't think too much of Grocery when we wandered in on a Fri night  - there was 0 wait and the decor was plain jane. But, that attitude changed so quickly. Servers were incredibly genial and helpful. Kudos to the menu writer, bc I'm a sucker for ingredient lists. We ordered: Crispy Farro Cake: So delicious, and recommend House Smoked Organic Salmon: Never really liked smoked salmon, but this was amazing in a salad esque plate Slow Rendered Duck Breast: the meat was incredibly tender and flavorful Gingerbread Steamed Pudding: A little bit too sweet for me, but tasted like winter goodness This has to be one of my more favorite places to eat in recent memory - seasonal new American food at its best. I do wish they'd do more w the decor and make it cozier/romantic as I'm on the hunt for an 'our' restaurant. I'd rather not go on to the next one...

This is one of my all-time favorite restaurants in the city.  I should disclose that I'm a huge Batali fan.  Say what you will about his empire but I've never had a bad meal at any of his restaurants.  The ambience at Casa Mono is just perfect (though being located at 17th and Irving helps it a lot).  Each time I go, I somehow end up at the same table, in the front at one of those desk/tables where the water glass has been hidden inside the table.  It's prob less cramped than the majority of the restaurant and allows for less noise and plenty of gazing into the other person's eyes.   Reservations at a decent hour (8:00-9:30) for dinner are as elusive as the waitstaff can be but I will gladly go through all of that for the food.  The sweetbreads are crunchy on the outside and densely pate-esque on the inside.  I order octopus almost any time it's on a menu and was not disappointed.  The duck is cooked perfectly and disappeared so fast, I caught myself wanting to order a second.  The Lamb suffered the same heroic end.  The quail managed to come out tender while somewhat crispy.   I wish I could have shrunk myself to the point where it would have become a huge turkey-sized quail.  We had the Juan Gill ($15 bottle marked up to $40 which in my book is fair since it's a good value wine) with our meal and it was just perfect with everything.  The wine list is rather extensive and you'll find plenty of great choices.   Proportions are small but the dishes pack a lot in taste.  Batali is usually very good at providing a contrast in textures and manages to combine flavors in new and provocative ways all the time.   Anyone who's not happy with Casa Mono should not eat there, that way, those of us who do like eating there can actually get in for dinner..
Forget Gino's and order (correctly) a cheese steak at Pat's.  The meat was great but I was struck by how fresh the bread was.  It goes beyond the hype.   Awesome!

I don't understand the bad reviews for this place! $8 for 6 amazingly delicious fresh oysters and a glass of (admittedly crappy) chardonnay or beer ...how can you go wrong?! Went here on a date on a Sunday at 5pm, the place was jam packed, good vibe. Service was not amazing but forgivable as it looked like rush hour just hit. My date had fish & chips following the oysters....btw they make their own horeseradish, amaze... I had the steamed mussels in a lemongrass broth which came with fries for $15. It was so delicious I'd drink it straight. Entire bill for two starters, two mains and four drinks was $55, for fresh seafood in the West Village, that price is unreal.

Went for lunch and my salmon roll was the fishiest I ever tasted... yuk. Not sure why this place is packed, maybe the ambience? It is cute and cozy inside and they do have interesting window displays. I really wanted to like this place but still can't get that fishy taste outta my head to go back and try again.

Horrible service. I saw a customer accidentally break a glass and then clean it up while the owner watched not offering to help. We left 30 minutes later and the floor was still wet from her soda and I could see broken glass still on the floor. The owner seems to be mean to the employees too. The food is absolutely terrible. Do not eat their vege pita, aka their soggy, diarrhea-flavored menu-afterthought. They also do not make good home fries and they charged us for extra sodas after asking us if we wanted refills. zero stars! Oh, and i got sick too...
Good food, good prices on wine.  I had a meat stuff pepper with spatzel it was very tasty.  Must have a reservation unless you are going early.  I enjoyed the caesar salad.  Everything tasted fresh.

I've been here a couple times and I had the same experience each time: the atmosphere was inviting, the food was superb and the service was off the charts outstanding. Great place to enjoy brunch with someone, a friend, your mom, a date, etc. Oh, and let me also recommend ordering a mimosa or two to go with your brunch!

I love this place when were in the area! Great sliders, great price! Bacon cheese burger makes my mouth water. They are soo good. Get a side of fries, and the black and white shake or if you want to con't on drinking, beer and wine is cheap. I'll be back with more friends!

Hmm I guess I should have read all of the reviews or called ahead but when we came here at 11pm Sunday night, they had already closed the hot entree section (open only during lunch and btw 5-9pm for dinner).  We were left with only the prepackaged hot and cold entrees and sides but even then they had already ran out of a lot of the hot stuff.  And no bulgogi in sight!  :(  We decided to just grab a couple of small side dishes before heading somewhere else for a late night dinner.  The spinach tofu soup was probably the best thing we tried.  The fried chives and veggies were super soft and soggy and the jap chae was a little on the dry side.  Aloe vera juice was yummy.  However, the prices were ridiculously cheap and some of their other items looked really good so I will definitely be back during regular dinner hours to try some of their other stuff.

The boss man ordered from here yesterday since we stayed late.  VERY VERY good.  This great flavor that makes you risk a burnt tongue, you know what I mean?  One star off for being a floppy slice.  Crust is awesome.

Good food (tried the kebab sliders which were delicious. The chips and dip was ok. The proscuitto pizzette was quite good as well.) Our server was lazy. We had to ask for water 3 times! Then finally we got some water.
The best pizza in NY and the cesar salad is great too.  The tables are a bit close together but that's jsut b/c the pizza is so good!

Hidden away on the second floor of the popular East Village dining district, this Japanese tea house is so unique that it's as if you are sipping tea in a tea house in Kyoto.  The wonderful tea aroma and the serene ambiance makes this place idea for a special date with friends (limited to only small number of friends).  Although small, it comes complete with a tea room and superb selection of Asian tea.  But my favorite has to be their artistically and deliciously prepared Japanese dessert course.  The 3 course dessert omakase with tea pairing is heavenly as the chef delicately prepares variety of desserts and surprises you with gentle and fresh flavors.  I've been there several times with 1 or 2 other friends and we've never been served the same dessert as one another. The service is always excellent and the chef even offers private cooking classes on weekdays.  Japanese tea ceremony is performed every Friday and Sunday (see their website for detailed schedule) so not only can you enjoy delicious tea but also learn about the art of tea making and drinking.

Nestled in the college town of Princeton, Blue Point has all the makings of a stellar eatery--excellent location, nice ambience, attentive waitstaff but, unfortunately, the food falls a little flat. I started off with a butternut squash soup that was pretty tasty but the lobstercakes that followed tasted like they were made from canned seafood--never a good thing. I had crabcakes as an entree and, while Baltimore will always reign supreme in this category, Blue Point put forth a pretty decent offering.  All in all, nothing was garbage but nothing was mind-blowing either.

tiny but really nice place...3 pitchers of sangria and tried the meatballs, chicken skewers and garlic shrimp...I am ready to go back to try more.  what was nice is I did not feel rushed which is surprising due to the size of the place, so kudos for that!

AMAZING! The North End Bistro is definitely my new favorite place to dine on dates or with family in the Princeton area.  The staff is extremely friendly, helpful, knowledgeable, and attentive. I ordered the Lobster Roll and was thrilled with how delicious it was.  The wine is locally bought from Hopewell Valley and sold by the bottle (prices range between 20 and 25, GREAT deals).  The menu was very diverse, I can't wait to come back and try everything! There are even plenty of vegetarian options. Overall, my dining experience couldn't be topped. I will be going back with all my friends as often as I can. DELICIOUS! Also, it's incredible that they have a parking lot!! That's almost unheard of in this area and a huge plus for the restaurant in my opinion.
Very friendly and serving just about the best thai food I have found anywhere. The curry is amazing. I love the pineapple fried rice. It's all great.

We came to New York on a family holiday trip. My husbands family are Italians from upstate New York. We heard how fantastic it was and decided to try it. This is one of the best places I have ever eaten....EVER. I recommend every entree-we were with a huge party and I tried it all. Don't miss the tiramisu or the ricotta cheesecake! We will be back!!!!

Over a year later and still LOVE the food. It is my go to for good Puerto Rican without having to go into the city. Trouble is the staff is still AWFUL!!! They are so disrespectful and nasty. They continue to act like you are bothering them. they are always on their cell phones while you wait for them. If you have a question forget it they roll their eyes at you. I would eat here much more often if it wasn;t for the nasty nasty nasty staff.  AND PLEASE PUT YOUR TIP JAR AWAY. Even when I do tip you are still as rude as always. Tips are for good service not because you decided to show up to work!!

I love french fries. Seriously, LOVE them. I fell in love when I discovered this place. And then I made my friends fall in love with it too when I took them there. You just can't go wrong. Have fun experimenting with the variety of sauces. And yes, FF in Europe are usually served in a paper cone. Points for authenticity.

This place's chicken is no joke, really good stuff. But seriously? Not offering chicken until 3:00pm on Saturdays? Only breakfast items until 3:00pm on Saturdays? That's so ridiculous. Get it together guys, seriously.

This sounds lame, but this thai chef makes the best pad thai I have ever had. I know pad thai is pretty standard dish at thai places and people always order it, but I have never been a fan until now. I was trying to keep costs down and ordered off of the lunch menu (there were no curries ont he lunch menu) so I got the pad thai - YUM! The service was very friendly. The waitress and owner/manager overheard that it was my aunt's birthday and they brought out the dessert with a candle - very thoughtful! Both my mother and aunt loved the meal - these women are hard to please and complain about everything ;P I would definitely like to come back!
Delicious! Definitely will be going back!

Unfortunately, we were very disappointed with this restaurant. We have tried some amazing sushi throughout the city and based on reviews, we were expecting excellent quality and service, especially for their price. For the price, you would expect quality. Further, about four of the items we asked for were not available. We get that, especially when it comes to sushi, but then whatever else we order should taste wonderful and shouldn't be so visually unappealing, especially with sushi! The decor is uninteresting and rather cold, whereas some great sushi restaurants give you the atmosphere to fit sushi dining. The waiter was also unhelpful and rushed us in our order, considering they didn't have many items on the menu. Even if it was not so expensive, not worth it. Disappointed.
Amazing sea food, heaven for oyster lovers. outstanding service, great atmosphere and a special variety of beers. We really enjoyed!

i love the sweetbreads, chorizo dish, potatoes, and cozy feel of this place.  This place is super small but nice.  The hostesses here are known to kinda discriminate.  Wait can be 1.5 hours long but the tapas here are awesome****

I can tell this place has the potential to be great and I like hibachi but I noticed some inconsistency on how it was cooked. My scallops went on first and came off last and they where cooked beyond done. I asked for myt steak rare knowing at the way the guy was cooking I would be getting Medium (which I wanted and what I got). The chef didnt use oil at first which I know led to the really dry-overcooked chicken. All in all it was an ok experience with good friends and really good Magic Hat beer but it really wasnt anything special.

Stopped in here for a snack and a drink while waiting for friends and for PS1 to open up on Saturday.  So happy to stumble upon this place.  Just moved to the city and had no idea there was such cute and sophisticated places in Queens.  Place had a wait for a table, but I was lucky enough to score a seat at the bar.  Ordered a side of beets and a mimosa.  Was pleasantly surprised to also get a little plate of mini pastries- whole grain bread, carrot cake, and a chocolate croissant- YUM!  The beet where super good.  Wish I was staying for actual brunch.  Staff was very attentive and I was able to chat with them a bit.  Will definitely be back.

My friend and I dined here last night and we really enjoyed it.  The Tropical Sun smoothie was awesome and I def recommend the potato stuffed dumplings, #13 I think.  Overall for the price this place was awesome.

I'm a big lover of diners but I can't stand when the home fries are not good! Mine were dry, cold, and mostly inedible fried pieces of potato. Low Prices luckily made up for the quality. I got one of their specials- California omelette. Great concept and executed quite well. Waitresses were friendly and it had a nice open, airy atmosphere. It also seemed to be clean. Three stars for an average place. Avoid the homefries.

Service was great, the place is a little too dark and a bit too loud. The food seemed more promising than it was- appetizer of rib terrine was tasty and crab croquette also good. My main course was the special cod with tomato broth. Not very tasty. Bland, uninspired. Not worth finishing and I rarely leave food on my plate (like mama says). My friend got the whole dorade which was very good. Another friend had rib sandwhich - good but not amazing. Dessert was doughnuts with ice cream which I've had before in another restaurant where they were better. I wouldn't go back to eat, but i would say its worth going one time.

Delicious, fast, and affordable. This restaurant is very close to my apartment and is the perfect stop for fast and delicious food. I had the chicken kebab pita with sides of falafel and hummus. I would get it again! The chicken is very well seasoned and juicy. I think next time I will get the plate instead of the sandwich. The spicy sauce is full of flavor but is very hit so make sure you spread it out and don't get a bunch in one bite! I will definitely eat here again soon!

Easily one of the best meals I have ever had.  Kanella definitively lives up to its reputation, and then some.   The atmosphere is cozy, unpretentious, and without any frills; qualities that carry over to the food and service.  Our table ordered the following starters: dips of the day, manti, the fattoush salad with pomegranate, and the flatbread plate, all of which were out of this world.  The manti may have been the best thing I had all night.  I'm still thinking of the flavor produced by the  combination of spice, brown butter, and greek yogurt.  One of the dips of the day was a pumpkin feta, which was unlike anything I have ever tasted. For my entree, I ordered the rabbit's leg, which all of the staff raved about. Don't get me wrong, it was amazing, but I may order the lamb kofta next time as I prefer something with a stronger flavor. All in all, a really memorable experience. Our server was incredibly knowledgable and enthusiastic.  Flawless. I really appreciated the simplicity of everything here; the decor, the menu, the food. Often times, the simpler the better.

Hoagie Haven certainly is a Princeton institution like many of my fellow yelpers have stated. Even though it seems as if this place just caters to one particular customer, everyone at some point finds himself or herself dining at Hoagie Haven. During the early to mid 90's, before I became a resident of Mercer County later that decade, I would leave the hustle and bustle of NYC behind for the tranquility of West Windsor and Princeton Junction for the summer. There were less than a handful of things to do for the youngsters at the time, but the one thing everyone did was some how bring their high, underage, or legally drunk ass to Nassau Street to dine at then two late night eateries, PJ's Pancake House or Hoagie Haven. Hoagie Haven took care of my belly many of nights; drunk, sober, or just plain ole hungry after work. There was nothing like grabbing a sandwich and finding a seat on the benches, the curb, to enjoy that sandwich in the crisp summer air. My favorite was always the Chicken Parm no cheese, no sauce. Uh? Yeah... Fried Chicken cutlet with lettuce, tomato, and mayo is on the menu. Naturally you have to at least order a cheesesteak once in awhile. Once I put aside my no pork rule from my misguided youth, I introduced myself to the bacon cheesesteak. Other than the staff and a few additions to the menu, the place has not changed much. The steak-umm meat cheesesteaks are decent. They probably won't receive any cheesesteak awards but they will satisfy your hunger, and get the job done. FYI...they are still a little cheap with the meat in my opinion. I had a cold hoagie twice. It was good once, but eh eh the very next time. Lack of consistency yeah, but they have proven that they can make a good sandwich. I just refuse to relive the negative experience again. I have certainly eaten less from Hoagie Haven as of late because I am getting older, but I suggest that everyone at least tries it and those of you that haven't had it in awhile grab yourself In the words of Randy Moss... Straight Cash Homie

I have tried so many southern style burritos in the US, and this is by far my favorite. The taste of their meat is far superior, and surprisingly, even the guac. Only downside: populated by hipsters learning Japanese on their iPads.
It may seem a bit pricey but the food you are getting... it is worth it. Very delicious french cuisine and a great atmosphere.
Delish. Lives up to the hype. The buns and the ramen are the way to go!! Be prepared to wait for a table but worth the wait

If they accepted credit cards, they'd have 4.5 stars.  The food was typical quality NYC sushi. The other bits on the plate (I ordered the tuna avocado maki) were flavorful, but not overpowering. As an entrée I had the Heritage Pork Betty with optional farm egg and a bowl of rice. Doesn't get much more delectable than that. The cilantro was also appreciated helping to catch your bearing with all the richness.   Sencha green tea was also very good. I'll be back.

I went to Kefi for the first time today and I was pleasantly surprised.  I saw it in Daily Candy and suggested it to my friend who wanted to stay on the UWS.  She can be a picky eater so I wasn't what she would think of it. We came without a reservation at 6:30pm and they sat us in about 10 min.  It's deceptively large inside.  We thought they were going to sit us in the back and we found out that there is a set of stairs leading us downstairs to another section. The menu had a decent selection of seafood, meats and a handful of vegetarian selections.  The descriptions can definitely be improved.  The dishes were in Greek and the description was basically a carbon copy of the dish name so they were not helpful if you don't speak Greek.  The good thing was that our waitress was knowledgable and could make her recommendations.  She was very pleasant and helpful. We also wanted a bottle of wine but didn't know what to get so the 'sommalier' was called.  We told him we wanted a light and crisp white, and suggested four wines.  We went with one with a medium body and low-medium price of the four bottles.   I should have written down the name of the wine but it was $36.  I highly suggest it. Now... let's talk food.  We ordered several appetizers and one pasta dish.  The spreads were really tasty: eggplant, caviar/cheese, tomato paste, and yogurt.  The eggplant and caviar were my favorite.  The octopus with bean salad is absolutely delicious.  I tried to convince the carnivore next to us to order it next time, but I think I sold his wife and son on it.  The octopus was stewed so it was soft.  Even my friend loved it.  I'm so proud of her.  We ordered a side of cauliflower which I would have been fine without.  It was simmered in a broth with olives.  The cauliflower was so soft that it was mushy.  Lastly we had the orzo with spinach, feta and shrimp.  There were only about 4 pieces of shrimp but the dish was lovely.  We ordered an orange dessert but it wasn't very memorable.  I suggest going some place else for dessert.  I was told by the child next to me that the ice cream is good -- he had pomegranate and chocolate. Someone was playing around with the lights to the right mood but it was weird because I could see my food one second and not the next.  Overall the experience was great.  Even though the restaurant was packed by 8pm, I didn't feel rushed to leave and the service was very attentive.  I know this because I dropped my knife and someone immediately brought me a new one before I could ask.  Then they brought our dessert without spoons but someone else saw and bought two over 30 seconds later.  I spoke with people around me and it seems everyone had been to the old location.  I lived right by it and never knew about it!  I was told that the food is still the same but the restaurant is about four times larger.  I will definitely be back.

Little Spoon gets 3.5 stars, and I'm rounding up because they're new in town. I am a total sucker for brunch, and I was so excited to try this place out this morning. After seeing pictures online of the adorable decor, it did not disappoint. It seems like the back patio is a really nice spot, so it's a bummer it's already so chilly. The weather is also a bummer when you're waiting for a table because there is little to no space to wait inside. We braved sitting outside in the cold for about 15 minutes today, although it seemed that many people left in that time, deterred by the wait time / standing outside.   I got a vanilla latte that was a bit too sweet, but still made really well. If I am being really picky, I wish they had some house-made flavor syrups. My boyfriend and I split the breakfast burrito with sausage and the scramble of the day, which had squash, ricotta, pepitas, and pesto. We also got a side of the vegan scrapple just because, well, who else serves vegan scrapple? Our server was extremely prompt and the food came out quickly. However, as others have mentioned, the portions are definitely small, the breakfast burrito much more so than the scramble. I feel like it should have come with potatoes or a side salad or something because I ate my half in about 4 bites. The bread that came with the scramble however, was really tasty, as was the jam. Unfortunately, the potatoes were pretty bland. Looking around, it seemed that most tables got 2 main dishes and split a third, like the fries. We had tried to order a baked good to start, but despite their advertisement, the baked goods were lacking. They had cookies, brownies, and tarts, but no scones, muffins, etc, so we ended up without anything. The food was definitely well made and the staff was friendly and attentive. I wish the portions were a bit more substantial, but I'll probably be back to try it again!

the worst manager i have ever met!  he is EXTREMELY RUDE, and clearly accommodates to girls he'd like to sleep with.  ruined my night by being so rude.  only go to this restaurant if you don't mind being treated by a 25-year old hipster on a power-trip!

Pretty good Italian food, except there seemed to be something just slightly off about everything. The appetizers are very small, and when my bolognese arrived, it was pretty lukewarm andthen got cold quite quickly. Was fine, but I wouldn't necessarily come back.

I'm a beer girl so I like to go somewhere that has a wide selection.  This place has a ton of different options to choose from which is nice.  The food is decent but its more about the atmosphere and drinks for me.  Pretty cool place.z

A very solid 3-star spot. We ended up here after seeing "Seminar" (w/Alan Rickman; go order tickets now) because we wanted a place that would serve up real food at 4 PM. Everything was very good, with standouts including the black bean soup, the guacamole and the strip steak. The desserts were lackluster. Still, options in the Theater District at 4 PM are limited, and I wouldn't not come back here.

Supercilious waiter and day-old croissants--cannot fool a couple of New Yorkers.  Used to like this place for its ambiance, but even ambiance cannot cancel out such attitude.  No excuse with its own bakery next door!

I'm going to basically agree with the sentiment on here.  Very good ingredient first food.  Had really excellent crab toast, carrot and avocado salad and halibut.  The preparation of the carrot (deep flavor substituting it for a protein) was one of the more interesting dishes I've had in NY (I eat out plenty).  I found myself thinking about the food more after this dinner than anywhere I've eaten in quite awhile. They also have a well constructed menu and wine list. Why not 5 stars?  A few reasons. 1.  It is painfully loud. Maybe they should get some carpets from ABC carpet.  I wouldn't go with a group larger than 4. 2.  It's a scene with models etc.  Maybe that's your thing, but I don't personally feel it adds to the experience.  I found myself laughing at the collections of people and behavior at some of the tables...i.e a family of 4 with small children eating at a table for 8 at 11pm.  Wife was clearly a model/had been one.  Other restaurants probably wouldn't have tolerated this sort of thing, but I suspect they were special. All this excitement makes getting reservations exceedingly difficult if you don't have a personal assistant to stake out your reservation (to be clear I don't really hold against them being popular maybe just a bit on how/to whom they seem to allocate reservations). 3. I don't know why some places do this, but can I have one server to take care of me for the night?  I think we had three people.  It's strange and disconcerting.  I mean to bring over my meal or whatever fine, but why is one person explaining the menu and another then taking  my order?  Bizarre. Overall though its a destination place and deserves to be.  I'll be back, but there are some things holding it back.

This might be my favorite place in Philly. I guess it's just the combination of everything they offer that has me obsessed. I get the same thing every time I go-vegan beef nachos, frozen margarita. I don't know what they put in that vegan beef sauce, but it's good enough that every meat-eater I've forced to share with me (the "small" is more than enough for two people for a meal) has enjoyed it. Vegan beef nachos, margarita. That's all you need to know.

I was excited to try this place because I'm on a locally-grown kick. The food was great, but it really has more of a lunch menu than dinner. So, because it didn't have a full dinner menu or really many side options, I was a little disappointed.  I had to keep reminding my dinner companion why this place was cool, and why I had wanted to eat there.  Also, she's a skinny lady who doesn't eat much, but even she was hungry (as was I) two hours later.   That being said, the place is cute with great decor and it gave us a reason to go to the Chelsea market which was fun.  And the food really  was great--just not quite right for the dinner I was looking for.

This review is long overdue.....I have been to Cuban Petes on 3 separate occassions, the first time by choice the 2 remaining times at the request of friends. Food I've had much better cuban food. The first two times eating here I was so underwhelmed it was just blah. I come from a Latin background and this just wasnt the same as what Im use to. The last occassion here I was pleasantly surprised and enjoyed the apps as well as my meal (pernil) Could this have been a fluke? Who knows but I wont be coming back to figure it out. Staff I wouldnt use pleasant to describe the waitstaff, they are more on the brusque side. No pleasantries, a lot of rushing you and poor followup on all 3 of my visits. I understand your busy and turning your tables is part of the job but you arent giving the people who are out to enjoy a nice dinner out any reason to want to tip you well. You get back what you put out. Ambiance Cuban Petes decor is just lovely,  all the different dining areas are decorated so nice and the cute little outdoor area is my favorite, its almost like your in another world. Petes Im not sure if you are aware noise level factors into your ambiance. Each and every time Ive visited I think I lost just a bit of my hearing. Can you turn DOWN the SPEAKERS just a few decibles please!!! I think my party and I said "What" more times in one sitting than I care to count. Now I love the live musicians you have going on as well that makes it fun and its great to see and hear something different every now and again. That being said you might want to consider either moving where these musicians play or having them play for shorter periods b/c again the noise level is way to high to enjoy your meal. Oh Petes I had such high expectations of you after hearing so many wonderful things but you have fallen short on to many levels for my liking. All I can say is....Adios....

This at one time was the finest  restaurant in the state..I have their cookbook and use it!...Service at lunch was terrible but out server was pleasant..Did the taste of Hartford which was very reasonable..Salad over dressed and under seasoned,,Long wait to order and even longer to arrive...EVERY COURSE...We did arrive late for lunch but with 6 people max in dining room expected better..Would love this place to come back to its heyday but management needs a heads up...Love the atmosphere please be what u used to be!!!!!!!!!

I've been here for dinner a few times with my family before and the food was good and pretty authentic, so we decided to try their dim sum today. Big mistake. The reviews that complained about the Beef Chow Fun and other dishes running out quickly were true. They were even short on utensils too! We waited a long time for tea because they didn't have enough tea pots, and we were only given two forks instead of four because apparently they didn't have enough of those either. When we asked for the Beef Chow Fun, the waiter rudely told us we should have ordered half an hour earlier, and then walked away before we could begin to order another dish. They seem to be very understaffed, too. Needless to say, the service was absolutely horrible. Despite that, the food was decent and it wasn't too pricey. But I probably wouldn't come back for dim sum again.

I used to come here all the time when I lived in the neighborhood, and recently went back again for the first time in years. The interior is now very chic, whereas before it looked like your average diner. The menu has changed a little, but the food was delicious as usual. The carrot-curry soup was amazing. My falafel wrap was good as well. They also have a well-stocked bar now, which I don't remember from before.  I wish they'd come to Brooklyn!

We were excited to dine here, as we'd been waiting all winter for the restaurant to open. The food was not bad (though not outstanding) but the service was awful. Our waiter took our order and came back 20 minutes later to ask what we wanted again. Another 20 minutes later, he came back to ask us if we were ready for our check. We reminded him that we had not yet received our food. He said he'd go check with his manager to see about our order. The food came out eventually, though altogether, it took over an hour for us to get it after we'd placed the initial order. Definitely a disappointing experience and we don't plan to return.

I have been here a few times over the last year or so and this is probably the best Thai place in the area. The food is fresh and well cooked, and the decor is readily cute, comfortable and kitschy. I would definitely recommend the Pad See Ew with beef and a glass of Riesling.

Jean-George Vongerichten's  8th restaurant in the city, Perry Street is a very sleek and minimalistic restaurant which includes minimal ornamentation such as simple hanging lights. However, the comfort of the wood tables and the soft white colors also made me feel like we were in someone's living room. You can tell, as soon as you enter, that it was designed by Richard Meier, the same architect who designed the parent building in which it's located. Located at Perry Street and West Side Highway, the restaurant's window front also provides amazing sunset views! We decided to start with cocktails instead of wine for a fun change of pace.The Thyme Lemonade cocktail was refreshing and a not too sweet take on the traditional lemonade. The Citron Vodka was mixed with club soda and a lemon thyme syrup, resulting in a delicious cocktail which went down far too quickly. We were in no mood to rush and therefore decided to split a small appetizer between us before ordering our appetizers and main course. The chilled Peekytoe crab salad did not disappoint! Unlike any crab salad I've ever had, it was topped with fresh summer vegetables, crisp to the bite, and a champagne mango vinaigrette. The smooth crab flavor against the fresh, crisp vegetables left me craving more than just a small plate portion! We followed our waiter's appetizer recommendation for the appetizer course. Tuna is one of my favorite fish, whether grilled or served sashimi style, so I knew I couldn't resist their signature dish, rice cracker crusted tuna. On the menu since opening day, this dish was served with a Siracha emulsion which was perfect for dipping. Always a sucker for sweet breads, Bo ordered the appetizer special which was a summer take on sweet breads, paired with freshly grilled peaches and a Siracha glaze. I don't care for sweet bread so can't directly speak to their flavor but I know Bo loved them! Choosing a main course was a more difficult task as many items sounded wonderful, especially the fish dishes! I finally decided on the pistachio grilled cod accompanied with summer vegetables and chanterelle mushrooms. Unfortunately, the dish was lacking flavor though the cod was cooked perfectly Bo's chicken was the real winner of the evening as it was a creative and perfectly executed spin on the southern classic, fried chicken with creamed corn.  One boneless breast and one boneless thigh were served with rich creamed corn that was perfectly seasoned.  The chicken also came with an interesting scotch bonnet hot sauce which enhanced the flavor even more by contrasting the creaminess of the corn.  Bo thought that it was one of the best dishes that he's had in a while. The service continued to amaze us through the final portion of the meal, a complimentary serving of strawberry French style macarons. I personally don't care for these one bit. I'll take a coconut macaroon over a macaron any day if I have my choice. But, according to Bo, who loves all things French, these were soft and delicious with a subtle sweet strawberry flavor. Overall, we were both very pleased with the service and meal. While I'm not sure we would go again, as there are so many restaurants in New York City,  I would recommend it to anyone. The sunset views and friendly service made the atmosphere more relaxed than stuffy. The dishes were all very reasonably priced for New York City, especially the main courses.

I had the lunch special Teriyaki Chicken Bento box and 3 roll Maki combo (Eel Avocado, Spicy Tuna, and Yellow Tail Scallion) for takeout today.  The prices are very good in comparison to Tokyo Sushi down the road (which in my opinion is way too expensive).   The sushi was not the best.  The fish tasted ok, but the rice lacked flavor and the seaweed was soggy.  In addition, the spicy tuna tasted a little too sweet.  The rolls were well sized and I was definitely full after the three rolls. The chicken teriyaki was decent, but the chicken was relatively dry and chewy.  Sauce tasted a little more Chinese than Japanese.  The white rice was good, and the rest of the items were what you would normally expect from a Bento box. Overall, the two items were good for the price, but I have definitely had better (Yutaka in Somerville has much better sushi).  Due to the close proximity to my home, I would probably come here again.
Best pho in Philadelphia, hands down.

Had dinner there for the first time. The asparagus was done well. My salmon was dry. Great all day happy hour prices on Mondays. $4 house wine, $5 cocktails, $3 beer and 1/2 priced apps. Had a good glass of house Pinot Noir and house Chardonnay.

I'm a sucker for fried chicken, and a sucker for pie, but having the two together as both the signature dishes sounds mind blowing so I had to try it. Expect a wait, especially on a saturday, but the it was less than 20min. The place is small and crowded, typical for ny standards, but the weather was nice enough that we sat in the back where they had outdoor seating. I ordered the fried chicken box, and my friend had the chicken and waffles. The chicken was hot, crispy and the seasoning was good, but didn't expect the biscuit too be AMAZING. I would say the best I ever had so far. My friend thought her dish, chicken and waffles, were okay, the waffle was too thick, and the syrup or sauce was kinda weird. As for the pie, our first choice (which I can't remember) was sold out so we settled for an apple pie. I was kinda disappointed, I can't say it was bad, but it was nothing special. If they could somehow incorporate their biscuits into the pie menu (like cobblers) that would be great. If I was in the mood for fried chicken (I always am) and in the area, I would stop by.
