I can't recall the number of times I've been here, but let's just say I've started going to NP when it was at the corner of 8th and Christian.  The staff knows us, but that really doesn't help you get a seat faster or get their attention either.  I mean, they're good at what they do, don't get me wrong.  The food is delicious and cheap (dinner for 2 with a beer each can be $20 with tip).  I only give it 4 stars because when you're trying to get the waiter's attention, sometimes they pretend they don't see you. One of my favorite things to order is Bun Bo Hue and that big plate of something that comes with things like grilled shrimp on sugar cane, ground beef wrapped in grape leaves and meatballs you wrap in rice paper...I don't know what it's called because I just point or order by number.  They get it. Another plus is they open at 10AM.

I have been coming to Olea since they opened. I don't live in the neighborhoohd anymore but still make it a desitnation stop. The food is never disappointing. I had the Cicken & Pork Paella yesterday and it was amazing! It was devoured by my friends right down to the crispy rice at the bottom of the cast iron pan it arrived.  Oh and I had one of the best Manhattan's ever made.
Best ethiopian food in Philly.  This is a tiny cafe with good service and no ambiance.
I would make the line shorter if i could

Choose this place randomly since I was taking my mother to see If/Then the musical. Ended up being a FANTASTIC choice. Even though they were just opening, we were served immediately. The festive decorations during christmas created a warm and cozy feeling, especially since it was raining outside. Their drink menu (beer, wine, ect) is to die for. The food was unique and absolutely delicious.

A no-thrills, great tiny diner! Very reasonably priced. Fast service. I did a standard eggs, bacon, potatoes, and toast breakfast.  Everything was delicous. You go there hungry, they feed you, you leave happy. Not much more to say!
So yummy! I got french toast and my husband got steak and eggs. He loved it, and the french toast melts in your mouth. I can't wait to go again. There can be a wait, I'd say it's worth it.

Upon our return from Greece, we were going through some sort of food withdrawal.  After reading several reviews, we decided to check out this Greek Taverna.  We were not disappointed.  The menu and food were authentic, the service was great and BYOB is always a plus.  Greek salad and Halloumi were the perfect start.  Mussels Saganaki and the Swordfish steak were equally delicious.   Really looking forward to going back!!

Like everyone else my friends and I were HUGE Top Chef fans... my boyfriend and I arrived early for our reservations and took 2 seats at the bar for a drink... we decided on 2 glasses of Chardonney... the bartender had us taste test the wine. now some may call me trashy or maybe I'm not going to the right places but we had never been somewhere that has done that so we were off to a good start!  Now knowing that we were going to Harold's restaurant there was the obvious 'oh I hope I get to see him'... which fortunately while we were still waiting for our now late friends apparently really good friends of his were seated next to us at the bar and he came out to have a LONG chat with them practically sitting on my lap (still has his pencil behind his ear!).  So after I got over gawking at Harold I decided to have a glance around the restaurant and I nearly had a stroke because my season 2 FAVORITE top chef SAM was having dinner in a booth which lucky for us when our friends finally showed up we were promptly seated right next to his table!  Of course we had wine.. I sadly don't remember the name but it was a nice white.  For appetizers we shared the duck meatballs, crab salad, and the rock shrimp salad all were DELICIOUS!! For entrees we all did something different and passed them around so we could all have a taste I know there was the duck, ravioli, red snaper, and I forgot the other because I was so enthralled with the side of spinach and broccoli with pork belly which just melted in your mouth.   To end off the fabulous meal we each had a class of moscato and shared the rhubarb desert which was very good.  I will be back.

My breakast experience at cafe luluc was amazing. I ordered the pancakes (they only have one option for pancakes, but that's really all you need). They were, as promised,  crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside.. perfectly perfect. The two pancakes were big in size so they were very filling and  under $9 so that's also a plus! The atmosphere is very friendly and diner, like. Cafe Luluc is worth a visit!!!

I've been going here for years and alwasys got the chicken club. As I said in my last review its always good. This time the chicken was kinda rubbery. Idk if it was an off day but I hope they get there stuff together.  You lost a star for that one

Interesting spot near China Town~Crawfish was not as good as I expected, but the king crab leg was amazingly delicious! We did special sauce and medium spicy. It was not spicy at all, so if you want something hot, go with the level above spicy. Next time, will still get king crab legs, and may try the lobster:)
Yeah go to say you've been bit don't expect a great steak. Better than Geno's but that's not saying a lot. Service was better too.
Cute place and great food! Loved the burrata (creamy and delicious!), mushroom truffle oil pasta and the cheesecake! Definitely coming back here! Service was good, too.

We came here because of a recommendation from a friend, we were soo disappointed.  Yes the prices are cheap and the portions are pretty decent, but you get what you pay for.  We started off with the chicken livers, this was our fault, we should have read the menu more carefully as we assumed it would be some type of pate or mousse, but it was a plate full of chicken livers, the portion was ridiculous for two people and really overwhelming.  We ended up packing half of it up. For our dinner we had the gnocchi which was too cheesy and the tagliatelle alla bolognese, so yes the pasta was fresh, but the sauce was not impressive.  The bolognese tasted like each of the ingredients that was used to make that dish, and not enough time was given to the sauce for flavors to develop, very disappointing.  If you want a cheap Italian meal, this is the place, but not memorable, we'd rather pay a little more for higher quality.
Toroniku Ramen (slow cooked pork with soft cabbage)!!!  They have kimchee=)  and the Gyoza is awesome too.

We recently got married and brought 12 guests here for dinner. We've been eating here occasionally since Above opened.   We have always had a good dining experience and our wedding dinner was no exception. The outside terrace is a pleasant alternative when the weather is warm. The staff is always professional and the food is always good.  A little pricey on some menu items but not more expensive than you'd expect to pay in a very good restaurant I've lived in south orange for almost 40 years and this is the best restaurant in the area.

There were no open tables, so we set up shop at the bar. The bartender was attentive and friendly, even if his accent was harsh. The guy was nice enough to give us directions to a 24-hour Kinko's, not too shabby. We ordered two pasta dishes, and they came out in a reasonable amount of time. While not upscale Italian cuisine, Trattoria Trecolori was a great find in the theatre district. The reasonably priced entrees were refreshing in midtown. I'd go again.

I've been to this place a couple of times now and have been thoroughly impressed by the food each time. The portions are huge, even if you get a "small". Each entree comes with rice and peas, steamed/boiled cabbage, and a side salad. They put this sweet dressing on the salad that is pretty delicious. I've had the jerk chicken and the oxtail. Both were perfectly cooked. My oxtail last night was falling off the bone tender. The gravy was the perfect consistency too, not too goopy. My friend got the curry goat, which was also tender and spiced really well. I also tried the lemonade last night, which they put brown sugar in according to other yelpers. It had a wonderful tangy, sweet, yet smoky flavor;probably the best lemonade I've ever had. The seating area upstairs is tiny, but really cute and homey feeling. I am subtracting one star though  because it was pretty uncomfortably hot and humid up there even though it was pretty cool outside. Also, the service got a little spotty last night at the end. The woman who took our order forgot about us after she brought us our meals and we really wanted dessert! Overall, I would say this place is one of my favorites and although I am not a Caribbean food aficionado, it is the best Caribbean food I've had in the city thus far.
Best square slice ever.  Sauce on top, crunch on the bottom, cheese in-between.  Oh my!

Rude rude service. Very very loud at long table. Felt rushed. Very arrogant. Pastas are very average. Had a microwaved chocolate soufflé that came out 2 minutes after ordered....burning hot. Won't return. Looks authentic but it's not.

I'm a huge sushi fan! I love this place, even their delivery is impressive and I haven't complained once. Until recently....usually I order if I don't have the time to visit. but a day ago when I placed an order for delivery, they told me they don't do delivery and hung up. I'm really disappointed.

Having lived and traveled throughout Turkey, I can tell you this is about as close to the real deal as you're going to get in the States.  Aside from the fact that they serve Greek salad (which happens to be very good, but it's neither a real Greek salad nor would you ever see anything Greek in a real Turkish restaurant), the Turkish beverages and food were the most authentic I've experienced outside of Turkey.  Our party of four started with Turkish red wine, beer (Efes), and an assortment of appetizers--calamari, stuffed grape leaves, sigara borek, Greek salad, and breads--all outstanding.  Our main courses--doner and iskender kebabs and karides guvec (shrimp casserole)--couldn't have been better and left us little room for dessert.  We just couldn't pass up the baklava--perfectly done, deliciously moist.  We've eaten here before and found the upstairs a lot quieter ... downstairs is busy and loud, but fun.  Lots of outside seating, but it was a gorgeous night and everyone else had the same idea.  Service was impeccable.  Dinner for four, including two rounds of drinks and tip, came to $240--not bad for Manhattan.  Of all the places we've eaten in New York City, the four of us agree Beyoglu is right at the top of the list.

I've been here numerous occasions because it's THAT good. Compared to other Thai places with the similar pricing, the quality of the ingredients are different! I usually get the Beef Pad Thai. The beef they use is so tender and delicious! Plus their Thai Ice Tea is FUN! You can customize it yourself and make it as sweet or less sweet. The ice they put in the drink is actually frozen Thai Iced tea which I crush up with the spoon they give and eat it like a dessert! The service is always very polite and nice! But I do not recommend sitting at the bar by yourself and expecting the bartender to chat with you. Their English is not very good..which is why they aren't so talkative with the customers in general.
best burger in nyc

Only positive is that its super cheap.  Walked in the faint smell of garbage and stickiness everywhere; the floor, the table, the menu etc.  I ordered some pork dumplings and the beef brisket noodles.  The dumplings were ok, but my bowl of noodles was disgusting.  The herbs were old (as evidenced by their color), the brisket was extremely tough and fatty, the noodles tasted like last night's spaghetti, and the broth was a la campbell's chicken noodle soup.  Gross, just gross.

Stopped by for early dinner on a Sunday afternoon. We sat outside on their nice patio.  Food is average and prices are a little high for the portion size. I ordered the pasta with mushrooms. I think it was $19 and about the size of an appetizer portion. Bread was very good. Wine list is very pricy, so this is not my kind of place considering there are so many BYOB places in the area.
overated pizza with uneven balance of cheese,.  Great if you are a tourist looking to just sample an institution.  Try Grimaldi's if you want a real NY pie.

Although I did not eat here I did have some drinks. Beers.. so I can say much about how they bar tend. The environment was chill, they had some live music that night. There were a lot of people there so it looks popular. I had already eaten but a part of wished that I didn't I saw this great pot roast come out with potatoes and all the fix ins. The person who ordered it was in our group I asked how it was and she said it was great. Can't beat pub food when your out drinking!
A bustling atmosphere: lively, loud and fun.  We (group of six) didn't have dinner here because we ate elsewhere and only stopped in for coffee and dessert.  I had the tiramisu--delizioso!

Despite other reviewers, I personally love the food. I think the chips-n-dip with the horseradish cream sauce are AMAZING and since it's in my neighborhood, it's a nice place to go snack and grab beers. (By the way, the burgers are fantastic.) However, my feelings towards the establishment are luke warm. The bartenders over all have seemed friendly and helpful when describing their selection (which is a pain to see, for the record,) but the service can be really hit or miss. I brought a friend from out of town who asked when she served us our drinks if they had Pepsi or Coca-Cola products. She basically laughed at him and said, "We don't have either, we have just 'Cola.'" Confused, he asked if they had any other sort of sodas like..mountain dew or the likes and again, he was met with a pretentious laugh that made the entire table uncomfortable throughout their time there as they felt they were being judged. Every simple request, "Do you have barbecue sauce?" was met with a "no," and another snotty laugh or better yet, an eye roll as she slunk off into the kitchen. Also, I should add that they wouldn't serve me alcohol because one person at the table didn't hand an ID and it was during lunch time. I can stomach the liquor lockdown, even not serving run-of the mill products because they market themselves as a gastropub and pride themselves on their unique selections..however, I cannot even begin to digest servers who either don't care, don't show up, or make their table uncomfortable. As I've waitressed for five years, it's just stupid service! Just a tip for the waitress (who got 15% she still didn't' deserve): The nicer you are to your patrons, the more they'll tip you! On a lighter note, not ALL the servers are miserable or condescending. I had one really friendly girl who helped me pick out a beer that I absolutely loved and despite having a packed station, she managed to get us our food, drink, and checks within a reasonable amount of time. I guess that's why she works days and the others work nights.
Great breakfast menu, fantastic atmosphere and reasonably priced for Time Square.

AWFUL. Unbelievably slow service (hello, it's an AIRPORT, people are not here to leisurely enjoy one sushi roll).  On top of that, they don't seem to understand their own menu. Then after an hour the roll was made wrong, and when I pointed it out, I had to explain what the menu said, and then explain the difference between cucumber and avocado. The last straw was the obnoxious woman behind the counter just saying "thank you" to each complaint in a mocking voice. Airport food and traveling is bad enough - don't make your trip worse by going here to eat.

My sister-in-law had her birthday party here and it was lovely.  They gave us the back area which was super comfy and relaxed with the nice couches and cozy atmosphere.   The service was great, very helpful but not overwhelming and the tapas was perfect for everyone to have something to nosh on (great selection of cheeses, meats, olives, etc. as you'd expect).  And of course there was a nice selection of wine and they thoughtfully brought out a bunch of glasses to keep the table stocked as new people arrived. I've also been here for a book club group and it was equally enjoyable.  All in all, a great low key vibe with excellent service and good wine.  Perfect for any group gathering, from a book club to a birthday party!

Had the cuban sandwich and fire roasted corn for lunch. Maybe the corn wasn't such a good choice, because a bunch of it got stuck in my teeth. The cojita cheese made it nice and yummy though. Mmmmm, cheese. The cuban sandwich was also good. I wonder what kind of ham they use. Could have use more cheese on the sandwich. God I love cheese. Anywho, it was really busy here around lunch time. Obviously they're popular with the kids. They take credit cards, which surprised me. Don't bank on having a table to sit at. Maybe they're a little bit overpriced. I don't know. You decide. If you really like cuban sandwiches, you'll probably like this place.
Didn't think it could possibly live up to the hype. But - best pizza I have ever tasted. Just go before Dom dies.

Better than Bread... Occupying the corner formerly known as Bread Tribeca, Distilled did a great job of revamping the space into a cool bar/restaurant covered in dark woods and dimly light with sepia like incandescent bulbs. The service at the bar was good, bartenders put on a decent show putting together their cocktails and were engaging with everyone bellying up.  I should warn you though, when it's crowded, people will be constantly yelling over your shoulder for a drink.  The food was a good but not great, I expected more since I heard the chef is former from one of the MomoFuku restaurants.  I really enjoyed the BLT which was an interesting take on the classic, swapping out pieces of crisp bacon for grated.  Everything else I tried, the Wings, Roasted Cauliflower and Country Fried Duck & Waffles were a bit lackluster.  Price point is what you'd expect of an upscale pub in the TriBeCa area, but I think there is some room for improvement if they are going to become a mainstay. In short, good not great and prepare to lose some hearing if you're sitting at the bar during a peak time.

Excellent service and food. The pizza is delicious, and the specials are wonderful. Sometimes the restaurant can get quite loud, but aside from that, there is nothing to dislike about this place. I can't say that I've had a bad experience here yet.
Great happy hour - awesome vibe with the live jazz. Pistachio goat cheese ball and a wine flight is a great way to enjoy a few hours.

Really good pizza in a fun atmosphere with good beer. I was here once years ago during my heavy drinking days & I remember being in the back room.  It was a daze but I've recently been back for pizza when the place wasn't crawling with drunks & hipsters. They aren't as popular as Sally's & Pepe's it seems but they still offer good crispy thin crust pizza.  I've had the infamous mashed potato pizza & it was pretty good.  They don't offer special pizzas but have plenty of topping options available.  I follow their Instagram feed where they're always posting something mouth watering.  My last trip I tried to replicate a buffalo chicken pizza with blue cheese I saw. Their beer is pretty good.  I go for the pizza & the beer is just an added bonus.  I can't think of an offering of theirs that blew me away but for $8.50 a flight you can sample them all. I also love the fact that they're open 365 days a year.  My first trip was on Christmas Eve where we met my family half way from RI.  If I lived closer I'd come on Wednesday nights when Manic Productions promotes free shows.  I'm still pissed off I missed the time the Hold Steady played for free one night!

I throughly enjoyed this place. To me this is what good south Philly Italian is all about. Simple ingredients, good beer and most of all MEATBALLS. Just the sheer size of this beautiful mixture of beef and veal is enough to send me into a blissful state. With the home made ricotta cheese on top just makes this dish so great. The staff is always friendly and the bar manager is a super cool guy.

Sansom Street is one of my favorite streets in the Rittenhouse area, so sitting outside at Melograno was really pleasant. Its great location also came in handy when my fiance and I decided at the last minute that we wanted a bottle of wine. (You can buy a bottle right around the block, so he did a fast wine run as I held the table!) They have a few vegetarian (or could easily be made vegetarian) pasta dishes, such as what I ordered - the Ravioli di Magro. It was tasty for sure, but could have gotten better ravioli at a lower price somewhere else. My fiance loved the Funghi Arrostiti appetizer.
The food is sooo goood. Best sushi ive ever had, my boyfriend enjoyed the general tsos chicken lunch special. worth the price! But theyre always soo busy and only have two waitresses, they need help!

The food is creative, you can tell this guy knows his stuff. Wine list could have more reasonable choices, though I did love the $40. rioja . The ambiance reeks of pretension but the staff couldn't be warmer. I think it's overpriced which is why I gave it only four stars.

Great NY Noodle Town definitely gets 5 stars for cheapness and quickness of food. Unfortunately, I am just not crazy about the food.  Sure, I'll come here when it's late at night and I'm with a bunch of friends, but it is by no means my favorite noodle place in Chinatown. That's all I have to say.

Who said one can't get good, cheap food in SoHo? The menu is not extensive but at Pepe Rosso you can find many staples of italian cuisine at a damn honest price. I had a pasta with vegetables and a glass of wine for under $15, and bread is included. Even that they post all kind of "unfriendly" warnings on the walls, I guess that just adds to the local charm.
amazing white.

*Overall 3.5 stars* Decor: 4/5 Service: 3/5 -Average, nothing special Food: 3.5/5 -I went with the recommended: Milanese. The pesto had way too much oil and I felt sick after eating only half. s3-media4.ak.yelpcdn.com… -Delizioso Panini was WoW. This was much better. Not oily and quite refreshing. Generous slices of prosciutto cotto & fresh mozzarella. I could not taste the anchioves and the mustard was a good touch but as Kenny C. pointed, he wishes it was Dijon mustard Right now the panini are hit & miss. I need to try their other items for a more accurate rating.

I cannot say better things about the food in this restaurant! I'm itching to come back already, yummmmm We got the crostini misti to start, which was four different bruschetta and was awesome! For dinner I definitely recommend one of the homemade pastas, they were the best thing we got for sure. I got the spinach gnocchi with Gorgonzola cream sauce...literally haven't had anything this delicious since I was in Italy! Highly recommend this dish! The boys got the cheese ravioli with a blush sauce, which they also really loved. My other friend got the penne all arrabiatta, which was good but the penne wasn't homemade, and she said ours were better. For dessert we had the tiramisu and a chocolate mousse dish that the waiter recommended, both delicious! Tiramisu was better if I had to choose one. IMPORTANT: it's cash only, so hit the ATM before you go! Totally worth it, I'm craving the food again already! And make a reservation, it's a smaller place. My only less-than-wonderful comment I have is that both red wines we tried (Chianti and Cabernet) were not very good, and we struggled to drink them. I love my red wine so I was a little upset about it but the food was so good we didn't mind. Maybe go for the white wine instead!

Reaaaallly like this place. Great ambiance, trendy, hip and the food is good. I'm a big fan of the gigantic chandelier within a glass column. I tried to snap pics of it with my phone, but the lighting was too dim. I felt like I walked into a club, and I always wondered if this place secretly transforms into a club late night.. or weekends. But alas, it is just a restaurant. The entrees here are all very decent, but the presentation is where Room Service excels. I'm a fan of the pineapple fried rice and pad thai. The rice is served in a cone shape - fun! The service is always excellent here and the prices are reasonable. Fellas, this is a great date place.

I love this place.  The food is fresh and delicious. An unusual spinach salad has goat cheese, walnuts, and dried apricots with the most amazing fresh pesto dressing.  Yum.  Espresso lattes are good but the assortment of chai tea lattes is awesome.  There's a chocolate version I save for special occasions when I've been very, very good and deserve a treat.  I live around the block and have always found the service polite and very accomodating.  Breakfast outside on a Saturday morning is a great way to kick off the weekend--bring your dog and chat with neighbors.  Oh, and after 6:00 p.m., sandwiches and salads are reduced to $5.00.  Such a great deal when you're too tired to make a meal after work and want something healthy.

lovely outdoor lunch spot. great staff, good food. gluten free pasta options. I had the quinoa selvaggio. not the most delicate dish - intense on the cheese and butter, but tasty and much better than the fare in most of this neighborhood filled with tourist traps. also right on the park.
Very nice staff. Food comes quickly, and is consistent. Family friendly.

Mayhem. A zoo of beautifully gargantuan proportions. A place you have to see to believe. It's a re-store-ant. Selling it's wares through it's restaurants placed around and between it's shopping space. That's a lot of it's. My friend dined at the Pesce (fish) station/resto. We tried the grilled calamari and shrimp with meyer lemon over micro greens, and the grilled octopus. Delicious. Another highlight of the meal was the olive oil. I wanted to drink it out of the bottle. We also dined at the dessert counter. Panna cotta with salted caramel and a simple streusel topping. Delicious. My advice to those who may be a bit daunted by the experience is to just dive in. Don't think about where you're sitting, just take your time, sit, eat, and enjoy. The only way to appreciate 'la dolce vita'.

I'm very surprised to see the high rating for this restaurant. Please let me set something straight. First of all, this restaurant is very expensive. We spent close to $100 for two people with no drinks and the tip. The food was not that good. The best thing on the menu was the Creole, but that was served in a very small portion in a very small bowl. The rest of the food was  unexceptional.  Much of it was fried. The service was very good. However, one waitress barely spoke English and had trouble communicating when we asked questions about the menu. I have traveled all over the world, and have no problem understanding many languages, but there was definitely a language barrier here. The atmosphere is quaint. However, I would not go back.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed my favorite brunch place in Brooklyn yet. I've never had a bad experience here, coming about once a month for almost a year.   There is usually a wait for brunch, regardless of what time you come.  But the way that the host handles the people waiting is wonderful - the wait time quoted is always accurate (for better or worse), there's no inside spot to wait but everyone is usually happy to wait outside since the food is so good. I've gotten a few different egg dishes, and various sides, all have been delicious.  My favorite by far is the burekas with scrambled eggs.  The burekas are these little pastries filled with feta cheese, olives and other deliciousness.  I'm not a big fan of Israeli salad, but it's very fresh and my girlfriend is always happy to have my share.  The labneh cheese is my fav.  It's great to eat with anything, eggs, crispy dough, straight off the fork.  The crispy dough is the only thing that's been underwhelming - mostly it's just a bit oily for my taste. On my last visit I got a potato pancake as a side and it was great.  Very large, well seasoned, all around awesome. The price is pretty good considering all the egg dishes come with coffee.  Sometimes I'll get a mimosa, but this isn't a great place for drunk-brunch since most drinks are $8+ and there's no drink special. I could come here every weekend.

Risotteria is GREAT for gluten-free diners - the staff is very knowledgeable and the  menu is amazing.  The breadsticks are delicious, but I have been a little disappointed with the risotto (the star of the menu) the few times I've been there.  I keep expecting the risotto to be more flavorful, but it always end up being bland.  Also, the seating is very tight and you are practically sitting on top of the people at the table next to you.  Overall a great find for gf eaters though - I fully appreciate their efforts to make an allergen-friendly menu!

I'm sad that I just discovered Sanford's a few weeks before I move away from Astoria. It's my new favorite brunch spot, thanks to the décor, fast and friendly service, and their attention to detail. The chips that came with my fiancée's wrap were homemade from thick slices of potatoes. The wheat bread they served with my frittata was nutty and chock-full of whole grains. The cole slaw was very fresh and made with red cabbage. The main dishes were excellent as well. I had a Florentine frittata and she had a chicken and avocado wrap.

I was coming here with high expectations that I would be getting close to the best xiao long bao in the US.  I ended up very disappointed.   Their xia long bao may be very authentic, but if that is the case, I don't like authentic.  This place is worth trying out at least once, but I won't be back. I thought the dumplings had plenty of soup inside.  However, I thought the soup and meat filling were greasy and had too much fat.   The meat in the dumpling was also fatty enough and/or finely ground enough that I found the filling mushy.  I would prefer a thinner broth with a leaner meat filling. I came at 11AM which is right around opening time on a Saturday.   There was no wait at the time, but the place quickly filled up after and there is table sharing.
theres something about their pizza. I swear they put crack in the sauce or something.  its open until 4am added plus
Kyoto has Fresh Sushi that's nicely prepared by a pleasant staff.

Maharlika, wow, you're fancy. This is definitely not yo mama's (or your tita's, or your lola's) home cooking. For a girl used to seeing Filipino food at turo turo restaurants, potlucks, and meals prepared at home: Maharlika's dishes really made me look at my culture's cuisine differently. Surprisingly, the head chef is not Filipino, but a Dominican who has spent time in the Philippines. Chef Trinidad, I loved your interpretation of the dishes and you absolutely have my seal of approval! I went to dinner with a group of 8 people after making reservations. I was happily surprised how knowledgable our waitstaff was, despite not being Filipino. One waiter we had named Topher described himself as "Pinoy by tastebuds", classic! Our waitstaff was able to describe in detail the whole menu, and took care to explain foods such as the beloved Balut (haha!) to unusual condiments like Bagoong. Even though I was familiar with everything on the menu, I thought they all did a really thorough job explaining especially for those who aren't familiar with Filipino cuisine. For my meal, I had one of my tried and true all time favorite dishes, Kare Kare. I am typically used to having Kare Kare with a thicker consistency with the sauce (addition of crushed toasted rice and crushed peanuts), but I thought Chef Trinidad's interpretation was still damn good. The plating also looked gorgeous too, and that's something I thought I'd never say about Kare Kare! Chef Trinidad's version had a smoother sauce that had a great peanut flavor, accompanied by bok choy, eggplant, and three small, medium and large oxtails. It was extremely satisfying and I would order it again. Also, big ups to kalamansi water! That was my first time having kalamansi in a drink, and I actually think it is better than old fashioned lemonade. I know I have a lot of (non-vegetarian) friends out there that haven't tried Filipino food yet, and I would love to bring them all here for their first introduction. I don't advise vegetarians/vegans to come here. The only things on the menu that are veg friendly are veggie side dishes, and one dish (puqui puqui). Filipinos sure do love their meat! Maharlika is without a doubt one of my new favorite restaurants. I can't wait to try their brunch menu next.
Came here for dinner a few days ago.  We had the ramen and steamed bun.  The ramen is legit and the steamed bun is also legit.  The sauce on the steamed bun is Awesome!!!
Great food. Loud inside location but worth the noise. Visiting friends but difficult to have a conversation. Loved the salsa.
This pizza is the best! So yummy. I came here on a tuesday night with some friends and was so impressed with everything. I will definitely be a repeat customer.

This was my first meal my very first time in NYC. There was quite a bit of a wait for a Tuesday evening. I ordered the tagliatelle and my friend ordered the gnocchi. I've never tried gnocchi that was so large, puffy and... crunchy. But they were yummy, nonetheless. My tagliatelle was very rich and good. I also ordered a side of brussel sprouts which were cooked pretty well. I really wanted some salt but couldn't grab anyone's attention so gave up. Other than that, the staff was pretty friendly and it had a very cute interior.

Chain food? Yes.                  Ample seating? No GREAT HANGOVER FOOD! Since 1971, says the pic on the wall. Perfect NYU location for students on a budget. Can you really go wrong for $2.50 for a Falafel sammich? No. You get about 3 fried falafel (you can also order 3/$1) in your pita, topped with LT, tahini. Their falafel are very herby in flavor, which I like. Their Eggplant is nothing to scoff at either. Love the skin on that. Their hot sauce also has kick. It will trump any Vindaloo sauce. Not worth paying double for a platter. I'd rather have 2 sammiches. Must try the lamb schwarma next time. I haven't been to Taim's or Azuri Cafe yet, but this is up there w/ Alan's and Sam's. GO!

Best tiny Italian restaurant in NYC. I've been coming here for nearly 10 years and its still very very good. Ive taken countless friends here and now they come here too. Waitstaff is always the same so you see familiar faces. I can't speak for the pizza but you can't miss on the pasta. My personal favorite is the taglierini sorrento. It's buttery seafood goodness. My favorite pasta dish of all time.

I've tried to eat at this restaurant twice before but each time the servers would accommodate older people who would arrive after me, so both those times I just left and ate elsewhere.  Well, considering my boyfriend and I live around the corner from Dmitri's, and it is frequently a busy restaurant so we assumed it must be good, we gave it a third shot.  It was a rainy Thursday evening so we were promptly taken to be seated elbow to elbow with another table of two.  Considering there were other tables available, I requested a different table in which I waitress politely said she'd prepare.  When we were seated we received our water, had our bottle o' red uncorked and unpoured into small rimmed glasses that only allow you to take the smallest sips(I feel sorry for those with BIG noses!) and were verbally given the specials.  My boyfriend is hearing impaired, so he did need them to repeated, and considering it's such a loud atmosphere, they should offer the specials on paper.  Soon after we were brought some warm, grilled pita bread, which would have been tasty if it wasn't burnt on the grill, accompanied with a low quality olive oil, red wine vinegar and some herb which did nothing for the tasteless dip.  There was also some bread in the basket so I asked if they had butter, and they said they had no butter.  Okay, fine.  We ordered our appetizers, shrimp scampi and steamed mussels.  The shrimp was very fresh, yet the dish very salty.  The mussels were served in a SOUP of bland garlic broth, topped with giant slices of tomato, spinach, green pepper and onion.  Interesting to say the least.  I thought maybe music could tone down the loud atmosphere, and when I requested some be put on, I was told there was music on but the noise inside exceeded it.  There wasn't any on though because we were seated below a speaker, and would have heard atleast a faint sound at any more silent moments.  Finally we get our entrees, Fried Flounder and a Mediterranean whole white fish, which came filleted as a requested, both served with sauteed spinach and yellow rice.  The flounder was very fresh, but like our other dishes, bland.  However, my white fish was incredible.  A very rich, savory, melt-in-your-mouth goodness.  My white fish aside, the service, portions, food, prices were just good.  It's too loud, small, and nothing on the wall that is appeasing to eye. I think next time I want some fresh fish at a BYO, I'll head a few blocks down and try to get a table at Little Fish.  Mmmmm.

I've been visiting this new establishment twice, both times i walked out with satisfaction. I liked the black milk bubble tea, the bubbles were cooked in perfection and the tea was perfectly flavored. Their mango smoothie was yummy too. Btw, i also tried their fried chicken wings, very tasty and crunchy.  They sell ice cream, noodle soup, and breakfast. I'll definitely come back and give each of them of try. thumbs up:)

Don't get me wrong the food is good. But every time I would like to order something seems like they're closing early. I think they're going to go out of business. Every time I walk in there there's never anyone there except at the bar

While a blizzard hits brooklyn, I think everyone agrees it feels good to stay in warm and cozy and have someone else cook for you :-). I decided to order in sushi at a reasonable price. This was the quickest delivery service I've had in Brooklyn thus far. My sushi was here within 20-25 mins DURING the blizzard. They have a good variety of reasonably priced platters and sushi is pretty good. In $22, I had miso soup, beef broccoli appetizer, 20 sushi rolls, delivered fresh/quick to my door again DURING the blizzard!!!! This place is pretty cool. Try it.

Never disappointing.  Never surprising.  A bunch of creative above average rolls.  Hibachi s average.  Chicken and steak are good.  Shrimp was very good.  Salmon was not good.  Service is above average.

My husband and I attended UPenn almost 10 yrs ago and heard many good things about this place then. We've continued to hear raves over the years so when the UC Dining Days promotion came up, we decided to finally try dinner. The restaurant was easy to find and it was easy to park. It is converted West Philly row home, which I found charming. It reminded me of college.  We were seated at a table for two and we were very close to the patrons sinking next to us.   We were given the promotional menu and the standard menu. The promotional menu was a bit disappointing as it had two appetizers, two entrees, and one dessert. If you take into consideration that their standard menu is pretty small, I guess it was not that bad selection. While the options on the promotional menu were not bad, they were not the most appealing to us. We ordered the heirloom salad and mac and cheese appetizers. The salad was very disappointing. When I imagine heirloom tomatoes, I picture colorful big tomatoes. The salad was served with two tiny tomatoes, two mozzarella balls, two little balls of watermelon, and something else. The mac and cheese was rich, so a small portion was perfect.  For entrees, we ordered the salmon and scallops. I don't care for salmon, but their vegetarian was not appealing (a dish of various mushrooms). I really liked my salmon. For dessert, we ordered the lemon curd and chocolate ganache. Both were good. I don't know if I would return here because it is not in our neighborhood, but it was good for a night out.

My boyfriend brought me here for my birthday and it was quite possibly the best meal I have ever had.  The produce (especially the beets) was incredibly fresh and flavorful.  The seafood was outstanding.  I had the scallops with lemon juice and peppercorns to start and they just about melted in my mouth.  For my main course I had the arctic char in a carrot and basil sauce- the sauce was intensely flavorful but did not mask the fish.  My boyfriend had the Chilean sea bass and it was an outstanding blend of delicate flavors- perfectly balanced.  Some reviewers have complained about the lighting but I thought it was perfect for a date.  Oh, and how could I forget dessert!  Their homemade sundae with salted caramel ice cream is a must-try.  It is topped with caramel popcorn which sounds strange but definitely works.

Just got back from my first trip to Ippudo (Monday, December 28th), and had what potentially could have been a very good meal ruined by some awful service, not from the waitress, but more from the manager and the host/hostesses that ran the seating arrangements.  I really hate when I lose my appetite even before I've been seated.  The ramen was solid-- had the "modern" ramen and probably would have enjoyed the food if I hadn't been owned multiple times in one meal.   Probably would have given it 4 stars, although, I've had better (Daikokuya out in LA).   My problems with the service/ management: 1.  Put ours names down at 6:30pm and did not get seated until 9:30pm for a party of 5.  At 6:30, we were told that it would be 2 hours max.  At 8:30, we were told that it would be no more than 40 minutes, but likely about 20 minutes.  It was not until 9:15 where we had 3 different people from our party ask about our table that the manager decided to do something.  Their solution was simple (which I suggested, might I add)-- put the 5 of us at a table for 4, which ended up being fine.  This problem could have been solved hours ago, as we saw parties of 4 who came in 1.5-2 hours after us get seated before we did. 2.  After squeezing us at a table for 4, would not let an additional 6th person join our table, even though there would have been more than enough space for that.  The manager basically told us that one person in our party had to leave, or else the 6th person would have had to just wait all over again.  Ridiculous.  Even the waitress thought this was the most absurd thing ever, and apologized on her manager's behalf.  It's really disappointing to find this type of management at a restaurant that serves high priced ramen, but I would get better service eating in a mall food court than at Ippudo.   I will not come back here again, unless the management decides to invite me back and do things correctly.  It is not waiting 3 hours that bothers me-- it is being disrespected time and time again at a restaurant that is at a price point where I don't have to deal with these shenanigans. Do they have an e-mail or person I can speak to about the service I received? PS:  You can't take out or bring left overs home.  Talk about wasting food, what a joke.

I will give this place 5 stars bc I think overall its an awesome place. I will start with telling you that its always packed with a nice older crowd. BYOB!!! have been there several times and have always enjoyed myself. The food I give a 4 out of 5 stars. They have some great appitizers and its not too pricey. Nice atomosphere. I have always gone for dinner so has always been really busy about 30-45 min wait. They dont make reservations. Nice place to take your friends and family or your date. Not very kid friendly.

i ended up on her on accident. i promise, it wasnt the 1300+ reviews. while wandering around downtown, i was looking for something quick and cheap to eat so i logged on to my trusty yelp app, searched nearby and this gem appeared. of course, the reviews helped but the sheer fact it was 2 blocks away made it an easy decision. when i got there, the line was about 30 deep. "hyped" was my first impression, but was willing to wait and check it out. i ordered the mixed meat over rice bowl and this thing was HUGE. and only 6$! the meat was seasoned perfectly, i ordered extra sauce (copied the guy in front of me, ha) and it hit the spot. i walked it to times square where they  were filming a cooking show and enjoyed my meal. i even had leftovers that i ate right before dinner and was good as ever. 5 stars for these guys, sooooooo gooood.

At this moment, Totto ramen is the best ramen in the U.S., I think. but they used to be better!  Actually the first time when I went to this place with my friend(she told me totto ramen is good) I was so happy and excited! Because, imagine! you can eat great ramen in the place where I live! it couldn't be better in my ramen life. First few times were very good overall, I tried few kind of ramen and found out Miso is the best(I do not recommend other kind), then I've keep ordering Miso ramen. However..., I don't remember exactly when, but Miso ramen taste getting worse(but still #1 in NYC), inverse proportionally, the line getting longer and longer. Everyone! just let me tell you something. Coolest style at ramen place is just order, eat asap because you should eat before the noodle absorb soup and gets dull! don't chatting so much, then pay and leave.  This is the manner at ramen place just like you hold your fork in your left hand and knife in right hand:) I understand some ppl will think we are not in our country so do not force you to do our custom but I think this will make less/shorter line. 2hrs standing and waiting in NYC cold weather is not worth for $10 ramen....

I came in here on a Tuesday evening for a quick drink with some friends for the first time and it was fun. Its a little dive bar right off of Bedford with very cheap drinks and nice bartenders. They have Lone Star beer and a shot of tequila for $5 and Budweiser and a shot of Jager for $5 as well. Most bars I've been to charge $6 minimum for a Jager shot alone so that deal can't be beat. I'm also pretty sure they had Black Label beer and a whiskey shot for $4. I love the shot and a beer drinking technique so I'll be coming back.

I've been waiting for a long time to try this restaurant and it lived up to my high expectations. The restaurant was decorated beautifully and my friends were all in admiration. They also had a great playlist going which set a fun, upbeat ambiance. The hostess sat us at a round table for our party of 6 which let us converse easily. For appetizers, we shared the crab toast, avocado and carrot salad and glazed doughnuts. One friend emitted a loud "oh my god!" after biting into the crab toast. It was as good as I heard it was. I was also impressed by the carrots which were so much tastier than I thought possible. I enjoyed the lemon doughnut as well. I ordered the burger (Michelle Obama got this when she came to the restaurant). I liked that it wasn't ginormous like so many burgers in NY. The herbed mayo and pickled jalapenos really made this burger unique and delicious. My friend got the spinach and goat cheese omelette which she didn't like because the omelette was all egg yolk. It gave the omelette a strange consistency and taste that she wasn't used to. Everyone else liked their dishes though. Service was spectacular and our waitress was sweet and attentive. I'll definitely come here again if I can snag another reservation. Also for parties of more than 4, they require a credit card and it's $45 pp if you are a no-show.
This place is terrible.  Really.  Stay away. ...still here, huh?  This is why I have to wait in line for 20 minutes to get their cheap, amazing sesame pancakes!  Damn you, Yelp!

5 stars means a place should be (one of) the best of the best in its category. Far too frequently, I find Yelpers overly generous with their ratings; for the record, this is my second 5 star review (and I think I'm going to downgrade my other 5 star review)! Having read all the press and hype about Di Fara, my expectations were raised to super high levels. I prepared myself for disappointment - after all, how can any restaurant live up to this much anticipation? The wait was as hideous as advertised; my friends and I were third in line (before opening) Sunday afternoon, and it still took over an hour to get our pizza! Tons of restaurants talk about "beauty in simplicity" and letting "ingredients talk for themselves" - precious few manage to execute that well. Di Fara was a mind-blowing experience for me; up until that point, I never realized pizza could be that good! I've had pizzas with traditional, top-notch, imported produce and all that jazz... but none of them come close to the magic of Di Fara! I wish I could pinpoint what made this pizza so great - the fresh cheese, basil, dough, or generous pour (this isn't diet food, folks) of olive oil - but I'll leave that to the folks with the better palette. All I know is: it works, and works great! Back to the point of simple ingredients: I enjoyed the plain Sicilian (square pizza with thicker crust) much more than the Sicilian with sausage. So if you're not sure what to order, just stick to the plain.

The food was pretty good. Great fries. Excellent ketchup. But... "The Jankelowitzes always worked front of the house," (from NY Mag review). I would be surprised if the manager I spoke to was family, so utterly uninterested was he in my request/reminder that sugar be served with espresso when it's set on the table. I waited several minutes, as my espresso cooled, trying to get the attention of the waitress who ignored us and who had been fairly unhelpful all evening (when we asked for descriptions of a couple of items on the menu, her response was curt: when my husband paused for a moment to consider his order, she tapped her order pad like a diner waitress over loaded with customers-the place was less than half full at the time; later, when I asked for a spoon for the broth with the mussels, she brought a teaspoon!?!?) So, when the espresso was served without a side of sugar, I thought who trained her? Soon after, a mention to the manager that the waitress should have brought sugar along with the espresso illicited from him a blank look of "I don't understand you." I asked what language we were all speaking, although I'm quite sure everyone was American. When the fresh espresso was served, it came with sugar and without apologies. The unpleasant attitude of the waitress and the dismissal by the apathetic manager certainly make me not care about going back to or recommending this (my) neighborhood restaurant. There are so many other places with good fries to choose.

First things first - let me clarify that this review is of the "Valentine's Day" prix fixe only.  That being said, a few observations:   1.  We are new to the area, so I searched on open table for Saturday night availability when my wife and I were fortunate enough - first time in six months - to have someone to watch our two wee ones at home.  I happened upon the Peacock Inn, found a reservation at a normal dinner time - 8:00 p.m. - and booked a day ahead of when we planned to dine.  I didn't think much of the request for credit card information (big mistake) at the time.   2.  Receive my confirmation email with the fine print that a $95 charge per person would be levied if the reservation was cancelled within 72 hours.  Given that I made the reservation the day before we were planning to eat at the Peacock Inn, it seemed that we were most likely on the hook for the prix fixe.  (Admittedly, I probably could have cancelled had I called the restaurant immediately, but given the relatively good reviews and babysitter availability, I figured we would splurge.  Plus, places like Agricola and Mistral that we really wanted to try did not have reservations available.) 3.  A small aside, but since when is Valentine's Day an entire weekend?  I understand using Valentine's Day itself to hike up prices and force a prix fixe on dining patrons, but an entire weekend?  But I digress... 4.  As for the actual dining experience?  Without a doubt, bar none, the best part of our entire meal was the pre-dinner cocktail from the bar.  Peacock Inn's barman is a regular mixologist.  Incredible martinis with particular high marks for the olives stuffed with bleu d'auvergne.  Our first two courses were nice with items featuring can't miss favorites such as foie gras and sea scallops.  Then came the main course.  Now, I understand portions may be a little smaller in a prix fixe.  That being said, the butter poached lobster "entree" - a 40+ dollar item on the regular a la carte menu - was literally 1/4 tail and a claw of what I would estimate to be a one pound lobster.  In all seriousness, it took two bites to eat my entire main course.  Thankfully, I had a short drive home to get something else to eat.   5.  Conclusion?  Both my wife and I have lived in "big" cities for extended periods - New York, DC, Philly - and have eaten some pretty expensive meals.  Not that the previous sentence makes us experts, but I can't say we've ever left a more expensive meal less satisfied than leaving the Peacock Inn.  I really don't mind paying $95 a head for a tasting menu or a prix fixe - there are some incredible restaurants that serve seven courses for that price - but a nearly $400 dinner tab with drinks shouldn't leave a diner to satisfy his or her hunger with whatever snacks are left over at home.  While what we did eat was satisfactory, the value was below par.  Ergo, a "meh" rating from this Peacock Inn diner.

It is a uniquely British thing (and perhaps German) that kebabs and Gyros are eaten from a greasy takeaway. The Canal Street Grill in Yardley, Pennsylvania proves that this isn't so. Located on a little side road near the canal (not surprisingly), this family run restaurant is casual, bright and cheery. You find a mixture of families, small groups and couples in here. Whilst the restaurant doesn't have a liquor licence you can bring your own wine (BYOB) - they'll give you glasses and open the wine for you without paying corkage. The food is Greek/American themed, by and large, though they do have some salads clearly influenced by oriental cuisine. You can order salad platters, where you can choose a selection. Many main courses offer the choice of a Greek Salad - this comes recommended, They also have burgers, buffalo wings and a handful of Greek and American/Italian influenced main courses, but The Canal Street Grill is justifiably famous for its Gyros (the Greek/American name, I suspect, for our Donar Kebab). You have a choice of lamb, chicken or steak (none of it carved from what looks like a giant leg). These are delicious. Fries and a Greek salad are offered along with the Giros, and the portions are enormous. You'll certainly not go hungry. Prices are reasonable - a giant Gyro will cost you just short of $10 - a side order of fries and Greek salad adds only another $2.00. You'll pay around $20 for the most expensive item on the menu - and most are far cheaper. They also have a lunchtime and a children's menu. This is a lovely little family restaurant. Tucked away down a little side street, it would be easy to miss. That would be a shame. There is a small car park, and they take Visa or cash. Enjoy.

What a great place. We are so fortunate to have a variety of food in this city, and Nam Phuong is one of the great treasures in that category. The menu is extensive so we were able to take clients there knowing we could all find something we would like.  The service was quick and easy. The waiter was knowledgeable and helpful. Parking is tight but we borrowed a spot from a close business nearby.   If you want good vietnamese food or if you want to learn more about vietnamese food, this is a good place to go.
Love this place! Hatville is our go to for corned beef special.

After trekking through the Museum of Natural History my crew was starving. The food court was jammed, so we left to see what was available. Glad we did, because we had a much better meal here than we would have otherwise. The food was delicious, but just a little too salty for me. This would have been a four star review, except for one thing. When we went to be seated, we were told there was a half hour wait unless we wanted to be seated outside. It was chilly out, but they assured us we would be fine because we would be seated near the heaters. Um...no. We tried, but eventually had to ask the waiter if we could be moved inside because it was just too cold. The waiter, and the rest of the staff were wonderful and got us inside ASAP.

The Bar Room is a great experience before you even sit down. As you walk in, the room has been made to look at least twice its size by cleverly placed mirrors and lighting fixtures. Just below the ceiling level, there is a beautiful mural that reflects throughout the eating area. The food did not disappoint either. I went there for brunch and had their Garden Omelette, which was incredibly fresh and filling. My friend had the Bar Room Benedict and was also singing praises afterwards. The service was friendly and efficient, and the prices were very reasonable. I haven't tried any of their drinks yet, but will definitely be going back to try out some of their cocktails and to soak up the atmosphere again. I highly recommend The Bar Room to anyone who wants to eat at a classy place without hurting your wallet.

I've been here a dozen or so times for lunch, brunch, and dinner and every time has been solid. Great food, nice service, atmosphere conducive to speaking and a good catch-up.  Perfect place in particular for a girl's lunch, casual lunch, or glass of wine with pasta at the bar.
Food is amazing and service is outstanding ! If you visit this restaurant, make sure you have coffee and pandebonos !
everything was good - ceviche mixto, chicken, empanadas, etc.. the place is pretty loud but bearable

Chicken tikki, curry fish, and egg masala is what we ordered. With only one family in the place we thought that the food would not take as long as it did. It came out hot and spicy. Emphasis on spicy!!! Worth the wait? Hmmm... See I really love the cuisine. Was it the best I ever had? No. Will is satisfy my craving? For now. We commenced to eating our food and the place filled up. Not a seat open in the house. This was good right? Wrong answer. Nope. This meant that he although a very nice person, was serving ALL of those people TOO!!!! We waited 15 minutes to pay get the bill and another 10 to get my card back.  Will it be the first place I think of the next time? Nope. You can read my other reviews to know where I will go from now on. I felt like I cheated on them with a cheap flusy. A moment that I would like to take back.

Popped in for happy hour before a concert, ended up staying for food as well.  Happy hour is well worth it up at the bar, definitely take advantage of it!  We were able to enjoy our wine and small plates at a leisurely pace which was great.  We ordered in stages to gauge our hunger. Their food can be a bit pricey.  The Duck Ham Panini was well worth the price and I highly recommend it but the Veal Meatballs were no where near worth their price (they were just okay). They have a great selection of wines and I look forward to returning for another visit.

I did lunch with a friend at the new incarnation of Shinju that is Fat Salmon yesterday, and was impressed with how this restaurant has grown.  It is a true testament to the management and excellent food to be so successful with a small establishment in the current economy.  The head chef, menu and much of the staff remain largely identical to Shinju.  It seems like more specialty rolls appear on the new menu, but my old favorites were there as well.  They have increased their prices slightly, but not as much as I feared when I first heard about the move. Our meal consisted of naked gyoza with spicy tuna, sleeping volcano and rolling fire rolls, and a few pieces of nigiri and sashimi.  The food was all excellent.  I am impressed when a sushi place not only offers brown rice as an option, but gets the texture right to work perfectly in sushi. I am surprised to read complaints about the service.  I have always found them to be friendly and efficient.  Sometimes the food takes a little while, but when it arrives, the complexity of the preparation and presentation makes it obvious why.  This is not a restaurant for hurrying. The decor is a complete turnaround from the humble dark wood that I so loved at Shinju.  The new space is much more sleek and fancy, typical of what you would expect from a high-end sushi restaurant.  This, combined with the liquor license application in the window, makes me believe that high-end sushi restaurant is where they are headed.  This is not a bad thing in itself, but the city already has a couple of those.  I will probably always feel a little nostalgic for the tiny, unassuming neighborhood  place that you would hardly even notice walking by.

Made a reservation here for my birthday brunch on a gorgeous Sunday in May (customer service over the phone was great).  Food was delicious, with bottomless mimosas, sangria, and maybe  one other option for $20. Side note - it seems they might be phasing out the bottomless drinks :( so check before you go if that's an essential part of your brunch experience.  The food really is fantastic though. The space is not necessarily small, but not large, and accommodates a decent amount of people.

Better Bites For Reeeeaaal! Hallelujah for Better Bites and healthy eating in Downtown Newark! Better Bites sets the bar high for healthy eating in Newark, let alone healthy eating in the USA! The food is fresh, healthy, delicious and fills ya' up! What I Love: -A small salad will fill you up and then some! And you can feel good about eating any of their salads. For example, a small Salmon Salad is only 354 calories and contains 40 + g of protein! Better Bites manages to add the perfect amount of dressing to give that baby flavor without making the salad soggy! -The store is clean, pleasing to the eye, cute, well organized and bright inside -The food is fresh and you can definitely tell! -The Smashed Sweet Potatoes are "the bomb"! For only $2.49 you get just the right amount in terms of portion size. They are absolutely scrumptious with a side of amazing! -Friendly Staff (but not overly-friendly) who knows what they're doing! -Turkey Bacon, Brown Rice, Whole Wheat, Bison and low fat Cheese  available. -The proteins are cooked well! Not dry, not over/ under cooked and seasoned appropriately. -Nutritional Information Provided -$10 Minimum for all credit/ debit transactions -Unfortunately, truly healthy food is typically more expensive no matter where you go! Based on the taste, flavor and quality of the food, I personally believe that everything on the menu is priced appropriately.

4 starts for that yummy square slice. 5 for the atmosphere. Seriously, a place like this reminds me of why I love living in Brooklyn. A 20 minute train takes to you to a completely different world.  To Jersey. But in Brooklyn

The reason that I gave only two stars is mainly due to the awful service.  The food should get 3.5-4 stars.   We were two large parties next to each other on a weekday afternoon for lunch.  The first offense happened when the food runner/server spilled hot oil from a pasta dish all over the legs, iPad and phone of someone in our party.  He did not even apologize and no one came out to remedy the situation.  After the incident, the server barely came to check on us.  We sat there for a very long time with empty plates until someone finally came by about an hour to check on us, in the meantime, the bus boy was clearing our table and took away a glass of wine right from under my nose that I was not finished drinking.   After we left the restaurant, the other party we were with was just finishing up eating and overheard the waiter complaining that he got a crappy tip.  Bad service = crappy tip.  Better training needs to be implemented in this establishment. We will not be back!

Food was delicious and the service was good.  I went with a party of six. on a Wednesday night, to celebrate one of our colleagues. Everybody liked their food and the waitress was kind and attentive enough.  We all cleaned our plates. The atmosphere is pretty cool too. It's nice to go to a restaurant in a neighborhood where it is easy to find parking. I'm really surprised by some of the other reviews that have slammed this restaurant.

Delicious margaritas! Giant empanadas. If you get the empanada sampler, hope you have a party to share it or you may not have room for their giant entrees. I got the yellow arepa with morcilla (blood sausage.) It was just okay...Morcilla was a tad dry and it was really nothing special. However, I drooled over my boyfriend's meat platter! It was delicious. Even the rice was impressive. Great place for brunch. The restaurant has a decent amount of seats. Luckily there was no wait.

I took my son to dinner for his birthday. The service was great we sat outside on a nice Friday night in Philly. The beer menu was unbelievable and our server was great with suggestions. The meal was good too, mussels and burgers were delicious. Good pub food, not a place to expect a great steak. The fire pits add atmosphere and took the chill out of the air. Definitely going back there!

Lupa has recently become one of my go-to restaurants in the West Village. It serves fine dining food but the atmosphere is not pretentious.  The service is always considerate and attentive.  This week my husband and I braved the cold weather and went in for dinner around 8:30PM, we called 20 minutes ahead and requested seats at the bar.  We only waited for a short time for our seats.  While we waited, the general manager gave us some glasses of nice Barolo.   We ordered beets with straciatella, gnocchi with sausage and fennel, spaghetti carbonara, and the chef sent out a barley salad of some sort.  We ended with a chef's selection of sorbets and gelato the star was the pumpkin spice gelato.  It was awesome! Overall, we had great food with solid service in a welcoming atmosphere.   The music is also awesome!
Best Pizza Ever!

Had dinner with a couple friends here and it was pretty good. We ordered the new york strip, a fish plate, brussel sprouts and broccoli raab. Overall good food, good service and great environment. I think Carroll Place is solid and great for happy hours. Dinner was okay but the happy hour energy of the first floor was the main draw in my opinion.

I love the décor here; country home atmosphere with wooden furniture and animals and paintings on the walls.  The cuisine is American and I recommend the chicken and creamed spinach.  ARTICHOKE DIP.  Its crispy and cheesy on top and it is delicious! But other than that, the food was so-so.  The menu is typical farm to table type food and the prices are pretty reasonable.   The drinks are a great here though.  Red snapper!

Everything here is delicious from the jamon iberico to their fine selection of meats and cheeses. It's like foodie heaven. Recently I had a lunch here of the despana sandwich and the churros y chocolate. Perfect. Not much seating but it's not designed to be a restaurant.

So this review will be brief, as my usual overly wordy reviews are usually about food and I've only eaten the food here once.  I have been here a number of times for drinks because it's a popular destination when you're looking for an outdoor boozing area in downtown New Haven.  And those of you who live down here know that chill outdoor loitering areas are hard to come by!   My issue with Geronimo's isn't so much the setting or ambiance, because the covered large patio holds a lot of people without ever feeling overly crowded and the heat lamps even make hanging out there enjoyable when it's brisk out.  It's more that everything here, from the food to the booze, has that downtown New Haven premium in terms of price.  They are very stingy with their pours of alcohol, which is a big pet peeve for me.  I understand the logic in trying to maximize your profit per pour, but a nice pour is what keeps me coming back for more, which equates to me spending more money in the long run.  Our first and only meal here was just too expensive for the sub par quality of the food that was served. Sure this is a solid place to grab an expensive weak drink and enjoy the airy, outdoor atmosphere, but I never really find myself staying here long and it's usually just a pit stop for those out and about downtown Havey nights.
Food was okay but way over priced. Service was slow. We went here for my bday only because the original restaurant I wanted to go to was closed. Definitely a waste of time and money.

This is as quintessential New York pre-theater dining as it gets. Dark, cozy, exposed brick, tasty but not-too-adventurous menu, waiters who are actors-between-gigs... it could be awful, but in this case it's a winning combination. I've lived here 8 years and generally hate all Theater District dining, but this was lovely.

Tried their carne asada with guacamole. I expected this place to be better than if not at par with Chipotle, but this place was just okay. The steak wasn't marinated as well, and the taco wrap is just like any other. Although the steak is pretty fresh, and I would actually come back to try their other meats.

Geez I used to go there since 2007 ! They changed management and chief around 2012 or so . that chief does not know how to season SPICE right. If anything says spicy It just every thing turn to be overly spicy and killed the harmony of other ingredient. I used to love the spicy creamy tomato sauce on eggs on brunch. little bread to come with was also cute and good, it was very delicious. now it turn to be overly spiced watery(not creamy ! )oily sauce. bread was something I don't care regular bread. ALSO I got the mussle dish at dinner, it did not mention about any spice (it said white wine or something) then that was very very spicy. I like spicy food but not some chillie pepper dumped in exsessive amount into dish. Horrible , horrible.   Whoever turn this place to this condition has bad taste on their mouth. I m sad that they lost stable good taste they used had.

My family and I eat here frequently, and I thought that it is about time that I write a review. We really love this place - the food, the people and the place. We have never had anything that wasn't good, and not infrequently have dishes that are exceptional. I am a Caesar Salad lover, and Pulcinella's version is my absolute favorite. The pizza is wonderful, and compares favorably with what I had when I worked in Milan, Italy. I don't order many entrees myself, but other folks that I dine with do, and they are always satisfied and often enthusastic. Finally, the desserts are great and it is always exciting to try the new offerings. Handicap access is top-notch, which is important to us. We often eat here before concerts at the Flynn, as we can get in and out without any hassle. The bottom line - we love Pulcinella's!

I love Pio Pio.  Seriously, this my favorite takeout in the entire city.  Bad day?  Chicken and a pint of green sauce.  Good day? Chicken and a pint of green sauce.  Yep, that's all I need.  I've gotten takeout multiple times from here and also dined in.  The dining in experience wasn't optimal--it's super crowded, the wait was long (and the hostess lied multiple times about the wait time), but the drinks are good so that helped.   In summation: Get a rotisserie chicken, a pint of green sauce, rice and beans.  That's all.  You won't be sorry. GREEN SAUCE IS AMAAAAAZZZINNNGGG.
Good guac and tequila drinks. Pro tip: don't do what my friends did and get kicked out for bringing a sixer of Coors Light in here.
Simple but very good. They run with the idea of doing just one thing but doing it well. Very reasonable prices for good sliders and a cool atmosphere.

Another place in Princeton that would go out of business immediately in any other town. Mediocre sashimi and sushi - nothing horrible, but the service and decor is "college town" quality and the prices are "nice restaurant". There was literally nothing memorable about the meal except the foolish "rules", which were off-putting. If you're that cranky, start a business that doesn't serve people. In summation: Eh.

I love tapas. I love that my taste bud can go through so many experiences in one sitting. Amada is a great place to go for tapas because they are so accommodating. My bf and I got a free dish on the house. We also got out plate of olives for free because it came out late. Lots of complimentary dishes. Go and have an adventure with your palate.
I love the small plates here enough to give a full five-star update. You can't be disappointed here.

I'm a huge sushi fan and on my recent trip to NYC I wanted to find some good sushi. I searched for sushi places and decided to give this one a shot. I was so impressed! Great atmosphere and great food! The prices cannot be beat. My boyfriend and I got three rolls and he got a beer and the bill was $25! $25!! Best deal in the city!

Had their top of the menu item, called Sweetness. Tasty, but come on, how can melted cheesed between two greasy slices of bread not be? I could have made this sandwich and I can't cook. So I think the ratings for this place are inflated. They reflect the awesomeness of grilled cheese, not the awesomeness of Melt Shop. There are grilled cheese places deserving 4 or 5 stars. Queens Kickshaw in Astoria, for one.
Omfg best halal food ever, hands down, game over. Yes, I know the line is long. Suck it up and get in line. You'll be glad you did.

I was surprised to see how small this place was. There are lots of 2 tops that are basically right on top of each other. For the location and portions, the prices are amazing. The food is delicious as well. I ordered the brie as a appetizer and the salmon as my entree. Both portions were much larger than anticipated. The brie had honey which i originally thought was weird but it is actually really good. Everything except for the actually size of the restaurant was good. It's hard to actually enjoy your meal with people bumping into your table constantly.

This bar/restaurant gets 5 stars from me because they are: 1. attentive 2. food is delicious 3. prices are reasonable 4. tvs everywhere 5. cocktails strong I love their truffle fries, they are cooked to perfection. When I visit other restaurants, I order a side of fries with each meal and nobody has come close to how they fry their fries. Kudos Station House, you have the best fries in the city. Yes, better than Pom Frites. But, what do I know, try it for yourself. Also, for a bar/restaurant, I was delightfully surprised on how good their steak and fried chicken were. Great job guys!

Sloww service!  I sat there with my family for 15 min waiting for someone, anyone to come by to take my drink order.  I started to get antsy and my left leg started to twitch, my eyes got blurry! I needed alcohol...   I didn't know who my waiter was so  I wave the bus boy down to get our waiter ...Unfortunately even after knowing who our waiter was he wasn't seen very much, I had to ask other employees to find my waiter for me.  To his defense (he was actually a nice guy) I believe he was taking on a full job as the maitre d' too, but facts are facts....the service sucked. Shishito peppers too much yuzu salt, too salty.   The pork belly buns , the meat was tender but the sauce was a tad too sweet.   I ordered some cooked rolls the lobster tempura roll and the fois gra roll was pretty good.  Ramen was small and decent in flavor, $12 for noodles and soup  no meat and to add meat it's + $4 making it $16 big smacaroos for 1 regular bowl of noodles.. that's  pricy on the pricey side. All in all the service and the price for the noodles are turn offs for me, I don't see myself making any special trips here, but if I were desperate and in the area maybe....
Soco is so good! Best chicken n waffles :) yum

It was a frigid day and I was visiting from a sunnier place. I special-ordered a spicy tuna don, and it was amazing: gorgeous, and a perfect play of sweetness, crunch and spice. Also, excellent jasmine tea and very speedy service. I'll be returning.

After reading mixed reviews, I'll give it a mixed review. Some things were outstanding, some weren't. The roast pork Banh Hoi was truly good and almost up to Hanoi standards. The Banh Xeo (pancake) was only ok. We also had a special that was pretty good, but the lemon grass chicken was disappointing. I'd definitely go back, but I'll have to start working on what the right things to order are.

I randomly came here with my brother and friend for brunch today and was pleasantly surprised.  I don't normally equate Mexican places with quality brunch but this place proved worth it. It was a warm but sunny day so we snagged a great table in the shade. For "El Almuerzo" I tried out the Ofrenda Omelet.  It consisted of mushrooms, green peas, onions, Chihuahua cheese, salsa roja, avocado and home fries. What a delightful combination, especially the cheese which was grated onto the home fries as well. My friend and brother also enjoyed their selections and we all agreed that we would like to come back here to try  "La Cena." Thumbs up for the service as well.

Had sunday brunch here with my linesisters. was really good. I got the Silk Breakfast Sandwich. It came with home fries. Very yummy not too heavy. The Silk Cakes are really good. My sister loved the wings she got. I will definitely be back for brunch and to party :)
not worth the hype...

The art deco decor is beautiful, cocktails were wonderful and well made, and I love the backyard patio. Most of the staff members were courteous and friendly, all except the server who was incredibly rude to me for no apparent reason. I sat with a few of my friends in the backyard patio, enjoying a pleasant conversation over a few drinks, our server came over and greeted everyone except me and proceeded to take everyone's order except mine. I had to stop her from leaving my table, without taking my order over three times!  Now, I don't know what I did to make this women behave in such a manner, but I felt completely alienated by this person. I am not one to claim racism, but I was the only one in my group, who wasn't of a light skin complexion, and was treated differently without uttering a word --  I call that racism. I didn't move to Bushwick to face any sort of racism or classism, if I wanted to deal with the latter I'd move to Manhattan. That being said, I will not let one person at an establishment take away from all of the the good that a staff has done. I will continue going to this bar, like I have for the past 4-odd years that I've been here. Now, if I have to deal with this same ignorant behavior, I experienced with this particular person -- I will personally name them on my updated post. Hopefully, that won't be the case.

One of my favorite spots. I cannot pick one dish to recommend, it would be an insult to all the others! With an array of dishes the menu will make you dizzy. I order something new every time!
