Best of all is the price...very inexpensive for the amount of food you get. You will definitely want to go back again and again! Enjoy!

I love Ellary's Greens.  There is something here for everyone (organic meat/ fish or tons of yummy veg options).  I love to try a lot of things on any menu and like to have veggies as the majority of my meal so the having the option to build a meal from several smaller veggies dishes is very exciting.  The veggie dishes are creative but still simple.  The beets with pistachio coulis dish is probably my favorite.  The tuscan kale salad is also delish. The vibe is casual but the decor (mainly, the gorgeous green-leaf ceiling- which I want in my apt) gives it a fresh and whimsical feel.  It's romantic and grounding at the same time.  It's even more lovely at lunch when the sun pours in through the huge glass windows.  Perfect place to go on a beautiful day when you want to eat healthy AND feel treated. The waiters are friendly and the service is great.  I went with a friend and the server brought us a yummy chocolate chip cookie after our meal.  Oh, and, you can get a any of the sandwiches on a gluten free wrap!  AND there's an organic juice bar!!  My favorite juice is the Beauty- cucumber, aloe vera juice, and mint- so refreshing. It's safe to say I am a huge fan of this wonderful restaurant.

We went to this place over the weekend and ordered a rack of ribs, brisket and devil eggs.  The devil eggs and the brisket were good but the ribs were a little dry.  I was disappointed with the ribs as I did have high expectations after reading all the reviews but I have to say that the customer service was good.  I am not sure, if I will come back here again. Mei

We had a delicious brunch there! The pastrami hash is wonderful and plenty filling for two to share. The wait staff is delightful and kind. The only reason I'm giving a 4 star is that we look forward to returning and having an even more delicious meal
Great food, fast service(usually) and has a nice view. There is outside seating, perfect for the summer.

Dinner last weekend. Service was friendly but uneven. Two entrees came out a full 10 minutes before remaining two did. Appetizers and entrees were so over salted, they bordered on inedible. My lambchop was fatty and undercooked, and vegetables that accompanied the meat were also so salty!  Swordfish was blah. Gave one star for dessert. Baklavah was excellent. wanted to like this place, but won't go back.

Love. Maybe I'm just starved for good brunch places over in the 'burbs (NJ), but Petite Abeille embodies everything I love about brunch. 1. Delicious food. Waffle with mango, berries, and REAL strawberry sauce. Smoked salmon sandwich with egg salad and DILL! Lovely extra touch to help my love affair with dill. And fresh fruit. 2. Cozy decor: natural lighting, antique suitcases and bare bulbs. Transports me out of the crazy busy city and into a tranquil space (except it's still super crowded). 3. Friendly service (though a little slow at times). Cons: crowded and a tad pricey, but hey - this is NYC.

Why visit? Amazing brunch, Outdoor seating This is one of the first places I visited for a New York style brunch. The brunch here is just simply delicious and the restaurant itself is quite a cute one. It's a good place to go on a date or to take a group no bigger than six. They are renown for their pumpkin pancakes, but I myself enjoy their eggs florentine. The price is nearly unbeatable and the food will make sure you leave with a smile. This, in my opinion, is a must to show someone what exactly a New York brunch is suppose to be like.

Love the ambiance Hillstone creates, it's not too stuffy nor too casual. The live Jazz band, by the bar, adds a great touch to the overall dining experience. They don't offer complimentary bread but their Foccacia priced at $2 is a worthy appetizer. I had the Osaka style tuna roll; it was beautifully presented and equally tasty. However, it's hardly satisfying as there were only 5 pieces on my plate. I had to eat some of my bf's entree (ribs) to get full. Speaking of which, his ribs were very tender and the shoestring fries did not make the meal seem too heavy and dense. We will definitely frequent this place more often especially since it's located conveniently near my bf's apartment.

Dumplings you must have! It's inexpensive and delicious!! Looking at the menu on Yelp, i thought it was a mistake that everything was less than 10 dollars... But it's true! 5 fried chives & pork dumpling for $1.00! Can't get any better than that! I got 2 orders of the fried chives & pork dumpling, 1 order of the boiled chives & pork dumpling, 1 small hot & sour soup, & 1 plain sesame pancake. The hot and sour soup was very bland. It wasn't spicy or sour at all. My first time trying sesame pancake and it was really bland too.. Wouldn't really recommend either of it. But they are called Prosperity Dumpling for a reason.. Their dumplings are amazing!The dumplings are made from scratch.. and I mean from scratch as in putting the meat in the wrap, folding process & boiling, and then frying as orders come! So it's steaming hot! At first I thought this was a dine in restaurant. When I got there, I was totally wrong! This is more of a take out place than to really sit & eat, but they do have seating.. about 8 stools. Store front was so small that every time someone came in or left, the cold breeze would sweep through the entire store! Definitely recommend if you're looking for cheap & delicious food.

We have been to this restaurant a few times for brunch. Our main complaint is that the brunch menu is too limited. However, the dishes we have had are relatively good, just nothing extraordinary. The veggie burger on english muffin with pesto mayo was good, but was only chosen due to the lack of brunch options. We have also had two eggs any style, cinnamon roll, and the omelette...all of which were rather ordinary. The prices are relatively reasonable though, which still makes the restaurant an option...

They actually are like a 10/5 stars! NO WORDS TO DESCRIBE!!! Let's just say that I used to be a vegetarian and was converted into a chicken&rice fiend!!! The yummiest, most amazing Chicken & Rice cart!!! The only one I eat from!!! So good that I can eat it breakfast, lunch & dinner (I actually have...lol)!!!!  Best spot after a night of partying too! So sad I'm moving to the west coast....Seriously gonna Miss this Chicken & Rice cart. TO SUM-UP: AMAZING!!!! worth the long line, worth the money, worth a trip to midtown All this talk about chicken and rice is making me hungry....Going to go grab some now....BYE!
The teriyaki sweet potato fries... to die for!

Delicious! They were out of chicken for some dishes, but not all (a little strange) and out of the tortillas to make sopes. I had chicken huaraches and my husband had beef tacos dorados. The tortillas, which are corn-based so gluten free (yay!) are crispy and chewy. I tried my husband's rice, which was not dry, like you find in many restaurants. I also tried his beans, which had a nice flavor.  We split a tamal with mole sauce, which was a little spicy and delicious. The service was kind of slow but I attribute it to arriving a half an hour before closing. The restaurant itself is quite small with only about five tables.   On the whole, I really liked this restaurant and will definitely return.
OPEN FOR LUNCH ON FRIDAY ONLY!!! Saxon + Parole is a great place - just figured id keep everyone informed as their hours on here are wrong...

I have been to Buttermilk Channel many times, and it is always fabulous.  The atmosphere is very laid back, and the service is friendly.  Unfortunately they only take reservations for parties of five or more.  If you show up on a Friday or Saturday without a reservation, be prepared to wait.  The wine and drink list are great and the food is phenomenal. The house made pickles, the cheese platter and the chilled oysters are some of our favorite appetizers.  The honey-drizzled popovers they bring to the table are warm and delicious.   My husband always has the fried chicken, which is beyond amazing, as is the waffle and balsamic-infused maple syrup that accompany it.  I usually have the Friday pasta with lobster special, which you can sometimes find on a Saturday night, as well.  The desserts are always outstanding.  I truly feel that this restaurant lives up to the hype.  Can't wait for our next meal here.

The two specialty sandwiches I've had here were both amazingly fresh and delicious. I can never pass up goat cheese... Today while waiting for my sandwich, I browsed the other items they sell.. the picnic baskets are adorable, vintage-esque if not truly vintage, and cost between $20-40. Bags of LaColombe coffee are between $9-10, which is less expensive than other places I've seen. Unfortunately, I only go here when I want to treat myself..and if Ajia is closed.. just too expensive for routine lunch outings. Two negatives: the price, and breakfast stops being served at 11am (I would eat breakfast for every meal, if I could.)

While I agree with others that the service here is great, the value is not. The servers definitely up sell everything and while the food was good, again, 400 bucks for two people is just not reasonable unless you're in Paris on your honeymoon.

OK...been coming here for almost 30 years, but you really need to consider if you want to go to a wonderful brunch restaurant and get treated like a tourist just because it is the summer.   Is it really necessary to ask me basic restaurant related questions almost implying that I have  NEVER eaten in a restaurant before....was in the business for 10+ years actually??  And it is even worse to have a college student or aspiring actor or even a graduate of NYU who is old enough to be my child talk to me as if I can't read what's on the menu.   But the WORST is charging me $3.50 for an iced tea (in the summer no less) that is HIGHLY diluted to begin with in a glass FILLED with ice, remove the glass from the table before the initial iced tea is even finished and pointedly ask me if I'd like "ANOTHER" iced tea, all for the benefit of charging me another $3.50 for another glass of above mentioned beverage.  Really.....not everyone who goes to brunch in NYC in July is a tourist....maybe just an old time TriBeCa resident, who has patronized the place since the 80's who'd like a wonderful Eggs Benedict to start my lazy Sunday!!!  The foods great but the restaurant attitude of years gone by has got to go away!!!

I love the concept of a hole-in-the-wall place that serves one thing only: authentic Belgian thick cut fries. It's so simple and elegant. No complex menus with a million items to read through and decide. You get what the name says. Pommes frites. And pommes frites only. The only customizable part of your order are the dipping sauces. They offer a wide range of dipping sauces for an additional charge ($1), but don't feel pressured because they have lots of free sauces and garnish too (I like the frite sauce, it's just European mayo). It is a small operation (2 man job), but they don't skimp on quantity or quality. They expertly time the frying so the end result is almost always near-perfect. Craving fries? Here is your place!

Yup, the food is as good as everyone says.  Love the flat bread and bright green olive oil, love the whole fish specials, love the sauteed mussels, love the hummus, love the desserts.  Things I'm not crazy about - the wait (we live nearby and will only go if we can get there by 6 on a weekday), the cramped quarters, the rushed feel you get from the servers occasionally. Hint - if you forget to BYOB, you can pick up something 'to go' at the New Wave across the street.
Visited for the second time. The banana leaf fish is very good!

Absolutely a must must must. We ate at the location on the lower east side after visiting the Tenement Museum (another must).  I would never of thought Meatballs could be so good and mixed will amazing sides. The fresh cookie sundaes are also a must.

This restaurant has been on my list of places to visit for a while. So when I had the opportunity of venturing to Brooklyn n dine at the world renowned "Lambardi's" I felt like a kid on Christmas morning.  As we entered the establishment I was amazed at how big the place was. Granted there wasn't one big room but rather several tiny/ narrow rooms. I loved how the hostess walked us through the kitchen n past many other rooms to take us to our table. It certainly added to the ambiance (old school Italian eateries). I was so excited to finally be sitting in front of a table, at a restaurant I'd never thought I get to visit. However, that excitement turned to shear disappointment when the food arrived. We ordered the meatballs n bruschetta as apps n they were great, but the pizzas margarita & a pizza with mushrooms left something to be desired. While the crust (texture n flavor) were good the rest of it was lacking salt, cheese, flavor, flavor, and more flavor. I must say I have had much better pizza in the past at other pizzerias. I was in disbelief n for a while thought I had read the wrong reviews and/or come to the wrong place. Prices were reasonable but the waitstaff was not attentive and did nothing to make me or my guest feel special (waited 15 min for check after asking 3 times and no one offered un replenishments our drinks) . I got the impression that the reputation spoke for it self, rather than the food & service providing a reputation for the business.  Perhaps they had an off day, but I will never be back to find out. If you want to visit this famous joint to say u have eaten here great but if your in the mood for excellent quality pizza n service there's much better pizzerias out there to be discovered. Service: Below average Food: Average
The BEST brisket in NYC.  I've had Franklin and I've had Morgans.  Now I can gladly die of cardiac arrest. Only negative is the Texas Longhorns flag.  BOOO

Abates was packed and the wait too long so my husband and I decided to try Anastasio's. Liked listening to the 50's music while browsing the menu. Thought prices a little steep for the pasta dishes we ordered. Dinner arrived hot; serving size was ample, seasonings somewhat bland, and the frozen peas included in my dish disheartening. The salad was large but was all iceburg lettuce; one pepper slice, 1/4 tomato piece, 2 canned olives and a slice of cucumber; the dressing was tasty. Would I return - maybe.  There are so many better Italian restaurants on Wooster St. and in the general area.

I stopped in for a quick Lunch-Dinner (Linner) on Sunday afternoon and didn't indulge in the table-wide feast of BBQ that they offered for Restaurant Week (which I would've loved to do but it wasn't on my dime!) I wasn't that hungry so I opted for the brisket salad with lime vinaigrette which sounds weird, like whaaaa brisket on a salad?  I've never even had brisket before, but this was juicy, flavorful, and delicious so it might have been just the kick I needed to try something other than pulled pork and ribs from time to time. The salad was surprisingly really filling, chockfull of cheese and black beans and that delicious lime dressing.  I also dipped the pieces of my brisket in the small bottles of sauce they offered and all tasted wonderful. The people I was with split an order of the chicken/cornish game hen and it looked superb.  They had nothing bad to say about it. The coke was definitely not the coca cola I'm used to, but it wasn't bad.  It tasted old fashioned and homemade.  Maybe I missed that part of the menu. Overall, based on the tenderness of the brisket, I will absolutely be back here in the future to actually devour a whole feast of BBQ and sides.

I love this Vegetarian restaurant.  The Falafel sandwich is just fantastic - spicy or not, depending on how yer feeling.  The staff is lovely and efficient and even if there is a line it moves quickly. Yum!

Looking for a well-made delicious burger with fries made like mom used to make from real potatoes? Hit up this place every Wednesday for the York St Cheeseburger.  You'll find me chomping down on it at the bar or on the great patio in the warmer months. And speaking of warm ... The staff never fails to be just that. But if you're looking for a watering hole on a budget who can resist the Beer Bash on Thursday and Sunday evenings. Gotta love when all you need for a fun night out with a great mix of people is just a $20 bill.

The Jeffrey is a most welcome surprise addition to my usually boring/ E. midtown work hood. The beer selection is fantastic, the ambiance is dark and cozy and the crowd is laid back. I sampled some of the happy hour brews (wish they offered more) and a yummy hot pretzel, both were perfect.  My co-worker and I both had other plans that night but wished we didn't so we could just hang and enjoy the vibe. Only downside was our server, she was sweet but maybe stoned? She couldn't remember anything we ordered or even that she owed me change from the bill - she was all, "Oh you wanted that money back?" Poor thing I was harshing her buzzzzzz.

I used to come here when it was Q Bar which I enjoyed. When I came back into the city and saw Q Bar had closed I was pretty bummed but figured I'd give the new place a try. The food is absolutely delicious! Everyone needs to try the pork tacos with spinach tortillas. Absolutely amazing. I'm dreaming of those tacos right now! And add a pitcher of margarita and I'm all set to go.

Great service and good food, but for the prices and reviews I was underwhelmed by the food. It was good, but I expected great. The potato gnoccis were honestly bland and the butter with salt they gave with the bread was salty rather than flavorful.
I'll keep this short and sweet. Good Dog Burger with any type of their fries should make you very happy...and if it doesn't you probably don't enjoy rainbows or smiling either.

Came here for a work outing with a bunch of NYC executives.  We had the "Bomarzo" room downstairs. Now don't get me wrong, I generally wouldn't be caught dead in midtown for dinner, ever.  Usually anything above 14th street is a huge no-no for me.  I made an exception because this was a work event, and was not disappointed (it helped that I had door-to-door subway service there). Very nice place on the inside, I was immediately impressed.  Nice lighting, good decor with nice, dark, rich colors.  The room we had downstairs was nice and big.  They had a bar set up on one side of the room with beer, wine and all the top-shelf liquor you could drink.  Bartender was VERY friendly and gave us fantastic service. We didn't order off the menu - it was set up through one of our EA's so there was a set menu with appetizers and mains.  They came through every minute or two with a large plate of appetizers and they were DELICIOUS.  The smoked salmon was amazing, the tuna tartare was delicious, the crab cakes were off the chart and the chicken skewers were honestly some of the best I've ever had. I was talking to a partner through most of dinner so I missed out on most of the mains but I was able to grab a heaping plate of a rigatoni-type pasta with a very good meat-based sauce.  Definitely some of the best pasta-esque food I've had in awhile. Desserts were then laid out - the cannoli was amazing.  One of our lead execs dropped a perfect "leave the gun, take the cannoli" line at some point that was pretty classic. Overall a great experience.  I'd love to come and order off the menu and see what else they have to offer!

*music:  is good but a little too up beat for dinner time. I know other similar Thai places that play house/trance but more of a mellow beat. *food: Tom yum is pretty good. Could be spicier. crab ragoons had a lot of cream cheese and little crab. Sake wasn't impressive. Pad Thai was too sweet. I've been to Thailand though so maybe I just have high expectations :)

SERVICE: had an awesome server girl... she was cool! Took photos for us and came back to make sure if we needed anything else before happy hour is over. FOOD: (1) Oysters: I like em raw east coast oysters! 5 stars $1 each... CHEAP! (2) Calm Chowder: DRINKS: (1) Happy hour beer: $3, 5 stars! (2) Happy hour sangria-thing: $5, 5 stars! **OVERALL: Happy hour oysters and beer! Go for it! Cheap and nice!

As previously mentioned in other reviews, service w/attitude but the food is not bad; Just not good enough to merit another dine-in experience. - The Ho's comment was definitely accurate. Not off to a good start when the restaurant is half-empty and the Ho's are busy chit-chatting while we're standing there waiting to be seated. - The unisex bathroom? Wha.. why? Glowsticks? House music pumping into the bathroom stalls? Each stall was dimly lit by a lone spotlight.. I felt like I was squatting in a prison cell. - We were seated at a table against the mid-section with a fucking shelf jutting out of the wall and into my dining companion's neck. We ended up moving the table several inches into the aisle so he doesn't have to eat with his head cocked to the side. The saving grace was the meatloaf. It was actually very good even though I had to ask for ketchup. The haricot verts it was served with was decent but the mashed potatoes were oily and salty.

There are a lot of good restaurants in this city, but gone are the days of having an amazing dining experience. The attention to detail, and that detail being YOU is why you go here. There's really only 1 item on the menu that you need to get and it's the "Menu Tasting" The chef selects and you enjoy. The staff is amazing. It doesn't matter who took your order because whatever you ordered shows up in front of you.

Star #1 is for the mussels. This is THE spot for mussels in Old City, maybe in all of Philly (well, if it weren't for Monks). We tried the Dijon variety, and couldn't believe how large and sweet the meat was and how incredible the sauce was. We couldn't get enough bread to sop it up. Star #2 is for the calamari. Or really, the flavorful aioli. Yum. Star #3 is for the atmosphere and location. Cobblestone on 2nd and Chestnut leading to a perfect mix of dim and twinkly lights with music that's not too loud and a crowd that's only a little rowdy. Star #4 is for the staff. Attentive and friendly, we had a great experience even though we took up a 4 person table for 2 of us and didn't order proper dinners. They kept us happy! Star #5 is for the BEER. Oh the beer. The list I looked at first was just the draft specials. AND THEN I OPENED THE MENU. Craft beer lovers, unite, and visit Eulogy. You are guaranteed to find something you love and probably many you haven't tried yet.

I reserved my hunger, having only one slice of pizza while in Manhattan because I wanted to give this cheesesteak the attention it deserved. It was 1:30am when we pulled up and had just slammed two pints of Stella at some roadside chain in New Jersey, so my appetite was primed for this experience. There were some hookers hanging out and we chatted about my sunburn while I read the stupid ordering rules. I ordered slowly on purpose because there's no line and I hate rules. They put some crappy sweet peppers on my sandwich that I had to pick off after drunkenly realizing how crappy they were. The bread is good, I'll give it that - but take away all the boasting and built up shit and this sandwich isn't even as good as one in Albuquerque or San Francisco. I would normally give four stars but minus one due to complacency.

Great pizza! I like the wings too - not too well done and tons of sauce (how I like 'em). My husband ordered a baked ziti dish and sausage. He said it was "ok." Good size portions. Delivery on Sunday @ 6 pm took about 40 minutes.

Wine is super, service is great, atmosphere is out of this world. 5 extra stars for being able to see Mrs. Portman here. apparently, she's a regular and the waitstaff is all chill about it. Will definitely be going back.

Came here with a group of friends for brunch on Sunday.  The food was fantastic, and I would definitely come back again to try more of the menu.   The only complaint is that the service was sub-par.  The waiter generally seemed impatient with us when we asked questions about the menu, and argued with two of us about our orders when they came out not quite right.  We weren't asking unreasonable questions or for any fancy substitutions - it detracted some from the experience.

I been here a couple of times actually and never gave a review.  I remember the first time I was here couple of years back and man it was the BOMB!  Then as the years go by, whenever I'm in town I'd go get my cravings fixed and they never disappoint! (Though this last time I went, some of the dumplings broke because they were a bit dried...) For those of you that are first timers: First you gotta make sure to eat them when they come out of the kitchen.  Don't wait around! You come here to get the dumplings (Alright maybe the scallion pan cakes too).  But don't you rush to eat it either, cause the soup is HOT.  Take your time and slowly caress the outside layer until the skin breaks (JK just bite the damn skin people!).  As the juice come running out, proceed to drink the soup, make sure you don't burn yourself!  Also some folks likes to eat the dumplings by dipping the dumpling sauce they provide at the table.  I personally do; it gives it another kick to the dumplings.  Go ahead and give it a shot.
Late happy hour. Come early to grab seats. $4-$5 lychee martinis. That's all you need to know.

It's difficult to find chinese FRESH hand made noodles outside Asia. But the name itself caught my attention. Inside the restaurant you can see how they swing, pull and make the noodles all by hand. The traditional way. And the noodle soups are definitely worth coming, because it's not only the meat and the soup which makes this place worth coming, the highlight is obviously the noodles itself. Besides we got fried dumplings which was a great side dish. I think we paid $10 each. It's cheap and it's CASH ONLY.

Not only the best sushi place in town. But probably one of the best ever been too. All my friends and family that come down here also want to go! Favorites; spicy Kani salad, Yankee roll, crazy dynamite roll and romantic roll!
Pasta delicious and crazy packed. Lovely people

Terrible terrible service. We tried to catch the attention of a waiter and he just ignored us. Even if he wasn't our tables waiter he could have let us know he would send our waiter over instead of ignoring us.

Went here with my gf for a quick dinner. She tried the one in Japan so she wanted to see if this was comparable. I got the Grand slam and she got the single chicken curry. Portions were definitely generous especially for the price. Also got a side order of fukuzinzuke which was japanese red radish. Food was good and she said it's comparable to the one she had in Japan. So this would be a good place to get lunch/dinner to go in the city.

I loved this little gem of a restaurant! Delicious perogis and you can mix the kinds  (I did potato/cheese and mushroom/sauerkraut!) Service was super quick -- by the time my friend went around the corner to buy beer and got back (Byob) our food was on the table! Great place to go for a homey and stuffing meal.

Late on a Friday night, not a lot of choices in the area, we found ourselves here a few minutes before the kitchen was closing.  The waiter was a bit annoying rushing the popcorn to our table and telling us that the kitchen would close very soon. He had this air about him seeming to  "nudge" us to order something simple to make HIS life easier. His look of relief that we just ordered salads confirmed that he was dieing for closing time. It wasn't even that busy, maybe he had a hot date. LOL. By the end of our meals we totally forgot about him.   I had a fuji apple salad.  It was well presented.  It was a fun plate to push your fork around and discover what was under all those apple slicea.    The baby arugula suprises you and then yummy yummy yummy. Cool casual venue to just chill, laugh with your friends and have fun.   We left happy.  Will come back to try other menu selections, and definitely earlier in the night. Would be nice if they sifted the unpopped kernels from the bags of popcorn they serve.  We had to hold those in our hands until the bag was empty and then threw them in there.  ;\ Later hours please!!!!

Servers were nice and efficient but the foods were underwhelmed. We didn't understand the hype. Is that because we didn't drink? Oysters with Mignonette ($36 for12) - The oysters at The Lobster Place in Chelsea Market is so much better and many to choose from, and pretty tasty even though I'm standing to eat. Steamed Mussels - another disappointment. The Thai broth didn't make me want to soak up with a bread. How mussels could be tasteless. I guess no seafood on Monday applies here. I want to believe it was their worst day but I felt bad for my friends from Tokyo to treat me for this lunch. The famous burger - perfectly cooked, medium. It was good but not that special especially for the price. It was good as Umami Burger except the price, $21 vs $15.5 (Classic $12 + fries $3.5) and you get your choice of fries. To my surprise, I did enjoyed the string fries with rosemary. Cuban sandwich ($19) -I read a good review but what we got was just okay, nothing very special. Tasty Prosciutto de Parma and the aged gruyere didn't help this gamey pork that was in the sandwich. Usually acidity from piickles help  a bit but not this one. Crème Caramel ($9) - everything we had, so far, were below 4.5 start so we didn't expect much from the dessert but it was excellent. We all loved this gelatinous Spanish-like firmed custard pudding with a light caramel sauce. We did not understand why we needed to wait for a table even the place wasn't packed for early Monday lunch. We waited outside for good 30 minutes but no one check us but we noticed may customers were showing up. I found that waiting outside was not a good idea because people after us got their table before us. I checked the name list that was left unattended and the name after us were erased. I suggest do not wait for your table outside. Big group of French tourists next to our table were waiting for their food and they were very chatty, high energy and being very French. The time we were about to leave, I noticed how very quiet the table got. The excitement has left the table and eating quietly, not like French anymore.
Burgers were heavenly. My boyfriend and I will return.

I know this is one of the iconic cheese steak places in Philly... but it always makes me a bit ill. Tastes good going down... its the later that I could live without. Go there once if you must but there are definitely better places to get a great cheese steak

This place belongs in every town! Yum yum yum. If you're a vegetarian or a health nut or just want a change... def try this place! You'll be hooked :) I read some of the reviews written by other customers who say the same thing (food is great across the board) but have said a thing or two about pricing... Someone once told me - "You pay for what you get" ...  If something costs extremely cheap (such as a $1 burger at Mickey D's), then it speaks for itself... there's a reason for it.  It's up to you... I love Mickey D's... but I also love being healthy and knowing what I put in my body is going to make me feel and look good. To the contrary, this place is atually cheaper than Cosi, Panera Bread, and better quality than Chipotle, etc.... At just under $11 you can get the salmon salad and a drink!  That's grilled salmon and fresh yummy salad mind you. This place has their items pretty fresh, not precooked or pre-made to be popped in a microwave - pulled chicken made fresh at the establishment, or bison grilled fresh with no hidden perservatives.  This place is def not pricey (or over-priced)... in fact I'm surprised how well priced it is!  I compare this place to a five star sit down restaurant but quick and a lot less expensive... if you haven't tried this place, you'll know what I mean when you try some of their menu options.  I was a bit surprised to see people complain about the pricing but then again, they are probably comparing it to the vicinity such as McDonalds, Subway, Dunkin Donuts or some of the buffet type places... I personally compare the whole 9... quality, pricing, look, cleanliness and promptness. Just wish they had more locations for days I'm off or have meetings elsewhere.

Visiting for the holidays.  I had the Hoagie omelet. Was with a party of 8. The omelets, home fries and pancakes were delicious!  Our server was Amy, and she was great. Quick, helpful, with a dose of humor!  Wish we lived closer!

What a pleasant surprise!  I was in town for a show at the Wellmont Theater, my first time ever at this venue since I usually find plenty of shows in the city..  So arriving in Montclair and starving, the search for a place to eat before heading inside the Wellmont began.   We stumbled upon Ah' Pizz and I love Neopolitan Pizza (Motorino, Luzzo's) so decided to check it out.  We were a little disappointed in the lack of booze but the owner kindly explained to us the BYO policy and how ridiculously expensive liquor licenses were in the area so none of the restaurants serve alcohol.   Okie dokes, on to the FOOD!! OMG...we had the bufala mozzarella pie and a special pesto pie with soppresata and a cheese who's name I can't remember but it was a sharper than provolone taste and was heavenly.  The owner took care of us and he was fantastic, very friendly and knowledgeable and you can tell he knew his stuff and was passionate about it to boot.  We scarfed down our delicious pizzas, and were both surprised that the slow eater ate in record time--it was THAT good.  The ingredients are of great quality and it makes a huge difference in taste, and the pies are cooked to perfection.  True Neopolitan pizza.  I also had a peach iced tea that was made in Italy and I didn't even know something as simple as peach iced tea could taste that good.   Just when I thought I was stuffed, the owner comes and offers us dessert.  All of a sudden I had a little room left.  It all sounded amazing, but we opted for the cheesecake (but I do want to try the gelato one day).  As the owner brings the cheesecake he tells us it is the BEST homemade cheesecake.  HA! Yea...ok buddy..we're from New York, we've had good cheesecake! Yet as SOON as I took a bite of that creamy, silky, more than PERFECT slice of heaven, my eyes got huge.  It was unanimous, it was definitely the BEST cheesecake we have ever had...EVER!  That's saying a lot.  The texture and taste were impeccable, and the crust was perfect. I think I need to go see some more bands at the Wellmont pretty damn soon.
Love this place, I go there almost every weekend for my Indian fix. The staff is very attentive and the food is great. I haven't found one dish I haven't liked. Highly recommended.

Best Xiao long bao I've had. The place is cash only like most Asian places. You share a table if you have a smaller group, but makes the wait faster. They had two types: Xiao Long Bao with crab meat pork, and Xiao Long Bao with only pork. I preferred the original, just because I was used to the texture and taste, but the crab meat pork xiao long bao was different, not in a good or bad way. We also ordered the beef noodle soup (quite bland, although the menu indicated it was "slightly spicy) but the beef itself was extremely tender and flavorful. The snow pea tips were cooked perfectly. Overall a pleasant meal, even when sharing a table with complete strangers. It was like a hibachi meal... but without the distractions from the awkwardness...
OMG! Delicious! Yes, it's a small spot but food was great!  Defiantly going back.  We had the Lamb platter for 2, it was more than enough.

what a treat.  i actually stopped eating falafel for several years after consistently getting mediocre bland falafel accompanied by extremely uninspired fixings at various other places.   this place is legit, fresh, tasty, and is how falafel was meant to be.   I now feel like a born again falalel consumer.  oh la la.

Pizza is very good. Service is AWFUL. Granted, their menus tells you to be "patient", but we ordered 1 large pizza (and waters) and it took over 1 hour and 10 minutes. For that reason, I'd never eat here again. The waiter never checked in on us. They dropped off the wrong pizza 1 hour into our "wait" and before I could even say "excuse me, this is not ours", the guy just walked away!

The idea of pizza via food truck has fascinated me for a long time. Luckily yesterday I was able to  have Pitruco for the second time. My first experience was at the night market, when I dragged Clay straight from the trolley past all the other vendors so I could finally get some of their pizza before the line was out of control. After a 10 minute wait (the line got long quick after us) we placed our orders for half margarita half salami and were quickly handed our pies. I was little disappointed they were only offering two varieties but it is totally understandable for that type of event. And the speed at which the cook the pies really makes it some of the best food at the event. The crust on the Pitruco pizza is perfection. Definitely one of the best in Philly. The toppings are minimal in a good way as well. Yesterday I was lucky enough to try the famed Spicy Garlic I have been hearing so much about. We went for the additional cheese at no cost and I urge you do to the same. It was phenomenal. The thinly sliced garlic and loads of red pepper really make a great pie. The crust again was outstanding and this time there was no wait. At $6.50 this is definitely the deal of the century because I found it to be enough to split.  Now if only I worked downtown and could indulge on a regular basis.

I came to eat and enjoy the free sangria deal. The offer was not honored , even though we were a party of three people, and only wanted 1 free sangria ($5.00). I got all sorts of excuses for them not being able to honor it. When I asked to speak to a supervisor, our server explained how he wasn't available. Although, she was in charge, she wasn't able to . So, if you go for the offer FORGET ABOUT IT .. The food is tasty
We had an overwhelming experience with that small yet cozy place. The food was great and a quality service that is satisfaction guaranteed. See you there!

I've been there for drinks previously at their great bar. Nice scene, and bartenders that know what they're doing. For dinner, I had a main course of ragu of rabbit and lamb sausage. It was excellently prepared and a very interesting meal. The others in my party had equally interesting meals. I'll have to add this to my rotation. When it is warmer out, they have outdoor tables in a courtyard.

the night started off by seeing a raging fireplace outside when walking into the restaurant. We were greated by friendly employees at the front, one appeared to be a manager who directed to the lounge for cocktails while we waited for a table in the diningroom, I guess everyone wants to eat at 7pm. We grabbed a glass of wine and listened to the live music when we were called to our table. They thanked us for waiting, that's a nice touch. Our server was prompt and efficient, she was very knowledable of the menu and wine list. we split the salad with pears and phyllo triangles filled with goat cheese, amazing. my date had the Miso Salmon and I ordered the Sirloin with blue cheese...Wow! The waitress suggested a bottle of wine off the wine market, tasted like $60 bottle for $24. We shared a dessert, apple pie, again, wow. What a great place, atmosphere, food, service and value...this place is a homerun and we'll be back for many more experiences.

This place is exactly what you want when you are looking for Banh Mi. The best implementation of the french inspired Vietnamese sandwich I have ever had!  The bread is dead on, the pork is perfectly grilled, and the vegetables are fresh.  The place looks like a dump but it is the real deal.

G*ddamn this place is amazing!!! I think it's the combination of the fact that they're super tasty and freshly made. But the fact that you can get 5 gigantic two-full-bite pan-fried dumplings for the low, low price of just $1 is amazing to me! Yes, the potstickers are a bit on the greasy side, but they're also super juicy and flavorful. I also bought a bag of 50 frozen vegetarian dumplings for my friend for just $11. The pork and chive ones, the same that they make into potstickers, are just $9/bag! I wish I lived in NYC, I'd be here every time I visited Chinatown. And their hours are amazing too, 7:30am - 10pm. I visited for lunch and came back for breakfast a few days later! I'll definitely be back to visit Prosperity Dumpling the next time I visit NYC.

A few blocks from the F train 2nd Avenue station in Manhattan, past a host of young over tatooed New Yorkers and in the middle of the lower Eastside scene is a place I have grown to be very fond of.  Its Italian enough for me as most of their dishes have pasta. The food is excellent and incredibly priced for New York or anywhere for that matter. The service is good, friendly and usually if not always good looking. I had the walnut salad with goat cheese to start and the pasta dish with the sausage as the entree and I was very content. I haven't tried the desserts yet , that will be on my next visit. The location is stupendous in my opinion. Narrow low rise side street with a good mix of freaks and wannabe freaks but that is what gives the lower eastside its charm.

Maybe we picked the wrong dishes or the wrong night, but there was more that was wrong about our meal than there was right. The Pad Garlic with Tofu had a nicely-flavored sauce, but there was nothing "Thai" about it; I've had very similar dishes at many Chinese restaurants. When we go to Spice in Belleville, their curry puffs are like little clouds, just heavenly. JoeyThai's curry puffs are like little rainclouds: heavy, sodden, and greasy. And beware of this dish: "Ant Climbing Trees." Here's the description: "ANT CLIMBING TREES   12.95 Savory wok fried pork with toasted coconut, crunchy peanuts and crispy  dried shrimp. Served over glass noodles, Thai mint and Vietnamese basil." Honey, that pork was so white and bland, it might've actually been chicken (not sure); there was NO toasted coconut or crunchy peanuts. Instead of crispy dried shrimp, they used jumbo shrimp which tasted BAD, and there was ALOT of flavorless noodles and one basil leaf. That dish was so bad, it went into the garbage! We do recommend Spice in Belleville (not to be confused with Spice II in Montclair). The food is consistently great.

This used to be my go-to spot for delicious no frills Chinese, but the quality has gradually declined, and they finally began miniaturizing their portions with the small plastic containers found in Midtown Chinese joints.  Even eat-in portions are smaller, and cuts were made across the board where it counts.  Meat dishes have less meat, noodle soups have more soup and less of the good stuff, and to make matters worse, a recent price hike went into effect.  There are other great Chinese restaurants in Chinatown, but this place has the momentum now, so the owner most definitely wont lose any sleep.

This is the second time I have visited this fine dining establishment and I have been impressed each time, and can't wait to go back whenever I am in Burlington. Last time I had the localvore omelet, which is made with whatever local ingredients are available at the moment, which is awesome, and tastes great. This time, I had the special french toast made with cranberry orange bread (so delicious that when I got home, I looked up a recipe for cranberry orange bread to make at home!).  Only wish I would have ordered some veggie sausage as a side to have with it. He had the eggs benedict, with said veggie sausage that I fell in love with. The hollandaise sauce was homemade but a little too lemony for my tastes; he loved it.  We also had good service, and arriving at 9:15am , had no wait for a table. I love that this place is local, organic, environmental... everything I love about Vermont all wrapped up neatly in this place. Thanks for a great breakfast!

went to Amada on a regular bases when I lived in Philly, way before Chef Jose Garces won the Iron Chef title. we'd go for birthday dinner, graduation dinners and all kinds of occasions. i love the white sangria and melon con jamon. flat-bread is a great choice too! I can't really think of anything I don't like from here! we usually go and try out lots of different things. but my fiance and I were disappointed last time we went. most things were just over salty and over greasy. and everybody seemed a bit overwhelmed. however, the service was still great as always. we'd probably give it a try some other time.
It's a deli, to set your expectations. There is seating and it's cuter than most delis, but it doesn't feel like a restaurant. All the food is excellent and cheap. Can't wait to go back!
Dependable pub food in a cool old bar, in a cool town. Worth visiting with the right expectations.

If I could give it a half star, I would. Overrated in every aspect, proving having choices doesn't mean a thing. Dined here on a Wednesday around 5, so the crush of the post-work crowd didn't hit yet. Either way, I waited for a server and watched as the bartender chatted with a friend while I was a few feet away, sans menu, drink or acknowledgement. When the waitress finally arrived after 15 minutes of hopeful staring on my part (and the man next to me was brought his sandwich on burnt bread) she didn't have a menu for me. She disappeared for another 10 minutes and came back with one, by now it was 5:30 and my appointment was looming. I asked what was fast and what was part of happy hour (I had to ask, since she just stood there). She said the pizza was fast so I ordered the mushroom. The beer arrived with no head or flavor. The cutlery and the napkin it was in were dirty. I was not given a plate for the pizza, so I had to chow down with no napkin, knife to cut the slices off or plate to eat it in. It felt like camping but with a much higher price tag. As I finished eating, she came over to check on me. At that point I had used a tissue from my purse as a napkin and gave up on the ice water I'd asked for. I told her to wrap the pizza up and bring the check. That she brought quickly. I then sat, as the crowds filed in, waiting for her to pick up the check. She actually started coming my way, and I held up the billfold, but she darted away. I went to the hostess, who was the best part of this whole experience, and she cashed out my bill as I told her I had to go, but I wanted to pay. I don't think City Tap will be here much longer, since I asked a few folks and they say a beer with no head usually means a greasy, dirty glad
Great food but the original in FOREST HILLS still has the best food of all the locations

Who doesn't love a good bowl of Ramen in light of this Winter's recent weather. I have been waiting to check Ippudo off of my restaurants list on my iPhone, and it was worth the wait.  Standing at the bar for the 30 minutes prior to seating didn't even change my feelings on the meal that awaited me.  The steamed chicken buns were so good we thought, why not order the pork buns as well. The main event of course was the beautiful bowl of warm Ramen broth with a perfectly cooked poached egg. Worth the wait, but arrive early!

They managed to fit us in with a last minute reservation. Thought we didn't have the best table, the food was amazing. I had the foie gras and duck ravioli. In a word - phenomenal. The service was equally amazing. Oh, and the bread basket. I really can't fault them on anything. I can't wait to go back...I loved it (can you tell?)
Ordered the meat lovers and there was hardly any meat on the pizza. I was also very salty...probably wont order from there again

This place can be expensive, but worth it. The paella was $30, but came with a half lobster and tons of clams/mussels/oysters, calamari and shrimp.  Their fries are garbage, so I stick with rice (which you can keep and eat everyday for a week) and vegetables.  The beef ribs are ok, lots of grizzle and not a lot of meat, but very tasty.  The real winner was the Eurogrill burger.  Ham, bacon, cheese all served on a Portuguese roll- for 10$ it was fantastic.

I love a well prepared, thin crust, plain cheese pizza.   The sign of a truly well made pizza is a plain pie cooked well. This was perfect. The crust was think throughout. Nice and crispy edges. The center was moist from the amount of cheese. The sauce was delicious and the pizza was not oversauced. The cheese was thin sliced fresh mozz, and omg was amazing. The only thing, it needed a pinch more salt, but that's personal preference. Have been here several times and perfect pizza each time. I order a small and there is enough for one person to enjoy a lunch and take the other half home. It holds up nicely and you can just toss it back in the oven a few minutes for a great snack.

This review is just for the downstairs bar/lounge -- Came here for an OkayAfrica sponsored event on Saturday and despite it being V CROWDED, I had a great experience. The space is beautiful beautiful beautiful, the crowd was considerate (not a drink spilled!), sound system among the best I've experienced (similar to Monarch in SF), solid drinks, AND the doorman was incredible--totally calm and good natured despite the massive line outside and the mild chaos inside. Will definitely be back for a more low-key night.
It took 23 mins for my HaloHalo order.Crazy!!Lack of anticipation on their part. Banana/Jackfruit pie is my Fave part.

We came here from New Jersey. And this one beats a lot of NJ Indian restaurant hands down. We had the veggie buffet and it was authentic South Indian food. My friends had the chicken tikka masala dosa and were raving about it all. We ended it with the pan-kulfi. It has a unique kick to itself. Nice place with the right mix of spice and authenticity.

If I am near the Shop-Rite on Olden Avenue and I am not sure what I am in the mood for, 9 out of 10 times I choose Mamma Flora's. First of all, everytime I walk in there the owner/manager greets us with a big smile and warm welcomes. He seems to remember all of the regular customers and is extremely pleasant/attentive. Now on to the food... Everything is made to order so if you don't want onions/tomatoes/etc. they are very accomadating. I LOVE the "Insane fries". I pretty much order them with anything that I get. They are cheese fries but better...with corn, onions, jalapenos, olives, and I don't even remember what else. But they are good! I have also had their cheesesteak, pizza, and soup, which were all delicious. I have never tried their pasta dishes or sat down to eat here...I kind of forget that I have the option to do so. Their takeout tastes so good I am sure that it would be even better served immediately. Overall, great food, friendly atmosphere, and pretty good selection of bottled sodas and iced teas/juices (yes that matters to me). Definitely give it a try if you like casual, sit-down Italian restaurants.
shishito peppers, duck ramen, pork belly buns, chorizo fried rice. enough said. I've found my new favorite place for a Japanese fix. yummo.

The food was amazing. I had the Southern Comfort breakfast with fried green tomatoes, sugar-cured bacon, grits, and eggs... delicious! The food garnered this spot the 3 stars I gave it. The looooooong wait in the cold and the fact that we were asked to leave immediately after paying for our meal due to a need for our table turned me off, times two. Go early on the weekend or during the week if you don't want anything to take from your experience!

I wish I could give 10 stars! The food was outstanding, the tastes creative (Loved the quinoa salad and the succotash appetizers.) But what really sets this restaurant apart is the flawless service. Every single member of the staff was friendly in a genuine way, helpful and attentive. We had a medical emergency during our meal and the staff handled it with grace, professionalism and the utmost care. We are so grateful and hope to return sometime to enjoy the fantastic food - without the drama!

The Chicken Pie is good. Not mind blowing but good Delicate wafer like crust. Menus are on chalk boards on walls which is interesting.  Cool kid type music and dark atmosphere.  Lots of good beer as expected.

One of my favorite Italian places in NYC. Fresh, tasty and the ambiance is perfect for a date or a relaxing evening with friends. The Tomato, Basil and Mozzarella pasta is to die for~!! The pasta is fresh al dente and the texture of the pasta is just amazing. The Lamb chops are also one of the best deals in NYC $27 for 4 shanks of lamb and made perfectly. What more can you ask for?  This is the combination I order every time. Everything else is also great except maybe the artichoke salad.. that just didn't have any flavor. (this is not on the regular menu anyway) Only Con is that it is cash only. so be prepared. ($100 for 2 and you should be safe)

This place is so cute. It is child friendly. The desserts are tasty. The coffee is good. I didn't have a meal but this place is beautiful. You can pay  for your stuff and sit out front or you can sit inside. its very spacious and clean looking. Very chic!

I have been meaning to come back here for a while now. Decent prices for the value. I had garlic chicken and garlic shrimp, and I have no complaints. The sangria is on my top 3!! I am always chasing the the perfect sangria and this went so well with my meal. I loved the spanish chips. I can not wait to go back

While this place is pretty good, I think 'Desi Chaat House' close by actually has better chaat. Where better means that the flavors and textures are better balanced and more carefully chosen, and the quality of the ingredients also seems superior. The Mood Cafe chaats seemed to all taste pretty much the same. Of course Hassan is quite a performer, while DCH has much quieter service - I'm guessing that's why this place gets so much more attention. My experience is based on just one visit to each place, so YMMV.

Great place to come for ready-made Korean food. Every time we come to Korean town for late night karaoke, we end up here picking up take out.  I love the convenience of everything here.  They recently changed the design so that it buffet and shelves of prepared food would be easier to move around but now the intimate feel it once had is gone and it feels more like being at school cafeteria. Many of my favorite dishes (apple fruit salad and tuna sushi) have also disappeared, at least during my last few visits. Overall, it's just an average experience now. Don't expect great tasting food because it's not - it's about the convenience.

I've been there several times over the last couple years and it seems like it's getting worse. A couple years ago I was impressed by the tapas and combinations, the drinks, the plating, and the hospitality. More recently after two more visits I was disappointed. I shared tapas with my girlfriend and we agreed that some were greasy and others just kind of dull (including the one recommended by the server). She had a barbecue sandwich that was fine, but she hoped for more. I had fish... and I can't remember more about it than that.... We expected more for the price, simple as that.

Not sure what all the fuss is about. About the burger, where's the beef? Not only was the patty small, the bacon over powered it, it had 4 small pickle slices on it and the Tomato was  the size of the bun and it over powered the taste. There needs to be more balance in the tastes. BTW, I love me some grilled cheese. The grilled cheese sandwich was also over powered by the bacon and tomato and bread. They make a point to tell you it is Irish cheddar and I was all psyched up to eat it. Then I could barely taste the cheese. The fries were fine. Service was fine, atmosphere was fine. It is popular not a quiet date type of place.  The prices were reasonable. Not bad not great!
Chipotle on steroids circa 1998 MLB.  Home Run City.

Had dinner here again last night after first visit in Oct '13 and place is consistently great. It was very crowded with lots of people waiting outside, but we had an 8:45p reservation and were seated immediately upon arrival.  Friendly hostess and wait staff. We started with calamari app which was excellent, then had the chef special cod fillet (waiter recommended) and the standard menu item pork chop.  Both were exceptional.  Followed that with the German chocolate torte - very light and perfect to share.  Bartender makes a great dirty martini, fyi. Overall experience was excellent and I'll def be back.

Absolutely amazing! The pork belly buns, squid, and ramen were out of this world. All the servers work as a team so you don't have to wait around for your own waitress/waiter to receive service. If the menu is confusing, they will explain everything to you in a clear manner because the servers are very well trained and know everything on the menu. This restaurant is immaculate all around, including the restrooms and decor is great. Only negative thing I'd add is that there's a bit of a wait (and you cannot make reservations) but the food is very much worth it. Stop reading and just make your way there NOW!!!
Love...Always stop in when I am in town. Perfect date spot, great for meeting up and moving on or staying the whole night until fat and happy.

In 14 years living in NYC, I haven't eaten Indian food that well-prepared, with that outstanding a spice combination and a fresh-herbed flavor profile.  Just amazing, across the board.   On a trip through NJ with my family, we were so lucky to find Kochi, and I'm writing this with a belly full of it.  We ordered the boneless goat appetizer, the Attirachi Curry, Shrim Milagu Curry, and an  off-menu turkey dish served Varutharachathu. And we tried all the deserts- the carrot halwa being my favorite by far. We ordered all the Kerela dishes, recommended by our host, a very cool friendly South Indian who could speak at length about the spice routes - and the greek, roman, and egyptian archaeology in his state. We asked to meet the chef, a super soft spoken guy named Mathew, also from Kerela, who we thanked like crazy for an amazing night of great food.

I cannot believe that I have not yet reviewed this wonderful, wonderful locale. Here goes: My boyfriend is a *bit* of a beer snob (if there is such a thing. . .?) and I don't really care for beer myself, so as you can imagine it is hard for us to find a place where we will both be happy with what is on tap. Lets just say that: good food + good atmosphere + beer that he likes + beer that i like = VPB!!! I seriously did not think that such a place could exist on this Earth. It is amazing. The food is not bad, either. I love the veggie lasagna, and the pulled pork po'boy is delish! My boyfriend was almost brought to tears the first time he saw bangers & mash on the menu (slight exaggeration!).

Ambiance, drinks, food and service are all spectacular.  In this cool and quaint two story building, you will find a great little bar with an updated, but not too trendy look.  I loved how they pour the wine at the table.  It kind of makes you feel like you are eating at the bar.  Very comfortable there.  We had the oysters, hamachi and grilled romaine apps.  One of us had the sea and shellfood bowl.  You will be amazed.  The wine, beer and drink list is great.  Great place for friends, significant other or a small group to hang out.  Highly recommend.

If you're gonna do something do it right! Fries and only Frites. Some of the best Frites in the city if not the best. Pick a couple or a few of dozens of sauces , ketchups , mayos, you get the idea. They're crunchy and delicious. Perfect munchies!

This has become one of my favorite hangout bars in the whole city. The cocktails are impeccably made and reasonably priced, and the lofty high ceilings/exposed bricks constantly remind you that you're in TriBeCa. Give the Sweeter Heater or the Moroccan Martini a try.

Delicious! It was the Friday after Thanksgiving and what my boyfriend and I wanted more than anything was a meal that didn't have a shred of turkey in it. What we found was super friendly service, delicious sushi and apps and a full bar. This place has boosted to my favorite sushi place in the city. The baby octopus was spectacular! We couldn't finish all the sushi, so our waitress wrapped it up with much care and we had it the next day. Can't write enough good things and can't wait to come back.
Great for brunch and dinner. Staff is so/so friendly but the chef and Food make up for it. Great Eggs Benedict and excellent Coffee selections. Nice relaxing spot in LIC

My experience here was amazing but since the reviews here are plentiful, let me just tell u the best thing was the kiwi sorbet ...amazing. most places dont like to make kiwi sorbet b/c of the seeds.... ...it was addictive (warning though, there's a nut crumble mixed in so beware not only for allergies but the crumble is like a nut shortbread and it actually can overpower the kiwi, I ate around that darn crumble though).

Went here for dinner with my boyfriend  last night and had a fabulous time. I highly recommend the Moroccan mint tea to end the meal. We had the Bronzino (fish) which was excellent. The cous cous with Moroccan sausage was ok but not that exciting. Everything is made right there in front of you basically (the rest is only one room). I would definitely go back.

I've been to the "other" place and loved it.   This place? Service is exceptional.  I mean really really spot on. Food with this menu - eh. We started off with 3 cheeses - they were pretty good. Followed by the artichoke on brioche.  This was actually pretty good too. Then we had the octopus (awful - salty - fishy - slightly chewy) it came with what tasted like pickled celery and capers. We also had the prosciutto and figs.  2 small figs split in half and so much prosciutto we didn't know what to do with the left overs. I wish we had more figs :( Our last small plate was the ribs.  Would have been great if they were slightly warm and not so dry.  It's difficult to eat cold, dry ribs. Oh well.  I'll go back when they change the menu....

Tasty oysters and accommodating service. I came with a group of seven and within a 30 min wait was seated in the happy hour area. The food was fresh and tasty, though I would not recommend the oyster shooter - quite bland and have had much better. Also, the happy hour is only served in the bar area, so make sure you're seated appropriately.

Mark meets the mark on St. Mark's Pl.  Totally catching the party vibe of the neighborhood, the interior is cute if not a bit intimate, although it's basically a burger and beer joint.  But, even the "sliders" are relatively high play, and don't be fooled, their "sliders" are more like the size of a small burger...  I way over-ordered.   The beer comes in overflowing pils glasses for not a lot of money.  The skin-on fries had a surprisingly delicate quality for this more rustic preparation.  And the 4 condiments including BBQ and jalapeno, were a great pairing.  The chef was quite fun to chat with and clearly loved what he was doing. On my list for next time is the pecan pie and the Guinness milk shake...  totally wild and creative idea.  Burgers and fries aren't my usual fair, but this place made it feel worth it...  so did our waitress Donna.

I went in once for their Sunday pizza special.  The owner was grumbling about credit card fees and reluctantly took my credit card.  He made it a point for me to bring cash next time.  With such a poor first impression and unremarkable pizza, I won't be back.  The pizza places in West Windsor and Plainsboro are much better and won't give you grief when you pay with a credit card even if you're there just to grab a slice.

The most unbelievable fried chicken I've ever had. I talked to the chef afterwards and was misty-eyed about what I'd just eaten. He told me he likes to think of his food as orgasms for your mouth and that's pretty much what it was. The mac and cheese, collards and fried green tomatoes were also out of this world and WHAT did they do the bacon to make it look/taste like that??? I'm in love!
One of the best diners in the area

Efficient service and great value. I've been a few times and my favorite dish is the Udon noodle with beef, which comes in a delicious, thick sauce and will run you up less than ten bucks. Bubble tea is the best I've had in New Haven, curries are spicy. Overall a far superior alternative to the relatively nearby Ivy Noodle. This isn't exactly the place to go for warm and friendly service, but they get the job done and I haven't had any problems thus far. Not much in terms of atmosphere either, but I suppose I'm more the type to prioritize taste and value over appearances. And to be fair, the outdoor seating is quite pleasant if the weather is right. Overall, I'd recommend to anyone on a low budget who wants some quick, tasty noodles or curry.

Tasty thai food, great prices.  Now a go-to spot in the neighborhood.  It gets busy, so be prepared for a short wait.  The restaurant can be pretty loud, service was a little slow (but I forgave them since it was packed).  I will be back!

Pretty solid dining experience, but nothing really stood out in any regard.  The best part of the experience was our waiter, I would come back to try their brunch, but wouldn't necessarily come back for dinner.

I am a fan of Michael White but I was VERY disappointed with Osteria Morini and have no plans on a return visit. We know and LOVE Sarah (not our server) who told our waiter to take good care of us, but honestly, he didn't care less. I opened with the farro/bean soup (superb) and ended with the Branzino (good, but nothing memorable).  We also had the Roasted Rosemary Chicken (good, but still nothing special). There is nothing technically wrong with the food, but they are expensive for a casual Italian eatery. The service on the other hand is a major concern. There were several issues (all small in nature) that makes it difficult to accept the $130 price tag (not including alcoholic beverages)  that came at the end of the night. 1)  When we were seated, my partner went to the restroom to wash his hands while the server poured only 1 glass of water.  I thought this was strange and figured he wanted to pour a cold glass, but the water was warm/room temperature. Then when my partner arrived, he never filled his glass.   2)  We ordered a bottle of Pelligrino and the server removed the 2 water glasses (that I was drinking) from the table.  He poured the water, but it was warm.  When we said something, he left, then came back to say it was just unpacked and was not put on ice yet.  The server offered to take it off our bill but we said we just needed ice (and lime), neither came.  Had to ask the server at another table.   3)   Soup comes and we asked for salt/fresh pepper.   The pepper never came, and the salt was less than a quarter of a teaspoon.  It's salt folks.. not truffles. (A salt and pepper shaker would have been fine) 4)  Switched to club soda with cranberry juice.  They brought over a 3 or 4 ounce glass of cranberry juice, then had the nerve to charge $4 for the cranberry juice in addition to the club soda!   Seriously Mr. White... can you step in here and tell me what this is all about?! 5)  Noticed 5 servers just chatting in the corner at one point and no one came in to check in on us, nor did anyone give the impression that they cared.  From the lackluster welcome to the overall service, these are not professionals.  They can and need to take some lessons from Sarah on what it means to be genuine and offer warm, friendly service. 6)  Charged for club soda refills (lame) Oh... and when did coffee become $7! I have no problem dropping $100 for a good meal but this is ridiculous and its time to say STOP! Now I'm annoyed, again!  Stay away!

Worst service and food! My friend and I came by for an early Friday dinner.   Strike 1:  It was hot and we decided to have ice cream floats.  One was coke, one was root beer.  Service messed up the order and then told us to swap drinks - not even offering to make new drinks Strike 2:  We were very hungry and got some biscuits to start off.  The biscuits were rock hard - sort of like when you overheat something in the microwave. Strike 3:  Main course.  We had burgers.  Once again warm and rock hard.  My friend couldn't even cut hers with a fork. Strike 4:  Serve proceeds to sit a family of 6 next to us and basically on top of us at a table that seats 4.  They come with luggage, etc and we are effectively trapped in a table next to the section divider. Strike 5:  My friend gives the waitress our her credit card to just get out of here.  And the waiter proceeds to ring us up on a bill that is $40 more than our bill and refuses to provide an itemized bill. Strike 6:  After having to get the manager over to sort of the bill issue the restaurant does not provide a voided copy of the originally wrong bill. Net:  for the first time ever left a $0 tip at a restaurant and had to call the credit company to report the vendor and the transaction.  Keep away!! Manager's excuse:  we have a new chef and wait staff.

This place is great. Love the beer selection. Love the vibe. Hell, if I were a NY mag critic, I would pick them too! The only thing that I'm disappointed in is that their happy hour used to go until 7pm, so when a hardworking girl like me came home from a long day at work (after 6), she could get $2 off her favorite microbrew. Unfortunately, they changed it to 6pm and I can no longer enjoy the good deal. I feel so left out! Who are these people that get out of work (& get to the bar) before 6? And can they order me a cold one?

I've got to say, I love this place. This is the place my boyfriend and I go to on special occasions. I've been to Italy, and this restaurant is the real deal. If you're looking for American-Italian food and want what we traditionally think of as spaghetti and meatballs, this place may be a shock. If you're looking for flavorful, comforting, creamy, mouth-watering food with a home-like experience, then go to Skappo. I adore the mother, who is the sweetest. Ok I may be biased because the first time she saw me she exclaimed that I was beautiful. She's had the restaurant sing Happy Birthday to my boyfriend, and "send him positive thoughts for the year". One of her sons takes breaks from cooking to play guitar and sing. When I'm there I feel like I'm back in Italy where I spent a few weeks in a remote town, New Haven and "the real world" are light years away. This place is an escape from the "posh" overpriced restaurants and the bro-bars of New Haven. It's pricey but believe me, it's well worth it. I highly recommend the Crostini con Pere e Gorgonzola for a starter, which is toasted bread with pear and gorgonzola that is a blend of crunchy and melt in your mouth goodness. The vegetable soup is usually wonderfully done. Menu items change due to the season, but those are two staples. Everything is fresh and delicious and the best service in town. I've debated writing a review because this place is a great secret, we've never been when it's too crowded but we also don't want to see this place go out of business! The family is so great and deserves much success!

Ehh. Dined there six times. The first time was fun being inside the old bank building. Kind of cool. Food was ok, but pricey. But it seems like the menu rarely changes enough to keep me interested. If I see another one of those oversized white bowls coming out of the kitchen I will fall off my chair. Great restaurants keep innovating, which union league does not. Solid, traditional, boring French food. There are so many better restaurants within a three block radius, why go there more than once? Service ok. Drinks over priced...this isn't nyc fellas. I would say that this is a good choice for a special occasion where the parties have not dined there before. Other than that save your money and go elsewhere.

What can I say about this place except for it is probably the best tex mex place I've ever been to on the east coast. The atmosphere excellent, the service is excellent, the food is very tasty, and the price is just right. I would definitely recommend having the blackened catfish fajita.

Food: 4.5 Stars Being originally from California, my standards for authentic Mexican foods can be high.  El Vez offers authentic dishes which embody good Mexican cuisine.  El Vez offers a variety of options on their menu.  Their guacamole is fresh with a variety of delicious options.  The coup d'état of their menu has to be the 'Tacos Al Carbon for 2'.  The chicken is well prepared and the steak is juicy and flavorful.  El Vez offers quality ingredients and stays true to the basics in Mexican cuisine preparations. Service: 3.5 Stars The service and bartenders at El Vez are considerate and prompt in their service.  Servers are not as knowledgeable about their restaurants food as those in other establishments but provide very good service. Ambiance: 4.5 Stars El Vez has a very chic and unique decor.  Having the bar as the center piece of the restaurant adds to the social environment.  The restaurant is great for dates, casual dining, and going out on weekends for food/drinks.  El Vez is definitely one of the most unique and trendy restaurants in Center City. Price: 4.0 Stars Meals are moderate to high end in pricing but definitely worth the asking price as the quality of ingredient is high, as well.  Drinks are also moderate to high end in pricing but strong, delicious, and properly prepared.  The margarita pitchers are definitely a good option for groups and the bar selection is strong. Location: 4.5 Stars El Vez has a great location in Center City found just east of Broad Street on Sansom.  The restaurant is easily accessible as a center piece of its area.  El Vez is located near other popular bars/restaurants/lounges as well. Overall Impression/ Miscellaneous: 4.0 Stars El Vez is a great restaurant and ideal place to socialize and drink.  The social atmosphere, location, food and drink selections make the venue a top Mexican restaurant in Philadelphia.  The only drawback is the popularity of the restaurant, which is a good drawback to have.  Even though getting a table for dinner can be a long wait on weekend nights, the bar makes waiting an almost pleasurable experience.  I would definitely recommend going to El Vez for dinner and drinks.
5 stars for the pizza alone. The plain pie is perfection. You *might* get better pizza in Italy.

Cash only ! And tepid tap water. So far. very small place, open air, very nice staff just kinda laid back.  i thought both the entrees at the table were decent, i actually enjoyed mine, (the feijoiada), more, as leftovers the next day! caipirinha was decently strong, i had 2, and was pleasantly buzzed. i have attemptedd to come here on a Saturday night in the winter and it was packed to the brim. it was nice on a casual Saturday afternoon .

For what it is, you really can't do any better than this cart. The amount of food is plentiful, the price is more than reasonable, and it is an experience in and of itself. Since most of the other stuff has been hit to death, I'll make a few recommendations: -The lamb is excellent, and the chicken is very good too. -Getting either meat over rice is a bigger meal (and more bang for your buck). That said, the flavor of the sandwich is very good too. What I would do is team up with a friend and split both a sandwich and a meat over rice. Works nicely. -For the love of all that is holy, ask for the red sauce on the side and put it in small amounts at a time. I like spicy more than almost anyone, and putting it in by anything more than a dab from a fork at a time will cause major problems, especially the first time. -Get the white sauce on it there. Damn good. -Be ready for a line. We got relatively lucky both times I went, but be prepared to wait for a while and be ready to want to eat it immediately. All in all, it is some good eats at a great price. If you can live with yourself long enough to wait, taking it into Central Park (just a few blocks north) can work very well too, as long as you bring napkins and drinks to absorb the heat.

A tiny and great place to grab some lunch, dinner, or dessert crepes. You're best to take your crepe on the go because there's 3 stools and one little bench. Although a tiny place, it is a cute place and you get to see your crepe being made. I was looking for something savory, so I ordered a Shrimp Avocado Salad crepe. The crepe had shrimp, spinach, avocado, carrots, wasabi tofu sauce, and Thai chili sauce. It was so pretty, I almost didn't want to eat it. Took a bite anyway and it was delicious. The shrimp avocado was sweet, light, fresh, not greasy, and filling. $9.50 for a delicious crepe is so worth it. The staff makes the crepe really quick once you have made your order. I have to come back and try the sweet crepes.

I can't tell you how good the sliders are because when I'm at Mark my stomach is fairly full of beer and there is room for one thing and one thing only, A GUINNESS MILKSHAKE!! The Guinness milkshake is so delicious and it probably gets you a little boozed up too which can't hurt. The ice cream and everything really brings out the coffee character of Guinness which makes this milkshake so delicious. It's sweet but definitely not too sweet which is exactly how I like dessert to be. The alcohol in the beer cuts the creaminess of the milkshake too which I like. I've also had the espresso shake which was A++ but the Guinness shake has a coffeeish taste to it too and it's made with beer, therefore, it is superior.

My boyfriend's father is a died in the wool, South Carolina, food snob/good old boy type...  A stubborn old school perfectionist  that takes his preparation of meat & shellfish to a level rarely seen in even the most serious amateur chef. He has a meal that he refers to as his Pee Wee Gaskins meal, a meal to end all meals. I have had a few meals at Diner & Marlowe & Sons that will forever stay in my memory, perfectly cooked pork belly with cornbread I still dream about, the most heady coq au vin, a fennel soup, punch you in the face salads, even a humble porgy that has lived in my sense memory. I have never been disappointed  by a meal at Diner or Marlowe & Sons. And, I have always had competent, if not great, service. The places can be obnoxiously over crowded & the music at Diner too loud, but chefs Sean Rembold and Dave Gould definitely makes my list as contenders to make my last meal.

Wow this is such a little hidden gem. Why haven't we met before. Deciced to eat at the bar and perhaps my best decision of the evening. The bartender chip was amazing, informative and friendly . We ate the fluke crudo over apple to start alongside the pate and pickled vegetables. For entree we had the pork tenderloin. This is without doubt one of the best dishes I have had in ages..I truly didn't want it to end Finished with the brioche, pear and ice cream. Perfect finish to a great meal. Drinks are top notch.
