This place actuallly knows how to make real cocktails.I recommend the new fashioned and fake Russian. This could be a one of my top 5 in the  west village. Cosy and non pretentious its a must visit.

Went here for a late dinner (9pm) with some relatives. Atmosphere is casual and upbeat. We didn't have to wait too long to get seated (lucky us given it was the weekend!) I got the steak salad with arugula, endive, red onions, goat cheese, tomatoes, and balsamic. First off, I ordered this because it had pretty much some of my most favorite ingredients (steak, arugula, goat cheese and balsamic!) The dish arrived in a pretty large portion and it exceeded my expectations! The meat was perfectly cooked and juicy. The strong, tangy flavors from the goat cheese and balsamic basically was in harmony with the peppery arugula and clean tomato. I would definitely order this again!

This place is over hyped. Seeing five thousand plus reviews on yelp, I made up my mind to experience the food and ambience at this place. We all know that vegetarians always find hard to have choices on menu. But just one vegetable ramen on the menu. Does that justify the statement on yelp - that vegetarians go nuts for this place? We arrived at this place for a Sunday afternoon lunch, and got a table after 10-15 minutes. Seeing the menu, the staff suggested that the best and only choice will be to have vegetable buns and vegetable ramen. My husband is a non-vegetarian and prefers fish so he opted for a fish appetizer. The vegetable buns were quite good and fish was just OK. Coming to the vegetable ramen - noodles with 2 pieces of sweet deep fried tofu in a wasabi seasoned hot water bowl and no vegetables. I was really disappointed paying fifteen plus dollars for just glass noodles simmered in hot water. The photo would have justified all. My husband was already disappointed with the fish and he decided not to order anything else. Coming to the service, the staff is very friendly and they have a peculiar way of greeting the customers, you will like it. But for me a perfect meal in any restaurant is value for money which combines both food and service. For me it was a disappointing Sunday afternoon lunch. Just to let you know this is not my first time having vegetarian Asian cuisine, have tried Korean, Chinese, Vietnamese and of course Thai and had much better experience at all these places As a vegetarian, I will suggest keep low expectations when you go to this place. If you like it, you will be happy and if you do not, you will not feel bad! :)

Lunch is great - affordable Israeli-inspired cuisine and pretty authentic stuff. Highlights were the chocolate mousse dessert, shakshouka and the Israeli sampler. I've had better hummus elsewhere, but this was definitely good enough and the pitas were warm and homemade which is worth at least a star in my book. Good sized portions, nice decor. Only weak point on food was charging $3 for lamb merguez sausage that was essentially one link cut into small pieces and served in what looked like a mini ramekin - something you'd put ketchup in. Seriously guys, $3 for that? Only less than ideal thing is the unpolished service. Our server was slow at best - at the end of our meal she completely turned her back to a nearly full restaurant to shine silverware at the counter, making it impossible to flag her down. The other server sauntered over and took 10 minutes to get a bill. I have no problem with servers who want to make you feel relaxed and don't rush you, but once I beckoned the second server to help with the bill, my original server went totally missing. No thank you or anything. I'm certain the Israeli owners, who DEFINITELY know a thing or two about service wouldn't have been thrilled to see this happen. I'll definitely be back because I love the food and the ambiance, but it would be nice to see the service mirror what you'd find in a place like this in Israel. :-)

I thought that it would be appropriate for me to let you know how my boyfriend and I were treated today when we went for lunch at your establishment. To start off, we come in there either on our own or with our families at least 3-4 times a month for lunch/brunch/ dinner. When we come we typically bring a bottle of wine with us or we drink water as the great food is the only reason we come there. Today was a different day. It was about 95 degrees out today, a slow summer saturday, and when we arrived at 11:30am there were about 15 tables in total (inside and out) that were seated. We had just got done walking around town and both had two small iced teas in hand, as it was scorching outside. The hostess proceeded to sit us down and mentioned that since we had drinks already, they couldn't be there. I said that it shouldn't matter as we will be ordering lunch and an appetizer, as we normally do. She proceeded to go to the "manager" and let him know about our "outside drinks". He immediately came over to tell us that we could not have them there. I asked "Why not? It's all the same as having wine or water when we come in anyhow." He said it was different, i saw no rationalization in his thought process. Mind you we never leave there spending less than $30 and usually for lunch it's about $40 for the two of us. We immediately picked up our drinks and walked out. Needless to say, your restaurant lost $30-40 AND  your wait staff, which had already been making slim bucks due to the lack of tables, also lost money. It's a shame. We ended up trying Cianci, across the street and will definitely be going back there again as their food was delicious, prices fair and they couldn't care less that we had brought our iced teas in with us. I actually ended up ordering an additional drink from them. We feel unfairly treated and give a lot of business to your establishment. It's just a shame we were treated so poorly by the management.
I went back and its even better. I highly recommend getting the Thai mussels

While it's certainly satisfying, I can't help but wonder...what am I actually putting into my mouth? Look, you get what you pay for, and at $6 bucks a plateful, it's almost equivalent to two whole meals. That said, I wouldn't go out of my way to get it or eat it more than once or twice a month. The real deal: Get the red sauce. Skip the white. Do not think about what's in there.

This place has such a great atmosphere for peaceful studying or having a nice brunch/lunch with friends. They have great bagels and coffee, and the staff is very nice. Overall I love this place, and I wish I still lived in Fairmount so I could go!

Turkish Kebab House likes to keep a low profile because it's "the real deal." So says New Haven's premier food reviewer and his contacts in the local Turkish community. I'm not one to question either of those authorities, but I am here to tell you that the House is well worth the trip for juicy meats, tasty appetizers, and the kind of atmosphere that is at once foreign and distinctly American.

I had brunch a few weeks ago with a girlfriend and it was amazing!! I heard so many great things about Ela and was not disappointed. We ended up sharing a Kobe burger and I believe the braised short rib benedict. Both were deliciously on point.. Can't wait to go back for dinner. Only complaint was the limited wine selection and the bloody marys sounded amazing but didn't live up to their unique descriptions.

Jeera is a very small space- one table for 4 and three tables for 2- which makes it ideal to come with a single friend or for takeout. My drunken noodles were very flavorful, not too oily, with a generous amount of meat and just the right degree of spice. 5 stars for service! Since it was a slow Monday afternoon I was expecting some banter between the kitchen and the front (and hence slower customer service) but all the staff seemed extremely focused on delivering the best experience possible for diners. The host/waiter was extremely attentive and friendly so I always had everything I needed. Will definitely be back!

Taverna Kyclades is one of my husband's favorite restaurants and has been for years but I never reviewed it. We decided to go today as he was off and it is close to my massage place. We haven't been in a few years. We thought since it is not the weekend there would be no wait. But everyone else had the same bright idea we had. We were told it would be a half an hour wait. But we ended up waiting for an entire hour. Because of my health issues I am not up to waiting for an hour. The wait did cause my body distress. We had to wait standing in the cold too. The hostess took our name and added it to the list.  But people came in and were speaking Greek. I happen to understand a little bit of Greek and some of them got there after us. It's similar to the treatment my husband receives at certain Cantonese restaurants where non Cantonese  speaking people have to wait and he goes to the front of the line such as Mei Li Wah in China Town Manhattan. They do give seats more quickly to Greek speaking people even if they show up after you and even if the line is long. So I will not be going back any time soon. My health prevents me from doing so. Having said that the food was still good. But they used to have Fava beans with tomato  sauce on the menu. Now it is Lima beans with sauce. There is a difference to the uninformed. growingtaste.com/vegetab… The sauce was more runny than it used to be. The beans seem to be the only dish that has changed since our last visit. I had the fish of the day. It is the best sea food in my opinion in the 5 boros and though not quite as good as I have had on the Jersey Shore it is much better than any cooked sea food I have had in NYC and any other Greek restaurant in the 5 boros. My husband had the pasta with sea food and agrees. I have been to all of the high end sea food restaurants in Manhattan and pretty much gave up on cooked sea food in the 5 boros with the  exception of Taverna Kyklades. I usually eat sea food on the Jersey shore and it is great! But Taverna Kyklades is a close second. Everything we have ever had here is good. We have had most of the salads and all of their meat dishes between us. The chair I sat in is coming apart and was rocking back and forth. It was too crowded and busy to complain but I am pretty sure it will soon fall apart. Fortunately for me it held up during our meal. But it was pretty uncomfortable. I didn't want to change seats with my husband because the sun was really bright where he was we both had to wear sun glasses (inside) But the restaurant was cold since the door was open due to the long line. The server was really nice and a really hard worker. The bathroom was pretty dirty and the bathroom is small and right outside the kitchen so there is a lot of foot traffic. Today is National cherry pie day so I skipped dessert so I could have cherry pie at home! thenibble.com/fun/more/f…

Lo Monaco's has the best Italian food, period.  No matter what Italian restaurant I eat at, I compare their food to Lo Monaco's.  The ingredients are fresh and the owners are wonderful.  They have a pretty small dining room but my family usually does take out and regularly orders their large trays of food for parties.  The pasta dishes are amazing and the calzones are full of cheese and ingredients.  This is the place to go if you want real Italian food.

We love Tavola! Thanks to other Yelp reviews, we tried Tavola when we were in the city and staying close by. We loved the food (especially the homemade pasta and the "real" thin-crust, toasted, delicious pizza), the service was good, and the atmosphere was friendly and energetic. We only wish they was a Tavola on our side of the continent. I have recommended Tavola to friends, family, and business associates, all of whom have thanked me for the great recommendation. Next time we're in NY, the first thing we'll do is eat at Tavola!

Cafe Gitane is one of my all-time favorite restaurants in New York. My go-to dishes are the avocado toast and the vegetarian couscous. Both are sooo delish! I've tried over and over to recreate the avocado toast myself and I just can't quite match it. Con: It's a pretty small place so it can be a little hard to find a table for dinner/brunch, especially if you have more than 2-3 people. Highly recommend!
Great falafel, will definitely come back! They also have a great juice as a side.

Visited today for the first time for lunch. I had the Rocky Hill hamburger without the egg. It was just ok. I asked for medium rare and it came medium. Another person also had the same experience. The fries that came with it were good but not extraordinary. For the price charged I expected much better. The service was just ok. We were left alone for too long without checking on us. A person in our party had to go get the waitress. All in all the price was too much for the quality of food served.

Before coming to El Rey for the very first time, I had only heard rave reviews about the atmosphere and food. Walking in, I really dig the laid back feel of the place, especially in comparison to other Stephen Starr joints. I ordered the carnitas tacos and was beyond disappointed: portions were surprisingly small, and the meat that was in my tacos was mostly fat -- expected somewhat with carnitas but since the meat is diced/cubed and not shredded, the meal was a ton less appetizing and even with the sauce added, had virtually no real flavor. Super disappointed. May try again, but would not recommend.

I just listed Asiana House in my Yelp profile as the last meal I would have before I die. I think that means I LOVE the place. The house rolls are all amazing and the deep fired tofu and seaweed salad are excellent. The service is not overly fast but well worth the wait. Heading there for my birthday in a couple of weeks! Yay me.

A fun place to visit if you're in the area and you need something to hold you over until your next meal. The frites here come in 3 sizes although a regular cone is more than enough to share if you feel like a light nibble. What makes these spuds fantastic? A crispy shell and a fluffy interior that's what. And there's a treasure trove of sauces available on the side if you like to dress up your fries from rosemary mayo to vietnamese pineapple. They also make a respectable poutine outside of Quebec, if you're looking for the satisfying diner staple in Manhattan. To start with the fries are a nice shape, thickly sliced they hold their own in the dish. The gravy, a tasty chicken base is thick and applied generously in each order. However, the cheese curds here don't pass the 'squeaky' test and are served too cold so they take awhile to meld properly with the fries. There is not much seating inside so take these babies to go and enjoy!

I ate here once years ago and remember thinking it was nothing more than a glorified pizza joint (and not an exceptional one at that). I was surprised to hear this was the location selected for a luncheon to celebrate the service annviersaries of three colleagues. Amalfi's proved to be nothing special. I didn't have pizza but I would have preferred it over the bland and ordinary food. The eggplant rollatini was rubbery and tasteless and smothered in what I truly believe was just unseasoned canned tomato puree. The chicken marsala was equally flavorless, and the sauce was only slightly better than the tomato sauce. This place is obviously afraid to season anything. Garlic is probably not even in their ingredient list. The broiled tilapia wasn't bad, but it wasn't anything spectacular. The best part of the meal was the grilled vegetable medley, unfortunately, the portion size was obnoxiously small. Speaking of which, their ice cream dessert amounted to probably 4 tablespoons of freezer burned low quality ice cream -- not enough to satisfy a sweet teeth. (We stopped at Ed's Creamery in Pennington for the real deal on the way back.) The coffee was so bad I couldn't stomach more than a few sips, but I'm a coffee snob, so that doesn't say too much. For a business luncheon... or any luncheon since the place was pretty much empty, the service was extremely slow and poor overall. The wait staff was unattentive and never came by to check if we needed drink refills, how we were enjoying our meals, or if we needed anything (I resorted to eating my ice cream with a fork because I couldn't wait long enough to ask for a spoon or else I wouldn't need one anymore). Our waiter was spilling coffee from the carafe all over the place as he poured it into mugs. I was thoroughly disappointed and embarrassed to celebrate such an accomplishment for my colleagues here. When I celebrate my 15 year service anniversary in two years, you can bet it won't be here. I hope Villa Francesco's in Pennington will still be open then.

Zero Stars for Bigoted Behavior. There is a serious management problem at Brickyard. On two different occasions I have been with a large group of friends of different races.   In both instances snide racial comments were made by both bar and waitstaff about the race of my friends.  Obviously not to our faces but amongst each other when they assumed no one was listening (ironic considering they are mostly undocumented workers from Ireland).  Even radicalized comments and conversations of customers are not only tolerated but encouraged. It's a shame because Brickyard is an ok bar, but I cannot abide by their bigoted behavior.  It you appear to be anything other than White, Enter At Your Own Risk.
As a californian, this is as good as pizza gets for us! Great NY pizza experience for our first time in NY.   Just wish it didnt get soggy!
Awesome service for the New York standard. Prices are relatively OK. The meals are excellent and will definitely come here again!!!

The food will make you slap your mama! The service will make you kick her while she's down.  Awesome Restaurant all around. I went with two friends we had pancakes, the eggs with apple platter, and their smoked salmon on greens platter. It was so delicious and the service was 6 stars and it came with a drink.  Yaaaaay! Loved our waiter (and he had a cute accent) and the greeter. Well worth the wait for a table. The body Mary's are some ofthe Best I've tasted and the price is very reasonable. Our great waiter took pictures of us and was quite the character and a great cellphone photographer. He really earned that tip. Go there now!

Wow this place is amazing!  Fantastic wines and cheese parings at very reasonable prices.  3 friends and I went after dinner and ended up ordering an additional btl and cheese board bc it was so good. Next time, will have to try the food.   I recommend this place for anyone who likes good wine and great cheese.  I'd go either on the early or late side since it's become so popular.  Our waiter was full of energy and accommodating, even at the late hour we went. We closed it down and didn't want to leave.  Other ppl seemed to have indulged so much in the unforgettable wines that one customer vomit right outside.  That's not a bad thing, I think :) We'll all be back very soon!
Good burger joint that has phenomenal onion rings.

On a tuesday night, close to midnight, some of us wanted something to eat...and there were chicken and waffles to be had at cafeteria.  Despite the fact that all the other restaurants seemed to have taken a sleeping pill and gone off to sleep, cafeteria was packed, lively and the food was good.

I've been wanting to go to this place for over a year, and live in the neighborhood, but every time I walked by they were closed.  Apparently they fixed their weird hours, so I was excited to finally eat lunch there on a weekday. For lunch options the food is overpriced, and the selection is very minimal.  For health reasons I can't eat spicy food and after inquiring about the hot level of the wings I was told (and heard him repeat later to another customer) that they weren't spicy at all and that "a kid could eat them".  He was very wrong.  I even ordered a side salad thinking "well that can't be spicy", but it totally was.  I get that it's a Caribbean place, so yes most things would be spicy, but come on I really only went there to accommodate friends who like spicy things.  Have other options on the menu! Overall maybe I'd go back at night for a drink or happy hour, otherwise I'd skip this place.

OMG Can you believe NYC finally has The Boiling Crab- err, The Boil?! The restaurant is on the smaller size, so if you want a guaranteed seat right away, come right when they open at 5. Especially if you have a large group. Right when you get seated they dress you up with a bib and gloves. My advice, skip those gloves. They're the cheap blue thick plastic ones which you do not want your tongue to come in contact with. I wish they would replace those with clear very thin plastic ones. The food is pretty incredible, the BOIL sauce is more on the garlic-y side. I always get the shrimp in the Boil sauce, which never disappoints. Cajun fries compliments the shrimp perfectly. You can ask for extra sauce and seasoning on anything. Staff is very attentive, although the bus boys are too eager to get your ass out. They magically appeared the second I was finished with my last bite and will take away the  table cloth along with everything else on the table WITHOUT asking you if they can do so. They also stand right next to your table whilst staring at your table so that you feel uncomfortable and leave right away. Also, they don't have drink specials. Cocktails don't taste special enough to warrant the price tag.

My review on this place is not based only on the food, but also the setting that made the meal that much more enjoyable. Sitting with a front row view of Rittenhouse Square on a beautiful fall day with warm heat lamps directly above us while enjoying an already incredible brunch made the entire experience that much more memorable. I would highly recommend this restaurant, especially if its a nice day outside and especially for brunch! Service was also great and all of our meals were brought to the table at the perfect time. We were told we would have to wait 20 minutes but were seated within 3 minutes. The first course consisted of bread that was fresh and crisp to perfection. What stood out as memorable to me was how soft and spreadable the butter was - something that is rare. Usually I battle to soften hard butter or smash it with a spoon onto bread far less warm and delectable. Next up was the French onion soup. The perfect bread-onion-cheese ratio but most importantly not overly salted - something I've found to be common with this soup at other establishments. The cheese was spilling over and crusted all over the bowl in a aesthetically pleasing way and tasted amazing. The smoked salmon tartine was my favorite by far. The salmon had no fishy taste and was perfection, delicately balanced with a variety of toppings and a light, fresh salad. Currently drooling thinking about it. The chicken liver parfeit was also rich and yummy.

"Best $27 burger...it had  better be!" March 08, 2010 - Likes it - Though this is not my scene anymore, it was in the NYU 80's, the Black Label $27 burger is worth the price, if you can believe it. At midnight, we still needed a reservation to get in. Huh? I am usually sleeping at this time. If you like LOUD, young girls in short skirts, GREATEST burger (don't you dare get cheese on it...so the server told me!), mighty fine bone marrow and just a great NY late night scene, then this is for you. I think I can handle it once a year, but boy, 2 days later, I am craving that fantastic burger. So what if it was pricey, it was fabulous! You only live once. Enjoy it!
The only thing I like about this place is their late night delivery.  Its very convenient.  The sushi is decent too.  I've had better but I've also had A LOT worse.
GREAT

The bartender is awesome and hilarious! He made me my non-alcoholic fruity drink, no questions asked, and my boyfriend liked the beer. I don't know what kind he had but he's into special beers. The bean soup I had was so smooth and delicious! I usually don't go for bean soups but this is definitely an exception. I also had the spring salad with spinach and salmon which was also surprisingly good. The outdoor seating area in the back looked nice, but we just sat in the front at the bar.

My husband and I went to Del Monico's tonight for dinner. We both had Filet Mignon, scalloped potatoes and fresh vegetables. A house salad is included. The dinner was  awesome. The prices were great and the staff was excellent. We loved the ambiance. It was a beautiful night, so the doors were open to a beautiful breeze. There is also outside dining. We will definitely be going there again.

I tried two dishes here during my last visit. The cod and the pasta with the eggplant and mozzarella. I would definitely recommend the pasta entree, but the fish was pretty forgettable. The service was great as well and that's why I boosted the rating a star.

Creative Italian comfort food. I had beef stew and leek ravioli. The daily specials were all tempting and as someone who loves fall food, I was excited by their use of squash, pumpkin etc. The standard menu was primarily limited to brick oven pizzas. I watched the bartender wrap blue cheese stuffed olives in prosciutto and then drop the delectable mix into a dirty martini. I will most definitely return for one of those.

Cramped, isn't the word. This place is tiny.  But they say the best things come in small packages right? This place reminds me of your best friends cramped East Village apartment.  That is if your best friend made amazing Indian influenced creative food.  It's tapas style and I have dreams about the ginger scallop dish.  Seriously, it is one of the most interesting delicious scallop dishes I have ever tried.  In fact I could eat this dish every day for the rest of my life and be the happiest girl on the earth--yes, it is that good. Come here with only one, maybe two other people and prepare to be greeted by the super friendly chef and eat food that will delight and challenge your tastebuds.
I've only eaten at the bar, which is very small, and the food was ok.  With so many choices so close by, I would opt for somewhere else

La Viola is a cute restaurant with good service, good for a big group (which is rare in Philly). The food was just okay, pretty middle-of-the-road quality Italian food. Nothing terrible but a little pricey for what you got. The food came quickly though, the waiters were kind and accommodating.

Not bad, although I've never ordered pizza here.  I always get the gyro which is nothing special when sober, but superb when not.  Advice: go get wasted first, then come here. I kinda like the unshaven dude-with-a-'tude behind the counter.  He's definitely a no BS type and I'm quite partial to the impersonal business approach.   It's an ugly place, but if you're drunk enough, chances are you won't even notice. Gyros-away!

I found this place the day before I was leaving New York City and it was my favorite thai restaurant! The mojitos were fantastic, the apps were great, the pad thai was DELICIOUS! yummmm I wish I was still living there so I could go again!
I just really have nothing bad to say. Evenings spent with wine and snacks outside Tria are always amazing. The waitstaff is fabulous, too.

Ajihei serves the tastiest sashimi and nigiri around the Princeton area in my opinion.  I find their fish usually explodes in my mouth flavor-wise, which I can't say for every sushi place I've been to.  I'm especially a fan of the salmon at this place.  I also like their donburi.  Their roll selection is a bit limited, which I am fine with, but for some people who are more interested in extravagant rolls you may want to go elsewhere.  If you are looking primiarly for fresh tasting nigiri and sashimi though I can't think of a better place. The place does get crowded though, both between popularity, the small seating area (maybe 25ish people can fit?) and the fact that there is only 1 sushi chef, who is admittingly in my opinion a great sushi chef but he's still only one.  The wait staff is fairly good at filling drinks, but they too seem to only have 2 or so at a time so they can get busy.  The decor is nothing much to write home about, and the lack of an actual sushi bar where we might be able to talk to the chef is a little disaappointing, although with the traffic the place gets he probably can't justify spending too much time talking while business is going on. Food arrives about as fast as you can expect with just a single sushi chef, which might be a bit longer than you are used to and depending how many people are there.  Definitely give it a try if you are around the Princeton Area and love sushi but it can be a bit expensive, a bit crowded, and a bit slow.
Very tasty, a must if you want to try something different and get the V.I.P. treatment! Very friendly staff and will definitely  be coming back again!!

New (Jan. 2011), fantastic full scale taqueria and Mexican restaurant in Fair Haven. As authentic as it gets: Mezcal and Taqueria #2 quality. Note to all, this place is all about the food, no liquor license yet. Venture away from the burritos, try the chilaquiles, tacos (de lengua or buche, this latter cut is delicious and hard to find), and the vegetarian options too, the produce is super fresh!   You know good things will follow when you are served warm chips with fresh homemade chile salsas to start. Clean, simple decor, and friendly service.

My friend and I used to have a "yak @ Yak" night every week. We'd meet, order momo, and catch up on a week of chit chat covering everything from boys to work to what to do with the extra fuzz between Brazilians. Regardless, yak provided a great ambience, even if the live band was a bit loud at times. After all, the mostly Tibetan and Nepali patrons seemed to really dig the live music! The momos are good, but not as great as some of the nearby take-out ish spots. And the ambience is great (aka it's a gentrifier's dream come true!). The chai is nothing to e-mail Kathmandu about, btw.
What an incredibly odd & eclectic menu.  Food was pretty good and the wine/liquor selection is good too.  Nice atmosphere, even if it's a little loud.

My family and I tried Pig & Prince for the first time last week.  We were intrigued, since its chef is not only a Nutley native but also a Chopped winner, and we had heard good things.   First off, the converted train station interior is gorgeous.  I kept gazing up at the rafters.  The place was not very crowded, but it was a Wednesday night; I'm sure a reservation is a must on the weekends.  Our server was friendly and attentive without being overbearing. Most of the people in my party ordered one of the impressive meat dishes, including wild boar, venison, and duck.  All the entrees came with really interesting, creative, and most importantly delicious side dishes.  Everyone loved their meals, and I definitely want to go back and try some of the inventive risottos.   We got some desserts to share, most of which were great, although the breakfast cereal custard did not go over too well.  The cheese platter we got as an appetizer was a little underwhelming too; I liked the dipping sauces more than the cheese, and there wasn't enough of them. Overall, the food and service were excellent, but the prices were definitely special-occasion-only.
When I first found this place, I was going a few times a week. Mainly for their sesame tofu lunch special. It's really spacious and the staff is really great.
The Stache pizza is soooooo good!!! Great wine selection. Nice service. Love it.

Today, my friend Kate ordered a gluten-free pizza. Two slices in, she noticed deep fried vegetable bits throughout the pizza. Kate has Celiac disease so being gluten free is not an option. She brought the pizza back and the chef gave her quite a hard time about it. He told her that the vegetables were all mixed in and that "there's nothing we can do" except make another one -- puzzling, considering that a second pizza would have the same effect. Kate is now ill because of this pizza and will be for the rest of the day. After much wrangling, your chef finally agreed to give Kate a gift card but not her money back. A gift card for more gluten, perhaps?!

by far the freshest sushi I have ever tasted.... this place is straight up authentic so if you are looking for a trendy, dimly-lit joint with fancy rolls and an extensive sake menu, then it is not the place for you... this is for the diner who truly wants to experience the best flavors and really appreciate the fish and all it has to offer... decor/service/portion size? nothing special.. it's the music in your mouth that will want you coming again...

Yum!  The rice platters are great for the occasional splurge in midtown.  The empanadas are delicious and cheap.  The Cuban sandwiches hit the spot.  Stilllll not the best I've had but when I'm having a bad day at work... this is the place I'm going to eat at during lunch.

Love this place! The tacos. The margaritas. The bartender. The service. Seems to always be packed but we got a table rather quickly and I'm so glad we waited. I love Mexican food. I don't know what to say...I just do. I never get tired of it, but I don't always get amazed by it...and this spot...well, this spot came close to amazement for sure. It was a good time. Great energy...great atmosphere...and seriously delicious food and drinks. I'm sitting home in the midst of Blizzard Nemo just wishing I could be at Taqueria instead...thanks a lot Nemo...you're really ruining my day!!

Food is consistently good but I wish they would go back to the "Jersey Diner" menu I loved as opposed to the current, limited "bistro-like" menu.  Burgers are good (especially the turkey burgers for those of us who like to watch our diets) and are served on 'baked-in-house' rolls.  Omelettes are very good too, but I do miss the diner mainstay open-faced sandwiches (turkey, roast beef, etc).  My wife and I loved coming here twice-weekly but the prices seemed to have gone up quite a bit while the menu has shrunk.  We still go, but maybe once a month.  We now prefer to travel a bit out of our way for our 'Jersey-diner-experience' fix.

Rarely have I been treated with such a sour and unfriendly welcome. I went to Garces the other day to meet someone for a Happy Hour cocktail at 5:30. I walked several blocks to get there in the 90 degree heat and when I arrived, I was exhausted and thirsty. When I walked in, there were literally TWO other customers and about 20 staff on hand. I said, "Hi, I'm meeting someone here in a few minutes. Could I have a seat?" The hostess would barely make eye contact with me and said, "Do you have a reservation?" I was made to feel like since I didn't have a reservation, it was unlikely that I was deserving of a seat in this fine dining establishment. The drinks were okay. The wait staff was friendly. But I will never go back.

Hmpf. $40 steak... nothing special. The attitude of the host before my group of four even sat down was more than enough to sour my opinion of this place and the unmemorable meal did nothing to elevate it.  The host refused to seat the three others in my group until I sat down... even though they pointed at me through the window since I was on my phone.  When I got in, I couldn't find them since the "waiting" area was at the back of the bar.  The same hostess (I'll call him that) that banished my group back there SAW me walk in, wander around, and then go back outside, and did nothing to direct me their way.  Our server was quite nice, but she couldn't remove my bad mood from her coworker and the about-average steak certainly didn't make me feel better either. Nice decor though.

I'm not a fan of places with glitzy decor like Room Service.  There's some kind of cognitive dissonance between the food I'm eating at the ambiance of the place.  Regardless, seating was well spaced out (the chairs suck though), service attentive, and food delicious.  Food, of course, is the most important thing at any restaurant and Room Service delivered. Surprisingly, for such an [attempted] elevated environment, the food wasn't that expensive.  Probably the only thing that I felt was a ripoff was the mojito I got.  It was good and boozy... but yeah, a mojito is a drink anyone can make at home so now that I think about it, I'm not even sure why I got it. This place, because it's in Hell's Kitchen and kind of hip, usually has a wait for tables.  I'm not sure what their reservation policy is but if you're going with a date the wait shouldn't be that long.  Order yourself a silly mojito while you wait on your date.  It's definitely a decent date spot.  I was seated in a dark nook, which was kinda cool.  Dark nooks attract, or at least can let you get away with, certain kinds of behavior.  Yeah so, ladies meeting their first okcupid date at this place... serial gropers will be even more encouraged in this dimly lit restaurant! lulz.
I see they now have an unlimited mimosa brunch deal...can't wait to go back to try it!

One of my favorite places in NYC! Waiters are very nice and speaks good Japanese! 1 time out of hundreds, I experienced that my dish was not enough hot, and told this to the Japanese chef (because I was at the counter table). He was very sorry and happy to change my dish ASAP. Very good service, good foods & reasonable!

Loved this place!! My husband and I walked past at dinner time and saw their happy hour special which is appetiser, entree and drink for $15!! The food is so delicious, service amazing and ambience is romantic. We had the stay chicken skewers and vegetables spring rolls to start and then had pad thai and 5 spice chicken. All the food was so yummy!

Delicious dog! I got the Philly and everything was grilled to perfection! This is a real authentic dog, not like the stuff you get at the Costco food court or an MLB game. I loved that the bun was grilled, and it was the right amount of bread per meat and toppings. Your dog even comes in a little paper holder, which helps keep everything in place when you are eating.
My neighborhood "barbershop."

I was excited to try V street in the first few weeks of opening.  Although I'm not a vegan, I have really enjoyed Hip City Veg, Charlie was a Sinner, Vedge, and Blackbird.  Also, shout out to Blue Sage in the burbs, check it out if you get a chance.  Back to V Street... The set up is interesting, I got there first so put my name in, and they took my cell phone number, so you can actually leave to grab a drink somewhere else if the bar is full.  Apparently the bar had a wait list as well which was confusing.  I tried to sit down when some people got up, but was told I couldn't.  I was not a fan of the beer and wine list.  When there's a wait list at the bar, and a wait for a table, it's tough to ask the bartender any questions, so some better descriptions would be appreciated.  I ordered the cider which was super sour.  I actually felt really bad because it was my mistake but I did send it back and switched to the Riesling which still seemed off, but I wasn't going to send another drink back.  My friend had a red but it was super chilled.  The fancy cocktails looked good and I'll definitely try one of those next time.  At the table I had the pumpkin beer which was also a little sour, but interesting.  I guess next time I need to google things before I order them. As for the food, I loved the Langos, it's like a vegan gyro.  The crunchy papadums were light and airy, the jerk trumpet mushrooms tasted like BBQ, and the mushroom dan dan noodles were great.  We tried a few other things too, the only dish I wasn't a fan of was the carrot choripan. I'd probably go back for happy hour and get more of the Langos and the papadums.  Price was $50 each for a group of 5 who had several beers.  The staff was friendly, especially the hostess.  She checked in numerous times to update us on the wait.

I just got back from eating here, the food, as usual, was great, the service however is another story. We sat down and got our food, 5 minutes into chowing down; I felt something on my arm, I looked down, and a huge cockroach was walking across the table and my plate. It was a reaction to say "oh my god, that's a huge cockroach" I didn't mean to call attention to myself, but when you look down and see that, it's kind of a reaction. After that, I continued eating. I work in the service industry and I realize that these things happen. The cockroach probably cam from outside, since the restaurant looked clean, and it's a pretty open space. That didn't really bother me. What did bother me is the way the two girls behind the counter handled it. They looked at me scowling, like I was trying to ruin everyones meal, one of them even looked at the other and said "did that really just happen?". Now, I did not, and wouldn't ever ask for anything to be comped off the bill, as I know the wait staff didn't put that roach on the table, but jeez. At least come over and say, "sorry about that huge disgusting bug that just ran across your plate", at least share a laugh about it. Instead they treating me like I was a total jerk for being grossed out. Kinda a bummer I won't be coming back because the food was great, what a shame.

I loved this place!  I did come after the usual lunchtime rush has had its fill, so I really can't say how they hold up under pressure, though... The waiter was very friendly, but he seemed a little confused; at one point he brought us a Coke and Sprite which we hadn't ordered (we'd stuck with water).  It was an honest mistake, I suppose, but five minutes later I saw a waiter bring the wrong pizzas to another table. The pizza itself was fantastic, although they could have been a little more generous with the toppings, considering the price and their reputation.  Overall, though, I was pretty satisfied, despite my inability to taste the crushed red peppers.

I went there for breakfast based on the yelp reviews. Food was mediocre at best. Service was with a smile. Very busy, loud, and not enough room. I ordered my food to go because of this. When I got a table a hundred feet down, I opened my styrofoam container to fin

Easily 4 stars (if you're looking for a good restaurant with a relaxed vibe). Depending on the occasion, maybe even 4.5 stars (if you're looking for an intimate lounge with tasty food). I expected something along the lines of Sakagura (low-key, underground, deliberate decor). Instead I walked into a bare-walled squarish room that felt a lot more like a cafe/teahouse (think Cha-An or Radiance) with low lounge chairs, a zen garden in the alcove, and bossa nova in the background. This is a great date spot; I'd suggest a table for new dates and the bar if you want to sit closer (the tables are a bit long so you feel like you're further away from the person across from you than you would normally be). Cocktails were deliciously refreshing. I loved the Type C (yuzu yuzu yuzu!). For food, we ordered a la carte: miso cod, oysters, uni croquette, wagyu short rib sashimi, assorted sashimi of the day, uni & ikura rice, and, of course, Japanese pickles! I'm glad we skipped the tasting menu, which seemed a bit boring and included Morimoto-style veggie fondue, mini burgers, and pannacotta. I would highly recommend ordering a la carte and sharing a greater variety. It's a short menu so it's probably possible to try everything between 4 people. While I can't say I would return for the food alone, I enjoyed everything we ordered and expressed my fair share of yummies & exclamation marks. Given the attentive service and the comfy ambiance, I see myself returning more than just once.

Kind of pricey. I guess I expected a ridiculously huge sub for $9 but it was about a 6incher...well loaded steak & cheese, pretty edible although the meat quality was kind of meh. The place just feels skeevy, bad vibes, etc. - the doorway into the place looks like a black hole tattoo & hep B parlor.  It's pretty chilly inside, and the fluorescent lighting doesn't warm things up at all. Drab, in a word.  Then, the God posters on the wall in the dining area are just...odd. I'm not especially anti-religious, but I tend not to patronize businesses that push religion...kind of a conflict of interests, I guess. If you get stuff to eat in, don't expect plates - your food will come out as if it were to go, albeit without the plastic bag.  Fold out the greaseproof paper and go to town.
love this place and has great service and staff

Todays brunch were really good! We had the homemade Mozarella, Greek yogurt w granola, Frittata and French Toast, everything was really good. Good espresso and ok Bloody Mary. The pastries were so fresh. The brunch is way better than the dinner!

My dream restaurant. Just go - I can't imagine how you'd be disappointed. Puts California to shame! Service - immaculate. Each dish described down to every detail (if you want to hear it). Great recommendations from our server as well, we followed almost all of them and were not let down. Food - phenomenal. Rare combination of 5 stars across the board! Loved the creativity and emphasis on farm-to-table. And the wines...yum. Ambiance - loved it! Busy but not too loud/crowded, very nicely done. We loved it so much we tried ABC Cocina the next night. Also great but quite as good in my opinion.

For those of you that don't know what bibimbap is: It's a Korean dish composed of seasoned vegetables and Korean marinated meat (or tofu) over a bed of rice. Then you mix it all up with gochujang (Korean chili pepper paste) and enjoy! Now my reivew: Sometimes I'm just jonesing for some Korean food and this place always hits the spot. The owner is very nice and always accommodating. They have decent sized portions and the vegetables are always fresh and well seasoned. Definitely one of my go tos when I want bibimbap. It's also extremely quick and healthy so I never feel guilty after eating here. Everyone should give this place a try!

Cheap,great quality dumplings had the fried pork and the boiled shrimp dumplings delicious and a bottle of snapple $5.25 OMG. The only drawback super tiny area where u can sit, but who cares at these prices. Will be back soon

Jury duty in the cold NYC winter meant only one thing - I could finally grab a cheap weekday lunch in Chinatown! Entrees here sell for as cheap as $5 a bowl for the basic vegetable & egg noodle soup. I ordered the #1 House Special Noodle Soup, only $7.25 for a delicious bowl of knife cut noodles, ox tail, beef tendon, tripe, beef slices, and a fried egg. I wish the egg was more over-easy, but the tendon and beef slices were great. The noodles were also too soft for my liking, but I think that's a matter of preference. The older generation of Chinese people just really like their noodles soft, but I need that al dente texture. The noodle shop keeps a container of cilantro on every table, and I was not shy about shoveling spoonfuls and spoonfuls of the herb into my beef broth. The broth is on the lighter side and one of the better broths I've had in Chinatown. When you order, you have the option to get hand-pulled, knife cut, or rice noodles. Definitely try the knife cut noodles - I love the irregular length and texture of the noodles. If you sit near the kitchen you can see the chef slapping the dough against the table and pulling the dough into long noodle strands. What's the secret ingredient to making that springy, chewy Chinese noodles? "Jian shui" ("kan sui in Canto), aka lye water, is high in alkaline and gives the dough that yellow, chewy texture. It toughens up the dough and gives it that nice firmness. If you make noodles at home though and decide to add in lye water, be careful!! Lye, depending on the concentration, can cause severe burning or blindness. An easier alternative is to use dehydrated baking soda instead of lye. I had no idea they had seating downstairs until I saw a group of 10 magically disappear behind me. Next time I'm trying the pan fried noodles.

My cousin brought me here as one of her favorite places and I left a fan as well.  This is the perfect place for a summer afternoon. The outdoor seating area is huge, with tones of picnic tables both under and outside the overhang.  If you want a quick service go with the half pie.  Ready to go all you need to is grab a few drinks, paper plates, and napkins and go to town.   Definitely go for the center pieces.  I started with an outside piece, and was a little unsatisfied at first, but as soon as I moved onto my 2nd (and last) piece (an inside one), I could totally see what my cousin was talking about.  Great doughy crust with a nice layer of sauce and cheese - all you really need for a good slice of pizza.   The leftovers were just as good as the first go around - a key component in a good pizza place.   This is not the place to go for gourmet pizza, service, or decor, but for a summer chill afternoon, it's pretty perfect. They also carry Spumoni, which makes this the full italian experience

Seriously Sally's??? I love how people try to make a competition between Pepe's and Sally's when really there is none. Although I had been to Pepe's several times and loved it each time, I thought I would see what the hype is all about and honestly I went in with my eyes open. Although Pepe's line is always much longer, Sally's seemed to move 10x slower. Seriously in a line of 10 people it took us over an hour and 1/2 to be seated. Once seated, the server was just not nice, and there was one or maybe two for the entire dining room which was filled. I am used to New Haven style of pizza so I like a little crisp/burn to my edges but once this pizza finally came out it was literally charred! You could not even distinguish toppings! Rather than complain to our absent waiter, we decided to just leave, vowing to never come back.

So this place has too many things on its menu to not go...but when the Times said its biscuit belong in a "biscuit museum" I knew I had to check it out. The place is small - dark, kinda that dive bar aesthetic...but in a cute way...but after that, all similarities end.  We sat at the bar - just because I enjoy doing that...and the bartender Rob was super nice and accommodating (it did get very busy & crowded.)  Service was great. I guess the menu is changing constantly - I happened to be sitting next to a guy who is an investor in the place (I didn't know that at first) but there were so many things on the menu I wanted -- he overheard us and made some recommendations - he was quite the salesperson but his recommendations were spot on, so kudos to him & his super smart investment! I love short ribs, period.  They have short ribs...and this short rib comes with a potato pirogi!  uh, you had me at hello!  The short ribs were tender - not braised in a wine sauce, though.  Caramelized onion topping...but regardless, you won't need a knife. I love pretzels.  Whatdya know?  They have a handmade pretzel-- but it gets even better!  It comes with sausage!  The only way you can improve upon carbs is to throw some sort of sausage or pork product with it...and they did! You're like stop.  but wait, there's more...They have fried chicken... It's a whole half chicken.  My friend likes the dark meat - so she took the thigh and the leg, while I had the boneless breast... but come on, fried chicken is about the crispy skin...and that was delish - oh the chicken breast was very tender too!  Just when you're thinking, wow, fried chicken that is juicy and crispy...it gets better!   There's this biscuit that is fluffy and buttery - and tender...but to me had a pork flavor to it (do they use lard?) is that not butter but bacon grease that's slathered in the middle?  I'm not sure, so I guess I'll have to go back and keep trying them. For dessert we had the sticky toffee pudding...now I'm a sticky toffee, bread pudding dessert eating kinda gal - so this was caramel-y and delicious. PLUS they give you a cookie at the end - a chocolatey rice krispy-ish yummy cookie. There are still so many other things on the menu that I need to try...they have gumbo, bacon peanut brittle, wild mushroom flatbread- which smelled awesome - I saw two people order it.  Homemade potato chips, a pork belly appetizer... I think I might change my name to 'Redhead.' WIth the food above,  two half bottles of prosecco and a redhead fizz cocktail (that was light and had my fav elderflower liquor in it)  came to $55/person with tax, tip, etc. And note: they don't serve food on Sundays - but I was told they will start sometime next year...

Hungry...dinnertime...Steak Kebobs... the meat was juicy and sauce was flavorful... but be forewarned, they're a bit messy. Meat juices/sauce tends to leak out the back. $7.50 total. Food is served wrapped in foil on paper plates, but they do bring it to you. Also, the guy at the counter gave me and my friend a free sample of Fiddle Heads. That's probably not the norm, but it was a nice bonus. Ahli Baba's doesn't have a whole lot of seating. They're the tall, bar-like tables that are not conducive for long conversations or dinner, but perfect if you're eating alone or want a quick bite.
Super small but it felt cozy rather than cramped. Get the lamb sandwich!!!

My sister and I decided to eat at Sobaya when I visited her in NYC last week. We both grew up in Fukuoka, Japan and are pretty picky about Japanese food, particularly when it comes to soba and udon. This place was incredible and delivered us with some yummy food! We started with the agedashi tofu, and she got the kitsune udon while I got the ebi tempura udon. While the broth was a bit more smoke-flavored than I would normally prefer, the shrimp was cooked perfectly and her kitsune was delicious. Not gonna lie - I was jealous that she got a fish cake in her noodles and I didn't! The only reason why I'm taking off a star is because of how pricey this place is. I understand it's New York, so things cost more, but we ended up paying around $80 for two bowls of noodles, a small tofu dish, and a small house sake. With that said, I will likely visit again the next time I come back to the city! Oishisoo.
Good coffee, solid breakfast and lunch choices, and cute ambience.  The food is always tasty and service is always friendly.

A very good standby when you have guests in town - a celebrity chef name and very nice servers.  The salads/appetizers are fine, but the $23 pasta special is a nice change and there are likely to be at least two pastas you want second helpings of...Cramped space and yes, I did see a small bug crawling on the wall (it is on the bottom floor of a townhouse in the theater district restaurant row after all)...

I'm so happy I decided to check this place out before moving out of my Rutherford apartment.  I will definitely be back even though I'll be living in Hoboken soon. First- the service. Our waitress Jessica was awesome. Not realizing how late it was, we went in about half hour before closing with a bottle of wine. As someone who's been in the business a while, I know how fast I would've rolled my eyes at the sight of a couple coming in so late. But not Jessica. I felt bad and offered to order our food to-go, but she was so nice and accommodating that I didn't feel uncomfortable staying. Kudos to Jess for being patient, attentive, and friendly.   Now onto the food. We started with the artichoke special. YUM. I don't know why more places don't fry artichokes. But the real star was the burger. I looooove me a good burger. Since it was my first time i had to keep it basic so I ordered the classic Americano with American cheese.  Also had the fries with truffle aioli. Jess recommended the Filipino burger for my friend which I tasted and it was delicious! My burger was cooked to a PERFECT medium. Juicy, flavorful, and fresh. The fries were outstanding and don't even get me started on the truffle aioli. Must. Try. Truffle. Aioli. Soooo good. The Filipino was really flavorful, but just a heads up to you medium rare fans out there, the Filipino has pork in it so they can only cook it med well plus. This doesn't change the juiciness however. Overall, it was a great experience. Food was awesome, totally worth the few extra bucks you'd pay for fast food somewhere inferior. The place itself is bright and cute, plus great service. Oh, and byob is always a huge plus. It's also right across from Mason's Cellar so go grab yourself a bottle of wine or some craft beer and give this place a try. It's absolutely the best burger you'll have for miles. A+ Can't wait to experiment with the rest of the menu next time

all the food are inexpensive,  and good quality! ! Love it. The place is clean, good music. Specially the pineapple pork is my favorite.  A tilapia entrée is only $8, it's not bad at all. It came with two pieces fish, and the  fish are in a nice sizes too.

Really great place for yakitori. The interiors are serene and refined. Sit at the bar and watch the master chefs at work. The specials are written in Japanese on wooden plaques hanging on the kitchen wall, which are turned when the item is sold out. All of this make the place so authentic. The yakitori is superlative, and remember to choose whether you want the skewers grilled with salt or sauce (I recommend sauce). If you are feeling adventurous, try the chicken cartilage or other innards. If not, get the beef, chicken, or other vegetables. The wait can be insane, so plan accordingly.

I had a wonderful experience here. I loved the small appetizer special option, where you could try any 3 apps for $22 . The sausage and broccoli rabe was my favorite. It was spicy! The fried calamari was cooked perfect and my sangria was delicious. I ate at the bar and we received 20% off our check which was nice! I love good food but even better a good deal on good food! I would go again!

I literally can't believe what I'm reading - is this place owned by someone in NYC whose ass we love to kiss? Because i certainly would like to know. That ass must be terrific. NEWSFLASH: The King Is Naked. No amount of talking about its fine invisible clothes ( tasty food ) would change the fact that it is a rag (crappy, overpriced food). It is the place that makes deep fried bacon taste uninspiring. Let that sink in. That's right. What should be an orgasm inducing experience for any non-vegan ( and immediate run for the hills experience for the later ) has been reduced to that fleeing feeling of money going through one's fingers paired with a though "Should. have. gotten. take. out". The only two things that are going for this place are decor and the bartender. Decor is great. Loved it the moment we walked in. Hell, it really put us in a good mood where i nearly convinced the date that we should get a table but being the people who go out more in a month than most we opted for the bar ( service at the bar in good restaurants is always infinitely superior to the service at the table. If the restaurant is lousy the bartenders still tend to do better ). We were right. The service was fantastic. The bartender was a doll with the only unfortunate part being her need to be placed in a box and match ze expectationz of ze establishment. Now the uglies: 1. Oysters. Oh. My. God. Have you heard of this thing called "Interwebz"? Marvelous invention. It has this thing called "youtube" which has tons of how to videos - here's one the kitchen prep staff needs to watch urgently: youtube.com/watch?v=Uy-r… That's right. The clowns could not shuck an oyster properly - they forgot to slide the knife under goodies to separate the goodies from she shell. I know, who expects the oyster on a half shell to actually slide?!?! What kind of a preposterous idea is that? Well, apparently, it is the same kind of preposterous idea as the one that says "There shall be no sand in the oyster." I guess no one bothered to check. I mean why would the kitchen do that?! It... it... it... just may force the cook ( the place has no chef, trust me ) to come up with a new item to deal with sandy oysters ( hello, it is called weather. you have to pay attention to that when ordering your goodies. I know. It blows my mind too, and I'm not a chef. I'm just OK with a knife. Oh and another thing. The shells laid on the frisee. 2. Snapper crudo.  I feel I shall again refer you to the interwebz - this time the lovely site known as lmgtfy.com. See, we can enter lmgtfy.com/?q=red+snappe… and magical things happen. Dozens -- no, probably hundreds --  of recipes to serve as inspiration ( or to rip them fair and square ). You know what all of them have? All of them have this magical ingredients known as  *seasoning* aka salt, pepper, maybe some other spices. Maybe some marginally well distributed lemon zest. Even that would work... but how the hell do you get all the zest into a single clump one person out of two manages to ingest completely and fully? Oh, well, if you are at the Red Cat on Friday night you totally get a single clump of the zest and nothing else... no salt.... no pepper... no seasoning... but but but wait, you know what we have ? Frisee! That's right, we have frisee! Don't you think it is lovely and green and tasty?! Oh wait, you mean you, like, had it before. So you know that in the unseasoned way it tastes like crap... Well, you aren't our usual customers - it seems they would have a hard time distinguishing tilapia from salmon if the salmon was cut thin. 3. At which point we arrive at... head cheese. Pathetic. Uninspiring. Unseasoned. Utterly forgettable.  If there was any "crispy egg yolk" it must have been there on a quantum level where if observed it were to change its form and disappear. However, you know what it did have? Frisee. That it certainly had. 4. And finally the star of the show... Bacon. Tempura. One's mouth is supposed to water just at the thought. Except that we are at the Red Cat, where the cooks like using terms that they don't understand - somewhat akin to a 5 year old using  "thermonuclear reaction" to describe himself taking a sip of a warm milk. There was nothing "tempura" like about it. Hell, there's more tempura-ish things at the "warm prepared food" buffet of Whole Foods. But you know what it did have? That's right. Frisee. Because it is frisee that makes the experience so awesome and wholesome that one wants to come back. Frisee makes world a better place. We thanked our lucky stars for not committing to do the entire dinner and moved on.

The specialty pizzas are quite delicious; the one we had was something like a vegetable combo with yummy feta and sun-dried tomatoes.  Others ordered a pizza margarita which is quite possibly the most patriotic looking out of the others I'd seen before; nevertheless it looked great.  Here I was also introduced to fried ravioli which everyone should try at least once.   The prices, I think, were as expected, although the service could use some tweaking; a sharp ear for taking orders correctly is absolutely key.  In addition, the typical paper plate distribution once the pizza arrived, at first, evoked a negative recollection of other rundown (which this place isn't) pizza joints, but having noticed that the placemats too were made of paper, I realized I shouldn't have expected fine china.  Come to think of it, why even use placemats at all?  No biggie.

I've enjoyed every meal that I've had at Beau Monde.  The beautiful decor, friendly service, and delicious food makes this place a perfect setting for any type of get-together. The last time I went, I couldn't decide between two different sweet crepes.  The waiter actually surprised me by combining the two different types of fruit that I wanted into a single delicious crepe! Overall, an excellent experience every time--and a go to place to bring out-of-town friends.

This restaurant is a solid 3 stars.  First off, just getting inside was utterly confusing.  There was a sign out front that pointed to the back, so we went around the back and ended up in the bar.  If we would have gone in the front (which seemed to be blocked off with huge flower pots right down the center of the stairs), we would have ended up right in the dining room - which is where we wanted to be.   The food was good, but I felt like it was a bit overpriced for bar food.  And, it is bar food.  Albeit with a Hungarian flair.  Honestly, it's been less than a week and I don't even remember what I ate.  So, that pretty much sums up my meal - neither good nor bad enough to remember.  I do remember that my Mom got a Hungarian Kolbász sandwich.  The sausage was pretty good, but the accompanying kraut was just ok; It would've been better if it had been cooked with the sausage and not just by itself.   Also, the waitress, while nice, couldn't tell us what the special "pork roll" was.  Both my Mom and I are originally from Pittsburgh.  We don't have pork roll there.   And, when my Mom asked, the waitress looked at her like she was an alien and said "Well, it's pork roll.  Seriously?  You don't know what pork roll is?".  Awkward...

This is some seriously fresh and deliciously prepared food. The medium rare duck breast is one of the best things I have ever tasted. The Locke is a spin on a mimosa that hits your palette with ease and specificity, and the Argentine pizza was a treasure I won't be forgetting anytime soon.

A mom and pop store with home made Mediterranean goodness. Discovered this place through Paypal promotion - $5 credit! So on my way to aycd brunchy with my bestie, decided to make a quick stop. I went with a small home made hummus to take home. The hummus was the perfect dip for my carrot sticks (i'm sure for all the pita chips/bread too!). Creamy yet light  - i think i can just eat a container of it all on its own. Will definitely stop by again to try all the small dishes on the menu!
Great for a grown-up night out.  I always get the Mandalay Curried Chicken Salad for lunch.  Their salads are delish.  Desserts are super delish.  Nice piano music.

This place is absolutely beautiful. I went to ABC Kitchen on my recent weekend in New York.  My friend and I just wanted the salted caramel sundae and a glass (or 2) of wine, which we told them as we walked in. They led us to the cutest little "dessert table" in the back corner of the restaurant, complete with sweet little pieces of china.   The sundae was heavenly, the Pinot Noir the same, and our server was really great.  Very friendly and funny. It's a little on the pricey side, but its completely worth it.

Looking at the menu, I was surpised this place got the loved by vegetarians designation on Yelp because there weren't that many veggie options to choose from. I still felt like I was getting the shaft. But enough of my whining.... We started with the plantain chips and the guac. The guac was pretty bland, but at this point in our trip, we were learning not to have high expectations for Mexican food in NYC. The tangy red and green salsas helped a lot. I asked the waitress for her recommendations on veggie empanadas, and she suggested the spinach pie and mixed vegetable (cornmeal empanada). The spinach, which our server said she loved, was also bland. I was expecting more bite from feta and dill like you would with a spanakopita. The veggie was ok, but the cormeal crust was inferior to the regular flour. The veggies were likely a frozen mix. The saving grace was my husband's viagra empanada. He absolutely the loved it! He said the seafood inside was high quality which is amazing given the low price. He might stock up on a few of those to go for a snack, but I don't know that I would bother trying Empanada Mama again.
This is a neighborhood gem -  the dishes are all carefully crafted and super tasty (even the pastas are not boring), the decor is nice and the staff pleasant.  Look forward to going there for brunch.

Portions are very small. Good food but over priced in my opinion. Service was poor. Ordered coffee and it took at least 10'minutes to get coffee or spoons. Coffee was cold. Blood Mary was awful. Tasted like it was made with ketchup. The pork belly was good. Very rich. The duck was too fatty. Shrimp chips are overpriced and from a packet. Will not go back. Poor value for the food.

Ok we 're here now.  Driving by, saw the place was packed.  They don't take reservations so we walked in sat down and ordered a bottle of chianti.  Excellent!   Then the meatballs... The MEATBALLS !   Better than grandma made.  We licked the dish , then ordered more ! We got our main courses.  Unreal!   Pollo rollatini to die for.  Son got lasagna.  Absolutely delicious!   This place in the South Slope is an absolute gem!   Homemade food that is cheap and incredible !   We'll be back.  But I'm not telling too many people.  Don't want to spoil it!

Pro's:   Pretty tasty comfort food in the middle of Chelsea.   Good service, and the staff seems to laugh and have fun together Good cocktails Extensive menu Outside dining and big open doors/windows Con's: $13 for a cocktail and $10 for a no-name Chardonnay is pretty steep for a place like this Dirty and smelly bathrooms Because of the bathrooms, I can't imagine what the kitchen looks like Food kind of pricey for the quality/taste.  We ordered "Sliders" and we received two tiny little sliders for $9.  I would have rather ordered a regular burger and split into four for the same price.   1 glass of wine, 1 cocktail, 2 Diet Coke's and 2 appetizers for $50+tip.  It should have been $30-35.
Great food and the best beer list in town.  Definitely a fun place to grab dinner and a drink!

In the interest of full disclosure, I am a regular of this bar. I come exactly once a week, on the same night, to enjoy the same happy hour with the same bartender. I meet a group of friends that I enjoy speaking at reasonable levels with, and this is a perfect bar to do it at. The musical tastes are good, and not too loud before it gets crowded. During happy hour (M-F 4pm-8pm), draughts are $4. They have Smithwicks and Boddingtons, and that is enough for me to be happy. They have a book of menus and bringing takeout into enjoy while drinking is not a problem. That being said, I would not be caught dead here on a Friday or Saturday night.

I love this place, I came here with my girlfriend for a special date and I don't regret it. We started off with the Roti Massaman, the pancake it self was really good, reminded me of the Chinese onion pancake. The massaman curry was the best I've had, they added just the right amount of coconut. For my entree I got the Drunken Udon a Noodles and the plating shocked me. The noodles had lots of chicken and squid inside a wonton wrapper bowl. Aside from the visuals, the dish itself was really delicious too. The noodles were cooked perfectly, the chicken and squid were great compliments does too. This is one of the best Thai restaurants I have been too, highly recommended.

Misery Loves Co. is an old-school red truck that you might find parked at Burton, Maglianero Cafe or in front of the Champlain Mill in Winooski. The food that is created in this vehicle is simply amazing. On any given day you may find on offer a delicious burger, The Saltie (with salt cod fritters), Porchetta, and the best fries to be had in Chittenden County. They are served with an old bay aioli and fried with fresh sage leaves - amazing and addictive. The people behind Misery Loves Co. have done stints at various local restaurants, and are obviously too talented to not eventually find their way to their own brick & mortar place. But for now keep an eye out for the red Winnebago and enjoy the delicious stuff being handed through the window.

This is a New Haven classic.  Not perfect, not inexpensive but consistent and consistently delicious.  The menu shows restraint when wearing it's tie a little looser could be beneficial in a university town but when we go for lunch we watch table after table of professors, students and other Yalies fill the tables.  An admirable wine list completes the picture with more respect paid to newer appellations in recent years, but for the complete experience I generally keep it French.  Starting with a glass of champagne, a bottle of Rhone with dinner and completing the meal with a glass of calvados.  The reinvigorated cheese menu caught our attention on our last visit so we tried and loved the Stichelton.  Every time I come here I appreciate a perfectly polished place-setting, a beautiful room and precise service.  The skate at lunch is the best excuse for a glass of wine before five o'clock I've encountered in years.

The past week I went to Gyu Kaku for dinner. I know this restaurant because of a friend of mine recommended it to me. I was with my girlfriend and we tried to be there the day before but it was too crowded. As we did not have a reservation the wait time was about forty (40) minutes, so we made a reservation to the next day. It is really easy to get there from the City Hall, so my girlfriend and I got there a little bit earlier. We got there 15 minutes earlier, but the guy in the entrance sat us in the table before the reservation hour. The place is really nice; it is decorated accordingly to the restaurant theme. The bad thing was that beside of us sits a big table that was very loud. When we sat, the waiter presented himself and asked us if we had already eaten in a Japanese style bbq. As we said no, he started to explain us how works the restaurant. Then, he brought us the menus and filled our cups of water while we were choosing. For appetizer we ordered: the French fries with cod caviar sauce and the fried shrimp dumplings. The fried shrimp dumplings are excellent you do not need to add anything because they have a crunchy outside and a lot of flavor inside.  However, I prefer the french fries with the cod caviar sauce. The sauce is a little bit spicy but it has a unique really good taste. You cannot leave without trying them. As main course, we ordered: the harami skirt steak, the New York strip steak, the spicy pork and the shrimp garlic. The steaks were really good I love how they were marinated; besides, the cuts were thin so they cook quickly. The spicy pork took a longer time in the grill to be ready, nevertheless, they were really good and I really love spicy food. The good thing of this restaurant is that they bring you the food really well marinated so they have a lot of flavor. Finally, for dessert, we ordered the mochi ice cream; my girlfriend and I never tried it before. They brought us four mochis, so we ordered one of each flavor. Unfortunately, they were out of mango's mochi; so they brought us two of vanilla, one of green tea and one of red beans. Personally, I am not a big fan of the green tea. So, I did not like the green tea mochi, even though my girlfriend loved it. The others mochis were really good. The texture of the mochi filled with the ice cream is an experience that you must try. At the end, we had a great time, the service was kind and courteous, and the restaurant was not too expensive. I think that Gyu Kaku offers you a different atmosphere that takes you out of the routine. I really like the Japanese bbq style restaurant. I am sure that I will go again and I strongly recommend it.

Nice little Italian restaurant to have a candle light dinner at. Food is good, servers are good, but if you go on a busy night... You'll be stuck eating bread at your table for a while. Parking is not to your advantage for this place. You need to park on the street, and when the main street is full... it's side streets for you, which is still walking distance away.

Bottom line - know what you're getting into/what you like before you come You like - plain and very fresh sushi, then - come and enjoy! You like - interesting and creative sushi, then - go somewhere else like Sushi of Gari To me, it seems that the key to this restaurant isn't so much the slicing and ingredients, but choosing fresh fish from the markets.  Note that I didn't get anything else aside from the sushi.  Instead I had the Sushi Omakase along with additional pieces to try to get closer to full. So yeah, good sushi, but I prefer paying for more interesting creations and although it was good, I likely won't be going back any time soon.

I ordered today on grubhub.com The food took more than an hour to get here, when it finally got here the order was completely wrong and cold. The delivery guy asked me to signed the reciept and waited for his tip before he would give me my bag, my front desk receptionist had the tip so i asked him to wait a minute he still would not give me the food i paid for even after the brought it 30 minutes after the expected delivery time. I ordered chicharron which cost $5 and they gave me a baby portion of pork rinds(yea they were the ones you can buy in a bag for 99 cents). The Mazorca (corn) was too salty... I don't recommend this place at all. I was beyond angry and was left starving.

One of my favorite places to eat.  I come every time I visit my Uncle in Queens.  Fantastic soups, the papaya salad is great and so is just about everything on the menu.  We always order a few different things and eat family style (our preference) to get as many different tastes as possible.  The bill is always less than expected.  Good service, but make sure you get there early or you will have a long wait.  It is a jewel.

I visited towards the end of the evening and the place was empty. I asked if I could sit in the window table and get dessert and coffee. Was told no, can't sit there unless having dinner. I get the need to reserve for dinner, but no-one was going to use it and I didn't feel like being shoved in the back. I left, unhappy and unwelcomed.

Overrated. This place has potential but misses the mark.  It is far from a well-executed culinary experience and far too overpriced to be a casual night out with friends.  The negatives --- -we waited a long time for a table despite having a reservation,it was freezing in there (the first time that I ever had to complain to the staff to turn on the heat), the portions were tiny!, we waited 20 minutes between each of our four courses.  The deserts were the only "course" that was a reasonable size but they were far from tasty.  One of the deserts that we ordered was the cookie dough in ice cream.  I figured that was a safe bet...how do you screw-up cookie dough and ice cream - - but it was nasty.  The cookie dough tasted like salt!  There was more salt in the cookie dough ice cream dish than there was in all of the other courses combined.  I had a great time with the company I was with but I will not be returning here anytime soon.

I met Amin (Bitar's owner). I returned the molded pita bread last week and got refunded for it. He apologize and I did appreciate that, since I always buy my pita bread from Bitar's! I'm so happy that he could also help me do a bakesale at his store so that I can raise money for the Arthritis Foundation. I  and my team "CHEF CHERRYL" will be walking a 5k on Dec 4, 2011 in Metuchen, New Jersey. If anyone is interested to join my team or want to support me on this great cause please visit my personal webpage: jbrmetuchen.kintera.org/… Thank you for your time reading this!! Che

Kam Buffet is a very good Chinese Buffet, my family and I just loved it. My fiancee is not a social person and has never been out to eat in any restaurant. We went to Kam's for my birthday this year, and he fell in love with the place. He wanted to go back yesterday,trying to  use  the excused that since hurricane Sandy knocked out the lights we should just go back to Kam's and skip trying to cook in the dark. How funny is that ?
