Quaint is hugely overrated by Yelpers.  I live in the neighborhood and have eaten there at least four or five times...for brunch as well as dinner.  The ambiance must be driving a lot of the praise insofar as it's hip, faux-Manhattan bistro-ish.  But he food is completely average and unexceptional.  And the service is just about as indifferent and self-absorbed as anything I've ever seen.  For instance, I sat at the bar on my most recent visit waiting for the bartender to finish his extended discussions with the other staff to get my entree from the warming rack.  By the time it arrived, it was so lukewarm as to be almost inedible. Don't think I'll be going back anytime soon.

I got the cheesesteak with whiz. It tasted pretty good, but I had a few problems with it. The steak was not chopped up like most other good steak joints. It was also expensive $8.25 for just the sandwich and $2.00 for a fountain drink. What a rip off! Did I mention the 30 minute line around the corner at 3pm in the afternoon. It's just not worth it. Oh and my stomach was ruined for the rest of the day. Without going into details let's just say I wasn't able to make it out last night. Carmine's is better and so is Lorenzo's right around the corner.

I came here with a friend on lunch break. We were craving Vietnamese food and this was pretty close. First off, the place was tiny - about 6 tables. So definitely not good for large groups. The place was run by chinese folk. Now I didn't get the banh mei as people stated so it may be different. I'm from SoCal originally so there are certain expectations for that such as fresh french bread smell and the aroma of ham/Vietnamese meats should be in the store. That was not observed here so I decided to go with other meals. APPETIZER:  We shared the spring rolls - which are the fried meat egg rolls. I expected the rolls to have the rice paper wrapper, however, the rolls came out with the chinese egg roll wrapper making the wrapper slightly crunchy rather chewy & crispy when its rice paper. Not too authentic. The biggest issue I had with the roll is that the meat tasted frozen since the meat wasn't too soft but hard and clumpy. The rolls came out a bit flattened and brown on one side so they were oblong rather round like a roll. This may be due to the fact that the roll seemed to have been warmed up & lightly fried (or refried) on just one side. While it did have meat, the wrapper made the roll not very palatable. They weren't greasy at all (which may be a plus or minus?). The rolls were hard and semi-cold rather warm. MAIN DISH:  I did order the Bun Thit Nuong - (vermicelli with charred BBQ pork). The portion size is appropriate in the typical asian plastic bowl. However, the bun was slightly thick, dry as if it had been made earlier in the day. The noodles were slightly undercooked and hard since I had to bite and chew the noodles more than normal. They were skimpy with the meat. The meat was interest - definitely not salty, but the flavor had more of lemongrass rather a charred, smoky and soy sauce taste. It was very light and not too memorable. It wasn't greasy. SERVICE: This was mediocre, they had to keep track of people coming in ordering to-go so getting our check was a bit a slow. The service actually included one glass of warm tea and no refills-nor did they ask about water or soda when ordering. I was kind of disappointed at this place after reading the reviews. It's definitely something to eat and it's something to pass the time with Vietnamese food, however not too memorable.

I recently went to Catas with my husband and two friends. We went on a Groupon so that entitled us to a tapas each, an entree each and a glass of wine, sangria or beer. We all went for the sangria, so the waiter gave us a large pitcher (much more sangria in the pitcher than 4 individual glasses). We were very pleased with the service, attentive but not intrusive. Our server knew the menu, able to explain the entrees and their accompaniments. All four of us chose different tapas and entrees. I previously read a glowing review of the sweet potato empanadas so I ordered them and was not disappointed. The filling was creamy and flavorful and the pastry quite lovely. My husband enjoyed the fava bean and choriso tapas. Our friends ordered the stuffed peppers and garlic shrimp. They were happy with both. The 2 men ordered the steaks. My husband ordered the hangar steak which he liked, tender, the sides were great as well as the sauce. His complaint was the the steak itself lacked flavor. Our friends rib eye was delicious, he enjoyed it very much. And as others have commented, the sweet potato fries are lovely. My other friend had the stuffed chicken and I had the whole grilled fish. We both enjoyed our dishes completely, the sides being just as enjoyable as the protein. If you get the fish, beware of the many bones. We were too stuffed to order dessert. In looking at the menu pricing, I would most definitely return for another meal as Catas. Oh, make sure to go to the bathrooms, they are something else.

Great food, and an ever greater bar, this place is pretty cool! The staff is pleasant, friendly, professional, and the atmosphere is very nice :) Note that it is a bit pricey, but well worth it, if you ask me

This is one of my favorite places in Manhattan. It's loud and always jam-packed, but such a scene and the food is grand. You cannot go wrong with the burger and fries. But the desserts are good also, especially banoffee pie. Yum.
soup dumplings!!!!!
I'm a regular at this restaurant.  Never had a bad meal.  Great pricing, consistently good meals.  What more can you ask for?

I invited my fiancé for dinner before theater I choose this place because of the good reviews but I was very disappointed about the service and food quality I order house salad, chicken parmigiana that was only bread, the rigatoni vodka was watery lack in sauce I could do better vodka sauce, the waiter never ask me how was my food only came twice to take my order and give me the check. I wil not recommend this place to my friends.

Went here last night for the first time after being made aware by a friend that I had missed the best falafel spot in the city. I went in having my reservations, as I have lived in town for years and felt I was fluent in what the city had to offer. How could I have missed this gem for so long?   We both got standard falafel with hot sauce and it was one of the best I have eaten. Reasonably priced and filled you up completely. The sandwich was so big my friend couldn't even finish theirs.  No need to order anything else, although the complementary pickle bar was definitely worth tasting. The staff was so nice and accommodating. We got here at 845, when they were about to close, sat outside and they told us to sit, relax, and enjoy. They were not in any rush and insisted we should not be either. Will definitely be back soon for more.

This place has delicious Thai food for soooooooo cheap. Love, love, love the spicy noodles with shrimp. Also, they have amazing tiger shrimp rolls and summer rolls. A must try if you are into Thai. Cool vibe on the weekends. Bar tends to get packed in the front while people wait to be seated. They have cool music and the decor is very trendy. Staff is quick and so is the kitchen.

This was a GREAT tour.   our guide was very knowledgeable about how all of the pizza places in the area make their dough, the sauce & cheese they use, and their ovens, etc.  This was the case for the places we went to and any place that we walked by....even some that don't exist anymore.  He would stop the group and talk about a place and how good it used to be and why they went out of business. We went on the Village walking tour.  We hit three places and had a slice at each.  Water was provided.   The guides know all the business owners well and get some liberties (getting behind the counter, pulling an unmade dough from the tray to show us consistency, etc).  Our guide would just ring up the next shop and place the order while we walked to the location.  They would have it ready right as we got there.  Since you pay Scott's, you don't have to worry about paying for the slices, etc....they bring them to you and you eat it and then discuss afterwards. Our guide was able to provide a history and information on many other parts of the Village and it's businesses.

I just had the Pan fried big dumpling, wonton soup noodle with duck, and the shrimp balls.  I really like the fried dumpling, it was doughy and crunchy on the bottom which is the way it should be.  The wonton noodle soup could use more meat and veggies stuffed in the wontons, but overall it was still pretty good. One complaint that I do have is that my cup of tea smells and tastes like detergent.  Maybe they took it out of the washer a bit too quick. The bill came out to about 23 bucks for two so its not exactly very cheap, but a fairly good value.

After a recent visit to Acacia on my birthday I was extremely underwhelmed. When we first read over the menu we thought "Wow, we're in for a great meal!  Everything sounds delicious!"  Then they brought out the cold bread and olive oil (not EXTRA virgin...almost clear and tasteless olive oil and no butter) and we began thinking "Well, the first course has to be good!"  We were wrong. After what seemed like an eternity our appetizers arrived.  The "Chilled Jumbo Shrimp and Lobster Cocktail" should be called "3 Room Temperature Medium Shrimp and Minced Lobster Salad".  The cocktail sauce was squeezed on top of the shrimp with what looked like a tube of toothpaste.  YUMMY!  The "Thai Vegetable Spring Rolls" were greasy and flavorless.  The peanut sauce was OK but I've had better out of a jar. Next up was the "Duck Breast and Confit"  Average at best and overcooked...also no duck confit..just a sliced breast and duck leg with mushy risotto! "Spice Rubbed Tuna" was obviously frozen and not fresh.  The color was light pink at best and the presentation was extremely sloppy.  Needless to say we will never return to this overpriced faux fine dining establishment. If you still want to try it out after reading this review I suggest you bring A LOT OF WINE.

Went to Frying Pan on a weekday but the chilly winds helped my friend and me decide to go elsewhere indoors for a glass of wine and something to eat. Le Grainne Cafe is really cute inside.  Small and quaint, but has such a variety of people dining at any given moment.  Didn't have a wait but filled up pretty quickly as the night progressed. Food: -mussels with tomato, black olives and pesto: good portions, very flavorful -linguini with spicy shrimp: pretty good, but not mind blowing Kitchen was ridiculously late with our linguini, but we got a free crepe out of it.  Not gonna lie, I'm not a crepes person but their crepes are pretty good -- nutella and banana, delicious. Staff was really nice too, one of our (guy) waiters had quite the sense of humor. Will definitely be back.

i cross this cafe few times, but i even go in... until today. Each time i corss there, i talk myself that I must be try once! today, i eat breakfast with my gf. we order Euro breakfast, the savory crep with egg and smoke salmon/ Panini signature with prosciutto parma with mozzarella, tomato and basil pesto. Those taste excellence and full of stuff, also the drink is good too! Especially is the hot chocolate, not too sweet, strong coco taste and smooth. (even i m not a coffee man) I can said the Cappuccino taste better then Starbxxks a lot!! xd... Overall, thats the best cafe in Bensonhurst.

Please, Yelpers, I beg you...stop going to these types of places during their busiest hours and then writing how long a wait it was! As Jade wrote, you gotta scheme for the best hours to go (weekdays between 2 and 5 is ideal if you're a jobless loser like me or if can swing a sick day here and there). Only order what is made, what is out. Don't wait for mushroom or sausage or pepperoni---do that you'll be waiting forever. The old man moves like molasses so there's no point in going outside the sphere of that. If, by luck, you have an option, take the square over the round and take extra slices, even if you're not sure you'll eat 'em....Better to have a little extra...You'll never get a second helping any other way.
Got bad food poisoning from the catfish and/ or tartar sauce.  You might want to avoid them if you go...  As for me, I won't be returning.

I'm a few years older and wiser! Less drinking, more experience this time around. Line long as expected. Weather sucked very cold, wind strong. Plenty of drunks to keep the experience real and entertaining. Ordered the mixed plate with rice and gyro sandwich $10. Handed the guy a $20, he gave me my food and asked me to move along, but did not give me $10 in change back. I asked and received. I stood around to see if this was more than a one time instance. Well guess what seems they are taking advantage of folks who've had one too many to drink and aren't watching the financial transaction take place. While very opportunistic , let a very bad taste in my mouth. They have lost my business forever.
Salted caramel is the BEST!

This restaurant has great atmosphere the lighting is a little dim but understandable for type of restaurant/Bar. Kids eat free on Sundays my daughter described her meal as scrumptious. The wait staff this kind courteous helpful and talkative.  the manager even came over to check on us which I always appreciate. ***Special note*** The murder burger is really to die for ....not for the faint of heart....beautifully cooked burger nice flavor the whole Burger is deep fried leaving the bun with a not to sweet donut like taste....very greasy BUT a MUST try once experience. My wife describes the atmosphere as one of those Disney Epcot theme restaurants that your love.

You won't find a nice group of people to buy your meats from.  It is like stepping back in time when your neighborhood butcher thrived. Quality cuts of meat and deli products. For the high quality and great service the prices are very reasonable.

Remembering Paisano's as a pizzeria with a juke box in the back as a kid growing up in Rutherford back in a day, I wanted to like it when they transitioned into a more upscale, bistro-type eatery and the downtown became a restaurant destination of sorts. Having not been in town for several years when I first visited the new Paisano's, they did not disappoint. Visiting them numerous times the past several years, Paisano's never disappoints, including our last visit a couple weeks ago. Consider it a reliable, go-to dining choice. Deceiving in size from the outside, the restaurant is spacious on the inside, split into two parts and a backyard patio. There is also seating out front. The exterior is well done,  a classic, upscale bistro look and a welcome change from its original storefront.The décor is tasteful, running somewhere in between casual bistro and upscale restaurant and is byob.The wait staff are always on top of taking care of diners wine service.  Pricing lies somewhere in between moderate and pricey, but is good value nonetheless. Pasta is made fresh on premises, or, at least was. They likely still make pasta in-house. Typically, my visits include four or five other people, and everyone comes away happy. There is one waitress there that is on her game and is fantastic-I wish I could remember her name-she is usually there on Saturday nights. Things we ordered multiple times include the Apple & Endive Salad, ($6.95)  stuffed eggplant ($7.95) and Caesar Salad ($6.96) for appetizer /salads. Price is about right for the portion size and quality. Entrees we have enjoyed are Zuppa de Pesce, ($29.95) Linguine with white clam sauce, ($22.95) Chicken Parmesan ($21.95) Branzino, ($27.95) Penne Vodka ($18.95) Grilled Salmon, and other seafood specials. Once again, price is about right for the quality and portion size. Paisano's is not one of those pretentious upscale restaurants that equate small portion size with quality.....and high prices. One of our diners loved the Branzano, another Pear Ravioli. ($20.95). One of our diners thought even the chicken parmesan was outstanding. Tiramisu, chocolate mousse' and creme brulee' are always very good. Like most restaurants, there are occasional glitches: One time, my father had to wait almost 30 minutes for his salad-the restaurant must have run out of greens and ran to the market for romaine lettuce. Another time, I waited 40 minutes for gluten free pasta-and an extra $6 charge- Again, likely prompted a trip to the market. Getting seating you want isn't always greeted with immediate enthusiasm. However, these are manageable bumps in what is usually a positive experience. Paisano's will never be confused with a classic, four star, Wine Spectator restaurant. That being said, Paisano's is steady and reliable and might be a better choice than fading top Italian restaurants in NJ like Scalini Fedeli.

Unfortunately I was too full from eating all day to try the ramen here.  I wanted to see what the hype about the pork buns were about.  It's good to have the pork bun every once in awhile, but honestly for $4/bun it's not worth it. I must try the ramen on the my next  visit.

Very good food, high prices considering what they offer. Nonetheless this is a nice dinner spot. I ordered the frisee country salad that came with croutons, lardons, and a perfectly poached egg. Yum! My friend ordered the spicy chicken dumplings, which I sampled. I must say they were quite odd. They tasted like buffalo chicken dumplings. The dumpling wrapper was a bit too thick for my taste and too chewy. However my salad was absolutely outstanding. The lardons were crispy, salty, and smoky. The silky egg yolk, served as kind of a dressing in addition to the actual dressing. The salad was perfectly dressed as well. The frisee was fresh and beautifully colored. Presentation was outstanding. For dessert the had so many tempting options, but my favor swayed with the mini donuts with caramel and jam. Oh my gosh, they were so addictingly good. The donuts came in a cute little paper cone and only four or five actual donuts (thank goodness). They were covered in sugar and cinnamon, crispy on the outside and soft and fluffy on the inside. The side sauces for dipping the donuts in were delicious. The caramel sauce was thick and creamy, absolute heaven. The jam sauce was also delicious. I alternated sauces between bites. A wonderful meal and the perfect end to a so-so day.

Was looking for a local restaurant with online ordering and loved Soho Pizza & Grill's variety.  I ended up ordering the mushroom chicken with a side of meatballs.   Online ordering through yelp/delivery.com worked seamlessly. Delivery happened within 30 mins and with a smile. The meatballs came in a very tasty sauce that was simple and not overly spiced (hate that) The mushroom chicken was very tasty and i found myself saving the gravy to use over a pasta dish the next day.   All in all, a first experience from a restaurant I have never tried and will definitely be ordering delivery from again. Keep it up guys!

This is a great little spot right in the theater district. The food is really yummy, though some items are yummier than others. I have to shake my head at some other yelpers who complain about price increases...I don't know about you but my rent and bills have gone up in that time frame, I'm sure the restaurant has felt the same pinch we all have. I don't call it "selling out", I call it "modern economy".  Overall the prices are still pretty darn cheap for the area. You do have to be careful though as with any izakaya or tapas joint, those little plates can add up if you're not careful. 2-3 plates per person is more than enough food to satisfy. As others have said, seating is tight, and unless you get here within 30 minutes of opening, expect a sizable wait.

Chili: From best to worst in a week.  Last week my wife and I stopped in and I had a hankering for some chili.  I ordered and was pleasantly surprised to find that the chili was some of the best I had ever had - not too spicy, nice and thick and they even put a piece of pot roast in the middle with sour cream to top it off.  I told my wife that I would come back anytime just to get the chili.  So back we came this past Sunday only to be sorely disappointed.  I was so looking forward to the same chili but when I took my first spoon it was so hot I could not even eat it.  My wife, who likes spicy food, tasted it and said it was way too hot for her too.  Plus, no chunk of pot roast in the middle either!  You have got to be kidding me!  My advice to Plan B - learn how to be consistent with your recipes.  Had your chili remained like it was the first time I tried it I would have kept coming back for more.  Now I am hesitant to even go back to Plan B for anything much less the chili.

What can I say, as a fan of wet and saucy bbq I was hesistant when u walked into ferry st. Bbq. But the moment I bit into the pork ribs, I saw the light. The pork was soooo tender and you can truly taste the smokiness in the meat. Each bite was a delight. My wife and I git the half rib half chicken combo w a heaping serving of yellow rice and salad. All for a jaw dropping price of $14 dollars. Who can ask for more. Awesomely delish food for cheap. I definitely would recommend anyone who wants portuquese bbq to patronize this little gem.

Really Really Good! I drove with my kids from Manhattan to Brooklyn just for the pizza,, We made a day out of it... we got there at 2PM last saturday and got our pizza right before they went on a break around 4:15 The place was packed! but it was worth it... just seeing how he makes the pies was fun and then when we actually got ours the feast began. Go try it!

One of the best bars I've been to anywhere. Interior has a cool throwback feel, but the sounds and scene is very modern. Bartenders all super personable and know what they're doing. Food was delicious and the drinks were strong. Its location right across the street from Eugene O'Neill theater was clutch for post-Book of Mormon shenanigans. GO THERE and enjoy yourself.

One of the best burgers I've ever had. I got sick of people talking about those boring tasteless 5 Guys burgers. This place uses steak meat and loads up with eggs, cheese, lettuce, etc (the works) The fries that go with this burger along with their special mayo is enough reason for me to break my usual healthy turkey burger eating. They offer great pricing and hospitality. Now I usually go to the one on Lafayette Ave in Newark but this one isn't as packed =) (still busy though)

We've been twice.  The first time it was mindblowingly good, but very crowded and loud. The second time (exactly one year later) it was TERRIBLE.  All the food was greasy and gross, and the bar was out of ingredients for the first FOUR drinks we tried to order.  (Why not just tell me what you can actually serve instead if making me guess?). When we finally did manage to order drinks, they were really gross and I had to force mine and my wife's down so I wouldn't be wasting $25. I'm not sure what happened in that year, maybe they lost a chef or had a crazy night, but I'm not gonna risk going a third time after that experience.

Hipster haven for Mexican food.  The environment is too dark to care about cleanliness.  The tequila's are great.  The food isn't exactly authentic but it's leaps and bounds above taco bell. I dont understand the juke box.  Lady Gaga and Mexican?  Not exactly.

This place is fun/different, and has good food. I went to the Chelsea location, which I understand is larger. My friend and I went on a Sunday, late morning, and somehow just missed a huge crowd (line). We didn't have to wait at all. Our food, beverages, service were all satisfying! I don't think the food is anything special, but it's certainly a step up from diner-, chain restaurant- or too-touristy-restaurant quality food.

Well I have already reviewed my el numero uno cheesesteak place and it's Jim's right down the block :) But Ishkabibble's was the joint I stumble upon when Jim's had a line that could wrap around the city of Philly 3 times. I wasn't overly impressed but I was hungry!! The cheese fries were a thumbs up. The steak sandwich it was a little dry, unlike other places (eh hem..Jim's) where the grill is going all day long and it's nice and grezzzzzzeee, :) this was a tad dry. but it was still tasty. I suppose if I were ever in a dilemma and need a cheesesteak and Jim's was too long of a line for my quick meal fix, I'd go back.

Over-hyped? Yes, totally. Overpriced? Mmhmm!!! REFUND PLEASE! My sister and I went to NYC recently and were told to try the ramen here. After almost getting lost in the subway system, we finally arrived at Ippudo Ny at 3:10PM (though knowing that the restaurant would close at 3:30PM for break. However, since we were only in NY for a total of 3 days, we decided to risk and wait). After a 10-minute wait, we got seated and were immediately asked to order. We told the waitress that we would need a few minutes as it was our first time there and wanted to explore their options. But after a quick run to the kitchen, our waitress came back with her pen & paper ready... rushing us to order. Now, I understand that the kitchen probably had to close but considering that there were other customers who walked in after us, I was annoyed at the fact that they didn't give us the few minutes that we asked for. After all, we were giving them business. Now, onto the food. In my opinion, the ramen was pretty damn salty! I'm not sure if it was the MSG but boy was I thirsty afterwards!! I've had better in LA that did not cost nearly as much. As suggested by our waitress, my sister and I ordered the Shiromaru Hakata ramen. I ordered the lunch combo that came with a salad and a bowl of eel rice. My sister, on the other hand, ordered the ramen with a soft-boiled egg and Kakuni braised pork belly as additional toppings. Unfortunately, when the food finally came, we realized how small the portions were and decided to place two orders of extra noodles (Kae-dama). After nearly pouring the ramen down our throats, another hostess handed us the check. Without gratuity, our bill came up to be $44 (to me, this is pretty expensive when the portions were that small and that this was only lunch). Although my sister and I both felt that the restaurant did not live up to our expectations, we still tipped them reasonably (at 20%). HOWEVER, when the hostess came back to collect the check, she looked at the receipt and gave us the dirty look. She then proceeded to say, "I'm not sure where you're from, but in New York, we normally tip at least 25% or however much you think our waitress deserves to be tipped!" Now, it's one thing for a hostess to say that to a customer but it's another to say it with an attitude and so loud that the tables next to us turned around to see what the fuss was about! Humiliated and mortified, we tipped a total of 30% just to avoid her from giving us any more dirty looks. Let me just say, after contemplation, we shouldn't have tipped at all! Tipping is optional and customers should never feel forced to tip more than what they think their waiters/waitresses deserve. Needless to say, unless there are no better ramen places in NY, we will not be returning. As noted by other Yelpers, not only is the food just mediocre but the service is just T-E-R-R-I-B-L-E!! The only (slightly) good thing that happened was the short wait. Otherwise, I would have flipped a table.

Finally got around to review Carmines.  We were there in late October, right after the hurricane.  Wanted to try the "new" 2nd Ave. Deli, but the lights were out in lower Manhattan. Even though Times Square was bustling we decided to see how long the wait would be at Carmine's.  Wonder of wonders, even though the place was jammed we were seated in the back right away. The service was not as terrible as previously mentioned.  Maybe the hardships that were evident in NYC made everyone a little nicer than usual which included our waiter. Forgot what we ordered, but it would have been better if we were a group of 3 or 4 instead of 2.  Lots and lots of food, but it was good down home Italian-American that any Italian Mama would be proud of.   Thanks New York City and Carmine's.  You showed a brave face in a time of adversity.

This place is a soul food dream come true. From the delicious food to the amazing eating soundtrack (if you play Aaliyah or 112, I can't NOT dance) to the kool-aid of the day ... quite an experience. I had the President Barack Obama with Macncheese and potato salad, my friend got the Gabrielle Union with cheesy grits and it was plenty of food. Complimentary corn bread don't hurt. We arrived on a Sunday night at 7pm and had no wait, but I can definitely understand lines to get in. Very easy to get to from the 2 Train. I will meet you again Amy Ruth!!!!!!!
OMG, one of the best pizza margherita! My hubby had the special pork chop. He enjoyed every bite.

I love this place for brunch, they always have great service and delicious food.  Its an awesome neighborhood spot that I always bring out of town guests to, even my little niece who isn't quite ready for a full meal in a restaurant (they even have crayons on hand just in case). My favorite dish is the poached eggs with roasted tomatoes and haloumi cheese but you should definitely try the tuna salad too - so good with dice avocados in it and served with a really nice salad.  The duck bacon is also a must if you are getting brunch here - such a unique flavor that it makes you wonder why you've never seen this on a menu before. Bottom line is you will not be disappointed if you visit Jack's Wife Freda.

Do yourself a favor and skip this burger.  What I dislike more than hype about mediocre food is mediocre food itself.   I was really excited to try this burger and really wanted to like it.  The space was small, but they definitely made use of every inch of the space.  The blaringly bright TV screen near the cash register at the bar really distracts from the cute and intimate atmosphere.  Why even bother dimming the lights and bringing out the candles? The chef's choice is to cook the burger at medium. Fine - I usually pick medium rare, but I've found that often times, the juices from a medium rare burger render the burger buns mushy, flattened, and intolerable to eat. Given that fact, when I say I want a medium cooked burger, I'm expecting the burger to be cooked medium.  You don't tell your barber you want a 1 centimeter trim and walk out with half a foot of hair chopped off from your head (although I feel like that happens more often than it should). Do you feel my frustration yet? We ordered the burger (off the menu), which was priced slightly above average in relation to some other joints in the area (Whitman's Juicy Lucy $11, Bareburger $10, 5 Napkin Burger $14).  The burger consists of a sizeable beef patty topped with a slice of cheese and caramelized onions sandwiched between 2 toasted hamburger buns.  A generous helping of potato fries comes on the side.  If you're opting for a healthier option, for $2, you can substitute the fries for a side salad. The beef patty was cooked much too well-done to be considered "medium" and lacked seasoning.  My friend said that buns reminded him of the McDonald's buns, but that was a compliment on his part as he has an unhealthy obsession with their Big Macs.  The sweet caramelized onions were a nice touch and added flavor to the burger, but it wasn't enough to remedy the overcooked patty.
Fantastic food, especially the specials! Service was also great. Really can't go wrong with Tia Pol.

Amazing subs, I usually go with a hot roast beef w mozarella and gravy. My only complaint is that there is no dedicated pickup line at the register. If you order ahead and go in when it is very busy to pick up subs you still have to wait for everyone to order and pay before you can even say you are picking up an order.

I have ordered and sat at this place many times. Their order time is super fast. They got me my order in 20 minutes. Portions are nice and big, ingredients are fresh and delicious. Spring rolls are the BOMB, all kinds of really neat herbs and grasses thrown in there. The vermicelli is my favorite. I will take it all ways!.

OK. I will enter the debate on "The Best Falafel In Town". And I will start out by saying, it's NOT Mamoun's. Now, Mamoun's has its charms (namely, it's as cheap of a lunch as you can get, basically, and the baklava is truly great), but WHY, oh WHY would you go here when you can walk 10 minutes into the West Village to the temple of  falafel? But that aside, Mamoun's is OK. But just OK. Very basic. Watch out for the hot sauce. IT'S HOT!
num num num... loved the ramen and steamed pork buns... although waited a long time and the bar is quiet small...would definitely go back!
Great food in a relaxed environment. We tried multiple appetizers and four different main dishes. They were of consistently great quality.

Enjoyed a very nice dinner at Char no.4. I made Sat night reservations for two at 8:00. We arrived a few minutes early but were greeted and seated immediately. The restaurant was packed. I think every seat besides our reserved table was full. We sat in the back, waiter came over quickly for drinks. He was very friendly, and knew alot about bourbon so i asked a bunch of questions and got some good info. My wife and i had fried green tomatoes, they were pretty good. She had the crab cake and i had the house cured lamb pastrami. The crab cake was very good and the pastrami was so good i ordered it after the meal to go so i could eat it the next day. She had the hanger steak, it was tender and delicious. I had the shrimp and grits and it was also very good. Nice stiff drinks, very good service and nice and comfortable, will def be back soon!  oh and i also had the butter pecan ice cream and it was very good!

After a good night out, this establishment was the one of the only place open nearby. It's hit or miss at this place. One thing was good--pork bone medicinal soup--the rest (fried rice, greens, stir fry dishes) were forgettable. Perhaps we should have stuck to the more common dishes. $70 meal and they don't let us pay by credit card! The owner's wife served us, so obviously that part was great.

Black Sesame Creme Brulee is indeed out of this world. 4 stars only because the other item we tried - green matcha ice cream - was really disappointingly sweet and flavorless. Decor, ambiance, menu otherwise is stellar.
The absolute best. The people here are friendly and no nonsense. The food is incredible.

I walked by this lovely place the other day about an hour before I had to board my plane to Miami. It wasn't that busy so I walked in, took a seat at the15-seat bar, looked around to drink in the atmosphere and proceeded to sit there for FIFTEEN MINUTES while the three young men (count 'em, three) behind the bar patently ingored me. Now - I'm old enough to know how to get a bartender's attention, however, it simply wasn't going to happen. As a chef and restaurant owner, there was simply NO excuse for not at least acknowledging a person who was sitting there for that long.  One of  them should have at least said to me "Hi, I'll be with you in a few minutes," but sadly, no. Had they been employees at my restaurant, I'd have fired all three of them. Regardless, after 15 minutes (this is no exaggeration, I timed it) I got up and left. All I can say is that they were lucky it was me, not my cousin who is one of the top food and restaurant critics in the country. Chances of me ever going back: zero.

We came on the recommendation of a NY resident. Otherwise we would not have known about it. This place is a small mom-and-pop place out in the middle of nowhere (and by nowhere, I mean not near a subway station cause I had to walk and walk for blocks building up my appetite before we got here) We had good timing cause we got the last table before a line starting forming out the door. Well I should say, we got the last two seats at a table that already had two people sitting here. Awkward, since it was a first date. I felt like we were eavesdropping. But really there's only like 5 tables and like 3 seats at the counter. A lot of people were getting it to go though. One waitress took care of the whole place and it was plenty. She would take our order and then just slightly yell it over to the kitchen, which is right there. They have a selection of about 15 different ramens. I'm no expert so I just stuck with the simple No. 1 - the kambi. I think the main difference is the different type of broths. Although the description on the menu doesn't mention anything about what's in the bowl besides the ramen and broth, it came with onions, pork slices, half a hardboiled egg and seaweed. And you get to pick from like 5 different kinds of noodles. I just went with the thin noodles, which were recommended on the menu. I really liked it -although it was very salty (due to its soy sauce flavor). It was cold that night and the hot bowl of noodles. My friend had the wahoo with chicken and wavy noodles. I got to try some of that and it was equally as good. Not the best ramen I've ever had but you could just tell it was very authentic and delicious. Oh and prices are moderate ranging from 10-15 bucks a bowl.

I have now had dinner at Morton's, Capital Grille, Ruth Chris, Old Homestead, and Strip House.  Without a doubt, the best tasting steak was at the Strip House.  The dry rub and the high temperature cooking made the outside tasty and the interior perfectly pink and juicy. However, it isn't perfect.  For example, for two people, it isn't very private.  There is about one foot between tables.  It is a little noisy.  I do like the atmostphere at the Capital Grill better.   I had outstanding service at all places. Since we like desert (especially chocolate), we ordered the chocoate cake which is enough for six people.  They should make a smaller portion.

The broth for the beef noodle soup was watery and lacking in heartiness. The noodles had the needed qq bounce. The meat that was in the noodles was tender and flavored just right. The fujianese wonton soup had this light but hearty broth. The umami flavor was delicious and just warmed you right up. The dumplings were heavy handed on the chives and skin is thinner compared to other dumpling places. They are also sweeter.

Went to Delizia's for the second time tonight. The last time was about one year ago and nothing has changed much,unfortunately. The pizza was undercooked and very doughy and thick. I mean c'mon this is Jersey you have got to do better than that. I ordered the fried Calamari for an appetizer. It was overly breaded and chewy. Something you would expect at TGI fridays. The chicken Murphy was in a watery sauce with  increadibly white chicken added on with too few peppers and onions. My  3 kids were more interested in my side dishes of pasta which wasn't too bad, hence the second star. So I had to tell my kids before we left the restaraunt, "Take a good look around"  which means that daddy and mommy will not be bringing them back.

Danny Meyer's success is built on an entrepreneurial formula of a restaurant interior designed to exude warmth, a staff trained in the arts of customer service and branded hospitality, and a top notch menu that manages to ride the food trends while retaining the familiarity that most diners prefer. Take Maialino for instance. It is Meyer's take on a Roman trattoria and while you would never walk into this restaurant and fancy yourself having stumbled upon a portal to Trastevere itself, every detail in this restaurant will make you want to stay. The large windows, the bar overlooking Gramercy Park, the bread section, the spacious dining tables, the wine cellar, everything comes together to provide a warm and cozy atmosphere. Coming here for lunch when the abundance of natural light makes the space feel even more airy is a wonderful thing. And so is sipping a glass of vino by the bar around dusk. Combine this with a staff that is friendly and attentive without the annoying hovering and a two hour lunch is not so hard to imagine. Then there is the remarkably authentic food. It is Italian cooking like you've experienced that night you stumbled upon a little trattoria inside a palazzo after you daydreamed atop the Spanish steps. Each dish is simple and each ingredient fresh. Fresh pasta is not drowned in sauce but folded with eggs and cheese. It is the humble cacio e pepe or carbonara that makes your meal memorable for the sheer simplicity of it. And of course, lest you forget that 'Maialino' is Italian for piglet, the signature dish Malfatti al Maialino is arguably one of the best pasta dishes in New York. For those who opt to veer away from hearty dishes of suckling pig or braised rabbit, the seafood dishes are an excellent alternative. On a recent restaurant week lunch sea bass was served with a fregola and cucumber salad that was light and refreshing, perfect for one of New York's hottest days. For dessert there is the obligatory panna cotta and tiramisu but the crostatas, tartlets served topped with fior de latte, and the creamy torta della nonna are highly recommended. Or perhaps a simple affogato will do for satisfying that craving for sugar and caffeine.

I've heard good things about Leunig's since I came to Burlington. I came here for brunch once but didn't get a chance to have a dinner meal here until last week and I'm pleasantly surprised by how much i liked it. I came for the "Bistro Dinner" special. For 15 bucks, you get an appetizer and an entree from a set meal. I was worried the entree would be small, but i thought it was well-portioned. Everything on the normal meal is pretty expensive and I would definitely have to think twice before coming here for a dinner. We got the steak fries, and cavatappi carbonara. The steak was good, though i would discourage getting it cooked more than a medium-rare. It seemed to be a sirloin cut and I would worry if it was cooked much more than the rare that we got. The wine demi-glace was sweeter than most, which was great for me cause i don't like the red wine taste all that much. The fries were well done. Great crispy exterior and fluffy inside. The carbonara was also good. Well balanced. I always worry about carbonara sauces being too heavy and creamy. It was not here. The roasted tomatoes added acidity and the bacon added the saltiness needed to keep everything in check. In addition, when i came for brunch, i got the corned beef hash. It was definitely the most unique corned beef hash I've ever had. Instead of salty bliss, the corned hash was surprisingly sweet and different. I love sweet and savory together, so i really liked it. If thats not your thing, then be warned. I want to come back for their early-bird brunch special, 10 bucks for an appetizer and an entree. Overall, Leunig's was an easy choice for their specials or for a dinner when you wanna treat yourself out to a more expensive meal

We love German Restaurants, and try them out wherever we go.  We have been here 3 times, trying to give this place a chance to shine.   Unfortunately, the food has never been anything more than average.   There is always a big crowd here, and it is a fun, loud crowd to go drinking with.  The beer selection is Excellent, and embodies the spirit of a good German bar.  This in itself, earned this place an extra star. The food has never been more than a 2, unfortunately.  We have had the wienershnitzel, rouladen, and sausage platters.  None have been great, and the sides of dumplings and spatzel also were very average.   I can see the appeal that this place holds for the neighborhood.  Lots of regulars, lots of friends, and lots of beer.  For that, it succeeds.  But for authentic German food, it is just average.
This place was so delicious. My boyfriend and I tried the curry chicken and jerk chicken with cabbage, festival and rice and beans. Highly recommend stopping by and checking it out!
Great breakfast. The pancakes are crepe-like and fantastic, excellent omelets too. Love the place and much better than the run of the mill diner food out there.

Good food, great service, happy me :) Ordered some food for delivery - not only was it early (by ~25 minutes), but it was still piping hot when it arrived (literally, I couldn't eat it for a few minutes)!  Pretty much your standard Americanized-Chinese takeout food, but with a massive amount of vegetarian selections (with the Buddhist/mock meats).   Holding back on the last star bc of the General Tso's - good flavor, good amount of meat, but not as crispy as I expect it to be. Fresh ingredients, healthy portions, friendly delivery guy -  *two thumbs up*

I wish I could have added another star!  The Food and atmosphere are AWESOME.  I ordered the chicken and waffles, and my mind was blown!  The waffles are absolutely AMAZING!!! They catch you off guard, they're so good.  You would figure the chicken would be the star, but the chicken and waffles are equally amazing! I cannot wait to go back!!!
This is a great little sushi spot. The Wayne roll and Moshi Moshi rolls are great! They make a lot of rolls with apple. BYOB - great service :-)
We arrived late and the kitchen was about to close at 11:05 on 12/26 and the host and hostess found a way to get us in. Made our night! 5 stars all around. Will be back!

Finally a real gyro! Line wasn't too bad, service is fast once your order is taken. My gyro was cooked perfectly and the sauce [they call it white sauce] was excellent...now let's talk french fries wholly @#$% they were GREAT, almost a lite tempura taste to them...MMM. For $7 I got the sandwich, fries & soda...I'm back next week
Always on the to-do list when I am in Philadelphia! One wiz 'with please....

What I love most about this city is it's uncanny ability to continue to surprise you. The moment you think you've tasted the best sushi this town has to offer, you wind up shocked and in complete gastronomical awe with something new making love to your taste buds! Tucked away on 43rd street in a pretty inconspicuous location lies Sushi Yasuda, hands down some of the best sushi to ever touch these lips. If you're going to come here, you must do it right and get a reservation at the bar...reminded me of all those small carved out restaurants in Asia where businessmen would go right after work to eat and get sloshed. The whole experience and aesthetic at Sushi Yasuda is fulfilling, from watching the sushi chef craft each morsel of fresh sushi for you, to the decor mimicking the zen-like ambiance in Kyoto.. this place does it right! The sushi was flavorful and probably some of the freshest fish I've eaten in my entire life. Each piece was crafted to perfection, with the rice being at room - warm temperature. We went through the entire round of sushi offerings and I fell in love with the Arctic Char, the fresh-water and sea eels, the fatty tuna, the octopus and the scallop (o lord, the scallop). If you're looking for a traditionally inspired sushi experience, Sushi Yasuda is the perfect spot. Even in Mr. Yasuda's absence, this place kills it!!! Don't miss it!!
Why spend $20 at a supermarket for a basket of boredom when you can go to Brancaccio's for the most perfect and unbeatably delicious Italian food. Cocohat

A monthly regular at Corner Bistro. This place is a no frills bar serving some damn good burgers. On a paper plate, your choices are limited with a hamburger, cheeseburger (add cheese) or bistroburger (add bacon + cheese) or a chicken sandwich. All are really good and well done. Also they have McSorleys on tap, so it's a winner either way given the price vs quality. Would highly recommend, even though Regis doesn't (HIMYM).

One of the best ceviche places in Brooklyn! I love mixto and pulpo ceviches the most. Tried most of other things on the menu and  haven't had a bad dish. Everything is fresh and tastes great! The staff is friendly and attentive. Full dessert menu and coffee!

One of a handful of providers of cask beer in Queens.   The cask beer is dispensed by handpump and is always in good condition and they have a well selected rotating collection and its always available.  That's great.  However it seems they serve the cask beer in a smaller size than the keg beer.   That bugs me tremendously.  It also makes no sense.   Since cask beer, unlike keg beer, is alive and fermenting in the cask, it needs to be fresh and hence sold quickly.   That apart, this is a very nice place that looks great, full of a lively crowd and with an appealing little backyard (that is, however, too often closed).

Little Owl might be one of the cutest restaurants in West Village and possibly in all of New York. We made a reservation before we found ourselves in the cozy restaurant, happily sheltered from the humid and rainy New York weather. After having perused the menu, we decided to split an order of the meatball sliders, the ricotta ravioli and the lamb fillet. Not too long after, the sliders and the ravioli arrived. I'll admit, I was a little shocked by the size of everything. The sliders are mini-sliders. I was able to hold a slider in between my thumb and forefinger. But the taste made up for everything. The buns were soft, the marinara had the slightest bit of zest and the meatballs were spiced and flavorful and juicy. As for the ravioli, the sauce was once again tangy and complimentary and the ravioli was toothsome and not too rich. Then the lamb fillet came. Unsurprisingly, this was rather small too. But it was good. And crispy. And full of lamby goodness. The side veggies were quite delicious as well. Overall, I am glad I went to Little Owl. The service was great, the food was good and the atmosphere was quaint and homey. The cost of our meal, however, was another story. For four tiny sliders, four little raviolis and two small slabs of lamb, the total came out to about $60. Not the cheapest meal we've had, obviously.   But I regret nothing!!

I wil not return to restaurant. The food was way overpriced and there were few selections to choose from. The quality of the meat was nothng special but the worse than the food was staff. The meats was so salted to he te taste. Boring bread, bland salads and whole fish served with creepy head and tails.. clearly they are focused on a high volume of one time customer and tourists wh want to take a selfie with a steak in the Meat Packing District. with beef prices continuing to rise I would not be surprised to see this commodity of a steakhouse close.

This place stinks... literally. Smells like the carpet needs to be cleaned. Still has christmas decor up.most of all the food is so mediocre, the person who answers the phone for orders is rude and to top if off the delivery person reeks of cigarette smoke.

This is exceed my expectations 3 fold!  It gets 5 stars from me because, the food is soooooo delicious, the drinks are great, the service was prompt & courteous, and the atmosphere is the kind that makes you come back over and over with friends to hang out. I went for lunch (about an hour and a half after they opened) and the place was packed.  It was about a ten minute wait. I can't even imagine it after work or on the weekends.  I cannot wait to go back.

Overdue review! When travelling back to NY this past May I was excited to see my friend and when she asked what I wanted to have for dinner I told her ramen. There seems to not be any slamming ramen restaurants in the Pacific Northwest so I was hoping to be impressed and Ippudo definitely lived up to the hype! I've been told that this place is notorious for the dreaded 1.5 hrs+ wait regardless of what day of the week it is (in fact the friend I was with had walked over to another restaurant, ate some soba, walked back to Ippudo and still waited a bit for her table) but we only had to wait maybe 20 minutes! Lucky! Get the buns with the shrimp omg! And whatever ramen is their special of the day. Seriously, you won't regret it. Considering the price and location it isn't too bad... though i wished there were more pieces of meat served than what it came with.

This place was eerily similar to a Cuban version of the Olive Garden - from the staff uniform to the business formula. I walked in early evening on a Saturday and was practically ignored by the hostess who seemed she'd rather flirt with her co-workers than do her job (a trend I noticed throughout my experience with the staff). I was by myself since my friend hadn't shown up yet, but I was still hovering around the hostess stand, so... yeah. I had to practically call her over to get a table. I was easily seated in the dining room and promptly received water by a gentleman working who told me my waitress would be with me "shortly." It took her a while, but oh well. I glanced over the shimmery menu while waiting for the waitress and my bff. The items were definitely tempting - especially all of the different plantains! My friend arrived and we quickly ordered our meals since we were sort of in a time crunch. We started with the plantain appetizer served with a garlic dipping sauce - yum!! I definitely recommend it. They were like fresh potato chips, but better, and definitely addicting! I went for the salmon salad, which was alright. The salmon was way overdone. Edible? Yes. Decent? Nah. The waitress didn't come over to check on our meals for at least 10 minutes and by that time it was too late to tell her that my salmon was overcooked and dry. The rest of the salad was mixed greens with some fruit and red pepper on top. I had the dressing on the side, which was also odd since there were two dressings - one sweet, almost mango - and the other seemed more Asian inspired. I had to practically douse the salmon with the mango dressing in order to give it some flavor and moisture. I liked that I could find an OK salad in this area, but at the end of the day it was just OK.

Great service by Dominiqu, great food, tasty beer (Naughty Nurse probably my favorite) and a nice visit with Conner, the manager. Only regret, headed home after a week and a half of business. Ate here six times over the week and a half and still don't have a favorite dish, but the Salmon is very good. Thanks Dominiqu, Virginia and Conner.

Grilled octopus, cold pea soup with chilled halibut... lamb chops grilled to perfection, mon Dieu The place is small, but it serves big flavors without overbearing sauces and seasonings. Very nicely done.

Wow, this place is crazy popular and so small.  Finally visited after coming super early and still having to wait.  My first margarita was crazy good but the second one was just ordinary.  Should've sent it back.  The food was pretty declines and tastes homestyle Mexican.  I can see why this place is so popular.

Great place, had lamb instead of my usual....chicken and garlic sauce.  Amazing! Service was really good, but we went on a slow night.  P.s. The lamb was done with cumin and hot peppers, the waiter said it was closer to traditional food....so worth it.  12.00 was the price for the dinner entree, very fair for the quality, too!

I am sad to say I agree with the other user that came here with groupon.  We had a reservation when we walked in it was 75 percent empty. We were seated after a few minutes at a table facing the kitchen and bathroom in like a little pocket of noise.  My husband asked to be moved and they didn't seem to want to, when we thought about leaving they started suggesting tables that had reservations in an hour and a half.  We were refused a window seat but did get a better table. We brought our own wine which they did not serve like the water pitchers they were thrown on the table and never looked back. After waiting quite a while someone took our order and 2 of the smallest Caesar salads I ever saw came out. Dinner I got battered chicken with aragola on the side.  My husband got chicken peppers over brocelli rabe. Both dishes were good but dry. We ordered a side of pasta which was good. The chocolate cake was very rich and dry.  Too chocholatty for us. More whip cream would have been nice. You had to ask servers for things like more water, they never seemed to be on our side of the room as it was empty. The bathrooms had holes in the walls, 80 dollars a couple and the floor was dirty too. It also took way to long for our table to pay as the servers were busy complaining about the only table on our side and their tip. And yes after the long waits between meals it took 2 hours and yes both window seats I wanted were empty when I left. Don't waste your time go to bellissimos down the street the food is only a little more and the service and food are a lot better.  As well as the decor.
everything good except the mac & cheese. Service is slow and stood there waiting 30  min before getting seated

Its a stylish gastro pizza pub ala Stella, their white pizzas has creme fraiche (giggle) and they offer truffle oil among their many toppings (eye roll).  I guess the pizza is NY style, small and crisp. The dining room is cramped and the chair legs and bar stools flare out which means getting around or dining is tight and jostly.  We saw many well behaved babies last night and it was pretty loud in there, poor servers have to practically yell. I did not see TVs, but I hear there are 3. Their beer selection is good/great and a dining companion who'd been to Italy liked their selection of Italian beers. A recent write up said their "scampi shrimp" was the "best shrimp EVER." I found them overcooked, greasy and steep at $18. I would not get them again, I would not recommend them and on return visits i will avoid all the small plates, except maybe salad. Pizzas comes in one size and start at $6, toppings extra. Family style small plates also available. Based on our experience I view this place a cramped and stylish a small step up from the perfectly good pizza and beer across the street. Amazing, that a new place can make any other place on P'shunk seem open and airy. Lastly, the menus has punctuation issues where a "-" is used both to connect 2 ideas "oompaloompa pizza - red pizza with orange meatballs" and as comma in the list of toppings "basil - garlic" Does that mean they have basil AND also garlic or that basil/garlic mixed together is one topping? Style over substance.
Service was fast and the food was so delicious! Not many tables so get there before the lunch rush! No complaints and will definitely be back soon!

Went yesterday and fell in love!! Delicious food, healthy organic ingredients , in a great space-- what more could you want.?? I had the red rice, chicken salad and kale salad with  a bottle of the homemade pomegranate iced tea.  Yummm!! Would reccomend to anyone and everyone!!

I was out and about during lunch today, so I figured I would stop in at Peppers.  This is a pick up your food and go kind of place - there is no seating, just a counter where you order and can see some of their offerings.  I got a beef patty ($2) and a brownie ($1).  The beef patty was decent, but kind of dried up.  The brownie, I regretting getting right away.  The worker put one brownie in a bag and then for some reason (which I probably don't want to know about), removed that brownie from the bag, placed it back on the tray, and selected a different brownie for me.  I considered this to be pretty odd. Anyway, I don't know that I'll be back here.  While the location was convenient for me and there was plenty of parking to be had, I think I would rather travel down Albany Ave to Scott's for any future beef patties.  With all the tastier offerings nearby here, this place needs to step up their game.
Was here again and it was great again. Noodle dishes and green curry are very good. Green curry is very spicy.....yummy. Worth the trip.

This is my 3rd time here! Food: Tasty! Considering I'm a meat eater! (sorry! But, at least I'm open minded to vegan, right? Lol). I was very surprised at how much flavor was in the Wac Jr on my first visit. Don't get me wrong. If you're a meat eater, it doesn't compare. HOWEVER, it is def a great alternative. I took off one star only bc it is pretty pricey. I've never spent $9.50 on ANY kind of burger. But, it was def worth it. I tried Chunky Monkey milkshake and I Am Happy shake - great taste! especially Chunky Monkey! Their chickpea patties on the wraps are good. Needs a bit more flavor, but not complaining at all! Maybe a little more serving of the Kale Slaw though, which tastes great! Tried the Drunken Chicken. It was ok. I think the BBQ sauce was overwhelming the natural taste of the chickpea patty. The day I ate this, my Kale Slaw was so overwhelmed by dressing that the Kale was soggy. No bueno. Also has the Cherry blossom tea. Nothing exciting. Hoping today's experience with the Mexicali and Strawberry Fields tea is better! Service: They are so kind. They bring your order out to you in great timing. Prob 10 min wait. Everyone has such a good energy, which is vital in customer service. Very clean, great ambiance! Check out the restroom! You instantly teleport into another dimension! #truestory lol

I was really looking for something special with the reviews. However, I just did not taste it in my slice. I had a plain slice while my wife tried the slice with fresh tomato's. Hers was definitely the better choice. I will give it another shot but it wasn't all that. Not bad mind you just not above anything else that you can get around here. Certainly not better than Vince's or Charlies in the Northeast. Or Tony's for that matter. Service was prompt and friendly.

Things that are minimal at Cafe Condesa: -The square footage -The attitude -The tab This place does tiny-village-bistro nearly perfectly.  The space is cozy, the service genuinely friendly, and the food?  The food is good.  If the food were amazing, this would be a five-star-find for sure. After scanning the simple, single-page menu, the hubs and I settled for sharing the brie appetizer and chicken mole entree.  Both were delicious, if just a little lacking in creativity.  I mean, Brie+honey+pine nuts=tasty, but definitely something I could make at home if I wanted to.  The chicken mole was also pretty good, but I kind of coveted the skirt steak that the guy at the next table was eating....next time, next time. Anyway, splitting both dishes was more than enough food for our light dinner.  Throw in a couple of glasses of wine and we had a lovely night out for 50 bucks!  We will definitely be back.

Had the most bizarre experience here tonight that will make me never come back. (Not that I would have anyway) Firstly the ramen here is pretty good (which is not the reason for the one star, more on that later). I had the miso ramen which was yummy for a chicken broth based soup. At first it tasted like I was eating chicken soup which I wasn't used to but I adjusted to it after biting into all of the yummy components of the dish. The pork was succulent, the egg was fully cooked (some say it should be runny), and the noodles were good. The broth was a little too salty to me. I'd say the best part of the dish were the noodles, they had the perfect level of chewiness and nice yellow color. My friend who is averse to pork had the same dish with chicken instead and it was not nearly as good. The chicken had that leftover chicken taste and was dry.  Was the ramen good, yes, was it better than any run of the mill ramen place on Saint Marks or anywhere else, no. It definitely didn't hold a candle to Ippudo. So here is why I'm giving this place a one star, after I paid and left, an employee ran out of the store and tried to force me to give a bigger tip in front of the crowd of people waiting outside. Maybe this was some sort of triumph for waiters everywhere but I found this extremely unprofessional and ridiculous. Admittedly, I left a bad tip. However, I think my tip was justified. After waiting for an hour we were finally bustled in and sat down. Oh, I forgot to mention they don't take cash so I had to run around the corner to the bank and take out money (with all the hype and business they get they can't upgrade allow credit?) There was water in cups already at our table. We ordered the food and when it was ready, some guy who wasn't our waiter quickly plopped my dish in front of me with his thumb almost in the ramen. I thought he was someone who just came into eat because he had a winter jacket and hat on then I realized he worked there. He yelled miso ramen in my ear and I asked him if it was the chicken or pork because my friend and I ordered both and he just yelled "miso ramen" again. Luckily another guy (I think our waiter?) had the next dish and said that's the pork and this is the chicken and more carefully placed it down. During the duration of our meal our water was not refilled. After we finished our bowls were quickly taken away and they laid down the check. I left my usual tip of just doubling the tax but then as I was putting on my jacket I realized they didn't even do anything. We waited for an hour in the cold only to be rushed in and have our food thrown down at us and be rushed out. So I subtracted a dollar from my tip bringing it down to an admittedly bad tip of around 12-13 percent. After we left someone who wasn't our waiter ran up to my friend and I (in front of the crowd of people waiting) and said something about how the tip was too low and he showed me the bill. I asked him if there was anything on the receipt or menu about a mandatory tip and he said no but in New York you usually double the tax and leave atleast 17-18 percent. I should have went off on him about how I'm from New York and the service sucked and I'm within my right to leave a crappy tip but I was so shocked I just said no and I didn't think the service was good. He gave me an evil look and walked away. Was I a jerk for leaving a bad tip, maybe, but I thought the service was bad and I'm within my right to leave a bad tip. I don't go around leaving bad tips everywhere. I leave a standard tip of doubling the tax and rounding up and I leave even more if the service was great. If you are a waiter you should ask yourself why the person is leaving you a bad tip instead of going outside and hounding them down for a dollar. Screw this place, the ramen is run of the mill and the employees are weirdos who don't understand the tipping system. **Also, I just read this place has a C rating in the other comments! Might not have even tried it if I knew that. Maybe health inspectors don't like it when you are hauling in bags of eggs from the grocery store and dropping the cartons all on the floor. Yes, I witnessed this while I was eating. If you read the other reviews here I think you'll find a pattern of poor hygiene and sanitation at this place.

I had the spare ribs which were not as tender as i would have liked, but they were still pretty good. Someone in my group also said that the chicken was undercooked too. It had a good price and both me and someone else in my group loved the yards root beer. This would be good for anyone who likes bbq a lot like me.
Very enjoyable meal. The mushroom and traditionelle were tasty and the sucrees apple flambé was a perfect dessert.

My friends and I headed to Philly out of hunger, but when we got there we didn't really know which restaurants were good, so we wandered around until we found this joint. The menu was decent, the place looked pretty busy, and we just wanted food in our stomachs ASAP, so we went in. The tea had this odd watered down taste. My friend's cup had some nasty gunk stuck inside it, which I suppose was foreshadowing. We ordered steamed pork xiao long bao, vegetable pan fried noodles, chicken with rice cakes, and crispy salt baked squid. Each item seemed to have its own problems. I'd say that the best dishes were the vegetable pan fried noodles and the chicken with rice cakes. Even then, the pan fried noodles had too much seasoning, and the rice cakes were decent, but a bit bland. The squid was VERY far from crispy, and I found it to be very bland. My friend said that the taste of sesame oil was overwhelming. The xiao long bao were okay, but some of them stuck so easily to the paper and the soup spilled out everywhere. Whoever said that these xiao long bao are comparable to those at Joe's Shanghai in NYC is clearly lacking a few taste buds... and I think that Joe's Shanghai's xiao long bao are overrated, so that's saying a lot. Next time we decide to do a food detour to Chinatown, we'll make sure we head toward the one in Manhattan, not Philly. I let myself down.

I have been eating here occasionally for years. The food is almost always good and generally never disappoints (save for the occasional leftover dry rice). The portions are healthy and the meat always tender. Dev's is great. I won't give it an additional star because the one thing that is consistent - the service is slow as molasses regardless of whether you call it in or order at the counter. I enjoy their food, so I endure. Their carrot cake is great, too. I usually get the jerk pork/curry goat with rice and peas and steamed cabbage. My daughter loves their roti and plaintains. Unfortunately, I just don't get there often these days and miss it!

Came here with the family late afternoon yesterday mostly because of the Craig LaBan review from the Inquirer.  I also read the Yelp reviews which were mostly positive.  I wanted to try some great BBQ and my birthday was right around the corner along with my anniversary a few days ago, it seemed like a good place to come.  The kids were supposed to be at home with the sitter, but she bailed and we ended up with them. Fette Sau is in a wonderful industrial like setting with exposed beams.  You line up cafeteria style and order by the pound for meats and then sides.  They come on a metal tray with some brown paper.  You can then try and get your picnic table (on a 5PM Friday we did not have to wait too long but it was very crowded by 6PM).  Alcoholic drinks are at another station, and you get your own silverware and plates near the entrance.  Sauces and napkins (paper towels) are at your table. We decided to buy a lot of different things, and then take home what was left over.  1 lb each of the St. Louis Ribs, pork belly, Black Angus Beef Short Ribs, and Pulled Pork.  1/2 chicken, and sides of mushrooms, sauerkraut, coleslaw, baked beans, and potato salad.  The meats are sold by the pound, the sides come in small or large (and the difference is not that much.) "Why is everything burnt?" my kids were asking and had to be told, "It's not burnt; it's blackened."   For the meats, everything was a winner except for the Short Ribs (but the leftovers were great with my eggs the next morning!)  My son loved the chicken, my daughter really liked the St. Louis ribs, and my wife liked the pulled pork.  I liked it all especially the pork belly.  The blackened meats were not a turn-off, and had decent seasoning on them all.  There was a vinegar sauce which we did not try, a sweet which my wife really liked, and a spicy which was a gorgeous dark thick sauce with some nice heat to it.  The sauces really perked up some great meats. For the sides, the mushrooms were out of this world, sauerkraut was nice and crunchy, baked beans had a peculiar flavor but we liked them anyway, and the coleslaw was a loser.  It was made with red cabbage and was too sour to be liked.  The potato salad I was the only one who really liked it as the rest of my family thought it had too much mustard taste to it.  I liked the huge chunks of potatoes and did not mind the mustardiness. For drinks, the self-serve water had too small of plastic cups.  They had plenty of beer on tap, but none of that Coors or Miller or Bud crap which my wife likes.  She had to go with the lightest beer they had which was a pillsner and she was not too fond of it.  I got an awesome Jacks Cider.  I went back later for a cocktail of a lemonade which had whiskey in it.  Wife hated it; I liked it.  They have a lot of different whiskey to purchase. For dessert, we got two bacon brownies.  They pretty much make bacon and cut it up and put it in the brownie mix.  The brownies we got were not spongy, but a little too hard and although you could see bacon pieces, I don't know if you got the bacon flavor.  I think we should have went for the key-lime pie. As a bonus, the head chef was out and about and I asked to see the kitchen.  He showed me, and it consists of two $30,000 machines which do the grilling, and a couple of flash ovens.  Even the chef "apologized" for not being too much to look at, but as I said it still makes awesome, kick ass food. With drinks, desserts, taxes, tips, our meal for the four of us (with plenty of leftovers) came to about $160.
The grilled chicken salad is the best. I get it Everytime I go there. Do yourself a favor and try it.best salad on the block.

One of the handful of great taprooms the city of Philadelphia has to offer! I even found a rare Victory beer on tap. The bartenders are friendly and well informed and can suggest anything great for you. I like that they offer 2 types of large bottles to drink there or to go.   The food is fantastic! Our group of 6 had ordered various items from the menu;all of which were delicious. There's a hint if Polish ethnicity behind a lot of the foods there:cabbage,kielbasa,pierogies. I can't wait to go back!

The short: a reasonably priced pizza joint in lower Manhattan, featuring instant service and fantastic crust, but disappointingly sparse toppings and no refills. The long: Pizzas start at $20 for 18 inches, which is not terrible for lower Manhattan sit-down. We 3 guys ordered the standard Margherita pizza to start with. To our amazement, the pizza literally came in about 6-8 minutes, hot and fresh. Wow, that was fast! It tasted great too, really fresh tasting margherita sauce that wasn't heavy but not watery. The cheese was in chunks, good portion. But the most special part of this pizza was the crust. It was a crunchy exterior with a warm and chewy interior. And not oily so no cheating with a sear effect! Delicious! Unfortunately it was thin so we were still hungry, but that's not their fault. We ordered a sausage pizza to fill us up. This one also came real fast and we started to chow down. But to our real disappointment, there were probably maybe 10-12 tiny sausage slices on the entire pizza. I mean I get it, times are tough now. But seriously? Come on! $3 for 3 oz of sausage? That's a rip anywhere, even Manhattan! Plus the pop costs $2 per glass, they fill it half with ice, and it's no refills. So to summarize, come get the pizza, it tastes great. But if they gyp you on the toppings, don't be surprised. It looks NOTHING like the toppings in the photos from years past that are posted here. And sneak in your own Coke so you're not paying for a glass of Coke-flavored ice.

After walking up and down Church Street searching for a Saturday lunch spot with 3 other friends, we settled on this spot. The result was unremarkable food, sluggish service, and a sleepy ambiance. SETTING: The interior is your run of the mill bar/pub with dark masculine interior, a big screen TV (that happened to be showing some strong man or tough mudder competition of some sort). Perhaps it was telling that most other places on Church Street had a wait, and this one was barely half full. SERVICE: A little on the slow side considering how empty the restaurant was, but otherwise nothing much to note. She didn't really seem keen on going the extra mile to split the check (although she probably would have done it if we asked her to--both parties were too lazy to make the effort). FOOD: I ordered a black bean burger with sweet potato fries, which was whatever. I'm not sure why the patty came out the color it did, but it was deceptively edible. One of my friends ordered a Heady Topper, which is apparently a rare thing (Aside from the occasional Stella, I'm not much of a beer junkie), so that was kind of cool. Other than that, no real highlights from the food. All in all, an experience invoking little emotions. I probably wouldn't return on my own volition...

They are busy , they are really busy ! I made a reservation that was two days prior , I mean two day prior for a dinner is overrated. My reservation was on a Sunday but I didn't know where to go for dinner on Sat , so I canceled the reservation and had take out. It was really good, despite being take out. Taco Tasting Platter This platter consisted an assorted selection of sea bass, beef, chicken, carnitas, and mahi taco. They sea bass taco was so tasty ! I had a bite of each, they were all really tasty but I didn't really like the shell. Red Snapper a la Veracruzana The fish was cooked to perfection, so tender and juicy, very fresh ! Chicken Quesadilla it's an open face quesadilla, it seemed more like a pizza to me . It was good but not amazing , couldn't remember much of it. shrimp enchilada it was my favorite dish of the night , it really hit the spot, this will make a great comfort food. would definitely come into the restaurant next time and try there cocktails.
Best brunch in NYC. Lemon ricotta pancakes rock.

Royale disappointed me after reading all these reviews here. I came here for a bday so there was a good amount of people (~20 people), but my burger took about an hour to finally arrive. It's not fun having to watch other people eat while i'm starving! After telling a different waiter, she brought the burger out within 10 min so the 2nd star is for her. Otherwise this review would be a 1. I got the Cheese Royale burger and it had uneven seasoning. I would get bites of saltiness and then the other bites were bland. As for the onion rings and fries? A bit too soggy for my taste.

If you ever decide to go to Salute be sure to have a game plan because this place is always impossibly crowded! Despite it's remote location off the main drag of downtown Montclair, patrons flock to Salute for a truly wonderful Italian experience. The atmosphere is rustic Italian almost like a market feel with produce hanging in baskets and a fairly open kitchen. It's rather dark but the windows are usually open and outdoor seating is offered, weather permitting. The service is just ok but everyone is very friendly and the owner/host-with-the-most is charming and charismatic. I really love the menu selection and the fact that it is pretty safe to say that you will thoroughly enjoy whatever you order on the menu. I had numerous chicken dishes here and enjoyed each and every one. The appetizers are also excellent. With the right appetite and the willingness to wait, you can really have a great dinner here. It's perfect for family dinners or dates. There are also a few TV's that show games, etc. so you don't have to deprive yourself of Sunday football to have some great Italian food.

I usually sit outside on the patio, which during colder months is enclosed and heated. The menu is pricey considering the quality of the food, but I guess your paying Princeton prices.  The appetizers - namely, the nachos - are a good sized portion of yum. They offer some decent beers on tap including Bass, Smithwicks, Sam, Stella, and Pilsner Urquell; however, the red wine selection (by the glass) is pretty awful. They offer a vegetarian option or two, but it's usually a wrap or your typical frozen veggie burger.  Don't be surprised to find lackluster service.

A cliche of a popular place shouldn't be this good.
