We started with a deliciously meaty, nonrubbery octopus salad with vinegary, thin fennel and pretty green and kalamata olives atop a bright purple radicchio bed. To help whet and appetize us further, we snagged the pear starter with herbed goat cheese, complex honey and a dainty little pile of arugula. Someone noncolorblind person in charge cares about aesthetics. Soon thereafter... the pizzas. ooohhhh boy. I'm a pizza eater for sure, but I don't have a fancy vocabulary about regions and supposedtobes. The crust was burny but not too crunchcrunch, the sauce was yummy and not yucky. Ovest: The ricotta was sweet and thick, and sparely dolloped atop the big salty salame slices. I didn't notice the promised garlic. Arugola: As usual, prosciutto, arugula and razor sharp parmesan make a good team. Our white wines were a little boring, but the gorgeous wine tree on the corner of the bar was not. And neither was the foxy gentleman pouring. Yow.

How does my girlfriend's  neighborhood fave go from three stars to two?  Terrible service.  If it's not the audacity of not being credit card convenient in the 21st century then it was definitely last night's I don't care attitude from our waitress.  Service was erratic and sloppy.  How do the tables to my left and right receive their entrees before us if they entered the restaurant afterwards?   What restaurant delivers one entree and not the other.  If we entered as a couple chances are we wanted to eat together.  This should not be lost on you.  Ever. Finally I left a .70 tip.  I thought you deserved less, but I was so furious that I left the change for my convenience.

Had the ropa vieja. Delicious. They could add more meat, but it tasted like home. Being born in Miami, I've been craving a good Cuban meal. Tina's provided that to me for lunch. Decent price point and good flavor. Gotta have me some arroz y frijoles.

Plenty is actually short for Plenty o Awesome food and service. I still visit here when I'm in the area and still receive great tasting food. I thoroughly enjoy the taste of the sandwiches and they stay true to their Passyunk staple. No complaints here.

Whenever I crave Fresh Noodles this is the Place Good stuff. Dumplings are pretty good along with soups wich are Amazing. Small restaurant looks like a Dive but we are in Chinatown not Midtown. Did  I mention Guy Fieri stopped By!!!

This is my favorite dumpling place! Hands down! For all the Vanessa lovers out there, the difference between these two dumpling place are Prosperity has more meat in their dumplings and Vanessa has more vegetables. So depending on what you like more of, that would factor your decision. For me, it's meat :) and yes I did a test run between these two dumpling houses. Sometimes I question what meat was used, 5 dumplings for $1??!! But I learned to stop asking questions a long time ago, especially when it relates to food.

If you want to feel like you are in Japan without actually going there this is the place for you. I have been to the one in Japan and this is as close as you can get. Great Sake selection and the experience at the grill is a must. Nothing like eating freshly cooked food.

Whatever happened to customer service!  First walking in the hostess was talking to another staff member and did not even acknowledge customers walking in...no hello, can I help you...so we decided to go to the bar.  Found 3 seats at the end of the bar which had a weird "L" shape at the end.  Drink menu too "out" there.  Ordered drinks to which the bartender seemed like he was doing us a favor!  No napkin under drink.. bartender actually pushed the drinks in front of us....very, very poor....felt like I was at Applebee's or TGI Fridays.  For the price of the drinks, at the very least we could have received a hello!  Two more of our friends came in the bar to meet us and had a hard time getting the bartender's attention so our friends could get some drinks. The bar was not that busy....and the bartender could not handle it.   The bartender totally made the experience bad....previous Lahiere's, which we have gone to many, many times, the bartender Chris Canavari was always cordial, courteous and knew how to make a drink!    Bring in Chris for great customer service!!!          The 5 of us walked out after our drinks and went to another "grill" down the street.  Why stay for dinner after that!

As you enter into this small restaurant, you immediately can smell the aroma of Ethiopian spices being cooked. The menu has so many vegetarian options. While I got the spiced tea made with cloves, cinnamon and cardamom, my friend ordered the Ethiopian coffee. Both were very potent and good. For appetizers, we ordered the Veggie Sambusa, similar to an Indian samosa with lentils. I wish they gave us a dipping sauce or something to go along with it as it was very dry. We ordered the veggie combo where we can pick six items( Aterkik Alicha, Atkilt Salata,Shimbra Asa, Misr Wat, Shiro, Misir Alicha). I highly recommend the Shiro and Misir Wat as they were my favorite. The injera bread was rolled up and simply soft and delicious. We used that to dip into our puréed lentils. The waiter also gave me spice powder and hot sauce as I like it very spicy. The food here is amazing and definitely worth checking out.
Excellent food... Loved it even though it broke my tooth!

This place was TERRIBLE.  All I could think of was "Over".  Overrated, overpriced, over-hyped.  I joined a coworker for his birthday dinner, which he had booked ahead of time and also put in for their $200 pork butt "feast".  The place was empty since it was a snowy Tuesday.  First off, the hyperly rude manager wouldn't budge at all about us moving two tables together so birthday boy sat between the two tables and used a chair as a table while the party was split between the two.  Next came the more mind-blowing event of the night.  When they brought out the "pork butt" it was actually a pork shoulder and puny.  Look, I grew up in Indiana and we know pig.  This place knows how to bend over their customers and that's about it.  The pork was so-so, but I've had better at high school graduation parties.  $200?  C'mon.  That's like $90 a pound and a good portion of that was bone and a thick layer of fat.  Apps were also so-so, but can anyone explain the $12 for pickled vegetables?  As anyone with any kind of experience making canned / brined vegetables knows, you do it in a large batch.  What should have been FREE was $12.    The rest of the food was bland, riddled with thick layers of fat or small portions for the price.  As for the mythic pork buns?  The reason they melt in your mouth is that 95% of it is fat!  And after shelling out $45 (each, the bill came to $540 for the party) most of us then went and got food after that since we were all still hungry! Save your money, sanity and health and go anyplace else.  I wish I would have done the smart thing and go to White Castle and saved myself $40.

My twin kept raving about this place, how friendly the staff is.  She's a regular there, and often gives them a shout out on her IG NakiaTakesNewYork.  So we went there on Saturday for dinner and I must say I was thoroughly impressed.  Albeit the seating, you're literally sitting next to strangers and sharing a rather small table.   But hey I didn't mind because the food and drinks were so flipping amazing! I would totally recommend the lychee martinis which are only $5 during happy hour. I got the Lo - wer east side mien with chicken and shrimp and it was really good. And the won-tons are absolutely divine. So I would totally recommend this place, great food and affordable prices.

What can I say about blend on the water that hasn't been said before! Wow what an amazing experience! The food the service just the total package! I had the crispy areas to start... Perfection!!!! Came on Monday and it was happy hour all night. You can't beat that! Was greeted by a gentleman who was quite the eye candy I might say lol very professional and ensured quality service to me and my date! I will definitely be back soon! Blend on the water you have a new fan!

Lots of tasty claw meat on a perfectly buttered top cut bun, just as it should be. Just a kiss of mayo, nothing else. You get the lobster roll a slice of pickle, a bag of Cape Cod chips, and a choice of Maine Sodas (I tried the Sasaparilla ) for $17. What more can you ask for? Next time I will try the Taste of Maine, which is a sample of the Lobster, Crab and Shrimp rolls.

I recently dined at blend on the water . I must say I was in aw with the restaurant it self it was beautiful with breath taking views . The service is extremely attentive from the moment you walk in and your greeted by Syeda at the deskshe is  very sweet welcoming efficient and professional . I was accommodated as promptly as possible considering it was a Saturday night and my party did not have a reservation . We even received a text when our table was ready . The server Michelle was truly awesome very knowledgeable of the menu and friendly and made us feel comfortable .Michelle even noticed our food was taking too  long and with out us having to ask she came told us that she would find out what was taking so long . I've been in the hospitality industry for quite sometime  and that kind of initiative could turn a bad situation right around which it did . The spiced shrimp were to die for I honestly think it should be an entree as I could not get enough, next time I go I  will just order three of those. We ordered the churrasco and the pollo a la plancha . The churrasco was cooked just as I ordered and it was succulent and juicy  but smaller than I had imagined very thin but other wise yummy.  The pollo a la plancha which by definition should be grilled, it was not , might of been poached (truth in menu laws people) but my friend said it was still very good although she preferred my chimichurri sauce to her mystery sauce.  Over all it was a great experience, I did forget to mention how delicious they're passion fruit margaritas are OMG . I would definitely return and recommend it to my friends .

Went to BurgerFi around 12:30 on a Friday. The restaurant had a solid crowd but it was not overcrowded. This was my first time there so I ordered the BurgerFi cheeseburger(just a regular cheeseburger with L, T, and house sauce) & fries. It was a solid burger, better than average, but not the greatest burger ever. Sauce was pretty good with some bold flavors and better than having the typical ketchup on it, so I would definitely recommend getting that. I received a hefty portion of fresh cut and golden brown fries so no complaints with that item. I would say the burger and fries are comparable to Five Guys. I haven't been to the other burger chains like Elevation Burgers, Shake Shack, etc so I don't know how it compares those places. The service was fast. They gave us a buzzer for when our food was done. We waited about 5-10 minutes for 2 cheeseburgers and 2 fries. The tables were clean &, the cashier was super friendly. The burger, fries, and small soft drink came to about $13 which is average for a meal in center city if you go to some of the other food outlets or terminal. Overall it was a good experience and I would definitely visit again based on the taste, price/portion and service.

This is where brunch starts and ends in Philadelphia. I'm not saying its the best, but its my barometer for all other brunch spots I go to. The food is reasonably priced, they have a great selection of vegan and vegetarian items, and the portions are huge. Also, the servers are great people who don't blink when you give them multiple cards or take all their small bills. My favorites on the menu are the stuffed French toast (check the specials menu for interesting variations), the barking chihuahua, the greek salad, and any of their burgers.

I am not sure I would wait in line for two hours, but we had a very positive experience here. We showed up at 5:15 on a Sunday and were seated right away. We had eggplant salad and a whole fried porgy (a special, but judging from other reviews one that seems to be available somewhat frequently). Both were very fine, with a rich and complex blend of flavors which I might be too unsophisticated to deconstruct.  The fish relied heavily on tamarind, and I might have to experiment more with that spice at home. The ambience was surprisingly quiet and charming for such a trendy restaurant. This is a contrast to the cramped and loud vibe that characterizes some other NYC restaurants that try to be hip. One con: weak cocktails. My girlfriend got a gin and tonic that was seriously lacking in gin. We overheard the waitress tell another table that the cocktails are not very strong.

Pretty much amazing. Great concept. Great location (though I haven't actually been there I just looked at the map). Great staff. Great product. I was looking for somewhere to get delivery from on a Saturday afternoon after a loooong night of celebration. I had heard about plenty some time ago from a friend who I don't consider to be particularly knowledgeable in food so I had put it on the back back burner of my mind. I came across the amazing reviews on yelp, saw they delivered and I was all set. Called them up and the woman on the phone was very patient explaining menu items and offers to me as well as very informed about their products. Me and a friend ended up going with one tasso ham panini, one pulled pork sandwich, a side of mac and cheese, a side of green beans and bacon, and a side of some kinda brussel sprout casserole. All were phenomenal. The tasso ham was so great. Everything was cooked to perfection and retained just the right amount of flavor and texture. The food is hearty and plentiful as the name would suggest, but you never really find yourself overwhelmed by grease or fat. It is used sparingly yet liberally at the same time. Paradoxical. Anyways, HIGHLY recommend. The prices are not cheap, but they're not astronomical either. I'll have to venture to the actual storefront soon to see the whole package, but from what I experienced this past Saturday I have no doubts that the entire operation is top notch.

Ate here for the first time last week. It was a wonderful experience. My cousins were in the area, so we came into the city to meet them for dinner. I was not familiar with the are so I searched the internet for an Italian place on W 56th St and I am so happy I came across this place! We made a 7:30 reservation, but unfortunately my mother and I were running late. They were so nice and accommodating although we didn't get there until almost 8. Our server was very knowledgeable about the menu including the wine selection. To start off, they sent out bruschetta on the house and we ordered a caprese salad; caprese would be a good size for one or two people. I got the homemade gnocchi: DELICIOUS and the perfect size. My mother and my cousin cleaned their plates as well; they each got some sort of pappardelle dish. My cousin's husband was the only one who hadn't eaten much of his dish, but he is definitely not one to complain. The server noticed he hadn't eaten much and asked how he liked his dish and he insisted it was okay. When the bill came, they had taken his dish off the bill! I was very impressed, sets a restaurant apart with such great service. For an Italian restaurant in the city, especially with such great service, prices are reasonable. Next time I'm in the area, I will definitely be dining here again!

The pizza me and my friend ordered was a margharita with pepporoni. It was good, but I wouldn't come all the way to Brooklyn again for this because there are all the other same quality, if not better quality places in the city. It was still some tasty pizza. However, I'd like to give a 4-star to their Porchetta sanwich. It was 2 slices of suckling pork with a touch a mayo and sprinkle of the pickled onions on toasted baquette. Crunchy bites with juicy and flavorful meat in the mouth was a great experience. The lettuce was slightly dressed and perfect - it was fresh and crispy. I would prob just go to the madison sq park location for the porchetta sandwich, if they make it just as good.

One of the most memorable meals I've had in a while... The staff was friendly & knowledgable. The wine list was extensive and REASONABLE. The bar tender even asked if we were OK to spend $48/bottle on our selection, a great California Cab. Maybe, I'm a jaded, snobby NYer, but that was a breath of fresh air. The artichoke salad and the Paella were both incredible... CANT WAIT TO GO BACK!

I knew this place was going to be good, I just wasn't prepared for how good it really was. Recently opened, this place is super cute with a rustic feel. The decor isn't fancy at all, feels like an underground space that specializes in something and this is clearly the food. We started with the mac and cheese and that really set the stage for what we were about to experience. It was nice and creamy with a bit of crunch from the ritz cracker topping. A little pricey for the portion we received, but definitely delicious. Not a must try, but it's worth trying. More importantly - the chicken and waffles. He had the parm and I had the specail mikes hot sticky chicken and when they dropped the plates on the table, I knew I was in for a treat. I never eat chicken skin, even when it's fried, but no piece was left untouched or uneaten. I inhaled the crunchiness of the skin, with just the right amount of kick. The chicken was so juicy and not one piece was dry. Rip open the skin and the chicken is steaming on the inside. They know how to cook chicken. Don't even get me started on the light, crispy waffle that was paired with this piece of heaven. Eaten both separate and with the chicken, it was just perfect. If there was such thing as perfection, it would be a plate of chicken and waffles from Sweet Chick. Service was amazing. They were so friendly, didn't rush us and gave us their recommendations on what to get. As soon as we finished our food, they were right there ready to take our plates. The place was slowly getting packed, but not once did it feel like we were being rushed out. You have to try this place and one you do, you'll be hooked!

Went here for lunch to order espresso, coffee and paninis. Espresso is bland and diluted whereas coffee was flavorless and luke warm. Food quality used to be fantastic but now panini are served cold and dry. we complained to the server but he didn't respond to our lack of satisfaction. So one star to food and service quality!

I've been to this place a number of times.  We went there recently this past Saturday night and guess what, it was busy! Awesome! This little hole in the wall place serves some mighty delicious pizza.  We had a large pizza with onions, bacon and the other half sausage.  It was fresh and the crust was crispy.  I just remembered this place today and have been craving pizza, so I find myself writing about it. Tell your friends to  at least try it out.

I'm glad I live 1000 miles away, or else with places like this filled with food and people so easy to love I would never ever see my toes again. The ladies behind the counters rawk! Liz and (I'm so bad with names, so I will just call her beautiful lady 2) put my first night in philadelphia to bed with their warm smiles, and awesome sense of taste as I just let them fix me up with my cheese steak the way they liked it and it was goooood. Provolone, onions, mushrooms, and then I threw some flaked peppers and jalapenos on the top to be finished with a Yuengling... Damn. this place is money... Sitting next to regulars who celebrate their birthdays here and hungry Phillies fans while watching the game on the little flat screen it was a nice glimpse into daily Philadelphia life.

Anything I've ordered here has been delicious and well-priced. The service is very good too, with polite and attentive staff. If you celebrate a birthday here, tell the waiters and they'll sing! The song is pretty hilarious, even if they don't mean it to be. Whenever people want to go to PF Chang's up the road, I suggest this place instead. Better food, better prices. Not overly sweetened and modified for tastebuds of people who don't know how to eat asian food.

I honestly don't understand where such high ratings are coming from. I  decided to check out Tabare relying on Yelp and i must admit this was the first time it let me down. Went there for dinner yesterday. While the empanadas are pretty good, the menu is very limited. Staff seems like they don't know what they are doing. Brought us wrong orders twice, while the restaurant was nearly empty. We spent a long time waiting for our food and usually it is never an issue for me, as long as it is worth it! I had a special, pasta stuffed with cheese and spinach in lemon sauce. VERY VERY disappointing. My expectations of the place were pretty high so i was nearly crying after trying their food. The pasta was very bland and really unmemorable. Same goes for the swordfish. Season unevenly and not impressive. We decided to skip the drinks for obvious reasons. Only pro anout the place is very cute decor and super cute patio. My verdict: i won't be back.

Best pizza I have had to date in NYC. I used to live a block away from Adrienne's and the only thing I regret is not knowing about the restaurant the day that we moved into the neighborhood. My boyfriend and I always went for the square pizza with pepperoni and mushroom. One word - amazing. Perfectly crispy, mushrooms were cooked all the way through which is what I prefer (so many other places will just throw raw mushrooms on top of the cooked pizza). Even though we don't live in the neighborhood anymore, it is definitely worth going back for!

I'll cut to the chase - the food is 3 stars and the atmosphere is 5 stars.  Amazing place to sit outside in the spring / summer and enjoy the surroundings of the center.  The service is a bit slow, but nothing extraordinarily bad like some have alluded to.  Go here when you want to relax and not stare at the clock! As far as the food goes, it's run of the mill stuff.  Decent omelets, pancakes, and other breakfast options, but nothing to alert the presses about.

Went here for brunch with my BF, my friend and her husband on a Sunday...EXCELLENT!! Servers were VERY attentive and educated us on what was good, not and what wasn't available. The Apple cobbler is to die for..LOVED IT!! Great food and great service. Grits with shrimps and lobster...good..small portion but don't let it fool you, very filling:-)

With its' emerging popularity amongst the local natives, my brother and I like to call this place one of our secret spots.  We've been working on our foodie careers and Red Eye is definitely on our list of places to eat.  Every time we go, it has gotten better and better.   1st trip) My brother ordered the Turkey sandwich with the pear & brie. I ordered the Blue Velvet (roast beef with the pickled blueberries). Incredible.  The both of us were in awe of how delicious they were.   2nd trip) We came for breakfast with our mother. The Red Eye hash, the chorizo frittata and the green eggs & ham were all consumed. Super delicious. 3rd trip) This has been my favorite so far.  I ordered the same sandwich while my brother got something different that I can't remember but he said was delectable.  The dessert was the winner though.  Fresh mint ice cream for me and the coconut cream cake for him. Amazing.   I can see how the service can be a little spotty at first just because there really isn't a designated "hostess" type area. But otherwise everyone has been super chill and helpful.  The atmosphere is nice and relaxed. No yuppies or overbearing waiters, no loud customers on cell phones. Our next visit will be for dinner!

sunnyside hollaaa!!! (alright so i've only dwelled here for 6 months, but i'm damn proud of it!) this surprisingly clean and silverware laden restaurant with the non-greasy floor (like most places around here) is conveniently 3 blocks away from my humble abode. it's a gem and definitely a great intimate date place in the middle of sunnyside's mecca of fast food take out spots. i believe i've had the grilled chicken torta 3 weekends in a row. crispy chewy bread smeared with guac, refried beans, jalapenos, onions, lettuce, tomato,  and your choice of meat. never failed to hit the spot. my weekend roommate swears by the chicken burrito con mole poblano. their nachos are real NACHOS. not your nachos with cheez whiz and a dallop of sour cream here. there's enough toppings to go around for each chip. good toppings to chip ratio. i hate it when theres not enough toppings and you have to eat it consciously so your last few chips wont enter your mouth naked. definitely get the guac made to order and the tres leches...ohh yes the tres leches. once it came with mango chunks on top. so delishis. can you say flavor of loove??

Good food and drink but that's not what impressed me. The service was better than 90% of the restaurants I've dined in in NYC. The staff was friendly, accommodating and efficient. Even though we had an hour wait across the street everyone we came in contact with was helpful and a joy to be around. That's what really made this place stand out.

If you're going to have a full course dinner at a diner, then this would seem to be the place to go.  The main course may not be what a good, good restaurant serves but you will have a decent meal, at a reasonable price, and either leave the place with a doggie bag or feeling extremely full.  For a smaller eater, and I am not one, you will probably leave feeling very full and also with the doggie bag. The dinner specials all come with soup, salad bar, and dessert.  I thought their salad bar was great.  It had a Greek salad, creamed herring, peel and eat shrimp, beets, and the rest of the items that one finds on most salad bars. For my main, I had the twin filet of sole stiffed with crab meat.  I was glad to see that it was not drenched in butter like at so many other diners.  My M-I-L and the twin tilapia and said it was very good grilled.  Unfortunately, my crab meat stuffing was more bread filler than anything else and that was a little disappointing.   Our server was extremely accommodating and most helpful.   Obviously if you are looking to dine then go to a "restaurant" but if you have been on the road all day like we were, are starving, and want to have a decent dinner without frills then this "diner" is it.

The restaurant itself is cute and trendy. I would have to say the food is just ok. Stay away from the Fettuccine with Rock Shrimp & Lobster Broth. It is EXTREMELY disappointing. We also got the buffalo mozzarella and grilled tomato salad; cannot believe they charge $13 for this. It just wasn't very good. Two things I really enjoyed were the falafel crusted scallops and the hanger steak. Overall, food was not worth the prices. If you want a place with nice ambience and don't mind overpaying on mediocre food this is definitely the place.

One of the best Mexican restaurants in Philly hands down. Although it's not traditional Mexican they do a great job of cooking up innovative new takes on the classics such as crab and lobster tacos with mango salsa. They also make fresh guacamole to order, though at $12 a serving it's way over priced. There is definitely something for everyone here with poultry, meat, seafood, and vegetarian options. The drink menu is solid for a Mexican place with the required margaritas and tequila. The restaurant again takes a new twist on the old favorites with blood orange margaritas, pomegranite margaritas, no tequila margaritas, and some interesting sangria combinations. Service was pretty attentive except for refilling the water. The only things that keep this place from getting 5 stars is that it is amazingly loud and there are way too many smokers for my taste given that the bar is in the center of the tables. Be sure to check out the photo booth if you go in.

First time here. Food was delicious. Had shrimp and grits and the sauce on it was to die for. Our server was friendly. The beer was delicious! The only problem was it took long to get our food. Really long  and there wasn't a lot of people in the place. Overall, I would recommend it.

I tried the Masala Dosa ($7) but Ashiwad (Upland, CA) still remains my favorite for this particular dosa. My favorite item here was kati rolls. I had the Achari Paneer Roll ($8) which was grilled Indian cottage cheese cubes marinated in a spicy pickle rolled in Indian flat-bred. I will be coming back to try their other dosas and to get more kati rolls.

Of all the ramen places in New York, this is probably the best I've tried so far, though I have to deduct points for the 2 hour wait (how do people put up with the wait???). The pork buns were pretty satisfying - a lot better than the ones I've had at momofuku. I ordered the akamaru modern with extra braised pork belly and the broth reminded me of the broth at Santouka (my favorite ramen place BY FAR on the east coast), though slightly lighter with more of an upscale twist, but still enough complexity to leave me satisfied. I have to say this ramen is rather expensive, but I guess that's what you get for upscale/modern ramen!

Stopped in for dinner but ended up just getting a double round of the Thu special; Sam Adams and wings for just $8! The beer selection was very good, the wings were great as was the service and ambience. A traditional Irish band set up and started playing while we were there and they were lagit. Overall a great experience here. Oh and my buddy got the chicken sheppards pie thing which he said was very good also. Definately try this place. I liked it...

Took an online recommendation and tried this place out and it was fantastic. Just the sort of place you'd expect to find in this neighborhood. Menu is amazingly diverse; there's something for everyone who's willing to be adventurous.

The food was exceptional. I have a little problem with the douchyness of a place called the cafeteria asking me to remove my hat when seated in the "dining area." The service was great, the atmosphere was the usual new york crowded and loud. I had the chicken and waffles, my only disappointment was that the chicken is three pieces of bone-in, which took some of the joy out of the combo. The Mac Attack is to die for and the biscuits are descended strait from angels and rainbows glazed with the blood of unicorns.
The egg and bacon sandwich on a croissant is amazing!

I was very excited to try out Xochitl, the menu looked delicious and I'd heard so many great reviews from friends. I'm happy to report it didn't disappoint. It's in such a beautiful little corner of Headhouse Square. I actually screwed up on the reservation and made it for the wrong day so we showed up on a Sunday without an actual reservation. However they were able to seat us at a small table in the bar area. It worked out for the best because we were able to get the happy hour specials. I had a couple margaritas and they were really fantastic. They were definitely fresh. For an appetizer we had one of the guacamole specials that included pine nuts and cilantro. It was mouth watering. It they would have handed me a vat full of it and a spatula I would have polished it off. My only gripe about it at check time is that it cost $13, when regular tableside guac cost $8. Next time I think we'll just go with the traditional guacamole. For dinner I had the Bistec Azteca, which was a skirt steak with avocado fries. The steak was tender and delicious, although not remarkable. The star of the show was the avocado fries. Seriously. Why have I never had this before? Why have I never made this before? The hot avocado inside the fried outside was creamy and absolutely phenomenal. Thinking of it right now is making me hungry. Truly the star of the night. My husband had the pork tenderloin. Of the two meats I preferred his, the seasoning was strong, and I definitely recommend. For dessert we had churros with chocolate dipping sauce. They were your traditional churros and brought us back to churros for breakfast in Mexico. Xochitl is definitely my favorite Mexican restaurant in the city.

So good - my favorite is the sandwich with spicy pork meatballs and peso or parmesan cream sauce.  Interestingly, the simple salad that comes with the sandwiches is AMAZING and I normally really don't like salads. All the sides are excellent. food comes out very fast so be ready to eat!  Well worth the wait and there usually is one.  No reservations, though.

So good and so cheap. Reasonably quick considering how crowded they usually are. Bonus - you can get their dumplings frozen for future, at-home noshing. Recs - the fried pork bun and duck sesame pancake.

I would come here multiple times a week if parking weren't such a b*tch. But this place is so great! I have only visited on Saturdays because that is when they serve their smoked tomato bisque. I had to grab my waitress' attention to tell her that the soup had changed my life. I've had paninis, crostinis, and I have tried cheeses that I've never heard of in their cheese plate. Everything was great! You're going to have to wait since it is pretty popular, but the wait is worth it!

Bouley is definitely on the same level as some of my favorites Eleven Madison Park, Gotham Bar and Grill, and Daniel. I settled on the tasting menu and they allowed me to make a few changes. I changed my first course and dessert and they did not blink an eye! It was designed to be 6 courses but after all the freebies and extras it turned out to be an 11 or so course feast. The service was impeccable and attention to detail amazing. They came around with 2 different bread baskets. The first included a delicious apple-walnut bread and baguette (which I don't like) from Bouley Bakery while I looked at the menu. Then after my amuse they came around with three more - pistachio, raisin, and sourdough. Here is what I ate and yes every single course was absolutely spectacular. The tasting menu portions were very very generous and I left feeling very satisfied, if not even a little over full. They started me off with a pumpkin soup that had a ricotta crema and chestnut. This was fall in a bowl. I usually don't get hyped up about amuses but this was great. Porcini Flan, Alaska Live Dungeness Crab, Black Truffle Dashi- There had to be about a half pound of crab in this "little" pot. I do not know what the regular size is but if this was any indication it must have a pound of crabmeat in it. The broth was sinfully awesome. Chatham Day Boat Lobster Brown and White Honshimeji Mushrooms, Fresh Passion Fruit & Mango, Fresh Lychee, Hyssop- Wonderful lobster and the sauces were a great compliment. Again a very nice portion size which I was grateful for. Definitely not stingy with lobster meat- nice tail and big claw. Live Sea Scallops & Nantucket Bay Scallops Prepared in a Tandori Manner, with Spices Imported from a Friend's Spice Shop in Paris, Local Curried Cauliflower Puree- This was the lightest course with 3 little scallops and one large one. The spice was a very nice tough. Although this was my least favorite, the dish was executed nicely. Organic Long Island Duckling Roasted with Truffle Honey, Puree of Nevada Organic dates with Turnips, Julienne of Local Beets- This was a knockout of a dish. Perfectly cooked rare duck and nice crispy crunchy skin on it. The truffle honey sauce was incredible as I love the balance between the saltiness of duck and sweetness of sauce. Coconut soup with Pineapple granite and Yogurt sorbet- This was a pre-dessert but omg it may have been the best thing I ate all night! You would think this would be an after thought but I could have had five more. It was like the best pina colada I have ever had. The coconut soup, pineapple, and the sorbet were perfection personified. Amaretto Flan Caramelized Banana, White Coffee Mousse Amaretto and Vermont Maple Ice Creams- I subbed this because I didn't want to try the ubiquitous molten chocolate cake and I was not disappointed. I LOVE Amaretto and this was so delicious. The "flan" was like a 4 inch rectangule of amaretto custard and the tablespoon of bananas paired with the delicious quenelles of ice cream were perfect. As if that were not enough they gave me a complimentary dessert also which I could not finish. At this point I was bursting. Oh yeah and the petit fours tower too. So many treats and so delicious. Loved the atmosphere and the service was great without being intrusive. Overall, when putting it all together Bouley delivers the whole package- Food, Ambience, Service. I loved it and will definitely be back again.. and again.. and...yes again.

I love Top's!!! Huge portions, fast service, and tasty food. My fiancé got sick once after eating here, but I don't even want to blame them because we enjoy the food so much and continue to go back (we just avoid the seafood jambalaya)

Best soul food option in the New Haven area. I have always been please with the quality of service and food during all of my visits. Nothing lilke Soul Food on a Sunday to take that hangover down a notch or two. The portion are good and I always opt for the Church Plate (1 entree and two sides). The BBQ ribs are on point! Fall off the bone on point! I would definitely recommend dining here.

This place is really nice and a great addition to the neighborhood. The food is great, and they are friendly enough to kids, without being overtaken by them. As a parent, that is greatly appreciated, but as someone who likes to also have a date-night with my husband, its nice that it isn't overtaken. The staff are friendly and courteous, and the drinks are delicious. Also appreciated: the addition of a couple of more kid-friendly dishes, in case we do want to do a family dinner some night. Its odd that people were expecting a dive bar. Especially one right across the street from a church. This place is not a dive bar, but it is a perfectly lovely place to come and have a nice cocktail or a beer from their small, but fine selection of draft beers. My husband is a bit of a beer snob and he always finds something that fits his tastes (super hoppy, in his case).

. Disappointed bc the place is really cute.. Was doing take out. The staff was friendly but there was almost 0 lettuce.. or anything else.. Just some sprouts and a couple of cut carrots and radishes . The menu says everything green in it! Expected something more . Love the crystals and atmosphere but  idk if I'd go back. I judge a place by it's salad abilities ..

Why/When I tried it I went to Burlington with my girlfriend and her sister, who played tour guide over the New Year's weekend.  We read other positive reviews on Yelp! so we decided to check it out for our last meal of 2011. Location/accessibility Burlington isn't that big of a city, so many places are within walking distance of one another.  Parking wasn't an issue, even when we drove downtown at 11pm on New Year's Eve. Atmosphere A little loud, but hey it was NYE.  The wall decorations and menu selections let you know that freshness is the foundation of what this restaurant is all about.     Menu/pricing A wide beer selection, but the average beer price was $6-8.  The entrees are a little pricey, about $15 a plate.   Food The place prides itself on its fresh food, which I guess it gets directly from farmers in the surrounding areas.  The waitress brought out 4 sauces with cauliflower in place of the standard bread and butter at most restaurants--different, but fits with the "fresh" atmosphere of the place.  I recommend the Baltic Porter (beer) and Jericho burger--delicious. Service It took a while to get a seat, but on NYE what else can you expect?  We walked to another bar down the street for a drink while we waited. Grading I would absolutely go back to the Farmhouse Tap and Grill and I would recommend you try it too!

This place consistently offers great pizza, and also offers free delivery, which is an added bonus.  I love the fresh ricotta topping.  Their sandwiches are pretty good as well.  Management seems to care about giving the customer a good experience - when I had a pizza delivered with the wrong toppings on it, I called the manager and a piping hot replacement pie was at my door in 20 minutes flat, as promised.

My fiancee and I have been here three times for dinner.  Each time, they tell us they can't serve burgers.  The first time, it was a lack of buns.  We wrote it off as an anomaly.  The last two times, they gave us no explanation outside of "it's not a time issue."  How is a restaurant out of burgers (veggie and meat) three times at a normal hour?!?! When we have decided to stay for dinner, it has been okay.  In other words, there's no reason to waste your money here when there are so many other great places in the immediate area.
Grabbed lunch with a great client. Heard it was good but wow! Smoke shack burger rocked.

Order type: Dine in Order: Grilled cheese, corn bread, chicken biscuit. The service was fast and friendly and the food is very well priced. Unfortunately the food strikes me as essentially McDonalds with local appeal. The grilled cheese was just Kraft singles on white bread, the corn bread was good but was far from home made while the chicken biscuit was tasty but nothing to write home about. It's a piece of fried chicken, in a biscuit, with a pad of butter.  For it's location in the world it is a culinary oasis. There is nothing of Pies 'N' Thighs taste or quality for a while in any direction. Putting aside is local monopoly though it becomes little more than a fatty, salty, fast-food joint purveying simple American standards to upbeat electro-pop.

YUMS! I've been wanting to eat here for a while and finally got to check this place off my list after a concert at the highline. My gf and I exhausted and famished from a night of insane dancing decided to make a swift stop here before heading on the 2/3 back to brooklyn heights. The staff here were extremely friendly and nice. The food is very tasty! We got the Mac and cheese, spicy kale, and lomo saltado! Although I was a little disappointed in the the amount of food for the price, I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of the food! I can't wait to come back here and eat it again!

I love this place! How can you not crave their spicy chicken empanadas! It's the perfect appetizer to their grilled skirt steak (entrana a la plancha). I would definitely go here more often for dinner if their restaurant was bigger and there wasn't such a long wait on the weekends. But that doesn't stop me from ordering large amounts of empanadas for pickup for my roommates and me. Yummm. A must try if you just moved to Hells Kitchen. Oh also, you should dry their dessert empanada - trust me, I was slightly skeptical in the beginning too, but it's amazing. It reminds me of Rickshaw's dessert dumpling.

Great place for lunch -- though usually the line is out the door and it is a little bit of a wait. They always play late 90s rap and R&B, so really the main reason I come here is to get my 4 minute fix. Oh, by the way, the burritos are tasty too.

Came in here for happy hour today - only $3 for Narangasett on draft, and it's like $2 for a PBR or Miller High Life I think.  Great crowd, great bartenders, great for getting some writing or reading done.  Love this place.

I never "yelped"  before, if that is the correct term to use. But I was completely blown away with the decor and the atmosphere. The restaurant is completely beautiful ! With it's amazing high ceilings. The food was okay, a little mediocre for such a beautiful restaurant, I honestly was expecting better quality in food... But our server Jamie was completely amazing, very tentative and very quick to accommodate us. The music in the restaurant was extremely loud.... And there was so many people when we walked in it was almost impossible to walk thru the crowd. Besides this, I'll be back to grab a beer some time.

I've been coming to this spot for about 8 years, usually to listen to jazz at The Bar Next Door, which is the music room downstairs.  Great, intimate place to hear top notch jazz.  At the time of this writing the cover is $12/person with a one drink minimum.  On Sunday through Thursday, that covers the whole evening.  I think that it may be different on Friday and Saturday - I don't know.  If I go with a friend and I am going to stay the night, I buy a bottle of wine.  Food is also offered.   If you are in a chatty mood, just stay upstairs.  No cover to pay, and the listeners and players will both thank you.

Not that I'm aware of any other Ethiopian food in the area, but Mesob is excellent.  The first thing that hits you when you walk in is the wonderful smell of spices.  The injera is huge and just sour enough.  On a cold, blustery night like tonight, I wanted spicy lamb!  I usually go for vegetarian at Ethiopian restaurants, but not this time.  I couldn't help drooling over plates I saw go by me.  It's BYOB, meaning a bottle of wine would have been perfect.  Unfortunately, I was traveling for work.  It's not recommended that you go to this Ethiopian restaurant alone.  It's too much food!  I'll definitely add this to one of my favourite spots for the Clifton area.
Best marinated chicken breast anywhere.

I seriously love this place. I went for brunch with my boyfriend Jay and my friend Jason. We had a BLAST. We went at a good time, too (right before it got crowded). I had a wrap and fries that were AMAZING. The fixed price menu is the BEST THING EVER! Very inexpensive for a lot of food AND DRINKS! Who knew?!?!?!? They also have a wonderful selection of Tea (I'm a HUGE tea drinker). The location is wonderful, as well! It's right off the Broadway stop off the NW in Astoria!

i FREAKEN LUH-HUV this place...just not the brisket. you know, i thought that num pang could do no wrong...and then i ordered the brisket.  i was SUPER EXCITED to try it!  i had a good wait because i think that it wasn't a popular order that day. once my order was complete, i scurried upstairs to try it.  sadly, the brisket that i had was TOO TOUGHI  i don't know if it is sinew or exactly what the rubbery part is/was.  all i know is that it was super unpleasant and a waste of anticipation. undeterred, i returned a couple of nights later and tried the coconut shrimp sandwich.  the shrimps were cooked to perfection...meaty, tender and flavorful.  i also redeemed myself with a cup of the lentil soup.  it was smooth, tasty, and had just the right amount of texture with the fried onion garnish. and the corn.  c'mon now!  it gets me every single time!  i love that stuff! all-in-all, num pang ROCKS my world.  i'm thinking that i was the unlucky one with the junky piece of brisket, but no worries!  everything else is as is should be.... FREAKEN AWESOME!

I highly recommended this one. We (4 people) came here together and barely finished it. We ordered sorted seafood hotpot only and it is insanely huge. Do remember to bring at least 6 people here for one hotpot. Also they gave every customer grilled beef for free. We had a little bite and it is really good but we were so full. Highly recommended this one!
Excellent service wait staff is impeccable and friendly. Breakfast is really special they have a Basic breakfast for 3.95!

I went with three stars because we only had a cheese pizza and garlic bead with cheese. (Redundant you say? Well, Shut up.) Both were totally tasty, perfectly greasy, crunchy in all the right places, gooey and cheesy and even delish. Asked for a side of ranch dressing (trust me - just try it) and it came too. Bonus. Arrived in 20 minutes. Not fancy, just yummy stick to your ribs stuff. Their menu also has the standard calzones, apps, salads, pastas, sandwiches, etc. They deliver. To the bar around the corner, and I hear to other places as well. ;)

I love the scenery and the view of the place. My friend and I sat by the windows and it was such a perfect day to sit outside but you're actually inside. We came in for happy hour and our bartender and waitress were very nice! Drinks were great and beautiful! We ordered the passionate cocktail and I ordered dragon something.. I forgot but it was delicious! It was my first time trying the place but I felt like the food was similar to any other place. I chose pad thai and well it was good but nothing new. My friend ordered a mango salad with a champagne mango sauce.. and that was really good and healthy!

SHUT. THE. FRONT. DOOR. This place blew me away. The atmosphere is beautiful (floor to ceiling windows with a cottage-esque, cozy indoor garden speakeasy feel) and the food is simply incredible. It's on my (very) short list of places to visit again and again. I had dinner here over the summer, and have since come back several times for cocktails. I *believe* their menu changes seasonally; over the summer they featured a spicy strawberry gazpacho soup that blew my mind - spicy? sweet? savory? what the WHA? Their raw oysters were also very good - they had a selection of both East and West Coast varieties, which was interesting for me (an oyster newbie) since I was able to try both and observe the discrepancies. One of their cocktails (Sweet Ginger Brown) was featured in Time Out's "Summery Cocktails" roundup earlier this year, and it's probably the best cocktail I've ever had. Don't even think about skipping it. This place is perfect for almost any occasion - taking your parents, meeting someone else's parents, a forever-alone dinner...take a date here if you want to impress the person with your nonchalant coolness. You? You go to places like this ALL THE TIME. You got this. Also, cute waiter with the Irish (?) accent - call me :)

This is a tough review to write, because I've been looking for great Mexican food in Montclair -- and the food here really is great. But the service, which started out only okay, has steadily declined to the point that we may not return. If I could rate this a 2.5 I would, because service-wise I'd put them as a 1 or 2 star. Food-wise, I'd give them a 4. So here are the issues: 1.  The last few times we went, it took forever to get our drinks -- now, when there are chips and salsa down you need your water, too! So that's a challenge.  You also don't tend to get your water refilled during the meal, you need to ask. 2.  We have gone at least a dozen times over the last few months, and each time we order fajitas we ask to replace one vegetable with more of the vegetable that already comes with it.  The server always says, "it doesn't come with that" and we say, "yes, it does, we've had it a few times and that's how it always comes." Then when he brings out the food he says, "Oh,  you were right." 3.  There is always some kind of error with the meal -- the most common is whenever we ask for limes for our drinks we always get lemons. Now, as a European, I know that the word for lemon and lime can translate to the same thing in other languages. But it's every. Single. Time. 4. This may sound minor and I don't mean to be petty, but as I shared above, we've gone at least a dozen times -- and each time we go, it's like it's the first time we've been there. No recognition that we're returning customers. Again, I don't go to restaurants for an ego boost, but when you live in a town, you get to know the vendors. I can go into a bunch of places I've been to fewer times than Casa Piquin and at least have that kind of recognition and interaction. I've made that overture at Casa Piquin ("Yes, it's us again!") and they never seem to know what I'm talking about. Anyway, if you're looking for good Mexican food and don't mind mediocre service and a restaurant that does, as another reviewer wrote, smell overwhelmingly like the bathroom cleaner they use, then this place is really good. But I am sad to say that I don't know whether I'll be going back.

The food is nothing too special, but a really fun place to go hang out. They have cornhole on the lower deck, which is a fun way to waste a few hours with friends while drinking, and they have fire pits that you can eat/drink around outside (awesome!!) but just make sure to call and reserve them if you're set on sitting around the fire pit (the night we went all but one was already reserved, so we lucked out).
Great good, good atmosphere! Love the outside patio for a nice spring afternoon!

Buvette never ceases to satisfy my taste buds. I've been here enough to know their brunch is busy but worthwhile and their dinners remind me of long, lazy meals in Paris. The portions at Buvette, at first, deceived me because I thought they were too small (as they were plated on small plates), but that is not the case. Small is really the concept at Buvette. It is a tight space with a busy ambience, but if you are patient and willing to wait...you are in for a great meal. I also recommend most of their brunch specials! Some things from the menu I enjoyed: - Brandade De Morue (house salt cod with olive oil, milk & garlic) - Crq'Madame (classic ham, gruyere & sunny-side egg) - Belgian Waffle (topped with berries) - Cassoulet (pot of slow cook duck, pork & beans) - Beglian waffle (w/ egg & bacon & maple syrup)

Infini-T probably has the biggest selection loose leaf teas I've ever seen. And they're some damn good teas. You can sit down and get a pot (which at first seem a bit expensive) but you can get refills so it's a great deal if you're going to sit there for half the day doing home work and sipping on tea. They have a really cool eastern vibe and if you feel like getting you're "indian style" sitting (bringing me back to elementary school here) on, they have some tiny little chairs for you. This was also the first place I've had Turkish coffee, which I've grown to love. They even serve it with a little Turkish Delight. They have a good menu of little snacks and lunch foods. I've only tried their hummus but I was very happy with it. Aside from just the experience of sitting down there, they sell all of the teas, spices, and even the Turkish coffee for you to take home. I even bought the Turkish coffee pot from them to make it at home.

I'm going to admit this first of all, in case you decide you'd rather discount my review - this place is just a bit too Upper West Side for me.  I like my little brunch places, serving a specialized and thought-through menu of seasonal food, with a brunch cocktail mixed just for me.  Calle Ocho is definitely not that. The place is vast - much bigger than you'd think when you first walk in.  Past the bar it opens out into a massive light-and-airy room with seating for hundreds. The menu is also huge, though interesting in places and with some unusual things.  The portions were big and the food pretty decent.  They have the quite-entertaining gimmick of having a taco-cart continually making the round of the restaurant serving up mini tacos to accompany your meal - though I couldn't help thinking that I'd have been better off (and less out of pocket) going to an actual food truck. So, onto the reason that most people seem to go to Calle Ocho: the unlimited Sangria.  Yes it was sangria.  Yes it was unlimited.  Yes there were lots of different recipes.  But none of them were great, they were all insanely sweet, and (because it's aimed at an 'unlimited' audience) they weren't that strong.  Plus they're served up on a table over on one side of the restaurant, which means getting up and queuing every time you need a refill - it doesn't exactly make for a relaxed brunch.  Is being served from passed jugs of Sangria really too much to ask? There are massive signs all over the Sangria bar forbidding people taking more than one glass at a time, which makes it feel a little bit like you're sneaking drinks out of your parents' drinks cabinet (or is that just me?).  But, looking around the restaurant, you can kind of see why: big groups of people who are on the beginning of a night out on a mission to get pissed (in the English sense).  But, even if this is what you're looking for, unless you're bringing a coach load of friends from out of town, surely there are more interesting places to do it?

So I haven't been here in a while, last time was not great, but decided to give the brunch a chance. Sorry I did. $20 for buffet. Does not include drinks. So for two of us it was $60 with the tip. FOR breakfast? There is no other options. Just buffet. We did get there early which thank goodness, because the lady behind me was using her hands to paw thru the bagels. I had to explain what the tongs were for. She looked 40. They did have lots of options and an omelet bar.

Cozy place in the village (i.e. very dark with tables and chairs piled practically on top of each other.) But it works. My co-worker and I shared a fun date night together here. We were seated in the front room, right next to the guy rolling cigars in the corner (what's his deal? I thought it was kind of weird. Is he the owner? A friend? Renting the table??)  There was live music, which was fun, but also kind of loud. Found ourselves shouting our conversation at each other at times. We shared an order of the tamal cubano (pork tamale) and yuqita frita (deep fried yucca). DEFINITELY get the yuquita frita - it was so crispy and hearty and salty and wonderful! I ordered the seafood special of the night which was large, but not particularly amazing. My coworker's fish was much better (also a special of the night). She also raved about the sangria! We were so full at the end that we skipped dessert! Fun place, but a little bit pricey. Use a Scoutmob and it's a great deal.
Great concept and the staff is very enthusiastic. Maybe because they have new jobs? I can see how LES newbies would be into it, but true foodies know the truth.

One of my girlfriend took me here for my birthday after that i always came back i love their uni. a glass of plum wine. came here order a big sushi boat for like 5 people the sushi was fresh. Everything about Blue Ribbon really made my night awesome! The atmosphere here is perfect its not so crowded and they dont take reservation its first come first serve which is good about that the wait is usually not long at all. oysters are really good uni the best cocktail are perfect not too strong or light hamachi yellow is my favorite bone marrow their delirious here. Perfect if you have a date great service.

Coffee "chip" ice cream with great slabs of dark chocolate are made in the basement in stainless steel drums that go through a hard freeze, softening and final freeze process that yields the creamiest, most flavorful ice cream!
yes. especially if you're visiting and just out for a walk. class, character, and a good product. I will return.

The Halal guys are constantly at it. They really know how to work the corner of 53rd and 6th. I love the combination platter here which is chicken and lamb over rice. Gotta add the white sauce, barbecue sauce or the hot sauce for added taste. Warning that the hot sauce on the top shelf is super hot. I've come here a number of times after a night out and all I can say is the food tasted a million times better in a inebriated state. But then again doesn't everything. But really, this food did taste good and I felt great eating the platter that I was ready to go out on the town again. For most people, when they eat this stuff they will probably need to sleep. Who knows how many calories are in this, but who cares. The line looks long, but it moves along because these guys churn through the orders fast.

I haven't had much because I love the Seitan Wings SO much that I go back for them all the time here! And the fried piccolos... oh my. love sitting outside at the picnic benches, and I can bring my dog.
Just get the cemitas! The pictures you take on your phone of these ginormous sandwiches may disturb your friends and relatives, but nothing tastes better.

I use to live in Jersey City right around the corner from the original Taqeria Downtown. When I moved to the city I started having cravings for their tacos and was considering making a special trip to Jersey City to have them again (Yes, they are that good). But I found out that they recently opened a new location on the lower east side so I set out to find it. Like the Jersey City location, this spot is located in a small space with limited seating so you may have to wait a few minutes to get a table. Once you are seated, someone promptly takes your order and brings a basket of chips and salsa. The chips and salsaa was a nice addition as the Taqeria in JC did not serve chips and salsa. I ordered my favorite tacos, one steak taco and one pork taco, with a side of creama. The tacos where just as I remembered them. The steak taco comes with a spicy salsa on top while the pork comes with a mild green salsa. Both are topped with cilantro and onion and garnished with a raddish and lime wedge. Squeze the lime on the tacos and add a little creama and you have two of the best tasting, authentic tacos you can find. YUM! Highly recommended.

Went there last night to support my friend in her Quizzo host audition. Awesome beer selection. 2 cask ales. Fullers London Pride is such a great beer and they have it on draft. The owner seems really cool. And the food, which i didn't have, looked awesome. I really want to head back there for some fish and chips. The only drawback, all the douchey Penn Students. But  it's at 44th and Spruce, so that's to be expected.

Loved it, but this isn't your southern bbq joint that's for sure.  You will be set back some dough eating here..  You order from the counter and you do so by the pound.....or half, quarter, etc.  The staff does a good job ensuring you get the right amount of food for your group which is nice (but could be costly.)  We had some of the brisket and pulled pork then split some of the potato salad, burnt-end baked beans, and corn on the cob.  Everything was great, the brisket was nice and flavorful, although a tad more dry that I would have liked.  I loved the baked beans, thick & rich.  The potato salad was light and a good accompaniment to the meat.   My only real issue came with the sauces as I wasn't impressed by any of them.  I'll definitely return as the space has a great vibe, its a good hang alternative from Frankford Hall next door, and you can snack on some good food (even if you don't commit to a full-on meal.)

The food is delicious here and the ambiance is very romantic. After multiple trips there is not one thing on the menu that wasn't mouth watering. Place is small, gets crowded, and the front of house can be a bit abrasive...but they are accommodating. Don't hold it against it.

Recommended by a trusted friend, I was looking forward to Frank Pepe's and it did not disappoint. After visiting Yale, it was the perfect treat... the only thing more perfect would be getting INTO Yale, which has about a .00001% chance of happening; however, you will get a good pizza here 99.99999% of the time, according to my calculations. The service was not the best, but not really anything to complain about. I loved how one could see straight into the kitchen and see them making the pizza from start to finish. The pizza was not too thin-crusted, but not thick by any means either. The sauce was delicious and the toppings fresh. The broccoli was a great topping. A small was the perfect size for a nice snack for 2 before dinner. I'll only return on one condition: I get into Yale. ...for my sake people, tell Yale to accept me so I can taste the goodness that is Frank Pepe's pizza again!

I became a regular of this shop under its previous owners (when it was called Greenwells). I admit that, last November, when I heard that the shop was getting new owners and a new name that I was apprehensive -- what else was going to change? Thankfully, the new owners (Tom and Teri, who are incredibly friendly and quick with a joke) kept everything that was already perfect with this coffee shop (now called Cedarhurst Cafe), and improved everything else that needed work. My favourite thing about Cedarhurst is the ambience. This shop is like a little oasis  from the stressful bustle of downtown New Haven. From the central tree pillar to the yoga balls to the wood tables, the cafe has a very natural, very hipster-chic feeling about it. The rotating featured artwork helps to keep the interior fresh, too. Although I don't really have time to do it as much as I used to anymore, I still love to sit on the yoga balls for a morning coffee and laptop session whenever I can. There's always plenty of seating (which is shocking, considering how wonderful this place is), with lots of outlets and free wi-fi. The coffee here is some of the best I've had in New Haven, and now I try to make a detour and swing by the shop at least once or twice a week to pick up some of their light roast coffee to go in the mornings, even though the cafe is no longer on my morning route to work. The smoothies are also really good and made fresh on-the-spot; I like the Tropic Thunder best. As for the things that Tom and Teri improved: my chief complaint when the shop was called Greenwell's was their lacking food menu. Tom and Teri not only addressed this problem, but their solution actually has become another highlight for the cafe: this shop has some of the best muffins I've ever had! The muffins are baked fresh on the premises most mornings, and they are AMAZING (particularly when you can smell them baking from the sidewalk). I can recommend the cranberry, the carrot, the blueberry and the chocolate chip muffins. The chocolate chip cookies are also really great, particularly when they come straight out of the oven!  The egg, cheese and prosciutto sandwich is another highlight, although you should prepare yourself for a bit of a wait (~10 minutes or so) if you order it, since I think they make it from scratch in the kitchen. In conclusion, Cedarhurst is still my favourite coffee shop in New Haven. Definitely worth checking out.

The food was memorable and the service sublime.   We started with the outstanding octopus appetizer - Spanish rock Octopus - which was extremely tender and coupled with radicchio, hazelnuts and garlic.  Never having tasted octopus that wasn't chewy, I inquired about the preparation and was treated to an explanation in the kitchen by the personable Chef Ian.   For our main courses, we had the pork rib with polenta and the Scottish salmon with beets and horseradish, equally outstanding and creatively prepared.   This restaurant was truly a find - quiet enough for conversation, great food, friendly, attentive service and low-key ambience.   We'll be back on our next visit to Philadelphia!

This was the coziest (but still pretty classy) restaurant!  The lighting is perfect for intimate conversations (with good friends or lovahhs), and the decor is simple but charming.  Our waitress never stopped smiling, and the bathroom WAS great (Sara C., I know what you mean, it's like icing on the restaurant-cake).  The food was really tasty, and the tapas menu only enhances the cozy feel of the place... Sharing is caring, folks. *One thing:  If you're going to get a real "Greek" experience, this is not necessarily the place to go.  It's a mix of cuisines, and when I went with one of my girlfriends (who's VERY Greek), she was disappointed that they didn't offer a bigger variety of Greek fare.  But that's just her.  I liked the place.

Fantastic addition to the neighborhood.  Great beer and wine selection and the polenta is the best I've ever tasted.  The Broccoli rabe and the Cuban were also amazing.  Will be back to knock out the rest of the menu.

Went to Butcher Bar this weekend for dinner with a friend. We were quickly sat at a table, but the host soon realized that the table had been set aside for a party of four who were waiting. He came back and told us and was very apologetic, so we got up and went out front to wait. No big deal. They apparently have a backyard that isn't open for customers, but the host told us we could wait there if we'd prefer. We were fine out front, so we stayed there. After about five or ten minutes we got a new table. We split corn cakes and honey butter, which were delicious. I also tried the corn cakes with the original bbq sauce they had at the table, which was unusual, but it worked. I also got mac and cheese, which was even better. Perfectly cheesy and creamy. Then, I had the 50/50, a sandwich of half brisket, half pulled pork. It was fantastic. Again, I added the original sauce, which went very well with both meats. All the food was great and I had completely forgotten about the mixup earlier, but they hadn't. One of the butchers, who appeared to be in charge, came over and asked us how our food was and apologized for the inconvenience. He then insisted on giving us something for free to make up for it. We couldn't decide what to get, so he suggested ribs. A few minutes later, another butcher showed up with two ribs. He actually was bringing four, but dropped two. A couple minutes after, the first butcher was back with a plate of pulled pork to make up for the lost ribs. Both were outstanding. I then had a piece of apple pie, which was good, but forgettable. I'll probably skip it next time. Overall, great food, great service. There was an unfortunate mixup at the beginning, but everyone was friendly and they went out of their way to make up for it. I hope to be back very soon.
Have always been the best and remain the best.
authentic, delicious italain cuisine. Great atmosphere and service. Best best best!
The food was ok but it was too cramped/crowded for me.

Not as good as the Brooklyn location. The brisket was good, the ribs were ok, and the pulled pork was dry. The beans were good, but not spicy like the Brooklyn version. Service was very friendly and I liked that they have individual booths/tables rather than the long communal tables.
Food is good. Portions suck for the price. Given Philly's awesome food scene, this would not be high on my list to return.

I decided to stop by Rumbamba around 6:15 PM with the thought that since the Ay Arepa food cart on York Street was closing soon I would just stop by the restaurant and get the ingredients fresh. Big mistake! There was only one difference between my food cart fish arepa and the restaurant fish arepa - PRICE! While I can grab a fish arepa from the food cart for 6$, I was charged 13$ for a takeout fish arepa. The portion size was the same (good) and the flavors were the same (delicious!), however I now know that I should always choose the food cart above physical location. If you don't mind shelling out the extra money, the food is delicious. I can't speak to the dining conditions since my meal was takeout.

Outpost of small New York chain still the one to beat for the genre.  Their chefs work with speed and skill and extract the best from coconut milk, lemongrass, mango, galangel and other great Asian ingredients.  Finely balanced and addictive curries hard to match anywhere.  Superior roti canai and dipping sauce best prelude to large selection of Pacific Rim treats on large menu.  Little anglicizing of traditional recipes with food uniformly good.  Equal part Asian and Caucasian patrons demonstrates a seamless bridge between authentic and main stream trans cultural culinary sensibilities.  Aqua and Banana Leaf worthy clones but no match for this one for energy and authenticity.
An absolutely amazing experience! Food was heavenly and service was top notch. would def recommend to anyone looking for fine ding and look forward to coming back soon!

Translated as the Creole Corner, this Cuban joint is a hidden gem that many would not bother to look twice at. From the outside, this place is as formidable as the neighboring storefronts. It gets a bit cozier inside, with ~20 tables all tightly squeezed together. I ordered the Ropa Vieja ($13.95), Shredded Beef in Tomato Sauce, with choice of two sides. The shredded beef in tomato sauce was outstanding, tender shredded beef in a sweet and savory tomato sauce. Don't let the portions fool you, as they can be quite filling, on top of the two sides. My first side was the maduros, which consisted of 5 fat slices of fried sweet plantains, soft on the inside and caramelized with a slight crispness on the outside. My second side was the yuca con mojo (cassava with garlic). The soft yuca is sort of in-between a soft potato and taro, with what I would consider requires an acquired taste, slightly on the bland side except for the hint of garlic flavor. Other dishes I was able to try was the: - Rabo Encendido (sauteed ox tail in tomato sauce) which is Wednesday's special. Boy oh boy, three very sizable pieces of delicious fatty and tender ox tail that fell off the bone with a flick of the fork. - 1/2 Chicken Rincon Criollo, which I had high hopes but was met with pure disappointment. The chicken was slightly dry, and the crispy skin had little flavor. I would avoid ordering this dish. - Pork Chops w/ minced garlic and onions - The pork was extra crispy, almost reminding me of lechon. It was very tasty though ever so slightly on the salty side. Pork eaters, you won't be disappointed. - Side: French fries which were dry and tasteless. I ask myself how they could mess up such a simple side. Season with a little salt, dry the potato slices a little bit more before throwing in the deep fryer, and you'll have one tasty and crispy fry. - If you're looking for something indigenous to drink, try the Jupiña, pineapple soda. The only downside to this place is that service can be quite poor, erring to almost rude. When we were trying to understand the items on the menu and asked the waiter a few questions, he seemed to be a bit agitated and impatient. Also, he never came by once to check up on us or refill our glasses. Twice we had to get his attention, once for drinks and a second time for the bill. On the bright side, we took our time eating and hanging out here, and they never seemed to have a problem with that, which is most likely because we came on a Wednesday night and only 2-3 tables were occupied.
The pizza here is terrific. It rivals the best thin crust new haven pizza, and is a neighborhood favorite. Always packed on the weekends so go early. Food is good too!
Wonderful food and service!! Great filet mignon and duck confit!! The escargots were also amazing! Best wine bar! Wonderful staff as well :)

I'm love this tucked away (and out of the way,but so worth it!)  spot midway between Williamsburg and Greenpoint (I guess technically Greenpoint). It's spacious, with lots of bar space and tables (where you can even played fun games, such as Jenga).  The bartenders are all cool and made good recommendations on the massive craft beers selection.  My bf got a pretty good IPA (don't remember which one- but it was sweet ish) and I ordered a hot tody- a hot drink which had a bit too much bourbon for my taste (and cinnamon). I'm not much of a drinker but I do love my German-esque bar food, so I was really pleased with the special house made pretzels (which were so soft, buttery, and salty). They give you a choice to pick a special sauce-- from the special mustards to peanut sauce.. we got the Greek yogurt sauce which was like a yummy tzatizki.   It seems as though there are other very yummy bites here, which I will have to try next time: the Belgian fries, various Brats (they do make a vegan and chicken version, as I don't eat pork/beef.. and bf tells me you can get it ON the pretzel bun, yummy!), and randomly.. the Black Kale salad. Def a good place for drinks before you go out out or to dinner as they don't have any real entrees but I think this place was a great vibe and would recommend it to all. Plus I love the music choice- it wasn't like stereotypical angsty hipster music, but I actually heard some old school favorites such as "Are you That Somebody" by Aaliyah and "I like it Like that" by Hot Chelle Rae.. street cred, me likes!  Good German esque decor (with a cozy fireplace!), and though it seems like a beer place, they have a lot more going on.

This is a great little spot for lunch and take-out.  This is not the type of place that you bring a date or a big group. They serve breakfast all day.  They serve hot and cold sandwiches, wraps, etc... Plenty of beverage choices and sides. The best part? They have kiosks to order like Wawa!

Come here to be seen, come here for the cute waiters, or come here for the drinks and lounge downstairs, but do not come here for the food. The first time I ate here, I was so disappointed that I knew it must have been a fluke - so I decided to try it again a second time.  Surprisingly, they disappointed again.  While the chilled cucumber soup looked good on paper, when it sat in front of me, it was an inedible bowl of mint green spew.  The steak was not very good either. Downstairs lounge is small and quaint.  Bathrooms were adequate. The plus might be that it has outside seating and is open 24 hours? This was from experiences that happened nearly two years ago, hopefully they have changed.  Or perhaps I should go try their mac & cheese that so many have raved about.  But I just can't seem to do it.  Something about it just rubs me the wrong way.

My beau and I ordered the tasting menu and it was awesome. But, it was a ton of food and it wasn't necessary to have what I think ended up being 10 tapas - we were both stuffed but his wallet was emaciated by the end of it all.  I loved the albondigas (meatballs) while his favorite were the duck canapes.  Also, the green beans were fantastic.  We each had 1 cocktail and 2 glasses of wine. We should have ordered a bottle, or better yet brought our own as they have a corkage fee. His head almost exploded when the bill came. Next time: order 3 tapas each, make cocktails at home, order one glass of wine each. Save money. Have fewer heads explode.

Came there with four friends to celebrate birthday. The drinks were great (if a tad overpriced) and the service was a bit slow. The food was okay for midtown but nothing to write home about. We had a couple appetizers and individual entrees and it came to about $90 a person so it is an investment. It was kinda cool vibe but nothing terribly memorable.

This review is NOT for the food, which is quite good.  I dropped in with five people on a snowy night to have some drinks.  Much like some other reviews, the service here is not only very slow, but indifferent at best while bordering on rude.  The place was not even half full, but it took quite a while to get a few beers and a few drinks.  It was basically the staff hanging out talking to each other not paying attention to the customers.  When one person in our group asked one of the three people behind the bar for another drink, she scoffed and said I'm not the bartender (despite the fact she was hanging out behind the bar doing nothing).  When one person asked about the music (which everyone was enjoying) he was shot down with a terse answer and then the music was changed to the morose channel.  Note to owner - find a staff that cares more about the customers than hanging out and giggling to each other.  We would have stayed and spent much more money
Festive atmosphere, great service. made me wish I was still in college.
