Tips: - Let them know you're sharing and they divide the plate into two and didn't charge me anything additional. - There's outdoor seating available. - Street parking on South St. is for up to 2 hours. This place is FANTASTIC. Highly recommend and would be delighted to come back.

This is definitely among the best pizza places I've ever been at. Roberta's is a friendly atmosphere suitable for a casual dinner with friends. They've got a decent beer selection, but what you come for here are the pizzas. I've tried four of the pizzas here and loved them all. Especially their special pizza, which is folded (not like a Calzone though). And the Beast Master is excellent too. Definitely worth a visit!

First time at B&B and it was enjoyable. The food was the highlight and it is worth a visit. The interior is a cool space. It's dark and was very crowded and loud so be warned. Not ideal for an intimate catch-up or date, more of a fun place to start an evening. Drinks were good. The menu is almost bizarrely diverse - seafood, salads, tacos, fried chicken, and of course the burgers! However, after visiting with several people and all of us ordering completely different things, all of the various items were delicious (burger, fish tacos, couple salads, bison sliders). So I guess you can't go wrong.

Dear Rattle 'N' Hum, I owe you an apology.  You did nothing but offer me delicious beer and I caused chaos in return. This is what happened. Slightly drunk, slightly frazzled I ran outta the bar to go meet someone uptown and realized en route my credit card was not where it was supposed to be.  So I called you, RNH.  You were so nice on the phone (even though you clearly had a paying crowd to deal with) and spent a good ten minutes looking around before you took my number and told me you would call if you found the card.  You even called the next morning to sadly inform me it was never found.   That's when I opened my wallet and looked more closely.  The credit card wasn't missing at all, it was just in the wrong section.  DOH! I'm really sorry.  And you have really good beer and a great happy hour crowd. I promise when I come back I'll be better behaved. B

We went here during restaurant week and of course it was packed, so we sat in the last 2 seats at the back of the counter.  We got to see all the cooks in action, really close up.  Amazing!  We were fascinated by how perfect they were, never missing a step, never really even talking to each other.   The food was generally fresh and inventive.  The Calabrian salad was nicely sauteed, not completeley limp (which I would hate) and fairly spicy.  An inventive dish.  The Puglian burrata was offset very well by the arugula.  Sometimes a plate 'o cheese needs something to lighten it up, and the arugula did it.  The pan-seared gnocchi was amazing, the gnocchi were light and fluffy, not gooey and heavy.  The meatballs were stuffed with cheese, but not heavy-tasting, nicely seasoned. The only item that seemed off was the grilled sardines.  They didn't smell right and didn't taste very fesh.  But everything else was seasoned and prepared perfectly.  Barbuzzo is tiny and loud, but that makes it fun.

The group of 6 of us had dinner here before the concert at nearby tla. The food was very good - we had a variety of appetizers and the stand outs were the pan fried veal liver, the white bean salad and cicik with warm bits bread.  For the main course most of us had lamb kebabs.  It came on a platter with rice pilaf and vegetables.  The meat was very tender and seasoned well.  We also had ground lamb kofta kebab which was very good as well.  Desserts consisted of baklava and Turkish coffe.  I love Turkish coffe and it was brewed perfectly.  Overall a great dining experience just off south street.

Perhaps it was because of a Wednesday night, too cold to be out, or perhaps it's just because Hartford isn't a dining out kind of town... This dining room upstairs was empty but the bar downstairs was a different story. Food was excellent, flavorful and substantial. I had the Beef Shammi Kabab with the spinach rice and eggplant as my veggie. The beef kebab was tastefully seasoned right but a bid dry as it was made with extra lean ground beef. I asked for some yogurt and it was worked well. The eggplant was real good and presentation was lovely with the spice and yogurt mixed on top. My husband had the Kabeli Palow with lamb and potato as his veggie. The dish was well made but would pick another vegetable dish as the potato was boring. We skipped dessert as we were very satisfied. Nice ambiance, dimly lit dining area and private. Good service.  Worth trying if you're in W. Hartford!
The Shroomtown pizza here is nothing short of perfection

I am not usually compelled to write reviews but based on my experience tonight, the owner of this bar is a ROYAL douche bag and I highly discourage patronizing this business. While our bartender was pleasant and poured decent drinks, my friends and I will never step foot in this place again due to the jerk of an owner and his belligerent demeanor toward everyone at the end of the night. He swore at his staff and customers (us) and told us to get the f*** out. Seriously?! This is no way to conduct oneself or to treat customers, ever. As someone who loves to support local bars, and loves a good cocktail, this experience was a complete disappointment and I will not be returning. Do not patronize Ward III. It sucks. All around, a gross experience.

- would be a great place for a date - recommend: seared scallop special with mushroom risotto, the scallops (though there were only 2) were large and the perfect texture, the flesh was smooth, plump and sweet, probably the best scallops I've ever had - the crab cakes had a sweet coconut taste to them which I wasn't really a fan of but honestly I'm not a big crab cake person to start with, just had a bite of my nanas - the wine is a touch pricy at around $12-14 a glass - tends to be a short wait, but worth it and you can always have a drink at the bar until your table is ready - personable staff - quick service - very reasonably priced for seafood in any neighborhood and for quality of what you're getting - complimentary dessert (was rum cake, the evening I went but I'm pretty sure it changes by the day) - will have to come back to try their lobster roll and softshell crab options - everything bought fresh daily so the menu changes daily

My wife and I went to eat here based on yelp reviews, and we are so glad we did. We didn't have a bad bite to eat. We had the black bass, hamachi, eggs & caviar, hens of the forest (mushrooms), and swordfish. I won't describe the dishes, as other reviewers have done that very well (Katya D.) Everything was amazing, food-wise, as well as the service. We sat at the bar, and Andy (head chef) was great at explaining what we were eating and how he came up with the dish. He was really friendly, humble, and made the experience that much better. When he found out we were there to celebrate an anniversary, he even whipped up a dessert for us, on the house. It is great when you are able to find these hidden gems, where you go in not knowing what to expect, but then getting blown away when you do. One of the more memorable meals I have had, and I have been to several of the great restaurants in the city, so that is saying something. Most importantly, my wife also had a great time. We are definitely coming back to sample some more of the menu. You will not be disappointed.

Came here as a large group and had their 5 course prix fixe for parties of 11 or more which costs $60 per person. The 1st course: striped bass - (kumquat, cilantro, green peppercorn) was my favorite for the night.  I'm a huge raw fish fan and loved the flavor this dish had. 2nd course: country ham with redeye gravy.  The gravy has instant coffee, sriracha and a bunch of other ingredients in it that you would never think to mix together yet it tasted awesome. fuji apple kimchi - (maple labne, jowl bacon, arugula) - apple kimchi...isn't very spicy so even those who don't like spice can eat it.  very unique. 3rd course: steamed buns - (pork belly, hoisin, cucumber, scallions) - one word: delicious. seasonal pickles - nothing special.  We got a mix of pickled carrot, cauliflower, beets, regular kimchi with daikon, and pickles. 4th course: bo ssäm - (whole pork butt, oysters, kimchi, rice, lettuce) - the pork butt doesn't look like a lot but our table of hungry eaters didn't even finish!  It was very flavorful.  There was lettuce to make a wrap with the meat and sauce.  It came with 4 different types of sauces: ginger scallion, kimchi puree, korean spicy sauce (the kind that isn't really spicy at all), and a kimchi  that is less pureed.  Some people make a wrap with their oyster too.  I found it tasted better on its own...personal preference. market greens with xo sauce - good and balances all the meat in the meal. 5th course: pancake cake - edwards bacon, black pepper butter - this was weird.  the pancake was made into a cake shape. and cut into tiny cake slices.  A few of us felt this was too salty.  Pancakes aren't suppose to be salty.  A few said it tasted odd until eaten together with the bacon.  The black pepper butter is unique and tasty.  Overall this is probably just not my idea of an ideal dessert.  Unique but my least favorite out of the whole 5 courses.

This place is perfect for reunion-type gatherings or a treat-for-the-kids family night out.  The portions are ENORMOUS!  We ordered 4 entrees and 2 appetizers for the eight of us, and there was still way too much food left.  I was particularly fond of the mussels diablo (piles and piles of mussels) and linguine in clam sauce (SO much clam meat! YUM!).  My friends enjoyed the good ol' meatball spaghetti and veal parm.  The Tony's house wine was also a good deal for a large party.  The service was GREAT and the atmosphere in the restaurant was a blast (fun and cozy, but not rowdy).  Will be back again when my friends are in town!

The best falafel I ever tasted!! Fresh and fast chicken platter omg party in my mouth.. Lol I drive once a week from Long Island here.. Well worth it...and the prices are great!!! Keep up the good job guys!!!!

PT is my little Italian cellar around the corner. Come hungry - cos this is good old heavy Italian fare. The appetizers are amazing - I wish I could just eat appetizers, in general, but then I would not get to try stuff like the Pork Ossobuco which - come to think of it - might have been a special but ought to become a regular as it's fantastic! The thing about this place that brings it home is the ambiance - its so perfectly lit, all woody, filled with candles - Don't go here with somebody you don't really like cos you might end up proposing or something... Staff is always super helpful and sweet!

Perhaps I should stop religiously reading Yelp reviews until after I have a tried a place. I feel like this place was way too hyped up. Not saying this wasn't a great meal, it just wasn't as great as I expected it to be. The way people were describing it I was excepting colorful fireworks of flavor, texture and an absolute orgasmic experience. Well, think of the meal as the testers for the big show. A few sparks but nothing that lit the whole sky up. We ordered a fish dish and the hanger steak. The fish dish was so blasse I can't even remember it and the hanger steak, although made well- was absolutely forgettable. I felt like I was more intrigued with the side dishes than the actual entree itself. The do have a great wine selection and the duck meatballs certainly live up to....something. Not a terrible place but not one I'd itching to frequent again any time soon.
They have the best  French Toast in Hartford. I would request them to include few more vegetarian options.

My parents just love this restaurant and they are old fashioned so when it comes time for a anniversary, birthday, special occasion for them, we typically end up here.  I certainly wouldn't  call it spectacular, but with a menu as large as theirs, one would be hard pressed to not find something on the menu that they liked.  The creamy garlic dressing is awesome at best.  I always look forward to the salad at a minimum for that very reason.  The bread they serve is always fresh and coated with honey, so that is also very good.   The lobster bisque varies in quality each time we get it, sometimes with limited chunks of "lobster" or imitation crab, other times extremely thick.  This clearly indicates that it is homemade, I just wish they would put more real lobster chunks in the soup that they call lobster bisque. The ambiance is nice for a group setting or a casual dinner with friends.  There is always plenty of room and the noise level always seems to remain moderate.  I am sure we will continue to go here since my parents are so attached.

Portlandia much? First of all, as someone mentioned in another review, their entire menu needs a translation. This kind of creative naming works well if you're sitting inside and can take your time to read your own individual menu. But when you're standing on the street corner it adds tons of unnecessary waiting time while the hipsters in front of you have no choice but to ask a thousand questions before they can order. Secondly, every time I go I feel like I am awkwardly standing around wondering if its time for me to order or not. Inevitable the hipsters in front of me will move off to the side and I'll move up to place my order. But the girl behind the counter isn't looking at me. Or sometimes she will look at me and say hi. Which is very nice, but what I'm really looking for here is some clue from you that you are ready to take my order that I have been waiting to give you for 10 minutes now. Perhaps a good thing to try would be, "Hi! Can I help you?", or "hi, are you ready to order?" or, "Hi! Be with you in just a second!", instead of briefly acknowledging me and then looking back down at your hands. So I order a flat bread or whatever they call it and a coffee to go. I walk down the block with my dog a little because in my experience it takes a little while for your order to come up. When I come back a cup of coffee is sitting on the counter getting cold and a couple more hipsters are ordering. I look the counter girl in the eyes as she puts two more coffees on the counter for the new people in line. She says nothing. The hipsters step to the side again and only the one coffee cup is there. Still she says nothing. So I have to ask, "is that my coffee?". "Yep!". So you see me here and I'm looking at you for a clue and you say nothing at all until I ask? What kind of customer service is that? Then my wrap comes up and it's in a little paper sheath with the end poking out. I asked for it to go and this is clearly not the best way to take something away from the window so I ask for a bag. She puts the wrap in the tiniest paper bag ever. The bag barely, and I'm not exaggerating BARELY fits the wrap. It's hardly any better than the little brown paper sheath the wrap came in! So now without a proper bag I have to carry a sandwich, a coffee and a dog leash back home. Is it really too much to ask to get a bag that actually fits my sandwich? Not to mention the fact that she spilled half the kale off my wrap while trying to shove it into the mini bag. So by the time I got the sandwich home (which is only right around the corner) it was no longer hot. Which didn't matter anyway because the damn thing was so salty it felt like it was actually burning the corners of my mouth. And this is not the first time I have had this problem. It seems all their food is way over salted. I have tried three different wrap/flatbread things and pizza bread over the course of a year and they're all way over salty. Just their baked goods alone are wonderful. As a bakery, I highly recommend them. I also remember enjoying their grits once upon a time but at this point I'm thinking I'm going to just cut my losses and only ever buy bread or cookies from them. It seems to me that this place's popularity is all in the "coolnees" of it. Everyone loves to feel like they are in on this little secret of a place in the ghetto that serves out of a window, Oooh. Well, I'm sorry but I'm not falling for it. I have given it no less than 5 chances to impress me. Bedford Hill is only a block away and their coffee is far superior and they can make you a simple but phenomenal egg sandwich on a croissant that will make you dream about it. And you don't need to be "in" on the secret language of the menu.

I would so kung-fu chop this place in half, Kill Bill style with my samurai sword made of ramen and ginger, spilling the soy sauce blood all over the walls. I agree with Stella that this place is an absolute rip. I was craving noodles and was too poor to buy a bowl so I sold my kidney. Got a bowl of ramen, and boy, do I wish I still had my kidney, because the overload of butter clogged up my liver. Damnit, Ippudo, you've killed me with your sodium heavy, cheap portions of barely passable noodles. I will seek revenge in a different life form. Ramen is so much better in Flushing, Queens and half the price!

Have been here twice. Both times I was able to get seated decently quickly considering for a weekend dinner. Service was a bit slower my second time here though. The #1 reason to come here is for the oyster special. The price is on par for what you will get for blue point oysters at other places for happy hour specials, but you get an extra beer or wine and the special is at any time. I think the oyster special probably bumps the restaurant up a star because the other food just cannot compare. But do not be afraid to get other oysters in addition to your blue points, especially the kummomotos. In addition to the delicious oyster special, the downtown lobster special is pretty good. it comes with a lot of food and a decent (1.25 lb) lobster. It is at market price and was $20 when I went during the summer. The lobster mac and cheese is great too. However, the lobster roll is nothing compared to other places. It is smaller compared to other places and comes on a piece of white bread instead of a roll, very disappointing. Overall the entrees are quite expensive. I would just stick to the oysters and maybe some of the appetizers and soup.

Not your typical Asian restaurant. Cool room, hopping crowd, good food.  This is a great place to go for a party or out for a fun evening with a group of friends.  The room is attractive: a large bar up front and a huge, spacious dining room to the back.  It's dark, with very atmospheric lighting and a cool, niche-filled stone wall along one side, with tall-backed booths below.  The decor is natural, cool and inviting, with just a hint of a retro feel. Feng's an interesting blend of Asian cuisines.  There's Sushi and other Japanese staples, but there are dishes with a Chinese feel to the spicing.  You'll see a few dishes with a Hoisin treatment.  You'll also see some Thai curry on the menu, too. Loved the lobster latte; a really unique take on lobster bisque.  The Autumn of Connecticut and Number 93 sushi rolls were very different takes on sushi, with amazing taste combinations and textures.  Entrees are unusual and beautifully presented. Can't speak for the desserts, since each time I've been, we've gone elsewhere for that, but hope to try them soon.
Great Place for right priced food. Excellent BBQ Chicken Dinners and Cheesesteak Sandwiches Friendly Staff Very Clean I visit almost every time I am in the area
great food, great service and reasonably priced tasting menu @ 110 pp.
This place is nice but the menu is very limited. Food is very good, as is the service. Space is really small, so make sure to get a reservation.
The food here is not the worst or the best Mexican food I have ever had. The price is decent, and ok waiters. I don't think I will be returning to this place.

One star = for the dry but decent baklava. Delivery = 45 mins promised, a little over an hour Fried turnover combo appetizers = were mostly fried dough with little filling. Aushak "Dinner" = three pieces of thin dumpling with little scallions herbs and spices.  "Served with minted yogurt sauce and ground beef," = a cold watery soup, with tiny specks of beef floating in watery sauce. Did I mention cold? Not luke warm, but cold. Dinner with rice, bread and salad = dinner with imaginary rice, bread and salad. Salty yogurt drink = watery, little flavor We are still hungry.

3.5 Stars.  Soooo, I like Blue Ribbon Brasserie but I'm clearly not in love with it.  Stopped by on a rainy Monday night for dinner and from the very beginning service is attentive, though at times it feels like they're hovering over your table just a bit too long. There's a long list of entrees, though honestly none of them really seemed to stand out.  So we opted to try a handful of appetizers, including: 1) Sea urchin (special) - Something tells me that uni isn't supposed to taste like a mix of salt water and floor cleaner.  FAIL. 2) Escargot - I'm glad the server told me when I ordered that Blue Ribbon doesn't do the usual garlic and breadcrumb preparation.  Instead, their escargot are sauteed in a port wine sauce that's accompanied by slivers of french bread and bacon.  Quite tasty, although a little on the salty side. 3) Fried oysters - Deep fried oysters served on the half-shell with what appears to be creamed spinach with a touch of horseradish.  Good texture, and the tastes offset each other well.  Six to an order. 4) Beef Marrow & Oxtail Marmalade - Easily the star of the evening.  Three beef bone sections with baked marrow served with toasted bread and a oxtail marmalade.  The beef marrow was liquid fatty deliciousness.  The marmalade was good, although remarkably similar to the port reduction used in the escargot. 5) Seared foie gras (special) - Honestly, neither as rich nor as unique as I had expected.  Two smallish slabs of foie gras served over a bland polenta. 6) Mixed greens - Fresh greens, slightly tangy vinagrette.  Tasty, and neither special nor amazing. Thought we could get off cheap by avoiding the entrees, but the total damage for six apps and two glasses of malbec came out to $150 incl tax and tip.
Everything is authentic and good to the core. The sugar pig shoulder, the xiao long bao, tang yuan, etc etc. Too many to name. The only star taken away is because the joint is way too busy! I
Food was great, but service was prickly.  Our waitress was borderline rude.

While I had the most attentive, professional and one-of-a-kind service from my server "Jadelyn" - (sp), I couldn't say the same for the maitre'd who kept me waiting for a tad too long while getting my table ready. I had the following: - Barley and butternut squash risotto (good) - Pork croquette (alright, a tad salty for me - I could have done better with another dish. I guess I was thinking more schnitzel-like when I ordered this) - Mango lime cheesecake with salty macadamia nuts, mange cubes and a mango sorbet (super way to end the meal) Nevertheless, Jadelyn made the meal a fantastic experience. I was even given a gift card for my next return. How sweet. I look forward to trying another entree so look out for the upcoming 5-stars :)

Went out with friends to try some Korean BBQ. The ambiance was really nice, clean, the service was really good. The food was a autentic NY style Korean BBQ. The side dishes whre nice and fresh.  Overall a really good experience. I fyou are in the area and craving some korean bbq this is the place to go.
go go gooooo... coolest, delishes, bestess in the restess :) love the place

I lived across the street from this place for 4 years, and my best friend still does. This was a near every other day place for me to go to and grab drinks, tapas, etc. WAS. The food is quite delicious, amazing variety, and their cocktails are GREAT -- their barkeeps definitely take pride in their work! But ugh, I know this is somewhat par for the course in NYC, but I can't deal with it.... so many times I have been there and members of the rodentia family have frolicked and scampered across the floor. For a while now, all I can do is manage a drink there, but food - no way. Can't make myself do it...

It is a small restaurant and it was bustling with guests the evening we visited. So typically NY it is quite a noise level in there. It is very charming though and the staff is attentive, knowledgable and helpful. As it was the night before the NY Marathon, we wanted to stock up on carbs and therefore eat pasta. They have a lovely selection and they are all delicious. However, one Portion of Ravioli consists of 5 pieces and we ended up having to order again.

(this review is for gourmet to go, not govinda's upstairs) i used to like this place, but then i guess i got less patient (seriously some of the slowest service ever) just as they started raising their prices, decreasing their portion sizes and somehow making the same previously good ingredients taste mushy and gross. avoid avoid avoid. also $5 for a sliver of stale cake? fuck that!

Honestly, Vic's is pretty much my favorite go to place in center city. True the fish could be fresher (if only we were in Tokyo) and the place could be bigger, but you just can't beat the tuna dumplings and the $10.95 3 roll special. It's always busy at dinner, so be sure to come before 6:30pm or be ready to wait a little. You can always sit on the window sill and sip some green tea (complimentary) while you wait. I dream about the Alaska Roll. The simplicity of salmon and avocado is just something that can't be beat. Yellow Dragon is also a go to favorite. The sweet mango is a perfect compliment to the fish. Lastly, finish off any meal with the Naruto roll. The cucumber instead of the nori (seaweed) on the outside is a perfect palate cleanser. I'll give you a buck if you try it and don't agree. I would leave you a note about the tuna dumplings...but I think you've already been convinced about them right. You read the other reviews didn't you?

OMG! I have found my new BBQ go to spot in Brooklyn. I stopped in one evening to try the food and placed a take out order for their bbq kansas ribs with potato salad and collard greens. They had live music playing when I arrived and I must say it sounded pretty good. The restaurant decor reminded me of an old fashioned bar saloon that you'd see in an old western movie. The staff was friendly and wasted no time in greeting customers and offering their help. When I got home and tried the potato salad I was amazed. One of my co-workers mom makes the absolute best potato salad I have EVER tasted and she must've sold her recipe to dinosaur bbq-an exact duplication. The kansas ribs were also excellent and the sauce was full of flavors other than sweet sugar. I wrote this review immediately after tasting a few bites of the food but I hadn't yet tried the collard greens. But based on what I've tasted so far I'm sure the collard greens would be just as delicious as the rest of the food. I'll definitely be returning in the future.

Our initial destination was Caselulla, but as we approached the wine bar I peered through the glass window and saw that it was packed so I searched for another wine bar in the area and fatefully found Ardesia, which is conveniently located on the same street a few avenues away. Upon entering, I immediately bookmarked this place in my head as a great date spot. To your far left, there is a comfy couch nook, straight ahead is the bar and to your left and right are sit down tables. They have a generous wine list as well as food menu from Artisanal Cheeses to Duck Banh Mi?! Yes, Duck Banh Mi. Did I try it? Unfortunately, no but we did order a cheese plate to accompany our wine. Our waiter was extremely patient and helpful albeit it wasn't as packed as Caselulla. This wine bar has a little bit of everything - finger food, sandwiches/salads, beer (tap and bottled), wine, dessert, dessert beer/wine, coffee and tea. If you're in the mood for something light yet fulfilling, and want to catch up with a friend or impress your date, this would be the perfect spot. They also have outdoor seating for warmer days/nights. TIPS: + Happy Hour is Monday-Friday 5-7 PM $6 glasses of wine // $5 draft beers + Sundays 4-11 PM they offer oysters and champagne + GET THE CHEESE PLATE

This rating and review only applies to the Khan Kabab Express.  For people who have never been, this is a TINY place (probably about 3 or 4 rectangular tables) that has a bunch of different types of food vendors at counters along the periphery.  Basically a Desi food court.  I've eaten at a couple of the places, but the only one that is consistently good is the Khan Kabab Express.  It's a tiny stall but they have a pretty big menu.  The best part is they make the food right in front of you so you know it's fresh (as opposed to some of the other desi places that sell you food they made 2 weeks ago - see my review of Supreme Kabab & Curry).  The chicken tikka is really good and their white sauce is pretty amazing.  Don't go expecting any kind of ambiance or service.  I only get take-out.

Yes, they have very good meatballs. The best? Maybe not, but a lunch or dinner here is a nice treat (dinner seating can be a long wait, so I do lunch here-it is the same menu). The meatballs,sauces,and sides come in a variety of combinations too numerous for me to mention. But they are all pretty good. The specials are well worth getting especially the vegetables of the day-do not overlook the Specials Board. Last comments: the decor is cute and the staff is very pleasant and attentive (something very important to me).

Out and about on a Friday night and me and my date were off to try something new. I'm always skeptical but I need this. I need a new palate experience. As we enter the dimly lit restaurant, we are greeted by a man with a pretty rad smile, we decide, it's worth a shot. And let me just say... I love Costanera! Ambiance: Amazing customer service. I mean, really... I haven't been at a restaurant where I came out remembering just how ridiculously kind and attentive everyone was without being overwhelming. I truly appreciated the impeccable service. Food: Oh, the food... spectacular. Their Pescasdo A Lo Macho was such a delightful dish. I had the Churrasco A Lo Pobre and I couldn't stop Yumming! Everything was so good! I'll definitely be visiting again soon... very very soon!
YUMMY. It is what it is.

i am not a big ramen fan..but i LOVE kim chee bowls..but when my friend recommended Ippudo i had to try it...first i love the bar. the tabletop is clear with dried ramen in it!...i ordered a bowl of ramen and the pork buns..the ramen wasnt bad but a little pricey considering it was just ramen but i can tell they make their own noodles and it was pretty fresh..but the pork buns were delicious!!!! the pork isnt your traditional pork buns u can get at any chinese dim sum/pastry place..it was in a steamed roll (like those served with roast duck) and it was sweet with a tiny bit of spice to it..the pork melted in my mouth!....i am still craving the pork buns to this day....a must if you visit NYC

Bar is a great place to hang out. I generally hang out in the restaurant portion of this establishment, but I've hung out on the bar side on several occasions as well. I would recommend the pizza and salads to anyone who plans to eat there. The mixed greens salad with pears, bleu cheese, and candied pecans is to die for! And the mashed potato pizza is out of this world.

Nick's is the truth. I'm not sure what the question is or what false would be considered but I just know Nick's is the truth. For someone who travels a lot, it's ironic that I don't venture anywhere South of Washington Ave in my own city but today was a first, and a delightful one at that. I got the roast beef combo, which just means solid pieces of roast pork, a little au jus, and some sharp provolone. The menu is limited which is expected of places like these but who needs a thousand different combos when you just have some awesome meat, some great cheese, and have all that wedged between so fresh bread? Also, try the gravy fries. Yes, they taste as good as they look in the pictures.

love love Love... everything was great and delicious. waiter was so kind and helpful. i think that the Astoria has really really cool place after MP's grand opening.we have some great places which are cooking really good tasty food but unfortunately they are not fancy at all. I can't take my girlfriend for a dinner in Astoria( except the Italian restaurant on 31st street) but now i do. They have pretty good wine selection but still needs to improve.  appetizers are amazing especially octopus. it was the best octopus that i have ever had. I will go another time to get only some seafood and their Greek white wine. Thanks for everything...Those five stars for the food and my responsible waiter... other things will be okay  for a while I think because they just opened up the store that is why I am not judging them badly since we have so many disaster store around when I compare with them MP is doing great job.

Who couldn't be a fan of all-inclusive sangria? Normally, I'm not even big on Sangria, but they were very creative and had many different blends, loaded with fruit. DELISH! The menu is sort-of a Pan-Latin fusion, done up for the Upper West Side. I ordered the Pollo Ranchero, which was good, though portions are small to moderade in size. My friend liked her crab-cakes but said she preferred the pollo. The plantains are yummy, half are green tostones and half are ripe platanos, perfect for dessert! The bread basket was great too--the pao de queijo really made me want to go back to Brazil! Warning: Sunday brunch is BUS-Y. We had a reservation for 3:15 and thankfully they allowed us to change it to 1pm, surprising since, when we got there, they were completely booked and were not even keeping a waitlist. The only caveat is that because the place was jam-packed, there was always a line for sangria (mostly waiting for more clean glasses, which they ran out of often). But overall a great dining experience, and I left with a big sangria smile on my face and enough of a buzz to be able to withstand the cold and browse the outdoor flea market and cute UWS boutiques.
Great food! Awesome, laid back atmosphere. La Columbe Coffee! Adam is the coolest dude ever.

Been here twice, it's got a warm feel to it, the food's pretty good but it's nothing to write home about. It's just another option. Hmm.. I wonder about those amazing experiences the other reviewers are having... maybe I should spike my chai!

Real Italian food and better yet: great service! House wine was delicious and very affordable and we did not feel rushed (didn't get the bill shoved under our nose after 20 min, something that can happen a lot in NYC).

A friend and I visited Thai Palace on a Thursday evening, and had a pretty average experience. The service was fine-- neither terrible nor spectacular. The hostess (she may have been a manager) made a point to come over and ask how things were at one point, which was appreciated. I ordered pad thai, thinking I'd check out Thai Palace's take on a standard. It was somewhat disappointing. The entire dish had an odd, almost fluorescent orange tint, and there didn't seem to be many ingredients beyond noodles and shrimp and perhaps a teaspoon of crushed peanuts. There is no shortage of Thai restaurants in greater Hartford, so I wouldn't feel all that compelled to try Thai Palace again.

The positive - You will discover that yes, pizza can be this good. The negative - You won't really enjoy eating pizza most anywhere else. The pizza with truffle oil (sorry I don't remember the name) was AMAZING.

Very interesting cocktails that I haven't seen anywhere else! Menu looked good- especially the veggie/vegan options but didn't try anything. Nice bartender, didn't rush us at all. Good craft tap/bottle selections, laid back environment. Two very different environments on the first and second floor

Great service from Jason. He was cool, attentive, calm and funny. The appetizers were amazing(calamari and beef tartar)and really set the bar pretty high. Entrees were not as impressive ( swordfish and barramundi) but still didn't ruin the experience. Would definitely go back!

The worst Thai food we've had...EVER! I wouldn't even call it real Thai food. More like fast food mix of Chinese with a couple of leaves Thai basil leaves tossed in. $50 delivery of garbage... That's where it went. Don't waste your money.

I actually just came back from Cafecito! Definitely going to go back. The ambiance and vibe was just right for my me and my date. It has kind of a romantic but casual vibe to it. The drinks here during nonhappy hours are pretty standard ($8 for a strawberry caipirinha). As for the food, my date ordered the churrasco (skirt steak with chimmcuri sauce $15) and I ordered pollo empanizado (breaded chicken $13.50). Both came with a side of rice, beans and some fried plantains. My chicken was a little dry for my taste (but according to my date, he said it was fine) but the seasoning was DELICIOUS. We also ordered some yucca fries ($4.50) and they were to die for! They were very crunchy. I would definitely recommend the yucca frites + the churrasco. The staff is very quick and on point, especially for a busy Saturday night, which is something you don't find very often and is always a plus! You should check it out!

Glad we came here for dinner during out NY trip. Compared with all the Korean food I had in the US, this is definitely on the top of my list.  The food was delicious and authentic, and the atmosphere was very comfortable and great for any occasion. I totally recommend the seafood pancake and the cold noodles, very refreshing for the summer time.

I had dinner with my waif at Next Door on a busy Friday night. Very friendly staff and nearly to attentive, however good service. We chose Monkfish and the number one Burger in NJ. All the food was of very good quality and the desserts were excellent.

Sweet little wine, pizza and pasta bar. The homemade pastas were delicious, though the portions a tad small. The rabbit ravioli was the special that day- yum! There is a wood fired pizza oven, and they offer their pizza's gluten free, which is nice (I tried a piece, very tasty). Love the wood and brick interior. We brought the baby, and it was a little snug (narrow space) with the stroller, but the staff was incredibly nice and accommodating and let us keep the stroller folded up in the front. Downside was we sat near the back by the oven and it got really hot (must be super cozy in the winter though!). There is a fan that points down to those seats, once we saw it (a bit late) and asked for it to be turned on, it was a lot more bearable. I tried the vanilla cocktail, but I'm think it melted too quickly because it was a tad watery!

Almost as good, more customizable, no 1 hour waits, and 60% of the price of Ippudo. I'm a happy noodle slurper to have found this place. The tonkatsu basic broth is rich and garlicky and the thin noodles are slick and silky. Gyozas are delicate and crisp. Yum-oh. Cool art on the walls too!

Great beer selection and food, although we were primarily there for drinks after work.  If you're looking for a nicer place and get away from the dive college bars around the corner I highly recommend the malt house.  Just make sure to review your bill when closing your tab as they tend to add things which were not ordered.  Trust me, as its happened numerous times to me and my friends.

I don't know how much I recall of this place since you basically don't go there unless you're... let's say happy.  However, it's such a great place to curb a craving.  If you're in the area after midnight and are starving but can't quite tell why, check it out!

Amazing Belgium fries with more dipping sauces then you know what to do with. Happen to stubble upon this hole in the wall last time I was in NYC. Perfect place to get a mid day snack and hit the road.

I went there on the first day they had the full menu available. Sandwiches, a wide variety of pastries, soups: it's pretty straightforward cafe fare at a good price and high quality. I thought the latte I had was every bit as good as ones I've had in Center City and Manayunk. I gather that the breads and some (if not all) pastries are by Le Bus. They use Illy beans and have a nice selection of non-coffee drinks (Fizzy Lizzy sodas, etc.) There's a surprising amount of seating for a relatively small storefront, and things are designed such that it's filled with natural light despite having no south-facing windows. I can see it feeling a little tight when all the tables are occupied, but that's a pretty minor complaint. All in all, it's a very nice addition to an emerging neighborhood.

This place is not overrated! LET'S KEEP THE HYPE GOING! The steak salmon with the lemon potatoes is the bomb! What doesn't hurt like a bomb? The prices for food at this place (during lunch time)! I ate at this place with my mom during the afternoon and everything we ordered came out to around $25. The problem? The wait! My mom and I had to wait around 30 minutes to be seated and there is not much space to stand around in this restaurant. The restaurant is very small too! In fact, this restaurant has an outdoor section that is converted into an indoor section in the winter season. I was actually escorted to the converted area to be seated, but it was cold in there. There are light fixtures high above the tables in the converted area to keep customers warm, but the heat from the light burns the head after a while! I give this place a go though. Cheap, good food! P.S. Don't eat here for dinner because some of the dishes served at this place costs more money in the evening/night. Check the website for details.

These five stars are for brunch.  I've never had dinner here, but brunch was truly lovely.  Not a bargin, but the food was delicious.  The resturant is such a cozy place to  linger with friends.  Biscuits were so good. I also had  one of the best cocktails of  my life here, an apple cider bellini.  Yum!  I'll have to go back for dinner.
Decent ramen but nothing special. It's very oily and salty. It's tiny so expect to wait. It's also cash only. Not sure it's worth the inconvenience!

I love Cheryl's -- I was first introduced 3yrs ago & it is still one of the best spots in Brooklyn. I've been for brunch & dinner several times & delighted each time. For dinner - I recommend the creole shrimp -- very yummy. Seasoned and flavorful.  Jerk wings are also tasty. Great staff.. cozy place. Great date spot.  In the summer, the garden is open out back for outside dining.. However I don't recommend take-out..the portions are not equivalent which makes paying $30 unjustifiable - dine in.

Wow. Ever see movie "Meet the Parents?"  Remember that hysterical scene boarding the plane. He was only passenger and was told he could not board until they called "group 4."  Just had that experience here. Every single table was empty and still would not seat me until my wife arrived. Too unaccommodating  at this price point. Said my goodbyes and walked out.
The falafel sandwich is delicious and only $2.50. It's open late and it's the perfect little snack. I love this lil spot.

Burrito Box is delicious!  I work in the area and sometimes after a long night, all I want is a burrito or quesadilla before making the trek back to the Q train.  Burrito Box is a lifesaver at these times! I've always been impressed by their food, but this past week when I went, I got a seitan burrito and omg - it was heaven.  I've got a new favorite and I can't wait for my next burrito.  Sooo good!  A little expensive but that can easily be remedied by splitting with friends.   I only wish there was another location near my house!

So I decided to check out SoCo last Thursday..  Glad I made a reservation cause the place was packed. We were seated right  away which was a plus.  Started with the wings which were very tasty.  The non-alcoholic watermelon majito - tasty and refreshing. Main Course - short ribs very tender. Could of used a little more sauce but not bad. I thought about ordering the chicken and waffles, which apparently is the signature dish, but seeing it close-up on someone else's plate did not look as appealing. Mac and Cheese -disappointed. Overcooked? My order was too hard on top and rather dry underneath. Oh, and there was live music, which added to the enjoyment of being out on a summer's night.

Came here for dinner with a group of friends and it was an awesome dining experience.  I had the king crab legs and shrimp.  The king crab legs were meaty and sweet. The shrimp were large and fresh. I had both of them with the spicy boil sauce which is a combination butter, o' bay, and lemon pepper. One of my friends had the lobster which he said was delicious.  I also tried some crawfish which was quite tasty as well. The service was also good which is a big plus. I would definitely come back here again however my arteries might pay for it...

Holy Shiz this is good! So good that you'll want to order seconds. And you would totally do it, too, if not for that nagging little voice of reason in your head reminding you of gluttony. After you forcefully shut down the voice, you're still left with the potential embarrassment and guilt of actually finishing an entire meal and ordering another while people anxiously wait outside in the cold for your table.

BEST pizza in Brooklyn!!! After getting the hot, right out of the oven, sicilian slice of pizza, I would get a spumoni ice right next to the pizza window. OMG...i am in heaven... O... how I miss Bklyn.....x3

don't let these other reviews fool you. this is a horribly run, scum bag organization.  can't wait until they fold. besides deliveries taking forever, regardless the weather conditions, distance, time of day, any possible variable, it's always the same, even at nearly 1am.   overpriced (~$8 for 3 boneless wings?  oh that's right, they're "weighted".  my ass they're weighted.  by who?  please, send me a print out of my "weighted" order showing me that i have my half pound worth in 3 slabs of chicken), and everybody loves a delivery charge.   let alone how sloppy everything gets delivered.  bags are always dripping with sauce.  the delivery drivers might as well just stand in the road and punt the order to my house.   tonight, they decided to "shape" my boneless order in the form of a penis.. i called to complain and they were so convinced that the BONELESS WINGS COME LIKE THAT.  so they come like that, survive the breading and deep frier, and mold into the shape of a penis.  (yes, balls included). fucking disgusting.  "Jeffrey" was the manager, don't know who the cook was.  it was the night of december 14th. i will be contacting everybody possible.  the BBB, the owners, everyone.  i will discourage any and every human being not to go to this 'restaurant' that is run with a 10 year old mentality. i was a regular, now i will never spend another dime with them. how stupid do you think i am?  fucking with my food is one thing, questioning my intelligence is on a different level.  when is the last time you have seen a boneless strip of chicken in this shape?   look for yourself:   i.imgur.com/3xJvg.jpg ps - to the dork below who says "i don't understand how this place is so low rated, it's the best wings places around" -- just because it's the ONLY wings dedicated place around, doesn't make it good.   there are plenty more horror stories from this place, there just aren't enough people on yelp to share them.

Yes, i am giving only one star. I was googling "best Pancake in NYC" on an early Sunday morning because i haven't had pancakes in a very long time and i felt like looking for a place that has a real homemade pancake like i would do them at home. So "Clinton Bakery" popped up and my partner and i made us on our way to Clinton St. A very long line of annoyed/waiting people in front of their cafe welcomed us. The hostess inside informed us that the waiting time will be 2,5 h if we want a table. The hostess yelled into the crowd for everyone to keep them posted.  I had to say " i'll pass" and we've decided to have breakfast somewhere else. All other people remained strong and wanted to keep waiting. The long waiting time made me feel the pancakes there must be really good. Two months later we called Clinton Bakery spontaneously in order to ask how long the waiting time would be and they said 1,5 h. ( both times on the weekend) Last week by coincidence i had an appointment at Clinton St so i just walked across the street on a late Sunday afternoon to Clinton Bakery and the waiting time was then "only" 45 min. My partner and i wanted to try it out this time. Finally after waiting the 45 min we got seated and I've ordered:  ("Pancakes with Warm Maple Butter, Wild maine blueberry, banana walnut, or chocolate chunk  $14" ) as written on the menu. I got asked what i want and i mistakenly thought there is at least blueberries or a banana included  I  said want the  "chocolate chunk". 15 min later. I got served a high pile of layered pancakes with chocolate chips inside and i must say the pancakes were the worst and cheapest diner quality i ever ate in my life. The pancakes are made of some kind of instant powder maybe such as "Aunt Jemima", and tasted terribly dry and the flavor wasn't good either of course. Actually the pancakes had were abolutely flavorless. it was hard to swallow it down.  The chocolate chips were soft end melted inside but that did not help. It came with a creamy caramel sauce on the side  too less to overcome this dryness and the pancakes were hard to eat. I noticed after 5min that i had to add much more syrup, in order to be able to eat it. ( i actually dont like too much sugar) My boyfriend said in the same moment:" Is your pancake also this bad as mine? and we both agreed on, that the " best Pancakes " as written in new York Times are not made at Clinton Bakery. Then you can also take the time and go to one of the Irish Diners in Sunnyside, Queens. There you would really get a 3 times better prepared " instant powder" pancake and they make it taste softer with a rich flavor and serve you a richer or nicer decoration with more exciting ingredients. ( a bit ice cream ,or fruits, whip cream, or anything else.) The pancakes at Clinton Bakery were utmost simple. The other pancakes at Clinton Bakery come only with some blueberry sauce and blueberries, maybe the artificial caramel sauce on the side. Or just banana and walnut etc. Hope this helps to give you an authentic impression. I haven't tried a burger there and we won't come back. The waiting times are so or so uneccaptable, especially if it gets colder outside.
Burger was alright but I was waiting for better... Food is cheap, vibe is kinda cool.
Love this place! Service is great ! Good is awesome! I bring friends over here all the time :)

My dad and I went here on a Tuesday afternoon. Nice outdoor seating (and big indoor space), decent coffee, and good vegetarian options. I got a cheese/tomato/avocado/chipotle mayo sandwich and my dad got an omelette. I'll go back for dinner sometime!
Jambalaya, fried chicken, collards, MAC and the Mississippi mojito were amazing. Dig in.

V-nam Cafe has amazing comfort food (for me) and at unbeatable prices. The Clay Pot Ginger Chicken Rice is seriously amazing. The banh mi was good but a fresh baguette would put it over the top. This cold weather means I'm planning my next visit soon so I can work my way through the rest of the menu. Additionally, the yelp hours are wrong for at least the weekend. I stopped by one Saturday and V-nam was definitely no where near opening at 11:30 am.

Last night we took my wife for her birthday dinner here after family highly recommended it.  We were a party of 6.  We were disappointed with the experience.  It should be noted that the restaurant was not very busy so the review that follows is not based on a rough night at the restaurant. When ordering, we asked the server about ingredients for dishes and she did not have answers or offer to find out.  Fifteen minutes later, the server asked me to confirm my order, which I did.  Forty-five minutes after originally ordering, we inquired about our meal and were told  it would be out in 5 minutes. The delay was explained as a kitchen issue.   Ten minutes later,  a different server apologized and said that it would be out in 5 minutes and delivered a complimentary pastry.  We asked what was the pastry and the server said he did not know.  Another 10 minutes goes by when the server says it will be out in two minutes.  Four of the six dishes came out ten minutes later.  One dish was cold.  All dishes ordered broccoli and the broccoli was almost raw. The other two dished owed were nowhere to be found.  Another server asked what was ordered which seemed strange because the person who took our order had written things down and she was still present.  At that point they said they would have it out in about 2 minutes explaining that they were not sure if the dishes made were for our table or another table.   Five minutes later, a person who appeared to be the manager came out and said that the order was never placed for the two dishes. This is well over an hour after originally ordering.  We were assured it would be out within five minutes.  Five  minutes later, they asked my son if he was willing to have another pasta  because spaghetti takes too long to make (not sure why spaghetti would take longer than any other pasta).  Ten minutes latert the food came out with spaghetti rather than the amended request of rigatoni.   The food sent back for coming out cold came back hot but was dried out while most of us had completed our meal when the last two meals had come out.  T he restaurant did not charge for the two late meals. But, the  aggravation was not worth the discount.  Two of the servers were pleasant and were given tips for trying to help out but the original server and the server who brought us the complimentary pastry were given nothing based on their indifference to customer service and a complete lack of knowledge of what they were serving.  Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this restaurant.

This truly is as good as it gets! A quaint little place in a cute ares of town, the food here is amazing. Granted we did get the chef's choice menu, which includes a salad, appetizer, pasta, and meat entree, the balance with which it was presented cannot be beat. It was $40 per person but well worth every penny. The selections change from time to time but will surely delight. You have to be present to put your name in since they don't take reservations, and on a weekend night, can be a long wait.

Food is very good, authentic Malaysian, for reasonable price. The biggest let down is that they don't accept credit card!; I had to run out to get money from ATM, had to keep my guests waiting! Atmosphere is very casual and noisy. Chicken / Beef satay is excellent.

Very good, intimate neighborhood Mediterranean on the UWS. Attentive staff, relaxed vibe and good fare, with some creative twists to Med classics such as eggplant with tahini instead of ricotta. It's easy to over-order and even easier to over-eat.  The small plates are great to share, making this a good place for a date or a small group.

I used to live down the block from the location that would become Stone Park Café, so I was quite intrigued when what I used to know as an unused storefront (and one time bodega) was now a trendy looking cafe/restaurant serving breakfast.  My friends and I wanted brunch, but not just something for McDonalds or something.  This fit the bill perfectly.   We sat outside, something I rarely do but it was super comfortable (and the weather was perfect).  As pigeons wandered by and kids played across the street in the park, we enjoyed each other's company and then tried to figure out what the heck we were going to order.  The problem is simple: everything on the menu looks insanely good.  Finally I settled on an egg white omelet with spinach, onion and garlic.  Truth be told, the garlic is what sold me.  Roasted garlic?  On an OMELET?!  You damn right I'm going to try that! Omelets are one of those foods that rarely have a middle ground.  They're either very "Meh" or they're awesome.  Stone Park does them AWESOME.  The roasted garlic was so flavorful and soft it melted in your mouth.  The spinach was perfectly cooked and the eggs were moist and springy.  Excellent stuff. The service was very laid back and chill, but friendly and efficient all at the same time.  This reflects the general mood of the restaurant's setting, so I was very pleased to see such consistency.   I'm a fan of Stone Park for sure and look forward to going back in the future.
Horrible place and decoration and I was charging more than in menu simply ripped off. Cash only. Stay away. Frozen food not real italian. Tasted like two shits in bucket f- it.

As I get ready to flee the country, I realize this is yet another go-to place that I haven't reviewed.   Though it looks a little more like a bus stop inside than its predecessor Shinju, Fat Salmon is reasonably priced, the fish is very fresh, and the preparation is solid.  If there's a downside to it, I guess it would be the slightly hard decor and over-abundance of slightly gimmicky rolls.  But if you just stick with the straightforward options, you won't go wrong. The fifth star is for consistency over a bunch of seminar dinners and random stop-ins, though, not because it blows you away.

i tried this place bc i heard good things and wanted thai food quickly.. sorry, this is really crappy desperation thai food. The chicken had a peanutty sauce but made me nascious after eating too much.. not sure if it was undercooked. The "pad thai" noodles were just the thin rice noodles with a flavor of pad thai and without anything like peanuts, shrimp or chicken. Save your $ and go to the taco cart.

Living in the Bay Area all my life, I've always been exposed to great burritos.. La Victoria and Iguanas in San Jose, El Farfolito in SF..  I must say, out of all the (terrible) burritos I've tried in NYC over the past two years, Dos Toros blows them all out of the park!  The only thing missing is the orange sauce from La Vic's.. But I find myself saying that after eating any burrito that isn't from La Vic's.   I went with the burrito w/carne asada, the habanero hot sauce (extra) and guac.  DELISH!

Great first time experience, came with a friend. Edamame Ravioli - great creamy filling, but only 3 pieces to share. Mongolian Barbecue Beef Short Rib - so tender, meat literally fell off the bone as we touched it, great sauce too. Korean Beef Fried Rice - strong seasonings, packed with flavor. Crying Chocolate - so rich, nice treat to top off a great meal.

This is the most brilliant and delicious scam ever: they lure you in with a $15 steak, but they don't take reservations, so of course the wait is 2 hours every single time. Oh, don't worry, they also own the bar next door! So what happens? You sign up for a $15 steak, end up spending the next two hours getting sloshed on wine and cheese platters next door, and by the time they text you for dinner, you're so drunk you order the entire menu, including whatever silly vegetable specials they have for that day (stinging nettles?!) Maybe this is just what happens to me every time I go here? Please tell me I'm not the only one? So the first time I came here, I brought my boyfriend, who at the time was in the Army and on Leave in NY, because he wanted a good steak. They sat us right next to a window that had a tattered, dirty American flag as a curtain, and I immediately saw his jaw tense up. "This better be a damn good steak," I thought; "fucking Williamsburg and their insouciant irony," I mentally added. He's now obsessed with this restaurant, and we've returned several times, so suffice to say the steak is good enough to overcome the blatant desecration of the symbol of the country he fought for. Sweet!

The ramen here is delicious!!! This is by far one of the best ramen I have had. If u plan on eating here, I suggest coming about 30 min or so before they open cuz this place gets packed fast! I came here with my bf on a Friday and we were there 30 min before they opened and the line was already forming. We got the miso ramen and the spicy ramen. Both were delicious. My bf really enjoyed his spicy ramen because the spicy broth was very good but his noodles were not as good or the same as my miso ramen. The miso ramen noodles do taste better as it seems it's more hand made. The broth for the miso ramen is also very tasty. It is more thick and has a lot more flavor than all the other miso ramen I have had. Overall, both my bf and I love this place, so I definitely recommend it!

Went today grabbed a bunch of bagels to go. Service is crap and rude. My order was screwed up top to bottom. And the pig couldn't keep his eyes and comments out of the young ladies curves..  Who is Managing this sleaze

We went to this spot to grab a glass of wine and I LOVE IT!!!!! It was quaint, quiet and had a great atmosphere.  I would go back in a heartbeat for brunch, lunch or dinner.  One thing that was great was when we walked in you immediately smell all the yummy food because the chef is cooking right behind the bar.   It makes for a great time and you actually can see your food being cooked. I hope that everyone that lives in NYC checks this place out!

Was my go-to place for take-out indian when i was in school. Lunch buffet is great, and got fat off of all the galub jamun i had afterwards. Reasonably priced, and would recommend to those looking for serviceable indian food.

I came here for lunch with my Loan Officer and her staff...The food was to DIE for. I ordered the Penne pasta ala vodka with Shrimp...My 3 coworkers all ordered another dish And told me the legend behind the RigaTony gravy...special plum tomato sauce made from special tomatoes imported from Italy and the secret sauce made at home..I was like Yeah, right..The restaurant was under construction but the owner and his brother were kind, sweet, and attentive. The food was incredibly captivating to the palate and the soul.. when I looked up my 3 coworkers cleaned their plates..Weeks went by and I found out they ordered Rigatony Anthony...I ordered it and it lived up to the Rigatony Legend..Pasta was cooked aldente,  the chicken melted in your mouth, the mushrooms, sauce were well balanced and exceptionally seasoned..I did what any girl in my position would do....I joined the Karate school 2 doors down so that I can have RigaTonys anytime without gaining weight...My Mamita didn't raise any fools.LOL..Thank You RigaTonys for feeding me.

This place is the real deal...no bullshit, & definitely no fajitas! If your looking for a traditional mexican feed, then this place is great bang for your buck. The service is prompt, with the waiter making recommendations which were spot on. The tv was playing an 80's cult movie Fast Times at Ridgemont High, with every nude scene attracting applause by the punters and staff alike. A great vibe with everyone there out to have a good time. I highly recommend the Pollo Flautas (chicken crispy tacos in a flute like shape) & the Pollo Tostadas (Mexican salad on top of a corn tortilla). Fresh & delicious. The margarita's are also great. I'll definitely be back!

Fabulous, unique brunch. The sheep's milk ricotta with honey on toast is DIVINE...and what a massive portion of ricotta!! Hubby and I were nearly full after sharing this dish but still immensely enjoyed the Salumi Misti (selection of thin-sliced cured meats) and the Uovo Modenese (their version of eggs benny but made with a salami hash). First-rate brunch in Tribeca!

Great artichoke slice, but the crab is not so good. I know, I know: what was I doing getting crab in a place like this.  Probably got bird flu. I would have given them four stars but $4 a slice is pushing it.

Love this place. The decor/atmosphere is perfect for a low-key night out with the girls, and the dinner food is solid. The chicken meatballs and grilled cheeses are good. The red velvet cake is to die for. I'm pretty picky when it comes to this cake variety (as in I refuse to eat it if it comes with vanilla frosting and not cream cheese frosting), but I think Penelope's is one of the best in the city. Super moist cake and they are generous with the cc frosting.
American number one burger is ok.

I'm obsessed with this place, and I've been meaning to write a review for a while. Huge portions of delicious authentic Greek food at an affordable price! Yeah, there's always a wait, but they'll totally hook you up with a free glass of wine or beer while you count down the minutes to happiness. My favorite things on the menu are the Greek salad, broiled scallops, the crab stuffed filet and the fried peppers. I'm a big fan of the lemon potatoes, beets and horta also. Give me some lemon wedges, and let's go to town. Pro tip: Get there early and you may just get to try that glorious custard/phyllo dessert. The last few times they've been all out by the time I've finished gorging myself.

One of my absolute favorite restaurants in the city.  I've spent a lot of time in Italy and the food here is as close to authentic as you can get without going there.  I can't say enough--just love it.

This is a very busy restaurant and the front of house needs to be more efficient if they are going to manage high volumes of people. I was told a wait of 45 minutes which in fact ended up being two hours. That's fine if I had known this at the beginning however the three hostess failed to handle the complexity of booking a table for three. The food is good but take some time in your business to train the staff in organizing the queues of people waiting to be seated. We watched several people who arrived after us to be seated before us. Simple ignorance of the staff ignoring us and not even making eye contact when listening to our complaints. Prepare for the wait of the table and its by no means worth a wait of two hours.

Now I was back and the drunken noodles were almost better than what I had the other time.  The flavors were surprising and delicious.  They kept me waiting and without me saying a word brought me extra apps.  NICE!
So good - only tried the traditional sandwich but it was executed well. full flavor, and the pita was fluffy and soft. SOOOO GOOD ! By far, one of the best falafels I've had !
Lombardi's pizza is one of my favorite places to go when I'm visiting NY. Their pizza is so amazing good!

Burger meat is great, menu is extensive, adult shakes are delicious, service is a little slow, prices are high. I would return. Burgers: My rare burger was pink but not as bloody as I'd like rare to be. The burger itself had a great flavor with a nice char, though my char/crust was a little too thick on the bottom. This is a good, thick burger, though. I got a Southwestern burger bowl and it was a good, low carb choice. The cheese was not as melted as I would have liked, but whatev. My partner built his own burger with fresh mozzarella on it. The mozz was good - soft, thick. The bun was just alright. We got no sides. Shakes: I got a strawberry shortcake shake with vodka, cake mix, strawberries, and icecream. It was good, and the whipped cream was great, but I couldn't taste the liquor. My partner's shake was out of this world. Bananas foster definitely had rum in it and a great burnt caramel flavor to go with the bananas. I could drink that forever. Our two burgers and two liquor shakes cost $50. You are paying for the cool factor. Service: We went at 8:15 on a Friday night. There was no wait. Our food was a little slow coming out, though. We left around 9:45. So, 2 people with two burgers and two shakes took an hour and a half. We also got our shakes after our food, so we were sitting around for awhile with nothing to eat or drink.

Great food and atmosphere Came here on a small trip into South Street. Decided to stop here to get some brunch. I believe I got the eggs benedict and hollondaise sauce. The meal was pretty delicious. Me and my friend sat on the table outside, and it was very pleasant to watch cars and people on the street pass by, albeit it was a bit cold. My friend made several small requests regarding the meal and they honored it pretty well. I would definitely check this place out again.

I have no idea what happened to this place. It used to be a terrific, if overly MSG'd restaurant. I think that there are new owners. the food was overly greasy, under seasoned and gross. At least I have an MSG headache. We all feel sick.

This was the second time I have been to Macs and had another pleasant experience. The waitress that took care of us was pretty attentive and very nice. My friend even commented she was even super quick on water refills.  The gravy fries were really good; everyone enjoyed them.  The atmosphere was pretty laid back. I would go back again.

I had breakfast here because it was very close to the motel that I stayed at. Ordered the corn beef hash with two eggs. The eggs were find and the toast that came with it was good too. What I looked forward to eating was the corn beef hash and that was a disappointment. It had a very bitter taste and salt didn't help at all. The waiting service was exceptionally friendly, but the food was the main turnoff.

Yum Burger and Truffle fries. Burger is massive!  Worth the 1/2hr wait.  I've been one other time and had the ricotta pancakes, but I prefer the burger. Truffle fries are always always always good. I have had better, but you can never go wrong with truffle oil. Our waiter was so happy it was weird, but it meant for very attentive service. Its a very hipstery vibe, but not the snobby type. Cute, squashy atmosphere, and very generous with the condiments. I like this! Get the Coffee. Especially the affogato!! The icecream is delish and they give you a double shot of actually good coffee.

Went to OPA based on having one of their drinks at an Octoberfest Block Party.  Ordered the Scallops & Octopus appetizers, both very good, but somewhat small, a couple more pieces would have made it a really good sharing appetizer.  We ordered the Pastitsio and again it was a bit small, but it was very tasty, we were able to share this as I don't think either of us were too hungry.  Finally as a post dinner snack we got the cheese board, this was definitely enough to share with plenty to satisfy both of us.   The atmosphere of this place is very nice, however it kept getting hot then cold, my date was constantly putting on and taking off her sweater. I have heard that their gyros are worth trying and I may give it a shot sometime.  All in all this was a nice place for a date.  Good food, good drink, reasonably priced.

Brought my staff here for Christmas dinner last year. Despite having a reservation we waited over an hour and then ate at the bar. Not what I was hoping. Food was good and once we ordered, the staff was pleasant but for a place in this price range, the experience was unacceptable.

Ate an early thursday night supper here. Restaurant filled up quickly as we ate. Pleased, but not dazzled, with the two standards what we ordered, steak tartare and coq au vin. Did not try one of their cocktails, but wine and beer were reasonably priced. Real draw is the atmosphere; a place where everyone seems to enjoy themselves. High noise/activity level appeals to the clientele. Service was the only facet that did not impress. Our server was pleasant, but lacked knowlege of the menu intracacies and wine list. Did appreciate that two managers stopped by the table to chat.

Came here on a Monday night and still had to wait 2 hours!  But, it was totally worth it! They use an iPad to set up your reservation and call/text you when they have a table ready.  It was pretty efficient - our group just shared snacks in other LES places like Katz  until they called us. I came with 3 other friends, so I was able to try a bunch of different meatballs.  We ordered the bolognese meatballs with parmesan sauce, spicy pork meatballs with the meat sauce, chicken meatballs with tomato sauce, and the beef meatballs with mushroom sauce.  Every one of these meatballs was delicious!  Though, a clear favorite would be the spicy pork meatballs with the meat sauce.  Did I taste sriracha in that meatball? Don't forget to order the ice cream sandwiches.  I got a chocolate chip, vanilla ice cream sandwich.  The cookie was a little overdone and it was perfect with the ice cream because it added this crispy texture to it.  It was to die for. The shop is small with a wine bar & bar seating and a long table in the middle.  I actually liked the long table - it's kind of cool that we are sitting next to complete strangers eating and enjoying meatballs.  AND - we get to check out what they ordered before we make our decisions.   Also - the bathroom is cute...and huge in proportion to the establishment.   Overall, love this place!  It gets 5 stars from me.

Best thing was the fries. We ordered a crab poboy it was dry.  Not enough sauce.  It was very overpriced.  We also had the gumbo it had a few scraps of food in broth.  It was the worst i have ever had.  We also tried to use a entertainment coupon for lunch and was not able to because it was brunch.  I have never had brunch at 2 pm on a Saturday. I would not recommend this place and i will never go back

I have not reviewed this place - shame on me. As the 4891th reviewer, let me officially assure you - this place is LEGIT!  I know there are carts on all corners of this intersection, and I have been assured by MANY New Yorkers that ALL 4 carts belong to the same people hence the food tastes the same. But true to my uber FOBBY self that reveals itself in NYC particularly, I will duly wait in line at the cart right outside Starbucks. I have always only eaten here and I will always only eat here.. yea, I am weird that ways! I always get the chicken over rice withe extra yogurt sauce - the chicken is moist, it's flavorful - it's like a spoonful of chicken heaven in each spoonful, I would change NOTHING about this place - except maybe have someone police the place for all the super ghetto people who refuse to clean up after themselves X-( Regardless, no trip to NYC is complete in it's fobby goodness without a bowl full of chicken over rice from this place - also, lo behold dear reader, this place gets 2 - not one thumbs up from my sister too..!!

Went here last night for dinner with my husband. Got there around 7pm and already the place was very crowded. we luckily didnt have to wait for a table but i assume people who came after us did. got three appetizers- fish tacos, carne in plantains and arepa con carne. the plantain was the best and unlike anything i had ever had. the other two dishes were good but nothing unknown. we had beer so i can't speak for the drinks but the price was right- $4 each! i would def go back

Imagine a shrunken Flat Iron building and that is the space that Bite inhabits. It must be  an impossible feat to prepare the food they have here for hungry souls looking for a quick, cheap meal on the run but they do an excellent job as the constant long line confirms.

Absolutely unbelievable. Gato is across from my apartment and since I'm lazy, it's high up on my places to eat list. But that's not to say it doesn't deserve this 5-star review. I have not had a single dish there that didn't knock my socks off. I don't care whether you like octopus or not, EVERYONE MUST TRY THE OCTOPUS. It's like ayahuasca trip level life changing.

Not bad. Good for a quick lunch when you can't find anything in the Times Square area to your liking. The place itself is very small. It generally caters to people taking food out rather than dining in. Basically you order up front and they'll call you when your food is ready. It didn't feel as clean as I would've liked it, but it wasn't intended to be dine in anyway so I understand. I got the chicken katsu curry single and while not a gigantic portion, it was filling enough for me at the time. I'd probably order the double next time since it wasn't a big price difference, but you get a little more. The curry was good. It had strong curry taste that wasn't overpowering and went really well with the rice. The chicken itself was somewhat dry though and they put this sweet sauce on top of it that I didn't like very much. I would've been happy with only the curry and the rice I think. They have free water for their customers which you serve yourself so it was a nice touch. For what you get and also considering that you are in Manhattan, the prices are affordable. It's not something extraordinary for me though so it won't be one of the top places to come try again.
Food was ok.  Installations were ok.  Service was ok.  Overall ok, nothing fancy, nothing worth mentioning except that service was quick.

Great bar. Chill but intimate... I was digging the motif. Behind the bar there was a wide selection of yummy drafts, including one of my favorite hard ciders. I was totally feeling it here and I look forward to a return trip!

Came here for brunch this past Sunday with a $15 Restaurant.com gift certificate, which I purchased pre- Sandy. Even though they're no longer doing promotions with Restaurant.com post-Sandy, they were still incredibly kind about my gift certificate and accepted it. It seems they were hit hard by Sandy as they're literally a block away from the water. However, things seem to be back to normal as they're excepting credit cards now! I had the Fish Tacos with a side of guacamole that was delicious! Fish was blackened and had a great flavor. Only complaint was that there was only two tacos and they were rather small...definitely not enough for one meal. My boyfriend ordered the Sausage, Biscuits and Gravy which was absolutely delicious! It was an incredibly large portion which is why the tacos seemed so small in comparison. 2 Biscuits cut in halves so a total of four pieces with sausage and gravy poured on top. Also came with two eggs and your choice of grits or potatoes. We went with the potatoes and they were great! Even though my portion was much smaller- we shared his entree so it ended up evening out! Last, but not least we had to try the Cowgirl's Famous Ice Cream Baked Potato. The name by itself was just so intriguing. At first, we thought the dessert was truly made from baked potatoes...but that's not the case. Haha its more of an ice cream sundae designed to look like a baked today? Although the giant dollop of cream on top is actually sour cream (not whipped cream). It was ABSOLUTELY amazing and we surprisingly devoured the whole thing. I'm not even a fan of chocolate and i absolutely loved the syrup that they had on the bottom. It was simply amazing and a great way to jump start a lazy Sunday brunch! Would definitely come back again. yelp.com/biz_photos/cowg…
