Very impressive selection of macarons, both in the wide selection of flavors and in the flawless appearance of each individual piece.  With the wide variety, there are bound to be likes and dislikes in terms of flavor and internal consistency (depending on the filling), but each of the six I tried were impeccably constructed and enjoyable.  The only flavor that was a miss was the Caramel with Salted Butter, which could probably be more appropriately titled as just plain Caramel than trying to invoke the ever popular salted caramel taste.  Of course, there is also the issue of paying $3.50 for a silver dollar-sized confection--buying Ladurée macarons is certainly not value shopping--but an indulgence now and then to experience the superb tastes and quality is worth the occasional splurge.

Yes yes and yes! No need to reiterate what others have written....except maybe, get the Nutella calzone if it's on the chalkboard. Broke our Yom Kippur fast here last night after visiting Greenwood Cemetery and Prospect Park's Memorial Grove. And now we want to make it part of our annual tradition. Or just move there so we could eat there on a more frequent basis. Yes folks, it is that good! Date night, family night, just go.

I would have given this place 4 stars because the food was delicious, but since the wait was a nightmare, I had to take away 1 star. The restaurant is small. We were told the wait would be 45min. Urm.. more like 90 min. You should just double whatever number the hostess tells you. We went to a bar nearby to wait but after 45min, there was still no call. Therefore, I called them instead. Nobody picked up. I waited another 15min, and finally somebody picked up the phone and told me there was still no table. I wish they had the courtesy to call me instead and inform me of the latest status update, so I would know whether to order another drink in the bar or get ready to head over. My  friends and I decided to go over to the restaurant and wait. We stood there for at least 20min. We were told that the table in front of us would become ours once the guests left. Those idiots had been sitting there for the past 3 hours and still refused to leave. They have to be really free to leave work at 5pm sharp, make it down to the Lower East Side, and attempt to spend their whole evening there. We decided to use the STARE-DOWN technique to make them leave. They took 10min just to sign their bills, then continued to sit there and talk. OMG!! We need a hostess who can tell these retards to get the f out! They finally left and we were seated. Grapefruit margaritas!! We ordered three of these immediately to calm our nerves. We also ordered guac and chips. The margaritas were delicious. The  guac was incredibly fresh! They don't really give you enough chips for  the guac though. We shared the following platters: Enchiladas de Mole: Pretty good, lots of beans. Barbacoa: shredded lamb. This was my favorite. The lamb was so tender and full of flavor! Camarones Borrachos: fresh shrimp sauteed in tequila and other things. I couldn't taste the tequila but it was delicious. I don't know if I will come back here  because I'm afraid of dealing with this nightmarish wait.
Upgrading to four stars. Truth be told the drinks gave me a major hangover but not sure if that was specific to the drinks or to my old age!

I've been here 3 times in the past month and definitely coming back for more. So far I've tried: Chicken Rice - this is so good the Boy had it the 2nd and 3rd times we came here. I have only tried two other places that makes better chicken rice and neither of them are in the USA. Hokkien Char Mee (KL Style) - Very authentic and very good. I have had a couple that were slightly better in KL itself, but this is easily 90th percentile anywhere I've tried. Definitely ordering this again at some point. Chow Kuey Tiao - Again, very authentic and very good. I like mine a little spicier than they make it, but I would think it's not hard to ask for more chili in the dish. Sizzling beancurd - This is fried tofu served on an iron heated plate with a sauce containing meat, peas, carrots, etc. We had white rice with this and it was excellent. Tofu was tasty and well fried and the sauce was savory. I prefer this made with egg tofu (they use regular tofu), but it was still good. Cold soy bean milk with grass jelly - I love grass jelly but I'm always too lazy to shred it myself at home, so I order it when I go out. They basically use the commercial sweetened soy milk you can buy in bottles at Hong Kong Supermarket around the corner, so if you object on principle to paying $3 for the cup when you can get the whole bottle for $2.79 avoid this. It comes with a VERY generous helping of shredded grass jelly though, so I'm a happy camper! The bill for 2 usually comes to ~$20 including tip/tax. Service is efficient, English-speaking, and pretty friendly. Subway is right around corner and I have usually not had problems finding parking if I came by car. It's a small place and if you are sitting on the bench that's installed along the wall be warned that the bench is a bit narrower than you'd expect... the person with the smaller butt/shorter legs should sit inside and let the other person take the regular chair on the outside!

You know its a popular place when you come here at 3am and the line to get in is halfway down the block! We were a bit impatient and gave the doorman a little 'incentive' to move our group to the front of the line which he did.  We were seated in less than 10 minutes.  It was suggested that I try the Mac and Cheese which I did.  It was so rich that I couldn't finish it all!  I wish I could have tried some of the other things on the menu and been awake enough to appreciate them a little more!

I have been here a few times. It has a friendly environment and there is outdoor seating on a nice day. My boyfriend had the eggs benedict with hollandaise sauce and really enjoyed it. I've had a number of their omlets and enjoyed them.  The bread basket is the best!!

My friend and I heard great reviews about this place and decided to go for Sunday brunch. Unfortunately, I cannot comment on the food because I wasn't allowed to sit down. I had walked 2 miles to meet my friend here and was told that I could not sit until she had arrived. I asked the tall man with glasses if I could just sit at one of the many empty tables because I was thirsty, where he told me that they are usually busy on Sundays and could not seat me until my friend arrived. So I awkwardly stood in the almost empty cafe waiting.  I understand the policy when there is a wait or you are busy, but this was not the case and I felt unwelcome. The man then came up and said "your friend should pay the bill since she is making you wait". I was so uncomfortable that I just left. I have worked in the service industry for almost 10 years and would never treat a customer like that. We wanted this to be our new brunch spot, but now we are never coming back.

We ordered the special, the roasted pig with a crispy top, over a bed of sweet potatoes, excellent. The wine was great, Primitivo, a pinot noir. The restaurant was packed, we waited in a full bar for our table, we got in time and waited 20 minutes.  Very good place. The carcioffi fritti was good and the octopus didn't have a strong flavor, so i liked it.   The service was outstanding, our waitress was very polite, nice and professional.  The desert was delicious, the grape sorbet was yummy. The entrance and bar of the Gramercy Hotel is beautiful. I recommend it and will come back.
Not your typical greasy or bland breakfast place.  High quality and consistently good.  Consistently delicious.  Get there early to avoid the crowds.

Cash only. (Fairly common in this whole area.) Rude (RUDE!!!) service.  (They act like they are doing YOU a favor allowing you to eat their pizza - think "Soup Nazi" in Seinfeld.) LONG (long) lines.  After being told the long line would take 30 mins but waiting over 70 mins, we finally got a table.  We were now STARVING (our fault for already being hungry when we came). We quickly ordered.   They brought us someone else's pizza (one, when we ordered 3)... we had to wait a LONG time, staring at this delectable looking pizza, until a server finally noticed that we needed them.  We told them this was not our pizza.  They took it away.  Period.   Eventually, our pizzas came (1 cheese, 1 pepperoni, and 1 that was 1/2 veggie and 1/2 sausage olive - $2 extra per topping, even if you are doing only half... so the $16 pizza turned into a $28 pizza)... they were AWESOME.  We INHALED them.  4 people ate almost 3 whole pizzas (we expected to have a whole pie leftover and instead left with about 4 pieces). YUM! But was it worth it? I guess it was fun to try, but there HAS to be pizza that is as good where they actually WANT your business.
LOVE the eel bibimbap!!!!!:)

I feel duped!! I kept wondering how they came to their under 500 calorie claim, as it didn't seem to add up.  How can something with ingredients such meat, cheese, pesto, etc., AND bread add up to only approx 300-400 calories?  Without sacrificing relatively good flavor?? Lo and behold, on the very last page of the menu, at the bottom of the page, I see that calorie counts do NOT include bread.  How do you have a section for panini's and wraps, list calorie counts, but then state that the bread/wrap is not included?? Well, for those of you who are calorie/carb/points counting, feel free to add at least an extra 200 calories to the listed calorie counts in the menu--bringing the calorie count for most of their panini's/wraps to well above 500 calories.  What kind of trickery and dishonesty is this??  So disappointed. Just be honest and avoid the gimmicks, Fuel!  And how about you actually list the calorie/carb  count for the panini bread/wraps that you  conveniently excluded from your menu. And if I'm wrong, and somehow misread or misinterpreted the menu, I would love for one of the owners to address this....if not, I'll take  your silence as an admission of guilt.

Went here for brunch with my gf to catch up and it was AMAZING!!!! From the coffee all the way to dessert everything was delicious. The one guy Gabby I believe was his name made the experience even better. He was nice and welcoming, gave my friend and I great recommendations, and came back to check on us with delightful conversation. Great experience can't wait to go back.

Went here for a Sunday brunch with the wife.  We arrived around 2pm and waited for about 30 minutes, not bad.  We were sat next to the window and was comfortable. The busboy and waiter promptly attended our table and our course we ordered the Prix Fixe menu. $14 for either a mimosa, bloody mary, screwdriver, or just plain OJ.  Also comes with a free refill.  Coffee or tea is also included.  We both ordered a mimosa which was good. I ordered the crab cake benedict and my wife ordered the wheat pancakes.  The food came out pretty quickly and were both delicious and fulfilling.  The crab cakes were deep fried and I prefer mine's non-breaded.  Nevertheless, great way to start out the day.  They have an extensive brunch menu and quite a large selection of pancakes and french toast. The ambiance was trendy and of course with loud music which seems to be an Astoria prerequisite. The crowd was less pretentious than a city or Brooklyn brunch joint. The service was great and the food was good.  It's a little small but 24 hours, 7 days a week.  Glad we discovered this.  Great value. PS, be sure to mention the free refill to your alcoholic beverage.  The waiter will NOT tell you this.

This restaurant is a beacon of southern hospitality.  I commend Maysville for the service, a bit less for the food.   My dinner group of six ladies had reservations at 7pm. The restaurant kindly seated the party despite being short one straggler (me).  We were seated near the entryway, in front of a large, unfinished, black-and-white drawing of a horse.  Because our dinner time and table location coincided with a Friday happy hour, it was bustling with raucous professionals.  If you're on a date or aim to preserve your hearing, request to sit deeper into the restaurant. We started with oysters for the table.  At $3.25 per oyster, it's not a particularly cheap appetizer.  The oyster was served on the half-shell, on top of kindling straw that was smoking just slightly at the ends.  It was a unique presentation, seeing that most oysters at other establishments are served on ice. BORING.  But is presentation alone worth the $3.25 price tag? You decide. We each ordered a different entree from the menu (there were only six entrees available, so it worked out well).  I ordered the slow roasted arctic char, and paired the fish with sparkling wine.  The dish wasn't memorable, other than the fact that it was over salted.  Actually, everyone's dishes were a bit over salted... What WAS worth the price tag: the complimentary cornbread muffins.  They are portion controlled, so you don't feel guilty eating all four of them on the plate.  Did I mention that they're complimentary? NOTE: I research menu offerings prior to sitting down for my meal, and I did the same for Maysville. The online dinner menu differed slightly from the in-house menu.
Pizza is awesome. Suggest the buffalo chicken! Good as it is in NYC. People behind the counter are also very hospitable !!!
I had a buffet here on a Sunday. It was okay, I'm not the biggest fan of indian food though... There was always water on the table, which was nice. The Nan (bread) was really good.

Came here on friday night with two of my friends. I made a reservation a couple of hours earlier, and was seated right away upon arrival. We got there around 6:15 ish, and the place was already pretty packed!! The decor of the restaurant was stunning! It was really modern and wonderful. We decided to order the rock shrimp, kobi fried rice, Szechuan chicken, shrimp and lobster dumpling, and the peking duck. Our food arrived pretty quickly, not all at once though. We really enjoyed everything, I love the peking duck most of all. The szechuan chicken came last basically when we were almost done eating. It was average, but maybe because we were quite full. Wanted to order the dessert, but was too full. There is always next time though!!

Had a great time here this past weekend with my pals. We ordered a bunch of sushi and some drinks. My new favorite roll is the m&m which has marinated meat inside. I know it's unusual but it was delicious. Service was great, our waitress Jes was really friendly and made good suggestions. I couldn't give this place 5 stars only because I wish the alcohol prices weren't so high but I guess that's what you get for being in Center City. But I'll be back regardless for the good sushi and atmosphere.
Good food. Reasonable prices. Great atmosphere.Highly recommended!

Coffe is a bit expensive, but it is good. The food is good too. I like this place bette than mugshots for so many reasons. If you want coffee or good food and enjoy the neighborhood this is your place. I bring my lap top and do some work during the day. I bring my daughter in a stroller on a weekend after a run.mi bring my parents so they can look out the windows and people watch. Lol. The best part is that this iscacgreat place to just get out of the house by yourself and relax. Lol.. I like how all ages and all types of people are there. If you don't like kids then you should go to a cramped Starbucks on 20 th street.

Stopped in while visiting family in Brooklyn- so glad we did! Loved the comfortable atmosphere, laid-back and very homey. Dishes are served family-style & come to the table as they're ready, great for sharing. We enjoyed radishes with uni & shrimp butter, chili spiced Chinese long beans, delicious whole trout & egg noodles with duck sausage & bok choy. Menu changes daily with providers & produce sources provided.  Will definitely be back next time we're in town!
Really good ambiance, good hookah, good service.

While visiting from California and we had 5 hours in Manhattan.  I've been to the City multiple times but my husband hasn't so we had to squeeze in as many tourist traps as we could.  How do you fit in the Ground Zero, Statue of Liberty, Times Square, Top of the Rock, Central Park, etc into 5 hours?  The key here was prioritizing and one of the items that climbed to the top of the list was NY Cheesecake. While at Times Square I said he HAS to have Junior's.  I typically go to Viniero's but with a big time restraint we had Junior's and happy we did.  We grabbed the strawberry and chocolate.  It was gone faster than you could say "Naked Cowboy"  My husband doesn't have a sweet tooth but he KILLED them.  If we didn't have so many other stops I'm sure he'd want a third!
Good place for Mexican food. Everything was really fresh, the guacamole is a must it was really good. Accommodating for vegetarians. Place is really clean.

If the line wasn't a 45 minute wait it gets the full 5.  Pizza is different for different people.  For me - this is nearly pizza perfection.  Thin, slightly charred crust, sweet, tangy red sauce, stringy fresh cheese.  The half pepperoni was top notch, not greasy but spicy with a crisp! It is pizza love!
Fish & Chips and Pimms Cup was awesome as was waitress.  Manager was an not nice and had waitress apologizing for him behind his back.  Not good.
this isn't your overpriced hipster pizza. this is real italian pizza done the best way. the pizza is absolutely delicious, seriously get yourself a pie!

Excellent quality of food - rivaling the great steakhouses out there, unfortunately, the price tag is on par with those steakhouses as well.  Service was excellent, and the food was fantastic.  The ambiance of the place does not match the high prices.  This is a business dinner or special occasion type of place, and the open dining area was not very cozy, and was a bit noisy.  With a bit of improvement in this area, they would have earned a 5th star from me.
Great food :)

I have nothing but love for PYT. Great food and drinks. Great Music. Great People. Great prices.  It's sort of like Cheers, where everyone knows your name. The staff is super-friendly, super-cool, and super-stylish. In the summer, it's the spot to BE because of the outdoor seating and the great location at the Piazza. The burgers of the week are PHENOMENAL, and it just has a great vibe. The grilled cheese is kind of amazing.  It's just the place to go for a drink, have a bite, and chill with friends. Who doesn't want to do that!

A couple weeks ago I came out to the area for a business trip and stayed at a hotel near the airport. My coworker and myself needed to grab dinner nearby and I took to Yelp to find a restaurant. I did several searches and this place always seemed to pop up with plenty of stars. So we went around 6:30pm on a Thursday night. I have to say parking seemed inconvenient. The restaurant is located in the middle of a neighborhood, so you have street parking where you can find it. Luckily, the parking fairy was on our side and someone was leaving right when we pulled up. We went to the restaurant side rather than the bar. I noticed the bar was packed, but we weren't in the mood to deal with a loud, cramped bar after flying all day. The restaurant was very nice. Nicely decorated and rather quiet. A lot of open space,  which I like. I don't like being elbow to elbow with people. I noticed a lot of reviews saying that service was terrible, but ours was spot on. However, that could also be because it was the middle of the week. We never had to wait for anything, the timing was perfect. We started with the bread and salad that are complimentary. I enjoyed the salad, it was very light with just enough flavor. My coworker wasn't a fan and wished there was more dressing. We ordered appetizers: crab stuffed mushrooms and empanadas. They were really lacking. The empanadas didn't look like any empanadas I've ever had before, and they were EXTREMELY dry. They did have a good flavor, but the dryness was not appealing and i couldn't finish eating them. The mushroom were absolutely terrible. I don't know what I was expecting, but obviously it wasn't that. The crab mixture was very wet, and VERY fishy. I get it, it's from the ocean...but I have never had crab that fishy before. All I tasted was that fish flavor, like it was a bite full of sea-water every time. Definitely not a fan. For our entrees, we ordered hot rock courses. I got filet mignon and shrimp, she got filet mignon and tuna. OH. MY. GOD!!!! I'm not religious, but this food made me question if God exists. WOW! One of the best meals I've ever had in my life. The meat was so thick and perfect. Cooking it on the stone with the garlic butter. Every bite melted in my mouth. It was sensational. The entree came with a side of rice and chips. I was so full after all the meat that I couldn't really eat the rice and chips, but I at least wanted to taste them. I loved the flavor of the rice. Very tasty. But I wasn't a fan of the chips. They were cold and just felt like they had been sitting out a little too long. But who cares!??!!?! Filet Mignon on a hot rock!! Finished everything off with a strawberry cheesecake that was very good. Perfect way to end the night. Needless to say, I slept very well that night. If I'm ever back in town, you better believe I will be back there ordering more hot rock entrees. I'll be sure to steer clear of the appetizers next time.
Smallest tacos in the world.  Go somewhere else.

I LOVED this place. The banana lassi alone would have been enough to keep me coming back here. But the food is outstanding. And cheap! The Chili shrimp and the avocado/potato salad were my two favorites of what we tried. The veggie dumplings were also delicious--tender inside but a bit bland and in need of soy sauce. And we got a noodle dish that was good too. And of course the paratha was a necessary order. But back to the shrimp and the salad!!! I wish I knew all the flavors that go into both of those dishes. Cilantro? Lime? What else???? They were both really tangy and the shrimp was just the right level of spicy. It's making my mouth water just thinking about them again. I would never think to pair avocado and potato chunks like in that salad but it makes so much sense!! Two caveats about the place: 1) The buttery/salty tea. My sister ordered it to give it a try but I don't think either of us would order it again. It's like savory chai with butter melted into it. It tasted more like broth than tea. I'm not saying this is a problem with their version of the tea. I'm saying I wouldn't order that particular thing again as a beverage to accompany a salty meal. I would stick with the banana lassi. 2) The place is TEENY. There are like 5 tables and that's it, and there's not a lot of place to wait around inside there. Just a heads up if you're trying to go on a busy night.

Great coffee, amazing food, and a very comfortable environment.  A small French bakery in the middle of West Hartford.  The croissants are extraordinary.  I love the sound of the accent in the back.  No matching tables, soft music in the background, it's wonderful. Note: Free wireless and thank you for having a super-clean bathroom. One of my new favorite places.  Nothing like it.  It is something to write home about...

My husband and I have been meaning to go to The Good Fork for years. A few weeks ago we finally made the trip. It was fantastic! I've been to many of the most critically acclaimed restaurants in NYC for work functions or special occasions and I was so pleasantly surprised to discover that The Good Fork outshone them. The Pekin Duck Breast is a must! Also, don't miss the tempura onion rings: a small twist on a classic. So delicious! My shared an appetizer, had an entree and a drink each and then shared dessert. With tip included the dinner cost just about $100. Not bad for the best meal/evening we've had in NYC! Also, the space is small and cozy. Would be a great venue for an engagement party or other intimate occasion.

I love French Food, yet La Sirene turned out to be too washed up in butter, too fusion like, too modest in appearance, and too expensive to really hit the "it" factor for French food.  With almost stale bread to start and slow service, I felt myself to a bit unwelcome in the restaurant.   The Seared Filet Mignon Topped With Foie Gras, Shallots, Port and Red Wine Truffles Sauce was delicious but unable to rightfully justify its price.  Though good quality filet with the rich red wine taste complementing but not overpowering the truffle, the dish was simply too rich to enjoy past a few bites.  It was not French Food, having recently returned from Paris, but Americanized to the greatest extent.  The dessert of Iles Flottantes, Crème Anglaise et Caramel aux Amandes tasted like sweet tofu, and we reluctantly argued about who would finish it because no one liked it but wasting food is a no-no when it comes to small portions and expensive prices. After all the reviews of La Sirene, I expected great things.  After my return from Paris in which many a random cafe was better than La Sirene, I was sorely disappointed by New York standards.

My wife and I came here for lunch on a weekday. It's a small place in Nolita but we were seated quickly. I had the spaghetti and meatballs and it was fantastic - but what would you expect in this part of the city? Service was quick and attentive, food was outstanding. The tiramisu we had for dessert was also good.
The food is great. Sandwiches are delicious. They now serve beer and wine. The restrooms are always very clean. The waitresses are always very friendly and Smiley.

I had a horrible experience here. The guy taking my order said he didn't know how to make a Reuben which is on the menu. He then wandered away and left me standing there on my cane.  He came back and told us again he couldn't make the Reuben   Meanwhile another guy came over. I got tied up with this utter nonsense. I will Never come here again. My whole family was with me to witness this debacle. Poorest service I have ever seen. And no apologies either.
Awesome syrian food. Front end is carry out, but the back room is like you are in a desert tent.   Authentic down to the way the sauces are serviced in raised silver cups. Chicken ouzi  was great.

Lunch with friends on June 12. Two of us ordered one of the specials, Scallops, on rabe with Quinoa pilaf. I had to ask the price of the dish which was twenty dollars. Thought we were going to lose it when the meal was presented with TWO that's TWO SCALLOPS!!! Ten dollars per scallop??? And they were not extra large scallops just average size with the greens just surrounding them. The presentation was laughable. The pilaf, while very good was only the amount from half of a large serving spoon. Stick to a sandwich as our other friend did. Also the chef is heavy handed with salt. $35 for the two scallop plate, one glass of wine and coffee! Make sure you eat plenty of bread.

I was introduced to Ethiopian food about 15 years ago and I had it both here and in Ethiopia. Now, I am NOT saying that I am A expert on Ethiopian food, but I believe I've had my fair share of both home cooked and restaurant prepared dishes. So that being said I know what I like. Now, after several visits to Walia I can say that the food is consistently good and the service is always great. If you want to try something new and never had it give Walia a shot. Yes, I know this is the moment you been waiting for, I give Walia five and a half bow ties out of 7.
Food good. Service poor. Overpriced and noisy. Won't be returning. But in fairness I want to say they were very accommodating to my elderly parents who have mobility problems.

One word describes my overall Frankford Hall experience: meh. Likes: the ample seating, the lighting, the games at the tables. Dislikes: paying $8 for one sausage (and having to pay extra for a bun), the onions in the cheese dip that comes with the pretzels, the paper plates everything is served on, not knowing what idiot is going to plop down at your table and make himself at home, the lame bouncers at the door, the valet parking. Try this place once, if you want. And then stick to the other local bars and restaurants. The "experience" just didn't live up to what this place is clearly shooting for.

I was excited to try this place based on all the rave reviews. While it was a solid meal, it not live up to all the 5 star reviews I browsed through.   We had to wait about 10 minutes with a 1pm reservation, but that was nothing compared to what other reviewers were forced to endure. Service was decent, and our food came out quickly. All positives there.  It's definately a see and be seen sort of place. The food was good, (we had the classic eggs benedict and the benedict johnny), just not great. I'd probably give them another shot if I was in the area, but will not be going out of my way to go back.
Great authentic Mexican flavors, highly recommend the carne asada tacos. Hidden little gem in the East Village.

They have now increased their prices to $7. I think that now that they have a restaurant, they think they're all high and mighty and can charge higher prices! Additionally, it seems that food quality has gone down. The meat has become tasteless and the portions seem a bit smaller. The last time I got served, by the time I found a seat, my food was already cold. You would think it would be fresh since there is a huge line.

This review is for the gyro platter. That was some good grub.  It comes with fries, greek salad and of course the gyro.  What else can I say? it certainly met my expectations.  So next time I'm in the hood I'll try the pizza, sucks to be 3000 miles away.

The crispy, cracker thin pizza crust is fantastic and everything is really fresh and very high quality. Deliciousness in every moment. But the gnocchi, oh the gnocchi...I couldn't hear it was so amazing. All senses disappeared far into the background as my taste buds sang their love and joy. Fantastic!

Cute place. A little on the authentic side and then also catering to the masses with their menu. I'd say it sounded all unique but ultimately it was fried rice etc. Portions were smaller than I wish BUT I ended up being full anyways. Fried rice dishes and noodles were about $15 so definitely more on the pricier side. I had the curry fried rice and it was quite spicy. The pork belly buns were really tasty and tender. They have a nice backyard seating that's heated for the fall. Great service. I'd just say expensive for the type of food ie drunken noodles

Been here a couple of times, twice for Brunch and once for dinner.  Love the warm rustic atmosphere, wooden furniture, and, forest cabin feel.  The wait staff are friendly and attentive (sometimes a little busy).  Definitely go for brunch, the food's delicious.  Most recently, I was there with a group of four and we all polished our plates clean.   The only drawback is the wait which could be around 45minutes depending on when you go.   But I plan to go again - haven't had a disappointing dish there yet.

I like the food here a lot.  They manage to be both inventive and classic at the same time.  If you're afraid of the exotic rolls, they have a "regular" sushi menu that you can order from with the standard spicy (insert fish) rolls and (insert vegetable) rolls.  I've had most of the items on the menu and have enjoyed almost all of them, save for the disgusting dessert rolls.  Those things are just plain wrong. What I especially enjoy about Miya's are the house-made sakes.  My favorite, of course, is the Chili sake.  It starts out sweet and light and turns into an inferno as its moving down your esophagus. I'm also a big fan of the fried ice cream.  The dough is chewy on the inside and crispy on the outside without being too oily.  I haven't seen it in a while on their menu though, I think it got replaced by the disgusting dessert sushi :( Overall I'd say that if you aren't too adventurous when it comes to food, Miya's is not the place for you.  There are a lot of great hits but also some horrific misses (which thankfully are few and far between, but they do exist).  If I could I'd go here exclusively for the flavored sake.
Great chicken wings: Persian spiced wings! Casual atmosphere in a great Brooklyn neighborhood.

Wandering through the area and came upon Carroll Place looking for somewhere to stop for a tasty beverage and a snack. Sat at the bar and the very nice bartender offered us some great suggestions and we decided to even stay for dinner. Shared the rosemary wings and the house made pappardelle. Everyone supposedly raves about the wings- and they were alright, but I'm from Buffalo so that's hard to compete with. The pappardelle was definitely fantastic. I wanted to lick the plate. Really liked the ambiance of this place and will come back!

Shocked by the low reviews! I'd say its a 3.5 star. 1) They have happy hour on a Saturday- you know that's worth a star. Sure its a buck off but still I appreciate the effort. 2) They have a burrito bar. The bar has warm tortillas, black beans & toppings (sour cream, cheese, pico de gallo, etc). If I was vegetarian I wouldn't have to pay for more than drinks with this bar available. 3) Ambiance---sure the place is not much bigger than  a closet but in DC that's standard so I wasn't bothered by that. Its dimly light with deep chocolate brown furnishings. If I was there with a beau I'd feel compelled to give him a smooch in this setting! 4) Food prices were decent- Steak quesadilla- $11- not bad in this economy 5) Food & drinks were decent.  I got a margarita and a few shots- all were good. Food---hey its quesadilla, chips and salsa--you really cant screw that up. Sure its not authentic Mexican BUT the food is still tasty. I had a good time here. Decent food, prices and service. No 2 stars from this gal!

Awesome restaurant! I make sure to swing by here for dinner any time I'm in the city. Food is always fresh and amazing. There's really nothing bad on the menu. Their meatballs are especially good. The dining area is always packed and full of excitement, and you can strike up a conversation with those next to you and make a new friend while you eat. The wait staff is the fastest I've experienced, no kidding. There's always someone bringing or taking something away from your table. Last note: The panna cotta for dessert is splendiferous, don't miss it!
I really did not feel the food was that good.  And, the prices were high considering the small portions and diner ambiance.

Tria - i dig for many  3 reasons: good beer selection, good wine selection, and great cheese.  What more can you ask for?  I definitely prefer the spruce st location over rittenhouse.  The spruce st location is larger and just more "chill". I feel like the one in rittenhouse is so small that we're on top of each other. Beware of the egg toast.  When I ordered it I had no idea it came out a raw egg on top of fluffy toast. Needless to say that wasn't the best experience twds the end of a long night of drinking.  BUT! My next visit to the other Tria on Spruce overshadowed that traumatizing night. I strongly recommend trying the truffled mushroom and fontina is waaaay better.
Nice atmosphere, friendly staff. Split pea soup: flavorful Spring Rolls: bland Red Curry Vegetables: delicious Pad Thai Vegetarian: excellent BYOB

Well worth the trek to tiny Pell St, the wait, and the crowd. I would like to believe the soup dumplings are reasonably authentic by the crowd mix and by the fact that my friends from Shanghai give the soup dumplings their stamp of legitimacy. The soup dumplings are such a mess to eat if you've never had them before-I thought the cartoon instruction (at the bottom of this page: joeshanghairestaurants.c…) was a joke, but, in retrospect, I would pay more attention before attempting to bite into these. So juicy and so filling. Even with side dishes, I was completely full and each of us paid less than $10.

We're almost ready to never make brunch at home again after finding Rose Water.  They have a lot of vegetarian options and change their menu periodically.  Not only is the good delicious but the decor has a way of making you feel relaxed.  Try the cucumber mint juice and the rose water lemonade.

Who wouldn't want to pay $4.50 for a meal that most restaurants would charge $15.  The truck not only has chicken, ribs, steak, or burger crepes (with your choice of veggie and sauce), but it has sweet crepes with your choice of pineapple, strawberries, blueberries, etc.  Why spend your lunch money at the over-priced student-center when you get can get delicious food at this gem of a place. Cheap and tasty.  Once you have a bite of these crepes, you'll be back, everyday!!

man I be eatin at pies n thighs whenever i be in williamsburg and it be some good azz food yo it makes u wanna drop down and get yo eagle on, an really lets ya nuts hang u know. But i be tryin to pay wit a hunnid dolla bill cuz dats all a homie like me be carryin around u know racks on racks bands a make her dance. and da waitress tell me "we dont take hunnids" I be like man what it is this shyt so i put that motha fucka on ma debit card

Me and my husband went to this place desperately looking for food at 1030pm and we were pleasantly surprised by the pizza and penne all vodka. They made it fresh and perfectly. Such great hospitality on the owners part with making our food fresh and the sauce was perfect. I would go back to this place on a normal visit not hunting for food late night. Excellent service! Excellent food!

For a seasoned South Indian family like mine, the first experience itself was very disappointing.  None of the dishes had enough spice or flavour and was far from the authentic South Indian cuisine.  Surprisingly there was no plain curd . We had to request for replenishment of some of the items.  The Masala dosa had hardly any masala in it.  The Desserts were not upto the mark.  The service was okay.  The price was  high (Gratuity was also added automatically to our bill )  for the less than ordinary ambiance and poor taste.   All of us felt nauseous  for a long time  after the meal.

The pizza itself is great...but the service? Not so much. Even getting there at opening and getting a table right away, it took about 45 minutes to get our order in. I wasn't expecting it to be speedy, but 45 minutes for an order? It's worth waiting for, but just pack a granola bar or something if you're hungry. You're going to be waiting a while, especially if you're starting by waiting outside. Also, it's cash only. Bring a couple twenties and some smaller bills.

Another typical chinese takeout place catered for "americans". Its always busy here but only with caucasian customers so this means nothing is authentic here just your brown sauce on every dish drowned with grease, MSG and oil, the chicken here tastes like rubber, beef? dont even try is it even beef? noodles have a bleach flavor this can't be good for you. Sushi? I dare you. Service? be prepared too wait long, price? Its higher than other chinese takeouts. This place used to be good when the original owners and cooks were running it. Hamilton has NO good authentic chinese food period! Go north NJ.
You want corn? This is the perfect place for you! The food is ok, not my favorite but the corn is the best thing on the menu!

I go to Airlies a few times a week for breakfast and/or lunch...this place is well run and the menu is so extensive! If you go for breakfast I would recommend the everything bagel! So yummy and fresh! For lunch I would recommend the steaming Asian cow, almost cord on blue(sp?), chicken salad, hugo boss...really just anything...I haven't had a bad sandwich there! The owners and workers are super friendly..check it out you won't be disappointed!!!!!

This has quickly become one of my go-to places in the neighborhood. I haven't come across anything bad on the menu (and I've had about everything at this point), but, more than anything, I can recommend the Howling and Brothers Grimm. Considering that the bread is made fresh with each order and the variety and quality of ingredients that go into each wrap, the sandwiches seem like a steal for around $9. Good for anything from a quick lunch to a late night snack (they are open until at least 4:00 AM on weekends).

I'm completely biased towards Hill Country, but really like this place.  The ribs were mostly a dry rub and had good flavor.  For my own personal tastes, I would have like them a bit more tender and caramelized.  I love that they have vinegar cole slaw and it was refreshing.  The fatty brisket is very moist and flavorful.  I also really enjoyed the pulled pork, but got the sandwich and it was literally impossible to eat.  The bun fell apart and I ain't eatin barbeque with a fork and knife.  The burnt baked beans were also tasty and included some pulled pork. The seating is first come, first serve, which can be frustrating.  My other peeve with the place is that the smokers are in the restaurant it seems cause my clothes smelled terrible after.

One of my all-time favorites in Philly. Although a little pricey for my taste, everything I've had on the menu has been delicious. The fried rice is definitely the best bang for your buck (especially at happy hour prices). And the Graffiti Bar out back is very chill and open most of the year. The Scorpion bowls are fun, but even more fun if you get in good with the bartenders. Otherwise, definitely check out their cocktails, which change up every now and then and are usually pretty unique!

This review is a bit overdue, but I absolutely loved Trattoria L'Incontro.  They have so many specials and so many delicious dishes it was hard to choose!  I went for my birthday and it was very special.  The short ribs were phenomenal!  The service was impeccable and I can't wait to go back.

I went for brunch with my brother.  The food was decent but we felt that both of our meals could easily be made in our own kitchen.  Basically, there was nothing "special" about the flavor/taste of the food that would make us want to come back.  There are better brunch places in the Ft. Greene area in my opinion.

I'll keep this to the point. Everything was delicious. We got every type of crab on the menu, the crawfish, cajun fries and papaya mango salad. Everything was amazing and we each left dinner planning our next visit. This place is all about shellfish and they do it right. Fantastic.

Great! Someone said they posted a review and now it's gone--there are two separate "Danny's" on Yelp so it is probably posted in the other listing. They are both the same place! One says Marazzos and the other says Parkway Ave Anyway, I don't normally like pizza but I ordered with my boyfriend and loved it! Thin pie and just the right amount of sauce. Good quality ingredients on my boyfriend's all-white pie. I hope they continue to get more business. We will be ordering more frequently to check out their weekly specials :)

Service Only: We called to place our order on a Tuesday at 5:33 and were told that our two orders of drunken noodles would be delivered in 30 minutes. They arrived at 7:02. When we called throughout our wait, we were simply told that the food had already left. We called back the first time and they said they would call their driver and then let us know. Another 15 minutes passed with no word, so we tried calling back. They must use their caller ID, because they didn't pick up until we called back using a second cell phone. We tried to cancel the order, but we were told that they would have to check with the driver just in case it had already been delivered. I had already started making something to eat to feed my two children (who were starving by this point) when the driver pulls up. He claims that there was no way that the food would have been delivered in 30 minutes; for some reason, he had come from Milford (?????!!!) to pick up my order from the restaurant and then deliver it to us. Anyway, I wish I had a better experience with the delivery, since the reviews for the food are awesome. Maybe I'll try it again when I'm downtown and can easily pick it up.

Low-key Dominican cafe serving very authentic food selections (sister restaurant to the Papasito).  Great outdoor sidewalk seating (but only in warm weather months). Recommend the Roasted pork or Cuban sandwiches for a quick lunch.  Mofongo, pig feet, and tripe soup are included on the main entree menu.  Mashed green plantains, cassava sticks, and croquettes stand-out as appetizer selections. Leave room for homemade bread pudding, three milk cake, or guava with cheese for dessert. Take-out available (best option for the winter months -- severely limited indoor seating).

I don't get the hype around this place. I've heard so many friends talk about how great this place is and it's only subpar at best. Food was kinda gross and cold and the dumplings weren't really that good. While their prices were great, the food was not. I won't ever return. Would rate zero stars if I could! Edit: not only that but it also made me incredibly sick! I threw up all night and felt rather horrible. Definitely never grabbing food here again.

There were a few things that stood out. I loved the lemonade that I got - I believe it had mint and a hint of cucumber in there. Very refreshing and highly recommend. I would totally come back just to have that alone. My friends and I also shared the biscuits and gravy, which was amazing. The sauce is very similar to the chicken and waffles so I would probably recommend that as the meal. Some parts of the restaurant needed work. For example, when my friends and I arrived, there was no hostess for us to put our names on the list so we were waiting there idly for a while. I think the frustrating part was that there was a huge area of the restaurant that was open, but it wasn't cleaned. It looked like a huge party had just left, but the plates and everything didn't get cleared off for a while (even after we were seated). My dish wasn't really that great either. I got a basic meal with eggs, toast, and bacon. It was satisfactory, but there wasn't a lot of food and the bacon was burnt, which I didn't really like. Overall, I would definitely come again to give it another try and I think it's worth the visit if you order the right food.

Having moved in the past week, I was looking for a place to fulfill my usual 2pm breakfast needs in my new neighborhood.  Based on the Yelp! reviews, I headed over here and was not disappointed.  Fried-to-order ham, egg and cheese on an English muffin, and a 16oz. coffee for $4.50?!  Yeah, Henry St. has a new regular.  I'll likely be heading back for my 6pm lunch.

4 stars for more than 700 reviews? Really? I had the Minca Sio. t's just a normal bowl of ramen. There's something lacking in the soup flavour.. the umami taste maybe?? haha. The gyoza here are good but then again, most gyoza I've had at ramen places are pretty decent. I have had better bowl of ramen at the ramen place 1 block away from my home. Ippudo and toto - I don't even know why they are mentioned here as comparison.

This has to be one of my favorite restaurants... ever =) When I used to live here, it was my family's go-to place for special occasions. Now that I'm back, it was already my birthday-dinner choice, and it was just as great as it's been. Their buckwheat savory crepe choices are mouth-wateringly well-seasoned, both if you go from their 'suggested' list, or if you make your own. Their sweet crepes are made with a lighter wheat, and, well, you can't really go wrong with any of the combination options. The wait staff are always helpful and friendly, they have great specials, and while their by-the-glass wine list isn't very extensive, it does not disappoint. They even figured out how to put a candle 'in' my dessert crepe for the obligatorily embarrassing singing of "happy birthday"

There's nothing in the whole wide world like a southern girl... or southern food. Not much can speak to your soul like a preacher man or fried chicken. Especially if it's a Sausage Gravy Smothered Fried Chicken. Being from the great state of Texas, I've had lots of gravy but none on the level of what I devoured at Jacob's Pickles. Little morsels of ground sausage infused in delicious gravy still gives me the good feelings. The slogan here is Beer, Biscuits, and Pickles. I had doubts, but another amazeballs item is their biscuits. I've long held the belief that biscuits are on the lower end spectrum of the bread list, but no longer! They're so fluffy, won't stick to the roof of your mouth, and can be slathered with house strawberry and orange preserves, honey, and maple butter. Jacob offers many different pickled vegetables, so I am certain you can find one to suit your taste. There is always a wait, but you can put your name down and they will text you when your table is ready.

My other burlington home. I have eaten lunch here a few times over the year on visits to Burlington and Warren area to ski. After taking in the Church street scene for a bit it is always great to grab a bite at Leunigs. Last time by I had a duck confit dish that was delicious. Two thumbs up!

I had been wanting to come here for ages and managed to get a reservation when my family was in town - and we were not disappointed! Given it's a fine dining place, I was expecting it to be quite a formal, stuffy environment, but I couldn't have been more wrong. There is a great lively atmosphere to the place. We had the three course menu and every course was delicious. The service was really good - our server was knowledgeable on the menu, able to guide us through it and suggest wine pairings. My favourite place I've eaten in NYC!

I think it was the combination of ambiance and great food that made my visit to Supper so good.  The reviews i read were mostly good but i was scared that we would have to wait a while to be seated.  fortunately, it was somewhat of a late night dinner on a weeknight.  my date and i did not want to sit in the communal sitting area so we decided to wait for our own table.  we did go next door and had a glass of wine.  we waited probably 15 mins but it was fine and our table was fine too.  the place was much larger then it led on when i first entered.   i thought the bread was just ok.  a little dry but i did think that the garlic white bean side was a good pair.  gave it a nice little kick.  we had the polenta with wild mushrooms for an appetizer and it was sooo delicious.  the flavor of the mushrooms paired with the polenta was awesome.  then we had the Shaved Mushrooms, Celery & Pecorino Toscano Salad which i also loved.  i thought the pecorino cheese was tasty with the celery and mushrooms.  really refreshing and light and a good pair with the rest of our meal.  my entree was the priest stranglers.  id heard of this pasta but never had it.  i really did like it but couldnt finish my plate because i had already had so much other food.  my date had the fedelini.  and he seemed to enjoy it because he finished the whole thing.   although we were stuffed, we did have dessert.  i had a cappuccino and we shared a tiramisu. it was so light and delicious.  it was a perfect ending to our meal.  i love taking a long time to eat- as long as the company is good.  and it my case it was.   great dinner date place.  and really nice on chilly night when you feel like you need something hearty to eat.

This place is a true delight!  The last two Sundays I've been running errands in the LES or Chinatown and wanted a quick and cheap breakfast sandwich.  I took a stab at searching for "sandwich shop" on yelp and I saw this place.  I can't believe I was so lucky to find it.  I have now been twice and just got a simple egg and cheese on a biscuit.  It was only $4.95 and it was amazing.  They put a lot of egg on there and the cheese is melty.  The biscuit it excellent as well and I really could not have asked for a better breakfast sandwich.  I agree that it's small and not the most comfortable seating, but if you are getting something to go or wanting to stop in for a quick meal then it's perfect.  It's not a place to come to brunch with a group of friends. On my way out today they stopped me to give me a fresh and delicious beignet that they had just taken out.  Both the beignet and this place are true treats!

Overall, a good cappuccino.  Strong coffee flavor, with a smoky aftertaste.  I normally prefer a more creamy consistency, with a sour tinge at the end, but I didn't much mind the taste of Toast's cappuccino.  Verging on $4 territory, it's a pricey drink.  Although I didn't sample, the fold menu looked intriguing.  Also, went on a cold day and the seating area was the opposite of toasty.  Worth the visit though.

I went to Room Service few months ago . we found this place accidently looking for another restaurant in this aria and let me tell you .... I loved it !!! the food was so delicious and beautifully decorated ! I can't wait to go there for more! I'm getting hungry even now just by thinking about it !!I do have little complain about the service but I can get over it since everything else was so perfect :) hopefully next time we get better server who wants to pay little more attention

I tried this place on 7/5/14,,, ordered a slice of sicilian pizza,, Oh man this is how sicilian should be,, thick, airy crust,,, perfect amount of sauce and a lot of cheese...  Lets just say,, I am a fan of this pizza joint... Its a small place, offering a couple of tables and a small bar to eat, like 5 stools...On 7/6/14, i ordered 2 whole pies, a pep and a cheese pizza.. Lets just say it didnt fit in the boxes lol..  It looked great,, had the nice crisp to the dough,, It wasnt the best i ever had but it was very good...  I would come back here for the sicilian for sure,and if i am ever  in the area again I would try other stuff,,, like a sausage roll,, or a calzone or a hoagie...  If someone were to ask where to get a good slice,, I would recommend this joint for sure... Try it, it definitely is a NY thin sliced pizza..

In the warmer months this place is gorgeous. It is like walking into a peaceful secret garden just steps away from the noise of the street. I really enjoyed the decor with hanging lamps, flowers, plants, and garden decorations. The food i've tried has been so so. I enjoyed my platter of hummus, babaganoush, and stuffed grape leaves... However, the tabbouleh was made with quinoa instead of bulgur wheat and not really seasoned at all. We also got a lamb and quinoa dish and though the lamb was good the quinoa had no spices whatsoever, just plain quinoa so it was really bland. On the contrary, I've been there other times for just hookah and tea and both the hookah and tea were great. The service was also very good. This place is good for hanging out with a group of friends. I'd definitely come back here for some hookah and ambiance but probably not for the food.

Came here for lunch, minimal to no wait since we arrived when it opened. Tiny space, but the food speaks for itself. Ramen was really good, I couldn't finish a bowl of ramen for the first time, I ordered the big bowl, but never thought it would be so filling that I couldn't finish it. Meat was well portioned, the broth was tasty, this was a bowl of good times. It's definitely a place to go for ramen, it's a bit of a trek since I rarely venture to the upper east side, but on the rare occasions I do, I'll be sure to come back again.

If you are looking for some great tasting pizza with a spectacular view of the city skyline, go to Grimaldi's down by the Brooklyn Bridge. The wait can range anywhere from 10 minutes to more than an hour long, but if you happened to be in Brooklyn, it's not a bad stop to make. Patience is a virtue and it is worth the wait to see that steaming hot pie come right in front of you. I suggest getting a large pie, which is eight slices in total, and any topping that suits your fancy. The tomato base is slightly sweet and the cheese isn't very heavy on this thin crust pizza, so request for extra cheese if you're a cheese lover. If you are a fan of personal space, this is not the place for you! The tables are set up like a family-style sit down, so you'll be sitting very close to your neighbors. So close...you can reach over and grab a slice of their pie if they aren't looking! For those who are unable to make it to the Brooklyn location, Grimaldi's does have two new locations in NYC. The first location is right off the Long Island Expressway near the Douglaston area. The second location is right in Manhattan around west 20th st and 6th avenue, where Limelight use to be located. Both are fairly new and not quite well known as of yet, so check out those locales for some fine pizza!

Probably the best Korean in CT. My family and I have been coming here often since it opened. My mom is 100% This is real Korean BBQ- grills in the center of the table, vent on top, and mountains of banchan, mountains. I think 12 side dishes come out when you order. I don't love the frozen pork belly. In a place with that decor and for that price, you expect fresh. However, the menu is great. We love the clay pot soups and they even have street food classics like dukbokki! Great for big groups in fact, I recommend you bring at least four people to split BBQ with- makes it economical- there is a ton of food!

Stopped by here mid-barcrawl for a snack.  Wow.   Completely filthy, but damn good.  Amazing pile of sauces, too. Perhaps this is sacreligious, but, Vol de Nuit's fries taste better.  They do.  Sorry.

I went here for brunch the other day on a friend's recommendation.  I was disappointed.  I got the bacon eggs Benedict; eggs Benedict is my go to brunch dish so I get it a lot.  This one I couldn't finish.  The hollandaise sauce left an unpleasant aftertaste & the bacon was inedible; it was so thick and burnt.  The english muffin was also very burnt, impossible to cut.   I did get biscuits though which were delicious!  I should say that, my friend got the pumpking pancakes which he enjoyed, I didn't try any though. I would not recommend this for brunch place.

Had some friends in from out-of-town this weekend (first Philly visit) and of course the cheesesteak was one of the main attractions.  I have taken loads of people to the historic King of Steaks, and they always love it - and so do I.  I have enjoyed this local icon countless times, in countless varieties.  Yesterday I had a mushroom steak, whiz wit - tasted as good as ever. The argument is old as time.  Some will say Pat's, some will say Geno's, Tony Luke's, Rick's, Jim's, or any of the lesser know neighborhood spots throughout the city.  In reality, you'll get a good cheesesteak at any of these fine establishments.  But in the end, if you're in it for the experience it's got to be Pat's or Geno's.  I make this statement with the tourist in mind.  My local friends and I rarely visit these landmarks unless it's to indulge an out-of-town guest.  But I must say, explaining how to order, and the mystique that surrounds someone's first trip to the birthplace of the steak sandwich gives me a nostalgic feel.   Although I've enjoyed more Pat's steaks than I can count, I get a special feeling when I approach the front of the line to order one of the greatest, most famed culinary creations in the world.

Cheap yet surprisingly good pasta Usually I'm not a pasta person-- my general feeling is that if any idiot can cook it, it's probably not worth paying a premium for. But it's pretty cheap at Da Andrea ($10-12) and surprisingly really really good. At least  the pappardelle is (sweet sausage ragout w/ truffle oil), I confess it's the only thing I order. Add on a $6 glass of respectable house red and you're good to go. Downside is it can get pretty packed, but you can always fall back on Pepe Verde next door if you don't mind the waitstaff-free style dining.

This is a Thai-Viet fusion restaurant. Considering that it is located in Hell's Kitchen, where there are Thai restaurants on every street corner. OBAO rises above the rest. We came here based on a friend's recommendation. We're glad that we did! The vibe is full of life and energy. The design is modern with emphasis on Thai-Viet culture. The Buddha on the wall and lanterns are prominent. I started the night with a cocktail drink called "Thai ladyboy"--how befitting! I believe that it is a concoction of vodka, cranberry and jalapeño that mixes really well together. We ordered the Michelin recommended steps and it did not disappoint. Appetizer: Crispy pork belly; pork with caramel glaze served with pickled green papaya. Spare rib on sugarcane; with spicy honey mustard glaze, crushed peanuts, and hoisin peanut dipping sauce. Entrée: Beef Luclak; seared flank steak, tomatoes, lettuce, onion and bell pepper. Clay pot shrimp; comes with glass noodle, shiitake mushrooms, ginger, bell pepper and onion. The portions are perfect for couple to share and it comes with exquisite plated presentations. The waiter was pleasant and attentive. He had complete knowledge of the menu. He gave suggestions and answered all my questions. For its price value and customer service, I must admit that coming here is one of my best Thai dinners.

Wierd policies.  We were told they didn't take reservations - we were a large party - but they would take our name and time and have a table ready for us. Which is different from taking a reservation how?  When six out of eight of us arrived we were told we couldn't be seated till we were all there.  Now I can see if two of eight arrived, but six is still a decent number I think.  The hostess was really snotty about it too, with a snarky "that's the policy" and a sneer.  Too bad.  The food was really really good, the waitress was very nice, the coffee guy was a hottie.  But the start of the meal colored things a bit.

Went for dinner Saturday night at 6 p.m.  It was great!  We had the butternut squash flatbread with arugula and the grilled octopus for appetizer.  The octopus comes with a chickpea "cake" that was out of this world good!  They were both delicious!  For dinner I had the spaghetti squash with asparagus and tomatoes.  It was just like having pasta only better!  My husband had the rib steak with peppercorn sauce and french fries.  The steak was cooked just the way he wanted - medium well and he said it was fantastic!  For dessert we had the creme brulee and nutella eclair.  The desserts are small, but they are just the right size.  We didn't feel bloated; we felt just right - well fed!  The service was great too.  Our waitress was always there when we needed her!

From start to finish, every aspect of my meal was amazing. Hummus, fried cauliflower , eggplant bruschetta ....wow.  Their poached eggs was on a piece of rustic toast with scallions, pearl onions and a special orange sauce. The Service was pretty standard, they were there and attentive and that's what counts. Loved the atmosphere. Will be back.

I am not one to write reviews so either it has to be a phenomenal place or awful place. I wish I could give it more stars because the food options and brunch especially is wonderful. I love the outdoor seating especially now that it is warmer out. The thing that made me write this review is the first time I dined here was few weeks ago for brunch outside with 1 other person. We waited 15 minutes to be sat in order for them to get the tables cleaned, which takes 2 minutes. Regardless, I didnt let that annoy me too much, but it took them atleast 5 minutes to greet us and take a drink order. Now this may not seem long to the average person, but next time you sit down time it, 2 minutes seems long when you first are sat. I have worked in the restaurant industry for many years, there is no reason even if you are busy not to atleast take a drink order. It took them a while to get back to us for our food order. Luckily our food came out quickly. Once we received our food though we had no condiments on our table. We were never asked how our food was or if we needed anything. My second time there was last saturday to take my mom out. Once sat outside, it took a waitress yet again 5-10 minutes to greet us and take a drink order, which she said it is not her table but she took it anyways. Like we cared, we just wanted to be taken care of (no offense). This time took so long we were all ready to order everything luckily. When my mother received her french onion soup, it came out luke warm. Our server again didnt ask how everything was, so i had to get up to ask someone else to tell our server the soup was cold. Once it came out the second time she informed us that there was fresh cheese now on it that was forgotten the first time. lol. Once we received our meals, we were never asked how everything was. When finished, she said she'd bring us the check not once asking if we wanted anything else or dessert in which I had to ask for a dessert menu. Lastly, of course expected not one person at the host stand said thank you have a wonderful day thanks for coming. Nothing. This place disappoints me because I would go there much more often if the service was at all decent. The food options like I said and the food itself is great, location love it, but service in any place makes it exceptional--- a place to want to go back. I truly hope they clean up their act...
decent ramen place. get the ramen.

Delicious breakfast in a small diner-style cafe. The menu stars biscuits, muffins, frittatas, and other breakfast staples. Our frittata was really delicious and I liked the coffee served in metal mugs. Service was great.

I probably should have reviewed this place when this happened, I fully admit this happened over a year ago, but I am on a review writing binge and feel this shouldn't be left unsaid. Anyway, I Came here with a friend, we ordered the prix fixe and 2 glasses of wine. We were enjoying our salads and generally chatting it up when my friend suddenly went silent and dropped her fork and went grey and said " Whats that" Upon closer inspection it was 1/2 of a grasshopper ( the back legs still moving yo..) She had eaten the other 1/2! My friend looked at me said " oh god, I need a cigarette" I told her go outside,  I will handle it. I called the waitress over she apologized and said, does your friend want some more wine? I said, maybe I am not sure we're going to stay. She did refill the wine. My friend came back in and said she did not want to stay, which I can totally understand. I went to the back, and told them we were going to leave. They actually had the balls to try to charge me for the dinner, I told them we were being really cool about this considering she just ingested a bug, and werent making a scene. You know what her response was? " Well the salad is organic" Are you kidding me?! I paid for the wine and left, I should have just walked out, or paid and told everyone as I was leaving about the bug, but I was more concerned about dealing with my traumatized friend.
Love the grilled cheese with apple.  Gets a little crowded at Happy Hour and the lack of bathrooms can make this place super annoying
Best Cuban food I've ever eaten here in NJ and I'm half Cuban...Me and my family travel all the way from Old Bridge, NJ to have their Rabo Encendio , Ox Tail just great.
This place is the authentic and best pizza place! Even better then Lombardi's. Do drop by and try it and you will thank me for it.

I tend to judge different places based on different standards. While Ive given meals 4 stars that weren't necessarily as good as Alta, I was judging Alta pretty hard in comparison to other tapas places Ive frequented in the city. With that being said, I thought Alta was a fantastic place, with great food, great service, and perfect for large groups. However, I think it paled in comparison with other Tapas places Ive been to around the city. Many of the dishes were home runs while many left a lot to be desired. I'd go back to have a fun meal with a group of friends, but I'd personal never take a date there. A few of the winners: Crispy Brussels Sprouts fuji apples, crème fraiche, pistachio nuts Bacon Wrapped Dates & Olives stuffed with almonds Danish Pork Ribs roasted with kecap manis & coriander
Smoked coconut club! Enough said!
Really excellent Thai.  Pleasant dining experience.
Don't even remember when I started going here. All I know is I come back annually for my large iced tea water ice and pretzel rods when it gets warm out.

What happens when you combine great ingredients, gourmet cooking, convenience*, and super service? You get Quick Fixx, and I ALWAYS need my fixx. They had me at hello and this love affair may never end. Things to get: THE CHICKEN CUTLET. Some of the best I've ever had, and coming from a family where schnitzel is a staple, that says a lot (Google that if you don't know, if you do know, then you also know that if my grandmother saw this, she'd be pissed). What do you get the chicken cutlet with? The Greek Orzo Salad. You also add it to any custom pasta you create. Custom pasta. Yes. That's right! You can make your own dish, whether it's pasta or salad. AMAZING. I go for that pretty often, and find myself stuck on a combo of penne/rigatoni, chicken cutlet, creamy tomato sauce, broccoli, onions, mushrooms. SO SO GOOD. Big tip: you may want to split a pasta dish with the roomie, friend, or spouse... add a salad and you have the perfect meal. Don't heed my warning and you may feel a little stuffed. Either way, I've got my fixx - go get yours! *Convenience (as defined by Merriam-Webster's Dictionary): the ability to order delicious food via phone for pickup, in store, or online through the food service of your choosing (grubub, foodler, and many others).

I believe we Yelped up Lupa.  We had empty belly's and were in the middle of our lower Manhattan pub crawl. The place was PACKED.  People everywhere waiting to get in.  We almost didn't walk in. I owe it all to Silly Bands (ask your tween).  The gorgeous Maitre'D happened to be wearing three of them.  I asked her where she got them...blah, blah, blah. She ended up giving me one of them for my daughter and sat us right away at the family style tables. w00t!!!! We started with the Marinated Olives, Brussels Sprouts and Proscuitto.  The Brussels weren't as good as mine...they were okay. My husband had the Butternut Squash Tortellini which delicately melted in my mouth.  I had the Hangar Steak with Mushrooms.  I had to cram every last bit of it in. We washed it all down with the Barbaresco Pelissero 2004...nom, nom, nom.  Perfect pairing. Thank you Yelp.

Came here for brunch...i ordered steak and egg...and friend ordered a pizza...have to say...it was definitely on a saltier side....I previously came here for dinner....but I don't remembered being this salty...oh yeah...it's no longer BYOB... boo...

This is a small place, cute and quiet. I went there for their sushi lunch special which came with soup and 2 rolls. They would not let me substitute any rolls, even for an up charge. I had the spicy tuna roll and shrimp tempura. The rice was very loose (not packed well around the roll) and the taste was mediocre. Overall the presentation of the sushi was messy and I was not impressed. Probably wouldn't go there again and I live a block away.

this is a great, small, cozy place for some good venezuelan food.  the arepas and yuca frita are really good, and there is a good variety of traditional fruit juices also. this place seems to be family owned, so it has more of a "local" place feel to it.  its never been super crowded, which is nice also.  there aren't that many tables, but its good for 2-5 people to have a good meal, and its not really expensive either.

Let me start off by saying that I've been to PF Changs in general probably 8-9 times in the past. After last night's experience though, I think I'm done. This place is too trendy, pricey and overrall full of itself to get my money any longer. I went with family last night and it was, for the first time, empty. I can only hope people finally realized it is not as good as the hype and the trend is dying down. Having had good experience with their fish entrees, I ordered the Ginger Salmon. Considering it's name, I thought it would have a ginger flavor. Nope, it didn't. The waitress took it back and upon the manager's recommendations, they put in an order for the Grilled Salmon asparagus something. Now, why they couldn't just redo the Ginger Salmon I don't know. The manager brought the new one out (of course everyone at my table was already done eating), apologized and told me I will love this new dish and it is full of flavor. Umm, nope. This one was the exact same as the last one except they grilled the crap out of it. Ugh!!! What is going on with this place. Usually everything is salty, but at least that is some kind of a flavor. They took it off the bill which was nice (it was an 18.50 entree with no flavor) but come on. I don't recommend this place considering it's not authentic, everything is crazy overpriced, the staff is slow and drinks are ridiculously priced too...and apparently their cooking staff and management are idiots. My bf loves this place but after this, he can go there alone. Oh and I agree with another poster. Instead go to Sunny Garden which is a short walk away behind the Pep Boys. That is a great place for authentic Asian fare. Screw PF Wangs.

I went here reluctantly and I should have followed my gut. It was very crowded, loud and an hour and half wait to sit outside. We sat in a room that was so loud I couldn't hear anything. Our waiter was very nice but service was a little slow. I was on the fence about what to order and went with the crab cake dinner, BIG mistake. It must have been under a heat lamp because thee greens is came with were wilted. It also came with asparagus which was a total joke. It was so thin and overcooked and the crab cakes were frozen, there were no chunks of crab meat. I never send food back but I was not about to settle or pay  for a mediocre meal so I sent it back. I never send food back and don't like to be rude but honestly it looked so disgusting. I got a burger instead which came out quickly and was delicious BUT that night I got violently sick. My husband ordered the linguini with shrimp, it was a small portion, had no flavor and we had to ask twice for Parmesan cheese. Needless to say I would never go back to Sunset Pub & Grill or recommend it to my worst enemy.

Forno's is a Spanish restaurant on Ferry St, an area of Newark that has a lot of Portuguese restaurants. Having been to Spain, I can say that the food at Forno's is not up to Spanish standards, but the portions here are gigantic, so you do get your money's worth here.  Entrees can easily be split by two people. This is not somewhere you can go to for a quick lunch as service is very slow.  They serve both red & white sangria, but neither of which are good.

Awesome oysters, yes. Cute, warm, friendly waitress, check. Some cocktail special that was yummy with great big ice cubes. Gettin' pretty happy at this point. Truffle fries, over the top. Yellowtail hamachi with melon and cucumber, wowsa. Chocolate molten lava cake. I am coming back. You betcha.

When you tell someone you're going to scarpetta the response is inevitably "oh, they make their own pasta" and indeed the pasta course was the standout here along w/ excellent fish entrees. Had to wait ~20m w/ a reservation but once we were seated, service was attentive and helpful. Four stars and would definitely go again but still feeling like Convivio is the better new NYC italian if you're looking for someplace to indulge.

I recently moved to the neighborhood and I have a feeling I will soon become a regular here. The vegetarian sandwich is delicious and all of the vegetables were extremely fresh and crisp. I recommend adding sriracha or hot sauce to your sandwich for a bit more flavor and kick. The salad rolls are also top-notch! The staff is very friendly and accommodating and you can eat in or get your food to go. Quick, cheap, fresh, and tasty- what more could you ask for?

This week, while we were visiting friends in Ludlow, they suggested a restaurant in Springfield that they enjoy. I'm from Rhode Island and the prices at restaurants are pretty high. That's what I was prepared for. I ordered the escargot appetizer and the Black Rock rib eye with a lobster tail. The waitress was a doll and very helpful. The food was excellent and the prices unbelievably reasonable. The portions were so generous that I brought half of it home with me. I so wish that they would open another Black Rock closer to my home in RI. I highly recommend this restaurant. By the way, the house Cabernet was delicious.

SOOO GOOD!!!  Best pizza I've found in my neighborhood so far. The crust is perfectly cooked, the ingredients tasted so fresh. I love that they put fresh basil on after the pizza was cooked and not before like some other places do.   Staff was very attentive and friendly. I think this will be my go-to pizza spot in the Jerz.

Ok street meat weirds me out but this place is a staple in NYC. This place is so famous that people want to BE them. They actually have cart IMITATORS. Haven't you heard? Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery. I found this out because I was looking for this cart for my touristy friends to try while i was at work. In doing so I found several articles by legit NY publications warning patrons that if you want the original "cart guys" then look for the ones with the yellow jackets and yellow bags with red writing. Oh hello organized chaos! Their meat is very juicy and it's flavorful. It's a mix of lamb/chicken but I think you can get them seperately as well. It's unlike any street meat I've ever had (then again I've only had about 3). They give you an ample serving and their hot sauce is really pretty damn hot. Oh and it comes with a white sauce that is calorie-ladenly delicious. Considering the massive lines at 3 am, this place is worth bringing the after party.

Oh Sophie's, if only I could order a bucket of green sauce with a side of roast pork, I could die  happy! This place is great.  Real deal, no frills Cuban food served cafeteria style by a cheerful bunch.  I always get takeout, since I've found that if you take it to stay you leave smelling like roasting meat and garlic... not that there's anything wrong with that.  Have only tried the oxtail and pernil, both were super good and served with huge portions of black beans and yellow rice.  Decent prices, and you can easily get two meals out of a $9 order of pernil and sides.

I was all over Yelp during a mysterious flight delay in Cincinnati trying to find a decent place to eat near my Times Square hotel. I would be arriving a little bit after the lunch rush and didn't have any commitments until later that night, so I wanted to get all Anthony Bourdain and find somewhere really excellent and out-of-the-way to eat. Then hunger took over. That adventurous part of my brain that was willing to trek through hot, tourist-laden streets to find some rare cuisine was voted down by the rest of my body. Cold beer. Big sandwich. Primal urges took over. After the delay, the transportation to the hotel, hotel check-in, a maze of elevators and a thirty-second refresh, I was ready to eat my stick of deodorant for lunch. I didn't need to, thankfully. My co-worker and I stepped downstairs and across the street from our hotel to Junior's. Junior's is big. And orange.
