The menu looked mid-century home-cooking-ish, and the beverage selection included beer. We were sold. Despite hot afternoon temperatures, we were inclined to sit on the large front patio. Being cooped up in an airport and a commuter jet will do that to you. We were served complimentary pickled beets, coleslaw and pickles to start. Unusual, but kind of fun and funky. Pickled beets are a food I hate particularly, but I tried them anyway. Not as bad as I remembered from my childhood. The coleslaw was very vinegar-y, mouth-puckering almost. The pickles were pretty much... pickles. I ordered the egg salad sandwich on challah with fries on the side. The fries cost extra, and the egg salad sandwich with no side already cost north of $10. What? It's bread and egg and mayonnaise, some of the cheapest ingredients on the planet. The egg salad was creamy, though quite bland. The challah crumbled by the time I was finishing my sandwich. The fries were pretty good actually, crispy and hot. I washed it down with an excellent Brooklyn pale ale. My colleague ordered potato salad to accompany her reuben. I tried a bite - creamy, tasty. Nothing special though. Our server was good, the patio was pleasant despite the noise of Times Square and the heat. I can't justify giving Junior's any more than 2 stars though. Maybe the more expensive entrees are better. Maybe the bakery attached is really excellent. My experience though was squarely two stars - overpriced, bland food with day-old bread. To its credit, I had a relatively nice time sitting outside having my beer and fries. And I didn't have to eat my travel-size deodorant for lunch after all.
I'm hoping Abaleh will eventually open a place in the five towns. We could use an Abaleh here. Food is excellent. Restaurant is immaculate. Friendly staff. Love it!!

I think this is the first 5 star review I have given! Loved the food here - salad, wine, appy's, main course: baby lamb chops, the other person got duck breast.... For starters make sure you get the zucinni and moussaka (sp?) we were practically licking our plates. Main dishes prepared beautifully and full of fresh flavor. Salads are great - large portion. Lots of warm bread and a white bean spread that was awesome. Didn't have room for dessert, OMG we ate so much that I felt guilty! Make a reservation because it gets crowded ... Also, on the pricey side, but worth every penny! I can't wait to go back...

We picked this place based on the (overrated) review on Yelp. The food looks better than it taste; kinda bland. Portion is on the small side. Overall I'll give it a pass but unlikely to return given the abundant choices in Philly.

This is a very "hole in the wall" pizzeria, but the food is some of the best in the area. The garlic knots are awesome, although I do have to warn ya, they are potent. Definitely for garlic lovers. The eggplant parm slice is pretty solid as well. I don't think i've ever had anything from here that I wouldn't order again. Well, maybe the calamari, but what can you expect from a pizzeria. I come here for lunch all the time. The prices are fairly reasonable as well. YEA Carmen's!

I'll give it two stars because during lunch hour(s), this place is jumping, and the food is fresh and fast.  However, I work the nightshift, and when I leave my job either at 4 or 6 a.m., my brood is craving "the crave", and it's like this White Castle is a totally different animal during the early a.m. hours.  Real castle burgers can only be purchased at none other than White Castle.  There's nothing like them anywhere else really (not counting the frozen variety in supermarkets which I tend to avoid).  Which can only explain why, after years, yes years, of very poor early a.m. service, and very poor a.m. food quality, is why I would return during "normal" business hours.  Avoid this place at all cost during the early morning hours.  The crew really doesn't want to service the customer because they're too caught-up in either checking in a supply delivery, or, doing their electronic bookkeeping tasks on those small register units, etc.  I've gotten served some pretty old and dried up garbage during those hours than I'd care to mention.  The supervisor on duty will actually try to deter you by saying "well, I'll have to do a grill, it'll take a little longer", meaning they'll have to make fresh burgers (Hey, what a concept!!!??  Fresh food!!!! imagine that!!??), and you'll have to wait.  It got so bad at one time to the point, I got home (after using the drive through) and called them to report the questionable food, and thankfully, one of their daytime mgrs, a nice guy (obviously really interested in good customer service, and I don't think he's there anymore for that reason), gave us a whole brand new, fresh order when we returned (and then some).  I noticed another reviewer said they've found the place locked during the early morning hours, and I'd have to agree.  I'd gone to the drive thru speaker, got no response (again, too caught up in other tasks other than servicing the customer), drove around, parked the car, got up to the door, and it's locked.  You know, if you're a 24 hr establishment, then be prepared to offer your services 24 hrs; and if not, then close the place up and reopen when you're able to do so.  Reporting a complaint on their website, or even speaking to one of their field mgrs (when they call you back) is pointless, because they'll just send you an apology letter with coupons for free burgers; instead of just addressing, and correcting, their issues, of which there are many during the afterhours and early a.m. hours.  This place needs their upper mgt to drop in on them during those early hours and see for themselves what goes on, but that'll never happen.  I think they already know, and they just can't find a staff willing to stay on with them.

Slightly on the expensive side, but worth the money. Charming atmosphere that blends a rustic country look with gorgeous lanterns and modern touches. Fork coat hangers are one of many small details that make it unique. Despite being full of patrons, the wait on a Saturday night wasn't too bad - and we found the wine bar next door to be a great place to kill some time. Red Cat's menu is wonderful (and vegetarian friendly), with a mix of American and Mediterranean options. Even the apps were elegantly crafted. I loved the sauteed zucchini with almonds and peccorino. For my main, I ate eggplant parm - and while I can be picky about eggplant, this one was worth savoring. Unfortunately we did not have room for dessert. The pear and fig crostata sounds delicious.

Small place with hardly any seating, but we wanted some authentic NY pizza, so we stopped by one evening after roaming around Times Square and shared a slice of marguerita pizza.   It was incredibly greasy, to the point of dripping.  It distracted from anything else going on with the pizza.

Come here and order the grilled corn off the cob with whatever entree your order!!  It's sooo good!  I had the skate wing which I didn't realize also came with corn.  It was good but the side dish one is better!  The skate was well cooked and was well seasoned also.  I found it quite tasty and it was well complemented by the flavors of the bed of veggies.  But those at the table who ordered the sauteed local flounder thought it wasn't very flavorful and a bit tough.  The old bay fries are fine, but being a girl who grew up in MD, the supposed old bay flavoring was waaay too subtle!  Barely different than normal fries.  Overall, I would return again!

The food was really delicious, but especially thier Classic Italian dishes. The Service is also wonderful, even when the restauraunt is packed. Our server (Barry) was pleasant, knowledgeable, and very attentive.

Ling helped me put together a birthday dinner for my husband.  She was really helpful and made things go very smoothly.  We were kind of high maintenance too, five separate checks and a half an hour late.  The sushi was fresh like it should be and their Sushi boat was a good decision, very well put together and exciting when it came out.  They even gave us a surprise bday treat.  This is a local business that is well worth the time and very reasonable in price.  Would love to do another party here.

Amazing kale salad with squash, mushrooms and barley. Great fresh juices-detox. Chipotle chicken and artichoke sandwiches looked amazing. Very healthy, delicious food with cute ambiance. I completely forgot I was in NYC for a minute. The service was slow but my meal was so good, I almost didn't mind.
Great place for brunch! They make an excellent Bloody Maria.

Great food from a seasonal menu at affordable prices. This place is a real find in an increasingly gentrified Hell's Kitchen. It's small but friendly; come early to avoid a wait! Best of all, BYOB or hit the wine store two blocks south. Best bet: mushroom cigars. Personal fave: Goulash!

Delicious breakfast omelet with superb crispy potatoes fried with onion but not  greasy.  Cute decor and a comfortable atmosphere.  Would definitely go there again to try out the other creative breakfast specials.  Good decor, good neighborhood vibes and good food add up to a winner.
I tried a little tiny bit of everything and it was all GOOD!!!

It's a spacious, open bar/restaurant feel that's decent for catching your particular game.  They must have 30 or 40 TV's so there's always a spare for every sporting event.  I enjoyed some potato skins for starters, which were interesting because they were cut and served as "cross-sections" rather than your traditional (sometimes dry) shell, and they were loaded with great toppings.  Interesting take!  The french dip sandwich was also tastey, with nicely tender beef and au jus full of flavor.  This is my personal favorite sandwich, so it definitely passed my "dip test" with flying colors!  My only complaint might be that it seemed that they skimped on the amount of fries a bit, which was disappointing.  Otherwise, great experience - check it out!
Fabulous burgers.

Good food, great for groups and kids, good service, cash only.  BBQ pork, pan fried mussels with bean sprouts, coconut rice, bean thread casserole with pork and shrimp are the go-to's  Some meals have been better than others.  I think all the hype has definitely hurt the quality and consistency.

The Yelp summary of a two-star review- "Meh. I've experienced better."- really encapsulates my experience here. More thought on concept than on execution. I do love the feel of the room, and I'd go just to sit at the bar and have a drink and admire all the little touches and the vaguely steampunk vibe... but I wouldn't come back here to eat.  The dishes seemed a bit anemic, and not fully considered; I had a lentil appetizer that didn't really work as a starter, but really could have worked as an entree with, say, some seared scallops. All three of us were not exactly dissatisfied with our meals, but underwhelmed.

Cool place for a quick bite to eat  ($$ - decently cheap) if they have space (they only have like 5 super small tables in a row). I got the chicken and potatoes special which was excellent. Their hummus was okay, but not great. The place is small so don't expect to have a private lunch here... Definitely a perfect spot for a little shopping sustenance.

Been to Bianca's numerous of times and although there is almost always a wait for a table, its cash only, and its a pretty tight space, I continue to love this place. Good fresh food, the right amount of service, cute ambiance and reasonable prices make this little hole in the wall one of my favorite Italian restaurants in the city. The dishes that stand out for me are: shrimp and calamari skewers, beet salad, gnocci, frutti de mare; lasagna (really good), and tiramisu.

Came here on 8/17 for the first time, the Mussels (Gigantes Beans, Feta) is a must try, and the trout with the broccoli rabe was amazing too. However, as someone who cares about food taste also food presentation, it's not satisfactory here.

Summary: fine but fairly generic food, noisy, b.y.o.b Review: The food at La Viola was not interesting or innovative, but overall fairly tasty. My salad was not good - came with a remarkably bland cheese. But, my pasta was tasty and my girlfriend enjoyed the veal medallions. Tables are right on top of each other and the place is very noisy. Have to yell to be heard across even a small table. BYOB is nice.

A friend took me here for Happy Hour...Let me tell you - I fell in LOVE with this place.  I really liked the specials offered during happy hour - $5 drinks and menu items were $4 & $5 respectively.  The cheesesteak egg rolls & BBQ chicken were delicious!!   The beer list was respectable, and the speciality drinks were tasty.  I have been thinking about this place since my visit, I will definitely be back and bring friends so they can see what all the FUSS is about.

It was an unexpected turn and a review of Yelp that brought us here for lunch.  It was a great brunch meal and drinks.  The make your Bloody Mary's were delicious.   The wait staff were informative and attentive.  Only downside was the 2nd floor seating.

Best bowl of ramen I've had outside of Japan! Totally worth the wait in my opinion and better than the local competitors. Wished there was one in Virginia. Ippudos is definitely one of my all time favorite restaurants.

We've been coming here for years partly out of convenience since it's one of the few Vietnamese restaurants in the area and partly because it's always been consistently good and very well priced. If I had written this review a couple of years ago it probably would have been 3 stars, as their service used to be a bit on the slow side and the food was just ok. However for whatever reason, in each and every one of our recent visits both the food and service have been noticeably much improved! I'm not sure if they've hired a new cook, but I've definitely noticed an improvement in all of their dishes. The broth in the pho is much deeper and richer in flavor now, not like other places that simply taste like a bouillon cube in water. Other favorites include the sweet potato nest, spring and summer rolls, ginger beef rolls, lemongrass chicken and DEFINITELY the banh mi (Vietnamese sandwich - not on the menu, but up on the menus listed on the mirror/wall). When they first put them on the menu a while ago they were completely wrong - they didn't even come on a baguette, they were on a chewy Italian sub roll. But since then they've really perfected their recipe and they're exactly what you want in a good banh mi - nicely grilled pork, fresh cilantro, crisp pickled vegetables and sliced peppers on a warm crusty baguette. Add some sriracha and you're in banh mi heaven, and for 5 dollars this is truly a great deal! Also the restaurant is BYOB, so you can really have a nice meal without spending much money at all. This week we had a bottle of wine, two large bowls of pho and a Vietnamese sandwich for 19 dollars, talk about a cheap date! Just a great family restaurant that continues to satisfy and strive to improve!

I come here at least once a month. It is definitely some of the best Mexican food I have had. My mother in law, who doesn't like Mexican, has completely changed her tune after coming here, it is that good. Their enchiladas verdes is phenomenal.  My husband always gets the fajitas which he is obsessed with. Great atmosphere. I try to go before the crowds; service gets slower after 7:30. My belly is always happy when I leave.

Growing up Korean means that you are exposed to very traditional food sometimes. Luckily for me, I grew up Italian :) It doesn't mean, however, that I am not well-versed in Korean cuisine or etiquette, and I know poor Korean food and service. Seoul has neither poor cuisine or service. It's actually pretty darn awesome. It's actually better than the place I went to in K-town in NYC. As far as Korean restaurants in the CT area go, this is certainly the best one so far. It is a pretty nice place when you walk in, even though it's in a strip mall plaza near West Farms. I didn't have high hopes, but the pictures and menu looked fantastic, so I figured, "why not?" The first thing I noticed were all the Korean faces at the tables - always a good sign. I was there with two other people, and in an effort to branch out (because I *always* order dolsot bibimbap if it's on the menu), we opted for "Combination A," which is listed to feed three people. It had bulgogi, kalbi, and chadol-baegi. It came with soondubu, kimchi-jeon, steamed egg casserole, and banchan. While the online menu suggests it comes with alcohol, it doesn't, but it didn't matter. There was SO. MUCH. FOOD. Like, so much, that the three of us didn't finish it - it would have easily fed four people. Our ahjummas (waitresses) were very good and they seemed happy when I called them that. Their English isn't the *best* so we did need to translate a bit with the Google Translate App, but in the end, it was pretty awesome and they were not overbearing. The bill for just the combination was $95 before tip, but given the amount of food, I wouldn't hesitate to pay it again. It's a fun way to introduce my American friends to Korean food, and it's a great social atmosphere. I'd love to go back and try the japjae, kimchi-jjigae, and of course, the dolsot-bibimbap.
Yum yum yum!!!! The only downside to this D-liscious establishment is that it is a little bit overpriced.  A must try!

Great espresso!  Right up there with Grumpy's and Sweat Leaf.  Definitely the only place in Astoria for a coffee snob. The food is pretty decent.  All vegetarian mostly brunch food (i.e. breakfast sandwhich, grits and eggs, etc...)   They can get backed up but the staff is very nice.  I've never had a bad meal here.

While strolling along the west side I stumbled across a cute little thai place. I would call it sweet and petite. like the name connotes, simple and good! Try the Yen Ta Pho if your a vegetarian, most other dishes make me want to try meat, but I wont, hehe. Excellent yuzu lemonaide, very yummy to the tummy.

Yes, I realize this is a big touristy spot for white people but whatever, the soup dumplings are still delicious.  They're basically pork dumplings filled with a delicious broth when you bite into them.  The Shanghai noodles were also delicious fat home-made noodles sauteed with beef and spinach.  The roasted duck was also fantastic and tender and the meat just fell off the bone.   They seated us at a round table with a party of 7 people.  At first I thought it would be a bit awkward, but they were hilarious and entertaining table of trannies and gays.    The service was extremely fast and despite the long line out the restaurant, we only had to wait about 30 minutes for a table.

So good and authentic.  We went early on a Friday night, called about an hour ahead to make a reservation, which was no problem.  We sat out on the sidewalk on one of those gorgeous NYC nights.  All of our servers (and about 6 different people served us) were extremely friendly, and not just hired off the street.  Seemed that they were part of a family or maybe from the same region of Europe.  And they just took turns refilling our waters, bringing more bread, in general, making sure we were taken care of.   The food:  half the price of any other Village Italian restaurant, and twice as good.  First, the bread is yummy, even if you're not so starving you're about to eat off the next table.  And cheap carafes of pretty good wine.  We got the calamari to start...and it's grilled!  A much better preparation than fried.  And they did it well.  I got the gorganzola gnocchi...perfectly cooked, better than some I had even in Italy.  My brother, who notoriously NEVER finishes his plate, had his pasta arrabiata polished, sauce and all gone off the plate.  We were much too full for dessert...and even as the restaurant was getting more packed, they didn't rush us out at the end of our meal.  We even had to ask for the check after sitting for a bit to enjoy people watching. The location may be a bit of a walk from the trains for some...but I live 4 blocks away, and catching a sunset over the Hudson (two blocks away), was the perfect end to a great meal.  HIGHLY recommend.
Fun concept. I've been once, but I found the stir fry to be delicious and big enough for 2. I'm pretty excited for the one on City Ave to open.

Color me unimpressed.  Some friends and I ate here on a Saturday night, so of course it was super crowded.  I ordered some Thai pasta that wasn't anything to write home about.  About a month later I called and said that I wanted to have a birthday party there (the location is great) and I was told that they would be able to accommodate us even though our party was relatively large (12 people).  When I called back in the middle of the week to confirm, I was told that they'd already booked another party, so pretty much my friends and I were SOL.   Haven't been back, won't be back.

My family has been coming here for at least... 40 years now (since they came from Hong Kong), and it's still our favorite. Every time we come to NYC, whether it's Brooklyn or midtown, we have to stop by for dinner and the next day's lunch. Not to mention, it's so affordable! We always get the Tang Jai Jook and Wonton soup (with extra wontons on the side). Plus, the... [not sure what it is in English] oily bread sticks(?) are delicious in the jook. This jook is the perfect balance of beef, different types of peanuts, and slighty salty congee topped with peanuts and scallions. I have literally dreamed about this dish, and I haven't been able to find it anywhere else! Whenever we try it elsewhere, it always lacks flavor and depth. We've even tried replicating it at home and can never imitate the same texture and balance of flavors. The wonton soup is perfect. The wontons don't have too much of the peel, and the filling is delicious Be sure to get extras on the side because you'll want more for your bowl of noodles! We usually get take out (the street's pretty busy so parking can be challenging), but the few times we've sat, we have ordered other items off the menu, and everything is pretty good (the roast pork and duck are some of the better ones in Chinatown.) Service can be faster for sit down, but the man at the register is always friendly and quick.

Hands down my favorite restaurant - it never disappoints! Great food, great atmosphere. Some nights I binge on tapas. My favorites are the bacon wrapped dates, octopus, and falafel wrapped artichokes. Other times I go with the evening special - fish dishes are always stellar. I bring ALL my out of towners here to help them fall in love with Brooklyn. Fantastic brunch spot too.
Absolutely shocked how good the spinach and artichoke pizza is. Have it hot/worth the wait if there's a line/calling ahead works sometimes/tip the guys on the left. Enjoy.

Like every man I love good baked meat. Steakhouses are my thing and I have tried many of them. Had it ever happened to you that you eat a steak and cannot say a word because that moment of silence and deliciousness in your mouth is a blessing? That's how I feel in this place!
Spectacular and inventive food, stellar service, real and personal attention from the two world-class chefs that own it.  A perfect addition to Passyunk East and by far the best BYO in Philadelphia.

I love Red Eye Cafe for its welcoming staff, amazingly healthy and delicious food, and awesome prices.  I'm from WI and have eaten more grilled cheese sandwiches than I can count, but their grilled cheese with onion jam was out-of-this-world!  And it came with a salad and soup, all for $7.  Red Eye has a cozy ambience for these chilly days and when warm weather returns, try their lovely  small outdoor garden.  A great addition to the Montclair dining scene!

There, under the glaring fluorescent lights, arms sticking to the oilcloth table covers, wondering what we were doing in a mexican place in Hartford, I toasted my two colleagues and paused to wonder if the screws working at the connecticut boys truancy detention center across the street ever brought back a nice plate of chivo (barbequed goat) to the wee lads in their care. The chivo, which is what prompted me to write this, was on special that night, and was surprising to say the least.  I had expected chunks of lean, gamey goat meat with bones and gristle.  My typical goat experience being at haitian places favored by cab drivers with bloodshot eyes and questionable past careers which despite their vehement denials clearly include time served with the tonton macout. Instead what i got was much more akin to ropa vieja; shredded, tomato based barbecue sauce. Super tender, super tasty, very very good. We had started with guacamole and chips and some random salsas. All quite good, especially the dark red smokey salsa picante. Margaritas were being consumed, the place looked and sounded authentic as hell.  So goat it was.  Excellent goat as it turned out. I ordered a tres leches cake which was light and delicious, with an indefinable perfume, maybe rosewater or orange blossom or something.  also excellent. My friends got carne asada and a chicken burrito (he's a native connecticuter (connecticutite, connectican?) and flan.  the flan was a little dense but still quite delicious.   I also want to specifically mention the service -- a sweet, sweet mexican girl who patiently translated the menu and made us laugh. El Sarape.  Take the gamble, venture into the Hartford barrio...it's much much better than you think.

I was expecting my first slice to greet me with that "mmm soo good" sensation... unfortunately, I was not... not only do these pizzas look no more appetizing than your local pizza, they LACK FLAVOR. The taste is fine, but it's not anything extraordinary. It's a healthy alternative to a grab and go kinda place. A fresh mozzarella pie with barely any cheese, at $28 you have to be kidding me!?! Tried my first Lombardi's pie with meatball and roasted red peppers... similar to the cheese, it was hard to find a bite with either. If they were less skimpy, I would say this place would deserve 3 stars, but even still... there is no taste and nothing special here. My suggestion, try Two Boots Pizza around the corner or Saluggi's a couple blocks away in Tribeca. Your taste buds will thank you.
This place is awesome! Fajitas are great and Carl is the best! Definitely a must go This place is awesome. Great food and great service. The people are really nice. Definitely a must go!

I love this place! The food is great and being byob is also a plus. The real reason I love it is because of the staff. Everyone is always very friendly, especially Beverley. She always makes me smile! She's super friendly and always nice to talk with. If you don't go for the food, at least go to enjoy her company.

Food was excellent. We had the recommended pho bo and pho ge. Both were delicious and hearty. Plates came with a lot of meat and these are large plates. Our kid had chicken fried rice that he said was the best he'd ever had. Overall service was friendly but not very professional as appetizer came in with the soups. But staff apologized and didn't charge us for it. Great little joint. Will definitely recommend.

delicious paninis! it's small cute cafe that felt very authentic and truly brooklyn. i got the smoked salmon, avocado, goat cheese, truffle oil panini...i felt it was good, but the goat cheese and truffle oil overpowered the panini. it was hard for me to eat the second half of it. the salami panini, the other hand, was delicious! Meat was cut very thin. crepe was good too! i will be back.

We came here last night on a double date and had a delicious meal, with great service. This restaurant looks small when you walk in, but past the bar there is a large covered outdoor dining room (with heating). The restaurant was surprisingly quiet, even though every table was full. Our waitress arrived right away, and was extremely helpful answering questions and giving recommendations. We ordered a bottle of wine and some appetizers to start. My boyfriend and I split a salad with caramelized pear and gorgonzola, with fig dressing. For my entree, I ordered the toasted whole wheat pasta with tomato and mozzarella - it was delicious, and the portion size was perfect. My boyfriend ordered the pesto pasta, which was also amazing but definitely creamy and heavier than some of the other menu options. Throughout the meal, our waters were promptly refilled and our waitress was always in sight, checking on us occasionally. I didn't have a single complaint about any of the food or service, and would love to come back soon. I'd highly recommend trying this gem of a restaurant on the UES. Try making a reservation first - it filled up quickly even on a Sunday night.

This is my favorite restaurant. I do not throw those words around lightly. Also, notice I didn't say it like "this is my NEW favorite restaurant" or "this is my favorite BBQ restaurant". No, there is no qualifier to this place, and I've never said that folks. I first had them at a rooftop BBQ where they catered. And they were soooo delicious. Not a month after that event, a group of four of us took the trek out to Red Hook. Here's the thing. It's not the easiest place to get to. But knowing what awaited us, we knew it'd be worth it. Thursday night at 7pm is sparse (I hear it gets pretty packed on the weekend). And the decor is so cool. Almost exactly how I thought it would be (sans any sort of saw dust), but there were two bars, two dining areas, very country barn-esque. Our bar tender was super cool. I ordered the town tea (peach tea vodka), and because I'm not an alcohol-loving gal, it was absolutely perfect. And the way the ordering of the food goes...it's just cool guys. Laid back, watch them cut and weigh the meat, have it piled onto a giant silver tray. It's just great experience. Pulled pork was probably my favorite, the sides (are the stars of any BBQ for me)...the beans, the cornbread, the mac & cheese, the slaw...just heavenly. I love the spice of the beans, the honey glazed top of the corn bread, the cheeziness of the mac, the how perfect it goes with everything-ness of the slaw. It's just an awesome place for a great meal. And you don't feel like a bloated fat pig after. What BBQ that's delicious doesn't make you feel guilty about all that you ate. And then the live music! It was just such a perfect compliment to the mood of the entire experience that is Hometown BBQ (you could picture floating down a swampy river on a lazy summer afternoon). AND the people! I mentioned the awesome bartender, the cool guys at the food station, and the sweet boss man (reminds of a teamster, but somehow even cuddlier). I cannot wait for them to actually sell their delicious sauces! If they were closer/easier to get to, I would be there at least once a week. But for now, it's like that guy (or girl) who is so cool, but doesn't even try.

I love the shrimp parm here. I order it with a side of spaghetti and either share it with my daughter or I get two meals for myself from one order. I think it is fantastic! My wife often gets a slice of their caesar salad for dinner.

This is my favorite breakfast spot. Apple pancake is awesome. It is not a traditional pancake.  They bake it in an oven and has more of an egg like consistency. Comes covered in this cinnamon glaze. It is very filling and could easily be shared by two people. Staff is attentive and friendly.

Very disappointed. My food wasn't even edible. Bleh!! The guacamole was the most unappetizing that I've ever seen, the shrimp was funky, and the pico de gallo (which I LOVE most places) was just plain bad. I'm also surprised that nobody has mentioned the fact that they received a B sanitary grade...for having evidence of mice.
THis place is great,Only problem is the hours from 7pm till early in the morning,is not very convenient. Beware long line for the cart.

Quaint little spot in Chelsea. Great for sharing a bottle of wine with close friends and third dates. The butter they serve here is the real deal! Creamy and rich- just as butter should be! It's served in a large ramekin and filled to the brim. So be ready to eat like the French do and slather it on thick! Service can be somewhat slow although everyone who works here is friendly, knowledgeable and kind. All in all, a great departure from the usual in Chelsea. If you're stuck in Port Authority, La Grainne is a great escape.

Yemen Mocha. Dumpling sampler. I don't know what drugs they put into those two delightful items, but I end up craving them multiple times a week. Everything about this place is lovely. From the woman owner, who is sweet as pie. To the sugar cookie that comes on the side of your tea or coffee. To the adorable doily the cookie sits on. To the unique plates and mugs your order is served with. Just.... adorable.
Carbs never tasted so amazing!

ok, i finally managed to force myself not to get their delicious apple, brie and chicken sandwich. it took me 5 minutes of going back and forth which i'm sure perturbed my coworkers but i did it (only because i had that sandwich the day before!) the chicken pot pie was AMAZING. i'm not sure if anybody mentioned it here, but it has butternut squash!!! i go crazy for that orange goodness. who wudda thought to add it to pot pie?! great, now don't even try tearing me away from ordering the pot pie every single time now.

The Max Group always does the best. On a Saturday evening, we had no trouble getting an early booth, (5:30) with a beautiful view of the restaurant  and its open kitchen. Service was attentive and friendly, and the food was perfect. Overall one of the best dining experiences, but that's a Max for you!!

Ok TOPS is TOPS excuse the cliche but this bright shiny big diner is diner perfection it seems to be in the middle of an industrial section of Newark it has its own lot so that is excellent it looked like a packed house parking lot wise but we found a spot Sunday evening about 6 we were starvin marvins and were seated right away I did notice they had the ball game playing on a built in TV in the lobby there are also benches so if you need to wait there is entertainment Our friendly waiter came right over to ask if we wanted some drinks iced tea and really good iced coffee started us off and a piping hot loaf of bread with butter then menu does offer shakes which will be on my list for the next time there is everything on this menu as any decent diner will offer opting for my usual diner fair was a grilled cheese on rye it was perfect my dining companions had bbq chicken man oh man I almost wanted to taste it instead I tried Barry's mac n cheese baked perfection with crumbs on top how yummy Daniels BIG burger and I mean big burger came hot and juicy and he was so happy Tyler also downed his perfect burger in complete happiness portions are huge ...really Andrea's cobb salad was one big filled with fixings bowl she loved it Im one of those can I try yours people so I tasted her salad and her blue cheese and it was real good when it came time for dessert we we so stuffed we had to pass but I saw yummy looking cakes in the glass case (next time) our server was attentive and friendly our beverages were refilled this diner really rocks go eat there
Amazingly cheep spectacular food! The sesame pancake with duck is delicious.
Loved the food.....just loved it. Ordered the biryani and some prawns. Was to die for. The ambience is average and the service is ok. But I guess for me the food and flavors made up for it.
HUGE portions! Friendly, quick service. Good prices. Varied options, including vegetarian. Very cute little place!

One star off the the following: It's pricey ($9 for a tuna sandwich), and it's noisy (not the place for a serious conversation). On the other hand, the food is great, ditto the coffee, ditto the staff (very Chelsea), ditto the music. My favorite 14th St -area joint.

I was a little underwhelmed by this place after hearing rave reviews from colleagues and friends! Ordered the Plato don, a massive platter with shrimp, tilapia, and additional condiments (guacamole, black beans, rice etc) but taste wise it wasn't anything special. I couldn't quite put my fingers on it but it tasted similar to Chipotle tbh. On the flip side, lovely ambience and decor. I probably would not come here again.

Cute little French bistro in the heart of the West Village. Cozy & small, the wait was just 10 minutes for our table of 4. After three bottles of BYOB champagne later and a very delicious eggs benny & top-notch homefries, we rolled out of there full and floaty. 4 solid stars, bordering 5

I ended up at Trumbull Kitchen tonight for dinner and was pleasantly surprised that it was restaurant week during my visit - $20.12 for dinner...not bad!   The atmosphere was noisy, but nice.  The service was extremely friendly and helpful.  The food was pretty good too.  I enjoyed the vegetable soup, lobster pasta and tres leches cake. All in all a very good place!

Nice small neighborhood work spot for my lunch break. They serve early breakfast and lunch throughout the day in this small spot that provides only bar counter service with one cook behind the counter. It's diner style but super small. You'll get your usual diner fare but the standouts are the special hero sandwiches. The munchie i ordered was roast beef cheese onions on a toasted hero. Ample portion at a cheap price. Great for a lunch but nothing outstanding which wows ya. Fries were good though. It's cheap eats with basic service.

This is my favorite restaurant in NYC. It is straight comfort food, served with amazing drinks.  I've had the crab cakes and the country fried steak while I was here.  Both were very good, decent size portions and hearty.   However, the drinks were the best part.  I love their mixed berry mojito, which is pretty strong without having too strong of the alcoholic taste.  The first time I ordered it, my friend and I each got one. We were buzzed by the time we got seated, and regretted the fact that we didnt' order the carafe.  We'd have been stumbling out, but it would have been sooooo good.

Absolutely wonderful Lebanese-inspired mediterranean restaurant, with a  tremendous variety of mezzes to choose from. If you have the time and are looking for lunch that runs about $25 per person this is a place you won't want to pass over. This won't be a traditional or ethnic meal, but that's not really the point.  Note that I said Lebanese-inspired, not Lebanese! The plates have some modern touches when it comes to complimentary flavors (think whifs and zesty garnishing) but it all works very well. The wait staff at Ilili was incredibly helpful and attentive, and certainly charismatic. Our waitress was more than happy to "play trivia" with the items on the menu if we had any curiosities. Water glasses were always full, and empty plates were readily cleared. Excellent service all around. Seen on my table were (in english) Lamb Sausages, Falafel, Artichoke and Heart of Palm salad, Phoenician Fries (sage and garlic), and Duck Kebabs.  Dessert was a Lebanese Snowball, aka Halva with pistachio sauce. Everything was absolutely delightful. You'll love the food here too!

Went here on sunday prior to the Jets playoff game with friends. I had previously heard that others were saying there would be a large wait, but due to the rain and off peak hours as soon as we walked in we got a half tray. Easily the best sicilian slice I have ever had. The corner slices are amazing and the sauce to cheese combination is perfect. A little grated parmesan and red pepper even brings out the flavor more.

The most overrated burger in NYC. It's good for an $8 burger, but the bartender is extremely arrogant, lazy and likely racist. Took him 10 minutes to acknowledge our presence at the bar because he was too busy chatting with a buddy and some girls. Table service is no better (I didn't see any servers). Only go here if you are white and live in the neighborhood. Otherwise, many better options all over the city. if you are the owner of this establishment, I would highly recommend reconsidering your staffing decisions. Your business could likely double with better staff.

Really? Empanada Mama is ok but not worth standing around and waiting for.  What I tried was ok but I've had better coming out of my mother's kitchen.  I prefer a little more crunch and less doughy shell.   Their cheesesteak empanada were good, service was decent but the place is incredibly cramped so if you have an issue with personal space, please stay away.  Wasn't too keen on the hip hop music playing and I didn't care for the "mood lighting".  They're 2.75 empanadas people, no need to try so hard.
Really nice place to enjoy good food, good drinks, AND good service. Everyone is super polite. The food is fairly priced and yummy. GO!

PIZZAAA! I love the olives they use for their pizza! It's salty as hell, but delicious! I honestly don't like leaving the city just because it's such a pain, but grimaldi's really isn't that far AND I would definitely make my way there again! Though I jst found out they have a location in manhattan as well, so I guess I won't need to? My friend and I ordered a small regular pizza w/ sausage, olives and fresh garlic. OH boy, the fresh garlic made the pizza just THAT much better. Next time though, I'll have to add extra basil! I have to say this is one of my favorite pizza joints. Try it if you haven't!

ugh. flies, non-labelled questionable food, waiters giving wrong information, rude service at the meat counter, bad lighting, ridiculous prices you only find out when you go to pay, and to top it all off, i realized after drinking out of my glass for an hour, that it had lipstick all over it.. and i do not wear lipstick.  Just no.

Small fairly traditional French menu with a few little twists - beautifully executed dishes. Despite the somewhat cramped space and tiny tables the vibe is relaxed. Noteworthy: the chocolate mousse so rich and thick it came with two spoons standing up in it. Delicious, maybe share it with someone though ... The garden area looked especially nice to sit in.

It's never a good thing when you have a reservation and still end up waiting for a table, even if it's only a 10 minute wait. The room seemed to be nothing more than a glorified cafeteria with very high ceilings and a noise level that made us feel like we were at a Devils game. The disappointment continued when they were out of the shrimp appetizer, and this was at 6:30; no excuse. The food overall was decent, but none of it was hot, and the portions were barely enough to satisfy my 2 cockatiels.  I then tried to change my dessert, and was told I could not. The coffee was undrinkable, not because it was barely lukewarm , but it had a chemical  soapy taste. The service was fair at best. Regretfully, I cannot recommend Nico, and we won't be back.

Put a fork in it. And eat it all up. Abe Fisher was a remarkable experience from start to finish. We did the prix fixe. Carrots and chopped liver first. Liver rivals the best foie gras in taste and texture but no geese were harmed in the making of this spectacular 1st course. Next, sweet and sour meatballs and the must-try pork belly Reuben. 3rd, lamb (outrageous goodness) and gefilte fish ( how many more exquisite flavors can you pack into one plate?), followed by dessert of bacon egg cream and apple strudel, both a miracle of modern confection. Also, special bonus, chef sent out salami and eggs dish for us to try. The staff is outstanding. Every server and manager is top notch, best in the business. Cocktails are awesome. Yes! Go! Enjoy!

One of my favorite spots in the city. Reasonably priced with awesome service. They have a wide selection of oysters and craft beers. The pasta with clams and breadcrumbs was delicious and I am not usually one to mix fish and cheese. The complimentary rum cake tops off the experience nicely!

The chicken is wholesome and filling. The sides are delicious, especially the Mac and cheese. This is our second time back and we'll be sure to do it again. We had the beets and feta along with the corn muffins. Seems like you can't go wrong the side choices. Atmosphere is casual and the staff is friendly. We are lucky to have a great local spot like this.

Their bulgogi sandwich is one of the best I have ever tried. It's moist and juicy with the perfect amount of spices. Even though the bread they put the bulgogi on is a little hard, it doesn't bother me as much because the meat is so darn good. I also recommend the fries with the spicy mayo. Delicious!
Good place to eat. Best I have seen with German food in the City. The prices are decent. Vander

I am always in search of a good Hot Dog stand so in entering Jordans new location on State St. it's an ideal hot dog joint { I say that with respect } good size tables if you wish to eat there the menu is extensive Dogs,Burgers,Mac, turkey burgers and turkey dogs something for everyone I had to try their Chili Dog with fries perfectly cook my wife had to try the Mac and Cheese drinks both of us had a old favorite Foxons cream soda Wow great lunch, by all means it is a very good choice.

chicken. beans. and rice... it doesn't get any easier. And Margon definitely "gets it". while i've never seen a dirtier can of Dr Pepper in my life than the complimentary one which came with my lunch the food was very good. you could feed three people with the tray of beans and rice and while the chicken was a bit dry i noticed there was none left when finally coming up for air at the conclusion of my afternoon feeding. Very friendly staff + a ton of food for $8 and change = get here asap.

I've had a love affair with Chinatown ever since I was 14. Where else can you get cheap food and fireworks in a 10 block radius. Well times have changed and now you can just get food and one spot I love is NY Noodle town. It's your regularly decorated Chinese spot communal tables and all. The roast pork was really good but a little sweet. The Soup was out of this world. Served with roast pork and shrimp dumplings this place hits the spot anytime, even in the summer. But be careful, it's a nighttime hot spot so be ready to wait.

I came here with a girlfriend for brunch this Sunday and we loved it. Minimal wait time at 11:00 am, maybe ten minutes, though it was raining out.  Staff were accommodating (my friend needed stroller space) and our food was delicious and perfectly seasoned, IMO. She ordered red flannel hash with a side of parmesan grits, I had sausage & eggs.  Both came with a nice mesclun salad which didn't seem like an afterthought - the dressing was tasty and we both cleaned our plates. The house-made sausage was some of the best breakfast sausage I've ever had, and the grits were a-maz-ing - so creamy! The place is loud enough that a few minutes of baby fussing went fairly un-noticed, but we still felt like we could have a conversation. I would return!

Truly loved this place! Definitely a hidden gem. Started with the Spanish olive tapa plate. Some of the olives were stuffed with garlic-best olives I have ever had. Came with some yummy bread to pair with the olives as well. Had the picante sandwich which had this incredibly good spicy chorizo, manchego cheese, spicy peppers and this amazing bread. Such an awesome sandwich. Also had the flan for dessert which was very good. I highly recommend the tempranillo wine they have as well. Amazing dinner! I bought some chorizo and prosciutto to bring home too since it was so good.

In the grand universe of pizza, a 2-star may seem a bit harsh, but this is New York City.  I tried this place on the recommendation of a friend from NYU: ) - "If you like artichoke and spinach dip then a slice of this pizza will make your day." I had high hopes and upon squeezing myself into this hole in the wall, i saw only four types of pizza, which in my book is a good thing. Shows faith in the product. I paid my $4.50 and wiggled my way back into the rain outside. i found the nearest awning and folded for my first bite... I was expecting the savory goodness of Spinach and Artichoke, but instead found a mouthful of okay crust covered in salty Alfredo. and not even good Alfredo. Just a weak white sauce whose only artichoke (despite the eponymous restaurant) flavor was in the two little pieces of heart, and severely lacking in the spinach flavor which often saves the pair in the dips I've had. In the end, I only ate the whole thing because I paid five bucks. and i am of the opinion of always try a place twice, but if i do i am going for the crab or something with a red sauce. ps- another issue with this places name is "& Brewery". Stella and Bud Light as the only drafts and Bud in a can should get your liquor license revoked when you are so bold to call yourself a brewery.

I ordered for delivery and boy was I disappointed! The pizza was cold and seemed old! I also ordered a Nutella cake and it was a whole bunch of scraps thrown together which I payed 6 dollars for! I had ordered from here before and was very happy! something must be going on, new management or something. Highly disappointed! I should of known not to order, my friend recently said he went there and got treated poorly! DONT ORDER HERE! If you want to have a good experience.

El Rey is definitely an el disappointment. I went here with a co-worker for lunch and found it to be over priced (even for Stephen Starr) and not that great. Although I am definitely not the authority on Mexican food, I have been to the Yucatan a few times (read more than most). The sopes at El Rey barely resemble the actual dish. Yes, El Rey tries to fancy them up with steak but that is no excuse to charge $10 for two tiny sopes that barely had any of the fixins associated with real Yucatecan sopes. I could have lived with $10 sopes if they had filled me up like the clueless waiter said they would but they didn't. I had to spend another $9 to order a plate of decent (not great for the price) tacos. When you add in the way too expensive Stephen Starr drink line-up and tax the bill came to $30 for just my lunch.  My money would have been better spent at La Lupe or Taco Loco (the taco cart on Washington). Stephen Starr is getting too big for his britches, it's time he stopped charging so much for his name and focused more on satisfying his customers.

Wowzers this place is soooooooooo good. I mean really good fries and really good dip. Luckily when we got there, there wasn't a long line. I asked the staff what dip was good. He actually let me try his favorite, and I loved it. I believe it was the mango-ish sauce. They were very friendly and sweet, which always make a place that much better. It is a bit pricey for fries but its worth it. I will def be back to try some cheesy fries!!

Service was terrible. They never came around to refill our drinks. They gave our table the wrong order, then told us that we were wrong. They were extremely rude and refused to remedy the problem. The food was mediocre. It may have been better, had we gotten what we asked for. I would not recommend this place.

I love Bella's.  It's where I go when i want to treat myself to a spectacular breakfast -  both the environment and the food are a balm for the troubled soul.  My favorite time to visit is a weekday morning, on the early side, when the restaurant is very quiet, and you can savor their choice in music  - I've never been there on a weekend morning, but I can understand why they are crowded. If I could, I'd give them an extra star for their consideration of my need for Gluten Free food - I just order scrambled eggs, potatoes and and fruit salad or sometimes their fantastic apple-bacon.  Because of how their kitchen is organized, I've never suffered from cross-contamination with bread products.   And - the cafe au lait put me in mind of Paris, not Starbucks.

The last few times I've eaten here the beef tasted a bit "off." The service is reasonably good but the food is a bit below the average neighborhood Chinese restaurant's. Joyce, the woman who runs (owns?) the place is incredibly rude and it makes the meal unpleasant if you interact with her.
I went to Marzullos this weekend for dinner with my family. I was very pleased! The service was great and the food even better!

My big fat Greek family and I went for my dad's birthday last weekend. We go here about once a year, and always except a 45 minute to 1 hour wait. The food is worth it. However, this time, we left very upset. First of all, we were seated (all 11 of us) next to the kitchen - it was so loud that we couldn't have conversations. Our tables were so close to other tables that the waitress literally had to make us move each time she passed by - how can I enjoy a meal if you disrupt me every couple of minutes? My father was speaking to his cousin in Greek about the unusually long wait is and how he felt pressured to eat his meal right away because the waitress kept coming and asking if we were finished. (The wait was a bit over an hour this time). The hostess overheard and decided to barge into our conversation and tell my father, in Greek, that we were, in fact, seated sooner than anyone else that night. Maybe to Americans this would not be a big deal, but to Greeks, interrupting a conversation in such a demeaning way is beyond insulting, especially to someone much older than you. I don't think we will ever go there again. I understand how much pressure the staff is under because of how busy they are on weekends, but that is no excuse to be rude to customers who were in no way rude to you. The whole meal was rushed and we were basically shooed out of the restaurant.

Great Place. Great for groups, met some co-workers for after dinner drinks. They have plenty of seating and regular tables to make you more comfortable. The noise level is pretty decent, we were able to have normal conversations with each other. As for the food: I ordered the salt and pepper ribs and the Mesclun salad....... DAYYYYUUUMMM. Who would've thunk that regular salt and pepper ribs could be so tasty.  This is hands down one of the best meals I have had at a bar!!!! We also ordered The Nutella Ricotta Calzone, which is AMAZING!!! It's enough for 2-3 people, it's warm gooey but not too sweet! Geez, I'm salivating just thinking about it! I'm a happy chick, can't wait to go back!

We have always loved this place for both the atmosphere and pizza. We usually go in the summer and enjoy the outdoor seating. Recently we went for an early dinner with our toddler and could not have been more disappointed. Both the bar tender and the waitress made it abundantly clear that they don't like having children there. No strollers, no kids at the bar, no kids walking around. I should mention it was 5:30 and almost empty. We were made to feel very unwelcome and ended up taking our pizza to go. Do not come here with kids if you want to feel your business is welcome.

What an amazing tasty sandwich! Was really sad that they ran out of the pork belly today. But went there for the first time, and the Pulled pork was amazing! Delicious definitely coming back again on my way to class

If you love food (and, to a lesser extent, crowds) you will love RTM. It offers nearly every category of food you could want, multiple fresh food grocers, a beer garden, a diner, butchers, seafood stands, snack shops, candy stores, and even authentic Pennsylvania dutch (on weekends) selling cakes, pies, breads, etc. It makes everything extremely accessible, too, by being located within the same building. It does get very crowded, especially on weekends but, to me, that adds to the charm, making it an excellent place to people watch in Philadelphia (while staying warm and VERY well fed). For the tourist, it's a MUST SEE. For the Philadelphian, it's the mecca for great, inexpensive, different foods.

Me and my similarly big-stomached friend came here last year, splitting the meat plate (I forget the name, but it was like 2 pounds of meat for $30). The service was good and the food was quite enjoyable. As good as the smoked meat was, we actually liked the rice even more, and I wish there had been more rice (which is a surprising statement coming from me).

This restaurant is near impossible to get into.  There is always a huge wait.  My friends and I went on a Friday night and the wait was two hours, so we left.  I returned a few weeks later on a Saturday afternoon around 1 for lunch, and there was no wait, but it was very crowded.  This place has a big bar and looks like a fun place to come at night. The chips and salsa are yummy, and I had a cheese quesadilla, which was also pretty good.  My friends had chicken quesadillas, which they also liked. I'd like to come back, but you definitely need to come at an off time or be prepared to wait.

I give this restaurant 3.5 stars. I rounded down because I don't think it deserves 4. Yelp says it opens at 11 so we show up at 11am for breakfast. Come to find out they said they won't be opening until noon. We really wanted to try this place out so we killed time and came back around noon. We were craving more of a dinner/lunch type of Filipino food like kare kare. Unfortunately, they were only serving breakfast. The breakfast menu was very limited. We ordered sisig, longsilog, and the filipino fried chicken with ube waffles. The sisig is over-hyped and I'm not too sure why it had a lot of ratings.. It wasn't good to us. My boyfriend really loved the longsilog! The filipino friend chicken with ube waffles was a bit weird at first but after a couple bites, we learned to love it! We had a pleasant experience but one visit is enough :) Thanks, Maharlika :)

This place is amazing! I love their Sicilian squares and their Spumoni and ices are too die for! No matter how full I get I always want more. The place can get really busy sometime especially in the evenings. The restaurant is amazing as well, just make sure if you are going to eat in the restaurant that you come early and in a small party as they do not take reservations. They will try their best to accommodate, but if it is busy and they have customers they will give away your table.

This is by far the best restaurant i have been to. I am Portuguese and to eat very authentic food away from home is extremely rare. every time i am in the area and go out to eat this is my only option. the price is cheap for the amount of food you get and the quality is unbeatable. if you want to try some good Portuguese food this is the place to go.

The lunch specials are amazing. I got grilled shrimp with a side of rice and my bf got quail with lemon potatoes. I don't know which was better, they were so good! The Greek salad is authentic Greek and a must try appetizer. This place was packed at lunch time on a Monday afternoon, that's how you know you are going to eat well.

Superb food, friendly service, great ambiance and the best smoked bluefish roulette I've ever tasted. An extensive selection of wine as well (I recommend the Vin de Pays du Vaucluse). Move over Applebee's, there's a new Sheriff in town.
Wandered in here with a friend and was wonderfully surprised by the excellent selection of beers on tap.  But, the must try snack here is the bacon popcorn.  Spicy and delicious!

I think Sanford restaurant it is a 5 star place. What can i tell about them. From the moment you come in ill you leave you just have an amazing experience. I agree with Amy it should be renamed "I love this place" The food it is delicious and the people there are very friendly and nice. I have a lot of dishes which i like from this place that why  i will leave it up to you to choose your favorite. Give this place a try i guaranty you wont get disappointed. ciao

Went due too all the hype.  I thought is was good, but there is much better elsewhere.  ie. parts of Brooklyn and Manhattan.  Waiter service wan't bad.  They had a full bar, which I enjoyed a few drinks with my dinner.  I went during the week, so wait wasn't bad.  Overall, enjoyed it, but rather go to another pizza place.  It is on the better side of many Manhattan pizza places, but there is better.
The best Italian  food I have had to date, real authentic. Very small and crowded, but well worth it. Must have the hot roast beef with free mozz.
Best Polish restaurant out there :)

oh jacobs pickles, why don't you take reservations? I've been trying to eat here for awhile but always felt let down when the wait was an hour or more.  This past Saturday night, however, we had time to kill before a party so we put our names down and went elsewhere to grab some drinks. The hostess told us an hour but the time increase to almost an hour 30. Finally we got seated.  The wait staff seemed to be small in number and therefore extremely busy.  Wait times were slow, unfortunately from the start. To eat, we had the biscuits and fixins which were pretty good but I felt the biscuits could've been warmer/fresher. For my main I got the salmon which was recommended by the waiter.  The salmon was excellent, perfectly cooked and seasoned but I thought the side to the salmon was very odd. It was mushrooms in a cream and cheese sauce. Did not work with the salmon.  My boyfriend had the mac and cheese which was quite tasty and the portion was huge.   I would only come back here if you can make a reservation for a large party. Otherwise, try your hand somewhere else

I was taken there for my Birthday last week.  The reservation had been made 3 weeks in advance. When we arrived, the host said there was only 1 table available and it was right inside the door, in probably the worst spot in the restaurant.  After declining that table, we were told we could wait at the bar for a better table. Seriously, if I take the time to make a reservation in advance, I do not expect to be given the worst table in the restaurant. Either they overbooked or can't manage their reservations. We waited 25 minutes for a better table. The food was good, the server was nice, but the rest of the staff and the host were marginal. I would not go back. For the price, there are much better restaurants. Also, the decor seemed to be a cheaper version of another of their restaurants.

So happy they opened a really good bar/restaurant with food that is done with imagination & distinction. This is what a gastro pub should be. This place is around the corner from my job and it's becoming a weekly lunch destination. I've had the duck tacos, the lobster sliders, the kale chop salad, the warm barley sweet potato, and grilled chicken sandwich. I love it all. Oh and try the sriracha mayo for your fries or as a spread for a sandwich. YUM YUM YUM.

The food is amazing and really unique for Philadelphia. The cuisine reminds me of living in the South and that may add bonus points to this review. The hush puppies and mac and cheese are to die for and there's plenty of veggie options for my vegetarian lady. Plenty of meat options to feed my cave man needs. Service is mostly good. It's usually packed but the wait for food is never too long. The beer list is amazing. A ton of choices and good details on their menu. Plus, the staff is knowledgeable about the beer. Hit this spot up when in Old City.

Went last night for the launch of their new menu. Food was heavenly. Highlights were the (chicken) liverace, the octopus and the lamb neck ragu. Only things keeping this from being a five star review are A) the bartender served us two glasses of wine after dinner ($16) and took my $20 off the bar never to return with change and B) the bad acoustic duo that made me want to leave. Not only were they of quite modest talent, but they were way too loud. You don't need a microphone in such a small place, nor do you need to play and sing as loudly as you can. It's acoustic in a small room, it should be at a pleasant level.

I came here with my dear friends and I ate a fish (Pan Roasted Halibut). Yes a whole fish for my birthday dinner after our trip to Aquarium.  Other than my fish, my friends got the Grass- Fed & Pastured Beef-- bunch of meat including a mad huge *rare* steak. It was pure lovely. Apart from the good food, the attentive waiter, Diner also has this cool interior design and cozy atmosphere that I loved. Yes I recommend you try it if you are in the neighborhood. However, be patient for the possible long line!

I had never really had the chance to become acquainted with Mexican food until recently: SF where I had amazing, basic, pared down no-nonsense beauties at Tacquerias in the Mission and gorged on moles/tacos/cemitas for 3 straight days in Chicago. The tacos here have great corn flavor in their tortilla; just the right size; flavorful, wonderful fillings...I will definitely be doing numerous repeat visits. It's a great reliable addition to Chelsea Market, I'm so happy they opened!

Really great cocktails. Food was good but not amazing (we had the burger & the sausage roll). The biggest problem I had was that the menu was not really descriptive, if you are going to add vinegar to your fries or wasabi mayo to your burger, you may want to let people know that. Service was good but also not great.  Place was buzzing though, so that might be why.
The suckling pig was nothing but pork shoulder served rather nicely.

I live close to the city and this is probably one of my favorite places to eat during the summer. My first time here was during restaurant week in Philly with one of my gf. The food is amazing and I love the whole atmosphere of the restaurant. The staff is great and the drinks are incredible! The Shrimp Ceviche, The Pollo Annatto is the best on their menu! This is probably the first Starr restaurant that I like so far. I recommend this restaurant for large groups, or a small date. I took my boyfriend the second time around and he enjoyed it as well. Great menu, staff, and location! Overall, I am never disappointed with this place!

My boyfriend and I decided to try Thai Palace this weekend since we recently tried Thai food for the first time. We walked in and continued to stand at the door, waiting for someone to seat us, for about 5 minutes. An elderly woman with a walker and what looked like her daughter walked in after us. Finally, the hostess came to help us and told us, "They go first," and seated the elderly woman and her daughter. We were a little puzzled since we had walked in before them, but maybe they had put their name in ahead of time or something. A little more explanation would have been nice. We were seated and put in our orders. Our soups came out pretty quickly. I ordered the Thai Chicken Noodle Soup and my boyfriend ordered the Tom Kha Gai. Both were decent. While waiting for our meals, we kept hearing a creaking sound and couldn't figure out what it was. Finally we realized that it was the large picture above us - it seemed like everytime a door opened to the kitchen, the picture would move and creak. Kind of creeped us out a little. Our meals were brought out - Pad See Yu for me and Pad Thai for him. We were both a little surprised, as the portions were a little on the small size. But for $8.95, that's what you get. My boyfriend ate all of his noodles but felt that his chicken seemed a little processed. My meal was yummy and I won the clean plate award this time. While we were waiting for our check, some commotion happened at another table closeby. A group of older people had received their food, and apparently they had ordered something else that was taking a bit longer to come out. The waiter told them that it would be out soon and the crotchety old man said, "Tell him to keep it". The waiter went away and came back 5 minutes later with some type of fish dish that had such a nice presentation - he brought it to the table steaming hot and the shouting began - the man said, "Take it back, I don't want it," and his loudmouth wife has to chime in and yell, "He can't eat it, he can't eat it". The waiter even offered to give it to them for half price, but they refused it. Now...I know that it's poor service to have part of your meal come out later than the rest of it, but if you could see the work that was put into putting that meal together, most people would have still taken it. My boyfriend and I almost told the waiter that WE would take the fish for half price! I was sure to shoot the wife a dirty look on our way out. As for going back to Thai Palace - we would probably go back if we wanted thai but didn't want to drive far to get it. Since we've only had thai twice, we don't have much to judge it on, but I think this place is second best compared to the first place we tried.

I was in Philadelphia for a night, and heard so much about this place, decided to try it out.  However, I have to say I was a little disappointed -- the flavor combinations were a bit off.  The lavender truffle honey that came with our cheese is no comparison to the ground pepper truffle honey I've had at Otto in NYC.  Some of the dishes are gigantic in proportion (like the serrano ham with figs salad, which is good but very basic) and others are tiny.  The only real treat was the crab-stuffed peppers...all the other dishes we ordered were unimpressive and likely replicatable them at home.   Overall, a decent meal, but nothing amazing here.

Jane has great music and the brunch menu offers a good variety. Server was prompt with drinks and after we ordered our food was able to upsell us some 'starters'. We ordered biscuits and cheddar grits - biscuits came out, but grits did not. Followed up with the server and she said she thought we wanted it with our meals - but we wanted it as a starter. Food took a bit of time (half hour) and arrived cool, fries were cold. A bit disappointing because of the wait... Had higher expectations because of the wait time and reviews.. I think service could also use an extra person when it's this busy, as tables could use more attention.
Gotta love their Sicilian slices. Just to have the sauce over the cheese gives it a lot of flavor. Definitely a must go to spot during the summer. Get some good pizza and ices with a warm atmosphere.

OMG, yum! There are so many flavors to choose from (I like the mexican ketchup) and the free samples are generous. My cousin came here from Japan 3 years ago and craved these fries. So when he came back again this year, I went with him 3 times in a week. Which is a lot, when you don't eat a lot of greasy, fried foods. But soooooo good.

At first glance this looks like a totally trap like many of the other places right on Church St. That said I'm sure it can be, but that hasn't been my experience. They have a good beer selection and know how to pour a black and tan which most places fail at. The bartenders are friendly and provide quick service even when the place is very crowded. The best part about this place is the live music. The stage is small and the audience is super close to the bands. They also seem to have pretty interesting local bands play on a regular basis.

Went on Friday night. It's Monday morning and I'm still in pain. Ordered the squid in basil sauce as an entree, something I've had before and know I'm not allergic too. I'll spare you the details but Worst food poisoning in my life. My friend had a spicy noodle entree and he did not feel well the next day either. We split tiger shrimp rolls and calamari for apps. Tons of Thai in the area that not worth going here again.

Refreshing remix to the sardine bar. This spot fewtures several hoppy beers and seasonal treats. Make your own six pack or get a tasty Indian cheeasesteak - yes- tikka masala cheesesteaks, samosas, wings etc. Its all so good. Awesome staff too.

It always pains me to do a review update and bring a place down two stars but I really had no choice.  An amazing beer menu alone, will not keep a place in business and Cask Republic needs to recognize this.  They've COMPLETELY missed the mark during Restaurant Week.  This is a time to showcase the skills of the kitchen, make sure that the staff is on their most attentive behavior and shine so that people will revisit your establishment.  Did Cask Republic miss that meno?  Because after leaving there I felt that Cask went the opposite route and skimped on their food, and gave their best waitstaff the week off because people were only paying $28 for three courses and they'd probably not return. Let me explain.  Restaurant week is for showcasing your food, usually the selections are seasonal and diverse.  Cask Republic was on point with their RW menu but the execution of these selections is what was off.  The sweet potato clam chowder, salty.  The pulled pork spring rolls, oddly indescribably disgusting and the fig & goat cheese salad with grilled onions was weak and by weak I mean it should have had more than two pieces of fig and 3 small crumbles of goat cheese with mesculine greens.  Also, don't advertise that there are grilled onions on the salad if you aren't going to grill them because raw onions are a serious deal breaker for many diners.  Shortly after our appetizers plates were cleared our dinners arrived.  Papardelle pasta, rib eyes and scallops were placed accordingly in front of us.  I don't believe in extreme portions as there is no reason to consume the amount of food that some places give in one sitting however, the petite portions of food that we received for this dinner was laughable.  I ordered the scallops with  butternut squash risotto and was shocked to see a tablespoon of risotto in the middle of my plate with 3 small scallops on the outside of the dish and two stalks of grilled asparagus across the top.  I've ordered scallop dishes from many establishments but have never received any less than 5-6 extra large scallops let alone the 3 small ones that I received here.   The person consuming the papardelle said it edible yet underwhelming and the consumers of the rib eyes stated that it had good flavor however, they expected much more than 3 oz.  Also as a side note, when choosing between the scallops and another dish, the tie breaker was the risotto served with the scallops.  Butternut squash.  It would have been nice to have actually tasted this flavor in the risotto.   After consuming our food, our desserts had arrived and we had a chance to chat up the waitress for a few minutes.  The group that I dined with just so happened to be HUGE Innis & Gunn fans and were surprised to see that it was not on the menu but in the "beer cellar's" windows.  The response from the waitress was "yea, those are for show".  This made absolutely no sense to me but whatever.  Our desserts had come to the table and within 2 minutes we had decided to send back 3 of the chocolate puddings because they were completely inedible.  First, I shouldn't have to cut pudding and second, the chef clearly does not make proper use of gelatin.  This was the stiffest, most odd textured pudding I've ever had.  The two chocolate lovers at the table made jokes about how we would have rather had been served a snack pack.  The waitress upon returning the desserts seemed angered that we didn't like them stating "well, I thought it was good when I had it a few days ago".  I'm sure it was great a few days ago but this batch was disgusting and it's not like one of us sent it back, three of us did, gross. All in all, I like the atmosphere of this place as well as the beer list as it is on par with some of my other favorite beer bars.  However, I may go for appetizers only or skip dinner all together.

A favorite for brunch! Super crowded on weekends so we try to hit up during the weekdays when possible. Huevos rancheros is awesome and the bf is in love with the hot sauce it comes with. Pulled pork tacos get two thumbs up!  Seriously Yum!! Delicious coffee. Wonderful service! This place makes me happy :)

Really delicious!  Burmese food is so good.  We had their tea leaf salad, which was really unique and tasty.  Chopped lettuce with peanuts, it had a sweet and sour taste, very refreshing with crunchy nuts.  We also got their thousand year bread (fried dough, how can you not like it?) with potato curry (curry is key so you can dip the bread!).   We also got their jungle chicken which tasted like key lime pie, creamy good- chunks of chicken in this creamy, lime sauce.  Their chicken curry was pretty good, but would try something else next time- it was just chunks of chicken in a sauce. Definitely try their tea leaf salad and their thousand year bread!!  Their dessert is pretty good too, lots of coconut flavored good stuff!
Paesano sandwich was amazing. So flavorful and delicious. You've got to try the crispy lasagna sandwich with a fried egg. Unbelievable!  They really balance flavors and the bread is soooo good.
i'm from los angeles, i dont think this is a very good take on "cal-mex" food. sloppy, chipotle is cheaper and better. go there. they also dont' have lettuce? the meat is also very terrible quality.

Definitely my favorite Asian food in Orange.  They have great lunch specials too.  I would highly recommend the Chicken Shanghai Noodle Soup with udon noodles and the Szechuan dumplings.  The owners are very gracious and accommodating.  It seems like they use the freshest ingredients and everything is made to order.

The atmosphere is opulent, the food delicious and the drinks superb. The Lounge have real fruit juice in them. My daughter is vegan and they had some very good choices for her; not just salad. You won't be disappointed.

First time at an Indian Restaurant. I ate from the lunch buffet....they had some  choices, it tasted very good..I like that it was no overly spicy. I have had homemade Indian food before and i found it to be too overwhelmingly spicy for me , but this was perfect. Only thing, very very slow service. Only one waiter that day. Even though i did like the selection at the buffet, I did notice they did not have enough vegetarian options for those who do no eat meat. The samosas were delicious as the mango lassi which we got for free for checking in that day. Not sure if I will go there again, I think i want to try a different Indian restaurant to compare.

Ate atTeresa's for lunch on a Friday prior to Christmas.  My friends and I had a 1 PM reservation that we made on open table.  When we arrived at 12:57...there was a "crowd" waiting to be seated.  We were told we would be seated soon and they were "working on it".  Well 45 minutes later and after they seated people without reservations before us we were finally seated.  Needless to,say I give "front of the house" a rating of 1!  No apologies given..not even a complementary dessert!   Onto the food.  Our waiter was pleasant and accommodating...food was delicious.  Had the arugula salad, eggplant starter and the mezzuluna !  Mezzuluna was out of this world!  Would return just for that!  Food was good....would definitely return for the food...but the front of the house needs to get their act together!  Seriously!  Christmas is not an excuse

After reading the reviews of this place, I decided to try it out tonight. I thought it was very good and tasted fresh. My only complaint is that I ordered the Shrimp Lo Mein and though it's delicious there was only like 6 small shrimps in a huge container of lo mein. I had to literally fish around the mountain of noodles to find the shrimp. It would be great if they treated it like their other dishes and gave good portions of the food. Also, the spring rolls tasted like grease and bread with very little filling. I would make those just as fresh as the rest of the food seemed to be.
