Besides that, the customer service was great when I went to pick it up and overall I enjoyed my meal!

As if this place need another high review...but I only must. This place is for the whiskey loving- small kitchen inspired- comfort over white table cloth- pioneers.  The place is small, kitchen is the size of, well, probably my bathroom. The ventilation is not great here, so leave your fur coat at home. There are probably 10 bar seats and 2 large tables for 5, 1 small tables?  Standing around seems to be an option also and welcome. The interior is really causal, wooden panels tables and bar. A divey-feel. Its definitely more a bar than a restaurant.  I didn't noticed a host/hostess. You go in and find your own seats.  The staff are very young and looks like they just came out from an episode of Portlandia. We came here for casual drinks. Vast selection of local distiller whiskey choices. The staff here are super great. They answer the dumbest question without their nose in the air, they would give generous pour and really tried to educate your curiosity.  I've heard the sandwich are great here, (maybe bad ventilation was on purpose), but we can't stand not eating when smothered by the smell of butter and steak.  So we order the steak special of the night. It's no grade A beef, but the meat is locally sourced and I've heard they butcher the whole cow at once. Super fresh and legit. The preparation was simple and delicious. This is definitely one of those neighborhood joint you don't want ruined with  too much publicity.. But goods things happen to good places. I just hope i can to enjoy this place for a few more months before it gets too popular!
Excellent Greek style pizza.  And they serve beer in frosty mugs.  Prices are good too.

I have eaten my share of authentic Mexican food.. but this food made what I had before a joke. The pollo.asado burrito was so fresh and they actually give you a generous amount of chicken and guacamole. I was full and could not stop eating. Well worth the 10 bucks. Will come back to try the tacos.

There is no better place in the country that has a better cheesesteak (fried onions, extra american and mayo). The roll is perfection. The Meat is perfection. The Cheese is....well you get it. The roast pork italian is light years ahead of Tony Luke's and the beef and cheese is just as tasty. There is absolutely zero you could complain about with this place.

Came here for lunch on a weekday, right at 12:01pm, and the place was completely full already.  So I waited about 30  minutes, went in and ordered their regular ramen which was really good! I also got a side of their AVOCADO- SOO FREAKING GOOD!!  They soaked it in this soy sauce mirin marinade, and the avocado was SO soft and flavorful, absolutely delicious!!  I also got a side of their cheese corn, which was a small piece of corn with melted American cheese on top- not that great.

Cute little place - gets 3 stars in my book because we could get a table on a Friday night with a pretty last minute reservation. Portions were small but tasty. I'd go here for a special nice out but certainly not on an empty stomach. That being said, I'd come back here if there weren't too many other options for a nice night out. Ambiance is nice and the outside eating area is pretty cool.

Market Table is no Market Fable! ....That was bad, but I'm still somewhat proud of it. Top. Notch. It's been almost a week and I am still fondly fantasizing about my dinner here. Everything from the crispy jumbo soft-shell crab craftily stuffed with pesto to the angus strip loin over fontina fondue, cauliflower side-dish, bottle of Garnacha, and pineapple upside down cake rocked and shattered my world. My father was also extremely impressed with his creative scallop crudo and tremendous veal cutlets over fava bean puree. The portions were rather large, the service was impeccable, the ambience charming and yet unpretentious, and the location was unbeatable. Carmine Street is a haven for foodies and wine-o's alike. Another note about service - I came here with my father, who likes to make it his personal mission to suck the blood (Russian expression) of all waitstaff anywhere that have to deal with him. He is probably responsible for the resignment of most waitors in the tri-state area. He is that bad. But Market Table -- he loved, and for the first time in his life, tipped 20%. I don't know that I'll be coming back with my dad, but I will absolutely be coming back for a special occasion in the hopefully-near future.
This restaurant is great for special occasion we r vegetarians & they did a very good job for special requests...
brunch was the bomb

This place was just okay. I went with my family. The server was super annoying. She wouldn't leaves us be for more than 2 minutes at a time. Oh and she sat at our table like we were friends. Creeepy.... The food was okay. Nothing to really go on about. It was also a little over priced, but hey I guess you're paying more for the experience and annoying waitress than good food. My opinion: the place is overrated.

A little late in putting in a review for Blue Ribbon.  My friend and I went there last winter and the food there was just AMAZING.  We both loved the escargot.  It's not your usual escargot served w butter.  This came in a rich sauce which we used bread to dip in.  Yumm.  My friend ordered the skate which he loved and I had the paella.  I think the paella was good but I really liked the skate (I had a bite of it). Overall, I think the place is worth every penny.  The only downside is that the seating is a bit tight.  But overall a nice romantic restaurant that serves quality food :-)

I was really excited to try this new addition to the neighborhood but I was very disappointed. When we first arrived the hostess completely ignored us and went to sit another group only to not return for while. We were finally seated by a random server and it was at a high top with backless stools even though there were two regular tables open. It took some time to flag down the hostess, still not at the stand, to request a regular table. Food took FOREVER to come and was cold upon arrival. The portions were small and the food was bland. DO NOT get the french toast burger. I am somewhat adventurous and maybe done right, it could be a good dish but it was terrible. The smoked salmon platter was pitiful with a few small pieces of terrible salmon and some cucumbers. They could learn a thing or two from a Jewish deli. I may give it another try but not for brunch.

I don't review very often, but this time I found it necessary.  We ate here lastnight for my birthday with another couple. Although my husband and I enjoyed our meal, ourfriend had to send his back, and he is not known for doing so. However, my main reason for writing this review is because our party of four was charged an automatic 18% gratuity...and our server didn't bother to tell us or in some way indicate the addition (didn't circle it or anything) . We didn't actually notice until after e were adding our own 20% tip. (Being in the service industry myself, I believe in tipping well unless the server really messes up.) But when we realized what our server had done we all got quite upset. Please understand we would happliy have paid an automatic gratuity...but adding it without telling your guest is simply a sneaky way of trying to get double tipped. It's shady to say the least. And frankly I don't understand why she felt the need to do this on a party of 4 people. Nor do I just blame her...a server cannot usually add an automatic gratuity without some sort if manager approval/override ...I have to wonder what made them think it was necessary in this case.  I've been in the service industry for over 10+ years...mostly high-end...I assure you I know how to behave myself in public and be a good / polite guest.  Management has assured us that this is not their normal business practice and has asked us back. How beever, I don't think we'll be back any time soon.

Get food from the deli. Sausage, egg, and cheese was the move 3 years ago. Buffet is a rip off and super expensive. Cool area upstairs for studying and a quick recluse. Hop out the window to get some cool rooftop action if you can navigate. Otherwise get your $0.99 drink they have to honor and run away from the rest. 3rd star only because they were open 24/7 and that's pretty priceless in a college town. Thanks for the times G'Heav.

Good Cheap Eats China-Town!  You won't be breaking the bank when hungry.  Show up, sit yourself down, pour yourself some water cups are at your disposal.  Then order away.... -I'm a fan of the pan fried hand pulled noodles -Any of the hand pulled soup noodles rock too -Baby Bok Choy with Garlic Every item $7 or less. You can't beat that!
It's definitely not worth all the hype. I've tried plenty of other places that are a lot better than this and the food actually made me very sick the next day

Small, Salty and Oil-laden portions.  This alleges to be a Mediterranean Cuisine in the Spanish tradition.  Rather than the predominant flavors being high grade olive oil and garlic, it's salt and a vegetable oil blend that is certain to make your small portion only a "quick rental".  Sit near the bathroom.  The seafood stew was a ladle of salty, oily broth, devoid of rice or anything to balance the overwhelming salt.  The first time I visited, I did enjoy the paella rice, except for the overcooked seafood that tasted like bait.  The service was very pleasant however the management seemed used to frequent complaints and followed me out seeking feedback.

This place has been our favorite restaurant since my wife and I moved to Rutherford from the west coast. It is home style and very inviting and friendly. Steve is usually behind the counter marshaling the troops and Andrea is taking orders. . charming folks. They have a hard working and friendly crew. ... Javier usually serves us and he is a really nice guy. We usually go to Steve and Andreas for breakfast and we have a blast. The omlettes are great served with toast (I like rye) and potatoes, spiced and delicious. The coffee is always fresh and just the right strength for multiple refills (and they keep em coming) and yes they have heavy cream. The pancakes are somewhere in between crepes and american pancakes.. and boy are they delicious. The pancakes do tend to burn a little so even though most of the people go for the blueberry pancakes, my wife and I prefer the short-stack. Lunch is great. Many of the items are named after customers. My favorite is the London broil sandwich.. it melts in your mouth. My wife likes the steak wrap. But they throw something together if that is what you want.. a BLT or Steak and eggs.. right up their alley. I think they're open for dinner only a few days a week and the hallmark is huge portions. It is mostly Italian fare and I love it. We haven't gone there for dinner enough but we're going to try to :)
Great place. Everything was absolutely delightful - .  food - service - .hospitality.    Takes us back to  Bavaria.  My wife loved the Weiner schnitzel.  Last Stammermax I had was in the Saarland.
The best Veal Osso Bucco I've ever had. Great waitstaff, too.

Great new addition to Hells Kitchen. The beer and bacon sampler was great. The jalapeno bacon was my favorite. We got the grilled cheese and grilled chicken sandwich as entrees. Both were very good. Service was very good as well. We will definitely be back!

This is the 3rd location I've been to (in addition to South Norwalk and Fairfield), and must say this is my favorite based on atmosphere/decor. It's a really cool space. That said, the food itself is almost identical to the other locations. One thing Barcelona is good at is consistency. We split an assortment of 6 tapas that ranged from average to superb. Highlights: blowfish tails, hangar steak with truffle oil, and serrano ham & manchego croquettes. Also, as with all locations, an excellent wine selection with a range of affordability.
One of my fav Italian restaurants in the city. Great pastas and wines.   The decor/vibe is a bit much...loud/busy...but the food/wine/service delivers.

Terrible Service!  The BBQ was good.  The burger, just ok.  A bit bland.  The food was not good enough to outweigh the awful service.  Wow.  We were a ten top in a, relatively, empty restaurant.  I ordered a salad and got it when I was almost done with my meal.  The sides that were supposed to come with the meal came out after I was finished.  Forget about water.  We were eating outside in some serious summer heat.  You had to beg for a water refill.  The server had no idea what came with any of the meals.  One of my friends asked, politely, for the sweet potato wedges he ordered 3 times.  The third time, he didn't want to but I made him ask.  The server said, "we're still waiting," with a bit of an attitude.  She never said anything about the wait before that.  When we asked for the check, we said we'd split it up ourselves but the server insisted on doing it and it took forever.  then she came out and said she couldn't figure it out, so we were back to us doing it.  This whole process took 30 mins, with no water refills.  Terrible.  Of course, she added 20% tip onto the bill, which she would have gotten regardless but did that without a mention.  The time we waited for our food and the bill were ridiculous.   To sum up, BBQ was decent, not great.  Service was some of the worst I've experienced in a while.  Definitely ruined the meal.  We will not be back.

We went in on New Years Eve at lunch with 4 adults and a baby in a car seat. It's cramped for such a group, but they happily accommodated us by storing our bags at the counter. I had the BLT with tomato jam and it was delicious. My daughter had the open faced Black Bean sandwich with avocado and it was also yummy. The cappuccino was perfect. This was my first time there and I was not disappointed.   I can't wait to go back. The service was great as well.

3 of us went to dinner here for the first time earlier this week, on Monday night.  For a Monday night, we were surprised how busy it was, but they told us our wait should only be 15 minutes.  15 minutes came and went, and other groups started lining up at the door, many of whom had reservations, but their tables weren't ready (people were just sitting after dinner and wouldn't leave).  We almost left after waiting 45 minutes but then were finally seated.  Most of those who had reservations waited at least 30 minutes or more after their reservation time to get a table.  The food was decent, but I wasn't as blown away as some of the other Italian places I've been to around Montclair.  The service was awful though, and between that and the wait, it's unlikely we'll ever go back there.  If it was a Saturday night, I could understand, but a Monday??

Just one thing: best huevos rancheros I've ever had! This place is lovely. I love the style, the waiters are usually super nice, there is no more than a 20 min wait and their food is really good. Absolutely nothing bad to say about it.

Just had mother's day brunch here and it was yummy!  We tried most items between the 3 of us (eggs Benedict, bacon, sausage, pancakes, waffles, French toast, blintzes, home fries, penne vodka, Lobster ravioli, assorted fruits and veggies, donuts, cannoli, so many cakes).  We didn't have any of the fish, chicken, beef, or ham dishes.  No particular reason, just went for the other stuff.   Almost everything was great.  The pancakes, French toast and waffles, while delicious, were cold and didn't feel super fresh.  Everything else was perfect. Highlights were the home fries, the pastas, the orange juice, the donuts, and the cheesecake. I would absolutely recommend and go again.

Horrible! I ordered a taco salad to be delivered. It consisted of ground beef (no taco seasoning), soggy nacho chips, lettuce, tomatoes, CUCUMBERS (when is the last time you saw a taco with cucumbers) and NO CHEESE! It was so gross that I threw it away after a couple of bites. I only gave this place a star because they gave a generous amount of this horrible salad and the delivery driver was super nice!

They have been open for only 7 weeks as of end of August 2014, so I can understand how the first review might have been right, but my experience on week six was on the money. On our arrival at the location, we were impressed with the nice clean exterior of the building and colorful outdoor umbrellas in the rear outdoor seating area. There is parking right behind the restaurant. We were greeted and seated right away. The interior has been cleanly decorated with a few authentic touches that let you know this is a Puerto Rican restaurant. If you miss the few family photos, the background music is another clue this Puerto Rican food you are about to eat. The family photos also make you feel right at home. Our server was very pleasant, telling us that she was new to her role and enthusiastically said "we'll work through this together" which we did. It was not any work at all and she did a great job. At one point after we ordered our appetizer, two gentlemen walked out of the kitchen and immediately greeted us. They were the owners. We spent a few minutes chatting it up and they showed us around the place and the seating on the second floor, a good place for a party. We ordered the tasting appetizer which is really big enough for 3-4. It had multiple portions of several things which, unless you're familiar with the food, you're not going to recognize by name, so I won't name them. Let me just say that there wasn't a thing on the plate that we didn't like. The kitchen sent out a coupe other tasters that were not on the standard platter and they were great too. Nothing that was fried was greasy. Our lunches were authentic and tasty, with all authentic flavors done in balance. This is high praise for this cuisine as my wife is a fantastic cook and in the many Puerto Rican restaurants we've visited, she's has never come close to having praise for any of them. Yet this time, she could not stop talking about this place. Her exact words were "they nailed it!" It's a BYO-Wine which is another one of my favorite traits of a restaurant. Don't let the bar fool you, it is just a place to pull up and eat. Good if you're eating alone. Come explore this cuisine done well. We are going back this week with a couple of chef friends. I cannot wait.

I've been to Salt & Fat twice now and both meals were wonderful. The room itself lacks some character (it seems like they didn't bother changing the decor of whatever establishment was there before), but it is more than compensated by the food and service. Here are my personal favorites among the fairly short list of not-so-small plates to share: - Lobster - The pea puree, sweet heirloom tomatoes, guanciale and parmesan crisps work really well with the plump chunks of lobster and create a delicate, sweet combination of flavors and an interesting mix of textures - Uni toast - uni, lardo, enough said... - BLT buns - I still prefer Ippudo's pork belly buns, but these are solid - Oxtail terrine - Crispy outside, very soft inside, complemented very nicely by the onion puree and the mushrooms - Duck breast - amazing! 2 big pieces of perfectly cooked duck breast with sweet lychees, bitter-ish frisee and a great jus I wasn't a major fan of the shaved foie gras (I think the cinammon and bacon overpower the foie gras taste) and the fried chicken (I thought it tasted slightly burned but everybody else at the table loved it, so maybe it was just me or my piece). Service was spot on - both servers were very friendly, relaxed, helpful and seemed to genuinely enjoy working there, which is always a good sign. It's not cheap but it won't break the bank, especially considering the quality. This has already become one of my go-to places to take out-of-town visitors who appreciate good food.

I bought a Groupon for this restaurant. It was pretty standard sushi; delectable, fresh, raw, etc. etc. I don't remembering ordering a lot of food, but it felt like I ate so much. There were also a lot of choices on the menu (always good). I enjoyed the sushi the way I would at most sushi restaurants. I have no complaints and I probably would go here again.

I came here for dinner, but from what I've read weekend brunch is where it's at. The space is very large by New York standards and I thought the decor/ambiance was nice without being distracting. Spanish music is a bit loud, but not unbearable. I had the adobo chicken which was fine, but the potatoes that came with it were really great. The others I went with were vegetarians and enjoyed the tilapia and veggie paillard. The host, waitress, and coat check attendant were all very nice.

disclaimer: i'm not really qualified to write about beer, but this is where i discovered a new favorite wine. if you want an endless list of beer choices in philly, this is the place to go.  seriously, the menu for beer was at least 4 pages long with each option listed in about 10 point font. i'm more of a wine drinker and usually go for a merlot, shiraz, pinot noir or chardonnay.  but after hitting up belgian tavern, my new favorite is the riesling.  yum-my!
Wow. Really yum. Yum salmon salad. Yum eggs Benedict. Ok cheese grits. Homemade biscuits yum. Cool vibe. Q.E.D.

Delicious sushi! I went on a date here for lunch and we just got the chef's special because we figured we couldn't go wrong. It was great! I tried things I wouldn't normally try, and I loved almost everything. Only thing I wasn't a huge fan of was the sea urchin, but that's just not my cup of tea in general. The atmosphere isn't really my type of place, but I still had a great time.

It's not all just hype, the soup dumplings are legit. Had the pork and crab dumplings and they were very tasty, rich flavor... I wanted to order seconds. Not sure why people are raving over the scallion pancake, I didn't think they were anything special. A couple next to us ordered either Seasame or a type of General Tso chicken and it looked so good I wanted to ask to try a piece. Isn't that why there's communal seating? ;)   The communal seating isn't terrible but it isn't a fancy or clean looking place. It's Chinatown.  But the dumplings are def worth a visit.
great place.  fresh, tasty eats at good prices...
yummyyy i love italian..everything! its a fun spot, went for a friends bday and had a good time...good for big groups!
even my white friend likes it! haha..the place is hard to find, but I look for it everytime i am in new york
Nothing bad here!!

Oooooooooooh! Burn me in the arm with a cigarette because this halal spot is nowhere near the best in New York City.     My biggest & pretty much only concern was the chicken's lack of flavor. The taste was reminiscent of boiled chicken; I felt like I was eating a salad. I don't buy Halal to eat rabbit food, I buy Halal for it's greasy, savory, deceptively unhealthy, meaty charm. I don't know why the meat isn't marinated; maybe they're trying to appeal to a healthier demographic. Maybe it's all in my head? No it isn't. I've sampled this spot several times.     Even with their sauces, the food is just okay. But they never give enough yogurt sauce and it takes quite some time for it to actually be absorbed. Honestly, I'd stand in line for just the sauce. This place kind of killed any craving I had for Halal.

I really like this place; it's equally suitable for (a tasty) dinner or just a glass of wine at the bar. The pizza is also really and truly yumtastic. You almost think they're joking with the Gowanus location, though. (The NY Times agrees with me on this, BTW: nytimes.com/2008/03/16/n… ) But hey, they're classing up 3rd Avenue, and I hardly blame them for that. I kind of want to walk down for some pizza and wine now, actually. Maybe I shouldn't have written this and tempted myself.

CASH ONLY.  Meat lovers, your heaven awaits at Modo Mio.  I'm not talking your average carnivore options here... I'm talking about selections like goat, lamb, carpaccio, rabbit, calf's liver and veal.  There are limited options for those who are faint-of-heart when it comes to adventurous foods... but if you feel like taking a chance you should do it at Modo Mio.  They do it right. I was lucky enough to have my first visit just a week or so ago... and it was probably the best BYO i've been to in Philly.  You MUST do the Menu Turista - the portions are not too big and you get to try several things on the menu for a great price.  I believe they change up the menu fairly often, and the selections online don't always match up with the selections of the day.  Ask the server's recommendations - they did not disappoint.

This was the worst customer service I was ever given. We were greeted by a hostile hostess who told us they were not seating until 4. We then made reservations for 4 pm where we waited 15 min once seated and no wait staff came over to our table. The staff was extremely unprofessional, screaming in front of guests and not letting us know they were out of food that we ordered. After the wait staff finally came over to us we received dirty water... As well as 3 other tables. Our food was nothing special and we sat for 10 minutes without silver wear. On top of this experience we were charged full price and no one even apologized that our water was dirty and that they had given us an awful experience. I would not recommend this place to anyone.

Can't keep away and i'm a vegatarian ! The Som Tam ( papaya salad ) excellent ! All tofu dishes A1 :-) best brown rice ever! Nat owner very friendly and eager to make you feel at home ! Home made steamed veggie dumplings !!! Been there sooo many times feels like home ! Lunch, dinner & snacks !

Table 87 is my new favorite pizzeria in Brooklyn by far. As far as the pizza itself is concerned, Table 87's pizza easily surpasses Monty's, Fascati's, and My Little, and I would even say Grimaldi's and Juliana's. However, it is still not as good as Lucali's. That being said, I would go to Table 87 over Lucali's because of its friendly and relatively quick service, and its variety of foods, including pasta dishes, burgers, paninis, etc., two qualities which Lucali's lacks. And even though Table 87 can be fairly pricey, relative to its competitors, its personal pie is certainly cheap, and is the best in the business. On an ending note, I have to recommend the hot soppressata as a topping--after your first bite, you won't want another without it.
This popular, lively restaurant serves good Thai food in a setting with nice decor. The prices are reasonable, and the serving sizes are generous.

Yum Yum!!!  I love their grill pork's feet... it's so good!  The meat will fall off the bone delicious... also they added some new dishes to the menu as I was informed on the previous visit... not sure if the spicy cod roe intestine's was new... but this dish was amazing... really good w/ drinks!  I'm not too sure what the name it was actually called... will def. visit a 2nd time since it was my friends who bought me there and ordered the food... Remember to call and reserve tables in advance as I was told they do not take walk in's!!!!

This restaurant has a minimalist ambiance, but don't let that fool you - the exotic & inventive dishes are delicious here. This is one of my favorite places to eat in NYC. Try the lightly carbonated Nigori sake and the sweetbreads. Yum! I had a great experience with the service and don't understand these other reviews. Apparently hundreds of other people feel the same way because there are always crowds of people waiting outside for a seat, even in the dead of winter! The service was really good to me & my date the last time I was there and we thoroughly enjoyed our experience. I highly recommend this place.

I've been a fan of Walter Foods in Williamsburg for many years, but only started visiting the headquarters this year. I have yet to be let down. My last meal was on this past Saturday evening. Beet Salad. A mound of sumptuous assorted greens with an amazing dressing, and goat cheese to die for. The beats are cut down into slim chunks, so they're easy to divide up across every glorious bite. I wish I had one in front of my right now. Blackened Catfish. I am astounded at how good this piece of fish is at $16. The hot pepper mixes so well with the cabbage cole slaw. The tartar sauce sat on the table next to my plate, completely unused. Why ruin such wonderful flavor? Catfish tasted light and not the slightest hint of brine. Outstanding, especially considering the price.

Came here for a date last week with my boyfriend. The drinks here deserve a 5 star review. I went with this vanilla bourbon drink and it was absolutely delightful. The place loses a star because I couldn't personally find an entree that I would enjoy on the small menu. However, we did order all of the sides and each were amazing. The Brussels sprouts were mouth watering and the sweet potato fries, heavenly. All in all, I had a great date and left smiling. Definitely a cute spot to take your so.

we didn't eat here, just sat at the bar, but the food looked great, all French and very authentic. great lunch spot on the weekends and probally very busy in the evenings. Staff were really cool and friendly, had a real old fashioned , french feel. Call in for drink if you are walking by and see for yourself

Good coffee. great pastries, best bagels and a terrific breakfast sandwich with turkey bacon.  My friends from Israel were very impressed that the staff speaks Hebrew! La Va Cafe took an abandoned old corner in my neighborhood and turned it into a beautiful cafe that has helped transform South Street West.  Recently I met a friend there who asked if he could afford lunch because it looks so pretty - he ended up paying for lunch.  The art shows are always interesting with a young spirit.
This place was delish! The service was fabulous. Dimitri was an amazing server and took great care of us! Definitely coming back here

Living near to Pies 'n Thighs reminds me of when my old office installed vending machines that dispensed coconut M&M's: had convenience not introduced us, we'd never have met. PnT is one narrow cut above fast-food, and accordingly priced: $10-$11 for 3 pieces of fried chix, brisket or pulled pork, one biscuit and a dirty Southern side. The food is dense and heaping. $4.50 buys one (very small) slice of (also quite dense) pie. I wouldn't recommend coming out of your way for PnT - not unless you really, really like fried chicken, and/or feel shameful about patronizing KFC. But if you want to come to Williamsburg to see me, and we happen to grab a bite in the neighborhood, then I can't guarantee that PnT won't happen.

We got a reservation within an hour of when we singed up on Yelp. Started with the stuffed mushrooms, then the salad, and the chicken Marcella.  Our waiter was great. A lot of fun. Food was fabulous with big portions. Don't forget the Oreo, Hot Fudge Sundae.  What a way to top it off. Great location right on Times Square.  Great atmosphere.
Delicious and a friendly owner. He actually sat at a nearby table, talked with us, and gave us free tiramisu

I came to New York with two goals in mind: fit in 7 meals a day and eat at at all the highly rated macaron shops. I was going to turn my week's vacay into a foodie's dream come true! I mainly had macarons for breakfast before I hit up the art museums. Laduree hands down had the best macarons for me. I tasted a few staple flavors like pistachio and vanilla (mmmMmmm my love for vanilla know no bounds!). Other flavors included orange blossoms and violet cassis. The box that the macarons came in were so cute! I didn't have the heart to throw it away. It is also probably why the macarons are so expensive. From what I understand, Laduree has they macarons shipped overnight from their original shop in Paris. You should never have macaron the day that they are made anyways so these macarons are still as fresh as they get! The shell was perfectly firm and textured. Not greasy, not hollow..perfect. My favorite was the orange blossom flavor. Overall, I the flavor of the ganache was very light unlike those macarons from Bouchon (my 2nd favorite). It really depends on your preference. If you want true parisian macarons, definitely hit this place up.

Audrey Claire is a pretty plain Jane. Walking the block on a cold Philly night a BYO was calling. A pregame have you. We entered around five to a somewhat sparsely populated restaurant. The decor on the inside is plain, and you get a fine look into the kitchen. It's pretty intimate, and I enjoyed the look of the bathroom. Although a negative on a cold night, if you are seated by the door, you will not only be welcomed to a chilling atmosphere but also cold food. After our order went in the restaurant got packed. For one I would like to add that our server was out in left field. You could see him texting on his phone and chatting up other servers. By that means the service blew. We nearly had to beg him to bring out our food and check. If it weren't for the attentive host I would probably give this place two stars. So I decided to ordered the seared Brussel sprouts and Grilled Octopus. The Brussels were recommended by many yelpers, however, the chef instead of searing them burnt the oil in the pan, and the Brussels, thus leaving a somewhat foul taste. For the octopus, the serving was generous and tasted good, but mislabeled on the menu. Once furiously cold, due to the door opening and closing, lost most of its yummy taste. Finally, if you are into plating, don't be surprised here. The food is just thrown on a plate. Would I ever come back here? No.... this place is very basic, but I also can't say to avoid it.

My husband and I finally made it over to devils pocket and it started bad but ended great let me explain.  Being business owners ourselves we rarely get out, hence the reason it took awhile to write this review.  We came in a few Sunday's back and originally sat at the bar this is where it started bad.  The bartender I believe her name was Janay? Had an issue with a gentleman who was unhappy with HER service and his wait time.  We walked into this and were ignored as Janay? walked outside to vent about him and then when she returned to the bar continued to complain about the owner and how he left instead of addressing this, never runs the place correctly, ect. (very unprofessional.)  We then got up after being ignored for all of that time to instead grab a table.  We were greeted by Andrea right away and this is when our experience turned right around.  She sat us at a comfortable table where my husband could still see the TV and was on top of our table even though she was busy until the very end.  The food was outstanding, we finished every bite.  If we didn't meet Andrea and move to a table we would not have returned.  She said something when we asked about the business and ownership (curiosity from the bartenders terrible thoughts of him) that had my husband and myself remember why we started our own business in the first place. "That she genuinely cared about the establishment and both owners who were great guys with talent for this, so she works even harder to make sure it does well because it's important to her that you both succeed." We wish we had 10 more just like her at our place.  Keep up the good work! Not many places have great food, great vibe, and staff (minus one) that care more then just about the dollar.  Wishing you all the best!!

This is my Philadelphia staple.  I've paid El Vez a visit the last four times I've been to town and the food never disappoints.   We ordered the basic guacamole, which is decent but at $14, it seemed  bit on the pricey side for avocados.  There are several other guac flavors available but ramp up in price.  There were four of us, so we went with a pitcher of white sangria (available, even though it's not on the menu).  If you haven't been before, and you're a meat eater, I would suggest going with the beef tacos.  The meat comes fairly tender with a nice barrage of toping on three corn tortillas.   The crowd is filled with a diverse group of folks, tourists and locals alike.  I would suggest reservations on Thursday through Sunday.
Went there last night for a birthday. Staff were great. Drinks were great. Food was fantastic. My wife wanted to order the octopus again for dessert. I will be going back soon.

In the midst of my Internal Medicine rotation, I managed to find the time one glorious weekend morning to make it over to Clinton St. Baking Co. for their renowned pancakes. And because it was February, Clinton St. was in the midst of their annual Pancake Month, during which special pancakes are offered each day. On the day when I stopped by, the special was described as "Pancakes with Crunchy Bananas, Cinnamon, Chili, and Chocolate Sauce." If you put bananas and chocolate on anything, I'm sold, so I had to try these pancakes out. The pancakes themselves were quite impressive: a nice exterior that was griddled to a nice crispiness, and an interior that was incredibly fluffy and moist. I liked the fact that there were bananas cooked into the batter and not just thrown on top as might be done at some other places. I would have liked some more flavor from the chili and cinnamon, as neither really came through and seemed to be overpowered by the chocolate sauce and fried bananas. In the end, what really made the dish was the side of maple butter, which was insanely delicious. I would seriously consider bathing in a tub full of maple butter and just lathering myself with it all over, because yes, the maple butter is that good and no, I don't care if you're judging me now. Okay, so the pancakes were good. Really good. But the wait is prohibitive, particularly on a weekend morning. Even if you get there when they open (like I did), the wait can be up to two hours. The pancakes are damn good, but I doubt I'd ever wait an hour and a half again for breakfast. And $15 for three moderately sized pancakes is definitely on the pricey side. All in all, I'd say that it's nice to try out the pancakes from Clinton St. Baking Co. at least once, but I wouldn't go back on a weekend morning. There is supposedly no wait on weeknights, and they have the same menu, so maybe I'll return for dinner sometime when I'm craving pancakes. But until then, I'll probably stick to getting my pancake fix from my favorite diner in Jersey.
Great food, great atmosphere and great service! Favorites: Mint Lemonade, Pork Belly Sandwhich, Fish Tacos
The waffles deliciously good, perfect with fresh strawberries and banana on the side.
Wow. So so so good. And so affordable! This is a perfect restaurant for meeting up with friends and sharing a wide assortment of things. Delicious!
Great staff. Good choices of music. Such delicious food. Everything is great. You wont regret going for brunch or dinner.

please, if you are really looking for a cheesesteak, DO NOT get one from here.  Soggy, gristle-filled awefulness.  There are so many good options in the city- none of which are anywhere near this intersection.

Love this place for its friendly attitude and amazing service - really xceptional waitstaff. When their dishes hit genius level, it's incredible..but everything is great, not a single dud and some dishes I actually dream about! Ha! They could use a little more seasonal menu updating here and there or dinner specials because I live around the corner and would be there all the time if there was just a tiny bit more variety. Overall it's just a really wonderful place to spend time and you leave feeling like you've been with people who care about your experience. They recognized us after the second visit and we always feel so welcomed and fussed over.

Came here for dinner with a group of friends one night.  Was very excited to get a chance to try this out since I have heard loads of good things about it. One of our friends is vegetarian and has a gluten free allergy, so she was very happy to see that they had gluten free bread as well.  I had the Gruyere grilled cheese with caramelized onions, cornichons, and pickled red onions.  The flavors all melded really well together and the bread was amazing.  I was pretty full off half of my sandwich and the salad, but it was so delicious.. I ate the entire thing. I am dying to come back for brunch and try the potato cake.  There wasn't much of a wait when we came for an early dinner around 7pm one night.  The vibe here is great and they have a long list of beer options.  Too many to choose from, but all great choices I bet. Service was attentive.  Everyone was working together and checking on all the tables.  Can't wait to come back and try their Fall menu!

For someone who works in the area stopping by to grab a slice or two would be great but as I walked in, I was directed to a small take out window on the side of the building. I waited and waited until one of the guys in the back "noticed" me. Finally I asked for for 2 slices and they cheaply said we don't do slices only pies... that turned me off at first. Fast forward a week later, decided to give Papa's another try. Phone line was busy for at least an hour, ended up driving over instead. Ordered a small, 6 slice $12 pie. 30 minute wait. Pizza was good at first, quickly became cold and the pizza became tough to chew. Customer service to could be a lot better, especially at the tiny take out window. Be more attentive to your customers and offer slices to a working community.

Today we made reservations for 12 noon brunch however we were delayed in arriving. We called to let them know we would be about 1/2 hour late. When we arrived a bit later then that due to finding parking- we were immediately seated. They were crowed with a long line of folks waiting to be seated. Our waitress was excellent throughout the meal- answering any questions we had. Our food was promptly served- my husband had the fish dish and I had the steak salad. Both were excellent. We also had a side of rosemary fries- perfectly done. I enjoyed a mimosa Cosmo and my husband had about 4 cups of "the best ever" coffee. This was our 4th visit and we were not disappointed. We are now planning our next trip into the city.
Crazy good avocado toast.

I love this place. Hard not to like any restaurant that took the place of a shoe repair. But that's not why I like it. I actually like it, for itself. Because it's awesome. The service is my favorite kind, the kind where they make you feel like you're in their home and they're your friends who are bringing food to you. I'm always a fan of a place where servers and bartenders can wear what they like -  as they would if this what their home. That being said, the food is usually fantastic, great place to come with a date or a friend and order a couple apps, some small plates which can be cheese, charcuterie, crostinis, olives, etc. (5 for $30). The music is appropriate and the ambiance is always perfect, combination of cozy, rustic and chic. The mussels I had last night however were just...bad. Very bad. They were tough, not very fresh tasting and way too powerful. Every mouthful felt like drinking seawater...overall bad. I'd give it 5 stars if not for the mussels incident and if the wine selection was slightly larger, but it's still a favorite of mine!

This is one of the best brunch places in the city. It has such a "home cooked" feel to it, unlike some other brunch places that feel a bit mass produced. Don't get me wrong-- those are great too-- but Penelope feels like it transports you out of the city into a cute little shop with amazing brunch food. You can read the other reviews to find out --- everything on the menu is amazing. You really can't go wrong. But remember to allow 1-2 hours for the wait and enjoy the free coffee while you wait!

Went again today,  the parking lot needs sweeping.  But again the food was great ribs and cole slaw. I didn't eat there because there were some flies outside, but good luck finding outside seating without flies in August in Vermont. Great BBQ .

This place is an ageless wonder! The simplest menu! A very simple concept! Old-fashioned excellence will never go out of style. The onion rings definitely live up to the hype! I ended up having two servings! My burger was cooked to specifications, so there was no problem. The Ice cream was AMAZING! I brought friends and they were all pleased! Everyone ate too much. I'm still stuffed! The missing star is because the table server was not very attentive. I noticed the service staff always has its back turned to the dining area. We had to wave for attention multiple times. Still the server was sweet! Please, do not EVER close!

We adore Taste of Tuscany. We always get takeout rather than eating in. If they delivered we would probably eat their food twice a week or more. My husband has a weekly games night, and they always get dinner from ToT. It's the highlight of my week. We love their sausage and peppers, their pizza is to die for, and their marinara is exceptional. This is not a "date night" restaurant, but that's not the point. They make terrific Italian food at reasonable prices. Highly recommended!

Ordered pork/duck egg congee and clam with black bean sauce. Clam was decent but congee tasted like water and pork was overly cooked and in huge chunks. There is also a forced minimal charge of $8 that you must have. With so many other restaurants around, I would stay away from this.

One of the strangest experiences I've ever had.  From walking over there from our hotel to walking out their front door afterwards, nothing went as expected.   Lets just start with the walk over.  We were passed by a mildly shady man, with a backpack over one shoulder, walking hastily in the same direction we were headed.  Two blocks later a cop pulled over, this man threw his hands in the air, and he was placed in the back of the police car.  Almost no discussion, this guy just knew he was caught.  One of the weirdest things I've ever seen.  Moral of that story, not the greatest area.  Lets just say we decided to call a cab for the way home. When we got there there were already people waiting outside.  After that crowd started to dwindle down I noticed this girl who basically walked in, said hi to her friend who worked there and sat down at the table that was sure to be ours in a few moments.  I became annoyed and stood right at the door so we wouldn't be skipped over again.  Short time later they said they had room at the sushi bar but needed to clear it off.  I don't enjoy sitting at sushi bars because they're small and I am not, but at this point we had no other choice.  Well just as we walked in another table up front opened us and requested that instead.  Problem averted.   Now I was a little perturbed with the situation thus far, but that was all about to change.  Our server was this thin guy with glasses and an afro.  He was our guide through the magical journey that is Miya's Sushi.  I'm going to have to be general with the food because if you've seen the menu they are absolutely insane, but I did post pictures.  We started off ordering a pitcher of one of their alcoholic concoctions, the Kama Sutra (my wife's idea), and it was quite yummy.  While we were debating over appetizers our server asked us if we had ever eaten here before because we had to try the Tokyo Fro.  About a minute later he brought one out before we could even tell him we wanted it.  Holy crap that thing is amazing.  It's a puzzle to figure out how to best eat it (we ended up using our fingers), but that sauce is to die for.  Good call on his part I decided to save the rest of my appetite for my sushi.  I ordered three rolls, but have no clue what the hell two of them were (there's a pic of my plate on here).  Each roll was more unique than the last. The Italian Stallion is the one I do remember and that was just WOW.  So many flavors going on, but that marscapone cheese stole the show.  One of the other rolls was a special with scallops and the last I have no clue.  It really didn't matter what was in there because it was just too good to even think about.  My wife got some roll with cream cheese, peanut butter, avacado?, and honey and she loved it.   Needless to say we were stuffed and highly satisfied with our visit.  Then he brought out the check and it was a lot less expensive than I expected because we got the Tokyo Fro on the house.  As we were paying our bill with another worker who stopped over to take our check, our server (who was super busy) quickly just told us not to leave just yet.  I'm thinking they had to fix the bill or something so we stayed put.  Well a moment later I see him walking out of the back with a huge drink order.  5 beers and 5 shots.  Well guess where he brought it?  He grabs the two guys from the table next to us and says "This is how we do a sake bomb."  It was my first but will not be my last.  What will always set this one apart though is the chili-pepper infused sake which left an amazing heat in your throat after you finished downing it.  Couldn't have wrapped up the night better.  Left about a 40% tip after that.  The walk and the wait were forgotten about.  What an experience.

The food remains three to four stars; it's going down in my book to two stars because of cost and service. My family has been coming for years, and the experience isn't what it used to be. On a recent visit, server was brusque and rushed us through the meal. Our plates were cold in the middle (even the liquid chocolate cake!), like they'd been pre-made and just warmed up. Moreover, the food didn't have the depth of flavor you'd expect given the claimed quality of ingredients. They're just not able to deliver a "dining experience", which is what they're marketing. It's not *bad*, but it is no longer worth the prices they ask. Go somewhere less trendy and give these guys time to recover.

I've been here twice already I will say that I like my first visit a bit better but the second was good. I met the owners. They're very nice people. The fries are pretty good and so is their burgers. I hope they stay in business for a long time.

I give them 4 stars for the delicious pizza.  The service is just okay.  I always find the servers snobby, as well as the bartenders.  The pizza is really good - but you have to like super thin pizza.
the only reason to go to bushwick

Times Square is a black hole for good food, since it typically caters to hick tourists from Nowheresville, who don't know the difference between foie gras and grass.  Fortunately for me, Sake Bar Hagi is only a few blocks away from my office and provides me with reasonably priced pitchers of beer, sake, and superior bar grub.  This izakaya has become a happy hour stand-by for me.  It is the kind of place you'd go to with your friends if you want to get sloshed and satisfy your hankering for salty food. But ever since the NY Times and Anthony Bourdain gave Hagi some love, it's gotten so packed, even on weekdays.  If you get there around 6pm though, there's hardly any wait.  Unfortunately, the service can be slow sometimes -- but it's cause they're busy, which is usually a good sign anyway. RECOMMENDED Most of the small plate dishes are cheaper than yo momma.  Get the fried chicken gizzards, yellowtail collar, sea eel tempura, wasabi octopus, beef liver sashimi, okonomiyaki (seafood pancake), takoyaki (octopus balls), fried chicken, soft shell crab, cod roe spaghetti, and of course, some sake to wash it all down with. NOT RECOMMENDED The bacon salad.  It's as lethal as Chris Brown's fists.

Friday night in NYC and we headed to the " Famous Lombardi's Pizza" The line was long, the wait was long, the place packed to the brim and since it is by comparison the Herald Sq Macy's of Pizza shops I was definitely expecting the pizza to blow my mind or leave an impressionable impact. But there was nothing special for me. Between the large Margarita pizza and the medium vegetable mushroom and sausage pizza they satisfied my hunger but not a hearty delicious craving for pizza. I guess it all comes down to preference of how you like your pizza. I like a lot more cheese than sauce and  a nice medium crust but this place or at least the orders we made were stingy in all areas.

Baby Blues? More like Baby Euphoria! This place is awesomesauce! I went to this spot on a Saturday night and had a phenomenal time. They had a full open bar with a wide selection of whiskey and scotch, which I thoroughly enjoyed. They had several cold beers on tap, but even more beers by the bottle. The bar area was a bit cozy, but the crowd of people was chill and easy going, so it wasn't a big deal. The service was also great. The bartenders clearly know what their doing and the staff is friendly and fun. The atmosphere is really casual and everyone is down to have a good time. Let's not forget this is a BBQ place. I tried some of the brisket and, of course, their wings. Soooo delectable! They also leave a variety of sauces on the table for you to sample and choose. Maybe it's 'cause I'm Asian, but I loved the XXX hot sauce and I highly recommend it if you like some heat on your meat! Other pros: (i) BB BBQ is on OpenTable so you can earn dining points for eating here; and (ii) they have a charging station where you can charge your cell phone for free while you hang out! I don't really like going to University City to drink and/or dine, but with the food and the service here, I'm definitely willing to make the trip. Will definitely come back again!

Most amazing Greek restaurant I have been too. The place is nice and clean and their service is great. The octopus our server recommended was amazing. The eggplant dip is die for. And the best drink ever is the cucumber martini. The who staff is friendly and fun. I would recommend anyway in this area to go to this restaurant!

Disappointed. I used to LOVE their smoked salmon panini, I've had the best one here,  but since when they changed the panini bread, they don't taste the same anymore. The new panini bread is hard and chewy, believe it or not, it really makes a huge difference. This is actually the 2nd time I ordered from them since they use the new panini bread, hoping they might switch back the old bread, but disappointed once again. And the smoked salmon is way overcooked, the perfect one I had was kind of raw in the middle, I just hope they can keep the consistency.

The best fried chicken ever! There's a sweet brick walled back room to savor your meal. Loved the grits, greens and biscuits. Can't wait to try the Huevos Ranchero for brunch. It looks like take-out from the street, don't be fooled, there's room for everyone. It's about time we found a restaurant with great food and no 'tude.

Any restaurant that you can go into at 2 am and get a gourmet meal is fine by me (especially when compared to your other options at this hour)...their fried chicken was amazing, highly recommended, along with the catfish

Great pizza, great staff. The aplomb of how management treats their customers made me a patron for life. That's fantastic news, because their pizza is amongst the most delicious in the city. Occasional colabs with other Philly shops are fun. They do traditional pizza, plain and with customary toppings, and also really unique pieces of pizza art. Thank you Pizza Brain.

Just a local diner located in an airport.  I had a roast beef sandwich with fries. It was pretty good.  Not too flavorful but what do you expect from an airport diner? Service was good but my waitress seemed to be a little bit weird and not too helpful. The other employees did a better job serving me. The menu was similar to a Johnny Rockets or any other traditional diner. Prices were reasonable so that was good. If your a beer drinker,  choices are very slim to nothing, so that was not a good look for me. Overall it's am average place with more to be desired.

This has recently become my new go-to pizza place. I love the fact that they deliver and the service is fast and friendly. Their pies are authentic NJ fare, with great tasty crust.  I love their garlic knots which I always get and are awesome.  I've also had good luck with their subs which were large, well made with quality meats and great tasting rolls.  Lastly, they've been kind enough to throw in an item as a freebie from time to time which I thought was an awesome gesture and has won me over as a return customer.  To be honest, there are a lot of good pizzerias in the area, but Cafe Antonio's good, honest food and fast delivery.... keeps us coming back for more!

I came here with my boyfriend on a Monday afternoon (around 1:30pm) and we were seated right away. The place was a lot smaller than I expected it to be so be prepared to sit very close to the party next to you. The guys making the pizza are at the back of the restaurant and you can actually watch them work with the dough, toppings, and the coal oven which is pretty nice. PRICE - pretty decent for a whole pie, we ordered a small with two toppings and a soda for under $20 PIZZA - I must say that I first experienced the thin crust, authentic pizza at Lombardi's in lower manhattan and expected much more from Grimaldi's. Reading the raging reviews, I thought Grimaldi's might take the lead as my favorite pizza joint but it didn't cut it. The crust was good but the bottom wasn't as crispy as the ones from Lombardi's and the selection of toppings was definitely not up to par with the selection Lombardi's provides. Nonetheless, it was definitely enjoyable on a cold winter day and it was definitely better than a regular pizzeria. Grimaldi's is a very casual and laid-back restaurant and the staff is friendly. All NYC natives should stop by at least once and you can tell that many tourists make an effort to make a trip here as well. However, as we were leaving the restaurant, a short line as already formed outside so I guess we lucked out with the waiting in the cold!

Pros: This NH style, thin crust pizza outside of the Wooster St realm is pretty damn great, and the mashed potato/bacon pie is one of the most noteworthy cuisine items in the New Haven area. Jeff's beers are generally solid. The bourbon selection, though not deep, has a few gems in the bunch (e.g., Blanton's, High West Bourye) that are very reasonably priced. Live music in the front room on Wednesdays is usually pretty listenable. Cons: Parking can be a bitch. The beer lines have a tendency to give the brews a buttery nuance that puts a regular damper on my brew guzzling. The service has been less than attentive at times, but nothing deal-breaking. Awful "house" music is a staple here, attracting terrible club rat types, along with wasting an entire back room for drinking and eating on these "dance" nights. All in all: a very worthwhile dining and drinking experience, so long as you're lucky enough to skip the back room on techno night.

We arrived about 20 minutes before closing and the hostess was nice enough to check with the kitchen that there wouldn't be a problem. We were seated after a 10 min wait and were promptly greeted by our server. We shared the olive/onion appetizer; the olives were large and meaty and the onions were crisp and tasty. I thought the menu said almonds would join the party, but they were absent. As it was later into the evening than the usual dinner hour, we each decided to go with an appetizer as our entree. I went with the wings and a side of fries and my wife went with a salad that contained gorgonzola, pear, etc. The wings were so-so. First off, they were still connected to each other and weren't separated like you would expect. The sauce was a rootbeer-based BBQ sauce, and in my opinion, was somewhat on the weaker side. The wings could have been cooked a bit longer so as to crisp up the skin. The meat was tender and tasty. There were four wings served, for a grand total of eight pieces. The salad, I was told, was decent. The fries were the highlight. Rather, the dipping sauces for the fries were the highlight. The spicy mayo, the ketchup, the rootbeer-based BBQ (better on fries than wings), and some mustard seed mustard. We had fun with the sauces mixing them all up. End of the day, when you take service into account and the ambiance, I was swayed from leaving two stars to three.

We've gone back several times this past year, and have been very well satisfied every time; so there isn't much sense in spending a lot of words on it.   Most recently was last Sunday, and if I could give it a 4-1/2, I would.   As before, we found the service to be competent and correct;  we told the servers that we were in no hurry, and they paid attention, bringing the courses as we wanted them -- there was no sense of "eat and get out".   The food was excellent, certainly as good as one would get at any upscale bistro in Manhattan.  The portions were large, and while the prices are a bit high for NJ, this is, after all, Montclair, and as I've written before, you don't get this quality of food for cheap.  And the place is BYO, so you'll save a few bucks on the wine. The parking  situation was a bit better than usual -- maybe because it was Sunday -- and I was able to park only about a block away.  And there IS a muni lot around the corner from the restaurant. I asked whether cassoulet would be back on the menu when the weather cools down, and was told "yes".  I don't think I'll wait that long before our next visit. If I could offer one suggestion for improvement it would be "get an espresso machine".   I really missed my cafe filtre after dinner.

Consistently good.  Really solid beer list.  High tops in the front, nice bar in the middle and dining in the back.  There's also outdoor seating when the weather's nice.  I typically get the maple wings which are great and I rotate between the hamburger and pork chops depending upon how hungry I am.  The hamburger and pork chops are excellent.

Best sushi in NJ. I felt like I was in Japan for an hour. Great service. Nice people run this place. Creative presentation and "beautiful food" (as the lady with me said over and over.) Want good caviar but are not rich? Go here. All you need to know about caviar to enjoy it here, is that the pink one is the salty one and the orange one is the unsalted one. You don't have to speak Japanese either. Just point at the pictures and tell them how many. They let you use a fork too.

Mouthwatering veggie burger! It had feta, tomato, cucumber and the tzatziki sauce was oozing out- still thinking about it  2 days later :).  My husband had the fish tacos- not as good as the veggie burger but still  tasty.

So I finally got to taste this pizza and it was well worth the wait (which I confess was a bit long).  But I would do it again.  Pizza done to perfect with succulent pepperoni.  I will be back for sure.  Again and Again and Again... Loved it.

So the wife and I had to kill some time between a wedding ceremony and its reception not long ago and while we battled afternoon traffic trying to figure out where to spend this unexpected amount of free time Sara tells me about this place she went for a work lunch the other week. Being only a short distance from the reception hall I figured why not. Now when we walked in we were duded up nice. Me in a suit and tie and Sara in a very pretty dress. I thought we were gonna be way too over dressed for an after work/weekend hangout spot. Actually I thought we blended in very nice. The marble topped bar and dark wood decor kept the place looking classy while the wait staff in black or white collared shirts and jeans kept things casual. The wine list looked killer and even though I was not in the mood for wine I did see a couple of options I wanted to try. I had a specialty manhattan which was ok. Then I had the barkeep mix me up a good ole manhattan which was MY-T-fine. Glad to see that bartenders are still skilled at making the classics. I'm only giving three stars cause I didn't partake in the full experience so next time I'll hit it up right and give a full review.

Some of the best thin crust pizza you can find in northern New Jersey. So many different toppings to choose from to make a good pizza. Nothing too special about the drinks to pick from but the bar is a nice place to sit and have a drink while waiting. Whole wheat pizza with sausage and onions is awesome. As is the white pizza with spinach. Probably my favorite that I've tried thus far. Their appetizers are just as good. Highly recommend the blooming onion. And ask for extra sauce, that stuff is awesome! The only downfall of this place is it gets crowded fast. They don't take reservations so if you want to sit down at 6:30 get there an hr early to wait on line.

Over the course of the years, I have heard many things about the different Shake Shack's in NYC, yet never got around to trying them. Luckily, they decided to open one in Philly, so I could skip the trip up north. There has been picture after picture online of people waiting in long lines to eat at the new Shake Shack in Philly. Apparently these were all for lunchtime, as when I went here for dinner, there were only 6-7 people in front of us. There was a woman handing out menus (which seemed unnecessary with such a little amount of customers in the restaurant, and with the menu posted humongously on the wall). Ordered a ShackBurger, Shack-cago Dog, fries, and a Peanut Butter milk shake (don't worry it was between two people)/ The burger comes on a potato bun, and I am not impressed with it at all. By far the worst part of the meal. If looking for a quick burger go to 500 degrees or Starr's Square Burger instead. It tastes ok, but is also super small. The Shack-cago dog was much better, with the frankfurter having quite the snap to it, and covered in your typical Chicago-style hot dog toppings. Fries were the thick crinkle cut, that look like they come from the Ore-Ida freezer section. Despite my prejudices for these type of fries, they were still rather tasty. The star of the show was the Peanut Butter milkshake though. I would definitely come back here to sample some of their other frozen goods. They have quite the list going with delicious sounding mix-ins like Truffle cookie dough, and termini bros cannoli shells.

Im new to the area, so I have to try out the restaurants in the area, and boy was I disappointed by this one. I ordered the Chicken it was flavorless, the beans tasted like they came out of a can ,and the Plantains were not fried fresh, they tasted as if they had been laying around a while. and the rice was just bland....I was disappointed. Coming from New York were expectations to high? No.... all I asked for was flavor, and they would have a regular customer...I guess not.

Went here for a special weekend with my parents.  They absolutely loved the place!  Good food, good drinks, great atmosphere! The only issue was the service.  It took a while to get anything we asked for and it wasn't particularly busy. I will definitely come here again though!

5 stars for ambiance! Great intimate date-friendly restaurant in the Theatre District. It's a favorite for theatre-people and is great pre or post-show. Intimate dim lighting. Cute bar with a pub/cellar vibe, complete with friendly, chill bartenders. Not too formal, but not too casual either. Coat check is available and she is very friendly, as is the hostess. They accommodate very well at this joint! It is intimate and away from the touristy trash down the road. Also, celebs often frequent. Service is very friendly and very attentive. They answer questions about menu and dishes very well and make great recommendations. The menu is very simple so if you don't like anything on it you're kinda screwed, and the only thing I order regularly is the cheeseburger with fries. It's an NYC-theatrical institution and will always be a recommendation by the wait staff there, definitely not the best in town, but very good. The meatloaf is also good. The other sandwiches seem dry from personal experience. All prices reasonable (2 $-signs in my opinion). Excellent dining experience for a couple looking for a cuddly candle-lit quiet night out, or a small group. Intimate, delicious, non-pretentious, convenient and cozy!

I use to call this "crack pizza" because it is addictive.  I was going once, twice a week for awhile, and even now we go at least once a month. I lived in Italy for a year and I'm from NJ, where we have lots of Italian Americans making top-notch pizza with family recipes from the homeland. This is one of the best pizzas I have ever had in my life. Thin, thin crust, yummy chunks of tomato and perfect cheese. I'm an athlete and I need carbs, but no one wants too many carbs - I have never gained weight from my frequent trips to DeLo's. We are all pretty greedy about our DeLorenzo pies in my family, usually we each eat more than a half pie. My boys go for pepperoni, I go for plain. For lunch I'll eat an entire "small" which is a few cm less in diameter than the large.   Other than pizza, there are delicious salads, the heirloom tomato being ridiculous.  (Good). There is no dessert.  It's byob. There is birch beer and other soda, by the glass or pitcher. I disagree with any reviewer who says the waiters have attitude or rush too much. There can be quite a wait to get a table, but everyone is agreed on it being worth it. Go for lunch if you can, there is never a wait then. Closed Mondays I believe, and no lunch on weekends.

Supper was definitely one of the highlight meals from my trip to Manhattan. Sadly though, I can't remember what exactly I ordered. I just know that it was GOOD! Must-get appetizer: Grilled Polenta with Gorgonzola. Simple, yet utterly delicious. I am so stealing this idea. I know I ordered a veal special, I'm not sure what else it came with. I want to say that there was duck AND prosciutto invovled, but that's a lot of stuff going on. Maybe it was just duck? It was definitely yummy. Not a whole lot of food, but I was satisfied nonetheless. Cousin Jess got the Orecchiette Bolognese, which was also a great chioce. The little ears of pasta hold the sauce well, and mmm, that sauce is on point. Basically, their specials are killer! Couldn't tell you what the other two ordered. Sorry. The Hazelnut Panna Cotta for dessert was mildly disappointing. The Panna Cotta was great, but when they say drenched in chocolate sauce, they mean it.. Totally smothers all the other flavors on the plate. Very friendly staff and charming ambiance. It can be loud next to the kitchen, but watching the chefs go at it adds to the experience. The back dining room has a more reserved feel. Oh and the narrow booth next to the kitchen where we were seated is more suitable for a cozy 2 instead of the 4 of us, and we're relatively small people. There's also outdoor seating (I assume for brunch and/or warm-weather) and a cool bar next door so you can booze it up while you wait.

Service was extremely slow for an uncrowded Saturday afternoon.  We sat at the bar and only had drinks.   The cocktail list was creative and the menu looked great, food-wise.  We'll probably be back to try some bites - hopefully they'll figure out their service by then!

Went here for lunch with a couple of friends and we were pleasantly surprised!! We all got a lunch special entree, which came with soup and a huge portion of food for under $10!! I got the egg drop soup and the chicken with cashews with fried rice. The soup was delicious.  The entree was great as well. Although the chicken portion of the dish had too much sauce for my liking, it was still good and the rice was very yummy. I had to take half of it home they give such big portions!! We ordered a California roll to share, which was delicious. They also have a bowl of crispy noodles and duck sauce and a hot pot of tea and teacups on the table, which was a nice touch. The service was great. We were greeted and seated as soon as we walked by the people working at the front at the registers. Our waiter was very friendly and our food was brought out quickly. The restaurant is big and pretty clean. The menus, however, were sticky, and a couple of other things around the restaurant looked like they could use a wipe-down, but nothing horrible. We will definitely be coming back!!
Nacho, and chicken quesadillas.... Yum. Service is nice friendly bartenders.

The deli is amazing! food is always fresh, and the people are always friendly. If theres something you want thats not on the menu, they will do their best to make it up for you. Ive been to the restaurant next door, and for the price, the deli food is more bang for your buck. Also when the power goes out, they are always online!!

Thank Goodness for the Groupon discount! Still spent additional $100 on top of the $70 for $120 deal. I'll tip my hat off to their freshness. The Hamachi melts in yo mouf! Although their sushi is fresh, Zento is quite too expensive for their serving sizes. $8 for a hand roll that you can devour in a single bite is ridiculous. Oh. Don't get the Ramen. I was just curious toward the end of my meal, and you really just need to order the sushi! The ramen noodles were too thin to be ramen, and the broth was more on the salty side for my palette. Also, appetizer Calamari was also too breaded! Not enjoyable.

I wish they still had the cash payment no tax because it use to be super cheap then. Still very reasonable and probably some of the most authentic Korean food in midtown, even with K-town so close. It's a little hard to find as you have to go through a corporate building to get here and past the freight elevators. The sign isn't exactly large either. While the offer American deli selections, stick with the Korean food. The bulgoki is one of their best dishes but their specials are also great and well priced.

This place is by far one of the better and more interesting dining options in the neighborhood. I seriously could not stop saying wonderful things about my experience in the 48 hours after my meal. There was a 50% off Scoutmob coupon (up to a $25 discount), so for whatever reason this doesn't give me extremely high hopes for the food - but it exceeded my silly/unwarranted expectations. We shared the truffle mac and cheese which was rich and flavorful but a bit too loose/watery for my taste, still a decent dish. We did family style for some entrees - fish and chips, seafood risotto and chicken parm. The seafood risotto was great, the fish was fresh and cooked perfectly. The fish and chips were pretty delicious, not the best I have ever had - but compared to the other places in Gramercy that serve them I'd put them high on the list. What shocked me the most was the chicken parm, it was delicious and I have high standards for dishes with Italian origin. The pasta underneath the chicken was in a creamy white wine sauce that was so tasty, I liked it better than the traditional red sauce soaked pasta that's typically underneath parm. The service was excellent, our waiter was working for the first time but was so friendly and accommodating. The only complaint I might have is that the space is small and tight, and it was a Friday night so it was packed, wish there was more space to eat/wish it were easier to here. Overall Ponty Bistro is that restaurant that you'd take Mom and Dad to when they are in town, or bring a cute date out for a not-so-typical meal. I will definitely return!

Saw this truck parked near Old Slip Park in the FiDi one day and since I was in need of a new lunch spot decided to hit it up. I saw a decent line forming outside of this truck at about 12:30pm and was curious about the small buzz developing. I did some research on Yelp and the next thing I knew I was at the front of the line ordering. I gave the Lemon Chicken Cous Cous a try. I'm not an expert on Cous Cous, nor do I prefer it over rice, but since I rarely eat it I thought why not. The order came in a huge aluminum tray, reminiscent of the The Halal Guys truck trays. Unfortunately, the tray was not filled to the brim, but the serving size was more filling than I anticipated. The order included lots of cous cous (as it should have) and chicken. Sides inside the dish comprised of large chunks of potatoes, carrots/yams and chick peas. The cous cous, potatoes and carrots were good, but the lemon chicken was a disappointment. I felt like I was eating a regular chicken and rice dish substituted with cous cous instead. The chicken was pretty much like halal meat and did not have any lemon flavor or sign of seasoning. As I said disappointing, especially at $9! I'll probably have to give other dishes a try from here, but at the steep prices they are selling them at it's hard to want to come back after a letdown like that.

Very conveniently located for me, just about a 10 minute drive. Love the atmosphere, the quirkiness, and the chalkboards all over the place.  It feels very home-y inside, very cozy.  I've been several times before, but most recently went this past weekend because I'd been craving the tomato soup with grilled cheese croutons! Always spot on.  I definitely over-indulged this past time because not only did I have the soup, which is a meal in itself, I ordered the veggie burger also.  I told our server to surprise me with the side, and she chose onion rings.  Perfect! I was only able to eat a few bites of my burger, but took the rest home and had it later, and it was just as delicious.  My friend had a chicken cutlet sandwich, which he said was one of the best he's had... even though I don't eat meat, it looked phenomenal!  I have tried several things on the menu, but never had breakfast, so I think my next trip to the Spicy Green Bean will be for that.
Rex is the best coffeeshop in the neighborhood. Great coffee, great pastries, and great place to get some work done!
Fajitas and Abita!

This is our go to place for local pizza and we recently tried Lebanese style food.  Ali, the owner, was enthusiastic and informative about the platters.  Chicken kabobs were great, the rice was very good and the vegetarian platter was an excellent change of pace.  We will likely order the middle eastern style food again.

This was a friendly warm and cozy cafe with fantastic service.  We all ordered the big breakfast and the bacon was the nicest I have had in a while with perfectly poached eggs.  Coffee was quick to arrive and had a mellow flavour and I love it when you get to enjoy your coffee first then food arrives after.  We are from New Zealand and this was our first morning in New York so thanks for making it such a cool start.

Came here and tried 4 different types of burgers - Truffle burger, Umami burger, 5 spice duck burger and the seared tuna burger. Were the burgers tasty? Yes. Were they on the small side? Yes. Were they worth coming back for again and again? No. Out of the 4 burgers, the truffle burger was the all around favorite. The Umami burger was just eh. The duck burger looked promising when it came with fried crispy skin pieces sprinkled on top, but was disappointing when you ate it. The seared tuna burger was just fine too. We ordered fried pickle spears as a side too. The app only came with 4 spears - so small! And on top of that, all the crust fell off with the first bite. There are much better fried pickles pretty much anywhere else. This place may be worth trying once, but have no urge to run back there any time soon. There are bigger, better, cheaper burgers all over the city. Shake Shack anyone?
