All though the drinks were a reasonable price the waitress asked if we needed anything else we said another round of drinks and she never came back at all. We started buying our own drinks at the bar. Also, they did allow some really rude and intoxicated people to scream at the top of their lungs "everyone get the F*** out" numerous of times. As a first time experience I will never go back to that hassle. I want to go to a place where civilized people go.

Barrio Chino embodies all the reasons why I am simply not cool enough to hang out in the LES. I dropped by on a Saturday evening after catching a show at the Rockwood Music Hall and its patrons were spilling out onto the sidewalk. Hipsters and impossibly trendy folk chowing down on delicious Mexican fare over salt-rimmed margartias and caiprihinas. A Nigel Barker lookalike will take your phone number and give you a ring when your table is ready. I took this moment to drop into Earnest Sewn across the street and marvel at the overpriced denim. There was a brief 20-25 minute wait and we were seated at the bar, tucked away in the corner. I took a moment to take in the minimalistic decor, the Chinese laterns and adorations strung across the room, the chill and hip atmosphere, and the open kitchen producing plate upon plate of Mexican edibles. I ordered the caiprinha and fresh lime margarita. Both were expertly prepared and decidedly strong. After sucking two of these down, I was pretty much prepared to go barhopping on Rivington. We ordered the Platos Mexicanos which is a sampler of several dishes on the menu. This isn't your TGI Fridays appetizer sampler. This dish comes chock full of grilled steak, guacamole, Mexican cheese, chorizo, and black beans. Alongside, we ordered the pork and steak tacos which were absolutely flawless. The meat was tender and flavorful, topped with citrus and onions. Fresh corn tortillas were served alongside this meal which were quite handy for mopping up the homemade guacamole. I also found the cactus and shrimp salad to be quite tasty despite the lack of swine (kosher friendly). See, not all 'scenes' are full of pretentious hipsters in fedoras and leggy aspiring model/actresses. Once in a while, the food impresses and not just the crowd.

I pass this place on my way to work every week, and I looked up reviews and they were all dynamite.  I decided to stop in tonight; I'm eating a falafel sandwich as we speak.  And I don't want it to end. FREAKIN DELICIOUS.  The sandwich is huge, scrumptious, and well worth the inexpensive $6.  There's flavor in every single bite.  EVERY.  SINGLE.  BITE.  Unfortunately they were out of the latkes, but the nice guy behind the counter recommended the stuffed grape leaves which were delicious. New go-to spot for sure.

This place was really great, I came here with two Serbian people in the group and they assured me the food was spot on authentic (I truly believed them considering how few tables around us were speaking English!) The smoked meat platter and cheese platter were a fantastic start, that "appetizer" spinach pie ended up being my whole entree, so good and so huge! My friends ordered pork shoulder, chicken kebabs, and "Karadjordjeva" which was a thick pork & cheese schnitzel thing... all of it was fantastic! Will definitely go again!

I agree with Keith R.  as far as tapas in Philly, this may be one of the better restaurants since I'm comparing to those tapas restaurants in the SF area. Fun, happy, hip and great to come with friends.

Let me preface this by saying that I went here with a party of 25..... the experience may be different with a smaller group. We made reservations, but it still took them 10 minutes to seat us.   OUr waitress was OK considering the size of our party.  She got everyone's orders right and was very patient. Took a while to get our drinks.  But when they got there, they were good! It was about 1 hour before our chefs got to the habachi tables to prepare our food.  Again, I'm assuming it was due to the size of the group.   He served our rice first, then our meat/fish.  By the time the veggies and lo mein were served, I was done with the rice and my fish.  The order of it seemed odd to some of us.  I found the food to be a bit salty.  They put soy sauce on everything they prepared some most of the items had the same taste. Some complained (to us) about the charges on the bill.  Seemed pretty average to me -- about $25 per entree and $6 for cocktails.

A must for Falafel lovers.. and those looking for an alternative to greasy pizza at 3am.  If the line's out the door, don't be discouraged - it goes quick.  Just amuse yourself with people watching.. or overhearing interesting conversations. Falafel sandwich with no tomato is my favorite.

Extremely overrated oily Pizza. Soaked my paper plate completely. if you absolutely LOVE dripping Pizza- then this is your place. Oh, and the waiting time- is phenomenal.- come early in  the AM, to be able at lease see the counter in the PM.

On first look, the Riverside Grille Bar and Grille in Clifton seems to have an identity crisis.   It's part sports bar, part local hangout for the older crowd, part late-night hotspot for the younger crowd.  One corner is something of a quiet dining area for families and couples, while the other end is for dart games (with a growing following).  Oh, and then there are the private catered parties.  Plus poker night and trivia night.  Occasionally they try to squeeze a live DJ or a band into the dart area. The owners, Joe and Frankie, are trying to shoehorn a lot in here; the Riverside is comfortably sized but not all that big, and is not divided into rooms.  It tries to offer "something for everybody".  But there are times when things don't mix all that well.  As some other reviewers note, the bar area can become quite noisy even with just a moderate crowd.  And the staff sometimes turns the music up too high, to make things even worse (unless you enjoy a nightclub-at-midnight atmosphere).   They sometimes close the place for a few hours for a private party; at other times you can still get in, but unless you thrive on that nightclub atmosphere, you might not really want to.  And when the dart games get hot, watch out when trying to get to and from the men's restroom! So yes, in a way, Frankie and Joe are trying to do many things not always entirely well.  And yet . . . I keep going back.  There's a certain charm to the Riverside, despite the occasional annoyances.  It's the kind of place you can build a relationship with.   A lot of the people there on any given afternoon or evening are regulars or at least occasional repeaters.  And the regulars and repeaters are a nice mix of young and old, male and female, working class and professional, with racial and ethnic diversity to boot.   The staff and the owners honestly do their best to make everyone feel welcome if not always completely accommodated (if you are aren't in the mood for a public-addressed trivia contest, don't go on trivia night).  The menu is nicely varied and prices are quite fair (even a vegetarian like myself has several good choices here, even if the Riverside is not usually thought of as a hangout for finicky health fanatics).  And the food is quite decent and consistent.  You won't have a memorable dining experience, but neither will you have a regrettable one.  There are usually blackboard specials that generally are in the realm of "comfort food", e.g. beef stew or sausage and peppers. If you don't know the area, the location could seem a bit out of the way, wedged in with the Passaic River and a major highway (Route 21) on one side, a residential neighborhood to the north, and an industrial park to the south.  But the somewhat remote locale can work as an advantage also; the Riverside's parking lot is fairly large, and additional on-street parking is easy to find and not far from the door.  Your first experience at the Riverside may or may not impress you.  But I'd recommend that one way or another, you give it another shot.  If you are a nice person yourself, the place tends to grow on you, because a lot of other nice and unpretentious people spend time here (and the staff are also nice people).  If you can put up with good food and drink and decent prices and some occasional inconveniences, this could be your kind of place.   Despite the Riverside's mixed identities, it's true and honest feeling usually shines through -- a nice place where nice people break bread and share some time together over a drink (and maybe a football or baseball game).

YUMMY: BONE MARROW IS AMAZING..melts in your mouth. Oysters were very good, we also got claims.. :) I got the catfish which was well cooked..i wish it was thicker and less cooked, and then my friend got the steak. Depending on if you like it more burnt on the outside you should be aware it was very crispy. It was def a late night bar atmosphere, there was basically no line on sunday evening but filled up around 7pm. The service was pretty fast, the waiters should have been able to give more recommendations in my opinion, and the old fashion floor (thus tables tilt back and forth) was a bit too much.

really enjoyed my brunch here with my girlfriends! the food was delish, the mimosas flowing (though more champs, less OJ would make it perfect!), the owner delightful, and the server a hoot. we had a blast!

Love the food, and like most patrons, the grilled corn is amazing. The prices are great. Very cheap for NYC and portions are a generous size for the price. I came often when I lived in New York and go whenever I visit.   The reason I can't give it 5 stars: Due to it's popularity, the place is overcrowded. By way of illustration, imagine the inside of the Manhattan bound A train on a winter day, an incoming blizzard, and JFK and LGA just closed.  Yes, it can be that packed. Expect a 1-2 hour wait. The tables are small and packed next to each other in a very small restaurant (typical Manhattan sized apartment) and you are most likely to eat sitting ON strangers.  Worth it? At least once.  Don't be surprised if you're eating across a celebrity. I ate across from David Duchovny with family post-but-recent sex scandal. Awkward!

Must. Get. More. Buns! Best ramen I've had in the city and hands down the best pork buns around. Just go. Get the pork buns and the Karaka  Men spicy ramen you won't be disappointed. If you don't like spicy, order the Akamaru Modern. Full of flavor and delicious. Adding the soft boiled egg is a must. Absolutely worth the 1 - 1 1/2 wait.
A can't miss if you have time in Philly.
Went there for my bday The food was good tasty nothing crazy amazing. But I will go back bec I didn't try the chicken and waffle

Pro: The ambiance was beautiful~ a lot of rose, you can smell them even in your seat. good spot of dating or to impress your mate. very romantic ~ con: food was over priced. especially the $100 steak. Please avoid that. if you are a foodie, this is not the place.  to impress your first date, definitely Yes!!!!

After a long time and only an OK experience, I finally ventured back to Sampan since my friend wanted to go for his birthday. Wow! What a difference a few years can make!! The food and drinks were great!! My friends and I were really hungry (i.e., greedy) that night so we ordered way too much food, but none of us regretted it at all. The birthday boy enjoyed his leftover for days! Just a quick run down of what we ordered: Apps/Small Plates: Edamame Dumplings Shrimp and Lobster Dumplings Crispy Rock Shrimp Crab Wontom Tacos Calamari Salad Mains: Beef Short Rib Shrimp Pad Thai Kimchee Fried Rice Roasted Broccoli (side) Did I mention it was only 3 of us!?!? LOL. Everything was fabulous but I highly recommend the crab taco and the beef short rib. Service was good and the place was packed. Will def go back in the future and I'm glad I decided to give this place a second chance.

My Dad grew up in Northern Jersey and talks about Rutts Hut to this day. He took me there when I was a little boy and I've been back 2 or 3 times as an adult. I don't know if it is the atmosphere or the hot dogs or the family history... maybe a combination of all three. But I really can't speak highly enough about Rutt's!

Well I usually love this place but unfortunately my last experience was exceptionally bad. I was there around 6 on Sunday and the cashier was amazingly rude. just absolutely atrocious. While waiting for my food I over heard more gossip about her co-workers than a high school gym room. I love the food here but seriously, I don't need to be part of whatever the restaurant has going on behind closed doors. I had a couple questions about my sandwich and was met with a combination of general uncaring and felt like I was being almost yelled at. Ill be sure to avoid her from now on. Wish there were two different rating scales on here, one for food and one for service.

Great service, Great food, Great vibe.  That's all I ask, and they nailed them down as they could.  It absolutely made my evening.  I am going back for any chance I get. Make sure to sit at the counter.

My sister and I went here for lunch and while the food was wonderful, the service was not good. She never checked in with us and was very hard to find whenever we needed anything, from drinks, to plate clearing, to getting the check. She ended up forgetting our drinks and brought them out at the end of dessert. I think the problem with the lunch in general was an overly full house as the courses took too long to come out, and they assigned too many tables to our server. I would not come here again for lunch.

I really like this place, I think the food is very delicious. Every time I go there, I am seated right away. The chips are very good and fresh. All the staff are very nice. The food is delicious but I think it could use more flavor. The price is good, definitely a good place to go.

I came with a large group of friends for dinner. They sat us in the back at two tables separated from the other patrons, which was a good move for them (it let us do our own thing without disturbing anyone else), and also felt like more of a private dinner. They set up a fixed group menu, and everything that came out was delicious. The drinks were also great (the spicy margarita), and service was excellent. Only downside was that it was pretty expensive, but given the quality no one was complaining (and when you keep the liquor flowing, you only have yourself to blame).

Might be my favorite restaurant in Astoria!  This place is fantastic.  Although its very busy and you usually have to wait a while.  The fish is very fresh and cooked to perfection.  I had the red snapper and it was excellent.  The lemon potatoes were great also.  The typical Greek complimentary was very good.  Very nice service, they asked if it was our first time there because they did not recognize us.  It was our first time there, and they said it in a nice way, implying that they know everyone who eats here because they all become regulars.  After that first meal, i will become a regular also.

Great American food in an old fashioned soda shoppe. The food is very "American" and home style. The place is in an old soda shoppe and it has a great atmosphere. It is on a really great street in Montclair, NJ. You'll really enjoy the experience.
The breakfast was above average.  The cheesecake was at best average.  I thought the cheesecake would be a lot better!

Yum! Fresh, fun food that feels pretty healthy. For lighter meals, the Chicken Souvlaki or Bulgur Fritter are fresh and filling without being overwhelming. The Sheep Milk Ravioli is small but melts in your mouth. The Swordfish was ok but not as flavorful as the rest. The Chocolate Mousee and Halva was amazing -- rich and decadent. Definitely share!

GREAT PLACE!  Fantastic food. (Gruyere Panini for me please!!)  Even better service. And I am a huge fan of their beers.  Evan is always changing out their brews for new flavors!  Great seasonals!! My favorite  spots in the Princeton area
Some of the best fries in New York.  Definitely worth checking out.  Only four stars because the line is way too long on a friday or Saturday night.  I say stop by during the week.

This is perhaps the first or second review I've ever written on yelp and I've been on yelp for a while. Yerba Buena is one of the most amazing meals I've had in a while. The drinks from the bartender were delicious and the food was phenomenal. My friend ordered from the restaurant week menu (fish tacos were melt in your mouth good, I didn't try much of his skirt steak to give an opinion, and his crepe dessert was delish). I ordered these cheese/jalopeno croquettes, they're like adult cheese balls but fried with gooey cheese in the inside. My salmon was perfect. This place left us speechless and on cloud 9. The manager of the place came by to check on us and the rest of the tables too. Thank you Yerba Buena!

I read the yelp reviews before coming here and I have to say it made me a bit nervous since there were great reviews and not so good ones. However, I decided to try it anyway and that was a great decision! The food, atmosphere, and service were all great! I went there on a Tuesday night and couldn't have been better received. The place wasn't too packed so there was a lot of attentiveness without being annoying about it. Oh and the drinks were on point. Totally recommend this place hands down. No complaints here.

Interesting new takes on Lebanese food. Had a delicious lunch of kibbe made with steak instead of lamb, but wonderful just the same. Baba ganoosh was good, but my favorite had to be the little cheese sticks wrapped in filo. Nice big room, and not crowded for lunch.

Philly has always had better restaurants than DC.  But I used to take solace in the fact that DC was good at throwing a great Happy Hour.   That was.. until I went to Tria's Happy Hour.  We ducked in to avoid the rain - we stay to enjoy the wonderful food, wine, beer and appetizers. We waddled out stuffed and happy and best of all... I could tell my mom that I went to "Sunday School".

The closest thing to Roscoe's Chicken and Waffles I have had (yes, I'm a huge fan). Ordered the Rev Al Sharpton - the basic chicken and waffles with dark meat. The Fried chicken was solid - the quality doesn't blow you away, but moist and tender, with generous portions. I was a little disappointed with the waffles - it was (like the chicken, bigger portion than roscoes, for those who know. but,) a little dry, and nothing to write home about. because clearly, i do that... Still I love chicken and waffles, and I love the vibe of the place, and beggars can't be choosers, so I would definitely come back to this place. Lastly, what's a great soul food joint without a sunrise to top it off. Fruit punch and lemonade mixed to perfection. Add some Frank's Red hot sauce, and you're golden ;)

I came here with my family after a very large brunch and really was not hungry. The waiter came to take our order and I told him I don't know what I want so he took everyone's order then came back to me. I told him I am not sure as of the moment and he said "um ok. so what do I do?" well, you are the waiter.. he seemed very confused as to what to do/why he is there. The service was overall slow and it is so dark in the restaurant. The thing that really bothered me was that they kept playing sets from Ultra and EDC. I mean, that's just really not fitting for this restaurant. Imagine sitting with your parents and there is a beat playing and all it keeps saying is "I don't pop molly I rock tom ford" Kind of strange. I tried the bok choy and the tom yam soup. They were good but nothing special

The first time I had this chicken I was starting a diet.  Well the diet went to the wind and I had to hide some of the chicken in my pocket so my sister wouldn't see me eating it later when I got home.  LOL.
Just stopped by for happy hour and enjoyed some suds and one sausage.  Good, but nothing out of this world. The atmosphere seems good and worth coming back to for a whole dinner.
Really good prices for such a big falafel sandwich! It will fill you up/perfect for a good quick bite in the area.

My wife and I went to ULC for our 2nd Anniversary. The food was absolutely amazing I would definitely recommend the tenderloin and my wife loved the lobster. Our waiter was very helpful and told us about the history of the building which added to the experience. The drinks were great as well. The only reason ULC doesn't get 5 stars is due to the ambiance, which was a little stuffy, nothing exciting for a couple in their 20's and a older crowd. All and all I would recommend this place for the food, but don't expect a trendy fun atmosphere.

This is a really nice place, peaceful atmosphere, well lit and decorated. It could be a friends' outing or romantic dinner. It has a modern feel but amazing Chinese food. We shared a spicy stirfry (topped with sweet potato, squid, beef tripe, shrimp) and 2 orders of the crabmeat soup dumplings. HEAVENLY. The dumplings are really juicy and taste exactly like they do in Shanghai. And be careful with spice level. If you order medium spicy for the stir fry bowl, it is spicy, spicier than your buffalo wings. Lychee iced tea is great, but I only got it because they didn't have bubble tea today :( FYI: the cursive r in the title on their exterior could easily be mistaken for a z. Don't worry, it's definitely Sakura you're walking into, not Sakuza. They do take the rare Discover credit card, and the receipt includes tip denominations for 15% and all that. I didn't see any parking lot, but it's pretty close to the Convention Center so there are public lots galore. My only complaints: the teapot is a bit old and spilled tea too easily, and water has to be requested (altho, granted, this is Chinatown we talking abt, where ice water is not a thing). All in all, a great place if you want authentic chinese or your good old general tso's haha.

I haven't had anything other than their breakfast offerings but the place makes good breakfast sandwiches. It's also awesome that you can customize them. I prefer to top my bacon, egg and cheese with a hash brown and grilled onions-so fucking bomb, especially when you're hungover. It's also not crazy expensive like some other places in the area.

Tiny little crepe joint off of South Street. I came here with a friend for brunch. There usually is a wait, so be prepared. It's a bit pricey for the amount you get, but it's worth it for the French bistro experience. They have crepe suggestions or you can make-your-own, which I recommend. I've had a mix of the savory crepes, always wanting to return for a sweet one.

We had a Friday night reservation and were seated promptly at the most perfect window table. I really loved the charming, somewhat "oldschool" vibe here. We started with the charcuterie plate: didn't do much for me. My bf had the NY Strip: seasoned and cooked perfectly; highlight of the meal. I had the Roasted chicken: very moist, but slightly bland. We finished with the apple pie: hard to go wrong there. Our waiter was somewhat awkward and not very personable, but he was attentive enough. So, I guess in short, loved the space and the charm, food and service was just A-OK (hence the 3 stars).

The Maine style lobster roll was great, and at $16 is a real value considering how much lobster they pile in. The roll was buttery, crispy and delicious. The fries were also really good. It's a little awkward that where you purchase the food and where you eat the food aren't in the same building, but that would have only been really annoying if it was raining. It's worth the trip out to Red Hook for sure!

Living in Harrison for a year and Kearny for 2, this the best place for pizza and Italian food for delivery in both areas.   Just know that on any given night, delivery averages about 45 minutes. If you get pizza by the slice, their slices are huge and worth the price which is still super cheap even if adding toppings.  (They add toppings to plain slices and do not have any white pizza by the slice) Entrees come with salad and bread and you can choose between penne, spaghetti or linguine pasta.  Love the 3 meat sauce with spaghetti, salmon picatta, and chicken marsala. Meatball parm sub is consistently good. If you like disco fries I would opt for the gravy on the side, although I find it a bit runny/watered down.  Pizza fries are better.

I came to Maysville for an early Sunday dinner. It was quiet and the place looked gorgeous.  The lighting and decor are warm and inviting so I was in a great mood.  Then I had the food.  We had the brussel sprouts, the grits with ham, poached egg duck confit and the crispy duck entree.  The brussel sprouts were just flakes that were way too saturated in oil.  They were also remarkably bland.  The grits were also bland except for the ham on top, which was waaaaay too salty and overpowering for the creamy grits.  The dish tasted like a mixture of pure butter and salt.  No other discernible flavors could be taken away from it  The poached egg duck confit was good and the crispy duck was also good, but nothing spectacular.  These two were nothing outside of just basic and good.  This restaurant has so much hype and I visited due to its inclusion in Eater NY's Essential 38 AND Heat Map and was sorely disappointed.  Not worth the money.

Wish I could give this place more than 5 stars bc I absolutely love it!! I've only tried their breakfast options but there was nothing I ordered that I didn't heavily enjoy. My favorite so far has been their omelets and the Graso dish platter. When ordering an omelet I always opt for egg whites and my favorite is Omelette #3 with ham, cheddar, mushroom and broccoli. The omelets come with either a hash brown or home fries. Both options are fantastic. It also comes with toast but I don't usually get it. I've also tried their iced coffee and it tastes freshly brewed every time. The Graso dish platter comes with any style eggs, bacon or sausage, home fries or hash browns, and toast. So affordable and soooo delicious!!! This is my go-to breakfast spot hands down!

Excellent!  Found this place on yelp and was not disappointed.  Everything came out as a small dish and was hearty and delicious.  We had the meatballs, beat salad and the uovo pizza.   All were fabulous.  We were early for our reservation so we say at the chefs table; ie bar behind the cooks.  So enjoyed watching them prepare all of the delicious meals.  Great spot to eat

A great location but skip what they call a "salad bar". The food is okay but the work ethic between husband and wife is off putting. The husband is friendly, kind and mindful. The wife, who runs the front counter, has been abrasive and easy to scare away customers. If I didn't have to deal with HER moods I'd enjoy the scene. Skip this and try Logan's a few doors down. Quality food, service with a smile...all genuine.

Runner & Stone, where were you when i lived a few blocks away, and there was NOTHING on 3rd Avenue? I guess I'm glad you're here now, even though it's a trek to get to you. And trek I did for lunch one day. The sandwiches are pretty good--fresh, inventive, and flavorful (the squash fritter one almost tasted like a doughnut!)--though I wished they were a bit bigger. As for pastries, the brownie was more like fudge than a brownie--skip it, unless that's your thing--but the lemon poppy cake was fantastic

Let's keep this simple; this is not a food blog. * If don't want to wait, then make a reservation. * If you think it might be too expensive, stay home. * If you're coming here for brunch lower those expectations, its brunch duh! * If you think this place could be douchie, there are plenty of places to eat in Brooklyn. That being said, keep an open mind and just enjoy the delicious food.

Used to work down the street from this spot and never even noticed it, it's that small.  Went on a Saturday night with my mom around 6:00 and was seated right away.  We were both offered a complimentary glass of wine while we looked over the menu.  We wound up splitting a salad and each ordering pasta.  Good food, good service.  Couple months later we had a family dinner with 13 people in the back of the restaurant.  It was a tight squeeze but we all were able to fit and the service was good.  The place can get loud b/c it is smaller but all in all it is a good spot.
Dumplings are freshly made with very little msg and maximum taste.

Delicious, authentic, cheap, and friendly. I was walking by today and stopped in for a chocolate banana crepe ($6). It was after closing time, but no problem -- we were seated and set up with two coffees. Highly highly recommended.

Stopped in for ice cream take out last night, as I have done periodically over the past 15 years, although havent gone in a while . Was pleasantly surprised at the service I recieved, Yound ladies at counter very polite & courteous, Manager Ceasar very helpful, and friendly, surprisingly knew the special touches we like (no marshmello sauce, extra peanut butter etc) the ice cream was fresh & made right. Restaurant clean & bathrooms in order. We also love to come after nine for half price appetizers.

Stopped in here for lunch today, got the shrimp and avocado wrap, excellent.  White peach sangria was good, refreshing, not very peachy, but had plenty of booze-soaked fruit floating about in it. The Bayou is cool, classy New Orleans, think elegant Garden District not sleazy Storyville.  Exposed brick walls mixed with wainscoting,g audy chandeliers, movie posters of Marlon Brando and Vivian Leigh, bathrooms named Stella and Stanley, and an antique-framed portrait resembling a Frenchified version of Pope's THE RAPE OF THE LOCK.   The lamb and the seafood jambalaya makes me want to come back.

Simply delicious! Best wings around,.. AND CLAMS?! Pfft!! My favorites! They have garlic bleu cheese *rolls eyes, pats belly* Mhmmm - I inquired, it's homemade! Seating is very limited, few tables up front, bar stools & 1 table party room (~15ppl) in the back.

So, I've known Bed-Stuy for years, but we've just recently started dating. Our love story typical - girl meets hood, girl falls hard for hood, girl gives hood space to find itself... SUD is Bed-Stuy after a mentorship program - authentic (with its charming exposed brick interior, faux-fireplace and neighborhood feel), confident (with a lean menu of about 17 items), and personable (with what seemed to be a three man team - 1 bar, 1 kitchen, 1 front house). What you need to know: ***We walked in at 6:45 to a empty room (I consider this a plus, but some may not). ***Greeted by a friendly host/waiter who let us choose our seating. ***Host/waiter was very knowledgeable about the menu ***Selected crostini sampler - delicious and is the number one reason I'll return.  We ordered two off menu and the crostini of the day - salty, savory, goodness. ***I can't remember exactly what I ordered but it was tasty ***I CAN remember exactly what my BFF ordered - black ink pasta with calamari - it     was yummy and I will order it myself upon my return. The wine selection was decent, but I'm no connoisseur.  However, what totally blew me away was how reasonably priced the entire meal was.  I'd give the food a a solid 3.5 but I happily round my entire experience to a 4. I shall return. As for me and Bed-Stuy...well generally "my taste is, a little high maintenance," but I will say SUD has our budding relationship off to a pretty poetic start.
Not fantastic. Sadly, they're among the few pizza places that deliver to my area, so sometimes I have to settle for them.

A solid addition to the burgeoning Bowery boulevard. First, the kinks.  Albeit a quite busy Wednesday evening, it shouldn't take the bar 10 minutes to fulfill an order.  The drinks were good at least, but that wait time was silly.  Also, my martini came in a small glass with a tiny side carafe (on ice) for a self-controllable refill.  If this added a few minutes to the delivery time, it should be scrapped immediately.  Just give me a full glass with a full drink, or charge me less and give me a small martini.  A cute, but impractical idea.   Also, some tables are WAY too close together.  It's NYC, I get it.  You have to pull tables out to get in, I get it.  But in this case it felt like we were dining with, rather than next to, the people next to us.  Their conversations were interfering with ours, and both tables next to us made comments like, "I guess I should eat with the other arm" (to avoid bumping). But, S+P deserves 4 stars on the merits of its food, service, and ambiance.  They've done a nice job with the lighting, and creating a cozy equine theme (a bit gimmicky, but so what).  The service was just a little overbearing - I felt at times the waiter was trying to sell to us, rather than pleasantly facilitate our order.  But he was working hard and the the dishes were well-timed.   The food is what really solidifies the 4-star rating.  For such a popular area, the Nolita/Noho zone of NYC is really not a mecca for great food.  Most restaurants around here are average at best, so I think the S+P effort stands out.  I'd call it "satisfying" rather than "amazing", but I mean that in a complimentary way. The oysters we had were very fresh and delicious.  The mushroom mousse pot was a tad too sweet, but I gobbled it up with enjoyment.  My wife's branzino (not well regarded in the recent NYT review) we found to be quite good.  A bit light on flavor, but prepared well and altogether pleasing.  My steak (the bone-in NY strip) was served pre-sliced - a concept that's grown on me over the years with bone-in cuts - cooked to my liking, with a round, beefy flavor. We shared the almond apple cake for dessert - this was average at best.  Maybe we should've gone with the NYT reviewer on this course. I think S+P will be successful, especially with a little fine tuning that is sure to come with time.

You have to rate a restaurant for what it is, so I'm judging Ivy Noodle as a cheap, quick-serve Chinese-style diner. If I was rating it as a proper full-priced Chinese restaurant, I'd probably be giving it a 2.5. And if I was rating it as a standard Chinese take out, I'd be giving it a 4.5. What puts this place as a cut above the run of the mill take out joint is their full, clean seating area with both booth and bar stool arrangements. Although decor is nothing to shake your hoo-has at, it is a better look than what the prices would suggest, and certainly not as dingy as it could be. The owners/staff are extra friendly and good with babies, sickly old people, and foreigners. Our server was playful with my son (baby), tolerant of my wife (French), and helpful with my mother (sickly). In fact, my mother told our server that she couldn't eat much due to an upset stomach. So the nice lady recommended a kanji dish (mushy rice) and said that she would put some ginger in it. Afterwards, she came around to ask my mother if her stomach was feeling better. Awesome gal. As for the food, it's perfectly adequate. By American standards, the portions are small but correct for the price. As for the culinary standard, I feel it's a step up from generic take out. It has a homemade and somewhat authentic quality to it. I ordered the teriyaki chicken rice bowl and thought it was delicious but nowhere near enough to satiate my appetite (6 ft, 185 lbs). Luckily my wife has a small appetite, and I was permitted to finish her shrimp dumpling noodles (which we rated "pretty good"). We also ordered some teriyaki sticks as an appetizer, but unfortunately those were a little dry and stringy. On the whole, worth it for the price if you have a small-to-medium-sized appetite.

I've had the Veggie Pork and the Veggie Chicken Vietnamese sandwich and salad. I love them both; but i prefer the veggie pork. Tip: get the salad to take home and make sandwiches with your own rolls, you'll end up with 2-3 for the price of one... We had a bubble tea one time that was bitter and just kind of "off" tasting. Its a little cramped quarters. You can order mild, medium, and spicy which is great!

I've had 3 dinners here, all under very different circumstances, and all 3 have been  Unforgettable Experiences. I love everything about this place. First, the location - it's tucked away in a little enclave in the West Village, and it's hard not to get excited when you're standing outside the entrance, eavesdropping on the intriguing buzz from inside beckoning you to enter. Take the few steps down, swing open the door, and you'll be instantly greeted by the refreshing sound of drunk, merry people, as well as a long bar top that feels sexy, rustic, and straight out of Spain. Or some place like that. I've never been to Spain so I could be making this up. From there, you can either sit on the first floor, which is a fine option, though I'd say try to be seated upstairs (Alta does mean 'tall', why stick to the ground dammit) so you can soak in the beauty of the decor while gazing out over the balcony at the diners below. Upstairs also feels much more intimate if you're on a date or with a friend looking to catch up in a quieter environment. If you're in a group, though, downstairs is definitely the place to be. Cocktails - they may be slightly pricey, but Alta makes these bad boys STRONG. The Jalapeno Margarita makes me grateful that I was born, and the potency of the Spanish Manhattan is great if you're a dude looking to get over any first-date-jitters, or if you're a tough ass girl that likes her Maker's Mark (in that case, call me). The sangria is supposed to be mysteriously potent though I haven't had a chance to try it yet. Food - here we go. Below are some must-order dishes, and no matter what your tastes are, no matter how nasty you think some of the ingredient descriptions sound, no matter what life-threatening allergy you think you have, you simply must get the following: -Fried Goat Cheese with Lavender-infused Honey - a less manly-sounding appetizer has never been conceived. But one bite and you'll squeal, regardless of your gender. It's phenomenal. -Bacon Wrapped Dates & Olives -Warm Vegetable Salad - I HATE ordering salads at exciting places like this, but my companion insisted. I stubbornly refused to share any of it with her, then got curious. I had a bite, peed myself, and then almost got broken up with because I was battling so intensely for the last bite. -PEI Mussels with lobster sauce, lemon, and cilantro -- get some bread to mop up the sauce, it's fantastic. -Skirt Steak w/chimichurri & potato puree -- shared this with a friend, couldn't stop thinking about it all evening. Then I hit my 4th Spanish Manhattan and forgot everything about this dish except that I absolutely loved it. One negative - service could use some work. The food itself comes out blazingly fast, but the servers haven't been the friendliest lot...they're JUST nice enough to acquit themselves, but nothing memorable that could help make an outstanding meal truly phenomenal. Regardless, can't wait to go back and try some of the other dishes on their delicious menu. Overall, a must-visit.

We  Diners, Drive-ins and Dives! A couple weeks ago we went on a lunch date to this  Cuban Triple D spot and we cannot rave enough about this Corona hole in the wall.  The Vaca Frita was literally the best beef we have ever eaten.  See what we ate here: goo.gl/ha5uMY

food: onion soup - bland, lacks rich caramelized onion flavor, beet salad - decent but nothing to rave about, steak sandwich & frites - best thing out of the whole meal.   service: okay probably won't go back

Hey. It's PAT'S. What do you want? One of the things I miss and crave the most from home, and one of my guaranteed stops when I'm home for a visit. As many have mentioned, it's right across the street from Genos, and those of us from Philly are pretty loyal to one or the other. For me, Pat's steaks are just more flavorful, better made and more delicious. I also think their fries are better. And they serve Coke. And, when you look at the two businesses, it should be apparent which one is better. Genos must need all that neon for a reason. #Justsayin. One note to all of the reviews about rude behavior: It's part of the thing. Call it ambiance or whatever, it's part of the experience of getting a cheesesteak in South Philly. At Pat's you are expected to be ready to order, to know HOW to order and to not hold the line up. If you can do those three things, you will get what you ordered lickety split and enjoy a delicious meal. It aint fancy, but it's not supposed to be. If you don't like it, go to the Four Seasons and leave the rest of us alone. If you are new or just visiting and are nervous, that's understandable. We're not unreasonable. So ask the people around you while you wait in line. Or follow my handy guide for newbies... 1. There are TWO lines. One for cheesesteaks and one for fries/sodas. You can't get fries in the cheesesteak line. You can't get steaks in the fries line. It is best to bring at least two people. The cheesesteak line is almost always longer, so the person in charge of fry ordering should wait until their partner is fairly well along in the cheesesteak line before stepping up to the window so that you both come out with food at the same time. 2. Fries. You can and should get cheese fries. They are drenched in Cheez Wiz and are AWESOME.... the type you have to eat with a fork and the type where there's a big pool of cheese down in the bottom of the cup. 3. CASH only. Don't ask about credit cards. You'll look stupid. Like the Soup Nazi on Seinfeld, it's best to have your cash out when you order. 4. Ordering. Do it right. They have gotten a bit more lenient in recent years, but there was a time in which a bad orderer would be sent to the back of the line. You say two words and two words only: the type of cheese followed by WIT or WITOUT (ie, with or without fried onions). Yes, you can get other cheese and other stuff but I highly recommend Wiz Wit for your first time out (see next point below). The only other words you need are numbers (as in "TWO Wiz Wits"). 5. Wanna be branded as an outsider? Order something other than Wiz on your steak. Yes, there are other cheese options, but orders with Provolone are like announcing you're not from around here. You traveled all the way to an odd corner in South Philly to sample a REAL Philly cheesesteak. So suck it up and order a REAL steak -- WIZ WIT is all you need to say. 6. Tables. Red picnic tables line the sidewalk all the way around Pat's. Ideally you should bring a third person whose job it will be to troll the area for an available table and snag it while your other two people do the line thing in point #1. I've gone to Pat's at all hours of the day -- steaks for midnight snacks, steaks for breakfast, and it's extremely rare to go there and find a bunch of empty tables. At the very best, it's not jam-packed. So having a table scout can pay off big time during busy times. 7. Parking. Pat's and Genos are located pretty much right in the middle of a neighborhood, separated by a neighborhood baseball field. The only option is street parking. It's tight and hard to find sometimes. If you suck at parallel parking, bring someone who knows what they're doing. Not the place for rookies. Or take a cab from a safer locale. That's it! Good luck and happy cheesesteak!!!

We walked by one Saturday and on impulse, decided to give this place a try. Fortunately, we were very early in respect to dinner so we managed to get seats at the bar (tables were booked up for the night). After getting drinks, we ordered the Balut, Oxtail and Sigsig - all of which we'll quite delicious and well executed. Compared to various other Filipino restaurant we have tried in the city (traveling out to Queens to do so), these dishes seem much more flavorful in terms of spicing while lower in general fat content. I am definitely a fan of the food... And the incredibly friendly staff who skillfully worked the bar while walking us through foreign elements of our dishes.

Great soup dumplings. I was ecstatic when I got on a Cathay Pacific flight and they served them in business class. Made the 20-hour flight that much better. I've had the other entrees here and it's pretty standard. Go for the soup dumplings.

WE were in the area and some friends recommended that we try this new pizza resturante.WE were suprised to find that they had  a great variety of  food chioices on their menu. The service was friendly and fast. I had the lasanga which was made perfectly. I love potato croquets ( ponzarotti ) they wre great i actually had them wrap 3 more to take home with me. The prices wre very reasonable. I would recommend this place

Best and most popular dim sum place in Philly. I've been to the old location twice and this was my first time at the new place. The décor is much more modern and the place itself is a lot larger. If the old place was a scooter, the new place is a train. Food was great like every other time..had the Xiao long baos, toro cakes, shrimp dumplings and the shu mai. Service was mediocre, wait staff was extremely attentive but did not look happy or genuine - just like 95% of other Chinese places (don't worry, I'm Chinese.)
the 1st place i have ever tried chicken skin & pork belly...this cant be good for you. avoid the sautee shrimp w/ chili sauce, not good To R: I never got your text!

This is one of the best meals I've ever had.  Israeli cuisine, for the win! The space instantly transports you to Jerusalem, it's so lovely.  The lights, the stone work, the stained glass all create an atmosphere somewhere far away from Philly.  The fact that it's raised on a hillside helps support the illusion. The menu is predominately small plates meant for sharing, and it's very well curated.  Before I even had a chance to see what I could eat, our server asked if we had any dietary restrictions.  Why yes, I do!  When I told him I was vegan, he was so happy to accommodate me, it gave me that warm tingly feeling.  So often, I feel like I putting people out, but he made it his job to make sure I had a fantastic meal, and that I did. Sam and I agree on very few things when it comes to food, but our mutual love of hummus will bond us for life.  We opted for the classic Hummus-Tehina with laffa and were absolutely floored.  I could wax poetically about that luscious, creamy hummus and the fresh, warm bread for an hour if you let me, but I'll spare you.  It was the best. Next we shared the fried cauliflower, which was excellent.  It wasn't heavy like you'd expect something fried to be, but light, crispy, and hot, with that meaty texture you can get when cauliflower is treated right.  Instead of yogurt, our server suggested it be tossed with tehina, and it was great.  I love when a restaurant doesn't just leave things off to make it vegan, but reworks it a bit so you have an equally delicious dish. Then Sam and I went our separate ways, and I had the spiced eggplant while he opted for the kofte.  I don't usually seek out eggplant and I tend not to cook with it at home, but this was spectacular.  Grilled eggplant topped with a creamy garlic tehina and harissa, over black lentils, it was so flavorful with just the right amount of spice.  I cleaned my plate and was so sad when it was over. Sam enjoyed his kofte, which looked like two meatballs over top a thick, chunky orange sauce.  While I had more than enough to eat, he probably could've used another plate of food.  What can I say, veggies and fiber go a long way! You might've noticed that each of my dishes featured tehina, but by some magic, each presentation was completely different from the last.  While my calcium intake skyrocketed by the influx of sesame, my taste buds were kept entertained. My server warned me that my options would be limited, but I had such a feast, and I didn't even eat everything I could have!  If anyone in your party has a dietary restriction, bring them here.  The service and the food will make everyone so happy.

Have you ever thought to yourself, "Gee, wouldn't it be great if Devil's Alley had a slightly expanded menu & beer list but wasn't in as good of a location?"  If you have, Smokin' Betty's is the place for you.   On my first trip I ordered the Tur-Duck-En Burger (with orange-cranberry relish) which I had been eagerly anticipating for some time.  It wasn't mind-blowing, it was merely reminiscent of a very high quality turkey burger; you are likely to notice more of difference in color and texture than of flavor.  John Madden is rolling in his grave.*  The french fries tasted as if they were frozen.  The grilled vegetables--fennel, onion, zucchini if I recall correctly--were also kind of lackluster.  Sadly, this meal was a disappointment and it led me to hold off with my review until a follow-up visit so as not to let it sour my overall impression. Today's visit turned out slightly better, though there were some minor complications.  Like the Tur-duck-en Burger, I have also put serious thought into ordering the Lamb Burger.  I made an attempt but they were all out at lunch, so I had to go with the Betty Burger (with pickled jalapeno, grilled corn, smoked mozzarella and "mojo sauce") as my back-up.  This was actually quite good, possibly better than the Devil Burger.  The baked beans, though, appeared just to be beans in barbecue sauce, and they did not even begin to approach the beans at Devil's Alley.  The onion rings, like the fries, are almost certainly frozen. I've been here twice now and I'm generally indifferent towards this versus Devil's Alley.  Its nice to have a few more solid beers to choose from--the Blond Betty reminds me of Flying Fish Exit 4, the two or three others I've had we likewise pretty good--and additional menu options but from what I've tried the food falls just short.  Overall, I'd probably stick to the more established location for the time being. * Not actually dead.  Yet.

Came back today for lunch and brought a few colleagues. Had the Ashak again, knowing that it would be good again, and it was!! Ordered their lamb korma; tender meat and flavorful. It's a stew with lentils and they serve it with pita bread. My colleagues enjoyed their food as well.

Typical trendy NYC eatery with trendy mac-n-cheese and trendy long waits. I've been here 3-4 times, but never eaten inside. Even when I was home for spring break, we sat outside for dinner in 50-deg weather. I can't remember if there were heat lamps... are those a West Coast thing? Cafeteria is pretty much an upscale diner. You don't come here for their sushi. I got a lamb dish once that was literally melt-off-the-bone wonderful. When I took my brother here, he sniffed at the prices but couldn't stop raving about the avocado in his sandwich. The fries are good. And yes, the mac here does live up to the hype - but maybe just once. The mac attack flavors are great (mmm truffle), but they're so thick and cheesy they're hard to finish. The wait is insanely long. If you didn't already wait 30 minutes to be seated, you will wait another 20-30 minutes for your food to arrive. I've eaten here at both busy and off-peak times and the food wait is just as long. And finally, the most memorable aspect of Cafeteria for me - this one cute gay waiter actually recognized me on my third visit! And it wasn't like I went three times in one week either. If that doesn't scream fatty status, I don't know what does.

We needed to grab a quick bite to eat before a show at the Wellmont Theater (which by the way is a nicely renovated!) so we decided to try Sushi Hana and sit at the sushi bar.  The restaurant had a reasonable crowd and didn't seem overly busy so we thought it was a good choice to get in and out.   Well, that's where the problems began.  Firstly, the servers were literally hovering over us.  I think mostly because they were waiting for their sushi orders to be made.  But c'mon people, there are customers sitting at the counter.  Give us some space!  The one waiter took our soup order which we didn't see for almost 20 minutes.  We were hungry, curtain time was getting closer and closer and there were waiters everywhere with no food in sight.  Secondly, when we needed one of them, they all just miraculously disappeared.  Was I still thinking this was a good choice?  Hmm, second thoughts were beginning to creep in... Luckily, the sushi was surprisingly good!  The lone sushi chef, Tony,  was working like a mad man.  He must have made 30 sushi rolls all within a very small amount of time and we just watched in amazement.  I can't say the fish was of the best quality, but Tony sure made them tasty (try the Spider-Man roll!!).  We ate a truck load of sushi all in about 10 minutes.  One thing to note:  the sushi menu at the bar didn't match the regular menu at all.  Half of the items were missing on the bar menu which made it a bit confusing.  Luckily, Tony knew exactly what he was doing and what we wanted.   I doubt I will ever be back here again but thanks to their saving grace, Tony, it turned out to be a decent dining experience.

My husband and I came here last Friday. We ordered the potato and pancetta caramelized onions, applle and goat cheese pizza as our appetizer. Well, I know pizza is not an appetizer, but my husband insisted to order, so...Anyways, we really like the pizza! It's very different from all the other pizzas I've ever had! There wasn't too much gost cheese, so it wasn't very filling like pizzas in New York or Chicago. It was very special! I ordered Penne garlic scape cream, pine nuts and seasoned breacumbs as entree. The pasta was very well cooked! Quite chewy but not too hard! Love the texture, but I thought the vegetables in the pasta was a little too salty. My husband got the pork butt milanese, argula, balsamic pickled onion, and tamato. It was actually a large piece of fried pork chop. My husband and I both like it a lot! The pork butt was not dry at all, but I wish it came with some sauce! We also ordered the baby jesus cake was also good! It was also something very different from the cakes you usually get from a restaurant or bakery. Service was a little slow at the time, but it was a good experience overall. I think I'll be back!

This place is awesome.  I started out with a beer and clearly realized that I needed to switch to Bourbon.  We had a group of about 5 for a buddy who actually used to work there and they were great hosts. The head chef is a really nice guy and super talented.  The food has a great mix of flavors and didn't have one thing that wasn't above par.   This is a great flagship for the Flatiron area that isn't well known yet for fine dining.  This isn't Golden Corral so bring your wallet, but will be well worth the expense. Hope this helps!

This spot is equal parts good food and romance.  The decor is beautiful and the service is very good.  We came here on Valentine's Day, so it was packed.  However, we still got our food on time and didn't have to order from a prix fixe menu (always good). The menu features something for everyone, so with that said, I wouldn't consider Balthazar an overly-French restaurant.  Don't shy away just because you don't like French food.   I had the bar steak, which was awesome.  Pretty much everything we had that night was exceptional.  The only downside (which isn't really a downside when dining out unless you don't get what you pay for) is that Balthazar is expensive.  Come for a special occasion and bring lots of money. Tip:  Great place for spotting celebrities.

I LOVE this place!!! I always order 6-8 tapas to split among the table and I always leave full and happy! I would suggest the goat cheese fritters, datiles, papitas and pequino rellenas. All are amazing and a must have when I'm there. They are BYOB so bring your favorite wine and have a great time!
Always a great meal.  I have eaten there since they opened  and I always enjoy seeing the owners and workers  all are very nice.

A short wait at times, maybe 15 minutes. The meatballs were pretty good but it was the mash potatoes that hit home. So delicious. It's a very tight and cozy place, but it lends itself to the little sweet town shop atmosphere. Would definitely come again!

Great place for a real homemade breakfast. French toast was amazing. My boyfriend had the Ham and cheese omlette and just loved it. Our server Angelina was perfect. Very friendly and was there when we needed anything.

Shawarma (when cooked through...sometimes they don't want to wait). Baba sandwiches are great. The chicken kebab sandwich is EXCELLENT. But watch out for the extremely deadly hot sauce. All the pastries are excellent. Go across the street for a good lady finger too.

Modo Mio is one of those places that you have to find out about from friends or you won't even know it exists. It's almost like a hidden and well guarded secret that you don't want to let out to the public because it will get overwhelmed and abused. Seriously if people out in the open only knew how good this place really is you'd never be able to get there. Right now it's not so easy - better call a week ahead to make your reservation! If this is not enough for you then know the food is absolutely top notch unbelievable. It's the restaurant you take your best friends or the hottest date to if you really want to impress them. All that without having to rob a bank because for what you get the prices are vert friendly. So is the staff. I went twice already and I am most definitely coming back for all special occasions!

My wife and I were so excited to have been able to get a table here last minute during a recent weekend in NYC. Unfortunately Pinto didn't even come close to our expectations based on the review we had read. The crab cake was dry and mealy and our entrees were less than stellar. The dumplings werent bad and in fact were the best thing we ordered. It was a bummer since we expected so much better!

So good! The house is very quaint, ingredients are excellent (organic ingredients, local meats), and incredibly accomodating. The half hen was so tasty and my vegetarian friend was so pleased with her main course! Veggie friendly! The desserts are a must try, especially the goat cheese / cheesecake!

It's like eating in a cafeteria. You pick what you like and pay by the pound or get the ones that are pre-packaged. The food is good. This is the place you stop by when  you crave Korean and don't want to wait. Place is packed with people and the buffet selection is only available during peak lunch/dinner times.

Six or seven months ago I would have agreed this was worthy of four stars but now they just seem kind of spaced out. Because the vegetarian options are limited, I stick to brunch options here. My staple is the breakfast quesadilla which is appropriately proportioned and comes with a side of home fries. However, today we didn't remember it came with the side of potatoes and ordered extra. Our server did not take any opportunity to alert us of the included sides, nor was it indicated on the menu, and thus we had way too much spuds and took the side home. (To be eaten when and with what, I don't know) Also I alerted the staff that there was no real sugar on the table only artificial sweetener. Because my cappuccino was a bit bitter I wanted to sweeten it up a bit but was left staring at pink, yellow and blue chemical  packets. The woman who I alerted briskly and doubtfully took the sugar bowl and scrounged through it like she was looking for lost treasure. Finally agreeing that no there was no sugar, she snatched the bowl from our neighbors table with no excuse me, apology or thank you to them. I realize that these are little gripes which in no way reflect the quality of the meal. However, a little attention to customer service can make or break the experience. Oh, and did I mention we waited forever for our change. Yes, in fact we would like our change. You thought all that was your tip? You know what they say about assuming.

Avacado fries were totally totally amazing.  I once went there and ordered these "to go".  Got some weird looks from the staff, but totally worth it as I scarfed them down when walking down the street.

I came here on a Friday night and there were still tables available, which was great! I found the place to be a tad loud even though it wasn't full. To start, I got a baby arugula with beets and feta salad. It was a very refreshing salad, but it also isn't a very original idea. Enjoyed it nonetheless. As the main, I got the Fettuccine with mussels, clams and shrimp in a shellfish ragu. The dish was alright. I found the slices of garlic in the pasta sauce overwhelming every time it was in my biteful of pasta, I wished they were smaller pieces. The homemade fettucine was enjoyable, but not as good as other homemade pasta I've had. And the sauce was slightly fishy, but tolerable. It was a good experience, but I've had better Italian food.
Its one of my favorite place! The food is definitely really good, the staff really nice! I love it!! Un de mes endroit préfère! La nourriture est super bonne, le service est très bien! J'adore!
Had the hash browns with eggs and pecan pancakes, was fresh and delicious! The place had a log cabin feel to it. Found a new breakfast spot!

this restaurant is a gem and a work of love. Marc Forgione consistently deliver a great dining experience worth of the best restaurants in new york. this one is really one of my top in new york for the intimate rooms with a gentle buzz but not a funeral parlor. very knowledgeable waiters who can really talk their way out of my insidious questions, the food is a twist of American food and a more modern approach such as the hamachi tartar always exceptional, the lobster chili and the pecan dessert's voluptuous. too long for listing all my favorites, it is almost all the menu.

Arrived on a Friday afternoon to a long darkish bar filled with old men watching soap operas and then old westerns.  To be specific it was General Hospital. History buffs will enjoy the all wooden phone booths just past the sign for "telephones, ladies, and mens restrooms."  The bartender was friendly and served us some cold brews with a smile. We stayed for 2 each then headed on our way. Yes, there is a digital jukebox but we dare not interrupt GH or the westerns. Not a place we'd feel compelled to come back to but glad we stopped in and visited once.

Awesome brunch here. The venue is pretty spacious for typical brunch places. Came here on a Sunday with a friend and got a seat right away. We tried the pancakes and the breakfast burrito. Both were very satisfying as I was craving them for the longest time.

Awesome pizza! Went here with my husband and two friends and shared three pies. Some different wonderful flavors but also traditional styles as well. You might have to wait, but its worth it. Good service, great meal and reasonable prices!

Years later, the Manor maintains its upscale and elegant banquet hall feeling.  This is still a quality spot for holding a formal dinner or other occasion.   We came back recently to hold a friend's birthday dinner (they also offer a buffet dinner section that requires nicer-than-casual attire).  It was a real success!  With tax and tip, we each forked over $60, and this included the vast buffet selection (including the steamed lobsters) and 4-5 tables of dessert heaven. Afterwards, we went upstairs to their "lounge" area and danced the night/calories away.  The DJ wasn't very good at playing our requests though.  Soft drinks and coffee/tea is included with the $60, but beware if you get what they deem as specialty drinks.  My capuccino ran me an extra $7. Their outdoor space is stunning and still remains elegant and classy for tons of special occasions: a romantic pre- or post-dinner stroll, wedding, engagement, etc.  You'll find it hard to believe you're in NJ.
